reviews.review_text: This very, very good.  I cooked this in the oven.  Placed all wet ingredients in large saucepan and added the juice of one lime.  While I brought this to a boil, I pan seared three large chicken breast in about 4 Tablespoons of olive oil, seasoned with a generous amount of salt and freshly cracked pepper.  Once seared on both sides for about 10 minutes total, I added the chicken breasts to the hot and boiling sauce.  I then put this in a 350 degree oven for 60 minutes.  I started brown rice on the oven top, and once it was done I added the cream cheese to the saucepan for the last 15 minutes.  Stirred well, and placed 1/2 of a chicken breast on the bed and rice and with sauce, and served.  It was delicious.  I can see substituting sour cream, or cream, or Velvetta for the cream cheese.  It is important to use a very flavorful salsa since most of the flavor will come from the salsa.  I used Green Mountain medium, but will use Clint's or Jardin's Medium Salsa next time.  This will be excellent with tortilla wrap as a left over or main course.

What a great, easy concept: black beans, corn, chicken and salsa. Classic! This is a wonderful base recipe that can be tweaked any way you like to suite your family's taste.   I could see right away that we would like it a bit spicier, and 8oz cream cheese sounded a bit too much for us.  I added a few cloves of garlic and an envelope of southwest marinade and halved the cream cheese.  I had read in the reviews that the sauce could be a bit thin and my experience with crockpot cooking bears this out on many recipes.  The sauce on this however was perfect.  One factor may be that my crockpot lid is missing and I used a similar corelle lid and so it was not as "tight" and probably allowed steam to escape and so reduced the sauce.  We really liked it.  I think it was just a tad too spicy for my kids so next time I might try the taco seasoning suggestion from some reviews, but all in all, for quick easy prep, good taste and family satisfaction, full marks!!  Thanks for a wonderful recipe!
note: to avoid tough chicken (some reviews complained of) be sure to stop it as soon as the chicken is done.

attributes.source_text: we would like it a bit spicier

reviews.review_text: As the recipe is- I most likely would have just given it 3 stars.. But I threw a LOT of add in's that made this a keeper for our household, thanks for giving me the backbone recipe to play with to alter to our liking.. I followed the recipe sorta until step 2.. I started out with 2 frozen chicken breast, I added 2-3 tbs. minced garlic, a dash or two of cayenne pepper, some Tony's seasoning salt, pretty sure I threw in some chili powder also, 1/2 cup of shredded yellow cheese, and the last hour I pulled all the chicken apart, using the side of the crock pot and 2 forks.. The first night I served it over Jasmine rice with salsa and sour cream as a garnish, the second night it had thickened up a bit, so I took 4 large flour tortilla's and placed 2 on  a cookie sheet, spread the chicken mixture over the tortilla, sprinkled cheese over the top and placed the remaining tortilla's on top. I baked them in the over at 350 for about 10-15 mins. Took em' out and cut them up like you would a pizza. Again using salsa and sour cream as a dipping sauce.. My kids actually liked the second way better than the first.. Bottom Line- this is a GREAT recipe that just needed a little spicin' up for my family's taste buds.. ;)

attributes.source_text: My kids actually liked the second way better than the first

reviews.review_text: We liked this recipe a lot.  It does require additional seasoning and depending on your crock pot/slow cooker, perhaps less cooking time.  My slow cooker cooks really hot and fast, so I have to cut back on the cooking time for everything.  I would love to have a slow cooker that I can set the temperature as well as a cut off time.  Mine only has low/high and 4/6/8/10 hour settings.<br/><br/>Modifications: I used thawed breasts and seasoned generously with Tony's cajun seasoning.  I can see where this would be VERY bland if you did not season the chicken.  Another VERY important thing: I used green salsa (Herdez brand-not chunky) instead of the usual red chunky salsa.  I think this made a lot of difference in the appearance.  It does not come out with a pink sauce if you use green salsa.  The thought of it being pink sort of turns me off. <br/><br/>We ate this on top of rice and also on flour tortillas and it was very tasty both ways.  Some fresh cilantro would be good on top of this too.  <br/><br/>Great leftovers!

In fairness to the original recipe, the ingredients I had on hand (and I really, really wanted to make this), were 'close', but I had to adapt it somewhat, due to MY pantry ingredients on hand. It still turned out simply delicious and hubby and I loved it. I had 3 good sized chicken breasts which I defrosted in the microwave, pan seared to almost cooked, then sliced them down a bit to quicken crockpot time due to a time issue, added a large can of refried black beans, cream corn, and salsa. I also threw in a package of low-sodium taco seasoning, some good shakes of hot sauce, as we like a bit of heat, did the 2 fork chicken shred method when the chicken became cooked and tender. Near the end, I added 4 wedges of Laughing Cow Light cheese and a couple of generous blobs of low-fat sour cream. Yummy! We will used what's left this evening as others have suggested for soft tacos or 'enchilada style', baked with enchilada sauce and cheese. I know I had to substitute close ingredients, but I always have more confidence with that when I read others as well. Thanks so much for sharing. Will make it again soon with the exact ingredients!

attributes.source_text: hubby and I loved it
when the chicken became cooked and tender

reviews.review_text: INCREDIBLE!!!  I used a jar of salsa verde and unfortunately I forgot to get corn, but it was still great, great, great.  Next time I will put in a tortilla and double the recipe so hopefully there will be leftovers.  I will make this again and again!  Thanks!*update*  6/23  I do make this a lot!  I usually now make it using a cooked chicken from the deli and I shred it myself.  While I'm shredding the chicken I allow the cream cheese to soften.  I place all the ingredients in a pan and cook it on the stove and it's ready in no time!  I will only make this using salsa verde.  When we made it with a red salsa we really didn't care much for the appearance or taste.  I also add cumin and chili powder to this. Sometimes I'll add just a bit of chicken broth to keep the chicken moist. (Only when I'm making it stovetop with pre-cooked chicken.)  We usually leave out the corn.  Most of the time we serve these in a tortilla, but we have made this in the crockpot and served with tortilla chips when we've had guests.  EVERYONE really, really loves this!!

attributes.source_text: served with tortilla chips when we've had guests
to keep the chicken moist

reviews.review_text:
This dish just BLEW ME AWAY!!! I could have fallen face down into the plate and inhaled til I died. The only change I made was to add 4oz. green chilies on top of the salsa. Served it over rice. I live alone, so this made a ton of food for one person, but I would have not cut back one ounce of anything. This is once that I look forward to eating leftovers til I explode. There will be lots of "replays" on this one for me, and I really can't imagine the leftovers lasting very long. Being a real bean lover, I'll probably add another can to all the leftovers, and will also add one at the beginning the next time I prepare this. The dish could surely stand up to the addition with no problem. Thanks for a real keeper!
Edit to add:  After eating all I could, I had quite a bit of leftovers.  I shredded the chicken and turned them into burrito filling.  The leftovers made 12 large burritos.  These are excellent from freezer to microwave, and no doubt work perfectly for OAMC!  These 12 large burritos make 24 meals for me...with the addition of a side salad of course.

This is such an easy and versatile recipe that is so delicious!  I thought that the recipe sounded like it needed some seasonings.  So before adding everything I seasoned to chicken with salt, pepper, onion powder, garlic powder, and a little cayenne.  I used aprox. 4 med. sized chicken breasts and added everthing together in the crock to cook for about 4 hours on high.  After throwing the cream cheese in, I probably cooked another 45 min. to an hour so it would completely melt and incorporate in the sauce.  The chicken came out sooo moist it was falling apart!  This made A LOT of sauce with the chicken so I served it over egg noodles.  It was so flavorful and creamy!  It made a lot of leftovers for just the two of us. Love this recipe, the bf said to give it 10 stars!

reviews.review_text: I REALLY did want to love this, especially after reading reviews to make the most of everyone's comments.  We opted to use fresh organic chicken breasts, extra spicy salsa (to counteract the cream cheese), and regular-fat cream cheese to get the best possible outcome.  As easy as this recipe was to make, it did not live up to expectations.  The chicken did shred easy, but the rest turned into a very dubious-looking greyish pink mixture.   Looks aside, the taste wasn't terribly impressive. I LOVE all of the ingredients individually, but together the taste was bland and the corn, normally a family favorite, was a bit of a "texture violation" amidst the cream cheese chicken shreds.  It really just tasted like shredded chicken with cream cheese and corn (the bean flavor is completely lost), which wasn't very appealing.  At the end of the day, this was a mediocre chip dip for us.  The next morning, it started to look even more dubious and nobody could bring themselves to try it again.  Terribly sorry, but this recipe just didn't fly for us. :(

This is a good base recipe, but it definitely needs tweaked to be made more to our liking.  I followed the recipe to the letter this time and we found that it was very, very bland.  If I make this again, I will definitely spice the chicken up and use hot salsa.  Also I will add canned chiles.  It was a decent recipe, just not a favorite in our household.  UPDATE: Made again 2/13/13 and used a 24 oz jar of Great Value Hot Salsa and stirred in cooked rice just before serving and this tasted much better.  Our family likes things a little spicy, so the hot salsa and the extra quantity really helped to make this something we can enjoy often.  Thanks Jen.<br/>UPDATE: Made for a third time on 3/30/13 and used a homemade salsa from this site ( Recipe #485128 ) and the recipe was sooooooo much better.  I am even bumping the star rating from 3 to 4.  I want to love this recipe so much because it is so easy, but it still needs a little more work.  I will continue to tweak it on days when I need crock pot meals.  Thanks again Jen.

INCREDIBLE!!!  I used a jar of salsa verde and unfortunately I forgot to get corn, but it was still great, great, great.  Next time I will put in a tortilla and double the recipe so hopefully there will be leftovers.  I will make this again and again!  Thanks!*update*  6/23  I do make this a lot!  I usually now make it using a cooked chicken from the deli and I shred it myself.  While I'm shredding the chicken I allow the cream cheese to soften.  I place all the ingredients in a pan and cook it on the stove and it's ready in no time!  I will only make this using salsa verde.  When we made it with a red salsa we really didn't care much for the appearance or taste.  I also add cumin and chili powder to this. Sometimes I'll add just a bit of chicken broth to keep the chicken moist. (Only when I'm making it stovetop with pre-cooked chicken.)  We usually leave out the corn.  Most of the time we serve these in a tortilla, but we have made this in the crockpot and served with tortilla chips when we've had guests.  EVERYONE really, really loves this!!

reviews.review_text: Everyone seems to love this recipe, but I cannot understand why or if I did something wrong. I used fresh chicken, and black bean soup instead of plain beans. Yes it was easy, but I found it to be very rich, and somehow bland. The next day it was even worse, as it was sticky and the beans made it too pasty. I found the flavours didn't blend and it just tasted like corn and beans with too much cream cheese. I was the only one that ate it, but I will not make it again. ---bacongirl - So, you changed the recipe, and gave it perfect marks? But I changed the recipe and gave it a low review, and it doesn't count? I'll give you that maybe the stickiness was my fault, because the chicken wasn't frozen (I thought the soup would compensate) but I am not the only one to complain about it being bland. In fact, some reviewers suggest adding pepper flakes, Tabasco, garlic, butter etc. and LESS cream cheese. Exactly my point! Adding soup (with more flavour than plain beans) has nothing to do with it being bland, or tasting like too much cream cheese.

items.name: Creamy Cajun Chicken Pasta
items.description: Make and share this Creamy Cajun Chicken Pasta recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Place chicken and Cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat.
In a large skillet over medium heat, sauté chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Reduce heat add green onion, heavy cream, tomatoes, basil, salt, garlic powder, black pepper and heat through.
Pour over hot linguine and toss with Parmesan cheese.

reviews.review_text: OMG this is an awesome recipe. Before making this I read a lot of the comments and tweaks then I made my version. I cut my chicken breast into cubes and added Tony's Creole seasoning. I also used a pound of medium shrimp that I took the shells and tail off of. I dusted those in a separate bowl. I let those marinate a few hours in the fridge. After a few hours I took the meat/seafood out and let come to room temp. I used a cast iron old 3 notch Lodge frying pan. I sauteed a carton of white sliced mushrooms. Once cooked sat aside in a bowl. I then cooked the chicken. Sit that aside in another bowl. While the chicken was cooking, I minced 3 cloves of garlic, 1/2 T of fresh basil from my herb garden (Acutally it was a small handful), 2 green onions sliced and 3-4 T of sundried tomatoes in oil. I added some of the oil from the tomatoes to my cast iron skillet and added the garlic, basil, green onions and sundried tomatoes to the skillet. I sauteed this for about 2 minutes and then added the heavy cream. Let is simmer a few minutes then I added back in the mushrooms. Again simmers a few minutes then added the marinated raw shrimp. I let the sauce cook the shrimp because I wanted the flavor of the shrimp in my sauce. I added back in the chicken. I used penne pasta and while this cooked I put a small amount of parmesan into my sauce. Drained my pasta and added it back into my Enamel Cast Iron Dutch Oven. I decided to use the dutch oven to boil the pasta because I wanted to use the heat left in the dutch oven to keep the dish warm. I put the pasta back into my Le Creuset Dutch Oven and added the sauce mixture. I then added about a teaspoon of red pepper flakes for the heat. My husband came home about an hour later and we ate it about an hour later. The Dutch Oven kept it warm and the time frame of waiting to eat it allowed the dish to mari a bit more. It was one of the best meals I have ever made and my husband totally agreed. He made me write down the recipe as he was eating his second dish. We are already coming up with other additons/tweaks to make it not better but maybe different. I do not think this dish could get any better then the way I made it. Awesomeness at it's best!!!

reviews.review_text:
Not sure what else can be said about this dish, honestly.  It really does taste like something you'd pay mega bucks for at a high-end Italian restaurant.

I doubled the recipe here and there; meaning, I doubled the spices, used about 1 1/4 cups whipping cream, and used about 8 ounces of linguine noodles.  If you're like me, and not a huge chicken fan, you'll want the extra noodles.  Don't skip the chicken, however, because the juices and seasonings are what absolutely make this dish.

The only issue we had was with the sun-dried tomatoes.  Maybe I got the wrong kind, but they added absolutely nothing to this dish except for a dab of color.  We ate around them because they were tough and chewy.  I couldn't chop them because they were so tough, so I wound up tearing them into bits, which was hard enough to do!  I think I'll either skip them next time or maybe add some chopped red pepper for that color.  I did cut the chicken into thin slices, but will be sure to cut them into EXTRA THIN slices next time.  I've not cooked much with chicken, so dummy me thought the strips would shrink!  This recipe is so easy to make that even the most novice cook will come out looking like a professional chef!  This is yet another Yowza recipe, as in "Yowza, this is good stuff!"

To sum it all up, this recipe tastes amazing.  It's very easy to make, and easy to switch up with your own variations without losing the integrity of the dish.  Quick to prepare, as well.  If you haven't already tried it, you need to try it soon, and I think it'll soon be part of your repertoire.

This was wonderful!  The best part was, it was done in 20 minutes - and I started with frozen chicken!  To get dinner done fast, I partially thawed the chicken in hot water for 3 minutes, then sliced it still frozen, sprinkled w/ seasoning, and tossed in a hot skillet w/ olive oil and butter.  While that browned, I sliced a red bell pepper and the green onions, then put the pasta in boiling water (10 minute count down).  I added the bell pepper and onion to the pan and sauteed 2 - 3 minutes til the chicken was done before adding the cream and seasonings, subbing fresh basil for dried.  After it simmered for 5 minutes, I added 1/2 a can of diced tomatoes that I had in the fridge.  Since I'm not good at reading carefully, I also stirred the fresh parmesan in to the sauce instead of sprinkling on top, but it was just fine.  I only wish I had omitted the salt, because the cajun seasoning was already salty.  I know better.  :)  I also doubled the recipe, but used only 2 cups of cream, as recommended by another reviewer, and it was plenty of sauce for a pound of linguini.  I pan-seared some zucchini on the back burner for the last 5 minutes and had a restaurant quality dinner on the table in 20 minutes!  This is one very satisfied family, and one very happy cook.
Thanks for a great one!

reviews.review_text:
OMG OMG OMG.  This was undescribadly fantastic.  I really wanted to try something new and different, but with the ingredients I had on hand I was skeptical I would find something.  SUCCESS!!  
I planned on doubling the recipe because leftovers make my life much easier.
Being that my husband is the pickiest eater I always have to remove every trace of vegetables in a recipe. *sigh*  When I told him about this new recipe he said, "Sweetie, I don't really want anything too spicy, okay?"  Normally when I try new somewhat spicy recipes they come out much spicier than planned.  But, from the reviews I know I'd be safe.
HAHAHA  Too bad I ended up using 4 tablespoons instead of 4 teaspoons cajun seasoning.  Whoops.  I tried fixing my unknown error by adding sugar to the sauce.  I think I added about 1/4 cup before I realized that it wasn't going to help enough.  Though the sweet and spicy taste added a cool kick to the recipe.  I might even add sugar in the future.
I only had two cups of heavy cream so I used what was left of some half and half.  The sauce seemed so extremely thin to me so I added some cornstarch to get it where I wanted.
I served it over angel hair pasta and ended up using a Mexican blend of pre-shredded cheese on top.  I could have sworn I had parmesan, but I couldn't find it.  Next day I saw it underneath a bag of mozzarella.  Story of my life.
Even though it was by far MUCH spicier than we expected (I swear I need to learn how to read again) we both loved it.  My DH said that he would want it again - which is no small feat.

reviews.review_text: The beauty of this recipe is in the ease and versatility with which you can get big delicious flavors from the ingredients in a few steps. It is a great basic recipe that allows you to tweak it with different ingredients and still get wonderful flavors. So first I read the other reviews then I tweaked it with what what I had in my freezer and pantry. I used shrimp instead of chicken. I also used the terrific homemade recipe listed for the Cajun seasoning since I had those ingredients handy. I will be using this seasoning for other dishes. It's great. Since I like a spicier kick to my food I increased the amount of Cajun seasoning to 4 tsp which I added to about 1 pound of shrimp. I marinated the shrimp in a bowl for 1/2 hour. Finely chopped a shallot. Sauteed the shallot in butter then added the shrimp. Set the sauteed shrimp and shallots aside. Shrimp cooks very quickly and becomes chewy when overcooked. Separating them from the sauce prep helps to ensure that they won't be overcooked. Using the same sautee pan, I increased the heavy cream to 2 cups and added 1/2 cup of water, seasoning the sauce with the other ingredients listed to taste. I added 1/2 cup grated parmesan cheese directly into the sauce, melting until completely smooth. I then returned the sauteed shrimp and shallots , ensuring that all of the juices were scraped out, along with the shrimp back into the prepared sauce. This Cajun alfredo sauce over linguini was super delicious and decadent! The spicy taste is mild. But the Cajun seasoning sits in the back of the throat, definitely giving a "kick up" to the flavor of a basic alfredo sauce. The hubs and I loved it. I could also see the sauce topping grits or rice. Yum!

reviews.review_text: So yummy!  My goal is to try a new recipe every week and as I was searching I saw this one with its awesome reviews.  I printed it out and bought the sundried tomatoes and heavy whipping cream- I already had all the other ingredients which was great!  I read through the reviews and made a few notes as to what others had tried when they made it.  A few things I did differently:  I coated my one chicken breast with 2 T cajun seasoning, then added a T of flour to the chicken to help coat it and possibly thicken the sauce later.  Then I cooked the chicken in the butter and added 8 oz of sliced fresh white button mushrooms.  I let them cook a little and then added 1 chopped garlic clove and the green onion and let them wilt down.  A few minutes later, I added the rest of the ingredients to the skillet and let it all come together.  I dumped my cooked linguine in the skillet when it was done and stirred it all together.  Sooooo wonderful!  The cajun seasoning coated chicken added a great kick when you ate it.  My family loves mushrooms so it was a great add for us.  Hubby was amazed at the flavors and said it was "Olive Garden" quality food.  My VERY picky 2 yr old even slurped down the noodles and sauce.  Thanks for the fabulous recipe!  We will definitely be making this regularly and I encourage everyone to try it.

reviews.review_text: FANTABULOUS!!!!  This dish was sooooo good I have to give a play-by-play.  I added 1 lb of halfed whole white button mushrooms.  For the sundried tomatoe I went to my freezer and grabbed a few of Mirj's "Oven-dried tomatoes" (which I have freezer bags full of) instead.    The only other thing that I used that was a first for me was the cajun seasoning.  Ironically, I had just purchased Pampered Chef's Cajun Seasoning.  I doubt this had anything to do with it, but I have never used a pre-mixed cajun seasoning before.  I layed a bed of pasta on a platter and poured the sauce over it all and served it "family style."  We could have NEVER guessed what we were about to experience.  Honestly, with the exception of a straight-out alfredo, this is the best pasta sauce I have ever had.  The flavors just dance around in your mouth, not too overpowering, but they let you know they are there.  The entire meal my husband and I were scheming up different ways to make this recipe and we both agreed that we would like to try it with shrimp and also do just a veggie-version with lots of mushrooms, yellow/red/orange peppers, etc.  We are no food critics...but to us...this dish IS restaurant quality and is earning a spot in the front of the pasta section of my cookbook!!!  Thanks, Lorac, for this OUTSTANDING recipe!

reviews.review_text: I used this as more of a guide than an actual recipe but it turned out really well! First, I marinated my chicken strips (thighs rather than breasts because I prefer them) in some heavy cream and bay leaves. After an hour, I took the bay leaves out and seared the chicken in chaabani fused olive oil and then added some four until a roux was formed. Then I drained some of the excess oil and cream off. I added my diced tomatoes (rather than sun dried) and green onions along with Cajun seasoning, garlic & onion powder, salt, black pepper, and dried basil. I mixed that together and then added gradually more and more heavy cream. As my sauce thickened, I boiled some salted water and cooked some linguini until al dente. Then I tossed the hot noodles in my chaabani oil until coated to prevent sticking. reviews.review_text: So yummy!  My goal is to try a new recipe every week and as I was searching I saw this one with its awesome reviews.  I printed it out and bought the sundried tomatoes and heavy whipping cream- I already had all the other ingredients which was great!  I read through the reviews and made a few notes as to what others had tried when they made it.  A few things I did differently:  I coated my one chicken breast with 2 T cajun seasoning, then added a T of flour to the chicken to help coat it and possibly thicken the sauce later.  Then I cooked the chicken in the butter and added 8 oz of sliced fresh white button mushrooms.  I let them cook a little and then added 1 chopped garlic clove and the green onion and let them wilt down.  A few minutes later, I added the rest of the ingredients to the skillet and let it all come together.  I dumped my cooked linguine in the skillet when it was done and stirred it all together.  Sooooo wonderful!  The cajun seasoning coated chicken added a great kick when you ate it.  My family loves mushrooms so it was a great add for us.  Hubby was amazed at the flavors and said it was "Olive Garden" quality food.  My VERY picky 2 yr old even slurped down the noodles and sauce.  Thanks for the fabulous recipe!  We will definitely be making this regularly and I encourage everyone to try it.

reviews.review_text:
OMG OMG OMG.  This was undescribadly fantastic.  I really wanted to try something new and different, but with the ingredients I had on hand I was skeptical I would find something.  SUCCESS!!  
I planned on doubling the recipe because leftovers make my life much easier.
Being that my husband is the pickiest eater I always have to remove every trace of vegetables in a recipe. *sigh*  When I told him about this new recipe he said, "Sweetie, I don't really want anything too spicy, okay?"  Normally when I try new somewhat spicy recipes they come out much spicier than planned.  But, from the reviews I know I'd be safe.
HAHAHA  Too bad I ended up using 4 tablespoons instead of 4 teaspoons cajun seasoning.  Whoops.  I tried fixing my unknown error by adding sugar to the sauce.  I think I added about 1/4 cup before I realized that it wasn't going to help enough.  Though the sweet and spicy taste added a cool kick to the recipe.  I might even add sugar in the future.
I only had two cups of heavy cream so I used what was left of some half and half.  The sauce seemed so extremely thin to me so I added some cornstarch to get it where I wanted.
I served it over angel hair pasta and ended up using a Mexican blend of pre-shredded cheese on top.  I could have sworn I had parmesan, but I couldn't find it.  Next day I saw it underneath a bag of mozzarella.  Story of my life.
Even though it was by far MUCH spicier than we expected (I swear I need to learn how to read again) we both loved it.  My DH said that he would want it again - which is no small feat.

reviews.review_text:
I just wanted to correct my typos.. it's the same review! 

Okay, I just made it last night, and had leftovers today for lunch.. And OMG, I thought it was good yesterday.. it's was even better as leftovers! I'm one of those people that can not handle chicken and then eat it.. so I decided to use shrimp and make enough for the next day dinner (or lunch). My changes to the recipe were as follows.. 1 1/2LBS RAW SHRIMP, 16oz ANGEL HAIR PASTA. I coated my shrimp with my own desired amount of my CREOLE SEASONING (probably a cup), plus additional garlic powder, threw in the basil and black pepper at this time. 4TBLBS BUTTER, 3 GREEN ONIONS (TOPS AND BOTTOMS), 2 CUPS HEAVY CREAM, 1 CAN DICED TOMATOES, added my black pepper and basil to my shrimp coating. I just melted my butter, then threw in all together the green onions, heavy cream, tomatoes. Heated thru, then added my shrimp.. heated thru til shrimp turned translucent, about 5 mins. Then tossed in my Angel Hair Pasta and Parmesean cheese. It all came together very quickly! It's definitely a 30 minute meal.. We had salad and garlic bread to accompany. Thanks soooo much for sharing! The flavors were sooooo good!

reviews.review_text: I made this last night for Valentines Day and it was absolutely delicious! I used one large chicken breast and two andouille sausages which I sliced up and sauteed with some minced garlic and then threw it in with the chicken. (I found the andouille sausage at Target thanks to another reviewer.)   I doubled the Cajun seasoning because I wanted to make sure each piece of chicken was totally coated. Other than that, I followed the recipe as written.  I think the key to the sauce is not to rush step 3.  After I reduce the heat, I made some homemade garlic bread and cooked the pasta which took about 25 minutes and at this point the sauce was perfect. It bubbled ever so slightly while it simmered and I stirred occasionally.  Since this is incredibly fattening I may try to make a healthier version as others have suggested but I am not sure how that will go over with my BF now that he's had the real thing. I'm thinking this recipe will be for special occassions if I want to cook it as written (with all that fat). :)

attributes.source_text: I made this last night for Valentines Day

reviews.review_text: DH and I have given this 5 stars from the first taste but I'm writing a new review because after making this several times, I have learned a few things that may help others.  One time I substituted half and half but the sauce never thickened properly and I won't try that again.  Tonight I used my food processor to make the sauce.  I put a quarter of a medium onion in the bowl along with the sundried tomatoes and a spoon full of bottled minced garlic.  Added the spices and pulsed until it was pureed.  Then I poured in the heavy cream and pulsed a few times to combine (don't pulse too much or you'll have whipped cream).  I sauteed my shrimp (instead of chicken) in the cajun spice until they were partially cooked and then poured in the sauce.  After simmering a few minutes I turned off the burner and tossed in some cooked thin spaghetti.  Coated the noodles in the sauce and tossed with parmesan.  This was the best yet!  Next time I'd like to pair this dish with some squash, zuchinni, mushrooms, and brocolli sauteed in the cajun butter!  Yummy  :)  Thanks again for this recipe!

reviews.review_text: Words cannot express how much I loved this one! I do think it's quite heavy, but I always make the original recipe first, then try to make some low fat tweeks! It was seriously as if I was mmmm'ing at every bite! I am a salt lover and thought the salt level seemed quite high even when I left out the added salt. Next time I think I will take the cajun seasoning down to 1 and a half teaspoons and I usually add salt to my pasta to flavor it but will skip it next time for this recipe! I was out of green onions and didn't have any sun dried tomatoes, so I used about 1/4 cup chopped vidalia onion and 2 small tomatoes chopped. I threw them in with the chicken to soften up a bit and it made a nice gooey syrup with the chicken juice and butter that was in the pan. My terribly picky 3 year old who won't eat anything we eat for the most part actually tasted it then asked for a bowl!!! I could have died from shock that he loved it! Millions of thanks for this great recipe! Next time I will for sure be using fat free half and half and maybe 1/2 a cup of cream! THANKS!!!!  UPDATE: I used half Tony Creachers Creole and half Old Savannah Spice Co. Cajun and it was PERFECT!!!!!  Thanks!!!!

reviews.review_text: FANTABULOUS!!!!  This dish was sooooo good I have to give a play-by-play.  I added 1 lb of halfed whole white button mushrooms.  For the sundried tomatoe I went to my freezer and grabbed a few of Mirj's "Oven-dried tomatoes" (which I have freezer bags full of) instead.    The only other thing that I used that was a first for me was the cajun seasoning.  Ironically, I had just purchased Pampered Chef's Cajun Seasoning.  I doubt this had anything to do with it, but I have never used a pre-mixed cajun seasoning before.  I layed a bed of pasta on a platter and poured the sauce over it all and served it "family style."  We could have NEVER guessed what we were about to experience.  Honestly, with the exception of a straight-out alfredo, this is the best pasta sauce I have ever had.  The flavors just dance around in your mouth, not too overpowering, but they let you know they are there.  The entire meal my husband and I were scheming up different ways to make this recipe and we both agreed that we would like to try it with shrimp and also do just a veggie-version with lots of mushrooms, yellow/red/orange peppers, etc.  We are no food critics...but to us...this dish IS restaurant quality and is earning a spot in the front of the pasta section of my cookbook!!!  Thanks, Lorac, for this OUTSTANDING recipe!

reviews.review_text: AMAZING DISH, PERFECT VALENTINE'S DINNER! I hadn't planned a meal and only had a few hours. I had everything on hand except for the cajun seasoning and heavy whipping cream. I doubled the sauce and cooked 6oz pasta instead of 4. Other reviews suggested doubling because they wished they had leftovers, and today my BF and I are both already excited to have the leftovers for dinner. I was nervous about the seasoning so I bought 2, Tony Chachere's Creole Seasoning and McCormick Cajun Seasoning. I  started off with 2tsp of each, but ended up using about 3 of each as well as cayenne pepper to taste because I'm a hot-spicy junkie! Tony Cachere's was more of a seasoned salt, and McCormick's was more seasoning with a little sea salt. The half and half was on sale, less than a quarter the price of the heavy cream and it worked out wonderfully. I added cooked Andouille Sausage just because my BF loves meat, and stirred in 2 big sliced links with the cream. The sausage and chicken were great together. I know there were plenty of reviews, but that's how great this dish was. I can't wait to make it for a party! THANKS LORAC! Wow, so heavenly...

I also probably doubled the garlic, because I like garlic (and the husband doesn't complain!). I made this over spaghetti, because we like the thinner pasta, and I will definitely make this again with the right stuff, and it'll be even better!! Thanks.

reviews.review_text: First of all...THANK YOU! My lovable but slightly spoiled boyfriend deemed this "a dish his mother would be jealous of", something I am fairly certain he has never said before. I made this twice in the past two weeks, the last time for boyfriend and several friends, one of whom went back for seconds and thirds :) I read quite a few reviews and wound up combining a lot of the suggestions. While the chicken was cooking in the butter, I sauteed chopped red onion, red bell pepper, green bell pepper, chopped garlic, basil, salt and pepper. I can't imagine making it without the bell pepper. After adding the half and half, as opposed to heavy whipping cream, I added flour to thicken up the sauce, after stirring until all the flour dissolved, I added in the veggies and allowed it to simmer for a few minutes. While it was simmering I sliced two handfuls of cherry tomatoes in half and tossed them in as well, they were a nice relief from the spicy chicken. Once again thanks so much for this wonderful recipe!

reviews.review_text: I used this as more of a guide than an actual recipe but it turned out really well! First, I marinated my chicken strips (thighs rather than breasts because I prefer them) in some heavy cream and bay leaves. After an hour, I took the bay leaves out and seared the chicken in chaabani fused olive oil and then added some four until a roux was formed. Then I drained some of the excess oil and cream off. I added my diced tomatoes (rather than sun dried) and green onions along with Cajun seasoning, garlic & onion powder, salt, black pepper, and dried basil. I mixed that together and then added gradually more and more heavy cream. As my sauce thickened, I boiled some salted water and cooked some linguini until al dente. Then I tossed the hot noodles in my chaabani oil until coated to prevent sticking. I then put the chicken sauce on the noodles and tossed to combine then tossed a few additional times with fresh grated Parmesan until it reached the desired texture and flavor. I garnished with a bit more parmesan and would have with additional green onions but I no longer had any.

My cajun seasoning mix is very spicy - I used 4 tsp for the pound of shrimp, and it was perfect for our tastes. All this raving, and I haven't even mentioned how easy it all was - thanks so much for sharing this recipe.

reviews.review_text: I will come as no surprise that another family found this recipe to be fast, easy and very tasty. Because I made this on the spur of the moment, I had to substitute some of the ingredients, but I doubt this negatively diminished the flavour in any way. I love recipe # 34011 (Cajun Style Oven Fries), and make the seasoning up in a vat, using it not only for the potatoes, but for anything calling for Cajun seasoning, and I used some of this for the indicated amount of cajun seasoning here. I also didn't have any heavy cream on hand, so I used 1 1/2 cups of 10% cream and boiled this down. It did split, but was not noticeable when I added the noodles and parmesan cheese to the sauce. I just added parmesan to the mixture until it seemed to hold together, so I'm sure it was in excess of the 1/4 cup called for. This seems to be a very forgiving recipe for making this type of last minute alteration. If it was this good with my changes, I'm sure it will be even more wonderful when made as written.

First of all...THANK YOU! My lovable but slightly spoiled boyfriend deemed this "a dish his mother would be jealous of", something I am fairly certain he has never said before. I made this twice in the past two weeks, the last time for boyfriend and several friends, one of whom went back for seconds and thirds :) I read quite a few reviews and wound up combining a lot of the suggestions. While the chicken was cooking in the butter, I sauteed chopped red onion, red bell pepper, green bell pepper, chopped garlic, basil, salt and pepper. I can't imagine making it without the bell pepper. After adding the half and half, as opposed to heavy whipping cream, I added flour to thicken up the sauce, after stirring until all the flour dissolved, I added in the veggies and allowed it to simmer for a few minutes. While it was simmering I sliced two handfuls of cherry tomatoes in half and tossed them in as well, they were a nice relief from the spicy chicken. Once again thanks so much for this wonderful recipe!

items.label: Best Ever Banana Cake With Cream Cheese Frosting
items.name: Best Ever Banana Cake With Cream Cheese Frosting
items.description:
This is one of (if not) the BEST banana cake I have ever tasted! I thought the oven temp of 275° sounded a little low, but this cake baked up (and rose) beautifully in my oven at this temp after pretty much exactly one hour. I do not know if the little "freezer trick" to this recipe is what ensured its moistness or not, but I did it, and it was exceptionally moist & delicious. Would be interesting to see if it still came out as great if this step was skipped. All I know is that I followed this recipe EXACTLY as stated (except that I had no buttermilk, so I subbed with a mix of lemon juice & milk) and I got exceptional results. So moist and yummy...a dense cake, similar in texture to a carrot cake... I personally would not call this frosted banana bread :o)  Depending on the amount of frosting you like you can decide whether to half the recipe or not. I used the full recipe and had some leftover. I sprinkled on the chopped walnuts and threw this baby in the fridge and cut it the next day...TO DIE FOR! I really liked it slightly chilled, but great at room temp too! It got better each day it sat, I always make this cake at least the day before I need or want it.  I was extremely pleased with this cake and will be making it over & over again!! So glad I came across this one!! (on another website).


(* * Just to update the recipe, (based on some of the reviews), the baking time may vary based on individual ovens. It was RIGHT ON for my oven, but some others have stated it has taken 1 hour 10 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes, and my sister just informed me that it took 1 hour 30 minutes in her oven!!!!!)
instructions: Preheat oven to 275°F (135C).
Grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan.
In a small bowl, mix mashed banana with the lemon juice; set aside.
In a medium bowl, mix flour, baking soda and salt; set aside.
In a large bowl, cream 3/4 cup butter and  2 1/8 cups sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs, one at a time, then stir in 2 tsp vanilla.
Beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk.
Stir in banana mixture.
Pour batter into prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for one hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Remove from oven and place directly into the freezer for 45 minutes.  This will make the cake very moist.
For the frosting, cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth.
Beat in 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Add icing sugar and beat on low speed until combined, then on high speed until frosting is smooth.
Spread on cooled cake.
Sprinkle chopped walnuts over top of the frosting, if desired.

reviews.review_text: Best cake I have ever head.  Apple cake has been my favorite for decades, and now banana cake surpasses it. <br/><br/>I baked mine at 350° F for an hour.  225° would not have done it in my oven.  Another recipe suggested 350° for 30 minutes, also way too short in my oven. <br/><br/>I added a small bag of chocolate chips.   I did not freeze the cake as suggested (I only had a glass pan), and it was still the moistest cake I ever had.  They formed a layer of chocolate near the bottom, but still was very tasty.  <br/><br/>I did not use any lemon (my women hate lemon, and can taste even the smallest trace in my recipes).  Did not substitute for it.<br/><br/>I also used less than 2 cups of sugar.  Although I am diabetic, this is worth the decadence (but not the full amount of sugar).  I HATE Splenda.   You can reduce the sugar even more to suit you. <br/><br/>In my grocery store, I had to look for confectioner's sugar (also labeled as powdered sugar), instead of icing sugar.   <br/><br/>Leaving the walnuts out to be added on individual slices was perfect.  My daughter is allergic to them.  (Such a simple solution -- I am ashamed to admit I have been leaving them out entirely -- I missed them in my recipes). <br/><br/>As others have, I expect I will experiment with other fillings (pumpkin, apple sauce, etc).  A wonderful base recipe for a variety of cakes.

reviews.review_text:
Not much else to say besides what's already been said.  Definitely ample moisture...

My mom is pretty much a dessert connoisseur, and she's really loved it too!

I can see why some reviews included that the powdered sugar measurement might've been a bit too much, but that frosting is definitely great!  And I'm usually not much of a frosting person...

I followed the recipe for the most part, except:

* I used fat free buttermilk (not by choice - it was the cheaper buy, for the smaller quantity I preferred) instead of whole - didn't seem to make a difference.

* The last of my vanilla extract (pretty much exactly two teaspoons) went to the cake batter.  For the vanilla extract that the frosting called for, I happened to have some Breyer's Vanilla Bean ice cream in the freezer, so...yep, you guessed it!  Put a few teaspoons of that right on in there.  And it seemed to really work out!

* I loaded the batter with the chopped walnuts (I love/prefer walnuts in desserts, for the most part) as well as sprinkled them on top of the frosting at the end, as suggested.  Great turnout!

* Oh yeah, and also as mentioned by other previous reviews, the cake definitely took a bit longer than what the recipe calls.  I kept the oven on 275 the whole time, and the cake required  total of about an hour and 40 mins., give or take a few minutes.  Best thing to do is to keep an eye on the cake after about 30-45 mins., to get a feel for it in a 275-temp. setting (I started checking on it after about 50 mins.).

reviews.review_text:
I really liked this recipe but I tend to make tweaks to recipes to make them healthier so my version of the recipe is still a work in progress. My first attempt made the following tweaks:
- whole wheat flour instead of refined flour
- only 1 cup (organic unrefined brown) sugar for the cake and 1 cup icing sugar for the frosting
- only 3/4 the amount of butter stated and the rest made up with olive oil

I also added some lemon juice to the frosting for added flavour.

Cake was done within 50 min!

The result: just sweet enough for my taste without losing flavour. Not quite enough banana taste and cake was a little dense for my liking. Frosting was perfect (can do with even a little less sugar).

Next attempt: I will add more banana and 1/2 teaspoon more baking soda, as recommended by one of the reviewers, to lighten up the consistency. Will reduce icing sugar for frosting to 3/4 cup. Also, after cooling the cake, will cut in half, spread more banana mixture on top of one half and layer the other half over. Then spread the frosting over the top and sides for a tall, hefty banana-y cake.

Any comments on the above and other skinny tips for this cake would be welcome! Skinny recipes mean we can eat MORE!

this is ridiculous!  i mean really.  it gets moister by the day!  i wasn't going to use the freezer method because i was so afraid of shattering the glass pan so i waited 15 minutes before putting it in..crossed my fingers and... no crash!  i baked in a 9x13 and honestly it took about 1 hr 45 min!  i had to turn the oven off at the last 15-20 minutes since i didn't want it to get too brown.  i also made a small batch of icing just to put on a couple pieces and honestly i prefer it without!  someone said this is just the same as banana bread, that it didn't have the light fluffy cake quality to it, and i totally disagree, this is very much a banana cake :)  SO delicious, thank you for this recipe!
Feb 2, 2010 UPDATE:  I made this again and here's the difference -> first time i made sour milk with milk and vinegar since i didn't have buttermilk on hand.  This time i used buttermilk and i didn't freeze straight away (maybe after 30-40 minutes i put it in hoping it would work, i got distracted when it came out) and the cake turned out a hell of a lot more dense!  So i don't know if it was a combination of using buttermilk and not getting it in the freezer right away or if the sour milk is just less thick therefore made a much fluffier cake for me??  Anyway, thought i'd post the difference!  Cheers :)

I have given this recipe 5 stars for the ease and texture of this cake, ( although I didn't put it in the freezer , it is not a dry/crumbly cake at all .) My kids didn't  give me time to frost it! My mum always frosted her banana cake with a glaze type frosting made using confectioners sugar, a dash of vanilla, a tsp softened butter and some lemon juice. It seemed to add a zing to the banana flavour of the cake. I will try that tomorrow if there is any cake left!!! But I agree with other reviewers that it doesn't really need frosting. I did take on-board  a few of the suggestions made in other reviews , so what I have ended up with may not be a true representation of the original recipe. I used 2 cups of quite flavourful & quite ripe bananas but the finished cake flavour was milder than what I was hoping for. This may improve with sitting a day or two in the fridge ( if it has a chance once my DH finds it!).  I used SR FLOUR ( self-raising ) with no additional raising agents and it rose beautifully . Used 2/3 cup of brown sugar and 1 & 1/3 cups white sugar, and it is plenty sweet enough. I didn't have buttermilk, but used 1 cup milk and 1/2 cup light sour cream. I was going to add a pinch or 2 of cinnamon but forgot! I think it would enhance the flavour nicely.
I used 2 x 9" round tins , which were done in just under an hour at 150C / 300F. The cakes measure approx 2 inches in height now that they have cooled. A good height as individual cakes , but would be impressive stacked with a filling between. Will definately make again.

reviews.review_text: This cake was VERY good!  If you like banana bread, you will like this!  I took heed of the other reviewers and scooped out about a cup or so of batter and made a dozen mini muffins and put the rest in the 9X13 pan.  I found that my cake did not overflow this way otherwise it would have :-) This cake was done in my oven after an hour and 10 minutes at 275 degrees.  So depending on your oven, you might have to cook more or less.  Try checking after an hour and go from there. I let this cake cool for 20 minutes or so and then put it in the freezer for the 45 minutes.  Didn't like the idea of putting a steaming hot pan into the already packed freezer!  Anyways, the cake came out moist!  I altered the frosting b/c I myself am not crazy about super sweet cream cheese frosting but wanted a little cream cheese taste.  So I made a buttercream and cream cheese frosting by mixing 4 oz cream cheese, 2/3 cup shortening, 3/4 cups butter, 2 cups powdered sugar and one tsp vanilla.  This gave me a light, not too sweet frosting that I really liked on this cake.  It had the cream cheese taste, but was light, creamy and not too sweet. If making as directed, I would not put in all of the powdered sugar right away, as I think it might be too much. Check the taste after adding 2 cups and adjust to your taste! Kids and adults loved this. Thank you for the recipe Rhonda!

reviews.review_text: Two days after baking the recipe my 40-yr old daughter said, "FANTASTIC. The strong banana flavor made this cake so delicious we ate the whole thing before lunch.%u201D I didn't have buttermilk so added 3 tsp of white vinegar to 1-1/2 cups of milk. In error I grabbed and used baking POWDER instead of SODA, yet the batter was light and fluffy. Using a bundt pan, I greased it with shortening then (per instructions from another cake recipe) I put small pieces of semi-hard butter in each seam 1/2 inch apart then dabbed a spot of almond extract on top of each piece. Had so much batter, I made four muffin caps. After pouring batter into bundt pan, I left a 2-inch space at the top for fear it would boil over. For precautionary measures, I removed the top oven rack and put cookie sheet under bundt pan in case batter ran over sides (it didn%u2019t, but was close). All baked for one hour. I whisked baked cake to the freezer and took it out in 45 minutes later, storing it in a container with lid and zapped the whole thing in the refrigerator. Later that day I discovered cake was heavy. One slice showed %u2018solid matter%u2019 had formed on what had been the bottom in the bundt pan (may have been result of using baking powder, not soda). Two granddaughters wanted seconds, saying cake wasn't sweet but it sure was good! Their Mom had one piece and noticed denseness; she, too. However, didn%u2019t mind it saying it was very tasty. The day after baking the cake it was highly flavored with the taste of banana. Hoping to use frosting to make a banana glaze, I added 1 overly ripe mashed banana, 7 Tbsp warm milk and 2 cups of powdered sugar (3-1/2 was too much). Didn%u2019t glaze, but daughter liked so well she fingered it out of the bowl and ate it on the way to her home. I will make the recipe again. Instead of using baking powder, I will use baking soda (a lesson well learned). Hint: easier mashing bananas if they are placed in a zipper-lock type bag. Thanks for a great recipe, Rhonda.

reviews.review_text: Yep, it's true. The texture of this banana cake it out of this world. It's the moistest cake I've ever made, banana or otherwise. The freezing technique produces a faintly crispy outer crust that holds together a supremely tender, fresh-tasting crumb.  The cream cheese frosting is, in my opinion, lily-gilding, but I loved it anyway.  My oven is slow, so I had to bake this for a full 1.5 hours.  I also used 1 tablespoon lemon juice in the 1.5 called-for cups of regular milk to approximate the buttermilk, which I didn't have on hand.  Worked great.  Three large, very ripe bananas produced just the right amount of banana mash.  My only concern with the freezer technique was that the hot pan raises the interior temp of the freezer, which can put other frozen foods at risk for bacterial growth.  However, when I took the pan out (and be warned that it will still be warm even after 45 mins. in the freezer, so you'll have to continue cooling it), I felt the other frozen foods and they were still pretty well frozen.  The frosting recipe makes more than you will need, but I like that in a frosting recipe. :-) As for storage, I simply put a sheet of plastic wrap over the surface of the cake.  It was just as moist the next day as the day it was baked.  I will be making this again and again.

reviews.review_text: After reading all the reviews, I though I would give this cake a try. I made three 8 inch layers and one 5" by 12". I used 2 cups of bananas because I had extra. I consider myself an expert when it comes to cakes and pies and definitely this is one that I will add to my collection. I owned and ran a cafe for over 20 years. I have made several different banana cake recipes and this by far is the best. One thing that makes this cake exceptional is the method in which it is prepared. reviews.review_text: This recipe is one of my new favorites and makes excellent cupcakes.  Do not skip the freezer step.  I have tried the cake both ways, and the freezer step makes a big difference.  I used regular milk, not buttermilk, and I left out the lemon juice.  I made 18 cupcakes and a small (7 x 11?) cake.  Each pan of six regular sized cupcakes took exactly 30 minutes to bake perfectly.  The cake in the small Pyrex pan took 50 minutes.  I used all purpose flour, and neither the cupcakes nor the cake rose much, but the texture was light and airy-- perfectly "cakey."  I did not find it to be at all dense or heavy (like banana bread).  To prepare my pans, I used paper baking cups for the cupcakes and sprayed the Pyrex with canola oil spray.  Both worked well.  For the frosting, I used one (eight ounce) block of cream cheese, one stick of butter, and a (one pound) box of powdered sugar.  I had just enough frosting for the cupcakes and the small cake.  I served the cupcakes/cake Thursday.  Over the weekend, I had people calling to ask for the recipe.  They said they had never had a cake so moist, light, and fluffy.  The banana flavor was great; I don't see the need for added flavorings or spices, though I'm sure they don't hurt the recipe.  I tried a cupcake Wednesday night (immediately after finishing a batch), and it was good.  The one I had for breakfast Friday morning was even better!  This is now one of my top three favorite cakes, and I hope to make it again and again.

reviews.review_text: Yep, it's true. The texture of this banana cake it out of this world. It's the moistest cake I've ever made, banana or otherwise. The freezing technique produces a faintly crispy outer crust that holds together a supremely tender, fresh-tasting crumb.  The cream cheese frosting is, in my opinion, lily-gilding, but I loved it anyway.  My oven is slow, so I had to bake this for a full 1.5 hours.  I also used 1 tablespoon lemon juice in the 1.5 called-for cups of regular milk to approximate the buttermilk, which I didn't have on hand.  Worked great.  Three large, very ripe bananas produced just the right amount of banana mash.  My only concern with the freezer technique was that the hot pan raises the interior temp of the freezer, which can put other frozen foods at risk for bacterial growth.  However, when I took the pan out (and be warned that it will still be warm even after 45 mins. in the freezer, so you'll have to continue cooling it), I felt the other frozen foods and they were still pretty well frozen.  The frosting recipe makes more than you will need, but I like that in a frosting recipe. :-) As for storage, I simply put a sheet of plastic wrap over the surface of the cake.  It was just as moist the next day as the day it was baked.  I will be making this again and again.

reviews.review_text: Two days after baking the recipe my 40-yr old daughter said, "FANTASTIC. The strong banana flavor made this cake so delicious we ate the whole thing before lunch.%u201D I didn't have buttermilk so added 3 tsp of white vinegar to 1-1/2 cups of milk. In error I grabbed and used baking POWDER instead of SODA, yet the batter was light and fluffy. Using a bundt pan, I greased it with shortening then (per instructions from another cake recipe) I put small pieces of semi-hard butter in each seam 1/2 inch apart then dabbed a spot of almond extract on top of each piece. Had so much batter, I made four muffin caps. After pouring batter into bundt pan, I left a 2-inch space at the top for fear it would boil over. For precautionary measures, I removed the top oven rack and put cookie sheet under bundt pan in case batter ran over sides (it didn%u2019t, but was close). All baked for one hour. I whisked baked cake to the freezer and took it out in 45 minutes later, storing it in a container with lid and zapped the whole thing in the refrigerator. Later that day I discovered cake was heavy. One slice showed %u2018solid matter%u2019 had formed on what had been the bottom in the bundt pan (may have been result of using baking powder, not soda). Two granddaughters wanted seconds, saying cake wasn't sweet but it sure was good! Their Mom had one piece and noticed denseness; she, too. However, didn%u2019t mind it saying it was very tasty. The day after baking the cake it was highly flavored with the taste of banana. Hoping to use frosting to make a banana glaze, I added 1 overly ripe mashed banana, 7 Tbsp warm milk and 2 cups of powdered sugar (3-1/2 was too much). Didn%u2019t glaze, but daughter liked so well she fingered it out of the bowl and ate it on the way to her home. I will make the recipe again. Instead of using baking powder, I will use baking soda (a lesson well learned). Hint: easier mashing bananas if they are placed in a zipper-lock type bag. Thanks for a great recipe, Rhonda.

I would suggest removing from fridge for at least an hour to let it come back up to room temp for fullest flavor. <br/>Modifications I made: Cake: Used 4 medium bananas (to give you an idea of how many banans);  reduced sugar in cake to 3/4 c total; used 3/4 c. canola oil (in place of butter); used 1 1/2 c. milk with 1 1/2 T of vinegar stirred into it in place of buttermilk and lemon juice. From: Jackie G. Jan.. 14, 2009.  i
I just finished preparing this GREAT recipe.  There are a few things I have to point out. Rhonda, YOU already mentioned the cooking time variable.  Well for me, I checked it at 1hr.10min. and both my husband and I DECIDED TO GIVE IT AN ADD'L. 10 MIN. and then I proceeded from there but now I know , even with my fairly new oven, I should have baked it 1hr 25min, because when it came from the freezer, the center had fallen but I WHEN RIGHT ON TO THE fROSTING STAGE. In the Frosting recipe you state 3-1/2 ciups "icing" sugar.  I think it should have been clearer.  I normaly make this same frosting using "POWDERED" sugar but by "icing" sugar, I used "super fine" sugar of which I only had 2 cups so I then I used 1-1/2 cups of Powdered sugar to make up the 3-1/2 cups called for. Well it all mixed well but the grain of the 'super fine' sugar still could be detected.  ALL POWDER SUGAR next time as it stays quite smooth. Even with these minor mishaps THIS CAKE IS ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS.  The center we discarded  but the next time I bake this cake my BAKE TIME  WILL BE RIGHT.  So, I still give this CAKE 5 stas with the Frosting made with POWDERED SUGAR. Yummy!

I agree with the consensus.   This cake is excellent.  Very moist.  Wonderful banana flavour.  For the cake, I used splenda and made buttermilk from skim milk and lemon juice.  I was concerned after creaming the butter, splenda and eggs:  the mixture looked like it was curdled.  I carried on figuring all would be well and it was.  I added the nuts (1 cup of chopped walnuts) to the cake batter.  For the frosting, I used light cream cheese and cut the recipe in half, further reducing the amount of icing sugar to just 1 and 1/8 cup as others suggested.  The frosting was plenty sweet, although a bit soft.  This made it very easy to spread, but I almost wondered if it would fall off the cake.  Baking in a 9x13 pan took about 1 hour and 20 minutes.  Immediately after taking it out of the oven, I put it outside in our -20 degree winter weather for about 1 hour.  I don't have a big sweet tooth and thought I would enjoy it even more with a little less sweetening.  The frosting, while very good, added to the sweetness, so I'll likely omit that in the future, except for special occasions.  This recipe is going to beckon me when I see the overripe bananas!  Thanks.

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°.
Whisk dry ingredients; set aside.
Combine wet ingredients with a hand mixer on low.
To cream, increase speed to high and beat until fluffy and the color lightens.
Stir the flour mixture into the creamed mixture until no flour is visible.
(Over mixing develops the gluten, making a tough cookie.) Now add the oats and raisins; stir to incorporate.
Fill a #40 cookie scoop and press against side of bowl, pulling up to level dough (to measure 2 tablespoons of dough).
Drop 2-inches apart onto baking sheet sprayed with nonstick spray.
Bake 11-13 minutes (on center rack), until golden, but still moist beneath cracks on top.
Remove from oven; let cookies sit on baking sheet for 2 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool.

reviews.review_text:
Great recipe!   With only a toaster oven, my first foray into cookie baking required modifying the baking time and temperature.  Around the 6th time making these cookies, I got a proper 1/4 size cookie sheet ($8.99), silicone liner ($6.99) and cooling racks (2, $9.85), followed by a wonderful timer ($9.99), around batch 12 or so.  Not wanting to wait to put the cookies on the cooling rack, I discovered that if I put the cookie sheet on a damp towel that had been in the freezer, the cookies could be removed within about 30 seconds.
 
Then, I continued modifying until I arrived at the following:

[NOTE:  I was 'forced' to eat dozens upon dozens of cookies before baking the final modification.  But these cookies are healthier  -more fiber, less white flour, gluten, sugar, and salt - and yet they still satisfy my incredible desire for sweets.  ALSO:  These are soft cookies, no crisp edges, probably a result of less sugar and using a toaster oven and having to change the time (less) and temperature (lower).]

SALT:  I added no salt, in part because Clabber Girl Double Acting Baking Powder has 65 mg in every 1/8 teaspoon.  So 2 teaspoons, the amount I use, has 1949 mg of salt or about 2/10ths of a teaspoon (0.18), and partly because I have high BP.  (I haven't cooked with salt for years now, and I  don't miss it.)

FLOUR:  1 cup unbleached white flour + 1/2 cup organic brown rice flour (no gluten) + 1/2 cup coconut flour.  Coconut flour is naturally sweet (need less sugar) and has no gluten; it also does not add any coconut taste.

BUTTER:  I also eliminated half the butter, substituting Spectrum Organic Shortening, a non-hydrogenated vegetable shortening (no trans fats), and since butter is 60% water and shortening has no water you have another reason for saving the raisin soak water.

SUGAR:  1/2 cup white & 1/2 cup brown sugar, instead of 1 cup of each.

OATMEAL:  2 cups old fashioned oats + 1 cup quick oatmeal, which absorbs more moisture.

RAISINS:  Following others suggestions, I soaked the raisins for an hour, but I then saved the liquid to add to the batter.  Coconut flour is very high in fiber and needs an equal amount of liquid to be added.  (Besides which the soak water adds raisin sugars and flavor.)  HOWEVER:  Only begin adding after having added the flour and half the oatmeal.  If the mixture is too dry, add 1/2 the raisin water.  Add the remaining oats, and as needed, 1/4 to 1  teaspoon of raisin water at a time until the batter is the right consistency  - not too dry or too sticky.

CINNAMON:  I love cinnamon, so over time, I ended up putting in a heaping tablespoon.  Even at a heaping tablespoon, the cinnamon stays a background taste, and cinnamon is good for you.  Amazon sells cinnamon supplements.

WALNUTS:  Why not?  Walnuts not only add taste, they add good oils and fiber.  1 1/4 cups toasted walnuts, coarsely chopped.  (If the walnuts are chopped too finely you can't taste them, too coarse, you can't get them in the cookies.)

BANANA:  One very ripe banana mashed into the walnuts to assist in the distribution of both.

ASSEMBLY ORDER:  To assist in the distribution of both the raisins and the banana/walnut mixture, both were added to the batter prior to adding the flour, which was gently folded in to avoid developing gluten.

With that one exception, I followed the original recipe's assembly order with regards to mixing, creaming, etc.  (I finally got a hand cranked mixer ($19.99) for creaming as using a whisk after my recent heart attack meant taking several hours for mixing and creaming  --  hoping to get a hand held electric mixer sometime soon.) 

BLUEBERRIES:  I kept all of the modifications, but substituted two, 5 oz packages of DRIED WILD BLUEBERRIES.  The soaked blueberries added a great deal more moisture than did the raisins and I had to add an additional 4 tbs, of quick oatmeal and several tablespoons of flour so the batter was no longer sticky and the cookies could be flattened with my fingertips.  However the blueberries are expensive, over $5 for one 5 oz package.  The next time I'm going to use just one package and see how they turn out.

reviews.review_text: Being a major oatmeal raisin cookie fanatic, I've tried 99% of recipes that catch my eye (which would be ALOT - camera & photography skills out here are a lil too good) so I've had this saved for YEARS and finally decided to try and rival my own favorite. Once on a roll with the ingredients, I realized I had to dump the 1t of kosher salt all in & all of a sudden came back to life: this might be rough. I hate reading reviews of people who did their own thing: how would I know if yours are any good/better if I did my own thing right off the bat, right? So 1tsp it was. 1C granulated, 1C packed brown,... 2 eggs - "oh god, and this will spread." BTW, I'm not sugar shy...but this is a lot for the small pallet of sweet you get for taste buds. By the time I spooned 2t of vanilla in, I was just hoping for the best. The first tray came out super spread-y, touching each other, with super crisp browned edges & I got weary about how quickly I'd taste the pang of sweetness so I went ahead and refrigerated the rest to help thicken 'em. That didn't do much. They are definitely chewy, look like the main picture but there's just a sharpness & FULL BODY extract-sugar-sweetness that makes this a just-one-cookie delicacy experience. Two max, & I need a drink or dessert to go with it. I don't like one-trick ORCs so this won't rate high on my list and now realize how this got away with so may 5s - most people who loved it did their own thing.

reviews.review_text: I have found my oatmeal cookie recipe! I followed the recipe almost exactly - the directions are very well done. I followed the technique as written, except that I used my Kitchenaide mixer (creamed wet ingredients on high for 5 minutes, stirred flour on low about a minute just until it disappeared, and stirred in oatmeal and raisins on low for about 45 seconds until all oatmeal looked moist). I would suggest letting the batter rest for about 15 minutes after you're done mixing because my first batch spread out and got crispy, but all batches after that were perfect. Also, my oven cooks unevenly so I wound up having to turn the cookie sheet halfway through. I had no problem with them spreading and they deliver the chewiness as poromised with just a little crispness around the edges. My son, who HATES anything with oatmeal in it, has eaten 3 already. The only changes I made to the ingredients were that I added a half teaspoon of cinnamon, I stirred in some dried sour cherries that I needed to use up in place of raisins, and I added a little over half a cup of chocolate chips. This is the first oatmeal cookie recipe I have made that has turned out well. Phenomenal cookie! Thanks for posting, Bev!

reviews.review_text: To my surprise, I learned while making these cookies for the second time that I had accidentally improved the recipe the first time I made them.  I had doubled the recipe and didn't realize that I forgot to double the amount of oatmeal. (I used only three cups of old fashioned oats for the double recipe.)  I took the cookies to a church event and everyone loved them, even people who said they usually don't care for oatmeal cookies.  While preparing the cookie batter for the second time I saw that the recipe required six cups of oatmeal.  That's when I realized that I hadn't put in the correct amount the first time.  I added the six cups.  The cookies are much tougher and harder to chew.  I don't like them nearly as much.  I recommend using half the oatmeal, especially if you're making them for someone who isn't a real fan of oatmeal cookies. I also followed another reviewer's suggestion to soften the raisins by boiling them for a minute or two and then draining the water.

I adjusted some ingredients, due to diabetes and trying to eat healthier.  I used 1 cup APF and !cup whole wheat flour. I added 1 and 1/2 tsp cinnamon. I used 1/2 cup real butter and 1/2 smart balance.   I used half real sugar and half fake sugar.
For the brown sugars I used 1/4 cup fake brown sugar (which equals 1/2 cup) and 1/4 cup real brown sugar (due to the too sweet reviews).  I also soaked the raising in 2 eggwhites and 2 tsp vanilla in a sandwhich bag while I was getting everything else together.  I did still add one whole egg and another egg yolk to the sugar mix.  I added the soaked raisins at the end as recipe calls.  I also added  1 cup crushed walnuts.  It was the best healthy cookie I have made yet. My hubby really liked it and I'm sure my kids will eat them until gone.  I made these really big only 33 cookies came out of this. They came out fluffy but slightly moist. So they are like a mini meal.  Thanks for a great base recipe.

I had no problem with them spreading and they deliver the chewiness as poromised with just a little crispness around the edges. My son, who HATES anything with oatmeal in it, has eaten 3 already. The only changes I made to the ingredients were that I added a half teaspoon of cinnamon, I stirred in some dried sour cherries that I needed to use up in place of raisins, and I added a little over half a cup of chocolate chips. This is the first oatmeal cookie recipe I have made that has turned out well. Phenomenal cookie! Thanks for posting, Bev!

reviews.review_text: Fantastic cookies.  Had to make some subs:  gluten free flour for wheat flour, soy marg for regular marg.  And, I added 1-2 cups of semi-sweet chocolate chips.  I think once I also subbed 1 1/2 c white sugar and 1/2 c. molasses for the sugars-- made a chewier cookie.  Really like this recipe.  Got rave reviews from people who don't have food allergies.  Found that it is good to keep dough kind of half frozen-- cookie bakes better that way (more puffy instead of flattening out).  I think it has to do with the gluten free flour.  I also like to make the dough and let it sit in the fridge for about 3 days before baking the cookies (then it goes into the freezer for a short time-- maybe 15-30 minutes, then baked).  I think the flavors seem to blend more then, for some reason.  This is a really great recipe.

reviews.review_text: I was on a search to make something different than our regular staple chocolate chip cookie and thought I would make an oatmeal cookie but didnt have a great recipe until I found this one. I read some of the reviews and thought, this is the one I want to make. Well I have to say these cookies were awesome. I took one of the reviewers suggestion and soaked my raisins but I choose a mixture of French Vanilla Kahlua, Frangelico liquor, and a bit of Peach Schnapps. Oh let me tell you these cookies did not stick around long at all. The combination of the liquors in the raisins gave a wonderful vanilla aroma and just made the cookies taste wonderful. My son said the only thing that would have made these a bit better was a bit of walnut included so I am going to give that a try today! Thanks Bev for a wonderful recipe! I highly recommend!

reviews.review_text: To my surprise, I learned while making these cookies for the second time that I had accidentally improved the recipe the first time I made them.  I had doubled the recipe and didn't realize that I forgot to double the amount of oatmeal. (I used only three cups of old fashioned oats for the double recipe.)  I took the cookies to a church event and everyone loved them, even people who said they usually don't care for oatmeal cookies.  While preparing the cookie batter for the second time I saw that the recipe required six cups of oatmeal.  That's when I realized that I hadn't put in the correct amount the first time.  I added the six cups.  The cookies are much tougher and harder to chew.  I don't like them nearly as much.  I recommend using half the oatmeal, especially if you're making them for someone who isn't a real fan of oatmeal cookies. I also followed another reviewer's suggestion to soften the raisins by boiling them for a minute or two and then draining the water.

reviews.review_text:
I adjusted some ingredients, due to diabetes and trying to eat healthier.  I used 1 cup APF and !cup whole wheat flour. I added 1 and 1/2 tsp cinnamon. I used 1/2 cup real butter and 1/2 smart balance.   I used half real sugar and half fake sugar.
For the brown sugars I used 1/4 cup fake brown sugar (which equals 1/2 cup) and 1/4 cup real brown sugar (due to the too sweet reviews).  I also soaked the raising in 2 eggwhites and 2 tsp vanilla in a sandwhich bag while I was getting everything else together.  I did still add one whole egg and another egg yolk to the sugar mix.  I added the soaked raisins at the end as recipe calls.  I also added  1 cup crushed walnuts.  It was the best healthy cookie I have made yet. My hubby really liked it and I'm sure my kids will eat them until gone.  I made these really big only 33 cookies came out of this. They came out fluffy but slightly moist. So they are like a mini meal.  Thanks for a great base recipe.

reviews.review_text:
Incredible!!! I have made two batches and the first batch I forgot to add the cinnamon. I added a splash of rum to the water that the raisins were soaking in as I wasn't sure how much to add. Although the cookies were great tasting and puffy when they came out of the oven they fell and were flat and chewy even though I chilled the dough first. Update - just noticed the five stars didn't take so came back to add them in.  This recipe deserves more than 5 stars.

reviews.review_text:
Absolutely amazing oatmeal cookie recipe. I've been looking for a good recipe for ages - I hate when my oatmeal cookies don't stay soft once they're cooled! These are perfect and stay just the right texture whether it's 5 minutes or 5 days after they come out of the oven.
I've made them three times now - I added cinnamon once because I love it, but they're fine without. Also, every time I nibble a bit of the uncooked dough I think "oh, right, I meant to cut back on the salt" but the end result works. I love when certain ingredients are just on that edge between enough and too much, and that's how I feel about the salt level in this recipe. Any more and it would be too much, but the current amount is great.

I've chucked my other oatmeal cookie recipes out. This is it.

attributes.source_text: stay soft once they're cooled

reviews.review_text: These were absolutely devine. I like to munch a healthy cookie sometimes in the morning with my tea because I don't eat breakfast and these cookies are to die for. So soft and chewy with a hint of crispness around the edges. My favorite kind of cookies. I went ahead and used instant oatmeal. Only realized it when I was about to put it into the batter. I had read some reviewers also did with great results so I wasn't worried. They turned out fantastic even with the instant oatmeal. Thanks so much for your delicious recipe Bev. Too bad my DD is missing this batch cause she is a cookieaholic. She will have to wait for her next college care package. Forgot to say this is the first time I actually made the amount of cookies the recipes says it will make. In this case 36.

reviews.review_text: These will probably never be my favorite cookies, but they were very good. I did make quite a few changes. I soaked the raisins in hot water and spiced rum which turned out nice, but I still subbed semi-sweet chocolate chips for 1/3 of the raisins because we don't like a lot of raisins in our oatmeal cookies. Next time I might just make them with only chocolate chips. I added 3/4 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp nutmeg & 1/4 tsp cloves. I also subbed splenda and brown sugar twin for 1/3 of the sugar and brown sugar and wheat flour for 1/4 of the all-purpose flour to make them a little healthier for me. And finally I used half quick cooking oats and half steel cut oats which I think changed the texture in a way that's kind of hard to describe, chewy and almost crunchy but still very soft and moist.
