reviews.review_text: Cooking is not my favorite thing to do; however, I love to look at  recipes. For my friend's birthday, I decided to make her brownies from scratch, a feat I have never before attempted. I doubled the recipe for a 9x13 pan. It was very easy to put together. The cooking time was definitely longer than the additional 5 min. for double the recipe; more like 10-15, but it could have been my oven. Still, I just kept an eye on the brownies once 30 minutes passed. Other than doubling, followed the recipe exactly. I added chocolate chips to the batter. They came out very moist and chewy, which is how I prefer them. They were very rich and chocolatey. My friend was quite happy and pleased with them, as was I. Definitely a recipe I will keep and make again in the future. Maybe even one that will break me of using boxed brownie mixes all together.... ;) LOL Awesome recipe! Thanks for sharing.

reviews.review_text: Sooooo EASY, Sooooooo Quick to make, soooooo versatile, and sooooooo gone in a flash -- even though I made a double recipe two weeks in a row!!  Used the brownie ingredients as listed, except I doubled them and used a 9x13 pan for baking.  I checked the brownies at 20 minutes, and they were already done.  But that could just be my oven.  The first batch I made, I cut up some peanut butter cups and added to the batter.  Very good.  The peanut butter cut some of the sweetness of the brownie.  I had leftover Mounds bars from Halloween, so I cut those up and used those in the second batch I made (I used the fun size, 12 oz bag, and I cut each one in half).  The Mounds bars made the brownies seem even more chocolatey.  These were my favorite (I'm a chocoholic).  You would definitely have to love chocolate for the Mounds addition.  Very moist, very good flavor.  Will definitely make again and try otehr variations.

Aug 4, 2008  WOW!! These were good! I wouldn't call these a brownie. Mine were more like a flourless torte. They were super, super moist. I didn't have large eggs and used 6 medium since I doubled the recipe. I don't know if that was what made them so wet-ish. Whatever...they were so good. I used a bag of Hershey's milk chocolate chips and some cut up large marshmellows since I didn't have the miniature. I will be making these again and I will use large eggs next time to see if there is a moisture difference. Thanks so much for sharing this recipe!

I've made these again but with the correct size eggs.  They were very different from my first attempt.  These are the perfect brownies!!!  We doubled the recipe and used dark chocolate chips.  I can't imagine finding a better recipe for brownies.

Great brownies.

UPDATE:  The first few times I cooked these they seemed thin.  So, I doubled the recipe and cooked them in a 8 x 11 pan and resulted in the thick, chewy brownies I was hoping for. I only added about a half cup of walnuts and that seemed perfect. I thought 1 -2 cups would be way overboard on the walnuts and 1/2 cup was just right. reviews.review_text: Fun in the kitchen!! I had a great time choosing what to put in these brownies. My choice? Marshmallo and peanutbutter- just like my favorite sandwhich when I was young( a very long time ago)! Reeses now makes tiny little peanut butter cups- perfect for mixing in (and how could you go wrong with more chocolate)? I mixed in some mini-marshmallo's. Now I know why I never came across these as a baking ingredient before---they puff up and all go to the top of the brownies. Well, they may have looked like a bad science experiment, but they sure tasted great. We loved the flavor combinations. Next time I'll mix in the Reeses,pour half the batter in the pan, swirl in some marshmallo topping, then follow with the rest of the batter on top.Hopefully this will result in a more appealing looking treat.

This is my go-to recipe for brownies, & everyone that eats them is in awe of how delicious they are! I give the recipe out quite a bit these days. I always double the recipe, & add in a tsp of baking powder for a little fluffiness to them. My favorite add in is peanut butter m&m's, which I usually put about 2 cups in (almost the whole 16oz bag) & then finish the bag off while they're baking ;) I've tried: white chocolate chips & maraschino cherries drained & chopped, white chocolate chips & macadamia nuts, reese's chips w/ chocolate chips, old fashioned peanut butter wafer candies crushed with chocolate chips, mini m&m's, mini reese's cups, peanut m&m's, and even crushed up heath bars with chopped almonds. Everything you can think to add is amazing in these tho, so have fun with it :)

excellent brownies!  easy ingredients and easy to make too.

i've not tried them without mix-ins but they are very fudgy and gooey with!  if you are looking for a cakey brownie, keep looking cause these are dense and rich with a strong chocolate flavor!

i took the suggestion of someone else and added candy bars!  OMG!!!  my personal favorite was twix and milky way (love me some caramel!) but i made some for my dad's birthday and since he's not a caramel fan i used 3 musketeers which i may have liked just as well!  i did not care for adding snickers as i thought it made the nuts taste a little burnt.

when i doubled the batch, i used a glass pan (greased) and had to cook about 35 mins.  single batch in foil worked out perfect at 25 mins.  i do suggest letting them cool (it's not easy, i know!) before cutting and eating as they are much easier to work with then.

reviews.review_text: I finally had a chance to make this recipe today, only with one small change.  I made it in a loaf pan instead of the 8" square.  I baked the brownies for 20 minutes and they appeared to be a little under-done.  I left them in for another 5 minutes and they looked gorgeous!  However, after they cooled and I cut a small piece to try them, I found that they had probably baked a little too long as they were a lot more cakey than I had imagined, based on everyone's reviews. I've chosen to not give an actual rating since I didn't use the correct pan (not the recipe's fault), but the recipe does get 10 stars for taste - they're really delicious!  I'll definitely make these again, only pull them out about 5 minutes earlier.....they'll probably have a fudgier texture that way.

I would suggest just adding one 3/4 cup of chocolate chips. Some day I will make these again, but adding Reeses Peanut Butter Pieces to them. Hope they turn out better than the ones I made with the chocolate chips.  I am only giving this recipe 2 STARS. reviews.review_text: I have made these twice. The first time I followed the recipe exactly, though I thought 1 cup of chocolate chips ended up being too much. Also my brownies did not get done at 350 for ~35 minutes. They were still way too gooey, though they tasted great. This time I substituted one ripe banana for 1/4 cup of the butter and only put in about 1/2 cup chocolate chips, and I baked at 375 for 10 minutes, then turned it down to 350 for the remaining 20. They turned out perfect! A little more cakey and definitely a some banana flavor, but I like that and esp. like reducing the fat. They were still very moist. Next time I may try substituting Splenda granular for some of the sugar, too, to reduce the calories further. This is definitely a great basic recipe and fun to play around with.

Not like you need another review, but here we go! :p This is a wonderful, easy, and versatile recipe! I never buy boxed brownie mix, and this recipe just gave me another reason not to! I added in semi-sweet morsels, peanut butter morsels, and butterscotch morsels. Decadent, delicious, and devoured! And I don't even like chocolate..... DH sends you many, many thanks!

*Update 1/3/12: I just made these again and I ended up making caramel cashew brownies!! I made a caramel sauce (recpe #69479 http://www.food.com/recipe/caramel-sauce-69479) and folded in some crushed salted cashews, mini chocolate chips, and the thickened sauce. After baking, I sprinkled the remaining cashews on top and drizzled/covered it with the leftover caramel sauce. Delish!!!

First I made them plain w/ chocolate chips and I thought they tasted just like a brownie should taste, DH loved them (they were great warm and cool). items.description: I'm publishing this recipe because I'm sure that there are other families who have members, who don't know how or have forgotten how to make ice when the ice tray is empty.
instructions: Empty the ice cubes that are left in the trays (if there are any left) into the bin.
Take the trays over to the sink and fill them with cold water. (Hot water will freeze faster and more clear).
Place the water filled ice trays back in the freezer.
Replace the ice bin if you had to remove it.
Shut the door to the freezer.
Be sure to leave for around 4-6 hours at least to make sure it is frozen.
If you want to experiment, you can freeze things like fruit infused waters or juices.

reviews.review_text: I wanted to make this recipe here for boiled water: <br/>http://www.food.com/recipe/boiled-water-422354<br/>but it called for ice cubes so I had to look up this recipe.  <br/><br/>My mother-in-law told me that I should use "twice boiled still water" to make crystal clear ice cubes.  That confused me.  I mean, what do I do first?  Boil water or make ice cubes?  <br/><br/>Well, I asked my MIL and she said I didn't need ice cubes to boil water for ice cubes.  Whew.  I mean, I'm writing this comment to let people know.  If someone doesn't tell us, how are we going to learn?  <br/><br/>So I half-filled a pot with water to boil it without adding ice cubes and it seemed to go okay at first.  I kept waiting and waiting for it to finish boiling the first time so I could boil it a second time.  You know what happened?  It turned to steam and disappeared!  It wasn't "still water" it was steam.  How can you boil water twice and still have water to make crystal clear ice cubes with so you can make real boiled water?  <br/><br/>Well, after trying this step six or seven times and getting the same result each time, I decided just to use half-boiled water to make ice cubes.  I mean, I couldn't let the whole pot of water turn to steam again, so when the water was half boiled away I took the pot off the stove top and poured the water into the ice cubes trays.  I had to use hot pads to pick up the trays and put them in the freezer (another step that anyone failed to mention).  I was disappointed with the results.  I had to throw it away.  Let me tell you what happened.  <br/><br/>I was so excited I made so much progress with the recipe that I went looking for my DH to show him the trays in the freezer but when I opened the freezer door a whole bunch of steam came out in our faces! The water was turning to steam anyway, even though I had taken it off the stove!  What's a person to do?  I try and I try and I try.  <br/><br/>I mean, I come to this site looking for cooking help and you need to be an expert or something to use the recipes.  When are people going to put up recipes that are simple enough for beginners?

I only gave this a 3 star because the endeavor to create the beautiful ice cubes in the picture ran a few hundred dollars and the expense was not previously noted. The first batch of ice cubes I made were all wedges leaning to the right. So then I made some adjustments. One the second try I rotated the tray of water so that the right was on the left and the left was on the right. This time the ice cubes once rotated back then leaned to the left. I was scratching my head beginning to think that somehow the water was alive and trying to escape the confinement. I then moved the shelves around making sure there was nothing creating the slanted wedges of cube. I proceeded to try again...not luck still wedged to the right. I thought then that maybe my freezer was slanted. I filled the tray once more placing it diligently on the shelf in the freezer. With the freezer door open I proceeded to lift the left side of my freezer and then my beloved boyfriend closed the freezer door once we were certain the ice cubes would be perfect. We each took turns holding the side of the freezer for the suggested two hours. Once the two hours we up we opened the freezer door only to find that we held up the wrong side of the freezer. My love was upset at this point and refused to help me. So I then had to call in the professionals as I could not hold the freezer on my own. The land surveyers came to the rescue. It was determined that the hill that my home was residing on was shifting and the foundation was no longer stable. Supports are now needed and the home has been red tagged and determined unsafe to live in. Fortunately so far I have only payed the surveyers... I am now waiting to here back from a contractor about th e support for the home. On another note my parents let us move into their home while our home is red tagged. Her freezer was level and I finally got to try the recipe again... Perfect! ....though no longer sure it was worth the effort. Bland, cold and they don't last long once water is added. The recipe was spot on though. Thank you for sharing!

OMG! YESSSS!!! FINALLY!!! PERFECT!!! I am sending this recipe to my family and friends right away!
I don't eat ice but like to keep it around in case of injuries. Everyone else though, seems to love it and freely help themselves to it when they come over. They love my ice but can't seem to figure out how to make it for themselves. They continuously get upset when they go to the freezer to get ice and none is there. Then I get angrily blamed for slacking off. Because I don't eat ice, half the time, I am unaware there is no ice or only one cube left in the three trays located in the freezer.
I have made many, many attempts through the years to explain the ice making process with no luck. I have wanted to pass my wisdom on but my instructions... even though they are identical to yours... are met with bewildered blank stares.
Maybe... (!) with the help of these instructions, they will FINALLY empty... (!) the... trays... in-to... the... binnnn..., ... add... wa-ter... to... the... emp-ty... i-ce... tr-ays...(!) and... pu-lace... them... in-to... the... freez-zer(!) If this recipe works, I will be "DOIN' THE DANCE!" Thank you! Thank you! Thank you!
For 30 years, I have done my best to get everyone to understand that empty ice trays left on the counter tops DO NOT MAKE ICE ! This concept just seems to be too difficult to grasp. Understanding that empty ice trays placed in the freezer FAILS to make ice every time hasn't caught on either no matter how often I have presented this teaching. I have just about given up hope. This recipe is soooo cool! I can't wait to see the surprise on their faces when they finally (hopefully) make actual ice for themselves! The only modification I think is important and crucial to add to this recipe is a sixth step that stresses the importance of "repeating steps 2 to 5 without fail each and every time you do step 1 !
I can't wait to see real homemade ice again! If I could see you, I would hug you!

This is a workmanlike, versatile recipe. Those who want to up their game will want to move on to Hand-made Frozen Water-Marinated Water. A bit of extra time and effort, and possible serious injury, but a crowd-and emergency-room pleaser and well worth it.

Ingredients:
For the water: 2 c water
For the marinade: 1 c water.

Directions:
1. Fill medium-sized bowl with water
2. Drizzle in marinade, one teaspoon at a time
3. Cover with plastic wrap and leave at room temperature 24 hours
4. Uncover water carefully, and with a silicon spatula, gently scrape the condensed marinated water on the underside of the plastic wrap into a small container and set aside
5. Open freezer door
6. In each hand, gently scoop one handful of water from bowl (do not discard remainder, though no one knows why)
7. Gently put hands as far back in freezer as possible
8. Use right shoulder, then chin, to close freezer door
9. Remain motionless for 10-14 hours
10. Remove hands from freezer

If you are able to open hands, you will have two uniquely shaped frozen delicacies, and usually only mild frostbite. (If hands are too frozen to unbend fingers, place on countertop and rest at room temperature.)

Slide each Frozen Water into an espresso cup and garnish with reserved condensed Water-Marinated Water.

Beverage pairing: Steamed Ice Cube Tea

For a more delicate version, see Hand-made Frozen Water-Scented Water.

I loved your recipe!  I knew it would be a big hit in our house and it was!  However, I underestimated the cooking skills of my family member, which surprised me because they typically don't have much trouble in this area.  I don't want to say their ongoing failure of the stupidest nature was related to the fact that all members of this household other than myself are of the male gender, but I'd prefer not to credit their shortcomings to genetics either.  Anyways, as I observed their efforts I found they were in fact following your recipe for ices CUBES (as in the plural of cube) but they were producing unified cube sets, I found I more specific directions were needed to help them overcome this ice block. After discovering the nature of their continuing failed attempts at producing cubes rather than cube-unit connected by a healthy, and ridiculously strong sheet of ice cementing them together. This is where there tweak comes in.  (I hope this helps other cooking-challenged persons out there or those of you just having a little trouble with getting the knack of this seemingly simple recipe.):

*The top of the the tray is NOT the fill line.  Fill the tray enough so that the individual compartments are completely filled.  Any excess water covering the separate compartments will be removed in the next step.  Next, gently tilt the tray from side to side letting excess water pour over sides of tray into sink.  Continue to tilt tray from side to side until there is only enough water remaining to fill only the compartments.  Also, by doing this, the water will fill all the compartments in your tray evenly and thus produce the uniform sized cubes of professionals!

Thank you again for your recipe!  And I hope this helps anyone who was having trouble mastering this one!

Despite my difficulty in finding suitable water, I finally settled on some bathroom tap water as my potential ice choice. I excitedly skipped downstairs to the kitchen with my tray, but ALAS!! All the water had escaped. I think the above receipe really should include instructions on how to carry the receptacle in question to the freezer so others do not make my mistake. My next journey to the freezer was more fruitful. I managed to place the tray inside on a suitable shelf. After following the next instruction dutifully for 3 hours, my wife opened the freezer to find me near death. ALAS!! Another mistake on my part, as I thought I was supposed to accompany the ice tray into the freezer, shutting the door behind me. I can only imagine how many others are still stuck in their freezers. Despite this, I ploughed on, and patiently waited for my ice to form, with each passing moment more painful a wait than the arrival of my child (wife confirms this). I think opening the door and checking on the forming ice every 5 minutes seems to help create a more solid shape. I also placed a pack of cold lozenges in on the same shelf. I don't know what they do, but after explaining my recipe to my neighbor around hour 3, he convinced me that it would work wonders. Finally, feeling confident, I took the ice out of the freezer, and carefully extracted a cube from the tray. I was surprised it was so cold, as it wasn't described in the recipe, it's much colder than water. On reading some other reviews, it seems others have had the same experience. All in all, a great recipe, and I had the best day trying it out. Thoroughly recommended. 5 stars.

My husband bought me a new stand mixer (it's PINK:D) and I have been scouring the internet looking for recipes to break in my new toy. I tried my hand at various breads, and pies, but nothing this difficult...I'll admit that I was intimidated; even though the instructions were very detailed, it took some encouragement from my hubby and 2 glasses of wine to brave this one. (the wine may have been watered down by all of the ice in it though...no worries over irresponsible cooking). Everything started out ok...I put the water straight into the mixing bowl to save time and avoid the step of putting it right in the freezer...I tried to mix it on a med-high setting, but it just flew everywhere:( I may have to practice this step some more. Next, I turned on the oven to 350, poured the water in the trays, and popped them in. (once again, trying to save time, and cut back the 2 hour freezing time...) but to my horror, the trays started melting...in a panic, i grabbed them out without oven mitts, but I just popped some ice from the freezer onto the burns, and the swelling subsided. En route to the oven with said half melted oven trays, I tripped over my hubby and daughter playing floor hockey with an ice cube, and thus spilled the precious liquid everywhere. Sigh. As tempting as this recipe is, I think I'm going to have to hone my skills before attempting again...

I really wanted to try this but unfortunately my water pump on my well went out. After pondering my sad situation for the better part of the day I came up with a pretty clever substitute... ( not to toot my own horn mind you). I found some left over ice cubes in a tray, dumped them in a bowl and waited. It took a couple hours for them to change so after watching them for the first hour or so far I decided to make better use of my time waiting by evening out all my uneven shoe laces, and putting a conditioning treatment/ detangler in all of our toothbrushes. And alas.. finally the cubes ( much to my suprise) had changed to the perfect substitute! I took the bowl and dumped the freshly morphed contents into the trays and placed in the freezer. This gave me plenty of time to polish my driveway, as well as flossing the rocks out of my tires. In only matter of a few more hours I opened the freezer and VIOLA!!! I had what I would call for all intents and purposes ICE CUBES! I am sure the origional publisher of this recipe might be able to tell there was a substitute.. BUT.. I made do with what I had. I hope to make this again soon... maybe over the weekend as it did take about 4 hours all together. It was very tasty though, I do suggest printing this off and adding it to your recipe stash.

My wife and I have been dining at the Palms for ages and from the beginning we have been a huge fan of their ice cubes - so smooth and cold - just perfect. We've become close friends with the manager, but no matter how many Gin Fizzes I feed him, he refuses to share their recipe. I've gone to great lengths to try to duplicate this at home, but have always failed miserably. We even tried to sneak some home one night in my wife's purse, but when we arrived home, they had some how gone missing and my wife's bag was a soggy mess. With much trepidation and little confidence, I gave your recipe a go. I was anxious and kept checking on them every five minutes for what must have approached 15 hours with nary a positive result. Additionally, for some unclear reason, my ice cream and leftover chicken stock both melted and had to be discarded. I had given up hope and passed out dejected and exhausted on the couch. I had forgotten to discard the unsuccessful recipe before my brief respite and when I awoke and went to pitch my disastrous attempt, I was astonished to find perfectly smooth, cold, ice cubes at my disposal.  My wife and I quickly broke some out and tried them with some tepid tap water - perfection - just like the Palms! My only complaint is this recipe takes much longer than the implicated two hours. I recommend anyone using this recipe to make it at least 24 hours prior to serving. Other than that, it's perfect. I can't wait to see the look on the Palms' manager's face the next time he comes over and finds out I've finally duplicated their recipe!

attributes.source_text: perfectly smooth, cold, ice cubes

reviews.review_text:
Where to begin with the fallacies of this recipe? Let's start with the missing items from the ingredients list. It only mentions water on the list, then in the first step of the directions, something called trays is mentioned. I racked my brain for a few minutes on what these trays could be. I went to the source of all modern day knowledge for some assistance, Wikipedia. A quick search for trays told me a tray is a shallow platform designed for carrying things. The examples of trays listed there include a butler's tray, a cafeteria tray, surgical trays, seed trays and a darkroom tray. I went out and purchased these items expecting to use them for this recipe, boy was that a waste of money. None of them aided me in my quest for ice cubes and a cold beverage. Thinking I hit a dead end, I realized this recipe was on food.com so where else should I go but the food network on TV. I sat on the couch drinking hot beverages for a week straight hoping to find out something that mentioned these "trays". Nothing. I didn't know what to do. I cried, paced back and forth, banged my head against the wall, called my mom, and then it hit me. I don't know why my kids were throwing that ball in the house but it hurt. After a few more hours, I decided to start from scratch. I went to my favorite search engine, livorobot.com and searched for "ice trays" and voila, I now know what trays are being referred to. Turns out I could just pick these bad boys up at the local grocery market.
Now that I have the trays, I found I can basically skip over step 1 for the first attempt since I've never used them before. Direction step #2 was self-explanatory to say the least so good job on that. Step #3 got a little tricky because there was no descriptive way to perform this task. When I finished step #2, I was physically located at the kitchen sink and step #3 tells me to place the trays in the freezer. They must have had a completely different kitchen layout as I cannot reach the freezer from the sink. My first couple attempts at performing step #3 left me drenched with a wet floor to clean up and trays flying everywhere. Long story short, please add "gently take the water filled ice trays from the kitchen sink over to the freezer and place them in there", emphasis on gently.
Directions step #4 is also self-explanatory if you actually own a bin to keep ice in. Step #5 I found to be a very key point but again is missing pertinent information. Once I shut the freezer door, how can I see the water, ice trays or ice cubes? This also brought me to a point where I was unsure what the next step would be. I see at the top under total time that there is a 2 hour cook time involved but I did not see any step in the directions that would even hint at using any cooking appliance. I got to the point where I was tired of drinking hot beverages so a few days later, I decided to throw all caution to the wind and stray from the directions by opening the freezer door. I found the water that was poured into the trays had turned into ice without any actual cooking at all. I began using the ice immediately and haven't looked back.
Once I was finally able to enjoy a cold beverage with ice cubes in the glass, I decided to get on here to write this review and warn others of the potential mistakes of following the directions as marked and stumbled upon a gallery of 6 photos of ice cubes. I realized if I had only gone here first, I would have been able to view a photo of an actual ice cube tray that was eluding me for the first couple weeks of my toil. I also realized how convenient it would be to ship ice cubes to all my friends in a small white envelope as shown in photo #3. One of my friends is currently attempting a weight loss routine and was over the house the other day before I was able to figure out how to make these ice cubes. We were discussing meal plans for the day and she suggested having an ice cube for dinner or maybe just sharing the run off but sadly I still did not crack the code for these babies yet. It's great to know I can easily ship them through the local mail to my family and friends.
The other good thing and one of the main reasons I came across this recipe in the first place is the fact that we're talking about lactose and gluten free ice cubes. Most of my family is allergic to both so this will come in very handy in the future. There are also many other great health benefits of these such as being very low in carbs, sodium, cholesterol, saturated fat and calories as mentioned in the categories this recipe is listed under. I can't begin to tell you how wonderful it was to know all of this and then taste the refreshingly cool benefits of the first batch of cubes in a glass of ice cold water. I hope you can master this recipe with the tips I have provided and can enjoy the same euphoria as I have.

attributes.source_text: taste the refreshingly cool benefits

reviews.review_text:
I've gone over and over this recipe, and have not had any luck teaching it to my husband, or elderly father who lives with us. I understand how painstakingly laborious it is to carry the tray to the sink, BUT THEN to open the freezer and place it inside was just too much. My husband is just  starting to recover by watching extended periods of ESPN, and my father had to take an Aleve and then a two hour nap. Thank God I was there to wipe the sweat from their brows, and to cheer them on, because I don't think they would have made it halfway to the freezer door with out my help and encouragement.

Maybe if you could provide a video attachment of how to complete this task, and then within the video break it down into small, manageable steps for our family members to try to emulate at their own pace.
Also, if they watch it beforehand, they can start to mentally prepare for this argewious task.

My suggestion is to train and film retired circus monkeys filling and freezing trays of ice in a similar home environment. Hopefully, this would be a simple and effective way to help our family members see that this is not just fantasy, or "pie in the sky." This really can be done.

Remember, this recipe is not for the faint of heart, or for individuals who possess a XY chromosome. 

Save yourself the frustration and splurge by purchasing a bag of ice at your local grocery store.  And make sure you buy a bottle of margarita mix to go with it.

I love this recipe ... but I did make a few changes. ;) First I I layered my counter tops with paper towels so as not to get water all over the place. Next, I took the ice cube trays out of the freezer and set them on the paper towels. Then I went back to get the bin and set that on the counter as well. Unfortunately that must have been just long enough for some condensation to form on the bottoms of my trays because when I tried to empty the cubes from them the paper towels were all stuck to the bottom of the trays. Ugggh! Once I got that all straightened out I started to remove the cubes from a tray to put in the bin and one popped out of that bugger so hard it landed on the counter, skidded all the way across it and flew off and went completely airborne, finally landing right in the cats water dish. Wow, who knew a cat would get so mad over a little water in the face. Anywhooo, once I got all the cubes in the bin and the trays filled up and back in the freezer it occurred to me that if I had just followed the recipe as it was written I probably wouldn't have had all those troubles in the first place. Sheesh, making ice cubes is hard! That must be why nobody else in the house makes them but me. This recipe is a lifesaver. Thanks Chrissy!!

I was totally out of ideas for what to take to our family reunion last weekend at Lake Texoma. It was going to be so hot and I just didn't feel like taking something hot, like tater tot casserole, etc. Then I found this recipe and literally began to rejoice! My kitchen turned into the Hallelujah chorus!

My biggest tip is to be sure you leave enough time when making the ice cubes as this cannot be rushed. It really does take two hours.

Second tip: this needs to be served right out of the freezer. It just won't keep otherwise. We live in Dallas and left for Texoma at about 9 for a family lunch that was served at noonish and the ice cubes were all watery when we arrived. But my family still loved it! I just think it would have been better had we been able to serve it right out of the freezer.

Finally, this recipe is gluten-free, lactose-free and is low carb. That wasn't clearly stated in the recipe and when my cousin asked if it would upset her kids' stomach (like every other effing thing they have ever eaten), I wasn't sure and we had to pull out my son's iPad and look it up. Thankfully, it was something they can eat.

I am convinced you could serve this to anyone, no matter what their allegeries, real or imagined, and be fine.

Thanking you so much for posting this.

attributes.source_text: what to take to our family reunion last weekend
my family still loved it

reviews.review_text: This recipe literally saved my life.  I had spent years trying to create the perfect ice cubes, and failed every time.  I missed my children's first words, their first steps, birthdays, holidays, anniversarys. Having guests over was humiliating, I was embarrassed serving asymmetrical, shams of ice cubes.  My husband and I began to argue all the time, he was tired of having to drink room temperature ice tea after working 10 hours at the power plant.  It got so bad that I couldn't even look at an ice cube without becoming angry over my many past failures.  My husband filed for divorce and moved with the children to Wyoming.  I was on a path of self destruction, lashing out in public whenever I saw someone with an ice water.  Then, I finally reached rock bottom, I was arrested and spent 6 months in jail for risk of injury to a minor after I destroyed a young girl's lemonade stand in a fit of rage.  When I released I vowed to seek help.  I searched the internet high and low for the perfect ice cube recipe, when I stumbled upon this life saver.  I was optimistic after reading the reviews, so I gave it a shot.  Let me just say these were the best ice cubes I've ever enjoyed!  Perfectly frozen and symmetrical, and low carb too!! Since finding this recipe I am enjoying life again, I frequently have guests over, and get countless compliments when I serve these ice cubes.  My husband has moved home with the children and we are working on our marriage.  I've even decided to give back to the community, volunteering my time teaching other tortured souls who have not yet been successful with their ice cubes.  I honestly don't know where I'd be if I hadn't found this recipe, it saved my beverages, my marriage, my family, my friendships, and my life.

attributes.source_text: I frequently have guests over, and get countless compliments when I serve these ice cubes

reviews.review_text:
Firstly, I must start out by mentioning to any owners of pet dragons, especially the mother of dragons, this is a horrible thing to feed them. I almost had to rush mine to the vet, but unfortunately my insurance does not cover 'mythical creatures'. When asked to see the dragons, I told them they were too tired, and they automatically assume I was lying. Just in case you're wondering, my insurance, not many people have it. It is suppose to be the greatest insurance that ever is, and will be. But I did not come here to complain about insurance, did I?

This 'ice' is insanely difficult to make. The daunting task of freezing water. Mind you, obtaining a freezer is tough work, too. Not long after I set off on my journey for the one freezer to freeze them all, I bump nto a big, blue, police box. Out of nowhere, I walk the same route every day, and all of a sudden, I look like I just ran smack into some 1960's show. Not moments after that, a very tall, yet young looking fellow, stepped out and apologized. Said he came here by accident, and wanted to know if I had seen any rather strange activity. He seemed like an excited fellow, said he was looking for Clara. I only knew of one Clara, my neighbor, but again, irrelevant. I told him no, when a buzzing noise emitted from his pocket. He pulled it out, ran off and shouted "Geronimo!!" The lunatics you run into these days. Anyway, I finally made it to my local wal-mart. Seeing how I've never owned a freezer before, I must've asked 5 people before I got someone who wasn't old, and spoke english. I told them I wanted to make ice, and they suddenly started speaking to me rather slowly. It was annoying, but chances are I wasn't going to find another guy like him anytime soon, so I endured. He asked if I have a refrigerator. When I told him I did, he explained there is a freezer on the top of every refrigerator. I felt like an idiot, and left the store, seeing how it was pointless to purchase something I obviously already have. As I left, I turned a few corners to see a man in a black overcoat and jumped off a building. I'm not sure who he is, but I overheard a man crying out "THAT MAN WAS MY ONLY FRIEND." If that was true, then I feel sorry for the man. As I continued walking, I passed by a creepy looking statue. It didn't look like other statues, and yet, it did. I kept walking, but felt like I was being watched. I Finally got back home, and was greeted by my dragons, Potter and Voldemort. I feel like they don't like each other, and one of them doesn't have a nose. I keep meaning to get help for him, but again, my insurance company is run by a bunch of idiots.

If you find yourself in the middle of the desert for days, with no access to water, how is one suppose to make this, exactly? Even at home, nearly 70 attempts, before I finally got the water to stop moving before putting it in the freezer, and don't ask me how, I just did it, ok. 2 hours and 2 minutes? I can wait that long. So I did. At least, I tried to. There was ongoing noise outside, and on the news there were a bunch of people going crazy, I mean blowing up a football field, really? I flipped the channel. Apparently, more people, going crazy, including a man dressed up in red, white, and blue, a man in an iron suit, a guy I'm sure all the ladies dig, with a big hammer, and an enormously big green rage monster. I could of sworn I didn't clean my room today, because I got high.

Finally, after 2 grueling hours and 2 minutes later, my ice was ready. At least, I thought. Just then, the same man who came out of the police box I saw earlier, burst into my house, shut the door, and introduced himself as 'The Doctor'. I didn't know anyone was sick.

He looked around the house, and after looking displeased, he told me 'Don't blink'. I have a disease that causes me to be unable to do so, so I told him, and he left. Not even so much as a goodbye, rude.

Anyway, after I FINALLY got to pull my ice out of the freezer, it was stone cold and insanely hard to chew. I threw this monster of a creation out my window, and decided after a long day, it was time for bed. I had attempted to search for my weekly bottle of rum, to be disappointed once more. Empty. Again. Why is the rum always gone? In addition, not long after throwing this 'ice' out the window, I could've sworn I heard a guy shout "MY LEG!"

This is an awful thing to make for people. how can you enjoy it? And what's this talk I hear about something called 'ice cream'? Eh, no thanks.

Even Chef Gordon Ramsay himself would yell "ITS RAW" in anger and disapproval.

PS: My other neighbor, whom I have yet to learn his name, really has to stop calling me in the middle of the night. I don't know who he thinks I am, butt I am most certainly not his 'preciousssssssssss'.

I was thrilled to find this recipe!  I'm not that great a cook and this one sounded like something even I could handle.  I decided to make this as the main course for a rather important dinner I held in our home.  It was the first time my husband invited his boss and his wife over for dinner. I was really nervous since I am a newlywed and so inexperienced in cooking.  I wanted to impress his boss and his wife, as my husband is hoping for a promotion, and this special dinner might be just the ticket to that new job.  I followed the recipe step by step.  I was so proud when I set these little beauties on our best china.  Unfortunately, for some strange reason, his boss just sat there looking at his plate like he didn't know what to do.  I tried to fork one, but it just kept slipping away.  My husband followed my lead, but when he went cut one with his knife it shot off his plate and took his boss's eye out.  We spent the rest of the evening in the emergency room waiting area.  Our stomachs were growling so loud that at one point a nurse came in and told us we would have to keep it down, as there were patients trying to rest.  Needless to say, my husband did not get his promotion.  Where did I go wrong?

attributes.source_text: as the main course for a rather important dinner

reviews.review_text: All my life my family enjoy the ice cube made by grandma. When I was little girl, always, I beg grandma, ?Please Babushka, teach me secret ice cube recipe.? Babushka only smile and say ?No, my Golubka, if I tell, no more secret.? Then the terrible thing happen, the tractor accident and Babushka die. We serve the ice cubes at funeral banquet. Everybody like. Then we run out and nobody know how to make more. Whole family is crying: ?We don?t have the secret! The ice cube secret die with Babushka! Terrible day!? For thirty years we drink ice tea with no ice. We drink turnip juice with no ice. We even drink pickle juice with no ice. Everybody curse grandma and spit tea on ground. We have no joy in life. None. Only misery. Now today I am find secret recipe on interweb. I am make the cube of ice in coldbox like you say. Family come home from work on farm: dirty, sweaty, smelling very bad and in bad mood like usual. Then I bring out ice tea with the cubes of ice I have made thanks to your recipe. At first family not trust that Babushka still dead. Uncle Yurly put stake of holly branch through heart of coffin just be sure. I bring more cube of ice and family believe. Now we have hope again. Now come the happy times again. So much I am looking forward to keeping this secret from my own little granddaughter!

OMG!!! The ice cubes are so delicious when I tried it for the first time it didn't turn out that well because I heated the ice cubes a little because they were too cold I think its because my tray looked a little different than the tray in the image so I had to go shopping and finally found a tray that matched yours then I tried the recipe and that was the most amazing thing I've ever eaten and because my friends birthday was coming I thought of making her a ice cube cake but instead of only water I added mentos and mints in the ice cubes and then took a very large glass then i added water and left the ice cubes and water freeze for awhile and added the frozen ice cubes on water then added water and continued this till there was only a half space left and on her birthday when i showed her the ice mentos and mints cubes cake in a cup she was so happy (note my friend likes coco cola with everything from snacks to dinner to lunch to breakfast) so she thought it would be nice to pour a little of coco cola into the glass and after like 15 minutes(the cake was nearly melting) she tried to drink the juice and she cried

attributes.source_text: she was so happy
on her birthday

reviews.review_text: I love this recipe! My now ancient mother used to tell us how, when she was a kid in Brooklyn, they used to find this solid cold wet substance poured out onto the streets after people had laid out the bodies in their best rooms, of beloved relatives who had recently passed on. They would later dump this stuff outside to let it melt into the streets in the hot summer sun, where the local neighborhood kids would play with it and suck on it till it was just a wet stain on the sidewalk. This recipe seems a much more delectable version of that childhood fun and it's so much more convenient too, than having to wait for beloved relatives to expire. Besides, mostly this has become a bygone practice. You simply can't find this stuff on the streets much anymore. Except of course in third world countries (Kentucky, Mississippi, Haiti, Uganda....); but then it's usually just dumped onto dirt streets and of course it becomes crunchy then and there's just not the same degree of pleasure in it. Thanks so much for the recipe of this nostalgic substance of which I really have no memory of whatsoever and can now experience anytime!

items.label: Pancakes
items.name: Pancakes
items.description: This is really a great recipe! It is fast, simple and you usually have the ingredients on hand. I never use a mix! I got this from my sister years ago, and I have shared it many times.
instructions: Beat egg until fluffy.
Add milk and melted margarine.
Add dry ingredients and mix well.
Heat a heavy griddle or fry pan which is greased with a little butter on a paper towel.
The pan is hot enough when a drop of water breaks into several smaller balls which 'dance' around the pan.
Pour a small amount of batter (approx 1/4 cup) into pan and tip to spread out or spread with spoon.
When bubbles appear on surface and begin to break, turn over and cook the other side.

reviews.review_text: Okay so I've been reading through these reviews and I think the problem isn't the recipe so much as the lack of thorough instructions. I've been making pancakes for years so I already know the DOS and don'ts. For those who are having issues first off either use buttermilk or milk mixed with a tbsp of vinegar(buttermilk substitute) this allows for a thicker liquid. Second melt the butter first and allow it to cool while you mix the other wet ingredients and get the dry ingredients together. Add the mixed dry ingredients into the milk and egg and then after slightly mixing this do you add the butter in, not before. Finally DO NOT OVERMIX. I repeat DO NOT OVERMIX. You should only use a whisk for the wet ingredients. You should fold the flour into the wet ingredients with a spoon or spatula until just incorporated. The batter will be extremely lumpy and this contributes to the fluffiness of the pancakes. Let the batter sit while you heat the griddle/pan about 3 mins and then cook. I use this recipe all the time and it is perfect every time.

attributes.source_text: contributes to the fluffiness of the pancakes

reviews.review_text: I used this recipe tis morning, 08.0.2009. It really is a great recipe when you're wanting something that is quick & easy.  The only changes I made to the recipe myself was that I subsituted 1/4 Cup Egg Beaters for the 1 egg requirement, used 1 Cup fat free milk (batter was a little too thick for my liking), and only used 2 Tsp Baking Powder as I felt that 3 Tsp was too much.  Otherwise, the mix came out great and I was able to make 6 pancakes that were between 5 to 6 1/2 inches in diameter, and 1 pancake that was about 3 1/2 inches in diameter.  So, a total of 7 pancakes total ... not bad for such a small amount of mix.  Pancakes had a wonderful buttery flavor and while they weren't as think as the pancakes pictured. They had a great buttery taste.  I also used a non-stick griddle pan (11" x 11" square) so did not grease or butter the pan before placing batter on hot surface.  And just wanted to say that I had no sticking issues with the batter.  I also wanted to mention that if you didn't want to use the 2 tablespoons margarine or butter that you could substitute 2 Tbs Canola oil, vegetable oil, butter substitute, or olive oil.  For pans/griddles that do not have a non-stick surface, you can carefully take hot pan off stove and very lightly spray with butter flavored cooking spray (i.e. Pam) to ensure batter does not stick. You can also use butter or margarine but will only need a very light coating of melted butter/margarine/substitue butter in order to coat pan/griddle surface.   I will definitely have to try this recipe again using real egg and 2% Milk as well as possibly adding some blueberries, apple & pecan, cranberries, or chocolate chips to the mix and come back to let all know how those combinations work :)

attributes.source_text: Pancakes had a wonderful buttery flavor
They had a great buttery taste

reviews.review_text: 5-stars simply due to the great flexibility of this recipe.  Fantastic and easy recipe! Easy to make with readily available ingredients!  I doubled the recipe, which made 8 6-inch pancakes.  I also beat the heck out of the eggs, sifted all of the dry ingredients, and used 1-cup wheat flour and 1-cup bread flour.  I agree with others that the batter isn't quite as liquid as you might expect, but for me it wasn't a problem.  You just might not get the tell tale bubbles you are used to to know when to flip them.  As long as you watch the sides of the pancakes are becoming firm and dull, they are ready to flip.  My pancakes were SUPER fluffy and so delicious!  This recipe will become a staple.  I would suggest lowering the baking powder to 2 tsp and adding a splash more of milk, but even without sifting or without sitting, these turned out super fluffy!

attributes.source_text: My pancakes were SUPER fluffy

reviews.review_text:
Excellent pancakes!  My kids ate them up like crazy and said they were as good as Nanny's scratch pancakes, which they love.  I admit it -- we have been a lazy "pancake mix" family for years and the kids were getting tired of them.  I had tried scratch pancakes before, but they were never very good.  So I am delighted to find this recipe.  It really is so easy to put together and the taste is way better than a mix. 

Two points:  1) When I added the melted butter to the cold milk and egg, it clumped up.  But I kept whisking hard and the clumps dissolved.  Is the right way to do it?  2) As the batter sat for a few minutes waiting for the pan to get hot, the batter rose up like a souffle!  It was not even pourable.  So I added a couple splashes of milk to thin it out.  Didn't seem to hurt things so maybe I'll add a little more than 3/4 cup of milk next time.

Thanks!!

attributes.source_text: My kids ate them up like crazy

reviews.review_text: Very good light fluffy classic pancakes.  I made these with whole wheat pastry flour (it still has the health benefits of whole wheat flour but acts more like white flour, ie without the denseness typical of whole wheat flour) and some partially-thawed organic raspberries.  Quite good.  My one qualm with the recipe is that this is a very basic recipe- so, you should provide more instructions on how to cook the pancakes.  If someone who never made pancakes came across this, they would not know what to do- I recently was looking at an Indian recipe and it said "cook as you would puris" (or something) and I found it quite frustrating because I had to search for a recipe for something else to figure out how to cook the recipe I wanted to make.  But, for those of us who know how to make pancakes, these are very nice.  So many pancake recipes call for buttermilk and this one is nice in that all the ingredients are typically on-hand (unlike buttermilk, at least around here- that stuff is no good for anything but cooking with).  These also hold "extras" well; I had no problem with uncooked spots around my berries as tends to be common with some pancake recipes to which berries are added.  Thanks for posting- I really do think this is a 5-star recipe, but the directions are just not 5-star directions.

attributes.source_text: Very good light fluffy classic pancakes

reviews.review_text: Easily my favorite pancake recipe. I had been laboring with the recipe in The Best Recipe book but it was such a temperamental recipe that I turned here in desperation. This recipe is easy, forgiving, and doesn't have that baking soda taste so many quick breads do. I've made it several times following the recipe exactly (which is a huge aberration for me, the lady who never follows any recipe) and today I had to sub in one part baking soda and two parts lemon juice for the baking powder. Once again, it turned out delicious, tender, fluffy, and wonderful. Today we served them with a very thin layer of buttercream frosting, topped with macerated strawberries. We've had these both with blueberries poked into the top of each pancake as well as homemade blueberry syrup. I intend to try these as the pancake batter for 217026, Japanese Pancakes. Thank you for a real keeper.

attributes.source_text: tender
fluffy

reviews.review_text: So this recipe is really unclear and maybe because I’m still not pro at baking, I don’t get it as well. First, I find the step of adding liquid to the beaten egg is strange. Adding liquid to egg already beaten wouldn’t make the air bubbles disappear? Two, how should I mix the milk and the eggs, and the batter with the flour? With a spatula or a whisk? Three, should the egg be in room temperature since we are beating whole egg? I tried this recipe twice. The first time I tried it, the pancakes were very dense, I mixed the ingredients with a whisk and I made 6 pancakes. The batter was very thick. The taste was great, I reduced half amount of sugar and salt; however, it was dry and too dense to eat. The problem could be the mixing. I used a whisk to mix the flour, using a whisk might over mixing it and create gluten to the flour so the product will be hard at the end. The second time I reduced the amount of flour by less than 10g. I might not beat the egg enough this time. I didn’t mix well the egg with the milk and butter because I was afraid by mixing it the egg with the liquids will damage the beaten egg. Then, I added the flour and I got A LOT of bumps which didn’t happen last time. I also let it rest for 5 min and at the end I got a very liquid batter. It’s worst than last time because the pancakes were more dense I will try a third time and see if it works, if it doesn’t I’ll say goodbye to this recipe Seriously I would like to try different ways to make this pancake a several times, but with this amount of flour and butter, I don’t have the stomach for them??

This is a great pancake recipe!  They always come out light and fluffy.  My suggestions are to add some vanilla and cinnamon (I don't measure, but I would estimate I add about a tsp of vanilla and a 1/2 tsp of cinnamon - it might be a little more) .  Also, I don't like to cook with margarine, so I use butter.  Don't add super hot butter to your egg mixture (unless you LIKE scrambled egg pancakes!), let it cool a bit.  Then add just a small drizzle and incorporate thoroughly to temper the eggs.  Then pour the remaining butter while mixing thoroughly.  I mix all the ingredients together thoroughly before adding the flour.  Once the flour is added, don't overmix (flour + moisture + agitation = gluten, which is great for breads...not so much for tender products, like pancakes!).  Also, I usually double the batch, then we freeze the leftovers.

attributes.source_text: They always come out light and fluffy
They always come out light and fluffy

reviews.review_text: I don't like leaving negative reviews, especially on recipes that have a 5 star rating after over 1 thousand revews, and a food.com video. I'm just not sure that I was making the same recipe as those other reviewers. I did see some other negative reviews and also some notes that this recipe "used to" (not sure what that means) call for 1 tbsp. baking powder instead of 1 tsp., which would make a difference. So in the interest of full disclosure, here is my review. These pancakes weren't BAD. The flavor was alright. I did add some almond extract, so I can't vouch for what they would have tasted like w/o that. I was seriously disappointed in texture though. I was expecting fluffy. These were not. Even though I let the batter set for 10 minutes as suggested by some. They were flat, dense, a bit rubbery and eggy. I might give this a recipe another try with the 1 tbsp. of baking powder, but probably I'll just move on to a different recipe. I know I've made pancakes that were not anymore complicated than this recipe, but much fluffier.

This is similar to a recipe I've used for years out of an old Betty Crocker recipe.  What makes these fluffier than most recipes is the 3 teaspoons of baking powder.  Most recipes call for less and are, therefore, less fluffy.  I didn't have much white flour and used mostly white wheat flour.  It worked just fine.  I suggest that you live a little and use melted butter rather than margarine.  I made blueberry lemon pancakes like this:  added the juice and zest of one lemon to the liquid ingredients.  After putting the batter on the griddle, I sprinkled frozen blueberries on the batter.  A nifty trick is to mix the batter in a large measuring cup and then pouring the batter from that.  Much easier than spooning it on the griddle.  Thanks for the recipe.  I will definitely make it again.

attributes.source_text: What makes these fluffier than most recipes

reviews.review_text: After so many high ratings, I guess I had too high an expectation for this recipe. I have been using a IHOP copycat recipe that we like, but just had to give these a try in case they were a new favorite. They weren't bad, just not as good as what I had already been making. I should also mention that we, unfortunately, have gotten used to sweeter taste of more sugar in the batter. (Slap hand -- bad, bad people.) The family heartily ate this recipe, as we love pancakes, but there was just something missing. If you're looking for a good recipe and aren't used to a sweeter taste, I'd recommend this one. Unfortunately, we've gone to the "dark side" of that white granulated stuff and it's hard to do without once you've had a taste! (Smile.)

attributes.source_text: The family heartily ate this recipe

reviews.review_text: I originally came across this recipe on another recipe site. The person who posted the recipe stated, the recipe was from their Betty Crocker's Cookbook, 6th Edition. It also stated to use 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil, instead of 2 tablespoons of melted margarine. The vegetable oil at least doesn't curdle the milk, like melted margarine does. These were good pancakes. Made 8 (4-inch) pancakes instead of 9. I did add 1 tablespoon of ground flaxseed to the batter, to add more fiber to our diet. While I've been using my Pillsbury Pancake recipe for many years, this was a nice change, and will use this recipe again, as these pancakes were a bit hearty and quite filling. My husband and I were quite full after eating 3 pancakes each.

I didn't have any buttermilk in the house to make my tried and true pancakes, so did a search for pancake recipes and picked this one based on the high rating. I followed this recipe exactly with the exception of adding some vanilla to boost. They were dense, had very little flavor, and were very salty. I don't know if I over mixed or didn't let the batter sit long enough before cooking the pancakes, but their texture was rubbery. I would suggest cutting the salt in half or even eliminating because baking powder, alone, adds a salty flavor. I think the two of them together was too much. These were not a hit with my family. They all agreed that they would rather have Bisquick pancakes than this recipe. Next time I'll be sure to have buttermilk in my fridge and make our favorite buttermilk pancakes!

These are THE best pancakes I have ever made OR tasted. They are so fluffy and light and taste so delicious. They are also WAY easy to make and I always have all the ingredients in my cupboards. A friend came over for breakfast and helped me make them--she couldn't BELIEVE how simple they were to make and how great they turned out. She left with a copy of the recipe. My husband likes them way better than the pancake mix from the store. I add a teaspoon of vanilla an extra tablespoon of sugar and a dash of cinnamon. I also needed to add an extra 1/4 cup of milk (probably because the elevation) and they still came out nice and fluffy. My kids love when I make baby pancakes by dropping a tablespoon of batter into the skillet one at a time--they eat their entire helping. THANKS SO MUCH!

reviews.review_text: This is a great recipe for light and fluffy pancakes.  Because of the ratio of flour and baking powder, I found by sifting the flour with the sugar, powder and salt(or mixing the dry ingredients very well before adding) would lessen the chance of tasting the baking powder. Plus, you won't have to mix as much, which will result in a fluffy pancake.  The batter was just a little thick, but adding just a tablespoon more made it easy to drop onto the griddle.  I have made these pancakes several times and highly recommend these over any store bought mix!   I have even doubled the recipe and froze the pancakes for later use.  Thanks for sharing this easy, wonderful pancake recipe. Try them with real maple syrup if you can, you won't be sorry!

attributes.source_text: fluffy pancakes

reviews.review_text: I am sad to say that these didnt turn out all that well for us to begin with. I, unlike others, had way to thin of pancakes, and I could taste the baking powder in the pancakes....it was nasty.  The also were VERY flat, probly because of the runnyness (sp) of the batter.  BUT....once I added in a little more flour, and some more sugar, the nasty taste dissappeared, and they were thick pancakes, and very much liked at my home.  I did use whole wheat flour as well, and added some cinnamon to the mix (as another reviewer did).  My oldest boy, who usually eats 6 pancakes can only get down 2 with whole wheat, and it helps with the pocket book because whole wheat is so much more filling.  I will use this recipe again, with my added changes.  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: they were thick pancakes

reviews.review_text: LOVE this recipe!  I have tried so many frozen pancakes and recipes using bisquick etc... and they always turn out dry and not flavorful ...... a friend gave me this recipe and OMG!  YUM!  they were PERFECT!!!!  the only thing is i have to learn exactly when to flip them over - i always have a hard time w/that so at times i have one side that is too pale or overcooked but even when that happens they still come out good! lol so its a matter of getting the right color - but these pancakes never fail in taste and its consistency LOVE them!  they even freeze perfect - pop in microwave for a minute - and still just as tender and yummy!!!!  FINALLY great pancake and always have the ingredients on hand... THANKS! (wanted to add i ran out of reg. flour and had bread flour only on hand and it worked perfect!)

attributes.source_text: still just as tender

reviews.review_text:
This is a great recipe. I had tried another one and they pancakes were flat and chewy. This one was easier and the pancakes came out fluffy and very good. I used 3tsp of baking powder that some of the other reviewers said were in the original recipe to make the pancakes fluffier (I prefer the fluffy pancakes) and I also let the batter sit for 15-20 mins per other reviews.

I used almond milk because that's all I had and it worked fine. I also added vanilla, cinnamon and nutmeg for added flavor. They were a hit with everyone. 

The batter was thicker than normal pancake batter but I found that it helps make the pancakes fluffier too. I made a few and then added some milk to thin the batter and the ones I thinned weren't as fluffy as the first few. This recipe is going in my permanent recipe file.

attributes.source_text: the pancakes came out fluffy

items.label: Kittencal's Italian Melt-In-Your-Mouth Meatballs
items.name: Kittencal's Italian Melt-In-Your-Mouth Meatballs
items.description: Cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more Parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com
instructions: Mix all ingredients together in a large bowl.
Shape into small meatballs (at this point you can place on a jelly-roll/baking sheet and freeze to use later, or cover with plastic wrap refrigerate up to 24 hours before using).
Drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce, do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs.
Continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes (depending on how fast your sauce is simmering 40 minutes total should fully cook the meatballs).
After the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired.
**note**  you may also bake the meatballs at 350 degrees F for 25 minutes or until cooked through.

reviews.review_text: Seriously, what is there for reviewer 313 to say that hasn't already been said? These meatballs were deliciously moist and flavoursome, but I'd expect nothing less from one of KITTENCAL's recipes. I made them from a 50/50 mix of beef and veal/pork, which I always find an appealing balance of flavours. Except for using less salt, and adding some marjoram to the oregano and parsley, I made them exactly to the recipe. I baked them first for about twenty minutes - in silicon mini muffin pans because there's then no time-consuming shaping involved and because the silicon pans release the meatballs with such ease. Then I dropped them into the simmering sauce mixture, which I had on a low heat and simmered for longer than the specified time. They smelt wonderful while they were cooking. For the sauce, I used MarraMamba's The Simplest Tomato Sauce Ever (Marcella Hazan) 273976 to which, on this occasion, I had added some red wine to replace most of the juice from the canned tomatoes. I used a low-fat milk. Made for Zaar Stars Tag: what else?

attributes.source_text: These meatballs were deliciously moist
flavoursome

reviews.review_text: I needed a recipe for meatballs for a party, and knew I could rely on KittenCal to come to my rescue. My only caveat was I wanted to accommodate my one gluten-free guest, without singling them out, so I had to substitute the bread crumbs in this recipe. If you cook GF all the time, you probably already have a go-to solution for this, but I really only need to go GF on the rarest of occasions, such as this event. At any rate, I came upon a safe alternative* by pulsing some organic whole grain oats (oatmeal) in the food processor until they were the consistency of bread crumbs, then substituted them in equal measure. I also increased the milk ever so slightly. The result was *maybe* a little more "solid" of a meatball than I would have liked, but it seemed to have little to no effect on the flavor. In fact, of all my party foods for the evening, the meatballs (in Recipe#73362) were the ONLY dish to completely disappear! Everyone raved about them, several asked for the recipe. I think next time to alleviate the texture issue, I may go for a ground beef with a slightly higher fat content (I'd used 90/10), and perhaps cut back a bit on the oats as they do tend to absorb a lot of the moisture. But other than that, it was (as I expected!!) smooth sailing and a great result. *NOTE: for me it was a "safe alternative" because my guest does not suffer from celiac disease, but merely suffers from upper respiratory congestion when consuming gluten. if you need a truly GF alternative, be sure to pick up some CERTIFIED GLUTEN FREE whole oats to use in your meatballs [but you likely already knew that. I'm just sayin' for those of us that aren't fully aware.]

attributes.source_text: I needed a recipe for meatballs for a party

reviews.review_text: These are great! I bought extra lean ground beef (95% lean) and doubled the recipe. I used Italian-seasoned breadcrumbs, garlic powder, regular salt, and dried parsley. I also added the optional oregano. I baked them at 350 degrees F for 20 minutes on a foil-lined jelly roll pan, and then finished them in simmering spaghetti sauce until we were ready to eat (probably about 30-ish minutes). I wore gloves (which I already have for cutting jalapeno peppers) when I mixed up the ingredients, and I used my cookie scoop to make uniform-sized meatballs. After they were all scooped out, I just rolled them a bit (still with the gloves on) so they were more round. From the doubled recipe, I got 72 meatballs. I used some for dinner and froze the rest. They were the perfect amount of "Italian meatball" spicy-ness. My husband said, "Where do you think the saying 'That's a spicy meat-a-ball!' came from?" Hehe. :) These would be great on a meatball sub. Now I just need a perfect spaghetti sauce recipe. Thanks for posting these, Kittencal!

attributes.source_text: the perfect amount of "Italian meatball" spicy-ness
"Italian meatball" spicy-ness
My husband said, "Where do you think the saying 'That's a spicy meat-a-ball!' came from?"

reviews.review_text: I wish I could give more than five stars for these meatballs!! I have always bought pre-made store bought meatballs, just because mine always fell apart or were tough after baking in the oven. I decided to try this recipe when I was having company over one night and wanted to go all the way (I even rolled my own spaghetti noodles) and I swear I will never buy store bought again! these are simple to make, and they cook up beautifully tender and have such remarkable flavor. I have made a few batches of them so far and have decided that if I am rolling meatballs, then I'd better just ROLL MEATBALLS! I make a double or triple batch of the meat and take a few cookie sheets and the bowl of mix to the dining room table, turn on Oprah and roll till I can't roll anymore. I have used this recipe for the meatballs in Italian wedding soup, simply simmering the balls in the chicken broth instead of the tomato sauce. My freezer is currently stocked with these delightful little meatballs in "Kittencal's Italian Tomato Pasta Sauce" and I have already given this recipe out to many friends. Thanks again Kittencal. My family loves you!

reviews.review_text: I made several modifications for taste and because certain things I didn't have at home. For taste instead of salt I used 1 1/2 seasoned salt. I used 1 1/2 garlic powder, 1/4 teaspoon basil because I didn't have any oregano. I also added about 2 tablespoons of chopped onions. I then used 2 teaspoons of dried parsley because I had no fresh. I baked them for 20 minutes at 350. Then I put them in the sauce. Before putting them in the sauce, I tried a small one. It was delicious. It was the best meatball I ever had. You may say I changed the whole recipe. What was changed was the flavor, but the moist comes from the right amount of meat, milk, cheese, breadcrumbs and eggs; Which is what I was looking for. Now I have a meatball recipe that's edible and moist. I was tempted to not put them in the sauce. The are not dry at all. Thanks...

Very nice recipe. I used meatloaf mix (beef, pork and veal) along with an extra small amount of ground beef. I also added dried basil. The meatballs were very tender. I did have extra grease in my sauce due to cooking the meatballs in the sauce. Next time I am going bake/fry the meatballs just a little to eliminate some of the grease. Other than that this is a great recipe. I do have to admit that this recipe saves time by cooking the meatballs in the sauce.

UPDATE--  My family waited a day after cooking the sauce and meatballs before we ate it. It was absolutely perfect.  The flavor of both the sauce and meatballs were amazing. The meatballs were very tender.  For the most part the meatballs did not fall apart. A couple of meatballs did - no big deal. I am going to nix what I stated above and not fry the meatballs ahead of time.  I'll just try and remove some of the grease with a spoon.  This recipe is a keeper.

reviews.review_text: I had no idea what to make for dinner and as I was reading through reviews came across this recipe...  I had all the ingredients on hand so it must have been fate!  I took your recommendation of the 1lb of beef and 1/2lb of pork... and used 1/3c of parmesan, garlic powder, only 1 tsp salt, 1/3c organic 2% milk, a dash of oregano and 2Tbs of dried parsley...   I chose the dried/powdered ingredients to make this recipe super fast and easy to clean (one bowl, cup and spoon!)  I chose to bake mine first since I was defrosting the sauce in my crock pot and I wanted to make sure these would cook through in time for dinner since I started it late...  These were the most tender meatballs I have ever had!!!  Just delicious and perfectly seasoned...  I might try some fresh basil in them next time instead of oregano...  I let them sit in my sauce in my crock pot for close to 4 hours...  We can't wait to try them in meatball subs soon...  Thanks for posting!!!

( love garlic ) I upped the rest of the ingredients. Made these into about 2 1/2 -3" meatballs. I got 18 out of this. I roasted in the oven at your reccomended 350 degrees for about 35-minutes. There is only my hubby and I, so I used 4 meatballs in my sauce and froze the rest - 4 in a qt. size ziplock freezer bag and put all the bags in a gallon freezer bag . My hubby doesn't care for meat in his spaghetti sauce but he said he wanted these meatballs with spaghetti NEXT WEEK!! Now he's planning my weekly meals, lol. reviews.review_text: This is a wonderful recipe that gives you wonderful directions and results in delicious meatballs.  If you have any questions the Chef, Kittencal, is very helpful and informative.  I made a double batch of these for a party.  The only change I made was rather than using regular breadcrumbs I put garlic croutons through my food processor to use in the meatballs.  I baked these in the oven, then froze them several days prior to party day.  I also made and froze recipe #153093 which is what I served with them.  The morning of the party I took out the meat balls and the sauce and let them thaw until ready to use.  While the meatballs were heating in the oven I heated the marinara sauce in the microwave.  When all was hot I stirred them together and served them in a chafing dish to keep warm.  They were a big hit with everyone! reviews.review_text: These really are amazing!  I come from a large Italian family and it's frowned upon to use anything other than the "old family recipe", which frankly, wasn't very good!  Everyone I've made these for (including my dad who still compares everything to his mom's cooking) were skeptical, especially about putting the meatballs in the sauce raw, but they were instant converts after dinner was served!  My entire extended family claims these are the best meatballs they've ever had.  And that's actually a little funny since I also used turkey instead of beef, which the men in my family generally refuse to eat because they claim ground turkey tastes like cardboard.  However, they loooved these even after I fessed up!  I've made them using just ground turkey, and when I can find it, I use turkey sausage as well. I also use store bought sauce (another sin in my family!)because it's easier, and the sauce ends up tasting so great that no one has ever complained! My aunts now think I  may not be such a failure in the kitchen after all!

These are so awesome! Much better than the dry, dense meatballs that Grandma used to make. I always loved her fabulous sauce recipe (#434051) but I modified when I posted it to add meat to the sauce itself because her separate meatball recipe was practically inedible. But these are very delicious, moist, chewy meatballs that even my true Italian DH loves! He asked that I brown them slightly and drain them before putting them in the sauce, which took some of the fat out, and made them crispy on the outside. Other than that, I made just as the recipe says. I used 2 parts lean ground beef and 1 part ground pork, the larger amount of salt and Parmesan as Kit recommends and we thought it was perfect. I made a double batch and froze some which will cut down on the prep next time. They do take a lot of time, but they're so worth it!! Check out my pic of them cooking in the pot -- they're really beautiful too! Would make a nice hearty dinner to serve for friends or family. I'd give them 10 stars if I could.

Update: I always think that spaghetti sauce is better the next day. In this case, I was disappointed that the meatballs lost a lot of their flavor. That said, I think next time I will add more spices as some other reviewers suggested. Maybe I will also use pork sausage instead of plain ground pork. I'll let you know how it turns out!
