reviews.review_text:
Love it love it love it!!!!!!!! have made this many times (just getting around to reviewing it), and my family thinks its great! have halved and doubled it, with great results.I have averaged 6 bananas for the 2 & 1/3 cups called for, and the recipe is beautifully moist.
The *only* problem that i have had is that when I have cook it in a traditional loaf pan, 60-65 mins isn't done. I have gotten around that by dropping the temperature to 325,so the top doesn't burn and leaving it in for approximately another 30 mins ( average 90 mins total )..
But my preferance is to just use my mini-loaf pans :) A full recipe fits 6 mini loafs just right, and they are all cooked through and beautifully golden brown in about 50-60 mins ( depends on how often our 12 y/o opens the door, lol ). Muffin tins work well.. i think i had 20 muffins, last time i did that.
Oh, and the poster was absolutly right - it is GREAT toasted...especially with peanut butter.
Thanks for posting!
ETA: five years later, *still* the best banana bread recipe that I have found, and I keep trying new ones.

reviews.review_text: This recipe was amazing!!! I had some very ripe bananas and a mood for baking that day. I wanted to make some bread pudding but then changed my mind when I saw this recipe. This is the best banana bread I have ever tasted, not even the banana bread used at my favourite breakfast place to make "Banana Bread French Toasts" is as good as this! I did tweak the recipe a little.  I only used half the amount of butter called, and to make up for the missing fat I added a half a cup of unsweetened apple sauce. I also added vanilla extract, cinnamon, nutmeg, cranberries, raisins, pine nuts, walnuts, pecans, and some semisweet chocolate chips. Since I only had two medium bananas and it wasnt enough to make it moist, I added some milk(like a Tbsp) also to add the moisture the oats would absorb. I know this sounds like a lot to do, but it was just that i had some extra time and various ingredients in my pantry. I baked it for 55 minutes at 350 degrees F. It came out perfectly brown and crunchy on the outside but I very moist on the inside. My whole family loved it! They even asked for more!(something that my sister rarely does, or my mother who doesn't like chocolate chips!!!) :O. I will deffinitely make this recipe again very soon. I'm probably going to try to bake them in muffin tins as Bogey'sMom suggested. Thank you very much Shelley!!! I loved it.

reviews.review_text:
This is one of the best recipes involving baking that I've ever seen. I didn't want a ton of banana bread, just enough for one person, so I halved the recipe. Sometimes when you do that, things don't turn out quite right. However, with this one, I felt like nothing could go wrong. Like another reviewer did, I added a bit of cinnamon in the batter. I don't even think that it needs vanilla. Unfortunately, there wasn't enough brown sugar in my cupboard. I added a bit more white sugar. That didn't take anything away from the wonderful flavor.

For those who are concerned about their bananas being "overly ripe," I would just make sure to mash the bananas well so that they really mix into the batter. If the batter is nice and gooey, the bread should come out moist.

I left it in for about an hour, so that time worked well for me. I'll definitely be using this recipe again soon!

reviews.review_text:
Original review:
I have never given a low review, but I thought this was way too gooey for my family.   It seemed like it was undercooked, but I baked it for the 65 min. in a bunt pan like another reviewer suggested (I would not even like to think of what it would have been like in a loaf pan), and the toothpick came out clean, so I am going to say this is what is supposed to be like.  If you want a traditional banana bread, try another recipe.  If you want a banana mush, you would probably like this one.  I guess my family just likes the more traditional bread.  It does have a nice flavor though, just not the right texture  for us.

Gave it another try:

I made this again (I actually did not realize it was the same recipe I had used before).  I replaced 1/2c flour with bran, and added one tsp. vanilla, and some dates that I had on hand.  The texture this time was great!!  The flavor was great!!  This version was gone by the end of the second day.

Not that this recipe needs yet ANOTHER RAVE review; but I just can't resist. For years and years I'd used my grandmother's recipe for banana bread and then came across this one and decided to try it. My family absolutely LOVED IT!! They actually would request that I buy extra bananas in order to make this bread. I also ran into the problem with the cook time when baking in one larger bread pan but have since tried it in smaller bread pans; muffin style; and bundt pan...all of these have turned out fabulous. Another thanks for posting such a fantastic and basic recipe that works well with any additions. One addition that I've made that I've not noticed others posting is to replace 1/2 cup of flour with instant oats. Texture changes slightly but is still very moist and adds a little more nutrition for the family. ;-)

reviews.review_text: This is amazing, no wonder it has so many great ratings! If you don't like it you either a) did it very wrong or b) don't like bananas.  To be exact, I had used a TBSP of butter for another recipe and so I used the remaining 7 TBSP from that stick and used 1 TBSP of apple sauce to compensate.  I also used egg substitute.  As a reference, I used 2 large bananas and 2 medium bananas.  I had no idea how many cups 2 large bananas was, but it turned out to be about 1 1/3 cups.  I usually add chocolate chips or nuts to my banana bread, but this time I decided to be a purist, and I was rewarded for my simplicity.  It took my college-dorm-kitchen oven the full 65 mins, though I checked at 60.  Oh yea, and this is only 7 ingredients!  Incredible!  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: don't like bananas

reviews.review_text: This was a great rtecipe. Our local supermarket sells bananas when they are spotty(I like them this way best)  and they sell  them like 5 lbs for 25 cents, so I am always  buying these things and challenging myself on how to use them up. This recipe  fit the bill nicely. I doubled the recipe, and found after I had  mixed everything  I didn't have two loaf pans, so I used a pie plate and hoped it would work out. It did, and they were both ready after 45-50 minutes. Also, I didn't have enough brown sugar so I used regular sugar, and it worked out fine also. I have had a loaf devoured hot out of the oven, and one for the rest of the week, and I will be baking tons of these for the freezer. Thanks for sharing!

This was a super easy recipe. Prep time was a cinch, as was clean-up.  I added some vanilla extract per one of the reviews.  I normally add walnuts to my bread, but b/c of a tree nut allergy in the house, I had to come up with something else to add.  I added about a cup of fresh blueberries and some dried cranberries to the batter.  What a wonderful addition. Next time I'll add more blueberries as I loved the flavor it added. I used 5 very ripe banana's and the bread was super moist.  I had enough batter left over to make 6 muffins in addition to the loaf.  I'd like to reduce the butter next time also and replace it wtih applesauce and add some chopped up apples to the batter as well. This is a keeper.  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: the bread was super moist

reviews.review_text:
Well, it too me long enough to find out how good this recipe is.  My DW presented me with 3 very ripe bananas and wanted to throw them out.  So I looked up Banana Bread Recipes and decided to try yours.  WOW, how moist and just super great.
I did add 2 more large bananas that were not overripe, and it worked out real well.
I added 1 teaspoon of cinnamon and 1/2 teaspoon of freshly ground nutmeg and 1 teaspoon of pure vanilla extract.
Absolutely excellent. 
I baked 8 in large muffin pans and 1 in a mini bread pan.  The muffins were ready in 30 minutes and the bread pan took an additional 15 minutes. This is now a must to make at least once per month if not more often.
Thank you for posting and sharing this great recipe with us.
"Uncle Bill"

attributes.source_text: how moist and just super great

reviews.review_text: I prepared this recipe using 4 overripe bananas, which came out ot be only 1.5 cups. I added one snack-size apple sauce which brought it up to 2 cups. I lacked the extra 1/3 cup but made no adjustments except to put a tad less than 2 cups flour in. Used a potato masher to mash the bananas, I also added 1 tsp vanilla a good shaking of cinnamon. It made 12 muffins, which I filled almost to the top with batter and baked for 40 minutes. The result was a lightly crisp top and a moist inside. My young kids devoured these and my only regret was that I couldn't have made more to share. I'll be buying extra bananas from now on - some to eat ripe, and some to overripen to make these muffins again.

a moist inside

reviews.review_text: First off, Shelley - thank you for this recipe - in a word, YUM!  Secondly, thank you kokeshi doll for the idea of the bundt pan - worked great (I uploaded a picture - check it out - there's still steam coming off the cake!)  It took about 40 minutes to bake in the bundt pan and was perfect texture inside and nice-n-crusty outside.  Also, thank you Gato, for the idea of vanilla, cinnamon and nutmeg - the additions were good ones although next time I'd add even more cinnamon (maybe like 2 tsp) and about 1/2 tsp nutmeg.  I'm not sure the vanilla added much - I'll try it without next time.  Also, since I only had 4 bananas, I was a hair short on the 2.5 cups - I think 5 would have been right about on.  Anyhow - all together it's a keeper.  Thank you!

attributes.source_text: nice-n-crusty outside

reviews.review_text: Oh My Goodness!! Where has this recipe been hiding all my life? The simplicity and ease of mixing all the ingrediants was so very out of "character" with my old (now garbaged banana recipe).. when telling hubby I would join him in a few, was just going to make Banana Bread, he said "yah okay.. the game will be over by then" - well what a surprize he got !! Said... you decided not to make it? Told him it was already in the oven and baking!! Reply "no ways" (me **giggling**) I did take heed to "keeping an eagle eye" on the oven for burning, but, I got lucky! I hardly could wait the 10 mins for cooling time - the outcome was... 5 thumbs up and thank you so much for sharing this recipe!! Absolutely declicious!!

OK,Ok; I just had to add my two cents worth to the comments. In my books, simple is best with classics like this. I used half w/w and half white flour. The bananas required to make 2 1/3 cups mashed were 6&7 (made two loaves with small bananas) To one loaf, I added 1/2 tsp.cinnamon. Both loaves were well done within 60 min. with a nice dark brown crust. The brown sugar and large measure of bananas made the texture very dense and flavourful. I enjoy the lighter cake like muffins  made with yogurt or sour cream but these loaves are classic. From now on when I see a bag of really ripe bananas for thirty cents, I will grab them and use this recipe.Thanks for sharing.

attributes.source_text: the texture very dense

reviews.review_text:
I've made this several times now and it always comes out perfect.
Let me start by telling you -- I am a former banana bread hater. The consistancy was just not for me. I'm one of those people that will eat to be polite, so I've tried a few BB in my time, all of which did not do it for me. That is UNTIL I made this for my family. I needed to do something with bananas-gone-ripe and my hubby loves banana bread. I tasted it and lo and behold LOVED IT!!! Yes, it's moist, but not gooey. I don't know what's so different about how this is prepared, it's the only recipe I've personally prepared, but the bananas blend seamlessly into the mixture and you just don't get those gooey bites other recipes tend to leave.
This gets 5 stars for converting me!

attributes.source_text: I made this for my family
it's moist

reviews.review_text: I was looking for a good recipe to use up the the 4 really soft bananas on my table. This was the best choice I could have made. It was really fast and easy to throw together with my mixer. Not too many ingredients either. The changes I made were that I used whole wheat pastry flour instead of all purpose, and canola oil instead of butter (and I used only half of the amount called for in the recipe). I don't eat eggs, so I used Ener-g egg replacer for those. My bananas only came out to 2 cups worth, but it worked out just fine. Oh yeah, and I made muffins instead of a loaf. The results were golden brown, moist yet springy delicious muffins. I think this will be my banana bread/muffin recipe from now on. Thanks!

reviews.review_text: The most favored food in our house is banana bread, so I had to search for the highest rated recipe, which just happens to be yours, and try it.  WOW!!!!! It is wonderful!!!!!  It is the most moist and flavorful banana bread that we have EVER eaten.  The only change that I made was to add a few chopped nuts to one half of the top of the unbaked batter.  My husband and I both prefer walnuts in our banana bread, but our boys don't like them, so I put them on top of "our half."  Now everyone can enjoy banana bread just the way they like it because I will only double, triple, or even quadruple this recipe when I make it.  This way, it will last more than 15 minutes.  Shelly by the Sea, you have made a family very, very, very happy tonight!!!!!

items.label: Scalloped Potatoes
items.name: Scalloped Potatoes
items.description: Here's a great scalloped potato recipe that's so easy and absolutely delicious. The leftovers are just as good, maybe even better, the next day. This is one of my favorite and most prepared recipes, from my 1971 Florence Junior Welfare League cookbook.
instructions: In a small sauce pan, melt butter and blend in flour.
Let sit for a minute.
Add all of cold milk, stirring with a whisk.
Season with salt and cayenne.
Cook sauce on low until smooth and boiling, stirring occasionally with a whisk.
Reduce heat and stir in cheese.
Place a half of the sliced potatoes in a lightly greased one quart casserole dish.
Pour half of cheese sauce over potatoes.
Repeat with second layer of potatoes and cheese sauce.
Sprinkle the remaining cheese on top.
Top with some paprika for color.
Bake uncovered for about 1 hour at 350°F.

reviews.review_text:
This was very good! I doubled the recipe, added leftover ham and baked it in a 9x13 to make it a main dish. Based upon reviews I found here and on another recipe site I did make a few slight changes: I made more sauce than what the recipe called for- I about tripled the sauce. I made a roux with 9 T of butter and flour. I whisked in 5 cups of milk and added seasoning salt (instead of table salt), garlic powder and onion powder. I didn't measure- but I think probably added approx. 2-3 teaspoons each. After the sauce thickened I added 4 cups of shredded cheese.

I used my mandoline to slice 10 potatoes very thinly. I spread half of them in my stone dish and added a few dashes of seasoning salt, garlic powder and onion powder over them. Then I sprinkled chopped ham and a little shredded cheese over it and spread half the sauce mixture on top. I repeated with another second layer and topped it with about a cup of cheese. (Next time I will add more.) I covered it with non-stick foil and baked it at 400 degrees for 45 minutes. Then I removed the foil and baked it an additional 25 minutes. This helped the top get a nice crust without burning. When I took it out it looked more "soupy" than I anticipated, but after it set a bit it was just right.

I will definitely be making this again- as a main dish with the ham and without as a side dish. I think next time I will try it in the crockpot. Oh- and another tip I read to cut down on the baking time, but didn't try,  is to microwave the potato slice for about 8 minutes or so. Thank you for sharing the recipe!

attributes.source_text: to make it a main dish
without as a side dish
This helped the top get a nice crust without burning

reviews.review_text: So far I have made this recipe twice. The first time was exactly to the recipe and I was not super impressed... I felt like it was missing something! My husband liked it alright. I think it was just a little bland for us, so I modified the recipe to suit our taste. :) First, I used these new "Rooster" potatoes and a grater that had a slicer on the side. As mentioned in other comments, IT WILL SAVE YOUR LIFE. Well, it'll just save time actually. :P All jokes aside, using something to make the potatoes the same size will be worth it. As far as making the roux, I made a bit more than the original recipe called for. I used 5 tablespoons butter, cooked one whole chopped onion in until the onion was translucent, added 5 tablespoons of flour and let it sit for maybe a minute. Then I added 2 cups of milk, 1/2 cup at a time mixing it thoroughly before adding more. I omitted the cayenne pepper the second time, added salt and pepper and added about 2 1/2 cups sharp cheese, stirring again slowly. Layered the potatoes with the mix, topped with lotsssss of cheese, and baked for about and hour and 15 mins. Looooooved it!

I have no business cooking. I have no idea what I'm doing, so I find recipes on Recipezaar with high ratings, scour the comments for hints and say a little prayer before any attempts in the kitchen. While these potatoes are delicious, I thought I would share what I learned in case there is anyone as desperately in need of help in the kitchen as me.

First, I bought a mandolin specifically for this recipe, and I'm glad I did. Saved me A LOT of time. However, in putting half the potatoes in, I didn't separate them carefully enough... so in some cases, it was as though the slices were three times what they ought to have been.  DUH. Next time, I will take the time and care to lay the potatoes out in a single layer with a tiny bit of sauce alternating each layer to keep them from sticking together and not cooking thoroughly.

Next, I made this recipe the day before because I've heard they taste better the second day. The first day, I tasted them and was worried that in putting the amount of salt called for in the recipe in that I had over-salted and ruined them.  But the next day, they weren't salty at all - they were perfect. (I cooked them the full hour; the next day, let them come to room temperature for an hour and then re-heated them at 350 for 30 minutes. Due to my not separating the slices enough, some of the potatoes were STILL not quite done.) But if I were to plan to eat them the same day, I would cut way down on the salt.

Hope no one needs as much help in the kitchen as me (if they do, they probably need another adult to watch them to ensure they don't end up killing themselves in a tragic vegetable-peeler-incident), but if so, hope this was helpful. Overall, this is an amazing recipe that even *I* couldn't ruin!

attributes.source_text: they weren't salty at all

reviews.review_text: I'm giving this 4 stars even though it didn't work out for me as it should have. I was making a 3-qt casserole and for whatever reason, I only doubled the sauce, when it should have been tripled (or so I thought, read on). However, when I poured the sauce over the potatoes, it just stayed on top like a jelly. It was so thick that it didn't seep down at all. Another third of sauce would not have fixed that. I think the problem was that as soon as you stir in the milk, you need to pour it over the potatoes? I really don't know. That's the only reason I give it 4 stars instead of 5. Also, it took a good 1 1/2 hrs - 1 hr 45 min for the potatoes to get tender, BUT it's a larger casserole and the temperature was reduced (I'll get to that later) and that problem has nothing to do with this recipe. Flavor wise though, it was really good. I just poured some half and half over the top until it was about 2/3 full, stirred it up and guess what? It turned out delicious and not runny at all! It didn't take away from the flavor so the sauce did not need tripling, it just needed more liquid. Oh and I didn't peel the potatoes. I never do. I'm not sure why anyone does. It provides a beautiful natural color and let's you know it didn't come from a box. Finally, I had to reduce the heat to 325 since I had three things baking in the oven.

reviews.review_text: First a  ?Thank You? to Vicki<br/><br/>I prepared this Scalloped Potatoes dish to accompany a broiled NY steak with mushrooms and onions. Along with roasted garlic bread with Steam Spring Asparagus and Hollandaise Sauce.<br/><br/>One enjoyment of preparing and serving a meal is when conversation at the table softens and becomes mute. This happened as everyone focused on their meal.<br/><br/>I did make ?some adjustments? to the recipe.<br/>1- I used Yukon potatoes.--since I had several ?left over?<br/>2- I used ¼ heavy cream with the 1 ¼ milk<br/>3- I used ?white cheddar cheese? within the warm milk- per your instructions to melt.<br/>4- Then I layered the potatoes---2 by 2 and brushed the milk mixture between the layers.<br/>     I topped each layer with ?a bit? of ?Yellow Sharp Cheddar?<br/>-  I also added a bit more cayenne ?.about a teaspoon full--in the over-all total use<br/><br/>Topped everything with the Yellow Sharp Cheddar ? and Paprika.<br/><br/>I wish I had taken a picture for it was a ?perfect Betty Crocker? moment.<br/><br/>The dish remained moist....and quietly exotic.<br/><br/>Thank you....

attributes.source_text: The dish remained moist

reviews.review_text: I always laugh when I read these reviews.  Everybody says, ?I changed this? or ?I added that?.  Sometimes so much it ends up being a completely different recipe, so they're not really reviewing THIS recipe, they?re reviewing THEIR recipe?.  I followed the directions as well as I could.  I hated that the measurement for the potatoes was in CUPS.  Very hard to measure cups of sliced potatoes.  Why couldn?t it say something like ?5 large potatoes? or ?2 lbs. of potatoes? or something more accurately measured.  I was really just guessing if I had the right amount.  Also hated that it said ?sliced thin?- I need to know how thin.  I used the second setting on my mandolin because the first setting was like thin potato chips.  I baked them the day before because I read all the comments that they taste much better the second day.  What I will say is that they were delicious.  Very tasty with warm, homey, mom-made flavor.  The bad part was some of the potatoes were still too firm.  I baked for an hour the first day and an hour the next day and still too firm.  Maybe I had too many potatoes?  Maybe I didn?t slice thin enough?  I will try them again though because they were tasty.  I guess I?ll try slicing them thinner ? maybe a slicing attachment for my Kitchen-Aid mixer will have more thickness options.

To Chef #965732: Try mixing the potatoes with a little of the sauce - do it by hand, to be sure each piece is coated. Then layer it per the directions. Also, you can use the shred tool of a food processor, too. A mandoline is nice to have, though. Wish I had one.<br/><br/>This hand-mixing helps in other recipes, too, like when you're browning onions and don't know how much butter to use - and if sometimes the onions scorch because they aren't in contact with the butter. Melt the butter in the pan, add it to the onions (or potatoes, whatever), and mix by hand to coat all. You can have about 1 T extra butter, but any more is counterproductive.<br/><br/>Potatoes Ana is a favorite of mine. The potatoes are paper thin - that's vital. Hand mix with melted butter to coat all, and bake till golden. There should be several thicknesses of potato in the pan. You can season to taste, but pepper is all I need - and salt at the table.<br/><br/>This is a yummy recipe, but I just HAVE to add garlic, and scalloped potatoes just aren't scalloped potatoes without at least some onion. You can use paper-thin slices in the layers, or just grate some over each layer.

I'm sorry, but I don't have a food processor anymore, so this did take a while to make, and my expectations were higher....I doubled the recipe fo make in a 9x13 casserole dish.  I followed the recipe, except for cooking 1 hour and 15 minutes.  The potatoes were diced small, which usually works for me, and I never did have any luck with putting cheese on top, and leaving it uncovered - it always turns out chewy and a waste.  I'm afraid they were still hard, and I ended up microwaving my daughters' plates, since they couldn't wait any longer, having to work tomorrow.  I put the rest of the casserole for me back in the oven, and covered it, for another 45 minutes.  I asked what they thought of the taste, and got just ok's from them.  Hubby's not so fussy, so I'll ask tomorrow when he has the left overs.  And, we'll see when I get to have mine.... Sorry, It seemed easy, but  I think they should be covered, to cook all the way through, and especially if there is cheese on top - or add the cheese at the end of cooking.  I could've cut them really thin, but the very small chunks should've worked, too.

My family and I were extremely disappointed in this recipe. Maybe because I was psyched to find one that had so many fabulous reviews. I am an experienced cook and can handle any recipe, difficult or easy. This was so bad, that before I wrote this review I made it a second time so I wasn't critical of a recipe I did not cook correctly. I read all of the reviews and took extra precautions -- soaked the sliced potatoes, dried them, grated fresh cheese, and used a bit of cream to make it taste extra special. First, I would NOT suggest making it the day before. I did that the day before Easter dinner. Came out grainy. The second time I made it, it was acceptable, but a far cry from a 5-star recipe and we are not a fussy family. We are sort of boring quite frankly -- we don't like fancy stuff and this recipe is really bland. Maybe my cheese wasn't flavorful enough, not sure. I will continue to look for something that wow's my family and guests -- thank you to everyone who writes in and makes suggestions, as I listened to all of you. Happy Cooking!

attributes.source_text: I did that the day before Easter dinner
the day before Easter dinner

reviews.review_text: This was a big hit in my family.  I made this but did make some adjustments based on previous reviews.  I added onions along with my scalloped potatoes.  I also added fresh minced garlic and some onion powder to the sauce for taste.  I followed these instructions and the dish came out perfectly.  There was some grease but not as much as I thought based on reviews.  Most of this cooked out when I left it in the oven to stay warm while I finished the rest of the meal.  The instructions were perfect and the results matched the instructions.  The sauce thickened up as written during the slow boil.  I seasoned to taste and I poured it over my scalloped potatoes that I cut by hand.  Used 4 russets for this recipe.  This recipe was quick to make without using a food processor.  I used a box grater for the cheese which took all of two minutes...the potatoes where peeled and cut  in 10 min...this was a well written and accurate recipe.  The cook times were spot on and the results were excellent.  Thanks for the recipe.

attributes.source_text: This was a big hit in my family

reviews.review_text: I was looking for an easy scallop potato recipe since i lost my Betty Crocker cookbook.  I saw this and was surprised that I had all the ingredients in my refrigerator. So I decided to try it. I have a food processor but thought that I would try to cut the potatoes thinly with my knife and since I have only one hand it wasn't that bad to do surprisingly.  So I followed the directions and decided to add a few more ingredients like onions, and bacon bits.. My whole kitchen smelled so good.. I was very happy with the turn out. I did not separate the potatoes like others I finely sliced them and put them in the dish. Added the sauce and added a little more cheese on top. Oh my goodness they were great.. not too much salt, like little red riding hood... they were just right. I can wait until tomorrow when they say they are better.. son't know if they can get any better than they were tonight.. PS I usually don't write a review for anything.. but I just had to do it here... have a blessed day :)

I have to admit.... I am not a big Scalloped Potato fan, but hubbie is. So I tweeked these to make them how I like them and it just so happens, hubbie loved them too!
I started by cutting a clove of garlic in half and rubbing the cut end all over the bottom of the casserole dish. Then I pulled out my mandolin slicer- which in my opinion is essential for scalloped potatoes! That or some other way to make all the slice the same thickness ( cheese grater, food processor, talent...) And I slice up 2-3 large potatoes and 3/4 of a large onion. I also minced up the rest of that garlic I cut in half earlier- these I added to the casserole dish as directed (mixed together randomly). I followed the directions from there- except that I added another minced clove of garlic to the butter/flour mixture before I added the cheese (garlic powder would probably work well too) as well as some smoked paprika, salt and pepper and a touch of cayenne pepper. I baked it uncovered but had to throw tin foil over it for the last 20 mins so it wouldn't burn. It was so good!!! And I don't like Scalloped Potatoes! Yummmmmm.
I may have tweeked it by adding garlic, onion and a few other spices, but the basics were Vicki's- and I thank you!

attributes.source_text: hubbie loved them too

some smoked paprika

reviews.review_text: I tend to use recipes as more of a guide; that being said this got me to where I needed to be in getting scalloped potatoes on the dinner table. I soaked my potatoes in brine most of the day to add a bit of salt, I finely diced and caramelized about 2/3 of an onion and used it to flavor the sauce prior to adding my grated cheese, to assure the texture was not ruined I strained the sauce through a very fine mesh sieve to remove any of the onion that did not liquify, added my cheese and assembled the dish to bake. I did use heavy cream rather than milk, we tend to have 2% around and I don't like cooking with that. I considered putting a bit of browning on the potatoes prior to assembly, that would have added a bit more depth to the flavors, but decided against it as this was planned as a side to a more mild pork dish that I wanted to be the star. Knowing how to get the roux just right is key to this recipe, I went with just a bit darker than white bread crust...

attributes.source_text: getting scalloped potatoes on the dinner table
this was planned as a side

reviews.review_text:
We decided to make our own scalloped potatoes this Easter instead of buying a box like we usually do.  Well, this recipe is so easy and delicious I will never buy another box of scalloped potatoes again!

I saw Tobey_day's review that there was too much salt, I am curious if tobey used _unsalted_ butter, which I think is what the recipe should say, or if he used _salted_ butter, which may be implied especially for someone who doesn't do a lot of cooking (I submitted a correction to that end).  I also used kosher salt instead of table salt, which overall tends to be less salty.  The end result was a tad under-salted if anything, but I don't know that I would change anything next time.  In general, this recipe is now going to be one of our holiday staples.  Thanks for posting it!

attributes.source_text: this Easter
one of our holiday staples

reviews.review_text: this is a great recipe for augraten potatoes..scalloped do not have cheese...My mom use to make a great dish..but so simple..she just sliced potatoes thin...put in a greased pan..whatever size you want.then would put down a layer and salt and pepper it and sprinkle a little flour on top of the layer then repeat about 3 times...then she would dot the top layer with a pieces of butter and she would take whole milk and pour it over the potatoes until it barely covered the potatoes..she would cover the pan with foil and bake...at least an hour..if you check and it is has a lot of liquid..remove the cover about 15 min before the hour is up....sometimes she would add some ham between the layers or a little garlic powder...so simple and so good!! This is so good..you do not need cheese...for scalloped potatoes.

I have terrible morning sickness, so I am limited to the few things I can handle: potatoes, white rice, cheese, milk, cream of wheat, and oatmeal. Not too exciting. After brainstorming for something different I could do with those ingredients, I found this recipe. Growing up, my mom only ever made the boxed scalloped potatoes although her mac and cheese was always homemade and these two things are made almost exactly the same way. Go figure. Anyway, on to the recipe. I made only minor subs based on what I had - about 2/3 medium cheddar cheese and 1/3 monterey jack, half almond milk and half whole milk, and I halved the recipe entirely and made in 8x8 pan. It was all cooked through in one hour and tasted good considering my morning sickness. The only thing I'm worried about is that I could see a lot of grease from the cheese and butter, and grease is not something that settles well in my stomach. If it digests well, I have a winning morning sickness recipe on hand. Thanks Vicki!

First time making scalloped potatoes. Not super common where I'm from (Italian area of southern New England) but common where I moved to (central PA), so I figured I'd learn to make them. Really easy, actually, as long as your knife isnt dull as a chapstick to cut the raw potatoes. I kept the skin on mine for texture. I was worried about the sauce not being thick enough when I was cooking it, but as soon as you add the cheese is balloons and becomes this awesome, creamy sauce. I think I'll add ham or pancetta to it next time. Four stars for two reasons: one, it needs WAY more seasoning, maybe on the potatoes themselves, and two, I had way more cheese sauce than potatoes, which ended up being super oily after baking. I used three big Russet potatoes, so word to the wise, use more. I'm making it again tonight with these tweaks. It tastes just as good, if not better, when reheated. Delicious.

attributes.source_text: becomes this awesome, creamy sauce

reviews.review_text:
Mmmm, I agree they are maybe even better as left overs. Sometimes when sliced potatoes are only baked, they still have a raw taste to me. I parboiled the sliced potatoes for about 20 minutes and added extra cheese, then baked for 45 minutes. I think parboiling enhances the flavor and the potatoes soak up more of the yummy cheese sauce. They were excellent! I am making them again for the second time this week. Thanks for posting!

Update:  We found out DH has Celiac disease and can't tolerate gluten.  This recipe adapts to gluten free easily by using a gluten free pancake mix, such as Bob's Red Mill, instead of flour.  It is just as delicious and I still make this every week!  You might want to tag this as gluten free when made this way.  Also I have included sweet potatoes and that's good too.

"Delicious!!!" was my son's response after he took a bite of this dish!

My husband's favorite meal as a child was scalloped potatoes, and he was really excited that we made some from scratch this evening. I used Yukon Gold potatoes, a dash of garlic powder, and a four-cheese mix rather than cheddar. The recipe was simple to put together, and the results were outstanding. They came out perfect!!! I served them with baked pork chops and apples (http://www.food.com/recipe/baked-pork-chops-and-apples-90771). It was a great combination that also paired well with a Spanish wine (currant flavor in the wine was great with both the cheese and the baked apples!). This was one of the best meals I've made. Thank you so much for posting. I've already been asked to make them again, and the family voted that tomorrow night should be leftover night (I'm usually stuck with the leftovers as much lunch since I work from home). FANTASTIC!!

items.label: Oven-Fried Chicken Chimichangas
items.name: Oven-Fried Chicken Chimichangas
items.description: A fast and healthier way to serve Chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. These are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. I like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.
instructions: Mix chicken, picante sauce or salsa, cumin, oregano, cheese and onions.
Place about 1/4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla.
Fold opposite sides over filling.
Roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet.
Brush with melted margarine.
Bake at 400°F for 25 minutes or until golden.
Garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side.

reviews.review_text: Oops, I don't think I've reviewed this yet.  I made this many weeks ago and it was really simple and quite tasty.  I baked a chicken breast to shred for this, used dried oregano instead of fresh, and divided up the mixture into two bowls - one I added Mexican blend shredded cheese, the other I mixed in Soy-Sation brand jalapeno jack and cheddar shredded blend (this was for me, because I can't digest dairy).  I used Pace medium chunky salsa.  I brushed the tops of the rolled tortillas with canola oil instead of margarine, per a reviewer's suggestion.  These baked up so lovely and the chicken mixture was flavorful.  Following another reviewer's suggestion, I cooled leftovers on racks and placed in freezer bags.  Reheating one chimi for about 2 mins or less on high in the micro worked perfectly for me, I ate my leftovers in less than a week.  My bf, on the other hand seemed to like his (made with real cheese lucky guy), but he hasn't eaten his leftovers yet, lol.  Thanks Miss Annie for a delicioius chicken chimi/OAMC recipe.

reviews.review_text: This was a really great alternative to fried!  I added frozen corn, 1/2 a can of refried black beans stirred into chicken mixture, garlic, chili powder, roma tomato chopped, 1 can diced tomatoes with jalapenos and some red pepper flakes.  I sauteed the chicken breast with Hot and spicy taco seasoning packet.  Needless to say I had alot of mixture...luckily I had plenty of tortillas.  I ended up with 12- 8 inch tortillas and 6- 6 inch tortillas.  The kids loved them and we have plenty left-over for lunches.  I lined the cookie sheet with foil as suggested and sprayed pam on top of that so clean up was a snap.  I used olive oil but the larger ones didn't seem to get golden like the smaller ones so I may try the butter on top next time.  Thanks for an awesome recipe!  The kids want these again next week!!! I topped the chimis with warm green chile sauce, cheese and sour cream and served with pinto beans seasoned with cumin and oregano (to incorporate the flavors of the original recipe). reviews.review_text:
5 for a great dish
5 for flavor, but I did have to alter it to my tastes.

But a great dish, and I loved them baked.

I did use a good salsa. I do love spice, lots of it, but I cut back on the cumin and oregano.  However, I used a very flavorful good salsa, a more plain salsa or picante may require more seasoning. My salsa was a "more gourmet blend," so it had lots of seasoning already.

I did use a Mexican blend of cheeses too.

My garnish was simple a green enchilada sauce, sour cream and diced olives.

If I was home I may of served over a bed of lettuce with some fresh diced tomatoes and scallions, but I was at work (making it for co workers) so I didn't get that fancy.

I did spray with olive oil vs margarine, and they turned out golden brown.

It was easy, great taste, much healthier and I enjoyed them.  Very very good.

Black beans would be another good addition to them, but the chicken and salsa was perfect.

Thx for a great easy quick recipe.
Kim

items.label: Fannie Farmer's Classic Baked Macaroni & Cheese
items.name: Fannie Farmer's Classic Baked Macaroni & Cheese
items.description:
To me Fannie Farmer's recipe is the only "real" Macaroni & Cheese. It's from my 1946 edition of "Fannie Farmer's Boston Cooking School Cookbook". With time on it's side - this recipe is hands down the best for traditional, homemade baked macaroni & cheese - comfort food.

Please Note: If you use CHEAP CHEESE you will end up with a BLAND and FLAVORLESS DISH!
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Cook and drain macaroni according to package directions; set aside.
In a large saucepan melt butter.
Add flour mixed with salt and pepper, using a whisk to stir until well blended.
Pour milk and cream in gradually; stirring constantly.
Bring to boiling point and boil 2 minutes (stirring constantly).
Reduce heat and cook (stirring constantly) 10 minutes.
Add shredded cheddar little by little and simmer an additional 5 minutes, or until cheese melts.
Turn off flame.
Add macaroni to the saucepan and toss to coat with the cheese sauce.
Transfer macaroni to a buttered baking dish.
Sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Bake 20 minutes until the top is golden brown.

(You can also freeze this recipe in zip-lock bags for later use - once you have mixed the macaroni along with the cheese sauce allow to cool to room temperature before adding to your freezer - I generally pull it out the night before and allow macaroni and cheese to reach room temperature; I then add the macaroni and cheese to a buttered baking dish, sprinkle with bread crumbs and then bake for 20 to 30 minutes, until golden brown on top and bubbling.

reviews.review_text: I've made this so many times over the past couple decades I no longer measure the ingredients and just "eyeball" it instead. The roux is the backbone of this recipe, and the only part "engraved in stone".  I've used all 2%, or whole milk, a combo of those with varying fat content creams, added cubed ham, sliced cooked leftover sausages, broccoli, mushrooms depending on what needs to be used up in the fridge.  Usually I add a bit of mustard, dry or prepared, sometimes cajun seasoning or a spicy pepper seasoning, always a bit of onion and garlic powder, maybe worcestershire and/or tabasco. Nutmeg is good too. Any of those seasonings amplify the cheese flavour. Sometimes I use all (store brand, aged) cheddar, but DD likes a little emmental added.   I butter the breadcrumbs by melting some butter in the still hot pan I made the sauce in, then throw in the crumbs, maybe a bit of parsley and a bit more grated cheese without turning the heat on again. Other than learning to make the roux, it's hard to mess this recipe up.<br/><br/>Add a simple salad or vegetable side to stretch it to serve at least six and this is infinitely tastier, cheaper, and healthier than any fast food alternative.  Krap Dinner isn't worth the shelf space in the house.

reviews.review_text: jensafrk commented that this recipe ''tastes like raw flour.'' The problem may be in making the roux, which is the carefully cooked, equal quantities of flour and butter. You must begin with low heat and the mixture must be stirred constantly to avoid scorching the flour. Start by melting the butter over low heat. When the foaming begins to subside, add the flour (do not include the salt and pepper yet) and stir constantly, watching the color of the mixture. It should become a light, nutty brown color. This may take five minutes or so. Do not go by the clock, but rather by the color. If the process is stopped too soon, while still white, it will taste like raw flour. If it gets too brown, the flour has scorched and it will taste burnt. As soon as the color is right, slowly add the room-temperature milk/cream in increments, continuing to stir constantly. When all of the milk has been added, turn the heat up to medium high and continue stirring until it begins to bubble, then reduce heat to a simmer and and continue stirring until it thickens. You now have the basic white sauce, béchamel, upon which many other cream sauces are built. In this recipe, that is a cheese sauce. Add the salt and pepper at this point and continue the recipe.

This is really the only recipe you need for mac & cheese. It is perfect EXACTLY the way it is, but since we are cheese-a-holics in our house, I played with different combinations of cheese to get the strong flavor I was searching for. My favorite pre-made mac & cheese is Stouffers, so I am constantly trying to match that taste. After many experiements, I found a combination that is actually BETTER than Stouffers. I use 2 cups of sharp cheddar (the sharper the better), about 1 1/2 cups of finely shredded parmesean, and about 1/2 cup of shredded swiss (just enough so as to not overpower it). The combination is SO amazing. The key is to add the cheeses slowly into the white sauce while it is just warm...not boiling. Sometimes we don't even bother to bake this because it's too good to wait for. On the days I feel like baking it (I agree with those who say it's a completely different dish when baked...just depends on what you're in the mood for) I have come to love using Italian seasoned Panko bread crumbs for the topping. My kids love the crunch. I read that one reviewer wasn't sure how to use the bread crumbs...just melt the butter in the micro for a bit, then add it to the crumbs and stir them up, then sprinkle them on the top. The great thing about this recipe is that you can use is as a base for whatever your flavor mood. Add mexi-cheese and green chiles for a yummy mexi-mac, add diced ham and broccoli, chicken and sun-dried tomatoes, or whatever you are craving. My favorite, though, is to just make it plain with my three cheeses. I, too, have converted from the 'blue box' to this recipe. I actually find it just as easy as making the blue box...with a FAR superior result. A true time-tested classic. As my daughter prepares to leave the nest (she is a Senior in high school) I have been teaching her 'survival' recipes, and this is definitely one of them. Every self-respecting cook should have this in their repertoire. I didn't for the longest time b/c I was intimidated by the whole roux thing. But I found that practice makes perfect, and once I conquered making roux, it opened up all SORTS of new recipes for me. So if you haven't tried it, DO! And if you burn it (goodness knows I did plenty of times) then START OVER! It's just flour and butter. It's really easier than you'd think, and SO worth it when you taste the results. Thanks so much for sharing this PERFECT recipe!

Ok, I am going to fess up right here and now to "jumping to conclusions."  I have long been in search of the "best" macaroni and cheese recipe.  To do that, I went straight to the top of 'Zaar, and started making the #1 rated recipe.  I loved it, and it got rave reviews, but my best friend here didn't deem it "perfect", although she wasn't clear on exactly what was missing.  So I began to peruse the "runner ups" and found this recipe.  The first time I made it, I could see that it was going to be better than #1.  It is creamy, rich, and delicious.  I have varied the recipe every time with the following modifications and NOT ONE of them made it any less delicious - 1.  Lactose (almost) free using Cabot cheddar cheeses (no lactose) and Lactaid whole milk.  2.  Low(er) fat - using regular 2% milk, one 8oz Velveeta (less fat than Cheddar) and 1 8oz 50% less fat Cabot.  I also need to point out to any reviewers who find this "bland", the seasonings are on you.  You need to taste it when you are making the white sauce to be sure that is well seasoned, and taste it again after the cheese is added.  I add Cayenne pepper to every macaroni and cheese I make, and I am sure at the end I added more salt and pepper.  Only way to make a dish perfect is to taste it all the way through.  Kudos, Carla, this recipe has finally been deemed "perfect."

reviews.review_text: This is how my mother always made macaroni and cheese. The only difference is that she taught me to make a basic white sauce (or bechamel) like jehaas (12/30/10) describes above. The butter/flour mixture, which is always made up of equal parts of butter and flour with a little salt and pepper, needs to be thoroughly cooked (5+ minutes), whisking constantly, before the milk and cheese is added or the result is an unpleasant raw flour taste. For a thicker sauce, either add less milk or more butter and flour. Do the opposite for a thinner sauce. Once you get this sauce downpat, it's the foundation of many dishes. To deepen the flavor, I sauté chopped onions until they're transparent and then add minced garlic that I cook until it's just past raw. I usually stir that into the flour/butter mixture before I add the milk, but it can be added after the sauce is cooked. Unless you're adding major heat with hot peppers (not my preference), nearly all of the flavor in this dish comes from the cheese. I use good cheese. It's a great way to use up any bits of cheese that are hanging around in the refrigerator. A combination of good melting cheeses (like Jarlsburg, fontina, brie, gouda, edam, havarti, gruyére, butterkase, Dubliner or Swiss) is vital, and then add smaller amounts of some sharper or different favored cheeses to round out the flavor. I don't like bread crumb toppings, so I skip that step. Although it's not necessary, I usually put foil over the dish while it's baking so it doesn't dry out, then remove the foil to brown the top. Putting it under the broiler for a few minutes also browns it nicely.

I wasn't sure if this meant whipping cream (at least I knew not to use whipped cream!) or table cream or what, so I bought both and after taste testing the table cream in a can seemed richer so I went with that.  After making the sauce I taste tested it since I wasn't sure if the ten slices of cheddar were enough..sure enough it didn't seem cheesy enough to me so I tossed in 4 slices of American (all I had!).  Also wasn't exactly sure how to butter breadcrumbs so I sprinkled them on top and then just drizzled butter over them.  Even with these issues it turned out SO GOOD!! I have never made mac and cheese from scratch and the taste was just to die for!  My only complaint, though, was the breadcrumbs.  Next time I might try out some Panko breadcrumbs or just leave them off altogether.  SO even with all of my issues, the end result still turned out delicious, making this an absolute keeper for me!  Can't wait to try it again with a great high quality cheddar.  Thanks for posting this!

reviews.review_text: This was DELICIOUS! I even made a few modifications based on personal preference and was hoping for the best, because the first time I ever made baked mac and cheese it turned out mediocre and my husband and I were disappointed. I knew it had to have been a faulty recipe because I am admittedly a very good cook (not just my own opinion either lol), and after finding this one I am confident the other recipe was just all wrong. <br/>Like everyone else said, this is creamy, rich and delicious! <br/>The slight modifications I made were using half & half instead of cream, (as I was stirring I felt that the sauce looked too thick even before adding cheese so I added an extra 1/2 cup of half & half). I also used 1% milk. These are just flavor preferences for me, but they have the added benefit of cutting some of the fat as well. For the cheese I used Kraft's Shredded Triple Cheddar blend (Vermont White Cheddar, Sharp Cheddar and Mild Cheddar). The blend of cheddars really made the cheesy flavors pop, especially since two of the cheddars were "sharp". I also added a dash of cayanne pepper for a little zing and topped with EVOO coated Panko breadcrumbs (with a dash of s&p). If you would like an extra crispy top, Panko are the way to go! EVOO (Extra Virgin Olive Oil) is a great substitute for butter when using breadcrumbs and again helps ease the fat intake. Yes, EVOO is still an oil and thus fatty, but it's a healthy fat. :)<br/>I will be making this recipe time and again and I will be playing with add-ins in the future as well!

reviews.review_text: I have an 1896 fannie farmers boston cooking school cookbook which I inherited from my great gramma. She is the first one who first made this dish for me when I was a child. My gramma and mom ALWAYS made mac and cheese this way. Lazy me slipped into making the "blue box" when my children were young because it was quick and easy, and have to admit I still use occasionally as a quick side, although I always found it to be too "velveety" tasting. I bought velveeta once and thought it was gross, reminds me of that disgusting yellow american cheese. (my opinion only, but I really don't like the stuff) Anyhow, getting off track here, I saw this recipe on here, and had to make it again, the recipe is the same in the in the 1896 version of cookbook by the way, now my husband in general HATES macaroni and cheese, reminds him of school cafeteria food. I made this last night, following recipe exactly, and he ate half of a 9 by 13 baking dish of it with sliced fresh tomatoes from the garden, couldn't believe it was mac and cheese and tasted this, and bought memories of gram and great gramma back to me. Thank you for posting. The only other comment is if you want 'blue box or velveeta" stay with it, they don't do it for me, this is a different grown up flavor which is wonderful. Don't mess with the original. This is fantastic, despite the time involved, always worth it.

reviews.review_text: This recipe truly is a classic. It even includes the classic mistake of misidentifying nutmeg as black pepper. Black pepper is fine and it doesn't hurt this recipe one bit. But people have been mistaking nutmeg for black pepper in cheese dishes for centuries. I think it is time for Americans learn what French and Italian cooks have always know as a fundamental rule of cooking with dairy products: nutmeg in very small quantities intensifies the flavor of milk. The difference is subtle, but nutmeg introduces another level of complexity that just isn't in the dish without it. I hope someone will try this recipe with a tiny pinch nutmeg in place of the pepper and report back. My feeling about the dish with nutmeg is that the it doesn't seem to change, but that it seems as if the milk and cheese are way higher quality, as if angels made the cheese and the butter was made that morning. It is, of course, just flavors that were there all along, opened up by the tiniest bit of nutmeg.

Also to the reviewer who said cheap cheese doesn't make a difference, to that, I respectfully disagree. Splurge. Mac and cheese like this should be made with utmost care and the finest ingredients. I find that when it comes to dairy, price does matter. You can't tell me there's not a difference taste wise between X-Brand sharp cheddar cheese, Cracker Barrel and aged Wisconsin sharp cheddar from your nearest cheese shop. Same thing with butter. Yes it will taste good, amazing even with cheaper ingredients because this is a fool proof recipe, but it ain't at it's best, trust me. <br/><br/>Now I'm not saying go to your nearest farm and make some butter, but y'know, you'll taste the difference in butter that costs 2 bucks for four sticks as opposed to 6 bucks for four sticks...<br/><br/>My mom, my grandma, and my great grandma have used Cracker Barrel extra sharp cheddar in their mac and cheese all their lives, and mine so I'd definitely give that a whirl.

This is now our go-to recipe for mac-n-cheese. The first time I made it I used high quality white cheddar and American cheese slices (I was worried it would turn out tasting funky!) and the creaminess was out of this world. I added the American because the cheddar was really sharp and I wanted to subdue that a little. I had read somewhere that the white cheddar made for a less gritty cheese sauce and I feel that that is true. We made the macaroni again tonight but used just yellow cheddar and we actually skipped baking it because we got a late start on dinner. It still turned out really good. To make it without baking we simply mixed the cheese sauce into the cooked pasta and served (no bread crumbs, no baking). I do recommend baking, though, as the taste it amazing but if you're pressed for time it's also okay to skip that part. Also, we have a really large family so we needed to make more servings than this recipe serves. We did not double the roux part (flour and butter) but we did add more cheddar and of course more pasta. The sauce still turned out really thick; you can always thin it out with more milk if you find it too thick for your liking. Hope my comments help!

attributes.source_text: the creaminess was out of this world
The sauce still turned out really thick

reviews.review_text:
ok..this is AMAZING ..i did make changes tho! and i had to share, because it was better than any Mac n cheese i have ever had. so i looked over many reviews and followed allot of suggestions...i did double the recipe (big eaters in this house hold) I added Dry mustard, and garlic ( 1-2 teaspoons) a tiny pinch of nutmeg. I used Extra sharp cheddar, (4 cups) about 1 cup of pepper jack and here is where it gets a little different but good , i added gorgonzola (about 1/4 cup) and i had Dubliner cheese with Stout ..added about 1/8 cup of that. and because i love gorgonzola and bacon..i had to add a couple slices of crumbled bacon. i also added abut 1/2 cup of Parmesan , ..and even though i put too much cheese in it already, i had some shredded "mexican blend cheeses" in the fridge so i put two huge handfulls of that in as well.
Simply delightful , will be making this as much as i can. If you like stronger cheeses i highly suggest making these changes!

This was wonderful!  To prevent the flour flavor, I wisked the roux (butter+flour) over a low flame until it was medium brown color.  I used 3 cups of cheese (12 oz), per hubby's request: 1 c sharp cheddar, 1 c fat-free cheddar, 1 c extra sharp white.  I removed the white sauce from the heat before adding the cheese, and the cheese was still able to blend in smoothly (this technique prevented any chance of overcooking the cheese).  It's important to season the water before boiling any pasta; I used salt, bay leaves, and paprika.  To season the sauce, I added cayenne and paprika (in addition to salt and pepper).  I didn't use breadcrumbs.  Next time, I'll let the white sauce cool a bit before adding some of the cheese; I like when there are strands of cheddar throughout my mac & cheese.  I will also try to increase the proportion of fat-free cheese (or replace some cream with milk), since there was a bit of extra grease on top of the mac & cheese when I pulled it out of the oven.  Thank you for the recipe!

Wow! If I could give this 50 stars, oh I would. Though I had to work with some limitations: my butter burnt a bit because I got distracted but I actually think it gave it a really nice smoky flavor! And my milk had gone sour so I had to toss it and freaked, but decided to use 2 cups of cream since I had plenty. I used 1/2 tsp sea salt and a few shakes of black pepper and mustard powder in the "forming" stage. When the mixture started to thicken, I added the cheese and it totally melted on impact and made THE smoothest, creamiest cheese sauce EVER. (This was such a relief because the last few times I tried to make cheese sauce it hardly incorporated or melted except for on the bottom of the pot.) Even just eating like that without baking it tasted awesome. I used Kraft Naturals sharp cheddar and next time I do this? I'm so going to use Tillamook smoked cheddar to give it a really smoky down-home flavor and intentionally get the butter a little burnt!

reviews.review_text:
I looked everywhere for a recipe for baked macaroni and cheese that was CREAMY and never got the result that I did today when I made this recipe.  I've been off of work after surgery last week and was craving a comfort dish...This is IT!!!
I followed the recipe with only 2 differences in the ingredients... 1- I used 1/2 sharp shredded cheddar cheese (Sargento) and 1/2 american cheese (Land-o-Lakes) at my husband's request.  2- I added approx. 1/4 teaspoon of onion powder and garlic powder with the salt and pepper to the flour before adding to the melted butter.  
I used my 3 1/2 quart porcelain coated dutch oven coated w/about a teaspoon of butter.  I reserved about 2 tablespoons of the shredded cheddar and put that on top instead of bread - crumbs. I took the cover off and broiled it for 4 minutes at the very end for a crispy, bubbly, brown beautiful top.
I thought this recipe came together as stated in the directions....  It really was perfect!! =-)  =-)

reviews.review_text: I was disappointed with this recipe. It had no taste at all. I used a good quality cheese (Cabot Extra Sharp Cheddar) and I shredded it myself. I used Creamette macaroni. I have made white sauces before and I understand how they must be treated. I used the prescribed 4 cups of cheese. I used the called-for salt and pepper. I stirred and stirred and stirred so not to burn the sauce. The colour of the cheese sauce was dark grey, not the colour of the cheese at all. I don't know what happened, but it was the most bland, non-cheesy tasting mac-n-cheese I've ever baked. The buttered bread crumbs were dusty and disgusting. The whole thing was dry and without flavour. I checked the recipe to make sure I hadn't omitted anything, but the flavour was definitely NOT there. I followed the recipe to the T. I made no additions nor did I tweak any ingredients. I chose this recipe because I have made other recipes from the Fannie Farmer cookbook and REALLY loved them! This was served at my Christmas dinner and I was  really embarrassed that almost no one finished their serving. When I tasted it, I understood why. I don't know what happened, but I will NOT be making this again.

attributes.source_text: This was served at my Christmas dinner
This was served at my Christmas dinner

reviews.review_text:
Everybody loved this mac and cheese! I mostly followed the recipe - only differences were I added mustard powder and a clove of garlic to the flour. And I used cheddar, colby, and monterey jack cheeses.  I skipped the breadcrumbs just b/c we don't really care for breadcrumbs on mac and cheese.   It didn't take that long to make - and the little extra time (and constant stirring) you do put into the white sauce is def. worth it.  
I made this for weekend guests - and b/c I would prefer to visit w/ friends instead of being in kitchen the whole time, I made it up a day ahead and fridged it - so I just had to pop it into the oven.  I'm always a little worried about trying something new for guests w/o doing a test run, but w/ all the rave reviews and the good instructions, I was pretty confident. And sure enough -it was very rich and creamy, w/o being too heavy.  It was very delish -all the good reviews can be trusted!  Many thanks!

items.label: The Best Easy Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
items.name: The Best Easy Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
items.description: I clipped this recipe from Taste of Home magazine several years ago and have found it to be the best-tasting easy beef and broccoli stir-fry. It is credited to Ruth Stahl. I often use charcoal chuck steak, which is very tender and lean. I also like that it doesn't call for any unusual ingredients.
instructions: In a bowl, combine 2 tablespoons cornstarch, 2 tablespoons water and garlic powder until smooth.
Add beef and toss.
In a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat, stir-fry beef in 1 tablespoon oil until beef reaches desired doneness; remove and keep warm.
Stir-fry onion in remaining oil for 4-5 minutes until softened. Add the broccoli and cook for 3 minutes until the broccoli is tender but still crisp. Return beef to pan.
Combine soy sauce, brown sugar, ginger and remaining 1 tablespoon cornstarch and 1/2 cup water until smooth; add to the pan.
Cook and stir for 2 minutes.
Serve over rice and garnish with toasted sesame seeds (optional).

reviews.review_text: I can't believe how great this recipe came out for me.  Usually SOMETHING goes wrong, but not this time.  Thank you so much!  <br/><br/>I wasn't sure how tender my beef would be, so I did what some others did too, and doubled the sauce, so the beef could marinate in it while I prepared the vegetables.  Since I was marinating the beef in the sauce, I didn't do the first part with the corn starch, water and garlic, so I just added the garlic to the sauce.<br/><br/>Didn't have broccoli on hand so I used green and red pepper cut into fine strips along with my onions, also cut into fine strips so they would cook quickly.<br/><br/>It came out fantastic!  Amazingly just like at the Chinese restaurant!<br/><br/>Next time, I'll try the dredging in cornstarch part and see how that comes out.  It was so good, I can't imagine how that would make it better though.  Also, I'll try it with the broccoli or fresh green beans.

attributes.source_text: Amazingly just like at the Chinese restaurant!

reviews.review_text:
Give this recipe a try - you will not regret it!!!

"Awesome" (per my dinner guests) and I have to agree whole heartedly!! It definitely had an authentic taste to it. Super easy recipe that exemplifies that keeping it simple really works!

Although, like many reviewers, I did make a few changes as well:
sweet brown rice flour rather than cornstarch, minced garlic rather than powder, grated fresh ginger root rather than powder, olive oil rather than vegetable oil, organic cane sugar rather than brown sugar, organic reduced sodium soy sauce, and I added a teaspoon of Better than Boulloin Beef base.

I think that with quality beef there is no need to marinade the beef. Dredging as instructed is the way to go to ensure a good base for the sauce. It also seals in the moistness to prevent chewy beef -thereby ensuring tender beef!

I paired it with Jasmine tea spiked with Japanese Cherry wine ... which was a huge hit as well. The kiddos had Japanese sodas ; )

attributes.source_text: "Awesome" (per my dinner guests)
It also seals in the moistness
thereby ensuring tender beef

reviews.review_text: I haven't tried making a homemade stir-fry in a very long time. My first and last attempt 25 years ago, was a complete disaster. But then again, my cooking skills back then were in the infant stages. I followed others suggestions, skipping the first step and marinating the beef for a couple of hours... I'm not sure if I would do that again. The flavor was great but it was a bit overwhelming... I would like to taste the beef rather then just the sauce/marinade. I also found that the sauce was a bit thick. I like it thinner. For a lighter sauce, I would add less cornstarch next time. I like to cook with fresh ingredients if possible, so I used fresh ginger instead of ground. I was surprised to learn that 1 tablespoon of fresh ginger is equvalent to 1/4 teaspoon of ground so I ended up using all of my fresh ginger. Be prepared if you plan on using fresh... I almost didn't have enough. I also added 3 fresh garlic cloves to the recipe in addition to the ground garlic. Added about 1/2 a teaspoon of crushed red pepper as well which gave it a nice spice and at the end of cooking, I tossed in about 1/4 cup of scallions. All in all it was a hit. Thank you for the recipe... I'll be making it again with the few adjustments.

attributes.source_text: gave it a nice spice

reviews.review_text:
I LOVE this recipe! It was soooo yummy!

I had to say that I found the recipe when just looking for some beef stir-fry. I had a leftover of around 150g beef and I was looking for a way to use it. I have to say that I am terrible with preparing meat, it just never turns up right. I dont know, they say it should not be that difficult, but for me it is always a disaster.

That is why I was so surprised when I tried it. The meat was so tender, and wrapped nicely with the sauce.
I improvised with vegetables, and instead of just broccoli, I added some frozen wok mix that I had with broccoli, carrot, small corns and some white thing that I dont know what it is.
And it was great! Next time I will just put a bit more vegetables, and maybe some time try to add some more spices (maybe hot paprika). But as it is the recipe is great!

My friends saw the picture I took of it, and I got so many nice comments so I will have to invite them all for dinner soon. ;)

Thank you Chris!

attributes.source_text: The meat was so tender

reviews.review_text: Well, after making this dish, I wondered why I even bothered.  Wait, don't get me wrong...I NEVER order or eat beef and broccoli stir fry at Chinese restaurants.  I think I always stayed clear of the beef and broccoli for fear of not knowing exactly what cut of beef I was eating.  Then I made this recipe and I don't think I am a fan of beef and broccoli stir fry.  I used chuck steak in this stir fry and it was pretty good, and it definitely wasn't tough.  So, thanks to Chris from Kansas for this recipe....I got to try a new cut of beef (chuck steak).  Normally I only eat rib eye, but now that I have experienced chuck steak, this will def help keep costs down when preparing other recipes that call for beef.  I won't make again, just because I am not a beef and broccoli kind of girl.. But, by all means, if you like beef and broccoli stir fry...I suggest giving this recipe a try.

I was so impressed by this recipe that it caused me to sign up to Genius Kitchen just so I could express myself! I'm a good cook and a reasonably accomplished baker, but I'm always on the look-out for recipes of faves so I can do them myself - such as beef with broccoli. This was my first try and it was OUTSTANDING! To the point that I'm thinking of sending a link to others (unheard of from me). You can't go wrong, even with adjustments simply because a specific ingredient may not be on hand (e.g. I used chopped onion because I didn't have a whole one). And that's one of the best parts - the ingredients are pretty much what most cooks would have in some form on hand anyway. Bottom line: It's a great base recipe, easily adjustable to what's on hand and individual chef's taste. I'm looking forward to trying out with other flavors and/or meats such as pork, chicken, or shrimp. Happy cooking!

wow....i've been trying to avoid using pre-packaged sauces/mixes and processed foods these days.  wanted to try to make my own broccoli beef without that usual packaged spice/sauce mix that probably is loaded with MSG......i found this.  WONDERFUL.  i followed some of the suggestions and marinated the beef first.  and since money is so tight these days, i actually used leftover beef (rare) from a roast i had fixed previously. (cant wait to try this with a nice fresh piece of kansas beef!)  i then attempted to "dredge" the wet marinated beef in the garlic, cornstarch and water mixture (it was a little weird lol, but it worked).  this is an easy dish, excellent flavor.  the ONLY thing i changed is i added a few drops of sesame oil to the vegetable oil when i stir fried for a bit more flavor.  excellent.  thank you chris from kansas!!!!

I didn't think this tasted the same as the restaurants here but this was very good.  I made it as is with the exception of reducing the ground ginger to about 1/3-1/2 tsp. which was perfect. One tsp. would have been overwhelming.  I also added some minced garlic when I stir fried the broccoli.  Need to definitely marinate or season the beef which I didn't do.  Having more flavor in the beef would have made this a 5 star recipe.  10/18/12 UPDATE:  Instead of doing Step 1, I mixed 3 Tbs. cornstarch, 3 Tbs. soy sauce, 1 Tbs. brown sugar and 1/2 tsp garlic powder and marinated the beef in this mixture for one hour.  I followed the rest of recipe except added 3 minced garlic to the broccoli and onions during the last 2 minutes and reduced the ground ginger to 1/3 - 1/2 tsp.  Yummy!  My husband liked this better than the Chinese restaurants.  Thank you, Chris, for posting this recipe.

attributes.source_text: My husband liked this better than the Chinese restaurants
My husband liked this better than the Chinese restaurants

reviews.review_text: Let me start off by saying my husband would have given this 5 stars, but I'm the cook so what I say goes. I'm a huge Chinese food fan, I even served it for 3 years and ate it almost every day I worked. So I know what Broccoli Beef is supposed to taste like. While this recipe is very, very close; there was still something lacking. It is a great base to start from. I've made a form of this recipe twice now. The first time I put all the ingredients in a crock pot to tenderize the meat. The meat was tender, but the veggies were mush. The second time, I opted to marinade the meat in all the seasonings/water for about an hour in the refrigerator first. Then I drained the marinade and saved it to add back in after I stir-fried the meat and veggies separately. Maybe the fact that I used low sodium soy sauce is the problem. I don't know, but I'll keep trying.

attributes.source_text: The meat was tender

reviews.review_text: This was great! It did take longer than 25 minutes, but #1: I am slow (I like to take my time, it's relaxing) and #2: I doubled the recipe. Doubling it served the 6 of us. I used fresh broccoli (Cutting up 8 cups of it was hilarious, I kept losing count of how many cups I'd cut!). Also, I used top sirloin steak rather than the round steak. Otherwise I followed the recipe exactly. I give this a 4 out of 5 because I felt the sauce was a little strong (but no one else said anything, so maybe it was just me). I think it would be better (that is, not as strong) if I added more veggies- either more broccoli or onion or add something completely new, like carrots (as someone else suggested). Thank you for sharing this recipe! I will be making this again!

Really good! Even my kids liked it!<br/><br/>I did spice it up and add a bit more garlic (that's how we roll...)<br/><br/>Here are my notes:<br/>I put the beef in a bag and added the cornstarch and garlic powder to coat - then added 2 tbsp rice vinegar with water. Marinated for 30 minutes. I also added crushed red pepper to oil before frying.<br/><br/>To the sauce I added 1/3 cup oyster sauce, fresh garlic, fresh ginger, more crushed red pepper, and only 1/4 cup water (we like our sauce thick and I find the heat loosens it up).<br/><br/>Also topped with toasted sesame seeds and fresh green onions.<br/><br/>Next time I think I'll add the sesame oil as well as recommended in an earlier review.<br/><br/>Can't wait to make it again!

attributes.source_text: Even my kids liked it!

reviews.review_text: I used many of the suggestions from the reviews and this came out excellent except when using oyster sauce, I should have cut the soy sauce amount in half.  I used all fresh ingredients, no spices.  I also cooked the sauce separate from the vegetables and meat so it could thicken on its own and not overcook the vegetables and meat.  I was going to use New York Strip for the meat but was unable to find the cut I wanted so I used London broil and marinated it in beef stock, fresh garlic, and some Simply Asia - Sweet Ginger Garlic Seasoning for 75 minutes.  I also used beef stock for the sauce and added fresh ginger, fresh garlic, and oyster and Sriracha Hot Chilli sauce.  It came out very well and I will make it again with a few modifications to the amount of soy sauce.

This was really excellent and easy, too! The garlic/cornstarch coating really made the beef taste extra special, and it is a technique I may use in other stir fry dishes, too.  I used about half the oil and low sodium soy sauce to make this a little healthier, but I don't think it took anything away from the flavor. The broccoli took a bit longer to cook through, but it was worth the wait. Thank you for sharing such a great recipe!

**Updated. Living in Japan, I had a harder time finding the round steak or chuck steak (at a reasonable price), so I used super thin sliced beef (packaged for use in nikujaga), "fresh"ginger from a tube, and even used small green peppers instead of the broccoli (due to price), and this was still phenomenal. Super versatile recipe. I can't thank you enough for posting this one.

attributes.source_text: The garlic/cornstarch coating really made the beef taste extra special

reviews.review_text: This was so easy to make, and just what I was looking for! Perfect recipe as is! I made the broccoli beef two nights ago. And last night I used same recipe, but made peppered chicken instead..I did that by adding fresh coarse ground black pepper to the mixture that the meat gets coated in..and switching the broccoli out for celery. Followed all recipe steps otherwise. Both my dishes were perfect leftovers for breakfast too! Melt some butter in a fry pan, add rice and the meat/veggies..cook till hot..scoot to one half of the pan, melt some more butter, scrambled 2-4 eggs.. Once eggs are cooked, mix in with the rice and stuff.. Heat through. Serve on plate and top with soy sauce to taste. Mmmm. Definitely a keeper recipe.

attributes.source_text: Both my dishes were perfect leftovers for breakfast too!

reviews.review_text: This doesn't need another review but it was that good. I've tried other recipes that said they were as good as a restaurant and found them to be lacking. This one was. My husband, whom does not like chinese food raved. I doubled the ingredients in step six, added 1 tbls of oyster sauce, 1 tsp red pepper flakes and 3 cloves of minced garlic and used it as a marinade. Then when I cooked the recipe I skipped step 6. It was amazing. One of those recipes I keep thinking about and wanting more of. I also left my chuck blade steak slightly frozen and sliced it extra thin. Just delicious. Thank you for really having a restaurant quality recipe and sharing it with all of us! Outstanding. Probably one of the best recipes I've pulled off 'zaar.

reviews.review_text: This is the best recipe ever!  I made it tonight for my daughter and son-in-law, who had flown on business all day, and for my 9-and 10-year-old grandchildren who were a bit skeptical.  It was a monster hit with everyone.  The picky 10-year-old took a second helping.  The beauty of this recipe is that you can do the preparation in advance and make it in just a few minutes.  I used a grass-fed angus top sirloin and followed the suggestions of other reviewers to skip step one and marinate the beef in the liquid.  With good beef like I had, I would follow the recipe exactly next time. No marinating. I used the Asian Stir Fry vegetables from the produce section at Trader Joe's.  It was such an amazing meal that I am going to make it later this week for my husband, who missed tonight's dinner, and because I simply can't wait to eat it again.

reviews.review_text: OMG this is so good.  As the reviewers before me, I used the sauce to marinate the london broil steak I used for several hours and then made another batch of sauce for the cooking.  I used fresh ginger grated but next time I will use more then I added, didn't measure but I could have used more, I am a little afraid of ginger as it can be overpowering if too much is used.
