reviews.review_text: i used a pkg of vegetarian beef strips which have less flavor then real meat so i added a veggie beef broth cube and didn't bother pre-cooking since they're already cooked. i should have lessened the soy sauce a bit because of this, even using reduced-sodium it was quite salty. the corn starch was staying a little grainy so i added an extra 1/3 cup water and covered to simmer for 10 min. pre-mixing the sauce wasn't really needed so i just threw everything in the pan. added a little extra sugar and a tsp of liquid smoke. this was quite tasty! served on it's own since i didn't feel like the extra carbs so it would have lessened the salt had i used it. next time i think i'll add some mushrooms, preferably fresh shitakes.

The version in restaurants is vastly better than this. This recipe requires putting in the fully cooked beef in with the sauce and cooking for a couple minutes for the sauce to solidify. This results in dry bland overcooked beef. Also garlic powder and ginger powder are vastly inferior to frying minced garlic and ginger in oil to boost the flavor. This recipe has 1/3 of soy sauce which is a lot and only 1/8 cup of sugar which results in a very sour recipe. Other recipes have 1/4-1/3 cups of sugar. And there is just too much beef and barely any broccoli. This recipe is also missing cooking wine, sesame sauce, and sesame seeds that real Asian recipes have. Also the picture above is missing all the sauce this recipe has.

items.label: Southern Buttermilk Biscuits
items.name: Southern Buttermilk Biscuits
items.description: These buttermilk biscuits are authentic. This recipe came from my great-great-grandmother, and was handed down to all the women in my family, and we are all Southern. I am the first one to commit the sin of using a food processor (lol) but I find it works very well. I would put these biscuits up against anyone's - they are perfect in every single way. I hope you all enjoy them.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 450°F.
Combine the dry ingredients in a bowl, or in the bowl of a food processor.
Cut the butter into chunks and cut into the flour until it resembles course meal.
If using a food processor, just pulse a few times until this consistency is achieved.
Add the buttermilk and mix JUST until combined.
If it appears on the dry side, add a bit more buttermilk. It should be very wet.
Turn the dough out onto a floured board.
Gently, gently PAT (do NOT roll with a rolling pin) the dough out until it's about 1/2\
crusty\

reviews.review_text: This was my FIRST attempt in making buttermilk biscuits.  Actually any biscuit at all.  I usually have bought bisquick or canned or frozen.  Wanted to try these myself.  Things are getting to the point where its cheaper to make things homemade.  This was so easy to follow.  They will come out every time if you follow the directions and take them literal.  I literally barely touched the dough when kneading it out.  The less you touch it the better it is.  I don't have a food processor so I used a blender.  Worked perfectly!  I even used my hands to make sure the butter got worked in.  Also, make sure your using exact measurements.  If things seem dry to you then you used too much of something.  I didn't use a whole teaspoon of salt.  I used probably 3/4 teaspoon.  I thought 1 whole teaspoon was a little much.  It's also good to use unsalted butter.  Having it cold is ideal!  When you pour in the buttermilk you just use a spoon to make sure its all incorporated.  Its ok if there are lumps.  I wouldn't use a whisk because you might accidentally over mix.  Make sure you do use plenty of extra flour for the surface and your hands.  The dough will be pretty wet and you will need it.  After folding it over 5 times you just pat it to the 1/2 thickness.  I used a small glass to make the shapes since I dont have biscuit cutters.  I didn't knead or reshape the dough that was left over because they would be tougher than the first.  I just tossed it.  I used most of it though.  This is a great recipe and I will be adding to my recipe cookbook and I will be making these again.  Thank you!

Fabulous biscuits!!  I think I finally have the perfect biscuit.  Here is what worked from the other reviewers:  whoever came up with freezing the butter and grating it with a cheese grater--brilliant!  And ditto for the recommendation to freeze the flour and buttermilk for about 15 minutes prior to using.  FOR HIGH ALTITUDE:  I live in Colorado and needed to increase the baking powder by one full teaspoon; they do need the salt, so try not to skimp (unless you are serving with sausage gravy).  I also very much agree with the reviewer who suggested regular salt over kosher salt.  I did not use a rolling pin, but did knead genlty with my hand after turning the dough out onto the board and I cut with them glass jar.  My mother-in-law is a wonderful cook and married to a true southener and she makes great biscuits!  I was always too intimidated to try and afraid of any kind of baking at high altitude.  I cannot recall why I went looking for a recipe but am so glad I came upon this one. Really yummy--thanks for sharing your recipe.

I just made these this morning and WOW, the best we have ever had! This is definitely a NO-FAIL recipe if you follow the simple directions exactly as written. I used my food processor to do the flour,baking powder,salt and butter, then added the buttermilk after the flour mixture was looking 'mealy' as I call it, lol.  However I didn't have real butter so I used stick margarine instead. Processed all, was still a lil dry so added a lil more buttermilk, processed til the dough was 'wet looking' as it says in the directions. Next out of processor onto a flour covered counter top, only moved the dough around enough to cover it in flour, then patted it down and cut out the biscuits. For tall biscuits I placed them together, sides touching on the cookie sheet. Baked as instructed except we live in the mountains at 4016 elevation so took mine about 18 minutes to 'brown'. When done I patted margarine over all the tops, this gives extra flavor and keeps the tops reasonably soft. We had these with my homemade sausage gravy and we both have decided no other biscuit can compare to these... Unbelievably moist, airy and delicious!!!  Thank you so much for sharing this awesome recipe :-)

attributes.source_text: Unbelievably moist, airy and delicious

reviews.review_text: I've been looking for a good, keeper biscuit recipe and after trying a few, am so glad I found this one.  They rose beautifully, were light and tender and delicious.  They were the texture I've been looking for and they tasted wonderful.  My few adjustments were as follows.  I added a couple of teaspoons of sugar as I like the subtle richness it adds to biscuits.  I was too lazy to cut in the butter myself, or to haul out the processor, so I tried using my small countertop electric chopper.  Perfect results.  Also, I used buttermilk powder, but instead of mixing the powder with the dry ingredients and using water as ususally recommended, I mixed it with the water and used the resulting buttermilk since I didn't want to overmix and didn't want to take a chance the powder wouldn't be evenly distributed.  Again, perfect results, and lots of pride, as they brought me many kudos. Highly recommended, and my biscuit recipe of choice from here on in.  Thank you!

attributes.source_text: were light and tender
were light and tender

reviews.review_text: I made these exactly as written. I'd never tried biscuits before, as being from Australia, they are not a common thing. We do have the similar but sweet British scones, which are served with jam and cream. I used the food processor like the author, and found it to be easy. I did find the wet dough hard to work with as it kept sticking to my hands. I'd be grateful for any tips on this. I was also not sure if you are supposed to flatten the dough again between each fold. Like another reviewer stated, the ones I pieced together from the leftover dough turned out better than the first ones, which makes me think that a little kneading may be ok. I may have flattened the dough a little too much before cutting because mine weren't super tall. This may have partly been due to the cutter I used which was a Tupperware double sided one, where it has two different sized circles on each side. I used the bigger side, but it probably pressed the cut rounds down too much. I know an old trick with scones is to actually use a small drinking glass to cut the rounds and keep them nice and high. Mine cooked a little too fast, which I was prepared for as my oven runs hot. The taste was buttery and savoury, which was strange being used to sweet scones, but not unpleasant. This recipe is probably not something I'll make again but I enjoyed trying them.

attributes.source_text: The taste was buttery
and savoury

reviews.review_text: OH MY GOSH!!!!  I have been trying to bake the perfect biscuit for 17 years and believe me I have tried many unsuccessful recipes.  These were light, fluffy, and speckled with little golden spots of color as they came out of the oven at exactly 10 minutes.  I didn't have baking powder without aluminum so I used regular.  Also, I was out of buttermilk so I put a T of vinegar in a cup and added enough milk to make a cup and let it sit for 10 minutes.  I will make these again with real buttermilk.  Thank you so much P4 for telling us not to use a rolling pin.  I am sure that is the reason for my many failures.  (I have always worked biscuit dough kind of like bread dough).  I took the advice of Luvbakin and pressed my dough into a square and cut that into squares.  I placed them close together on a baking sheet and ended up with the best biscuits I have ever made.  I served these with "Sausage Gravy and Biscuits" by Kelly Cameron found on this site.  Thank you so much for sharing this delightful recipe.

attributes.source_text: These were light, fluffy, and speckled with little golden spots of color
These were light, fluffy, and speckled with little golden spots of color

reviews.review_text: These biscuits are literally life.<br/>I've tried making biscuits before, and they turned out like bland wannabe cookies, and because I live in Georgia, I have a responsibility to make biscuits that are en pointe.<br/><br/>I made them one Sunday morning, and I'm planning to use this exact recipe for the rest of my life.<br/><br/>Although, I recommend not baking them touching each other, because they may look all weird, but still taste flawless ;)<br/><br/>Pros:<br/>? They do not need to be brushed with butter before baking to look like store-bought biscuits<br/>? They are 100 times better and fluffier than store-bought biscuits<br/>? The compliments I have gotten are as follows, "They are the best biscuits I've ever eaten... They are really big, yet light." "MMHHMHMHH."<br/>? They rise about 110%<br/>? They look perfect<br/><br/>Cons:<br/>? None<br/>? No comment

reviews.review_text: These were very, very good, but flat. Fearful of over mixing (first time biscuit maker here), I barely touced the dough and those turned out nothing like the picture here. The ones I "pieced together" at the end, expecting them to be the ones that did not turn out well, actually fluffed up a lot more than the first ones. So some mixing/kneading is definitely necessary. I think it will just take some trial and error on my part. Also I suspect my baking soda and powder are older than I realized, though that doesn't account for the second batch being fluffy and the first not. Either way, the flavor is excellent and I will be making these again and again now that the tip on the food processor worked out so well. Just be aware it is definitely possible to undermix as well as over mix. There is such heavy handed warning here about over mixing that it actually made me fearful to handle the batter. That was a mixtake.

attributes.source_text: actually fluffed up a lot more than the first ones

reviews.review_text: Made these for the first time today. Followed the recipe exactly ( I did have to add about an 1/8th cup of buttermilk - as the recipe suggested I might). I believe I have may have "over-kneaded" a bit as I noticed the dough begin to get a little "elastic" as I was pressing it out the final time. 5 stars for flavor and consistency! Very light, with a buttery hint, very fluffy! I gave 4 stars only because the yield was very different for me. When I patted it out to a 1 inch dough (I like the giant fluffy style), there was only enough for maybe three or four biscuits at about 2.5" diameter. I continued patting it out until it was about a half inch dough, then got eight total (one from kneaded scraps), but then, after baking, they were only about 1.25 inches high instead of the big 2"-3" I was hoping for. Otherwise, the biscuits themselves are 5-stars! Will make again and adjust for quantities as needed.

reviews.review_text: Very light and flaky biscuits!  I've never been able to make a good biscuit unless it was from a mix until now.  These took only a minute to throw together and turned out really tender and light with a nice crispy top.  I used 1 tsp vinegar   3/4 cup milk and let it sit for 5 minutes before adding it because I didn't have any buttermilk.  Loved using the food processor to do all the mixing!  I thought the dough was a little too wet at first when I took it out of the processor, but after patting it out on the floured surface, it was just right!  Only reason I gave this 4 stars is because I only got 12 small biscuits out of the whole recipe and I patted the dough out to about 1/2 inch thickness to get that so mine weren't as high as some of the others in the pictures.  Next time I will double the recipe or plan to make two batches.  Mine also took about 15 minutes to get that golden brown color you described, but that was probably my oven and not your recipe.  Thanks for sharing this quick and easy recipe!

reviews.review_text: I had buttermilk i needed to use up and I thought I'd give it a shot. Glad I did. Mine were NOT pretty but they were amazingly tasty. Just WOW! I halved the recipe since the hubby views biscuits as a poor substitute for toast. He's a northerner so I make allowances. Anyway, I was concerned about measurements because several of my measuring spoons are MIA but I must have gotten close. I used a small food processor and put the dry and butter mix back in the freezer for a bit. I think I added a bit too much buttermilk because the dough was a bit sticky when I went to pat it out. I was really worried that they would be too crumbly since good biscuits have a reputation for being finicky. I shouldn't have worried because these came out of the oven as the most delicious biscuits I've ever had. Even hubby reluctantly agreed they were excellent. I'll absolutely make these again when I need to cook for a larger crowd.

attributes.source_text: Even hubby reluctantly agreed they were excellent

reviews.review_text: As I was having Thanksgiving, I wanted to make my own buttermilk biscuits. I went through many recipes, but when I came upon this one, and all the great reviews, I thought I would give it a try. As I was doing all the cooking, I was so happy to see that the biscuits could be made ahead of time and put in the freezer. I made the dough the night before, used a juice glass for a cutter, placed them on 2 small cookie sheets, covered them with tin foil, and put them in the freezer.  I yielded 12. Next day, as turkey came out of the oven to sit, I took the tins out of the freezer, foil off, and right into the preheated 450 degree oven. Only needed 15 minutes to bake. They were so delicious!!!  My family couldn't stop complimenting me.  My daughter thought I bought them from Williams-Sonoma!  Thanks for a great recipe!!!!

attributes.source_text: As I was having Thanksgiving
My daughter thought I bought them from Williams-Sonoma

reviews.review_text: Wonderful, tender, yummy biscuits! Perfect! Didn't notice it called for unsalted butter, next time I'll need to reduce the added salt because they were a little too salty as a result. I tested some with butter brushed on top before baking, some with oil, and some with nothing on top. Surprisingly, the butter-brushed were the least browned on top, which was better because I needed to cook them at least 14 minutes to get the centers done and the top was getting too brown on the others. Wasn't sure whether the pan needed prep, so I oiled the pan.. next time I'll butter the pan instead. Lastly, it was a little difficult for me to shape and pat gently.. I suspect it would be much easier with the rolling pin and a little more flour on the dough board. May try it next time, see whether if I'm gentle with the rolling pin, the results are still perfect.

attributes.source_text: tender

reviews.review_text:
Just tried this tonight... makes a fine biscuit: Light, airy, neutral taste... fat content is not too high, so they still taste very light even at room temperature or warm for 6-8 seconds in microwave.
Just to re-emphasize your point.. Don't Overwork.. Pat it out and cut 'em out.. only flour the immediate surface for handling and cutting. Quick and easy to make.
I've included a pic of them on the wire rack.. note the "rough" ones that I just pushed back together and cut from scraps.. still very light as I didn't work them at all... used every bit of dough.
Next time I want to try the "freeze and use later" hint to see what I think... I don't.. rather SHOULDN'T... eat that many biscuits at one time.. :D
Made an old fashioned bacon-grease gravy (since I was making bacon too..hehe) to go with it and easy over eggs with home-made yogurt.. a fine meal!

reviews.review_text: I lived in Georgia for four years and while there, my best friend (native Georgian) tried over and over to 'teach' me to make biscuits.  Well I could never get the hang of it and she didn't have a recipe...she just eyeballed everything and they came out wonderful every time!  During a discussion on the boards someone mentioned they couldn't make biscuits and Mean Chef offered to teach them.  Being an avid admirer of Mean Chef's skill, I knew immediately I wanted to be included in that 'Biscuit Making Class'!  Today, Mean Chef took the time to walk those of us who have been 'biscuit impaired' through the process of biscuit making in Q & A (on the boards) using this recipe and I finally experienced success!  Even the biscuit that was from the scraps was tender and fluffy...absolutely delicious!  Thank you Mean Chef for taking the time to do this for us on 'Zaar!

reviews.review_text: Beautiful biscuits, P4!  Thank you for an easy recipe that was a big hit with my family tonight.  We had 'breakfast for supper' and these were perfect.  (I like mine with grape jelly!)  Anyway, I  used a pastry blender instead of a food processor and they were still PERFECTION!   Also, my baking powder did have aluminum sulfate in it.  I used it anyway and it worked out fine.  I'd never noticed that ingredient in baking powder before and wondered what difference it would make without it in this recipe.  (?) Tomorrow I plan to find a different baking powder without the aluminum, then make some of these and put them in the freezer as you suggested.  How nice that will be to just pop them in the oven, but making them on the spot is absolutely no problem anyway!   Thanks, again, for a wonderful recipe!

reviews.review_text: At first it was greatly disappointing at how my biscuits turned out......but that was shortly outlived after I waited for one to cool.  The taste is amazing!  It was my own fault by how they didn't rise to the size of a normal biscuit because I simply patted them out a little on the thin side except for a few that I obviously did correctly.  But no one cared even our 2 1/2 year old that is pickier than my husband loved it, she was basically trying to rip it out of my hands.  I will be making this again for sure.  GREAT recipe.  First time I have made Biscuits that were edible.  The directions were crystal clear, just operator error when it came to estimating how thick to roll them out.  But still so very melt in your mouth tasty, I imagine this to go along nicely with some fried chicken and mashed potatoes. YUM!!!

reviews.review_text: These are amazing! I'll never use another recipe. I'm a Texan currently living in Australia and I've grown up on biscuits these are the best I've ever eaten. I've converted many recipes since living here but none ever have been quite like the ones from home...until now that is. I used 90g of butter and used my thermomix and kneading only about ten seconds or so after combining everything. I normally do biscuits by hand like my grandma did so it may be the thermie that made these so light and fluffy but I've made scones before in the machine and they do not compare to these. I used three teaspoons of baking powder because a Tablespoon here is four tsp. I changed nothing followed directions exactly fantastic biscuits my whole family said they were the best they've ever had and I got a yield of 8. All gone in a flash!

reviews.review_text: These are the best homemade biscuits I've eaten... and that it tough to say considering my father made me a lot of biscuits growing up! They were a breakfast (and sometimes dinner) staple, along with potatoes and eggs. But yeah... this recipe makes a perfect buttermilk biscuit. They are moist, fluffy, not too baking soda nor baking powder tasting. They have a ton of flavor due to the buttermilk, to the point where I just don't see myself making biscuits without buttermilk anymore! The only changes I made were that I actually added a heaping tablespoon of malt powder (I like that subtle flavor in my biscuits!), and I would say that next time I would set my oven to 430 instead of 450 because the tops browned pretty deeply before the middle of the biscuits cooked. No big deal though! This is definitely going to be my new, permanent biscuit recipe. Thank you for sharing it!

items.label: Simply Sour Cream Chicken Enchiladas
items.name: Simply Sour Cream Chicken Enchiladas
items.description: Easy to assemble, deliciously creamy and a great choice for once-a-month cooking. And there is NO canned cream soup in my enchiladas -- Hope you give them a try!
instructions: In a frying pan, cook chicken and onion together in oil over medium-high heat until chicken is just done.
Divide cooked chicken evenly between 8 tortillas; add 1 1/2 tablespoons cheese to each tortilla.
Roll enchiladas and place seam-side down in a 9x13\

reviews.review_text:
I have not tried this recipe yet, but I am going to. Looking at the ingred., it would have been my guess that it poss. would need something. (at least spices)

Ingred:
chicken, onion, tortillas, cheese 
/ butter-flour, chicken broth-sour cream, green chilies

But here is why I am writing: 
The chef stated: "There is NO canned cream soup in my enchiladas." 

(Other than added spices), could it be that it IS the "missing something, but can't put my finger on it" ingredient?

Also, as most experienced cooks know: A can of cream soup can add "consistency" to ingrediants of this type, and also add a little more flavoring.

And think about it, it would give even more options to play with, besides playing with the spices.

Cream of Chicken, Golden Mushroom, Cream of Mushroom (etc.), might be able to even find some type of "Mexican" style cream soup.  

This chef obviously has a great base recipe, no doubt.

But I, for one, am not only going to play with the spices (possibly different spices, on different days), I am also going to play in the cream of soup isle, too. I am going to double the fun. The possibilities are endless!

Again, congratulations to this chef, and I cannot wait to play. 

This recipe (as a base) is a "goldmine", and the endless possibilities are bits of gold.

I bought deli-style garlic herbed chicken from Sprouts. I then diced it and sautéed it in olive oil with onion, some fresh chopped Jalapeno, cumin, and 1/2 pack of taco seasoning. I made up the tortillas with the chicken and cheese mixture. (I was able to make five big ones with the chicken package.) I sprayed the dish and poured just a little bit of red enchilada sauce in the bottom of it before putting in the rolled tortillas. I made the roux with the butter and flour. I added in a small can of the diced green chili peppers along with the sour cream and the rest of the can of the enchilada sauce. I poured all of it over the tortillas. It was a lot, it filled up the dish. I then sprinkled a blend of Mexican cheese all over the top. I cooked it at 400 for only 15 minutes. After I took it out, I sprinkled fresh cilantro over it. It was a beautiful dish and smelled yummy. The guys absolutely loved it! They like things spicy, so I might try the Rotel next time. I am not sure. These were the best enchiladas I have ever had! Thanks so much for the recipe Deb!!

attributes.source_text: The guys absolutely loved it!

reviews.review_text: Awesome recipe. I have to make alot of our food from scratch because of allergies . I realize not everyone has the time . I work full time as well. But you can batch cook one day and get many different quick meals for a few days that you can just heat up . Flavor is what your personal tough is . I love cooking a 5# chicken with veggies in my instant pot for 15 hours .You not only get meat for 2 /3 meals but chicken broth, 2 quarts,and then cook the bones with some more veggies again for 15 hrs for some great bone broth,2 quarts. I used a mixture of white and dark meat in this recipe , made some roux and then add fresh stock to make the sauce instead of canned soup. Yummy . My husband requested a few little chucks of green chili into each tortilla before rolling and half on them got black olives on top. By the way I did 8 in flour and 8 in corn tortillas, as someone mentioned the corn taste better. My family just loved these and liked both , but hubby said he really liked the corn ones very much ! I usually use just flour. Served with canned black beans and shredded iceberg with avocado and fresh salsa on top. Thanks for all the great tips !

attributes.source_text: My family just loved these
hubby said he really liked the corn ones very much

reviews.review_text: My boyfriend and I both enjoyed this recipe. It wasn't the greatest thing I've ever made, but it was good for what it was! As for changes, I adapted some of the suggestions from other reviewers here, including adding garlic and cumin to the chicken-and-onion part of the recipe. I also tried to chop the chicken up as much as I possibly could, instead of just dicing it, per someone's advice here, and I think that worked out well. I'm also a big cheese fan, so I put a lot more of the monterey jack cheese both in and on top of the enchiladas than what the recipe mentioned, and I also added some leftover shredded mild cheddar cheese to both the inside and top of 'em. I used two cans of green chiles instead of just one, and I also added jalapenos (and a bit of the jalapeno juice), for some extra kick and flavor, on top of the enchiladas once all of the other ingredients were on top and before I put it all into the oven. Anywho, partnered the enchiladas with some quick Spanish rice for dinner that first night, and it was just great! Ate up all of the leftovers during the following few days. I'll probably make this again at some point... The only thing I could see doing differently is being sure to not have them in the oven for too long - the top was a bit hardened and crunchy rather than the softer, borderline-liquidy layer I had anticipated. It was still great and probably didn't make much difference, as everything underneath that layer was surely soft and moist, but would still like to try for next time!

reviews.review_text: I make enchiladas and have not used this recipe...I use rotisserie chicken...the breast...I fry onions and garlic and add a few red pepper flakes and sauté...then add my cooked chicken and a sprinkle of taco seasoning. and a small can of green chilies..not spicy. Remove from pan and let cool a little and then stir in sour cream to make a pasty mixture...put this in corn tortillas and put echilada sauce over...bake...I like to add cheese on top the last 10 min. this way you have a creamy mexican spiced center...you can add more pepper flakes if you want spicy..or add a dash of ceyanne to the enchilada sauce....and a nice saucey outer...I also like to spinkle finely chop green onions or cilantro on top before serving and serve with a simple crunchy salad...just lettuce and cucumber with a little avocado....this is the best...you can fry the chicken..put in the refrig. the nite before...add the sour cr. and roll them right before you are going to make them....add sauce and bake...you can add a little rice or black beans to the mix...I use this over and over and it is great!!!!!

attributes.source_text: not spicy

creamy mexican spiced center

reviews.review_text: Awesome sauce!  Yes, I am a recipe tweaker, but hear my case...it was just what I was looking for, like a needle in a haystack...a recipe without creamed condensed soups. Well, I started with a recipe that did call for a creamed soup and came across this one for inspriation.  I cooked the chicken breasts in a crock pot with 3 stalks of celery and 1 whole, chopped onion, seasoned with pepper & Adobo garlic salt. I let that cook until done. Set the chicken aside, and took all the veggies, juice from crock pot & a can of chopped green chiles and pureed adding broth to that to equal the amount called for in the recipe. Made the roux...and the rest of the recipe as follows. Loved it. Kids all but licked their plates (unknowingly eating onions, celery and onions). Served with my black beans and rice. Thanks for saving me from a creamed soup compliation! We will definetly be making this one again. For the enchiladas I used onc side of the the dish pepperjack; the other 1/2 sharp cheddar (for the kids). YUM!

attributes.source_text: Kids all but licked their plates

reviews.review_text: This is a great recipe and I have added it to my notebook of go-to recipes!  I usually have all the ingredients on hand to make this, so that is a plus as well.  I used the breast meat from a rotisserie chicken, sweating the onions first and then adding the chicken.  It did seem to me that the chicken would benefit from some seasoning, so I added about a half envelope of chicken taco seasoning that I happened to have on hand, along with a splash of the homemade stock made from the remainder of the rotisserie chicken, which I used in the sauce as well.  I used Mezzetta brand fire-roasted chili peppers, which taste a little smokey and have lime juice, cilantro and garlic added to lend extra deliciousness and a punch of flavor to the peppers.  I used a combination of monterey jack and sharp cheddar cheeses, just because that is what I had.  This recipe was as good as the sour cream chicken enchiladas I have had at a well known restaurant.  I believe theirs had spinach added, and I think that would taste great, too.   I scattered some diced roma tomatoes and cilantro leaves over the top, which made a very pretty presentation.  I served this with Spanish rice and avocadoes.  My husband was impressed by the dish as well.

attributes.source_text: My husband was impressed by the dish as well

reviews.review_text: I agree with Deb about messing with recipes.  I tried not to, but I couldn't help myself, so I added cumin to the chicken mixture (I shredded a store bought rotisserie) and I added a can of Rotel to it as well.  I added about 1/2 cup of medium spiced salsa to the sauce mixture.  I only had cheddar a mozzarella cheese, so I used 1/2 and 1/2 of that.  I also used corn instead of flour tortillas.  I used homemade chicken stock because I had the carcass from the chicken and I was out of canned.  You all know that's not hard.  Anyway...and I NEVER say this....I LOVED THIS.  So did everyone who ate it.  I am the first person to hate what I cook, and I can't wait to have this again.  I'd order it if I was eating in a restaurant.  My husband thought about the dish the next day and skipped lunch so he could eat the enchiladas when he got home.  I'm not kidding.  These are really really good.   I made rice and beans on the side and nailed that too.  This was an unprecedented night of successful cooking.  I'm not sure what happened :-)

attributes.source_text: My husband thought about the dish the next day and skipped lunch so he could eat the enchiladas when he got home

reviews.review_text: This was very good. I had a similar recipe from my mom. I did tweak the recipe per my laziness and tastes: instead of the fresh chicken breast I used 2 16oz cans of tyson chicken. It is in the can cooked, but I still 'cooked' it in the frying pan with the butter and onion as if it werent to get rid of that 'canned' taste. Plus using canned chicken made it easier to make it shredded chicken which is what I wanted. It breaks up real easy. The next thing I did was followed KansasGirls recomendation on using the can of Rotel Tomatoes with the green chilies mixed in. I think it was an excellent addition , and I mixed it right in when the recipe called for the chilies. I did not however use an additional can of chilies. I used the Rotel as a substitute. I also put refried beans on the inside before putting the chicken mixture on top and only made 4 tortillas instead of 8 so that I could have 4 stuffed tortillas. This recipe was very good, I will be making it again. I served it with spanish rice and the Bean and Cheese Taquitos recipe also located on recipe zaar.

OMG!!!!  SO GOOD!!!  In the past I wasn't huge on Mexican dishes, but since finding some great recipes (like this one) on this site, I am really beginning 2 think I may like Mexican. A short story here:  I wasn't ever much of a chef, but getting much better, again, thanks 2 this site. Just 2 prove my point, my idea of cooking was (notice past tense) popping a Stouffer's enchilada entree in the oven, one of my niece recommended (and she too is not a chef at all).  She said she tried the Stouffers enchilada with cheese sauce and didn't like it.  I had decided I would give this recipe a try, and then when I thoroughly read the directions I was a lil hesitant when I noticed the cheese sauce.  Well, let me tell U, I will NOT EVER buy Stouffers enchiladas again! Made exactly like recipe, no complaints, but may try adding some rice into the enchilada next time?  Or maybe just serving over rice?  This was easy and GREAT!   For someone who is watching there waistline, this was SO worth the calories!

attributes.source_text: I may like Mexican

reviews.review_text: These are SO good!  I'd give you 10 stars if they'd let me!  But then, I'd expect nothing less from someone with SUCH an awesome name!   hehehe! ... Okay, so I pretty much followed the recipe as is, with the following exceptions:  I used chicken meat I'd picked from the carcasses after butchering our home-grown fryers, so didn't need to cook the chicken.   I sauteed the onion, added that to the meat, plus the green chiles.  I ended up using 10 tortillas (had a bit more meat than one pound's-worth).    The roux was excellent as I used my own chicken broth, plus added 1 tsp cumin and 2 tsp chicken bouillon (sp?).  Oh, before making the roux I chopped another half onion, sauteed that in the butter for the roux.    I also added some "quesadilla" cheese to the top, which melted into the sauce and made it R-I-C-H beyond words!!!   At the table we added some scallion slices.  Mmm-good!  DEFINITELY A KEEPER!

attributes.source_text: made it R-I-C-H beyond words

reviews.review_text: Another satisfied customer!   A few things I did differently than the recipe:  I cooked the chicken breasts whole, seasoning with salt and pepper, then shredded the meat once it had cooled and gave a drizzle of fresh lime juice.  I then added just a bit of chicken stock to the pan and deglazed it, melted the butter and scraped up all the yummy chicken bits and made the roux with it that way it got a little more flavor and I only dirtied up one pan!   I used low fat sour cream and it was still a rich and delicious sauce.  I just used the cheese I had in the house which was white cheddar and parmesan.  I was a little worried about the parmesan but it really worked well!  I sprinkled some fresh cilantro on just before serving oh..and  I made the tortillas since I was out . The finished result was truly delicious and I think we will all be fighting over the leftovers.  A definite make again.  Thank you so much for sharing, Deb!

attributes.source_text: it was still a rich and delicious sauce

reviews.review_text:
These are wonderful & my family *loves* them. I make them using Taco Chicken (recipe 4957) I already have cooked. 

When I make it I double the sauce portion and put some inside each of the enchiladas as well as completely covering them with it after they're in the pan. I absolutely love the sauce, so the more the better for us!

If I was making this just for us adults I'd also double the green chiles to give it just a little more of a kick.

Another tip is this recipe is very easy to double & freeze for a quick dinner. I like to assemble enough enchiladas for another pan and freeze them on a cookie sheet, when they're frozen I put them in a large freezer bag. When it's time for dinner- all I do is make the sauce to put on top and place it on top of the frozen enchiladas. I cover it with foil & cook it around 30 minutes. Then I remove the foil, add the cheese on top and cook another 15-20 minutes.

attributes.source_text: my family *loves* them
for a quick dinner

reviews.review_text: As a vegetarian I searched for an easy, highly rated recipe to make for meat eating guests, since I couldn't taste the dish as I went. This recipe looked great. Made it over a month ago, then realized we had too much food and froze it. Followed the recipe exactly and prepared it right up until just before the baking step, then wrapped it well and froze it. Pulled it out yesterday to thaw overnight in the fridge, then cooked it tonight for 30 mins at 400 and served. My Dad, who loves my food but is a tough critic, usually gives my dishes about an 8 to an 8.5. He gave this one a 9.5. My guests chose to eat more of this rather than eat one of my famous home made desserts (though they did eventually cram some of that in too!). This was an out of the park winner....as told from the carnivores. I will definitely, DEFINITELY make this again and based on the tremendous reactions, cannot recommend this enough! Not only delicious, but a fabulous make ahead/frozen dish. Thank you so much Deb!!!

attributes.source_text: My Dad, who loves my food but is a tough critic, usually gives my dishes about an 8 to an 8.5. He gave this one a 9.5.
My guests chose to eat more of this rather than eat one of my famous home made desserts

reviews.review_text: I tweaked this a bit and loved it. The sauce I made a little differently. I added 1/2 packet of taco seasoning to it once it was thick and bubbly and then added the sour cream and about 8 diced pickled jalepenos and a can of drained,diced tomatoes with onions and green peppers. Oh yum is that sauce good :) I used 2 bouillon cubes in 15 oz of water since I was out of chicken broth as well. For the Chicken I used Rotisserie chicken (BBQ) seasoned with garlic/herb Mrs.Dash and a little cajun seasoning. I shredded it up in the food processor after it was warmed in the saute pan with the onion and oil. Topped the tortillas with meat mixture and mild cheddar cheese (what I had on hand) and rolled and poured sauce over the rolled enchiladas and topped everything off with the remaining cheese. Yum! I love this sauce...TY for a base idea to get me started.

attributes.source_text: once it was thick and bubbly
once it was thick and bubbly

reviews.review_text: I loved this so much more than my local restaurant's! I usually eat sour cream enchiladas because the red chili and green chili sauce burn the hell out of my tongue! I love the subtle, creamy flavor of this dish, not to mention a little kick from the canned green chilies.<br/><br/>My only reason for deducting a star was the texture. I followed the recipe to a T, and even though I'm adopted into a huge Mexican family, I didn't question the strange choice of softened flour tortillas. Big mistake. They came out VERY soggy and clumpy. It was too much for my gag reflex. I also tried not softening the tortillas, but they came out the same. Last night I made them with corn tortillas (white or yellow are fine) and they were MUCH better. I'd recommend sticking to these traditional enchilada methods if you like a little more crunch.

attributes.source_text: I love the subtle, creamy flavor of this dish
a little kick from the canned green chilies

reviews.review_text: Oh my gosh, that was good! I'm not much of a cook (trying to learn!), but this made me look so good! Since I wasn't able to dice the chicken quite as small as I wanted, I cut into small pieces, cooked it (no onions - someone in our house won't eat them), and then put it into my food processor for just a few pulses to make it perfect for filling. Followed the rest exactly, and it was absolutely heaven, and I'm usually not a huge fan of chicken. The sauce is to die for! Thank you for sharing this delicious and easy recipe!  ***Update*** Still a fabulous recipe, even with reduced fat sour cream and cheese, whole wheat tortillas and using canned chicken breast, making it a little healthier. Sticking to one enchilada per serving but with low-fat refried beans still made this filling but somewhat diet friendly. Very, very yum. I keep coming back to this recipe.

As if this recipe needs another great review, but there is a reason there are so many. These were simply awesome.. The DS repeatedly said "Honey, did I tell you how great dinner was".. Based on other reviews, I made only minor "tweaks". Since our preference is to shred the chicken first, I used 2 large bone in split chicken breasts. Seasoned them with garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, Mexican oregano, salt and pepper. Roasted them in the over for an hour. I also made sure I used the pan drippings in the sauce. I sprinkled the leftover seasoning mix on the chicken after shredding. For the cheese in the filling, I crumbled queso fresco cheese, then used the cheddar / jack blend for the top (I mean really, why not have more cheese!). Other than that, I made as stated. Although next time I make these (and there will be a next time!) I wonder if I should add some black olives... hmmm..

attributes.source_text: how great dinner was

reviews.review_text: We loved this recipe. I will admit, I read a lot of reviews before hand and tweaked the recipe based on comments. I used a Rotisserie chicken from the store and shredded it. I sauteed the onions in the oil with some Nature Seasonings. Once done I added the chicken, a pinch of garlic powder, pepper, salt and 1 tsp taco seasonings. I then added a can of original Rotel (that I drained of liquids first). I used this mixture and put into the tortillas with the cheese. The sauce I did just as the recipe suggests and I even used fat free sour cream. I added more black pepper to the sauce as well. We also served with a bunch of toppings. I topped mine with fresh cilantro, fresh diced jalapenos, lime slices and avocado slices. The others also topped theirs with salsa and/or hot sauce. I will be making this at LEAST once a month and sharing the recipe with others as well!! Thanks!!

items.label: Delicious Chicken Pot Pie
items.name: Delicious Chicken Pot Pie
items.description: This chicken pot pie recipe takes a little time, but it is WELL WORTH IT!! This is an all-time favorite in our family. Great on a cold winter day.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Saute onion, celery, carrots and potatoes in margarine for 10 minutes.
Add flour to sauteed mixture, stirring well, cook one minute stirring constantly.
Combine broth and half and half.
Gradually stir into vegetable mixture.
Cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly.
Stir in salt and pepper; add chicken and stir well.
Pour into shallow 2 quart casserole dish and top with pie shells.
Cut slits to allow steam to escape.
Bake for 40-50 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly and cooked through.

reviews.review_text: At last, the perfect recipe for a chicken pot pie filling that DOESN'T use that God-awful condensed soup or frozen vegetables.  I followed the recipe almost as written, but had to use mushrooms in place of potatoes because mine had gone bad before I got to them.  If anything was wrong with my version, it was the mushrooms, and I usually love them in everything else.  I used a whole box of fresh thyme to add some extra flavor at the very end...next time I'll use a variety of fresh herbs for a more rounded flavor.  I used whole milk instead of half and half, and the Kitchen Basics brand of chicken stock which  has virtually no salt.  I was surprised how much salt this seemed to need to get the flavor to where I wanted it, so I suggest not being stingy with it.  For the chicken, I used part chicken breast which I cubed and sauteed along with plenty of good old S&P, and part chicken thigh meat which I needed to use up.  The filling was divided between each of 2 pie shells, then topped with a second crust and baked as dirrected.  The result of all this was truly outstanding!  The Pilsbury pie crusts worked very well for this recipe.  The only other adjustment I'll make next time will be to add a generous half cup of frozen peas to the filling.  Thanks for sharing such a great recipe!  It really hit the spot on a cold, rainy day!

This recipe was 5 stars and more. It was so delicious and not hard to make at all. After reading all the reviews and looking at the recipe I had to agree it needed some spices. Did everything in the directions but added a pinch of nutmeg, some garlic salt, thyme, poultry seasoning, rosemary and about 1/4 cup white wine and I added a bit of frozen peas. For the top crust I used Pillsbury crescent rolls. The flavor was so yummy, we really enjoyed this dish so much. I had made the mixture the night before and then made the individual bowls for lunch in the morning. It took just and extra 15 minutes in the oven. But next time I make this I would like it to have just a bit more juice to it. It had creamy flavor but I would of preferred just a bit more liquid so I would add a little more broth and wine. The wine really adds a very nice rich flavor to the dish. Thanks so much for sharing your lovely recipe vincy....We loved it....

UPDATE: Made this again and went with adding the extra 1/4 cup of wine with an extra 3/4 cup of broth which was an extra 1 cup of liquid to the recipe in all. Perfect...and I measured the seasonings I put in and it was a pinch of nutmeg and a tsp. of the other spices mentioned above. It made this delicious dish even more yummy, had the perfect amount of creaminess...I would also like to add that I had timed myself and it was all done and ready to pop in the oven in 30 minutes not an hour.... So if an hour might scare some people off ..don't let it...This recipe is so worth going for and can be ready for oven in the 30 minutes.

Just back to add my stars ...they keep disappearing !!!

reviews.review_text: Delish!  This pot pie recipe is as good or better than a recipe that I've been using for years.  I like this one because it doesn't call for any canned cream soups. (I'm trying to cook less with canned and/or processed foods.) This was tasty made according to the directions, and easy enough to make, but I did have a few comments to add to the reviews.  For one thing, I only baked my pot pie for about 25 minutes or less - as the recipe says, it's done when the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbly.  If you set your timer for 45 minutes, you might end up with a burnt crust. I found it took far less than 1 3/4 hours to prepare and cook this.  Another thing, next time I will saute the carrots alone in the butter for a few minutes, then add the other veggies.  I will also cut the potatoes a bit larger, since they ended up falling apart. "Diced" potatoes are too small; 1/2 - 1 inch are a better size.  I didn't peel mine either, and they worked fine. I also added some thyme (just for a little extra flavor), and I used whole milk in place of the 1/2 and 1/2. It was still plenty creamy.  One batch of this fit nicely in my Pampered Chef 9" x 9" square stoneware casserole dish.   I will definitely be making this again, as the whole family enjoyed it.

attributes.source_text: It was still plenty creamy
the whole family enjoyed it

reviews.review_text: This was the first chicken pot pie that I've ever made! It was really delicious, and my boyfriend loved it!! (He's a picky pot pie eater.) I basically followed the recipe with a few tweaks per other reviews. 1) I used 4 cups of cubed chicken breast that I boiled in 2 cups of broth with a bay leaf. I used that broth in the recipe. 2) I did the potatoes and onions as stated, but omitted the celery and carrot and replaced with 2 cups of frozen mixed veggies. 3) Several reviews said it could use more salt, so I used 2 tsp of garlic salt (in lieu of 1 tsp regular salt), a pinch of paprika, and about 1/2 tsp of Italian seasoning. 4) The pot pie filling filled a 9x13" glass casserole dish perfectly. 5) I used store bought crust. I used regular pie crust for the bottom, and puff pastry brushed with egg white wash for the top. My 9x13 casserole dish used one box each of the regular crust and puff pastry. I baked the whole thing for 40 minutes... it was slightly too brown (since I used puff pastry for the top), so next time I will bake it for 30-35 minutes. Thank you for sharing!

attributes.source_text: my boyfriend loved it
He's a picky pot pie eater

reviews.review_text: DELICIOUS!!!  WOW!!!  I am so used to being disappointed in recipes, but not this one.  I made it according to the directions (a couple tiny mods as noted).  I so hate it when people totally modify a recipe and then rate it -useless.  First off, the directions seemed to indicate you should use the 2 pie crusts on top.  I used a 9 inch pie pan and used a store-bought crust on the bottom and one the top.  The filling was about 1.5 times as much as was needed to fill the pie, so I would do about 2/3 of the recipe next time.  Another little change is that I only used about 3 cups of cut up chicken as that is what I ended up with form 3 large chicken breasts.  And I added a little bit of poultry seasoning, which added a perfect taste to it.  It was great.  The right consistency, the right flavor, the right amount of salt, etc.  I will make it again!  Another little note - I boiled chicken breasts in 4 cups water with chicken boullion.  Then I shredded up the chicken and used the liquid as the chicken broth.  I put a little of the onion, carrots and celery into that liquid as well when boiling the chicken breasts.  I think it would also have been great with roasted chicken as well.  Thanks for the recipe.  I was looking for one that didn't call for frozen vegetables or canned cream of chicken, and this was perfect!

This recipe is dangerous. My son and I had three servings each! Adding herbs to the filling is a big upgrade. I used fresh thyme, fresh sage, and dried oregano. But I highly recommend even a few dried herbs. Thyme is always a favorite dried herb of mine because it still has a strong flavor even after long term storage. Oregano also maintains flavor. Other dried herb ideas might be tarragon, sage, or rosemary. Anything! It really adds to this great dish! The original calls for two crusts on top, but does not explain it well. I think both go on top, overlapping, because the recipe calls for a casserole (i.e., rectangular) dish, not a (round) pie dish. With some trimming and overlapping, the two round crusts can be made to cover the entire rectangular top. But I prefer crust on the bottom as well. So I use a slightly larger casserole dish, put two round pie crusts on the bottom, with a thin layer of crushed Corn Chex on top of the bottom crusts (to prevent the crusts from getting soggy). On top of the filling I like a biscuit type of crust. But the store-bought crust I used almost burned, so keep an eye on it. For the filling, I used carrots, celery, PEARL ONIONS (!), potatoes and chicken. I added a bit more broth than what the recipe called for (an extra 1/2 c) which made the gravy just a bit more saucy and not so solid. I prefer a biscuit crust on top.

reviews.review_text:
I am a full-time house wife and Mom, but I also work 4 nights a week as a cook.  The family I cook for really enjoys comfort food so I am always on the look out for quick, but tastey recipes that avoid any cream-of-goop-clog-your-arteries soup. This has been the best recipe that I have found on recipezaar so far. So easy to make I threw together 2 of them and both my family and my employers were clamoring for more!

I did substitute bullion for the broth (alas I was out of stock) and so omitted adding any further salt.  I also added a bit of summer savory which added a nice herby flavor.  Sage, thyme, or majoram would be good too I think.

Oh! And for a creamier texture I used half a cup of heavy cream instead of a full cup of half and half. 

I also made my own pastry (I try to keep as much of my cooking "homemade" as possible).  Sift together 1 C. flour and 1 t. salt.  Cut in 1/4 lb. cold butter or marg. till resembles coarse crumbs.  Whisk together 1 egg yolk and 2 T. ice water add to flour mixture and mix till it just comes together.  Let rest in frig for 20 minutes then roll out and top pie.  Easy-peasy and SOOOOOOOOO good.

attributes.source_text: both my family and my employers were clamoring for more

reviews.review_text: This was by far the most delicious chicken pot pie ever!  First off, I have never even attempted to make my own. Lately, the store-bought ones were seeming to have less and less filling, so I thought I would find a recipe online.  I chose this one because of the reviews, but mainly because it did not call for a can of creamed something-or-other soup that I never have on hand.  The only thing I did differently was to not include celery but added half a can of peas after sauteeing the veggies. And I sprinkled a bit of garlic powder into the mix.  Then I added all the juice from my chicken that I had sitting in the fridge (after removing the fat).  I also had to add a bit more stock, and glad I did because the crust (Pillsbury) absorbed a lot of it once it was cut.  OMG!  This was sooooooooooooooooo good.  My husband has been ranting and raving about it to everyone who will listen.  Thank you!!!!

attributes.source_text: My husband has been ranting and raving about it

reviews.review_text: I make this recipe maybe every other month!! The flavors are rich and perfect! I usually roast chicken or chicken breasts in the oven (with oregano, lemon pepper,lemon slices, garlic, salt,  black pepper, and olive oil) the day before or that morning, and then hand shred it. I skip the celery since my brother nor my husband like them. I do the potatoes, flour, and broth/half and half steps. At that point, I add in frozen peas and frozen carrots. I mimic the spices I used for the chicken at this point (dried oregano, lemon pepper, salt, pepper, dried onion powder since I omit real onion). I stir in the chicken and let it get nice and creamy. I then use pot pie tins and cover it with pie crust. Into the oven at 400 degrees for about 25 minutes...perfect!!! I freeze most of the pot pies (I get about six out of the recipe when cooked and cooled. Then, when I want one, I bake it at 375 degrees for about 30-40 minutes. Soooooo gooooooood! Thank you so much for sharing the recipe!!!

attributes.source_text: The flavors are rich and perfect
let it get nice and creamy

reviews.review_text: Just got done with dinner and both hubby and I are raving about this.  We both love chicken pot pies, but it seemed like such a task to make one.  This turned out to be super simple for my first one! Yes there is a little bit of prep that goes into it, but nothing more than what I usually tackle for a dinner.  I did make some adjustments based on other reviews and personal taste.  Used combo of butter and EVOO to saute veggies.  Added 2 cloves minced garlic to last 2 minutes of sauteing.   Sprinkled veggies with some poultry seasoning.  Used 1/2 c hvy whipping cream (because I had it) and 1/2 c 1% milk.  To thickened mixture, added 2 Tbsp sr cream, approx 1/2 tsp hot sauce (Tapatio) and about 2 tsp worchestershire.  Added approx 1/2 c thawed frozen peas. Bought rotisserie chicken from the store and used whole darn thing in this (we like it meaty). To finish, I brushed ready made pie crust with egg wash and sprinkled with parmesan cheese.  YUM-O!

attributes.source_text: both hubby and I are raving about this

reviews.review_text:
This is a great recipe with a little tweaking. All I had on hand was whipping cream instead of half & half. That made it delightfully creamy, but definitely upped the fat and calories. I also used a homemade turkey stock full of shredded turkey.

I doubled the recipe (for 2 pies), added 2 chicken bouillon cubes, one cup of frozen sweet peas, one cup of frozen sweet corn, a lot more salt (it needed salt badly), 2 tablespoons of minced garlic.

I made the mistake of putting one pie crust in the bottom of the pan. I should have placed them both on top to get "crusty". The buttery, flakey crust was great with this - I used a Pillsbury premade pie shell (don't buy the generic, it's subpar.)

Next time, I will definitely add the 3/4 cup of white wine and pinch of nutmeg and poultry seasoning that another reviewer suggested. That should make it just perfect!

attributes.source_text: That made it delightfully creamy
The buttery, flakey crust was great
The buttery, flakey crust was great

reviews.review_text: My DS's gobbled this up!  I followed the recipe except that I didn't have any celery (thought I had some in fridge but boys had been snacking on it) and omitted the salt b/c I was using canned broth.  I also used less than 1/3 cup margarine to cut down on the fat content.  Nonetheless, the pie was delicious and the 'sauce' was thick and creamy and tasted great- and no flour lumps!  I poured the hot and bubbly filling into a pie plate and covered w/ a single Pillsbury pie crust (from the dairy aisle).  It was definately done in 30 minutes and the filling had overflowed.  Next time I'll put a cookie sheet underneath to catch the overflow.   I'm not giving it 5 stars because although the directions were very well-written and easy to follow, it took a lot of time to prep, and didn't 'WOW' me enough to cook more than once or twice a year.  (My DS's would eat it every week if I'd cook it :-))

attributes.source_text: My DS's gobbled this up!
the 'sauce' was thick and creamy
the 'sauce' was thick and creamy

reviews.review_text:
I had to ask a stupid question:LOL:  but the chef was kind enough to get in touch with me:) Thanks!

WOW!  This is a wonderful recipe!  I don't know if I'll ever need to try another version after this.  I didn't really "measure" 1 c of all the veggies and baked off 4 large boneless chicken breasts seasoned with Paul Prudhommes Chicken seasoning and used store bought pie crusts.  The sauce was excellent, you could even eat it as a cream of chicken pot pie soup if you cooked the veggies a bit longer:LOL:  As soon as I tasted it I knew this would be getting 5stars=)   I did throw in some thyme, marjoram and a small bay leaf and a handful of chopped parsley.  You could easily add a handful of frozen sweet peas or sweet corn at the last minute before adding to the pie crust.  
Served this with cornbread with honey butter.  
Again WOW and thank you a bunch!

It was delicious but if I would've followed the recipe exactly as it was it would've been bland.  I don't measure things.  I'm like Rachel Ray, a little this, a little that and I continually taste to make sure everything's flowing.  I had to add a lot more salt and pepper and I also added a little garlic powder, paprika, and poultry seasoning.  I only had heavy whipping cream on hand so I used 1/2 cream and 1/2 2% milk.  Oh, I cut my time in half by using a rotissierie chicken from the deli.  While the veggies were sauteeing I deboned my chicken.  I had dinner ready in a snap.  One more thing...I'm not much of a pastry chef so I used a store bought pie crust and brushed it with an egg wash prior to baking.  This is a great chicken pot pie recipe but it does require a little tweeking...to your liking.  I think next time I'm going to try making it with fat free evaporated milk to cut back on some fat and calories.  This one is definitely a keeper.

Very Yummy, though the two pie crusts on top was a little odd. I am pretty sure one should have gone underneath but that was not the way the recipe was written!

I reserved my sauted veggies and added a little more butter to the pan, then the flour to cook off the raw taste and only used about 1/4 cup flour. I then added the stock and cream and got out any lumps before adding the veggies back in with the chicken. I also added some sage for extra flavor per some of the comments I read.

I wish I had made my own crust, but I was going for easy tonight and had two frozen crusts in the freezer. The only drawback to this was that they had a slightly sweet taste, but were otherwise very good.

I will be making this again and tweaking it to match my tastes. I like the inside to be less dense and more soupy... oh and the crust going all the way around. :)

UPDATE:  Added 3/4 C white wine and a couple of tbl of fresh herbs (sage / rosemary / thyme)  Added the herbs after putting in the broth and half and half.  Seems perfect this way.  Original:   I made this last night.  Everyone liked it.  Thanks to the other reviewers got some ideas and added some poultry seasoning, thyme, and rosemary to the chicken and then baked it.  My husband said I should have also added a bit more of the same seasoning to the pot pie mixture.  Will do that next time.  One other reviewer also said a bit more liquid is good - and she used white wine.  I am FOR SURE doing that next time too.  We used homemade crusts - also from this site.  I will for sure make this many times again.  Thanks for posting!  PS -- be extra sure to add extra liquid if you are going to have left overs.  Our left overs had very little sauce and was very thick...

I almost followed this recipe exactly and found that it was great! It is rich and creamy and full of flavor, my husband and I ate way more than we should have. I left out the celery because I hate celery and opted to use a frozen bag of mixed veggies (peas, carrots, corn and green beans) to avoid all the chopping and add some more textures and healthy bits. So I just cooked the potato and onions together until almost soft. Followed the directions exactly and then added the mixed frozen veggies in step 7 when you add in the cooked chicken. I just added what I thought was "enough" and everything looked chunky and well proportioned. I wasn't sure if I was supposed to have a bottom crust so I made mine with a top and bottom and it came out great. If you have left over chicken or perhaps pick up a rotisserie chicken and use the frozen veggies like I did, prep time on this recipe is about 20 minutes, which is awesome for a home made pot pie.

attributes.source_text: It is rich and creamy and full of flavor

everything looked chunky and well proportioned

reviews.review_text: SO SO SO good!!!  We used turkey breast instead of chicken, because that's what they had prepared at the grocery store, and I don't like cooking chicken.  The fresh veggies we used were celery, carrots, onions, and a can each of peas and corn.  After reading reviews, we added some poultry seasoning to give it a bit more flavor.  My husband really wanted puff pastry crust for the top.  It was good, but I missed the 15 minute timer, and the puff pastry was overdone.  I will have to watch more carefully next time.  For a bottom crust, I used my MIL pie crust recipe, and it was delicious.  We made 4 cocottes and a 7x11 casserole dish.  There was a little left that didn't fit in the dish, but that's what my 4 year old ate.  She found it less offensive without the crust.  I had some as leftovers today, and I'm excited to have MORE leftovers for dinner!!!!  YUM!

attributes.source_text: I'm excited to have MORE leftovers for dinner

items.label: Crock Pot Whole Chicken
items.name: Crock Pot Whole Chicken
items.description: Tender, fall-off-the-bone chicken! Skip the overnight refrigeration if you are in a hurry. For variety, eliminate the onion and substitute a quartered lemon or two, stuffed into the chicken cavity.  Chef Shapeweaver had a good suggestion:  Use Fajita Seasoning Mix #28011 as another variation.  Thanks!  The standard size slow cookers are a bit too small and a whole chicken won't fit.  You'll need a 6-quart slow cooker for this recipe.
instructions: In a small bowl, combine the spices.
Remove any giblets from chicken and clean chicken.
Rub spice mixture onto the chicken.
Place in resealable plastic bag and refrigerate overnight. (I usually skip this step because I'm always in a hurry).
When ready to cook, put chopped onion in bottom of crock pot.
Add chicken.  No liquid is needed, the chicken will make its own juices.
Cook on low 4-8 hours.
Note:  I highly recommend a pop-up timer in the chicken because some crock pots cook faster/slower than others (my crock pot cooks this recipe in 4-5 hours).

reviews.review_text:
A good recipe for beginning cooks, and those new to crockpots.
I just realized I had been using this recipe, but I thought I had come up with it! ;)
Around 2004 I found 2 recipes on "Zaar" (back in the days) and combined them. Roast Sticky Chicken and Crockpot Roast Chicken. The result is almost this exact recipe (which appears to have been posted in 2002).
The changes I make are: cutting down the salt and cayenne, adding about a teaspoon brown sugar to the rub, and a pat of butter to each chicken breast, under the skin. Oh, I will usually rub olive oil over the top to help the rub stick. Make sure to add rub under the skin, and cavity as well! When done just thicken the juices with a little cornstarch (in a sauce pan), or go all out and make gravy!
The texture of the crockpot chicken will differ a little bit from roasted, but I, and the many people who have eaten it, do not have a problem with that. 
Any one who finds the flavor bland, really should definitely check the freshness of their spices...and did you really follow the recipe to the letter? The salt alone, if you do not reduce it, is a lot of flavor. Was the correct sized crockpot used? 6 qt would be best, but I have used the round 5 qt on a small chicken. Crisping it up under the broiler does put this over the top, but I don't feel the need to do it often. 
If you get the technique down, then the variety is endless! Change the spices to your whim!

I am now in the process of making the chicken. I followed the recipe to a T and will have a follow up when it is done along with step by step picture's from beginning to end! My crock pot for some reason is much hotter than others. I guess you could call it a super hot pot. I have 2 crock pots and I chose to use the hotter one and will see if it gets a little crisp on the out side of the chicken.I set it on low because if I set it on high it would be done in no time and would loose the flavor of all the spices combining together on the chicken. I combined onion and fresh chopped garlic on the bottom of the crock and then sat the chicken on top of the onion and garlic. I put 1 tablespoon of lemon juice in also. Follow up ///// :There is no doubt that what ever you put in a crock pot will always be tender no matter what type of meat or poultry you put in it if you leave the crock pot go long enough.There is way to much salt in this recipe for me. I would cut the salt in half then go with the other spices. I had it in the crock for 8 hours. I added no water and there was 2 cups of broth for gravy. The skin was not crispy because of all the broth but it did have a good taste (minus the salt) if I would of cut the salt in half.

attributes.source_text: will always be tender

reviews.review_text: This is a wonderful crock pot chicken recipe.  I used a 6 1/2 pound Perdue Oven Stuffer Roaster and added 1/2 cup of shredded carrots and 1/2 cup of chicken stock to the onions  and it took about 4 hours on low and 2 1/2 hours on high when the timer popped up (in a 12 qt crock pot). Before finding this recipe, I always cooked my chicken in the oven or on the grill, but my husband likes this version so much that I will cook it this way from now on.  I think that three things should be noted on this recipe though...1) definitely use a pop up timer chicken when cooking this in a crock pot and take it out as soon as it pops up - otherwise it WILL be a little dry (made it twice and the first time I came home to a very dry chicken)  2) once the chicken "pops up", transfer it to a metal baking dish, pour some of the liquid from the crock pot on top to keep moist, and cover it with aluminum foil until ready to broil and 3) absolutely broil this just before serving.  I put my oven rack in the middle position and broiled it (i have a gas oven) for 10 minutes until it was crisp and wonderfully browned.  After the chicken was transferred to a baking dish (prior to broiling), I strained all of the juices and vegetables into a saucepan and thickened it with 2 packages of Knorr's chicken gravy combined with 1 1/2 cups of boxed chicken stock until nicely bubbly and thickened.  It made the perfect gravy and chicken.  Great recipe Kathy!

reviews.review_text: Absolutely delicious!  I used 3.8 lb. chicken which fit perfectly in a 4 qt oval crock pot. I did not have cayenne pepper or onion powder so I used Cajun seasoning and Adobo seasoning instead. I rubbed the spice mixture above and beneath the skin as noted by another reviewer and tossed the rest in the chicken cavity. While cooking in the slow cooker, the house smelled amazing!  I used a barbeque fork and a spatula to pull the chicken out of the pot. It was so tender it was literally falling off the bone! A quick 5-minute broil in the toaster oven and it was all done! This dish went very well with Dana-MMH's Greek Oven Roast Potatoes (#32566) as well as peas and carrots I had tossed into a chicken-flavored rice-a-roni dish. Such an affordable dish too! We purchased the whole chicken on sale for less than $3 (79 cents per pound) and we'll be getting 4 meals out of this one dish! I highly recommend this recipe to anyone interested in saving money without compromising flavor!

attributes.source_text: It was so tender it was literally falling off the bone!

reviews.review_text: This was amazing! Would give it 10 stars if I could. I also added carrots and celery under the chicken and stuffed some into the cavity. It took longer to cook than expected because I purchased a way-to-large Perdue chicken (with a pop-up timer) and started cooking it at noon. Because of the size I decided to cook it on high for 5 hours. The timer still didn't pop up but, because I wanted golden skin, I put the chicken in the toaster oven (at 500 degrees) and in about 15 minutes the timer popped up and the chicken was golden brown, juicy and delicious. I've cooked chickens with the breast side down (as Hadice suggested) but was unable to do so with this one because of the timer (which I didn't want to remove). I usually cook my turkeys that way and it makes the breasts very moist. I must add, the juice that formed was amazing!  Being in a hurry, I did not refrigerate overnight. Thanks you so much for sharing this recipe. I will be making it over and over again.

attributes.source_text: juicy and delicious

reviews.review_text: This is a great alternative to roasting a chicken in the oven.  I would reduce the amount of each spice if you are cooking anything less than a 4 lb bird.  DO NOT put any more than 1 tsp of salt, that is insanity. I used less than 1 tsp of salt, I omitted the onion powder and added lemon pepper seasoning.  Obviously the cook times vary greatly if you are reading any of these reviews. My 7 quart crock pot cooked a 3-4 bird on low in about 7 hours, yielding less than a cup of liquid. The liquid was strained and used to make gravy which was exceptional, if a little too salty.  Definitely crisp up the bird under the broiler for about 10 mins then wrap in aluminum foil for a few minutes before serving.  Very tender and juicy.  Throw all the bones, skin, onions, etc back in the crock pot, cover with water and cook on low for several hours to make some chicken stock which you can freeze for later use.  The aromas while cooking this recipe are heavenly.  I only wish a turkey fit into my crock pot because I would be making it this way every Easter/Thanksgiving/Christmas.  Enjoy.

reviews.review_text:
This was really good.  So good that DD, who might eat half a leg, said that I was to never make another kind of chicken, only this way.  And she ate a leg and a half.  Because I was trying to get her to eat something new I cut the peppers to 1/4 t.  I also was out of garlic powder and used granulated garlic.  While I liked it, I would have liked to have added more heat.  I put the mixture under the skin and inside the cavity forgetting that I was supposed to rub it on.
I usually add carrots, onion, celery and water to my chicken when I do it in my crock pot so I wasn't sure how this was going to turn out without adding liquid.  This made plenty of broth to make gravy with.  I served this over Recipe #26110.  It was so good with the gravy!  I wanted more broth so I cleaned the chicken off the bones and added the skin, water to cover and the fat that I had skimmed to make gravy.  I forgot about it and it boiled hard for an unknown amount of time.  It made a nice, rich looking broth.  Just as I finished staining it and was letting it cool we lost power.  I was to afraid to open the refrigerator and put something so hot in for fear it would bring down the temp of the refrigerator.  The power was out for hours and I lost the broth.  I was very disappointed.  I look forward to making this again.  Thanks for sharing the recipe.

reviews.review_text: This was FANTASTIC!,I have only had my crockpot a few months and I must say, this is one of the best things I have made in it so far! I followed the recipe exactly except that I cut the cayenne down to 1/2 tsp. and this was still plenty spicy for me. I did not have a ziploc bag large enough for the chicken,so I placed it in a stainless steel bowl and covered with plastic wrap, and popped it in the fridge overnight. I cooked it as directed on low and it was ready for me in 6 hrs. I too ,as others, thickened the juices with some flour & water and this made an unbelieveable gravy, did not have to add a thing to it, so much flavour! Hubby got up from the table and exclaimed it one of the best meals I ever made! We had the leftovers for supper again tonight and he is still talking about how good this chicken is!,as a matter of fact, our grocery store has roasting chickens on sale this week, so he picked up 2 more for the freezer today....something tells me I will be making this chicken again very soon!!!!!! Thanks, Kathy for a fabulous recipe!

reviews.review_text: I make this on a regular basis and the added bonus is the bone broth! I cut 2 onions in half and put them flat side down in the bottom of crock (to keep bird off the bottom). The I put my bird in breast down so all the juices in the back flow down through the breast (I cook my turkey butt up also). I typically only use basil, pepper & a tiny bit of sea salt, but occasionally add granulated garlic, onion powder and smoked paprika. When it is done, the bird is swimming in beautiful juices (broth). I use 2 large slotted spoons to transfer him to a serving platter and then run the juices through a fine stainless-steel colander. I put the strained juices in a tall round plastic container (mine is about 8” tall and 4” diameter so it is easier to remove the fat; but any container would work) in the fridge overnight and the next day, the fat is hardened on top and I remove it. What is left is a golden gel! I put it into freezer bags, ½ cup each. Snack bags with the zipper on the narrow edge work great. I keep them in my freezer until broth is needed and use one bag with a cup or 2 of water in place of a can of broth from the store. In the meantime, I have chicken for dinner and leftovers for other meals or salads. The options are endless. The skin and bones get pitched and I feel as though I have made extremely healthy food for my family because I have controlled all of the ingredients.

attributes.source_text: I have chicken for dinner

reviews.review_text: Made this for dinner tonight and it was delicious. Used some of the broth for gravy and the bones and the rest of the broth are simmering for soup base.  I cut the salt down to 1 tsp, but that is a little too light. 11/2 - 2 tsp would be better.  I was very liberal with the paprika which was a little too much, added chilli pdr instead of cayenne and omitted the onion powder because I didn't have any. I may use onion soup mix for the salt and onion powder next time. I have a new crock pot, for my 2kg (4.5lb) chicken I set it to auto which is high until it boils then low. Even my low is above the boiling point. I cooked it a total of 5.5 hrs, 3 hrs at low and 2.5 hrs at high because I thought it would't be done.  Next time I will leave it on low. Also I will put the breast down, it was a little dry. My comments are notes for myself for the next time I cook this, they are not criticism.  We really enjoyed this and I will definitely be making it again.

attributes.source_text: Made this for dinner tonight

reviews.review_text:
I am making this chicken for the 3rd time in the last month! I just put a 7 lb bird in the crockpot because my son, his wife and 2 small children are coming to visit from Chicago. These are the very important things I learned from reading many of the reviews. I cut my salt to 1 tsp, used half the amount of cayenne, and 1 tsp. total of pepper. I lifted the breast skin and put the seasoning under it, also 2 small pats of butter. I seasoned the cavity well and sprikled the rest of the seasoning over the rest of the chicken. In the cavity I placed 2 crushed cloves of garlic, slices from half a lemon and a large sprig of rosemary from my garden bended in half. This is what I have done each time and it has been amazing.

If you read a recipe and it sounds like too much salt or anything else use common sense and don't use so much. I think some of the folks are cooking these chickens too long, I have been able to lift the bird (carefully) from the crockpot with succulent, moist tender meat including the breast. My 6qt oval Crockpot cooks a 5 lb chicken on low in around 5-6 hours.

Like everyone says, chill that broth and remove the fat which will harden on top for some amazing chicken noodle soup! I have not tried putting the bones back in to simmer but plan to this time.

I NEVER expected this recipe to be so good and it it fabulous!!! Thank you so much!
