reviews.review_text: Although this recipe was tasty I am going to rate it just "Good"<br/>3 different peppers calling for 2 1/2 in total is an awful lot of pepper. I cut that back to 1/2, 1/2 and a few turns of my pepper mill.<br/>The fact that this recipe didn't call for any liquid whatsoever had me very skeptical so I did add a bit of water and chicken broth to the bottom. My chicken was completely thawed, maybe you are using a frozen chicken? That would make sense then that it makes its own liquid. Other than that I followed the recipe to a T, including the onion at the bottom. However, it was burnt to a crisp on the bottom due to no liquid. And I do mean burnt. I did cook it on low for about 6 - 7 hours while I was at work.<br/>I will try this again as I do like the flavor of the spice mixture (minus all the pepper it calls for) and will add some white wine, chicken broth and vegetables as other reviews have suggested.

This was beautiful and tastes great! I let the spices only sit for an hour and I forgot to put my onion in, but neither mattered where taste is concerned. Talkin' about falling off the bone- it most certainly did...and moist! I mean moist! I almost added a tad of water to the bottom because I was going to bed when I put this on, and I'm so glad I didn't and followed Kathy's directions because I had liquid all the way to the top. I have high and low on my crockpot, so I put it on high for two hours and dh cut it down on low for me and then it cooked for about 8 more hours. I know that seems like a long time but the chicken was perfect and moist. I didn't plan to cook it that long but I was exhausted and couldn't get up. Main thing is- it didn't hurt it one bit. I used the pop up timer as suggested so I am posting a pic. I will be using this recipe with the same spices again! Well deserving of it's stars! Thank you Kathy!!!

reviews.review_text: This has to be the BEST crockpot chicken recipe! I have used this recipe for a year.  First time I made this recipe, I did not have white pepper, so I sub'd it for black pepper, and I still do not have Cayenne pepper in the house. Tasted absolutely delicious!!!! Chicken falls right off the bone, and the juices are amazing "as is" over the chicken and mashed potatoes, or as a thickened gravy.  I have tried the rub on a pork roast, cooked in a CP as well, and it is delicious that way as well.  I have also used chicken pieces vs. whole chicken - equally as good!  I have even reduced the salt to 2tsp.  You can even by-pass the refirgeration part - I've used both, and the chicken is equally as good.  If chicken wasn't so expensive here in Canada ($10 for a large chicken) I would be making this every week!  We love, love, love this recipe!!!! Thank you so much for a wonderful family recipe.  Steph in Ontario

This is probably the third or fourth time I've used this recipe in one way or another and the bird came out perfect yet again. I have not actually done the overnight marinate with the spices (although the spices are great!) but every time I've made it, it gets better and better. In my crock pot, I have to cook it for 4-6 hours on high. This time I used the spices exactly but also added one quartered lemon inside the chicken along with about 3-4 ounces of amber beer in the bottom. I have not eaten all of the chicken (just a wing!) because the rest of the meal isn't finished yet but it's wonderful. I do believe that adding a bit of liquid in the bottom really helps with the cooking, at least in my crock pot. I believe I will be using the bones and broth plus extra veggies to make a stock that I will freeze for later.

I FINALLY got around to using this intriguing recipe and it will become a mainstay for sure!  Due to time constraints, I ended up using one of those oven bags, placing the 4 1/2 lb. bird...with no timer!...into it after applying the rub.  Bag directions suggested cooking time of a little more than 1 1/4  hours but a phone call sort of distracted my clock watching and it was more like 1 hr. 40 minutes in the oven.  Not to worry... chicken was perfect.  I immediatedly  picked the bird clean, licking my fingers as I went along (ssshhh!)... the flavor is just outstanding!  I used the meat for enchiladas. Talk about delicious!  My advice is to grab a couple good -sized roasting chickens when they're on sale and use this recipe to prepare them...Way better than a deli rotisserie chicken, bigger, MUCH CHEAPER, and wonderfully flavorful... GB

I have made this twice now and it is WONDERFUL!  The meat is fall off the bone tender, juicy and so flavorful!  Instead of putting onion in the bottom of the crock, I used an aluminum foil packet filled with cubed potatoes seasoned with salt, pepper and butter.  Oh my gosh, the potatoes were soooo good.  I used the leftover chicken breast to make Recipe #105202 the next day.  Yum!!!  *Update* - I've discovered if you add the bones and skin back into the liquid that was left in your crock pot, add 5-6 cups of water and whatever vegetables you have on hand (carrots, celery, onion) and cook overnight (12 hours) on LOW, it will make a WONDERFUL stock.  Filter the bones and veggies out, and store the stock in containers in the fridge.  After a few hours the fat will solidify on the top and can be removed.  The stock can then be frozen until needed.

reviews.review_text: Five Stars Kathy ! DH "not-so-fussed-on-chicken" actually liked it more than a lot of chicken recipes I have made in my efforts to convert him, so this makes it a keeper and a 5 star recipe in my book any day.  I'm glad that you mentioned that no liquid needs adding because I was a bit worried about that..  and yes it produced far more liquid that I ever thought so the bird wasn't dry at all. No pop up timers here, I cooked mine for 6 hours and it almost fell apart as I lifted it out of the crockpot. DH and I ate our portions with the meal and later nibbled the bigger leftovers between us, and I popped the bones and smaller scraps of meat into the crockpot later that night and made Recipe #55282 for chicken stock that turned out brilliantly. Thanks for a wonderful easy chicken recipe that DH less grudgingly approves of ...and that's saying something! LOL.

reviews.review_text: Great recipe for fall off the bone chicken! Skin doesn't crisp up, so spices wasted on exterior of chicken if you don't enjoy eating rubbery skin. Put rub on bottom of bird to ensure flavors absorbed by juices formed while cooking, but I put the majority of spice rub under chicken skin on the top part of the bird, so skin can be removed after cooking & allows meat to have tons of flavor. Used only small amt. of white pepper, omitted others & added little extra thyme (as well as using only 2 tsp. kosher salt as suggested by others). Put cut lemon in cavity along with carrots & celery on top of chopped onions underneath the bird. Took only 4 hours on high to cook 5lb chicken (in a 6 qt crockpot). Important to watch for timer to pop up to insure white meat is juicy & not over cooked. Everyone in the family liked this one....even my picky kids!

reviews.review_text: I thought the recipe was just OK. The chicken meat fell off of the bones, but the meat was also very dry and overcooked. Might be a very good recipe if a person wanted an easy way to prepare chicken for chicken salid or something with a gravy though.  06/26/09 - I have since learned that my crock pot runs REALLY hot.  I tried making this recipe again, and it only takes 2.5 hours on high.  Chicken was moist this time :-).  I pulled off the left over chicken and mixed it with the following 3 round T. chili powder, 1 chicken bullion cube, 2 T. vinegar (combo of balsamic and rice vinegars), and enough boiling water to make a sauce.  Tossed the chicken and sauce together.  Served on a bed of cilantro lime rice and black beans (1 can BB, salt, and heavy amount of garlic powder).  Had sides:  cucumber, bell pepper, tomatoes.  Yum!

items.label: Soft Snickerdoodle Cookies
items.name: Soft Snickerdoodle Cookies
items.description: These snickerdoodle cookies are so delicious, and they have the best texture. They are so fast to put together too! I actually got it from an old recipe that my Great Grandma had clipped out of a newspaper. Grandma always knows best!
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix softened butter, 1 1/2 cups sugar, 1tps of vanilla extract and eggs thoroughly in a large bowl.
Combine flour, cream of tartar, baking soda and salt in a separate bowl.
Blend dry ingredients into butter mixture.
Chill dough, and chill an ungreased cookie sheet for about 10-15 minutes in the fridge.
Meanwhile, mix 3 tablespoons sugar, and 3 teaspoons cinnamon in a small bowl.
Scoop 1 inch globs of dough into the sugar/ cinnamon mixture.
Coat by gently rolling balls of dough in the sugar mixture.
Place on chilled ungreased cookie sheet, and bake 10 minutes.
Remove from pan immediately.

reviews.review_text: This recipe shows 24 for the servings amount, but no where does it say that a serving is two cookies. It makes about 48 cookies when using the default ingredient amounts, and making one inch round balls.<br/><br/>After refrigerating the mixed dough I divide the dough into 4 even size pieces. I scoop up very rounded teaspoons full  (about one and a half teaspoons) of the dough which then comes pretty close to making the one inch size balls that the recipe recommends. Each quarter section of dough should yield 12 balls. Adjust your scoop size as you go along if necessary. I place these balls on dinner plates, 24 per plate and re-refrigerate for 15 minutes. I do not refrigerate the cookie trays. I then bake 1 plate at a time using two cookie trays 11.5"  x 15.5" (12 cookies per tray). Half way through the baking (at 5 minutes) I switch the trays to the opposite rack in the oven and turn them around for even baking.

Delicious, but it makes more like 5-6 dozen, not 24 cookies.  I used a standard 1/2 oz. stainless steel disher (Pampered Chef small scoop) which produced exactly 5 & 1/2 dozen cookies.  I also substituted baking powder for the cream of tartar as suggested by another member.  The cookies turned out perfect.  Because I used a baking stone instead of a cookie sheet, I could not chill the stone between batches (that would take forever).  I used parchment paper on a chilled cutting board to portion the batches out.  I allowed the stone to cool for 2-3 minutes between batches while the previous batch of cookies cooled on their parchment sheet on the counter before I removed them to a cooling rack.  I then transferred the parchment sheet with the new batch to the hot stone just moments before putting it in the oven.  This kept the dough cool until the moment it went into the oven.  It worked like a charm.

I read lots of the reviews and they do not do justice to how AWSOME these cookies are! SO easy my 3 and 5 yr old kids did it by them selves (with supervision). Since I'm in South America I had to alter it just a bit...BUTTER comes in 200g sticks here so I just used a whole one and we can't get cream of tarter,& baking soda is hard to come by so I added the two measurements together and put 3 TSP BAKING POWDER. And put the oven on the 160-180 C degree setting for the same time as the recipe said...along with the other review's tips I also put in the vanilla and melted the butter and stirred it in after it was coolled, as well as substituted 1 of the teaspoons of cinnamon that you roll them in, for ginger powder...They are THE BEST COOKIES EVER! I can't hardly stop eating them!.......so....here is an IMPORTANT TIME AND FIGURE SAVER TIP: the recipe can be doubled, refrigerate until firm, shape into 2, 2" diameter rolls, wrap in plastic wrap and freeze! when your ready for cookies, slice 1/2" thick slices, press into coating, place on cookie sheet and put in a COLD oven and turn it to the regular temp. for 20 min....my dough lasted perfectly a month in the freezer until it was gone.  This way you only eat as many as you cook and you don't have to make the dough all the time.

These cookies were a hit! I didn't have all-purpose flour all I had was whole wheat flour but for every cup of all purpose flour I just used 3/4 of whole wheat flour. I also didn't have enough sugar to mix with the cinnamon for the coating so I had to use confectioners sugar. When I tried the dough it did not taste good (probably because of the flour I used) and it was extremely sticky (it was the first time I made snicker doodle cookies) and I was very wary but after almost tripling the amount of sugar I was supposed to mix with the cinnamon (since powdered sugar is really dense and not as sweet) I decided to just put in the first batch and if they sucked it would have been my own fault. I put the first batch in the oven just to see if I should even put in the effort to continue onwards. When I took them out they were darker then the pictures (I used brown sugar instead of white and the flour was a light brown color also) but they were exceptional. My grandma at 90 who despises sweets, tried to talk me into giving her more cookies. My little cousins who were there were in love along with everyone else who tried the cookies. Even with my substitutions I had to make they turned out amazing. Hopefully next time I have all the correct ingredients they will turn out more splendid.

reviews.review_text: I must've read 300 or so of the reviews about these cookies and I have to agree with most of them. These things iz good!! It is a simple drop dough that comes together really fast, and bakes off just as easily. I made a double batch of the dough right before I went to bed, and portioned out a couple dozen balls with a #40 (3/4 oz.) Portion scoop. The next morning, I preheated the oven while showering. I was able to bake off 2 dozen cookies and get them cool enough for my wife to take to work, and still had time to sit down and drink a full cup of coffee. Total morning time invested? An hour!! I didn't run across any of the problems I read about in the reviews, though I did change the creaming method just a bit. First, I took the butter and clarified it on the stovetop till I had a nice brown butter. It makes the cookies even better, I think! Anyway, I creamed the cooled down butter with the sugar, salt, and 1 Tbsp of bourbon vanilla extract per batch. Using a hand mixer, I creamed the mixture on high speed for 1 minute. Using COLD eggs, I mixed them in one at a time on low speeds till just incorporated. I did it this way because I wanted to limit the amount of air that got mixed in during the creaming process, and using cold eggs sets the butter back up faster, which stops the emulsification of egg yolk and fat. This is key if you want those cookies that you had when you were a kid! At this point, I took the dry ingredients and sifted them into the creamed mixture all at once. I folded it all together with a wooden spoon till it just comes together. I only use this method with these cookies and a shortbread recipe my grandmother gave me. I used whole wheat pastry flour which weighs 4 1/2 oz. per cup. A.P. flour weighs a little more and bread flour a little more again. Sugar weighs 8 oz. per cup, 1 pound per pint. I did use the baking soda, though!! But rather than go buy creme of tartar for this and maybe an Italian merengue or two, I used what I had. Apple cider vinegar! It took me a couple times making them to get it right. It seems to work at 1 Tbsp per batch. For those who like a bit fluffier, chewy cookie, you can add 2 tsp cornstarch. This helps prevent some of the collapse when they cool and helps the outside with the crispness! Using a 3/4 oz. portion scoop, I got 51 cookies out of a double batch. I don't press them down, I just roll em and place on a parchment paper lined sheet pan. Bake for 11 minutes and check. The edges should start to brown slightly. If they aren't yet, another minute always finishes them off for me. I store the doughballs in the freezer for up to a month. After that the baking soda can start degrading. On a whim, I sprinkled the sugar mixture in the bottom of a small pyrex baking dish. I took the dough and pressed a cookie "shell" in the bottom of it and halfway up the side. Cover and place in the fridge to chill. I made a filling out of apples, a little fresh oj, and some of its zest, some brown sugar, cinnamon, ginger, and cardamom, and some sultana raisins lightly pickled in champagne vinegar and honey. I sauteed this for about 8 minutes or so, until I could add some roux and a bit of cornstarch slurry, and it was really, really thick. As it bakes it will release more moisture, which will thin it out somewhat. I put the COLD filling in the pyrex and put one cookie ball for every serving in the dish on top. I sprinkle liberally with sugar mixture and put in a 350ºF. oven, on the middle shelf. I set a timer for 15 minutes and checked it. I moved it to the top shelf because the bottom cookie was cooking a bit faster than the top. It was done at the 20 minute mark. Snickerdoodle apple cobbler. Yep.

attributes.source_text: get them cool enough for my wife to take to work

reviews.review_text:
These cookies are just as good as the review!!! The first time I made them, they did not turn out great from my own errors. I didn't have cream of tartar so I substituted by using lemon, I also made the cookie dough balls larger...either way, they didn't cook through well and were dry and the dough tasted bland. The second time I added a tablespoon of vanilla and instead of using 1 and 1/2 cups regular sugar, I used 1 cup and a 1/2 cup of brown sugar - I also replaced the regular sugar with brown sugar added with the cinnamon. Again, I didn't have cream of tartar...or lemon, or baking powder, or white wine vinegar (all of the things the
web says can be substituted for cream of tartar), so I didn't add any baking soda (since the cream of tartar is intended to react with the baking soda and make the texture of the cookie). I also rolled the entire cookie dough ball in the sugar mixture to cover all sides...and wow, they were SO good!! The center of the cookies were soft and doughy, and the edges got a little crisp. Perfect!

attributes.source_text: The center of the cookies were soft

reviews.review_text:
Thanks for this recipe! I've tried several snickerdoodle recipes now in search of the perfect cookie, and this worked great for me! I've always liked the flavor of snickerdoodles, but in general prefer soft, chewy cookies. These fit the bill and are the best snickerdoodle's I've ever eaten.

The only modification I made was that I lightly patted the balls down with my hand before baking (I didn't press them too flat) so they weren't too rounded. They still came out soft and delicious, but with a more "traditional" cookie shape. I also used baking powder as I didn't have cream of tartar, however, baking powder can be made by mixing one part baking soda to two parts cream of tartar, so with the amounts called for in this recipe it really amounts to the same thing anyhow.

These were so good, I registered just to leave feedback. I'll be tossing my other recipes and ending my search here!

attributes.source_text: prefer soft, chewy cookies
prefer soft, chewy cookies
They still came out soft and delicious

reviews.review_text: Will rate it with 5 stars just because it is so easy. I did use parchment paper on my cookie sheets and they still baked perfectly. For those wanting get to use margarine email I stead of butter, I always keep hard brick style margarine in my fridge just for this purpose. Soft, spreadable margarine email contains too much water. Was almost tempted to double the recipe when I saw it says 24 cookies. In my house that's like one round of snacks haha. But I stuck with just a single batch and I made about 72 cookies. They are crispy on outside and nice and soft on the inside. We love them. I will definitely make these again but am going to try adding vanilla and would love to incorporate cream cheese to see if I can add a bit of a different flavour and texture. Not taking anything away from original recipe because it's great. I just like to play around with recipes. ??

reviews.review_text: The extent of my baking career has consisted of scooping pre-made cookie dough onto a cookie sheet and baking for an instructed amount of time. So I was a little nervous about branching out to make my favorite cookie from scratch because I ironically have very high standards for Snickerdoodles (and also I put unnecessary pressure on myself by telling my family I'd bake them Snickerdoodles for Thanksgiving). Anyway, my family ended up eating every single cookie (I brought about 20 cookies but the recipe made about 48 and I kept the rest, doing the opposite of being thankful on such a day and hoarding the majority for myself without guilt). Everyone said they were perfectly crisp on the outside but deliciously soft on the inside and had just the right amount of cinnamon (of which I agreed with all of them). I've been told it is now a requirement for me to bring Snickerdoodles to any family get together.

reviews.review_text: The recipe was really easy to follow and the cookies wonderfully soft and fluffy. I had to keep it in the fridge longer - at least half an hour, for the dough to be easy to roll and cover. My cookies turned out looking completely different from the first few photos posted, which kindly threw me off a little, because my cookies spread and flattened out like sugar cookies [I had only browsed through the first few photos], so I placed them a little too closely to one another. I think that result has, to some degree, to do with my not adding cream of tartar, since I had none [I think it is the cream of tartar that adds a degree of er..'solidness']. One batch I made I baked for too long, which turned out in kindly dry and a sort of cakey consistency which I didn't like too much. So I would always go for undercooked instead of overcooked.

reviews.review_text:
AMAZING recipe. What I chose to do was to put the sticks of butter (2) in the microwave for about 20 seconds to soften them, this helped them mix easier. I mixed the ingredients using a KitchenAid mixer with the whisk attachment. I used a tablespoon measuring scoop to portion my cookies. I scooped them, rolled them in a ball, and them rolled them in a plate that had the cinnamon sugar mixture and then flattened them a bit, very delicately, so they would be better shaped. Baked for exactly ten minutes and perfection! Using the tablespoon measuring scoop yielded about 45-50 cookies. All delicious!
If you want very light tasting cookies and have the KitchenAid mixer, mix the butter, eggs, and sugar for about five minutes. Doing this adds air and makes it almost whipped. It tastes delicious and moist!

reviews.review_text: I haven't found a recipe like this for years. Chilling the dough and trays is essential. The key to this recipe is to cream the room temp butter (do not melt) and sugar together for five or so minutes before adding the room temp egg and vanilla. Only mix until well combined after adding the flour. It makes a thick sticky smooth dough. Dropping a slightly rounded teaspoon at a time into the sugar mix makes a 2" cookie, and several dozen more than stated. About 6 dozen. Do not roll them by hand into a ball, just drop, coat and bake. Remove from cookie sheets promptly to stop cooking. This gives the delicate crisp edges and chewy center we all crave. Replace the dough in the fridge between baking. I doubled the recipe and added a tsp of ground cloves to the sugar mixture.

reviews.review_text: Absolutely 5 stars!!!!! I was craving Snickerdoodles so bad last night and I'm so so glad this was the first recipe that came up in my google search. We followed the recipe to a T and they were so perfect! We cooked for 10 minutes and although they didnt look quite ready I took them out and off the tray anyway cause I LOVE cookies that are super chewy and not to crisp. These were SO great, flavor was amazing and even today the texture was chewy inside and crisp outside. I wish I could give this 10 stars!! Unfortunately while we were watching a movie and enjoying our cookies the dog jumped out and at a whole tray worth of cookies so we will be making more tomorrow :) Also! We ended up with 33 cookies and the first 24 were all pretty close together in the sheet, so make sure it is a small one inch ball and expect extra cookies. Perfection!!

reviews.review_text: Hello :) So, I attempted to make these, followed the recipe step-by-step, even used my brand-new KitchenAid mixer I received for Christmas... and the dough came out very sticky and bread-like....?! My dough didn't look like a cookie dough at all, and it was very strange. I couldn't scoop it after chilling it in the fridge, it would just be smashed all over my hand. That being said, I grabbed a small scoop with a spoon and let it bake for about 12 minutes - they came out delicious! But were very puffy and cake-like. To not waste the dough, my solution was to put it in a small casserole dish and bake the rest. It puffed up like banana bread!!? The strangest thing ever.. considering I read all the great comments about it. Still a tasty recipe, however I pretty much made snickerdoodle bread. Anyone have a solution?

It is a very soft, chewy cookie. Though, as many said, it does expand quite a bit. I would recommend whipping the butter and sugar together. Then sifting the dry ingredients to reduce the size of the expansion. The cookies provides a nice crunch and has a very nice soft center. Though it may vary how long it takes in the oven, due to how different ovens work. So, just keep an eye on them making sure they don't burn and are fully done. The recipe is easy to follow and simple to make. In addition to taking little ingredients. Though cream of tartar can be expensive. I didn't chill the baking sheet and cookies, and they turned out fine as well. These are great cookies and very easy to make. So, I would recommend them to a baker who is starting up. A very well done recipe.

reviews.review_text: I made these last night with my daughter. The dough was easy to handle and the recipe was simple enough. I added 1 tsp of vanilla extract to the batter which I think amped up the flavor. I will say I DONT think the full 2 3/4 cups of flour is necessary. I used the full amount and the cookies tasted flour-y and were soft but inherently dry. I ended up adding about another 1/4 cup of butter to the batter to combat the dryness from the flour. I would recommend using premixed Cinnamon/Sugar (which is in the herbs and spices isle at the grocery) for convenience. These cookies are FLUFFY soft....and stayed that way all through out the night. They remind me of the Snickerdoodles from the Classic American Cookie store in the mall. I prefer my cookies to have a bit of crunch on the outside, but for someone who likes cookies that are soft. I recommend.

My daughter wanted me to make cookies for her class. Her favorite are snickerdoodles but I hate making them because I hate my recipe. They always turn out crunchy. So, I went searching for a new one and out of the three I narrowed it down to, I am SO GLAD I picked this one. Honestly, the only reason being: Juju Bee said this was something her Great Grandma used. I love nostalgic recipes!! I made about 2 1/2 doz (I added about 2 tsp of vanilla). The cookies were amazing! They were just the right amount of soft and they stayed soft overnight. Completely delicious! I can't say enough good about them! Out of the 2 1/2 doz, 13 went to school. items.label: Panera's Cream Cheese Potato Soup
items.name: Panera's Cream Cheese Potato Soup
items.description: This is my favorite recipe for potato soup.  It's a copycat of the one they use to serve at the St. Louis Bread Company (Panera).  The recipe originally called for shredding your potatoes, but I never could get them to cook that way. I know they should cook faster, but I never could get it to work.
instructions: Combine broth, potatoes, and spices.
Boil on medium heat until potatoes are tender.
Smash a few of the potatoes to release their starch for thickening.
Reduce to low heat.
Add cream cheese.
Heat, stirring frequently, until cheese melts.

reviews.review_text: I am rating this soup with out stars, as when I first started making the soup, I found it to be bland, and saw that the soup really needed more potatoes. To make the soup more flavorable, I added a 1/4 teaspoon of garlic powder, and added it when cooking the broth, potatoes, onion, and spices. While I did add 5 cups of potatoes, I still felt the soup needed more potatoes, so I added a cup or two of southern hash brown potatoes (they were frozen, so I cooked them slightly in my microwave; just enough to unthaw them). I also added a can of whole kernel corn, (drained) and about 2/3's of a (4.5 ounce) package of Oscar Mayer Bacon Bits. The added ingredients made this soup taste really good!! By the way I should also mention... I did mash about 2 cups of the potatoes, (with a hand held potato masher) but next time I decide to make this soup, I'm going to add even more potatoes, about 8 cups, (that's 2 cups of taters per each cup of the broth) and I plan on mashing about 3 cups the potatoes. One more thing... the first day I made this soup, I had noticed, not all of the cream cheese melted into the soup, but on the 2nd day I reheated the soup, it finally did. I would suggest to others, to make this soup one day earlier prior to serving, so the cream cheese has a change to melt more evenly into the soup, and to possibly undercook the cubed potatoes just a bit, so when reheating the soup the next day, the potatoes will be cooked through, but not overcooked from making the soup the day before. Shawn, after I had made some changes to the recipe, and reheating the soup a day later, I found this soup to be more enjoyable to my taste buds. With the changes made, I would give this recipe 5 stars, but if made with out the changes and as written, I'm sorry but I would only give this recipe possibly 1 or 2 stars. Shawn, I do look forward to making this soup again, and I'd like to also thank you for the recipe.

We found this recipe to be really tasty! And, more importantly to me, it's really quick, easy, and not really that bad for us! Using what I had on hand, I ended up making this with: 4 tsp chicken base 4 cups of water, a tablespoon of bacon drippings, 1/4 tsp paprika, 1/4 tsp cayenne, no salt (the chicken base is salty enough), a few grinds of black pepper, a small handful of crumbled bacon, and a couple dashes of dill. It only took two medium-large potatoes to make the 4 cups required, and it was quick as a wink to put together with my magic chopper thingamajig. It took about 15 minutes to get the potatoes fork-tender; after which, I mushed some, turned the heat down, removed the pot from the heat so it'd stop boiling and not curdle my cream cheese, and then added in the Onion and Chives cream cheese. It took a bit for it to get worked it, but it finally melted down into a smooth pot of deliciousness. I topped it with a smattering of cheddar cheese and a bit more bacon.

I'm pretty sure my husband was thisclose to licking to bowl. Great recipe and seems like it'll adapt well to any changes your family might enjoy! This has to be the easiest, and tastiest, potato soup recipe I've ran across on here. This will come into regular rotation! Next time, I will likely add in another potato to fill it out some more and stretch that dollar even farther.

reviews.review_text: This is the first time I've reviewed a recipe, but thought I just had to. My many thanks to Shawn H for this recipe.. I live in the deep South and It never gets that cold here, but last couple of days it dipped into the 20s and we wanted a great comfort winter food. I had cream cheese left from the Christmas baking, so this recipe fit the bill. Although I did make a few alterations, all the credit goes to this cook. Another reviewer had said she used baked potatoes instead of boiled and sounded easier to me. I cooled the potatoes and added them last because they were cooked thoroughly already. Sauteed the onion, spices, then added broth. I also softened the cream cheese in the microwave, making it super easy to dissolve. The only thing I added was cheese and bacon (put crumbles in in last couple of minutes). I realized alot of people frown on Velveeta (I know, not really cheese) but I used a mixture of that and light shredded cheddar, adding with cream cheese. I did thicken with a bit of flour and evaporated milk, because we like a really thick soup. The flavor is just so good. Texture is great. This is definitely a keeper. Will be my go to soup from now on. Thanks so much, Shawn, for posting this!

attributes.source_text: we wanted a great comfort winter food

reviews.review_text: This is wonderful soup, probably the best I've made.  Subbed dried onion, about a tablespoon and a half since I was out of fresh.  Threw in some proscuitto (sp?) because I had some, but I think it would be equally good without.  I also had to use bouillon cubes and water since I'm out of broth...  shopping day is coming up.  Even with all the subs, this is fantastic...  Will double the recipe next time to have leftovers! Update:  We make this all the time now, and every time I have company they request the recipe.  Changes I've made: I add enough potatoes to just be covered by broth, so I don't measure.  I don't peel the potatoes, just cut into pieces.  I use Johnny's seasoning salt, which is wonderful.  After stirring in the cream cheese, I blend this with an immersion blender to break up the potatoes and mix the cream cheese all the way thru, then bring it back up to serving temp.  Garnish with shredded cheese, sour cream, bacon bits, and green onion as needed.  It's great with and without garnish.

attributes.source_text: every time I have company they request the recipe

reviews.review_text: Very good  (but I also added sharp cheddar cheese).   And like others I had problems with the cream cheese melting all the way (and yes it was room temp)  I think next time I will follow what others have done and put it in the mircrowave to speed up that process.   Also,  I cooked it in the crockpot (I love soups in the crockpot)   I added the cheese probably 30 min -40 min before I was done,  I had it set to high for 4 hrs   when 1 hr or so was left I put quite a bit of potatoes in my blender and mashed them up that way.   Oh I also added garlic, more potatoes, I used 4 cups of stock, 1 can of broth (due to more potatoes), and a little bit of cayanne pepper.  I also added a little extra of the other seasonings due to me adding broth and potatoes.  (that was the reason behind why I added cheddar cheese...I didn't have any more cream cheese...and I wanted cheeezzzy soup)  Well next time I will do that again and probably still add a little more cheese then I used.  So with all my additions...5 stars!!   and I served the soup with cheedar cheese and cut up bacon on top!

attributes.source_text: I wanted cheeezzzy soup

reviews.review_text: I give it 5 stars for how easy it is, how tasty it is, and how adaptable it is.  I've made it two times: both in  a crock pot on high with 6 cups cubed potatoes rather than 4 c...because the crock pot doesn't loose it's liquid and can handle the extra potatoes.  Dump everything but the cream cheese in for about 4 hrs on high as others suggested.  Once potatoes are done, I use a potato masher and chop the potatoes...but I leave bite-size chunks because I like it that way.  Set crock pot to low and add the cream cheese and stir it up until it's melted.  Then, before serving, dump browned crumbled bacon in it.  Brown a whole package, use what you want (like all of it).  Add a drained can of corn if you want, but DEFINITELY add crumbled bacon.  If you add the crumbled bacon too early, while cooking the potatoes, it'll get soggy.  I learned the hard way. So wait until you're about ready to serve.  (I was short on cream cheese, had just 2/3 of a block, but it still was good.)

SLAM DUNK ~ WELL DONE SHAWN!!! Potato soup is one of my all time favorites, and I have an award winning "family" recipe (restauranteers). I ran across yours, was intrigued by the use of cream cheese, and gave it a go. This was fabulous, my kids loved it, and my neighbors are wanting more! The only thing I added/changed was sauteed the onions in butter, along with 1/4 cup shredded carrots, 1/4 cup finely diced celery, and 3-4 cloves of pressed garlic (added during the last minute or so), until all veggies were tender; used an extra can of broth; when potaotes were cooked I removed at least 1/2 of the potatoes (for a chunkier soup), and added the cream cheese before taking a potato masher to the pot straight over the heat. I then returned the cooked potatoes to the pot, and it was done. The 1st time I made this I used both red & white small potatoes (semi-peeled) which needed to be used, and made up the rest with our home grown Idaho russets. EXCELLENT recipe, and definitely will never make potato soup any other way! Thank you ;)

reviews.review_text: My family loves this soup.  There are a few things I done different that made it taste richer.  Instead of cooking the potatoes on the stove top, (I think this maks them watery) I baked them in the microwave with the skin on.  I let them cool down and then peel them and cut them into chuncks. They stay together much better, and they have a much better taste to them. If you are using red potatoes, which I prefer, leave the skin on them.  I also saute my onions and garlic in a pan with butter really slow so they don't brown.  I put the chicken broth in the pot first, then the onions and butter.  I let the cream cheese get to room temp, and then use my wire strainer to mash the cream cheese through it with the back of a spoon.  It dissolves much easier.  After the soup comes to a slow boil, I add the potatoes and turn in down on simmer for a while.  When I serve it, I put crispy bacon cumbles on top along with cheddar cheese and green onions.  I also think it is good with a dollop of sour cream.  Bake a pan of corn bread, and you have the most delicious meal you could ever eat.  I use one cream cheese to one carton of chicken broth.  I have to double or triple this recipe......Yuuuuuum

made it taste richer

reviews.review_text:
While this may not be 'the' Panera bread recipe, we very much enjoy the simplicity of this adaptation. A good soup when cooked with ingredients as called for, but so easy to amend to your liking. Carrots, celery, fat or low fat cream cheese, real or imitation bacon, a little more potato, reduced sodium broth, there are so many options. I've made this soup many times, with many variations, and have yet to come up with a version I did not like.

Once the potatoes are tender, I scoop about two cups of them out of the soup and set aside. Since the cream cheese is softened at this point, a hand-held ricer comes in very handy for squeezing the cheese uniformly into the soup. Then squeeze the potatoes through the ricer, which not only thickens the soup, but helps to clean the cheese out of the ricer.

You might guess what is on the stove as I type this. :-)

attributes.source_text: Once the potatoes are tender
which not only thickens the soup

reviews.review_text: I am not going to rate this recipe yet because I have not made it but I do feel the need to comment on it.  After working for Panera (St. Louis Bread Co) for 14 years I have seen many soups and sandwiches come and go.  This particular soup seems like it was the original Potato Cream Cheese Soup not the one we have now.  Potato Cream Cheese Soup was a soup that they used from a company called True Soups and is much different from the one we have now.  The one we have now is Panera's recipe and is called Baked Potato Soup.  While many love this soup and do not remember the original I am am fan of the one from True Soups.  After I make this one I will update and let you know which one this is.  There was a post from Jeff B that said that he worked for Panera years ago remembers the orginal and I am sure he is right about the ingredients.

Great soup to warm you in winter!  Basic recipe is solid, and per the reviews, can easily be modified with additional ingredients and alternative methods to suit your taste and style.  I did not peel my potato (as this is simply how we prefer them).  I added 2 cloves of minced garlic and modified the prep by first sauteing the onion and garlic (in a little butter and olive oil) in a large wok until translucent and then adding the diced potato and allowing to saute/steam for another 5-10 minutes or so (not really enough to cook the potato, but allowed the onion, garlic and butter to blend with the potato).  I then added all to the heated, spiced broth and finished as directed (allowing the soup to simmer for 45-50 minutes).  I served with optional toppings of cheddar cheese, green onion and crumbled bacon.  Everyone loved this creamy, hearty soup!  I'll definitely make it again and again!  Thank you for sharing, Shawn H!

attributes.source_text: Great soup to warm you in winter

reviews.review_text: I created an account just to give a rating on this recipe. This soup was amazing. So, so good. Hubby went to Panera to get some hot potato soup one day after work and they had sold out of it for the day - he was heartbroken. Just had his heart set on that soup, but I didn't know how to make any for him. Looked up this recipe and figured I'd give it a try, never having tried Panera's soup myself. So glad I came across your recipe! This soup was so easy to make and it all came together beautifully right at the end. My husband and I fought over who would get the last bowl, just delicious. I listened to some of the other reviewers and baked the potatoes in the oven, then added crumbled bacon bits, a little minced celery and a few red pepper flakes. Absolutely delicious! Didn't take long to make me wish I'd doubled the recipe, will definitely do that next time. This was my first time making potato soup and it was amazing. Thanks for sharing such a great recipe!

reviews.review_text: Made this soup the other night and love it. However, I melted down the cream cheese in a saucepan before whisking it into the soup to see if it would help prevent curdling, and it still curdled. Oh well. A couple things I did different though was to had dill weed and chicken after reading Jeff Bloomer's review from about 4 years ago. He said he worked for St Louis Bread Co when they served this soup and one key ingredient to their taste was dill weed. And they'd also add tiny pieces of chicken to make it a little richer. I used canned chicken, and loved it in the soup. I also added some Watkins Garlic Pepper Seasoning to the soup, as we like a little more flavoring. It turned out great with the exception of a little bit of curdling, which you can see in my photo that I added recently. (Green square bowl with bread on the edge of it).

delicious
made this tonight after fixing picky childrens boring supper, very quick to make, followed the directions to the letter, even bought the seasoning salt for the occasion.  The only thing that went wrong is we were having a snowstorm here and so the liquid evaporated too quickly and I should have added more chicken broth, but I didn't cuz I was trying to stick to the recipe,  so the end result was a bit thick, but still totally delicious.  DH loved it and picky eater #1 tried a spoonful and said I was allowed to make it again and he would eat it....hahaha now that is good.

Thanks so much for sharing!!!!

update 10/22/09  I made this again, and this time started with more chicken stock to avoid the evaporation problem I had the first time.  This time I used neufchatel instead of cream cheese to cut fat, it was still delicious everyone loved it.

reviews.review_text: This is one GREAT recipe. Thanks for posting it. It is so simple and easy and quick to make. I memorized how to make it after just one time. I do use 5 cups of potatoes though and cut them small to cook faster. I do add extra onions and cut the cayenne to 1/8 tsp cause it was a tad hot. I tried it with regular cream cheese and another time with fat free cream cheese and obviously I can tell you which one was better tasting. Also, I cooked up a ham steak and chopped it tiny to sprinkle on top but be careful cause the meat is a tad salty. I found I didnt need any sprinkled cheddar or bacon. Just toast up some french bread to sop it up with. So creamy and delicious. I would never have thought to use cream cheese but its great. I will def have this as a stand by soup recipe and will share it with friends and family. Thanks!!!!

This was a good recipe for an easy soup!  I did jazz it up a tad for my taste (extra spices, bacon, and cheddar).  I used about 8 palm sized potatoes and it was just perfect for the broth.  I used a whole yellow onion b/c I love onion.  It's a very easy one to throw together and next time I think I'll use the advice of someone else and use a bag of the frozen cubed hashbrowns!  That will make this a seriously quick delicious dinner!  The cream cheese melted in just fine and while it cooked on the stove top I stuck bacon in the oven and they both ended up being done at the same time!  Oh, and my potatoe masher broke so I used the spoon that you can use to lift things out of oil that has the big mesh grate (not fine but a really big one) and mashed it with that and the back of a wooden spoon lol  Thanks for the easy recipe!

attributes.source_text: seriously quick delicious dinner

reviews.review_text: well I have to say, this didnt turn out very good for me.  I went exactly by the recipe.  The only thing is I didnt have the blocks of cream cheese but I had the containers, so thats what I used.  I wouldnt think using the containers of cream cheese versus the blocks would make that big of a difference, but I really thought this would be delicious from all the reviews.  I will make it next time with the block of cream cheese just to make sure that wasnt what ruined the recipe.  But I have to say this was very bland and boring.  I had to add lots more seasonings, and pile on top extra cheese, green onion, and bacon to try to make it taste better and have some flavor.  Ive had this at panera, and this recipe didnt do it justice.  I will make again sometime to see if it comes out better...but as for now, I give it 3 stars.

This is just about the easiest thing on the planet to make, and it's sooooo good. I was making it for a friend who had just had sugery and was having trouble swallowing. I left out the pepper because I was afraid that would irritate his throat, but it was amazing. He loved it, and so did I. I used lowfat cream cheese. Upadte: I made this again and doubled the recipe using 8 oz lowfat cream cheese and 8 oz fat free. Then I added about 1/2 lb of chopped turkey kielbasa... heavenly...
UPDATE: Lately I have been making this using homemade vegetable stock instead of store-bought chicken broth. I add chicken bouillon to the broth, and then since the bouillon already has salt in it, I don't add the seasoned salt, but I give a good couple shakes of garlic powder, onion powder and paprika.

attributes.source_text: He loved it

reviews.review_text: This was fabulous.  Make it today, and since I have 3 youngs kids and dont have time to cook it at crazy hour (5 pm) I made it ahead and then left it on warm all day in the crock pot.  It was great.  Also pureed with an immersion blend.  That was very easy.  I cut back on the salt to 3 tsp and left the same amount of cyenne pepper.  THe pepper makes it quite hot as in spicy but still mild soemhow with the potaoes.  Wonderful flavor.  Also I didnt have quite enough broth for the liquid so used water for the remainder and worked fine.  I orginally wanted broccoli cheese soup so I added broccoli floretts.  I boiled them on the stovetop and added them along with shredded cheddar cheese to make it a broccoli cheese soup.  So very good.  Very versatile recipe.  It was delicious too before I added the broccoli or cheese.

reviews.review_text: Finally, a potato soup recipe my picky husband LOVES! That alone is worth five stars, but it deserves the highest rating because everyone in my family loved it and it was so easy. I also used more than 4 cups potatoes (around 6 cups). I did not blend any of the soup/potatoes to help thicken the soup, and I will do that next time because I thought the soup was a little thin and I prefer a very thick potato soup, but it tasted so good that was a minor issue at best. I was not expecting so much flavor out of so few ingredients, but I was pleasantly surprised by the end result. I did add crumbled bacon, shredded cheddar, and a small dollop of sour cream to each bowl. I served this with sourdough rolls and salad for a fabulous and quick weeknight dinner. Thank you SO MUCH for posting this recipe! It's a keeper for us.

items.label: My Family's Favorite Sloppy Joes (Pizza Joes)
items.name: My Family's Favorite Sloppy Joes (Pizza Joes)
items.description:
I've tried many recipes, this is the best. I once 'dec-tupled' (10x) this recipe to sell sandwiches at a craft fair at my church. People were waiting in line to buy leftovers. Freezes well, goes up to the lake or camping well and is a hit on Halloween...it's no-fail. Easy to double, triple, etc. I've been making Joes this way for over 20 years.
***03-08-09, I just reinvented this recipe tonight when I went to make it for dinner and found I didn't have an 8-oz. can of tomato sauce (shame on me).  The family was upset with me when I subbed an 8-oz. can of pizza sauce and told them to suck it up and call them 'Pizza Joes' and then served them up with shredded mozzarella cheese on the toasted buns, top and bottom.  They loved it.  I left out the BBQ sauce in this preparation and just used a 1/2 cup ketchup.  Pizza Joes are good to go!
instructions: In a large skillet, brown ground beef, celery and onion.
Drain the fat, who needs it?.
Stir in remaining ingredients, simmer covered, 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
If Joes appear too'loose', leave cover off and let moisture evaporate.
Cook until it's the consistency you like for serving on toasted buns, with french fries and cole slaw.

reviews.review_text: Doubled the recipe using ground turkey, but made a mistake in the midst of my scurry and misread the brown sugar to be 1/4 cup instead of 1 tablespoon! SO, because I'd doubled the recipe I ended up putting 1/2 cup in - and it came out pretty damn good (even though I am probably sending myself into an early grave with all the sugar)!  Didn't have cans of tomato sauce (I know, Jude, shame on me) so I used 2 cans of tomato paste instead. As other reviewers said, I toned down the celery to 2 ribs total. Made it again with 3 ribs and didn't taste a difference. Before browning the turkey I added butter and kind of caramelized the onions a bit with some minced garlic before adding the celery - then turkey. Because tomato paste is obviously more dense I didn't drain the turkey after browning in lieu of having to add water (mmm - fat!) I only use Sweet Baby Ray BBQ sauce. Period. And now I have a reason to buy it in bulk at Sam's Club. Used 3/4 an onion total (didn't want to overdo it with the onion). Everything else was the same. On subsequent go at it I added some diced mushrooms to the mix and it was even better. Thank you for an easy and fail proof recipe!

attributes.source_text: it came out pretty damn good (even though I am probably sending myself into an early grave with all the sugar)

reviews.review_text: OK, I know the last thing this recipe needs is another review, but I just can't help it.  I had some stuff on hand I needed to use up, and with company coming, figured this was a good option, especially since one of my guests was a four-year-old little girl.  I doubled everything as I had two pounds of beef, and left out the celery only because I didn't have any.  I chopped all my vegies, including a green pepper, into large dice as I like chunks of vegies in my 'Joes' and used the Catleman's original bbq sauce.  In a word, these were simply awesome!  All the adults, as well as the kid, loved them and my friend even asked me to write down what I did so he could make them at home later.  This recipe goes into my permanent collection, and I will definitely make it again, though with a few minor adjustments.  I'll use just a little bit of celery, and maybe sub out the green pepper for a fresh Sarano chili, but mostly, this recipe is perfect.  I'm sure glad you shared it with us; now I finally have a sloppy Joe recipe I can be proud of.

attributes.source_text: All the adults, as well as the kid, loved them

reviews.review_text: 4 stars as is to the sloppy joe and 2 1/2 for pizza sloppy joes.  I was leary of adding celery to both so I doubled both kinds and used 4 stalks of celery in each plus 1 large. green pepper minced. To the sloppy joes, I also used double the bbq and the same amount for ketchup (dbl batch = 1 c. bbq and 1/2c ketchup) no S&P and used apple cider vinegar- oh and i used homemade bull's eye bbq sauce.  For the pizza version I used 2 -14oz jars of pizza sauce, 2 garlic cloves minced,no vinegar and no ketchup and only 4 celery stakes.  The sloppy joes the family loved with my changes as for the pizza joes my kids liked them but I felt that they STILL lacked flavor.  I will keep looking for a pizza joe recipe but will keep the sloppy joe recipe with my few tweaks.

reviews.review_text: I would consider these prize winning sloppy joes! I made a few changes, though. I used 1 small green pepper instead of the celery, I omitted the tomato sauce and increased the ketchup and barbecue sauce to 1/2 cup each, and I used 1 1/4 teaspoon regular mustard instead of the dry mustard. I used Sweet Baby Ray's Honey Barbecue Sauce. I used this recipe to make pizza burgers. To make pizza burgers, line a baking sheet with foil. Open about 5 hamburger buns so that there are 10 halves. Place the sloppy joe mixture on each half and top with a slice of mozzarella or american cheese. Sprinkle lightly with oregano and bake in 350 degree oven about 5 minutes or until cheese melts. Thanks for sharing this incredible recipe - I'll be making it often.

What a great recipe easy to follow instructions!!  Wanted to make sloppy joes and these are awesome!!  My family loves them and they are so easy to make.  I first sauteed 1 stalk of celery a little bell pepper, 1/2 onion in olive oil and sauteed til soft and chopped til fine in food processor (have picky eaters that don't like onions) than added it back to the pan with the ground beef to brown it and followed the recipe from there. I used 1 3/4 lbs. of ground beef and upped the bbq sauce and ketchup to 3oz each (a little over 1/4 c.) but kept the other ingredients pretty much the same.   I do think this recipe will be as good as the quality of the bbq sauce that you use.  I had leftover Bill Miller sauce (from a bbq place here in Texas) and we thought that was fantastic, so make sure you use one that your family loves.  YUMMY I will make these as often as I can. They were so well received that I had to make a batch for myself.  I agree with reviewers that said this recipe ages gracefully, flavors meld and the smoky flavor from my bbq sauce subsided a bit.  Well received my many.  I think the flavorings make this a winner of a dish.

Also the night I was making this, I ended up being in a hurry.  It went together fast and I processed all the veggies in my mini-food processor.  Went together fast considering I quadrupled it.

reviews.review_text: I gave this 4 stars. I was a little worried about the BBQ sauce in these but I don't think you even taste it. I've made these sloppy joes quite a few times since my first review. My future hubby and I really liked thess all except the celery no one in my family cared for the celery in these at all. My 4 yrs old newphew and 6 yrs old niece did not like these at all also due to the celery and asked me not to add it again and I won't. The first time I made these I used Kraft hickory flavored BBQ sauce. My sloppy joe sauce didn't thicken to my likeing until I removed the lid and allowed it to cook 5 more minutes. My celery did not get all cooked done even after the extra 5 minutes. Since my first review I've made these without the celery and you wouldn't even know it flavor wise they taste just the same as they did when I made them with the celery. My 4 yrs newphew woofed it right down but the 6 yrs old niece still didn't like them. I have since tried using Jack Daniel's Hickory brown sugar BBQ sauce and these are just as good. I'm guessing any BBQ sauce would make these taste great. I've even doubled the recipe and it turns out great everytime. Overall these were very good and we will have these again with no doubt. Thanks for posting a great recipe. Christine (internetnut)

reviews.review_text: Hey Jude, I used this recipe to make your Pizza Joes, but I'm sorry I have to say I didn't care for the end results. I thought the amount of mustard added was a bit much. It was quite potent, and that was the first thing I noticed/smelled after simmering the joes and removing the lid. One other thing I wanted to mention here, since I did doubled the recipe, I found I only needed to add 1 stalk of celery, diced, and I thought that was more than enough for this recipe. I did add some diced green bell peppers, as I like peppers in my sloppy joes. Jude, I would like to make your sloppy joes, but when I do, I will reduce the amount of mustard to a 1/4 teaspoon. Jude, I'm sorry I couldn't give your recipe a good review, but I am delighted to see others have enjoyed the recipe. Perhaps I would prefer the sloppy joes over the pizza joes.

Just made a double batch of this today, and it is divine!!! I've always hated the stuff in the can, so had given up on making Sloppy Joes, UNTIL I saw this recipe, read the rave reviews and decided to give it a try. Omgosh, am I ever glad I did!! Absolutely no comparison to the canned stuff; this recipe is delicious!! Only changes I made are as follows: I chopped the onions and celery in the food processor before adding to the meat, so that they would just melt into the mixture and add their flavor without being "chunky"; then at the very end, after tasting for seasoning, I added 2 Tbs onion powder & 2 Tbs garlic powder for some depth of flavor, and added a very small pinch of crushed red pepper flakes for a hint of heat just because we enjoy it, but the recipe is fantastic exactly as written. Served on fresh buns that I buttered then toasted in the toaster oven. Note: I browned the meat very slowly over med/low heat in order to break down the meat and cook it down into a smooth consistency. As a result, as we were eating the sandwiches, I realized this would make a GREAT hot dog chili. Yumm! Love this recipe; thank you for posting! :)

reviews.review_text: As is, I didn't care much for the flavor of this recipe, but that may be due to some substitutions. I was hoping for more of a tomatoey taste, so I added an extra can of tomato soup, some garlic powder, and even added a little A-1 steak sauce to give it a richer, less barbequey taste.  Turned out pretty good, but I would give the recipe as I initially made it a 3 star rating, but it gets 4 stars with my tweaks.  Would like to try it again with the celery to see if that helps develop the flavor.  Will definitely note that it really needs time to develop the right taste...the longer it simmered, the more I liked it!

items.label: Beth's Melt in Your Mouth Barbecue Ribs (Oven)
items.name: Beth's Melt in Your Mouth Barbecue Ribs (Oven)
items.description:
I almost didn't want to share this ribs recipe because this is one of the dishes that I make that keep my sons coming back home! These can be done with baby back or regular pork ribs. I have also made split chickens this way. The ribs are tender, moist and just slide off of the bone. I know that your family will love them just as much as my family does.
I noticed that some are unable to find hickory smoked salt. You can use smoked paprika or just brush the ribs with liquid smoke before applying the rub. The smoke flavor is nice because it helps give the ribs a cooked-on-the-grill flavor.
Also, the easiest way to remove the membrane is to work a spoon, or I use the tips of my kitchen shears, into the bottom center of the membrane, work it back and forth to form a "pocket," then I slide my thumbs in and work the membrane off from the center outward to the ends.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with two layers of foil, shiny side out.
Peel off tough membrane that covers the bony side of the ribs.
Season the ribs on both sides with salt and pepper. If using, divide the Hickory liquid smoke evenly over the ribs.
In a medium bowl, combine the light brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder and ground red pepper. Apply the rub to all sides of the ribs.
Lay ribs on the prepared baking sheet, meaty side down. BONE SIDE DOWN FOR GRILLING!
Lay two layers of foil on top of ribs and roll and crimp edges tightly, edges facing up to seal.
Transfer to the oven and = bake for 2-2 1/2 hours or until meat is starting to shrink away from the ends of the bone.
Remove from oven.
Heat broiler.
Cut ribs into serving sized portions of 2 or 3 ribs.
Arrange on broiler pan, bony side up.
Brush on sauce.
Broil for 1 or 2 minutes until sauce is cooked on and bubbly.
Turn ribs over.
Repeat on other side.
Alternately, you can grill the ribs on your grill to cook on the sauce.

reviews.review_text:
Like many others, I also have joined just so I can write a review.......I can honestly say, w/my hand on a bible, I have NEVER WRITTEN ONE OF THESE REVIEWS BEFORE.  

     Anyways, my wife bought a rack of spare ribs on sale at Wegmans a little while ago.  I am a guy and love to grill, but tonight I had the girls ( 1 1/2 and 3 1/2) while my wife was at work and there was no way I was gonna pull off doing ribs on the grill while watching them. I have also, NEVER made a rack of any ribs ever in my life, so I was very excited to do this. This was a big deal to me, lol.  Anyways, I started thumbing through the internet and "The Barbecue Bible" looking for tips on how to NOT screw this up.  I came upon Beths recipe and it was the ONLY one where I flipped though a bunch of the reviews and none complained about them being dry. Most of the other recipes had excellent reviews, but every now and again there was a complaint of how dry or tough they turned out so I decided to go with this one.  

     I can't express how amazing the ribs turned out.  They were fall off the bone and moist (even though I overcooked them a smidge.  I think 2 hrs and 15-20 mins would have been perfect instead of 2 1/2 hrs).  The rub was the only thing I didn't follow to a tea, but lets be honest, half the fun of cooking is making it your own, so I raided our spice rack.  I omitted the smoked salt, b/c I had nothing resembling anything smoked.  I added a WHOLE lot more spices though.  If it was ground, it was going in the rub; coriander seed, allspice, mustard, pumpkin pie spice (yep...you heard me correctly), cinnamon, minced onion, garlic salt, and a few others I can't remember off the top of my head.  

Cooked them exactly as it was written and the turned out fantastic.  I've already printed off the recipe and am trying to go through the spice rack again to remember what I put in the rub and rough amts.  Thanks again for a wonderful recipe.  My family LOVED it!

attributes.source_text: and moist
My family LOVED it!

reviews.review_text: This is my new go-to method for oven-cooked ribs.  Simply fantastic!  The meat was incredibly tender after 2 1/2 hours in the oven.  The meat wanted to come right off the bone.  We did cut in serving sizes by cutting the slab after every other bone.  Makes for a really meaty rib with meat on each side of the bone and eliminates some bones from each slab making more room in the pan to slather on your favorite sauce.  For time purposes I just used a store bought rub, but next time I will make the recipe given.  It was still delicious.  I also used the bbq sauce from the recipe for should be illegal oven bbq ribs.  We love that sauce.  I cooked the sauce on my stove-top for a couple hours and then it was ready to brush on ribs after they came out of foil.  We all ate until we were practically sick.  I was skeptical that this would be so good as I have made ribs in oven in roasting pan covered with foil and the results were okay but nothing like this.  The tight foil wrap does do something magical.  The recipe also gets an A+ for ease.  Could not be any easier and required absolutely no babysitting!  Thanks for sharing this recipe!

attributes.source_text: The meat was incredibly tender

reviews.review_text: Absolutely amazing.  I brought two racks of these these ribs to a pot luck holiday party tonight, they were gone in minutes.  People absolutely loved them.  I was quite skeptical as I did not feel there was enough salt in the recipe, there was no moisture added during cooking, and while cooking the house stunk of garlic.    Prior to cooking I watched a few youtube videos to get some tips.   <br/><br/>I purchased two racks of back ribs from my local butcher, they were pre-packaged from somewhere in Indiana and frozen. Fresh ribs in central Connecticut around Christmastime seem to be reserved for those who own pigs.   They thawed in the refrigerator over night. The next day I dried the ribs using paper towels.  <br/><br/>I searched for hickory smoke salt to no avail, so I made some myself.  Using coarse sea salt and Stubb's Hickory Liquid Smoke, (found at Big Y) mixed it together and then dried it in the oven on a cookie sheet at 200F for 10 minutes.   I did add more than the suggested 1 teaspoon to the rub, worked out well.   Smoked paprika was what I had in my pantry and that is what went into the rub in lieu of paprika.  Using wide heavy duty foil, doubling it and packaging them separately.  I allowed the ribs to soak up the rub for an hour in the refrigerator and the into the oven they went. At first I had the racks on two cookie sheets, by the end of the cooking I had put them onto one large cookie sheet.   I allowed them to cook for two and a half hours at 300F.  Opened them up, they were beautiful, not gray at all. <br/><br/>I allowed them to cool for a few moments and then basted with Sweet Baby Ray's Hickory and Brown Sugar Barbeque Sauce and broiled on each side.  They went into a serving dish covered with two layers of foil and were driven to the party and reheated in a 300 degree oven for a few minutes.  <br/><br/>Thank you for the fantastic recipe.   I will never add liquid to my ribs again!

I looked at several rib recipes that were similar, and debated which to review but decided this one really gave me the frame work, so I guess the stars are for technique and inspiration! I had a little less than 3 lbs of ribs, so started with about a 1/2 cup of brown sugar. To that  I added cayenne pepper, black pepper, dry mustard, cumin, onion powder, & garlic powder. After rubbing it on the ribs I lightly sprinkled them Old Bay.  I just poured a light coating of Trader Joes Kansas City style BBQ sauce all over the ribs then topped them with onions and lemon slices (I don't know why, but my mom always did this with her country style ribs) I used heavy duty foil so only needed  a single sheet each for the packet - this worked great - no messy pan!
I baked them at 325 degrees for 2 hours and 45 minutes. I then finished them off on the grill on low heat, adding extra BBQ sauce. The ribs were sooo tender and flavorful. The rub before putting on the sauce cave them a nice complexity. The cayenne add just a lhint of  heat which was a nice contrast to the sweetness of the BBQ Sauce. I served the ribs with Recipe #237137 and Recipe #263699.
Thank you Bethany for your inspiration!

reviews.review_text: Excellent!  I was looking for a an oven rib recipe and found this and glad I did cause it was so tasty!  My son loves ribs and I have never cooked or grilled bone in ribs before.  I had about 4 lbs of country style, bone in ribs, about 1 to 1/4 inch thick.  I had, on hand, Pampered Chef Smoky BBQ Rub which included the same rub ingredients mentioned here and I added that generously to each side of ribs.  I wrapped in the foil and refrigerated for about 3 hours. Pulled them out of fridge, sprinkled on some Liquid Smoke and added some sea salt and baked them at 300 degrees for about 2 hours 15 minutes.  Pulled out (very tender and falling off bone) and basted on Baby Ray's BBQ sauce (our fav too) and broiled as directed to get the sauce nicely caramelized.  We used forks, as my ribs were country style and not a rack; but it was tender and flavorful.  My son is not one to go looking for leftovers the next day but did with these ribs and luckily I had a few leftover.  I served this with a cheesy potato casserole and some green beans.  Clean up was a breeze with the foil; the baking sheet was not even soiled.  Will definitely make again for sure; thanks for posting!

reviews.review_text:
I am cooking these as I type, and am sure they are going to be fabulous. I just wanted to mention how easy it is to make your own barbecue sauce.  I don't like the super-sweet Baby Rays so much -- 19 grams of sugar in 2 tablespoons, plus my husband was just diagnosed with pre-diabetes!  

There are so many good recipes out there, but I saute a 1/2 cup minced  onion (not Vidalia -- which has as much sugar as Coca Cola, but a regular yellow onion),  add a minced fresh garlic clove for a couple minutes at the and of the onion -- on low, don't burn them.  Then add a cup of ketchup, or whiz a can of diced tomatoes in the blender, or add a can of plain canned tomato sauce -- whatever you have in the pantry.   Add a bit of cider vinegar, and whatever spices you like in BBQ sauce.  I like some coriander and cardamom,  a couple tablespoons of FRESH lemon juice and minced lemon rind from that same lemon.  The lemon rind makes the sauce, to me. If you want some sweetness, add a couple tablespoons of some of that jelly your family member or friend made that you got for Christmas.  I used Delaware Slaughter Beach Plum Jelly in mine.  Oh, and black pepper, freshly ground, to your taste, plus a couple shakes of hot sauce (I use Crystal's) if you like.  Let this just mellow at a very low heat while your meat cooks.  You'll be surprised how fresh and good it is, and not nearly as heavy as the commercial stuff.

First let me say that I always mess up ribs...they always come out as "burnt ends" (the whole thing)...dry, no matter how much sauce you put on it and barely palatable....this time I HIT IT OUT OF THE PARK!!!!!...The is hands down the best recipe I've tried and succeeded at (I'm usually a pretty good cook, according to everyone I've cooked for ... except ribs)  I did use Bobby Flay's Brown Sugar Rub (just because I already had rubbed the meat down), cooked the meat in the foil packet (I usually cook in a baking pan covered with foil...the foil wrapped meat definitely makes ALL the difference in the world!!!!) on a baking sheet as directed.  After 2 1/2 hours (probably could've taken them out at 2) I removed the meat (as suggested by another reviewer, turned the oven up to 350F), cut open the top of the packet, folded back the foil, drained some of the juice, then put my homemade BBQ sauce on the meat (I live in Austria and don't have the selection of sauce choices like in the states).  I baked them for about 30 more minutes turning them once and putting more sauce on them.  I took them out, placing them in a heavy covered pot to rest for about 15-20 minutes.  The smile on my husband's face said it all with a lot of "mmmm-ing" throughout the meal!  I love being able to share some great BBQ with him and my new in-laws (Vienna is NOT a big BBQ town...lol)...Thanks Beth for the great method of cooking.  I can't wait to try it on chicken as was mentioned in some of the other reviews.

All other ingredients I adjusted for 5lbs of pork ribs (since that's how much I made).

They came out very moist, and tender and I couldn't be more happy with the results. I used Sweet Baby Ray since it came recommended and it just happened to be in the grocery story I was in (I was surprised since I live in Canada), but to be honest, the ribs would have been just as good without the bbq sauce. the dry rub is everything but dry after cooking, and provides a phenomenal flavour.

reviews.review_text: I gave this recipe 5 stars just because it's easy, it's forgiving (if you don't alter the given cooking technique).  I prepared this for last night's dinner, and had plenty to have again tonight.  I didn't use the rub to slow cook them in.  I used the barbeque sauce I was going to end with.  While baking in foil, I did include the rub ingredients in with the BBQ sauce.  Of course, by the time you have completed the cooking in the foil packets, you have essentially boiled the ribs anyway, and the rub/bbq sauce has permeated the meat.  I drained them after cooking, lined another pan with heavy duty aluminum foil anb proceeded under the broiler.  This really made the ribs.  They were tender, easy to separate to eat, and were just saucy enough to kinda make a mess.  I loved them!  And, I have a few left over to put into the freezer for another quick meal!  I am very pleased with how this method turned out, and will definitely use it again.

reviews.review_text: Made this tonight for my grandson's birthday dinner; he is a BBQ ribs lover and requested them for his birthday.  These ribs were out-of-this-world!  I did 3 racks of St. Louis style ribs (about 11 # total) and they were devoured.  I followed the directions for double-wrapping each rib rack in foil then placed on a cookie sheet (was glad I did! tip for next time - cover the cookie sheet in foil too before placing the foil wrapped ribs on it). I tried removing the membrane, but didn't get it all, but it didn't take away from the taste or tenderness at all.  I doubled the rub and used it on all 3 racks and had plenty.  I used smoked sea salt and smoked paprika along with the other ingredients listed.  Baked for 2.5 hours because I had 3 racks of ribs in the oven.  I removed from the oven, turned the oven to 350, then drained the grease, cut into various rib sizes (2,3,4), then placed back on the foil (meaty side up), moving all of the ribs onto one foil-covered cookie sheet.  Brushed with Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce, and put uncovered back in the oven and baked for about 15-20 minutes.  These ribs held their shape and were melt-in-your-mouth delicious!  I tasted the meat before I put on the BBQ sauce and the meat was wonderfully tender and delicious just by itself.  Even my 6 year old granddaughter (who is a VERY picky eater) gave them a high 5 and ate all the meat on her plate.  This recipe is definitely a keeper!!  Thank you!!

reviews.review_text: The biggest problem most people have is finding the smoked salt.  I have found that the best seasoning for me is "McCormick's GRILL MASTER APPLEWOOD RUB".  It has a perfect blend of smoke and spice.  If I'm cooking only in the over, I follow the recipe as written.  If I'm finishing the ribs on the grill, I shorten the cooking time by 15 minutes.  The reason for that is that if you cook for the full time, the ribs are too tender and fall apart easily, and makes it a little harder to transfer them to the grill.  Shortening the oven time helps keeping the ribs intact, and the heat from the grill will soften the meat further.  For some people, shortening the cooking time might be preferable because it leaves them a little chewy and reduces the steamed meat flavor a little, so that it tastes just like the ribs were slow cooked on a grill for hours.  This is a great, easy recipe.

items.description: It was the Fall of 1987 when Pete Nyhus walked into our office, just to visit. We started talking about breakfast, and he reached into a wastepaper basket and pulled out a scrap of teletype paper. He wrote out this recipe, and my family has never used pre-mix since.
instructions: Mix the dry items first.
Combine the eggs and melted butter to the milk and slowly stir into the flour mixture.
Heat the griddle to325 F or the pan to medium high let sit at least 10 minutes while heating the griddle orpan.
These will be high, but light and fluffy -- .

reviews.review_text: Pretty darn good!  I got an idea from Dr. Kaley to mix up the flour a bit and did the half spelt/half all purpose unbleached to make it.  This was my first spelt experience and I must say that the flavor is much lighter and less, um, earthy than doing whole wheat.  Great way to get some whole grains into the diet and the guys all gobbled them up! update: I've made these several times and sometimes they don't come out as good.  I think it has a lot to do w the temperature of the wet ingredient. Warm butter, cold egg and cold milk don't mix!  Read a few reviews back and saw 1 other cook mentioned microwaving egg and milk for a few seconds before adding melted butter. Wish I'd read that before I just made the batch!

reviews.review_text: Pretty good recipe although I've been experimenting. The original recipe had this weird aftertaste to it; after reading into things, people seem to think it's the baking soda, but after reducing the sugar (1 and a 1/2 tablespoons instead of 3) and adding a splash of vanilla (I fill up the cap) it's usually pretty good. Although, I usually half the entire recipe so that there's no leftovers. When I try to make the full thing, it tastes too salty, so I plan on reducing the amount of salt as well. Sometimes it comes out a bit watery so I just throw in more flour and it's fine. Big, fluffy pancakes that hold up much better on the pan than the box stuff! They also cook a ton better, too. I have the most uneven stove ever, but these still come out fully cooked, and they don't run all over the pan when I pour them.

reviews.review_text: Have been making these the last few times the kiddos request pancakes and I LOVE them! A few changes I have made after reading the reviews... One I followed was Claudette's review: "I made this today for breakfast and it was very fluffy and delicious. I made some changes to the recipe (as I had watched quite a few others): I used only 2 teaspoons of baking power instead of a whole tablespoon as suggested in the recipe. I also added 1 teaspoon of baking soda. The recipe mentioned beating the egg white and egg yokes separately. What I did was I beat the egg white until it's stiff (like making meringue). I also added 1 teaspoon of vanilla. I mixed the milk with the egg yokes, vanilla, butter into the flour first, and then gently folded the beaten egg white into the batter. That extra step really makes the pancakes fluffy and light. The recipe makes 13 pancakes. We ate 6, and I'm looking forward to enjoying the rest next weekend!" I didn't particularly mix things that way. Still mixed as the initial instructions insisted. But I did add the baking soda and less baking powder. As well as the vanilla. Turned out great!

BEST pancake recipe EVER.  Hands down.
