reviews.review_text: I have never left a negative comment before so I'm sorry to say these were the worst pancakes I've ever made. Too much butter made them runny and burn before they were cooked. I knew it would be too much baking soda but I tried it according to the recipe anyway. That was the worst part-- the bitter taste. This recipe  needed vanilla and a little more sugar, less butter, with half the baking soda. I have made pancakes since I was very young and have never had them turn out this way. I should have stuck with my recipe instead of ruining my ingredients trying something new. (I'm sorry if this sounds harsher than I intended. It's hard to think clearly when you're hungry.)

I've tried several recipes (including taking a stab at coming up with one myself), and I thought the one from my mom's old Better Homes and Gardens cookbook was the best, hands-down...until now.  I think the butter makes the big difference in the flavor, and the baking powder is what adds the leavening that makes the cakes so light and crisp around the edges - just the way I like them! I had to use evaporated milk this time, but it didn't seem to alter the recipe at all. I'm just glad I made a double batch and froze the extras...breakfast all next week for sure! Thanks for posting this amazing recipe...and thank YOU, "Pete!"

These are truly fantastic pancakes, light, fluffy, filling without feeling like a rock on your stomach.  I was a little concerned with the amount of baking powder, but it happened to be just right (I use aluminum free baking powder, so no off taste), if you are not getting fluffy pancakes, I suggest you test your baking powder by placing a small bowl in your sink put in a tablespoon of baking powder, pour boiling water over the baking powder, if it reacts violently and overflows the small bowl, it is good, if it does nothing or just fizzles, get new baking powder.

items.label: Crock Pot Cream Cheese Chicken
items.name: Crock Pot Cream Cheese Chicken
items.description: I got this recipe from a nurse at work. We're always sharing easy and family-pleasing recipes. The sauce tastes like a creamy Alfredo sauce. This is great with noodles.
instructions: Place chicken pieces in crock pot and sprinkle Italian seasoning over chicken. Sprinkle with 2 tablespoons melted butter.
Cook on low for 4-6 hours.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a sauce pan and saute onion and garlic. Add Cream of Chicken Soup, cream cheese, and chicken broth. Stir until smooth.
Add this mixture to crock pot and cook on low for an additional hour.

reviews.review_text: A couple of notes for this. <br/><br/>First, Newer and older Crock Pot cook SO differently. I have 2. I can cook the same meal in both, and almost 3 hrs different in cooking time. Newer pots and MUCH hotter. So don't blame the time.<br/><br/>Second, it doesn't call for water, so DON'T add it. Crock pots don't need a lot of liquid.<br/><br/>Now, I tried this recipe twice, but failed to review; but saw this and it reminded me. I made it for me and then a friend - that I know loves these types of dishes. Not really my style, but I thought I would give it a try.<br/><br/>- I used boneless skinless; but, a mix of thighs and breasts<br/>- The first time, I made it as is ... it ok. Bland for me, not much flavor (but that is my tastes)<br/>- Time 2; I changed things a bit, but not the ingredients.<br/><br/>- I added a medium onion (not small), cut in half and thin sliced. Added to the bottom of the crock pot.<br/>- 1 garlic clove, minced<br/>- 2 tablespoons butter<br/>- Then added the chicken sprinkled with the seasoning. I used Good Seasons Garlic Salad Dressing Mix (in a dry packet)<br/>- Topped it with the soup and sliced mushrooms. DO NOT mix the mushrooms in.<br/><br/>Cooked 4 hours on low. Add the cream cheese cubed and mixed everything in. I also also suggest adding some white wine for a little flavor. Cooked another hour.<br/><br/>I didn't add the time this time because my friend didn't drink.<br/><br/>Done, and tender. I tossed in fresh parsley right before serving. <br/>Garnished with paprika for a little color.<br/><br/>I served over white rice; pasta would be ok too.<br/>-------------------------------<br/>Great idea; but, not my style and needed a few tweaks for my liking.<br/>But, we ate it all; it wasn't inedible at all - just not for me.

attributes.source_text: a friend - that I know loves these types of dishes

reviews.review_text:
This is a really great tasting, easy main dish  meal!  I made it exactly as written,,,except the time cooked.  It actually only takes about 1/2 the 7hrs to cook and I think had I not been here and watched it,,it wouldn't have turned out as well.  I think it would have burned around the edges.  I intended and started early enough to use your time stated, but after 2 1/2 hrs, turned my crock on the "warm" setting (newer crocks have this setting,,yay) until I added the broth/cream cheese mix.  I let this cook on low for 45 min and served over mashed garlic/tarragon potatoes. dh won'
t eat rice :( The 2nd best part was the next nite, I shredded the left over chicken,,(I'd taken it out of the sauce)added 1/2cup sour cream, a 4 oz. can of green chilis and 4oz. velveeta cheese to the sauce and some garlic powder.  I placed the shredded chicken and more shredded cheese in corn tortillas and pour the remaining sauce over them and had a pan of chicken enchiladas fit for a king!!  I also reserved 3/4 cup of the sauce and poured it over 2 chili rellenos (sp)I'd made!  Seems as tho I may have had a lot of left overs, but there're only 2 of us and we don't eat heavily,,so, this wonderful crockpot chicken made 2 fab different dinners....just enough shredded chicken leftover for soft tacos tonite....3 meals!!! (sorry this is long, just wanting to be informative on a great recipe)...thanks for posting,,,,Kitty  :)

I hate to do this, but I don't want to give stars this time, because I made a mess. I had made this recipe once before with 5* results, and forgot to review it (not sure if it was this exact recipe # ?). This time I used Recipe-ready Condensed "Cream Of" Soup (#29450) and Italian Salad Dressing Mix (#45804). It seems to me like these substitutions might work, perhaps with a bit less salt in either or both of them next time, since one problem I had was that the finished dish was too salty. I also used fat-free cream cheese, which might have contributed to my problems, so I won't attempt it again (I don't like the stuff anyway - too many chemicals). I know that I accidentally added the sauce nearly 3 hours before the end of cooking, which was a mistake I will take care not to repeat, as the sauce dried out and clumped up as a result. I will also use my regular crock next time instead of the Smart Pot, or set a timer, so I can go with exactly 7 1/2 hours and not be tempted to leave it on warm. I hope to try again soon, so I can add the 5 stars you deserve!

I varied this recipe a bit because I didn't have cream of chicken soup on hand, so I substituted cr. of Mushroom soup instead.  I also used leftover roast chicken that I pulled off the chicken bones.  Since the chicken was already cooked, I put it in the crockpot at about 5 pm, added the italian seasoning and butter.  While the crockpot was heating up, I made the sauce per the directions but added some fresh sliced mushrooms, a small can of stems and pieces with the juice and a few splashes of white cooking wine once the veggies were sauteed.  I substituted mushroom soup for the chicken soup, added the cream cheese, stirred to dissolve and added some uncooked spaghetti broken into one inch pieces.  Once it was mixed, smooth, the cream cheese all dissolved and the spagetti semi cooked, I poured the hot sauce over the leftover chicken and let it simmer in the crockpot.  The spagetti continued to cook and turned out perfectly and the mushroom flavor, combined with the hint of white wine was FAB!  I will definitely try the recipe with chicken soup when I have it on hand, but I will definitely add the mushrooms, spagetti and cooking wine again too!  

Cathy

reviews.review_text:
My first crock pot meal and I'm happy!! Varied the recipe due to Mom getting out of the hospital and not having supplies OR sleep so, I reviewed a couple dif chicken recipes and came up with this variation.

Used 4 chicken thighs. Rubbed butter on the bottom and sides of crock pot. Sprinkled paprika on skins and placed skin side down in pot. Let them cook for about an hour to brown a bit. (As I read some folks didn't like the white skin results.) Then I quickly poured about 1/3 bottle of Lawry's Teriyaki Sauce into the bottom along with 2 pickled garlic cloves (as some folks said cooking for long hours dried the meat somewhat...and I needed to get some sleep and wanted it to cook at the longest and lowest temp). After 6 hours of sleep, I went and checked to see if I messed it up. I didn't. The meat was moist and the skin was browned. I drained most of the juices and poured one can of campbell's cream of chicken soup in and spread it around and put it on "high" for 45 mins. I did not have the cream cheese. The gravy turned a medium brown and looked and tasted amazing on the chicken. A tad bit Tangy and Creamy. Yummy. I made some garlic dumplings by using the Bisquick recipe but added minced garlic from a jar and some of it's juices and teaspoon of butter into the mix before dropping in the boiling water. Delicious!! Thank you for the ideas to help out this old, tired daughter on her first Crock Pot meal for her ailing Mom!!

reviews.review_text: AMAZING!  Just thought I'd put in my 2 cents worth, with the other 300+ reviews.  I used boneless skinless chicken breasts and some bottled italian dressing, no butter, and no chicken broth.  The garlic clove I used was really big, probably counted for two.  I also added some pampered chef italian seasoning.  As others have commented, I cooked it a lot less than suggested, but I think that's to be expected when you're not using bone-in chicken.  I did spray my crock pot with cooking spray to avoid any baked on mess, as one reviewer had mentioned that it had started to burn around the edges.  We served it over whole wheat egg noodles and steamed broccoli spears from the garden.  I also chopped up some sundried tomatoes (oil packed) for my portion.  that may have been a little too much going on.  I might choose either one or the other next time.  We'd also like to try mushrooms with this.  We sprinkled some parmaesan cheese over everything.  Even my picky 3 and 4 year old girls loved it!  Tasted super rich and creamy, despite the fact that I used fat free cream cheese and healthy choice soup.  Tastes just sinful!  We're going to try making enchiladas with the leftovers tomorrow, as I read in another review.  Looking forward to more splendid results!  Thanks for posting!

reviews.review_text: Once again this site came through!  Oh my word!  The recipe was one of the best I have had.  We have a houseful to feed so finding a recipe that pleases everyone is a rare gem.  The flavours worked beautifully together.  With our large family I have to double all my recipes and I found myself short a can of cream of chicken soup.  Remembering the reviews I had read suggesting adding mushrooms I used a can of cream of chicken and a can of cream of mushroom.  I was also out of chicken broth so I substituted one cup water (remember I double everything) mixed with 1 tablespoon of chicken bouillion granules.  I used partially thawed boneless skinless chicken breasts each cut in half and had to cut the total cooking time  by two hours or the chicken would have gone from great to dry in a heartbeat.  The results were fantastic!  After dinner when we usually have a light dessert a couple of the grandchildren asked if they could have some more chicken with "that yummy sauce"!  If that is not a testiment to a great recipe I don't know what is.  Thanks for the wonderful post!

reviews.review_text: This was a real hit at our house!  Rich, creamy, and just as good as everybody says it is.  I have to admit, I had some misgivings about leaving the chicken to cook for four hours without any liquid at all, so I sloshed a wee bit of white wine into the crockpot first, just to be on the safe side.  I used a package of zesty Italian dressing mix and bone-in thighs with the skin left on.  Followed the recipe cooking times as written, and the meat came out just right-- tender, juicy, and falling off the bone.  I served this over egg noodles with a lot of sauce and a sprinkle of paprika.  Delicious!  Perfect winter comfort food, and just the thing to make when company's coming for dinner (that way, you can spread the fat and calories around instead of eating all those too-luscious leftovers yourself).  Next time, I think I'll toss in some button mushrooms while sauteeing the onion and garlic, and thicken the sauce a bit with cornstarch, as other reviewers have suggested.  GREAT recipe!  Thanks for sharing.

reviews.review_text: I have to say, even after all the positive reviews I had my doubts - I'm not a savory cream cheese kinda person, I prefer it in sweet desserts.  But I had several ingredients to use up and this recipe fit them, though I did make some substitutions to fit those ingredients.  I used one pound boneless skinless breasts but kept the proportion of the sauce ingredients the same.  I didn't bother to melt the butter, I just cut it kind of small and tossed it in around the chicken.  I used Garlic & Herb dressing mix, and cooked my chicken on high for 1.5 hours before adding the sauce.  I didn't have any onion or garlic, so I used powdered versions of the same.  Also, I used cream of mushroom soup.  Dumped in the sauce after mixing and cooked on high for another hour, served over short cut pasta.  Fantastic!  The chicken was perfectly cooked and wonderfully tender, and the sauce was absolutely incredible.  Everyone, even my picky toddler, loved this and I'll definitely make this again and again!

reviews.review_text:
"MAGNIFICENT"
I wanted to make a nice dinner for my husband yesterday but it needed to be easy to prepare.  I read tons of the reviews which were very helpful and tweaked a couple things.  My husbands word for this recipe was MAGNIFICENT!!  I used about 1/2 C. of Vadalia onion and 2 cloves of garlic, low fat cream of chicken soup and 1/3 less fat cream cheese.  Used only half of the dry dressing because of the salt, only 1 T of the butter and 3 lbs. of bonless chicken breasts.  Now for the sauce!  Some people thought it was bland soooo I skiped the chicken broth and used 1/4 of cheap, plain Sherry (instead of wine, more flavor) and 1t. of Italian seasoning to the sauce.  This is where it became MAGNIFICENT!!  Tasted sort of French.  I also only used 6 oz of the cream cheese, still so rich and creamy.  Put the sauce over the chicken and added 8oz. of thick sliced fresh mushrooms.  If you don't like muchrooms pick them out, it adds so much to the flavor!  A lot of reviews commented on the gravy being too thin or the chicken being dry.  Ours was so moist and tender that my husband actually asked me if it was indeed chicken he was eating?????  I was home so I did babysit this dish slightly for a crockpot dish but well worth it.  Cooked it about 2 hours on low then an hour or so on high.  Turned it back down to low for about 1/2 hour, made the sauce and added it, cooked about another 45 minutes on low. Then turned it to warm for an hour so the chicken could absorb some of the flavor and we could relax and have a cocktai!!  I also thawed my chicken before putting it in the crock pot and pressed out the water with paper towels.  Sauce was still slightly thinner than I would have liked so I will add a little tapioca next time.  Served it over spinich linguene.  Would have licked our plates if we could have!!!

reviews.review_text:
Made this for dinner tonight for myself, husband, brother in law, son, and mother in law. I did a few things differently. I used FROZEN boneless skinless chicken breasts, and after an hour on high realized they weren't going to be ready in time, so took them out and cut them into chunks, cooked them in the skillet and then threw them back in. I then did the saute and soup step, adding mushrooms to the mix and used white wine instead of chicken broth. I also added a shake of Italian Seasoning to the saute. I thought this needed a little something else, maybe some more garlic or more onion, not sure. But it was definitely GOOD! My husband liked it and said it was a keeper, he loves anything remotely close to an alfredo sauce. :) My mother in law said the same thing about it needing a little something but still ate THIRDS of it (she rarely even eats dinner with us!) and my brother in law the chef said it was just fine the way it was. I served this with tri-color rotini pasta which my two year old gobbled up and he also enjoyed the chicken, which made dinner a little easier on me since he normally hates what we're having.

All in all I will be making this again, maybe adding a bit more onion and garlic and perhaps using a different cream of soup? Thank you for posting this recipe! :)

reviews.review_text: Loved the recipe but did not use the crock pot. Wanted to make it during the week day and it would have had to cook for 8 hours and that would have been way too long.  Sauted chunk size peices of chicken (not all the way) with 2 tbl butter and italian seasoning package (pkg was larger then on this recipe and I think this might resolve why it wasn't seasoned enough), then placed in a dutch oven pot.  Sauted onion, garlic and 8 oz sliced mushroom with some seasoned salt (Lawry's ), pepper and a bit more galic powder.  Added low fat soup, low fat cream cheese and low sodium chicken broth, then added all to the pot and let simmer for about half hour. Did take the cover off the last 10 minutes because cooking anythink whether it be in a regular pot or crock pot, the condesation creates more water and will thin recipes out.  Served on white rice, only because I had pasta the night before.  Very tasty sauce which is quite rich and creamy without all the fat!

reviews.review_text: This was delicious, and unlike many other variations of this recipe I've prepared, the cream cheese did not clump or chunk up because it was mixed/melted separately with the other ingredients before being added to the chicken.  The big difference in my preparation is that we have one of those Deni brand combo crock pot/slow cooker/deep fryer, and even on the very lowest setting, we were able to make this dish in about two hours total (about an hour and a half on the chicken, and another half hour with the sauce).  So, make sure you are around to keep an eye on your chicken, as it seems like everyone else who has reviewed this has noted that it took far less than the recommended time to cook.  All in all, my family loved this dish, and we're about to try peppermintkitty's suggestion for the little bit left over, and make some creamy chicken enchiladas. :) Great recipe! "It's a keeper," as my husband said.

reviews.review_text: This recipe is SO good!  I think it may just be one of the best things I have ever eaten!!!  I used boneless/skinless chicken breasts instead of the ones called for.   They did cook quicker than the ones with the bones would, but now that I know that it only took 4-5 hours to cook in the crock pot, I can adjust the recipe and it would be a great one to pop in the crock pot while I am out.  We tried it over egg noodles the first night and fettuccini the second night.  Personally, we preferred it on the fettuccini.  I added some fresh grated Parmesan cheese overtop and it was perfect.  This recipe is definitely a keeper.  My Mom even had leftovers on day three (what little was left!) and she thought it was great too!  I cannot wait to make it again!  Super easy!  With a two year old and an 8 month old I can use more recipes like this!  Even the two year old loved it!

reviews.review_text: I had company coming over for dinner a party of 6 and with our family was a total of 10. I've never cooked for that many in one shot.  I wanted something easy that would feed adults and kids, I was worried because I had to increase the amounts, but thankfully this website allows you to up the servings and makes the ingredient modifications! I followed most everything except I added 3/4 cream of mushroom and 3/4 cream of chicken soup, I also used chicken breasts which I cooked on high for 2 hours and they were perfect. I was worried about adding the cream sauce to this because I thought it would be too watery, but over the course of the hour it cooked it became thicker.  Once we poured it over fettucini, it was so delicious!  Everyone, including the kids had seconds!  There were no left overs!  I also used low sodium broth, and soups, and reduced fat cream cheese.  It was perfect, my family has asked me to make it again, and it was so easy I will!  Thanks for the recipe

reviews.review_text: Oh Miss Annie!  I have to join the choir on this recipe.  Has to be some of the best tasting chicken to ever come out of my crock pot.  I did a couple things a little bit different.  The chicken was so well done when I made the sauce that I removed it from the crockpot and put it in a casserole dish with about a cup of the sauce and covered it with foil and popped it into a 225° oven just to keep it warm and to let it absorb some of that wonderful flavor.  Also discovered at the last minute that my Cream/Chicken soup was really Cream/Mushroom.  Used it anyway and added a small can of sliced mushrooms.  Divine, sublime!  Will be adding this to my 'make often, it's a hit' list!  Do believe I will use boneless chicken next time.  Had it with mashed potatoes, green beans, carrot/apple/raisin salad and lemon pie.  I can't walk now...just waddle!  But oh so happy!  Thank you so much!

Have had this receipe saved for a while and just made it over the weekend.  I started with 5 boneless skinless chicken breast which I cut up into bite size pieces.  I put them, the butter (I can't believe its not butter), the Good Seasons zesty italian dressing package contents,  the cream of mushroom soup and a little of the chicken broth in the crock pot and cooked it on low for 2 and a half hours.  Came back and added crushed garlic (equivilent to 3 cloves), onion powder, a large can of mushrooms, the rest of the chicken broth and a 1/2 cup white wine.  Let it cook for another hour and it was AWESOME!  Served it over whole wheat egg noodles and with mixed vegetables.  Liked the combo so much that we will add a small bag of the frozen mixed vegetables in the next time we make it.  Thanks for posting the original recipe.  We will definately make it again.

This recipe is DELICIOUS! My husband's reaction on his first is bite was "EXCELLENT, this is a definitely a keeper". This recipe can easily be cut in half if you don't need to feed 6 :-). I only  used about 1.5 lbs of chicken tenders and cut everything else in half (except garlic clove, I would use two cloves for the full recipe), I fed myself, husband, and four year old and still had enough left over for the next day for husband.   I actually toped this dish on RICE and it was awesome! I actually cooked the chicken on high since my crockpot doesn't work on low and the chicken still came out very tender (I used tenders!).  This has  definite Alfredo like taste to it, so, if you don't like Alfredo sauce, don't try to recipe but if you do, TRY IT, it's AWESOME! I love that you don't have to use so much butter (another recipe similar to this one called for 1/2 cup!) I'm going to make this recipe for family and friends !

items.name: Olive Garden Copycat Zuppa Toscana
items.description: This is a clone of the Olive Garden Zuppa Toscana. Tried and true, approved by former Olive Garden chefs.
instructions: Chop or slice uncooked sausage into small pieces and cook until browned and meat is ground in bottom of your soup pan over med-high heat.
Add onions, garlic, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes to Sausage and cook until onions are clear and aromatics of the seasonings blend together.
Reduce heat back to medium and place, potatoes, in the pot. and slowly add the Chicken Stock and water and stir. (use Chicken Bouillon envelope for extra flavor is Chicken Stock is weak).
Cook on medium heat until potatoes are done and stir occasionally. Once Potatoes are done, Add flour or cornstarch and simmer for another 15 minutes.
Reduce heat to lowest setting and sprinkle in your kale and cooked bacon and slowly pour cream while stirring.
Check for taste and then serve.

reviews.review_text: OMG, this was amazing soup! DH NEVER, and I mean NEVER eats leftovers and he requested this the next day! I added a 7 links of Johnsonville Mild Italian Sausage, casing removed, because hubby is a complete carnivore. Has to have meat, meat and more meat in any recipe I make. I also sprinkled the meat, before browning with red pepper flakes to give it a little kick. I used several tweaks from a couple of reviewers. (Thanks, Dans La Lune and 27 w/a foodie 4 year old) I saute'ed the garlic and onion in a teaspoon of bacon grease ( we save ours so I always have it on hand). I added it after draining and used 32oz of chicken broth and 2 1/2 cups of water. Something to note: Since I added a pound and a half of meat there wasn't much liquid after boiling for 20 minutes on gas oven, so I added another cup of chicken broth, since I planned on stuffing it with Tuscan Kale. I also used 3 quarters of a bag of Yellow Dutch Baby Potatoes, quartered, (they were soft after boiling for 15 minutes!) I added the Kale and a little over 1 1/2 cups heavy whipped cream after about 25 minutes since I was worried about the kale/liquid ratio. I then simmered on medium low for 15 min. and low for another 5. Served with garlic breadsticks. What a hearty and flavorful soup! Hubby said it was better than Olive Garden (probably because of the addition of more meat) and that it's one of his favorite dinners that I have cooked! ( He is the normal cook and I cook for the novelty of it or just to be sweet sometimes - yes, I have an amazing husband! Thank you Cycle Michael for posting and thank you, all you tweakers for reviewing, since I am always looking for ways to get a WOW from hubby!

reviews.review_text: As a huge fan of the Olive Garden version of this soup, I've been craving it terribly and had to try to make it. I followed the recipe pretty closely except I didn't use any Accent Seasoning and had to use the sausage I had on hand, which was Jimmy Dean's medium. That being said, the reason I love the O.G. soup is the flavor of the broth. That is definitely key to the whole thing. Unfortunately, I went against my better judgment and followed the cooking advice to saute the onions and garlic in the sausage grease. (I've only done this previously in recipes a few times and each time it was awful.) Well, that completely ruined it. All I could taste was the burnt sausage taste in the onions, sausage, AND broth. Should have known better. Next time I will saute the onions and garlic in butter and thoroughly drain the sausage. I also didn't like the taste of the potatoes. Will use Yukon Gold next time. The proportions were not right to me either. I plan to cut back on the sausage and add another potato or two. More salt and pepper was also needed. All that being said, it was a good base soup recipe, and if I hadn't used the sausage I used, it would have been much better. My husband actually really liked it, but it was nothing like the O.G. soup.

attributes.source_text: My husband actually really liked it

reviews.review_text: Yum yum yum... this soup totally blew me away... it's DELICIOUS.  As a former Olive Garden employee who has the taste of Zuppa Toscana burned in my tastebuds, I can truly say that my soup tonight came out as a PERFECT match.  I did customize this recipe with the help of previous readers, so I recommend following it like this...  I used 1 lb of hot Italian sausage, 3 medium to large potatoes UNPEELED, 1 small onion, 3 strips of thick sliced bacon, 4 cloves of garlic, 3 cups of kale (veins removed and sliced thin like ribbons), 32 oz of chicken broth, 2.5 cups of water, and 1 1/4 cups of half and half.  I removed the casings from the sausage and browned the meat in a skillet, then putting aside in a stockpot.  Then in the same skillet, I cooked the bacon and onions side by side, and put the onions in the stockpot, and went to work chopping up the cooked bacon and also putting in the pot.  Then I sliced up all the potatoes... leave the skins on!... it creates awesome ribbons in the soup that add texture and flavor.  I sliced them lengthwise and then in half into 1/4 inch thick triangles.  Then I put the chicken broth, minced garlic, and water and let boil for about 30 minutes, until the potatoes were tender.  Then I added the kale and half & half and let simmer another 15 minutes or so until the kale was tender as well.  Although the hot sausage left a reddish colored film on top of the soup, it properly seasoned the soup without needing crushed red pepper (which the real OG recipe includes).  Remember this soup should have a nice zing to it so I found that hot italian sausage worked beautifully.  What a fabulous soup for this chilly weather!!  Bon Appetit!

reviews.review_text:
WOW, I made this recipe for the 2nd time.  Since I was no newbie to it I went in with confidence & changed a thing or two. If your into Robust flavor, spice & don't mind a tip or two listen up... 

ONE- fry up some real bacon and let it hang on a paper towel once done.... 

TWO- please 4 the love of all that is good, saute those onions!!! (I would just throw them onto the leftover bacon fat and saute' from there) once the onions are translucent toss in the garlic and let it do its thang (watch it carefully so the garlic doesn't burn).... 

Three- if you Hispanic I know you have a little store bought Sofrito in the fridge (if you as blessed as I am, you'll have some of Wella's in a butter container or glass olive jar on hand) any who- toss a small spoonful of it into your onion mix, a pinch or two of some dry herbs (use common sense) and let it  saute... 

Four- Once that's done, toss the onion mix back to the pot, throw your sliced potatoes to the party and let them catch some flava -flave (I learned to throw in like 3 more potatoes to the recipe, if you are into a broth fest than use as many potatoes as the recipe asks)..

Five- b/cuz me and little man love spice I throw my hot Publix brand (it's the best) sausage to the mix and also add a tbs of red chili flakes - toss it all together for about 2 minutes,  then add all the wet ingredients.  Also, I add a mountain of the Kale (at least 4 cups, if u want 2 get crazy like me go for 5.. since it wilts away I don't see it being a big deal.....Besides I'm trying to add as much green to little mans belly as possible)...

Six - let the soup do what it does till the potatoes are tender and what I did was take a potato masher and gave it a mash or two for some thickness. (It's been record cold in the FL these past couple days and I wanted to get cheesy and make this nice hot green filled soup for me and my boy on a cold Sunday night so for the sake of my picture perfect day I wanted the soup a little heartier than brothy so I also added about a tbs of Wondra (thickener).  
This was our only course along with some garlic bread sticks and it was a freakin HIT!!! 
Enjoy!

reviews.review_text: This soup is a good base, but the directions are a bit unclear and changing a few things around makes it better.<br/><br/>Season (I used salt, pepper, cajun seasoning, and garlic powder) and brown hot Italian sausage (removed from casing), onion (only used half of a medium onion and gave it a spin in the food processor), four slices of bacon (cut into slivers with shears), and garlic (doubled the amount and put in food processor with onion) in soup pot<br/><br/>Drain (to prevent the soup from being too greasy)<br/><br/>Add chicken broth (I used 48oz of chicken broth instead of broth+water) and potatoe (1.5lbs with the skin left on, cut in half lengthwise and then cut both halves lengthwise again before slicing to about 1/4in) to pot.  Return sausage, onion, bacon, and garlic and stir<br/><br/>Cook on medium heat until potatoes are done<br/><br/>Taste and season if needed<br/><br/>Simmer for another 10 minutes<br/><br/>Turn to low heat<br/><br/>Add kale and heavy cream (bout 1/2 to 3/4c because 1 cup was too much)<br/><br/>Simmered until kale wasn't too crunchy

Oh...Ma...Ga!!! This soup was fantastic!! I made it today for lunch and DH said it was BETTER than OG's! I used hot Italian sausage, removed from casings, crumbled and browned on the stove. Even though I drained the grease, there was still quite a bit so there was an orange tint to the soup but this did not detract from the wonderful flavor at all. Next time, I may put the cooked sausage on paper towels and blot well to remove more of the grease. I used 2 "stalks" of Kale roughly chopped (excluding the stem), and the rest of the ingredients exactly as stated except I used the Wal-mart brand real bacon bits in a can since they didn't have the OM brand. Terrific!! Thank you for what is already a new family favorite!!
UPDATE: I've made this recipe countless times since I found it and it has been outstanding each and every time. I recently did it in my 7 quart crockpot (adjusting the recipe for more servings) and it was outstanding cooked that way as well. When making in the crockpot, if you slice some of your potatoes thinner, those potatoes practically disintegrate making for a slightly thicker broth, while the thicker sliced potatoes provide substance. It was a very nice change of pace for this already perfect recipe. Once I added the sausage and bacon about 2/3 of the way into the cooking time, the pre-cooked sausage also got more and more tender the longer it simmered. I put the chopped kale in the pot on top of the soup about 30 minutes before serving without mixing it in and it essentially steamed the kale leaving it a lovely bright green color that really made for a beautiful bowl of soup. Thanks again for one of my family's most favorite recipes!

reviews.review_text: I love this recipe, but I mostly only use it as a rough outline so I can make my own version! My boyfriend said the Olive Garden Zuppa Toscana is his favorite soup, and since I'm such a great cook ;p he wanted me to make it for him sometime. But there's one thing I said I would have to do, and that was--make it vegan. I'm a proud vegan and so far he's loved every meal I've made (except for the broccoli), so I thought this would be super easy! and guess what?! It was. All I had to do was replace any animal product with vegan alternatives. For the sausage I use Tofurkey's Italian Sausage, which he says does not even taste like fake meat. I've used it in pastas and of course hotdogs. I browned the sausage in coconut oil, which works fantastic because it catches all the spiciness in the sausage and gives it a wonderful kick. For the chicken broth I obviously used vegetable broth, which works perfectly, though I know many omnis who think there is no way you can make a great soup without that beef or chicken base (*cough* chef at my work *cough, cough*). I just sincerely disagree with their sentiments though :) For the heavy whipping cream I use canned coconut milk, it is pretty much the same consistency as whipping cream and it worked wonderfully. As for the bacon bits i just omitted any alternative to that as I don't real care for imitation bacon. So that's my version of this soup! I hope someone would be willing to give it a try! Perhaps you're an omni looking to dabble into vegetarianism, you can just replace the meat with tofurky! Or if you're a vegetarian looking into veganism then really give it a try! You'll be glad you did, cheese and milk products can be just as damaging to animal suffering, if not more, than the slaughter industries. It's also a very environmentally friendly way to live. There are so many benefits to cutting your animal and animal product consumption, but the first step, I believe, is to discover the facts and realities on your own. Do some research, start with your most basic questions on veganism, animal suffering, and how reducing your carbon footprint can be just as easy as changing the food you buy. I believe every effort counts, no matter how small the steps! PEACE and LOVE

attributes.source_text: catches all the spiciness in the sausage and gives it a wonderful kick

reviews.review_text: This is a fantastic base recipe.  Full disclosure, I have never had this at the Olive Garden, so I was never aiming for a taste memory.  I follow the basic recipe, with a slight change in order of of cooking.  I crisp up 3 pieces of bacon, and set them aside on paper towels, and then REALLY brown a half a pound of spicy Italian sausage in the bacon grease.  I remove the sausage and add the onions to the grease and fond that has developed, and get a good color on the onions before adding the garlic for a minute, and then the potatoes.  I add one quart of low sodium stock, and put the sausage back in, and simmer until the potatoes are soft, at which point I mash a bit of the potatoes to thicken the soup.  If it seems too thick, I will add a little water, but that has only happened one time.  I easily double the greens (I've used both kale and Swiss chard, I imagine spinach would be fine too), maybe even triple, I've never used less than 5 cups of chopped whatever greens.  At the last minute, I add half a cup of heavy cream. It is so delicious, and easy, and I can cram a boatload of greens into my son in the process.  Thank you for the recipe!

reviews.review_text: WOW. I'm a pretty good cook and soups are my favorite...and this will be made again in my household because it blew me and the family away. This was my first time making it but I still had no problem making a few tweaks. I sliced the potatoes into 1/4 inch slices and then quartered them, leaving the skins on. Another reviewer said they add ribbons and texture, and that person is correct. I cooked my sausage first and then removed the grease. Sausage flavor is great, but I didn't want to drown out the more delicate flavors. The bacon was up next, but I kept the drippings and added a pad of butter because...butter. I replaced 1/2 of the water with Marsala wine. Sounds crazy but the flavor depth will have you burning your mouth as you snorkelpork this ambrosia. I used Chard instead of Kale as it's more tender. I like my soups a bit more velvety, so I doubled the flour and whisked it into the cream. I added it once the potatoes were done so it could simmer for 15 minutes. With the cream I added 3/4 of a cup of freshly shredded Romano cheese because it's my favorite, and creamy soups are besties with cheese. All together this Italian nectar was perfect and just made my top 5 list for soups. Buon Appetito!

reviews.review_text: I loved this soup at the Olive Garden so when I found the recipe here I couldn't wait to try it. I made it per this recipe except for a couple of things: I pealed and then shred the sausage in to the soup pot I was going to use and cooked the sausage with a little bit of water while continuously stirring instead of putting it in the oven. It seemed faster to me. Then I removed the cooked sausage from the pot and continued with the recipe. I used fresh bacon instead of the bacon bits. I bought a small package of fresh bacon, trimmed off the fat and put enough pieces to cover a large plate (1 layer at a time) in the microwave for 2 1/2 - 3 minutes. Removed the layer and placed on another plate with paper towels to drain. Once cooled I sliced it in long strips and then cut them in small squares. It was delicious and my daughter agreed that it tasted just like the Olive Garden's. I served it with garlic bread sticks. Thanks Cycle Michael!!

reviews.review_text: Oh my gawd! This soup was freaking awesome!  I LOVED LOVED LOVED it!!!!!!!!!  As if this recipe needs another 5 star rating I'm giving it one anyway.  I don't know why I haven't made this soup sooner.  It is beyond easy to make, and it is spot on as far as flavor goes to the Olive Garden soup.  Every time I have every been to the Olive Garden restaurant I always have a cup of this soup instead of the salad.  I have been craving this soup for so long but haven't been to their restaurant in a long time so I figured I would make it at home after seeing the reviews for this recipe.  I am so glad that I did, and wish I would have made it sooner. I was tempted to use the hot italian sausage but that will have to wait until after our baby is born as most spicy stuff towards the evening gives me heartburn.  But I'm sure I'll be making this again and again and again.  Everyone loved it!  Thank you for a new soup to put in the rotation during the colder months.

I've tried this in the restaurant years ago, I've tried this recipe sans bacon because I didn't have any before and it was very good as is on food.com. But I want to put this recipe in my soup repertoire. Now that I'm a lot older and have to watch what I eat more closely I followed this recipe but made some substitutions. I added more broth for flavor (Trader Joe's low sodium is only 90 mg per cup serving), omitted the water, used half and half instead of heavy cream, used turkey Italian sausage & bumped up the amount potatoes (2large & 2small the extra potatoes add a bit more texture), onions g2) and kale (as much as will fit in the liquid I have). Because the turkey and half&half are a little on the lean side I did add about one tablespoon of Amish butter to sauté onions. I REALLY love the original recipe and I really love good food but I have to also try to be healthy as well so substitutions it had to be. ??

Great recipe! Exactly like OG's when made as written. I've made from 4X to 6X the original recipe for the potlucks I've attended, with no ill effects from giganticising it. I've recently taken to trying to lower the fat content by substituting half and half (on the second go around) and low-fat Coffeemate non-dairy creamer (for the 3rd try) in place of the heavy cream. The flavor remains good, but the consistency is definitely less rich. If you'd like to have a rich soup with less guilt, go with the half and half. If huge fat reduction with a good flavor is your goal, try the low-fat Coffeemate. They even have a fat-free version; but I haven't tried that. (Perhaps someone else knows whether the new fat-free half and half would work.) I have used the Ready Bacon from Costco each time and simply whirl the pre-cooked bacon in my food processor until it is finely chopped. My compliments to Cycle Michael for a fabulous recipe :-).

attributes.source_text: for the potlucks I've attended

reviews.review_text: Oh Heavenly Day! Nothin' like an Olive Garden fix 100 miles from the nearest one! I've made this twice (in the same week!) now and added extra potatoes each time to make it a bit heartier. 2nd time I used Yukon Golds as that's what I had & they were great too! Used leftover bacon from BLT's night before & just crumbled it. Also used spinach I'd frozen from my garden as neither kale nor swiss chard are available this far away from anywhere. (about 1 cup-which shatters into lovely small pieces if you squish the bag before it thaws) I was a little nervous as it seemed to turn the soup quite green when I first dumped it in. But that began to clear some very quickly & once I added the cream it looked 'normal' again. I've reheated it up to twice (absolute longest it's lasted lol) with flavor & texture just as awesome as fresh out of the pot! Will be making this & devouring it for many years to come!

YUMMY!! This is really close to the real thing. I added a ? teaspoon of red pepper flakes when I was saut?ing the sausage. I like to use red pepper flakes rather than use hot Italian sausage because hot Italian sausage would give the soup an unappealing reddish color. Plus, certain spices release more flavor when they are saut?ed. I used the one pot cooking method as soon as the sausage was cooked, I removed it and set it aside. I saut?ed the onions and the garlic in the same pot till the garlic was aromatic and the onions had softened some. I then added 3 cut up russet potatoes with the skins intact, 3 cups broth and 3 cups water and simmered till the potatoes were tender. I lightly mashed the potatoes in the pot with a potato masher to create a little more body to the soup. I added 2? cups of packed chopped kale and 1 cup of heavy cream towards the end and heated the soup over low heat till it reached serving temperature.

reviews.review_text: I'll admit that at first I was a bit skeptical for this recipe because copy cats hardly ever come out as good as you'd hope.  But I have absolutely no complaints at all for this recipe and I am a very hard person to please.  I crave this soup so often and it is the only reason I go to OG.  This recipe is the real deal.  When I made this I doubled it so I have a lot of soup left over.  I did change a couple things in the recipe, though.  I used half hot Italian sausage and half mild, but i used ground sausage to save the trouble of cutting it all up (I'm glad I did)  Then when I cooked the sausage, I cooked it in a big pot and had 5 slices of bacon cooking with it (only for flavor)  As soon as the sausage was fully cooked I put it in a paper towel to take out all the nasty grease (boy was there a lot)  Then I began on the broth which consisted of a chicken bouillon cube, 10 cups of water, 2 cups of heavy whipping cream, 2 bunches of chopped kale, and 6 potatoes (cubed and peeled).  Then I added the meat into the pot of broth.  After test tasting it a few times I realized it was missing a certain flavor.  So I added a few dashes of salt, ground pepper, a little oregano, 4 cloves of garlic and some onion.  But it still needed something else.  So I went through all my spices and found the flavor.  Fennel seeds.  Use very very sparingly.  I only put a couple of seeds into the soup.  Then I just let it cook on medium for about 45 minutes.  When it was does I extremely surprised at how good it was!  If you like Zuppa Toscana then make this recipe.  I promise you won't be disappointed!

I have never had this soup at Olive Garden, but it sounded good enough to try from all it's favorable reviews.   I am SO glad I did.   It's just delicious and my kids LOVED it.  I think the (8 ounce) notation next to the "cans of chicken broth" is off, however.   Normal cans of broth are more than 8oz -- I think.   I ended up adding more like 28 oz of broth and it was just fine.   The Kale was interesting for me.   I didn't have experience with this green before and I thought it would wilt up like spinach, so I didn't cut the pieces very small.   It didn't wilt much at all, so I was left with large chunks of this very durable stuff in the soup.   It was like I was eating leaves straight from the yard debris bin!   Next time, I would either chop the Kale up very small or use Spinach instead.  And I used real bacon, sauted up with the onion.  The rest of the recipe is worth repeating just as it is.   Many compliments on this one!

attributes.source_text: my kids LOVED it

reviews.review_text: I have now made this soup twice, The first time just as stated, It is close but not quite there. The soup is lacking because it has tooo much water and canned chicken broth does not lend much flavor to anything. Also there are no seasonings in this recipe to develop a deep rich flavor. Here is a step to develop some flavor, Sautee the onions with 1/2 stick of butter until translucent then add the garlic minced until the onions start to carmelize. Remove and set aside. In the pan add 1 tablespoon of olive oil and cook the sausage (removed from casings) until brown. Remove sausage from pan and deglaze the pan with 1 to 1-1/2 cup of white wine and reduce to 1/2 cup. In the stock pot pour in 64oz of CHICKEN STOCK and 3 cups of water and bring to a boil and boil the potato cubes with the stock and add the onion / sausage to stock when potatos are cooked and follow the recipe as normal. PS DO NOT USE THE BACON>>>>>

items.description: This recipe comes from the restaurant "Brennan's" located in New Orleans. No one has to know how simple and quick it is.  I posted this recipe exactly as it was in the book, however, if you like a little "heat" please feel free to add some cayenne pepper to taste.
instructions: Combine the seasonings and coat chicken breasts.
In large saute pan melt half of the butter and cook chicken over medium heat for about 7 to 8 minutes, turning once.
Pour the cream into the skillet and lower the heat.
Simmer for several minutes, stirring until the sauce thickens then add the remaining butter.
When butter is melted place chicken breasts on four plates and top with the sauce.

reviews.review_text: I've been avoiding this recipe because it sounded too simple to be outstanding.  Now I have to join the list of 5 star reviewers! It's so easy it would make an ideal dinner party dish for an inexperienced cook!  I used 2 large chicken breasts, halved, and this made 4 reasonable sized serves.  While I halved the amount of chicken, I did not reduce the amount of sauce.  However, I only used 1/2 teaspoon salt and, as I didn't have chili powder, I substituted 1 teaspoon mild paprika and a scant 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper.  Next time I'll increase the amount of sauce by 1/2 again and try it with the chilli powder (now I see other reviewers have said it doesn't make the dish too hot)!  I served this with Boxerwing's Frizzled Cabbage (with caraway seeds) and green beans and sliced red pepper, steamed and buttered.

This truly deserves more than 5 stars!! We truly enjoyed this dish. There were alot of mmm's all around! After reading all 130 reviews, I only made minor changes to it... I left salt amount as stated, doubled everything else and added 1 tsp of black pepper and 1/8 tsp of crushed red pepper. I had 4 huge boneless, skinless chicken breast and it was enough seasoning to coat them well. I let them "marinate" in the frig for about an hour. I used the whole 1/4 of unsalted butter to cook chicken in. I cooked the chicken on med/med high heat till done and removed from skillet. I used a pint of heavy cream to make the sauce. Cooked on med high heat till sauce was thick enough. Served with linguine and green peas. I have already been asked to make again next week. I enjoyed the seasoning so much that I now have extra already made up to use for the next time and on other meats. Thank you so much for this wonderful recipe!!

reviews.review_text: Being on my own for dinner tonight, I reduced the recipe to a serving for one.  I used a boneless skinless chicken breast *half* and quartered the rest of the ingredients (1/4 t salt, 3/8 t chili pwdr, 3/8 t onion pwdr, 1/2 t garlic pwdr, 2 T butter, 1/8 c cream).  I used kosher salt and the end result did not taste too salty.  I ended up using a little iodized salt at the table.  I'm also always looking for ways to use my smokey paprika and added 1/8 t of that.  I cut up the chicken into strips.  I wasn't sure whether to remove the chicken before adding the cream, but I did, and I think I guessed right.  This is delicious and quick & easy when you're one and don't feel like going to alot of trouble.  I'll make it for my family, too. It's a fantastic low carb dish!  Thanks for posting it Luby!

reviews.review_text: SO GOOD!  I had to use bone in chicken breasts since that was all I had and I was frankly too darn lazy to debone them :)   But only needed to cook longer, I pulled the skin off, dredged them in the spices, per the recipe (with a little shake of cayenne per some other reviewers' suggestions)and then set them in the skillet on med in the melted 2 tbs butter and covered them - had to add another 2 tbs about half way thru cooking time because the skillet was super dry looking, definitely could see and smell all the wonderful spices. Total cooking was about 20-30 mins, just kept checking the doneness.  This sauce was so rich, reminded us of a demi glace, so yummy!  I served it over penne rigate which was perfect since the ridges grabbed the sauce beautifully.  I was only serving two and the sauce was just enough for us with a little left over.  If you are serving four, I would highly recommend doubling the sauce and adding some extra spices maybe?  We'll definitely be making this again, thanks, Luby!

reviews.review_text: I made this for dinner the other night, but didn't eat any of it myself.  So I asked my husband to rate the dish, and he would give it 3.7 stars (very specific, I know...so I rounded up to 4). I asked him to explain a little more.  He mentioned that the meal was good, but it wasn't to the point where he just can't stop himself from eating more.   He said the dish looked as if it would have a very intense and powerful flavor just based on the coloring and the coating on the chicken.  But he was surprised that the flavor was fairly mild.  I served the chicken over egg noodles.  There was enough sauce to get by, but I can see how some people might like to double the amount in order to really coat any pasta they might be serving with the chicken.  My husband took the leftovers for lunch the next day.  I asked about the taste again, and he said that it probably tasted a little better the next day.  As we know, some dishes do taste better the next day!

reviews.review_text: My family went wild over this recipe even after I made the low-fat substitutions that Luv2Cook2 said she made.  Also, I used split breasts with the bone in and removed the skin because this was what I had on hand. I doubled the spices so I would have enough. Then browned the chicken in a large cast iron skillet sprayed with olive oil.  I then covered the skillet and put it in a 350 degree oven for 45 minutes.  After the breasts  were done, I added 1 cup of fat-free Half and HAlf (doubled that ingredient too) and finished it off on top of the stove.  My sauce was maybe not as thick as it would have been with heavy cream, but it was delicious over the chicken and rice I served along with it.    The chili powder flavor was delicate and not too strong.  We were very pleased with the delightful flavor of this recipe.  I will be making this again and next time I will use the boneless breasts because it will be quicker to make.  Thank you so much for sharing this recipe.

reviews.review_text: Swoon!  This is worth planning a WW week around it (remember, a portion of sauce is only 2 Tablespoons; anything over that eats into your dessert/snack allowance).  We had monster Perdue boneless skinless chicken breasts, so we used only 2 and created 2 fillets from each breast, which was the perfect portion; next time I might try pounding them gently to create uniform thickness, but mine were okay as is.  The recipe made just enough seasoning mix (I wouldn't change a thing).  The chicken pieces filled my 12" skillet, so if you need more than 4 portions, I recommend 2 skillets, which can be managed easily.  I let the cream simmer for an additional 30 minutes until the sauce pulled away from the pan, but it didn't thicken up to my satisfaction until I added the final butter.  This recipe cries to be served with rice. This recipe required no discussion about the rating; it goes directly into my Best of 2014 cookbook!  Made for Name That Ingredient Tag Game.

Loved the ease of preparation and the final result even if I did not make it exactly as stated. I am sure it is fantastic made as stated but I had to change some things due to what I had in the kitchen.  I sliced my chicken into strips, coated it the spices stated in the recipe, adding 1 T each of flour and seasoned breadcrumbs and 1 tsp. each of cajun seasoning and finely crushed dried oregano.  I subbed 1 can low fat evap milk for cream and left out the last bit of butter and added some Parmesan cheese at the end (thinkng I could also have used some low fat cream cheese for thickening instead of the Parmesan).  I didn't even have any good Parmesan, just the green can that the kids love so much.   Thanks for a really great quick and tasty recipe.

Being that I am from new Orleans and grew up on new Orleans food, this is only a new Orleans style recipe... I cooked this recipe expecting to taste something so different with the heavy cream and chili instead this was an imitation stewed or smothered chicken...we cook this similar dish frequently in new Orleans, with bell peppers, onions, garlic, parsley, and its breaded and fried in oil...then add water and let it simmer down to create the same dish, with a much better taste... although the flavor of this dish wasn't bad but it wasn't as rich as it could be if it was prepared differently from the recipe. I give this dish 4 stars for the variation of the new Orleans style recipe...I used chicken legs and my cooking time was longer, otherwise I followed the recipe and it was ok...I would make it again, but I would add other ingredients for a greater taste...Ive been eating this for years...

attributes.source_text: this is only a new Orleans style recipe

reviews.review_text: This didn't look like anything amazing, but due to the reviews, I tried it. I am so very glad I did- it was a huge hit. I have two children, ages 3 and 6, and for all four of us to agree on something is rare- they both gobbled this up, and DH has asked for it several times again. I used kosher salt and thought everything was just right. I have made it quite a few more times, and as with all leftovers (I always make extra) I have started playing a bit- I have added a good fragrant sweet curry powder instead of chili powder, and that was good, and also have stirred in a bit of peanut butter- a tremendous hit, especially with the children. If you are on the fence, please make this- something so simple and so delicious in such a short period of time is a gift in a busy household.

attributes.source_text: they both gobbled this up
DH has asked for it several times again
for all four of us to agree on something is rare

reviews.review_text: After reading a lot of the reviews, I decided to adjust the recipe to a spice level I thought my family would enjoy. So I started by reducing every thing knowing that I could add more spices if necessary at the end. I thought this recipe was excellent as a jumping off point. Just for my own reference - reduced salt to 1/4 tsp, used 1 tsp of chili, garlic & onion powder. Reduced butter to 2 tbsp plus 1 Tbsp EVOO, used 5% cream and increased cream to 1 Cup, thickened with 2-3 tsp cornstarch at the very end. The flavour is delicious but each cook has to know enough to adjust the seasonings to their own liking. The Peanut Gallery all said 5* and they loved it. This is going in our "favourites book". Thx Luby!

I'm giving this 5 stars because it was definitely a hit, not just to me but also to my boyfriend! I'm visiting my boyfriend for three months and I've been cooking for him since I got here. Most of the recipes I've been using were taken from here and I must stay I am very happy I have bumped into this. My boyfriend only cooks bolognese and frozen food from Marks & Spencer when I'm not around yet when he tasted this, he asked how I made it and if I could write down the directions in cooking haha! Have made this for lots of time now. :P<br/><br/>By the way, I didn't have butter so I used margarine instead but God, it was very scrumptious!! Thanks for the recipe, Luby :) xxx

attributes.source_text: not just to me but also to my boyfriend
when he tasted this, he asked how I made it and if I could write down the directions in cooking

reviews.review_text: Excellent bones to the recipe. It absolutely won't be as red as in the picture at the heading of the recipe. I mix it up a bit: A little less salt Saute thin sliced onion when cooking the chicken. I add a little bit of smoked paprika and or paprika (go easy but experiment to see what works). Also, depending on how potent or pungent your chili is, you might add more. Any boneless chicken works. We like thighs but we also use breasts cut in half. You might reduce cooking time if not using full breasts. I've added mushroom I've sauteed in a different pan near end of cooking and the family loved it but I didn't as I try to like mushrooms but actually detest them. Try the recipe. You can make it your own signature dish if you start with the ingredients and process as originally described.

I am just adding comments here, no rating.  I used this recipe as a starting point for my meal.  I used melted cream cheese, 1/2 cup milk and 1/2 stick of butter as the sauce (heavy cream does not reheat very well and I intended to make more than 1 meal out of this dish), lightly pan fried the seasoned chicken and then baked in the oven at 350 for 15 minutes.  I really enjoyed the chicken and would give that dish 4 stars overall.  I did not think that it would be fair to judge this recipe against the one I made since I deviated quite a bit from the original.
Next time when I am not going to make enough to have leftovers I will try it with the heavy cream as directed.
Thanks for the ideas, Luby

I'm giving it 5 stars because it is so easy and very moist. I enjoyed the flavor, but I do have a few notes.

I added only a pinch of salt which was plenty. I felt at the end of cooking I could always add a bit more salt if needed, but it definitely was NOT. A small pinch was plenty for me.

As you noted, I did add cayenne, but I like heat, so I did do that and I was glad I did.

Make sure to use Heavy cream, it will thicken naturally, half and half or milk will NOT, and using UNSALTED butter to me is important. As I said you can always add more.

For those who said the chicken took longer to cook. Yes, every piece of chicken regardless of weight can vary in thickness and therefore take longer. I pounded mine, just lightly in the center to make it a bit more even. I didn't flatten it however, just a light couple of pounds to make mine even. I cooked as you said, probably 6-8 minutes for me per side until golden brown before I added the cream, the chicken was close to being done at that point. You just got to adjust cooking time according to how thick your chicken is.

I didn't find more sauce was necessary. I enjoyed it as is. I thought the nice glaze it made was just enough.

I served mine over a yellow rice which I added some cilantro to, thin sliced the breast and laid it on top and then added chopped black olives as a garnish. Served it with sauteed green beans and shallots for a very easy dinner.

It was very enjoyable and everyone liked it. Salty was the only thing I thought was off. But again, that can be a personal taste.

Nice recipe!
Thx
kim

attributes.source_text: very moist
I did add cayenne, but I like heat, so I did do that and I was glad I did
for a very easy dinner

reviews.review_text: This recipe is what made me become a member of this site. I was over my aunt's house visiting for a week when she made this for me. I could not believe how great it tasted. I didn't want to try it at first thinking that this would be to spicy because of the chili powder. I don't do much more than mild sauce let alone chili powder, but it ended up blowing me away. I had to join and try this for my parents and siblings. I didn't have chicken breasts so I used tenderloins instead. Since there was 5 of us and they were rather small I cooked 15 tenderloins. I only doubled the ingredients and it tasted the same. Next time I might not add as much of the salt though. Thank you so much for opening my mouth to great food done right.

This is a REALLY GOOD dish!  i pretty much followed "mums the word's" technique except i cut the chicken breasts into strips and i doubled the spices.  i found that when i put the strips in the plastic bag to shake and coat, there wasn't nearly enough spice, so i had to double it.  i also added about a half tsp of cayenne....yummy!  i also upped the cream to 1 cup (the sauce is OUTSTANDING), i found that "simmer for several minutes" for me worked out to about 15...i then added about a tsp of cornstarch to thicken it a bit more.  i served this dish with rice...oh my GOD!  the way the rice soaks up the sauce...yeah!  definitely keeping it in the rotation.  thank so much for a delicious dish!!

Quick,easy and flavorful! I pounded 2 chicken breasts a bit flatter and cut into 2 inch pieces as another reviewer suggested,had enough for 2 adults and 1 child.The chicken was so tender and the sauce is awesome served over rice.I was worried it would be too salty and left out the salt completely(you can always salt to taste at the end anyway)I think someone else suggested leaving out the butter added at the end and I think I will next time too.I found it was great before and it did add quite a bit of oil to the sauce

I will definetely make this again as both my fussy eaters ate it all up and it got 2 thumbs up from my little one(the biggest critic!)Thanks for this recipe Luby, it's chicken gold in my opinion:)

attributes.source_text: The chicken was so tender
both my fussy eaters ate it all up
it got 2 thumbs up from my little one

reviews.review_text: I have to say I was very excited and had high hopes for this meal because of all the raving reviews. I went ahead and doubled the sauce as most of the reviews suggested. My family and I were not too impressed. This was just OK. The chicken turned out extremely moist and tender and that was about all we were raving about. We felt the sauce lacked in flavor. I did pour this dish over a pound of linguine and cut the chicken into thin strips before cooking them. Maybe the pasta took away from the sauce flavor??? I will try to make this again and next will not use it over pasta, and will also double the seasonings and probably add some more of my own. Thanks for sharing this recipe though.

attributes.source_text: The chicken turned out extremely moist
extremely moist and tender

reviews.review_text: We really liked this.  I did cut the salt to half and I tripled the spice coating since I used a whole bag of Trader Joe's chicken tenderloins.  The tenderloins worked very well with this dish and I sauted them in batches and added them back to the pan at the end with the sauce. I doubled the sauce and used 1/2 and 1/2. Cream next time! Served it with roasted asparagus and spaghetti and French bread slices.  My father ate with us and said it was fantastic.  He is a foodie so it was a BIG compliment. One of my sons needed to scrape off some of the spice coating as it was a bit spicy for him. The scraping was sufficient for him. It has a little "Kick" which pleased the rest of us. Thanks Luby!

reviews.review_text: Ok, Betty Crocker has decreased their boxes of cake mix to 15.25 ounces (but the price has stayed the same- go figure). Rather than going with the 1/2 cup of oil, I went with 100 milliliters which is about midway between 1/2 and 1/3 of a cup. I rolled them to about 1.5 inches, let the balls rest for about five minutes, and then I rolled them in my hand which had a scoop of powdered sugar in it. When complete, they looked like Russian Tea Cakes and I placed them on a foil- lined cookie sheet and baked them at 350 degrees F. My oven had been acting squirrely lately but I baked them for 9.5 minutes until the center JUST was done (it was slightly crumby but not runny). The only problem I ran into was room on my sheet. Next time I will bake half at a time. My measurements yielded 21 cookies about 2.5 to 3 inches in diameter. One other problem, they are randomly disappearing while they are cooling- next time I'll have to double the batch so they can make it out of the kitchen! :oD Thank you Karen=^..^= for a super recipe.

attributes.source_text: it was slightly crumby but not runny

reviews.review_text:
I made these this morning to bring to work and they were by far, the easiest cookies that I ever made.  I am now home from work with a totally empty container!  It's a good thing that I brought a copy of the recipe with me because several of the girls wanted copies.  Here are some of the notes that I made about this recipe:  August 22, 2008: 
1) My batch made 26 cookies. 
2) I used my Pampered Chef cookie scoop and Pampered Chef Stoneware cookie sheets. 
3) Roll all the cookies out first and place on the cookie sheets to "dry"; when all dough is used up, then roll the balls into the confectioner's sugar and place them back on the cookie sheets. 
4) Cool the cookies about 10 minutes on the cookie sheets before removing to the wire racks and they will stay together better. 
5) My bake time was exactly 10 minutes. 
6) I did not add the 1 teaspoon of vanilla; I stuck to the original recipe. 
7) Very easy and the cookies are very pretty.
I have also posted a couple of pictures.  This will definitely be a recipe that I use again and again as I think the possibilities are endless.  I think next time I want to try the strawberry cake mix like was mentioned in another review.  They, too, sound heavenly!  Thank you very much for posting this awesome recipe!

attributes.source_text: I am now home from work with a totally empty container!
several of the girls wanted copies

reviews.review_text: Wow these are good!  I don't buy cake mix so I didn't have any on hand or any other sweets either when DH said he wanted something sweet, we were celebrating his earning his martial arts black belt today so I decided to make him some cookies and I'd been wanting to try this recipe.  Well I made my own "cake mix" from the Hershey's chocolate cake recipe and stopped at the dry ingredients, then continued with the rest of this recipe.  On top of making that substitution I only made half a batch so it took me a little longer cause of all the ingredients I had to mix plus cutting down ingredient portions.  I used canola oil instead of vegetable, and let them rest a few minutes after rolling before dipping in sugar as suggested, once a little dry I dipped them first in Bakers sugar, then in confectioners sugar - this kept it from absorbing all the pretty confectioners sugar, so they turned out beautiful as well as delicious!  Bake time was exactly 8 minutes for me on a cookie sheet covered by parchment paper.  Thank you for a gem of a recipe - EXCELLENT!  Even with all those alterations and potentials for failure - they are DELICIOUS!

attributes.source_text: we were celebrating his earning his martial arts black belt today

reviews.review_text: I tried these out tonight and they turned out pretty good. I had the problem opposite to most review, my cookies didn't spread out into a cookie shape. I followed the directions exactly rolled them into balls then in the powder sugar with no problem and put them in the oven.  Although they did spread a little, but not much, they stayed pretty thick, which led to them having a cake like texture in the middle b/c they were so thick. If they had spread out and baked they would have been the perfect cookies. That was the only thing, other than that they are delicious and did look beautiful when I took them out of the oven.  Only took 10 minutes to bake. I also did fold in some coconut flakes into the dough at the end.  I thought they were pretty good and my DH just gobbled them up and commented they are the perfect cross between a really good cookie and a very dense cake. I would make these again but I would definitely make the dough balls smaller so that they spread out into cookies. As far as the powdered sugar being absorbed, i did have  a bit of a problem with doing that by hand, so once i made the balls i rolled them in powdered sugar in a small plate and very delicately transfered them to the cookie sheet.  Overall, good idea, great taste. I'll have to try again to make them better. Thanks for sharing!

attributes.source_text: my DH just gobbled them up
a very dense cake

reviews.review_text: This is a really nice easy recipe. The 'cookies' come out with kind of a fudgey-brownie texture with a nice sugar crunch on the outside. My brownie loving husband approved. It was also a great recipe to do with my young son who enjoyed rolling the balls in the sugar for me.<br/><br/>Since there are plenty of reviews already I wanted to add that this recipe made about two dozen cookies, since I didn't see that listed anywhere. Also wanted to add a tip for those saying that all the sugar gets absorbed while baking. My first batch came out exactly like that, and I had let the dough balls 'dry' for a few minutes like the author suggested. The second batch I rolled into balls and then had to leave for about 20 minutes to attend to family matters. Well, it turned out that this was actually the magic trick because that second batch just came out picture-perfect. This recipe is officially going into my box!

attributes.source_text: kind of a fudgey-brownie texture
a nice sugar crunch on the outside
My brownie loving husband approved

reviews.review_text: WOW - FANTASTIC! I had a white cake mix on hand and my cookies taste like sugar cookies. I baked them for 10 minutes in my oven (Maytag) and they are perfect. I made them  slightly larger than 1" and got 42 cookies. They are lightly browned on the bottom and chewy in the middle. It is very important to let the cookies cool and flatten on the baking sheet before you remove them. I placed my baked cookies on paper towels (instead of wire rack) on my counter top to decorate (easy cleanup.) I placed some M&M's mini baking chips on top of each cookie lightly pressing them into the chewy middle and used red sprinkles. I read an earlier review about placing a jelly bean in the middle of the cookie for Easter and using the devil's food mix and orange icing for Halloween. Great ideas! You could use food coloring to make red & green cookies for Christmas, red for valentines day, green for St. Pat's Day... there are no limits to this recipe. Karen, thank you so much for sharing this great recipe!!

attributes.source_text: my cookies taste like sugar cookies
chewy in the middle

reviews.review_text: Yum! Husband liked them- I incorporated your tips- let the cookies sit about 10-15 min after I rolled them in a ball- and then rolled them in the conf. sugar- They stayed frosted. And I only used the 1/2 oil that the original recipe suggested. Very yummy, and easy and quick to make. I baked them about 12 min at 370- I originally coooked them for 10 min but they were too wet in the middle so I put them back in for another cuple minutes or so. Delicious and easy. Thanks for the recipe Karen!  *** I made them again, this time with Strawberry.  Fabulous!!  Great taste.  I put them in at 370 degrees for 12 min but they seemed a little wet (but not bad) so I ended up putting the next batch in at 350 for 14 minutes..... the puffed more but looked more toasted on the edges.  I think net time I would meet in the middle-  like 360 degrees for 13 minutes........... also, I sprinkle a little confectioners sugar on after I pull them out of the oven and that makes them look prettier.

attributes.source_text: Husband liked them
the puffed more

reviews.review_text:
These are great easy cookies. 
I had higher hopes for them regarding taste but they do satisfy the sweet tooth.
I had seen the recipe on the side of a cake mix box but never tried it. I always keep premade stuff in the pantry in case there's a craving emergency and there's nothing else to eat LOL! The recipe on the box called for 1/3 cup oil instead of 1/2 cup so I used what the box said because I liked the idea of reducing the oil, used less powdered sugar on the top too and made them in little round balls. I think the 1/2cup oil would make the batter too runny and would make the cookies not hold their shape well. They look very pretty after baked with the craked tops. 
I flattened a few of the balls with a spatula and made Ice Cream sandwiches with them YUM!
Next time I'll try adding nuts to the batter. Thank you for posting the recipe, now I can throw away the cut out of the cake mix box.

attributes.source_text: they do satisfy the sweet tooth

reviews.review_text:
Amazing cookies! I used a store brand devil's food cake mix and added half a package of dry instant vanilla pudding mix and blended that with the dry mix before putting in the other ingredients. I scooped them out with my cookie scoop and skipped the powdered sugar all together. I drizzled white chocolate on top instead. This is a keeper and next I plan to use a white mix and dip in cinnamon sugar. Then, I'm going to go exploring for other cake mix flavors - can't wait! Thanks!!
Coming back to say I made these again today with the white mix, dry pudding, and almond extract, rolled in cinnamon-sugar, and they were super! Just so everyone knows, in order for them to be soft after they cool, they should look moist in the middle when you pull them out of the oven. Definitely let them cool on the sheet a couple of minutes before you transfer to racks to cool.

attributes.source_text: in order for them to be soft after they cool
they should look moist in the middle

reviews.review_text: These cookies were incredible! I made two different types. I made devils food with pecans and chocolate chips that I rolled in the powered sugar, and also I did strawberry with White chocolate that I rolled in organic coconut sugar. Both turned out awesome. With the size I made, I got about 2 1/2 dozen per flavor. We had 6 people in the house, and these cookies are not going to survive the night, all 5 dozen. I couldn't keep them out! I did decrease the oil to 1/4 cup, that was perfect and not too oily. The sugars stayed on just fine. I baked them at 350 degrees for 12 minutes. And since I only had one cookie pan, I would throw the batter in the freezer while the other batch cooked, and it made the dough easy to handle and roll. I am going to try lemon cake mix next, and then maybe spice cake with walnuts and raisins. Good luck! I posted a couple of pics so you can see what mine looked like!

This is the only cookie that my family specifically requests at Christmas, and I'm happy to oblige! I only get 12-15 cookies out of the smaller (15.25 oz) box of cake mix, but I prefer the cookies to be bigger - they stay nice and fudgy in the middle and crinkle beautifully. I usually have to add a tad bit more oil to eliminate all the dry spots in the batter, but not much. I roll out enough cookie dough balls for two cookie sheets before I start rolling them in powdered sugar, and that's plenty of time for them to "dry" and not absorb so much of the sugar. I use the quick bake convection on my oven, and at this larger size the cookies take 7 minutes to bake (14 minutes in a regular oven). As other reviewers have mentioned, you don't have to use Devil's Food mix - I used Triple Chocolate for my latest batch and they are unbelievable!

attributes.source_text: my family specifically requests at Christmas
my family specifically requests at Christmas
