reviews.review_text: I trusted the great reviews and I am so glad I did!  I was in charge of coffee hour at church, and I made three batches of this recipe the night before.  The first I made with red velvet cake.  I made the balls just a bit smaller than an inch, and when they were cool, I sandwiched them with cream cheese frosting.  Then I followed a suggestion in another review and used yellow cake with almond extract and pecans (I made two batches of these - so good!).  Finally, I made the original fudge crinkles.  I have volunteered for coffee hours several times, and I do not think I have ever had such an enthusiastic response.  People were ga-ga over them, especially the red velvet sandwich cookies.  Four people asked me for the recipes for all the cookies, and I had to laugh when I told them how I made each type.  So easy!  So good!  And not at all expensive.  Definitely the cookie I will make when I have a crowd to feed.  Thanks!

Okay- someone needs to SLAP my hand and make me stop eating these! I'm supposed to take them to a church cookie exchange! These are very yummy. I just took a batch out of the oven. I'm getting ready to cook another batch, but this time I'm going to follow your directions and make the balls only 1". My balls were about 3" and the cookies turned out HUGE (but they're still great!) And I added a nice thick coating of powdered sugar on top of the cookies after I dredged them- they came out of the oven with a good amount of powdered sugar still on them.
Thank-you SO much for this recipe! It's so easy, and unbelievably inexpensive! I had all of the ingredients except the cake mix, so I went to the store yesterday and picked up a box of the recommended cake mix, and it was on sale for 88 cents! A batch of FABULOUS cookies for 88 cents!!
THANKS!!

reviews.review_text: I've never been a baker of cookies, but my 4 yo granddaughter loves to "help" me in the kitchen and judging from the helpful reviews and the short list of ingredients, I decided to make these with her.  They are very, very child friendly!  After we formed the balls of dough (which is very soft and oily), I let them rest for a few minutes before rolling them in the confectioners sugar.  That worked fine, but I think I'll try the suggestion of chilling them the next time.  Balls were about 1.5 in in diameter and baked in 12 minutes on the middle rack (although I rotated cookie sheets, the cookies on the one that ended up on the lower shelf for the last half of the time were too dark on the bottom). I gave these cookies 5 stars for sheer ease of making, even with a 4 yo helper but they were also delicious!

reviews.review_text:
Funny cookie story time... I made 5 different kinds of cookies for my Christmas baking this year, many more complicated recipes, lots of expensive ingredients.. made these last, as sort of an afterthought, was just curious about them. Hands down our favorite cookie! Can't get over it! Going to make more batches, adding peanut butter chips, then using the strawberry cake mix and white chocolate chips. The possibilities boggle the brain! But just as written, they are delicious! (I rolled the balls in granulated sugar) Thanks SOO much for posting this recipe!

Update: I made them with the peanut butter chips, and they were awesome, but when I made the strawberry with the white chocolate chips.. well my daughter almost cried! She said they were the best cookies EVER! (2 of her favorite things) A total hit with all who have tried them!

reviews.review_text:
Ok, These are the best cookies I ever had! I would give ten stars if I could!! My sister made the cookies from box cake mix a long time ago, but I dont remember them tasting this good, and I dont think she rolled them in powdered sugar either, which makes a big difference in the taste. I followed the directions exactly and added about a cup of peanut butter chips and my son couldnt stop eating them!! I finally had to stop him I was worried he would get sick, or worse eat them all!! lol. This will be my cookie recipe from now on, and I cant wait to try different flavors and combinations. Thank you for this extraordinary recipe!! Ok I had to edit my review because the cookies were gone in 2 days with just me and my son eating them..lol and so I had to make some more today, but I didn't have another devil's food cake mix or any other for that matter and I wanted to try these with another flavor. So what I did was look up a recipe for a vanilla cake in which I found a very easy recipe that I was able to use and I just left out the wet ingredients and used oil in place of the shortening it called for. I also made half with vanilla flavoring and rolled them in a cinnamon/sugar mixture and placed a walnut in the center of each one. The other half I used almond flavoring and put chocolate chips in them and rolled them in coconut and placed an almond in the center of each one...lol. I was getting creative. Both came out really good, but I think my favorite is the devils food cake with the powdered sugar.
I made these again today, I just love these and so easy to make!! I used the devil's food cake and rolled some in finely chopped walnuts before rolling them in the powdered sugar. I love chocolate with walnuts. Again, EXCELLENT!!

attributes.source_text: my son couldnt stop eating them
with just me and my son eating them

reviews.review_text: Very easy and so good.  I already had everything on hand.  I used Pillsbury Dark Chocolate Mix.  The only problem was it was a smaller box than the recipe, but, I did not notice until after I mixed all the ingredients.  The dough was very greasy!  I added a little over 1/4 cup of flour, but, it didn't help.  I placed them in the fridge for over an hour ( doesn't have to be that long, I just needed a break) prior to rolling in the powered sugar and they still came out great!  I noticed that the 8 min mark is the perfect time yo take them out. Oh I also baked them at 375 as suggested in the notes.  They didn't spread much even with the extra oil.  They were perfect.  The batch I let go for 10 mins tasted sorta burnt snd was not and was not as chewy later on.  These are part of my Xmas tradition now.  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: part of my Xmas tradition now

reviews.review_text: WOW!  I had no idea that such yummy cookies could be made with only a couple of ingredients!  As per "tampacountess's" suggestion, I added some chocolate chips and an instant pudding mix to my dough.  ("Yellow" cake mix + pistachio pudding mix = pale green cookies that smelled awesome while baking, & tasted even better!)  I have an electric oven, so I'd advise any other electric folks out there to keep a close eye on their batches.  Mine took a little longer than 10 minutes, I popped them out as soon as they were slightly browned at the edges.  They were very soft/gooey, so I let them stand awhile before moving them off the baking sheets.  The cookies retained a wonderfully soft, just-baked texture.  Can't wait to try these again with devil's food mix & orange icing for Halloween!  Thanks Karen! :)

attributes.source_text: very soft/gooey
very soft/gooey
wonderfully soft, just-baked texture

reviews.review_text:
I was sick the week before Christmas so I was looking for some cookie recipes that were delicious and could be made quickly.  I am so happy I tried this.  My DS and SIL loved these--they could hardly stay away from them!  
At first these seemed a little soft and the balls got a little flat as I was rolling, but after letting the dough sit for a couple of minutes they were easier to work with.  I made the balls 1 1/2 inches and baked for 8 minutes.  Next time I make these, I will follow the chef's tip and roll the balls in the powdered sugar just before baking so they look prettier.
This recipe is a winner!  I have already given out the recipe twice. I love the simplicity of these but agree with another reviewer that these would be great with white chocolate chips and/or walnuts.

attributes.source_text: My DS and SIL loved these
My DS and SIL loved these

items.label: Pork Chops Yum-Yum
items.name: Pork Chops Yum-Yum
items.description: I copied this from The Orlando Sentinel months ago and just now found it. We eat pork chops at least once a week and this is our favorite.
instructions: Brown chops on both sides.
Place in greased casserole dish.
Mix all remaining ingredients and pour over pork chops.
Bake, uncovered, at 350 for one hour.

reviews.review_text: I cooked them on the stovetop only, not in the oven. I first browned 3 or 4 average size bone-in porkchops in olive oil and butter over medium heat. Then with a paper towel dabbed out the excess oil, leaving all the yummy crunches in the skillet. I doubled recipe for the sauce mixture. After I got the chops as browned as I wanted, I poured the sauce mixture over them and covered to simmer, reducing my heat to medium-low. I flipped the chops over about every 2-3 minutes until they were done. It only took them about 8 minutes to finish cooking. Next, I removed the porkchops to our plates and thickened the remaining sauce with a little cornstarch until I got the sauce as thick as I wanted it. I used about a 1/2 tsp dissolved in a little cold water, using a whisk to stir it around while it bubbled. I spooned the sauce onto the porkchops. I got mine thick enough that it wouldn't run all over the plate ( I hate that!) Next time I will definitely make mashed potatoes with it, because the sauce will be very good on them.  Thanks Brad for the great sauce, and thanks Chef Steveo for your good suggestions! I will definitely be making this again.

attributes.source_text: until I got the sauce as thick as I wanted it

reviews.review_text: I think this is the first time I've ever had pork chops that were THIS tender! Whenever my family has pork chops, they end up being in the oven too long and drying out too much. I browned the chops first with some oil (I added lots of black pepper to the meat too) and then removed the meat and made the sauce (I doubled the amount, used brown sugar since I didn't have any honey, garlic powder instead of garlic salt, and nixed the ginger) I poured that in the same pan, heated the sauce up and added cornstarch/water to thicken it slightly. Then I poured it over the chops, put it all in the oven at 350 for 30 minutes, and basted the chops with the sauce twice in that time. They came out SO tender!! I'd say don't skimp on using the oven. It's definitely worth it, just as long as you don't bake them too long. Even my family was impressed with how tender they were! And that sauce is to die for! I'm definitely making these again (and again and again!)

attributes.source_text: pork chops that were THIS tender
They came out SO tender
Even my family was impressed with how tender they were

reviews.review_text: I had 2 very thin boneless chops and kept all the sauce ingredients the same amount.  I used low-sodium soy sauce.  Because my chops were so thin, the oven would have probably been overkill, even if I adjusted the time.  I sprinkled each chop with black pepper, browned in a bit of canola oil for 45 secs to 1 minute on each side, while I whisked the sauce ingredients in a measuring cup, then I poured the sauce over the chops in the saucepan.  I covered and simmered on medium-low for 10 minutes, turned the chops over in the sauce and covered, cooking for another 10 minutes.  I removed the chops, mixed up a slurry of 1/2 tsp of cornstarch with 1/2 tsp of cold water and whisked that into the sauce.  I added chops back in, covered the pan and cooked for another 2 to 3 minutes.  Sauce thickened up into a glaze consistency and was just the right amount for the 2 (very thin, small) chops and a couple of cups of white rice.  Very tasty, "yum yum" is highly appropriate for this recipe.  This is sweet too, but not overly sweet.  I enjoyed this immensely and hope to make it again when my bf can also try it.  Thank you Brad Beckwith for a keeper. :)  Next time when I'm not in a huge hurry to make dinner, I'll also try marinating the chops first.

attributes.source_text: This is sweet too
but not overly sweet

reviews.review_text: Hi all - This will be long because I really, really hope to figure out what I did wrong - I hope there's some smart person out there who will read all this and comment - I DO want to learn and correct.  I cooked the Pork Chops Yum Yum last night. I have NEVER ruined pork this badly before. I read almost a hundred of the reviews, decided to do stove-top like most. I bought two boneless pork loin chops about little less than 3/4 inches thick but did not brine them (maybe I should have!).  I trimmed a little of the fat and added a little pepper and sauteed off the chops in about a tablespoon of olive oil - only 2 min on each side for fear of overcooking them - HA! Boy was I wrong! I minced a clove of fresh garlic and a good teaspoon of fresh ginger, and per one reviewer, made pole-to-pole cuts of half a large yellow onion. Once the meat was sauteed I put the chops on a warm plate for a minute while I sauteed the garlic, ginger and onions for about two minutes to sweat them a little and until the garlic started to smell good - I did this on a med low flame. Then I added the tripled sauce ingredients (as per many reviewers) So, used (for triple sauce - 3/4 cup chicken broth, 3/8 cup honey, 3/8 cup regular soy sauce and 3 tablespoons ketchup all went into the saute pan with the onion/garlic mix. Also per one reviewer (the one who suggested the onions) I added 1 tablespoon of apple cider vinegar because that is a normal ingredient in most Asian sauces. I put the chops back into the saute pan, brought the sauce up to a simmer and then turned the heat down low so I only had it "burbeling" (if that is a word) and covered the pan. Per another reviewer, I turned the chops every 5 minutes for a total of 20 minutes. I pulled the chops off to a warm plate and added 1 Tablespoon cornstarch already mixed with 1 Tablespoon water. And the sauce really needed the thickener. I brought the heat up and stirred for about 4 minutes at medium heat till the sauce thickened nicely. Served the chops over rice and broccoli on the side. Now, when I tell you that I am a pretty good cook - really I am, I have NEVER had to work so hard at cutting a good piece of meat! The chops were SO TOUGH that my life partner shoved them away in disgust. I ate mine out of shame but it was really hard to cut. Okay, smart people - what did I do wrong or where did I go wrong? Was it the vinegar that toughened the meat? Was the 20 minutes (already a much-shortened cooking time) too long? The meat quality was the best I could buy from the Vons (which is Safeway out here) good meat department - I didn't skimp on the quality! The sauce was okay - nothing special or different than what I would get at a local Chinese restaurant but certainly not what most of the reviewers mentioned - just sort of middle-of-the-road okay Chinese sauce. So, I am genuinely interested in what I must have done or why the pork toughened up that badly - never in my life have I had such a tough piece of meat. Couldn't even get the steak knife through it - had to saw and saw. So, I want to learn here and would be very grateful if someone or more than one person would comment on what I should have done or where I went wrong. I DO appreciate the time and thank you all for your thoughts!<br/>Citrus1000

This recipe is going into my prized recipe binder!

Easy as pie to make, which is a definite plus.  The one huge downside is that it really smelled awful while baking.  It wasn't a stench, it was more like an overwhelming sweet smell that nearly caused me to not even try it; I nearly just put it down the disposal.  Glad I tried it, though!  

Honestly, I wasn't sure about this recipe from the beginning, so I made it as an extra thing (a post-lunch, pre-dinner experiment), as opposed to planning a full meal around it.  The next time I make this, I'll be sure to also make pork-flavored rice or noodles, something that's not at all sweet, to compliment these chops.  

If you're thinking about using this sauce as a marinade, I'd like to suggest you follow the recipe as posted.  I think that sauce used as a marinade would just be too, too sweet.  As posted, the recipe gives just the right flavor and level of sweetness.

So, to sum it all up, it's a great recipe!  Quick and easy to make.  If your taste is like mine, you'll definitely want a side dish that isn't sweet to go with these chops.

attributes.source_text: just the right flavor and level of sweetness

reviews.review_text: Started off with 2 inch and a 1/4 center-cut bone-in pork chops. Heated cast-iron skillet with vegetable oil. Seared on medium-high on both sides then on the edges to lock in flavor. Took about 5-7 minutes each side and 10 seconds on side as I rotated the chops to from side to side. I had already measured out the liquid ingredients less the ketchup. Replaced the ketchup with maple syrup. Replaced garlic salt with garlic which I grated with a microplane along with the ginger. Once the chops were properly seared, I poured mixture over chops, lowered heat to low medium and covered with a dome lid for 5 minutes on each side was plenty. Not dry, still plenty moist. Removed chops from skillet and tented with foil for 3-5 minutes. The sauce caramelized on the skillet, but some of it did separate into a sauce. Was able to salvage enough for both chops. Was pretty excellent.

attributes.source_text: Not dry
still plenty moist

reviews.review_text: This is still one of our favorite dishes. I just made them a few minutes ago. Here is my latest. I did thme on the stove top. I oiled my cast iron skillet with canola, enough to cover. Seasoned my chops with my favorite seasoning, and browned chops each side about 4 minutes. In the meantime, I mixed my other ingredients for the sauce. Which I recommend highly that you double. If you don't there is no way there will be enough sauce and you will be disappointed. I too, like another reviewer used garlic powder instead of garlic salt. I then removed chops from skillet and added more oil to cover the skillet. Put chops back in the skillet, reduced heat to medium, poured sauce over chops, covered skillet with lid, and cooked on medium for about 15-20 minutes (thin chops), turning and basting with the sauce in skillet about 3 times. Served with rice and broccoli. I love this recipe!! Thanks!

Fellow reviewers weren't kidding - this sauce absolutely rocks.  Substituted garlic powder for garlic salt and added fresh minced garlic.  Did not taste ketchupy, just mellow, salty, sweet, and ooey-gooey yummy good.  Poked two pork tenderloins, marinated overnight, and made per Chef Steveo's review, but browning the meat on all 4 sides and simmering for 30 minutes, turning meat only once.  Removed the meat to carve and added a cold water-cornstarch slurry and let the sauce simmer until desired consistency was reached.  The 30-minute mark resulted in tender, juicy pork loin.  The sauce was absolutely amazing - I'm glad I doubled it (should have quadrupled, but I didn't have enough soy sauce left to do so.  Luckily, the sauce was a tad strong for my taste, so I was able to get more out of it by diluting with a 1/3 c of water.  Served the dish in the skillet to not let any sauce go to waste, and good thing I did!  People were scraping every last bit of the sauce from the pan onto their plates, using the loin slices as a spatula head.  So much for leftovers for tomorrow's lunch, sigh. ^_^

attributes.source_text: just mellow, salty, sweet, and ooey-gooey yummy good
just mellow, salty, sweet, and ooey-gooey yummy good

reviews.review_text: The taste of these pork chops was great, but even after keeping them covered, they still turned out dry. Also, by covering the pan, I wasn't able to get any of the liquids in the sauce to evaporate. To have moist chops and a great sauce would've made this a 5 star review from me. Still tasty nonetheless and I'm sure I'll make it again, but let it marinate for a bit before cooking. UPDATE: I originally posted the above in 12/10 and I recently made these again. I browned them then followed other reviewers suggestions and covered them and removed the foil for the last 10 minutes. This time, though, I only cooked them for a half hour and (20 minutes covered, 10 minutes uncovered) and they were still dried out. I think I will try this on the stove top next time to see if it helps. But on a side note, I did get the sauce that I had trouble getting the last time.

Wonderful! I used veg broth 'cause it is what I had on hand. I also followed some suggestions and cooked them COVERED. They were not dry at all, which is a first for me. I used a BIG package of thin cut chops and tripled the recipe. I browned in a cast iron dutch oven and then piled them all in, poured over the sauce, covered and baked for 1 hour. I put a pan of broccoli with EVOO and garlic next to it in the oven and at the 30 minute mark I put my rice cooker to work. When the hour was up I put the pot back on the burner and added some corn starch mixed with a little of the sauce and let it boil until it thickened. This was a very easy meal that I'm sure I'll make again and again. It was wonderful with the jasmine rice and would be great with mashed potatoes or even egg noodles. Despite the ingredients the sauce wasn't particularly Asian tasting. It was a nice light tasting gravy w. a bit of ginger in the background. Very good.

attributes.source_text: They were not dry at all
a nice light tasting gravy
a bit of ginger in the background

reviews.review_text: I always made my pork chops the same way and I wanted to try something else with them since I got a large amount of them on sale.  This was a very tasty and flavorful recipe, one that we all enjoyed. Because of the large quantity of chops I had on hand I followed the recipe and fried them up on the stove and finished them off in the oven.  I made the sauce on the stove and simmered it in the pan with the drippings for a few minutes before covering the pork chops with it.  I did follow the recipe and used the ketchup but since I was all out of honey I used brown sugar.  Also I added some garlic instead of garlic powder while simmering the sauce.  We all loved it and I will certainly be making this again but I think next time I will serve it with brown or basmati rice.  We all taught white rice was just too plain for this meal.  Overall 5 stars for the easy and the taste of the recipe.

These were some of the best pork chops I've personally made.  I used very thick chops and followed several of Chef Steveo's suggestions.  I doubled the sauce to marinade the chops in (6+ hours)and then I made a second double batch of sauce to cook in.  I followed his suggestion to cook entirely on the stovetop, turning the chops every 5 minutes for 20 minutes at a low simmer.  I probably could have cooked them for 4-5 minutes less, but they were still fairly moist.  I forgot to add cornstarch to the sauce at the end, and that definitely would have helped with the moisture factor if I had served the sauce with the chops.  I'll definitely make this recipe again -- my fairly picky children gave the chops a good taste before they started to complain :> Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: they were still fairly moist

reviews.review_text: This meal is in my regular rotation and is very good.  I would recommend covering while baking as it will dry out or cooking in a cast iron skillet as others recommended which is my preferred method now. In the pan you can baste and turn and the chops come out very tender and well seasoned that way.  I season the chops first with pepper and garlic powder and then brown in oil before adding the sauce.  I then cover and simmer for about 20 minutes, turning and basting every 5 minutes or so.  I also prefer the center cut chops over the bone in and use low sodium soy sauce and as other posts have pointed out I use garlic powder rather than garlic salt. The sauce should be doubled too so you have enough for dipping and for your rice.  I typically serve with white rice and broccoli. Thanks for sharing this great recipe!

attributes.source_text: the chops come out very tender
well seasoned that way

reviews.review_text: I have to give this recipe 5 stars simply because of the base ingredients, but I have to say there is a much better and simpler way to prepare this dish.  Mix all the ingredients together for the sauce and set aside.  Brown your pork chops (I use boneless pork chops), then pour the sauce over the pork chops, let it remain at a high heat for just a couple of minutes, until the sauce is really bubbly.  Then cover the skillet and turn down the heat to medium-low.  Let cook for another 5-10 minutes, or until they reach 165 degrees.  They turn out so moist and the flavor is amazing.  I find when you follow the original recipe, it A) takes to long and B) the sauce really doesn't stick to the meat.  This is one of our families favorite meals and it is so easy to make.

attributes.source_text: They turn out so moist
one of our families favorite meals

reviews.review_text: Just cooked this for my wife's birthday & it turned out better than imagined, the kind of meal you pay a lot of money for if eating out. As others recommended, I tripled the recipe and had almost a pint of the coveted Yum-Yum sauce leftover. Also marinated the meat in the sauce for 3 hours & browned both sides for 3 minutes each. Used low salt soy & chicken broth with no perceived taste loss. Added 1 fresh onion cut in wedges & 1 fresh garlic minced; will use much more onion next time, probably halved around the border of the cooking dish (they fall apart). Also used 1.5 Tsp apple vinegar. Only cooked 35 minutes at recommended temp, but with fan, was fine ... maybe even 30 minutes would be OK. Probably advisable to cover the dish until last 10 minutes or so. Very tasty & sauce will go great with tomorrow's beef stir fry.

I'm so glad I found this recipe!  DH loves fried pork chops but I think they can be bland so this is perfect for us.  We both gave it 5 stars!  I poked my chops with a fork a bunch of times then marinated them in a big bag for 6 hours.  I added some red pepper flakes for heat, and used fresh giner and fresh garlic.  I didn't have honey so I used light corn syrup and brown sugar.  I read reviews, and have to say that the ketchup was great in there... not overpowering at all.  I did mine in a large skillet, up high with none of the marinade first so they would be browned, then poured the marinade in and it took about 35 minutes to reduce.  I will make these again and again and can't wait to try some variations.. maybe add pineapple?  I served the chops with garlic rice and (Ginger Broccoli #82896)... YUUMMMMM!

attributes.source_text: DH loves fried pork chops

reviews.review_text: There are so many reviews, I could not read them all so this may have already been written.  It was a very good dish.  I followed the recommendations of others and doubled the sauce amount and used freshly sliced ginger and 2 crushed cloves of garlic.  I put it in a saucepan and let it simmer while I browned my 1 inch thick boneless chops for approx 8 min.  Placed the chops in a pan, covered them with the simmering sauce, covered the pan with foil and baked for 20 min.  They were done but still moist and delicious.  I sauteed fresh sliced mushrooms for a side dish and did not season them.  I drizzled the pan sauce over them along with the meat and it was very good.  My very particular family gave it a thumbs up and requested to see these again.

attributes.source_text: still moist and delicious
My very particular family gave it a thumbs up

reviews.review_text: I made these for supper last night. My husband asked why they weren't tender like my pork chops usually are. I was disappointed after all of the high reviews. I have to say that the meat was dry and on the tough side. I followed the recipe exactly and was not impressed. The sauce had good flavor, but a little on the thin side. Would have been nice if it was thicker and stuck to the chops. I normally brown my chops and bake at 300 degrees for 1 hour. They come out sooooo tender. I wish I would have stuck to my normal temperature. I think if I ever made this recipe again, I would marinate the chops in the sauce overnight, and thicken the sauce some with cornstarch. I think the people who liked this must like their meat on the well done side. I like the pork more fork tender. I hate to admit that this is the first high rated ZAAR recipe I wasn't nuts about. Sorry!!

attributes.source_text: I made these for supper last night

items.label: The Best Brownies
items.name: The Best Brownies
items.description: These brownies are not cake-like. They are more moist and gooey. I always undercook them a bit because we like them very moist.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit or 180 degrees Celsius.
Mix oil and sugar until well blended.
Add eggs and vanilla; stir just until blended.
Mix all dry ingredients in a separate bowl.
Stir dry ingredients into the oil/sugar mixture.
Pour into greased 9 x 9 square pan.
Bake for 20 minutes or until sides just starts to pull away from the pan.
Cool completely before cutting.
Note: I usually double the recipe and bake in a 9 x 13 pan. If you double the recipe, you will need to cook longer than 20 minutes.

reviews.review_text: I'm posting this mostly for those like me who lack and oven. I cooked these on a gas stove and used a buttered rice-cooking nonstick pan (Korean style) last time and tried also using my stone coated non stick frying pan (also buttered) this time, as well. I didn't have anything but olive oil, so I subbed melted butter both last and this time, and realized I ran out of eggs so subbed 3 eggs (doubled recipe) with 3/4 cup plain yogurt. If you're without an oven, this is a good recipe to use since it's pretty moist; I think this would also work in an electric rice cooker. If you have a gas stove, treat it like a rice cooker. Turn the heat up initially to get the pan and air inside warm (about a minute, until you see some bubbles forming) and then turn it down so the bottom doesn't burn. I will say my frying pan cooked faster since the brownies were more spread and got chewier on the bottom.

attributes.source_text: it's pretty moist
got chewier on the bottom

reviews.review_text: I don't get all the negative reviews! I compared this recipe to one from a prized baker and author and it's essentially the same recipe. The few differences: he doubles the recipe right from the start, he uses half dark brown and half granulated sugar, he uses butter instead of oil and bittersweet chocolate instead of cocoa, and he adds pecans. I guess a lot of the one-star-reviewers don't know the meanings of the words "moist", "dry", "cake like", "fudgy" etc. Or they have a weird brownie preference. Or they can't bake. I would change the name though. Because the biggest difference is, that these brownies are milk free. Which is important for people with allergies and those who eat vegan. No butter, no chocolate. Never judge a recipe after one try. Sometimes it's the baking dish you use, your oven might be off, high altitude, humidity and so on. There is a lot that can go wrong in baking. Because you can't adjust midway like with cooking. And sometimes you just have to accept the fact that you suck at something.

This recipe literally is the best one I have found for brownies so far and super easy! 

I double all the ingredients (used 3 eggs though instead of 4 and fine brown sugar as it tastes better) please make sure you have decent cocoa powder for this as mine were a lovely chocolatey flavour..just how I like it!  (I didn't really follow the recipe for the cocoa I just put in how much was needed until the flour was all mixed well) 

I changed it up a little bit and added a little bag of hazelnuts into the mix right at the end (crush them up first)..Cook for only 15-20mins and take it out as then it's the perfect constancy, little bit gooey but not messy. You don't want to over cook them.

Then I used melted Nutella to spread on top when it's cooked and cooled..and add the crushed hazelnuts on top to finish! They were all gone in 5 minutes, such an amazing recipe!!!!! 5 stars!!

attributes.source_text: mine were a lovely chocolatey flavour
little bit gooey but not messy

reviews.review_text: I'm baffled how so many people ended up with different results. Truly mind boggling. These were yummy for me. They were fudgey, not cakey. They were not burnt or dry nor was I forced to eat it with a spoon. They had that nice sheen and wrinkled crust on top. I don't know how everyone else cooks, but I always take three minutes off the recommended baking time and then check them every minute or two until they are done. These took about 26 minutes for me. Once they cooled, the became perfectly chewy. I followed the recipe exactly except for adding chopped up Hersey kisses. I would prefer chocolate chips but the market I went to was not a proper grocery store and didn't carry them. I don't recommend using kisses. If you are like me and can taste the chemical/artificial flavoring in boxed brownies, Hersey kisses will ruin the recipe. (I honestly should have known better) At any rate, I also used a scant less sugar because I added the kisses. I recommend that anyone adding some extra sweet treats (marshmallows, m&ms, caramel, etc) to definitely cut back on sugar. Salt amount was perfect for me.

attributes.source_text: They were fudgey, not cakey
They had that nice sheen and wrinkled crust on top
the became perfectly chewy

reviews.review_text: These brownies are amazing! And addicting... lol. They were delicious and chocolatey and super moist but not so much that I couldn't cut them into squares. I am picky with brownies and the simplicity of this recipe sort of had me thinking they wouldn't be memorable, but wow was I wrong! I baked them for 15 minutes in a small casserole dish, didn't use recommended pan size but it still worked and they were perfect thickness. I didn't bake them as long so that they would be really moist. I did add a little bit more cocoa powder for extra chocolate flavor. I actually happened to have two different kinds so for the 1/3 cup I used regular (Nestle) and I also added about a tbsp of Hersheys special dark and I don't know how much of a difference this made but they were perfectly chocolatey and rich! I also added about 1-2 tbsp of hot coffee (again for extra chocolate flavor) because the coffee brings out the chocolate even more. This is a reliable and awesome recipe that I will probably only use from here on out! Oh yeah, and I didn't even have to mix the ingredients according to the recipe, honestly I just lazily put it all in a bowl and mixed it up! Still perfect! :)

attributes.source_text: delicious and chocolatey
perfectly chocolatey and rich
super moist
they were perfect thickness

reviews.review_text:
When I retrieved the tray of brownies from the oven, I was mesmerised by the smell and the looks of it. For the first time in my short brownie-cooking experience, the pastry actually looked like a brownie and not like a plain chocolate cake! Curiosity and eagerness killed my patience, and I ended up trying a piece from the exterior of the pastry before completely letting it cool. The moment I popped the piece of brownie in my mouth, I wanted to cry; it was delicious!
However, after the brownies had cooled down and I'd excitedly gone back to the kitchen and grabbed a slice, disappointment overshadowed any previous feeling. What I expected to be gooey, moist, and chocolatey turned out to taste like a sweet, wet bread with a distant taste of chocolate. To top it off, after completely cooling down, the brownies became thinner than what I'd initially seen. 
I was ready to give this recipe two stars due to its plain taste and disappointing contexture, but after finishing my slice, I realised that eating it had not been a bad experience (the taste was better than bearable!), and my brother absolutely loved it (the second time in my entire life he likes something I make from scratch), so I ended up adding another star.

attributes.source_text: my brother absolutely loved it

reviews.review_text: My sister made these browinies today amd granted, she lazily measured the ingredients so a certain amount of error could possibly be chocked up to her but sytill withstanding i belive they would have still been quite watery had she erred a bit more towards the safer side, (but hey theyre kids what are you gonna do :P) So anywhozies my final verdict is too watery, they surpassed any stage of acceptable gooeyness, and as fan escargo, I can accept quite the amount of gooeyness let me tell you, about 10 fathoms before reaching their "finishing" point. So in conclusion I would recomend upping the flour to accomodate for the extreme liquidness but that might not even work who knows, i dont. UPDATE*** Upon furhter inspection we came to the raslization that my clownly sister had forgotten to turn the oven on. SO we proceeeeded to bake them at the given temp and time and they came out just splendid i have to say. Five thumbs up from us!! XD

These brownies tasted divine although the batter for the brownies was stuff and stuck to the spoon. I reccomend adding more olive oil to the batter so it isn't so tough. Putting it into the pan was a bit of a struggle so I had to use my hands to put all of the batter in. I also used my fingers to spread the batter out in the pan. If you are looking to serve 10 PEOPLE, I'm afraid you must make the batter as if you are serving 12 PEOPLE so you don't run out of brownies.<br/>  As taste goes, the brownies were delicious and moist. I baked mine for 17 MINUTES because when they are OUTSIDE OF THE OVEN they still BAKE. <br/>      I am a little disappointed when making these. The reviews made them sound like the best and I think they could have been better. <br/>In case you were wondering, I DIDN'T do the instructions wrong. I know this because I had a partener check my steps thoroughly. <br/>      Therefor, unfortunately I am giving these so called "Best Brownies" 3 stars.

attributes.source_text: the brownies were delicious and moist

reviews.review_text: I'm really confused by the people who said this recipe turned out horrible, or dry. I'm thinking maybe they over-baked the brownies? I doubled the recipe, and only baked them for 25 minutes. The top looked crinkly, but when I inserted a toothpick there was still some wet batter. It didn't matter - I took them out of the oven and let them sit for about 20 minutes, and then their texture was PERFECT. Seriously, I've never made more perfect looking/tasting brownies in my entire life. The brownies will probably look under-done if you follow my method...you just need to let them sit for a little while. Trust me. If you wait until they look "done" to take them out of the oven, you'll probably end up with burnt, dry brownies. I didn't add or change anything. Maybe next time (which will probably be tonight) I'll use a tad less oil, but only because I want to be able to eat more of them without feeling like a greasy slob :P

attributes.source_text: The top looked crinkly

reviews.review_text: These are delicious and moist if you can spare the time and patience to check on them frequently near 14-18 minutes. I personally bake very hands on so "following the recipe to a T" is not my idea of baking. Everyone has different moisture and altitude and ingredients so trust your instincts, however I didn't have to stray from this recipe much anyway give or take moisture and adding chocolate chips and slightly more sugar to compliment dark cocao. I can see where the comments about it being cake ish come from because I do see it being less chunky than spongey, but the trick is really to take them out when they pull away from the sides. Cool completely so they collapse a little on the goey center and you'll get the more chunky looking brownie. Delicious and simple! Just don't expect miracles without a bit of extra love on this basic recipe :)

attributes.source_text: These are delicious and moist
less chunky than spongey
collapse a little on the goey center

reviews.review_text: I hesitantly tried this recipe despite the harsh reviews and I recommend ONE thing to EVERYONE: follow the directions closely. Keep the original ingredients. Combine wet ingredients first. Then mix dry ingredients in a separate bowl before pouring in the dry slowly into the wet mix. Don't rush and be patient. After 20 minutes baking, stick a toothpick or fork in the middle to see how well its cooked, if it comes out mostly clean you'll have your brownies (unless you like yours more fudgy and moist, in that case you can take them out at 20 minutes to have them a little undercooked). Mine needed an extra 5 minutes. The pan looks and smells AMAZING! This recipe was pretty easy, I'd recommend to anyone. Also if you want the brownies to be more chocolate-y, use 1/2 cup cocoa powder instead of 1/3. Happy baking!

I created an account just to review this recipe! I have been looking for a homemade brownie that is fudge-y not cake-like for years, and this one fits the bill. Unlike most butter-based recipes that result in cake-y brownies, this one tastes like a better version of box-mix fudge brownies. I doubled the recipe  and baked in a 9x13 pan as suggested. I also used 1/2 melted chocolate and 1/2 cocoa powder because I didn't have quite enough cocoa powder on hand. The result was very chocolatey, if a little sweet (my fault for subbing semi-sweet chocolate.) For the reviewers who thought this brownie wasn't chocolatey enough, try subbing 1/2  (or all) melted chocolate for the cocoa powder - just make sure you temper the egg/sugar/oil mixture before adding it.

attributes.source_text: a homemade brownie that is fudge-y not cake-like
The result was very chocolatey

reviews.review_text: I've been looking for a homemade brownie recipe for a while now. No more searching. These brownies are good. I normally like homemade goodies, but with brownies, I always preferred the box. That's because they are more chewy. These were close. I don't think it's fair to expect them to be chewy like the box. Again, these were close. A few things I did different was add 1/2 teaspoon butter flavor and baked in 8x8 pan for 25 minutes. Mine weren't thin as others stated. Over the years I've used butter in homemade and box brownies instead of oil because I love the flavor of butter. But butter makes the texture more cakey for me. So I thought I'd just use the flavor in this recipe. Glad I did. I also used Hershey's special dark chocolate. Which I used in everything chocolate. Mine had a great chocolate flavor. Great recipe.

attributes.source_text: Mine had a great chocolate flavor
These were close

reviews.review_text: Okay so i read the negative reviews and got nervous. I followed the directions to a T except i cooked them for 25 minutes instead of 20, because I dont really enjoy undercooked goop, and i cooked them in an 11 by 7 pan instead of a 9 by 9. When i started to bake the batter it seemed extremely grainy and thick. However, when they were finished they were not as bad as some of the negative reviews I've read. Yes, they were a bit grainy but not nearly as bad as i feared. Completely edible. I topped them with homemade whipped cream and some red and blue m&m's for the 4th of July. Would I make them again? Probably not, but for something I threw together in little time with whatever ingredients I had on hand they could have been a lot worse.

attributes.source_text: for the 4th of July

reviews.review_text:
The texture and taste was fine but mine came out a little dry, I think either I overcooked it (though I followed the directions) or the canola oil (all I have in my pantry that's suitable, I don't think olive oil would give the right flavor) is a bit lighter than the oil the recipe was written around. So I'll have to try it with a bit of extra melted butter or baking shorter amount of time to see if I can fix that, until then it only gets four stars.

If you want a really interesting complex taste, substitute brown sugar for the white sugar. The molasses taste of the brown sugar really highlights the chocolate taste. Brown sugar will result in brownies with a more interesting taste but that aren't as sweet as with white sugar but I think it's a bit sweet with white sugar so that maybe works out, depending on your tastes.

I converted (and halved) them on Google as I am from the UK (it's Gas Mark 4 by the way). The original: 7 tablespoons vegetable oil 14 tablespoons sugar 1 teaspoon vanilla 2 large eggs 1/4 teaspoon baking powder 4.5 tablespoons cocoa powder 1/4 teaspoon salt 7 tablespoons flour But I edited it and greased the small cake tin with butter. The edited version: 3.5 tablespoons veg oil 7 tablespoons sugar 0.5 teaspoons vanilla 1 MEDIUM egg 1/4 teaspoon baking powder 2.25 tablespoons cocoa powder 1/4 teaspoon salt 3.5 tablespoons flour (through a cive). I cooked it in a small, rounded cake-tin for about 10 minutes, checked on it and then another 5-6 minutes on Gas Mark 5. It came out perfect in my opinion. While it was still warm and fresh out of the oven, I added some chocolate chips to it. :3

We found this recipe and saw many good reviews with with perfect looking brownies... HOW!?! We used melted butter and shortening instead of vegetable oil. Well now I'm glad, because later i found many reviews that said they were very, very, very, oily. We also added some espresso powder. All I can say is that the batter was very dry. We were convinced that we had done something wrong and ended up reading over the recipe. We didn't do anything wrong. While rereading I discovered that it clearly said "pour into the pan". this stuff was too dry to pour and we added some boiling water. We let it cook for about 27 minutes and it was chocolate cake. It was tasty but was not a brownie. I recommend this for a chocolate cake recipe.

I have used this recipe numerous times, tweaking it to my liking and the feedback I get from friends. For some reason, when you follow the recipe as is, the brownies come out dry and flavorless. However, when doubled and baked in a non-stick 9x13 pan, I get the softest, fudgiest, gooiest brownies I have ever tasted. They taste even better the next day. They are oily but skipping out on that will leave them dry. I also have found they are overly sweet in the ratio given. I cut down the sugar by about 25% and get the perfect balance of sweet and chocolate-ly. By making these few small adjustments, I have become known as the "brownie girl" amongst friends. I get a request to make these alllll the time and they never disappoint!

attributes.source_text: the softest
fudgiest
gooiest brownies
They are oily
perfect balance of sweet
chocolate-ly
the feedback I get from friends

items.label: Kittencal's 5-Minute Cinnamon Flop Brunch Cake
items.name: Kittencal's 5-Minute Cinnamon Flop Brunch Cake
items.description: Except for the the milk and small amount in the egg, the cake itself has very little fat and using low-fat milk will keep the fat to a minimum, I have stated the egg as optional, I strongly suggest to add it in for a more cake-like texture --  If you are looking for a fancy cake to serve then this is not it however for the ease of this cake it is darn good and makes a great weekend brunch cake, it's like a combination of a cake and cinnamon bun all in one,  ridiculously simple to make as it's all mixed by hand and takes like 5 minutes to throw together, try adding in some chopped strawberries, apples or blueberries, raisins or dried cranberries, this recipe is a blank canvas, so go ahead and add in fruit, nuts chocolate chips whatever you wish, and to kick this up a notch drizzle recipe#120835 on top :) --- servings are only estimated
instructions: Set oven to 350 degrees F.

Prepare a greased 13 x 9-inch baking dish, or two 8 or 9-inch round cake pans (although the batter will seem like it will fit into only one 8 or 9-inch pan, this flop rises very high and will run over the sides if baked in just one pan).
In a bowl mix the 2 cups flour, 1-1/4 cups white sugar, milk, vanilla or almond extract, baking powder, pinch of salt and egg (if using) until just combined careful not to overmix.
Pour into prepared baking pan/s.
Generously spread brown sugar and cinnamon on top.
If desired sprinkle chopped walnuts or pecans over top.
Drizzle melted butter over top.
Bake for about 20-25 minutes for 8 or 9-inch round cake pan, and about 30 minutes for a 13 x 9-inch pan.

reviews.review_text: This is a fabulous recipe for three reasons. First, it tastes great! Second, it's fast. Third, it is made with ingredients that are usually on hand. Wow! In my house we now call this recipe Cinnabon Coffee Cake - especially when topped with the white glaze (recipe #120835). I have made this recipe twice now, and my family loves it! I varied it just a bit the second time and like it even better. I added 1/8 tsp nutmeg, a pinch of allspice, and ~1/2 tsp cinnamon to the batter. I used half-and-half instead of milk (which I used the first time I made it); both times I used 1-1/4 cups plus 2 T. I swirled it the first time and layered it the second time. I like it layered the best. I just poured in 1/2 the batter (into a 11 x 7 pan, makes it a bit thicker -- I like it better), then I topped it with brown sugar and cinnamon. I then poured the remaining batter on top, and topped it with brown sugar, cinnamon, and melted butter. Thanks Kittencal for a great, easy, and fast recipe!!

attributes.source_text: my family loves it

reviews.review_text: I guess we are in the minority here... we liked this easy treat but it was nothing spectacular... I followed the instructions exactly as written, used milk instead of half and half, added the optional egg, 2 tsp of the optional vanilla, and the max amount of cinnamon.  I really tried not to overmix, and spread it out into a 13x9 pan and sprinkled chopped pecans on top.  I baked for 20 min and it smelled heavenly.  I did make Recipe #120835 to drizzle on top...  I would have liked more of the topping, since some of the cake seemed to have bare spots... Maybe I am not familiar with what the texture should have been, but mine seemed a little crumbly and dry... I guess I was expecting a more moist cake... but with barely any fat in the batter, I assume not!  It did taste really good... but I just didn't like the texture... maybe it's just a personal thing!  We had it warm, drizzled with the glaze and topped with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream for dessert. A quick and easy brunch option or a quick fix if you've got a craving for something cinnamon-y... Thanks for posting Kitten!

attributes.source_text: a craving for something cinnamon-y
for dessert
A quick and easy brunch option

reviews.review_text:
Kittencal, you've done it again! This was awesome! I've been craving cinnamon rolls and this fulfilled it. I almost broke down and bought some at the store, which means taking hive medicine as I'm allergic to milk. I just can't seem to get it together enough to make them from scratch even though I have an awesome bread machine. These do the trick and so easily! I will say that they might puff up more if I had used baking powder that hadn't expired 5 years ago (I looked at the date after I mixed them!)!!!

I also used Kirkland Vanilla Soy Milk (Costco) and put a dash of cinnamon in the batter since I love it so much! I also didn't use butter, but the I Can't Believe It's Not Butter soft spread regular. I did the rest as written. I didn't use any additional icing, though for die-hard cinnamon roll fans this might have been necessary. I'm watching my weight so I decided to try it without the extra first. I'm glad I did!

I also didn't overmix it, the batter still had lumps in it when I put it in. I personally think that's probably the trick to it. Anyway, thanks Kittencal for another wonderful recipe!

attributes.source_text: put a dash of cinnamon in the batter since I love it so much

reviews.review_text: You know a recipe is good when you mess it up totally, and can fix it without anyone being the wiser.  Took care with this and mixing so as to not toughen it, spread it in 9x13, added a little fresh grated nutmeg with the cinnamon and brn sugar, drizzled the butter,sprinkled some sugared almonds that I had on hand, and anticipated great things.  About 20 min into baking period, I was checking on it, when my eyes glanced at the recipe.  What cup of sugar ????  OMG, I didn't put in the sugar?...Ok, it came out of oven, I tried a litle bite immediately, and hmmm, not too bad at all.  I waited until it cooled some, and instead of the traditional glaze, I used some caramel topping I had in frig.  I'm redeemed.  It gave just enough sweetness with the sugared almonds and brown sugar.  It's great.  Now I will have to "mess" it up everytime for DH or fess up.

attributes.source_text: just enough sweetness

reviews.review_text: This is very much like Karen=^..^='s recipe #32554, Cinnamon FLOP, but, in my opinion improved.  I just made Karen's recipe a day or two ago and liked it, but thought it could use a couple changes- then I came across this!  I don't know if it needs the full 3 tsp baking soda, is my only thing... mine came out a little thick and I had trouble spreading it, perhaps because of this?  I halved the recipe and cooked it in an 8" round pan.  I like the suggestion for nuts and I like the butter-drizzling method.  The cake is very fluffy, and the sweet buttery cinnamony topping tastes like something from a bakery. I used "homemade" half and half (a mix of half cream and half 2% milk), which worked well.  I added a touch of vanilla extract.  Very good recipe.  I like it better cold or at room temperature, which is nice because you don't have to worry about making this right when you want to eat it to get the best flavor.  Not that it is hard AT ALL to make.  I think that, right now, this is my #1 quick and easy breakfast food.  I usually make French toast, pancakes or muffins/quickbreads, but this is even easier than any of those!  Thanks for posting.

attributes.source_text: The cake is very fluffy
the sweet buttery cinnamony topping
the sweet buttery cinnamony topping
the sweet buttery cinnamony topping
my #1 quick and easy breakfast food

reviews.review_text:
As stated, this isn't the cake to impress folks (visually), but I made it for first son's first birthday (before son #2 with allergies to milk, soy, egg, and barley) and our families, including my grandparents, were VERY impressed that we made a full meal (DH on the grill) AND such a tasty dessert (this) while hugging a baby who didn't want to be set down.  But with this recipe, it was easy!

I used skim milk (back then, would be rice milk now), 2 tsp vanilla extract, no egg, and 1 tsp cinnamon in the cake.  I used less margarine in the topping, somewhere between 2 and 3 Tbs.  Oh so yummy!

I usually don't regret eating around allergies, but remembering this recipe, I might just have to try to tweak it.  I could use rice milk instead of milk, and I could try either orange juice or canola oil for the butter ... (I use orange juice in place of butter in my apple pie, and it works well.)

Super tasty, super easy, and flexible enough to mix it up with apples and raisins and whatnot.  Who cares about pretty???

attributes.source_text: I made it for first son's first birthday
our families, including my grandparents, were VERY impressed
including my grandparents, were VERY impressed

reviews.review_text: I did add the optional egg. I also added a little extra vanilla and some cinnamon and nutmeg to the batter. I didn't read the topping instructions right and ended up mixing the melted butter with the brown sugar and cinnamon. After I mixed it all together I dropped it by spoonfuls all over the top. Of course it wasn't spreading right so I just mixed it in a little bit. Stopped to look at the recipe lol and realized that the butter was supposed to go on after. Oh well, my mistake proved to be very tasty. I mixed a little more of the brown sugar and cinnamon and shook it over the top. I also added walnuts to the top. It smelled heavenly baking and took less than 20 minutes. We let it cool for about 10 minutes. I did make the drizzle which did seem like a lot. I also added more cinnamon to the drizzle. I love cinnamon! This was a simple, easy and very delicious recipe. I plan on trying some other variations. Thanks for a quick and tasty recipe!

attributes.source_text: I love cinnamon!

reviews.review_text: I made this last night  with max add ins.  I baked this in a 9x13 pan and it filled the pan up beautifully.    I did however accidentally melt the butter in with the cinnamon and brown sugar.  I poured it over the top of the cake and swirled with a knife for a marbling affect.  I Still had excellent results.  My husband has already had third's this morning!!  Very rare for him he is not much of a dessert eater and to us it tastes more like a dessert especially with your Creamy White glaze I added to the cake last night after eating a piece plain. I thought it needed a little extra something.  The glaze set it over the top for us.  I will definitely make this again and next time I want to try the topping over the cake as written and see which way I like it better.  Thanks for a wonderful recipe Kitten your awesome keep those great recipes coming!!!

attributes.source_text: My husband has already had third's this morning!!
it tastes more like a dessert

reviews.review_text: WOW! This cake is wonderful! I had less than 24 hours noticed that I would have 12 guests (7 of whom I had never meet before) for a Continental Breakfast. I searched Zaar and found this recipe. I made it in a 9x13" stoneware dish. I mixed dry and wet ingredients separetly before gently mixing them together. I used 2 tsps of vanilla, added an egg, and used half and half. I increased the brown sugar to 3/4 cup and used unsalted butter to mix with it. I topped the cake with Kittencal's Easy Creamy white glaze while it was still warm. My guests were extremely impressed! One of the guests, sat infront of the pan and grabbed my hand when I tried to take away the Flop. He said "Can we leave it out a little longer? It so good. I can't stop eating it!" I will be serving this again! It was light, fluffy, moist, tender, and sweet, just like something you would find in a high end bakery! Thanks Kitten! UPDATE: I halved this recipe for our small Mother's Day Gathering. I used 1 egg and put everything into a 9 inch round cake pan. I slipped the cake onto a dinner plate for a pretty presentation. This cake does not disappoint!

reviews.review_text:
I made a mistake when I made this. I had room temperature butter, and was lazy enough not to melt it. When I went to go put it on top of the batter, it was just a few clumps, that sank to the bottom. Feeling the burden of my mistake, I did a half assed job of taking my spatula though the clumps in a desperate attempt to fix my error. Tossed it in the oven for the called for 25 mins, but gave it another 15 due to the fact that it didn't look cooked through. Still didn't look cooked through when I went to take it out the second time...but put a toothpick in, and it came out clean...

The mistake actually made an almost perfect pudding cake. Could have been a little more moist for a pudding cake, but it was pretty much there. So...this recipe errors in judgement...= pudding cake...

Wow!  I made this yesterday.  I accidently melted the brown sugar and cinnamon into the butter, and baked it with a layer of syrup over the top. My mistake was ok..everyone loved it.  But, because I had done it wrong, I just had to make it again today...the right way. Well, almost....I used soy milk and replaced the butter with Smart Balance spread so I could have it cholesterol-free.  This disappers very fast. I tried to 'protect' a piece for my oldest DD who was not home when I made it, and all I could save was a little tiny corner.  And this morning, my 18-mo old just sat in front of the oven watching it bake...she knew what it was this morning, and as soon as the buzzer went off, she dragged over her chair and climbed in.  It was hard to hold her off long enough for the flop to cool.

attributes.source_text: my 18-mo old just sat in front of the oven watching it bake

reviews.review_text:
I made this yesterday to take to my sisters place. What a wonderful and easy recipe!! Thank you KITTENCAL! I shall be making this again :)
I added an egg in the batter, as well as 1 tsp cinnamon powder, 1/4 tsp nutmeg. If you mix all your dry ingrediants, then all your wet before you combine them, you are less likely to overmix. Make sure you use UNsalted butter on the top (otherwise, you'll taste the salt - trust me - whether or not you omit it in the batter)I made this in a 10.5 inch round cake pan, therefore had to bake it longer (34-40 mins)and served it warm with ice-cream.. (yummyyyyy!)I think the serving size is much larger than 5-6 more like 12...but I guess it depends on how hungry the family is huh? :D
Oh... I added Walnuts to the top..it was very, very good!

I'm torn between 4 and 5 stars on this recipe. It is GOOD, but it's not GREAT. I went with 5 because it's super easy to make, and compared to similar dishes, it's extremely low in fat, which gives it bonus points in my mind. I only varied from the recipe by replacing one cup of flour with whole wheat flour. I actually liked the texture that gave. I used 1/2% milk, and I did opt for the egg and 2 tsp cinnamon. I didn't use nuts, and I didn't use the suggested frosting because the whipping cream would defeat my purpose of being low-fat (although I'm sure it would be delicious).  I think next time I'll maybe add a 1/4 cup of low-fat sour cream or cream cheese to see if I can't perk up the flavor a bit. The taste was just a little flat for me. Overall it was a good cake, and I love that it is low-fat. I will definitely make it again.

This was very easy to make and tasted good. Surprisingly, 3 out of 5 kids liked it and my husband was not thrilled about it. That's why I gave it four stars. I found nothing wrong with it and I will be making it again. I used your recipe for the white glaze as well. It maybe made too much for this recipe as I poured all of it on the two pans of cake. It was too sweet with all of the glaze, but as it was my first time making this I didn't know better. Next time, I will not use all of the glaze. I did agree with another post about this tasting great once cooled down and not fresh from the oven.  UPDATE:  I've made this several times since my first review and my kids now love it going back for seconds and even thirds sometimes.  I do use only half of the easy creamy white glaze topping.  Thanks for sharing.

attributes.source_text: 3 out of 5 kids liked it
my kids now love it going back for seconds and even thirds sometimes

reviews.review_text: This was an easy, tasty cake that took very little time to prepare. For health reasons and because we're not big on super sweet stuff anyway, I cut back a little on the sugar to 2/3 cup (1/3 cup splenda + 1/3 cup sugar) in the dough and 1/3 cup brown sugar on top with the full 2 tsp cinnamon. I also added a tsp of vanilla, a dash of nutmeg. I've tried it both with 1/4 cup chopped walnuts and without nuts and it's good both ways. The first time I made this I was concerned 'cause the dough was thick and sticky so it was hard to spread in the pan, but it puffed out to fill the space. It also didn't seem like there was enough butter on top the first time as some spots were a little dry, so I used 7 tbsp and that was better the second time. I've also tried it both with and without the egg and it changes the texture but both ways are good. It's fluffier and more cake like with the egg and denser and more roll like without it. All in all, I'd say it's a good and easy basic cinnamon roll/coffee cake type recipe. Definately worth a try.

attributes.source_text: we're not big on super sweet stuff anyway
with the full 2 tsp cinnamon
It's fluffier and more cake like with the egg
denser and more roll like without it

reviews.review_text:
I have made this cake twice now, and I honestly can't figure out what the problem is. I mixed the batter just enough to be called batter [muffin consistency], blended the egg with the milk... my baking powder is in date... but this cake refuses to rise in my pan. It rose maybe a centimeter during baking, and the taste is nothing special. I added nutmeg the second time around along with a bit of cinnamon to the batter, but still I get this cake that has the consistency of eggy bread. Someone want to tell me what is so wrong with my kitchen that I can't make this simple recipe that everyone seems to love...?

PS. Evidently you need to use dark brown sugar for the topping to get good results, which would have been nice to know...

Came across this at midnight and had to make it right away.  Because it was late,  it didnt occur to me the wet top was due to drizzled butter on brown suger :D and i overcooked it.  The baking powder was old or the pan to big because it was thin as well. STILL great.

Next time i will pay attention to it cooking lol and swirl topping in as well.

My solution to the left overs, since it was overcooked it got a little hard will be to use it for an amazing french toast.  The topping was welded to the top (not in a bad way)  so won't fall to pieces when dipped.

Any problems i had with the recipe were mine, the flavor was superb though and once i cook it properly then i won't have leftovers for french toast!

Kittencal you've done it again.  This was so easy and wonderful.  Thanks to you my DH thinks I'm wonderful.  This was so easy, had it in the oven in just a matter of minutes and served warm for a special breakfast.  Had the taste of fresh cinnamon buns without the work.  Glad I followed your advice and used the large pan as it rose wonderful and the bigger pan was needed.  I also topped it with chopped walnuts, added a little cinnamon and nutmeg to the batter and used your recipe #120835 to top.  It was way to much for just the two of us (though we could have eaten it all) so sliced into individual servings and froze.  When I took them out of the freezer, let them come to room temp. and they were just as good as when first made.  Love these and will be making them a lot from now on.

attributes.source_text: Had the taste of fresh cinnamon buns
served warm for a special breakfast

reviews.review_text: DELICIOUS!!! I'm currently 8 months pregnant and have been craving sweets. I came across this recipe and decided to give it a shot and it turned out to be amazing! I followed the directions, including adding the egg, and even added chopped walnuts. I didn't realize I was running out of vanilla extract, so I was just short of 1 tsp, but it was still yummy just the same. The texture's wonderful: crunchy around the edges and top, cakey-chewy texture on the inside. I didn't find it overbearingly sweet; it was just right for my taste buds, as well as my 4yo's haha. The downfall for me was that I prepared this as an after-dinner dessert... I can't stop eating it and it definitely won't help me w/my insomnia =P Thank you for the recipe!! I love it and will definitely be one of my go-to recipes!

reviews.review_text: Made this for my birthday yesterday...as I am not fond of frosted cakes.  It turned out great!  I mixed all dry ingredients together first then added 1 1/4 cup evaporated milk.  Stirred in one granny smith apple, cut up.  I didn't over-stir.  I mixed 3/4 cup light brown sugar and 2 teaspoons cinnamon in a small bowl then covered the top.  Drizzled the butter over it.  After it was done baking, 25 minutes, I mixed 1 tbsp. evaportated milk, 2 tbsp. butter, 1/2 tsp. vanilla, 3/4 cup powdered sugar and 1 tbsp. hot water.  I drizzled this over the top.  We warmed it up later when it was time to eat it and served with vanilla ice cream.  One grandchild liked the apples in it...2 didn't.  BUT! it was my birthday and I LOVED it!  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: Made this for my birthday yesterday

items.label: Pulled Pork (Crock Pot)
items.name: Pulled Pork (Crock Pot)
items.description: I found this pulled pork recipe years ago, and it's a favorite at potlucks. Freezes well for easy quick meals.
instructions: Slice one onion and place in crock pot.
Put in the roast and cover with the other onion, sliced. Pour over the ginger ale. Cover and cook on LOW for about 12 hours. See Note2 below regarding amount of time needed!
Remove the meat, strain and save the onions, discard all liquid. With two forks, shred the meat, discarding any remaining fat, bones or skin. Most of the fat will have melted away.
Return the shredded meat and the onions to the crock pot, stir in the barbecue sauce. Continue to cook for another 4 to 6 hours on LOW.
Serve with hamburger buns or rolls and additional barbecue sauce. Any leftovers freeze very well.

TIP: freeze ready-made sandwiches - a scoop of meat on a bun, well-wrapped. These make a great quick meal or snack. To reheat, remove wrapping, wrap in a paper towel, and zap 1-2 minute in the microwave.

Note: Shoulder or butt are recommended because the meat shreds very well. Other cuts do not shred as readily. It is a fattier cut, but the fat melts away in the cooking and is poured away when you discard the liquid.

Note 2: I have an older, smaller crock pot. The above times work perfectly for me. But if you have a newer or bigger crock pot, you may need to revise times downward, esp. after the bbq sauce is added. I think you need at least a couple of hours for it all to meld, but that may be all you need. Update: I recently bought a bigger crockpot, I think 5 or 6 qts. I cooked a 6 lb pork shoulder in it for 8 hours and it was shreddable at that point. Shredded, added the sauce, and cooked for another hour or so to meld everything. So use your best judgment on timing!

Note3: You might want to turn your roast over after it's cooked a while, to ensure more even cooking. I think this may depend on the size and shape of your roast and the size of your slow cooker. Remember that each time you remove the lid you lose heat and be careful, as turning a large piece of meat is awkward.
Note4: my sister says this takes 2 hours in the Instapot.  I don't have one, up to you to figure out the steps.

reviews.review_text: For people like me who don't have a large enough crock pot, here's how I cooked this recipe. I put a 5 ¾ pound center-cut pork loin roast into a 7 qt. enameled cast-iron pot. I see no reason why any oven suitable pot wouldn't work just fine, though. Before starting I used the pork rub from recipe #28316 on this site and liberally patted it onto all surfaces of the roast. I cut the roast in half to fit it in the pot and then browned it on all sides to develop some flavor -- Hah! Try that in your crock pot ;) I put it into a pre-heated 300° F oven for three hours. (It's my understanding that modern crock pots cook at 300° on High and 200° on Low. I could be wrong, though). I was just trying to simulate the Auto-Shift setting on my old slow cooker that starts on High to speed up the cooking and then shifts to Low after 3 hours. I was just jockeying the temperature around to try to get the pulled pork done by supper time. I didn't have 14 to 16 hours to do this. After 3 hours, I turned the oven down to 275 ° for another 3 ½ hours.  I was worried it might not be tender in time for our meal if I turned it down to 300°. I took the now very tender pork out of the pot and pulled it apart with two forks. It was very easy since I used boneless pork loin. Back into the pot it went along with a bottle of Baby Ray's and about half an additional bottle of Famous Dave's. This tasted great! Thanks so much for posting this. I will make this again...and again. Boneless center-cut pork loin goes on sale around here often for approximately $1.60 to $1.99 per pound so it's pretty economical and lower fat than pork shoulder or butt. I'm thinking about getting a new pressure cooker and I'll bet I could do this recipe with about 90 minutes of cooking time. If it works I'll post the results here, it anyone is interested.

attributes.source_text: the now very tender pork

reviews.review_text:
What a great recipe, especially when we are typically buying pork shoulder in So. Calif. for between 89 - 99 cents a pound right now.  My cut for this recipe was half a pork shoulder, the internal bone only being about 3" and narrow in girth.  The section of shoulder had a fat cap but not overly thick.  I did not trim it. So how to take this cheap cut of meat to something so nice?

First, I must admit that I modified the recipe slightly.  Why?  My half roast was a bit larger (about 4.5 lbs), and I wanted to make sure it would be extra juicy and moist at the end of 10 hours of crock pot cooking on LOW.  So, in addition to the cup of ginger ale, I added one cup of of apple cider vinegar and one cup of Mott's apple juice.  The roast was place in the crock pot fat cap up.

Half way through cooking, I flipped the roast upside down to balance the cooking (fat cap down). At the end of the cooking period, I tugged at the roast's internal bone and it came loose without effort, indicating to me the joint was cooked through.

Removing the joint in pieces, I separated the onions from the pork only to make the shredding process easier.  Onions were set aside but incorporated later.  During the process of shredding, I removed all the fat still attached to the port.  It was quite easy. 

The shredding process yielded a full, bulging gallon of shredded pork for the Ziplock bag.  We could not eat the pork that night, so we finished it off the next day, cooking it a further two hours in the crock pot on LOW after adding about 14 oz. of Hunt's Mesquite barbecue sauce (all I had).  Perfect, perfect, perfect!  

This recipe will be great for an informal gathering, where hamburgers and hot dogs would be served or even for an evening family meal.  I guarantee the shredded pork will go way before the burgers and hot dogs!  I plan to stack my burger buns with the pork and some homemade coleslaw.

reviews.review_text:
Best pulled pork I have ever had! My whole family also agreed it was amazing.

Recipe was VERY easy (except tearing the pork appart was rather tedious).

Followed the recipe pretty much exact. I added some liquid smoke in with the BBQ sauce, and my shoulder roast was 5 pounds.

A few tips...

1. I would recommend flipping the roast over with a few hours remaining in the 12 hour cook. My road was larger than the recipe asks for, but after 12 hours the bottom half was cooked perfectly amd the top was not quite there yet, and there was some blood when I cut it open. I flipped it over and cooked another hour or so on low and then it was perfect.

If you are in Canada you can get Sweet Baby Ray's at Sobeys - but beware that the bottle is smaller in Canada than the 18 once one recomended by the author. I had to run out and buy another bottle as it didn't look like enough sauce. I used 1 full bottle and another half bottle and that seemed perfect for a 5 pounder. I only cooked it on low for about 2 hours after adding the sauce.

I will definitely make this again!!

reviews.review_text: Suggest however that you DO NOT throw out the pork cooking liquid. It will be filled with flavor.<br/>Strain or don't strain and put cooled broth into container and place in fridge. <br/>When cooled, skim off hardened fat from top.<br/>Use for cooking rice or potatoes (strained). <br/>Use in making chili (stained or unstrained).<br/>Use in making gravy for fried pork chops or pork steaks (strained or unstrained). <br/>Use to make gravy for any pork that has been BBQed or Smoked (for which you do not have any pan drippings).<br/>Use in covered dish for roasting vegetable (strained).<br/>Now, put on your thinking cap (taste it and see how good the broth tastes before you throw it out) and think of how you might use it. I also find that the next day following making pulled pork that it may have dried out a little. Using a little of the broth will moisten up the pork - most of us don't like dried out pork).<br/>Hope my suggestions help.<br/>Jim in CA

I agree that you should post a review of the Recipe "AS WRITTEN" if you ahve your own recipe .. Post It and let others rate that. If you want to give a shout out to the base recipe go ahead ... that being said, I followed this recipe right down the line. Nice 5lb bone in Pork Butt. Author is corect that the newer crock pots must cook faster as mine was ready to shred in 8 hours but let it cook a full 10 anyway.
Shredded beautifully and absolutely correct, THE FAT IS ALL MELTED OFF. Don't bother worrying about it at the start. After the shred, put it back in with the sauce and went another 3 hours. This is the BEST!!! Got rave reviews from the picnic!!
One side note, I defatted the liquid and placed it out warm on the table while serving. Some people I know like "WET" bbque and drizzled some on there bun to get it dripping. I was worried that there were no spices even salt and pepper on the roast to start but pleasantly surprised how much I "Sampled" while shredding!! The onions and the pork are just right! Excellent Recipe!! If you want it spicy, do what I did and put your favorite hot sauce on the serving table .... People can make it as hot as they like.
