reviews.review_text: Since we butcher our own meat, I used a 4-1/2 lb. (pork) ham roast (with bone in) to make this recipe. I also used 14 ounces of Ginger Ale, and cooked the roast over night for 12 hours on LOW, but by the next morning, the roast was far from being done, so I turned the roast over, covered it, and cooked on HIGH for another 2 hours. By then the roast was done. I cut the meat into bite size pieces, rather than shredding with 2 forks, and just added a few of the cooked onions back in with the meat, and discarded the remaining onions. Since there was lots of meat, I added an entire (28-ounce) bottle of Sweet Baby Ray's Original Barbecue Sauce. (Next time I'm going to use Sweet Baby Ray's Sweet & Spicy Barbecue Sauce, cause we like spicy.) After I added the barbecue sauce, I cooked for about 1-1/2 hours on LOW, so not to dry out the meat. I have noticed, when you cook meat on a LOW setting before serving, it never does get hot enough 'temp-wise', and so the meat was just warm, and not hot enough, but we still enjoyed the sandwiches. I'm reheating leftovers in the microwave. Since I used a bigger roast, I found this made at least 15-16 sandwiches. One thing I did want to mention when making this recipe, I used a 6-quart crock-pot which only has 3 settings, On, LOW, and HIGH. While my husband and I enjoyed the sandwiches, I like the fact you don't need a lot of ingredients to make a delicious pulled pork sandwich. Thank you duonyte for sharing this recipe, it's definitely a keeper!

attributes.source_text: my husband and I enjoyed the sandwiches

reviews.review_text: This was AMAZING. I had 2 3lb partially frozen pork butts I had gotten on "clearance" a while back and started at a little after 12pm. (I had misread another reciped for tenderloin that only needed 6 hours). I cut off all the fat (just hate to bite into that-ugg and cut them in 1/2 so they'd cook faster and fit in the crock pot better). My only addition was a bit of minced garlic, a splash of hot sauce and most of the can of ginger ale to account for the extra pork - cooked on high for 6 hours until it the meat was tender enough to shred. (I checked it at 4 and it was still pretty solid) Then I drained the juice, shredded the meat with onions and added the bbq sauce -Sweet Baby Rays-with a bit of water to rinse the extra sauce out and let it cook on low until we were ready to eat about 7:30. OMG- This was as good as Mission BBQ! Now if I could just make Maggie's Mac and Cheese...... Sigh For those who don't like onions, I am NOT a fan at all. I only used 1 here but I did mix it in. I didn't taste it at all. I'll definitely be making this again. Next time I'll throw it in before work on low all day. I can't wait and I just finished the last of it last night......

reviews.review_text: So, I usually read a LOT of reviews and tweak a recipe accordingly.  For this recipe, I didn't have a lot of time and I didn't want to buy a whole lot of ingredients, so I followed it exactly as written.  It was AWESOME!  The whole house smelled amazing all day!  I put the pork, onion and ginger ale in the crock pot the night before, and then the next day, strained everything and added the bbq sauce.  (I will say that my husband loves KC Masterpiece, so that's what we used, he doesn't care for sweet sauce.)   I think the pork turned out awesome!  I did read the author's note about how newer crock pots may cook the pork faster, and you'll have quicker cook times, and I do believe next time I won't need as much time.  Even on low, the pork cooked quickly- I left the house all afternoon and turned it to keep warm til dinner, since the sides were burning.  Maybe only needs a couple hours with bbq sauce, but since the ginger ale part is 12 hours, not sure how that would work, for timing for dinner.  But great recipe as written, no need to tweak! :)

reviews.review_text: Wow!  Who knew that a crock pot could produce such amazingly authentic pulled pork!? I used a 4.5 lb Boston Butt Roast and cooked it on low from 11pm until 10:30 am, which I will say really stunk up the house while we slept!   I then left it on "Keep Warm" for a couple of hours until I was ready to start the "pulling" process.  The meat was so tender and just fell right into strings.  I removed 85% of the onions and discarded them because I wanted an authentic pork sandwich.  After putting it back in the pot with the BBQ sauce (Sweet Baby Ray's was perfect!!!) I let it sit on Low for another 1.5 hours.  It did dry up the BBQ sauce a bit, but everyone agreed that this made it better since you could really appreciate the pork flavor, and didn't have a mouth full of wet BBQ sauce.  I made a fabulous coleslaw recipe from Gourmet magazine (which I've posted to share) and served it on top of the sandwiches as is traditionally done.  Thanks for a super-easy fabulous recipe!  It was worth the smelly house!

reviews.review_text:
I am reviewing the recipe two ways.  One as written and one with a variation suggested by Doug MC.  Both reviews are for the pulled pork itself and its juices, not the pulled pork with the BBQ sauce since that would be totally subjective based on the type and brand of sauce preferred by each chef and a not good review of the recipe itself.  Also, I made the variation one first as I forgot the ginger ale, but had apples and apple cider vinegar on hand.

"As Is"  - 4 Stars:  Prepared as directed.  It was good and had I made this BEFORE the variation, I would have given it 5 stars as I've never made pulled pork and wouldn't know any different.  The recipe was easy and delicious, but lacked some flavor and didn't WOW me like the variation recipe.  I used Pork Shoulder Butt (that's what the packaging said that I purchased from Kroger).  I couldn't find a 4 pound roast so I bought an 8 pounder and doubled the recipe.  I'm not sure what flavoring the ginger ale gave it, but I couldn't taste it.  I cooked on low for 11 hours and the meat shredded easily, was super tender and juicy.  Like the variation recipe, we also took out the onions after cooking/shredding.  Also, we did not add the BBQ sauce to the meat and simmer in the crockpot.  Instead, I put the shredded pork back in the crockpot with its juices and let it soak it up on Warm.  Adding BBQ sauce to the meat and simmering is just not how my husband eats it in the south.  Plus, if I had eaten it using my husband?s sauce mixed throughout, I would have given it 2 stars.  I don?t like his sauce.  LOL.  Served for Thanksgiving Dinner with mashed potatoes, gravy from the pulled pork juices, and roasted asparagus.  My husband definitely gives this a thumbs up and likes it so this is a keeper.

"Variation" -  5 Stars:  Instead of the ginger ale, I wanted to try Doug?s recommendation of 1 cup apple juice and 1 cup apple cider since I had that on hand ? did not have smoke flavor and did not use it.  Everything else in the  original recipe stayed the same.  I have a juicer so I juiced a Granny Smith apple for fresh apple juice.  I also used Braggs Organic Apple Cider.  I Poured in 1 cup of each.  I put mine in the crockpot when I left for work around 6:30 am with onions on top and on the bottom.  By time I came home at 4:30 pm, the meat was falling off the bone.  I turned it off and pulled the pork with a fork.  It was so tender and juicy.  I couldn?t help myself and ate some without the BBQ Sauce.  It had a nice tang to it?.maybe the vinegar did that, I don?t know or the apples, but it had a different flavor than just the ginger ale recipe.  It was still amazing.  I gave some to my husband, but he didn?t like the onions because ?that?s not how they do it in the south where he?s from?, so I removed the onions and put the meat back in the crockpot and into the juices.  Since he is from the South and usually is served his pulled pork plain with the sauce on the side so he can pour it over the meat on his sandwich, that is exactly how I served it for dinner.   I heated the BBQ Sauce.  He used Famous Dave?s Devils Spit Sauce.  He has always HATED everything I have ever cooked in the crockpot so he wasn?t hopeful that it would be good.  On the contrary, he LOVED IT!!!!  Instead of a traditional Thanksgiving dinner this year, he asked for pulled pork ? MADE IN THE CROCKPOT!  Excellent variation to the original recipe.  Will definitely will be making this again.

reviews.review_text: This process for cooking pork works really well and is very flexible.  I had a 2lb pork loin in the freezer and decided to give it a try. In the morning, I put it in the crock pot exactly per the instructions.  When I got home (approx 10 hours later), the pork was fall-apart tender and smelled fantastic.  I shredded the pork, discarded the onions and fat/juice, and returned the pork to the pot.  I then added approx 16 oz of bbq sauce and 1/4 cup beef stock to thin it out a bit.  Let it combine for approx 45 min.  My husband is a proud Texan who loves pulled pork.  He said it was awesome, quickly scarfed it down, and went back for seconds. I've made this twice, and follow the recipe nearly exactly. I buy and use a single 20 ounce bottle of Canada Dry ginger ale, instead of just the one cup. After draining the crockpot, removing the fat and shredding the meat, I like to add a cup or two of a vinegar-based barbecue sauce to keep the pork moist without making it too sweet. Then I add enough Sweet Baby Ray's (or occasionally other sauce) to get it to the perfect consistency.

I made this for our SuperBowl party yesterday, starting off with a 6.5lb Boston Butt pork shoulder. It was JUST enough to feed 18 people with side dishes and other things included. We all got at least one good sandwich. The recipe was met with raves. It's a winner because you only have to spend about 20-30 "active" minutes on it (removing the fat and shredding the pork) and it will keep from 1 hour to 8 hours on low after you've prepared it for serving. It doesn't get dry, it just gets more tender!

keywords: c("Rice", "Mexican", "Lactose Free", "Low Protein", "Low Cholesterol", "Free Of...", "< 60 Mins", "Inexpensive")
items.description:
Are you craving that great Mexican rice from your favorite taco stand? Here it is. This is just like a good Mexican restaurant rice. Many recipes taste good... but the texture just isn't right. You know how it is... you have prepared scores of Mexican rice recipes but always have been disappointed. It may be delicious but kinda "gloopy and wet." Try this. Everything is pureed and cooked in. There are no chunks of anything... just dry fluffy rice with all the seasonings and just the tiniest hint of a tomato flavor. I will throw away all of my Mexican rice recipes- this is the one I have been looking for for years! 

I don't own a rice cooker but some people have had disappointing results using one. You will also need to adjust your cooking time if you want to use brown rice. I recommend following the cooking instructions as directed. Proceed at your own peril if you stray.

Enjoy.
instructions: Adjust rack to middle position and preheat oven to 350.
Process tomato and onion in processor or blender until pureed and thoroughly smooth. Transfer mixture to measuring cup and reserve exactly 2 cups. Discard excess.
Remove ribs and seeds from 2 jalapenos and discard. Mince flesh and set aside. Mince remaining jalapeno. Set aside.

Place rice in a fine mesh strainer and rinse under cold running water until water runs clear- about 1 1/2 minutes.Shake rice vigorously to remove excess water.This step removes the starch from the rice so it will not stick. IF YOU OMIT THIS STEP YOUR RICE WILL NOT BE DRY AND FLUFFY.

Heat oil in heavy bottomed ovensafe 12 inch straight sided sautee pan or Dutch oven with tight fitting lid over low-medium heat about 2 minutes. (The recipe is very specific about this but I used a 10 inch dutch oven and it worked out fine.) Drop a few rice grains in and if they sizzle then it is ready. Add rice and fry stirring until rice is light golden and translucent, about 6-8 minutes.  Be careful that the oil doesn't get too hot too fast or the oil will splatter.
Reduce heat to medium, add garlic and 2 minced jalapenos and cook , stirring constantly until fragrant, about 1 1/2 minutes.
Stir in broth, pureed mixture,tomato paste, and salt. Increase heat to medium high, and bring to a boil.
Cover pan and transfer pan to oven to bake until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender, 30-35 minutes.Stir well after 15 minutes.
Stir in cilantro, minced jalapeno to taste, and pass lime wedges separately.

Edited to add 6-15-05: If you can't get good fresh tomatoes you are better off using canned tomatoes. Don't use those awful hard and underipe tomatoes that are at most supermarket chains. Just be sure that the processed tomatoes and the one onion equals 2 cups. One the other hand- if you find that after processing your tomatoes and onions that you have less than 2 cups- simply add enough bottled salsa to make up the difference.

Edited 8-21-06: Do not skip any of the steps. It may seem stupid- but rinsing the rice to remove the starch is very important if you want fluffy rice. It will only take two minutes of your time but it makes the difference.

Edited 8-15-08: Leftovers are just as delicious the next day so this is a perfect dish to make ahead time for potlucks. This rice also freezes well. For Freezing Ahead: Cool, portion and freeze in a ziploc bag. To reheat from frozen: Place in a pyrex dish and warm in the microwave, stirring every 2-3 minutes until heated through.
You'll love this rice! Money back guarantee.

I have been looking for a great mexican rice recipe and finally found it. This one is great. My family absolutely loved it and we have lived in various southwest states so we are very critical. I made a couple of changes because I had to use what I had on hand but will be sure to have all the ingredients next time.
1. I used olive oil instead of canola because I use olive oil for everything and will not buy a bottle of canola for one recipe but it certainly didn't hurt the recipe.
2. I used canned green chilis because I didn't have fresh jalapenos on hand but will get some for next time. It was still delicious but fresh jalapenos would be better. I didn't think the pickled jalapenos I had on hand would have been good.
3. I had to use boullion cubes because I was out of chicken broth - homemade & canned. It worked fine but will use the real stuff next time.
Even with these three subtitutions it was still yummy but I will go with the exact recipe next time except for the oil. I followed the instructions to the letter and had great success. I live in Florida now and this is better than any of the mexican rice in restaurants here.
I love the fact that it is finished in the oven because it frees up the stove top for other things.
I served it with Chili Colorado, refried beans and flour tortillas with guacamole, sour cream, lime wedges and fresh cilantro as add on's. The family ate until they couldn't move any more:)

reviews.review_text:
I just made this recipe yesterday for my son's football team's pre-game meal. I made two batches of the single recipe, not knowing how doubling rice would turn out (I think the proportions are different when you multiply rice). Next time I will actually double it with the servings calculator and update my review, because I think it would help to have a large crowd review on the board.
Anyhoo, I followed the recipe, but because of time constraints, I used a bottle of Herdez Medium Salsa instead of the tomatoes/onions/jalepenos, and made up the volume difference (to make 2 cups of tomatoes per recipe) with pureed canned tomatoes. I did find that I HAD TO FRY THE RICE FOR ALMOST 15 MINUTES to get it to the proper color. I think this is the most important step in the recipe for insuring that your rice will be fluffy, so don't quit at 6 minutes if the rice isn't light golden brown. I also added a tsp of cumin per recipe at the end of the fry time and stirred for a minute more.
I put both single batches in one of the big dutch ovens I used to fry the rice, and baked for 40 minutes on 365?. I did stir the rice at the 15 minute mark and added thawed peas, carrots and corn. Then because I had an hour before I had to transport, I turned off the oven and let the rice sit in there to keep warm.
THIS RICE TURNED OUT PERFECTLY! I am not hispanic, but even our hispanic players said this rice was better than their moms'! A couple of players thought they were eating at a restaurant :D We were scraping the bottom of the pan, and could have used another half recipe. We fed 32 people off of this double recipe, but could have used more.
If you're considering this for a crowd, don't hesitate. It's so easy, esp. if you are using the bottled salsa. But err on the side of making too much, because they will want seconds or thirds!

reviews.review_text: I did as suggested just to be able to review the recipe honestly with the rice rinsing, even though I cringed at the thought of all that wasted water going down the sink. It was fluffy, but I get fluffy rice in a rice-cooker & also on the hob; stir once, cook until holes appear, then turn heat down & take lid off for rice to finish/dry out. If rice is wet, there's too much water. I rather think that quality rice (in the UK), that's standard or premium rice in supermarkets, has already been rinsed because the 'value' types are indeed starchy & gloopy & go hard if you leave it in the saucepan, almost need a knife to cut it next day. The advice in the 70s was always to rinse it, but we had to buy it in ethnic shops who imported rice then, & pick it over for 'bits', until it was produced commercially by supermarkets, nobody rinses now. I halved the quantity so didn't need to fry the rice so long, not so much rice needing contact with the pan/oil. I don't know what jalapenos look like or their English or Indian name - which wouldn't do me much good anyway because their aren't any names on them usually, they're just called 'long chillis, thin chillis, fat chillis' etc. So I bought 'medium green chillis' from my Indian shop & the flavour came through wonderfully! (I think some larger supermarkets do sell a tray of just TWO jalapenos for a horrendous price. I bought a big handful for pennies (cents) & have chopped them & put them in water in ice-cube trays & frozen for later use. Served with veggy-mince, kidney beans & tomato (a chilli?) with sweetcorn & spiced okra & pitta bread. No money back needed, we did love it!! (daughter did take for lunch too as suggested). Next time, I'll make the quantity suggested, but do it on the hob or in the rice-cooker. I will put some in burritos too, my new-found recipe for last year, with some veggy-chilli, mushrooms, okra etc - a nice lunch, maybe with salad. Lovely rice, thanks!

reviews.review_text: The consistency and moisture was perfect, the taste was great!  Had to use canned jalapenos because the store didn't happen to have fresh.  Omitted the cilantro for the sake of my BF, but if you like it I urge you to include it.  Used only 1 tablespoon oil in a 10 inch Le Creuset Dutch oven (red:)).  Also used a good quality vegetable broth instead of chicken because we're vegetarian.  I rinsed my rice (for the first time in my life!?) and didn't use Uncle Ben's brand (hate it).  I think the next time I make this rice I'll use more tomato paste because I really like the tomato flavor in Mexican rice.  I did, however, have one rather annoying problem with this recipe.  I used a blender to puree the vegetables, so I cut the onion and tomato into large-ish chunks and it didn't blend very smoothly.  Had to keep stopping the blender to mash down the veggies.  The next time I make this I will blend the veggies and at least some of the broth together so it goes more quickly and ends up more smooth.  I'm surprised no one else had this problem.  Maybe everyone else used a food processor?  Thanks Potsie!  I've been wanting to try this recipe for months now!

reviews.review_text: Hey Potsie, This was the best Mexican rice. I used canned whole tomatoes (with the juice). Tossed the tomatoes, white onion, 2 jalapenos plus 1 serano and 4 garlic cloves into the blender together. I know that is not quite the recommended procedure but I just can't help myself. Added 2 cups of the mixture plus the broth and salt to the rinsed and browned rice (a little less oil), then into the oven for exactly 30 minutes. I forgot to stir after 15 minutes and it was great anyway. For those of you who do not have a stovetop to oven pot or skillet, take foil and wrap the handles of your pot and lid (at least 2 layers) and it will protect them just fine from the oven heat-I usually use 4 layers just to be sure). The rice was excellent. I think next time I will cut back on the garlic just a little (I had really large cloves) and I will add the tomato paste even though I will likely use canned tomatoes again. Other than that, the texture was perfect and it is now one of my go to recipes when having Mexican food, which living in So. CA., is often. Thanks again for the yummy recipe.

reviews.review_text: Color me amazed. This was the first time I made this recipe. I thought for sure there wasn’t enough liquid for this amount of rice. But I trusted the reviews and it was perfect. 35 minutes in the oven at 350. Very simple recipe to prepare. I had to use what I had as I couldn’t make it to the store today. So one can of unsalted tomatoes. One yellow onion (white would have been better). 4 garlic cloves. Swanson’s unsalted chicken stock. I had no jalapeños, so I subbed some homemade taco/Mexican seasoning. I added the seasoning towards the end of browning the rice in oil, along with the garlic. I think the oil brings out the spice's flavoring. I only had jasmine rice. Jasmine rice is a longish grain rice but tends to be sticky. Used primarily in Asian cooking. I was surprised at how fluffy it turned out. But I do think that regular long grain rice would have been better. This will go great with the chicken enchiladas I’ve prepared for tonight. My husband doesn’t care for beans so when I make a Mexican dish, I always make rice for him. Beans for me. Ha! This is far and away the best Mexican rice I’ve ever tasted. And I appreciate that I can make a very low sodium dish but with plenty of flavor. Homemade Mexican seasoning is the way to go. It tastes better with the high quality spices I have here at home.

reviews.review_text: I have commented previously on this recipe. I am doing again because I wanted to reinforce my opinion. This recipe is outstanding. I have hunters in camp for about a two month period in NW Wyoming every year. This is recipe is one of the most requested dishes. When asked about the recipe, I merely reference folks to this site and Pot Scrubber. This recipe is truly versatile and can be made at home in the oven or at camp using traditional Dutch ovens. You can vary the intensity of "heat" by amending your use of chilies. You can make it mild with Hatch Green chilies or heat it up all the way with Ghost Peppers. My only real variation is that I skip the puree and use one pint of my homemade salsa(s). My salsas give this dish its own unique characteristics. This recipe always results in fluffy rice. In my opinion, this is really the only "Mexican rice" recipe that you need. It delivers the basic flavor and fluffy quality that will satisfy the most picky rice eater. Use your imagination and/or flavor preferences to change the spice or heat. But follow the basic directions. For example, substitute Goya Sazon seasoning for salt. I thank the author for sharing this one. It is truly the best in my opinion.

reviews.review_text: Excellent! Easy to make and made with ingredients you most likely have in your pantry already. Tomatoes are not in season here, so I used a can of diced tomatoes (drained and saved the juice in case I needed it). Put the tomatoes and onion in a food processor to puree. Definitely take the time to rinse the rice - it makes a huge difference! After everything was combined I covered and finished on the stovetop (about 30 minutes), stirring every 10 minutes. Fresh cilantro really enhances the flavor. The rice turned out perfectly fluffy (as promised). Mild flavor so will appeal to everyones "heat" palette. I like mine a little spicer, so added some additional jalapeño and salsa verde on the side. May add a can of diced green chilies when making next time for even more flavor. My new favorite rice! This recipe makes a LOT, so be prepared for leftovers (never a bad thing). I plan on adding as a filling for stuffed burritos, etc. LOVE the fact that you can freeze as well for a quick dinner later. Thank you Pot Scrubber for this incredible recipe!

reviews.review_text: My husband is Dominican, so rice is something I cook every day.  I thought I would try this to give a variation from white rice.  It was excellent!  However, for those of you who would rather not rinse your rice and still have it come out fluffy and not sticky, I can tell you exactly how to do it.  It is the same way Dominican rice is cook.  Follow steps 2, 3, 5, 6, and 7.  YOU DO NOT NEED TO PUT IT IN TH OVEN.  EVERYTHING IS COOKED ON THE STOVETOP. Allow all the water to boil out of the pot.  When you see air holes in the rice and a wooden spoon can stand on its own in the rice, then you reduce the heat to medium low and cover the dutch oven with a tight fitting.  Continue cooking the rice for 25 - 30 minutes.  DO NOT REMOVE THE LID DURING THIS TIME.  This method is great for cooking any type of rice dish and you only have.  When rice is cooked properly, the grains will actually split open down the middle and have a firm texture to them, and that is exactly what happens when you cook rice by this method.

I like the texture better cooked in the oven, but when I have enchiladas cooking in the oven already, I just finish the rice on the stovetop and it still turns out. reviews.review_text: Wow great recipe! I usually make my banana bread from a well known cookbook but this will be my go to recipe from now on. I used everything to the measurement, including walnuts. Plus I added half cup of dried cranberries. I didn't measure the bananas, just used 3 very ripe small ones. I added the 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon 10 minutes into baking because I started reading the reviews and saw the addition from someone's review. It was only out of the oven a minute then I put it back in. I ended up cooking it an hour and 10 minutes. After an hour I stuck a butter knife in the middle and it was wet. So I tested a piece from the end and OMG was it good! reviews.review_text: This was delicious!!!. I made two loaves: one for my niece and her family and one for myself. Everyone thought it was wonderful. I noticed that no pan size was given. For those who might be novices, I used this size Wilton non-stick loaf pan: 9.25 x 5.25 x 2.75”/ 23.5 x 13.3 x 7.0 cm. I made my loaves with butter and used the butter wrappers to grease the pans. After removing from the oven, I placed them on a wire rack for about 5 minutes, ran a knife around the insides of the pans, and turned the loaves out onto the rack, and let them cool right-side up for several hours. I have attached a photo of how I measured the batter in order to keep the two loaves equal and how they looked once they were done. Happy eating everyone! Thank you for posting this recipe.

I was out of sour cream so I made a special trip to the store to get some. My mouth was watering for this bread, I hadn't even made it yet and I could taste it. The phone rang as I was making this and I was proud of myself that I could do two things at the same time; talk and bake. The house was filled with the smell of hot banana bread. Yum. Ding goes the bell and as I walked into the kitchen what did I see but the sour cream unopened still sitting on the cupboard.
All's well that ends well as they say. The bread was moist and delicious even without the sour cream but not nearly as good as I imagined how it would taste if only I hadn't answered that darn phone.

attributes.source_text: The bread was moist

reviews.review_text:
You certinly have a unique background and equally an outstanding and unique banana bread that if I could, would gtive 20 stars!!!! I am learning how to cook at 6,000 feet, this being 
my first SUCCESFUL high altitude loaf bread effort.  My house smelled sinfully delicious - I can't remember any other banana bread smelling like this. And, your photo is exactly how it looks sitting on my kitchen counter.  At first I was a bit apprehensive because the loaf was so brown, but little did I know that brownness provided a very delicious crunchy, sweet texture. I am using this tonight as a alternative to using a shortcake recipe for strawberries and whipped cream.  Well done and thank you!

attributes.source_text: a very delicious crunchy, sweet texture
a very delicious crunchy, sweet texture

reviews.review_text: This is fabulous! I used pecans, and I followed the recipe exactly, except I added 1 teaspoon of cinammon. Perfect! And I don't even like bananas! Thanks for sharing! 1/29/10--I just had to come back and add to this. We LOVE this recipe at our house. As I said earlier, I don't even like bananas, and I can't get enough of this bread. I have tried a few different recipes, and this is by far my favorite. This will be the only one I make from now on. I am not a big fan of nuts in my cakes/cookies, so I usually leave out the nuts altogether (unless someone requests, in which case I can pick them out), and I have amended the amount of cinnamon I add to 1 and 1/2 tsp. It's wonderful.

I made this tonight after doing an online search for banana bread.  I have to agree with everyone else here.  It is so delicious.  I followed the recipe exactly as it's written.  Next time I'll try the cinnamon addition.  I did add walnuts but it would be just as good without or with mini choc chips or pecans.  I made 2 smaller loaves and my 18 year old son ate 1/2 of one of the loaves when I pulled it out of the oven.  He said it's the most amazing banana bread he's ever had!  So this is a success and we will use this recipe from now on.  Moist and delicious.  I'm giving it to a friend of mine to try.  She uses different flours in her baking.  I'll have her post a review when she makes it.

attributes.source_text: my 18 year old son ate 1/2 of one of the loaves
Moist and delicious

reviews.review_text:
This is delicious and also my first time at baking banana bread! I made no changes to the ingredients aside from not including any nuts.

I reduced the baking time to 50 minutes and covered with foil for the last 15 minutes of that baking time to keep the top from getting too brown. I was baking something in my oven prior to baking the bread at a higher temperature before reducing the temperature to 350.....not sure if that made a difference or not. Next time I may bake at 325 for 1 hour and see what happens.

I doubt if I will throw ripe bananas away again since I found this yummy recipe!

I could easily rate this 10 stars. Made these as I had way over ripe banana's and sour cream to use up, so glad I opted for this recipe.  Since I am shipping the majority of this to my daughter in college I opted to make muffins.  I made two batches which yielded 24 large muffins, which cooked between 25 and 30 minutes each batch.  Additionally, I used pecans in the recipe, which I used my food processor to grind them on the fine side.  This was so easy to make and very <br/>yummy!!  I am currently typing my review as I am eating a muffin.  Thanks for the recipe this will be my go to for banana bread/muffins.

Thank you Charishma for this WONDERFUL RECIPE. Moist, delicate crumb, easy to make and impossible to stop eating. That said, I did make a few modifications. I'm not very good at following a recipe exactly. Replaced 1/2c brown sugar for whole cup of white. Added 1 tsp banana extract as well as extra tsp vanilla. Also 1/2 c sorghum flour in addition to white flour. I can't say that I improved on your recipe because I didn't make it exactly, so I don't know. But I do know that your recipe was a GREAT starting point. I will use this recipe frequently as Hubby though this some of the best that I have ever made.

Take care Judy in WA

attributes.source_text: Moist, delicate crumb
Moist, delicate crumb
Hubby though this some of the best that I have ever made

reviews.review_text: Thank you for this recipe Charishma. It worked out great for me.   I made a couple of little changes as others before me suggested...I lightly buttered and then lightly sugared the muffin mould (very good idea)..I made muffins and baked for about 25 minutes or so...I use a silicone muffin pan which I love. I did add the chopped walnuts and 1/4 cup dried cranberries.  I had actually forgotten to add the sour cream and pulled the muffins out of the oven after 3-4 minutes, topped each muffin with about 1 tsp of sour cream and then swirled the sour cream into each muffin. This recipe is a keeper :)

This has become a huge hit with my new in laws (mom, dad, and two brothers).  I've made it three times in the past two weeks, each time sending half the loaf over to them to share.  I'll have to start making them their own loaf however, since they've become rather territorial with each other over how many slices everyone gets.

It's really a very good bread- moist, dense, and flavorful, but not too sweet, thanks to the sour cream (which you don't taste at all).  I've made it with walnuts, and without, and have decided that the final product is much better with finally chopped walnuts.

Three very ripe bananas seem to do the trick, and I use full fat sour cream and butter.

reviews.review_text:
HI!!! I HAD TO COME BACK AND EDIT MY REVIEW BELOW- THE BREAD IS SO GOOD AFTER IT SAT-YUMMY- I TRIED IT FRESH OUT OF OVEN AND MAYBE IT WAS TOO HOT_ I DON'T KNOW BUT IT WAS GOOD TODAY AND MY BF SAYS ITS REALLY GOOD SO I THOUGHT I WOULD COME BACK AND CHANGE...... I am keeping the below here just so everyone knows that it was WORTH coming back and changing the first review BUT then again it has 127 reviews!!!!
