reviews.review_text: I took this recipe and totally made it over as a healthier version. I used the Sneaky Chef flour combination (wheat flour, wheat germ, white flour mix) added some oat bran and used Plain Greek yogurt in place of the sour cream. I used 3 medium bananas. I added nuts for some protein (although the yogurt has a lot). This is amazing. It is a little more moist than the picture but my kids loved it and I don't feel bad letting my family eat it. This has such a wonderful flavor with lots of added fiber and protein, not to mention Greek yogurt has no fat. I will certainly make this again.

attributes.source_text: It is a little more moist than the picture
my kids loved it

reviews.review_text: With all of the rave reviews, I must have done something wrong.  I followed the recipe to the letter, and by the hour mark the toothpick came out gooey.  Left the loaf in the oven another 30min (approx 90 min baking) til the toothpick came out clean. Loaf immediately fell.  After it cooled I cut into it and it was completely raw inside. Wonder if it's my loaf pan.  Going to give this another try, it smelled amazing while it was baking, and the cooked crust tasted great!  Too bad the inside was still raw.  Every banana bread recipe I have tried ends up like this, even my grandmothers recipe stays raw inside.

This is my favourite Banana Bread Recipe!! I refuse to use any other recipe and i think it the sour cream that makes it special. With no electric mixer required this recipes takes virtually no time, in fact it takes longer for the oven to warm up than it does to whip the ingredients together. Nuts are optional, I've tried walnuts, almond meal and pecans are great too. I tend to omit the nuts (or just use almond meal) so even the youngest member of our family can enjoy it. With ingredients that are always on hand, you are sure to have the fastest moistest banana bread that will never fail. Thanks for sharing!!

attributes.source_text: fastest moistest banana bread

items.label: Greek Potatoes (Oven-Roasted and Delicious!)
items.name: Greek Potatoes (Oven-Roasted and Delicious!)
items.description: These potatoes are a staple in our home. Whether accompanying roast lamb or chicken, or just on their own, we have them a couple of times a week. They are delicious and the ones that get overly-brown in the pan and stick a bit are MINE!  Clean up is a little tricky with this recipe, unless you line your pans with foil, but I find that just filling the pan up with hot, sudsy water and forgetting for an hour (something I apparently have no problem doing ;-)) helps a lot.
instructions: Preheat oven to 420°F  A reviewer has suggested spraying the baking pan with Pam - that sounds like a great idea!
Put all the ingredients into a baking pan large enough to hold them.
Season generously with sea salt and black pepper.
Make sure your hands are very clean and put them in the pan and give everything a toss to distribute.
The garlic will drop into the water/oil solution but its flavour will permeate the potatoes, and this way, it won't burn.
Bake for 40 minutes.
When a nice golden-brown crust has formed on the potatoes, give them a stir to bring the white underside up, season lightly with a bit more sea salt and pepper and just a light sprinkling of oregano.
Add 1/2 cup more water if pan appears to be getting dry, and pop back into oven to brown other side of potatoes.
This will take about another 40 minutes.
Do not be afraid of overcooking the potatoes- they will be delicious.
Note:  I often melt a bouillon cube in the water; if you do, make sure to cut back some on the salt.

reviews.review_text:
Ev, since these were cooked on live fire, I changed the procedure a bit. Really wanted the recipe but it was 95 degrees and didn't want to heat up the kitchen.
I mashed the garlic between foil. Chopped up fresh Greek oregano and added both to the olive oil and lemon juice in a large skillet. I put the combination on low heat and infused the herb and garlic into the oil and juice mixture. By the time the garlic turned a light tan, the proportions were just right. Then I strained out the solids and brushed the tater sections with the oil/juice before miking 8 minutes. Then skewered them, put on the grill after brushing with the goodies. Turn, brush, turn, brush, etc., until done. I brushed them again with the oil/juice before serving.
I needt any water because of cooking the taters partially in the mike.
This was a real experiment, and they turned out beautifully. I used 30 red taters, unpeeled, about the size of an unshucked black walnut, cut in half.
We loved the flavor and am reserving the leftover oil infusion in the fridge for other uses, it's too good to throw away!
Thanks, Ev, for another winner.

I'm a little late in reviewing these great potatoes, but that just means that my review is based on three different tries! So here is what I learned: first of all, I made them in a glass baking dish and I did wipe it down with butter first.  After that, I followed the recipe exactly as stated and they turned out great!  I ended up roasting them for 40 mins - turning them in the liquid - and then roasting them just another 20 mins.  Then I let them cool down and, once cool, put them in the fridge overnight. Then, the next day, I let them come back to room temperature before putting them into a 350 degree oven for 40 minutes to reheat them - and they were perfect!  Very crunchy on the outside but sweet and creamy on the inside. I didn't try adding some chicken stok, but might next time! This really is foolproof and a great make-ahead recipe!

attributes.source_text: sweet and creamy on the inside
Very crunchy on the outside
sweet and creamy on the inside

reviews.review_text:
The first time I made them, they were perfect. The second time I made them, I lined the pan with two half sheets of foil and that was a mistake as the juices seeped through away from the potatoes. Luckily I fixed the problem at the forty minute mark. They remind me of middle eastern potatoes at a kabob place near here. Before we found your recipe we were known to go there just for side orderes of potatoes to go! Thanks for a great recipe.
Update: I am making these for Thanksgiving  dinner now, I saw they recently got a mediocre review and I thought I would comment, because I think there is no way you could make these properly and find them mediocre. (Unless you grew up with these kind of potatoes so are used to excellent potatoes and that is just normal to you) I thought, too, I would add that I cut them smaller than the ones pictured, I cut them in 4's lenghtwise the in fours width wise. Also I use a bit more garlic. As Evelyn says, you can't over cook these, well, I love them really browned so I actually cook them longer.  Right now I actually added almost twice the garlic and haven't turned them yet after over an hour in the oven because they are just now beginning to get the "nice golden brown crust". So be aware your oven could be different and try a bit different timing or proportions, but this is a fantastic method!

attributes.source_text: I use a bit more garlic
beginning to get the "nice golden brown crust"
I am making these for Thanksgiving  dinner now

reviews.review_text: Taste wise, this recipe is simply superb. I used the juice of one lemon, which gave the potatoes plenty of lemony flavor, and I went heavier on the garlic. I also had some chicken stock in the fridge I needed to use, so I used that in place of water, and I really think it bumped them up a notch in deliciousness. When I turned the potatoes over, I added a light dusting of sea salt, but didn't go crazy with it, since I used the chicken stock. Just one note: in my oven, to get them to even start browning, I had to increase the heat to 450 degrees. Both to decrease cooking time and for my own preference, I quartered the potatoes instead of cutting them into wedges. Oh, and I used red potatoes, skin on, because that's how I like it. =) All of my ingredients were organic, which I truly believe the quality of the parts had a lot to do with how excellent this dish turned out. I will be making these often! Next time I may add an onion.... yummy! I'm hungry again just thinking about it!

attributes.source_text: gave the potatoes plenty of lemony flavor
I went heavier on the garlic
I added a light dusting of sea salt

reviews.review_text: Holy moly these are great potatoes!  I lined a cookie pan with foil and sprayed it with PAM.  I also mixed everything in a large ziploc bag instead of mixing in the cookie pan (except salt and pepper which I cracked over them once they were on the cookie pan).  I had a small half sweet yellow onion I added, as I wanted to use it up, also used 7 garlic cloves instead of 4, as we like garlic.  (The house smells divine!!).  Otherwise, I stuck with the recipe as written and we also loved the really crispy, dark ones that looked burned the best.  I only had one potato that stuck and I turned all of them with two forks.  When they were done cooking I placed them on another parchment lined cookie pan and put them in the oven to drain any excess oil.  They were in there for about 5 minutes (oven was off but still warm), while our lobster tails were cooking.  Yummy dinner and the potatoes were every bit as delicious as the lobster!  Will definitely make again and again.

attributes.source_text: used 7 garlic cloves instead of 4, as we like garlic
we also loved the really crispy, dark ones
Yummy dinner

reviews.review_text: Outstanding, Evelyn! Easy to throw together - no need to measure - just drizzle evoo liberally on top of the potatoes, dried oregano to be thrown on top liberally as well, same with salt and pepper, and a strong squeeze of 2 lemons over a bag of fingerling potatoes, and you have enough to serve 15-20 (I had 10 over, but went big - the leftovers are great thrown back in the oven the next day!). Oh, I used WAY more garlic - I'm unable to use a measly amount like 8 cloves (for doubling)... I buy garlic by the pounds :) Anyway - I used fingerling potatoes, some cut in half lengthwise, some cut differently, and others (smaller) left whole. All of them were good! It marinated in the mixture for about 4 hours, then placed in a 450 degF oven, and let cook for quite a while - these just get better with longer cooking.

I varied my grilling method from Green Dragon Mom but enjoyed them just as much as she did.  I used the 8 potatoes evelyn/athens listed, but used large red potatoes unpeeled and cut into fairly large chunks.  I then used same quantity of other ingredients given.  For grilling, I follweed Green Dragon Mom's method up to the point where she drained off all liquids, nuked potatoes 8 minutes then placed the potatoes on skewers.  I only drained off half remaining liquid, did not nuke and placed the chunked potatoes on a double sheet of greased heavy duty foil.  I placed packet on upper warming rack of my gas grill, and grilled abouut 20 minutes while meat was grilling on lower rack.  I checked to make sure they were fork-tender, served with dinner and accepted raves from people sharing our meal!

attributes.source_text: I checked to make sure they were fork-tender
served with dinner

reviews.review_text: I can't believe I haven't rated this recipe yet.  I make these ALL the time since I found the recipe.  When I have fresh potatoes(small red, fingerlings, bakers) and don't know what to do with them, here you go.  I sometimes substitute lemon pepper for lemons if I don't have them, but otherwise I make them as is. Sometimes I'll prep them early and let them sit, and sometimes just throw and go.  And I ALWAYS line the pan with the RELEASE reynolds wrap, and clean up is a snap!  Just throw the foil away and there you go.  Otherwise, clean up is a bit messy.  I make these for a side item, or sometimes I just have these for dinner.  LOVE THEM! Thanks evelyn/athens for sharing a great and simple recipe. Keep them coming!!!!!!

attributes.source_text: I make these for a side item
sometimes I just have these for dinner

reviews.review_text: A HUGE thank you is sent with this review. I prepared these wonderful potatoes for a Medieval Feast for my daughter's class room.  The children just loved these potatoes and out of 40 children, I think at least half must have told me that they thought they were the best potatoes ever.  I prepared about 18bs of them and there was not one left!!  I found that the potatoes that turned out the best were done in glass pans or Pampered chef ware.  The ones that I cooked in metal pans lined with foil stuck to the foil terribly.  All that wonderful outer crust was stuck to foil. (Not to worry, I did not waste it, but picked at it later and nibbled on it myself.)  Therefore, I would not recommend using foil in the pan.  I have been wanting to try this recipe since joining Zaar and I am really glad I did as it is superior to my regular recipe.  So, 40 big thank yous for you today, plus one more for making me look so good!

attributes.source_text: for a Medieval Feast
The children just loved these potatoes
All that wonderful outer crust

reviews.review_text: I'd been craving greek style taters for some time and googled up/stumbled upon this recipe. I decided to combine it with recipe #215798, since the ingredients were exactly the same. Went and got the best kalamata olive oil I could find, a few white potatoes, a few pork chops and ran back home. Just couldn't wait to experiment with it! I quadrupled the amount of fresh garlic, sprinkled one pork chop and two potatoes with a bit of accent, kosher salt, oregano, bottled lemon juice and a generous amount of the kalamata olive oil. Then let the whole thing marinade about one hour, in the excitement almost forgot the coarsely crushed fresh black pepper!  Threw them in the toaster oven, turning each piece after about 40 minutes. This is a grainy picture I took with my camera phone when it was half way done. There are no other pictures because it was gone far too fast!

attributes.source_text: greek style taters

reviews.review_text: I loved the flavor of these, but I was scared that I COULD cook them too long. I reduced the recipe, for 2 huge potatoes. After 40 minutes, there was no 'white side' and I got scared that they were over cooking (even tho you say they can't be...) and I added water to the pan twice in the last 20 minutes or so. I should have reduced my oven temp; I would have not been so worried, but I was trying to follow directions, and working 3 'recipes' at once. I enjoyed the flavor of the potatoes, and I was super glad that I had used foil! I used 3 garlic cloves and lots of sea salt and fresh ground pepper. I will be making these again! Thanks for sharing, Ev! Made for ZWT.

These potatoes are delicious! I used non-stick foil and they didn't stick but were beautifully done. A great recipe, worth trying. I usually make roasted potatoes with just olive oil and herbs, but the addition of water and lemon was such an improvement that this recipe will replace my normal go-to side dish. They are cooked at a high heat for quite a long time.

I served them along with blanched fresh green beans that I sauteed in browned butter for a few minutes, then tossed in a few sesame seeds near the end; also, chicken breasts I brined and then grilled; and a big garden salad. Lovely meal, and it feels like a summer meal although today is January 1st, 2011...a beautiful warm day in Florida.

attributes.source_text: this recipe will replace my normal go-to side dish

reviews.review_text: I made these potatoes for the first time (I've been meaning to for a long time!) this week for my new family - I just relocated from Toronto to Winnipeg for love.  I needed something that was simple and delicious, and would go with my fabulous souvlaki - and wow, did this to the trick!  The only change I made was to use baby potatoes as that's what Harry had on hand (used 5 baby potatoes per large potato, probably could have used 6 or 7).  I cut the potatoes in half to soak in the wonderful juices, popped them in the oven as directed, and was rewarded with the best potatoes with the least effort I've ever had!  Thanks, Evelyn, for sharing this garlicky, lip-smacking, dish - reminiscent of my trip to Santorini years ago with my Mom.  This will be my go-to Greek potato dish from now on!

attributes.source_text: garlicky, lip-smacking, dish
my go-to Greek potato dish

reviews.review_text: Top-notch oven-roasted potatoes are like Bach's suites for solo violoncello.. the de-facto standard by which cellists are judged. Thus it should be with home cooks.. if you can make them well, welcome to the Hall of Excellence.. for they are difficult, capricious, temperamental and can easily go wrong.  For more than a quarter century my baked potatoes were burnt-skinned or undercooked, flavorless or oily...   NO MORE !!   This recipe is pure genius !  It has created a social upheaval in our humble household of a cat, two ravenous teenagers and a vegetarian wife. I feel like Mick Jagger with a gaggle of adoring groupies.. even the CAT likes them !<br/>It's the water that I didn't think of for 25 years.. ( who would think of baking with water !! )  and Evelyn mentions it casually, like the consummate professional she is, without hardly an underline.. <br/>In addition I use it as a basis for all kinds of exotic strains of oven potatoes. Sprinkle some Piri-Piri on it and you have the Mozambique variety, fiery and burns the teenagers into a subdued hush, rub cajun spices in the potatoes and you have a Louisiana Pirate Fantasy.. I even tried it with Teriyaki powder..( Cat did not like it...)<br/>One thing I noted was that the type of potatoes used really influences the outcome. My best choice was yellow, slightly waxier potatoes. I wonder what other people's experiences have been.<br/>Also for the first 45 mins I use a foil canopy over them, which I then take off for better browning. thank you Ev.

attributes.source_text: two ravenous teenagers
a vegetarian wife

reviews.review_text: OH MY GOODNESS - these were absolutely the most fabulous potatoes I've ever made or even tasted.  I followed the recipe exactly except I did use a bit too much lemon (lemons are bigger here), but it didn't matter.  I was testing recipes for a dinner party and usually steer away from potatoes (not my fave).  But I was making a lamb dish (Minted BBQ'D Lamb Chops - also VERY yummy) and this seemed to go perfectly.  It did.  Its like the potatoes just absorb every single flavor in the recipe and the consistency is perfect!  My female family members who usually take maybe one bite of carb, gobbled this up and even asked for more, which I unfortunately didn't have as I wasn't used to them eating potatoes... EVER.  Next batch will be made with loads extras - hubby's orders :)

attributes.source_text: I was testing recipes for a dinner party
My female family members who usually take maybe one bite of carb, gobbled this up and even asked for more

reviews.review_text: I made these tonight for diner and they are awesome.  When I used to manage this store many years ago, there was a greek resturant in the mall, that served potatoes similar to this.  I was prego with my daughter at the tme and I swear I must have eaten those darn things every day I was there.  I haven't had them i about 2 years so finding this recipe and making it was like heaven.  i follwed directions exactly except I used regualr salt didin't have any course salt but i still loved them.  I made enough to fil a 9x13 pan, and they were all gone.  Thanks so much for posting this I will make these for sure again and again, and your right the ones that are mopre and stick are definately mine.  Thanks again for bringing back a really good memory for me.

attributes.source_text: I made these tonight for diner

reviews.review_text: We were absolutely delighted with this totally scrumptious recipe, which we enjoyed with evelyn's Keftedakia (Greek Meatballs) Recipe #59573.  Had the meatballs not been SO delicious, we could all have so easily eaten even more potatoes – and nothing but the potatoes!  They were wonderfully crisp and SO flavoursome – just loved the fabulous blend of garlic, lemon and oregano - and what a bonus that they are NOT over the top in their fat content.  There was enough olive oil for flavour, and the lemon juice added heaps more flavour.  About halfway through the cooking, I added the juice of another half lemon.  No adding water for me: I love the flavour of lemon juice too much for that!  Sensational recipe, evelyn!

attributes.source_text: They were wonderfully crisp
just loved the fabulous blend of garlic, lemon and oregano
just loved the fabulous blend of garlic, lemon and oregano

items.label: Reeses Squares - 5 Ingredients & No Bake (Reese's)
items.name: Reeses Squares - 5 Ingredients & No Bake (Reese's)
items.description: These bars are EXTREMELY RICH and not for people with a fear of CHOCOLATE and PEANUT BUTTER (if those people actually exist)!!! Very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!
instructions: Combine graham crumbs, sugar and peanut butter and mix well.
Blend in melted butter until well combined.
Press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan.
Melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler.
Spread over peanut butter mixture.
Chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets \

reviews.review_text:
I took the idea from another reviewer to make a small portion - in my case a single serving.  I put 2 tablespoons peanut butter, 2 tablespoons powdered sugar, two tablespoons of graham cracker crumbs and a thin slice of butter (approx. 1/2 tsp) in a small ceramic container and warmed it for about 10 seconds in the microwave.  I mixed this together and it was pretty crumbly, but I didn't want to add more butter so I used a tart tamper (actually I used a heavy tamper from my espresso machine) and pressed the mix into a silicon muffin cup that I stabilized in a muffin tin.  When I got the mix good and compressed, I warmed up some milk chocolate in the microwave (only give it a ten second zap then remove it and stir well EACH time even if the chocolate doesn't seem to be melting.  Stop microwaving before it completely melts. Allow the residual heat to finish the melting so you can avoid scorching the chocolate).  I used a small silicon pastry brush to brush melted chocolate on top of the compressed peanut butter mix.  Then it went into the refrigerator and I went out shopping.

I broke the sound barrier driving home when I remembered my faux-reese's cup was waiting for me in the refrigerator. Yum, yum, yum.  It popped right out of the silicon muffin cup.  My dogs helped with the calories and this was lunch.  I sure am glad I didn't make a whole pan of these - too rich and too tempting, but making (and eating) one was sure fun!

attributes.source_text: this was lunch

reviews.review_text: Oh yes! A hit! A very powerful hit! My dad has become my biggest (cooking) fan, since I made these for him. But I did do a few things differently. 1) I made the batch exactly as called for, but I lined an 8x8 pan, instead of a 9x13, with wax paper. And then I did an extra cup or so of chocolate, and did a bottom layer, the peanut butter mix, and then the top layer. I then put it the freezer until it was cold enough to touch, but still able to be cut. Then it cut very easily into itty bitty bite sized pieces. and 2) with the extra peanut butter filling, I spooned whatever size spoonfuls I wanted onto wax paper, and stuck them in the freezer for about 20 minutes. Then I melted some dipping chocolate, and using a fork, I dropped them in, and used the fork to fish them out and drain the chocolate, before putting them back onto the wax paper. They cooled very quickly since the insides were already cold, and there was no cutting involved. I just peeled them off the paper and threw them in the tupperware container with the other cut pieces. Tell ya what! This is THE peanut butter and chocolate recipe! Christmas plates have never been so happy! =D

attributes.source_text: My dad has become my biggest (cooking) fan, since I made these for him
Christmas plates have never been so happy

reviews.review_text: I've recently started cooking about a year ago right out of university, and I have a tendency to get it wrong the first couple of times. But I have to say this recipe is incredible and so easy that I aced it on my first try. I read through many of the reviews and noted several of the helpful tips. Here's how I did it: I reduced the sugar to 2 cups and used icing sugar, I also reduced the melted butter to only 3/4 of a cup, lined the baking tray with foil before I added everything, and finally after I let it cool off in the fridge for about 45 mins to an hour I took the foil out of the tray and flipped the whole thing over so that the chocolate would be on the bottom then I easily cut it up into bite size squares right out of the fridge, it didn't crack at all! All in all an excellent recipe, everybody couldn't get enough so I had to make a whole other one the very next day. Thank you for a delicious treat!.

I'm sorry to say I was very disappointed in these. The ingredients and directions are quite easy to follow, but the result was to my taste nothing like a "Reese's", instead it was overwhelmingly sweet, and not inexpensive to make at about $5.00 a batch.

Since I've received so many unhelpful votes on my original review and this recipe is still getting raves, I decided to try again, and  test it with a Reese's expert, my dad(the man who could eat a box of the mini reeses in one evening).
This only change I made was to use a 15 x 10 pan, to thin out the base.  This change alone made it worthy of another star.  My "expert" said it wasn't good enough to be a true Reese's because it didn't have chocolate on the bottom, but he liked the over all taste and texture.  I think a little more chocolate, maybe another cup of chips, because of the thinner base would be in order.

attributes.source_text: he liked the over all taste and texture

reviews.review_text: I definitely think these taste like peanut butter eggs..not so much just like a Reese's...but for sure JUST AS GOOD!!! :)  I cut the recipe in half b/c I didn't want to eat it all by myself.  Which I am hoping no one else in my family likes them so I can keep them all but I doubt that will happen.  I have a lot of meetings to go to for my husbands deployment and I am always searching for easy but amazing things to bring and I think I found my next star :)  I pulled it out at 20 minutes and did like a rough cut and made 25 squares in a 8 x 8 pan, then 10 minutes later went back in and re cut and they were perfect.  I am definitely going to try what someone suggested by spreading a layer of chocolate on the bottom and letting it harden then putting the peanut butter mixture on top.  I am also going to throw in some coconut next time b/c they make me think of the pb egg we always ate as kids!  Thanks for this great recipe!

attributes.source_text: these taste like peanut butter eggs

reviews.review_text:
I made these as indicated in the recipe but when I tasted the mix,  it tasted like confectioner sugar not peanut butter. I therefore added an extra 1/2 cup of peanut butter. I was afraid to add more for fear the base would not set.  They set fine but I still found the sugar taste outweighted the peanut butter flavor despite mixing the heck out of it. I'm going to try it again with 3/4 cups less sugar but use 3/4 more graham cracker crumbs in order to have the same ratio of binding ingredients.  As far as cutting without cracking the chocolate, it's simple. Line the pan with foil.  Chill. Remove from the pan and flip upside down. Use a very long knife and cut across the 9" side peanut butter first. My knive is more than 9 inches so I could cut down in one stroke. Simply cut it the other way in two sections. Not a cracked piece!
My kids loved this regardless of my feeling the sugar was too overwhelming of the peanut butter.

attributes.source_text: My kids loved this

reviews.review_text: Very good recipe, I didn't understand what the graham cracker crumbs were for until I tasted my first bar, it gives it the perfect texture. I lined the pan with aluminum foil, even up the sides. The harder you press the peanut butter mixture into the pan the less likely it is to crumble. After the chocolate had set I just lifted the whole thing out of the pan and cut it on my cutting board, which made perfect, straight, squares even on the edges. I would cut these into 60 squares since they are so rich (10x6 cuts). If you cut them once the chocolate sets, then refridgerate until the chocolate is solid you can place in an airtight container in the fridge. About an hour before you want to serve them remove them from the fridge and place on plates. This will keep the chocolate as perfect as when you cut it, but you will get the perfect texture from the room temperature.

attributes.source_text: they are so rich

reviews.review_text: These were wonderful!  I made them for a Super Bowl party.  After I got home with the ingredients, my sister called to ask me to come over to her house to go to the party with her (and make this recipe at her house).  I was worried that it would take a long time to make the recipe AND refrigerate the chocolate long enough to set before we needed to be at the party).  Once at my sister's house, it took roughly 10 minutes to make this dessert.  I put it into the frig, but after about 10 minutes, the chocolate was still very soft.  So, I put it into the freezer for about 12-15 minutes.  It was perfect after this.  Though this was a dessert for our Super Bowl party, this was put out with the other appetizer dishes.  It soon disappeared!  I heard people make comments how they loved the texture of the peanut butter mixture.  I had several people ask for the recipe, and as it only has 5 ingredients, I was readily able to repeat it.  Thanks for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: I made them for a Super Bowl party
this was a dessert for our Super Bowl party
this was put out with the other appetizer dishes

reviews.review_text: Every year for Christmas I bake my usual and I always try 1 or 2 new recipes. This recipe was my try something new recipe. WOW! I'm glad I did! First I have to say that this is simple to make and so few ingredients makes it an inexpensive recipe. Secondly the taste. I don't think you could get any closer to tasting like a Reeses Peanut Butter cup than this! These are FAB! I was going to use semi-sweet chocolate chips but decided to follow the recipe and use milk chocolate. I really like it with the milk chocolate and will stick with the milk chocolate. I'm going to add this to my bake every Christmas cookie platter list. If I could give it more than 5 stars I would based on simple, inexpensive, few ingredients, impressive and terrific tasting! Thanks for sharing your recipe here at Zaar! Happy Holidays! =)

attributes.source_text: I'm going to add this to my bake every Christmas cookie platter list

reviews.review_text: These are absolutely delicious.  I wasn't sure what to expect since some of the reviews said this tasted more like Butterfinger than Reese's, but I found that they taste just like Reese's, and maybe even better.   I made a somewhat healthier version of these since I don't eat white flour or refined sugar. I had to make my own graham crackers using spelt flour and sucanat.  I also substituted sucanat for the sugar (I used a little less than called for) and I used grain-sweetened chips for the chocolate chips.   These are amazing and I will make them again.  The only downside is how fattening they are.   Thanks for a declicious recipe which is even more special to me because I don't eat store bought candy bars due to the refined sugar.  It's nice to have such an easy healthier version of my own to prepare.   My boyfriend loved them too.

attributes.source_text: My boyfriend loved them too

reviews.review_text: The first time I made these I thought I had everything I needed, but it turned out I didn't have enough powdered sugar.  So I used the one cup I had and 1 1/4 c regular sugar.  (1c reg = 2c powdered sugar)  Anyways this time I made sure I had everything I needed, and I didn't like them as much!!  My hubby liked my first ones a lot better also.  So my 5 stars are for the recipe being 1 c. confectioners sugar and 1 1/4 c. normal sugar with everything else being the same!  And for sure put wax paper in the pan no matter which way you make them!  Oh I also put marshmallow cream on 1/2 of it under the chocolate, and that's our fav. way to have it now... IT'S SO GOOD!!!  I only put it on 1/2 just to try it, but now I'll put it on all...  try it, it's great!  Thanks, great base recipe!!

attributes.source_text: My hubby liked my first ones a lot better also

reviews.review_text: What can I say that hasn't already been said?  When I saw this recipe, I decided to give it a try.  I love Reese's peanut butter cups, I love peanut butter, I love chocolate, and I love easy recipes.  So I figured this one fit the bill.  They were so easy to prepare after work.  BF told me to get them out of his house or he would eat the whole pan, so I left just a few there and took the rest to work.  Needless to say, they didn't last long; and I was chastised for bringing them in because people couldn't leave them alone.  I didn't change any of the ingredients, and this recipe could easily be cut in half for those who don't need an entire 9x13 pan of them.  Thank you SO much for posting this recipe.  It will definitely be made again -- possibly only half a recipe so I don't get yelled at again!  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: BF told me to get them out of his house or he would eat the whole pan
I was chastised for bringing them in because people couldn't leave them alone

reviews.review_text: I was actually going to give these 3 stars, maybe 4.  They were just too sweet for us!  So Sushiman just packed them up and took them off to the synagogue with him on Saturday morning.  The guys like to get together after prayers are over with a bit of whiskey and a something sweet to nosh on.  Good idea, I thought, get rid of them there!  After prayers were over and we were all hanging out in the courtyard of the synagogue, someone came up to me and said, "Great peanut butter bars!"  I had to smile.  Then I got another compliment, and another, and another!  By the time we walked home you couldn't wipe the smile off my face!  So these bars get 5 stars.  Jeez, I'd give them 100 stars if I could!  I haven't felt that good since Chia's asparagus recipe got me a marriage proposal!  I am definitely going to make these babies again, just cut back on the sugar this time.  I may not have enjoyed these bars according to the original recipe, but they made me feel great!  Thanks!

The goal here is to duplicate the taste of a Reese's Peanut Butter Cup and this recipe did just that according to my family (I can't eat the sugar). For my other peanut butter cup recipe you end up making balls of peanut butter dipped in chocolate. They taste great, but this is so much easier and still has that same taste to it. I will be making these from now on.  UPDATE: Let me start off with, this review is based upon my experience making them and the experience of others eating them.  (I can't eat sugar).  That said, they were easy to make - much better than the recipes were you make them into balls.  As for taste, I was told that it needed more chocolate, so next time I will make them in a larger pan and double the millk chocolate chips, however despite that everyone agrees they taste great.

attributes.source_text: according to my family

reviews.review_text:
I brought 36 bars of it to a pot luck, none came back home. These were universally enjoyed, though I will admit I was very suspicious of the recipe until the butter was mixed in. Be warned: This recipe basically uses an entire jar of peanut butter, an entire package of confectionary sugar, and two bars of butter.

We were out of graham crackers, so we crumbled a ready made graham cracker pie crust and smashed up some Swedish ginger thins for the remainder. We also used 8 Hershey's Chocolate bars, melted in the microwave at 50% power. If I was to make this recipe again, I would likely use better chocolate, perhaps something darker. It is tempting to add more chocolate than the recipe calls for, but it is plenty. Thanks!

attributes.source_text: I brought 36 bars of it to a pot luck

reviews.review_text:
These went over SO well :) I made sure to use "Hershey" chocolate chips, because...well, I wanted to be true to the fact that Reeses is a Hershey product. It was VERY convincing!
DELICIOUS! I DID use a bit more peanut butter than the recipe called for. Maybe 1/4 cup more was added to the base mixture before spreading it out in the pan. I spooned it in a little at the just because I felt like it was too sugary, with not enough of that Reeses peanut butter flavor. You have to be careful not to change the consistency too much, because those graham crackers need to absorb all that delicious butter (I used salted butter, btw...I think that makes a difference!) The addition of the extra peanut butter helped make it more authentic, in my opinion. All in all, YUMMY!

attributes.source_text: not enough of that Reeses peanut butter flavor
all that delicious butter
I used salted butter, btw...I think that makes a difference!

reviews.review_text: HOLY MOLY these made my eyes pop open after the first little bite! I made these with margarine and semi-sweet chips (that's what I had). I will take some of the others' advice and cut back on the sugar next time (there WILL be a next time!). I can pick out the super-sweet sugar flavor over the peanut butter, which saddens me. Lining the dish with waxed paper sounds like a good idea, too. And I'll try to keep better track of how long it took my little morsels to 'set'. This time I just ran back & forth to the kitchen. They certainly are delicious, but not quite like Reese's. They're more like fudge squares that we ate with a fork - and took a time-out halfway through to avoid extreme sugar rush. Any ideas how to make the peanut butter layer a little lighter & fluffier?

attributes.source_text: They're more like fudge squares that we ate with a fork

reviews.review_text: As if 280 ratings weren't enough... Good dessert but I was slightly disappointed by these in that they tasted a little too buttery. Things I may do different next time: 1) use ever so slightly less butter, 2) put in a larger pan so the peanut butter mixture spreads out thinner, 3) use natural peanut butter instead of a name brand with sugar in it, 4) mix some semisweet morsels with the milk chocolate.  Things that would've made the recipe itself more helpful: 1) note that the mixture of peanut butter, crumbs, and sugar will stay crumbly until the butter is mixed, 2) note an approximate chilling time for optimal cutting, which for me was about 20 minutes.  Thanks, though, this is very easy and my dept at work ate the whole batch!

attributes.source_text: Good dessert
my dept at work ate the whole batch

reviews.review_text:
Karen, even though you warned that folks who don't typically eat chocolate-peanut butter combos should stay away, I have to add a testimonial here from my household. My hubby won't eat Reese's. He doesn't like peanut butter cookies, etc., etc. And when I made these he groaned. But when he saw me eating these yummalicious bars with ecstacy written all over my face, he tried one. Guess what, everybody! Not only did he eat one, but he got a second helping (and these things are frightfully rich, even how I made them) and then ate more on successive evenings until they were all gone. He told me to make them again sometime.

This recipe seems fool-proof and easily adaptable. The amount of fat and calories scared me, so I reduced the butter to one STICK (1/2 cup) and only used 1 1/2 bags of chocolate chips. The texture, I believe, was affected: they were drier than Reese's peanut butter cups (which gave us an indication how extremely rich those candies are, too) but they were divine, absolutely divine. I'll continue to make them the "lower fat" (who are we kiddin?) way, because we loved em! So easy to make, too.

Thanks, Karen, for posting this recipe ten years ago. People like us are still discovering these and spreading smiles around our family tables.

attributes.source_text: he got a second helping
He told me to make them again sometime
these things are frightfully rich

reviews.review_text: Like this recipe needs another review! My husband came home yesterday and needed to make something to take to a pot luck luncheon at work, so we experimented with a recipe out of the local paper.  It was absolutely horrible, and time consuming to make. What I didn't know until then is the reason for the potluck was for sharing favorite recipes!  He was so deflated and burned out, it was Obvious which recipe he needed!  Fifteen minutes later, he had a 5 star recipe worth sharing.  We left them on the counter overnight; at room temperature the cutting was smooth and bars were beautiful.  I've found the taste is also best at room temperature, so if presentation is important, making these ahead without chilling will do the trick!

items.label: Chicken Tortilla Soup II
items.name: Chicken Tortilla Soup II
items.description:
I'm getting tired of seeing the so-called tortilla soup recipes running around that are nothing but a glorified chicken soup with tortillas added. Here's the real McCoy. Similar to the recipe at Houston's restaurant (modified, of course, to suit my tastes)

For a beef version check out my recipe #261711.
instructions: Saute carrots, onions, celery in corn oil, garlic, salt and pepper until  tender.
Add chicken broth and bring to boil.
Add tomatoes, Rotel, taco seasoning, and chicken.
Cut Tortillas into small pieces and add to broth mixture.
Let boil for 45 minutes or until tortillas are thoroughly incorporated into soup stirring occasionally to keep from sticking.
Reduce heat and add 8 oz. cheese. Simmer for additional 10 minutes.
Add milk and simmer for additional 10 minutes.
If thicker soup is desired, add more diced tortillas and let incorporate into soup.
Garnish with shredded cheese and broken tortilla chips.
Substitutions: 1 cup Masa Harina (Masa Flour) for 1 10 ct. package of corn tortillas.
Mix masa with 1 cup cold water, then add masa flour mix into soup.  If thicker soup is  desired, add more masa/water mix.
If you don't want  to use the seasoning packet, substitute 1/2 teaspoons cumin + 1 tsp, chili powder.
You can also use grilled chicken fajita meat for poached diced chicken.
NOTE: If you use FLOUR tortillas, as some people have, you WILL end up with a \
, this recipe is for CORN tortillas. Don't go blaming me and giving me a bad review because you used the wrong stuff.

reviews.review_text:
5 stars for the soup, but only 3 for the recipe. I found it confusing. I read many of the reviews, and it seems like the recipe has been updated since it was published in 1999, which is good, but I wish it mentioned that so you could know to ignore some of the comments. I still found it confusing - cup measurements for the onion, celery, etc., but ounces for the chicken (fyi, 12 oz of chicken turned out to be 3 cups in my kitchen). Also, what size tortillas? If you buy the little ones vs. the 8 or 10" ones, it can make a big difference. I was also confused by the direction to break them into pieces - tear maybe, but my tortillas were too soft to "break". Is the can of tomatoes optional? Or the dicing? It would have helped to have these things clarified.

That said, I did follow the recipe except where I made the following changes to make it a little healthier: cut oil down to 1T, used McCormick's Low Sodium taco seasonings, only used 4, 8" corn tortillas, only used 4oz of cheese in soup, used skim milk. For the chicken, I bought a rotissery chicken from the grocery, and I used every spec of chicken on it for the 3 cups. I think I agree with the reviewers who mentioned adding raw chicken to the 1st step as a savings - although it might not break down as much in the soup.

My tortillas took a LONG time to break down, and some pieces remained. I don't agree with some reviewers who said this was quick - with over an hour of cooking time (where you have to watch and stir), and multi-step prep, this was a weekend project for me. It did make a lot, though, I got 10, 1 cup servings from it, and I froze some for lunches. I would make this again, but I think I would try the massa harina instead of the tortillas, it just took too long and stressed me out.

I've made this recipe about 4 times a year for the past 3 years. I love this soup! I always end up with a bigger pot than the recipe specifies, which is awesome because it doesn't last long around here. I strongly suggest not skipping the Rotel-with-chilies step. If anything, use a little more. I like my soup on the thicker side as well, so I generally use almost double the tortillas. Just make sure you watch the bottom of the pot, because tortillas and cheese stick to the bottom and burn on pretty quickly. The only small critique I have is not with recipe but with the description. I believe the prep time was listed as 10 minutes. This is a gross underestimate. You have to boil the chicken, and this generally takes 15-20 minutes. You also have to chop onion, carrots and celery, and then saute all the veggies for at least 20 minutes. (You can do this while the chicken is boiling. I boil it in the chicken broth that will be the soup base.) With all the other steps this takes a minimum of 2 hours from start to finish. Even longer if you want to simmer it to allow the spices to meld and get better. All in all a great recipe.

First, although I lived on the west coast for decades and love and miss Mexican food, I'd never had tortilla soup, so I had no preconceived notion of how it should be made. I was pretty sure, though, that there was nothing autentico about the recipes with canned cream soups! I had a frozen whole chicken on hand and wanted to try something different, and yours sounded very promising. Second, thank you for giving me a use for the big bag of masa I've had since my silly attempt at making tortillas about a year ago. With things on hand I had to make a few changes. No Rotel, no precooked chicken, and only 2 cans of chicken broth.  I simmered the frozen bird (on lowest heat possible to keep the meat tender) in half water half broth, along with two dried chiles that I left whole, a small can of Herdez salsa, and plenty of cumin. When the chicken was cooked I removed the meat and put the bones and skin back in the pot, in a colander for easy removal, for ~2 more hours. My dear BF, who has had tortilla soup many times, says this is the best tortilla soup he's ever tasted. I LOVED it! This will be a wintertime staple for us. Thanks, Eddie, for helping us enjoy a taste of California while living in New England!

attributes.source_text: My dear BF, who has had tortilla soup many times, says this is the best tortilla soup he's ever tasted

reviews.review_text: This gets 5 stars for flavor alone, delicious. I had to modify it somewhat because of the ingredients I had on hand. No Rotel tomatoes,so I used a 28oz can of whole tomatoes, that I chopped. Three canned jalapenos, seeded and chopped. No corn tortillas,so I used a stale bag of corn tortilla chips that I pulverized. I needed to use the turkey broth and meat from the thanksgiving turkey carcass I cooked, (hence my hunt for a good soup recipe). The only thing I would do differently next time, is omit the cheese in the body of the soup, I'd just use it for a garnish. To me, it didn't really add any additional flavor, and just made a gloppy goup that wanted to stick to the bottom of the pan and spoon, even though I stirred frequently. I also omitted the first step of sauteeing the veggies, I just cooked them directly in the broth. Followed the rest of the recipe as written, and wasn't disappointed. It's addictive.

AMAZING!!!!! My husband and I ate this every day for about 3 days, and it was fantastic every single time! I did make a few small changes--I didn't have corn oil, so I used canola oil. I substituted vegetable broth for the chicken broth. After reading another reviewer's suggestion to start by adding only 8 tortillas, I did that and the soup was plenty thick for us, and I like thick soups. I used extra spicy taco seasoning to give it a little extra kick, and I'm glad I did. Instead of adding a can of tomatoes, I added a can of rinsed black beans, and in place of the chicken, I used 3 Morningstar Farms "grilled chik'n" patties ("fake chicken"). The only other thing I think I might do next time--and believe me, I will be making this many more times--is add some corn. Thanks for an amazing recipe! I wish there was still some left so I could have some now. :)

attributes.source_text: My husband and I ate this every day for about 3 days, and it was fantastic every single time
the soup was plenty thick for us
I used extra spicy taco seasoning to give it a little extra kick, and I'm glad I did

reviews.review_text: This soup is excellent! I was very glad to read other reviews which stated it freezes well because this recipe makes about 4 quarts of soup.  I followed the recipe exactly. I stewed fresh chicken thighs and used the broth instead of canned broth.  BTW: 4 cans of broth @ 14.5oz per can comes to 7 1/4 cups of broth. I also used the Masa Harina instead of soft corn tortillas and my soup was not grainey or lumpy. I took a hint from another reviewer and mixed the masa with a cup of cooled broth then stirred it into the simmering soup.  Overall, I was very pleased with the taste and texture of this soup.  The picture submitted by @ngdarlen looked so tempting, I also served sliced avocado along with the cheese & crushed tortilla chips to garnish, and I'm very glad I did.  The avocado with this soup had a surprising and delicious taste contrast. My dh said when he came in the door the aroma of this soup reminded him of our favorite Mexican Restaurant.  I will definitely be making this recipe again. Thanks Eddie!!

OMG this recipe is FANTASTIC!  So much so that this is one of my new fav soups and will be in our rotation regularly now!  VERY authentic tasting.... I have tried tortilla soup recipes before and you are right they are just broth and say crushed tortillas added on top that is it - this stuff was AWESOME!! I LOVE that the corn tortillas actually melted into it to make it that grainy taste - mmmmmm  I doubled the recipe because I always have to double a recipe for my family and holy cow this made the most soup i have ever had to - so definitely know it makes a lot - my 8 qt pot was WAY too small i had to bring out my mom's old 20 qt pot (i think its 20 but i know the 8 was too small! lol)  I followed as is - the tomatoes i used were diced green chiles and jalapenos (along w/the rotel ones) and i used the 2% milk - also threw in a can of black beans and some frozen corn crushed tortillas on top and added mexican cheese w/fresh cilantro on top.... MMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM  thanks!

attributes.source_text: make it that grainy taste

reviews.review_text:
This is the BEST soup EVER. Made a few changes:
I substituted chicken broth for a mix of low salt vegetable broth and some Better Than Bouillon. You really don't need to use the high salt broth, the taco seasoning has salt in it as well. I also replaced the chicken with Quorn Chik'n Tenders (vegetarian, taste EXACTLY like chicken, low in calories, fat, cholesterol). I didn't add the diced tomatoes (did use the Rotel) and used about 5 tortillas instead of 10. I topped my soup with baked matchstick-sized tortilla chips (homemade, toss with OO and bake in 350 degree oven until done, about 15-20 minutes). Oh, and used soy milk in place of cows. This makes quite a bit, but it does freeze well, so don't worry if you have extra (although it likely won't make it to the freezer, my boyfriend and I can eat this for every meal until it's gone, it's that good).

attributes.source_text: my boyfriend and I can eat this for every meal until it's gone

reviews.review_text: It is difficult for me to know how many stars to give this recipe for a couple reasons.  I no longer eat meat but tried this version when I still did.  Like many other reviewers, I revise this basic chicken soup recipe which has a slight Mexican influence.  Tortilla soup can easily be made cruelty-free, at least as flavorful, and more "authentic".  We replace the broth with a no-chicken broth or add more mild salsa (rather than spicy Rotel) and chicken-free flavoring (usually found in health food stores).  If you use more typical Mexican type tortilla soup ingredients, you don't need the chicken for flavor.  We love the tortilla soup without carrots and celery but with fresh cilantro, lime juice, real garlic, and drained black beans.  You can also add other kinds of beans and corn.

attributes.source_text: which has a slight Mexican influence

reviews.review_text: I love this soup!! Make it year round, and love the thickness and the ease of making it.  I got this recipe way back in 2003 when I was just learning how to cook and recall the daunting task of cutting up all the veggies. Now, 7 years later, I'm a full-time cook, know it by heart, and am begged for "my" tortilla soup recipe.  I do omit the milk and cheese for health reasons, however a package of blended silken tofu works great as a dairy replacement.  I love to add whatever seasonal veggie is available (including squashes, yams, and a variety of peppers) also whatever protiens I have on hand; beans, fish, shrimp, etc. instead of the chicken.  If you stick to the base of the recipe it always comes out delicious!  Thanks for posting this recipe, it really is my favorite soup in the world!

attributes.source_text: love the thickness

reviews.review_text:
Man oh man, is this soup good!  This is the best pot of soup I've ever made in my life.

I'm enjoying a bowl of this soup, which I cooked yesterday, right now for lunch, and it's even better the second day.

I didn't have Rotel, so I put four Roma tomatoes, a little bit of fresh cilantro, and some jalapeno peppers into my food processor and used that.

I had bought a deli roasted chicken at Sam's club the other day, so I picked the meat off that bone, put it in the food processor, and added that to the soup.  I also put the chick carcass into the soup as it cooked, removing it afterward, of course.  

I used four taco shells, crushed them, and added them to the soup rather than the 8 or 10 tortillas the recipe called for.

attributes.source_text: right now for lunch

reviews.review_text:
I tried this 2 ways. I made this for me and for a friend last night so I did 1/2 the pot as is - and then did the 1/2 pot with my changes.

Using the original recipe for me and it was very salty and I did not like the texture of the soft tortilla strips. Mushy.

My version ... I used 3 teaspoons fresh garlic minced.
My own taco seasoning, which is basically chili powder, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, cumin, paprika, cayenne, seasoning salt, black pepper.
But I didn't add any additional salt.
I used half & half vs milk which made it creamier and a better texture.
I did use the tortillas, but I ground them up in the food processor, so they dissolved much better and the overall texture improved.
I did use the spicy rotel as I felt it needed some extra heat.
I also added some fresh cilantro at the end for a bright flavor and a squeeze of 1/2 fresh lime.
And I garnished with fried tortilla strips, diced avocado, and sour cream.

So, overall good flavor but I felt it really needed some changes to get that fresh flavor for me.

attributes.source_text: which made it creamier and a better texture
I did use the spicy rotel as I felt it needed some extra heat
for a bright flavor
for a bright flavor

reviews.review_text:
Superb!!! I made it along with quesadillas for my husband's family, and they all loved it...even his dad who "doesn't like tortilla soup".   

I added a few things to my taste:

when cooking the onions/celery/carrots, I also through in some chopped anahiem pepper.  

After inorcorporating the tortillas, I added a little lime juice, a can of green chilis and fresh cilantro.  

And, toward the end, before adding cheese, I put a can of kernel corn in.  

Oh, and I used about 2 lbs of grilled fajita chicken instead of just the 12 oz. I topped with cheese, fresh cilantro and diced avocado.  

Again, it was awesome, can't say enough good about it! Way to go Eddie!!!

attributes.source_text: my husband's family, and they all loved it

reviews.review_text: This recipe was AMAZING! I wasn't sure how good it was going to be but it just hit it out of the park. I did everything according to directions except I sliced instead of diced the veggies and since my husband doesn't like tomoatoes a I used a can of tomato paste in place of the large can of tomatoes. Also, I only used one packet of taco seasoning, it tasted absolutely perfect, I think any more would have been too much. The flavor was exquisite! We all ate several bowls of this, even my daughter who doesn't like anything that isn't prepackaged or take-out loved it and asked to take some to school for lunch the next day. This is now going to be a regular on our menu, and by substituting low sodium broth it is actually relatively healthy!

attributes.source_text: my daughter who doesn't like anything that isn't prepackaged or take-out loved it

reviews.review_text:
This was just incredible.  5 of us ate the whole pot (which could have comfortably served 8).  It was thick and smooth, lots of flavor without being too spicy.

I opted for 1 cup of masa instead of the tortillas.  I didn't notice until it was too late, but I had "instant" masa.  It worked well, and I didn't have to simmer for 20 minutes to wait for the soup to thicken.  I think I'll use it on purpose next time. ;)

As for the other listed options:
- I used fajita-marinated chicken from HEB.
- I chose the Mexican blend cheese.
- I used the can of diced tomatoes.
- I used the 1.25oz McCormick original taco seasoning.

I also used low-sodium chicken broth and ended up having to add an extra 1/4 tsp of salt to make up for that.

attributes.source_text: It was thick and smooth
It was thick and smooth
without being too spicy

reviews.review_text:
Excellent! My darling hubby really liked this and he is not a soup man!
I actually followed a recipe! I did cook a whole chicken for both the broth and the fresh pulled meat. The extra meat was just a bonus in our opinion. Upon reheat for 2nd meal I used a can of whole kernal yellow & whole kernal white corn, just to add to the volume. Personally we will only use the McCormick's Taco Seasoning ( tried a different brand I had on hand for the 2nd time of making -not as good ) I have already passed this recipe out to several people - I hope they post reviews also! This recipe is now on the cabinet list, to stay with all the other tried & true - always ready recipes.

attributes.source_text: My darling hubby really liked this

reviews.review_text: My husband gave this 10 stars.  It was just like what I've had at some restaurants.  This recipe makes 12 cups, for us that would probably be 8 servings.  Unless I was feeding my f-i-l, then it would serve 6, maybe.  I didn't have monterey jack cheese and had to use colby.  I didn't have any chicken and had to use canned and used 15 ounces.  I think it was ok but I would rather use uncanned next time.  I also didn't have taco seasoning and used Recipe #2642.  My DD thought this was to spicy even topped with extra cheese and sour cream.  I don't know if it was the rotel with chili's (mild) or the taco spice that made to hot for her.  So I ate her bowl too :)  I will make this for company when I have the chance.
