items.label: The Best Chili You Will Ever Taste
items.name: The Best Chili You Will Ever Taste
items.description: This is the best chili recipe I have ever tried. I'm not sure where the recipe originated, but it is amazing! Sometimes, I don't bother adding all four cans of the kidney beans and it still turns out wonderful. Once anyone tastes this chili, they will be begging for the recipe!! Enjoy!
instructions: Heat oil.
Cook onions, garlic and meat until brown.
Add tomatoes, beer, coffee, tomato paste and beef broth.
Add spices Stir in 2 cans of kidney beans and peppers.
Reduce heat and simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Add 2 remaining cans of kidney beans and simmer for another 30 minutes.

reviews.review_text:
I have made this recipe several times with a couple of slight modifications, and everyone who has tasted it has loved it - many people have asked me for my version of the recipe. For starters, I use chuck instead of sirloin for superior beefy flavor. I also do not use any of the sugar. I also add 1 tsp of hickory flavored liquid smoke. Here's the whole ingredients list:

2 onions, chopped

10 or more cloves garlic, minced

2-3 lbs ground beef

2-3 lbs chuck steak, cut into small cubes, most of the fat removed.

2 (14 1/2 ounce) cans fire-roasted diced tomatoes

1 cup strong coffee or a couple of teaspoons of instant espresso

2 (12 ounce) cans tomato paste

1 can beef broth (or 1 TBsp of "better than broth" beef base and 12 oz of water)

3 1/2 tablespoons Heinz chili sauce (about 1/2 of a regular-sized bottle)

1 tablespoon ground cumin

2 tablespoons cocoa powder

1 tablespoon dried oregano leaves

1 tablespoon ground cayenne

1 tablespoon ground coriander

1 tablespoon onion powder

1 - 2 tablespoons crushed red pepper

1 tablespoon salt (or to taste)

1 teaspoon hickory flavor liquid smoke

6 - 8 (15 ounce) can kidney beans, black beans, pinto beans etc - make it as beany as you want - don't drain them unless the chili is already too runny

attributes.source_text: superior beefy flavor
hickory flavored liquid smoke

reviews.review_text:
Oh where has this recipe been all my life? I made this chili tonight and have discovered that I have lived with out it for far too long... It is absolutely to die for!!!

In reading the reviews, I decided to add the brown sugar slowly, one TBS at a time tasting as I went along. This recipe is definitely flexible and the world will not come to an end if you omit it all together. Intrigued by the complexity of flavors as I went along, I continued to add the brown sugar to taste and my measurements came close to the amount in the recipe. 

Because it is chili and it is fun to play...

My adjustments were as follows:
*2 Tsp bacon fat instead of oil
*Good quality beef
*Guinness
*Starbucks Coffee
*3 Tsp Chipotle in Adobo sauce instead of the chili sauce
*Good Cocoa Powder
*Ground my own spices
*Used 4 different fresh (seeded)chili peppers

As with all things, your sum will only be as good as your parts. Use the best and freshest ingredients you can get your hands on and they will speak for themselves.

This chili is definitely an award winner in my home!

Many thanks to AmandaAOates for sharing it!

I made this for a football party this weekend, & it was a pretty big hit. I had my doubts at first. I didn't have all the ingredients including the dark beer. I started making this about 12 hrs in advance of the big day & let if cook on low until serving - I recommend doing this if you can. For the first 10 hours, I was in a total panic b/c it was WAY TOO SWEET. Check out my name, I like sweet, but this was way too much for even me. The next day, 2 hrs before game time, i sent my friend to the store for a beer to add. Let me say this, BEER IS THE KEY INGREDIENT. She brought me an Amber Bock or Rock or something like that. I knew I didn't like Guiness - be careful which kind you get. Guiness is very strong and thick so ask a beer drinker or clerk first if you don't want to sample it yourself. I nearly wept with relief when I tasted it after adding the beer. It was completely cured of the sugar overload and tasted very yummy. I will make this again, but only if I have all the ingredients. Amanda thanks for sharing your prize winning recipe. It's a keeper, & I'll say it again, follow the ingredient list - Beer makes it better.  UPDATE:  Made this again and followed the recipe to the letter.  VERY GOOD - don't mess with the ingredient list until you've tried it out as written.  I thought the Cayenne pepper would make it too hot, but it cooked down to create a complex subtle flavoring - just a hint of heat.  Very good!!!!  Thanks again Amanda.  You ROCK!!!

attributes.source_text: I made this for a football party this weekend
it cooked down to create a complex subtle flavoring
just a hint of heat

reviews.review_text: Look my neep-noops, don't sit there and tell me this recipe ain't the shizzle. First off, yes, I realize this recipe calls for half a cup of brown sugar. Like a riddle out of a Tolkien book, this is the nut you have to crack. Ninjas, do not put brown sugar in a chili. Dear god. I mean, for the love of god, why would you put sugar in a chili. Are you baking a cake? No. You just passed the test. This is "supes obvi" as a millennial might put it. So, okay - you've crossed sugar off your list now, right? Good. Next riddle. You're making chili, right? You open your spice cabinet/ drawer/ what have you - what do you think you should go for? Good guess dude, it's that chili powder. Real talk: take out the sugar, add a tablespoon of chili powder in its stead. The rest of the ingredients are quiche, no doubt about it. Now what are you waiting for? This thing is going to take a couple of hours - get it on the stove! P.S. add a good helping of cheddar to your bowl and you'll be on in chili - what for it - heaven.

I did it this way...
with the 1lb of Sirloin, i cut off the fat, and put in in with Oil, while heating up, removed Fat ring and added Onions and garlic, then Mince and Sirloin Chunks, Cooked for aprox 5 minutes. then added as the directions suggested. I didnt add any brown sugar, but ADDED BY MISTAKE A TABLESPOON of oregeno. my wife doesnt like Kidney beans, so i only added one can of Chilli beans and made sure i mashed the beans i did add, whilst mashing the cubed Sirloin and any thinelse in the POT.

Make sure u use a LARGE pot, mine was close to flowing over, so be careful. the recipe does say 6 to 8 people,,,so maybe cut all in half if need be for just 3 to 4 people.

i used instant coffee instead of already brewed coffee and also OXO cubes with only adding a bit of water in the 6oz tins of Tomatoe Paste.

I have given the Mrs 3 tastings and so far so good....i will update you on the final reult shortly.

Genaron/ Aaron....following on from this...what a success...i have given samples to people at work...because i am a veggie, i need as many people to eat my food, to help fine tune the dish. so...i am going to start again with my review...
oil in pot high heat. put fat rhind salt and pepper a cook to get fat into oil. remove fat with tongs. add meat, this time i used brisket and rump aprox 1.5kg, kept 500 grams of rump back to cube in the last 1.5 to 2 hours. i didnt chop the 1.5kg meat, just left it so it would fit in pot in aprox 5 to 7 peices. the strings of meat are great when complete. add 12oz of picante tomotoes , a can of chopped tomatoes. a wodge of tomotaoe puree, 3 chopped onions, about 3 tablespoons of gravy granules 3 tablespoons of instant coffee, 1/3 of 855cocoa chocolate bar, a tablespoon of each of the following...onions flakes, onion powder, garlic powder, garlic granules, cayenne peeper powder, cumin powder, corriander powder, paprika HOT, chilli flakes, celery salt, salt and black ground pepper. add aprox 1 teaspoon of all spice. 2 tablespoons of chilli sauce, 2 teaspoons of hot sauce 2 teaspoons of soy sauce, 2 teaspoons of worceseter sauce. add one cup of water. done! place on lowest heat on smallest burner of stove top. stir every 30 minutes bottom up vigerously. cook for ...6 to 8 hours rememer to add the 500 grams of rump bite sized peices with aprox 1.5 to 2 hours to completion. for us, this meal last aprox 2 weeks, broken down to single meals and frozen in portions. again, my wife doesnt like kidney beans,,,hence no addition for them. 2 to 4 cans might work, yet...i have given samples

attributes.source_text: I have given the Mrs 3 tastings and so far so good
i have given samples to people at work
getting really excited about the richness
thickness of the over all result

reviews.review_text: This is one of those rare occasions when I am giving 5 stars to a recipe that was 4 star as we ate it tonight.. solely because when I cut the recipe down to serve 2, lessening some of the spices and the peppers, they reached a level where the taste was probably a hint of the true strong flavours, BUT that said, the taste WAS there faintly and I very much liked the hints of what I tasted. Therefore the potential of this recipe with it's odd mix of beer, coffee, cocoa, herbs and spices really did work! I did two things differently: I only used ground beef because meat is very expensive here in NL and I wanted to test the general taste of the recipe  before committing myself to two lots of meat in it, and I lessened the sugar a little (I don't think that effected the total result any) Please see my rating system: 5 stars for a recipe that was easy to make, has a unusual but tasty set of ingredients that I can't wait to experiment with within a smaller serving size to get just perfect for us! Thanks!

Wow this was great!  I chose this recipe because I was curious how beer, coffee and chocolate would work in a chili and was floored on how good it came out!  I thought I had a good chili recipe until I made this!  I was worried a few times during the recipe but stayed the course (like when there was so much liquid before it's 1 1/2 hr cooking time), but the sauce reduced as it cooked without a top on it.  I think it helped concentrate all the flavors better while making it thicker.  I was also concerned with the amount of chili sauce it called for.  When I tasted it after adding it, it seemed way too hot.  But the different flavors blended as they cooked, cooling it down some and was perfect the next day.  The only changes I did was: add a 1/4 c of brown sugar instead of 1/2 c; and added chili powder instead of chilis (because I forgot to pick them up at the store).  I also cooked the garlic separately in a different pan with oil (because I was scared to burn it) then added it to the mixture a couple minutes before the tomato, beer, and coffee.  I can see why people have used this recipe and won competitions!  I can't wait to try it again and wow someone with its ingredients and taste!

attributes.source_text: making it thicker

reviews.review_text: This was definitely a good guide for me to make a really delicious chili! Probably the best one I've ever made, but I did make a number of changes to the recipe. I doubled the garlic, and used 1 pound of spicy chorizo instead of lean ground beef. For the beer I used a dark porter which I would definitely recommend!! After that, I omitted the brown sugar and chili sauce and used about 2 tablespoons of maple syrup to add just a little bit of sweetness to the chili and to take the edge off all the heat! Broth was better than bouillon veggie base and water. About the heat... I used 2 red jalapenos and one poblano for freshness and flavor. I kept all the spices the same as listed in the recipe, but added an orange bell pepper to the mix. This made the spicy factor perfect for me (spicy but no burning), and if people wanted more heat they could add chili sauce (sriracha) to their own bowls. I didn't buy kidney beans at the store because I thought I had some... so I used the only beans I had which was 1 can of red beans and 3 cans of black beans. It came out DELICIOUS. The chunks of beef are a nice touch. Served with fat free greek yogurt, cheddar cheese, green onions, and freshly baked homemade cornbread! YUM

attributes.source_text: This made the spicy factor perfect for me (spicy but no burning)
to add just a little bit of sweetness to the chili

reviews.review_text: This is so sweet!  Tooth-achingly sweet! I made according to the recipe, although I only used 2 cans of beans...the poster actually said she cut the bean amount, so I felt that was okay on my first try on this recipe.  Maybe the extra beans take away from the sweetness, but I have always enjoyed a "meat" chili, not a "bean" chili, so tried for that. I enjoyed the mix of cubed sirloin and ground meat.....that is what I usually use.  I also do not use chili powder, basically making my own.  However, this chili is extremely sweet.  I can't say it is awful, but my mouth recoiled when I took a bite....it was expecting "chili", not candied baked beans.  This recipe is edible....but it doesn't taste like chili to me.  I'm giving this a 3 star, because it doesn't taste horrible, just not what you expect from chili.  I'm sad, because this is the first "new" chili recipe I've tried in years.....going back to my own tried and true recipe.***Letting this chili sit overnight lets the heat increase and temper the sweetness.  So I'm changing my rating from 3 to 4 stars.

attributes.source_text: lets the heat increase

reviews.review_text: I went nuts when my dept. head brought this in. I raved and chowed! I've finally made it myself, but now I think I'm taking a step back. Just a small step. As I was storing the leftovers--I hope to heck it made more than 6 servings!!--the aroma is amazing, but the taste was just too sweet. No biggie, 1/4 cup of brown sugar--or demarara sugar, but not dark brown...I used two whole seeded habaneros, one minced up, the other just chucked in sliced open; in addition to the 2 serranos halved and seeded and the Anaheim chili. Personally, I could have used 3 habs. I didn't realize what a pepperhead I've become! I used 3T chili powder, not being sure what Amanda meant by chili sauce. My stepson came up with the plan of dumping it over the potatoes I baked in the Weber. I went back for seconds, then another shot at the pan full I pulled before I added the chilis, for my DW who doesn't do hot. I think half the brown sugar, a bit less cocoa will do it. Chunks of sirloin were amazing!! burp.

The BEST is a tall claim but it's really good..better than I thought it would be! I too doubted it could be good without chili powder, and doubted the use of sugar in the recipe. It turns out that if you use cocoa powder, the sugar is a must to avoid a tinny bitter taste of unsweetened cocoa. The cocoa & cumin adds richness and the sugar rounds it out. Changes I made:
- espresso instant coffee powder (1 tbs) rather than 1 cup of brewed coffee. The amount of liquid was perfect as a result. Tastes great with corn bread, plain corn tortilla chips, and even better when reheated the next day (like most pot style recipes).
- I used only 2 red hot chili peppers and it was plenty of heat! 3 would have been overkill. If you don't like hot food, I may even recommend 1 chili. I'm the type of person that adds heat to most things I eat.
- I made it with just a tablespoon of sugar at first, but it wasn't enough. Husband and I agree that there was a tinny, vinegar, bitter taste. 3 tbs total of sugar fixed the problem.
- 2 cans of kidney beans rather than 4. Perfect balance of meat - sauce - beans.

I usually make a TX style chili too, which does have a smokier, more spiced flavor, but that recipe requires vegetable shortening. I like this recipe as a healthier version without compromising taste.

attributes.source_text: The cocoa & cumin adds richness
it was plenty of heat

reviews.review_text: The beauty of chili is that it can have a ton of different flavors, including sweet, spicy, smoky, meaty, etc.  A lot of people are knocking this chili because it's "too sweet."  As with all foods, if you come into it expecting it to taste like YOU think it should taste, then you will be disappointed.  Another beauty of chili is that you can throw just about anything in it.  I've used this recipe about 4 times (every time I've made chili) and modified it in different ways every time.  EVERY time I've made it it has been for a competition, and I've either won or placed in the top 3 every time.  Beer is great because it adds a great flavor (and the alcohol either burns out or is negligible for those parents out there).  I've started adding bacon and mixing up the beans, putting about a third each of chili beans, pinto beans, and black beans.  I also substitute Ro-Tel instead of tomatoes and chilis.  I don't really recall what the recipe calls for, but I always try to balance the sweet and not-so-sweet flavors.  Also, chili powder is not what gives good chili that flavor. Cumin, however, I have found adds a really good flavor.  I feel like I can never put too much cumin in my chili.  Great chili!

I can't quite give this 5 stars yet but it is darned close!  I was looking for a recipe to use in a chili cookoff and I'm sure this will be the one - with a few modifications.  I followed the directions exactly but should have taken note of the reviews about sweetness.  I did find it to be too sweet for chili and will cut the brown sugar AT LEAST in half the next time I prepare this.  I also added 1/2 cup of red wine and drained the liquid from 2 cans of beans to compensate.  I used canned green chilis and added about 1 T. of my favorite hot sauce as well.  I think the next time I make this, I will switch up the beans a bit and add 1 can of light kidney beans, 1 can of dark, 1 can of pinto beans and 1 can of black beans.  The color diversity will go well with the diversity of tastes and textures!

I really love the way these very interesting flavors blend together and I can wait to try this again, with much less brown sugar.  THANK YOU!

The ingredients in this recipe were somewhat surprising at first but when I thought about them the merging of certain flavors and depths made sense.  My boss and I made this yesterday in our restaurant for all of our employees that braved the weather and came to work.  We had to modify a few things since we are an italian restaurant and don't carry many of those seasonings.  However we did have a creole seasoning on hand used as an ingredient in one recipe so we used that to add the spices needed.  We used a mixture of Guiness and Moretti (an Italian Beer) for the beer requirements and regular green peppers since we had no chili peppers.  We also tripled the recipe to make enough for an entire restaurant staff.  Many eyebrows were raised over some mentioned ingredients until they tasted it....then no one could stop talking about how good it was and many bowls were refilled.  This was quite good and I would do it again for a large gathering.

attributes.source_text: for all of our employees that braved the weather and came to work
enough for an entire restaurant staff

reviews.review_text: I make this every year and the neighbors smell it from afar and come flocking. I made some adjustments that perfected it (in our opinion) over the years. I use 4lbs of ground venison and 2lbs of pork/beef meatloaf mix (cuz venison is super low in fat) - like i said, neighbors all show up so i make a lot. I skip the steak simply out of preference. I keep most of the other main ingredients the same level even tho I’m adding much more meat other than an extra can of white beans of choice and maybe some veggies if I’m feeling it. I also swap out the diced tomatoes for... wait for it... SALSA. And double it. It gives extra veggies and flavor rather than just diced tomatoes. You’re welcome. ??Also - instead of all that mix of spices i just add a whole bottle of chili powder. It’s a mix of most of those and MUCH easier. To each plate we add some Mexican cheese mix and i always have sour cream and fresh sliced jalapeños in case anyone wants some extra kick. Bon appetite!!!!

attributes.source_text: the neighbors smell it from afar and come flocking

reviews.review_text:
Thanks Amanda!  I just won a chili cook-off at our company using this recipe!  Even more impressive: we're in TEXAS!

Alterations:  I doubled everything to start, except the chilis, so it would be a bit milder.
For the dark beer, I used Guiness Draft.  For the sirloin, I used a couple of thick t-bone steaks, well trimmed and diced into 1/4 to 1/2 inch cubes.  For the ground beef, I used ground sirloin - when I browned the sirloin, I did not "powder" it, instead leaving most of the chunks about 1/2" or larger.

Most Important:  After the initial cooking of the chili in a large stew pot, I transferred it to a couple of crock-pots and left it on low for about 14 hours, stiring only once every couple of hours.

This resulted in a hearty chili that warms you to the bone and has several stages and layers to the flavor that the audience found most interesting and enjoyable.

Thanks again!

attributes.source_text: so it would be a bit milder
has several stages and layers to the flavor

reviews.review_text: I am a horrible cook, and even I made this chili taste AMAZING! I was so proud of myself. Great recipe! I made the chili for Christmas eve for relatives who had been traveling all day. Cooked the day before and reheated for dinner. Excellent. Made more than 8 servings. I had to make several modifications because my family does not eat red meat and I forgot some things at the store: Instead of beef, I subbed Morningstar Farms recipe crumbles (1 1/2 bags), I used chicken broth instead of beef broth, no chili peppers or paste, but I used 2 1/2 Tbls of chili powder, I also cut the brown sugar down to 2 Tbls, and finally, I only used 2 cans of kidney beans and added 1 can of pintos and one can of black beans. The rest of the listed ingredients were used. I was especially excited to use a bottle of Guinness draught in the dish. It was simply delicious. AND, still spicy enough for my sister! It was a big hit with my entire family!

reviews.review_text: I've made a version of this chili more than a dozen times.  After the 3rd time or so, I got my recipe just the way we like it and it is WONDERFUL!  It's the only meal my husband ever asks me to make and the only meal he will ever eat leftover.  I'm from Texas and didn't even know anyone ate sweet chili...ever.  So I've always left out the brown sugar.  We also don't eat chili with beans in it so I omitted that.  To make up for the missing beans I put a little extra sirloin steak, around 1 lb.  Even with leaving out the brown sugar, it was a little sweet for our taste, so I took out the tomato paste and used one small can of tomato sauce instead.  I use 2 whole anaheim chilis for the peppers.  The rest of the recipe is the same. I always serve it with warm cornbread and shredded cheddar cheese. It is delicious!!  Give it a try and don't be afraid to change it to suit your tastes!

attributes.source_text: the only meal my husband ever asks me to make

reviews.review_text:
I've not made this recipe but considered the ingredients and cooking method. Highest level concern is 101% daily value of sodium in a single serving? Not sure where this is coming from, but most likely: (1) Chili Seasoning - usually 1/4 salt. Better to make your own and leave the salt out or cut way back. (2) Beef Broth - lower salt varieties are available that cut the salt 50% (3) Canned foods used - beans, tomato paste, etc.

It is not difficult to reduce salt, and then the 1/4 teaspoon added during cooking can carry the flavor.

I also agree with - too much sugar, too much reliance on beer, coffee for flavor. And true chili has NO BEANS. My El Cid chili, recipe originally found here and I've changed it over the years, has my family and neighbors asking when I will make it again! Check it out at Food.com.

George Chimiklis, Stockton, CA

items.label: Better Than Olive Garden Alfredo Sauce
items.name: Better Than Olive Garden Alfredo Sauce
items.description: This is the best Alfredo sauce ever. This is several recipes combined into one. You can also add your choice of meat (chicken,  shrimp or even crab). The closest OLIVE GARDEN is an hour away and I will never drive that far again just for Alfredo sauce. I promise this is the best sauce ever. Definitely a dish you would want to impress your guest with.
instructions: Melt butter in medium saucepan with olive oil over medium/low heat.
Add the garlic, cream, white pepper and bring mixture to a simmer.
Stir often.
Add the Parmesan cheese and simmer sauce for 8-10 minutes or until sauce has thickened and is smooth.
When sauce has thickened add the Mozzarella cheese and stir until smooth.            STIR FREQUENTLY.
While the sauce cooks, boil noodles for 3-5 minutes.
Place pasta on serving plates and spoon sauce over pasta.
Garnish with parsley, freshly cracked black pepper and more grated parmesan (optional).

reviews.review_text: I’ve made Alfredo sauce before, I clicked on this recipe because I like to compare or see if there’s something I like or want to try and incorporate into my own recipe. After reading the recipe I had some reservations about the measurements, using angel hair pasta and most of all the mozzarella cheese. You should always use the type of pasta that goes best with your sauce, heavier sauce should have a heavier noodle so definitely go with fettuccine or if you don’t like fettuccine go with linguine or spaghetti. Also if you want a creamy, smooth, sauce do not use Mozzarella, and please use fresh grated Parmesan. If you don’t have fresh parm a bag of shredded parm will work however the fresh parm will give you a much better flavor. The mozzarella will make your sauce clumpy and I have never heard of it being used in Alfredo traditionally. These measurements are way off. I cook a lot and I don’t write mine down however I know I use more then this to feed my family of four. If you start your sauce ( using more cream ) slowly add your cheese let it thicken and you can thicken it to your liking and make as much as you need. Also add some nutmeg it’ll bring the flavor out in your sauce. I promise you won’t regret it. These little tweaks will get you a delicious and easy Alfredo sauce you’ll eat again and again. ( I also add grilled chicken or shrimp. Sometimes both depending on what the fam wants. Makes it that much better! )

I've made this before for a variety of pasta dishes and it will again be used for my granddaughters upcoming grad party in the form of white veggie lasagna. I ALWAYS use fresh garlic though it's a pain to peel sometimes. I also throw in cream cheese for a more full bodied sauce. In my home, fresh cracked pepper is the norm. I do not like wine in my sauce, but that's my taste buds, not yours. For the lasagna I'm making I'm figuring on whipping up 6 to 8 quarts Alfredo sauce. I'll start it in a regular pan then throw it all in a crock pot on warm to let it "mellow and mingle". I don't add the parsley to it when doing lasagna. Instead I chop fresh parsley well and throw it on each layer I build~ the rest? Black olives, split cherry tomatoes, chopped fresh brocolli, thick shaved carrot cut on the diagonal~ orange and purple colors, loads of mushrooms {Portabella and Maitaki}, a mix of Vidalia onion and scallions. I may even throw in some garlic chive blossoms as well. Chopped cauliflower, yellow sweet pepper, and fresh baby spinach. All this will be topping homemade lasagna noodles that I'm purchasing especially for this occasion. Whenever I shop I try to go as organic as possible {according to my budget} and like to support the local farmers who grow organic.

I make this often as it is one of my daughters favorites.  I made it again last night and noted my changes to make it more waist friendly.  I used 3 T. butter and 3 T. flour to make the roux.  I added 2 c. fat free half and half and stirred until it boiled.  I then added both of the cheeses listed and continued stirring.  To make it the consistency we like, I added 3/4 c. more of the fat free half and half and it was perfect.  You can add whatever you want as extras, but I typically add fresh diced tomatoes, frozen peas and either sauteed shrimp or chicken.  The possibilities are endless.  We like to use bow tie or a penne type pasta that holds the sauce. We typically have leftovers and never have a problem with separation upon reheating.  Maybe it's because I cut the fat content down.  Try this one, you'll love playing around with different ingredients to suit your taste.

attributes.source_text: one of my daughters favorites

reviews.review_text: Years ago Olive Garden had a recipe called Tortellini a la fini.  It was my favorite and I was crushed when it was removed from the menu.  I then discovered that I could make it myself and being afraid to make my own alfredo sauce I used jar.  Tonight I was out of the jar and decided to find a simple alfredo recipe and make my dish.  WOW - this was way better than the jar (of course) and was even better than the original OG Tortellini a la fini.  Big hit!  For the pasta I used the Bertolli herb chicken tortellini.  Sweet pea and cubed ham steak.  Heat all ingredients and toss... The sauce recipe could probably be 1/2 for the Tortellini as I had alot left over.  I think next time I'm experiment with cutting some of the fat by using some fat free ingredients or half and half.  But, it is VERY Good and simple.  I had no problem with curdling - but I didn't wait for the butter to melt before I added the cream.

I’m reviewing this because I got tricked into trying it by the good reviews. I did not read any reviews or I would have been more wary. It is, truthfully, only better than bottled sauce but not better than any homemade or restaurant sauce. I will not make it again. My advice - keep looking for a different recipe. Pros: tasty, easy (which added the second star to rating) Cons: as many others mentioned the sauce is gritty and separates. The proposed solutions mentioned in reviews did not help. I did get the cream very hot before adding Parmesan. I use pre-shredded cheese and one reviewer said pre-shredded contains ingredients that keep them from melting smoothly but I’ve never had a problem before. I whisked the entire time. One reviewer said it had consistency of clotted cream. If you don’t know what that is then I’d say it’s consistency was like cream of wheat. Not good. My family asked me why I changed sauces and said they did not like it. You can see unmelted gritty cheese in photo. It’s almost as if you sprinkled grated cheese over the bowl before serving. Also, does not make enough for a box of linguine (either 12 or 16 oz) unless you want just a small ladle of sauce over a big bowl of plain pasta.

A very tasty but simple recipe. Don't get hung up on making the full recipe if you are concerned about calories. I used 2 Tbsp. of butter, 1/2 cup of whipping cream, regular black pepper, romano cheese, fontina cheese (in reduced quantities), a spot of corn starch to make sure it would thicken properly, and stirred a Tbsp. or so of sour cream in at the end to give it a smooth taste. The sour cream is much lower in butter fat than butter is and it will create a little more quantity of this delicious cheesey sauce. We had plenty for two people for pasta and vegetables. My wife thought the sauce was one of the best she had ever tasted. My point is to use what you have available at home at the time, keep the proportions approximately the same, and it will turn out wonderful. Yes I know, the black pepper I used will leave telltale "black specks" in your sauce, but turn down the lights and ENJOY!!

attributes.source_text: this delicious cheesey sauce
My wife thought the sauce was one of the best she had ever tasted

reviews.review_text: The first time I made this it came out perfectly, and the whole family enjoyed it. At the time I didn't have enough heavy cream, so I substituted half of the cream with light cream. That was the only difference. Tonight I made it again - a bigger batch for a bigger crowd, but it was a failure. It looked and smelled perfect before I put in the mozzarella,but once I added it, the cheeses all clumped together and no amount of stirring gave it the correct, smooth texture. So I had watery sauce and clumped cheese. Totally disappointed. I loved the recipe, but I think next time I'm leaving out the mozzarella. The Italian half of the family kept saying, "but there's no mozzarella in Alfredo sauce." I guess they're right! As an aside: as an earlier poster said, I added oregano and basil in a ratio of 2:1 with the garlic, cream and white pepper phase. I felt the recipe had the right balance of saltiness and garlic.

attributes.source_text: the whole family enjoyed it
the right balance of saltiness
the right balance of saltiness and garlic

reviews.review_text: I found this while looking for a simple alfredo recipe to make an alfredo/chicken pizza, although I have no idea what olive garden alfredo tasts like (it's been 15 to 20 years since I have deen subjected to that crap) it turned out  pretty good. To tweak I cut the butter by about 1.5T and added about 2T of flour, used whole milk plus ~2 T of sour cream instead of heavy cream (didn't have heavy cream on hand), used roasted garlic and multiplied by four or five (I just roasted a whole head) used asiago cheese instead of parm (out of parm and didn't feel like running to the store) and I cut out the mozerella because I was happy with the texture and would be using it on the pizza anyway.

This was very good! Sorry, it was devoured before I remembered to take a picture. I cut up chicken tenderloins and sautéed them with a little salt and pepper. I made the sauce in the same pan that I cooked the chicken in and left that chicken essence in. I used bagged shredded Parmesan cheese that was along side of the bagged shredded mozzarella cheese in the dairy section. I read that some folks had trouble with the mozzarella cheese clumping...I didn’t. I just measured my 3/4 cup and sprinkled it in a little at a time stirring each time. It does make really thick sauce once it settles so either add a little more cream or use less mozzarella. I actually had the chicken Alfredo over rotini and it was delicious! Note: I did add a little salt to taste once the sauce and chicken were mixed together.

attributes.source_text: It does make really thick sauce once it settles

reviews.review_text: This recipe is great.  We added a few touches to make it awesome.  We added 1 1/2 pounds of shrimp.  We steamed the shrimp until just pink.  Set half aside and pureed half and added to mixture.  we added 1/4 cup of sliced scallions, 1/2 cup of diced roasted red pepper, and 1 tsp. of cayenne pepper for spice and a touch of fresh rosemary to taste.  Simmer all ingredients on low mixing frequently for 15 minutes.  If sauce is too thick, recommend adding some dry white wine.  Use other halfof shrimp for topping either whole or cut in 3rds depending on size of shrimp.  Also commend subsutituting shrimp with lobster.

attributes.source_text: 1 tsp. of cayenne pepper for spice

reviews.review_text: This is hands down the best alfredo sauce recipe and it does beat Olive garden. I also make a few tweaks to this recipe. First, I cook my chicken or shrimp in the pan coated with blackening seasoning and a little bit of butter. After that is done I take out the meat and add the butter for this recipe ( I decrease to 3/4 stick)  being sure to scrape up all the leftover blackened seasoning. I add a tiny pinch of ginger in addition to the the pepper and garlic. When it's about 5 minutes away from being done I throw some chopped sun dried tomatoes and the meat back in to absorb all the flavor from the sauce. The end result is a perfect, slightly spicy sun dried tomato alfredo. This is my go to recipe when I want to impress people. Magnifico!

attributes.source_text: slightly spicy sun dried tomato alfredo

reviews.review_text: This was the most awesome sauce I've ever made. I only made it once, and for it being my first time, I didn't stray from the recipe. It turned out great. Next time however; I am going to take some of the tips given in the comments and try them. The two that stood out were the addition of a dry white wine and 1/2 a cup of either cream cheese or gorgonzola. Both were suggested and both were given good reviews. There was only one thing about cooking it that I had to do... one recipe wasn't enough to feed my family of 5 but a double recipe was just perfect. Also you should note that when refrigerating leftovers, it does solidify but reheating does bring it back to a sauce. Only, the one thing I noticed was that when reheating, the butter separated from the sauce. But it blended back in when I mixed it with a whisk. All around an awesome recipe. :)

After makling this recipe for a couple months now, I have made a couple of tweaks in the recipe to create the PERFECT alfredo sauce. Firstly always use shredded parmesan, this may be harder to melt, so when I first put the cheese in, I take the heat up to a boil, then quickly reduce it so the cheese doesn't burn. Also I do not use the entire stick of butter, I take off about one tblsp. If not the sauce will not be thick enough. Last but not least, I add one tblsp. of sour cream. I also suggest using oragnic half and half as it has much more flavor. In my opinion this is the best alfredo sauce I've ever had, and my husband would have to agree!

attributes.source_text: my husband would have to agree

reviews.review_text:
This sauce is simple and classy. You can amp it up to your liking, I can not imagine anyone who would not like this classic white sauce. I will say it takes a lot of stirring but worthwhile things take time.

If you decide to make this after work it is a good idea to pull up a chair next to the stove for stirring duty. It's worth the buy cost wise because a little goes a very long way. It's so thick and rich you will not be able to eat much of it (due to the great taste you will probably try to anyway). Yet it is so versatile you can make many different meals with it. If it thickens (left overs) you can add a little milk to thin it out - it will not change the taste just consistency.

attributes.source_text: It's so thick and rich
It's so thick and rich

reviews.review_text: FOODGASMIC!!! but i was trying to find a good fettuccine alfredo florentine recipe and didn't find one i liked, but i found this and followed the basic instructions from some random others concerning the florentine.  So i got some frozen cream spinach and fresh white mushrooms.  Let the spinach thaw and using a large skillet and i waited till the oil was hot (on medium) i threw in the mushrooms.  When they're golden, leaving it on medium, i also threw in the cream spinach after about 3 or 4 minutes, it should be done.  Then i added it to my Better Than Olive Garden Alfredo Sauce, i admit it was an orgasm on a plate...and it reheated pretty well :]

Th Recipe is SIMPLY DELICIOUS! I used Garic Powder over the minced garlic however.  What I like best to use it with:   This is a GREAT idea...  Exactly how you would make Chicken Parmesen - but replace the pasta sauce with this Alfredo Sauce!  It is extremey scrumptious!!! I use skinless/boneless thin sliced chicken breast - lightly beaten w mallet, beaded, quickly fried then baked @ 350 with Mozz. atop for 30 min.(with some alfredo spread through the pan)  Lay chicken over penne rigate and top with this alfredo recipe!  This new way to experience chicken parm will WOW you!  Try it out

This was excellent.. i followed the recipe did add 1/2 cup white wine while cooking the garlic, and 1 Tbsp of flour with the cheese because I added the wine..It was fast and delish. Salt was on the table for an added dash.. Topped pasta with sauted red peppers,slices of sun dried tomato from oil, sliced onion, mushrooms, poached chicken breast * later sliced and tossed in with the veggies then topped with this lucious Alfredo sauce.. My husband said it was better than any pasta he has eaten out..Better than East Sides by far. The sun dried tomatoes were a last minute addition!

attributes.source_text: My husband said it was better than any pasta he has eaten out

reviews.review_text:
We are eating on this for the second day and I must say like many sauces it is better the second time around. The recipe is easy to make, but I found that using only the ingredients listed that the sauce lacks some flavor. I will tinker with it until I make it taste like I want it to. I am thinking some fresh garlic & maybe even some fresh mushrooms and spinach. Oh, who knows what I will do. :D
I don't care for Olive Gardens Alfredo Sauce so I can't compare the two. I do not like ANY of the store bought Alfredo Sauces so this one is definitely the winner.
Too easy but don't forget to stir, stir, stir!
Thank you for the recipe.

Delicious!  I don't what the Olive Garden is ( I imagine an Italian restaurant chain in the US ), but this is just scrummy!  I did reduce butter (per other reviews) to 2 Tbsp, reduce cream to 1c., added about 1/4c. cooking cream cheese, and only put in 1/2c or so of grated cheese and served on tortellini (this amount served 4 of us)!! Kids asked for seconds and husband wanted to know if I had saved the recipe.  I did throw in a tablespoon or so of fresh parsley, but I love adding parsley to all sauces!  Will be a regular around this house!!  Oh, always use fresh garlic and ground black pepper!!

attributes.source_text: Kids asked for seconds
husband wanted to know if I had saved the recipe

items.label: Absolute Best Ever Lasagna
items.name: Absolute Best Ever Lasagna
items.description: My family's favorite. This is a very meaty lasagna. We prefer it with cottage cheese, but you can easily substitute ricotta.
instructions: Brown ground meat, onion and garlic.
Add salt, pepper, parsley, oregano, basil, chopped tomatoes with juice, tomato paste; stirring until well mixed.
Cover and simmer 1 hour (or longer,but watch for getting too dry).
Cook lasagna noodles according to package directions; drain and set aside.
Spray a 13 x 9\

reviews.review_text: I see mostly 5 stars on this recipe.I made it today and didn't care for it. My wifes recipe is much more simple and tastes better. This recipe was too runny... probably from the whole undrained tomatoes. The only different thing I used was ground turkey in place of hamburger, but I did use italian sausage. If you don't like this, try my wifes more simple recipe: Brown 1-1/2 lbs. of ground turkey & combine in the frying pan, one 24 oz. jar of Ragu spaghetti sauce. In a bowl, combine 2 beaten eggs with a 12 oz. container of cottage cheese. Boil 6 lasagna noodles according to package directions. Spray a 13" x 9" baking pan with cooking spray. I use olive oil spray. Place 3 lasagna noodles on bottom, then top with meat sauce, followed by the combined egg and cottage cheese. Do the same with the next 3 lasagna noodles etc. Top with grated parmesan cheese. I would guess one cup of parmesan cheese or more if you like. My wife just guesses when she makes this. This is simple, the spices are in the Ragu sauce and this is cheaper to make! Everyone likes my wifes lasagna, so give it a try!

Very good! Not overly saucy, so it holds together well and slices beautifully. Great flavour! My fiance had never had - and didn't think he'd like - a lasagna with cottage cheese, but he really likes this one!

Didn't have Italian Sausage so used 2 lb ground beef. Used  fresh herbs in place of dried, and added rosemary to the mix. Didn't have 2 cans of tomatoes so used about a half dozen tomatoes from my garden (diced) with 1 can of stewed tomatoes. For the cottage cheese part I added one thawed and drained brick of frozen chopped spinach as another reviewer suggested to sneak in more veggies, as well as a generous grating of nutmeg (my no-so-secret ingredient for Italian cooking). I also opted to use the ready-to-bake noodles rather than the kind that need boiling, just because they're easier to handle and cuts down on clean up time.

I didn't want to make a full 9x13" pan of lasagna for just the two of us, so I did up two 8" x 8" foil square pans (each of which will feed us for 2 days). This resulted in lots of leftover filling, so using what I had on hand I also got two 6" round and one 4" round pie tins - perfect for single servings! Baked one of the 8" pans to eat right away, and the others went into the freezer for easy suppers later on. 

Thanks for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: Not overly saucy
it holds together well
he really likes this one

reviews.review_text: This was great although I only gave it 4 stars since I changed some things a bit according to other reviews. First I halved the recipe to use in an 8x8 dish. There's only two of us so it's plenty enough for dinner and leftovers. I used half a pound each of the meats, added an 8oz can of tomato sauce, 6oz of water and half tablespoon of brown sugar to the sauce before simmering. I added a good pinch of salt to the ricotta mixture but my own personal taste wishes I had added a bit more. I layered some meat sauce on the bottom of the pan first and used standard lasagna noodles that I left uncooked. (I had to break off the ends of the noodles to make them fit but it turned out great...I was a little nervous it wouldnt) I continued to layer, making sure I had meat sauce to cover the top layer of noodles so they wouldn't dry out. I covered with foil, cooked for 45 minutes and then uncovered to top with the mozzarella cheese. I continued to cook uncovered for 25 minutes and then I let it cool and set for 20. It turned out amazing and I'd be happy to make it again. It's a keeper!

I was a first-time lasagna maker, and I totally wowed my husband. I will definitely find the time to make this again. I did half beef & half sausage, half & half ricotta and cottage cheese, added a little brown sugar to the sauce, added spinach to the cheese mixture, and added one extra can of tomato sauce to make it go a little further. I used oven-ready noodles and didn't add any extra water or anything; as long as all your noodles are covered in sauce or cheese, it should turn out. I covered my noodles with a tiny bit of sauce (all I had left), then made sure everything was covered by the topping cheese, and then covered in foil just to be safe. No crispy noodles for me. I used a really big roasting pan because some people mentioned over-filling a standard 9x13, but I'll probably go with a 9x13 next time, just to stack everything a little thicker. Seriously, though. No complaints. So good.

attributes.source_text: I totally wowed my husband

reviews.review_text: Most lasagna recipes just fall short, I do not use them my signature lasagna is rich and dense and very flavorful, I make a very hearty marinara first, (using my own Italian seasoning blend, there are many good ones on the market use one you like) adding sauted course chopped black olives and crimini & porchini mushrooms also grated zucchini, I use only mild Italian sausage once all those are done I add them to the marinara, (this can be made way ahead and frozen) you can use no boil noodles or you can use the standard type and just soak them for 20 min in just hot water, I do not use ricotta cheese I find it too grainy on the pallet, prefer to use up to as many as 6 kinds of Italian cheese that I coarsely grate, layer in prepared pan, marinara - noodles -marinara - grated cheese blend - noodles - marinara - grated cheese blend, I do 4 layers normally, the last is making sure that top layer is all the remaining marinara and completely covered with cheese, then bake, make adjustments on time according to ho many layers and how big of a pan you use, keep an eye on the top so you take it out when it is just golden brown, large amounts can be cut into portion squares and frozen, so you can have lasagna when ever you want, just pop a 3 inch square into a microwave dish with a couple of tablespoons of tomato juice and in aprox 2 mins it's ready to enjoy.

attributes.source_text: my signature lasagna is rich and dense and very flavorful
my signature lasagna is rich and dense and very flavorful

reviews.review_text: This was my first time ever making lasagna. I made sure to carefully follow the recipe exactly, so no changes to it on my part. I have to say that I had no idea how expensive and laborious it is to make lasagna - I didn't have a lot of the ingredients on hand, so had to go to the store to pick up whatever I was missing, and the total was about $50, excluding of course the stuff I already had. The total time from start to finish, including all prep work and letting the lasagna rest for 20 minutes after baking, was around 4 hours. It was WELL worth the money, time and effort though! This was, hands down, the BEST lasagna I've ever had! My wife agreed and said I am the official lasagna maker from now on. Her sister had previously held the title for best lasagna, but she said I stole the crown. Since most things are even better the next day, we can't wait to see how it tastes tomorrow!

attributes.source_text: My wife agreed
Her sister had previously held the title for best lasagna, but she said I stole the crown

reviews.review_text: I made the recipe as written except that I used ricotta and I didn't have the tomatoes for the sauce, so I used a jar of Prego (1lb 8oz) instead.  I thought that the sauce looked good as far as amount and consistency.  Ok, I'll admit that I had difficulty with choosing the right size pan.  I have a metal 9x13, but that seemed too small, I was afraid my glass 11x13 had sides that were too small - plus it was too much overlap with the noodles.  I chose a larger glass pyrex that I have - it's about 10x14.  I thought that leaving off with the noodles was strange, but I figured the sauce would come up and around during baking.  It didn't, and the top was all hard and dried out.  Although the fillings/layers covered the area, they were thin, and the result was a very dry, crumbly lasagne.  I couldn't taste the sausage.  it was very disappointing.  I had about 2/3 of the pan left after dinner (for 5).  If I made it again (and that's a big if), I'd probably opt for the smaller 9x13 pan and put sauce on the top before the cheese.

My husband says to me on Wednesday morning, "Oh, by the way, I volunteered you to make a lasagna for my work.  We're having a Thanksgiving dinner."  Anyway, I went right to Zaar and looked up the best lasagna rated recipes and I decided on this one.  Needless to say, the dish came home totally empty from his work.  I wanted a piece of the leftover for another picture, but nothing left.  I just wanted to make a few notes, more for myself for next time than anything else:  I used 1 pound of extra lean ground beef and 1 pound of Bob Evans Zesty Hot Sausage Roll, 1 cup of chopped frozen onions from a bag, about 2 heaping tablespoons of minced garlic from a jar, 24 ounces ricotta cheese instead of the cottage cheese as that's what the hubby asked me for, reduced fat grated parmesan cheese and a 1 pound box of lasagna noodles.  Thanks for posting such a fantasic recipe that I know I will use again and again...

attributes.source_text: the dish came home totally empty from his work
We're having a Thanksgiving dinner
We're having a Thanksgiving dinner

reviews.review_text: This Lasagna is the absolute best ever.  I used oven ready noodles so I added 14 1/2 oz. of water to the sauce mixture for more moisture.  I also added 1 Tblsp of sugar to the sauce.  I used 32 oz of ricotta with 3 eggs & adjusted the seasonings for the cheese mixture accordingly.  (We love cheese).  I put a layer of sauce on the bottom of the pan first, (10X15X2 Coringware Roaster), then placed a layer of the oven ready noodles and so on, finishing with the sauce on the last layer of noodles and topping with some more parmesan cheese remaining mozzerella.  Covered with foil and baked for 40 mins, removed foil and baked 10 more minutes.  Gave 15 mins to rest and served.  I had never used the oven ready noodles before and will now never boil lasagna noodles again.  Awesome!  Made 2x in 2 weeks for family/friend gatherings.  This recipe is easy and delicious.  I will definitely use this recipe again.

attributes.source_text: for family/friend gatherings
for family/friend gatherings
for family/friend gatherings

reviews.review_text: This was a good flavorful recipe all in all. I am rating off the recipe given. I gave 4 stars bc the instructions are a little off and after making as is, for taste purposes I decided a few things I'd prefer changing. You'll have to add more liquid depending how long you decide to cook the sauce. I cooked as instructed and found I needed to add about one can of tomatoes worth of water. (Bc the noodles once baked will continue to soak up liquid). I like mine a little saucy. Also, 2 TBSP of brown sugar cuts the and is a must. Might seem like a lot but it's not. To smooth out the sauce I added about 1/3 cup cream (half n half). Bake time and temp worked great. >>Not re: the rating, I prefer to add another 1/2 lb mozzarella than what's instructed on the top bc we like ours cheesy! (Not changing the filling recipe). Great recipe to start and modify how you like. Thank you for sharing it!

I made the following changes to this recipe:  ground turkey/turkey sausage for the meat, 2 cans diced tomatoes for the whole, added one tomato paste can of water to the sauce, uncooked whole wheat noodles.  My husband liked the flavors, but said it was a little 'drier' than I normally make...that was probably from my tweaking, and I fixed this the second time I made it.  I have made this again, and added one more can of diced tomatoes (3 total) to the sauce mixture, and 2 small cans of water.  PERFECT!   I use regular whole wheat noodles (not the 'no bake' kind), and I don't cook them before I assemble the lasagna.  I like the texture and taste of the noodles more when they are cooked in the lasagna instead of beforehand.  The flavors in the recipe are really good and this was an outstanding lasagna!!  I use this recipe as my guide, and just tweak it to make it saucier for our taste!!

attributes.source_text: My husband liked the flavors

reviews.review_text: This is a really delicious lasagna. I went and bought a deep dish aluminum pan so I was able to put 4 layers of noodles, using 15 noodles.  Normally I only do 3 layers because I run out of room, but 4 is so much better tasting. I did mix half cottage cheese and half ricotta. Everything worked out in the proper proportions. The flavors were so yummy...I weighed the lasagna and couldn't believe it weighed 16 lbs. Quite a lot of reviewers say it was salty but I didn't find it was at all and I had added the salt when I was browning the meats. Maybe it is the brand of cheese being used that could make it salty. All I know is mine was absolutely delicious !! Also it was perfectly easy to cut and serve after it rested for 20 minutes. Thanks for sharing your wonderful recipe ratherbeswimmin.. Forgot to say I will post the pics I took when I can download to this computer.

attributes.source_text: I didn't find it was at all

reviews.review_text: This just became my new "go to" lasagna recipe which I've been hunting for.  It is delicious, simple and the flavours aren't complicated, which I appreciate...it is a great old school meaty/cheesy lasagna!!  My husband & our friends agree, "throw away your other recipe's that you've clipped, saved or copied from someone, this is the one".  Do try the recipe as is the very first time (it appears as though the author has edited it & updated it based on other reviewers comments, so trust it, it is current and easy to follow) but also be creative and make it your own next time by adding spinach and/or nutmeg to the ricotta mixture...or replacing some of the meat with chopped portabella mushrooms.  Regardless of how you make it your own, keep this recipe as your base.  It is wonderful and delicious!

attributes.source_text: great old school meaty/cheesy lasagna
great old school meaty/cheesy lasagna

reviews.review_text:
This recipe may be the start of a new Christmas tradition for my friends and family. I was excited to try this recipe based upon all of the reviews posted. I followed the recipe to the letter - used Ricotta - and only strayed just before I placed the pan into the oven by adding a thin layer of Provolone and Parmesan cheeses on top. I served the lasagna along with the Chopped Italian Salad (amazing) by NcMystery Shopper and the Italian Bread Casserole (wonderful) by Brooke the Cook in WI. There was not one morsel of food remaining on any of my 18 guest's plates. Everyone commented on how delicious the entire meal tasted and some even mused as to how shocked they were I could actually cook. All three recipes were easy to follow and recommend all three dishes be served as an entire meal.

I think this is a very good recipe and will make it again for large, casual gatherings.

attributes.source_text: on any of my 18 guest's plates

reviews.review_text: This is EXACTLY the same as the lasagna recipe I got from my best friend back in high school...in the late 60's.   It is INCREDIBLE & believe me, I've made lots of lasagnas over the past 45 years!  This recipe takes a bit more time, but what good Italian cooking doesn't? Leftovers freeze well too...if there are any.  I've even caught my dear SIL making a "sandwich" using cold lasagna, sliced into thick slices.  Oh...be sure to use a deep straight-sided baking dish. The Bobby Flay line of stoneware sold at Kohl's has a very nice one with handles that is great for this lasagna. This recipe is so generous it will overflow a standard 9x13 glass pan. And be sure to let it "rest" about 10 minutes before cutting or it will ooze it's cheesy goodness all over the plate!

FANTASTIC! My fiance said "don't change a thing about it". That means alot coming from a chef! The batch lasted the two of us forever and I ended up having to make more sauce (which I actually added more sausage to)! I topped it with homemade alfredo sauce and now this is going to be a staple. Definitely going to freeze 1/2 right away next time though! I would say if you like a heaping of red sauce on top then 1.5 times the sauce recipe (at least!)! OH! And 12 lasagna noodles are PERFECT for a 9 x 13 pan! What the heck am I gonna do with the extra 6 that I made?!!! Oh, Drown them in the extra sauce! YUM!!! Seriously, no doubts about this recipe. 
PS. I used Ricotta cheese and a Parmesan/Romano blend and spicy Italian sausage. I'm gonna use a bit more italian sausage next time though! That was the ONLY criticism from the man!

I love to order lasagna when we go out to eat just because I am too lazy to make my own.  I am glad my BF begged me for homemade lasagna this week since this was absolutely delicious.  From the tasty and meaty sauce to the way it cuts like a dream... this is a 5 star recipe all the way.  My BF doesn't like Italian sausage but when it was mixed in with the ground beef... it just made the sauce tastier than if it had been all beef.  I did add in just a tad more canned tomatoes ( just because they were in the fridge and needed to be used up)  and loved the fact that it made the lasagna a little "saucier" which is what we like.  I used 15 oz of ricotta and the remainder cottage cheese because the store had it on sale...  great combo.  I topped it with whole milk mozzarella that I sliced thinly... so stringy and gooey delicious.  Thanks for a keeper!!!

attributes.source_text: the tasty and meaty sauce
it made the lasagna a little "saucier"
so stringy and gooey delicious
so stringy and gooey delicious

items.label: Spinach Artichoke Dip
items.name: Spinach Artichoke Dip
items.description: Make and share this Spinach Artichoke Dip recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Mix together Parmesan cheese, spinach, and artichoke hearts.
Combine remaining ingredients and mix with spinach mixture.
Bake for 20-30 minutes.
Serve with crackers or toasted bread.

This was wonderful! Creamy and delicious! The only thing I changed was I used 1 c parm & 1 c Italian blend vs. 2 straight c's parm. Partially because Parm is pricey and party because I thought the blend would add to the creamieness. I also covered the dip with some extra parn and blend cheeses before baking. DH loved it, too. I put 1/4 of the recipe in a small pyrex and threw it in the freezer.. will update when I find out how it bakes up going this route because it's soooo much better than those store bought frozen versions and the recipe makes so much that you could easily put 4 or 5 containers in the freezer for later use.
UPDATE - I was just making this recipe again for a party and remebered that I was going to share about freezing - the one I froze, I just pulled it out of the freezer the night before and stuck it in the fridge. The next evening, stuck it in the oven and it came out as delicious and creamy as the original batch.

reviews.review_text: There are few foods that DH will eat that have cheese in them, and never when it's a main ingredient.  However, I was craving spinach and artichoke dip, so I decided to make it for the football game last night.  I split the recipe into two 9" pie dishes, wrapped and froze one, and baked the other.  DH & I devoured it!  He kept oohing and aahing.  I did make some tweaks to disguise the cheesy flavor.  I used half Parmesan and half 3 cheese Italian blend (Asiago, Parm and Romano), added the juice of half a lemon, and about a 1/2 teaspoon of crushed red pepper flakes.  The lemon and red pepper really complimented the rest of the recipe, and did their job to disguise the cheese.  I topped my half of the dish with extra 3-cheese blend.  :)  Delicious!  I'm glad I froze one for next time.  Thanks for sharing this recipe, Juli!

reviews.review_text: DEEEEELICIOUS!!! I sliced up some pumpernickel bread for dipping mine, but my 7 year old wanted to dip celery in hers. My 5 yr old ate it on chips. It is versatile and delicious.<br/>I did change a few things. <br/>1) I didn't have frozen spinach, so I chopped up some fresh. <br/>2) I used 1 cup of shredded parm and about 1 cup of small cubes of mozzarella (I had a big block and I didn't want to dirty my shredder, so I just chopped it into little cubes) It mixed and melted well. <br/>3) I read in a review that someone replaced the artichokes with mushrooms. I just chopped 'em up and mixed 'em in. I really think this was one of the key ingredients for adding flavor.<br/><br/>We give it two very happy thumbs up! I will definitely be making this again!! Thanks. :)<br/>6) I mixed this all up and then separated it into 3 parts (I wasn't making it for a party, just an afternoon snack) and put 2/3 into freezer bags and froze them for future snacking. The other 1/3 I put into a baking dish and sprinkled with a little more mozzarella and parmesan. I baked it about 25 minutes. It came out perfect!!

items.name: Peach Cobbler
items.description: I found this peach cobbler recipe on the internet from the Salt Lick Restaurant in Austin, TX. Everyone loves this recipe so much I have to make a double batch! Feel free to cut back on the sugar. Everyone has and the peach cobbler still comes out perfect. :D  Personally, I always use two bags of frozen peaches instead of canned.
instructions: Melt butter in a 9 x 13 inch pan.
Mix together flour, sugar, baking powder & salt.
Stir in milk & egg.
Pour evenly over melted butter.
Combine peaches, sugar & spices and spread over batter-DO NOT STIR!
Bake 35-45 minutes at 350°F until batter comes to the top and is golden brown.
Serve warm with ice cream.

reviews.review_text: I've tried several peach cobbler recipes and this is one of my absolute favorites. I've made it a couple times now and am going to make it again today. I have made a few slight changes to the recipe adding to them each time I made it until I had what I feel is the best cobbler recipe ever. First thing I wanted to mention is that having the milk and eggs at room temp makes a big difference. Make sure you let them out for an hour or so before making it. Personally, I don't like using canned fruit unless absolutely necissary so I use about 6-8 fresh and very ripe peaches. First I peel and slice them and add about a tsp of fresh lemon juice to keep them from turning brown as well as to add some acidity to balance out the sweetness a bit. Then I add the sugar which I add an add'l 1/2 cup to for a total of 1 1/2 cups and 1 1/2 tsp cinnamon and reduce the nutmeg to 1/4tsp. Then I mix up well, cover and place in the fridge to keep cool. I do the fruit when I set out the milk and eggs to warm so it has some time for the sugar and spices to marry with it before baking. Then I prep the dry ingredients. To me the orig recipe was great but there wasn't enough batter as I like to use 1 1/2 the amount of dry ingredients per batch with 2 eggs. I then measure out the dry ingredients and whisk them together in a med bowl and set aside till milk and eggs are room temp. Once the milk and eggs are ready I set the oven to preheat and place the baking dish in with the butter which I increase to 1 1/2 sticks. Then I add the milk and eggs to the dry ingredients and whisk together. I pour this over the melted butter and them add the peaches like in the orig recipe and bake till golden brown on top. It takes about 2-3 min longer to bake with the add'l batter. One last thing I like to do is once it's baked a little over halfway through and the batter has risen to the top and set is to add some raw sugar over the top and put it back into the to finish baking. It's absolutely amazing!!! Try it, I'm sure you'll love it!

I'm a self-described foodie who is constantly scouring the internet for good recipes. I tend to find something interesting and will play with it and tweak it until I have my own delicious version. I was raised on cobblers with the batter laid down first and the fruit laid on top. There are two different types of cobbler batters; the cake-like batter I prefer which is poured into a pan of melted butter and the "drop on top" biscuit type. Both are delicious, so it's a matter of preference. I will also convey that if the recipe doesn't bake properly, it's not due to problems within the recipe. Making sure the baking powder is fresh will ensure good results. I did play with this recipe because that's what I love to do. First, I used frozen peaches I picked from a tree last week. (Other than a good wash, I never prep my peaches before freezing. I freeze them whole, skins and all! When I need peaches, I pull out the amount I need, run them under warm water and peel the skins off with my fingers. Then, I slice in half, remove the pit and slice or dice as needed.) I also doubled the amount of peaches, and added 3/4 cup sugar and 2T fresh lemon juice. For the batter, I added 2 cups flour, 1T + 1t FRESH baking powder, 1/2t salt, 3/4 cup packed brown sugar, 2 farm fresh eggs, 1 cup buttermilk, 1 cup whole milk and 2t pure vanilla. I just pulled it out of the oven and I'm ready to dig in! The recipe performed beautifully. Again, if you're having trouble with the recipe, check your ingredients! If you like less sugar, then add less sugar! If you don't like a cake-like texture, find a recipe that has a stiffer biscuit-like dough. Note your preferences if you like. Just please don't criticize the recipe. That's just RUDE!

I've made this recipe several times now and it has grown into one of the top request treats in our home. I have found that it turns out best made with fresh frozen peaches and only 1/3 of the sugar in each- the batter and the fruit layer. Because the cost and quality of peaches are limited to season, in the late summer when they are abundantly available, peak quality and much cheaper, I will buy bushels, peal, pit and slice up, freeze in layers on a tray; once frozen transfer and store in a zip-lock freezer bag. Pre-freezing on a tray helps to prevent them from sticking together in the freezer bag for easier use and only taking the portion you require for recipes. If you freeze them while still firm they will be easier to prep to freeze (less fluid loss and defrost soft, sweet and juicy); therefore requiring a lot less sugar in recipe. This recipe makes for a super easy and loved dessert!

reviews.review_text:
Update:  I have been playing with this recipe alot lately.  1) because I always have the ingredients on hand  2) it is way to easy and 3) because I think I have come up with the right combination of sugars.  I have even cut the recipe in half and put it into a 8" glass dish to serve to 4 people.   The 2 cans of  peaches are not enough by themselves, so I always add frozen blueberries.  I drain the peaches and add enough blueberries to fill the dish.  I add 1/2 cup sugar to the fruit and let it marinate/thaw in the fridge.  I follow the recipe until adding the fruit, then I drain the excess liquid and place the fruit on top of the batter...then drizzle some of the extra liquid.  In the batter, I cut the sugar down to 1/2 cup and that is plenty.  I have used both fresh and canned peaches and both are acceptable.  August 8/2008 :
Ditto to all the comments! I cut 8 small fresh peaches up, making sure the juice dripped into the bowl and added some fresh blueberries I had on hand. Yes...both the sugars for the batter and the filling could be cut down. I used 3/4 cup sugar on both and I am quite sure that using 1/2 cup would be sufficient. I added 1/2 tsp vanilla to the batter and dribbled whatever juices from the peaches over on top. I have canned peaches in the cupboard for next time....but I did like the idea of using frozen peaches. I think they would give a fresher taste. Wonderful recipe Suellen...I will do this one again

We've had a lot of stone fruit and berries around this summer and I have been making shameful quantities of cobbler using this and other recipes. I would say that this recipe is my favorite thus far. I have made it with a variety of fruits and some tweaking so I'll share what we've tried and liked: 1. I've made it with any combo of peaches, plums, pluots, blueberries, strawberries, nectarines, and even mango (which I didn't care for). I would say that straight peach or maybe peach with a handful of blueberries is the best, but no variety was ever turned away, and it's always a great way to use up fruit that might otherwise spoil. 

2. The nutmeg is key to the flavor profile, please don't omit this unless you really dislike nutmeg.

3. I sub brown sugar for some of the white sugar in the fruit.

4. I cut back at least 1/4 c. of sugar in both the batter and the filling.

5. I tried (and REALLY liked) subbing buttermilk in place of the milk in the batter. When I did this, I cut the baking powder to 1 t. The buttermilk gave a nice sour tang to balance all of the sweet, and added to the depth of flavor. 

In all, a great recipe that is, and will continue to be a summer favorite.

reviews.review_text: Certainly a good base recipe for cobbler (seems like a cross with a buckle). Instead of one can ofpeaches I used a 16 oz. bag of frozen sliced peaches, a 16 oz bag frozen strawberries (cut into quarters), and 9 oz. of fresh raspberries. Tossed that with the amount of spices called for in the original recipe, added one tablespoon of flour, and one tablespoon of lemon juice. For this amount of fruit, I used 1/2 cup sugar in the batter and 3/4 cup in the filling (brown sugar for both) and added a teaspoon of homemade vanilla extract to the batter. Came out lovely, perfect amount of sweetness and fruit to cake ratio. Did mostly thaw the frozen fruit and needed to bake for just over an hour (at high altitude as well). Served with raspberry sorbet.... just plain yummy. Definitely use more fruit, and cut the sugar down unless you like candy sweet cobblers.

reviews.review_text: The beauty of this recipe is that it is adaptable. Originally, this Peach Cobbler called for 28 ounces of canned peaches. I only had 15. The one cup of flour was too much crust for so few peaches, so I split it in half and made Apple Cobbler too, with two fresh unskinned apples. My only worry was whether I had nutmeg. Until now, I had only tasted a frozen version of either peach or apple cobbler. That was all Mom ever bought for the holidays after her attempt at making homemade Lemon Meringue Pie. The meringue never set. It usually had to be warmed in the oven. Why make pies and cobblers from scratch when they can be purchased at the store ready-made? This recipe was delicious. My friend and I sampled each kind. She told me it smelled like Thanksgiving and Christmas in my kitchen. My church friends got mad because I didn’t share any cobbler. I promised to make it again to share. My friend suggested peeling the skin of the apples next time. I will definitely make this again, both ways. :)

reviews.review_text: First, thanks to Suellen for publishing this recipe. And, thanks to Bev, who reviewed it and gave me the ideas of using almond extract and various berries with the peaches! Used nutmeg and cardamom for spices both in the batter and filling. It took 20 extra minutes for mine to bake:50 minutes total. It turned out flawless, golden brown, and was a HUGE hit at the birthday party that I went to. :) I'm going to use this recipe from now on because the other cobbler recipe has twice the amount of steps and I couldn't tell the difference with the end product. Super simple to make, very delicious, a crowd pleaser! I'm making another one on Monday, for another birthday party, it was that good!

reviews.review_text: This recipe was great!  This was my first time making a peach cobbler (or any dessert) and I needed a basic recipe which I could tweak to make my own.  For this particular recipe, I found that you needed to increase the amount of peaches if you use the 9 x 13 inch pan (thus increasing the mount of cinnamon, nutmeg and sugar).  After the first time making the cobbler (which turned out pretty good), I used fresh peaches and more of the natural juices and a smaller baking dish.  I would strongly recommend not draining the peaches if you use canned peaches and just cutting back on the sugar.  I found that this is also a great recipe for blackberry cobbler as well!  Just substitute the fruit and it's great!  I would imagine that it would be great for an apple cobbler, too!  Very versatile - thanks for the recipe!

I made another peach cobbler prior to this one and they were like night and day.  This is the cobbler that I remember when I was growing up.  My biggest concern was whether or not the dough would rise--as the first cobbler did NOT.  This recipe was perfectly sweet with a crispy crust.  I only used 1/2 cup of sugar for the dough along with a few drops of vanilla extract, replacing vanilla soy milk for regular milk, and 1/2 cup of brown sugar for the filling.  I also used 2 large cans of sliced peaches, which filled the entire 9x13" pan.  I would love the tang of fresh blueberries added to this recipe.  Whichever way, it is definitely a keeper!

attributes.source_text: perfectly sweet
crispy crust

reviews.review_text:
My daughter and I were looking to use some fresh peaches we purchased at the local farmers market on a desert of some kind.  In our travelsm we perused several sites and finally settled on this recipe. 

We found the recipe to be very easy as well as tasty!  

We substituted 2 large fresh peaches for the canned peaches and instead of topping it with ice cream, we tried it two different ways; the first with half & half as if it were a dumpling, the second topped with whipping cream.  

4 out of 5 of us preferred the half & half and it seemed to tone-down the sweetness of the sugary peaches.  

Very nice!

attributes.source_text: the sweetness of the sugary peaches

reviews.review_text: Delicious and easy!  I subbed sucralose = 1/2 the sugar called for in the recipe.  Next time I will increase that a bit.  I also used low fat margarine (a bit less than called for) and the full amount of low fat milk.  I mistakenly included the juice with one can of peaches and it really did not seem to make a difference, except I had to cook it closer to 45 minutes.   This is not the peach cobbler that I am used to, but is yummy.  I am looking forward to trying it with sugar for company, some of the variations and with real butter (and no peach juice).  Served it warm with sugar free vanilla ice cream.

I hate to go against the grain, since all the reviews are so good, but frankly, I've had better peach cobblers.  First off, there is way too much salt in the recipe.  I did cut back on the sugar, but it was still plenty sweet.  I'm guessing if you used the full amount of sugar it would be too sweet.

The bread part of the cobbler was not very light at all, kind of heavy and hard.  So, that part I didn't care for.  I prefer my cobbler to be more crumbly and cake-like.  Maybe that was because the dough was started out on the bottom, under the fruit?  Then again, maybe not.

The spices were excellent, however.  I'll probably modify my preferred cobbler recipe to use these spice proportions.

I won't be making this again.

attributes.source_text: it was still plenty sweet

reviews.review_text: OH. MY. GOD! We LOVE this dessert! I loved how it was so simple to make. I thought it was a bit strange to put the batter over the butter then the peaches over the batter but was amazed at the result. This smells great when it's cooking away too! I use a large tin (820 gram, I think) of sliced peaches. The second time I made this I used only 3/4 cup of sugar to add to the peaches (because that was all I had left!) & it still tasted great. I serve this with cream but custard or ice-cream would go nicely too. I just adore this recipe & plan on handing it down to my kids when the time comes (in fact, I've already passed it on to a friend!). This dish is wonderful comfort food & perfect for winter. Thank you Suellen :)

attributes.source_text: We LOVE this dessert
perfect for winter

reviews.review_text: This was a great cobbler.  I loved it.  Hubby thought it was to sweet and so did everyone else. Overall they thought it was great just a tad to sweet. I think maybe the canned peaches i bought were maybe a little sweet which probably made this cobbler sweeter than desired.  I thought it was perfect.  I think ill make it again and cut down on the sugar next time or modify it by the sweetness of the peaches.  I agree with other reviews that it needed more peaches.  I think ill add another can of peaches next time.  The leftovers were amazing reheated and topped off with a little whipped cream. Overall great recipe and super easy to make.  I think ill try this recipe with other fruits also.  Its a keeper!

Fantastic!  My husband's favorite fruit is peaches!  I made this with him in mind and the person in our house who devoured most of it was my 18 yr. old son!  We heated it up and topped with vanilla ice cream and it was so very good!!  I invited my in-laws over for some too and they also loved it.  My mother-in-law, who loves anything having to do with ice cream, ate a huge dish of this dessert without blinking an eye!  Yummmmm!!!  In response to those who mentioned the sugar content...I used frozen peaches and followed the recipe exactly.  Both my husband and father-in-law thought it was a bit too sweet for their tastes.  The rest of us loved it.
