items.label: Melt-In-Your-Mouth Chicken Breasts
items.name: Melt-In-Your-Mouth Chicken Breasts
items.description: Make and share this Melt-In-Your-Mouth Chicken Breasts recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Mix mayonnaise or yogurt, cheese and seasonings.
Spread mixture over chicken breast and place in baking dish.
Bake at 375°F for 45 minutes.

reviews.review_text: I made this tonight and I must say it was rather tasty, however, I did tweak the recipe a bit after reading several reviews.  I used a 1/2 c of mayo and a 1/2 c plain greek yogurt (Oikos), two cloves of fresh garlic (finely chopped) and about a 1/4 c of Panko bread crumbs and the rest of the ingrediants but only using half of what it called for because I sprinkled some of the pepper, garlic powder and seasoning salt directly onto the chicken.  I put the mixture in the fridge for about 5 or 10 minutes and it set up like a thick paste- wanted the flavors to marinate.  <br/>There will be liquid in the dish but it was fine.  I served it with fresh stringed beans and roasted red potatoes.  My family loved it, I will make it again- it was really quick and very filling.  (Sidebar:  The chicken does tend dry a little after it cools down but use the 'drippings' to add the moisture-dipping each bite).  I gave it 4 stars only because I didn't follow the reciped to a 'T'.

attributes.source_text: My family loved it

reviews.review_text: I don't like mayo.  DH hates it & sour cream....condiments are contamination!  Skeptically I made this w/2 frozen breasts...1 w/mayo the other w/sourcream...with all the other ingrediants staying the same, (I did use seasoning salt, pepper and garlic powder sprinkled to taste (as much as I would normally sprinkle on my chicken))to try before counting on it for a meal.  They turned out wonderful.  No flipping, cooked in toaster oven, on reynolds release alum. foil, nice and golden on top, it didn't run off the top or anything.  I lied to DH - told him it was a parm cheese topping that I mixed up.  He asked specifically - I told him - they are different, 1 w/butter, parm cheese, spices, and the other I used oil, and different amts of spices and cheese.  I used toothpicks to seperate them.  He liked the 1 toothpick one equating to Sourcream being the winner over the mayo, but he liked the Mayo one too, and ate it also.  I have not, and will not tell him what it's made of b/c if he knew he would never eat it again, or try anything new again.  Very Tender, w/a golden brown topping, and underlayer like melted cheese, then a nice juicy breast.  Yummy, and will make again.  ---- Sooner or later he will be in the kitchen while I'm making it, and he will be so shocked.  LOL  -  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: he liked the Mayo one too, and ate it also
Very Tender
a nice juicy breast

reviews.review_text: This was super easy and REALLY tasty!  I notice some say it was too salty, so here's exactly what I did in case you wonder HOW mine turned out well.  I made the mayo topping exactly as recipe calls for.  Make sure you use SEASONING salt, not regular salt.  <br/><br/>I used an entire 3lb bag of chicken breast tenderloin.  I placed all of them in a layer in a 9x13 baking dish, making almost one solid covering of the bottom of the dish.  I then spread all of the mayo mixture on top of the chicken evenly.  <br/><br/>I baked for 45 minutes, uncovered.  Then broiled on low for about 5 minutes to brown the top.  The top wasn't really crunchy, but it was browned and yummy.  Under the chicken, a slightly creamy sauce formed that we spooned over the chicken when served.<br/><br/>If you're only using 4 chicken breasts and ALL of the mayo mixture, I see how it could be overly salty.  I'm guessing the way I made it is why it tasted perfect (not too salty)!

attributes.source_text: not too salty
a slightly creamy sauce formed

reviews.review_text: The chicken really does melt in your mouth, you can see the juice throughout when you cut it.  The mayo seals in the juices.  I made the mixture "Chinese style"; I added ground ginger, five spice, garlic and ground hot mustard, along with Montreal Chicken seasoning to it because I was making fried rice.  It took a long time for a crust to build and brown--I ended up cranking the temperature up to 475!  and then it started browning.   I think by adding more parmesan cheese it would help and a thin layer of the mixture.  The bottom did not brown but actually disappeared.  I would have like it more crispy.  The flavor though was excellent!  Next time (and there will be one) I will brush the paste on instead of spooning it.  I think it needs to have a thinner layer so that it will brown and crisp up better.  I had it in the oven for a total of 30 minutes--on 375 for 15 minutes and then 450-475 for 15 minutes.  Thank you for a wonderful idea--you can add any spices you like--it is a great mixture to start with!

attributes.source_text: you can see the juice throughout when you cut it
I made the mixture "Chinese style"

reviews.review_text: Fantastic!  My husband took one bite and declared this "miracle chicken!  I'm not sure what you did to it, but it's so juicy and you should always make it like this."  I'm not sure what that says about all the other ways I make chicken, so I'm on the fence whether to be flattered or offended.  ;-)  My almost 5 year old ate this and actually moaned with every bite, so it's a winner here.  I used a homemade mayo that was mostly olive oil based (too strong for spreading, but great in recipes to my tastes), and probably had a little less than a cup in the bowl.  After mixing this up, I just dumped it in a bowl with my chicken and coated it before putting it in a pan and topping with the remaining mayo mixture.  Cooked up perfectly in my convection oven set 50' under temp, but running the full time in the recipe.  Thanks for sharing. UPDATE:  This is also fantastic on catfish.

attributes.source_text: My almost 5 year old ate this and actually moaned with every bite

reviews.review_text: Funny thing...my mom had been raving about a chicken-mayo recipe for a few months and she made it over and over. I recalled this the other day and asked her for the recipe.  She said she hadn't made it in awhile and couldn't find the recipe.  I was bummed - especially since my mayo is about to expire and I wanted to use it up.  I decided to see what other chicken recipes I could find, and lo and behold, here it was.  I never even thought to look for it specifically.  Anyway, it was as delicious as I'd heard.  The only change I made was cut the seasoning salt down to 1/2 teaspoon based on a few other reviewers comments, and I didn't find it too salty at all.  My husband commented repeatedly on how good the chicken was and how moist it was.  I baked 45 minutes exactly and it came out perfect.  A real winner!

attributes.source_text: I didn't find it too salty at all
My husband commented repeatedly on how good the chicken was
how moist it was

reviews.review_text: I love this recipe because it's so flavorful, easy, & versatile as you can use any seasonings you choose. However, I would make the following suggestions: 1) don't use the pre-grated canned cheese 2) taste the mixture before you add salt as it's been my experience that the cheese adds plenty of salt (& I'm a salt lover) 3) sprinkle Italian seasoned bread crumbs over the top or unseasoned crumbs depending on your choice of seasoning. I have made this recipe as directed, as well as with omitting the recipe's seasonings & using Italian seasoning & minced garlic with Italian seasoned bread crumbs, as well as making it with creole seasoning & the Italian seasoned bread crumbs. All 3 versions have been fabulous. For those that have said the mayo mix has been runny, it's likely because they didn't pat the chicken completely dry before spreading on the mix.

I discovered our mayo was way past date, so I ended up using miracle whip.  I think I got it too thick because it didn't make the "crust" like it was supposed to.  But we just didn't eat the excess sauce and it was good.  It did taste "miracle whippy" but I like that flavor, so it was fine.  I would think with mayo, the seasonings used would come through more.   I ate the leftovers a couple of days later and it was still moist.  My 6 and 8 year olds gobbled it up and I was able to bribe my 2 year old to eat it, so that makes this recipe a winner :). Five stars especially because of how easy this was.  I don't like to touch chicken, so I used 6 of the schwans unbreaded chicken breast fillets.  Mixing the ingredients up was super quick.  In fact it took me longer to look for new mayo than to do the rest of the prep!

attributes.source_text: it was still moist
My 6 and 8 year olds gobbled it up
I was able to bribe my 2 year old to eat it

reviews.review_text: Ok, so when this recipe came to my attention (and how couldn't it with that mouth-watering photo??), it was recommended to use Greek yogurt in place of the mayo.  Always looking for a slightly healthier option, I gave it a go.  I replaced the mayo with yogurt and skipped the seasoning salt (due to all the 'too salty' reviews) and used salt, pepper, garlic powder, paprika, and thyme.  The recipe was definitely moist enough to 'melt in your mouth' so that was wonderful.  However, if you are looking for the crispy top that is touted on the picture, you're not getting it by using yogurt (even after a broil).  I will likely try it again with the mayo but for a healthier option that is still amazingly moist, go for the yogurt (and save a few calories!).  :-)  Thumbs up!!

attributes.source_text: definitely moist enough to 'melt in your mouth'

reviews.review_text: I am not rating this because I obviously did something wrong even though I prepared as directed. I did use two huge bone in breasts, but removed the skin.  They were so big that it took the whole recipe of mixture to coat them!  Since they were so big, I was afraid the coating would burn before they were done, so I tented them with foil and took it off the last few minutes so they would brown a little on top.  The sauce basically cooked off of the breasts and ended up in the baking dish.  It was incredibly greasy and just too salty.  However, the sauce did keep the breasts really moist and tender.   All in all, it is worth trying this again sometime.  When I do, I will update this review.  Thanks Denise in NH!

attributes.source_text: the sauce did keep the breasts really moist
the sauce did keep the breasts really moist and tender

reviews.review_text: I am not rating this recipe as I had made quite a bit of changes.  I used 9 chicken thighs....cut the recipe in half...used about 1 tsp of Dijon mustard and sprinkled the chicken with some Panko breadcrumbs..used salt, pepper and a mixed blend of seasonings in place of the salt, pepper and garlic powder.  (I can't use seasoning salt as it has MSG in it)  I cooked the chicken for 35 minutes at 375.  The chicken came out quite moist and flavourful.  This was one of those fast, stupid easy recipe perfect for those those nights where you are in a rush...but would not hold up to snuff for company.  Were I to rate it, I would give it a solid 3-1/2.  There is taste, but the colour is not very appealing!!!  Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: The chicken came out quite moist

reviews.review_text: We have both meat eaters and vegetarians in our family.  I used Quorn naked cutlets for the vegetarians and boneless skinless chicken breasts for the meat eaters.  I also used a light mayo.  But other than that followed the recipe.  It was enjoyed by everyone, which is rare in our house.  The chicken took longer than 45 minutes to cook but the breasts were on the larger side.  The Quorn only took 20-25 minutes and I did not defrost the cutlets before baking.  The only thing I may do differently is reduce the amount of seasoned salt next time.  It was just a little on the strong side.  I will be adding this to my cook book for sure. Thanks!!

Update:  I just wanted to update this review.  I had made this again and used Kraft mayo, and it did not taste as good as the previous time.  The first time I made this I used Hellman's.  My mother also made this using Kraft and they did not like.  My suggestion is to use Hellmans mayo.  I made this for my in-laws who came on short notice.  I wasn't sure if you were supposed to spread the sauce on the bottom too, but I did.  It turned out fantastic.  My DFIN kept saying "ooh, wow".  This is also so simple.  I was worried about the cooking time because I bought chicken from Sam's Club and they were 5 huge breasts.  It took only 1 hour.  I also served steamed baby carrots w/parsley, crescent rolls and a tossed salad.  Thank you for this wonderful and easy dish.  A must for when company comes now.

attributes.source_text: I made this for my in-laws who came on short notice
My DFIN kept saying "ooh, wow"

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe a couple of days ago using low-fat miracle whip and again today using Greek yogurt. It tastes alright, but neither batch looked like the photos with the nice crust on top. I followed the instructions exactly but both times, the chicken just looked like I'd smeared cream on top. It didn't have that golden look at all. I even tried putting the 2nd batch under the broiler for about 5 minutes but all that did was dry it out. I'm so, so disappointed. What I'd really like to know is how to get that baked, golden crusty look on the chicken, cause mine just looks ghostly and not that appetizing, even though the chicken is done. What's the secret?

Too much mayo, too much cooking time and too little flavor.  However, this extremely easy recipe is on the right track.  I've used this technique for many years to cook very oily fish such as bluefish or mackerel.  Cut the amount of mayo in half, add some flavor such as Dijon or whole-grain mustard, seasoned salt, lemon juice or...., and cut the cooking time down to about 25-30 minutes, and you'll have a real winner.  While you're at it, do try it on fish, particularly an oily fish.  The mayo does not add flavor; it just acts as a carrier for flavors.  If the internal temperature of the chicken gets over 165F, it's fully cooked and perfectly safe.  Higher than that and it starts turning cottony and mushy.  I gave this 3 stars as-is.  I'd give it 5 stars with my changes.

Came out great!!! After reading the reviews I made a few changes. I skipped the salt, added a few additional spices along with Dijon mustard (1 tsp) and sour cream (1 tbs) to the mayo mix. I tasted the mayo mix with a cherry tomato and believe it or not it would make a great, albeit heavy, dipping sauce! Also, I took the advice to apply the mayo mix lightly to the chicken. I  sprinkled a bit of Garlic powder on the chicken before applying the mayo mix. I also used a mixture of fresh Parmesan cheese & Italian breadcrumbs and added it to the chicken when it was half way done cooking. Served with a steamed potato & veggie mix and Southwest mac n cheese. We're full now :) Photo uploaded!

This came out wonderful! I had just 2 chicken breasts, so I halved the recipe. I used 1/4c mayo and 1/4c Greek yogurt; I halved everything else as well. I only put a dash of seasoned salt due to my mother’s high blood pressure. The chicken breasts I had weren’t thick but weren’t thin, so I adjusted the cooking time. I baked for 30 minutes and then raised the temp to 500 for about 3 minutes to brown them a little more. The chicken was tender and flavorful. The tang from the yogurt was a nice treat! Served it with cauliflower mash and broccoli. I’ll definitely be adding this to our regular rotation and will try it on salmon and tuna as well.

attributes.source_text: The chicken was tender

reviews.review_text: FORGOT TO RATE - THIS IS A 10 STAR! I actually grabbed this recipe back in 2012 and thought it sounded good, though I was skeptical about "melt in your mouth". But, I found myself in the kitchen throwing it together. I'm one of those who likes to add a little spice to dishes, so I added two things - crushed red pepper flakes, garlic chips; I cut the garlic powder down to about a 1/4 tsp and used Cajun bread crumbs. LOL... OMG... you are right on the money about melt in your mouth chicken. I have NEVER had chicken breast so juicy and tender, and the coating... dang. My favorite chicken recipe. Thanks for sharing!

items.label: Panera Broccoli Cheese Soup
items.name: Panera Broccoli Cheese Soup
items.description: Make and share this Panera Broccoli Cheese Soup recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Sauté onion in butter. Set aside.
Cook melted butter and flour using a whisk over medium heat for 3-5 minutes or until you see a noticeable golden brown color in your pan.
Slowly add in the chicken stock and whisk again to combine. Simmer contents covered (stirring occasionally) for 20 minutes on medium heat.

Add the broccoli, carrots and the sauteed onions, into the pot. Stir, add the milk and half & half. Cook covered over low heat 20-25 minutes but do not bring to a boil. This may cause the milk to curdle.

Add salt, pepper & nutmeg. Note: you can purée half of your soup in a blender or with a handheld immersion blender if you choose however it isn't a requirement. Continue to cook the soup on low heat and slowly add the grated cheese a handful at a time and stir to avoid clumps. Once all the cheese has been added is melted, remove from heat, and serve immediately. Suggestion: serve with crusty bread or in a breadbowl.
Refrigerate leftovers after they have cooled and store in a airtight container up to 5 days in the refrigerator.

reviews.review_text:
Followed to a T, and it is awesome soup. I think its probably better than Panera because it is fresh, no preservatives and probably less sodium. And I think Panera Bread is to pretentious for there crappy sandwiches, they are definitely proud of them. If you like broccoli and cheese soup this is a go to recipe. King Arthur Flour has a recipe for a "No-knead Crusty White bread" that went awesome with this soup.
http://www.kingarthurflour.com/recipes/no-knead-crusty-white-bread-recipe

Holy Crap, this is whats in there soup, yuck!
Broccoli cheddar (Water, milk, broccoli, pasteurized process cheddar cheese [cheddar cheese {pasteurized milk, cheese culture, salt, enzymes}, water, sodium phosphate, milkfat, salt, apocarotenal {color}], cream [cream, milk] carrots, modified corn starch, onions, chicken base [chicken meat in chicken broth {chicken meat, chicken broth, chicken fat, modified corn starch and/or rice flour, salt}, salt, hydrolyzed corn and soy protein, sugar, natural flavorings, potato flour, autolyzed yeast extract, carrot powder, turmeric], flour [bleached wheat flour, malted barley flour, niacin, reduced iron, thiamine, mononitrate, riboflavin, folic acid], butter [cream, salt], seasoning [salt, spices, extractives of paprika], soybean oil, mustard [water, vinegar, mustard seed, salt, white wine, fruit pectin, citric acid, tartaric acid, sugar, spice], pepper sauce [vinegar, red pepper, salt]).

I will stick to simple and pure, thank you.

attributes.source_text: because it is fresh

reviews.review_text: Yes, I have to admit, I am reviewing this recipe and made changes. But hey, it's 5 stars! I've made Cauliflower Cheese soup for years, a thousand different ways, and experience has taught me things I can't unlearn at my age. First, I cooked the onion in a little over a 1/4 cup of butter and then just added the flour to it to cook and proceeded from there,  which is what I've always done for other cheese sauces and soups. Secondly, it helps very much to stir pretty much the whole 20 minutes with a wooden spoon after the half and half and stock are added, as is customary with any white sauce-based soup. But always open to new ideas, I loved adding the broccoli after that and just cooking it in the sauce. (So much easier than my tried-and-true but extra-dirty-dishes method of cooking the veggies separately! Thank you!) The last change I made was that I added some shredded Monterey Jack cheese too, as I think the Panera soup is a bit smoother and creamier than a standard cheddar cheese soup and for me this made it much the same. But the gist of it is, I loved it and my daughter and I thank you!!!!

attributes.source_text: my daughter and I thank you

reviews.review_text: This recipe is excellent. My seasoning adjustments make it taste more like Panera's. My cooking recommendations are what works best for me for a busy weeknight meal. In a pot, add chicken broth. My favorite chicken stock is Better Bouillon paste (keep refrigerated). I add an extra half a cup of liquid bc I will be boiling veggies with lid on. Add the broccoli and carrots. I use frozen chopped broccoli florets with half of the stems removed and a bag of pre-julienned carrots (found in produce section near baby carrots). Boil covered over medium heat for 10 minutes. (This cooking time varies greatly by what kind/size pan you are using and your heat level. Take the lid of often to check. Only boil until carrots are tender.) I use my immersion blender to puree veggie/broth mixture bc my young children will only it eat it pureed. Otherwise, Panera broccoli cheese is NOT pureed. In a separate pan, make white sauce. Over medium heat, Sauté onion in butter. When onions translucent add garlic. Sauté. Turn heat to low. Add flour. Whisk. Slowly add heavy cream (not half and half). Turn heat off. Add cheese. It actually taste more like Panera if you use three cheese powder, but using 1/2 shredded Cabot cheddar cheese and 1/2 American cheese like Velveeta is desirable. This will be very thick. You want it to be! Turn heat back on low white sauce. Slowly add chicken broth broccoli and carrots mixture while whisking into white sauce. Stir in seasoning to your liking 1 tsp. salt, 1/2 tsp. pepper, 1 tsp. paprika, 1 tsp. white wine, 1 tsp. dijon mustard, and 1/2 tsp. hot sauce. (My young children prefer no white wine, 1 tsp dry mustard powder, and 1/4 tsp. hot sauce.) Another note: I have thickened soup with potato starch for gluten free. you can use lactose free real sharp cheddar cheese and soy heavy cream for lactose free options. I normally make Rhodes frozen dinner rolls to accompany this soup. I use the quick method. I defrost frozen rolls in microwave, so they will raise in 1 hour on my hot stove near where I'm cooking. We have green salad and fresh fruit for dessert. Viola.

attributes.source_text: for a busy weeknight meal
my young children will only it eat it pureed
This will be very thick. You want it to be!
My young children prefer no white wine

reviews.review_text: This recipe is a good base to start with, but after reading the reviews and trying it for myself, I have to give some tips. DO NOT ADD MILK. I didn’t even add any and it came out thick and creamy enough with all the cheese and half half. While your making your rue, steam the cut broccoli in a pot. Add a lil more flour to your rue to get it really get it nice and thick. I probably added half a cup extra flour just because I knew the stock and half half would thin it out and it came out prefect!! After I added the chicken stock to the rue covered it and let it sit 20 min, stirring occasionally as the recipe stated. During that time I made sure the broccoli was being steamed. I added a very tiny bit of butter and salt and pepper to the broccoli. After the twenty minutes I added the rue to the pot with broccoli and poured some chopped carrots into it + 2 cups of half and half milk. I let it sit for ten more minutes to have it cook the carrots a bit. For more seasoning I added a garlic and herb mix from ms. Dash, salt and pepper, nutmeg, and dry parsley. Then I added a good five handfuls of sharp cheddar cheese and am now letting it sit until my dad comes home so we can eat as a family. I’ve had little sips here and there to test it, and it’s so so good!!! It definitely doesn’t beat Panera, but it comes very very close!!

attributes.source_text: it came out thick
creamy enough

reviews.review_text: I haven't been feeling well and wanted this soup but didn't want to leave the house. I had most of the ingredients on hand, with the exception of half and half, so I did make some alterations. The results were amazing! I would try it with the half and half next time, I'm sure that would make it more like Panera's, BUT, I Must say, I love the way it turned out with my substitution(s). The adjustments I made we're as follows: Didn't summer the roux for 20 minutes because I wasn't feeling well and wanted to shorten cooking time. I used 4 cups stock (the whole box since I knew I didn't have the half and half) and added the veggies. I simmered that for 20 minutes, hit it with my immersion blender until it was about 1/3 pureed. Then I stirred in 1 cup whole milk and the cheese. When it was melted, I added 1 cup plain kefir (thick buttermilk would work too). I then added a little more milk until it was the desired consistency. It was delicious! Thanks for a great recipe!

This is the best recipe for broccoli soup I have came across!! I do not understand why people search for recipes just to change everything about it and then complain and rate low because it wasn't as good as they had hoped. First off why not try the recipe first and then make changes the second time if any are needed. The flour in this recipe is very very important. The first time I made the soup it was so creamy and delicious, I raved about it and my boyfriend begged me to make it again a week later so I did but this time the creaminess was this weird texture and I thought I had everything in the pot so I though maybe the cheese was no good or something since it had completely separated from the soup base. I gave it another try last week and the same thing, the cheese separated from the soup base. Came back to this recipe sine it worked so well the first time and realized I forgot the flour. Please learn from my repeated mistake and don't forget the flour. I have tried the Cracker Barrel Extra Sharp Cheddar, the Tillamook Extra Sharp and the smoked sharped and liked the Tillamook extra sharp the best. :) Yummmmmmmy this soup is amazing!! Thank you for being so selfless and not keeping it to yourself.

reviews.review_text: I just read about a hundred of these reviews...I think its funny how people say "this doesn't taste at all like Panera" and then go on about how they changed this and that part of the recipe when they tried it:-)   I have not yet made this, but when I do I'll be using vegetable broth (not sure if I should use that or chicken-style vegetarian broth).  Even so, a suggestion that might be helpful.  The people that say it was flavorless...my guess is if you use a high quality sharp cheddar like Cabot instead of Kraft it will make it much more flavorful.  And then it seems like most of the people that really disliked this recipe said it was much too thick.   The recipe didn't specify whether or not to cover while simmering, but that can impact how thick the soup is as can the size/shape of the pot and what your definition of a "simmer" and "low heat" are, among other things. Its easy enough to replace water that has evaporated or add more broth (depending on how the too thick soup tastes)...silly to grudgingly eat it or throw it out because its too thick!

This a very good soup.  I made it primarily because it's cold outside and my husband enjoys broccoli cheese soup.  I read many other reviews and in my opinion, much of the success of this recipe came down to the cheese . . . seriously, use good cheese. Someone wrote using Cabot cheese, I never heard of it.  However, as I sauntered the aisles of my grocery store I saw Cabot cheese and bought it.  It melted nicely and gave the soup a creamy cheesey "bite" aka sharp flavor.  Overall, my soup did have a wonderful consistency -- not too thin, nor thick.    I ended up using a lb of broccoli which was the way it came packaged at my store.  I will say, make sure you julienne your carrots to cook evenly with the other veggies; i.e., the broccoli.  My carrots had just a little too much crunch left to them, probably could have been cut thinner/smaller or cooked a tad longer.  I also sifted about 3/4 of the end product veggies from the soup and put them into the blender with about 1/2 cup of the broth to help the blending along.    I then put it all back into the soup -- I think this was a plus, some veggie pieces yet enough smoothness so  that it wasn't like baby food.  Spoiler alert:  When it was all finished, just for fun in my bowl, I did toss in a small pinch of the commercial brand monterrey colby/jack mix and think it sort added something.    Husband really enjoyed this soup.    I would definitely make this again.

reviews.review_text: I absolutely love, love, love this Broccoli & Cheese soup recipe! For those people afraid to add freshly grated nutmeg (1/4 tsp) you don't know what you're missing! It adds such a subtle touch to the soup. You will NOT taste nutmeg, if that's what's keeping you from trying. Like a few others, the only change I made was to add the butter and flour to the sauteed onions. I saw no reason to set aside. I did chop my broccoli into very small pieces to save time on cooking through. I also used my immersion blender to make a creamy blended soup. I do love biting into chunks of broccoli, however, due to tooth surgery I am unable to chew and this soup really comforted my hunger for delicious tasting food that doesn't need chewing! Thanks so much for sharing this recipe! Minor suggestion for those who said their soup was too thin, try upping your flour/butter ration from 1/4 cup to 1/3 cup.

reviews.review_text: I was looking for a good broccoli soup, not the fat bomb that this one is, so I tweaked it and it was delicious! I substituted the 2 cups of half and half and 1 cup of whole milk for 3 cups of chicken broth. I added the carrots and chopped broccoli immediately after adding the extra broth, which means that I shaved off 30 minutes off the cooking time. At the end I added the one cup of whole milk and the cheese, stirring all the while until hot and the cheese all melted, without letting the soup boil again. Since it wasn't quite as rich as the original recipe, I served the soup with seasoned croutons, delicious! P.S. On a whim I added a couple sprinkles of curry powder to my roux along with the nutmeg for a nice touch of heat--you might like that too! P.P.S. This is not the Panera soup, which I've never tasted, but just a suggestion for another way of making broccoli soup.

Ive made this recipe a hundred times. My family just loves this! Its definately a go to for my 5 yr old. She requested it again today for dinner. With as many times as ive made this, ive just tweeked a few things since it fits my family better. I use whole milk instead of half and half. We never have half and half on hand. And never the extra cash to go and grab some. I also add potatoes to fill it in more, my hubby eats alot lol plus feeding a family of 5 i gotta make sure it goes around. (think i just need a bigger pot) lol i also add fresh garlic. I use garlic in most foods i make. Helps us from getting sick so much! I add that when i cook the onions. I also do not have an emerson blender so i just use my hand mixer lol this is tho one of my hands down favorite soups. Kinda wishing i had crusty bread or bread bowls to go with it this time! We've never had it with bread before. All in all this is a fantastic recipe!! Thank you so much for whomever posted it!

reviews.review_text: This recipe was a win!! I'm going to list my changes based on our family's dietary needs in case it's helpful. We added more carrot (an extra cup) and I ran it through the food processor rather than shred it. We then partially sautéed the carrots with the onion as we wanted them to be done. We also used frozen broccoli florets as some of the reviewers said the fresh wasn't cooked through. This worked great and we will do it again!! Also, we used dairy free butter and cashew milk (in place of both the cream and milk). We also used gluten free flour and upped it to 1/2 cup and added in an extra couple tablespoons of butter, since other reviewers have said it was too thin. Our soup turned out thick and creamy. The flavor was excellent, and I loved the addition of carrot (who can complain about adding more veggies?! ;). This will be a regular on our dinner rotation.

reviews.review_text: Wonderful! I have made this many times now, as it my 6-year-old's most requested dinner item.  I always double the recipe so there will be leftovers.  It reheats beautifully - she frequently takes leftovers for lunch in a thermos.  I have never found it to be too thick, and I always simmer uncovered.  I use sharp cheddar (usually just the Albertson's store brand, nothing special) and it has a wonderful cheese flavor.  To those that say it is flavorless - did you add salt? I don't measure how much I use, just add a bit at a time until it tastes right, but it's at least 1-2 teaspoons (in a double batch).  I also add a bit of black or mixed pepper.  I like it better without the nutmeg, so have stopped using it, and didn't have any carrots the first time I made it and have just never added since.  I had this soup at Panera a couple weeks ago, and thought taste and texture were very similar.  I didn't taste nutmeg in their's, either.  I did have the cheese curdle once. Looking back, I think I did add all the cheese at once that day, instead of a little at a time - I was very distracted by said 6-year-old while making the soup that day. Even then, it tasted fine, the texture was just odd. Thanks for a wonderful, easy recipe!

reviews.review_text: made this soup for dinner last night. it was superb! i did make changes to the recipe tho..here is how i made mine: i took half an onion, 3 garlic cloves, 1 carrot and put it all in the food processor . i also quartered 2 red potatoes and chopped 2 bunches of fresh brocolli into little florets. then i melted 1/3 cup butter and sauteed all the vegis together for 15 minutes. added vegi stock instead of chicken stock, as well as 1/2 cup water and 1/3 cup milk. simmered it covered for 30 minutes. then i added salt and pepper and used a hand blender to blend it in the pot. finally, i added 6 ounces cheddar cheese (8 ounces would have been way too much for my taste- it was VERY cheesy..and served it! it truly was delicious! not bland at all..very flavorful and thick but definitely still had a soupy consistency (though i believe without the water and milk added in it would have been more like a dip than a soup, as one reviewer stated hers came out)

This is excellent! I wanted to make something special for the kids since it was cold and rainy outside. I did the best that I could with what I had in stock. I didn't have any fresh onion so I used onion powder and a little minced garlic. I didn't have half and half and ran out of milk, so I used 1 cup heavy cream and 1 cup water. I used beef broth instead of chicken and I didn't have any carrots so I added extra broccoli. After all that though I followed the recipe and even added the nutmeg. reviews.review_text: This is the absolute BEST broccoli cheese soup you will ever have. I first made this soup when I was fifteen, and now I'm going on eighteen. I'm a huge fan of Panera and almost always get the soup there. However, it is extremely nice to make it at home because 1) I feel like I'm on Master Chef and 2) it's an excellent soup when you want something homemade or on a cold day. Heck, it's always an excellent soup! I'm making it tonight, actually. Some might be worried about the nutmeg, but I promise you it's excellent! It adds a nuttiness to the soup and makes all of the flavors stand out. If you have any doubts about this soup, just make it anyways! I suggest not changing ANYTHING except maybe adding a clove of minced garlic in with the onions. But really, make it as is first.

reviews.review_text: I've never had Panera soup, but this recipe makes a delicious soup. Only changes I made were 2 cloves of garlic sauted with the onion, whole milk instead of half/half, and I only added about five ounces of cheese as opposed to eight. Seemed like 8 ounces was a bit much for such a small volume of soup. The soup thickened up beautifully. Creamy and thick without being overly rich. For those who complain that this has no flavor, I am baffled. My first guess is lack of salt. The soup does require a good bit of salt and pepper, but that's the nature of any recipe. You salt as you go, and add as much as you think it needs to bring out the flavor. My second guess is using a bland supermarket cheese. I used a good quality cheddar from Trader Joe's. Not expensive at all, but way more flavor than the bland rubbery stuff. I will definitely be making this again.

items.label: Easy Stove-Top Macaroni & Cheese
items.name: Easy Stove-Top Macaroni & Cheese
items.description: Make and share this Easy Stove-Top Macaroni & Cheese recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Cook macaroni according to package directions.
In medium saucepan, melt butter over medium heat; stir in flour, and cook for 3-5 minutes stirring constantly to form a roux; add salt and pepper; slowly add milk, stirring well after each addition.
Cook and stir until bubbly.
Stir in cheese a small amount at a time until fully melted.
Drain macaroni; add to cheese sauce; stir to coat.

reviews.review_text: This was a very easy recipe that anyone can do. The base makes a great gravy, (do everything except add cheese). I added a pinch of extra pepper. I had several packets of cheese that were almost empty so I used everything I had and it was a little more than 2 cups. I used 1c shredded sharp cheddar, 2oz white brick cheese (1/4c), 3/4 shredded Colby jack, 1/4c shredded Parmesan, and a 1oz tube of processed cheese (like velveeta) that I had from a sausage/crackers/cheese box. It was pretty thick once all the cheese was melted so I added an additional 1/3c of milk and stirred that in to thin it out just a bit. The flavor was really good. It was very rich, creamy, and cheesy. The seasonings were just fine for a simple mac n cheese but if you want to take it up a notch I'd also add garlic powder, paprika, and maybe some parsley. The only complaint I have is that it was a bit gritty. It was a very fine grit, though, so it was tolerable. I cooked the roux (constantly whisking)for about 3 minutes and it looked just fine to me- buttery and bubbly. Maybe I didn't add the milk slowly enough. My two year old really liked it and so did I besides the slight grit. I only had rigatoni noodles in the pantry so that's what I used instead of elbow macaroni. It was about half of a 16oz box and I still had plenty of cheese sauce left over that I saved in a separate container for more macaroni on another day. You can probably add an extra 6-8oz of noodles for the amount of sauce this makes. I just need to figure out how to make a completely non gritty mac n cheese- the only ones I've ever had made by anyone that were 100% smooth were from a box! EDIT: I did some researching and found what the problem might have been. I really think I did the roux correctly. Apparently adding the cheese very slowly (and preferably after taking the pan off the heat) is a huge key to getting smooth sauce in a recipe like this, which is funny because when I make alfredo it's never a big deal to dump it all in. Must have something to do with also having a roux involved. This is what I found online from a very experienced cook: Could be an unfinished roux (the butter, flour mixture). But most likely it's because the cheese was heated too quickly or too much, causing the protein to clump up. Suggestions: •Melt with less heat •Use a double boiler (to reduce hot spots within the pan) •Toss the shredded cheddar with cornstarch first (starch helps reduce clumping) •Add cheese in smaller batches (easier to maintain correct heat level and stir cheese in)

reviews.review_text: Let me just start by saying I read through 100's of the reviews as the first one really caught my attention. Anyway, flavor is a very individual issue. If everyone tasted everything the same then there would be no need for so many choices. I tried this recipe for two specific reasons, it was easy and many of the reviews stated that it was bland. I am currently undergoing chemotherapy and my taste buds are completely out of whack. Everything I eat right now tastes salty. I have tried almost all the boxed types out there and they are all too salty for me. So I thought I would try to make one from scratch where I could control the salt content. This is an awesome, basic recipe and if you read the reviews you can get a wealth of ideas on how to make it so that it tastes good to you. That is the best part of a basic, made at home recipe. That said, I made this recipe omitting the salt because the only cheese I had on hand were pretty high in sodium as it was. I had Gouda, Havarti and Muenster. Other than that, I followed the recipe exactly. It came out perfect for me. The taste was not overly salty, and the sauce was rich and creamy. I ate it as is, my daughter added to her own bowl, some white pepper, salt and a dash of nutmeg, and she loved hers. So please, don't judge a recipe as awful simply based on it being bland to you. There is nothing wrong with anyone's taste buds. Look at it as a canvas on which you can create the perfect dish for you, and when my chemo therapy is over, I am going to continue to make this dish, changing up cheeses and spices each time depending on what I feel like that day. Thank you Marie for such a great recipe.

reviews.review_text: Made this as written for the most part. I didn't realize my scale was off by an ounce so only used 7 ounces of pasta. We used Tillamook cheddar and real butter. Again, the key to white sauce is to cook it long enough so the sauce doesn't taste like flour. This was super yummy! LOVED how saucy it was, almost all of my family of 9 liked it!!  Thank you, we will be adding this to our menu!  UPDATE:  I have one child who requests this daily!!  But with the price of cheese I just can't do it. BUT we have had it about 3 times in a month as it is so easy and yummy.<br/>Update 5-3-13: you have to use REAL cheese. Not marble, not pre-shredded.. The preshredded stuff has rice flour added to it so it doesn't stick so your space will be grainy. Also, you need to cook your flour in the butter for a minute and then when you add your milk make sure to bring your sauce to almost a boil or even to a boil, then remove from heat and add your cheese then. This is NOT Kraft Mac and cheese, this is real food, dump and stir doesn't work. You do have to put some effort into it, but so worth it.<br/>We have used Tillamook cheddar, Tillamook white cheddar, cheap cheddar, sharp cheddar.. The key is CHEDDAR, and shred it yourself

reviews.review_text: Outstanding mac and cheese.  The sauce was the height of velvet deliciousness, and there was plenty of sauce.    I used lowfat milk, full-fat cheddar and real butter.    I took the perfectionist route and sprinkled in the flour (not having Wondra on hand), and I couldn't believe the texture.   I did have to add a little flour because I lost some to my fingers and countertop while sprinkling.   NEVER have I had a better texture in a cheese sauce.  NOTES FOR SUCCESS:   The flour needs to be added very slowly, stirring all the while.   It will clump if added quickly.   Just resign yourself to the zen of it, and enjoy creating a masterpiece.   The flour mixture needs to be cooked long enough for it to thicken.  If you've never made a roux or white sauce, try to find a video online.   That cooks out the flour taste and is also what thickens the sauce.   The cheese should not be packaged, pre-grated cheese.   The latter is coated with something to keep the strands separate, and it WILL effect the final outcome.   Lastly, if your heat is low enough, the cheese can be added in only two or three batches as long as you're constantly stirring.

reviews.review_text: Mmmm..yummy!! This one of few mac n cheese recipes I have tried and it now has become a household staple. If you are a die-hard Velveeta fan then you probably won't care for this recipe since the texture differs from Velveeta. I would recommend combining American and extra sharp cheddar at about a 1:1 ratio with some milk or cream and some salt (salt enhances the flavor of cheese). I think this would provide a texture more similar to Velveeta. Be sure to melt the American first and then add cheddar as the stabilizers in the American cheese will help stabilize the cheddar for a smooth consistency. Now, if you are a fan of Stouffer's mac n cheese or sauces made with a roux then you will enjoy this recipe. It is a good base recipe and versatile since you can add whatever you please (I add mustard powder and cayenne to mine and I'm sure probably add a little more salt ). If you are unfamiliar with making a roux try googling it, that way you can prevent an unpleasant consistency or floury taste. I also agree with a previous review on the quality of cheese you use, I personally love it with extra sharp white cheddar. Also if it seems too bland for your taste add another dash or two of salt, it really does bring out the sharpness of the cheese! :)

reviews.review_text: My sister was the first one to find this recipe and make it for a family cookout.  It was really really good and so easy.  I made it tonight for my family and it was a hit.  I think I improved on my sister's attempt.  I didn't do much different in the way of ingredients or amounts, but the cooking and preparation.  For everyone complaining about it's being grainy or floury, then you are either adding too much flour or you aren't thoroughly stirring out all of the lumps or making a lump free roux.  Don't use a spoon, use a small or medium whisk and beat it like you are angry with it!  Cut back on the flour some and whisk well until the butter roux is SMOOTH.  As you add the milk and heat it, remember lumps will REFORM so you have to keep whisking it to keep the lumps away.  It should be thick, not runny, but not so stiff you can't stir it.  The whisking should take a little effort if it's easy, then it needs a little more flour.  Don't go by the exact recipe all the time, you need to be practiced enough as a cook to recognize if something is too thin or thick by the eye!  Once you add it to your pasta, stir it very well with a wooden spoon, they work better than metal in my opinion and don't scratch your pots!  Stir is completely through.  Then turn up the heat some and let it begin to bubble.  This helps to thicken the sauce some if it's still too runny.  Turn off the heat and let it set, that will complete the thickening and setting process. If you follow these steps it should turn out pretty well!  Mine turned out great, even my two picky kids asked for seconds!!

reviews.review_text: PLEASE READ THIS REVIEW!!  I get extremely annoyed at those members who post these horrible reviews and then don't even bother to complete their pages.  As far as I'm concerned, they just "hit and run".  This recipe was featured the other day and I saved it to try.  I have just now completed it and it is delicious!  The only change I made was to use a Mexican style blend cheese, because that's what I had.  It is not grainy, gritty or disgusting.  Remember, the  cheese you select to use will dictate the taste of the dish.  I have no burned flour taste.  I completely melted the butter, whisked in the flour, whisked in the milk and then kept whisking until it was thickened to my satisfaction.  I left it a bit runny, because the starch from the pasta will cause it to "draw" up.  Removed from the heat, stirred in the cheese until it was melted and creamy, then stirred in the elbows.  Pure mac and cheese heaven!  This is a classic recipe and not to be confused with a boxed mix or that made with Velveeta.  Velveeta isn't even classified as real cheese (and I still love it!).  Marie, thank you again for another wonderful recipe.  This is a keeper and I will use it often because it's such a fast meal.  To those of you who left rotten reviews, "LEARN TO COOK" before you post such nonsense.  Also, if a man leaves you because you flopped a dish--men are like streetcars--another one will come along shortly.

reviews.review_text: This recipe was great! Making the sauce took exactly the same amount of time as cooking the noodles (12 min). I used a few more noodles than the recipe called for - I had about 9.5 oz left in a bag - but there was still plenty of sauce. DH and I agree that this recipe is exponentially better than 'the boxed stuff', and even my 6-year-old said, "I love them both, I can't say which I like better." Since 'the box' is in her top 3 favorite foods, that is high praise indeed. Sorry, love, but Mommy's not going to be pulling out the box in an emergency any more. You'll just have to get used to eating real food instead! UPDATE 12/4/16 - This is still my go-to recipe. It's very saucy, so I either add all the sauce knowing it will be somewhat "soupy" the first day, but will still be creamy when the noodles suck up more liquid in the fridge, or I just don't add all the sauce and instead save it to put on broccoli or even on toast, then under the broiler for a couple minutes. Yum! For those of you who find it bland, ADD MORE SALT!!! I know salt has a bad rep, but unless your doctor has specifically told you to reduce your sodium intake, it's not bad for you and it significantly enhances food's flavor. I'm not talking about a ton of salt, either, an extra 1/4-1/2 tsp will go a long way! Update 1/31/20: Still my go-to recipe! I see the noodles have been updated to 16oz (used to be 8oz). I've settled on making a 1.5 batch of sauce for 16oz noodles. Still very saucey, but not soupy.

reviews.review_text: The first time I made this recipe (exactly as written), it was not good at all. Just like some other reviewers, I had a floury textured sauce that wasn't smooth and creamy at all. Don't get me wrong, it was edible, just not very good. I don't know what the lady who made the "divorce recipe" did so terribly wrong. Anyway, after reading all of the reviews to try to figure out what I could have done wrong, I was more confused. Some people said maybe the butter/flour mixture cooked too long while others said it may have not cooked long enough. Well, I did a search for how to make a roux and the problem was solved...I didn't cook the butter/flour mixture long enough. For all of the people that leave ugly comments for others (like myself) that came up with a floury textured sauce, shame on you. The directions say absolutely nothing about how long to cook the mixture before adding milk. For anyone who is new to cooking, how should we possibly know anything other than what's written in the instructions?! Even if the author of the recipe would have kept it simple, but mentioned the word "roux", I would have at least known that there is something I need to know and looked up how to make a roux ahead of time. Unfortunately, I wasted a lot of ingredients making an unsatisfactory dish simply because of inadequate instructions (and inexperience on my part). The second time I made this (after learning the proper way to make a roux), it turned out fine and tasted the way homemade macaroni and cheese should taste...smooth, creamy and cheesy.

reviews.review_text:
Wonderful and simple!

I made this for my three young kids who are huge critics and don't hold back. Well, they LOVED it! Even my autistic daughter who is SUPER picky! She ate so much more than she would have from the boxed nastiness. 

One thing a lot of people may not realize is WHISK WHISK WHISK! Whisk the dry ingredients into the butter for a minute or two, THEN whisk in the milk. Then whisk the heck out of the added cheese.  

I forgot to grate my cheese beforehand so I put in on a low-med heat and would grate a bit, then whisk a few minutes. Back and forth like that until my cheese was grated, then put the heat to medium and whisked constantly until I could add my cheese. No gritty or floury taste at all, but I'm used to making cheese sauces with this process.

Also I didn't quite have enough marble cheese (just the type I had on hand - I reccomend an old or sharp cheddar for more flavour) so I added half a brick of original cream cheese and about 1/2 tablespoon of extra pepper. Was wonderful, and my kids loved it. 

Will definitely keep this on hand. No more store bought KD for us!

reviews.review_text: First of all, the lady who said she's now getting a divorce over this recipe is a drama queen. Can't even take a review like that seriously. I am a Mac n cheese connoisseur. It's been my favorite dish since childhood. I made this, it was ok... It has the creamy, it doesn't have the cheesy flavor I love, it's just not THE go-to recipe. Personally, I prefer a stovetop in certain situations. I like it to have the "idea" of a baked. First reason, if I have to reheat a Mac n cheese, stovetop is the way to go. It stays creamy, whereas an oven baked does not. It gets congealed. With all that being said, I know how to make a roux, unlike others here. It's not a "floury" recipe. You people just have no idea what you're doing. It's a basic roux. Equal parts fat to flour. You have to cook the flour taste out. Give the butter and flour mixture at LEAST 2 mins on the stove, it needs to "sizzle" while you stir it. The BEST stovetop Mac n cheese recipe I've found was in my moms old cookbook "joy of cooking" (not the new version!). It reheats well too. She just won't give me her book and I had a craving so I found this recipe. It's not BAD. It's just not awesome. More cheese maybe??

reviews.review_text: I don't think you can mess up this recipe even if you tried! I was looking for a quick and simple mac and cheese recipe. My go to recipe had way too many ingredients than what I had on hand. Viola I found this recipe online and gave it a try! It may be my number one recipe in the future since it was easy and really good. I did tweak it a bit because I was missing some ingredients. I followed the roux part and turned down the heat so it wouldn't burn (my stovetop settings tends to run hotter). I added the pepper to my liking, left out the salt. I didn't have milk, so I used 1/2 cup sour cream and 1 1/2 cups chicken broth mixed together, and slowly added this mixture to the pot. I then added a little more butter to give back the fat missing from not having milk. At this point I added Tony Chachere's bold creole seasoning and cayenne for a little flavor. Once it bubbled, I added 8oz of velvetta cheese and let it melt and turned off the heat after. Then added 1 cup of shredded colby/monterrey jack cheese blend into the pot. This dish was delicious, flavorful, cheesy, creamy and simple.

reviews.review_text: This turned out FANTASTIC!! I learned today that I never made my roux correctly...never cooked it long enough, this is the first time I got CREAMY, delicious cheese sauce. Thank you to the posters who corrected me! I used some extra sharp Tillamook and some sharp white Tillamook cheese and it was a little "sharp" for my 10 yo foodie son, but he still gave it 4 out of 5 stars =) I think I'll use just 'regular' sharp cheddar next time with a little white or extra sharp cheese, but made exactly as described and it came out amazing! OK, we used collezione pasta and I did add a little extra flavor...dijon mustard, paprika & nutmeg, but spices are just a personal choice. He said it had "too much cheese flavor" so I was trying to overcome the sharp. The recipe is spot on. Next time, if I have extra time, I'll try putting it in the oven with breadcrumb/butter topping for the last 10 minutes at 400 degrees, but I was going for quick and this is IT! Fantastic, Thank You!!

reviews.review_text: **PLEASE READ** I will like to say that this Mac N' Cheese do not have the wow factor. It tastes exactly like bland elbow macaroni mixed with cheese. For Mac N' Cheese lovers do not make this. I wanted to  make something fast, quick, and easy instead of the traditional way I make it which requires a little more ingredients and time. The positive things I'll say is its fast, looks like the photo, and my toddler ate it. My husband just smiled after taking about two bites.  Since the quantity was large I added  1/4 c. chicken broth, some softened cream cheese, little smoked cheddar cheese, and paprika. After letting it simmer for about 10 minutes, it was much more flavorful. I made this recipe exactly how the recipe instructed and it was not excellent, delicious, nor very good. All these 5 star ratings are rather baffling to me because if this is 5 stars you people have not tried really good Mac N' Cheese. If I'm pressed with time, I'd rather purchase the Velveeta Deluxe in a box before making this again.

reviews.review_text: This is a very good basic mac and cheese, and definitely so much better than the boxed kind (although the kid in me still loves an occasional Kraft mac and cheese)! Like several others here have said, you do have to know how to make a roux and make sure the flour is cooked through in the butter, just like the recipe states how to do. I find that extra sharp cheddar, which I always have on hand, is great for this quick recipe, and if you happen to have some chevre goat cheese, it goes good as well. The two cheese flavors go together really good and the goat cheese tends to make it extra creamy. A quick science-based suggestion as well that I just learned from the cooking show Milk Street: To keep the cheeses from being gritty at all due to their enzymes breaking apart and to ensure real creaminess without having to mix and mix, add about 1/4 cup olive oil (or other mild oil) to the cheeses, along with the spices, in a separate bowl and mash together thoroughly with a fork BEFORE adding to macaroni. The oil keeps the cheeses from breaking apart in the sauce. Turns out great!

reviews.review_text: I've been looking for a good stovetop mac and cheese recipe for months now. I've tried a few, but always end up with the clumpy curded sauce once the mac and cheese cools. I was worried about that happening with this recipe, but it didn't. Even after cooling in the refrigerator, the sauce is still creamy and cheesy and deliciously amazing! I read through the reviews before I started and I have to agree that the key to this recipe is to TAKE YOUR TIME! You really have to whisk/mix the ingredients and add them slowly to avoid any clumping. Keep mixing until you have the right consistency and then add more ingredients. Add the ingredients little by little at each step. Overall, I think this mac and cheese was amazing! I usually buy the velveeta mac and cheese because I like the sauce and the taste and it USED to be my favorite mac and cheese, but this recipe takes that cake. I WILL be making this from now on. No more box mac and cheese for me!

reviews.review_text: This was a simple recipe. If you had trouble with the flour/butter part of it you probably don't know how to make a roux. Melt the butter, stir in the same amount of flour as the butter and stir, stir, stir with a whisk. It should look buttery but creamy. Let it heat through completely and then start adding the milk very slowly allowing it to thicken as you whisk in the milk until you get the creaminess and thickness you desire. Then take it off the stove and add your cheese, stirring as the cheese melts. I was making it for my granddaughters who do not like anything spicy [they are 4 and 2 years old] so I used Kraft singles and Gruyere, grated from a chunk I had. I ripped the singles into strips. It was delicious although very mild and very creamy. They loved it. If it was for a dinner or for adults I might start adding other spices but kids, I have found, like it very mild. This was certainly as quick as a box of Kraft macaroni and cheese and much tastier. I wish I had a chunk of cheddar but I didn't so the Kraft Singles were okay.

reviews.review_text: I made this for my wife exactly as written with the exception of adding just a touch of garlic salt and dry mustard; we like a little zing in our sauce. It was absolutely delicious, and better yet, a quick recipe when you're in a rush. This, a small salad and french bread made the meal. I read the reviews and don't understand the confusion, especially those who gave this recipe low ratings. If you don't know how to make a roux, learn. If it tastes like uncooked flour it probably is. That's your fault, not the recipe. And always turn the heat off or remove the pan from the stove when adding the cheese, otherwise it will come out grainy. And for goodness sake, you find a partner, man or woman, who uses a delicious plate of macaroni over leaving you, then better off for you! You're better off without him or her. My recommendation is keep the macaroni, get rid of the bum! Marie, thanks for a great recipe, my wife and I loved it!

reviews.review_text: This turned out great. I ended up turning down the heat while making my roux. I used a heavy bottomed dutch oven instead of a medium saucepan. I went the full 5 minutes on that. 1/2 tsp of salt seemed like a lot but it has to season 2 cups of milk so it was great. I added 1/4 tsp onion powder and 1/4 tsp cayenne because my family expects me to do things like that. The milk needs to be added slowly so the flour can soak it up and it does need to get hot enough to bubble to get the flour to really swell up into a smooth sauce. I think it's basically a bechamel at this point. If you can find finely shredded cheese, it will be even smoother and a jack/cheddar mix might be nicer than cheddar. Cheddar can get gritty when it melts. Make sure you don't see any shreds of cheese before you add the next batch. I did not end up with too much sauce since I used the small elbows which made tons of surface area for the sauce to cling to. Just right. Not one bit gritty or flour-y.

items.name: Crumb Topped Banana Muffins
items.description: Make and share this Crumb Topped Banana Muffins recipe from Food.com.
instructions: In a large bowl, mix the flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt.
Mix bananas, sugar, egg and melted butter.
Stir into dry mixture until thoroughly combined, then stop mixing.
Fill muffin cups 3/4 full.
Combine brown sugar, flour, and cinnamon topping ingredients.
Cut in cold butter until crumbly.
Sprinkle over muffins.
Bake at 375 degrees Fahrenheit for about 20 minutes, until muffins test done.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes.

reviews.review_text: I happened to have 6 over-ripe nanas that were begging to be used and stumbled upon this recipe. I doubled the batch, added 1 tsp vanilla extract to the wet ingredients. I also added approx 1 cup toased, chopped pecans to the batter. I filled my first 12-muffin pan and thought I should try a mini chocolate chip version as well, so I added about 1/2 of a cup of mini chippers to the remaining batter. I was in truly pathetic form last night as I mistakenly baked the muffins at 350 for the first 10 minutes.  I happened to walk past the oven and realized that I had turned it on, but hadn't upped the temp to 375. I adjusted the temp and continued to bake another 10 minutes. They turned out fine, albeit a little flat on top..totally my mistake though. They tasted great and I almost foundered myself on the FOUR I ended up eating last night. This goes into the permanent file.

Googled this recipe because I had a few bananas going to waste. I made them with pecan bits. OMNOMNOM! The crumb top is worth the price of admission! Somehow, though, it dominated the banana flavor of the muffins. I will have to experiment with it to figure out how to get both flavors to pop.

I'm NOT an experienced baker, but this seemed pretty easy to me. I did have some problem getting the topping to the right consistency initially. I gradually added a little more butter, but then I realized I had too much butter and it wasn't crumbly enough, so I added tiny bits of more flour and worked it until it came out right. Probably just needed a better tool than a fork or something. Next time I'll try using slightly softened butter for the topping rather than COLD butter.

reviews.review_text: This is a wonderful recipe! I am throwing away my recipe from Food Network! I took another reviewer's advice, and made bread loaves out of this recipe, and their suggestion was perfect - Double the recipe for three 8x4 loaf pans, baking for 45 (I had mine in for 46) minutes at 350 degrees. The bread came out PERFECT!! I used 5 large bananas (which came out to about 2 1/4 cups, mashed) when I doubled the recipe. I used canola oil for the butter and substituted Splenda for 1 cup of sugar and brown sugar for the rest (that was for a doubled recipe). I did forget to double the oil and put a second egg in there, though! :P When I doubled it, I also used a little less than 1/2 tsp. of cinnamon in the topping. The batter was very thick, and I thought the bread was going to turn out dry, but it was perfect! I also found, like another reviewer said, that it was easiest to prepare the streusel topping by crubling it up with my fingers in a little bowl before putting it on the bread loaves. I have also made this bread with no streusel topping but adding 1 1/2 cups semi-sweet chocolate chips, and it rocked! I took a loaf over to our neighbors (whom I had not yet met), and I hope they will love it as much as we do. One of my friends, whom I gave half a loaf to (because that's all we had left) was mad that he didn't get a whole one. items.label: The Most Wonderful Gingerbread Cookies
items.name: The Most Wonderful Gingerbread Cookies
items.description:
This is my very favorite gingerbread cookie recipe. The dough is so firm and nice to work with and is so wonderful smelling that it is almost like a stress reliever. These disappear in lightning speed in my house! This recipe is adapted from a recipe in the Joy of Cooking and according to the entry they only have 3 grams of fat per cookie! If you want crisp cookies roll out very thin. Thicker cookies = softer cookies, thinner cookies= crisper cookies. If the dough is too sticky, chilling should help. 

**I noticed a lot of people have been having some sticky dough issues.  You need to make sure you let the dough rest at LEAST two hours. For some reason this helps make the dough more workable. I live in FL and we have terrible humidity, but I have never had a problem with sticky dough in this recipe.
instructions: In a small bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, ginger, cinnamon, and cloves until well blended.
In a large bowl (KitchenAid's great for this) beat butter, brown sugar, and egg on medium speed until well blended.
Add molasses, vanilla, and lemon zest and continue to mix until well blended.
Gradually stir in dry ingredients until blended and smooth.
Divide dough in half and wrap each half in plastic and let stand at room temperature for at least 2 hours or up to 8 hours.
Preheat oven to 375 deg.  Prepare baking sheets by lining with parchment paper.
(Dough can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 4 days, but in this case it should be refrigerated. Return to room temp before using.) Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease or line cookie sheets with parchment paper.
Place 1 portion of the dough on a lightly floured surface.
Sprinkle flour over dough and rolling pin.
Roll dough to a scant 1/4-inch thick.
Use additional flour to avoid sticking.
Cut out cookies with desired cutter-- the ginger bread man is our favorite of course.
Space cookies 1 1/2-inches apart.
Bake 1 sheet at a time for 7-10 minutes (the lower time will give you softer cookies-- very good!).
Remove cookie sheet from oven and allow the cookies to stand until the cookies are firm enough to move to a wire rack.
After cookies are cool you may decorate them any way you like.
I usually brush them with a powdered sugar glaze when I am in a hurry, but they look wonderful decorated with Royal icing.

reviews.review_text:
I wish I could give it 5 stars for flavor (it's a strong gingery flavor which I like), but 1 star for workability, and 1 star as a cutout cookie dough recipe. Figured this averages out to 2 stars. Maybe everyone is making blob gingerbread men or snowflakes and they're happy with that but there's too much rising agent and everything got poofy; lost the detail which is a shame. Piping and decorations will fix that but was hoping that wouldn't happen.

I tried to follow the recipe as written but think I didn't measure the flour like others who didn't have sticky dough problems. I also live in Florida like the author. I was taught that flour measurements are based on sifted flour which is aerated, but for lazy folks like me you can scoop and use a knife to cut air into the flour, or you can spoon the flour into the measuring cup. Scooping, tapping especially, will compact it and you'll measure out more flour. Maybe in the US we need to start writing out recipes using weights rather than volume; that would help with consistency. Anyhow it was incredibly sticky, even chilled. I started trying to dust the dough with confectioners sugar but went to flour after a while thinking it could use more.

I also tried someone's recommendation to roll the dough between two pieces of wax paper (I only had parchment paper but that worked fine), cutout the shapes, then without touching it further transfer the rolled, cut dough on the paper onto a cookie sheet and freeze for 10 minutes. This helped but just a few thoughts which might help others if they want to try this too. If you have a narrow freezer (side-by-side) plan for it by (1) making sure your cookie sheet will fit, then (2) rolling the dough onto a piece of paper that will easily fit on the cookie sheet. I first rolled the dough out too big hoping to use my big cookie sheet, but it didn't fit in the freezer. I had to use my smallest cookie sheet and the dough kinda folded and the shapes at the fold were messed up. The extra paper also got in the way when trying to place the cookie sheet into the freezer. I then cut the paper down to fit the cookie sheet before rolling the next batch.

I also found I needed to refreeze the dough a few times because they softened too much as I worked on transferring them to a new cookie sheet for baking. Keeping the frozen cutout dough on the cold cookie sheet helped them stay cold longer, but I could only successfully get maybe 4 or 5 cookies onto my baking sheet before it softened up. Using a small angled frosting knife really helped transfer the cutout cookies.

This makes EXTREMELY tasty gingerbread cookies that, as far as cookies go, are surprisingly low on the sugar content.  Aside from never having lemons on hand to zest when making these, have made them several times & followed the recipe exactly each time with the same VERY irresistible results!<br/><br/>Notes & hints:  <br/>- For those of you like myself who do not own a KitchenAid stand mixer, a basic hand mixer works fine for combining the butter, brown sugar & egg.  (A little elbow grease will be needed to combine everything by hand at the end, but that is a small workout that can be used to justify eating one more cookie when done!)  <br/><br/>- Follow the recipe to the letter, dividing the dough in half & letting both rest at room temperature for at least 2 hours as stated.  Yes, the dough is a bit on the sticky side when all ingredients are first combined, but dividing it in half & letting it rest for a few hours allows it to dry slightly, resulting in a very workable "Play-doh"-like texture.  <br/><br/>- Unlike several other reviewers who note sticking issues, have found on every occasion so far that the dough can be easily rolled out with minimal sprinkling of flour to keep it from sticking.  (The key to this may be with allowing it to rest as noted above.)  Have also easily rolled out, cut out, then transferred shapes to a parchment paper covered baking sheets with NO need to chill anything in the freezer first.  <br/><br/>Very well done - this is sure to be a family favorite for years to come.  Thank you!!!

attributes.source_text: surprisingly low on the sugar content

reviews.review_text: I made these yesterday. I live at about sea level, didn't change a thing in the recipe, and baked them for about 7-8 minutes. the thicker cookies turned out nice and chewy at 7 1/2 minutes. The thinner ones are crunchy at the same times. For me, this gingerbread turned out perfect. Not too spicy, not too sweet or dry. I haven't even put icing or glaze on them and I think they're perfect. I feel like this could become my "go to" recipe. I almost want to make another batch and try the thinner cookies baked at 6.5 - 7 minutes. I don't want to speculate on what some people are doing wrong, but that's how it is with some people and some recipes sometimes. I want to ask them if they used softened butter or creamed the sugar butter & egg long enough, or waited the 2 hours to roll them out, or if their oven is too hot, or if they rolled them out too thin. Even the scrap pieces with all the flower mixed in during cutting them out, and then rolled out into more cookies, wasn't dry for me. People who've tried them have had the same reaction as me.... "Man that's a yummy cookie" Thanks for sharing the recipe.

reviews.review_text: This recipe is awesome. Followed the recipe to the letter, and my cookies came out lovely. People in the comments are complaining about the dough being too dry, but I spooned my flour into my measuring cup, and the dough was extremely moist. It will be sticky while trying to get it out of the mixing bowl, but letting it rest for 2 hours wrapped in plastic wrap/parchment paper/wax paper/whatever dries it out quite a bit. Rolling out the dough on a floured counter was a nightmare, so I ended up just putting down a sheet of parchment paper, flouring that, then flouring the top of my dough to roll out. That worked really well. This dough soaked up the flour insanely fast, so I'd roll it out, flour it, cut a shape, and immediately put the shape on to a greased/parchment paper lined baking sheet. That method enabled me to pick up the cut out with out it getting too sticky or warping too much. I tried rolling, and just cutting out all my shapes at once and that didn't work. They just soaked up the flour while sitting there. This is probably the best tasting gingerbread cookie recipe I've tried, and I LOVE gingerbread. It made my apartment smell amazing, and the dough was easy to work with once you had a method down.

This is a great recipe for gingerbread cookie lovers; great ginger taste (a tablespoon had me sneezing for about a minute) which is the main reason why it gets my 4 stars.  However on the second batch of cookie dough I did a little tinkering.  The first batch I followed the recipe to the letter, but I think there is an issue of word usage in the directions.  It says after adding the last bit of the dry ingredients to mix until dough is smooth.  This dough will not be smooth but more like pie crust, so make sure you mix until well incorporated.  It will be pretty much a heavy chunk of heavenly smelling dough that can easily divided to chill.  Also with as much ginger this recipe calls for, keep in mind even after baking these cookies will have a strong ginger flavor which is great for gingerbread cookie lovers like myself, but be prepared for the non-fans.  A nice coating of Royal Icing can help in this regaurd, or the traditional raisins.  My second batch I reduced the amount of flour to 2 1/2 cups, and reduced the ginger by half.  Since gingerbread is used for cut out cookies there is the risk of the dough becoming tough using the dusting of flour to keep it from sticking.  There is already quite a bit of flour in the dough itself so you will need even less flour dusting than say with sugar cookie dough, however after repeated dusting and handling, reducing the cooking time won't help having a rather hard cookie after cooling.  Using a half cup less flour there is room for dusting and handling no problem, but make sure you chill at the very least 3-4 hours and keep dough you're not using in the frige.  Reducing the amount of ginger by half gives the cookie a more mild ginger flavor which appeals to children far better as well as those finicky "big kids" who want a more sweet cookie.  Otherwise it's a great recipe for a traditional Christmas cookie making it well worth your time and love.

reviews.review_text: Excellent recipe...I used it as is: didn't sub any ingredients, didn't need extra flour. I mixed the dough, then chilled it for about an hour. I was able to roll some to about an 1/8 of an inch, and it cut beautifully. One-quarter-inch was the best recommendation (easiest to transfer from counter to baking sheets). I accidentally baked them at 350, because I had a pie in the oven, and didn't realize the oven temp was not correct. The cookies kept their shape as they baked. I used a 3.5" cutter and baked them till they were firm at the edges (9 - 11 minutes). I cooled them and gathered them together on a tray and wrapped them. They were perfectly firm and chewy the next day! I decorated them and packed them the next day, and they were perfect. The flavor was great for them, since they were for young children. If I make these for others (adults), I would add more ginger (and probably some black pepper), but, honestly, the flavor was just about perfect for these cookies. Thank you for this excellent recipe; I will absolutely be using this as my go-to gingerbread cookies recipe for next year.

reviews.review_text: This is a great recipe, people who have bad comments on it obviously screwed it up. If you follow the instructions carefully and double check measurements you will have no problems. The dough will look dry af when you work it together. If you keep stiring and pressing the dough down it will eventually combine. If it's still too dry you've obviously added too much flour. The measurements are pretty precise. What I tried was keep rotating and condensing the pieces together in a bowl until it is combined and uniform with care not to actually knead it. Let it sit for an hour or two to "soak" up the ingredients and you will be fine. Note, USE FANCY OR ORIGINAL UNSULPHERED MOLASSES. Blackstrap molasses are bitter and not as sweet. It will ruin your cookies!!! This is a fairly spicy cookie, you can tone it down by adding a bit less of each spice. I added an extra 2 Tbsp of butter to jazz it up a bit and a bit less baking soda/baking powder so it doesn't spread as much as I was trying retain the shape I cut out! Good luck!
