reviews.review_text: Delicious! The few bad reviews made me pretty hesitant to try this at first, but I thought I would give this recipe a shot anyway. I definitely made some changes though. I did not use the measurements given but instead mainly used the ingredients list as a guide. I eyeballed my amounts.. a splash here, a dash there, to make sure nothing was overly sweet/oily. I didn't want very sweet noodles so I just used maybe less than 2 TB of sugar total, and maybe 1 TB of sesame oil. For my chicken I added a splash of sesame oil, omitted the sugar entirely and marinated it for maybe 4 hours. I used a light soy sauce too so the overall flavour of the dish was lighter and the chicken didn't burn on the stove. After cooking the chicken, I sauteed some zucchini and added some red pepper flakes for some heat. I also toasted the sesame seeds and added those at the end. Everything turned out GREAT in the end! A very pretty and tasty dish and it was so easy to put together. Thank you!

reviews.review_text: OMG! This is SO good! My family of 4 gobbled it up and I was really disappointed there was no leftovers! I followed the recipe exactly except I cut up the chicken and marinated it for 1 1/2 hours. Also, when you're mixing the sauce into the noodles, definitely use the whole amount. I almost cut back on it because it looked like it would be too much, but the noodles absorb the sauce giving the noodles more flavor. I had all the ingredients on hand and it was easy to make. The best part is how versatile this recipe is. It can be served hot, cold or warm so it's a year round recipe. It can also be changed up by adding chopped peanuts, veggies (broccolini would be really good with this) or some chili sauce. Like other reviewers have said, if you don't like sesame, then you will not like this diah. Thanks for sharing this! We will definetely be making this again!

reviews.review_text: This is an OUTSTANDING dish!! I love sesame! I am writing this as I eat and I hope I dont choke because I am the only one here..lol. Really though this has loads of flavor. I pretty much followed the recipe aside from using a sesame salad dressing instead of the sesame oil in the sesame noodles which cut down on the oily. I am waiting on my 10 year old son and his step sister to come in for supper to see their reaction to this recipe but no matter if they dont like it the more for me..lol. I also made some steamed broccoli to have either mixed in or on the side.. Too bad my boyfriend isnt here he is missing out on a great meal, and he loves loves loves chinese food! Oh well you snooze you lose, I guess...I will have to save him some! This does make a ton of pasta for the amount of chicken, but I could eat just the pasta by istelf, the next day for lunch or even a light dinner. Thank you Mirj for a easy and delicious recipe!

reviews.review_text: I made this after work for our dinner so I didn't have time to let the chicken breasts marinade for hours.  I sliced the raw chicken into thin strips for a faster marinade and marinaded them for about 45 minutes.  The smaller chicken pieces with a shorter marinade time worked well.  It was a quick meal to prepare. The recipe is well written and easy to follow.  Personally, I thought the meal was pretty good.  Not great, but not bad and would have given it four stars.  However, the other family members did not like the noodles at all.  They liked the chicken, but just couldn't eat the noodles.  When I asked them why, one said they were too sweet and another said he didn't like the taste of the sesame oil and he hated the seeds in it because they caught in his teeth and gums.  I guess I will not be making it again so that makes it a 3 star recipe.

reviews.review_text: Very flavorful and a nice break from the usual chicken dishes. For the sesame noodles, I used less than 1/4 cup sesame oil but the sesame flavor still came through a bit strong. (But then again, we're not sesame oil fans.) I cut down the sugar a bit, as well -- but the noodles were still a little too sweet for my tastes. The chicken was excellent, however ... complex flavors, rich and delicious! Due to time constraints, I didn't marinate but repeatedly basted the chicken with the sauce -- I didn't want to waste a drop! The sauce thickened and carmelized and made the chicken absolutely delicious. I used powdered ginger and added a few tablespoons of hoisin sauce since I had no teriyaki sauce. Next time I think I'll serve this chicken with jasmine rice instead of the noodles. Would have rated this 5 stars if we had liked the sesame noodles more ... still, an excellent recipe!

reviews.review_text: ****Rating is for noodles alone, with modifications***** First, I think it is very important to use low sodium soy sauce, second, reduce both the sugar & the sesame oil by at least half (that would be 1/8 c., maximum of sesame oil). Since I didn't make chicken in the recipe (made breaded, baked chicken breast tenders instead), I added some ground ginger & garlic powder with just a pinch of cayenne pepper to my sauce. items.label: MaMa's Supper Club Tilapia Parmesan
items.name: MaMa's Supper Club Tilapia Parmesan
items.description: Make and share this MaMa's Supper Club Tilapia Parmesan recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
In buttered 13-by-9-inch baking dish or jellyroll pan, lay fillets in single layer.
Do not stack fillets.
Brush top with juice.
In bowl combine cheese, butter, mayonnaise, onions and seasonings.
Mix well with fork.
Bake fish in preheated oven 10 to 20 minutes or until fish just starts to flake.
Spread with cheese mixture and bake until golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Baking time will depend on the thickness of the fish you use.
Watch fish closely so that it does not overcook.
Makes 4 servings.
Note: This fish can also be made in a broiler.
Broil 3 to 4 minutes or until almost done.
Add cheese and broil another 2 to 3 minutes or until browned.
Thank you Mama's Supper Club in Wisconsin.

reviews.review_text: I'm not a fan of fish, but my husband is. I made this today, for his birthday. We couldn't afford to go out to eat like I wanted, so I decided to make something myself. I went in search for a restaurant quality recipe for his meal. Since I had tilapia, I looked it up under ingredients.. Then, always click on the most favorite ones. This was the first one I found. I tried it out, and my husband LOVED it! I accidently added he lemon juice to the mixture, which ended up being just fine. I used frozen individually wrapped tilapia fillets. I was worried that they wouldn't cook right because they were frozen, but they did just fine. 20 mins or so. Then, when I made the mixture, I didn't think it was enough, so I doubled it. Yeah.. too much! So, I put it all on top and cooked it the 2nd time for around 20 minutes. I got impatient and broiled it the last 3 minutes because I was excited to feed it to my husband. I also dried my own green onions, and they worked just fine.. He loved it, and wants me to make it again. Its a good thing I made as much as I did. :)  Thanks for sharing!

reviews.review_text: Mama's Supper Club, Minocqua, WI, has been a staple in my life for 30+ years.  When I introduced the place to DBF a few years ago he is now a steady customer too, and recently ordered this off the menu.  He was surprised, pleasantly when he came home to THIS on the table.  It is very similar to the original!  I only used 1 pound of tilapia (I personally hate fish) but had 6 nice fillets.  I made the sauce as directed and used it all on the fish I had.  I was easy to put together while the fish was baking, mine took 15 minutes, then I also broiled the topping to get it slightly crispy as it is at the resturant.  I also used lite mayo and he didnt even know the difference!  I served with Dill roasted red potatoes, steamed broccoli and homemade bread....DBF ate ALL the fish and was scraping the remaining sauce from the pan with his bread.  He requested this one again...soon and rates it OFF THE CHART!  Its a good thing that when we go to Wisconsin I have to cook on a campfire cause Im afraid I would be having to cook this instead of getting to actually go to Mama's!  Thanks Crabbycakes for this one!!!!

attributes.source_text: DBF ate ALL the fish and was scraping the remaining sauce from the pan with his bread

reviews.review_text: Tasted pretty good, but will definitely have to try substituting the mayo w/greek yogurt next time and maybe swapping butter for coconut spread (a healthier fat) to save on some fat & calories. I only had 4-4 oz filets but used all of the mixture, so there was a good amount of butter in the pan when done baking. I didn't have lemon juice, only lime - so I used that, plus no green onions so added a 1/2 tsp of onion powder. I also used parmesan from a shaker container, but would like to try the grated parmesan in the pouches from the dairy aisle. As many other users mentioned, I did not get the golden browning I was looking for by baking alone, so I put mine under the broiler for 4 minutes until it bubbled up nicely. A very filling dish with good flavor.

This was my first attempt at cooking fish, and it turned out very well. It was very easy to make, and I had most of the topping ingredients already on hand. I also had trouble getting the topping to brown as someone else mentioned. I had to broil it an additional 2 minutes which browned it slightly, but I was also afraid of overcooking it, so I didn't cook it any longer. I also had trouble with the topping sort of sliding off the fish. We just slid it right back on, which didn't alter the flavor. My husband really enjoyed this, and said it was "restaurant quality" fish. Even my 4 year old who has never eaten much fish liked it. Despite my "browning" problems, we will definitely make this again. Thanks for sharing.

attributes.source_text: My husband really enjoyed this
Even my 4 year old who has never eaten much fish liked it

reviews.review_text:
Three stars for a well-written and successful recipe. I followed the ingredients and the directions exactly and the results were perfectly cooked. The only thing I had to add was a little bit of broiling to brown the top. I really should have taken a picture because it was a beautiful dish. However, the taste just wasn't to our liking. A few thoughts:

**Way too much butter - it could have been cut out completely because the fat in the mayo was plenty.

**Overpowering flavor - simply couldn't taste the fish. Which might be great if you wanted to cover up the taste of fish. In that case, save your money and use this over chicken.

**Maybe tilapia isn't the best fish for this dish. Our selection of tilapia is very thin and I actually overlapped a few of the pieces to make 'normal' filets. But the taste of tilapia is very delicate and didn't stand up to topping. Perhaps a fish with stronger flavor would work better in this recipe.

Thanks for a great recipe but it just wasn't for us.

This was a fabulous dish and I can't believe I hadn't tried it sooner. It got rave reviews from everyone, including our 7 year old that "hates fish." I agree with kadusey that it was just a bit too salty for me but I think it's because I used Tony Chachere's Creole Seasoning which is somewhat salty and my butter also had salt in it. I think next time I will use unsalted butter to compensate for the seasoning. When I cooked it, I screwed up and put the topping on the fish when I first put it in the oven but it turned out well. I baked it for 10 minutes and then hit it with the broiler for 7 minutes and it was very nicely browned when it was done. I wanted to take a picture but after my first bite, I devoured it before I remembered to get the camera. Thanks so much for posting! I'm sure this will be made quite a few more times.

attributes.source_text: including our 7 year old that "hates fish."

reviews.review_text:
This was a great recipe! I really enjoyed it last night and it went great with baked potatoes. I had to cut the recipe in half because I had less fish but the baking time still worked because of their thickness. I also used less butter, less mayo, and less onion (1 T each). I also used yellow onion instead of green onion which I liked better. I also added lemon zest in addition to the lemon juice which helped create a more lemony flavor which my family and I enjoyed. One thing I may experiment with next time is using shredded Parmesan instead of grated Parmesan. This could give it a richer, cheesier, and meltier flavor. I think that I didn't need to cut the recipe in half because then I could have covered my fish even more. The one weird thing was that my Tilapia topping didn't turn out quite as brown and even which could mean that it needed more than 5 minutes.
UPDATE 5/23: I have found the perfect combination: 3 T of unsalted butter plus the normal amount of everything else. Then bake the Tilapia for 15 min then broil it for 10 with the cheese. Finally I let it just stay warm in the oven for a few minutes before serving. This makes the cheese brown nicely, while cooking the Tilapia a little more.

attributes.source_text: helped create a more lemony flavor which my family and I enjoyed
which my family and I enjoyed

reviews.review_text: SOOOO delicious! I thought I had frozen Tilapia at home but it was catfish so I used that. Had to leave out the green onions so used about 1/2 teaspoon of onion powder instead. The fish was beautiful when it came out of the oven and tasted like it looked. I eventually convinced my 7-1/2 year old grandson who said "I don't like FISH" to take a bite and as I put it in his mouth he said "yuk....YUM!!!" and ate about 1/2 of mine even though he'd already had his dinner. My 3 year old twin granddaughters also loved it! I really could have eaten the topping with a spoon but for sure I will use this recipe over and over!! UPDATE: Made this with Tilapia and it is super good! For the seasoning salt I used a bit of Cajun seasoning.

attributes.source_text: my 7-1/2 year old grandson who said "I don't like FISH" to take a bite and as I put it in his mouth he said "yuk....YUM!!!"

reviews.review_text: Just what this recipe needs, another glowing review. But we loved this. Tilapia is not readily available fresh in Alaska so I used frozen filets. I increased the temperature (400Â°) and adjusted the cooking time accordingly. It turned out wonderful. I did not have any green onions and so I minced up some vidalia. I also used fresh lemon juice and  Old Bay's Lemon & Herb seasoning. Otherwise I followed the recipe exactly. I think next time I will add some capers. As I was eating it I kept thinking how good it would be with some capers. A wonderful new way to prepare this yummy fish.

Before the first bite was even swallowed, my husband mumbled, "wow"...then, between bites, "make this one again!" He reiterated 3 more times before finishing his meal, just to be sure I understood how much he loved this.  We halved the recipe, since the store was low on tilapia, and added a couple extra dashes of hot pepper sauce, to give it a bit more of a kick. 
Update: Have made this again and again for us and for company and still love it.  We now use just half the butter (and use butter substitute) and use fat free mayo.  We also leave out the seasoned salt, as the parm is plenty salty for us.  With these changes, the sauce doesn't "firm up" quite as well, but the flavor is still excellent.
Thanks again!

I made this with only 2 mahi-mahi filets that were the equivalent of 1/2 lb of fish.  I didn't think to reduce the recipe, so I had a lot of sauce!  

My sauce was soupy and wasn't really "spreadable".  I'm not quite sure what I did wrong except maybe use too much lemon juice on the fish (the extra rolled off to the bottom of the baking dish) or maybe it was that I tried to room-soften the butter in the micro and melted half of it.  Either way it was great-tasting and my roomie loved it!  

Also, I subbed half of the mayo with Arby's Horsey Sauce since I had a bunch of leftover packets sitting around.  It gave a nice tang to the sauce.

reviews.review_text: Wow very good! I recently just moved in with my fiancé and I have been learning how to cook on my own. This dish was so simple and fun to make! I am a very inexperienced cook and this wasn't difficult at all. I used onion powder and garlic powder instead of green onions and seasoned salt. I let the fish broil a little at the end too. It browned perfectly and the sauce cooked perfectly on the tilapia it barely melted off! My fiancé absolutely loved it and is starting to enjoy my cooking! He aw saying mmmmm with each bite and said it tasted like something out of a restaurant. Will definitely be making thi again. Thank you!!!

attributes.source_text: My fiancé absolutely loved it

reviews.review_text: This was absolutely delicious!! Even after baking, I could taste the lemon juice on the fish. I omitted the hot sauce, and also the green onions since I didn't have any. I used garlic salt instead of the seasoning salt because I didn't have any. The topping was delicious (you can't go wrong with butter and cheese) and the fish was so tender. I actually liked that the parmesan wasn't overwhelming, nor does it crust the entire fish. I baked this at 400 degrees in a convection oven for about 10-12 minutes before adding the topping, and then afterward maybe 5 minutes. I will definitely be making this again!

attributes.source_text: I could taste the lemon juice on the fish
the fish was so tender

reviews.review_text:
This was really, really good! I made it just as written, but I think I will cut back on the Old Bay next time, it was a little too salty. The kids didn't love it (due to the saltiness), but DH and I ate it up. Also make sure you spread the mixture smoothly over the fish. Definitely will go in the seafood file. Thanks!
Had to update this for one thing! Three days after this meal, I spread some leftover cheese spread on an onion bagel, stuck it under the broiler until brown, and had one of the best snacks in a long time! Thanks double now! We will be making the cheese spread separately just to spread!

attributes.source_text: DH and I ate it up

reviews.review_text: This has become a staple recipe in my house, for lunch or dinner. It satisfies my low carb quest, and my fish hating family just loves it. I do put it under the broiler after I put the cheese mixture on the fish, It kind of helps to set the mixture and gives it a complex flavor. and I always double the cheese mixture-- I like it cheesey. In addition, I use the season salt on the fish, as well as the lemon juice. For my non- low carbing family I serve this with rice pilaf and steamed carrots, or roasted brussel sprouts. I skip the rice and eat broccoli or brussel sprouts.

reviews.review_text: I'll start by saying I don't normally like fish... but I want to like fish and try new recipes from time to time, hoping.  I liked this enough to eat two fillets which is a big deal for me!  :)  I was a little dissapointed it didn't brown up... but I'll experiment with my oven and hope to get that to work.  I also would like it to be a bit healthier and hope that I can reduce the butter/mayonnaise some or make some substitutions... it looks like other reviewers have done so successfully.  I also think a little breadcrumbs mixed in would be nice so I'll try that.  But, again... I liked it!  I even liked it as leftovers which surprised me.   Thank you!  :)

This was great! kids loved it, sister, wife, everyone loved it! It did come out saltier than I expected, but I think that had to do with the romano cheese mixed in with the parmesan. I didn't have straight parm, so i subbed. Didn't have green onions either, so I used some onion powder to give the taste. I also doubled the cheese mixture, but I ran out of mayo, and subbed 2 tbsp. with sour cream. Lol...a lot of subs, sorry, but it was great. next time I will make sure to have green onions, plenty of mayo, and straight parm. This is a definite "monthly rotation" recipe.

items.label: Impossible Peanut Butter Cookies
items.name: Impossible Peanut Butter Cookies
items.description: These are the quickest, simplest peanut butter cookies that you will ever make and they taste great!
instructions: Mix peanut butter, sugar, and egg together until smooth.
Drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheet two inches apart. If desired, roll in extra sugar before placing on cookie sheet.
Press with fork; press again in opposite direction.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
Do not brown; do not over bake.

reviews.review_text: I have 3 favorite cookies and this is one of them! You can't get any more simple than this! I always take the other reviews to hart...so I also added the vanilla and made sure to squish them down enough.. After making these, I believe the other people's that turned out "crumbly" were possibly due to the following reasons: 1.They made the cookies too big.  2. They did not let them cool all the way. 3. The correct temperature for these cookies is a bit less than 350 as stated in the recipe.  These reasons are from personal experience. The cookies that were bigger than 2" diameter, fell apart. The ones I couldn't resist trying before they were cool, also fell apart and my oven only has a range 160-180 deg. C which is 320-356 deg F. However, the cookies that were exactly 2" diameter, cooled all the way (on marble) were the ABSOLUTE BEST pb cookies EVER! ....oh, and also since I always hated trying to get all the pb out of the measurer I coated the cup with veg.oil so it would just slide right out (also as not to waste any because pb here in South America costs $10 for 10 oz.jar!) ...OH! what you will pay to taste that memory again!

At first, I was extremely skeptical of this recipe.. but now I understand why everyone's giving it good ratings! The cookies came out really good and chewy! I followed the recipe, but I also added a few drops of vanilla. To make things less messier, I put the cook dough into a Ziploc sandwich baggie and chilled that down for a few hours. (It made rolling them out into even little balls WAY simpler)  I made this recipe twice: once in my regular oven and another time in my NuWave oven. ***Tip: REALLY FLATTEN YOUR COOKIES OUT EVENLY! THEY DO NOT AUTOMATICALLY FLATTEN THEMSELVES WHILE BAKING!*** They all came out really good. Although, I suggest letting the cookies cool down for about 5  minutes (or they WILL crumble) before transferring to a cooling rack... or eating them immediately!

attributes.source_text: The cookies came out really good and chewy!

reviews.review_text: I purposely did not put any stars on my review yet.  I'm undecided at this point.  The dough was VERY crumbly and hard to work with. I'm curious if anyone else had that issue.  I did mix up the dough and put it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes hoping that it would stick together better but it didn't.  Very messy to make into balls; I did not roll them in any extra sugar and they kept falling apart.  Hoped for the best...baked them for 12 minutes as suggested. I allowed them to remain on the cookie sheet for about 10 minutes before removing them to a cooling rack.  They smell good....taste? I don't know yet.  I'm going to bring them to work and see what the girls think.  I will update my review later.  Please let me know if anyone else had this issue about the dough not holding together. UPDATE:  Added 3 stars as the taste was very well received....

I really liked these because they were so easy and quick after spending hours cooking the main dish I made tonight. I will definitely make them again because they are just such a quick and tasty dessert to make up at the last moment. I might make the one with flour if I have a lot more time though but definitely will make this one when I need something easy and quick. I added 1/2 a teaspoon of vanilla essence to mine and rolled them in brown sugar. I think by doing that I increased the sugar a lot and they turned more toffee like than peanut butter cookie like but my husband liked them like that. To make them more cookie like I think it would be best to reduce the sugar a bit and not over cook them so they stay soft. I don't think its necessary to press them down too much because they spread out and expand during cooking anyway.

attributes.source_text: such a quick and tasty dessert
my husband liked them like that
they turned more toffee like than peanut butter cookie like

reviews.review_text:
Strawberryjane, you are a godsend!  I've been searching for *real* cookies that didn't have flour, and this did the trick perfectly.  These are very good, a little bite will tide you over.
I made mine small (got a full  two dozen), so I reduced the time by a minute.  Some of the first batch were a little too brown, so I doubled up the pans for the second batch.  These ones seem a little light now, I hope they are cooked.  I think for my oven, the trick is to double the pan, and cook for the full 10 minutes, and they will be beyond perfect.  I also stuck mini m&ms in half of them, to use up the halloween candy.

Hey Mysterygirl, these cookies were very good!  I did however, use 1/2 cup of chunky peanut butter, and 1/2 creamy peanut butter, plus I added 1 teaspoon vanilla extract to the recipe. I actually whipped up the cookie dough in the morning, then baked the cookies later in the evening, which the dough held together nicely. I used a small Pampered Chef Scoop, which is equal to 1-tablespoon, to help round out the cookies. I baked the cookies on a Pampered Chef Baking Stone for excatly 12 minutes, then let them set on the baking stone for 5 minutes before removing them to a wire rack to cool. I found I got 28 (2-inch) cookies form this recipe. I couldn't believe how good these cookies turned out, as I was a skeptic at first, and wondered how one could make cookies with out adding flour to the mix. Well, I'm no longer a skeptic, and 'am glad I tried making these flourless cookies, as they were very good, but I would definitely chill the cookie dough for several hours before baking them. One more thing, I did take another viewers advice about rolling some of the cookies in brown sugar before baking them, as they stated it gave the cookies a toffee taste to them. I baked half the cookies that way, but felt the cookie lost the peanut butter taste in the process. My husband and I prefered the cookies with out rolling them in any sugar, and since I chilled the cookie dough for most of the day, applying a criss-cross pattern to the top of the cookie with a fork, was easy and I had no problems with that. Thank you Mysterygirl, for posting this recipe. It definitely is a keeper!

attributes.source_text: felt the cookie lost the peanut butter taste
My husband and I prefered the cookies with out rolling them in any sugar

reviews.review_text: Well Eric I am writing this for my neighbor. He's a small 3 year old boy that lives next door to me and likes to help mom around the kitchen. When I ask him if he wanted to try to make some he shook his head yes and mom dug out the stuff and he and I (mostly him) made a batch. We also added a piece of chocolate to each one after cooking and let them cool as you suggested. (That cooling was hard for a three year old). To make a long story short...he had a cookie in each hand and was chewing on another one when I asked him if it was a 5 spot. He just kept eating shaking his head yes. LOL. So it's a 5 star from little Zack...and he wants to make some more. Good job Eric and thank you. From Zack and Chuck

he had a cookie in each hand and was chewing on another one
he wants to make some more

reviews.review_text:
These cookies are so amazing! I made them one night just because I had a craving for peanut butter cookies, but I was low on ingredients and I couldn't find my recipe for peanut butter cookies. I looked this up and thought, great a quick easy recipe. 

They do come out of the oven a bit softer than I thought, but they solidify beautifully. They taste amazing, seriously the best peanut butter cookies I've ever had. One batch makes about 18 cookies, I use a small melon baller to scoop them out. They were gone in about 15 minutes. My family loves them, and they're rather picky. My sister has a gluten intolerance, and these don't affect it at all.

I made a triple batch last night, 63 cookies, they are gone!!! They get inhaled. I'm never using another cookie recipe again. I wasn't sure how these would turn out, I'm so shocked at how much I love these cookies. Prepare to ruin any other recipe you've tried.

attributes.source_text: They do come out of the oven a bit softer than I thought
My family loves them

reviews.review_text: I couldn't keep my hands off these while they were cooling! Glad it only took about 10 minutes for a perfect finish. Because I have IBS, I used 1/4 cup of Eggbeaters, which equals 1 large egg, and this seemed to work out great. I used my fave pb, Jif Creamy and the amt of sugar called for. My mom used to also flatten her pb cookies with a fork dipped in granulated sugar, or a flat bottom of a glass dipped in granulated sugar. I should have refrigerated the dough for a few minutes as another reviewer had done, as the dough was super sticky and even with the sugar, a fork wasn't working well to flatten b/c the dough kept sticking to it. No biggie, I just used my fingertips this time. The time, oven temp and ratio of ingredients are PERFECT. I am always looking for simple recipes and this included stuff almost everyone has on hand. They turned out peanut-buttery with just the right amount of sweetness. Now, if I can keep from eating ALL of them before bf gets home from work, I can find out if he likes them, too (he loves pb cookies, but he gets store-bought ones most of the time, which I think are kind of dry). These are moist, cooked well, with a little bit of crisp on the outside. For me, this made 15 medium-large size cookies. I will write back and let ya know how bf liked them. Oops, got cookie crumbs in the keyboard...  Oops, almsot forgot to updsate.  My bf said they were good (I swear I have to yank his teeth to get any opinion from him about anything).  My roomie also said they were really good and her and I have almost finished the plate ourselves.  A great way to get a peanut butter fix.

reviews.review_text: I chose only easy recipes for my holiday baking because my time was limited but I really wanted to get some baking done.  This recipe did not disappoint!  Seriously, three ingredients, 12 minutes in the oven, cool, have a nice peanut-buttery day.  ;)  I would hold this cookie up against other peanut butter cookies that require a lot more time, work and effort.  If you like peanut butter cookies because you like peanut butter, this is quick and easy.  (PS: I used a small tablespoon 'ice cream' scoop and this was as un-messy as I think you could ever get with a sticky peanut butter recipe!)  Awesome! Thank you so much!

attributes.source_text: have a nice peanut-buttery day

reviews.review_text: I am amazed!  Making these right now and they turned out perfect.  Who would know there is no flour???  I am gluten-intolerant and have been wishing I could eat some cookies.  These are great.  Made them just as suggested and added about 1/2 tsp. vanilla.  Batter is perfect, cookies are delicious.  I didn't roll them in sugar, and let them cool on the baking stone for 5 minutes before removing.  Next time I will try using half Splenda half sugar as suggested by another reviewer.  These are sweet enough for me without rolling them in sugar first.  Reading some of the other reviews first was very helpful.

attributes.source_text: These are sweet enough for me

reviews.review_text: I've made these cookies several times because they're just so simple! 3 ingredients! But that was when I first started baking and I liked quick and easy. Now I like more of a challenge. But either way, why make any other complicating peanut butter recipes when you've got the perfect cookie right here? These are awesome peanut butter cookies and super easy to make. Great for beginners. Nice and chewy. Oh, almost forgot to mention, I always use just half a cup of sugar, and I bake them just a little longer. I got the recipe from the back of the KRAFT peanut butter jar ;)

attributes.source_text: Nice and chewy

reviews.review_text: Sorry, this didn't work out for us at all!  I did use natural peanut butter, so maybe that's why they didn't work.  The recipe seems to suggest that any kind of peanut butter would work, but Smucker's natural PB doesn't work at all!  I expect PB cookies to be a little crumbly in texture, but these could barely be picked up without crumbling to bits.  They tasted okay, but they weren't as good as PB cookies made from other recipes that I've tried.  This was the first time I've used a PB cookie recipe with so few ingredients, though.  I'm glad I tried them, but I wouldn't make them again.

I'm old school and honestly, I was very reluctant to try a flourless cookie recipe. Guess what? Broke people take chances. Tomorrow's payday, but kids don't comprehend that. They want delicious cookies NOW. So I tried the recipe. WOW. Flavorful, wonderful, easy and quick. Do what they others have recommended and reduce to a little under 3/4C white sugar. You don't need brown sugar, believe it or not. I used a little under 1/2 tsp. *real* vanilla extract. That's just how I roll. Give it a try. Thanks for this great version of peanut butter cookies, 5 stars-- would bake again!

I made these cookies this morning. Seemed easy enough. I used Jif creamy peanut butter and white sugar.. one large egg. I couldn't 'drop' onto cookie sheet. The mixture was just too crumbly. I had to squish it into my palms into a greasy little disk.. then I pressed into white sugar.. pressed with fork and baked. Maybe another egg would have helped.. not sure.
I got 17 cookies out of the mixture. The cookies are very delicate and crumbly.

UPDATED the very same day. I had to give it one more star because people said they tasted good and one lady wanted the recipe.

This recipe is AMAZING!!!! I absolutely loath dry,hard peanut butter cookies. One day my daughter and I were craving something sweet and I was feeling pretty lazy so I thought I'd give this simple recipe a try. I admit I wasn't expecting much at all.
These make the best soft peanut buttery peanut butter cookies you could ever hope for. The only negative (which really isn't) is that these are so simple we've made them about six times in the last few days. You can whip these up in just a couple of minutes and be stuffing your face with them in no time. This is one of my best recipe finds ever!!!

That is when I came upon this one.  This is a great cookie I just made some about 15 mins ago and my mother and I loved them. She told me that i think you have found a new cookie for christmas. items.label: Chicken Parmesan
items.name: Chicken Parmesan
items.description: Make and share this Chicken Parmesan recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Pound chicken to flatten.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Dip chicken in egg; then in bread crumbs.
Fry in butter in hot skillet, turning and browning for 10 minutes or until chicken is done.
Remove from skillet.
To skillet add spaghetti sauce.
Heat thoroughly.
Add chicken.
Place slices of mozzarella on top of chicken.
Sprinkle with parmesan.
Cover and cook until cheese is melted.
Serve with a side of spaghetti. Optional, garnish with chopped parsley and more parmesan cheese.

reviews.review_text: Wow! Not only was it cheap and incredibly easy to make, but it tastes just as good as the chicken parmesan you get at the restaurant. I will definitely make this again. I just cooked for myself today, but I think it would be a great meal to serve to dinner guests. I served this with angel hair pasta, but next time I might buy some good sandwich rolls and make chicken parmesan sandwiches. Also, I like to add a pinch of cinnamon on top of the melted cheese. I know it sounds weird, but I got the idea from a diner I used to go to; they would add cinnamon to their chicken parmesan sandwiches. I was somewhat nervous about making this recipe because I've never flattened chicken breasts before, but it was SO easy that now I feel silly for ever worrying about it! I flattened the chicken in the same ziploc freezer bag that I defrosted it in, but I didn't seal the bag because I figured the air trapped inside might have made the bag pop. Anyways, it worked great and didn't make a mess at all. Thanks for sharing this wonderful recipe.

Yummy! 
I also made some changes, I pounded the chicken only slightly, I fryed them until they were ALMOST done...leaving a little raw in the middle...I then sliced them lenght wise and tucked a piece of mozz. cheese in there, placed them in my glass pan, covered them well in a good sauce and then topped them each with another piece of mozz. cheese...some parm. and then fresh ground pepper and salt...baked at 350 long enough to also bake my yummy french cheese bread and ate...even my 2 year old ate this dish and she HATES chicken!! It was great thank you thank you thank you for this yummy addition to our family recipe's.

attributes.source_text: even my 2 year old ate this dish

reviews.review_text: Made this last night and was so happy I did!  I've never made or even eaten Chicken Parm, so wasn't sure how it would taste.  But it was delicious.  Instead of Italian breadcrumbs, I used a mix of Panko and freshly grated Parm with some Italian seasoning.  Also I dredged the cutlets in flour before dipping in egg.  Then once the chicken was browned on both sides, I put them on a foil lined sheet, spooned on jarred spaghetti sauce, a couple nice big basil leaves, the sliced fresh mozzarella, and then more freshly grated parm.  Then I put them under the broiler til the cheeses got super melty and gooey.  OMG, soooooo good!  I'll make this again and again.

attributes.source_text: the cheeses got super melty
super melty and gooey

reviews.review_text: Not that this recipe needed another 5 stars, :-) This was sooooooooo very good and super EASY!  I have a recipe for Chicken Parmesan as well, but it includes making the sauce from scratch and takes a bit of time, being that I no longer have time to just spend all day in the kitchen this was awesome!  I did make a few changes so that it can be wheat free gluten free and it still tasted great.  I used brown rice pasta, a big can of crushed tomatoes, and because I had some fresh mushrooms, diced peppers, onions, and fresh garlic I had to use up I added those by eyeballing them and satueed them before adding the crushed tomatoes. I also added 1/4 cup red wine towards the end of cooking the veggies to let it simmer for a few minutes.  I found some fresh motzerella cheese and can not believe how much of a difference it makes to use that vs a pre-shredded or block of that stuff is.  Super YUM!  This is soooooo good.

This was YUMMY.  
Must mention, though...I was trying DILIGENTLY to keep the calories low and I was sure I could do better than what was listed and when I figured my Nutrition Facts I came up with 609 calories and 25g of fat per serving! Maybe it was because of my spaghetti sauce...I'm just not sure.  I only mention it because some of us trace and track every morsel of food and this one might need to be figured individually. Then I removed them and kept them warm, and added the sauce to the skillet for a bit. I sliced the chicken into strips and served over small Penne with a little sauce and sprinkled with the parmesan (didn't have the mozzarella.) Served with a green salad and it was that easy! Took no more time than usual and produced such a lovely meal! Thank you!

items.label: Why-I-Joined-Zaar Carrot Cake
items.name: Why-I-Joined-Zaar Carrot Cake
items.description: On October 2, 2001, I discovered the Recipezaar Web site. I immediately joined so I could post a request for a recipe I had lost. In less than an hour, I had a reply: this recipe. Unfortunately, I never posted it into the database -- until now. My mistake. This cake was the reason I joined, and the friendly response I received was the reason I stayed!
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 9x13 inch pan.
Mix flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and cinnamon; make a well in the center and add sugar, oil, eggs and vanilla. Mix with wooden spoon until smooth.
Stir in carrots, coconut, walnuts and pineapple. Pour into 9x13 inch pan and bake for about 45 minutes. Don't panic, the centre will sink a little.

Allow to cool; when cool, ice the cake. You can certainly use your favourite cream cheese frosting to ice this cake, but the one I've included is highly recommended (I usually leave the cake in the 13x9 pan and just ice the top).
To make the frosting: Cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth; add the icing sugar and beat until creamy.

reviews.review_text: Looking for a delicious cake recipe and came across this one.  It looked like a carrot cake recipe I had clipped from a magazine many years ago, so I thought I'd check to see how it was different.  I discovered it was the same recipe (although the frosting uses only 3 oz. of cream cheese), but noticed the directions were a little more specific for the cake.  My recipe says to use sifted flour and then, before adding wet ingredients, says to sift flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and cinnamon into a large bowl.  Thought I would mention it as I think this helps to assure all of the dry ingredients are mixed thoroughly.  Additional comment (next day):  Another change, I think that makes the directions clearer is to use sifted confectioner's sugar (called Icing sugar in the recipe) and also add 1/2 teaspoon vanilla.  It made a nice creamy easy-to-use frosting.  I made my cake in two 9-inch round pans (baked for 40 minutes) and had plenty of frosting (using the 8 oz. package of light cream cheese) to frost both layers.

I just finished baking this cake and icing it.  I made this one today per my daughter's request. She informs me yesterday that she "loves carrot cake" so I decided to surprise her.  I uploaded 3 pictures - the first picture is of the plain cake just to show you that it did not sink in the middle and the other two are of the finished product.  I used a 9 x 13 inch pan and the size is just perfect. 45 minutes was the exact baking time too.  The icing recipe that is included with this cake worked out to be just the right amount also.  I only iced the top of the 9 x 13 inch cake. The only little change I did was to add a little bit of vanilla extract to the icing.  That's it! Otherwise, I followed this recipe exactly.  I can't wait to hear what my daughter thinks when she tries it.  I will update my review after I get her opinion.  Thanks for sharing this wonderful recipe!  Oh yeah, Lennie, let me know if this recipe would work for cupcakes too.  As I mentioned, portion control seems to be a household issue.  Thank again and take care.

Lennie, You should be ashamed of yourself for posting this recipe! If somebody doesn't intervene I'm going to eat this entire cake myself. I am reminded of the scene from Sex and the City where Miranda Hobbes calls Carrie and says "You'll probably need this information when you check me into the Betty Crocker Clinic."  Seriously, I never remember having made any cake from scratch, the boxed mixes are just too convenient and easy. I wanted to make something special for my husbands birthday. He is pretty fussy about his favorite cake, and finds most recipes too sweet for his liking. So I was a little concerned about all the sugar, between the cake and then the frosting. Thought I would cut some of the sugar from the frosting, but the other recipes I found actually contained more sugar. In the end, I followed your recipe EXACTLY. I will never make this cake again ... without inviting more guests to help us eat it. Having something that tasty sitting in my fridge is a lesson in self discipline. It is SO delicious!!

reviews.review_text:
Wow! I had no idea that I would love any cake so much, and that even with no chocolate in it!

Had it after thanksgiving dinner, and even though everyone was more than stuffed, they all had to have a piece!
Truely a quite simple, but extremely delicious cake!

I made it in two 8" square pans, and baked it for good 40 minutes.

For the frosting, I mixed the softened cream cream and butter together first and then slowly sifted in powdered sugar. Doing so I had a glaze like topping that then I gave a touch of orange zest to. To smooth it out I pur?ed it with my hand blender until smooth.
I then put the glaze between layers and on top.
I kept the coating quite thin, which was a good idea as this gave it a sweet touch with the hint of orange but without over powering due to excessive frosting! Which rounded up a perfect cake!

This recipie will definitaly be made now more than once a year! Many thanks!

Does this recipe REALLY need a 300th review?  YES!  It's THAT good!
I've had this in my cookbook  forever, and why I'm just now getting around to it, I don't know.  But I'm sooo glad I did, this is incredible!  I did cut the oil with applesauce (3/4 c applesauce, 1/4 oil), used only one cup of sugar, and some frozen sliced carrots that someone had given us.  I tossed those int he food processor and added them in.  The pineapple didn't get drained, thanks to my overeager little helpers,s o the cake was 'slightly' tough (could be from their enthusiastic stirring too!).  I baked this in 2 9" rounds, stacked with a layer of icing int he middle, and we ooh'd, ahh'd and moaned in ecstacy through the whole thing. There wasn't a crumb left..and they all want to have another this weekend!  Thanks so much for posting this jewel!

Probably more like a 3.5 rating, but rounding up because it's decent.  It's just not what I expect out of carrot cake (which is far and away my favorite kind of cake). First of all, the cake itself is a bit too salty.  And that's saying something, coming from someone like me who prefers salty to sweet.  I would highly recommend cutting the salt in half, especially considering that as is, it has 582mg of sodium per serving (more than in 3 oz. of salted potato chips).  Second, perhaps I've been spoiled by some really great carrot cakes, but I think this could stand to be more dense.  It just seemed a bit too airy for me.  That's a matter of personal taste, though.  Bottom line: reduce the salt, and if you're a fan of really dense carrot cake, you'll probably want to try a different recipe.

Let me start off by saying that I'm at a loss for words when it came to describing this recipe.  I have not had a Carrot Cake this good since my wonderful wife worked at a 5 star restaurant before we were married 18 years ago.  The French pastry chef made a carrot cake to die for, and would never part with his secrets no matter how much I begged.  When the kids started to come along, and she left her job I thought I would never be able to enjoy the wonderful taste and texture of his carrot cake. BOY WAS I WRONG!!!! 
 I was impressed by all the positive reviews and decided I'd give it a try, being hopeful that it would come close to the memories I held of that wonderful dessert.............so I made it for my wife,myself and another couple on a little weekend getaway.  I thought I died and went to heaven!!!!!!  Not only did this come close , but it blew it away.  This is FABULOUS!!!! Fit to be served in the finest restaurant. I only wish I could give it 10 STARS.  Thanks for posting this, all my other Carrot cake recipes are now in the garbage.

I used four pecan halves to garnish. The flavour and aroma were exceptional and made a very dense, moist cake.  Next time, I will vary by using half plain yogurt and half oil, also 2 eggs and an extra egg white. The recipe is a keeper for sure.

reviews.review_text: Well, after sitting and reading ALL 280+ reviews, I decided to make this recipe into cupcakes, to serve at my wedding in 2 days!  I realized that I had NEVER made my fiance his favorite cake from scratch, probably because I didn't think I liked carrot cake - WRONG!.  I just finished making 2 batches, and am thinking of making another, I am sure they are going to be a BIG hit!  They are SO moist!  I can't wait for them to sit a bit for the spices to come to full flavor.  The preparation went quickly- after grating the carrots.  I did incorporate a few changes as recommended in some of the reviews... 1) cut sugar to 1 cup,  2) 1/2 c. unsweetened applesauce for half the oil, 3) added 1/2 tsp. nutmeg & 1/2 tsp. allspice, 4) added an extra 1/2 cup carrots, 5) omitted coconut & walnuts to appease fiance and new in-laws =), 6) baked 18 minutes for cupcakes - yielded approx. 18 cupcakes per batch, using an ice cream scoop to measure.  I have only tried one w/o frosting, I think they will definitely be sweet enough once frosted, I like the extra spice, yet it isn't overpowering, I think the applesauce helps to "lighten" the finished product and reduces the chance of "sinking", and I love the pineapple! I used the frosting recipe, but added 1 tsp. vanilla.  Will definitely update after the wedding!  Thanks for the recipe! I am so glad I decided to try it!

items.name: Sesame Chicken
items.description: This recipe really satisfies my craving for Chinese food. I serve it over rice with a side of steamed vegetables. The sauce makes just enough to glaze the chicken. I usually double or even triple the sauce recipe to have enough to pour over our rice and veggies. It is a nice low-fat alternative to the restaurant-style Sesame Chicken.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 1 inch strips or bite size pieces.
Heat a large non-stick skillet that has been sprayed with Pam, over medium-high heat.
Cook chicken for about 6 minutes or until no longer pink.
Mix together honey, soy sauce, water, corn starch, ginger and red pepper flakes.
Whisk until no corn starch lumps appear.
Pour sauce mixture into skillet with chicken.
Cook until sauce thickens slightly.
You can add more water if sauce is too thick.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes or until chicken starts to soak up the sauce.

Note: Since originally posting this recipe, I have tried some of the suggestions others have made.  I do like it with a bit of sesame oil (be careful not to get too much, just a few drops at the end of cooking is good enough for me, but you might like more), fresh ginger is also good if you have it on hand.  I have tried it with garlic and it is good that way also.  I have also found that it is good with shrimp and pork. Basically what I am trying to say is, the original recipe is just a simple, quick and healthy meal I came up with when I was craving Chinese food.  I thought it turned out really great and wanted to share it.  I'm happy that so many of you have enjoyed it. For those of you that didn't care for it, I hope you can find one that suits your fancy some where else.

reviews.review_text: This was very good, but to me it seemed like something was missing.  I used 4 chicken breasts, used a bit less soy sauce, added 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes, use fresh ginger and added a bit of garlic and brown sugar.  I also had no sesame seeds so like others suggested I cooked the chicken in a teaspoon of sesame oil.  I thought that with the addition of the fresh ginger, garlic and brown sugar that this dish would really have alot of taste but it just didn't.  It almost kind of tasted like a salty chicken stock to me, but after I added some brown sugar it started taking on a sweeter more Chinese-type taste.  One thing I noticed is that when my chicken was done cooking (before adding the sauce) there was quite a bit of liquid in my pan.  I wasn't sure whether to pour this out or not so I just poured most of it out but not all.  Maybe I should have poured all of it out.  I decided to still give it four stars since it was quick, easy to make and healthy.  I will try this again but will double the sauce so it is less bland.

attributes.source_text: it started taking on a sweeter more Chinese-type taste
a sweeter more Chinese-type taste

reviews.review_text: Tried this recipe for dinner tonight over jasmine rice and it was wonderful!  I scaled it down for just one serving though.  I did modify a few things.  The first thing I changed was the amount of soy sauce.  When I scaled my recipe for 1 serving the recipe calls for 1/8 a cup (Two Tablespoons) soy sauce.  That is over 100% of the recommended daily sodium intake, so i cut that in half.  My other modifications were adding a splash of cider vinegar and a splash of rice vinegar.  I felt the sauce needed a tinge of tang and I think that adding these to my sauce really payed off in my final product.  The spice level with the ginger and crushed red pepper were in my opinion perfection!  It had just a small bit of spice in the aftertaste which is what I like in my Chinese food.  This was easy and delicious! Using a 4oz chicken breast and putting this all over rice I calculated was only 430 calories, not to mention free of processed sugars or any nasty food additives.  Cook this recipe up, you wont regret it!!

attributes.source_text: Tried this recipe for dinner tonight
The spice level with the ginger and crushed red pepper were in my opinion perfection!
It had just a small bit of spice in the aftertaste
which is what I like in my Chinese food

reviews.review_text: Very Yummy! I just got done making this, and like the others i made a few adjustments. I only used 4 pieces of chicken and cut into chunks coated the chicken with flour and deep fried it for two mins. For the sauce I tripled the amount. I only used 1/2 teaspoon of fresh ginger root and 1  1/2 teaspoon of red pepper flakes, and 1 tbs of cornstarch. Put chicken in skillet pour sauce over chicken coat and do not cover sauce gets thicker alot faster. Also another reviewer was wondering how to get the red color of the sauce i was wondering the same thing so i jsut added three drops of red food color to the sauce before pouring it over the chicken, It worked perfect. I was going to take a picture but it was gone before i could. This is a Very Fast very Delicious Meal.

Love this base recipe! I've made it at least a half dozen times now and figured out some changes I've done for my families tastes. I start with the same base recipe, but I cook two large teaspoons of smashed and chopped garlic to a bit of oil in the pan before cooking the chicken (could actually use more garlic, and may in the future try a tablespoon). I also add a 1/4 cup of hoisin sauce, I find it really helps make it even better. I only use dry ground ginger as I've found fresh ginger was just way too over powering. If I used fresh again, I'd only use closer to 1/4-1/2 a teaspoon. I'm not too sure how people found 2 table spoons of cornstarch too much, I find I have to add 3 to get it thicker or it is just too runny. I allow the chicken to softly simmer in the sauce minus the cornstarch for a few hours on low then turn up the heat and add the cornstarch mixed with just enough water to pour without being too thick so it doesn't clump. <br/><br/>Such a great easy meal. Perfect served with rice and veggies. Thank you thank you thank you for this recipe!

HEALTHY AND AWESOME!!!! DH and I loved this and will be adding it to our regular rotation! I used the full tsp of ginger and red pepper flakes and added two cloves of garlic and a tsp of sesame oil to the sauce. After the sauce had thickened I also added a frozen bag of stir fry veggies (snow peas, green beans, bell pepper). This thinned the sauce some (next time I'll add a little more cornstarch to thicken it up).  I also only had about a lb of chicken (4 breast halves) and there was just the right amount of sauce to cover chicken and veggies.  I served it with brown rice. A note to others: If you like spicy Thai food, you won't find this too spicy even with the full amount of ginger and red pepper.  It has a mild background heat to it.  If you are a spicy addict like my DH you could add some Thai chillies to kick it up a notch. If you wanted to sacrifice some healthiness this would also be awesome with cashews instead of sesame seeds.

attributes.source_text: DH and I loved this
It has a mild background heat to it

reviews.review_text:
I made this for my mom when I was recently in Florida visiting and she loved it. I served it over brown rice. It is so easy and gluten free (using gluten free soy sauce), and it is not fried. We had leftover turkey meat so I made a double batch of sauce and poured it over the heated meat, and then simmered it for a while to thicken it. It was fabulous! The turkey meat was so moist and delicious. One of the best recipes I have made. My family likes this one, and I make it quite often, instead of going out and risking gluten in my food.

This one is a keeper! Thanks so much for posting the recipe!

I Also wanted to add that when I make this, I use half soy sauce and half sesame oil for the full amount of soy sauce. I love sesame oil in this, it adds perfect flavor, very authentic.

Thanks for posting this! Great recipe!

attributes.source_text: I made this for my mom when I was recently in Florida visiting and she loved it
My family likes this one
The turkey meat was so moist

reviews.review_text: This was tasty, but the batch I made had adjustments based on previous reviews.  Doubled the sauce, added garlic while chicken cooked, added a splash of vinegar, used fresh ground ginger and a bit of sesame oil at the end.  With my adjustments I needed more cornstarch to thicken the sauce.  I used the lower suggested amount of red pepper flakes.  This dish definitely needs some spice to it, but I will reduce the red pepper flake even further next time.  I used the full amount of soy sauce but used a lower sodium soy, which was perfect.  This is a great basic recipe that uses ingredients you probably already have in your kitchen, and I'll use this again to give a new option to using up boneless chicken breasts.  Thank you Jenny.

I'm Asian but for my boyfriend, he prefers a more American route to Oriental dishes. So we tried General Tso's (http://www.food.com/recipe/super-easy-general-tso-chicken-148303) and we loved it. Everyone who tried it was asking for the recipe. With such success, we thought we'd try another. I love making sesame beef, but we found this recipe. He and I like to test the sauce before committing to it by adding the chicken. I took a taste of it (and mind you, these sort of tastes should be right up my alley) and I absolutely lost all my appetite. We ended up taking the chicken we fried and just eating chicken nuggets because we were both so disappointed and disgusted. I STRONGLY suggest using much less soy sauce. These portions for sauce are rather ridiculous. Even my boyfriend who loves to eat anything couldn't put himself through another taste test. It was a waste of delicious honey. It was a waste of time. I wouldn't try this again.

Very good low-cal recipe. I made this to take to work for lunches and it was quick and simple and heated up well.  My chicken came out a bit dry and tough, and I expect it is because of that long simmering time, which is way more than the chicken needs to get cooked through. Next time I will make the following changes: 
1) Cut chicken into bite size pieces instead of strips
2) Mix all sauce ingredients except cornstarch and sesame seeds and marinate the chicken overnight
3) Cook chicken in nonstick pan just until chicken is done, add cornstarch mixed with a little water or soy sauce at end to thicken, sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Overall a very good recipe and a great addition to my healthy menus. Thanks for sharing!

attributes.source_text: to take to work for lunches

reviews.review_text:
I give this 3 stars, hubby gives it 5, so we'll settle on 4 for this review. I think this is a matter of personal preference, but it just didn't suit my taste. DH thinks it tastes like Teriyaki Stix's teriyaki chicken, which he loves. I made it exactly as the recipe states except I cut the red pepper flakes down to 1/4 tsp. and I coated the chicken in cornstarch before cooking.

Hubby was helping me in the kitchen and before I knew it, he was adding sesame oil to the sauce. I don't know how much that changed the flavor, but sesame oil is pretty potent.

I recently started making bourbon chicken (#45809) and since the chicken (I also like to use tofu) are cooked in the same method, I can whip up both sauces for me and my hubby and we can both enjoy dinner.

attributes.source_text: hubby gives it 5
we can both enjoy dinner

reviews.review_text: If I could give it 20 stars I would.  Both of my kids (17 & 10) went crazy for it! My daughters exact words were " give it a VERY positive review!  I did add garlic and used about 1/4 cup honey (all I had) and about 1/8th cup agave necter.  It was SO easy and delicious!  I will definitely be making this one on school nights, since both my husband and I are music teachers and our kids are heavily involved in dance and band.  It was so quick and easy.......  Thanks for this great recipe!  I think it would be DELICIOUS made with tofu, chicken, shrimp, too!  My son said it would be good with beef also, but I don't eat beef so probably won't make that.... but I won't need to, because they loved it with chicken!!  Thanks again!

Loved, loved, loved it!!  I just made this recipe tonight for company and everyone loved it.  My mom took some home for her dinner tomorrow.  Easy to make.  
I decided to put some fresh, minced garlic, a small amount of sesame oil, a small about of soya sauce and a small amount of honey drizzled over the chicken and stirred in to marinate (a few hours).  If you like it hot, defintely use the red pepper flakes.  I used 1-1/2 tsps.

We also made stir fried vegetables on the side and had our guests serve themselves some rice, top it with chicken and sauce and then some vegetables.

This recipe is moving from my Recipes I'd like to try to my Recipes I love Cookbook.  Thanks Jenny!

attributes.source_text: made this recipe tonight for company and everyone loved it
had our guests serve themselves some rice

reviews.review_text: I've made this several times as written, including the tips in the final step about adding garlic powder and a little bit of sesame oil right at the end.  I never have fresh ginger on hand so I just add a bit more ground ginger, and I use low sodium soy sauce.  It's really good and definitely does satisfy that Chinese food craving.  It's still missing a bit of something for me but I intend to play around with it more and figure out what to add to give it that last punch, but at the same time, I like it enough as is to have made it several times.  This is definitely a great recipe to toy with and easy to change to suit individual tastes.  Thanks for sharing!

attributes.source_text: definitely does satisfy that Chinese food craving

reviews.review_text:
Great idea...I used our favorite teriyaki sauce (Soyaki) which already has the spices in it and some honey, although still added 1 tsp of the red pepper flakes and about 3 tbsp of toasted sesame seeds.  Because we like lots of sauce -- 1 cup soyaki plus because my guys like a sweet flavor I added 1/4 to 1/2 cup extra honey (could skip the extra honey if you don't want it as sweet).

I simmered the sauce separately, added the cornstarch in just a few TBSP of water and then brought to a boil, all while the chicken was cooking, then added to the chicken and let it simmer another 3-5 minutes.  Turned out great!  Served it over brown rice and with green beans on the side.

attributes.source_text: my guys like a sweet flavor

reviews.review_text: Tried this recipe last night. Added some garlic, brown sugar, sesame oil and green onion garnish, as per one of the previous reviews. The sauce was tasty enough, but next time I would amp up some of the spicier flavors, maybe add more ginger and garlic. The most prominent issue with this recipe, though, is the amount of chicken. We used only 3 chicken breasts, and still there was just barely enough sauce. Certainly not as much as I would have liked for the rice and broccoli that we served with it. It would have been helpful to know how many pounds of chicken, because clearly our grocery store packages breasts that are much larger than called for. Next time we'll use the chicken tenders our local grocery sells.

Meh. Not great, not bad. Was a little on the salty side, and I even used low-sodium soy sauce. I used 1/2 c. fresh squeezed orange juice and 1/2 c. water. I added a 2 shakes of the rice wine vinegar because the takeaway Chinese usually has a little tang to it, but it wasn't enough. 

I'm big on mimicking restaurant's, and I feel this fell short. 

Oh, and I boiled the chicken because I don't like to doubt the doneness of the chicken. Sometimes I'll brown it before adding sauce,  just to get the "effect". 2/5; Will revert to the top Bourbon Chicken recipe instead. Now THAT'S an awesome recipe.

The dish was easy to prepare but fell a little flat for some reason. The flavors were very good, but the recipe made a lot more sauce than I was expecting for the amount of chicken used. As for modifications, I would add a little more ginger and maybe a few more red pepper flakes to bring things up to a good, subtle, heat. I also substituted low-sodium soy sauce for full sodium soy sauce. Other than the few little tweaks, I would definitely make this again. I've even thought about how hard it would be to make the sauce and freeze it, then just thawing and cooking it when needed. I definitely plan on making this again. Simple, delicious, quick--what's not to love.

This turned out very well even though we had messed with it in a major way. With my current budget, chicken was out of the question. So we bought pork. (It was half the price) I think it still turned out VERY well. I enjoyed it so much that I licked my plate clean. No, really, I did! I also added some fresh ginger to the sauce as well. I loved the extra little zip that it gave it. Next time, we will make this with chicken but pork works in a pinch. All members of the family enjoyed it. Even my oldest DS went back for seconds and THIRDS! UPDATE - I have made this now with chicken breasts, and low salt soy sauce to make it that little bit more healthy. Still a keeper!!

attributes.source_text: All members of the family enjoyed it
my oldest DS went back for seconds and THIRDS

reviews.review_text: Mmmm"!!! this is a very good recipe, believe it or not I cut it down to one serving and it worked out just fine, and nothing was lost as sometimes happens when you cut a recipe down. I was looking for something healthy and quick for dinner, I am cooking for one at the moment and this was just perfect. I used ready cooked chicken breast I had in the freezer all chopped up so I just took out what I needed and I stir fried some veg and wholewheat noodles. It was fantastic This is one recipe that I will definitely be making again, and its better than anything you get at the takeaway Chinese where we live. Thank you for a great recipe.

attributes.source_text: something healthy and quick for dinner

items.label: Best Grape Salad
items.name: Best Grape Salad
keywords: c("Berries", "Grapes", "Fruit", "Nuts", "Low Protein", "Potluck", "Spring", "Summer", "< 15 Mins", "For Large Groups", "No Cook", "Easy")
items.description: I got this recipe from a coworker at the salon I work at. I didn't think it would be so wonderful and addictive! It's very creamy and sweet, and a great mix of flavors. It will be the best thing you ever use grapes for (except maybe wine!).
instructions: Wash and stem grapes.
Set aside.
Mix sour cream, cream cheese, white sugar and vanilla by hand until blended.
Stir grapes into mixture, and pour in large serving bowl.
For topping: Combine brown sugar, and crushed pecans.
Sprinkle over top of grapes to cover completely.
Chill overnight.

reviews.review_text: This recipe is absolutely heavenly! I made a quarter recipe, since I'm only making it for myself, and it turned out GREAT! I followed the recipe exactly, except that I roasted the pecans for about 8 minutes in the oven before putting them in, and saved a few on the side to sprinkle over the finished product. I mixed the brown sugar and pecans into the grape mixture rather than let it sit on top, since I thought it would be weird to have nuts and brown sugar sitting on the top...it seems like it would be grainy. Also, I didn't use the entire amount of brown sugar suggested, and I'm glad that I didn't! It was incredibly sweet even with the reduced amount, and I have an insatiable sweet tooth, so that's saying a lot. It really was still too sweet so I will reduce the brown sugar even more next time. I like the flavor that it adds but thought it changed the flavor of the dish a little too much (I taste-tested throughout and am not convinced that I like the addition of brown sugar at all). Overall a delicious recipe that I can't wait to make (and eat) again!!

I have made similar grape salads to this one on many occasions, and as always, they are very good. You can make this salad using just the green grapes, or using red & green grapes, or even using red, green, and black grapes. And if desired, using 2 or 3 lbs of the grapes instead of the 4 lbs. With less grapes, you have a bit more of the delicious cream cheese/sour cream/sugar mix. Depending on how much of the creamy sweet filling and grapes added, is ones preference. And that also goes for the brown sugar and pecan topping. Since today I only used 2 lbs of the grapes to make this salad, I topped my salad with just 1 tablespoon of the brown sugar, and 2 tablespoons of the chopped pecans, but in the past I have used 3 Tbsp of brown sugar and 2 Tbsp of chopped pecans. Again, the amount of topping ingredients added is a preference, but to be honest, I actually prefer this salad with out the brown sugar and pecans. That's just my preference. Thank you Jamie for posting this delicious salad recipe. It's definitely a keeper!!

attributes.source_text: the creamy sweet filling

reviews.review_text: This was a complete hit! I used 3lbs red and 1lb green grapes for the same reasons as others (they were a little tart). Also, I was almost through slicing my 4lbs of grapes before I realized that it said "stem" not "slice" the grapes. I was more than happy at that point to just toss in the remaining grapes - it actually made a nice variety for lack of a better word and will probably slice half of the grapes next time. I also chopped and toasted my pecans. This was a little on the sweet side for me so I may decrease the sugar next time, but the rest of the family and neighbors said this is a winner just as it is. UPDATE: I have now made this for two dinner parties and two work functions, this is THE most requested recipe I have ever made. I have also realized that it is important to let it sit overnight or atleast for a good 6 hours, it helps mellow out the "sweetness". This is such a good recipe!!

attributes.source_text: the rest of the family and neighbors said this is a winner just as it is

I have now made this for two dinner parties
and two work functions

reviews.review_text: Wow!  This is WAY good!  I wasn't too sure of the "dry" topping so I improvised.  I was cooking ribs in the oven, low and slow, so only had the stove top availiable.  Harkening back to a childhood favorite I decided to "cook" my pecans in butter and a dusting of salt (to die for!).  Mixed in the brown sugar.  The sugar wasn't melting fast enough for me and I was afraid of burning the pecans so I scrambled for a liquid.  1/2 & 1/2 was available.  Great!  A cheap take-off of a Praline!!  Just what I had in mind!  Melted the brown sugar right away and a quick taste proved I was on the right track flavor wise.  I then added a small amount of corn syrup, stirred and dumped on to a buttered piece of wax paper  hoping the mixture would "set".  It didn't really harden so I just dumped it in the cream cheese/grape mixture.  It turned it an ugly brown but it sure is TASTY!!  And definitely gives me something to work on in the future.  Dinner isn't even served yet and DH has asked twice where the "Grape Goodness" is...This is a keeper.  Thanks!!

attributes.source_text: DH has asked twice where the "Grape Goodness" is

reviews.review_text: I work as a nurse in long term care..today we had our annual Thanksgiving dinner for our residents and their families and our staff. I needed to make items that were good but could be made quickly. This recipe was absolutly the best. I made just as the recipe stated. I was a little "leery" about adding the brown sugarand pecan at the end covering it totally..I had the urge to add the nuts and stir them in and maybe just a touch of brown sugar..stirred in..but I resisted and am so glad I did. It was beautiful in a crystal bowl and colorful. I took home an empty bowl and many request for the recipe. My family was very upset that I didn't make them a salad also and felt left out. So I will be making this again tomorrow. Thanks so much for the great recipe!!!!! Cindy

reviews.review_text:
Wow, add my name to the long list of grape salad lovers.  I had never heard of it, until running across it here.  DH gave me a strange look when I brought him a bowl of it, but that look turned to pure ecstasy after the first bite.  I used green grapes, halved the recipe,and toasted walnuts in the topping.  Thanks for the tip of drying the grapes first, that kept the consistency perfect.  I will definitely make this again.  Love that vanilla cream sauce.  I don't know if it made a difference, but I used Roger Reginald's Melapone Mexican vanilla (mail order)which is double potent, according to the bottle.  It's certainly the best vanilla I've ever used and I recommend it. 
Thanks for a wonderful recipe, Jamie!

attributes.source_text: DH gave me a strange look when I brought him a bowl of it, but that look turned to pure ecstasy after the first bite

reviews.review_text: Addictive!  I got this recipe off of here a few weeks ago.  I have made it for 2 parties and it has been the talk of the party!  So many people request the recipe.  Since then, the people I gave the recipe to have told me they are receiving the same kind of reaction.  I'm going to a party tonight and will be taking it with me there.  I took one person's advice on here and roasted my pecans first.  I melt a little butter in a small bowl, add my chopped pecans and brown sugar, stir, spray a cookie sheet with non-stick spray, broil for a few minutes (watch or they will burn!) then put on top of the grape mixture.  Before it's time to eat the salad, I stir in the topping, otherwise you'll get people scooping up as much topping as possible and they salad on the bottom won't have any.  THANK YOU SO MUCH JAMIE FOR SHARING THIS RECIPE! :)

attributes.source_text: I have made it for 2 parties and it has been the talk of the party!

reviews.review_text:
3 friends gave it a 3, I gave it a 4 and one a 5.

A bit sweet for me and I even cut back a bit on the sugar to start with. I only made half a recipe which was plenty. A bit too much brown sugar on top as well. Too sugary.

I did use a mix of black seedless, red and green which was a nice blend for color.

One suggestion, I wouldn't be inclined to eat this at a party where it was served in a big bowl, maybe a large open glass serving dish, where you could really see all the colors and maybe on a pedestal. It really shows off the dish. Also something shallow so the topping and grapes were distributed evenly.

I would serve this in individual  martini glasses or a small ice cream dish to really show off the colors.

It was good, but more dessert for me. I will keep it on hand.
Thx for posting

attributes.source_text: more dessert for me

reviews.review_text: WOW WOW WOW WOW WOWWY, this is an awesome recipe!! We have eaten this with almost every dinner for the past 2 months (since grapes came in season and on sale) and were still not tired of it.  I didn't have any made the other day and when dinner was served the whole family asked " Where's the grape sald?".  My DD even passed up dessert for just a bowl of this.  I leave off the brown sugar, it's sweet enough already, and the nuts due to allergies.  I'm dreading winter when grapes go back up to $3 a pound.  The best recipe I have found on this site so far, andf that is saying alot because I have found a bunch of good ones.  Simple and delicious!!!

reviews.review_text: Talk about refreshing!!!  This is so easy and no one can believe it's ONLY grapes!  I used Splenda and it worked just great.  I used half Brown Sugar substitute and half regular brown sugar with the pecans and I toasted them in the oven as well (I think that should be part of the recipe).  I served individual servings on lettuce and there was nothing but  wilted lettuce left on every plate!  Two people told me afterwards that they don't eat sour cream (had I known this, I would not have served this dish) -- but they gobbled up every bite of it (much to their amazement).  Thanks for posting such a unique and wonderful recipe.

attributes.source_text: Talk about refreshing!!!

reviews.review_text: INCREDIBLE! Made a couple of small changes...added about 1/2 to 3/4 C fresh blueberries and used 1/4-1/3 C of brown sugar. With the natural sweetness of the red and green grapes and sugar in the cream cheese mixture, it would have been too sweet with a full cup of brown sugar. Definitely toast the pecans. That toasted flavor adds depth to the whole dish. The mouth feel of the rich velvety dressing with the snap of fresh fruit and crunch of toasted pecans was marvelous. This was my dish to pass for a July 4th party at the neighbors and the perfect addition to fresh avocado and tortilla chips, ribs, roasted potato salad and a medley of corn-peppers-black bean.

reviews.review_text: I can't believe I haven't rated this yet. Out of all the wonderful recipes that I have found on Zaar, this is by far the one I have made the most. It's so easy to prepare, makes enough for a large group and the leftovers are just as good as the first day. Now every time I show up to a party, all I hear is "where is the grape salad". The only thing I do different is to use almonds instead of pecans. Mainly because they are normally half the price. I also toast the nuts with the brown sugar in the oven for a few minutes for a little extra crunch. Thank you so much Jamie. This is a new family favorite.
