This is a new family favorite

reviews.review_text: This was SO wonderful!! I took it to a pool party yesterday and everyone there was copying the recipe. I used only red grapes, because the green ones at the grocery were sour.  I also mixed the chopped pecans and brown sugar, put them on a sheet of "quick release" aluminum foil, and put into a hot oven just until the sugar started to melt. (about 7-8 minutes, stirred twice) I love caramelized nuts, but am not fond of ones that haven't been roasted. I let them cool and crumbled them on top of the grape mixture. It was very easy and quick to put together and can be used as an appetizer, salad, OR dessert.  I'm making it again tonight for us to have here at home.  Thanks for one of my new favorites.

attributes.source_text: I took it to a pool party yesterday
can be used as an appetizer
OR dessert

reviews.review_text: This is a phenomenal recipe.  I made it the first time as described, but feel that I will take away 1/4 cup of brown sugar and nuts.  The topping seemed to overpower the grape portion.   Roasting the nuts, along with the brown sugar, really makes the flavors sing!  I would mix the cream cheese and granulated sugar first until creamy, and then add the sour cream.  It will make it smoother.  Also, make sure you dry your grapes thoroughly before putting them into the salad.  This recipes was served to two separate clients this week, and they have reserved this dish for the next prepared meal I make for them.  An excellent, yet simple recipe.  Thanks so much.

A coworker had brought a grape salad in for one of our covered dish luncheons, and I loved it. I decided to make this for my granddaughters birthday party so I searched on Zaar for the recipe. This tasted exactly like the one that I had a work. I increased the vanilla to one tablespoon. I layered the grape mixture and topping into three layers so that the topping would be more evenly spread throughout the salad. All the guests loved this grape salad. Even people that don't like grapes liked this salad. Thanks for the keeper, Jamie Renee.  Update:  This recipe is in my Top Favorites of 2009 Cookbook.

attributes.source_text: my granddaughters birthday party
All the guests loved this grape salad

reviews.review_text: Yum! I halved the recipe and followed the recommendations of others to mix the brown sugar and pecans together and then roast them. I also used 1/2 Splenda and 1/2 granulated sugar for the mix and Splenda brown sugar for the roasted nuts to cut down on the kcals. Also used low fat cream cheese and lite sour cream. I didn't cut the grapes in half like some suggested due to some complaining of too wet of a consistency, thought this would make it worse. But my mixture turned out perfect. And YUM!!! Thank you so much for posting Jamie Renee!! This one's a keeper!

A HEEEUGE hit at the family reunion. Thanks for this recipe I love it. I make it once a week now and eat it for BKFST & hubby eats it at night for the munchies. GREAT TIP: for home I "skinny" it up with light cream cheese, light sour cream and splenda replaces the sugar & I skip the brown sugar on top and mix the nuts in with the grapes. items.label: Roasted Asparagus
items.name: Roasted Asparagus
items.description: I got this recipe from "Simple Vegetarian Pleasures" by Jeanne Lemlin. I LOVE asparagus and am always on the lookout for new ways to make it. This is such an easy and elegant way to serve it.  The asparagus gets a slightly nutty flavor after roasting, which makes it even more yummy.
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Cut off the woody bottom part of the asparagus spears and discard.
With a vegetable peeler, peel off the skin on the bottom 2-3 inches of the spears (this keeps the asparagus from being all \
and if you eat asparagus you know what I mean by that).
Place asparagus on foil-lined baking sheet and drizzle with olive oil.
Sprinkle with salt.
With your hands, roll the asparagus around until they are evenly coated with oil and salt.
Roast for 10-15 minutes, depending on the thickness of your stalks and how tender you like them.
They should be tender when pierced with the tip of a knife.
The tips of the spears will get very brown but watch them to prevent burning.
They are great plain, but sometimes I serve them with a light vinaigrette if we need something acidic to balance out our meal.

reviews.review_text:
I just ate asparagus for the first time in my life, using this recipe, and it was fantastic!  I especially liked the texture of the roasted tips, almost kind of crunchy.

I wanted a light, quick dinner, and I went to Sam's Club today and picked up a carton of wonderfully sweet cherry tomatoes (Sam's has the best produce) and some freshly grated parmesan cheese, so I used them with this recipe.

I made some angel hair pasta, cut the cherry tomatoes in half, took some of the leftover olive oil/salt mixture that I had used to toss the asparagus in, added just a touch of garlic, and sauteed the tomatoes.  

I cut the cooked asparagus up into one-inch strips and added them and the sauteed tomatoes to the pasta, topped with just a little bit of shredded parmesan cheese, and thoroughly enjoyed it.

Thanks for the introduction to asparagus!

attributes.source_text: almost kind of crunchy

reviews.review_text:
This
is
amazing.
I love asparagus, but I've honestly never had it THIS good. I've been to several restaurants that have served it similarly and grilled, but as a college student in a dorm I have no access to a grill. I do, however, have an oven, and this is by far better than anything I've ever had.

I probably did use a little more salt and olive oil than the recipe called for (didn't measure), and squeezed some lemon juice over it all before it cooked.

I'll be making this as much as I can. Why have any other vegetable any other way?

We love this recipe! It's one of the few ways I can get my boyfriend and father (both meat men) to eat veggies! They both love the flavor which I find ironic since they hate all kinds of veggies!

I line a glass pan with foil, pour some olive oil over all of the asparagus, throw some salt on top and add fresh cracked black pepper! Superb!

Heads up cooks... be mindful that the oil does have a tendency to run over the sides of your pan because of the heat from the oven. Just keep a watchful eye that this does not happen or your oven will start to burn the oil that drips.

5 STARS! And a huge thanks!

items.label: Denny's-Style French Toast
items.name: Denny's-Style French Toast
items.description: I do not remember where I got this recipe, but my husband says it tastes just as good as what he had at Denny's. I am just amazed at all of the great reviews on this recipe!! My family loves it, so I thought I would share it here and I'm so glad I did because it seems you all love it just as much!!! Thanks to all of you who have tried it!
instructions: Mix together the eggs, milk, flour, sugar, vanilla, salt& cinnamon.
Heat a large skillet, or griddle.
When the skillet is hot, add 1 tablespoon butter.
If the butter smokes, your pan is too hot; turn down the heat.
Dip each slice of bread into the batter for 30 seconds on each side.
Let some of the batter drip off, then put in skillet.
Cook each slice 1 1/2-2 minutes per side until each side is golden brown.
Add more butter, if necessary, to cook all of the slices.
To serve, put on plate, dust with powdered sugar. Serve with butter & hot syrup.

reviews.review_text: I decided to make french toast today so looked for a recipe to see what different ideas I could get.  With so many reviews and all 5 stars, I figured this one was worth trying.  It was definitely worth it.  I had 2 italian buns in the freezer so that's what I used for 2 of us.  I cut them on an angle about 1 inch thick.  I did what CountryLady suggested with the cinnamon mixed with the vanilla.  I also increased the amount of cinnamon from 1/8 tsp to 1/2 tsp.  We even sprinkled some more on top with the syrup.  You really do have to be careful of the temperature of the frying pan.  If it's too hot, you will burn the toast because of the sugar content in the egg mixture.  At first when I was mixing all the ingredients together, it was really lumpy from the flour.  So I suggest using a whisk and really beat it to make it smooth.  My husband and I loved this way of cooking French Toast.  Thanks.

attributes.source_text: My husband and I loved this way of cooking French Toast

reviews.review_text:
Very easy and delicious! However, I found that no matter how low I set my stove, my slices were burning when I used butter to cook them. I switched to canola oil and things came out much better. I'd recommend just putting some butter on top when serving for that butter flavor (even better, whipped butter like Denny's does), or use only clarified butter to fry these up in your frying pan.

Mixing the dry ingredients together in a small bowl then adding to the egg mixture helps it all combine with no lumps.

I used Whitewheat bread, which was perfect -- just enough crust, thickness and chewiness to it, and did not soak up too much batter. I also added a tiny splash of orange extract (could also use orange juice,) since I've noticed when eating french toasts at restaurants, there's often hint of orange flavor that adds a bit of unexpected and sophisticated yumminess.

This recipe is a total keeper! Thank you for sharing it!

attributes.source_text: just enough crust, thickness and chewiness to it

reviews.review_text: I thought it was ok.  I didn't have texas toast, but I don't think it would make that much of a difference..  I thought it sounded interesting because it had flour in it.  When I mixed everything together the flour formed little flour balls, kinda difficult to get them to break up, but it didn't seem to matter, as they "cooked" out when I cooked the toast.  The reason I'm giving it 2 stars is because it's an AWFUL lot of sugar for something that doesn't need sugar.  To me, this was a lot of ingredients that didn't need to be.  You can simply use eggs, milk, vanilla and cinnamon and get the same effect (just a helluva lot less sweet)  I don't think you need all that sugar, you are already going to slather maple syrup on it.  I wasn't impressed.  I will stick to my own recipe as described above (less time, less ingredients and less sugar)

This is some of the best French toast I have ever eaten and definitely the best I have ever made!! I did learn a couple of things as I made it though... 1) It is probably best to use a high-quality, dense, rustic-type French bread such as that made by La Brae Bakery (which is what I used). I had a bit of egg batter left over at the end so I tried a couple of slices of Wonder bread. The toast made with Wonder bread was bland and mushy while the toast made with La Brae French bread was MUCH more flavorful and had a great soft/chewy texture. 2) It might be a good idea to cook a test slice and then cut it in half to see if the egg mixture has penetrated the bread sufficiently. Unfortunately, I had cooked almost all my slices before I checked and realized I really should have been soaking my dense French bread slices about 45 - 60 seconds per side. The recipe poster mentioned that she forgot the source of the recipe -- I am not sure, but it might be from Todd Wilbur's Top Secret Recipes. This is an awesome recipe; thanks for posting it!

reviews.review_text: I made this a brunch with my oven bacon (only way to go for bacon) Id have to say it was the best that I've tried so far. Used Texas Toast which I have never used before, only french bread slices. I really liked the Texas Toast except it's just such a huge loaf, I put the rest of it in the freezer to make more with it. I got 10 slices out of the recipe so after we ate I fried the rest & layed it on wax paper in the freezer then when frozen put in a plastic bag. I sifted all dry ingredients together then did the eggs, milk, vanilla together then put all in my Vitamix for a minute & had no problem with clumping. Think this will be my french toast recipe from now on, a 5* recipe for sure! Served with powered sugar, butter & real maple syrup.

reviews.review_text: I'll echo what another reviewer said -- it must be the flour that keeps this from getting soggy and tasting too eggy.  Whatever it is, it sure solved my perpetual French toast woes!  I used French bread, but it was the kind called 'twin loaves' that come 2 to a package.  They're only slightly bigger in diameter than a baguette.  Although I was just using what was on hand, this worked out perfectly for us.  Since nobody in our family has a huge sweet tooth, 2 or 3 of the mini-slices gave everybody a delicious little sugar hit without being too much of a good thing.  There were lots of very small clumps of flour floating around that refused to incorporate,  but it was way too early in the morning to drag out the mixer.  Didn't seem to affect the end results in the least, though.  Thanks for a winner, Earnhardt!

I love the way my kitchen smells after I make it.  Some things to mention: like Faeanne, my flour never quite mixes with the eggs, or if it does, it's only for a second and then I have to stir it again.  No worries!  You do not end up with flour balls on your french toast.  Also, today I made the whole shebang: butter, syrup, powdered sugar.  VG... but this recipe definitely stands on it's own, as well. We made the French toast as directed (but using skim instead of whole milk, and egg beaters instead of whole eggs - I know, I know, we're going to stuff it, so why bother?  It still tastes great, and I feel a little better.)  While that was cooking, my son mixed together 1/2 package of reduced fat cream cheese (Neufchatel), 2 tbs butter, 1/2 cup powered sugar, and 1/2 tsp vanilla.  When the French toast was done and still warm, we spread a slice with about 1 tbs cream-cheese mixture, and topped it with another slice of French toast.  We cut it on the diagonal, and each one of us had a half of this "sandwich" topped with maple syrup.  Better than IHOP!

items.label: Kittencal's Buttery Cut-Out Sugar Cookies W/ Icing That Hardens
items.name: Kittencal's Buttery Cut-Out Sugar Cookies W/ Icing That Hardens
keywords: c("Cookie & Brownie", "Kid Friendly", "Christmas", "Sweet", "For Large Groups", "Oven", "Refrigerator", "Beginner Cook", "< 4 Hours", "Easy")
items.description: You will not find a better sugar cookie anywhere you search, this will most likely be the only sugar cookie you will use, not only are these cookies buttery delicious, the dough is an absolute dream to work with, it rolls out easily and is easy to handle, also the cookies hold their shape when baked something many sugar cookies do not do --- make as many different colors as desired in separate bowls with the icing, the cookies must be completely cooled before icing --- plan ahead the dough must be chilled for at least 2 hours before rolling -- since these are topped with icing they are not a sweet cookie if you want a sweeter taste then increase the sugar amount
instructions: For cookies; in a large bowl combine butter with sugar, eggs, vanilla and almond extract; beat using an electric mixer on high speed until light and fluffy.
In another bowl combine the flour with baking powder, baking soda and salt; gradually stir into the butter mixture until well blended.
Cover bowl with plastic wrap and chill for 2 hours.
Set oven to 400°F.
Line cookie sheets with parchment paper (do not grease cookie sheets use parchment paper only).
On a very lightly floured surface roll out the dough into about 1/4-inch thickness.
Cut into desired shapes using cookie cutters.
Place cookies 2-inches apart on cookie sheet.
Bake 4-6 minutes.
Remove cookies to wire racks to cool completely before icing.
For the frosting; in a small bowl mix the confectioners sugar with milk (start with 1-2 tablespoons, you will likely need more milk for the perfect spreading consistency).
Beat in corn syrup and almond extract until the icing is smooth and glossy (if the icing is too thick add in a small amount more of corn syrup).
Divide into as many separate bowls as you wish for different colours.
Add in food colouring until desired intensity is achieved.
Paint the icing over the cookies using a brush, or dip edges of cookies into icing.
Allow to set on waxed paper.

reviews.review_text: I used the frosting portion of this recipe for icing my Christmas sugar cookie cut-outs yesterday.  I was searching for a frosting that hardens and allows for easier, neater cookie storage.  Only after making many modifications, the frosting turned out.  Like other reviewers, I felt the instructions for the frosting were unclear in terms of the amount of milk.  Far more than 1 tbs. is needed to achieve the right consistency, so I would suggest indicating the exact amount (or an amount closer than just 1 tbs.) would be much more helpful.  Plus once I finally reached the right consistency, I realized the flavor was lacking.  I ended up whipping 2 tbs. butter, 1/2 tsp. lemon extract and 1/2 tsp. salt into the mixture for more flavor and less tacky texture.  The frosted cookies did harden, as the recipe title promises.  The trick must be the addition of corn syrup.  Next time, I think I'll just add corn syrup to my standard butter-based frosting recipe.  Thanks for sharing your recipe!  Although it didn't completely work out for me, I did learn a new trick in the process, so thank you for that!

a frosting that hardens

reviews.review_text: I would give this recipe 10 stars if I could!I searched all over the net,and wanted to do cut outs this year.I didn't have enough butter so I did use 1 stick of butter and 1/2 cup shortening..I also DID use 1/4 cup more of the sugar,as I was nervous they would not be sweet enough.I chilled dough over night and then cut out shapes,and rolled between parchment paper..I DID also leave in oven about 8 min...I think everyone's oven is different.I made the frosting and put a bit into a piece of plastic wrap,twisted it shut,so that that there was a little ball of frosting,and pierced a tiny hole at bottom...Then went to town zig-zagging designs across the shapes...I then used sprinkles over the frosting and they hardened very nicely!Also-used the mouth of a small drink glass to cut out circles,put a 1/2 tsp raspberry jam in center and folded over,pinching the sides with fork tines,so it looked like a little half tart. I sprinkled confectioners sugar when they came out of oven....YUM!!!!GREAT RECIPE!

This is seriously the best sugar cookie cutout recipie I have ever made. I've made adjustments that work perfectly for me. Everyone raves about these cookies. First I don't measure the dry ingredients, I weigh them. Consistent results every time. I also use just vanilla extract but that's a taste preference. Using my kitchen aid mixer I add the eggs, sugar, salt, soda and baking powder first, then add soft unsalted butter. Start on low to combine, then turn up to high. Mix until light, fluffy and resembling buttercream frosting. This is when I weigh my flour out. I then dump all the flour in at once and turn it on low to combine. Once the dough is sticking to the beater I turn the mixer off and refrigerate the dough. It has to be cold to roll out properly. If you've ever worked with clay it's like that. 

Make sure you don't over bake them or over mix the dough when adding flour. They firm up as they cool. If you over bake or add too much flour or over mix they will taste bland.

This was definitely the easiest sugar cookie dough I have ever worked with. My daughter was home sick from school one day last week so we made cookies all day. We made this dough ahead of time and popped it in the fridge to chill while we made some other cookies. I divided the dough into fourths and only worked with one section at a time, leaving the other sections in the refrigerator to keep them chilled. I baked them for 5 minutes and they turned out perfectly and held their shape, which I loved. I will agree with some other posters that they are not very sweet, but paired with icing, they are wonderful and not heavy. I am going to make some to send to my daughter's class for halloween. I'm thinking of adding a little bit of lemon extract just because I like lemon. I found the icing easy to make. I just added milk a little at a time until it was the consistency I needed it to be, and then I divided it into different containers and added different food colorings. We used paintbrushes to paint the icing on, but I think next time I will outline my cookies first and then flood them with the icing. Thanks Kittencal, for a great, easy recipe! :)

reviews.review_text:
The "dream-to-work-with" dough is what lured me in, and yes, it definitely makes wonderful dough! I made a double batch for a toddler Christmas cookie-making party, and even at room temperature (things go slow with kids!), it rolled easily and was easy to "re-mush" and roll out again. For the second batch, I added 1/4 cup of Nutella Chocolate-Hazelnut spread after step 1, and added an extra 1/2 cup of flour. This made a nice alternative color and added a bit of flavor; it baked up just the same as the others. Now, the icing is the only reason I must dock a star! What a headache! 1 T. milk is NOT enough moisture for 2 c. of sugar! I must've quadrupled (or more) the measurements for BOTH the milk and c.syrup, and I honestly thought I was going to blow the motor on my hand mixer -- it was getting so hot! BTW, we also added more milk during the icing process since it was drying up a bit (things go slow with kids!); even so all hardened up wonderfully. Thanks for the lovely recipe!     

****UPDATE: This time they fluffed up and didn't remain smooth on top!  The only thing I increased was the sugar to 1 1/2 cups???

reviews.review_text: I too was set to try a different recipe when I came across this one.  This dough is fabulous to work with. The flavor is buttery without being too rich or sweet - the perfect foil for the icing.  Mine actually baked up perfectly with a little crunch on the outside while the inside was softer.   I subbed all vanilla as I am not a fan of almond flavoring. The cookies did not spread much at all.  I did chill my dough well in addition to cooling my cookie sheet down between batches.  The icing was just what I needed as I didn't really want to make a batch of royal icing. Instead of spreading it on with a spatula or putting it in a piping bag, I placed it in bowls with wide rims and held my cookies upside down and dipped them in.  I was even able to dip some of the cookies so they had multiple colors on them by dipping one color, allowing it to dry and dipping the next color.  My cookies were iced very quickly this way.   It dried firm and glossy and did not smear or smoosh when I layered my cookies on a serving platter and covered them with plastic wrap for transport.  An awesome recipe that has become my standard for sugar cookies.

reviews.review_text: I am in the middle of baking these cookies...I will be the first to admit I am a non-lover of making cut-out cookies.  But we are hosting a pumpkin painting party this weekend and though it would be a good idea for the kids to be able to frost their own Halloween sugar cookies. Will definately use this recipe again and suggest it for our annual Christmas "cookie day" sugar cookie (which, by the way, I mysteriously disappear when it's time to bake sugar cookies!) Update: 1/29/11: I used this icing recipe today and it was okay..a little messy to work with.  It seems to run off the cookie really easily so you have to be sure to watch how much you are using.  Found it a little hard to make the design defined, so I iced hearts with white, then splattered red icing on top.  They came out cute.

reviews.review_text:
Delicious, and SO easy to make.
Because I hadn't planned on making the frosting, I added 1/4 cup more sugar to the dough, and they came out nice; with the classic sugar cookie taste and a little more buttery.
Just because I knew I'd be tired after coming home from the beach today, last night I made up the mix and rolled it into two logs. And...because of boredom, an excess of energy, and some sprinkles that needed using up, I shook on sprinkles on all sides, then rolled it in wax paper to press them in. Didn't penetrate the dough as well as I had hoped, but it gave them a cute coloring to spice up an otherwise plain cookie.
Baked two pans at a time, and the bottom pan cooked for exactly 6 minutes. the top pan took longer, but I think my oven's to blame for that (old, gas operated, needs replacing, etc.).

Thank you for yet another recipe, Kittencal!
they all work so nicely; you should make a book out of them!

--Luna

reviews.review_text: Not so sure about the, "...not find a better sugar cookie anywhere you search" part.  Yes, the recipe was super easy and the dough was very good to work with for cut-out cookies.  However, these are very BLAND.  I made these for my daughter's teachers, but they were so tasteless, I opted to not gift them.  Per my oldest daughter's suggestion, we're saving the cookies for Santa, hoping he'll eat them. ;)   A cookie recipe shouldn't focus mainly on making the dough easy to work with; you also have to pay attention to the TASTE of the cookie.  What's the point in having a pretty cookie if no one wants to eat it?  Also, when the instructions to use 1-2 tablespoons of milk when starting to make the icing, is ridiculous.  Yes, we'll "likely" need more, meaning it's impossible to mix it without a lot more milk.  I was happy with how the icing hardened, but even that didn't taste very good.  My normally icing-loving kids wouldn't go near this icing.  Overall, not very pleased with this recipe and I would not go so far as to say it's the best recipe ever, taste-wise.  Needs some tweaking for taste, and not just extra sugar.

I just finished a batch of Christmas cookies with this dough and had a taste of one (with the leftover, could-no-longer-be-rolled dough) and it was delicious. I did tweak the recipe for high altitude and omitted the almond (preference) and doubled up on the vanilla instead. I have long been looking for a sugar cookie dough that was not only easy to work with (this one is a dream even as it warms up) but tasty. This is it. I need look no further and will use this recipe from here on out. I didn't make the frosting as I used sprinkles instead to make it easier on myself but in future I might try it. High altitude tweaks detail: Flour - added 3 tablespoons Sugar - decreased by 1 tablespoon Baking powder - decreased to 1/4 teaspoon Baking soda - decreased to 1/4 teaspoon Added 1 tablespoon milk for extra moisture Rolled the cookies to about 1/8 of an inch

reviews.review_text: Perfect recipe.  I had to make "Cat in the Hat" cookies without a cutter and really needed a recipe that would hold the shape of the traced/cut cookies.  These held their shape incredibly well.  They were also tender and flavorful and the dough was easy to work with.  As others have said, the dough isn't very sweet so you can pile on the icing and end up with the perfect sweetness.  I did let one icing color dry a bit before doing the next; this kept the colors from running together at the border.  If I want really perfect cookies, I will use regular icing to outline the various areas and then fill in with this icing.  One hint: if you want white icing, don't try to use regular vanilla-- it turned the icing tan!!  (I used the tan batch to make red and made a half batch with almond for the white.) THANKS!

reviews.review_text: These cookies were perfect. I loved the combination of vanilla and almond extract, and they were plenty sweet for me (and my kids). They tasted exactly like how I remember them from growing up. I made the recipe exactly as directed with two exceptions. I refrigerated the dough overnight, and I baked the cookies for 8 minutes. Like other reviewers pointed out, the dough is stiff after a lengthy refrigeration, but if you are patient, the dough warms enough after a couple of hours and is great to work with. I rolled the dough on parchment paper, cut out the cookies, removed the excess dough, and slid the parchment paper on a baking sheet. The dough did not stick to my synthetic roller or my fingers - it was great to work it as is. I didn't have to add any additional flour. Thank you for the recipe.

reviews.review_text: I have made these cookies several times now. They work great with cookie sticks. The frosting allows them to be individually wrapping without the frosting being squished.  Everyone has commented on how wonderful they look and taste. I have had numerous request for the recipe.In addition to the dough being easy to work with, they are very quick to make. I made over 100 cookies in about 6 hours. That is cooking, decorating and bagging. (I did make the dough the night before.)  My husband was Santa this year and he gave one to each child from Mrs. Santa. For those with lactose problems, I made a batch with Earth Balance vegan "butter" sticks and they came out wonderful. The almond extract is a must for flavor in the cookie. I used only vanilla in the frosting but I added a lot more milk so it gave a thin coating on the cookie. For the lactose free people I used almond milk.

reviews.review_text: Hand down the "BEST" sugar cookie recipe!  Not overly sweet and the icing hardens enough to make stacking or wrapping the cookies possible. Putting the dough in the fridge for a few hours or overnight is an important step to make rolling and cutting the dough easier. I kept the dough in the fridge and only removed enough to roll and cut and then repeated until all was used.  I kept the icing thick, applied it using a brush, and had no problem with it running.  My husband has never been a fan of sugar cookies and loves these as once again, they are not too sweet.  I made these for a Christmas cookie exchange and received rave reviews.  Now I'm getting ready to double the recipe. use a heart cookie cutter, and give them to neighbors/freinds for Valentine's day.  Thanks, Kittencal...I've never had one of your recipes be a disappointment!!

I just pulled these cookies out of the oven. They came out beautifully. The cookies kept their shape while rising just a little bit to make them soft. I agree with another poster in that you shouldn't chill them overnight. I did that and the dough was so hard I had to let it sit out until it warmed enough to handle. It was still fine once it was pliable. A warning for those who use Airbake pans: I needed to add an extra minute or two to the bake time. Six minutes left the cookies a little doughy on that pan but they were perfect at eight minutes. Six minutes was just right for my other calphalon baking pan. I can't wait to get some icing on these babies. The flavor is very mild and lightly sweet on its own. It will pair very well with some icing without becoming overly sweet.

items.description: Make and share this Chicken Noodle Soup recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Melt butter in large pot.
Sauté the celery, carrot and onion for 5 to 10 minutes.
Add  thyme, poultry seasoning, chicken broth and bouilion.
Bring to a boil.
Add noodles and chicken and cook on low for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with parsley.

reviews.review_text: This was an excellent recipe!! My Husband was sick so I decided to make him some soup. He's the chef in the family so I was searching hard to find the perfect recipe.... and whala...... this is it. I didn't use celery or thyme, I didnt have any on hand. I ended up using more carrots and onions.  I also added a pinch of curry powder as well to kick it up a notch. I doubled the spices and the added 6 cups of water to this as well so that we could haved more broth. I also used angel hair pasta... Basically I used what we had on hand and it worked out well... My husband (who is a cook) by nature, said he liked the soup a lot... I knew it was good once he said he liked it because he's a chef and it is very very very hard to TOP his COOKING  :)  Thanks for posting this delicious recipe.. it's definately in my for keeps...

reviews.review_text: My friend's kids are all down with a nasty flu.  I did 3 cans chicken broth and 1 can water, but still found that I needed to dilute it further with another 1 cup of water at the end.  I didn't bother trying to figure out how many cups 4 ounces of egg noodles would be, so I just did 4 cups.  Now that I have time to sit down and look at an online conversion I agree that it's too much.   I'd say 1-2 cups medium egg noodles are good (wish it wasn't posted in ounces, as 4 ounces is only 1/2 a cup!)  Didn't put potato in because although the kids like potatoes, we all like 'em baked with dollops of sour cream and butter - not in a soup.  I didn't put thyme because I don't cook with thyme.  I added oregano, some basil and pepper.  With the canned chicken broth, there really is no need for salt.  I used rotisserie chicken from Vons, which made it much easier - and fast!  I didn't use poultry seasoning and parsley (too much green deters the kids), and it turned out fine.  Otherwise, I followed the recipe as stated and it was a hit.  There was some whipping cream left in the fridge so I added that instead of the evaporated milk - I'd say it was about 1-2 cups worth.  Very good - the kids don't want canned anymore and asked me to "buy" more of this soup!

reviews.review_text: I've cooked many different types of soup, just never the basic chicken noodle until now.  I had a leftover rotisserie chicken, which I stripped and had just over the cups of chicken needed.  I used the carcass to make about 4 cups of homemade stock, and used another 3 of store bought.  Followed this pretty much to the letter, omitting the bouillon because the homemade stock was  already quite good.  I used tiny alphabet letters (6oz) for this soup was intended for my 18 month old son.  This made for a very noodley soup, perfect for a toddler to eat but if using those tiny letters, 4 oz should suffice.  This was absolutely fantastic, and I never seem to go wrong following any of your recipes.  Thank you!

reviews.review_text: Let me add my review of this soup - it was sooo yummy!  I live in FL, so we don't have many 'cold weather' days, but since it was rainy and gray out today, I just really was having a hankering for some soup.  I found this recipe and decided to try it based on all the great reviews.  So glad I did!  I first cooked the chicken (cubed chicken breasts) in the broth (I usually make shredded chicken for soup, but didn't have time - this worked just fine), then removed the chicken to cool and reserved the broth.  Added a little extra butter to sauté the veggies in, then followed the recipe as listed, except adding a can of evaporated milk with the broth and chicken.  Served with some crusty bread, and my family couldn't get enough!  Everyone (husband and 6- and 4-year-old) had a second bowl and demanded that I keep in this in the rotation for the future.  Thanks for posting!

reviews.review_text: Had LOTS of leftover breast meat from "Big Box" rotisserie chicken, plus the carcass.  Used 2x 32 ounce boxes of low sodium chicken broth, and added the skimmed juices from the original chicken.  This was wonderful.  I did add 2 packets of HerbOx chicken bullion, and I am a salt freak, but I think you absolutely do not want to add salt without tasting.  I will likely use just 1 packet in the future. I had so much volume of vegetables, that I did not use the potato -- thinking the noodles would be sufficient, and they were.  We each (2 0f us) had 2 bowls, and enough left for a lunch with added broth.  Thanks, MizzNezz for a lovely introduction to Fall (FINALLY !) -- the FIRST cool day !!

reviews.review_text: It is 90 degrees outside and you might be wondering why I'm making chicken noodle soup on a day like today.  My neighbour is sick and really likes chicken noodle soup, so I told her husband I would make a batch for them.  I planned to use my own veggie stock, but adding spinach to it made it a nasty green colour that I don't think would be too appetizing for someone feeling unwell.  Luckily, I still had some normal veggie stock in the freezer, so I used that plus a 48 oz container of Swanson Chicken broth, low sodium/no MSG.  I followed the recipe to a T.  It was absolutely PERFECT!  I chopped carrots, green onions, celery, a bit of parsley and some  celery leaves and sauteed them for a couple minutes in just a bit of butter.  Added the broth, 2 cups of my good veggie stock and 1 tsp of bouillion granules. Simmered that on the stove til it started to boil and transferred to a 4 qt crockpot.  After that, I cooked three boneless skinless chix breasts in the remaining bits of the soup in the pot, cut those to small pieces and added to the crockpot.  There were a bit of bits on the pan from the chicken, so I added some water to that, mixed it a bit and added it to the crock as well.  I used egg noodles that I added the very last after running through cold water.   I'm kicking myself for not taking a photo of this work of chicken noodle soup art!  I did score a bowl b/c the crock was going to be too full and I gorged it down.  Thanks for a fabulous and EASY recipe, Miss Nezz.  This will be my go to quick and easy chicken noodle soup recipe!

attributes.source_text: My neighbour is sick and really likes chicken noodle soup

reviews.review_text: My husband requested soup for his supper that I pack for him to take to work. It looks like I picked the perfect one to make! Everything about the soup is absolutely delicious! I left out the celery and poultry seasoning, used my own soup stock(not sure if it was chicken, turkey or veggie though as I didn't label any of it), and for the chicken I just used a rotisserie chicken from the grocery store. I can't say enough about how good this soup is! The husband had it at work tonight and couldn't stop saying how good it was, the kids each wanted more and more, and I've already re-heated a bowl up tonight and am fighting the temptation to have another! Thank you for this simple but amazing recipe!

reviews.review_text: Absolutely delicious!  I hate soup - especially broth based soup, but for some reason I was craving chicken noodle soup so I tried this one because of its high reviews and I'm so glad I did.  DH who is not a soup or a veggie lover ate it all and said it was really good, and even my 2 and 4 yr olds ate 2 servings each - 2nd serving requested after they'd had dessert!  They even asked me to pack them soup for their school lunch the next day!  I sauteed the veggies in olive oil instead of butter, seasoned the chicken in lemon pepper seasoning before cooking it in butter, I didn't have poultry seasoning so I used a packet of Sazon Goya commonly used in Cuban soups and stews instead, sprinkled some ground thyme and Kosher salt, and added a splash of half and half at the end.  Thanks for another great recipe MizzNezz!

attributes.source_text: DH who is not a soup or a veggie lover ate it all and said it was really good
even my 2 and 4 yr olds ate 2 servings each

reviews.review_text: This is a wonderful recipe!  It is so simple to prepare and can be made in almost no time.  Starting with the chicken already cooked eliminates a lot of the hassel in making this soup.  I didn't have any leftover chicken to use, so I cut up 4 boneless chicken breast into bite-sized pieces and cooked them quickly on the stovetop in a little butter.  I used a fine egg noodle (which gave me more noodle per bite) and it worked out very well.  I followed MizzNezz's directions exactly for a wonderful and very comforting bowl of soup  + a second bowl as well ; )  Thanks ever so, MizzNezz!!

I started making this soup last night and then had to leave for a meeting. I was worried about using thyme and poultry sesoning as I've never added spices to chicken soup before. I sampled the broth before I left and it was awesome, so much better & richer flavored than the ones I've made before. I've never added noodles either. My husband added the chicken and noodles and served it.  There were 17 people and I quadrupled the recipe.  When I returned from my meeting there was none left. My 7 little grandchildren (2-8 yrs old) had even eaten 2 bowls each. I'm glad I sampled the broth before I left.  Now I'll have to make it on a night I know I'll be home so I can sell what it tastes like with noodles.  Even though we live in Arizona, we still have cold nights in the winter.

attributes.source_text: so much better & richer flavored than the ones I've made before
My 7 little grandchildren (2-8 yrs old) had even eaten 2 bowls each

reviews.review_text: What more is there to say?! A fabulous recipe that was wonderful out of the pot and even better the next day after all the seasonings melded together. A can't-miss- recipe that I will make again and again not only for my family but for when I need to bring a meal to others. Thanks for posting! I agree with the posters who recommended using low-sodium bouillon and eliminating the thyme as it is likely already in the poultry seasoning (or you can try Recipe #23966). I would recommend chicken thigh meat or maybe a mix of thigh and breast meat as the breast meat sometimes gets too dry. Also, definitely stick with the medium or fine egg noodles ~~ the broad ones are too much.

Wonderful soup. I'm made other types of soup from scratch before but never chicken noodle, and I knew I could count on your recipe to be a home run, Mizz Nezz. Minor changes I made to this recipe were to use olive oil instead of butter for my lactose-intolerant hubby, and for a more savory soup I used a full bouillon cube and also a dash of red pepper flakes. Also, I did not have egg noodles, so I used cut spaghetti. The next time I make this soup, I'll nix the potato, as I don't think the recipe needs it with the pasta already included. Thank you for this easy recipe!

attributes.source_text: for a more savory soup

reviews.review_text: This is a very tasty soup.  Made this for my DM as she was "under the weather" and soup was just what she needed. I did not add the potato, and the celery was cut finely and I used pre julienned carrots, that I chopped up futher.  Knowing my DM preference regarding limited meats, I only used one chicken breast, flattened to and even thickness, and saute'd gently and cut in small bite size pieces.  I left out the thyme, per DM request to keep the spices to a minimum, but the soup was just really missing something.  Added the thyme and the taste was completely delicious!  Thanks MizzNezz for a delightful and easy meal!

My honey is sick today and requested I make some homemade soup. I don't usually follow recipes, rather just "throw it all in a pot until it looks right" but today I followed this one and it was Yummy!! (and easy.) I didn't have any premade stock in my pantry so I made my own with boiling water/bouillon. Also, I sauted the onion with minced garlic and omitted the celery. In place of cerlery I added green beans (frozen).  I was heavy handed with the poultry seasoning and thyme and the whole house smelled like heaven.  Thanks!

We were looking for a basic Chicken Noodle soup and found this one.  The addition of a potato is different from what we grew up on, but the thyme and poultry seasoning were exactly the flavorings needed to make this soup taste completely authentic.  Top that off with the fact that this goes together very quickly and without much effort - well, we loved it!  And have made it a number of times now.  The only change I made was to just dice the chicken and add it raw to the soup.  It still cooked well as the soup boiled and saved a little extra time.

I love soups, I love veggies, and I love lots of flavor.  Upon taste testing I found that there was entirely too much thyme for my picky husband.  In order to tone the thyme strength down a bit I did add additional chicken powder, season, and broth.  Had to use elbow noodles because I cannot find egg noodles. My 12 y/o and PICKY husband ate all of their soup! (husband has been known to toss dinner in the garbage)   I find that the longer the soup sits, the pasta soaks up all the liquid.  No problem.  I have more broth and seasonings to re-heat this soup for lunch tomorrow.  Thank you for this recipe.

attributes.source_text: PICKY husband ate all of their soup
My 12 y/o and PICKY husband ate all of their soup
re-heat this soup for lunch tomorrow

reviews.review_text:
The soup was good........but sorry, the thyme just put us off. I only added 1/2 tsp., but for us it was just too much. I am going to use the rest of the soup (without most of the broth) to make a chicken casserole. Maybe with a white sauce it will take down the thyme taste.
I know not everyone will agree with me, but this tasted so good as I made the soup, then after adding the thyme I couldn't figure out how to save it. I finally added some cream and it improved it enough that we ate it.
I will make this again......but no thyme ! The combination of veggies and broth was wonderful.
But for the thyme.....I would have rated this 5 stars.
Donna

I prepared this soup in a crockpot. I combined all the ingredients, except the noodles, and let them cook while at church. I then boiled the noodles and added them when we got home. It turned out well except we found the spices a bit overwhelming. Not sure if the longer time cooking would have made the difference or not but if I made it again I would definitely cut the spices at least in half. (We never could decide if it was the thyme or poultry seasoning or both that was so strong) I omitted the potato as my kids don't care for them.

Not only is this a GREAT soup it makes the house smell just like thanksgiving!!! This turned out just perfect and when DH comes home to taste this it is going to knock his socks off!!! I make my own chicken broth. (I save chicken bones from chickens that I have debonned) and boil them with a bunch of veggies and potatoes. When I strain it there is the most rich broth!!! When everything is in the pot I add some roasted garlic. Heaven is one word that comes to mind. My family thanks you and I thank you MizzNezz!!! You rock!!

attributes.source_text: the most rich broth
My family thanks you

items.label: Cracker Barrel's Hashbrowns Casserole - Copycat
items.name: Cracker Barrel's Hashbrowns Casserole - Copycat
items.description: I don't know if this is Cracker Barrel's actual hash browns casserole recipe, but it is close. This recipe can feed a large crowd and is good for a brunch.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and spray an 11 x 14 baking dish with cooking spray.
Mix the above ingredients together, place in prepared pan and bake for 45 minutes or until brown on top.

reviews.review_text: This recipe is (almost) the same one that my family has used for years!  It is a large batch and  great for gatherings. It is easy to throw together as well.   I accidentally left out the butter once and couldn't tell the difference, so I've been making it without the butter ever since.  I have used both shredded hash browns and country style hash browns with great success. I have also used a variety of cheeses, the substitution of about 1/4 cup of shredded parmesan cheese for the same amount of cheddar being one of my favorites.  Also, THAW the hash browns before you mix everything.  One of the most important things to make this recipe a success is to make sure that you stir the ingredients really, really well before you bake it.  In order to make this a 5 star recipe, I would follow my family secret and top the hash brown mixture with 3/4 of a cup of crushed corn flakes :).  I bake mine at 350 degrees for 30-40 or until the corn flakes are golden brown.  Delicious!!

attributes.source_text: great for gatherings

reviews.review_text: I've been making my own version of this since I saw something similar on the back of a bag of hash browns at the supermarket years ago, and I've also seen it made with Cream of Mushroom soup.  I leave out the soup altogether (most canned soups have gluten, which could kill my celiac diseased family),  substituting 1 cup (8oz.) sour cream, 1/3 cup buttermilk and 1 tsp gluten-free poultry seasoning.  I also use 2 tsp onion powder instead of chopped onion, add 1 tsp garlic powder, and I substitute 1/2 cup shredded Italian cheese mix (mozzerella, parmesan, romano) for 1/2 cup of cheddar.  Finally, I build the casserole in six layers- wet, potato, cheese, wet, potato cheese- and I top it off with gluten-free cornflakes.  This keeps the bottom layer of hashbrowns from burning, and ensures the wet ingredients and cheese are more evenly spread, while giving you a nice crust on the top.

attributes.source_text: giving you a nice crust on the top

reviews.review_text: I AM NOT A COOK.  I was forced to cook something for a holiday brunch at work and I didn't know what to do.  Googled "Best Hash Browns Casserole" and this recipe came up.  Read the reviews and comments and decided to give it a try.  I told my coworkers they had better have a back up plan just in case it didn't turn out:-).  I assembled it the night before (as suggested by one reviewer).  I chose to add 1/2 chopped red pepper and 1/2  chopped green pepper for color.  I took other suggestions and only used 1 cup of sour cream and 3 tablespoons of butter.  I sauteed the onions in 1/2 of a tablespoon of the butter and mixed the remaining 2 1/2 tablespoons with the cream of mushroom soup, sour cream, salt, pepper, sauteed onions, and peppers (as suggested by a reviewer).  I poured the mixture over the thawed hash browns and cheese and mixed thoroughly. I didn't have any cooking spray so I greased the dish with a little butter and evenly spooned the hash browns into the dish.  Placed in the refrigerator over night, took it out the next morning and let it get to room temperature before baking.  Baked at 350 and stirred after 30 minutes, as suggested.   I increased the temperature to 375 (looked extremely wet) and baked for another 30 - 45 minutes until it was golden brown.  Since it looked so good, I decided to just take it and have one of my coworkers do a taste test.  She couldn't stop saying how good it was and asked for the recipe. Needless to say, I brought home an empty dish:-).  Thank you.  Thank you.  Thank you.

attributes.source_text: for a holiday brunch at work
for a holiday brunch at work
I brought home an empty dish

reviews.review_text: I live in California :(  No Cracker Barrel's here, however, everytime we travel we route by a Cracker Barrel!  For me, it's this hashbrown casserole!  it's to die for.  Since we don't get to visit a Cracker Barrel all the time, my memory, is that this is sure darn close!  I have made this several times exactly as written and it's wonderful!  Today I just changed it up a bit, just for fun and thought I would share.  I used idahoan dehydrated hash browns from smart and final (3 cups) I had some bacon bits (the good kind from Costco) and added them, no idea how much, just added them, and I omitted the butter (that was hard to do, I add butter to everything) used jack and cheddar mixed (I shred my own....I think it tastes better than pre shredded, thank you food processor) and I swapped out the onion to 1 C of my Hubbys Onion Mixture  our home NEVER is without this in the fridge  Recipe 474468.  Oh and tried out the cream of mushroom soup.  So good!  As written or add stuff, Rhonda, this is a keeper, Thank you!

Loved this recipe, and so did all my little tasters.  I used 3 lbs of fresh, grated potatoes, which tend to turn brown pretty quickly.  And after grating it all, I squeezed out a lot of the excess water from them (just by hand).  I found I had to bake it for about an hour for the potatoes to fully cook - or perhaps just covering it for the 45 min would do the trick.  I also cut the butter in half (used 1/4 C) and mixed in 1 C of the cheese with the soup mixture, saving the other C for the top.  Since that all doesn't really seem to "pour," I mixed the potatoes into it and then transferred it all to the 9x13.  I only used about a 1/4 C of onions (since I don't care for onions that much).  This is so perfect for all those leftover potatoes you always have from larger meals. I can just freeze portions of this and heat them up when wanted. Great for breakfast or a side dish for dinner. But next time, I'm going to use my cuisinart for grating them.  :)

attributes.source_text: so did all my little tasters
Great for breakfast
a side dish for dinner

reviews.review_text: This is a recipe we have used for years--in fact I just made it last night.  I had to look up the base recipe because I hadn't made it in a while & was happy to find it here.  Great recipe, only for us it is a bit bland.  So the following are my amendments: first of all, I use Potatoes O'brien or just add diced onion & green pepper.  I cut the butter to 1/4 c., then I add about a tsp of Worcestershire sauce, 1/2 tsp or so of Rosemary, 1/4 tsp of Red Pepper flakes, & about 1/2 tsp of our favorite Steak seasoning (containing paprika, cumin, etc--a bit of paprika would probably work) & then to make it the main dish, I slice up a pound of smoked sausage.  Served with a nice salad & some crusty fresh bread & you have a lovely meal!

I have made this casserole three or four times now, and I always get many compliments and requests for the recipe. I have used cream of mushroom and cream of celery soup with the same great results. Like other reviewers mentioned, I have found that thawing the hashbrowns is a good idea, and omitting or using less margarine is fine. I used this recipe for a camping trip recently. I made up the casserole in a disposable foil pan and froze it (without baking). We then cooked it over our campfire. The casserole was still frozen when we cooked it, but our coals in our fire were quite hot. It took about 45 minutes to heat completely through. We stirred it about every 10 - 15 minutes to prevent the bottom from burning. It was the hit of the camping trip!

attributes.source_text: I used this recipe for a camping trip recently

reviews.review_text: This was just lovely - a spot on clone of Cracker Barrel's famous hashbrown casserole! It puzzles and frustrates me, however, that someone reviews a recipe, rather poorly at that, like Katchick, and does not even make the recipe as posted. When one alters it by using fresh potatoes (which turn brown and don't hold like a sulfited frozen potato) as well as cut out a significant amount of fat/fat- rich ingredients in a recipe (1 1/2 cups in this case) you will surely see and taste a difference. Hello. Better not to rate a recipe you change so drastically and end up not liking. Perhaps it was the changes that were made? Ya think? Makes no sense. Rhonda, you did a stellar job with this copycat recipe. If you are a fan of Cracker Barrel's famous recipe, you will not be disappointed. Thanks again for posting.

Made this for Christmas morning...everyone really liked it, but it was a tad dry by the time all of the gifts were opened.  I sprayed a 13X9 casselole dish with Pam; I too left the margarine out, and I sauteed the onions in about 2 tb. of butter before mixing with everything else.  I used part skim mozzarella and cheddar, reduced fat sour cream and regular no-name cream of chicken soup.  I took the advice of a previous reviewer and stirred the casserole half way through the cooking time, and cooked at 375 for a little over an hour.  Even with 6 adults, there was plenty left over as this dish is very filling.  Will definately make again with some additions such as bacon, sausage, different cheeses and soup.

attributes.source_text: Made this for Christmas morning

reviews.review_text: OMG!!! This is so close to the Cracker Barrel recipe and was so easy to make! I cut the recipe in half since I have a family of 4. I did not add the margerine because of previous reviews and because I am on the Weight Watchers program. I used fat free sour cream and 98% fat free soup. I cooked at 375 for 30 minutes the swiched it to broil for the last 10 minutes so the top would brown. The possibilities for this recipe is endless.....you could add pre cooked meats,add a variety of different cheeses, and even add peppers for a spicy taste. My whole family loved it and I will try to come up with a crockpot version for those days I have to work and don't want to cook. Thanks for posting this!

attributes.source_text: My whole family loved it

reviews.review_text: This was a flavorful, creamy hashbrown casserole but it did not come close to the Hashbrown Casserole at Cracker Barrel (unfortunately).  This is not a recipe for the calorie conscious with all the butter and sour cream but it is very creamy.  The one thing that I noticed is that the soup, sour cream, butter, and onion mixture is thick, and I had to spread it on top of the shredded potatoes.  The sauce did not move through to the bottom of the potatoes after baking, so next time I think I'm going to mix the potatoes with the cream mixture prior to putting it in the pan - mixing in some of the shredded cheese sounds like a good idea as mentioned by Joy1996.  Thanks for sharing your recipe!

attributes.source_text: This was a flavorful, creamy hashbrown casserole
but it is very creamy

reviews.review_text: I made the recipe exactly as written and I think next time I will take the advice of another reviewer and mix the hashbrowns together with the soup mixture before cooking.  The soup mixture didn't penetrate to the bottom of the dish and the hash browns on the bottom were a bit blah, but once i stirred it all together and put a little salt and pepper on it, i will say it was really good!  This will definately be a side dish in my house.  My son is very picky and won't eat anything that has a cream soup in it, and he had no idea there was soup in it. Thank you so much for a delicious recipe. I wouldn't change a thing except mix the ingredients together and then spread cheese on before cooking...yum!

attributes.source_text: This will definately be a side dish in my house
My son is very picky and won't eat anything that has a cream soup in it, and he had no idea there was soup in it

reviews.review_text: This is a delicious casserole dish! I made this for my husband who isn't typically crazy about potatoes and he ate 3 huge helpings! I cooked this at a bit of a higher temp and baked it long enough that it started getting crispy on top. I added some minced onion along with the diced onion. I don't think I added a full pint of sour cream...maybe 3/4 and I didn't realize until this morning that I forgot to put in any butter at all! To be honest, I don't think it needs it, I think it would have been greasy with all the cheese. I served this with grilled T-Bones and corn on the cob and the whole family ate more than one helping. Thanks for posting this, it is a definite keeper for us!

reviews.review_text: I worked at Cracker Barrel for several years when I was a student.  I worked in the gift shop and didn't ever think to get "the recipe" (most things came partially pre-prepared, anyway) I did eat it just about every day. :D  Anyway, this is very, very close to the real thing. How I do this:  I would suggest cutting back on the sour cream a little bit.  Also, they use COLBY cheese, not cheddar.  Add a little more onion and use a sweet white onion.  Use cream of celery soup (although I cannot attest to the chicken soup, as we make it vegetarian so our whole family can eat it.)  And mix that soup/butter/sour cream mixture into the potatoes instead of putting it on top.  Mix the cheese in, too.  If you eat at Cracker Barrel you will notice that the cheese is dispersed throughout the potatoes, not just on top.  Make sure to use plenty of salt and pepper. I brown mine in the broiler for a few minutes at the end of cooking to get it to have the same crispier texture that contrasts nicely with the rest of the softer, creamier potatoes.  The length of time that you cook this can make a big difference to the flavor.  It can even vary from restaurant to restaurant and even just depending on when you are eating there relative to when it was first prepared.  Longer times yield a softer potato with a nice crispy top...shorter times and the potatoes are firmer and the flavors just haven't melded as nicely.  For a fun variation, try adding some garlic, green onions and red pepper along with a couple of different cheeses.  Yum!

attributes.source_text: the same crispier texture

reviews.review_text: I don't know anything about how this compares to Cracker Barrel since I've never eaten there BUT I do know that this was some good grub. I made this to take to our Christmas potluck and it was excellent. I paid attention to all the suggestions in the reviews so I cut the sour cream in half, omitted the butter/margarine, thawed the hash browns first, added 2 pounds of cooked country sausage and baked at 375. This was to die for!! With all the dishes at dinner, there was a little bit leftover. I ate it last night and it was great heated in the micro for 2 minutes. I will definitely be adding this to my "go to" potluck recipe box. Thanks for posting and thanks to those that reviewed for their suggestions.

attributes.source_text: I made this to take to our Christmas potluck
I made this to take to our Christmas potluck

reviews.review_text: This is a really great tasting casserole! It may not have tasted exactly like Cracker Barrel's on the nose, it may have been BETTER! I tried a number of tricks from various suggestions with a few tweaks of my own and this was my plan: thaw the shredded-type hash browns, use only 1/4 cup margarine, use cheddar cheese soup, use only half of the sour cream (and I used fat-free), brown the onions first, and use fat-free cheddar cheese. I baked this about 15 minutes longer than called for. This was the most enthusiastic my saughter has ever been for a Zaar recipe! She came back for THIRDS! She loves this, and so does everyone else. Who needs Cracker Barrel? Thanks, Rhonda!

reviews.review_text: The first time I made this I made it exactly as directed, and I don't know how it compares to Cracker Barrel's as I've never had theirs, but the flavor was just okay. It was easy amd very creamy, but the sour cream flavor was overpowering and there wasn't much flavor otherwise. This time I subbed cream of mushroom for the cream of chichen and used the whole can of soup even though I halved the recipe; I cut the sour cream back to 3 oz to accommodate the extra soup. I also added an extra 1/2 cup of cheese and a clove of pressed garlic for personal preference, and about 2 ounces of cubed ham to make it a one-dish meal. It was really good this time. Thanks for sharing.

reviews.review_text: This was quite good. I thawed the hash browns before using and I mixed everything together except the cheese really well and then I stir in the cheese. This made it a lot easier to stir everything together. At first I thought there was too much butter but then I realized this kept the casserole from sticking to the dish and also browned up the top really nice. Even through supper was hours ago I keep going back to the kitchen for samples. It's only room temperature now but even tastes better now that it had a chance for all the flavors to meld together. Next time I will make this up in the morning to give it time to meld together and then bake it just before supper.

attributes.source_text: Even through supper was hours ago

reviews.review_text: Delicious! I have tried many versions of hash brown casseroles and this version was perfect for breakfast/brunch. Very creamy, not overpowering, and not too cheesy or heavy. My husband said it was very close to the restaurants version. I was afraid it would be too dry by not adding in extra liquid, but it came out perfectly. I did bake at 375 and for the last 10 minutes of cooking time I upped it to 400 to get a little browning on top. I didn't have cream of chicken, so I had to use cream of mushroom and added in a few dashes of chicken bouillon. It was great this way, but next time I will for sure make it with the cream of chicken to be more authentic. Thanks for the recipe!

attributes.source_text: perfect for breakfast/brunch

items.label: Pasta with Sausage, Tomatoes, and Cream
items.name: Pasta with Sausage, Tomatoes, and Cream
items.description: Delicious and satisfying... I don't remember where this recipe comes from, but it's a pleaser! Easily doubled.  Also, works well with gf pasta and sausage
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat.
Add sausage and crushed red pepper.
Cook until sausage is no longer pink, stirring frequently, about 7 minutes.
Add onion and garlic to skillet and cook until onion is tender and sausage is light brown, stirring occasionally, about 7 minutes.
Add tomatoes, cream, and salt.
Simmer until mixture thickens slightly, about 4 minutes.
(Can be prepared one day ahead. Cover and chill.).
Cook pasta in large pot of boiling water.
Drain.
Bring sauce to a simmer.
Add pasta to sauce and cook until pasta is heated through and sauce thickens, stirring occasionally, about 2 minutes.
Divide pasta between plates.
Sprinkle with parsley.
Serve, passing Parmesan separately.

reviews.review_text: I have been making this recipe for years with a few tweaks and I have to share them because honestly I think it makes the dish that much better. Use good quality canned whole tomatoes but instead of draining and dicing them, pour the whole can with the juices into a bowl and mash them with a potato masher until it resembles tomato sauce. This way it comes out with the texture of a spaghetti sauce with no big chunks of tomato for people who aren't fans (myself included). When you cook the sausage, break it into small pieces with a fork like you would with ground beef in spaghetti sauce. Once you cook the sausage with the red pepper flakes (don't skimp on them!), onion and garlic, add the tomato sauce and salt ( I also add 1/4 tsp black pepper) and simmer for 10 minutes on medium low heat. Then add 1/2 cup of heavy cream NOT 3/4 cup.. Trust me on this. Let that simmer for another 10 minutes. After this I put the sauce in Tupperware and refrigerate overnight.. It honestly tastes so much better when reheated the next day because all of the delicious flavors meld. The next day, reheat sauce in large pot and add drained pasta directly into pot. Stir to coat and serve immediately with lots of freshly grated Parmesan! Honestly guys this takes the dish over the top and I guarantee everyone will rave about it! My favorite recipe on food.com by far :)

attributes.source_text: with no big chunks of tomato

reviews.review_text: A simple, straightforward crowd-pleaser that's quick and easy to make and easy to modify according to pantry contents.  I browned ground chicken with honey and italian seasonings, swapped the italian plum tomatoes for cherry tomatoes and a can of regular whole tomatoes, added roasted red bell pepper, and added shredded monterey jack in lieu of the parmesan.  I wanted the cream sauce to reflect the sweetness of the tomatoes more, so I added some flour and a sprinkling of chicken bouillon granules to the juices that the canned tomatoes were packed in to ensure that the sauce wouldn't be thin or bland, and added this to the simmering sauce.  The entire thing was done at the same time the pasta finished cooking and the salad was made!  Regular rotation recipe for sure.

This was both super easy to make and really, really good.  I saw that the recipe only served 1-2 people, so I thought I should double it.  Once I got back from the grocery store, I just got lazy and put in the whole package of sweet italian sausages (which was 1.24 lbs instead of 1 lb), and used the whole 16 oz box of penne (instead of 12 oz). It wasn't that much more than the doubled recipe called for, but it ended up making enough food to feed at least 10 people.  Basically what I'm trying to say, is, that if you are making this recipe to feed a family, you don't need to double it unless you are feeding sumo wrestlers.  It makes way more than two servings, just as is.  Anyway, it was an awesome recipe and I will definitely make this again!

I gave this 3 stars. My 4 yr old newphew and I liked this dish. He said it was good so I gave it 3 stars. I like my dishes to have lots of flavor and I thought this was bland for my taste. I made this recipe as directed except I doubled the recipe and used whole tomatoes as I couldn't find plum tomatoes. I followed the suggestion of another reviewer that placed the sauce into a blender so I used my hand blender to crush the tomatoes. I don't think this affected the flavor but this made the sauce real thin. I cooked a 16oz box of penne to use in another dish and do to the sauce being so I thin I added all the cooked penne to the sauce. I followed suggestion of other reviews and I added 1/4 cup grated parmesan cheese into the sauce. I tasted it then added 1/4 a teaspoon basil, thyme, pepper. I added 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and I added a couple of sprinkles of cayenne pepper. This gave the sauce flavor but the cayenne pepper was a bit to spicy. When I make this again I will only add a sprinkle cayenne pepper. I will make this again as it is easy to make and when seasoned it good tasteing. Thanks for posting! Christine (internetnut)

reviews.review_text: **added note to previous 5star review:  i wanted to see if this dish would do well being made in a crockpot as i just got one to help me make dinners for my daughter and i while freeing up some time.  this can definitly be made in a crockpot, but the garlic should be sauteed in oil till cooked through first as i did not do that and it was soooo strong and turned green in color.  i also waited to add the cream until it was just ready to be served so that it didnt curdle.  so 5stars for in the crockpot as well.**i wanted to make this yesterday but as it was friday and lent i had to wait until today.  this was the first cream sauce i made and it was absolutly delicious and so very simple to make.  the only changes i made were using slightly hot sausage as i bought that by mistake and i was rushed so i didnt crumble and remove casings;i just cut up when it was partially cooked into small chunks.  this is a sauce that i can make once a week and wont tire of it!!!!!

Gets 5 stars because it's delicious, easy to make, a nice alternative to a red sauce pasta, a "flexible" recipe and enjoyed by both adults and kids.  Thank you for submitting! Followed the recipe mostly to a tee. Didn't have Italian Plum Tomatoes. Ended up using regular canned diced tomatoes and it worked out just fine. (Don't use the petite diced, though. Needed the larger pieces of tomato in there!) Also, I only had half a cup of cream, so used milk for the remainder. Again, was still yummy. I used a half spicy sausage and half sweet. Made the dish spicy enough to be enjoyed by my hubby and me, but not too spicy for the kids. You can always turn up the heat by adding more red pepper, if you like. I recommend using a noodle that takes on the sauce well: rotini, penne, ziti, bowtie... And make sure to cook the pasta al dente, then "let it rest" for 3-5 minutes in the sauce before serving. Great recipe! Has been added to the "Family Favorites" book of recipes. :)

reviews.review_text: This recipe was wonderful!!!!  I think this was the best recipe I've gotten off of this site so far!!!  My husband told me to put this recipe at the top of my list!!!  It was super easy to make and tasted fabulous!!!  When I was putting the leftovers in a dish, I thought to myself that 'I cannot wait to eat this tomorrow' (and I am not a leftover person).  My grandparents make homemade Italian sausage all of the time and I get tired of eating it.  This recipe gives me a great alternative and we will make this often!!!  I think I might try adding some fresh basil next time but it was great as it was!  I would recommend putting the pot on to boil first thing.  The sauce cooked a lot faster than I thought and I had to wait for the pasta to cook.  We loved this recipe!!!!  A total winner!!!!  Thank you for posting!!!!

reviews.review_text: WOW! Deeeeeelicious! I doubled the recipe and we have plenty for lunch tomorrow. This recipe deserves more than 5 stars - easy recipe, easy directions, clean up a snap, and chock full of flavor! I had everything on hand, too so no need to run to the store. I used sundried tomato and basil sweet sausage. I didn't have heavy cream so I made my own (3/4 c. skim milk and 1/3 c. melted butter and 1 tsp of flour = 1 c. cream). I had Rigatoni on hand and cooked it al dente (~ 12 oz). My 6 year old ate it up and said she wants this everyday! LOL. She's getting some for lunch tomorrow, as will I. She wants me to make this when we go to Myrtle Beach next week. I think our friends are going to LOVE this too. Thanks for posting...this is a keeper!!! - Also, this recipe (doubled) easily could feed 6 to 8 people.  My serving size is 1 cup for this recipe.  Served with a nice garden salad and a side of veggies (steamed zucchini), you don't need more than a cup of this pasta (although it's too tempting not to go back for seconds.)  Just read some reviews and I'm SHOCKED people are complaining it lacked in flavor or was bland.  My DH is as picky as they get, and he oooh'd and awwww'd about the GREAT flavor this dish had.  I didn't have to make any adjustments.

reviews.review_text: An incredibly quick, easy and delicious pasta dish.  I had some Italian turkey sweet sausage in the freezer that I wanted to use up and this was perfect. Other than that substitution, I followed the instrustions exactly.  For the pasta, I used the remainder of a bag of campanelle noodles ( just about 6 oz).  When I was folding the pasta into the sauce, I thought it was a little dry, but then again, I didn't know if this pasta was supposed to have a lot of sauce or if it just barely coated the noodles. I was tempted to add more cream but did not.  I am glad I didn't.  It was just perfect.  My BF and I both really thought it was terrific change from our regular spaghetti.  I think next time I will add in a little of the liquid from the tomatoes and add just a touch more red pepper flakes.  We both had a big bowl and there is still enough for 2 more servings.  Just a terrific pasta dish!  We enjoyed it with Recipe #18914... Thanks for a keeper!

items.label: Kittencal's Easy and Delicious Ranch-Parmesan Chicken
items.name: Kittencal's Easy and Delicious Ranch-Parmesan Chicken
items.description:
There are plenty versions of this recipe, this is mine and can be on your table in less that an hour, my family loves this chicken! --- the ranch dressing is the secret it holds in all the flavor and moistness while the chicken is baking and also adds flavor, I find that Hidden Valley Ranch dressing works the best but Kraft or any other brand will do, I sometimes top the baked chicken with mozzarella cheese or cheddar, but that is optional --- although I have only made this using breasts I imagine that chicken pieces could be used although you would have to increase the breadcrumb mixture slightly, you can marinate the chicken breast in the ranch dressing for a few hours in the fridge, although you will need more than 1 cup of dressing if you are marinating .... *NOTE* to avoid a soggy bottom crust, place the chicken breasts onto a flat rack on top the baking sheet, also it is important not to bake the chicken in a small baking pan, if you do not have a rack bake on a large baking sheet so any juices in the pan will spread out and not accumulate under the chicken causing a soggy bottom ---------------
FOR LOW-FAT OPTION: use low-fat Ranch dressing and omit the melted butter on top or use a healthy butter alternative such as Smart Balance 50/50 blend.
instructions: Set oven to 400° degrees (set oven rack to lowest position).
In a shallow bowl mix together the dry breadcrumbs with Parmesan cheese, seasoned salt, black pepper and garlic powder.
Dip the chicken into the ranch dressing to coat both sides (allow any excess to drip off).
Coat in the breadcrumb mixture.
Place in a single layer onto a greased baking sheet or line with non-stick foil (do NOT bake in a smaller baking dish or the bottom of the chicken will be soggy).
Lightly drizzle the melted butter over each breast (for low-fat option omit the butter or use a diet alternative).
If desired you can sprinkle black pepper over the chicken pieces       .
Bake uncovered for about 30-35 minutes or until the chicken is cooked).

reviews.review_text: The firs time, I made this recipe exactly as directed and it was delicious. Hubby and I really liked it, although Hubby said it it was not *quite* as good as his favorite, Kittencal's Moist Cheddar-Garlic Oven Fried Chicken Breast (Recipe #82102). It was simple and quick to prepare, and cleanup was a snap with the tinfoil. <br/><br/>I've made this a few times since then and I haven't changed the ingredients, just the prep. Three tips I would suggest to make this top-notch:<br/><br/>1) Even on the bottom oven rack on a cookie sheet, it still got slightly soggy. Now I bake it on a rack over the cookie sheet. The cleanup is not as quick, but it gives us that crispy crust we were craving. <br/><br/>2) Use high-quality ingredients - it really makes a difference. Use good chicken breasts, not those cheap frozen ones. Consider grating your own Parmesan and use a nice aged one. Make your own Ranch dressing. The bottled kind is just too sweet. And lastly, use a bread crumb that will help with the crispy factor. Panko is a nice choice but the herbs in an Italian bread crumb mix really bring the flavor up a notch, so if you use Panko, I would add some Italian herbs yourself.<br/><br/>3) Do not overcook the chicken. I can't stress this enough. Keep checking it and remember that it will continue to cook when you take it out. You should let it rest for a few minutes before serving to allow the juices to move from the surface back into the flesh. <br/><br/>Thanks, Kittencal! Your recipes are always 5 stars in my book!

reviews.review_text: You don't need another review to tell you this is good, do you? (LOL!) I was looking for a quick and easy way to do boneless, skinless breasts tonight for dinner (I HATE boneless, skinless ...!!) Fortunately I found this easy and tasty one, which I could shove into the oven! I didn't have the real US Ranch dressing, but had a creamy one very similar to that. It worked like a charm, and I'm afraid I used more butter than you stipulated ... I meant to drain off the extra fat, but after a while in the warming oven the meat had absorbed the sizzling butter! (ROFL!! Cholesterol levels and all that!!) My seasoning salt was a local one simply called "Cook Salt by Melissa", which contains sea salt, finely crushed coriander seeds, chilli pepper and ... something else, can't remember. I would have preferred battering the breasts with a meat mallet, which always makes them more tender, but my meat mallet has disappeared. Anyway, Kittencal, the breasts were great. To go with it I made plain cooked carrots with a little fine cumin, plain boiled potatoes and, I confess, frozen creamed spinach. Thanks for a really quick, delicious main dish!!!
