items.label: Yummy Crunchy Apple Pie
items.name: Yummy Crunchy Apple Pie
items.description: Make and share this Yummy Crunchy Apple Pie recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Use foil on bottom of oven rather than a cookie sheet under pie pan.
Prepare pastry for single-crust pie.
Place in pie plate and trim and crimp the edge; refrigerate 30 minute loosely covered with plastic wrap.
In a large mixing bowl, stir together the sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, and salt.
Add apple slices and gently toss until they are coated well.
Transfer mixture to pie.
FOR CRUMB TOPPING: Stir together brown sugar, flour, and oats.
Using a pastry blender, cut in the butter until topping resembles coarse crumbs.
Sprinkle over apple mixture in pie.
To prevent over-browning while baking, cover edge of pie with foil.
Bake at 375 degrees Fahrenheit for 25 minutes.
Remove foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes more, or until top is golden.
Remove from oven.
Cool on wire rack about an hour and serve!

reviews.review_text: Apple pie is DH's favorite and he's always begging for them.  according to him though "real apple pies have a top crust" so i've been putting off making this.  well, he wanted a pie and i only had a single pre-made crust (i have a horrible record w/ pie crusts, i just buy them :oops:) so i made this one and all the sudden i hear "i never said any such thing, you have to make this pie again!" go figure... i only needed 3 large granny smith, used my old fashioned apple peeler/corer so they were sliced pretty thin, and i upped the cinnamon to a whole tablespoon per DH's preference.  didn't need all of the topping, it was very heaped up after i got everything in the crust and i was worried it'd slide off in the oven, but it came out perfectly.  the pie settled after i took it out of the oven and was gorgeous.  i used a mexican caramel topping (cajita maybe?) and skipped the nuts - pure lazyness on my part.  next time i'll add the nuts to the crumb topping and make all else the same.  this pie is fantastic! I'm going to make 4-5 for thanksgiving so everybody can have 2nds which i KNOW they'll want.  thanks for such a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: Apple pie is DH's favorite and he's always begging for them
i never said any such thing, you have to make this pie again!

reviews.review_text: I am not going to rate this as I had changed the original recipe drastically...but I did use it as a guide.  I had used some fresh apples off of my friend's tree and some Granny Smith.  I made my own pie shell using JackieOhNo!'s Recipe #320803.  I took into account other comments regarding how sweet the filling and toppings were, so I cut the filling down to 1/4 cup sugar.  The topping I changed to 2/3 cup brown sugar, 1/4 tsp salt and 6T butter and kept the rest the same.  I used my Recipe #368718 for the final topping and omitted the pecans.  Although the other apple I used was tart, it was soft and didn't hold up against the Granny Smith, so the pie flattened out somewhat.  But that did not diminish from the taste.  As my DH grew up on different pies, he loved this one, so I would do this one again, with my changes!!!

attributes.source_text: my DH grew up on different pies, he loved this one

reviews.review_text: I've made this so many times, I can't even count them!  This is my GO-TO pie for all occasions! I've made it for gatherings, for parties, for gifts, and for contests!  (It's won three contests-best apple pie, best apple product, and best pie overall!  It also took third in a recent contest...I can't remember which one, though) I actually keep small containers in my spice cabinet marked "apple pie" and it has the sugar, flour, cinnamon, and salt already together for even easier preparation...if it can be easier!  I've made it with and without the caramel, and it tastes great either way.  My favorite is the crumb topping...it is just such a wonderful, buttery crisp flavor that melts in your mouth!  I've also tried leaving the skins on and off to see if that would make a difference-I find the texture to be better without the peel, actually, but taste-wise it really doesn't make much of a difference.  I love warming it in the oven a bit before serving and then placing a big scoop of vanilla ice cream with a slice of pie on a bowl!  yumyumyum!!!  Thank you so much for a great recipe!!!

for parties

reviews.review_text: I always considered myself a good cook, but not a great baker until I made this pie!  It is absolutely perfect!!!  It is the first pie that I made that actually was totally devoured.  Since I don't bake that much I did use Pillsbury's Pie Crust and baked it for 5 minutes in a 350 degree oven first and used MacIntosh apples instead of Granny Smith because we just went apple picking with the kids and had a ton :).  Other than that, the only other thing I used differently was instead of regular cinnamon I used Pampered Chef's Cinnamon Plus (lots of parties I went to :)) and sprinkled some on top of the crumb topping before baking as well.  Anyone who loves pecan pie would also love this recipe.  So many people thought that it was a pecan pie with apples because of the consistency. The only other note I would mention is that you should completely cool the pie before cutting.  My husband couldn't wait to get into it while it was still warm and it oozed out a bit, but the cooled pie was absolute perfection. Great Recipe Wendy...10 stars!!!

attributes.source_text: My husband couldn't wait to get into it

reviews.review_text: Made two MORE of these for our Thanksgiving feast (11/07)and SAD to report that there are NOT enough leftovers--and we want MORE!!!!   This is so good, I wish I could give you TEN stars:  * * * * * * * * * *  Hosted a 4-H Food Project meeting at my home earlier today (October 07)  --featuring "Fall Produce"... so I had six kids learning how to make a light-n-flakey pie crust, and THIS was one of the fillings we made, too.  I can't comment on the taste, since the girl took it home to her family, but I really WISH I could've tasted it...it looked beautiful--and the smell was exquisite!   We didn't add The Final Topping mainly because I didn't have pecans or caramel topping....however the young lady used cookie cutters of acorns & leaves to add to the crust/edging...with a egg-water wash & a sprinkle of baker's sugar crystals---it looked BEAUTIFUL!!!   Thanks, Wendy N, for a GREAT recipe.   I will be making this for my OWN family to try, too.

attributes.source_text: for our Thanksgiving feast

reviews.review_text: This is wonderful - seemingly sinful.  I had a guy tell me apple pie was his favorite, so in an attempt to impress him, I made him this recipe.  I'd never made an apple pie before,  but you gotta figure 240 or so 5 star reviews, everyone can't be wrong!  I made it, wasn't too hard, just peeling the apples was kind of a pain.  I think probably the canned apples might be a good quick substitute.  I also used the premade crust Pillsbury so that I could give it away in an aluminum pie pan.  I made two pies at the same time with 9 cups of cut up apples mixing gala and granny smith.  They went in as heaping pies, and even after cooling were something mounded.  My feeling is I probably could have used less apples.  But, they were awesome and gave one to my friend who absolutely loved it.  This definitely is a five-star and award winner at that!  Thanks so much for sharing your granny's recipe, Wendy N!  It's great!

reviews.review_text:
oh, WOW! apple pies have always been a specialty of mine, but this one really knocked it out of the park!! i made one for my neighbor who is elderly, and has confessed to me that she doesn't bake, and one for my friend's parents as a thank-you gift. they are PHENOMENAL! i used a mix of actually four different apples (fuji, gala, golden delicious, and granny smith), and the melange of flavors was amazing. i also added a squeeze or two of maple syrup to the apple mixture, which, for me, enhances the moisture of the pie. thank you so much, as i WILL be bringing a double batch to the thanksgiving family dinner! DEFINITELY five stars!
****post-thanksgiving UPDATE***literally, honestly the FIRST dessert to go. with nearly 20 eaters, this pie didn't have a chance! i had to make another, on the spot..seriously!

OUTSTANDING!  This pie was so very easy, had a scrumptious flavor, and looked beautiful.  What more could you want? I used a purchased deep-dish pie shell, which I baked 5 minutes before adding the apple mixture, to help keep it crisp.  
I made a few small additions: added 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg, 1/8 teaspoon ground allspice, and an additional tablespoon of flour to apple mixture.  I also used winesap/staymen apples because those were the ones I had on hand. I absolutely loved the Crumb Topping, which was much easier than a top crust. I omitted the Final Topping, as it didn't need it for my family. This pie is definitely a keeper and will find a permanent place in my cookbook.

reviews.review_text: I printed this recipe off on 10/11/2007. As of today I have made it 4 times. I make catered desserts for a small local pumpkin patch and this pie has been selling like hotcakes! Everyone says it is absolutely delicious but I'll have to take their word for it - I've never even gotten a crumb. The last 2 pies I made, I increased the ingredients by 50% and baked in a 9" springform pan to have an impressive piece of deep dish pie. This is a keeper - hopefully one day I'll try it for my family. They drool whenever I make one.  Edited to add that I finally got to make one of these for my family and now I know what all the raves are about.  This pie is delish made exactly as stated in the recipe.  Wouldn't ever change a thing.

attributes.source_text: I finally got to make one of these for my family

reviews.review_text: Delicious and so easy!  This was the perfect hybrid of apple crisp and apple pie.  I made this yesterday, and my only regret is making just one pie.  You can prepare in advance the filling (except apples) and topping (except cutting in butter) for a speedy assembly. I used a Pilsbury pie crust.  I peeled granny smith apples and cut slices thickly rather than thin.  I put about 2/3 of the topping on it and patted down firm, then put the rest of the topping on and patted down lightly.  When the pie is ready to serve, take your time cutting the pieces and carefully placing on serving plates to retain the proper pie-piece shape.

I can certainly see why this pie has over 200 reviews.  It is fantastic!  I made this to take to work, in fact I made two for work, and they were devoured.  Everyone loved them.  When my son saw the pies I made to take to work, he insisted that I make one that "we can eat".  So I made my 3rd pie for us.  I made exactly as recipe stated, using my own pie crust recipe,
Never Fail Pie Crust Recipe #68859   Only I did peel my apples, that is the way we prefer.  The smell was wonderful, and the taste even better. I highly recommend the caramel topping. I think this tasted even better the second day.  I will now use this recipe when I make apple pies from now on.  Thank you and (and your grandma) for this incredible tasting pie!

Amazing pie!!!  Would give way more than 5 stars if I could!!  I made two pies, but realized part way through that I was nearly out of brown sugar, so I was able to make the amount of crumb topping for one pie and split it between the two, and didn't feel like it was skimping at all.  I used 4 Granny Smith apples for each pie and they piled high!  I peeled and sliced them fairly thin, but think I will try thicker slices next time for chunkier bites!  I also left off the pecans as we don't prefer them, but I'm sure they would just add to the experience for pecan lovers.  This was an incredible pie!!  Thank you!!  I will be making this for special occasions from now on and just to show DH how much I love him!!

Fabulous pie! I used brown sugar in the filling and also added a teaspoon of vanilla. My apples were Cortlands, fresh picked from the tree in my yard. They are a jucier apple than Granny Smiths, so next time I think I'd add a bit more thickener. I peeled my apples and cut them in small chunks. Baked the pie for the first 30 minutes on the lowest rack and then moved it up to the next notch for the second 30 minutes. I used a stoneware pan for baking. My caramel topping was Mrs. Richardson's Butterscotch Caramel--I prefer it because it is not as runny as some brands. My family really enjoyed this pie and are already asking for more. Thanks, Wendy!

attributes.source_text: My family really enjoyed this pie

reviews.review_text: Very very nice apple pie!  Had some apples that needed to be used up, they tasted terrible.  So, I'm saying let's make a pie to my daughter and off we go.  However, dh comes in and says noooo don't use those they are terrible and will make the pie terrible, grumble grumble.  Daughter and I continue with our original plan and tell dh if it tastes so bad don't eat any.  Well we made it and I fully intended to put some sliced almonds on top instead of the pecans, as that is what i had on hand.  But totally forgot about it due to my daughters excitement about putting on the caramel.  Well thank goodness she only put it on hers and later when she said it was "a tad sweet"  I said sure it was due to half the jar of caramel on your one piece dear :)  All said, it turned some lousey apples into a mighty fine piece of pie.  Even dh had to admit it was good, since he ate almost half of it.  I will fix this again :) cutting down on the brown sugar, maybe only 3/4 a cup.  Thank you for posting this wonderful keeper WendyN!

I doubled it so I made 2 pies. My 2 teenage sons and husband loved it too. The topping is amazing. I bought a Pillsbury-Ritz deep dish pie crust. items.label: Crock Pot Taco Soup
items.name: Crock Pot Taco Soup
items.description: Make and share this Crock Pot Taco Soup recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Cook meat and drain.
Shred if needed.
Add all ingredients to crock pot.
DO NOT DRAIN CANS.
Stir.
Cook on high for 2 hours or low for 4 hours.
Keep on low until serving to keep hot.
Garnish with sour cream, shredded cheese, chopped green onions, or tortilla chips.

reviews.review_text:
This soup has an awesome authentic snappy taco flavor.I started off by seasoning six chicken thighs(bone in)with salt, pepper,oregano,
all season salt,onion powder and garlic powder.I browned the chicken thighs in a stockpot. I then covered them with water and boiled till fall apart tender.I then combined the remaining ingredients together in my crockpot. I used Bushes light red kidney beans and omitted the extra can of green chiles ( the rotel had plenty for me). I also used hunts petite diced tomatoes.I found that it wasn't soupy enough for me, so after the chicken was cooked and shredded, I just poured about a cup of the chicken juices into the crockpot.I cooked it for two hours on high. I went an extra step and made my own tortilla chips. I did this by cutting corn tortillas into strips and deep frying them in wesson conola oil. I then seasoned the chips with all season salt(while still hot).I put garnishes, such as; shredded cheddar cheese, sour cream, chopped green onion and of course the fresh tortilla chips in dishes and let my family choose their own. Let me tell you my kids loved it and each had 4 bowls apiece. They raved about it all night. Thanks, Lubie, for the awesome soup recipe.

attributes.source_text: boiled till fall apart tender
my kids loved it

reviews.review_text: i'm giving this a 5* rating even though i made several changes.  i used what i had on hand - 1can pintos, froz corn, can diced tom, 2lbs ground venison.  tossed in extra fresh veggies - celery, red & green bell pepper and cabbage.  didn't have any taco seasoning mix but i always make it up from scratch so that's what i did here. i was very hesitant to add the ranch mix (i like ranch fine but have a thing about putting it in most foods) but i went ahead and i'm glad i did.  can't tell it's in there but gives it a little something and makes it taste great.  not even close to watered down chili which is what i was a little worried about.  added some fresh garlic, beef base and extra water since i didn't have all the canned juices and threw in a soda can sized V8 juice to use it up.  it's not done cooking yet and it still tastes wonderful, can't wait for dinner! plan on serving w/ cheese, sour cream, scallions, and lots of jalapenos to spice things up for me and DH.  Maybe some cornbread, toasted tortillas, or chips on the side. This is definitely going on my regular rotation, thanks Lubie for a keeper!

reviews.review_text: Admittedly, I was skeptical of this recipe. A soup that doesn't start with water or broth? One that relies almost entirely on canned ingredients? I feared that the soup would turn out bland, but I decided to bite the bullet and try it anyway.<br/><br/>BEST. DECISION. EVER. Much to my surprise, it wasn't bland at all (although I may add a bit of cayenne next time, to give it more of a kick). I used 1 lb. of ground beef, which I browned on the stove before adding it to the soup. I didn't bother seasoning the meat while browning it. Turns out the soup has enough flavor to make up for it. <br/><br/>Some people here mentioned that the meat gets lost amongst the other ingredients - I didn't find that to be the case, but to each her own. It'd be awesome with chicken, too.<br/><br/>Didn't have pinto beans, so I substituted red kidney beans. Slow cooked it for four hours on low, mixed in some shredded cheese and sour cream, and now I don't have to worry about dinner for (at least) the next few days! Hooray!

Add another 5 stars from my husband and I to make 395. This recipe rocks!! The only thing I did different was to use Freezer Corn #68968 instead of the canned corn. It was the last bag of the batch, so it had a little more juice in it than the other bags. I turned my crock pot on and put the corn in frozen, then fried 1 1/2 lbs. of hamburger with dried onions. When it was done and still hot I put it on top of the frozen corn, added the rest of the ingredients and when I stirred it, the corn was thawed. The garnishes made it even better, especially the chips. We put this in our slow cooker at setting 3 1/2 for 2 hours and it was very flavorful. (We couldn't wait the extra 2 hours!) Thanks so much for sharing. My husband said you better not lose that recipe! ;-)

reviews.review_text: I have made this recipe several times now and its about time I'll review it! I have made this recipe with ground beef, turkey ground meat and chicken - it always has been awesome! I have to mention that I do not add the green chilies as we don't like the spicy dishes. I have served it garnished with sour cream and tortilla chips. Its a easy dish to prepare and put together in the crock pot. The only thing I struggle with is that I don't make this dish since I am gone for almost 10 hours a day when working and this recipe does not need that much time in the crock pot. So most times I will make it when its late on a Saturday evening and I cook it on high - two hours later - VOILA. Or I made it on a late Sunday morning for a lunch dish. Either way, this dish won't disappoint in taste, easy preparation and awesome leftovers!

reviews.review_text: Wowww, Lubie! This soup was amazing! Hubby loved it too, and had 2 big servings. Still was saying how good it was several hours after dinner. I used dry pinto beans which I soaked overnite, for the white beans I used cannellini, and frozen corn. I also used extra homemade taco seasoning from zaar recipe. (love the heat) I didn't add the ranch dressing mix, (didn't have any) but will try it next time. I also used ground beef. Had to add about a cup of tomato sauce and a cup of water just to thin out a little, but not too thin. (we like it a little thick) Simmered on stovetop in my dutch oven for about 5 hours. We had chopped lettuce, finely shredded cheddar cheese and sour cream for the topping on our soup. Served on the side, sweet yellow cornbread and tortilla chips. Hubby added lightly crushed tortillas to his boul in second helping. Since there is only the 2 of us, and this made alot I was able to freeze 2 qt size freezer bags, which will be 2 more heaping meals. This was definately a 5 star recipe! This was so easy, and with ingredients I always have on hand. Will be making this again many times. Thanks so much Lubie, for posting such a Great recipe.....carmen

I also used 3 pounds of chicken breast.  I "made" it the day before, heating it thoroughly, then left it in the fridge overnight, hoping the flavors would enhance even more.  And surely, they did!  The next day, I took it out of the fridge, and simmered on low for about 2 hours until it was thoroughly heated.  I made this in a HUGE 16 quart stockpot, which was very full.  I served about 35 people, and we had sides of a variety of bread.  Thanks so much Lubie for making me look good!  This one is a keeper!

Can't say enough good things about this recipe, it's a great meal for cold weather. It's very versatile, being able to add/subtract/exchange ingredients as one wishes. items.label: Pizza Dough for Thin Crust Pizza
items.name: Pizza Dough for Thin Crust Pizza
items.description: Note:This is one of the recipes I adopted in the Great 'Zaar Ophan Adoption of 2005. I hope you enjoy it.
instructions: Mix a little sugar into the warm water.
Sprinkle yeast on top.
Wait for 10 minutes or until it gets all foamy.
Pour into a large bowl.
Add flour, salt, olive oil.
Combine.
Knead for 6-8 minutes until you have a moderately stiff dough that is smooth and elastic (add a bit more flour if you need to).
Cover and let rest for 20-30 minutes.
Lightly grease two 12-inch pizza pans.
Sprinkle with a little bit of cornmeal.
Divide dough in half.
Place each half on a pizza pan and pat it with your fingers until it stretches over the whole pan.
Try to make it thicker around the edge.
If desired, pre-bake at 425 F for 10 minutes (I don't always do this).
Then spread with pizza sauce and use the toppings of your choice.
Bake at 425 F for 10-20 minutes longer or until bubbly and hot.
Makes 2 12-inch pizzas.
If you don't want to use all the dough, you can freeze it.
Take a portion of dough, form into a ball, rub olive oil over it and place it in a freezer bag (the oil makes it easier to take out of the bag).
When you want to make a pizza, take dough out of freezer and allow to thaw before using.

reviews.review_text: I think I found my new thin crust pizza dough recipe.  I think I pre-baked for a bit too long.  Next one I'll try without pre-baking.  Nice crisp crust that held all the topings really well.  I used 1 cup of ww flour, 2 1/4 tsp of bread machine yeast and 1/2 tsp of salt.  Oh, and I used my breadmaker which has rise time included in the timer.  Once it was ready, I punched down, split in two balls, lightly greased the balls and let them rise again while I got my toppings ready.  I rolled into a circle with a rolling pin.  I should have pierced the top of the dough a bit as I got some air bubbles, but no big deal.  Great recipe.  Update: 12/28/08 - I've used this recipe to make mini pizzas.  I rolled out the dough as thin as I could get it and used cookie cutters to make trees and stars for Xmas.  I poked them all well with a fork, pre-baked, then brushed them with garlic butter and sprinkled Parmesan and then let them bake a little longer.  I've also made single serve size pizzas, cooked them in a frying pan about 1 -2 min per side, let cool and then flash froze, so I always have some ready to go pizza crusts.

reviews.review_text: This is the thin crust pizza recipe I've been lookg for...forever!  I used:  1 c. WW flour, 1/2 tsp. salt, 1T. sugar, and 2 full tsp. of instant yeast.  I didn't proof the yeast, just whisked the dry ingredients together in the bowl.  I added the water and oil, then kneaded it for 8 minutes, adding flour by the T. until the dough was just barely sticky.  I let it rest for 15 min. while the oven preheated.  Then, I divided the dough, and rolled each half out on a well floured slippat baking mat.  As I rolled it, i continued to peel it back, and let it shrink, turning it, and adding more flour to the mat, as needed.  I stopped peeling/rolling when the dough no longer shrank back much from the size of the slippat.  I, then, rolled it just over the edges one more time, and turned it onto a greased and cornmealed baking sheet.  I pre-baked the crusts for 10 min., then topped and baked for another 10 min.  The crusts were gorgeous!  It was crisp, yet tender and held up well even in the middle.  This recipe is a keeper!  : )

reviews.review_text: I used this recipe for my pizza last night and I was not disappointed. The crust was crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. Instead of making 2 pizzas, I just rolled out one really big pizza (I think it was about 17"/18" in diameter) that was neither too thick nor too thin, and it took my oven about 12 - 15 mins on 220*C to bake it just right. I like the fact that the crust did not sag under all the toppings I heaped on it and even the leftovers taste good reheated. I did add 2 tbsp of milk powder and 1 tbsp of oregano to the dough, and I increased the salt to 1/2 tsp, since I felt 1/4 tsp would be too little. I can't find yeast sachets around here so I used 2 tsp of active dried yeast. I guess the brand of all-purpose flour I used wasn't all too absorbent so I had to add about 1 1/2 tbsp of flour while kneading. Next time, I'll divide the water into 3/4 and 1/4 cups and add the yeast to the 3/4, using the 1/4 a little at a time, if I need it. I think I'll make this again this weekend... maybe double the quantity (I prefer making just one x-large pizza at a time) and freeze half the dough. Might even try mini pizzas for when we have company over and their kids get ravenous. TY for posting, UC86.

As far as dough goes, this was by far the best overall and easy recipe (if you have a Kitchen Aid) however; I give it 4 stars because the crust (to me) needs a teeny bit more flavor. Used 2 cups bread flour and 1/2 cup WW.
I used my stand mixer - put in the water, then the "little bit of sugar" (1 tsp - is what I used because that seems to work for activating a yeast packet to 1 cup of warm water). Did have to add more flour because it was a little sticky but, did it by the tsp - easy. Put it on our cast stone and baked it first for about 5 minutes - IMPORTANT - if you do this, you must use "score" your dough (either with a utensil or fork) to keep it from rising up - we didn't at first and saw the dough puff up like pita!
All in all, once of the best I have made - nice and crispy, QUICK, and really pliable. Just if you need/like flavor, I suggest you add herbs, salt, etc. Very happy to find this recipe - just like all others, you have to make it your own.

reviews.review_text: Goes together easily. I opted for the cup of wheat flour and kneaded the dough and let it rise in my bread machine. If I make this again, I would try roasted garlic olive oil in it because I think it would add to the flavor which was very neutral which is nice in a way because it would go with a lot of different sauces and toppings, but the flavor just wasn't really anything special for all the rave reviews. It has a very crispy texture, maybe a little too crispy. I think either the cooking time is too long or the oven temp is too high as I tried pre-baking as directed in step 14 the first time I tried this, and the dough was basically done (very done in a couple of spots where the dough was stretched a little thinner - so I turned the oven down a bit after I put the toppings on), but as nobody else seems to have had that problem, maybe it's just my oven. Thanks for sharing anyway.

reviews.review_text: The first pizza I made with this is the one I uploaded the picture of. It had pepperoni, black olives, green bell peppers, a 4 Italian cheese blend, portabella mushrooms, and marinara sauce. I baked it to what I thought was done (13 minutes) and YUCK, I thought "how could anyone give this 5 stars, maybe I didn't bake it long enough" The next night I tried again with Grilled chicken, portabella mushrooms, alfredo sauce, green bell peppers and bacon and baked it longer (18 minutes) MMM!! OMG!! MMMM!! I screwed up on the bake time on the first one and totally messed it up because this crust is excellent. I was very nervous because this was my first "from scratch pizza crust" but it was very easy. Something to keep in mind, that messed me up on the first crust is that the cornmeal will make the crust look browned before it's done. Make sure your crust is crunchy before pulling your pizza out of the oven.

After 2nd raise I flattened it out and let it rest for 20 min covered.  Then I started shaping and rolled it out on pizza stone with cornmeal.  I prebaked for 12 min then put on the toppings. I use this recipe all the time to make pizza.  My husband refuses to allow me to order delivery or even the frozen variety anymore, and really, why would you want to when you can save money while maximizing flavor?!

I made five pizzas for my son's birthday party using this recipe, and the raves were declared for hours.

The only alterations I make is to season the flour with garlic powder, garlic salt, oregano, basil, and marjoram.

This also freezes really well.  When I made my pizzas for the party, I actually assembled the entire pie, wrapped it in plastic wrap, and placed the pie directly in the freezer.  When I was ready to cook them, I let them thaw, then baked them at 450 degrees for about 25 minutes.  I was concerned about the moisture content from freezing them, but cooking them at a slightly higher temperature solved that, and the pizzas were nothing but a grand slam with the crowd!

Awesome recipe!

I made this last night. This is PERFECT and we were so pleased with it. I had my usual trouble with measuring the yeast, but only because I buy the bulk instant yeast and the recipe is written for the little packets. My general rule of thumb is 1 teaspoon of instant rise yeast per cup of flour, so I used 1 and a half teaspoons for this recipe and it was perfect. I used my bread machine to make the dough, and the dry/wet measurements you cited were so perfect that I didn't have to tinker with it at all, which was a welcome surprise. Oh, and I also added a scant teaspoon of sugar, to ensure a good rise from the yeast. I baked my crust on the top rack for about seven minutes at 425, pulled it out to dress it with my sauces and toppings, then popped it back in on the top rack to bake until the cheese was bubbly and browning a bit. It was PERFECT. I forgot to brush the edge of the crust with some olive oil but that's the ONLY improvement that could have been made to the pie we had last night.

Our toppings: red sauce, chopped black olive, fresh basil leaves, mushrooms and Mozzarella one one half.... pesto sauce, chopped black olive, mushroom and Mozzarella on the other. Perfect, perfect, PERFECT.

I do want to add that since we've just moved, I couldn't find my rolling pin yet so I had to resort to hand-tossing the dough, and it worked BEAUTIFULLY. The dough was wonderfully elastic for it. It easily shaped to a big round pie; thin in the middle and perfect thick edges. I've never been able to do that before but this dough made it seem easy. We love paper-thin crust, and this one did the job beautifully. A definite keeper, thanks so much for posting!

I've made this several times and it's always great - but last night I took a couple of tips from another recipe, and it turned out FANTASTIC - best I've ever made - and the fam agreed. I used the exact ingredients from this recipe, only I used 1 T of sugar to be exact, and a pinch more salt. The changes I did make... I pre-heated (for a long time) the oven to 500, and instead of using a pizza pan, I used parchment paper only. Basically, I rolled out the crust on parchment paper that I laid out on a large cutting board. When the pizza was ready to put into the oven - I slid the parchment paper directly onto the oven rack. This cut the cooking time to about 10 to 12 minutes.

The crust turned out fluffier (and tastier) than usual, and the entire pizza crust was crispy (no soggy middle). It was absolutely amazing! We topped it off with bacon, basil, mushrooms and fresh tomatoes from our garden. Yumm. I'll be making pizza more often...

I did three modifications:
1.) I cut the recipe in half.
2.) I used beer in place of the water.
3.) I put it all in my bread maker on dough setting (1 hour 40 minutes).

This is a wonderful crisp crust.  This is my method for a good pizza (after using the crust recipe).  I preheat the oven to 500 degrees.  I have a cast iron pizza pan.  I press the dough out and put it on the greased and cornmeal coated pan.  Puncture with a fork all over, shake on Italian seasoning and grate on Parmesan cheese.  Pre-bake until just about golden, brown.  Add toppings starting with sauce, seasoning, cheese (fresh mozzarella), meat and veggies.  Bake for a bit (sorry, really just eyeball it) then broil to finish off for about 3 minutes on high.  

This crust has turned our golden, brown, delicious and crisp the two times I have made it.  No reason to try something different.

reviews.review_text: I used this dough recipe as the base for my first ever homemade pizza. I'm so glad I did! I will never have to search for another one! It's perfectly thin and crispy and makes for a great fork-free pizza. A few things I've been doing differently: I substitute 1 tbsp honey for the sugar, and I boil the water and then place a few stems of basil/oregano or whatever herbs I have around, and let it sit in the water for 10 mins to infuse it with more flavor. Then I remove the herbs and continue as per usual (adding yeast to the water). By this time, I find that the water is at the perfect temperature as well (not too hot, not too cold). Also, baking the dough for 10 mins prior to throwing on the toppings is absolutely CRUCIAL for a crispy base - Do Not skip this step! Sprinkle it with cornmeal for added texture. What else can I say? This is an easy & versatile dough recipe!

reviews.review_text: This pizza dough turned out great after a little trial and error.  The reason for the 4 stars is the 1st step says :  Mix "a little sugar" into the warm water.  How much is a little sugar?  I had to guess and added about 1/4 teaspoon the first time I made it.  This was my first time to make pizza dough and I didn't have a clue what the sugar was for.  I have now made this recipe twice and the second time I added 1 teaspoon sugar and it was perfect.  I pre-baked the crust with the first batch and it was much too hard, crisp and way overdone after adding the toppings and baking.  The second try, I added the topping to the dough and baked for 15 minutes and it was perfect.  I guess all ovens are different and I have now figured out how to make it in MY oven.  Thanks for the great recipe and I will be making this frequently instead of ordering out.

A wonderful recipe. I used 1 cup whole wheat flour but added a bunch more in kneading the dough, probably as much as a cup more. Preheated the baking stones while the dough rested for its 20-30 minutes, and readied the toppings then, too. I didn't precook the 12-inch crusts I made, and they held up fine for my ingredient-heavy taco pizza -- but for a crisper crust next time, I think I'll try prebaking the crust 5 minutes, then finish baking with the toppings. For delicious taco pizza: spread a 1:1 mixture of vegetarian refried beans and tomato salsa, then taco-seasoning spiced meat, a mix of cheddar and mozzarella cheese (heavier on the cheddar), and crumbled tortilla chips (Doritos are yummy here but plain taste great, too). Add salsa and shredded lettuce upon serving.

Excellent. I subbed 1 c. wheat flour for 1 c. of the APF and no one noticed! This will be my go to crust recipe from now on. Nice thin crust pizza; quick & easy to put together. Thanks for sharing!
***Update*** I made this dough to take with us camping and we loved it. I made the dough at home and placed in a Ziploc bag (double batch; froze one and chilled the other). Brought pepperoni, shredded pizza cheese & purchased pizza sauce. Placed a pizza stone on the grill until hot (lid closed), rolled out dough, placed on stone & topped as you normally would, closed lid and waited for perfection. We had this 2 nights for dinner (out of the 3 nights we stayed). Will definitely make this again and again. I also want to try making it into cinnamon buns or some kind of yummy breakfast pastry. Thanks so much for sharing!

items.name: The Only Chocolate Cake Recipe You'll Ever Need! (Devil's Food)
items.description: This chocolate cake is absolutely thee best we have ever had. It is so moist and rich, I never make anything else (unless I am short on time :) The frosting recipe included goes perfectly with this cake, but you can use any frosting you like. Try this once and you'll see why I call it "The Only Chocolate Cake Recipe You'll Ever Need"!!  Adding 2/18/06: I want to note that I recently used sweetened whipped heavy cream with vanilla and it was just as fabulous as the frosting recipe listed, plus much easier.  I also used hazelnut coffee in the cake and it added even more of a little extra something!
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F.
In a large mixing bowl, sift together dry ingredients. Add oil, coffee and milk and mix at medium speed for 2 minutes. Add eggs and vanilla and beat 2 more minutes. Expect batter to be thin.
Pour into a 9\
greased and floured pan or 2- 9\
pans for about 30 minutes. Cool in pans for about 15 minutes and then cool completely on racks.
While cake is cooling make the icing: Combine the milk and flour in a saucepan and cook over low heat until thick, whisking constantly. Cover and refrigerate until chilled.

In a medium bowl, beat butter, shortening, sugar and vanilla until creamy. Add chilled milk and flour mixture and beat for 10 minutes. Frost cooled cake and enjoy! The frosting sounds intimidating, but it is worth it! By the way, for some reason, we prefer this cake chilled, right out of the refrigerator. The rich chocolate and cool frosting just seem to taste best this way.

reviews.review_text: Admittedly I'm not the best cake maker (and it'll show in this review), but in my family I am generally regarded as the best 'cook'. So naturally my sister came to me asking to make a cake for my mother's birthday. She's an insane chocolate-lover so when I saw this recipe I knew I wouldn't have to look further. This recipe truly does deserve all the credit it has gotten up to this point!<br/><br/>All the ingredients are incredibly common, only needed a bit more butter, and the instructions crystal clear. You'd really have to try to mess this cake batter up when making it. Put it in a 9" x 13" for the recommended time and it came out beautiful! Unfortunately this is where my problems started, as always. After getting the frosting going I impatiently and mistakenly tried to remove the cake from the pan. The end result was not pleasant and the cake ended up in at least 3 pieces. Fortunately, however, I was able to mold what I had into a passable shape. Afraid it would fall apart at first touch I stuck it in the freezer for just under an hour hoping it would take shape (I'd seen this suggestion for putting the frosting on and figured it would serve my purposes as well). Luckily that worked very well and the frosting turned out light enough to spread without any issue. Stuck it in the fridge after I was done frosting and it turned out great.<br/><br/>It was by no means a perfect or even particularly "pretty" cake, but fortunately my family wouldn't know any better just by looking. As far as they're concerned it came out perfect! Will definitely be turning to this recipe in the future, favorited!

attributes.source_text: the frosting turned out light enough to spread without any issue

reviews.review_text: While making this, I wasn't so sure I would ever make it again, until everyone tasted it and raved about it. I put just as much focus on the presentation of a dish as I do the taste, I was disappointed at first, when the cake came out crumbly. Here are a few things I would recommend, and will do next time I make it, to make the process go smoother: 1. Line the bottom of the pans with parchment paper (I greased and floured the pans as directed, but the cake stuck to the pans and was very difficult to get them out). Others recommended using cupcakes for this recipe which would be good as well. 2. Ovens vary so set the timer for 30ish minutes, then babysit it for a few minutes longer. This cake will go from soupy in the middle at 30 minutes to crumbly and falling apart at 35 (at least mine did). Next time I will remove the cake just a bit before the toothpick comes out clean. 3. The icing: I followed the directions on the icing, and wasn't a big fan of how it tasted (only my opinion) so I added more to it, and tweaked it a little. I added 2 tablespoons of unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 tsp of vanilla and 1/4 cup of powdered sugar. Next time, I will make half again as much of that recipe. If you want to decorate the outside of the cake with the icing, I would recommend making either a double or 1 - 1/2 times the icing recipe as I barely had enough to ice the cake. The cake was so crumbly, I couldn't ice it without tearing the cake. I have a Wilton "candy melts" Melt-N-Decorate bottle that I used to squeeze the icing on the middle, sides and top. This worked great to put the icing in and squeeze it out on the cake. The nozzle on the bottle is really wide, so the process goes pretty fast. Once the icing was on, I gently evened it out with an angled spatula. I ran out of icing and time before our get together, and wanted to make the cake look prettier, so I quickly used what I had on hand at home to dress it up. I sprinkled toasted, chopped pecans on the top, lightly drizzled Hershey's syrup on the top and down the sides, and topped it off in the middle and along the top edge with angled squares of a Godiva dark chocolate ganache heart candy bar (Target has these in their candy aisle). As other folks have mentioned, keeping the cake refrigerated keeps it very moist, if it lasts that long!

attributes.source_text: keeping the cake refrigerated keeps it very moist

reviews.review_text: I just made this cake for a friend's birthday and it was delicious. I do want to say that it was a firm, moist cake, with intense flavor, but I iced it with a pretty standard chocolate buttercream icing instead of the white icing, as I wanted all  chocolate. I made 2 round layers, in some vintage pyrex plates, I turned the oven down 5 degrees and cooked it a little longer just to be sure it wouldn't burn or slump, as I'd never made it before. Turned out perfect. However,  the cake was slightly too heavy to be adhered together by the buttercream. As soon as we cut it, it started trying to mudslide and jump off the stand. Several people grabbed plates and claimed their portions just in time before it hit the table. All the pieces tried to jump off at once. There wasn't any left after, so that was okay, but it was kind of dramatic. We were all laughing. In future, I'm going to treat the recipe differently. I'll probably make it in one layer, or make a half recipe and cut into thinner layers to stack. We all agreed that it would be wonderful with cream cheese or mascarpone, and raspberry jam or crushed cherries, as a sort of improvised Black Forest cake, maybe some almonds, and chocolate on the top. I'll probably make this cake again, but not in the same way.  It was certainly easy to make and bake, I liked that, but it's not the basic delicious chocolate cake I was expecting. Delicious, yes, but a bit dense.

reviews.review_text: I made a gluten free, dairy free version of this cake and it turned out quite nicely. The cake was quite moist and had a nice flavour to  it. I would have liked a more chocolatey taste to it but this may be a result of using almond milk in place of regular milk and can be fixed by throwing in some dairy free chocolate chips in or possibly using a different type of dairy free milk. I was surprised how nice the coffee made the cake taste and everyone thoroughly enjoyed the cake (both celiacs and non-celiacs). The main change that I made to the recipe other than the milk was use 140g of the gluten free flour blend per cup of flour mentioned (the blend already had xanthan gum added to it but if someone were making it with a blend without the xanthan gum, they would just need to add a 1/4 tsp per "cup" of flour). I also ended up using a buttercream icing recipe for the icing since I didn't know how this frosting would do with a gluten free mix. Overall it turned really well and I received a lot of compliments for the cake. Thanks for the recipe.

I can't say enough good things about this delicious recipe, will certainly be making again! I'm eating some as I post this...hard as it is, I am being nice and saving my daughter the last piece of her bday cake for her treat tomorrow, haha!

reviews.review_text: I've been using this recipe since 2014 or so, and it's fantastic. My husband saw me making traditional buttercream frosting once, and he asked me to find a less-sweet alternative. This frosting is fantastic, and very customizable. I've made it with chocolate milk, almond milk and coconut milk with great success. I've subbed all butter for the butter/shortening mix. I've added cocoa powder or melted chocolate. It's very forgiving as long as the cooked mixture is COMPLETELY COOL, and you let it whip in a stand mixer for a long time. 10 minutes is not an exaggeration. As for the cake, the batter is VERY THIN. Don't be surprised! It will bake beautifully. I do find the moistness of the cake makes it prone to crumbling, so it's great for cupcakes or cake pops. I usually pair the cake with a mocha filling from The Joy of Cooking, and it's the only dessert my husband requests. It's also a favourite at both our works.

items.label: Really Good Vegetarian Meatloaf (Really!)
items.name: Really Good Vegetarian Meatloaf (Really!)
items.description: High in fiber and protein, low in fat, easy and really yummy! I've always thought meatloaf looks and smells so delicious and savory so, as a vegetarian, I decided to make a no-meat version! This is basically our favorite meatloaf recipe but with cooked mashed lentils instead of ground meat. The result is a very tasty dinner!
instructions: Add salt to water and boil in a saucepan.
Add lentils and simmer covered 25-30 minutes, until lentils are soft and most of water is evaporated.
Remove from fire.
Drain and partially mash lentils.
Scrape into mixing bowl and allow to cool slightly.
Stir in onion, oats and cheese until mixed.
Add egg, tomato sauce, garlic, basil, parsley, seasoning salt and pepper.
Mix well.
Spoon into loaf pan that has been generously sprayed with Pam (non-stick cooking spray) or well-greased.
Smooth top with back of spoon.
Bake at 350 degrees for 30- 45 minutes until top of loaf is dry, firm and golden brown.
Cool in pan on rack for about 10 minutes.
Run a sharp knife around edges of pan then turn out loaf onto serving platter.

reviews.review_text: I love this basic recipe because my 2 young boys will eat it, and it is so versatile as many others have noted.  You can tweak the ingredients to be whatever style you are in the mood for (mexican, add taco seasonings, italian, pasta sauce, etc).  As for changes to the basic recipe, I like to take about 1/3 of the cooked lentils and puree them with about 1/2 - 1 cup of vegetable broth in the food processor.  I find that this adds some needed moisture because this loaf can come out dry.  I also add a 2nd egg like others have noted.  I like to add a package of instant oatmeal instead of whole oats because my kids are texture picky.  I use some seasoned bread crumbs as well.  I have made this several times in the past and put nothing but dots of ketchup on top but just made it last night and in addition to the ketchup,  I used the glaze that was offered by another reviewer which is 2 tablespoons of brown sugar, 2 tablespoons of balsamic vinegar, and 1/3 cup of ketchup.  Mix this up beforehand and put it on the top of the loaf during the last 5-10 minutes of cooking.  It thickens up and it really gives a nice tangy taste.  We used the extra as a condiment.  I also left out the cheese this time by mistake actually but found that it was fine without it.  Overall, an excellent basic recipe.  Thank you for sharing it!  A time saving tip is to buy precooked lentils from Trader Joe's - you just have to open the package and start mixing.  I did this for the first time yesterday and found them to be great both taste wise and texture wise.

attributes.source_text: my 2 young boys will eat it

adds some needed moisture

reviews.review_text:
Another 5 star vote! I really wasn't sure if I would like this, but considering the rave reviews thought it was worth a try. 
I cooked the lentils about 20 minutes... there was no liquid left. During the last 10 minutes of simmering I added very finely chopped carrots and celery to the lentils and when done, mashed it all together.
I used colby-jack cheese and had no parsley so added a bit of oregano and some thyme too. I am not a huge BBQ sauce fan, so I used regular plain canned tomato sauce and just a few tablespoons of BBQ sauce (as other reviewers suggested) and used a total of 3/4 cup sauce (again, worried it might be dry).  Once it was all mixed up, it looked like A LOT and as I started filling a loaf pan, thought, no wonder some reviewers say it is mushy in the middle. So I broke up the mix into two loaf pans for 2 very shallow loaves. I added a bit of tomato sauce/BBQ sauce on top before cooking, covered with foil. After 30 min took off the foil and added a bit more sauce and then let it cook for about 10 more minutes. The texture was perfect! Crunchy outside, nice inside. My very carnivorous husband, who was NOT excited about this meal, was pleasantly surprised and ate 2 helpings. This is a great addition to our meal rotations. Can't wait to eat the leftovers tomorrow!

attributes.source_text: Crunchy outside
My very carnivorous husband, who was NOT excited about this meal, was pleasantly surprised and ate 2 helpings

reviews.review_text: This is a pretty good recipe and very easy to make.  Served with baked sweet potatoes or a salad, it is a very filling meal.  You do have to get the idea out of your mind that it is "meatloaf" like mom used to make.  I needed to make a few modifications, however, due to household dietary restrictions.  My version was completely vegan as I cut out the egg and cheese.  I also had to omit the oats because the oats that I have in the pantry aren't reliably gluten free.  Here is what I did instead: I soaked 2 tablespoons of chia seed to replace the egg.  Soaked chia seed get gummy like the consistency of egg whites after soaking in water.  Also, I added ground flax seed and cooked quinoa in place of the oats.  I added extra seasoning because of the omitted cheese.  In addition, I omitted the seasoning salt--I never use it as it is an unhealthy spice choice. I found that the recipe worked well when I made it ahead and allowed it to set in the fridge for a few hours as a make-ahead dish.  It held together better, and the flavors blended better this way.  I also added mushrooms and colored peppers as suggested by other reviewers.  Instead of ketchup or the BBQ sauce that was recommended, I chose to top the loaf with a fresh tomato from the garden.  Simply sliced the tomatoes and placed on the top before baking.  It really looked pretty.  I suppose that I  reworked this recipe a lot, but I had to because of the various food intolerances in our home!

I felt compelled to make this recipe given all the reviews it had received but did not expect it to be as good as it is. Vegetarian or not I cannot imagine a better meatloaf exists. This is the second time I made this. I doubled it. Here are the things I changed- I sauteed the onion, one finely diced celery stick, 8 garlic cloves (this is doubled), and one grated carrot and some homemade chicken stock concentrate. Added around 1 tbsp of browning sauce (I found it very pale the first time), replaced half of the tomato sauce with barbeque sauce, used fresh parsley. The first time I made the fungus gravy but this time and this made it truly amazing I used the sauce/glaze for meatloaf recipe  54257 and that was just right for double this recipe. I also think that this recipe only serves about 3 maybe 4. I am going to triple it next week for a family dinner. It is awesome as leftovers and makes beautiful sandwiches. I served it with root mash 88011 and french cauliflower 285468.
Thank you so much for this recipe it is sooooo yummy

Thank you for this recipe. I really enjoyed it! Made some substitutions and additions. Instead of using the seasonings and pasta sauce that have leanings of Italian flavors, I went with more of a rustic, savory flavors. I omitted the chopped onion, pasta sauce, garlic powder and seasoning salt and used the following instead: LENTILS - Instead of 2 cups, used 2.5 cups water to cook lentils. - Put three dried Bay Leaves in the water that boiled the lentils. (remove and discard the bay leaves after lentils are cooked) INGREDIENTS ADDED to Cooked Lentils and Oatmeal Mixture before baking - Two stalks fresh celery diced into small pieces. - 4.5 ounces canned crushed tomatoes (Brand: Red Gold) - Added the following spices into the crushed tomatoes, stirred and then poured into the lentil and oatmeal mix: 1T dried chives, 1T dried parsley, 1t Basil, 1/2t celery salt, 1t Thyme, 1/4t ground black pepper. - Added the 1 egg beaten and then put in 1T Andre's Steak Sauce (it added some nice moisture and binding to the mix). Stirred into the lentil and oatmeal mixture. - 1/2 cup instead of 3/4 cup cheese. Instead of Mozzarella, used a finely shredded white cheese blend (package mix) of Monterey Jack, Asiago and whatever else the package had in it. THE BAM FACTOR - Upon serving the lentil loaf I topped it with WHOLE CRANBERRY SAUCE. I found the lentil loaf to be really dense and kind of heavy, yet a bit bland in taste. Also, the color is not visually pleasing, The red color, semi-sweetness and texture of the cranberry sauce really balanced out the denseness of the lentil mix and added just the right balance of mild sweetness to the rustic spices. For the sides - I prepared Butternut Squash (boiled) and Cornbread Casserole. This was our Thanksgiving Dinner and we really enjoyed it! Thanks again for the recipe idea! ?

attributes.source_text: This was our Thanksgiving Dinner
This was our Thanksgiving Dinner

reviews.review_text: Five stars...easy. I own a restaurant in a remote area of Baja, Mexico, that features "north of the border" meals with a Latin touch.<br/>     In an effort to accomadate my vegetarian customers, I wanted to find a vegetarian burger, that used ingredients indigenous to our region. I had found several recipes and tried some, without success. <br/>     Then one day while continuing my search, I came across this recipe for a "really good vegetarian meatloaf". While reading the information, I found that this recipe could also be used for a veggie burger. Intrigued, I made a small batch, and pressed them out for burgers. My wife ate the first one right out of the pan. The second one she put on a bun with all the trimmings. I found the recipe I was looking for...and it is now a favorite on our menu. And...it is "really good". <br/>  It has been several weeks since I first wrote this review...several more weeks of serving this recipe to my customers. Each week, I get more compliments on this recipe. A friend told me the other day, it was the best he has ever had, and sadly he admitted, it is even better than his own recipe at home. A real winner...

reviews.review_text:
I have made this about 5 times now. Every time it's happily eaten by vegetarians and carnivores alike. When I mash the lentils I use my blender and add water to get a mashed potato like consistency. I think this is why it turns out a little more moist. It also helps to put some sauce over the top when you have about twenty minutes left in cooking it. Thank you for the recipe.
Update: Since writing this review I have tried the following things and they have turned out great.
1.) I've occasionally added another egg, although I felt guilty about the extra fat.
2.) I've added chopped celery,carrots, mushrooms as suggested by other reviewers.
3.) In addition, and sometimes in place of the cheddar cheese , I added Parmesan cheese.
4.) Per suggestion of my girlfriend, I use a hand mixer instead of the blender now. She said she preferred some lentils still in tact for texture. I usually cook the lentils until they are very easy to smash, so that the mixer can handle the load.
I just thought I'd share how versatile and forgiving this recipe is.

attributes.source_text: happily eaten by vegetarians and carnivores alike
happily eaten by vegetarians and carnivores alike
it turns out a little more moist

reviews.review_text:
10 stars!!! 

I will make this over and over and over again!

I tried to get the meat eating guests to convince my husband that this DIDN'T taste like real meat. They REFUSED!!!

It was moist, delicious, I had no idea that lentils could be so flavorful. Didn't even feel the oats in there but WOW WOW WOW!! 

I used mozerella cheese and it was delish! Went well with the sause which NO ONE COULD detect was in there. I guess the trick is picking out the right sause. I also used fresh garlic. I also put a splash more water in with the lentils and took them off the heat well under the time mentioned...as soon as they mushed easily with a fork. Oh, and I used extra sause. Maybe nearly twice as much as the recipe called for. I wanted to err on the side of moistness and it was a good move.

I couldn't get enough of this. All the guests had seconds (though the vegetarians were a bit creeped out by its "authentic" taste) and it is already gone, despite the fact that it was supposed to last a few days for left overs. It didn't. Had it for shabbat dinner and by lunch time it was totally gone, and just as tasty reheated as the first bite.

Probably would freeze like a dream. I cooked it at a super high heat at the end, leaving a bit mushy of a middle. But consistancy wise it was really terrific and the mushiness was just slight. I seemed to be the only person to notice.

Really, I can't rave about this enough. An absolutly FANTASTIC recipe that I want to make tomorrow. I can't believe it is so healthy! WOW!

WOW WOW WOW YUM YUM YUM!!!

One of the top recipes at the Zaar!!!

reviews.review_text:
This recipe shines as a leftover dish. As a lentil-loaf sandwich, this is fantastic! Wheat bread, mayo and a slice of american cheese...yum, yum! I ate it for lunch for a week and couldn't get enough of it. :-P

AND THAT'S NOT ALL: Another use for leftovers: Crumble up the lentil-loaf, toss with cooked rotini pasta, pasta sauce and shredded cheese. Bake at 350 for 20-30 minutes. Delicious!



Substitutions: mix of red/yellow onion, added carrots (not recommended), pizza sauce instead of plain tomato.

Recommendation: I find lentils come out better (less tough, easier to mash) if you boil them without salt. For dry lentils, boil 1 1/2 to 2 cups water (w/o salt!), add 1 cup dry lentils and bring to boil again. Reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes. The lentils should have absorbed most of the water and will be fairly easy to mash with a spoon. You don't necessarily need to add any salt to this recipe, but add it back in with the eggs.

attributes.source_text: I ate it for lunch for a week

reviews.review_text: This is fantastic!  I had to add a LOT more water (4 cups total) to get thing to come out right, but I'm using brown lentils (lots more fiber) and old fashioned rolled oats, not quick oats, so that may be the reason.  I made some substitutions (like most other folks): I went vegan, replacing the eggs with milled flax seed & water and omitting the cheese, swapped 2/3rds cup ketchup for the spaghetti sauce, a small dash of extra virgin olive oil to help retain moisture in the fridge, and used "Italian Seasoning Mix" instead of just dried oregano (this was all on my second batch).  Meatloaf is one thing I've hesitated to make since going vegetarian because I love "real" meatloaf so much, but this is better than any "real" meatloaf I've had (don't tell Mama!).  This recipe would also probably hold up good enough to make meatballs or even crumbled "beef" replacement for other things ... probably wouldn't hold up too well in chili unless you add it just before serving, but would probably work for other things like no-meat Hamburger Helper.  I'll try it out in those other areas ... if it works, that would be great, a much more reasonably priced beef alternative than the pre-packaged stuff.

Love it! I cooked brown lentils (they're cheap and flavorful) in 2.5 cups of water to which I'd added a packet of G. Washington Rich Brown (salt was omitted) until all the water had been absorbed and the lentils were mostly mush. My oats were Old Wessex Ltd. Scotch Style because that's what I keep in the house (I dislike quick oats); I think they helped give a nice, meaty texture. I used Swiss Gruyere that I'd found at a good price (stores well, too), and an 8 oz. can of (salt-free) tomato sauce because other reviewers mentioned a tendency towards a dry, crumbly texture. I didn't have an onion in the house so I hydrated some flakes I happened to have and I used store-bought chopped garlic in olive oil instead of the powder. I don't use much seasoned salt but the one I keep on hand and that I used for this is Penzey's 4/S, which is really yummy and definitely a cut above the stuff in the supermarket.
I've served it with the Fungus Gravy and am going to try it with a cashew gravy. Everyone to whom I've served it thinks it's great, even meat eaters! Thanks for a delicious recipe!

attributes.source_text: give a nice, meaty texture
even meat eaters

reviews.review_text:
This recipe surprised me with the amazing taste that the loaf had. I did a few substitutions/alterations... I came very close to adding a second egg as many reviewers stated they did so but I held off, as I figured curing mushiness was harder than remedying a dry loaf. It came out with the perfect amount of moisture.

I did not have eniough tomato sauce so I made up the diff with ketchup, a dash of liquid smoke and a dash of worcestershire sauce. I used fresh garlic instead of powder.

When I boiled the lentils I threw in a low sodium veggie boullion and some onion flakes. I did not salt the water.

I used 1/4 cup colby jack and a 1/4 cup 50-50 mixture of manchego and parmesan. I did not put a 3rd 1/4 cup cheese in. I followed others' suggestions and slathered some ketchup (with a few drops liquid smoke) on the top in the last part of the baking. I put it into a loaf pan that made it about 1 inch tall, baked for 18 minutes and then 8 more with the ketchup. Perfect!

attributes.source_text: It came out with the perfect amount of moisture

reviews.review_text: SaraFish, you're my hero!  This dish made me so happy.  The bf saw the mixture as it was going in the loaf pan and said, "Ooo, meatloaf!", to which I replied "kindof."  I told him it was more a lentil loaf and received a sad "please don't make me eat that."  Shockingly enough, this meat lover changed tunes as he shoveled seconds in his mouth.  He said he would give it four stars (which I'm guessing really means five stars but he just won't admit it.)  :)  I took Alydes advice and subbed in half chili sauce which gave it a little kick.  A must try.  I discovered midway through I only had fat free cheddar cheese and was worried, but I couldn't taste a bit of difference.  I even forgot to cover the pan while the lentils cooked and ended up having to nuke them and it still turned out fabulous.  Now you have me craving this again...  :)  This will be a great one to double and freeze in slices for quick lunches.  Thanks again!  Keep them coming!

attributes.source_text: this meat lover changed tunes as he shoveled seconds in his mouth
gave it a little kick

reviews.review_text: I cooked it for the first time tonight. I modified the recipe a little: instead of the tomato sauce, I made a sauce with ketchup, organic soy sauce, organic molasses, and vegetable broth (to keep it moist). I used tinned lentils, 2 eggs instead of 1, 3 big cloves of garlic, fresh basil, and added a couple of veggie wieners, all of which I blended in the food processor. In the last 10 minutes of baking, I also drizzled some more sauce made with ketchup and honey on top. It was delicious by itself, but an alternative would be to cut down on the sodium in the sauce that goes in the meatloaf, but make a mushroom gravy to serve on the side. The meatloaf cooked evenly in a 9x5 inch loaf pan and is about 1.5 in. high. You could easily double the ingredients and make a full-size loaf (but it is very rich as it is which makes the smaller portions appealing). We had it with a Romaine heart salad and were very happy with it. Thank you for posting the recipe.

attributes.source_text: it is very rich as it is

reviews.review_text: For my first try, I followed the recipe exactly, except I forgot to mash the lentils and ended up mashing after I had everything in the bowl.  It worked just fine, so don't sweat it if you make the same mistake!  I found the 4.5 oz of tomato sauce to be a strange measure, since it isn't sold in 4.5 oz cans.  I measured the required 1/2 cup + 1 tablespoon of tomato sauce out of the can; the moisture in the meatloaf was perfect and I don't see why anyone would add a second egg.  I thought it was a little sweet, though, so the second time I made it, I used 1 tablespoon of worcestershire sauce, 1/4 cup of tomato sauce and 1/4 cup of barbecue sauce.  It was a nice twist, but I thought the barbecue sauce was too overpowering.  I will try chili sauce next time, as that's what my regular meatloaf recipe uses.  I'm always looking for vegetarian meals that are high in protein... so many of them aren't.

attributes.source_text: the moisture in the meatloaf was perfect

reviews.review_text: Hi, I have to add an update to my review. I shared the recipe with a co-worker who shared it with a neighbor who shared it with the neighborhood and her co-workers and it started a lentil meatloaf revolution...everyone wants the recipe now...even meat and potato men! I thought it was good but dang I never expected this! What follows is my original review: This came out very good and flavorful. I made quite a few changes, some from ideas others posted. I used red lentils. I added a vegetable bouillion cube to the water for the lentils. I used a large white onion and added chopped up crimini mushrooms. I used smoked jack cheese. I added 2 eggs, a cup of barbeque sauce, 1 tsp. garlic powder, 1/2 tsp. black pepper, a dash of cayenne and left out the other seasonings. Then I put it in a loaf pan and spread it with more barbeque sauce. I think I could improve it by adding less bq sauce and cook it longer, it was a bit mushy. I cooked it for 1 hour. Thanks for the recipe to play around with. I've never made anything like it!

@ Pale Rose--what altitude are you at? That can affect your recipe. Are you using quick-cooking oats? That's another factor that's really important with this. The last solve I know of is to use rice (parboil it) instead of oats to absorb some of that excess moisture you are having trouble with. Cooking for longer results in the same problem we had with our mom's meatloaves as kids: it'll dry out. This is a REALLY great recipe and you deserve to have it come out the way that many of the other readers are experiencing it. I'm not sure what the final 'solve' will be for you, but I can honestly say that as an ex-chef, this is an example of "food magic" that I've always striven to achieve. Give it another try and let us know what worked for you-it'll help us all out. I'm sure you are not the only one who has experienced this, and it's gotta be frustrating to see all these high marks and not get the same result.

i had to use steel cut oats since i was out of quick cooking so i only used a 1/3 of a cup since it absorbs much more liquid. i also didn't have any parsley and don't like it anyway so i added dill. my lentils cooked much faster then stated here. they were mushy after less then 10 min and needed no draining. used fresh garlic and chipotle pepper for a little more heat and some smokiness. used cheddar and regular salt. cooked along side some potato and broccoli casserole. was trying this instead of the cottage cheese base one since the pine nuts in that recipe no longer agree with my nut allergy. at 35 min this was still a goo but my casserole wasn't close to cooked either so maybe they just don't do well trying to cook both at once. i may also have added more oats. gave it another 45 min. finally sort of solidified but the texture of this was pasty and gritty with no flavor. maybe i just don't like lentils but i will never make this again.

attributes.source_text: for a little more heat
some smokiness

reviews.review_text: I've never eaten meatloaf. I don't have a real tendency towards red meat and never have. However, my daughter is a vegetarian and I'm semi vege and hubby likes meatloaf. So, we tried it. My 2.5 year old didn't care for the texture, but she's been real picky on food lately and prefers broccoli over most foods at the moment. I made pretty much to the directions except I did add an extra egg as suggested by other reviewers. It came out well. Hubby says it's a little creamier than a typical meatloaf, but he wasn't sure if that was because of the sauce we used or the cheese. He wound up having seconds. I wasn't sure if I'd like it because I'm not into the meaty flavor, but I did. It's a new addition to our household. I did mean to add sun dried tomatoes but forgot them until after the mix was already in the oven. I could see this as being a kind of stuffing as well. It had the right texture. Hubby suggests it might go well in a taco.

attributes.source_text: a little creamier than a typical meatloaf
He wound up having seconds

reviews.review_text:
I've tried so many vegetarian "meat"loafs and this is by far my favorite. The texture is the closest to the real thing and my steak-loving husband actually prefers this over the real thing too. I always top with tomato soup for the last 10-15 minutes of cooking, it adds that additional sweetness that is so reminiscent of my childhood meatloaf. 

I prefer red lentils over green since they cook to a more mushy consistency and I don't have to mash them at all. If you like more lent in your lentil loaf, the green did add more texture but it also seemed a little dryer. I added a little more tomato sauce for that one.

I don't add any cheese (to save on calories) and it still came out great. I add worcestershire, italian seasoning, mushrooms and roasted garlic (that I roast beforehand and always on hand in my fridge). A side of mashed potatoes and greens... a perfect comfort food any veg or meatlover will adore. 

Thanks for the recipe!

it adds that additional sweetness that is so reminiscent of my childhood meatloaf

items.name: Country White Bread or Dinner Rolls (Bread Machine)
keywords: c("Breads", "Healthy", "Bread Machine", "< 60 Mins", "For Large Groups", "Small Appliance")
items.description: We think this is the best white bread recipe ever! It is a tender bread with a slightly sweet taste. My dinner rolls using this dough are so good, everyone always loves them. It doesn't take to long to make them when the bread maker does most of the work. The cook time is listed for the rolls only because everyone's bread makers cooks at different rates. Mine is older and a regular loaf will take 4 hours and 10 minutes. I have found that 15 balls of dough fit perfectly in the 9X13 pan with sides touching after raising the 2nd time but they can be made whatever size you want. I hope you enjoy this great bread as much as we do.
instructions: In bread machine pan, place all ingredients from flour through yeast in order as recommended by the manufacturer.
Select the basic bread setting.
Check dough after 5 minutes of mixing, if needed add 1-2T of water or flour.
Bake as normal.
For dinner rolls.
Mix in bread machine but use only the dough option.
Lightly grease a 9 x 13 baking pan (I always use a metal pan).
When dough is finished shape into 15 uniformly sized balls. I always grease my hands with shortening to smooth the dough out and it helps keep the dough from drying out.
Cover and let the rolls rise in a warm, draft free place until risen to the desired size.
I let them about double in size.
Bake in a 350° oven about 12-15 minutes until golden brown.
After removing from the oven, brush the tops of the rolls with melted butter.
Take out of pan and let completely cool before storing.

reviews.review_text:
Things I changed (because the way the recipe is written didn't work for me and my Cuisinart bread maker.... three times, it did not work):

1. I reduced the water to just one cup.
2. I used double the yeast (the recipe on Betty Crocker for dinner rolls is almost exactly the same, except it called for double the yeast).
3. Instead of the dough function, I used the regular white bread bake function and took it out before it started baking. After reading my manual, that apparently is the best way to go for any sort of dough you will reshape and resize afterwards. Thank God I learned how to read.
4. Do NOT, I repeat, DO NOT use store-brand flour. I used Stater Bros and everything has so far turned out miserably. I bought Gold Metal this AM and now everything is miraculously better. Maybe it's the heat prep change, maybe it's the water, maybe it's the flour - who the heck knows? I just know all of a sudden the texture of the dough is the way it should and it finally rised like it was suppose to. Sheesh!!!!

Otherwise, it's now cooking in the oven and hopefully it'll turn out.

My bread runnith over!  I made this in my bread machine, skeptical that it would even work.  

Lets just say my loaf rose and then some!  I just love the taste of this bread and even several days after, it was moist and flavorful. 

I don't think I'll be making bread any other way after trying this.  The only thing I will do, is run this dough through the dough cycle and let it finish rising in a bread  pan.

UPDATE: I forgot to add that I used regular flour when I made my first loaf.

My 2nd loaf went well. As I read some of the reviews I changed the oil to EVOO, and put it on the dough cycle.

I let it rise and baked it at 350 for 35 min so that the internal temp was over 185.  I just ate a piece and it is just as good, or better than my first loaf. 

Thanks again for posting this lovely recipe!

attributes.source_text: it was moist and flavorful

reviews.review_text: YOWZA! Yummy, yummy! The first time I made the rolls and they were gobbled up. Today I used the dough setting, turned out onto lightly floured surface, kneaded for 5 minutes with well-greased hands, pinching out the large bubbles as they showed themselves, rolled up and turned the ends under, then put into a loaf pan. Rubbed a little more shortening around on my hands, patted the top of dough so it wouldn't dry out, covered with a tea towel and let rise for 40 minutes. Popped into a 350F oven and baked for 20 minutes. I needed about 1 1/4 Cups more flour to make the dough come away from the sides of the ABM, but had used up all my bread flour, so I substituted with organic AP. Also used a "jumbo" size egg and 1/4 tsp. more yeast. FANTASTIC AND SUPER TEXTURE...MOIST AND DELICIOUS! Thanks for posting. This will be a regular in our house!

attributes.source_text: MOIST AND DELICIOUS

reviews.review_text: These were EXACTLY what I was looking for. Soft, flavorful, with a beautiful rise. I don't have a bread machine, so I used my KA. I proofed my yeast in the amount of water suggested (I always warm my water to 115 degrees). Mixed the egg, oil, sugar, and salt in my mixing bowl and then added the proofed yeast and gave it a light wisk. I didn't have bread flour, so used AP instead. I did need a little extra flour, but not much. And that worked great! Did the old fashioned, grease a bowl and put the dough in it to rise then punch it down method. Then I made my rolls and placed them in a greased 9x13 for a second rise. I got 15 wonderful rolls, just like the recipe said I would. I had to stop my youngest from eating them (he's my bread king). All I can say is "THANK YOU!!!" I can't wait to make a loaf of bread out of this recipe.

attributes.source_text: Soft, flavorful, with a beautiful rise
I had to stop my youngest from eating them (he's my bread king)

reviews.review_text: Very quick, easy, and yummy. Made on dough cycle using Bread Flour and ABM yeast.  Had to add an additional 1/4 cup of flour. Beautiful dough, made 4 small loaves. I used my oven setting for proofing bread (100F about 30 mins) then baked about 20 mins. We all loved it, especially DS who has requested another batch today. Thank you DDW for sharing your recipe! 10/20 Update: I made another batch today and baked in my ABM.  My loaf was so large that is covered the air vent in the lid.  I had to open and make a small indentation in the vent area.  The bread I baked in the oven was PERFACT! The crust on the bread machine loaf was tough and the texture was waaaay too dense.  It didn't have enough room to bake.  My ABM is a Hitachi and looking at my manual it suggests 3cups of flour for a large loaf.  It could be my bread machine can't handle the recipe. Still a 5 star recipe but I will only bake it in the oven from here on out.  Thanks again DDW for the great, easy recipe.

reviews.review_text: Oh my gosh. I almost still can't believe it, but I've finally done it. This is truly the first time I've made a bread with my bread machine that ISN'T DENSE! I have had no luck with my bread machine since I got it. All I wanted was a nice fluffy bread but I just couldn't make one... until now! I can't even begin to describe how happy I am. I followed the recipe almost exactly, though the only changes were that I cut down the sugar to 2TB and added a 1/4 tsp more yeast to see if I'd get a nicer rise compared to my past attempts. The loaf rose pretty well in the bread machine, and when I shaped my little dinner rolls (ended up with 16 balls of dough), boy did they rise after that! And they baked SO beautifully! A little brush of melted butter afterwards and they were golden and shiny and beautiful. The moment I picked up a light, super soft roll, I already knew that this recipe was a winner. So soft, so fluffy and light, and the flavour - wow! Just perfect. A little bit of butter in this warm roll and I was in heaven. I gobbled up 3 of them tonight and had to stop myself from eating the rest! We only have one single roll left. Hopefully I'll be able to eat it tomorrow, unless someone gets to it before me! Thank you so much for this recipe. I have faith in my bread machine - finally - and I am no longer destined for dense, heavy breads. No more!! :)
