reviews.review_text: i found this to be a very good,and slightly chewy bread.i only added 1/8 cup of sugar.it took 3 hours in my bread machine.as soon as it came out,i cut it and added a little honey butter spread,it was just so warm and soft.this will be made again.thank you for posting. — Dec 8, UPDATE:December 11,2005,made this again using bread machine yeast,and OMG!!! it made such a big difference.the different yeast made the loaf higher,lighter,and oh so much fluffier.and i slightly beat the egg before i added it.i added the ingredients in this order, water,egg,oil,sugar,bread flour,salt,and yeast,and i made a little "dent" in one side of the flour and added the salt,the made another "dent" on the other side adding the yeast making sure the yeast didn't touch the water. thank you again for posting this wonderful recipe.

reviews.review_text: UPDATE!!! I already reviewed this recipe in the past BUT I have to say AGAIN I chose to make this recipe and made an awesome loaf of bread last night!! This is gonna be my basic recipe- adding additions to it is awesome but alone it is fantastic too!! 05/10/09: Ha! I wrote my first review back in 2007. This recipe has been my go-to recipe since then. It never fails me. TIPS: I always beat the egg before I put it into the bread machine. I also use 1/2 white Better For Bread or All-Purpose flour & 1/2 whole wheat. I like to make the rolls. They turn out better for me when I shape them into 20 rolls. I freeze the shaped dough & keep in freezer baggies until I need them. Let thaw & rise while preheating oven. For me, the rolls take about 25 minutes to bake. Excellent! ~ Keli . . . . . . 

02/08/07:  This bread was outstanding on my subsequent tries on the full cycle. My first attempt on ExpressBake rated about 2 stars. That wasn't a total loss, tho, cuz the birds & animals loved it. ~ Keli

I never loved bread crust 'til I made this bread in my machine.  I love the crispy, flavorful crust as much as the light, fluffy inside.  This is my go to recipe for bread now.  I halve the recipe--it rises A LOT and always fills over 75% of my regular sized bread machine pan.  I also never check the dough (after 5 minutes of mixing) since the first time, and It always turns out perfectly. I probably wouldn't use it for sandwiches--the insides may be a bit too soft.  We just cut it and add butter to it with dinner, or add jams, apple butter or honey and make a light meal of it.  Leftovers do get stale a bit quick, but they make GREAT breadcrumbs that are still yummy after freezing awhile.  I can't attest to what the bread is like after completing the cooling cycle in the bread machine because we always rip that sucker out with potholders as soon as the fan comes on and scarf it down. ;)

Yea! I found a bread machine recipe that delivers!
This recipe( I made dinner rolls), was delicious. I used all ingredients as listed and also included the optional melted butter and shortening. 
I have a brand new ZOJIRUSHI HOME BAKERY X20 and have been trying various recipes the past week...most were dissappointing.

Since I don't have a bread machine, I searched the net for a comprehensive "how-to" on how to make bread. I found a very good article here: http://recipes.howstuffworks.com/how-to-bake-bread-cooking.htm I am not rating this yet, as I still have to make it. reviews.review_text: This was simply a great loaf of white bread for my machine!  I followed the recipe except for following Dorel's suggestion of using 1 tsp of salt.  All other bread machine recipes I find I need to cut 1/4 c of flour from the recipe, but based on so many others needing to add flour, I was able to use exactly what was called for, with perfect results.  My loaf also plastered itself to the inside of the lid of my machine, nice high loaf, and makes a great sandwich.  Next time I'd like to try CJSmith's suggestions-- adding oat flour, etc and possibly cutting some of the sugar for everyday eating.  Look forward to this being my new recipe from which to build off of.

Perfectly sweet, fluffy and still heavy like a dinner roll should be! I have many types of dinner roll recipes but this one is the one we have been searching for. I did not need to add the extra water. I oiled my hands like suggested and what a great tip that was! I will always do this. I would like to share another great tip on raising the dough- I used the bread machine for dough only. While you're doing the 15 rolls heat a mug of water up really hot in the micro and then put the mug in the corner to keep it warm inside.  Cover your pan with saran wrap and put it in the micro, leaving the mug in there too. It's the best way to raise the dough I have ever found! Happy Baking!

items.label: Award Winning Chili
items.name: Award Winning Chili
items.description: My husband and I created this recipe together. He won a chili cook-off with this recipe at work. We always use venison, but you can use ground beef or turkey.
instructions: In a medium Dutch oven over medium-high heat add the olive oil. Add the ground meat and cook, breaking up into pieces, until browned. Add the onions, bell pepper and jalapeno and cook until softened. Drain excess grease.
Add the tomatoes, tomato sauce, cumin, chili powder, salt, cayenne, paprika and 1 cup water. Mix to combine.
Add the kidney beans and black beans, mix and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 1-2 hours.
Serve with desired toppings.

reviews.review_text: This is a great base recipe. My guests wanted the recipe also. I tweaked the recipe a bit to suite my preference, but kept it very much the same. I added a large minced jalepeño, used 32 oz of beef broth to substitute for the water, added another 15 oz can of tomato sauce, added 8 oz of beef, 15 oz of hot Rotel tomatoes w/habeñeros, used 42 oz of black beans only, omitting the kidney beans, one bulb of finely minced fresh garlic cloves, and cut the cumin to 1/2 Tablespoon. I sauteed the beef, onions, garlic, peppers with 1 Tablespoon tumeric and 1 Tablespoon olive oil. I used extra lean beef so I had no reserve grease to drain. I will definitely make this again. The adjusted recipe serves 8 generously. For those who like it extra spicy, I served it with Chipotle pepper flakes on the side.

attributes.source_text: My guests wanted the recipe also

reviews.review_text: It looks, smells and tastes amazing! This is my first time actually making homemade chili, usually I just cheat and use the packet seasoning and beans and meat. Did a little adjusting with using 2 cans dark red kidney beans and 1 can red beans, 2lbs beef, and yellow peppers instead of a green bell. Also had to use canned jalapenos instead cause it's what I had in the cupboard. Ended up making 2 pots instead of one so I'll have some to freeze and eat next week or give to friends. I'm always paranoid about making enough so when I saw 6 servings I thought it was the 1/2 cup servings usually posted with the box meals I buy (which is never enough for my family lol). Surprise was on me, the poster actually meant a real, hearty serving! Amazing recipe, thank you so much for sharing it!!

I couldn't believe how close this recipe is to the one I grew up on. I did tweak it a little by not using jalapena, added 1 tsp dried Mexican oregano, 3 cloves minced garlic added to the meat which was beef. I also add an additional tsp of salt and about 1 tsp of black pepper. I did have the smoked paprika which I think helped. I only used 1 T of cumin and upped the chili powder another tbls. Also, I used beef stock instead of water, used onl 1 onion and lastly I added about 1 tsp of cocoa which intensifies the overall chili flavor. This is really a very good base to tweak to your taste. This is award winning for my taste now with the changes and to the judges for my friends job at the airport where it was submitted with 24 other entries. She gave me the check  for $250.00 and she kept the trophy. I think I should have gotten that too, but that's life.

Made today. Very tasty. My only varied from the recipe -1 Tablespoon of chili powder (not a fan of it too hot), only had jalapeno from a jar (not pickled), and pinto instead of black didn't have black and red instead of green bell pepper (indigestion with the green). I did read the reviews adding a little corn meal to thicken was an excellent call by another post. Main thing was the flavors of the sauce was very very good. I thought two onions would be over kill but NOOooooooo. It was the perfect amount. I used 1lb of beef bites...what ever it was..small bites of roast. It was leaner than hamburger. Added two cups of water due to the beef it needed time to cook til tender. Definitely will be making again but with black beans. I might add garlic but it's better than any recipe I've tried so far and any prepackaged flavoring kit.

reviews.review_text:
9/27/15, I also used this recipe to win a chili cook-off. With almost 30 entries of traditional chilis, green chilis, and others. I followed the directions exact, but used ground beef, a red and white onion, and a small amount of brown sugar. I also not only rinsed the beans but soaked them for an hour or so. I didn't have a Dutch oven but used a big pan with lid on stovetop. I had never made chili before so I had to go buy all the seperate ingredients, no chili packets. I tasted it a few times during the simmering and felt pretty confident it would place in the contest. It took 1st!!! It was so good! 
Good luck! This recipe is tried tested and proven. I will not be trying another recipe. This is the best!!

attributes.source_text: I also used this recipe to win a chili cook-off

reviews.review_text: So I seasoned the meat with part of the seasonings, cooked the onions before adding the meat, also added 4 cloves of garlic minced fine, did not drain the fat, omitted the green pepper and went for orange cause colors but used less, used canned and fresh tomatoes which allowed me to omit water, added tomato paste, cut back on the cumin, used twice the jalapenos, and threw in corn. It was just... amazing. I doubled the recipe cause I don't know portion sizes and I like to share. I also stole someone's idea to use sausage and ground meat. So to the recipe maker, this was a delight. If you ever want a taste tester call me. To the person who used sausage and ground meat I air fist bump you. You are the original VP.

Good base recipe, but a few changes are necessary for most people - the most important one being the amount of cayenne. I've made this recipe twice and both times my family and I have agreed it's too hot. The first time, I used the amount of cayenne recommended, and the second time I used less than half. Next time I probably won't add it at all. If you like hot chili, I recommend using half the cayenne. Granted, I used Rotel canned tomatoes as recommended, which had green chilies in them, but I got the mild cans. I never bothered adding the jalapeno - it would have been inedible if I did. If you aren't using canned tomatoes with chilies, more heat might be acceptable.<br/><br/>I added 1 tablespoon of cocoa powder which gave it a better flavor. I wouldn't skip this step. I also added 2 minced garlic cloves, more plain diced tomatoes, and a good amount of black pepper, and it was nearly perfect.

This was fantastic and very different than the regular chilli I throw together.  I think it was the addition of cumin, which I only added 1 Tlb instead of 2, just personal preference.  I also used 1 lb. of ground beef and 1 lb. of ground pork just to see what would happen, plus, we like LOTS of meat.  Everything else was made as directed.  It was quite spicy but since I have a hard time chewing Big Red gum because it numbs my mouth, I am not a good judge in that respect.  But with that said, I even loved it...and it is quite different from my regular can of chilli beans and beef and such that I usually make.  I have a chilli cook off at work in a few weeks...I might actually enter this year!! Thanks so much for the great recipe!

attributes.source_text: It was quite spicy

reviews.review_text: I went on a strict meal plan for health reasons several years ago, and one of my projects has been finding delicious food that fits my plan. I used this recipe as a base, and it makes the most fabulous chili. While I'm sure my recipe isn't as good as the one written, it has nearly 3 cups of veggies/serving. The seasoning mix is key here. Everything else you can play with. Beans, no beans, meat type with or without fat, veggie amount, even tomato amount. I use lean ground beef and add 1 lb cauliflower/2lbs beef while cooking. The cauliflower disappears into the beef. I also like adding the seasoning at various points throughout the cooking process. I feel like it layers/incorporates the flavors better. If you add a lot of extra veggies like I do (10 cups/lb of meat), up the amount of seasoning you use. The dish definitely does better after several hours of cooking. The flavors need time to incorporate. It tastes like disappointment if you grab yourself a bowl after less than an hour of simmering. It tastes like Cheat Day after 3 hours.

As another reviewer suggested, I added one more can of diced tomatoes and a can of chicken broth. I also used ground chicken. My surprise/secret ingredient was to add the cooked flesh of an acorn squash during the final simmering of the chili. It mellowed the flavor and added body and sweetness.....and no one is the wiser. Leaving out the meat and using vegetable broth would make it a great vegetarian chili recipe. Anyone who isn't keen on a spicy-hot chili would do well to leave out the cayenne and one TBSP of the chili powder. I used the entire jalapeno, so I can't advise as to what one TBSP of jalapeno is or isn't. All in all, a very satisfying, flavorful and super easy recipe that lends itself to a pantry ingredient staple. I'm happy to have come across this one on a cold, rainy weekend.

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe and added some tweaks I read from reviews as well as my own. I took this to my work chili cookoff and won! The tweaks are as follows: -1 onion instead of 2 -1 T of cumin instead of 2 -1 orange pepper instead of green (I thought it added nice color!) -1 whole jalapeño instead of 1 T -1 can of tomato sauce instead of 2 -1 can of tomato paste (I prefer a thicker, spicier chili) -3 T of chili powder instead of 2 -1 tsp of cocoa -1 can of beans in chili sauce instead of 1 can of kidney beans and 1 can of black beans -1 cup of beef stock instead of water All other ingredients were the same and I used ground beef (80/20) and smoked paprika. It was a crowd pleaser!

attributes.source_text: I took this to my work chili cookoff and won!

reviews.review_text: I love this recipe! It's our absolute favorite, my husband especially loves this. I have to make it for Superbowl every year. I use only ground beef, we don't like the turkey flavor. Everything else I follow expect for only 1 tablespoon chili powder and 1 tablespoon cumin because those two ingredients are so overpowering. We also like it with a big kick so I add a bit more cayenne than called for. The other addition is hot sausage links, I slice and cook them separately and then add to the chili when it's almost done. We use all the toppings suggested and corn bread to go with it. I put it in a crock pot on low to keep warm during the game and the by half time the whole thing was gone! Lot's of compliments on this one and since there were no left overs my hubby is demanding another batch ;)

reviews.review_text: DH says he wants this again. So did DD (5 years old) & another fellow. It is delicious along with being simple to make. I did tone down the heat by request. I used regular ground beef, no green pepper but I added big chunks of fresh white button mushrooms instead, no jalapeno, a good quality regular canned tomatoes instead of Mexican-style which I chopped, jarred tomato sauce, sea salt to taste, sweet paprika, only kidney beans as that is what I had on hand, plus the rest of the ingredients. I will make a version of this again insha Allah (God willing).

reviews.review_text: So, I have made this exact recipe over 50 times. It deserves 5 stars. (The original recipe on another site called for Rotel tomatoes by the way.) I've also modified it some. My best batch is the same but use both smoked salt and smoked paprika. Also, use two cans of Rotel using mild, original, or hot too adjust flavor. Do not drain Rotel. Then, you can add up to 8 ounces of water depending on how viscous you like your chili. Oh, almost forgot. After draining fat cook spices with meat, onion, green pepper and jalepeno before adding tomatoes. Sauteed spices bloom and make for a more robust flavor. I also add a teaspoon of garlic powder to the spice mix. Best.

OMG this was great! This will always be my go to Chili. My first batch made was exact as the recipe called for but the 2nd batch I wanted more beans and added 1 additional can. I used lean organic gr beef & I did find the smoked paprika to use. This recipe lasted 2 meals for 2 people so I doubled my batch to go further. My toppings was avocado slices on top with sour cream, fresh cilantro and jared jalapenos. I omited cheese due to the extra fat and really did not need it. My husband added Franks red hot sauce to his and he loved it and I did not. I think it took away from the original chili taste. It gets better after eaten the next day. All the spices seem to blend together.

Perfect! My usual go-to chili recipe is a complicated, 100-ingredient, 4-hours-in-the-kitchen dish. It's yummy but I needed something quick and simple that I could put together easily on week nights. This recipe is awesome! I followed it pretty much to a T, but used ground beef, added 1 extra jalapeño and 2 additional TBs of chili powder, and decreased beans to 1 can because I ran out :)

reviews.review_text: Very good base recipe.....I have make this a few times and have found out you can tweak this recipe and still have a good dish. I used turkey but venison is best. I substituted coffee for the water - black coffee is a must for chili, 1TS coco, rotel mild tomato sauce and rotel chili tomatoes for some extra flavor, did have the smoked paprika and it makes a real difference, and franks hot sauce for the cayenne and left everything else as is. I make many different chili recipes quite often and this one is a real winner, great taste! If you are thinking about giving this a try you have thought too long because it will be worth your while.

attributes.source_text: did have the smoked paprika and it makes a real difference

reviews.review_text: I know some people say beans don't belong in chili but, I LOVE beans in my chili and, so, I loved this chili with all it's beans.  I made this as is, though I halved the jalapeno, chili powder and cayenne to appease my husband's stomach.  Turned out perfect for us and all gave 5 *'s except for my husband, who says he prefers my old, boring chili...too bad, this is getting 5 from the rest of us!  Next time I'm using 2 cans of black beans, only because I LOVE black beans.  This was great with corn bread.  Thanks KelBel, I'll be making this again...whenever I want that wonderful aroma of black beans in my house :)

items.label: Soft Peanut Butter Cookies
items.name: Soft Peanut Butter Cookies
items.description: This is my mother-in-law's recipe.She was always baking and this is one of my favorite recipes she had.
instructions: Cream butter, peanut butter and both sugars together.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well.
Add baking soda, powder and vanilla.
Stir in flour.
Roll into balls, roll in sugar. Flatten cookies, using a fork, in a criss-cross pattern.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 350 degrees for 6-7 minutes or adjust to suit your oven and size of cookies!

reviews.review_text: I had to leave a review after my husband yelled from the other room, "babe these are @&$!-ing amazing!!" After reading the other reviews I used heaping amounts of the peanut butter and flour (rather than adding a full measurement if that makes sense). Used real, unsalted butter and all natural peanut butter. These came out so great. Not overly sweet at all despite rolling in sugar (also, I used bakers sugar both for the dough and for rolling) Afraid of having pancake cookies as other reviewers stated, I left the first batch alone in ball shapes. Once the timer went off, I checked and they had not fallen at all. They actually appeared to be not-quite done yet so I left them for a few minutes longer (probably a total of 10min. Shown in the photo when I realized they needed more time). They came out incredible. Lightly crisp on the outside and soft and *almost* undercooked on the inside. In the photo posted you can see them compared to the fork-flattened cookies. The second two pans I made I flattened the balls with a fork and they came out perfect. *note* typically in a cookie recipe I will bake on the shorter end (ex: this recipe says 6-7 min, so I went for 6). These actually come out perfectly soft with the full 7 minutes if flattening with a fork. Thanks for the recipe, I'm glad I tried it out!!

reviews.review_text: These are, honest to God, hands down, the BEST peanut butter cookies I've ever made! I made them a normal size, slightly smaller than the palm of my hand. The recipe yielded almost 3 dozen cookies for me and after everyone was done eating their fill right out of the oven, I only had about 8 for leftovers. It didn't specify which type of brown sugar so I used dark. I also didn't pay attention to the baking time, but instead took them out to cool when the outside was crisp and there was no give when I pressed on it. After cooling, the middle was still soft and chewy and the rim was slightly crunchy. Also, this dough is not like any other dough I've had for cookies. It was very wet and hard to "roll" into a ball. Don't panic! I thought I measured wrong and almost added more flour but it's perfect the way it is! I just scooped some with a big spoon, dropped and rolled it around in a bowl of sugar, and pressed it with a fork on the pan. All in all, my new favorite, go to cookie recipe. I'm doubling the it and baking again today! Thank you so much for sharing!!

reviews.review_text: I followed the recipe to the letter, weighing the ingredients, preheating the oven, so forth. The recipe says butter or margarine; I didn't have enough butter, so I used "I Can't Believe It's Not Butter" by weight. I looked up the weight equivalent. I used a stand mixer to whip and cream the wet ingredients with sugars and combined flour with sodas separately. I refrigerated the wet for 10 minutes before combining flour mixture. Spooned the cookie dough on a Wilton sheet and baked 7 minutes. They puffed up while cooking and looked nice when removed, but after cooling they went flat. Taste was correct, somewhat sweeter than I usually like, but they tasted fine, cookies were a bit chewy in a good way without crumbs. I'm convinced the full 1 cup of margarine was the culprit. Dough was very oily as I rolled them into balls while prepping. I added an extra 1/2 cup of A/P flour to try and make them stand a little better. It improved very slightly, but I was still a bit disappointed.

reviews.review_text: Lovely dough - Fantastic cookies!. Used my 1/8 cup cookie scoop (I like bigger cookies) and just plopped them off of the scoop into a bowl with 1 cup of sugar (could have used a bit less sugar, as I had about 1/3 cup sugar left over, but the extra sugar did make it easy to roll the dough around). Plopped the sugared dough balls onto parchment lined baking trays, and dipped fork into sugar to keep from sticking to cookie. Unbaked cookies were 2 1/4 to 2 1/2 inches in diameter and 1/2 inch thick. Total baking time was 16 minutes (Switched & rotated trays at 7 minutes). Ended up with 36 awesome cookies between 3" and 3 1/2" in diameter. Kids loved them! Great, easy recipe that will be a cinch to memorize - 1 of everything except eggs and flour! I bake cookies every Friday (Cookie Friday) for my family and will gladly put this recipe in the rotation. Thank you!

items.description: These are wonderful, quick cookies. It is one of the first things I learned to "cook." You can add more or less oats (3 cups work best for me). I have found that the weather makes a difference on the consistency, its best to make them on a nice sunny day.  Also,  It is very important not to boil them for longer than one minute.
instructions: Add the first six ingredients into a 4-quart sauce pan.
Bring to a rolling boil and hold for 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Add peanut butter into the hot mixture and stir until melted.
Add in vanilla. (almond extract is good also, but I only use 1/2 teaspoon almond extract with 1 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract).
Mix in the dry oats until they are completely coated.
Drop cookies by tablespoonfuls onto wax paper.
Let cool until set.

*Please remember that even if you do follow the recipe exactly, it doesn't always turn out just right.  I've had these not set up for me or be hard and dry.  But most of the time, the recipe is just right. I adjusted the sugar in the recipe by substituting 1/2 cup of white sugar for 1/2 cup brown sugar, this makes them more moist. I have also found that it makes a difference if you use quick cooking oats or old fashioned.  In my experience it takes more old fashioned oats than quick cooking and I like the texture of the quick cooking better. When you make it a few hundred times like I have you learn a couple of things:) Also, Chunky peanut butter tends to make them more dry and crumbly.

reviews.review_text: I had high hopes for these cookies. They seemed so simple, and I was looking for a chocolate-based cookie that was easy to make. But review reports of how sensitive the recipe was to this or that did have me worried. But I was determined to do it by the book on my first try (except using Nutella instead of peanut butter) ... and then do variations, if needed, should the resulting cookies still seem worth it. So I got everything going, and as I was ready to pour my 3 cups of quick-cooked oats into the just cooked hot mixture ... I realized that I had only 2 cups! Yikes! To be so far off on a recipe that required so much precision. Darn. I felt sure I was headed for disaster. I thought I might have some regular oats, but didn't. So I decided to add a cup and a quarter of unsweetened coconut flakes that I happened to have on hand, figuring that they'd absorb almost as much liquid as the oats. (The extra quarter cup would make up the difference, I hoped.) I mixed in the oats and coconut, spooned out the mixture into mounds onto wax paper ... and prayed that this last-second Plan B ad lib wasn't a total loss. They are FABULOUS!! Very fudgy in taste consistency (which I like), but pleasantly chewy, not crystalline or brittle like some fudges. So I'm loving my mistake! :-) What a great cookie recipe!!

attributes.source_text: pleasantly chewy

reviews.review_text: The recipe states that using chunky peanut butter will cause the cookies to be more crumbly or drier. This is because you are reducing the amount of actual peanut "butter" that you put in the cookie when using crunchy. To compensate for this, increase the amount of peanut butter. When using regular crunchy peanut butter, just add another couple of tablespoons. When using super chunk, I would actually double the amount of peanut butter. I have been making these cookies for at least a decade. As we have no central air conditioning, they are my go-to cookie in the summer, and all my boys love them! Also, the original recipe I use is almost identical, except that it uses half as much as butter, and the cookies still come out great. So those of you watching your fat intake might want to give this a try. One last note. If your cookies consistently come out too soft, sticky, or take a long time to harden, try boiling the mixture for a minute and 30 seconds instead of just one minute.

reviews.review_text: This recipe is amazing! I threw in some chocolate chips and white chocolate chips at the end for a little extra bling (I could also see adding nuts or raisins or cranberries). I also used half quick oats and half regular oats, and Hershey's dark cocoa powder because that's what I had on hand. This recipe is very forgiving, and I love that it uses ingredients most home cooks and bakers have on hand. And only one messy pot, one stirring spoon, one measuring cup, and one measuring spoon got dirty in the process. The cookies themselves set up nicely. Mine were a tiny bit crumbly, but I think that's the variation the author refers to. It's 115 outside right now, and even though I have ac, the kitchen has lots of windows and French doors and it gets a little warm in there. I literally dropped these cookies from a tablespoon with very little shaping, I do think next time I make them, I might do a little "roll in a ball and flatten down with a sugared fork" just to make them a little more uniform and a bit prettier. I think this would also help pack them down a little bit and limit some of the crumbling. There seemed to be a lot of the boiled mix compared to the oats, but I wanted more of that toffee-ish goodness vs more oats, so it worked out fine for me. Because my family has multiple food allergies, I tried the recipe again several times with a few safe substitutions. It worked just fine with coconut oil instead of butter, quinoa flakes or crispy rice cereal instead of the oatmeal, rice milk instead of dairy milk, and Sunbutter instead of peanut butter. These variations all set up a little differently, but the steps were exactly the same and the cookies still fit the bill as quick and sweet. It's a very forgiving recipe, so don't be afraid to make it your own.

This being Jamaica and the humidity and heat in the un-air-conditioned kitchen, making it feel like 92, I put the cookies into the fridge to cool (left one pan on the kitchen table so we'll see the difference). All that being said, even before they set, I know they are going to be winners with my chocolate loving hubby when he gets home because they were fab going into the fridge. reviews.review_text:
This recipe is very similar to one I got from my grandmother for peanut butter oatmeal cookies (basically, double up on the peanut butter and eliminate the chocolate chips). Her recipe calls for Quick Oats, so I've never tried using any others.

The one crucial difference between the two recipes is that in the one I got from my grandmother, you need to let the boiled ingredients cool for about five minutes before adding the peanut butter and other ingredients. Don't worry - it'll still be hot enough to melt everything. But I have found through bitter experience that if you don't give the syrup those five minutes to cool the cookies will not set.

Oh well, I guess that's the way the cookie crumbles....My daughter (11) made these and I told her...don't walk away while you are cooking the first 4 ingredients!  But, next thing I know I look at the pot and it's boiling and she's playing with her little brother.  So, I think they may have boiled about a minute and a half and though they were really really good...they did fall apart when they were supposed to "set" up.  So, I rolled (squeezed) the cookies into balls and they kept their shape fine!  The balls were golf ball sized because that's how big they were when I squeezed the cookies together..and I think they should be about half that size...like a whopper candy.  They were not dry but moist and chewy!  Thanks for the recipe...I love that I could let my daughter practice "cooking" and she got a refresher on fractions in the process!

reviews.review_text: This was the first time I ever tried a no-bake cookie so I wasn't really sure what to expect. (I've made rice krispy treats but those aren't really cookies.) I sort of eye-balled the peanut butter to 1/4 cup. This smelled really good. I had no wax paper so I just sprayed a sheet of aluminum foil lightly w/Pam. reviews.review_text:
If you follow the recipe as-is, this is extremely delicious. This has always been one of my favorite cookies ever and I was glad to find the recipe here since I lost mine. Yum!

It's important to follow the directions and add the first four ingredients first, like it says. If you don't boil it following the directions or add too much vanilla or milk the cookies will be gooey and not set up right. If you boil it too long, the cookies will be dry. I made this recipe following the directions and ingredient amounts exactly and it turned out exactly like it is supposed to.

Yum!! I do use crunchy peanut butter, because I love having chunks in it, but it's just as good with regular peanut butter too. These are really good cookies!!

People who don't make the recipe the exact way stated and then leave anything lower than a five star review really irritate me. If you want to alter the recipe, you should make the recipe first as stated and review it on that and then go to the tweaks section when you make it a second time your way. And for the commenter "CLS," it sounds like he/she didn't even make the recipe. I made the recipe exactly as stated (with the exception that I had about an extra 1/8th of a cup of oatmeal in my can so I just threw that in there as well and they turned out delicious and wonderful (and 12 hungry drill sergeants agree with me.) Great recipe and I love the addition of brown sugar. (I'm not a huge fan of almond extract so I did straight vanilla.) Thank you!

reviews.review_text: This recipe has a great flavor - I have made similar recipes before, but without the peanut butter, and I do like the peanut butter variation.  But, it simply never set.  I have no idea what I could have done wrong - it wasn't a case of humidity, as these were made in dry New England winter air.  The recipe I usually follow has similar proportions of ingredients (minus the peanut butter) but calls for boiling for 3 minutes.  I made sure to follow this new recipe to a T - boiling for no more than a minute, as another reviewer warned against.  My usual recipe sets up quickly - no refrigeration needed.  This one wouldn't set up even after significant refrigeration.  I kept it to use as an ice cream topping (and it's a very tasty ice cream topping.)  Very disappointing.  I suspect that changing the amount of boiling time would have made the difference.

My mother and grandmother always made these when I was a kid. I got a craving for some and this recipe had the best reviews. I used white sugar instead of brown (didn't have any), unsweetened almond milk instead of dairy (personal preference). I also added an extra half cup of oats because it didn't seem like enough. I also added hemp seeds simply because I add them to anything they'd be easy to incorporate into, and they're super healthy! Mine turned out perfectly and set up just fine. Altitude, temp, and humidity can greatly affect a recipe so to those who had bad luck, try again! And good luck not eating a couple spoonfuls before the cookies set up ;)

I made a few modifications: - I halved the recipe - instead of "cookies", I'm used to making fudge out of this. So, I poured everything into a small, flat pan at the end, so that it could harden and then be sliced--this makes the recipe a little quicker and faster. I believe I used too many oats--next time I will use 1 cup instead of 1.5 cups. I may have run into issues because I used larger oats. Tips: - The mixture boils extremely fast--have all of your ingredients pre-measured and ready to go as soon as you turn the stove on. - Microwave the butter on low power to soften/liquify it - Use finer oats if you can--this will make it easier to mix.

Here in New England these are a very popular cookie.  Everyone makes them for the holidays and for pot lucks, cookie sales etc.  I have even seen them sold along with lemonade at a lemonade stand some little ones had during their yearly yard sale.  This is just like the recipe I use, and they come out so good!  They are between a cookie and fudge, and that is why I love them so much.  Great for anytime you are having those overpowering chocolate cravings too!  Here we call them Chocolate No Bake Cookies, but no matter what you call them, they call you too.  Right to the cookie jar!  Word to the wise.  If you want them to come out like in the picture that Culinary Explorer posted use 3 cups of oats.  If they seem a little soft just let them sit out and harden for awhile, because if you add too much oatmeal they won't be shiny and fudgy and they will be like hockey pucks, trust me!

reviews.review_text: Made this last week for the first time with my 8 yo granddaughter. I did add additional oatmeal because the mixture seemed a little soft (not sure that I really needed to, but wanted to make sure they set).. These turned out delicious! Delicious!  Like others, I 'tweak' mine to be what I need.  I have a son who is the pickiest eater on the planet.  At not quite six feet tall, he only weighs 120 pounds.  He'll eat pizza and 'junk food', but as he is now eighteen, I've given up trying to lecture, nag or 'force' him to eat well. No one notices the difference, it doesn't change the texture at all, and I feel like the non-eater kid is getting a bit of a nutrition boost.  :D  Thank you for posting this recipe!!

items.label: Chicken Tikka Masala
items.name: Chicken Tikka Masala
items.description: This recipe appeared in the Chicago Tribune on 4/17/02. The dish has turned out to be extremely popular but be advised that it's very spicy when the recipe proportions are adhered to. Unless you want a super-hot dish, I recommend cutting back on the ground red pepper in the marinade. It may also be a good idea to remove the seeds and veins from the jalapeño chile in the sauce.
instructions: Soak bamboo skewers in water.
Thread chicken on skewers, and marinate (in the refrigerator) for an hour or so.
Discard marinade.
For sauce, melt butter on medium heat.
Add garlic & jalapeno; cook 1 minute.
Stir in coriander, cumin, paprika, garam masala & salt.
Stir in tomato sauce.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in cream; simmer to thicken- about 5 minutes.
Grill or broil chicken, turning occasionally, to cook through- about 8 minutes.
Remove chicken from skewers; add to sauce.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro Serve with basmati rice, naan or pita bread.
Note: You can make your own garam masala. McCormick also makes garam masala; it's available in super markets.

reviews.review_text: I had just about given up trying to make Indian food at home. But where we moved there is no Indian restaurant. What usually happens is, I will google "best tikka masala recipe," read the reviews, and choose the one with the most stars. In the past, I have wound up with a disappointing, bland dish and yet my entire house and clothes smell like onions/garlic. THANK GOODNESS I landed on this recipe! I was looking for something delicious to make and googled "most delicious food" images. Scrolled and scrolled until I landed on tikka masala and found these reviews. It was already dinner time by the time I found the recipe, so I refused to go shopping and used what I had. It was not the only the best CTM I have ever made but one of the best I have ever eaten! Here is what I substituted (and made the whole dish less than half hour): First: the only chicken I had was about a pound of frozen skinless/boneless breast from the freezer that had been cooked on the stove-top with salt and lemon pepper. (We keep this on hand in baggies in the freezer as it can be used in a lot of recipes.) This cut out the whole marinade step, which I didn't have time for anyway. For next time, I will will marinade, cook and freeze some chicken from this recipe to have it ready! So due to my time limitations, this all came down to the sauce. -I doubled the sauce recipe as many advised. -I didn't have a jalapeno so I used a small can of green chilies -I used cumin seeds in the garlic/chili saute instead of powder (then added more some cumin powder anyway) -I accidentally added extra paprika but no harm done at all -I added a diced onion to the saute before the tomato and then just enough tomato to keep the saute moist until the onion had a chance to become translucent. Then added the rest of the sauce. -Since I didn't use the marinade recipe and had ginger on hand, I minced a heaping tablespoon or two of ginger into the saute as well (so glad I did!) -I also used the juice of a lime squeezed onto the pre-cooked chicken I had defrosted in the microwave. -Since the recipe was doubled and a lot of people added more tomato, I used the whole 32 oz can of tomato pure (Didn't have sauce; this was thicker and it worked better because I didn't used cream.) -Didn't have cream, so substituted 2% milk. -Added a peeled, cubed microwaved potato. -Added some frozen peas. -I tried a couple of bites with just a splash of Natural Bliss creamer (which is sweetened). This was actually delicious but we preferred without it. I feel better eating this recipe without the heavy cream. Still ate too much! -Served with left-over white rice (re-steamed in microwave). -Didn't have fresh cilantro to garnish. Everything else and all other ingredients were the same as the recipe. Next time I will be more prepared but I was just amazed and so impressed that I got an authentic Indian restaurant taste in less than half an hour! Thank you so much for this recipe! I have bookmarked it and will return again and again!

attributes.source_text: authentic Indian restaurant taste

reviews.review_text: I have made this recipe about 1/2 a dozen times and love it.  After making it exactly as written twice, I now add 1 teaspoon of sugar and 1/2 teaspoon of nutmeg.  It seems to enhance the flavor of the sauce and soften the finish.  I also make this recipe with fat free milk rather than cream which significantly cuts down on the fat.  Using the fat free milk rather than cream leaves the sauce pretty thin.  To counter this, I have tried two methods.  The first method I have tried is simmering the sauce on low heat for about 2 hours.  This definitely helps.  The 2nd method I have tried is to create a basic white sauce (1 T butter, 1 T flour.  Melt butter and flour in pot together for about 2 minutes.  Add 1 cup fat free milk.  Stir/whisk frequently.  Will thicken in 5-7 minutes)  Add sauce ingredients to the white sauce.  In order not to add additional fat to the recipe, I saute the garlic and peppers with a squirt of non-stick spray.  Making these changes cuts the fat down to about 33% of total calories and the calories down to about 310 per serving.

I adjusted this immediately by taking out the salt (it is easy to get salty with curry dishes, so many spices used already include salt.) I also was out of Paprika (as a Hungarian, I should be shot) so I put extra Curry Powder into the sauce, even though I think Garam Marsala powder already has that. I had to go to a second Publix (same chain, different location) to find fresh ginger and the Garam Marsala powder (not McCormick but Badia brand). Fresh Ginger is cheap, but you only need an inch or so and the bulk packs have 20 times that. Use it though, the aroma as you mince it is worth the buck fifty.
  I simulated the Garlic Naan by  spreading fresh minced garlic and melted butter on a Boboli and grilling. I think Pita would work just as well.
  The next time , NO CINNAMON (not a big fan).  I will broil the chicken on a well-oiled sheet instead of grilling (the skewerâ€™s clung to the grill like Gollum to the Ring). This should keep more of the marinade on the meat as well.
 Maybe the time after I will forgo the sauce and rice and try a fusion with Pita and Tzatziki. If I do this I might integrate the cilantro into the marinade. This is turning into a fun way to eat chicken.

Excellent! Just like the dish I've ordered twice at an Indian restaurant in Seattle. The first time I ordered it my husband neglected his own dish that was different from mine and helped himself to my dinner! I followed the recipe very closely with a few exceptions. I cut down the cayenne in the marinade to 1 tsp because of my children. As other reviewers suggested I doubled the sauce but substituted the whipping cream for a can of coconut milk and added 1/4 cup of whipping cream to get 2 cups. I did not skewer the chicken but put the pieces on a vegetable grilling pan and broiled it in my oven. Because of the amount of chicken I had to do this several times. For convenience I think the next time I will just quickly brown the meat on the stovetop and let the sauce cook it the rest of the way. Except for that I would make it again exactly the same way. The basmati rice really complements this dish (another reviewer said the basmati rice tasted no different than the long grain rice she usually makes but there is a wonderful difference. With basmati rice there is no need to cover it up with sauce. It tastes great all on it's own or garnished with cilantro. You'll want to have the naan or pita bread to dip in the extra sauce. As others have noted, it also really helps to have all the ingredients prepped and measured ahead of time so when you are ready to cook it's just that easy. I'm looking forward to having this again! Many thanks to the person who shared this fabulous recipe!

reviews.review_text: I've made this dish scores of times now, and it's become one of my go-to's when preparing a meal for anyone who likes Indian. I do have a few thoughts that I think people might find helpful, so thought I'd take the time to register an account and add them. 1) The dish IS pretty spicy when measured exactly to recipe. I think it's perfect, but be sure that none of your guests are "heat sensitive." I had three people sweating and dabbing their brow once when I made it, and made sure to ask going forward. 2) I disagree with the top comment that it doesn't matter what cream/milk/etc. to use, that anything is fine. I made a sweet potato version for a vegetarian friend, and almond milk made a sub-par sauce. Similarly, when using skim milk to lower calories, the consistency was not nearly as good. Yes, the powerful spices override the flavor, but texture is important. To me anyway. 3) Buy great spices. I bet I made this a dozen times using McCormick and stuff from the grocery store, but for my birthday I was given some high end spices and it makes a HUGE difference. 4) Suggestion #3 comes with a caveat. As much as the great spices make it better, it is imperative to be careful how much you use. I'd start with using 1/2 to 2/3's the recommended amount if using top shelf spices. Great as they are, they can get overpowering. Not so much for the marinade, just the sauce. 5) If your local grocer has boneless skinless chicken thighs, these are even better for the grill. 6) Also disagree with a top commenter who said grilling wasn't needed, and just boil/broil/bake/sautee them. If you don't overpower the dish with spices, the wonderful charred taste of chicken goes wonderfully with the spice combination. 7) Last but not least, marinating the meat for longer (I tend to go for overnight), seems to provide a superior final dish. Seriously, if anyone is a fan of Indian, and is on the fence about trying this recipe, do it! You'll not only bookmark it, but probably memorize it!

reviews.review_text: Wow! I am an American and enjoy all types of ethnic foods but Indian is both my husbands and my own favorite.  We even had it overnighted from our favorite restaurant to us on our wedding day so we could have it the next day. I have attempted to make this dish many times and this is the closest I have ever come to if not better, restaurant quality.  Ok about this recipe...I read many of the recipes and made these tweaks.<br/>1.  Didn't want to grill and only wanted to use cook top method.<br/>2.  Marinated chicken as directed and then  tried to remove as much marinade as I could but found it difficult as it is thick, so the pieces were pretty much covered in it when I put them in the pan to cook.<br/>2. Heated the pan with butter, garlic, added all spices, added double the tomato sauce and then chicken.  Mixed really well.  Brought up the heat and then slowly started to add half heavy cream and half & half (save on calories...yea right).  Turned down to low and simmered.  Added a pinch more nutmeg but next time, will add even more.<br/><br/>I like my Tikka to be slightly sweet, so added golden raisins to sauce.<br/><br/>I used Jasmine rice and added golden raisins as well.<br/><br/>Yes this is very spicy, so next time I will cut back on black pepper or paprika.  If you don't like "heat", do it your first time around.

reviews.review_text: I made this tonight for my fiance who was coming down with a cold as I know that he loves Indian food, to make him feel better.  As soon as he took his first mouthful, his eyes became like saucers, and he couldn't stop raving about how amazing it was! I'd never made Indian food before, but I liked the 'easy to prepare' marinade and grilling idea for the chicken.  I didn't have the skewers, but lined a baking tray and grilled them under a medium grill, turning 1/2 way through for about 15 minutes.  Completely forgot to go out to the store and pick up coconut milk, but the whipping cream turned out just fine.  When I first added the cream, I was concerned that the sauce was a little pale, so I think I compensated by adding a bit more tomato sauce/additional chile powder/cumin to colour it up a bit, so it probably turned out a little spicier than the original recipe.  Picked up yoghurt which had a little honey in it by mistake, so the marinade smelt quite yummy, too.  All in all, a wonderful recipe that has my fiance purring like a kitten.  Thank you for posting!

reviews.review_text: Absolutely great great recipe!!!! I doubled it as guests were coming over. It was my first time making Chicken as I don't eat it myself. However, I added a bit of red color to make it look more appealing to the guests. Regardless of the color--it was just too appealing--even my mouth was watering..so I tasted the curry and whooooooosh--it was awesome! I marinated it overnight and cooked it for 8 mins at 200 and then shifted it to 350 till the chicken was cooked (it was certainly my first time making it). Kept the skewers on a brownie pan while it was cooking (someone told me it would be faster). Then moved the chicken to the broiler for 2-3 mins and then took them off the skewers and added to the curry that was on the heat while the chicken was being cooked. (Made the curry ahead of time as well--for the taste to set in well). All in all---it was a GREAT recipe. Everyone absolutely LOVED it. Thank you so much for posting this recipe.

reviews.review_text:
O. Wow. I. Mean. Seriously! We're still talking about this "far better than 5 stars" recipe. I skipped the skewers, just broiled the chicken pieces for 8 minutes on an oiled, foil-lined (oiled foiled... heh) baking sheet, 2nd from top rack, shuffling around once during cooking. The chicken turned out perfectly moist and tender.
Here are my minor ingredient adjustments... I used: 2 large chicken breasts, Greek yogurt, 1 tsp kashmiri chili powder (milder than, say, cayenne), 1/2 seeded and ribbed jalapeno and Half & Half instead of full cream.  I also used Penzey's spices exclusively for this recipe and WOW!!! I can't believe the difference between theirs and grocery store-bought. Miles apart. No, I don't work for them. ;)  Served over basmati rice mixed with peas, dry-toasted raw cashew pieces and cilantro, this was a memorable FEASTIE! Thank you, tgobbi, for this total keeper that's headed for my ~ENCORE~ cookbook!

attributes.source_text: The chicken turned out perfectly moist
perfectly moist and tender

reviews.review_text: I usually give out 5 stars under 4 conditions- If the recipe is 1) easy 2) quick 3) delicious and 4) not in need of major alterations for taste. This one met all these conditions and I couldn't believe how authentic it tasted and how right on point the recipe was! This is coming from someone who grew up on Indian food. I think I finished cooking and eating within an hour, as I prepared the marinade before I left for work. Since it's cold outside, I just used a stove top grill pan- I do recommend not skipping the grilling part. Mind you, I am watching my weight so I subbed in the light coconut milk, used nonfat yogurt for the marinade and sauteed the garlic/jalapeno in nonfat cooking spray. Also threw in a dash of cardamom.  Even with these low cal modifications, it was a hit! Can't wait to try the full fat version (smiles). Next time I make it, I plan to throw in some freshly cut tomatoes and have that simmer with the tomato sauce.

I used this recipe for my first attempt at Indian food. Wow! It turned out great! I'd say it's about a 4 star spiciness level. It actually isn't hard to make either--the trick is to get the right spices. If you've never been to an Indian market, I def recommend it! I was blown away by all the cool products at mine.

I made a few changes to the recipe: used olive oil instead of butter, replaced the cream & full-fat yogurt w/ non-fat yogurt, and at the end it was missing "something" so I added about 1Tbsp of honey--perfect! My sauce was a bit too thick (from using yogurt instead of cream) so I added 1/4C water. And, instead of grilling, I just broiled the chicken for about 10min.

Also I didn't buy any naan which was a huge mistake! It was really spicy so I ended up using whole wheat toast to sop up my sauce & cool my mouth--not exactly as good as naan is!!

Anyway, I definitely recommend this recipe!!

reviews.review_text: I have never tasted Chicken Tikka Masala, but it always looked delicious in the magazine pictures, and I always look for new chicken recipes to add to our repertoire, so I decided to give this recipe a try and I am so glad I did.  The recipe is 4 servings and there are 3 of us, so I thought we were going to have a leftover lunch portion for one of us for tomorrow.  The entire family loved it and DH who usually is very tentative when I try a new recipe went back to the pot and scooped out everything to his plate before we even started the meal.  I broiled the chicken and was not disappointed, it charred very nicely and we did not miss the grilled flavor.  I will go back and marinate and broil another batch or two of this chicken and freeze, so that when we feel like having it in the middle of the week, all I have to do is make the sauce and reheat the chicken right in the sauce.  I will also double the sauce next time, it was soo good.  Thank you so much for sharing, this is definitely a keeper!

reviews.review_text: Main Ingredient is Missing!! Coconut Milk! I would replace the 1 cup of whipping cream for the real stuff. Another thing, there are two brands of Garam Masala, Deer Brand, the better of the two choices is Deer Brand, and not Shah's Deer Brand. You will understand, Shah's is loaded with Turmeric Powder, and Deer Brand is loaded with Cumin, its green looking. The Deer Brand is better tasting, stronger cumin flavor, what Masala should tastes like in Indian Restaurant. I don't add nearly anything this recipe calls for. I fry up chicken on medium heat in olive oil, with 1 cup diced yellow onion, dice small, and minced 2 cloves garlic and enough Garam Masala, to turn the chicken green. Pour in one can of coconut milk after the chicken is cooked low heat. Occasionally stir. You can increase the flavor of the Garam Masala to your liking and heat level, since Garam Masala is spicy.

reviews.review_text:
Absolutely amazing. I've made this recipe 4 times so far, and it is wonderful. I have tried to grill and broil the chicken and found that both taste about the same. I will stick with broiling because grilling is too hard to clean up for me and the outside blackens too quickly and the inside doesn't cook as thoroughly. I have tried various levels of heavy cream or half and half, and my favorite is only use half the cream and use half and half for the other half. The cream really helps balance out the spice, so I won't skimp on the cream because my husband doesn't like it too spicy. I always make 50% more sauce than chicken, because I like the sauce so much on my rice.
I eat this with basmati rice (I use the rice cooker and put the basmati rice in like any other rice, except I add a pinch of whole cumin seeds.
I recently made this for a potluck and my Indian coworker says it's better than hers.

my Indian coworker says it's better than hers

reviews.review_text: I gave this recipe 4 out of 5 stars because OMG is it just me or is 2 teaspoons of ground red pepper maybe a tad bit too much? I did not discard the "marinade" ( it was super thick, so not sure how you'd do that in the first place) or skewer the chicken. I just cooked it in a skillet as I have other similar tikka masala recipes, then added the sauce ingredients after the chicken mixture was sufficiently cooked. I also substituted low fat coconut milk instead of the cream. At first the sauce seemed a little soupy but thickened up nicely when plated with rice. I like spicy food but this was just waaaayyyy too spicy. It was much easier than other tikka masala recipes I've tried and the flavors were great otherwise. I'm making it again and will cut the ground red pepper down to 1/4 tsp. this time. If we want it more spicy we can add it in after cooking and tasting.

attributes.source_text: thickened up nicely when plated with rice

reviews.review_text: I'm going to add to the choir here. Yup, I love Chicken Tikka Masala and yup, this recipe was every bit as good as my favorite Indian restaurant's. And WOW - I never realized the amount of cream that goes into it, so no wonder I packed on 5 pounds when I used to eat it for lunch almost daily! Made the recipe with only two tiny changes, as recommended: sauteed the chicken in the jalapeno and garlic, and reduced the cayenne to 1/2 tsp. (still fairly hot!). It was delicious! Sadly, I gave most of the finished product to my son and boyfriend because it was too rich for me. That said, now I'm going to play around with this: my favorite restaurant makes a veggie masala that's more tomato-based and has less cream. Going to make this again tomorrow with a bit of half and half and more red sauce, plus cauliflower, peas, carrots and chickpeas. It's fun to have such a good base to play with!

attributes.source_text: every bit as good as my favorite Indian restaurant's
still fairly hot!

reviews.review_text: Made this last night and it was amazing! Here are some changes I made.. 1) I completely took out the jalapeno and only put in 1 tsp of red pepper. It was the perfect heat. Wasn't too hot but gave you the right amount for the flavor. 2) I used lite coconut milk instead of half and half. I used lite to cut back on fat and the sauce was still thick! You just have to let it simmer long enough to reduce. It was still really creamy! 3) I broiled the chicken rather than grilling it. Some pieces got a little crispy which was perfect. 4) I also added thinly diced onions and red bell peppers in the sauce. I just sauted them with the butter and garlic for awhile until they got soft then added in the other ingredients. 5) You don't need to double the sauce. Unless you are doing more chicken than the recipe has. It has plenty of sauce in the original recipe. Highly recommend this recipe!!

reviews.review_text: I went looking for a chicken tikka masala recipe after having some Indian food take-out and loving it. So here's what I did:  I only used 1 tsp of red pepper in the marinade and 1/4 of a jalapeno in the sauce and it was plenty spicy for our tastes.  I also boiled some potatoes and cauliflower and added those to the sauce mixture. Because I was adding those things, I made 1 1/2 times the sauce and then ended up wanting to stretch it further so I added about 1 cup of chicken stock.  The sauce was a little thinner than normal but it was delicious!  DH, who adores Indian food, was absolutely delighted with this dish, as was I. I grilled the chicken in my cast iron grill pan in batches and it was so tender and moist. I served this over basmati rice and we gobbled it up!  I'll definitely be making this one again.  Thanks Judy for sharing this recipe!  It's a keeper!

reviews.review_text: I made this last night following the recipe to the T.  Came out great!  It's a little on the hot side as some other reviewers have reported, however, if you like heat, it's definitely not too hot where it may ruin the dish.  I think most of the heat was in the Marinade between the red & black pepper and the cinnamon, so if you want to cut some heat I would start there.  I tasted the sauce before adding the chicken and it wasn't very spicy at all so if you're thinking about cutting the Jalepeno, don't (Jalepenos aren't that spicy compared with some other chilis). Maybe use a smaller jalepeno if you're very concerned. If you can get 2% or whole milk yogurt, go for it.  Also, the Garam Masala can be picked up at Whole Foods for only $4.  McCormick also makes it so you may find it in some supermarkets but for $4, Whole Foods is the way to go!
