items.description: I've been baking these since I was a little girl. Nothing better than a glass of milk and a couple of warm peanut butter cookies!
instructions: Preheat oven to 375º.
Mix first six ingredients.
Add the rest of the ingredients.
Mix well.
Roll into balls and press down with a fork dipped in sugar or flour.
Bake for 10-12 minutes  on ungreased cookie sheet (I usually grease my cookie sheet anyway). Ovens vary so your baking time may be less. Just keep an eye on them.

reviews.review_text:
Ok, I feel the need to say that the recipe, as written, makes for a very crunchy, very hard cookie. I had to double the recipe and experimented a lot in order to get a good cookie out of this. I bake relatively often and have never had a problem with my cookies spreading and thinning as much as these did, so I eventually opted to refridgerate the dough over night and freeze the pan as well. Make sure not to grease your pan; I used parchment paper on mine to give the dough a little more stick. Even straight out of the fridge these cookies (tablespoon sized balls) only needed to bake for 6 (!) min. I let them continue to warm on the pan for two min before transferring to a rack. The cookies will seem not done all the way but they really firm up a lot on the rack. 

Even if you opt not to refridgerate I would suggest a cold pan, and make sure not to soften your butter too much before blending otherwise you'll end up with frisbees!

Like the original poster of this recipe, I've also been making these since I was a little girl back in the 50's. This recipe comes straight out of the Betty Crocker Cookie book, page 24. I wanted to make Peanut Butter cookies today but thought I'd do some research on Zaar; found loads of recipes but too many comments about cookies "not baking in correct time, too doughy, etc." I was also interested in a recipe that did NOT require chilling!! So, I went back to this time tested recipe, much to my family's delight. I've made these two way: with the sugar-coated crisscross done with a fork and also as Thumbprint Cookies filled with Grape Jelly when they cool. Either way, they are perfect for this early Autumn weather we're experiencing. Five Stars, for sure!

attributes.source_text: much to my family's delight

reviews.review_text:
After a failed attempt yesterday at baking oatmeal,raisin and chocolate chip cookies, I was a bit of baking however, I saw this recipe and thought, these look delicious. I quickly went to the kitchen to see if I had all the ingredients, (mainly peanut butter) and I did. The cookies are in the oven now and the smell is divine. Now that I've taken the first batch of PB cookies out, I can confirm this recipe is not only simple but makes seriously delicious PB cookies. 
I altered  things; 1, placed the dough in the fridge for 5 minutes prior to baking ( I find a stiff dough helps the cookies retain their shape when baking and 2. I sprinkled a little bit of brown granulated sugar in the fork indentations.

This is my favorite Peanut Butter cookie recipe.  A friend showed me a new way to use peanut butter cookie dough, you roll it up in a ball, place it in a mini muffin pan and bake it for half the time, then you take a Reese's peanut butter cup and push it down into the middle of each cookie cup and put back in the oven to bake for the remainder of the time.  The result is absolutely delicious and adds a great spin to this already yummy recipe.  (You'll have to allow each cookie cup to completely cool before turning over and removing from the mini muffin pan).  Thanks for posting and hope you get to try this great idea too! (photo submitted)

This recipe is so fast and easy to make! If you have kids, they can help without any patience lost!  My cookies were soft and stayed soft for days. My first batch I flattened out like a bakery cookie and baked those at 375, for 9-10 mins. but the rest I made thicker so I reduced the temp to 350 and they took the full 12 minutes.  The taste was good, just the right amount of peanut butter flavor (I used Skippy All Natural).  Mine tasted even better the next day. I would definitely use this as a holiday, make-ahead cookie.  The texture of mine were soft, had a slight crumble, but held their form perfectly. There are other recipes on here that do not include the criss-crossing and flattening; people say, "who needs fork marks anyway?"  Me, thank you very much.  I personally prefer the look of the traditional criss-crossed peanut butter cookie.  And for the record... I've made the others also and if you want a traditional peanut butter cookie, this is it!

attributes.source_text: My cookies were soft and stayed soft for days
the rest I made thicker
just the right amount of peanut butter flavor
I would definitely use this as a holiday, make-ahead cookie
The texture of mine were soft
had a slight crumble

reviews.review_text: This recipe is near perfection!  The cookie is crunchy on the outside, but chewy on the inside.   I made them exactly as the recipe is written, except I left them as balls and didn't flatten them down with a fork.  As many other reviewers have noted, these cookies definitely flatten ou.  That's why I gave 4 stars instead of 5.   Even without me flattening them, they were very  thin.  The next time I make these, I will follow user suggestions and add more flour and/or more peanut butter.   BUT seriously they are addictively delicious.

attributes.source_text: The cookie is crunchy on the outside
chewy on the inside

reviews.review_text: I used this recipe as a platform for an experiment of ingredients.  I made one batch exactly as stated, I made another bath vegan by using vegetable shortening for the butter and a cornstarch mixture for the egg, lastly I did one as a low calorie version with splenda for sugar, applesauce for butter and half the brown sugar.  They were all on the dry side.  I would definitely add a tiny bit more moisture to the mix next time.  The vegan ones were the best and I will attribute that to the vegetable shortening.   Thanks for the "control" for my experiment ;)

Made these tonight as part of my early Christmas baking.  Had a huge pregnancy-induced craving for peanut butter cookies, and these were exactly what I was looking for.  I increased the vanilla to 1 tsp and used Reese's creamy peanut butter.  I was going to try chilling the dough before rolling, but decided to just go for it and it worked out fine.  I used parchment paper and rolled the balls in sugar before pressing with a sugared fork per other users' suggestions.  Forming approximately 1 inch balls, I got 60 (2.5 inch) cookies.  I found that 10 minutes was way too long bake time for me (some of them ended up way overbrowned), so I tried some at 8 1/2 minutes but found ultimately that baking them for 8 minutes was ideal for me.  These would be fantastic with a cold glass of milk.  Thanks so much for posting! They were quick and easy and I will definitely be making them again...

attributes.source_text: as part of my early Christmas baking

reviews.review_text: I just made these and they came out very well. I baked for 8 minutes as some other reviewers suggested and they came out with a nice light golden brown bottom and blonde brown on top. Should be pic 35 once approved. I also used a sugared fork. I used Jif Creamy PB. These are lightly sweet not like other heavier and much sweeter recipes. My only complaint is that the pb flavor is also light. I personally would prefer that flavor be a bit stronger. Jif is one of the best pb's on the market so I'm not sure if I'll try another of the leading brands next time or maybe increase the amount of pb by another 1/4 cup or so. Might do both, I'll submit another review once I try again if it makes any differences. Overall I am happy with the results and will use the recipe again. Thanks :)

attributes.source_text: These are lightly sweet

reviews.review_text:
I just made these cookies; and they are fabulous!!! and very easy to make - if you love Peanut Butter cookies, this recipe is a must try. I made 2 batches, the first batch I followed the recipe, the second batch I processed/chopped about a cup of chocolate covered peanuts, I added the crushed chocolate covered peanuts to the mixture and then rolled them into a ball, floured them, and pressed them with a fork... so good! This would be a great recipe to make with children, it is so easy and so fast to make. I hope you try them.
Cheers, Sharon

Delicious!  I just took the last tray of these wonderful cookies out of the oven.  I ate a cookie from the first tray the second they came out of the oven because they smelled so good.  I made these cookies much bigger than the norm, more like a quarter cup dough for each cookie.  I increased the baking time to roughly 13-15 minutes.  The first tray I drizzled with a bit of melted chocolate since my daughter is a chocoholic, but the others I will leave plain.  They are simply delicious as is.  Thank you so much for sharing this recipe!

Good cookie. I used chunky peanut butter and a bit more vanilla. My cookies were on the flat side but that may be due to our very humid weather today. Here in Florida, it is a must to refrigerate the dough. It is too soft to work with if you don't. I used a 1 Tbsp scoop and got 38, 3 1/2 inch cookies that were sugar topped instead of flour criss crossed. 10 minutes is a good baking time. I put a chocolate chip in the center of each cookie when they came out of the oven. A very easy and quick recipe.

I would like to warn bakers that they WILL want to double this recipe.  By the time I was through baking the cookies there were very few left.  It was a big hit in our household, especially with my husband who is a peanut butter cookie expert.  I thought they were wonderful as they did not have an overpowering peanut butter taste.  By the way, in general, I do not like peanut butter cookies....these are the exception.  

They were so easy to make that I could have my 11 year old make these without supervision!

attributes.source_text: especially with my husband who is a peanut butter cookie expert

reviews.review_text: Thank you for posting this fantastic recipe. I've been looking for a "keeper" peanut butter cookie recipe and I believe this is it. They are delicately crispy on the outside and melt-in-your-mouth gooey on the inside. I made the recipe as-is, but added 1 bag of Reese's peanut butter chips. OMG! My only tweak next time I make them will be to add another 1/2 teaspoon of salt; I think they could use just a tiny bit more salt to balance out the sweet. Even without that change, though, they're phenomenal.

attributes.source_text: delicately crispy on the outside
melt-in-your-mouth gooey on the inside
to balance out the sweet

reviews.review_text: I am NOT a big peanut butter cookie fan, but this definitely changed my mind!  These cookies had the greatest flavor and were altogether fabulous.  I can't wait until DH gets home to try these (PB cookies are one of his faves).  I followed some of the other suggestions and used a sugared fork instead of floured and I also used chunky peanut butter.  To my surprise, the peanuts were not very hard and crunchy, but almost blended in with the texture of the cookie.  Anyway, I guess 62 satisfied lovers of this recipe (myself as well) can't be wrong!

I too remember making peanut butter cookies when a lil girl. Your recipe reminded me of "learning to cook" & tasted far better than I ever made them growing(one would hope).
	Delicious peanut butter cookies are one of my fave snacks. I replaced the sugars w/artificial sweeteners & instead of butter I used low-fat artificial butter & they came out amazing.
	So easy, quick, & fun to bake. Great for when one just has an itch to cook.
	Thank you for sharing your recipe.

attributes.source_text: one of my fave snacks

reviews.review_text: I wish I would have read the reviews before making this recipe.  The dough was way too sticky to roll.  I should have added more flour or at least refrigerated it before trying to work with it.  They did spread quite a bit and you couldn't even see the fork marks when they came out of the oven.  The taste was good and I liked the consistency, but I would have preferred a thicker cookie.  I was especially disappointed by their appearance as I had made them for gift-giving.

I loved everything about these cookies, particularly the lightness! I used all-natural, no-sugar crunchy peanut butter, followed the recipe exactly, and I think the sweetness level is fine.. even in the cookies where I hadn't sprinkled sugar on top. My friend wishes these were raised more, more like a traditional pillowy pb cookie, but I prefer this texture. They're not hard, a little spread (not too bad), and very light. I did NOT cool the dough, cooked 12 minutes, tried both an air pan and a dark sheet.. preferred the dark sheet cookies.

attributes.source_text: particularly the lightness
I think the sweetness level is fine
very light

items.label: Microwave Chocolate Mug Brownie
items.name: Microwave Chocolate Mug Brownie
items.description: This makes a delicious brownie for one in about a minute. 60 seconds makes a molten center brownie. 75 seconds make a uniformly done brownie. Be careful not to overcook.
instructions: In a coffee mug, add water/milk, melted butter/oil, a dash of salt and vanilla extract. Whisk well.
Add cocoa powder, whisk well. Add sugar, whisk well. Add flour, whisk well.
Microwave for 60 seconds. Center should be slightly molten. Careful not to overcook.
Enjoy with a spoon. Careful, brownie will be hot.

reviews.review_text: Great recipe! I made roughly the full amount the first time but found that I was totally full 2/3 of the way through, so going forward I've only made half the recipe with a couple modifications, yielding a final recipe of:<br/><br/>1 Tbs butter <br/>1 Tbs milk<br/>pinch of salt<br/>(vanilla, cinnamon, smidge of baking powder, whatever)<br/>1 Tbs cocoa powder<br/>1 Tbs brown sugar<br/>1 Tbs flour<br/><br/>In my microwave it takes 27 seconds. Garnish with a bit of powdered sugar. Yummmm!!!<br/><br/>Also, the nutritional information listed for this recipe is wrong.  Done as I wrote it above it's about 160 calories, so we're looking at 320-350 for the whole recipe (depending on how much flour and sugar you add).

I read quite a few of the reviews, then mixed and cooked this in a cereal bowl, instead of a mug. Melt 2 tbsp butter for about 20 seconds first (butter adds flavor), then added 2 tbsp milk. I used 2 tbsp cocoa powder, 1 tbsp sugar, and 2 tbsp flour, using a small wire whisk to mix in a tablespoon or two at a time. My microwave seems to be pretty hot, so it only took 55 seconds to get a nice dessert, completely done. It would be easy to throw a few chocolate chips on top as it comes out of the microwave. It just takes a minute for them to melt and is almost like "icing." Yum! I was happy to find this recipe because the individual packets now available in the grocery store for making a cake in a mug tastes great, but the first ingredient listed is SUGAR! This recipe was sweet even after adjusting the sugar to 1 tbsp.

attributes.source_text: This recipe was sweet even after adjusting the sugar to 1 tbsp.
it only took 55 seconds to get a nice dessert, completely done

reviews.review_text: I have made this several times with different tweaks. It's almost always a hit. I usually use less flour. Maybe 2 T. I use water rather than milk. And I always use dark, Dutch processed cocoa. Some tweaks that have worked: Use 1 T of whole wheat flour, 1 T regular - add a little bit more liquid. Use Better for Bread flour. Adding a tad of baking powder. Use brown sugar or part artificial sweetener. If it's too hot and you have impatient little ones, add a little milk on top at the end. -- Using all artificial sugar, sucralose, one time it came out too dense - not at all fluffy. I don't know about using any other type of artificial sugar. -- Also good, making part of it ahead of time - Put all the dry ingredients into a baggie and then mixing it well at any time before putting it into the mug that has all the liquid ingredients well-whisked in it. Then whisk the dry & liquid ingredients well. -- You can let the kids mix the dry ingredients for themselves (shake, knead, squeeze) and get several done pretty fast. [Mix the liquid ingredients for the next one as one mug bakes, then let kid add baggie contents]. It's like making magic together. I haven't tried mixing the liquid ingredients ahead of time. -- Other thoughts - adding nuts, raisins, or cranberries? I haven't done it - yet.

I really wanted something to satisfy my sweet tooth, with little effort. And that I got. I microwaved it and changed the recipe to make it a bit healthier.

I used 3 tablespoons of water and only 1 tablespoon of oil(I used smart balance vegetable oil)
I added 3 dark chocolate chips to the middle
Instead of using plain sugar, I used splenda baking blend, which is part sugar part splenda. And because it has a tendency to be so sweet, I only used 2 tablespoons of it.

What I got was a gooey center(from the chocolate chips) in 1 minute and 10 seconds without all of the guilt from the original recipe. It was super rich, i don't think I could have eaten another bite. Awesome! Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: It was super rich
What I got was a gooey center

reviews.review_text: OMG - 535 calories per serving and almost 25g of fat?!!? Not surprising with 2 tablespoons of BUTTER in each serving. (So really this is for food.com for featuring this as recipe of the week).<br/><br/>I'm sure it is probably delicious, and I'm sure I'll get flack for this, but I had to give this 1 star based on how bad this is for you. Paula Deen would likely love this recipe. Even if you split the dessert with someone, it's still pretty bad. No, I don't have to make this or eat it, I just hate to see a recipe that is so over the top BAD for you be featured. It's hard to not be overweight with things like this being promoted to readers....

THIS RECIPE IS DEFINETLY WORTH THE TRY!!! It's absolutely delicious and the brownie turned out so fluffy and just perfect <3 <br/><br/>TIPS!!!<br/><br/>I did make a couple changes to the recipe, though. First, I noticed the amount of calories and fat- 535 calories and 25 grams in a single mug? I don't think so! I decided it probably came from the oil/butter (plus we were out of butter anyways) so just substituted it for the same amount of water. <br/><br/>Second, a lot of people were complaining about it being dense so I added just a pinch of baking powder and voila! It was probably the lightest, fluffiest brownie (or cake for that matter) I had even eaten, it was soooo delicious with a perfect texture. <br/><br/>I cooked it for about a 70 seconds, but next time I might cook it for maybe 10-15 seconds shorter so that there's more of a gooey chocolate centre but otherwise this was flawless! <br/><br/>Next time ill probably add some dark chocolate chips or as some users we saying peppermint pieces or substitute creamy peanut butter for the butter/oil for peanut butter brownies. Also, putting a Reese's peanut butter cup in the centre to melt sounds mouthwatering too!!!<br/><br/>Overall I loved this recipe and I recommend you to use these tips for one of the best brownies you'll ever have!

attributes.source_text: the brownie turned out so fluffy
It was probably the lightest, fluffiest brownie
the lightest, fluffiest brownie

reviews.review_text: I just made this recipe. It ended up as cake in a mug because I left it in a little longer than 60 seconds. I still enjoyed it. The calorie count is probably a little less than the original recipe. On second thought, the egg probably evened it out. I used 2 Tbls. of melted Earth Balance Olive Oil Buttery Spread in place of regular butter, 2 Tbls. Almond Milk, 1/8 Tsp. Vanilla Extract, dash of salt, 2Tbls. Sugar, 2 Tbls. Chocolate Malt Ovaltine, 1 Egg and 3 Tbls. Self-Rising Flour. Next time I’ll probably take it out a little sooner so that instead of cake, it’ll be molten.

Satisfies the chocolate cravings!  I wanted something chocolatey, but it was getting late and I was tired.  These mixed up so fast, and with practice I could have these hot brownies ready in 3 minutes. The hardest part is letting them cool so you don't burn yourself.    They weren't that much like regular brownies, and a regular brownie would win in a taste test. But for something quick this is great. My husband wants them again, and I can see curling up in front of the TV  with a mug of hot brownie on cold winter nights.<br/>I've rediscovered this recipe. Making this once or twice a week, my excuse being that I'm not eating a whole pan at least. I love not having tons of leftovers to tempt me. Make sure to mix the ingredients in order for best results.

attributes.source_text: I wanted something chocolatey
My husband wants them again

reviews.review_text: Okay, it's total instant chocolate gratification.  But did you look at the nutrition facts?  ONE serving, one brownie, one cup, one recipe is 535 calories!  24 grams of fat!  OMG!  Then I looked at the Dietary Fiber....4.4 grams per serving?  How can that be, if you are using only 4 tablespoons of all-purpose (white) flour? You're not getting any fiber from butter, sugar and cocoa powder.  hmmm.  Something is suspect here.  It's a nice, easy, one-person treat, but how am I supposed to figure this into my diet plan if the nutrition facts seem to be screwy?

reviews.review_text: I needed something quick & easy that didn't require the oven on this hot summer Friday night. Just wanted a little end-of-the-work-week treat. This fit the bill! It would have been great with ice cream but I also had limited ingredients so, again, this worked nicely. I got a little confused because the recipe ingredients call for melted butter but there is no mention of it in the recipe...then I noticed the directions called for "oil" ... which translated to melted butter, although it's not the term I would have used. reviews.review_text:
This was fantastic! I've made it twice already. It takes no more than five minutes! 
The first time I microwaved it for 60 seconds- it only had a very small pool of liquid on the surface. The second time I did it for 54 seconds, with the perfect amount of liquid right on top. I thought that the Crisco oil i used the first time was a little too detectable. Butter tasted so much better, and the texture was still perfect. I used Hershey's  half natural coco powder half Dutch-processed. I highly recommend it to anyone who likes things very, very chocolaty.
This recipe is so far my favorite of all recipes I have tried so far on Zaar; for ease of preparation and outstanding flavor!

attributes.source_text: likes things very, very chocolaty

reviews.review_text: So if you follow the ingredient list exactly, the resulting cake will be a bit dry. To fix, just use 3 tbsp of butter, milk, flour, sugar and cocoa powder instead of the recommended amounts. This will make a very moist cake. The portion will also be slightly larger and you'll have to adjust your microwave time up from the 1 minute. I did 90 seconds in my 1000 watt microwave. It left the cake very slightly gooey, which was exactly what I look for in a brownie Just for the record: I did follow the recipe as directed first. I found the cake a little dry and then tweaked it .

attributes.source_text: It left the cake very slightly gooey

reviews.review_text: I'm leaving this review for the people who, like me, have searched through multiple brownie-in-a-mug recipes that ended up tasting like total dirt to find a good one. I have tried a handful of recipes that had good reviews and when they end up tasting like crap even though I followed the directions exactly, I wonder where I went wrong. This is FINALLY a decent recipe that actually tastes like a brownie and doesn't end up dry and bitter (but that can happen to any recipe if you microwave it too long, be wary). I think one of the secrets is to use melted butter instead of oil. It is essential to the way it cooks but doesn't give it an oily taste. If you don't like it to be too sweet, cut the sugar by a tablespoon or two. I also substituted milk for water, which I suggest doing in any cake/pancake/muffin recipe. I cooked it in a 1500 watt microwave for 60 seconds and it was just a bit too liquidy/molten for me so I gave it another 15 seconds and it was great. My end conclusion is that you're honestly just not going to be able to make a perfect tasting brownie like you would by baking a box mix in an oven for an hour by just throwing 5 or 6 ingredients in a mug and microwaving it for a minute, but that when you are craving a chocolate fix and want a decent brownie this recipe will definitely satisfy you! I really hope my review helps someone!

attributes.source_text: actually tastes like a brownie
when you are craving a chocolate fix

reviews.review_text: I ended up using Hersey's special dark for the cocoa powder along with milk instead of water and the melted butter instead of oil. I also have no flour at the moment! To replace the flour I tried grinding 4T of coconut flakes but it wouldn't bake properly so my mom suggested our pancake mix! I added 2T of the mix and it baked amazingly and it came out wonderfully. Super light and fluffy and the added coconut was an extra treat! This is incredibly sweet however so I will probably still play around with it to make it more to my tastes!

attributes.source_text: Super light and fluffy
Super light and fluffy
the added coconut was an extra treat

reviews.review_text: Delicious!  This recipe is so easy to make with ingredients on hand.  You can easily substitute milk for water, other flavorings for vanilla, and canola (or other) oil for the butter.  It's also good with a sprinkle of cinnamon in the flour.  I find that spraying the inside of the mug first with non-stick spray really helps with clean-up.  I also cut down the sugar in favor of a more "bitter" chocolate.  In my microwave it was ready in 55-60 seconds.  When in doubt, check it early.  It will continue to cook a little as it cools. The recipe is also a good choice for those who cannot or select not to eat eggs, or for those concerned with slightly underdone batter.

I made a food.com account specifically so I could post this review. I absolutely loved this recipe, even though I tweaked it quite heavily. It was delicious, and blows away all the other (gross!) brownie mug recipes I've tried.<br/><br/>Substituted butter with olive oil, decreased flour to 2 tbsp as recommended and substituted sugar with 2 tbsp of golden molasses because I didn't have any more sugar. Microwaved on high for 1 minute. The result was soft and fluffy, not chewy at all, very good flavor. Texture resembles cake more than brownie, but still delicious... I recommend this recipe to anyone who's looking for a quick chocolate fix.

The result was soft and fluffy

reviews.review_text: I'm a pretty lazy person when it comes to cooking. I was craving for something sweet or chocolate-y a few hours ago when I found this lovely recipe on tumblr. It took me around 4 minutes to get the ingredients(I'm slow, I know) and 70 seconds on the microwave. It turned out perfect for me! I changed the sugar to 2 tablespoons and it still taste pretty sweet to me. If anyone is wondering how mine tasted like; It tastes like domino's choc lava cake. Without the gooey chocolate in the middle. Just the way I like it :9

attributes.source_text: it still taste pretty sweet to me

reviews.review_text: Talk about yummy and quick!  I made this for my daughter's evening snack and she loved it!  I did make a few changes to cut back on the fat and sugar because she's only 5 1/2 and it seemed like alot for her.  I used only 1 tablespoon of oil and replaced the other with water (I'll use milk next time).  I also used splenda granulated (5 tablespoons) instead of the sugar.  Even with these changes, it still turned out really good.  I tasted it, it was fudgey good.  Thanks, Antilope for posting such a quick little treat!

items.label: Roasted Green Beans
items.name: Roasted Green Beans
items.description: A great alternative to fast-food French fries, my family and friends love these as a snack or hors d'oeuvre. No matter how many I make, it's never enough!
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash, dry well, and trim green beans.
Put green beans on a jelly roll pan.
Drizzle with olive oil.

Sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste (I like them salty so I use about 1 1/2 teaspoons of salt and about 8-10 grinds of the pepper mill). *Mrs. Dash may be substituted for salt and pepper as desired.
Use your hands to be sure all the beans are evenly coated and spread them out into 1 layer.
Roast for 20-25 minutes, turning after 15 minutes, until beans are fairly brown in spots and somewhat shriveled.
Serve hot or at room temperature.

reviews.review_text: May I add a comment and a tip? I've done green beans this way without having seen this recipe -- so many veggies roast successfully. This is delicious! When lazy, I roast the beans alongside a chicken and potatoes in the oven (all-in-one-meal!). You might also find it easier to toss the beans with the olive oil in a mixing bowl before it goes into the oven. Tossing in a bowl coats the beans more evenly and might even use less oil. Then tip into the pan. Another tip: if you can find flaky sea salt like Maldon Salt, salt the beans liberally when it comes out of the oven instead of before. Maldon has such a wonderful "sea salinity" taste and a very satisfying crunch!! I find Maldon is better used after cooking food instead of during, as the taste comes out better. Great of you to post this recipe, Seamouse!!

I made this dish quite awhile ago. I had made turkey burgers and decided to use the roasted green beans as a substitute for french fries. That worked out well. I'm writing a review now because of my husband. He really doesn't like vegetables. He'd be happy to simply have meat all the time. But, I can't make a dinner without some sort of healthy side dish. So, after having force fed himself the yellow squash and zucchini I made last night, I asked him, "Well, what would your favorite vegetable be then, if you had to choose." He replied with the roasted green beans and sweet potato chips that I make. So, I figured this dish deserves a 5 star rating and a review to go with it. I did add some minced garlic to the seasoning and the roasted green beans turned out great. (Oh, and I just put the oil and seasonings in a large Ziploc and shake away until all the beans are evenly coated.  And with some of the oil remaining in the bag, you know you've been spared some extra calories.)  I would like to try to get some a bit crispier, but I haven't figured that out yet. Any suggestions?

attributes.source_text: He replied with the roasted green beans
I did add some minced garlic to the seasoning

reviews.review_text: This was really good.  I normally fry green beans in the skillet, and this was similar to that, with less work.  I didn't really measure anything, just dumped frozen green beans on the pan, then drizzled oil, sprinkled the seasoning (salt and pepper), then tossed it all together with my hands.  After the 15 minutes, I added some chopped garlic when I stirred the beans, then let it all cook a further 10 minutes.  I'll definitely make this again, only I will cook longer, as my beans were cooked but not really roasted.  My own fault, since I left the beans frozen and didn't want to let the rest of dinner get cold.  The ones on the edges that crisped up a bit were heavenly.  Thanks for a new take on green beans.

attributes.source_text: The ones on the edges that crisped up a bit were heavenly

reviews.review_text: I am trying to make myself eat greens even though i cannot stand them. I eat broccoli sometimes covered in cheese but other than that none. The only way I can get greens down is if they are roasted and green beans definitely roast up enough to make me eat them! I put seasonal salt on them and I ate a cans worth (2.5 servings I believe).? I roasted them longer they shriveled up A LOT its about half the amount than when they are out of the can. I enjoy roasted brussel sproats but they are expensive--canned green beans -cheap and easy. After reading reviews I will definitely try a little parm cheese

I gave this recipe 3 stars. I rerated this recipe as the first time my family wasn't crazy over these beans but this time we liked them better. My 6 yr old newphew & 7 yr old niece didn't like these at all. My future hubby said they were ok which was the first review I guess I would agree. First of all I didn't make 2 pounds just a couple of handfuls to try these as this was my first time using fresh green beans and as that's what we had on hand. Mine didn't really look like the pictures the first time I made these mine looked liked they were have the size of the ones in the pictures. Maybe they didn't need as much time to cook as the thicker ones tasted so sweet and yummy. The first time I cooked mine for 25 minutes and the second time I cooked them for 20 minutes. Overall these did taste good. I will make these again! Thanks for posting a good recipe! Christine (internetnut)

attributes.source_text: this time we liked them better
the thicker ones tasted so sweet and yummy

reviews.review_text:
Our family loves these. What a healthy, nice recipe!
(Update) While I really liked them when I first made these, after a few changes, I am loving them even more. I used extra fine frozen greens beans from Aldi. I roasted them (frozen) at 420 for 40-50 minutes. I also omitted the pepper. I served them with balsamic reduction (just boil a cup of balsamic vinegar for about 20 minutes or until it reduces a little to make a light syrup). Soooo fantastic this way!! Would highly recommend trying them with the vinegar reduction.

attributes.source_text: Our family loves these

reviews.review_text: Wow, I was looking for a recipe to duplicate the green beans that my family always eats at our local chinese restaurant and looked all over.  I saw your recipe and wasn't expecting them to taste anything like them, however thought with the rating they had I had to try them.  They are the closest that I have come to their recipe.  We added 3 cloves of fresh minced garlic for 1 lb of green beans and next time would probably back off of the salt a little, possibly try a different flavor of oil, maybe peanut?  This recipe was a huge help Thank You!!!

O.  M.  G.  These are so darn good!

As someone who used to abhorr green beans in any form, I can honestly say that these are INCREDIBLE!
I recently have begun trying all those foods I detested as a ki, and although I found a couple of 'tolerable' recipes for fresh green beans, NOTHING compares to these.  
I made about a pound of fresh beans (all that I had on hand), and they were gone in minutes.

Thanks so much for such an amazing recipe- I don't believe I will cook them any other way ever again!

In the daily "What's for Dinner?" thread a few days ago I saw a mouth watering photo by fellow member, Love to Eat, of his supper.  One of the items on the plate was some delicious looking green beans.  I asked him which recipe he used, and he posted a link to this one.  I made them tonight and, wow, they are soooo good! items.description: Make and share this Mashed Red Potatoes With Garlic and Parmesan recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Put potatoes and garlic in lg pan.
Cover with water.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes, until potatoes are tender.
Drain well.
Mash with the butter, milk, and salt.
Stir in the parmesan cheese.

items.label: Ultimate Pizza Sauce
items.name: Ultimate Pizza Sauce
keywords: c("Low Protein", "Toddler Friendly", "Kid Friendly", "Spicy", "Freezer", "Stove Top", "< 4 Hours")
items.description: This pizza sauce recipe was given to me as a wedding present, written on the inside cover of a pizza cookbook. It is thick, saucy, spicy and delicious. I'll never use anything else on my homemade pizzas. I like to double or triple it and put it in Ziploc bags in my freezer.
instructions: In a large skillet, melt butter with the oil. Add the onion, celery and garlic and saute until soft and transparent.
Add tomato sauce and tomato paste and stir until smooth.
Add remaining ingredients and bring to slow simmer.
Simmer for 30-60 minutes (or not at all depending on your taste and time frame).
Remove the bay leaf and spread the sauce on your prepared pizza dough.

reviews.review_text: I made it in my blender after an accident with the first try so bad I had to throw it out. My husband already had his pizza dough made and ready. Second try turned out good. Watching salt so I did not add the parm. Cheese. Added no salt seasoning instead of salt. No bay leaf because they do not work in the blender. Came out really good. Oh saved a few trans fats by only using olive oil, no butter and that also cuts the salt a bit. Used one can of stewed tomatoes with one can of paste. Omited the celery because stewed tomatoes already has celery in it. Consistancy was perfect. All organic ingredients. The reduced salt is due to high blood pressure. The meats and tomato products have more than enough salt for one meal. Is that 999 mg of salt per serving? If not how many servings are you figuring? Definately will be using this again. If I have time next time will use the simmering method again. If your in a pinch for time, don’t be afraid of trying my method in the blender.

I make pizza often. From finding the best dough recipe to the best kind of mozzarella and of course, the best sauce recipe, it’s a never ending journey. Recently I came up with my favorite dough recipe. It’s simple and it reminds me of pizza huts regular crust, not thin. So now I was back to finding a sauce recipe that would do justice to my fantastic dough. I’ve tried all sorts of sauces. Cooked, uncooked. Whole tomatoes, crushed, raw, paste only sauces. I would be satisfied for awhile with some of them but eventually I went back to the drawing board. I like to have things organized in my life. Especially food recipes that I can always count on to be the same quality every time I make them. I came across this recipe for pizza sauce and like all the others, it claimed to be the best. Taste is a matter of opinion and everyone has their own, including myself, but I am the guy who does most of the cooking so unless I love what it tastes like, I won’t make it a second time. My wife is very easy to please when it comes to food. She doesn’t exactly love to cook, but I do. So, like my pizza dough, I needed to find a sauce recipe I could stay with forever. I’m happy to say I will consider this sauce recipe exactly that. Especially considering that I never purchased fennel seed before and when I bought it, at $5 for a container, I was hoping I won’t be stuck with an ingredient I will never be able to use again. Fennel tastes like whats in sausage. I have seen it in sausage but never questioned what that was lol. It makes perfect sense to me that it is a natural ingredient in pizza sauce. Ok, I agree with the opinion that when a recipe is posted, either you follow it to a tee, or don’t tell us how you “improved” it. So I feel when I tell you that all I did was use more than one garlic clove, it’s not like I changed anything about this recipe. A garlic clove can be many sizes right? There are very small ones and medium size and huge ones. I used several small size ones because it’s only going to taste better with more garlic! I read most of the comments. The majority of them gave high ratings and I always go by the comments and suggestions and ratings of most items I purchase now a days. The one particular comment by several people was the thickness concern. Some of you said you added more sauce. I think that’s fine if you add more sauce to thin this out just a little bit because the intended taste will still be there. Too much sauce and the original flavor will be diluted. Anyway, I love this pizza sauce and I will recommend it whenever possible to my friends. Thank you for sharing it!

Wow! Thank you!

I've made over 50 batches of this by and now double or triple each time. Use fresh basil and oregano and you'll be surprised how much it adds to the quality of flavor!

I use the julienne slicer on my guillotine slicer to make finely chopped onion and celery for the best texture.

What more can you ask for in a sauce?: Fresh veggies, low salt per serving. You only need about 2 heaping Tbs for a 9 inch pie. D E L I C I O U S!

But I have to add a comment regarding the best part of this recipe: Use this as your standard pasta sauce to! Thin with a little water to your liking, add just a dash more salt. Throw in cooked Italian sausage for a meat sauce and use it in your lasagna, stuffed shells, spaghetti with meat sauce, etc. recipes too!

reviews.review_text: I made this for a dinner party.  I accidentally got nominated the designated chef for the group after I showed up with a lamb Napolean one time.  Not that I mind, I enjoy this.<br/><br/>This is one of the few times I've taken a recipe 'as is,' partly because I liked what I saw, and partly because I don't have a lot of experience with Italian dishes.   <br/><br/>Gotta tell you, this homemade pizza may have been the best dinner party we've had in a long while. reviews.review_text: i see alot of people substituting alot of ingredients in this recipe, which kinda defeats the purpose. ive been using it for years, this is a genuine sauce recipe from someone who knew better than us. for instance, the fennel is a key ingredient so dont skip it. once i didnt have any so i added a bit of vodka which to my suprise worked ok but not the same, dont be lazy go get the fennel. a can of puree tomatoe is the same as a sauce/patse mix or try diced tomatoe's ran through a good chopper for a chunkier juicer style sauce. other than that you can sub fresh parsley and a bit of celery salt for celery in a pinch. i always increase the sugar and black pepper for a nice contrast. and maybe even add some red pepper to taste for a spicier version but dont go nuts with it.

This is an excellent pizza sauce. The only change I made was swapping the fennel seeds (I didn't have any) for crushed red pepper. We loved it and I will make more and put it in the freezer. Thank you for a great recipe. Update: I have made this sauce for quite a long time. I use the fennel seeds now along with a pinch of red pepper flakes. I agree with others that this recipe is too thick to simmer so I add 14oz of water using the tomato sauce can plus the tomato paste can as a measure. I then simmer it on the very lowest setting on my gas range for 60 minutes with only a spatter screen as a cover. It thickens up perfectly and is still the best sauce I've tasted.

The pizza sauce is authentic and tastes like the real thing, in less than half the time.  However, I found it would clog up and burn at the bottom. Even at the lowest setting on my stove, despite using a non-stick circulon pan. I was surprised that no one had experienced this problem  in the reviews. Adding sugar or salt increases the boiling point of any liquid making it easy for a thick liquid to scorch or burn, even at low heat. To avoid this problem there are two solutions.  Either make the recipe 'as is'  whilst stirring continually.  Or leave out the salt and sugar until the end and add it in the final minute or two. Even then you may need to watch the pan and check on it from time to time.

I just started learning to cook so when I say this was easy...it was really easy.  Like many I did do some adjustments.  I don't like celery so I left that out and I added crushed red peppers to spice it up.  Other than that I used everything else and it was great!!!!  I never had fennel seeds  or a bay leaf but I was pleasantly surprised.  I only made one pizza and froze the remainder sauce.  Oh and we also used a little sauce for dipping.

reviews.review_text: Yes, awesome. I put the celery, garlic and onion in a small food processor to make a fine texture before I saute. I grind the fennel seed in a coffee grinder to a powder. Lastly, I use the 6 oz can of tomato paste, but instead of 8 oz of tomato sauce, I use a 28 oz can of San Marzano D.O.P. peeled tomatoes. After the garlic, onion and celery are sauteed, everything goes into an electric countertop slow cooker, for 2-3 hours, at low, stirring every 1/2 hour. The results are the finest pizza sauce you will ever have. I store portions of the sauce in 1 quart freezer bags for future use. it will last in the freezer 3 months. Thanks for posting this recipe.

#2.  This time I doubled the batch, omitting one can of tomato paste and doubling the sauce.  I adjusted seasonings to account for the switch.  I also left out the fennel seeds. The Moghul Emperor's servants in the past used it a lot and therefore all Moghulai cuisine uses Fennel. The parmesan cheese also contributes to the flavor. I am going to stick with this recipe. Actually all the other ingredients are what I usually use... but now my pizza sauce is truly No.1 !! reviews.review_text:
This pizza sauce is fantastic! The texture was perfect, and the flavor was outstanding.

I did make a few changes by reducing the oil to 1 tbs. and omitted the butter and salt. The first time I made it, I didn't have fennel and it was very good. After tasting the sauce, I decided to add 1 more tsp. each of basil and oregano, as we like these flavors a lot.

10-3-10 Second time I made this sauce I added 1/8 tsp. fennel and that changed a very good sauce into an EXCELLENT one...so much better than store-bought sauce or sauce served on deli pizzas. I always quadruple the recipe, and it makes 2 quarts - enough for the freezer!

Thanks for sharing an outstanding pizza sauce recipe. This is the BEST!

This is a fantastic recipe.  I've made this several times now (1st time exactly as listed) and would like to share what I've learned. While we like the depth fennel adds we also don't like to bite into a strongly flavored seed.  We have since skipped it.  (Perhaps it would work well if ground or in a spice bag?)  I've also cut the celery and increased the onion to 3/4 cup (only because we don't generally have cellery around).  We also like slightly sweet/spicy so we've upped to suger (I use brown) to about two teaspoons and have added crushed red pepper for some great heat.  Finally, we have taken to adding red wine (about 1/8 to 1/4 cup) and then simmer for about 1/2 hour or until there is no longer an alcohal smell.  It adds a great level of flavor!  Thanks SAMS_Club, this is our new favorite!

attributes.source_text: we also like slightly sweet/spicy
we also like slightly sweet/spicy
have added crushed red pepper for some great heat

reviews.review_text: Just made this sauce for the first time. I was trying out making a pizza margherita using Jeff Hertzberg and Zoe Francois's method in their "Artisan Pizza and Flatbreads In 5 Minutes S Day". I needed a sauce and found this one. Wow!!I was raised in a city with a large Italian population. This is by far the very best sauce I have ever had. I feel like I just indulged in the very best gourmet pizza ever. I will absolutely make this many times in the future. Make enough to freeze in ice cube trays for later, then pop them out into a freezer bag. Take out what you need. You will never regret having this available.

Really good recipe, the fennel seeds definitely made the sauce (I'll start adding fennel seeds to any new future sauces I make). I followed the recipe to a T, my only complaint was how thick it was when beginning to simmer (there is no way it could simmer for an hour being as think as it was). I had to add water so it would not burn on the bottom of the pan. Next time I'll try using more tomato sauce.  However at the end of 60 minutes of simmering it was a perfect thick consistency. Great recipe which helped me distinguish the use of fennel seed is what I've been missing all along when making pizza sauce.

attributes.source_text: it was a perfect thick consistency

reviews.review_text: Yummy!  We felt like homemade pizza last night and this sauce looked really good...  and it was!  It was quite thick even before I simmered it and since I was not going to use it for a couple of hours, decided to add in a 1/4c of water so it wouldn't burn.  I was leary of the fennel seeds but added them in anyway...  they made the sauce!!!  This is a very hearty and flavorful sauce...  most of the time I prefer a "fresher" tasting sauce but this one was perfect for a a nice cheesy pizza...  I used only half the recipe for 1 12in pizza so I have the other half in the freezer, ready whenever we are craving pizza again...  Thanks for sharing!!!

attributes.source_text: This is a very hearty and flavorful sauce
It was quite thick even before I simmered it

reviews.review_text: Mmmmm!  I have been using this sauce for a year now and it is the absolute best!  It keeps well in the fridge and I always have it on hand.  I like to add a lot more of the sugar and wine to make it nice and rich (I really love sweet red wine and will use any excuse to use half a bottle of it!) and I usually just use tomato paste and no sauce because I like it really thick.  I also add chopped up carrots and/or mushrooms depending on what I am using this sauce for, and blend it all up so it is nice and smooth.  This sauce is very versatile, as it can be used for pizza, wings, pasta, meatballs, and most other Italian tomato dishes.

items.label: Tuna Casserole
items.name: Tuna Casserole
items.description: Make and share this Tuna Casserole recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Cook egg noodles to al dente in boiling salted water; drain well.
Preheat oven to 325°F.
Mix all ingredients together in a large casserole dish, reserving 1/2 cup of cheese.
Sprinkle reserved cheese over the top.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Serve hot.

reviews.review_text: This is one of the better tasting tuna casseroles I have ever had... especially with the modifications.  I chopped the celery and onion and sauted it in a pan w/ a little olive oil until barely tender.  I added a small can of portabellas (though I think fresh would be even better.)  I also added a cup of frozen peas that I thawed on high for 2 minutes in the microwave.  I then added the tuna and soup.  I reduced the mayo to 1/4 cup and added in 1/4 cup of sour cream.  I also added 4oz of cream cheese and a few American cheese slices.  I stirred in about 4-5 oz of sharp cheddar and then added the black pepper and a little garlic pwdr and garlic salt.  I then stirred in the pasta and transferred it to the casserole dish.  I topped it with the remaining 3-4 oz of shredded cheddar cheese and french fried onions.  My kids all loved it and said to save the recipe so I can make it again!  Thanks Tara and to everyone else for their suggestions, which encouraged my modifications! :)

attributes.source_text: My kids all loved it

reviews.review_text: Here's some long overdue praise! I forgot to review your wonderful recipe when I first saw it but I happened upon it the other day and wanted you to know it has been an inspiration to me for a long time. I use more tuna, 12 oz. drained and flaked, and regular milk. I also cook all the vegetables before adding them to the tuna mixture. I saute the onions and fresh mushrooms with 2 cloves minced garlic, a little celery and bell pepper in a bit of olive oil, then add about 10 oz. of frozen mixed vegetables (you can use your favorites), season and cook all until done. I do add a cup of shredded cheddar to the tuna, noodles and cooked vegetables before topping with another cup of cheese. I call this a "favorite comfort meal made special". Thanks so much!!!

This was really good Tara. I tweaked it quite a bit but I tend to do that w/ all recipes. I used fresh chives and parsley from the garden. I used mushroom soup as I didn't have celery soup. I also used some mushrooms that I had cooked and put in the freezer for those times when I'm out of fresh. Today was that day to use my mushrooms which I'm sure was more then six ounces. My family loves mushrooms so no problem there. I also added frozen peas. I had to increase my temp and cook time due to my oven so I did cover it w/ aluminum foil that I sprayed first. I also had a tiny piece of left-over salmon that I had a garlic mayo sauce on top. This worked really well. Everyone had seconds. I increased the recipe for six servings. It came out really well. I'll be having a midnight snack with this. Great recipe to use what you have on hand.

attributes.source_text: I'll be having a midnight snack with this

reviews.review_text:
I love tuna casserole and have been making variations of it for years. I've mostly used cream of mushroom but this version with cream of celery is excellent. I will absolutely use that from now on. My modifications were sauté celery first, then sautéed onions, fresh sliced mushrooms and a couple tbs minced garlic. Added all other ingredients to pan plus old bay seasoning, red pepper, less black pepper, onion powder, 1/2 cup frozen peas, 1/2 cup shredded parmesan (for some saltiness and more cheese), replaced half the amount of mayo with sour cream and used the entire can of evaporated milk. Heated in pan, taste/adjust seasoning, then mixed in noodles. Added to baking dish, topped with another 1/2 cup cheddar and fried shallots. Baked at 375 for 30 min.

Probably the best tuna casserole I've ever had, which is saying a lot! Stayed really creamy and had that cheesy, crunchy topping.

attributes.source_text: had that cheesy, crunchy topping
Stayed really creamy
had that cheesy, crunchy topping

reviews.review_text:
hee hee I. along with the other chefs, know you don't NEED another 5 star but you are getting one anyways :-)
I love my Tuna "casseroles" plain.. just tuna, cream of mushroom, noodles and peas right out of the pan.. but I read this and all the GREAT ratings and I HAD to try this!! 
And wow oh wow was this ever YUMMY!! I did tweak a few things due to being out of a few items, I used Cream of Chicken instead of Cream of Celery (bummer), I used cream cheese instead of mayo, 1/2 c of whole milk instead of a 1/2 can, and I added one garlic clove.. 
Tara.. this is one of the best Tuna casseroles EVER.. also the first one I evre actually baked!! Well,... great job and thanks!! I am a single mother, full time student, part time employed iwth a severely handicapped daughter and she SUCKED this down so fast I couldn't believe it!! I love the Zaar.. it's made my life so much easier!!! :-)

reviews.review_text: Very good tuna casserole.  I haven't made one in years and just had a sudden urge and I couldn't have chosen a better recipe, it's just awesome.  Because of little one's eating, I omitted the onion, mushrooms and celery but did use onion powder.  I took another reviewers suggestion and used 1/2 mayonnaise and 1/2 sour cream. The cheese I used was a 4-cheese blend and I used probably 1-3/4 cups.  Tara, thanks for sharing your wonderful recipe.  It will definately be added to my make-again cookbook.  I look forward to the day when I can use the chopped onion, shrooms and celery, because they will definately be a welcome addition. This recipe would easily feed 6 people, so there's going to be leftovers for lunch tomorrow.  YUMMY!

attributes.source_text: leftovers for lunch tomorrow

reviews.review_text: So, so, good.  I have had so many recipes for tuna casserole that turn out dry AND flavorless, and this one is very creamy and delicious.  I used Country Pasta brand homemade style egg pasta, which I really recommend; I also added a 1/2 cup of frozen mixed vegetables and I had to make my own recipe of condensed cream of celery soup since I didn't have any (found the recipe on southernfood.about.com)--can you tell I was determined to make this today?  It turned out better than I expected and the flavor was wonderful.  Thanks to you, Tara, I have conquered tuna caserole! Thanks!  PS Next time I will add a crunchy topping, I really did miss it.<br/>Update: Whoa! For a whole new level of deliciousness try adding equal parts plain panko bread crumbs and ground French's French Fried Onions to the top of the casserole during the last 5 or so minutes of baking!

attributes.source_text: this one is very creamy

reviews.review_text:
Really, really, good tuna casserole. I followed the recipe pretty much to the letter and it came out really creamy and wonderful, great to take to work for lunches! The only reason I didn't give it five stars was because of the celery and onion, even after baking in the oven they were still quite crunchy, and I'd made sure to cut them small. So, anyway, the next time I make this, and believe me, I will, I'll just sautee' the veggies a bit before adding. Thanks Tara!
Update! Didn't plan ahead for supper last night so it was tuna casserole to the rescue, used this recipe again only I remembered to saute' the celery and onions as I'd stated earlier. Must change this to five stare because it was wonderful. Really, really, yummy!
Thanks!

reviews.review_text: So, this month my funds are quite limited due to being laid off and accepting a job for FAR less pay.  Having several cans of tuna in the pantry, I wanted to see what I could make using this without buying too many extra ingredients.  Thus, I found this recipe.   It was fabulous!!! Although I live alone, I wanted to double it to have enough for lunch/dinner for the week.  I ended up having to buy 2 cups cheese, 2 cans cream of celery soup, and 1 & 1/2 cups evaporated milk.  The rest of the ingredients I had.  I did, however, omit the celery and onion, as I didn't have them, and I didn't feel like chopping them even if I had bought them.  I used elbow macaroni, but I didn't use it all (16 oz for a doubled recipe).  I added enough to be substantial, but not enough for it to, when it cooled down, absorb all of the liquid.  As I didn't add celery or onion, I added an extra (4 oz) can of drained mushroooms.  Doubled, this filled a 9x13" pan and an 11x6" pan.  I made this in the evening on 10-5-09.  I had it for dinner that night.  Today is 10-7-09 and in an effort to save money, I have had it for breakfast, lunch and dinner everyday since then.  One might assume I would be completely sick of it.  However that is not the case.  I am actually looking forward to my dinner of it tonight, and my breakfast (which should finish it off) tomorrow morning.  During the previous days at my new job I have spent upwards of $25+ in breakfast, lunch, and dinner alone.  With this casserole I have saved $65 dollars!  Believe it or not, I look forward to making this again soon, as it is that good!  Thank you for the recipe!

Very good!  I had to make a few substitutions out of necessity (was one fo those "miracle meals" where I searched for ingredients I had on hand & found this).  I didn't have cream of celery soup, so I used cream of mushroom and increased the chopped celery to 2/3 cup.  I used a bunch of green onions.  I sauted the celery and onions before adding the other ingredients while the noodles were cooking.  Only had 1/4 cup of evaporated milk so I added sour cream to 3/4 cup.  Like others I threw in a couple of handfuls of frozen green peas.
This filled a 3 qt. casserole dish which for us would definitely feed more than four ~ just FYI.  Came out creamy & delish!

attributes.source_text: Came out creamy

reviews.review_text: My daughter and I were also having a tuna casserole "Jones". :) I found this recipe (having never made one) and with it's ratings and the way the recipe read, thought we'd give it a try. It is now on our family rotation!  There are two things I did differently, just for my family...I used half and half instead of evaporated milk, and I drained the tuna (because my husband is not a big fish eater and I thought it would keep the casserole from being too fishy tasting, and it was delicious. Oh, I did add peas. This is the type of recipe I love! You can "tweak" it in different ways and it is still delicious. That is the mark of a great recipe! Thank you Tara, for sharing!

attributes.source_text: It is now on our family rotation!

reviews.review_text: I made this last night. I just had one helping, and decided I did not like it. My husband had 2 helpings before he decided it was just ok. The problem was the mayo. It was waaay to rich with it. I personally think it could have been left out all together. I'll give it one more try, and do what a lot of the reviewers did and use sour cream instead of mayo. And I usually absolutely love mayo, but it was just to over powering in this dish. Also I will use a bigger can of tuna. The recipe did not indicate what size can, so I just used the small can (and I only had one), and it was not enough tuna.... I did add mushrooms to it!  Like I said, I will try it again using substutions for the mayo, and then I will write a review again!

Yummy, creamy, filling and comforting! I loosely followed the ingredients and it turned out great. I made the following changes/alterations: I doubled the recipe and I omitted the mayonnaise completely. I didn't have cream of celery soup on hand so I used cream of mushroom. I had fresh mushrooms in the fridge so I used those instead of canned. I eye-balled the evaporated milk until the mixture was creamy and I used whole wheat penne pasta instead of egg noodles. I've tried a lot of tuna dishes but this one is the best, so far! Thanks for the help!

**Also wanted to note that I did saute the onions and mushrooms before putting into the dish to bake- this helped.

No fishy smell, and not too runny... my family loves it! I did squeeze some lemon and drained the tuna, just in case, since my family cannot stand heated tuna. I used cream of chicken (was all I had), and sauteed the celery, onions, mushrooms, plus a teaspoon of chopped garlic. I was wondering what it meant by 1/2 can of milk, but quickly realized it should be: 1/2 SOUP CAN of drinking milk, ie. the SOUP CAN from the cream of celery (or cream of chicken, in my case). I also sprinkled some cornflakes on the top for added crunch, and baked it in a 9" glass pie dish, and it took about 1 hour in my oven. Will definitely make again. Thanks for posting.

reviews.review_text: Well being reviewer 333 I had to give this one a try and see what all the talk is about.  I know now - I've always enjoyed tuna cassroles occasionally and remember them from my Mom so they bring back a lot of memories.  This one is full of creamy goodness and flavors that all blend so well together.  I followed the directions except had leave out the onions as found out DH had used the last of them, but did add Onion Poweder.  Wonderful, creamy, cheesy and so easy to put together.  I made it in the afternoon of a busy day and then just popped it in the oven before DH got home so a warm, comforting dinner was ready when he walked in the door.  Thanks for posting and you deserve all the glowing reviews.

reviews.review_text: Made this last night and it was delicious!!!! Made a few changes but nothing really to change the recipe. I didn't use mushrooms as no one likes them but me. I used cream of celery soup, poured the whole can of evap milk in since there wasn't much left after I took out 3/4 cup, used 1/4 sour cream and 1/4 mayo, as others suggested and added some velveeta along with extra cheddar. Also I added a cup of frozen peas. I put the peas in the boiling pasta in the last 2 minutes of cooking time. I absolutely loved this casserole. Very good and very easy to make-probably the creamiest tuna casserole I've ever had!!! Thanks for sharing this!

My family was less than thrilled when I told them we were having tuna casserole for dinner, but not only did they greedily eat the whole thing (even the picky one), they've requested to have this on a regular basis.  I had to omit the mushrooms because my family hates them (I love them and one time I might sneak them in), and I took one reviewer's suggestion about topping it with crumbled potato chips.  I also used whole wheat egg noodles, as that's what I had on hand.  This was rich, delicious comfort food, and unbelievably simple to make.  I'm taking it to a potluck next week, where I'm sure it will be a huge hit.  Thanks Tara, for submitting this absolutley wonderful recipe!

We were out of noodles, so I had to use rice, but the flavor combinations included in the recipe made for a delicious dish. I was going to saute the onions, but I loved the crunch! I even ate the rest of it cold this morning. And if you like a casserole cold, it definitely deserves 5 stars! We'll definitely keep this recipe on hand for another time soon. Thanks for posting!

reviews.review_text: Taste of childhood for us both! The DH grew up in England but his dad was American so they had all the usual dinner suspects growing up, and tuna noodle casserole was no exception. This was a very simple recipe and the taste took me back to 1989 immediately (1979 for him)! I added a few things that made it a bit closer to my mom's recipe: mushrooms, peas, garlic, extra cheese, and crushed potato chips on the top. The chips gave it a great crunch but, unless you are making this for a crowd who will devour the dish immediately in its entirety, I would actually avoid using them because they get soggy after refrigeration. Thanks for the trip down memory lane Tara!

items.label: Chocolate! Chocolate! Chocolate! Bundt Cake With Chocolate Glaze
items.name: Chocolate! Chocolate! Chocolate! Bundt Cake With Chocolate Glaze
items.description: Need I say more...CHOCOLATE! Decadently rich and moist. Add a scoop of vanilla ice cream and you're in Heaven.
instructions: Cake: Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour bundt pan, set aside.
In large mixing bowl, combine cake mix, pudding mix and chocolate chips.
In another bowl, combine water, eggs, and vanilla mixing well.
Add egg mixture to dry mixture and mix with spoon until just blended.
Pour into prepared pan.
Bake for 50 to 55 minutes or until cake tests done when wooden pick in center comes out clean.
Cool 15 to 20 minutes before removing cake from pan.
When completely cool, drizzle cake with Chocolate Glaze.
Chocolate Glaze: Combine all ingredients in bowl.
Mix with spoon until smooth.

reviews.review_text: I made this cake for my dad's birthday, and he really seemed to enjoy it. (I didn't eat any because I follow a low-carb diet, but it certainly looked good.) It was easy to make, too. I only made a few changes; I didn't have cake mix on hand, so I made used 1/3 recipe of the homemade cake mix listed on the About.com Busy Cooks site. I substituted brown sugar for the granulated sugar called for in that recipe since I had no granulated sugar on hand. To that, I added about 1/6 to 1/4 cup cocoa and 1/4 cup vegetable oil along with the rest of the ingredients listed in this recipe. I used 1/2 semi-sweet and 1/2 milk chocolate chips, as that was what I had on hand. I also added a bit of vanilla to the glaze as vanilla seems to be a standard addition to chocolate recipes. I would definitely make this for someone again!

attributes.source_text: for my dad's birthday
he really seemed to enjoy it

reviews.review_text: As expected, this is wonderfully chocolatey. Very very simple to make. The amount of powdered sugar confused me, so I used 1 cup and it turned out perfect. My mom later told me that 10x is the size of the grind of the sugar, 10x being standard powdered sugar. I made this in a 13x9 pan, and baked it for an hour. I greased and floured my pan, and next time I think I will use a little of the cake mix instead of flour. I used 3 tbsp of water for the glaze, because I wanted to make sure it would cover the entire top of the cake, which it did. Make sure you cut small pieces of this cake! It's rich and dense, and delicious! Wonderful with a nice tall glass of milk. We're keeping it in the fridge, since it's lasting a long time because you only want a small piece. It's good cold, and maybe tonight I'll try my piece warmed up.

attributes.source_text: this is wonderfully chocolatey

reviews.review_text: This cake was very easy and fast to make. Mine only took 40 minutes to bake.  I probably have a smaller bundt pan.  I made some mini-cupcakes with the leftover batter.  If you have a smaller pan be sure to check it before recommended 50 minutes.  I poured a little chocolate glaze over it made of chocolate syrup and godiva liquor to keep it moist and dusted it with powdered sugar.  I didn't use the glaze recipe on here because I made it in a wreath pan for family xmas and wanted to make sure you could see the shape.  I made a raspberry sauce to serve on the side by putting some raspberries, sugar, and water in a pan and simmering.  I strain the seeds out of the sauce.  I will definitely make this cake again considering how fast and easy it was.  It was also very moist.

attributes.source_text: It was also very moist

reviews.review_text: I have made this cake twice in the last 3 days and it is great!! The first time, I only changed the chocolate chips, since all I had was milk chocolate and I probably only used 3/4 cup. It was very moist and we liked it alone or with ice cream. Tonight I wanted to try the reduced sugar devil's food cake mix since we are trying to watch our sugar. I also used the sugar free pudding mix and probably only 1/2 cup milk choc. chips. I was worried when it was cooking that it was turning out way to dry, but it turned out very nice. Of course not AS good as the original, but when we added the (no sugar added) vanilla ice cream to the warm cake, it was SO great and you couldn't tell the difference (kids and everyone else loved it too!). Both times I used a 13x9 pan and then poked it many times with a toothpick after it baked. Then I would pour a little icing on to let it soak in, wait about 5-10 mins (if that!) and use the rest. I will definitely be using this recipe again, esp. the reduced sugar way so I won't feel so bad when I eat so much!!!!

attributes.source_text: It was very moist
kids and everyone else loved it too

reviews.review_text: I love to make scratch cakes but had to try this doctored up cake mix because it receives such rave reviews.  It's simple, quick and completely delicious.  One change I made was to add milk chocolate chips in the batter instead of semi-sweet chocolate chips. I'm a milk chocolate kind of girl and that is what I had on hand.  I would recommend taking the cake out before you think it's done.  It continues to cook after being removed from the oven and when it cools it solidifies even more.  It has a nice gooey and lava cake kind of texture when it's slightly underdone and that makes it all the more decadent. I think fully done tastes a bit more pound cake like. I like the icing but am not crazy about it.  Maybe a chocolate ganauche sort of icing might be better.  But I do recommend this recipe.  It's an attractive cake and so simple and very very chocolately and delicious.

reviews.review_text: I have to say, I felt guilty receiving so many compliments on a cake that was so easy to make.  After promising a Black Forest cake (that would have taken the entire day to make) I brought this to work for a co-workers birthday.  This was far better than any cake I could have ever made from scratch!  It was unbelievably moist.  I offered it under the name Choke-on-Chocolate Cake.  It is so rich you almost have to serve it with ice cream.  I'm making it again tonight for a birthday party and I'll be serving it with black cherries (bc there's no way to refrigerate ice cream)!  Absolutely that best cake I've ever had that came out of someone's kitchen, and better than nearly every bakery cake I've had.   I had many requests for the recipe.

I followed the cake recipe to the letter, but I baked it in a 9x13 pan (left bundt pan at dads in another state) It only took 45 mins for it to bake. I only used 1 cup of chocolate chips and that was sufficient.  I also skipped the glaze so my rating is strictly for the cake.

This is a fantastic cake! Very, very chocolately, the perfect recipe for the chocoholic.  Try not to overbake as it might affect the moisture.  However, for the baker with a perfection palate, I strongly suggest making your own "devils food mix". items.label: The Best Belgian Waffles
items.name: The Best Belgian Waffles
items.description: These waffles are super crisp on the outside, light as a feather inside and so scrumptious! Avoid removing them from the waffle iron too soon; they should be a golden brown. Enjoy!
instructions: Oil the waffle maker.
Sift the dry ingredients together in a large bowl.
In separate bowl, separate egg whites and beat until stiff peaks form.
In a separate bowl, mix together the egg yolks, milk, oil , and vanilla, stir slightly.
Add to dry ingredients and mix well.
Fold in egg whites.
Cook in waffle iron on medium-high heat for around 5-10 minutes.

reviews.review_text: I recently purchased a very old, almost antique-like (Norwegian made) waffle iron. It has two sides that open up like a fan with 5 heart-shaped sections. It's used on a cooktop. So, naturally, I wanted to try this iron out. I came across this recipe while looking for a good waffle recipe. I am using a regular waffle iron, not a Belgian one but I figured this would be pretty much the same, just thinner. The only change I made to the recipe was to use olive oil in lieu of the vegetable oil. (I don't keep vegetable oil on hand but have plenty of extra virgin olive oil.) I used less sugar because I don't need the waffles to be "sweet" especially, when we are dipping in pure maple syrup! Oh, and I also didn't read the directions ahead of time and didn't separate the egg yolk from the whites and had mixed it all together. I can only imagine how much more "light" it could have turned out had I separated the egg whites and created the "peaks" before folding it into the rest of the recipe...It still turned out awesome and it tasted even better than it looked! Unfortunately, I ruined the last batch because I left it too long and it burnt to a crisp :-( at least that was after everyone finished and the last batch was going to be a leftover I had planned to freeze and use another day. Thank you so much for testing this recipe out and posting!

Very good waffle recipe!  THANK YOU!  Only takes a minute to whip up the egg whites so I did'nt consider that to be a time consuming addition to the recipe.  I think that's the key to these being so light & fluffy.  We made some plain & for the rest, we chopped up cooked bacon & added to the batter.
One problem I ran into, not with the recipe, but with my waffle maker, I did'nt have a manual & could'nt find one online, spent more time just finding a recipe/site that would just give me some idea of how much batter to use & how long to cook!  Finally tried trial & error & will put here for anyone else who needs an estimate or starting point.
My belgian waffle maker is a magic chef model tsk-240b & I used between 3/4 & 1 cup batter & cook time was 3 minutes. Made 6 waffles. 
Hope that helps.

reviews.review_text:
I made a complete pig of myself last night with these waffles!  I have NEVER had such amazing waffles.  I didn't even want to ruin them with syrup and butter!  DH didn't have this same problem (chuckle) and loved filling those pockets with lots of both!  Made 16- 4"x4" deep belgian waffles.  I took your suggestion, Marie and left the waffles in a good long time..till the outsides were a deep brown (more than golden brown).  For my waffle maker (Villaware Uno Belgian 6 waffle maker) that was about 5 minutes per batch plus 1 minute to preheat the griddle before pouring again so keeping the other waffles warm in the oven was important.  Not to worry, the waffles in the oven remained crispy on the outside and soft on the inside..and the fresh ones were absolutely fantastic.  The flavor of these plain reminded me of funnel cakes at the fair.  Incredible and really, we could not stop eating them.  

A note about pouring..the batter puffs up because of the baking powder so you will probably need a spatula or spoon to help you spread the batter around the griddle so you get it in all the squares.  And, if you have never made waffles before, just get the batter level with the recessed area for the batter. Ridiculously good. Oh yeah, this is SO going in my tried and true cookbook.  I bet this would make fab pancakes too! I KNOW it would make good copycat McGriddle cakes (same flavor) using a egg poacher ring, maybe to get the height? Hmmmm....Thanks for sharing such a gem, Marie.

reviews.review_text: I was looking for my Aunt Ruth's waffle recipe in the family recipe box, but the box was so stuffed full, I never did come across it. So I resorted to the internet and found this one right away, and it is pretty darned close to Aunt Ruth's version of the perfect waffle. I don't use as much sugar (personal taste), may or may not use vanilla, love melted butter (1 cube melted) instead of oil and added to batter just before folding in the whipped egg whites. Note: For the novice waffle cook, have the eggs at room temperature and make sure you don't get any yolk into the whites or they won't whip up. My waffle maker is in two squares and non-stick which needs no oiling and gives up the baked waffle at the simple lift of a fork. Thanks so much for publishing the recipe. I would have been all day searching for Aunt Ruth's.

I am only knocking one star off b/c of the yeild and b/c Marie didn't state what size waffle her machine makes or how much batter to use per waffle.  Other than that, the recipe was easy, simple, very tasty and perfectly crispy on the outside --- just how I love them.  The only criticism I have is I only got 7-1/2 waffles and had I known that I would have doubled the recipe as I was making them to freeze for future breakfasts (should have read the other reviews...LOL).  BTW, my iron makes 7" waffles. I wasn't sure how much mix the recipe scoops onto the waffle iron, but in order to get a full size waffle on my iron, I had to use 2/3 cup per waffle.  These were excellent waffles and a definate keeper!  My husband said they were good, but not as good as the waffle mix I usually buy...hmmm.  I had to disagree and say these had an edge over to store-bought mix (Krusteaz).  My mom even loved them.  Thanks Marie!

reviews.review_text: I made these today and they were absolutely delicious! Truly the best waffles I have ever made. I think one of the important things to remember is to plug in your waffle iron before you start making the batter. I tried leaving the batter on for different amounts of time. If you leave it for only a few minutes, it will be a softer waffle, a few minutes more, both soft and crispy, and a few mintues more, a very crispy waffle. I made blueberry/raspberry sauce the night before which went perfectly with the waffles (plus some whipped creme and a little syrup). These obviously aren't low in calories but I believe if you are going to eat bad, eat quality... BTW- waffles freeze well. This recipe made 7-8 waffles on my iron. If you deflate your whites by beating them instead of folding them into the batter you're not going to get as many waffles.
