reviews.review_text: This was a great recipe with one tiny exception - it did NOT make 16 waffles. For the Belgium waffle maker we use, it made 7. in our regular waffle maker, it probably would have been 16 but that's not Belgium waffles. I 1.5X this and had a couple leftover for our family of 6 (though, we have a 1 year old and 3 year old... but also an 8 year old who makes up for their scant portions. Ü) I made it the first time as the recipe calls and it was great. The next time, as I do with anything I can, I added cinnamon. Also, I did half cow's milk, half almond milk. I would have used all almond milk but I didn't have enough. Still turned out great - which is pretty normal, being able to swap plant milk for cow's milk in waffles with no issue.

This is a very good basic recipe .. If it did not work out for you...you did something wrong ! I tweaked it by doing this : Use Brown Sugar : 2 tps of vanilla : 3/4 cup sugar 1 tbs water. DIY pearl sugar : Add the sugar and water to a small pot. Turn the pot on over the lowest heat setting possible and stir with a wooden spoon until small clumps of sugar form. Your goal is to clump as much sugar together as possible (minimizing the amount of loose sugar) while not creating any overly large clumps. If there seems to be too much loose sugar and not enough clumps, add 1/2 teaspoon of water and stir again. Having been to Belgium with my Father who is from there .. This is hard to beat ! Cook Time 4 min.

Wow, was using another belgian recipe but tried this just for something new, and Marie you are right, it is extremely light and crisp, unusually so.  Unfortunately only gave 3 stars for the following reasons:   I did the recipe exactly as listed but quadrupled it!!  (we make in advance and freeze in fours)
however mine came out quite thin compared to what I am used to and being so deliciously crispy yet stretchy tended to stick to the iron.   I'd made 4 waffles, so then added 1/2 cup flour and 1.5 teas baking powder and 2 teas vanilla to the rest of the quad mix.  Taste as per original recipe was nice, crispiness was really REALLY nice, very desirable.  However when I stacked one on top of another like I normally do to cool, it went very soft and floppy, so I am not sure how crispy they will be when reheated.  
I think this would be a lovely recipe when eating immediately but I would probably not choose to make it again due to the problems with getting out of the iron and going floppy quickly.  Would love to create a crispy thick waffle!

LOVED IT!!

I searched high and low for a great recipe for my new Belgian waffle iron and I found the best with this one. After making it exactly by the recipe a few times, I modified it slightly (though it was already delicious the way it was :-) They are light, crispy on the outside, soft on the inside when freshly made.

My modifications were:

1) adding 1 tsp vanilla
2) adding 1 Tb malted milk powder
3) being more generous with the sugar with a heaping scoop, not a leveled-off cup

My kids both love these waffles and the recipe is easy to follow and even turns out well when you goof, LOL.... I mistakenly added twice as much oil with one batch and they were still wonderful!

I make a half recipe of these which still makes 4.5 large waffles on my George Foreman grill/waffle iron. (And I cook the waffles according to my appliance's instructions, 425 for 7-8 minutes.) What we don't eat then gets stored in a freezer bag for later. They do get soft/chewy after they cool down or are stored in refrigerator, but they are still delicious! Just microwave for a few seconds and enjoy. My toddler likes them plain as a snack, they are that sweet and tasty. And I like that they aren't "crumby" for him to eat when not in his high chair.

items.name: Slow-Cooker Cheesy Chicken
items.description: Almost too easy, the chicken cooks in a creamy, cheesy sauce that is delicious over noodles. This freezes well, too
instructions: Place chicken breasts in the crock pot.
Mix the undiluted soups together with the garlic powder and pour over chicken.
Cover and cook on low 6-8 hours , until chicken is tender.
Serve with the delicious sauce over rice or noodles.

reviews.review_text: This is a wonderful dish b/c it allows so many variations.  I made this today with 1 1/4 lbs. of chicken breast, two 10 1/2 oz. cans of condensed cream of mushroom soup, one 4 oz. can of sliced mushrooms (drained) and 1 cup of shredded cheddar cheese, along with all the other spices listed.  I cooked it on high in the crock pot for five hours total.  On the fourth hour, I transfered the chicken breasts to a plate, shredded the chicken with a knife and fork so that it looked like pulled chicken and then put it back into the crock pot to cook for another hour.  The chicken was INCREDIBLY tender.  The only one issue I had (and this may have been my fault) was that there was some sticking and browning on the sides of the crock pot.  Other than that, this leads to a flavorful, thick sauce that goes great with the shredded chicken, and which I served over wide egg noodles.  Thanks so much for posting!

attributes.source_text: The chicken was INCREDIBLY tender

reviews.review_text: This is my second review and I'm reporting back after making this recipe over 10 times in many variations (broc chz soup, crm of mush, crm of broc).  The original recipe of 1 can cheddar chz coup and 2 cans crm of chx is the best yet.  However I do have a few pointers.  I have a newer, very large crockpot so it cooks quickly and doesn't do well when trying to cook small amounts.  I have found that using 1.5-2 lbs  FROZEN chicken breasts on low for approx 6 hours keeps the chicken very tender.  I add a small can of mushrooms and a small can of peas and also shred the chicken (should be very easy...tender...at this point) about an hour before its done.  I serve it over egg noodles.  Also, I use healthy request cream of chx soup (98% fat free, 33% less sodium) and that really helps cut back on salty taste since we're not big fans of salt.  Has become a staple in my house...I make it every week!  And leftovers are delicious! Reasonably healthy recipe if you make the subsitutions above.

reviews.review_text: I found this recipe yesterday and my husband and I were both excited to try it tonight.  After reading 9 pages of reviews, I was concerned that it would be bland so here are the adjustments I made to compensate: I cut the chicken into large chunks to better absorb the flavors.  I tossed the chicken chunks in a mixture of minced fresh garlic, garlic powder, black pepper, ground cumin, Italian seasoning, paprika, and cayenne pepper.  I mixed two cans of cheddar cheese soup and one can of cream of chicken together and poured them over the chicken in the crock pot, making sure the chicken was completely covered.  The chicken was ready in a little over 4 hours (on low in a newer 6 quart crock pot).  I added crumbled bacon (10 strips) about an hour before it was ready.  I boiled wide egg noodles, tossed them in butter, and stirred them into the cheesy chicken before serving.  (I would have put broccoli in it but my husband wouldn't have touched it then, so we had mixed veggies on the side.)  We thought it was "good", but I think it would have been quite bland without the spices and bacon.  Because I made so many adjustments to the original recipe, I did not rate it with stars, but my husband, kids, and I all agreed on 3.5 stars.

attributes.source_text: my husband, kids, and I all agreed on 3.5 stars
stirred them into the cheesy chicken

reviews.review_text: Quick, easy and delicious!  I did tweak the recipe a bit for our own personal taste.  I had to double the recipe for my brood and I used 4 cans of condensed cheddar cheese soup, 2 cans of cream of chicken, added the garlic powder as well as some poultry seasoning and pepper.  I tossed everything in the crock pot and cooked on low for about 6 hours.  An hour or so before dinner I shredded the chicken simply by giving the mixture in the crock pot a vigourous stirring then added a 16 oz bag of frozen broccoli and about a cup of shredded cheddar cheese. (We LOVE cheese!)  I used pot pie noodles cooked according to the packaged and mixed them in right before serving. My family loves it!

attributes.source_text: My family loves it!

reviews.review_text:
I was in a really big hurry yesterday morning, but wanted to throw something in the crock pot for supper. I did a quick search and found this recipe!
I only had one can of Chicken soup, so I ended up using 1 can of Cheese soup, 1 can of half-fat Cream of Chicken and 1 can of half-fat Cream of Broccoli. It was great! The breasts were still 1/2 frozen and I cooked it all on low for about 8 hours. Done to perfection and very tender.
It was served over a bed of whole-wheat macaroni with some sauteed broccoli and onions. As far as my youngest one was concerned, we were having mac and cheese :)
There is lots of sauce, so plan on serving it on something so none goes to waste!

attributes.source_text: very tender
As far as my youngest one was concerned, we were having mac and cheese

reviews.review_text:
Love this recipe everytime I cook it.  I change the soups I use, and always add a cup of chicken broth (this time I used Swanson's NEW White Wine and Herb broth).  For soups, most recently, I used a can of 98% Red. Fat Cream of Chicken, a can of Cream of Broccoli with Cheese and a can of Cheddar Cheese soup.  It was wonderful!  Usually, I'll also steam some broccoli and use some of the extra sauce over it.  I always serve it over egg noodles.  Yum!  

NOTE: if you use the recipe I just used, and make it into eight servings, my nutrition figures are just a little bit different:  248 calories, 7g. fat, 14g. carbs, and 33g. protein.

This is a very good and very easy basic recipe.  I have two words for all those people who complained about this recipe being too bland, spice cabinet.  I traded the garlic powder for about 6 or 7 smashed garlic cloves and I added 1 Tablespoon each chili powder and lemon pepper.  I also shook in about 2 teaspoons of ground white pepper.  I used a 4 pound whole chicken and cooked it on low for about 7 hours.  All those people who want a recipe that's good to go "out of the box" can go to the grocery store and buy one from Banquet or Swanson. After all, this is a cooking site, isn't it?  We, my son and I, used some of the chicken to make enchiladas and I mixed the rest in the sauce, sealed it in two bags with my Foodsaver and stashed it in the freezer.
We ate one of the bags for dinner tonight over egg noodles and it was fantastic.

attributes.source_text: for dinner tonight

reviews.review_text: This is a great base recipe for crock pot chicken. While I am not a huge fan of the recipe as written, my family loves it with nacho cheese soup (2 cans) and golden mushroom soup. We also have run into the problem of it becoming runny, which we remedy with stirring in some sour cream before serving. I followed the advice of another reviewer and dusted the chicken with spices and browned it before adding it to the crock pot and it definitely perks up the flavor. Cook time usually runs around 5 to 5 1/2 hours. Any longer and the chicken tends to get that weird texture that is somewhere between boiled and dry. So based on rating this as soley a base recipe that someone can build on, I give it 3.5 stars (rounded up to 4). The original is lacking seasoning and not cheesy enough. Cook time is definitely way off, too.

attributes.source_text: my family loves it

reviews.review_text: I have this dish in the crockpot right now and the kitchen smells awesome. I made this exactly as written, but I started with 2 pounds of frozen chicken tenders and poured the soup mixture over all. I did not add salt since canned soups are salty enough as is, but I did add almost a quarter teaspoon of black pepper. I will be serving this over noodles with a side of broccoli and garlic bread. From the look of it, there should be plenty of cheese sauce to pour over the broccoli as well as the noodles. This is sure to be a terrific family pleaser. I will return after dinner to complete my rating, but all is looking and smelling perfect at this point.  Update:  I was right, this recipe made for a wonderful meal.  For those who enjoy more spice, I put ground red pepper on the table to be added by individuals, especially me.  From start to finish, I cooked in the crockpot for 5 hours from frozen on the low heat setting.  Absolutely wonderful and not falling apart, just very tender and yummy.  Thanks Kathleen for providing my family with another super dish that will be made regularly in this house.  All thumbs up around the table!!

attributes.source_text: Thanks Kathleen for providing my family with another super dish
just very tender

reviews.review_text: I gave it 5 stars becuz it was easy and tasty and I used the exact soups & garlic powder called for.. But With so many reviews warning of its blandness, I decided to add in some broccoli florets and mushrooms during the last  half hour of cook time in the crockpot. They were frozen so I steamed them first, then sautéed them with fresh garlic in of all things, a tbs of bacon grease from the mornings breakfast. Then added to crockpot and served a half hr later over rotini pasta. It was very flavorful, the broccoli n mushrooms were the perfect consistency ( I was worried they'd be soggy), and the chicken was completely tender and pulled apart nicely with a fork. I cooked on low for 4 hrs in my large crock.  I think the base flavor, however, came from the original recipe, and not necessarily from the additions I made. My hubby & 14 yo loved this so I will make again.

attributes.source_text: the chicken was completely tender

reviews.review_text:
Was looking for something I could throw in the crockpot and make my boyfriend think I was a great cook. This was so easy AND easy to modify I was really able to make it my own for cheap and quickly. I have a newer crockpot, so it only took 5 hours to cook on low. Like many mentioned before me, I used Cream of Broccoli Cheese Soup instead of the Cheddar Soup. I also added some salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper for flavor. I cut up an onion and used some mixed frozen vegatables (corn, carrots, green beans, peas) for color and then poured it over bowtie pasta. I was so proud of my meal, I smiled the whole time I was eating it, and my boyfriend took the leftovers with him for lunch the next day. :)

This recipe is only bland if you let it be. I'll definitely make it again.

attributes.source_text: my boyfriend took the leftovers with him for lunch the next day

reviews.review_text: Really great base recipe, i did however alter it a bit... lol, i made this into Crockpot Mac and Cheese with Chicken, i cooked as directed for 3 hours with a bit of greek seasoning blend for flavor and 1 small onion chopped. Then i cooked up 2 1/2c. macaroni for about 7 min, drained tempered 2 eggs in the noodles 1/2 tea. ground mustard power and 1/2c. sour cream. After mixing well  I stirred it into the chicken/cheddar mixture, and let it continue to cook for 3 more hours, All in one meal, really great and everything was done at the same time. Excellent! Enjoy! *** Also added 1c shredded sharp cheddar before serving =-)

This was good. It wasn't excellent though, so I couldn't give it 5 stars. I used 1 can of cream of chicken, 1 can of cheddar cheese, and 1 can of fiesta cheddar cheese, to give it some flavor. I also added more garlic powder and some black & white pepper. It certainly was easy to make! I used 2 lbs of frozen chicken tenderloins, just put them on the bottom of the crock pot and mixed the soups together and then poured them on top. Took about 6 1/2 - 7 hours on low. Served it with egg noodles, and peas on the side, but we both mixed the peas in, which was good. I added salsa to the leftovers that I ate for lunch, and that was good too, but not excellent. This is good food, just not amazing. I might make it again if I figure out a way to enhance it.

Okay.. so I REALLY wanted to try this.  LIKE REALLY BAD!! LOL.  BUT I don't have a crock pot.. I know, I know.. a total faux pas but mine broke.  Anywho, I decided I would figure out a way to make this work in the oven.  So I diced up the chicken and coated the pieces in flour.  I then browned them on the stove top and then through them in  baking dish with the soups.. and VIOLA!!  A great oven duplicate!! Thank you for this recipe!! It was so yummy.. my super picky, brain damaged 3 year old loved it!! I love the Zaar it has made this single mom's life so much easier!! Also, I served this over macaroni noodles!!

attributes.source_text: my super picky, brain damaged 3 year old loved it

reviews.review_text: This recipe gets 5 stars because my DH and the kids thought it was 5 stars and because it made the house smell good. I gave it 4 stars for taste and 5 stars for ease of prep so in the end 5 it is. It is super easy to make and the sauce is good. I made it as written but next time will do some add ins like peas, mushrooms and/or onions. It is comfort food. I couldn't really taste either of the soups but they complement each other nicely. The lack of seasoning was a problem for me but the guys loved it that way. I served it on top of egg noodles and along side vegetables. Good meal. Thanks for posting Kathleen Traylor. Enjoy! ChefDLH

attributes.source_text: my DH and the kids thought it was 5 stars
my DH and the kids thought it was 5 stars
the guys loved it that way

reviews.review_text: This chicken was wonderful and the sauce was great over brown rice. I didnt have two cans of cream of chicken soup so I used one can of cream of celery. Added kosher salt, pepper, lemon pepper, and celery seeds than cooked on low for about 7 hous. Plated the brown rice than placed a chicken breast on top with some sauce over all that and served with green beans, fantastic supper for us! I will make this again and try the cream of broccoli soup like one reviewer did and serve with some steamed brocoli on the side. Thank you so much Kathleen for posting this recipe. Made and reviewed for the I Recommend Tag Game.

attributes.source_text: fantastic supper for us

reviews.review_text: I made this up over the weekend, and it was pretty good! I accidentally overcooked mine, so do be sure that you are able to shut off the crockpot at the end of the cooking time or yours will be too dry. We ate it anyway (for leftovers even!) so it's not the end of the world, but it would have been pretty awesome if I would have been home to flip the crockpot off. Also, I thought it seemed like it might be a bit bland, so at the end of the cooking I added a couple extra dashes of the salt, pepper, cayenne, and garlic. Definitely a good choice if you've got picky eaters in the house!! :-)

This recipe is easy to prepare, maybe it was just me.  After having no clue what to make for dinner (oven is on the fritz), I was excited when I found this one.  Had all the ingredients on hand and no oven, what more could I ask for.  I will say that the chicken was extremely tender, but I felt that the flavor was a little bland.  Also, if I were to serve it with noodles for a mac n' cheese side dish I would like a little thicker sauce.  All in all it was OK, I was a little disappointed after all the five star reviews.  Perhaps I'll try it one more time and try to tinker with it a little.

attributes.source_text: the chicken was extremely tender
what to make for dinner

reviews.review_text: We really liked this, but based on some reviewer comments we did make some changes.  First of all I seasoned salt and peppered the chicken on the bottom of the crockpot.  (chicken was placed frozen).  Next I used one can cream of chicken, one can cheddar cheese soup and one can of cream of broccoli. (That is what I had on hand) I also doubled the garlic because we love garlic.  Cooked on low for about 6 hours.  We served this over spaghetti squash and topped with some shredded mexican pepperjack cheese.  Chicken came out tender with none of it overcooked and the sauce was amazing.  Thanks Kathleen for sharing.

attributes.source_text: Chicken came out tender

reviews.review_text: My family loved this recipe.  It was super easy to make.  I did sprinkle salt, pepper, and garlic powder on the chicken before pouring the soup on top.  I did add more garlic to the soup than the recipe called for.  I served this over egg noodles and with steamed broccoli.  Next time I might throw the broccoli into the pot about an hour before it is ready.  Cheesy broccol - yumm!  I also thought about adding yellow and red peppers to the mix.  The chicken did not take as long to cook as stated.  I used partially thawed chicken and it took about 5 hours to cook.  We were all pleased with this recipe.  Thank you for sharing.

attributes.source_text: My family loved this recipe

items.label: Zucchini Bread
items.name: Zucchini Bread
items.description: This moist bread has been in the family for as long as I can remember. I like it because it's easily thrown together in one bowl and very moist -- perfect for a snack at work or school!
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Combine all ingredients.
Pour into two greased loaf pans.
Bake for one hour.

reviews.review_text: Very good, moist and so one-pan easy!  I did decrease the sugar to 1-2/3 cups, but that's only because I use Demerara or turbinado sugar, both are from the first press of the sugar cane and are naturally sweeter.  I added 2/3 cup coconut and used slivered almonds instead of walnuts.  Turned out great! This is a definite keeper (will probably use part oil/part applesauce next time just to make it a bit lower fat).  For the person who had trouble getting it out of the pan, don't flour your pan--plus, I've always found the metal bread pans work best!  Use oil, butter or vegetable spray to coat.  Let it sit in the pan 10 minutes on a rack after baking, then run a knife around the edges, hold the top of the bread pan with your hand/arm and give it a gentle shake.  Let cool on a rack before cutting.  Try it again!

attributes.source_text: moist

reviews.review_text:
Yikes. I expected a bit more from this recipe, given all of the glowing reviews.

The batter was very thick and oily. The oil was seperating from the batter when it sat out for 15 min. 

I made muffins with them and added some chocolate chips instead of nuts. I think that addition was fine, but the muffins just cooked weird. They barely puffed up and the zucchini pieces (I grated on a thick grater)  were still clearly visable in the bread. My daughter pulled out a chunk and refused to eat it because of that.

It seemed like an awful lot of sugar and oil  for the small amount of batter. They WERE moist, but not overly so that I would even have thought to comment on it.

I don't know. Maybe I made a mistake, though I did follow the recipe to a "T". 

I won't likely make this particular  recipe again and will search for something else. I feel like I used up a lot of ingredients on something that just wasn't that impressive.

Tastewise, it looked and tasted like an oatmeal batter. Maybe overkill with the spice. I don't know.

attributes.source_text: They WERE moist

reviews.review_text: I made this in my stand mixer, everything went so quickly because I could just dump each item in as it was mixing.  I started off with all of the wet ingredients and let those mix as I was measuring out the dry ingredients.  I got so into grating zucchini that I went a bit too far and added in 3 cups instead of 2 like the recipe calls for, but the bread baked just fine. I also added 1/2 c. pecans and substituted half of the white sugar with brown sugar.  I don't have any loaf pans (note to self) so I baked in a clear glass 9x13" pan and the bread was done in just about 40 min.  It is a beautiful deep golden brown color and filled my house with a wonderful aroma while baking.  It is moist and flavorful and I thought the sugar content was just right--I have a sweet tooth, though :)  Thanks for the recipe!

attributes.source_text: It is moist and flavorful

reviews.review_text:
Superb!  The flavours just linger in your mouth after a bite - delicious and subtle.  My family were eating zucchini and didn't know it!
I had a couple of questions - I don't use zucchini much but our neighbour gave me some, and I searched for this recipe so that I could find a way to make it palatable.  So I wans't sure how to measure the zucchini; I mean, I've seen recipes where you measure the grated amount and also squeeze out water etc. I just eyeballed a 2 cup size chunk, and grated it but did not squeeze. It looked like a lot more than 2 cups like that but still it came out fine.  
Also 3 tablespoons of vanilla seemed like too much? Did everyone else use 3? I only had about one tablespoon left so that was that, but again it tasted just great.

Thanks for the recipe!

attributes.source_text: delicious and subtle
My family were eating zucchini and didn't know it!

reviews.review_text: I have made this three times now, and we are enjoying it immensely!  The first batch I made as written, and ended up with fantastic zucchini bread that unfortunately adhered to the pans and so came out in a mess- a tasty mess!  The second batch I divided in half and replaced one cup of flour with 1/2 c flour mixed with 3/4 c cocoa powder and added 1c chocolate chips.  The other half I made with just chocolate chips.  These came out of the pan beautifully, so I don't know what happened with the first batch.  Today I made another batch and made some additions and changes- I reduced the sugar to 1/2 c brown sugar and 1/2 c white, added in 3 apples and 4 bananas that I mushed up in the processor, used only 1/4 c oil.  I forgot to add in a little more flour, so my loaves were very moist but very dense.  But they were fantastically tasty!  I will be playing around with the recipe a bit more, but love the fact that I could make it a little bit healthier.  Thanks so much for posting!

attributes.source_text: my loaves were very moist

reviews.review_text: I was too lazy to get out my cookbooks and search for one of the various recipes I have used for Zucchini Bread in the past.  It seemed easier to pull something up on Zaar.  This was the first thing that popped up.  However, I made some changes.  I substituted my homemade applesauce for the oil and then cut back the sugar to a little under 2 cups (due to the sweetness of the apple sauce).  I used a combination of shredded zucchini and yellow summer squash instead of just zucchini.  Also, I cut back the cinnamon and vanilla a little and added some cloves and nutmeg.  The bread was very moist and flavorful.  It had just the right amount of sweetness for a snack or light dessert.

attributes.source_text: The bread was very moist
just the right amount of sweetness
for a snack
or light dessert

reviews.review_text: I had never made zucchini bread because according to my family "it doesn't even sound good"  Well, I have a bunch of zucchini that I needed to use up so I made it.  The rule at my house is you have to try it.  If you don't like it, you don't have to eat it, but you do at least have to try it.  I left out the nuts, didn't drain the grated zucchini and had to substitute 1/2 melted unsalted butter for 1/2 of the oil because I didn't know I didn't have enough oil until I started throwing this together. Well much to my surprise, everyone liked it.   An even bigger surprise, everyone gave it 4 or 5 stars.  High honors from this crew indeed!!

Super easy to make and very tasty.  I made a few changes to the recipe - I added 1/4 tsp ground cloves, omitted the vanilla (not intentionally, I was out of it and didn't remember), I cut the sugar to 2 cups because I don't have much of a sweet tooth anymore.  I also used coconut oil, which I melted before adding to the other ingredients.  I think the coconut oil made the batter really stiff, as it solidified again when it came in contact with the eggs, which were still a little cold.  I toasted the walnuts before adding them.  I really like the whole 1 bowl, mix it all together approach - the bread came out with a nice, crunchy crust and no tunneling.  Lots of flavor, not as moist as I was expecting, which I think may be due to the coconut oil...

attributes.source_text: the bread came out with a nice, crunchy crust

reviews.review_text: First time ever making any kind of zucchini bread...and I was not enthusiastic about the idea (squash & sweet bread just seem like conflicting flavors) but halfway through the baking, the smell starting creeping through the house, and once the loaves were not "burn the taste buds off your tongue"-hot, I immediately tried a slice, then one more, just to make sure it was as good - it was.  I poured mixture into first loaf pan (no nuts) then added a handful of chopped walnuts to the batter so one loaf would have nuts.  Especially delicious with a little smear of butter...mmmmm mmmm!  Thanks so much, zucchini has never tasted so yummy!

This recipe was pretty easy, and rose well for me...however there is WAY too much vanilla!  I don't think it's very economical to use half of a bottle of vanilla when not necessary.  I actually thought it had a funny taste from too much vanilla....which I usually enjoy.  I did cut the sugar back like most to 1-3/4 c, but still found it very sweet.  I found that it hardly tasted like Zucchini Bread, which maybe that is why many people gave it such a high rating...?  I personally like to taste the zucchini, where others may not.  Just not so much our style although the recipe was easy to follow and it was very moist.

Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: it was very moist

reviews.review_text: The recipe is perfect the way that it is.  I made a few healthful changes and one flavorful one based on habit.  I used brown sugar for one half cup of the sugar.  I used plain, unsweetened applesauce instead of half of the oil (one half cup of each).  I also made the bread with one half whole wheat flour.  And, just because it is what I had on hand this weekend, I used one medium-sized zucchini and one yellow summer squash.  We've already gone through half a loaf and there are only two of us and it just came out of the oven an hour ago.  I'm sure I'll be making this again and filling up my freezer with it.

A full five stars from me and DH!  I had a few large zucchini wilting away in the fridge and decided to make this recipe up and freeze half for later.  I had already started making them when I realized that I was almost out of sugar, so I used 1/2 cup white sugar, 1/2 cup splenda and 1 cup brown sugar-can't tell the difference.  Used 1/2 white flour and 1/2 wheat flour and added some fiber powder as well...incredibly moist, very tasty.  Do note, however, that I made muffins which cooked in 25 minutes, the ones in the liners got stuck and the ones in the non-stick spray came out easily.  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: A full five stars from me and DH!
incredibly moist

reviews.review_text: Excellent, easy one bowl recipe! I used 1/2 cup oil and 1/2 cup applesauce, use 1/2 teaspoon less cinnamon and used 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg and 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves. I took some pecan halves from my freezer and put them in a single layer in a pie plate and spritzed them with butter spray. I microwaved them on high in 30 second intervals, stirring each time. Then I chopped them in my mini food processer. Added a great flavor! I made 1 standard loaf, 1 smaller loaf, and 12 muffins. My 2 sons and I prefer the muffins, because they cook through without being too brown on top.  They were done in 20 minutes. The loaves cooked 50 minutes and were too brown for me, but my husband loves that deep brown crisp flavor. I could even see baking this in a 9x13 pan and topping with cream cheese frosting! Thanks for posting a versitle, easy recipe that can be made so that my whole family gets what they want!

attributes.source_text: My 2 sons and I prefer the muffins
my husband loves that deep brown crisp flavor

reviews.review_text: I just made this today for dessert and it was so, so good!!  I loved how easy it was to make... just throw it into a bowl, mix and pour into the pans.  I made the "dough" before dinner and let it rest in the fridge till dinner was done and then put it in the oven.  It came out great!!  I was so excited to try it I ruined the first loaf getting out of the pan.. but it was worth it!  The second loaf came out fine from the pan once it was cooled.  I did use a splash more vanilla and i did add the cup of walnuts and it was glorious.  I look forward to having this for breakfast the next few days... Thanks for a yummy and easy zucchini bread!!

attributes.source_text: made this today for dessert
having this for breakfast the next few days

reviews.review_text: I cannot believe that this is so easy to make. Talk about maximum flavour for minimum effort.  A delicious moist bread. This has to be a budget stretcher to yield 2 loaves of bread.  I love a recipe where you don't have to beat those eggs and that butter.  Your directions were so easy to follow. My DS and DD didn't realise it was zucchini bread.  Do you think I should tell them?  Never!!  What a lovely way to use zucchinis, especially those oversized zucchinis.  I will definitely be making this recipe again and freezing some in slices for my family to take to work and school.  Thank you Friedel for sharing your recipe with us.

attributes.source_text: A delicious moist bread

reviews.review_text: Great recipe for Zuchinni bread. Moist and great flavor. I made it with chopped pecans. Added a small splash of milk just to help me mix it easier. Checked loaves after 55 minutes just to be sure my oven was on target. Mixed dry ingredients together first with an electric mixer just to blend all the spices good with sugar and flour. My grown kids just love coming over for Dads bread made with fresh zuchinni from my garden. I've sent pictures of the loaves to my sister in Kentucky so now I have to make it for her when she visits me in Calif. Ive made it with raw organic honey too. It was great also but that's another story..

attributes.source_text: Moist
My grown kids just love coming over for Dads bread

reviews.review_text: I wanted to like this so much.  It WAS easy to mix together.  But impossible to get out of the pan.  I greased (and floured) both of my non stick pans VERY well, and yet only half of each loaf came out.  And it doesn't take a full hour to cook.  45 minutes is more like it.  It develops a hard sugary crust and now, 15 minutes after eating a piece, I can't get the sugar taste out of my mouth.  WAY too much sugar.  And I LIKE sugar !!  I think you could easily do with 1 1/2 cups.  I would have added more spices, too...maybe some nutmeg, because, quite honestly, this just tastes like crunchy sugar.  Sorry.

items.label: Best Grilled Pork Chops
items.name: Best Grilled Pork Chops
items.description: This is a simple recipe I have adapted from Company's Coming.It is simple to throw together the marinade in the morning before going off to work and coming home to an easy dinner to prepare at night.
instructions: In deep bowl mix all marinade ingredients.
Marinate at least 2 hours.
Remove from marinade and cook over medium-high heat on greased grill for no more than 15 minutes or until done.  Cooking time for second side is shorter by 1-2 minutes.  3/4\

6-7 minutes maximum per side.   DO NOT OVER_GRILL, chops will become tough. After 2 minutes grilling on a side, rotate chops 45 degrees  for even cooking.  Turn over when juices pool on upper surface and meat appears to be cooked half-way through.

reviews.review_text:
Let me tell you why I gave it 5 Stars. I've been searching for a great pork chop recipe for years. So many of the moist chops have soup added. I've outgrown 'soup' based dinners years ago. I saw this recipe with a lot of reviews and a lot of stars, checked the ingredients and I had every single one on hand!! (when does *that* ever happen!?!)
Anyway..I start gathering the ingredients and found I didnt have any Light Soy, so I opted to substitute with Low Sodium Soy, I only had one Tablespoon of Lemon Pepper, so I used what I had and added a nice healthy squeeze of a real lemon juice and a bit of cracked pepper and then a pinch of thyme....the plot thickens, as I was also out of garlic (cant tell you how ironic that is for this house! LOL)...so I substituted with garlic powder. And THATS why this recipe gets 5 stars...it was STILL delicious!! It was sooo forgiving of my substitutions, that I KNOW when I make this next time [following the recipe] its going to be wildly awesome. Thanks for posting, Katie! this is a keeper.

These are NOT the "best grilled pork chops", they are the "best grilled pork chops-EVER." I really can't give this recipe enough stars, it's honestly restaurant quality. The chops were tender and juicy and absolutely bursting with flavorful (not a phrase I use often lol). I only made a few personal preference changes: added an extra garlic clove and used olive oil instead of vegetable. I did poke holes in the chops with a tenderizer "fork." Then, I dumped the chops into a bag with all the ingredients and let it sit in the fridge for about 7 or 8 hours. Grilled em for the suggested 15 minutes and they were perfect. If you're on the fence about trying this recipe, do yourself a favor and try it!

attributes.source_text: The chops were tender
and juicy

reviews.review_text: Love it! We all agreed they were very good (including two kids ages five and eight.) I made this two nights ago and doubled it for two dinners. For the chops I put them in a Tupperware marinade container and stuck 'em in the fridge. I also did boneless skinless chicken breasts that were frozen in a Ziplock bag, I pulled it out of the freeze and poured the marinade over them, sealed it up and stuck them back in the fridge. I did the pork chops the first night and marinated for about two hours, then grilled outside. Yummy! The chicken was done last night on the grill and they were great! Not dry like bnls sknls breasts can be on the grill. I did use olive oil instead of vegetable because I buy it at Costco in the huge plastic jug, and I used about a tablespoon of the pre minced garlic in a jar (Costco again) and the full amount of lemon pepper is essential! items.name: Steak (Or Chicken) Fajitas
items.description: These are so quick and tasty. You can use strips of boneless chicken breast instead of the beef. Feel free to double the marinade. The flavor is so great for such a short marination time. You can can do them up ahead of time and have the meat sit longer if you wish.
instructions: Slice steak into thin strips.
In bowl, mix together 1 tablespoons olive oil, lime juice, garlic, chili powder, cumin, hot pepper flakes, black pepper & salt.
Add beef strips and stir to coat, set aside.
Wrap tortillas in foil and place in 350° oven for 5-10 minutes or until heated through.
Cut onions in half lengthwise and slice into strips, cut your peppers into strips.
In large non stick skillet over medium high heat, heat remaining tablespoons of olive oil.
Add onions & peppers stirring for 3-4 minutes, until softened; transfer to a bowl and set aside.
Add beef to skillet, cook, stirring for 3-4 minutes or until they lose their red color.
Return onions and peppers to skillet; stir for about one minute.
To serve, spoon a portion of the beef mixture down the centre of each tortilla, top with your desired toppings , fold bottom of tortilla up over filling, fold the sides in, overlapping.

reviews.review_text: Good recipe, but I want to add some tips. Use flank or ribeye (boneless) if you can, but I used top sirloin like prescribed. Ribeye easiest to do in my opinion. I recommend not cutting up the steak just yet. Marinate for at least an hour, and if you have a foodsaver or similar , use it to marinate. Pan fry bell peppers and onions and and set aside once onions browned and translucent, or about 5 minutes on medium-high. Pan fry steak with all of the marinade, pour it in there. Watch temp. Around 120/130 is perfect or eye it for near medium rare. Remove steak and put on glass tray if you have and let it rest for at least 5-10 minutes. Leave it alone. Just before touching the steak after the cooldown time (~5-10mins), clean the pan (depending on mess). Drop in the onions and peppers over medium heat. Cut steak with the grain into nice long strips. Add steak back into pan to quick fry with onions and peppers for a couple mins.

Great flavor and very easy to do! I did two double batches of marinade, one for 2 lbs of chicken and another for 2 lbs of steak (eye of round) and it was just enough.  Less marinade would be very dry I think.  Meat marinated in the fridge for about 24 hours.  When cooking it, I started with the chicken and cooked till done then put in the oven at 300 degrees to keep warm.  Next was steak (same pan as chicken) which also went in the oven.  I didn't drain the juices and moved on to onions, peppers, mushrooms and hot peppers putting each batch in the oven while cooking the next.  This was a great way to feed a crowd as the prep work could be split up over two days and actually cooking everything was pretty quick which left plenty of time with guests.  I pulled the pans out of the oven and served it like a fajita bar with cooked fillings in one area and the cold toppings in another.  Served with Wholly Guacamole http://www.recipezaar.com/Wholly-Guacamole-8739 and Wonderful Salsa with Black Beans and Corn http://www.recipezaar.com/Wonderful-Salsa-With-Black-Beans-and-Corn-182724

reviews.review_text: Well, I guess with 113 reviews on this recipe, it goes without saying that it is good. It is just the right amount of everything in it. I marinated my chicken about and hour or so, and it was fantastic. I omitted the salt, though, just a preference thing. Otherwise, great recipe. Also, I had mine in a whole wheat pita pocket. * * * Update - I had leftover chicken and peppers, and I turned it into a chicken fajita pizza. Just make your favorite crust, about a 12 inch size, then I mixed 1/4 cup sour cream, and 1 clove garlic crushed, some of the chili powder, cumin, just a dash of the pepper flakes, I squeezed in some lime juice and just a drizzle of olive oil. Spread that on your crust, top with the leftover meat and veggies, top that with mozzarella. I baked mine on my pizza stone about 15 minutes at 425 degrees. It was fabulous!!! I like it when I can stretch one meal into two.

reviews.review_text: This recipe was excellent. I doubled the recipe and quadrupled the marinade. I used bison top sirloin steak, and let the meat marinate overnight. Since onions and peppers come in different sizes, you have to estimate what you need to get a good proportion of peppers and onions. I cooked the onions and green peppers until they were tender, and added the bison and marinade to the peppers and onions. Since the bison was slice very thin, it cooked quickly. Since we don't like very spicy food, I was hesitant to add the recommended red pepper flakes, but I did it anyway. It was perfect!! We all loved it. Since I doubled the recipe, I froze half of it for a future meal. A single recipe was enough for 3 of us.

reviews.review_text: I love Mexican food, especially tacos, and fajitas!  I worked in a few different Mexican restaurants for about 9 years, and even met my husband when we worked in a Mexican restaurant. Miss you on the east coast El Torito! <br/>I was skeptical with the five star rating, and even with all of the good reviews. My husband wanted fajitas for Cinco de Mayo, so I thought I would give this a try last night. I have tried many different recipes for marinades for fajitas, and they were mediocre at best. I just didn't think making fajitas was my forte. Wow!  I am so happy I did try this recipe. The flavors were beyond expectation. So simple, but so perfectly proportioned to complement each other. Putting everything together was very easy.  <br/>I did modify the instructions for the recipe a bit, but not the ingredients. I marinated the steak overnight, and then grilled it. Reading other reviews, I not only doubled the marinade, but tripled it since I had a larger piece of meat.  I cooked the veggies separate in a skillet, and added a doubled portion of the marinade to that as well.  The vegetables were scrumptious on their own. I have found my forever recipe for fajitas (even better than some restaurants), and I am very much looking to leftovers tonight :)  Yummy!

reviews.review_text: I have made this recipe MULTIPLE times with chicken and steak, both equally delicious. I substitute lemon juice for the lime juice, as I never seem to remember to purchase lime juice. However, it doesn't take away from the flavor. As per other reviewers, it is essential to place all the ingredients in a ziploc bag prior to cooking, which allows the meat to marinate properly. I usually double the recipe and it tastes wonderful. I have also subbed orange, yellow, and red bell peppers, but the sweet peppers are the way to go for the best possible flavor. You really don't need tortillas, if you don't want to make them true fajitas, as the flavors are amazing and substantial enough to be served alone. Because it worked out to well, I'll stick with a long marinating time!  I also salted the onions and peppers.  The final result was a fabulous fajita dinner.  I made this guacamole recipe which was also fabulous (added fresh minced garlic and subbed cayenne pepper for fresh jalapeno): http://www.food.com/recipe/guacamole-345790.  I will definitely make these again.  This was my first time trying fajitas.  Thanks for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: The final result was a fabulous fajita dinner

items.label: Creamy Garlic Penne Pasta
items.name: Creamy Garlic Penne Pasta
items.description: This is a delicious, super quick side or main dish. I got it from the back of a pasta box and it is yummy!
instructions: Melt butter and add garlic in a medium sauce pan.
Cook over medium for 1 minute.
Add flour and cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Stir in broth and milk and cook, stirring frequently, until sauce boils and thickens.
Add parsley, salt, pepper and cheese.
Stir until cheese is melted.
Toss hot pasta with sauce and serve immediately.

reviews.review_text:
Delicious!
Made this for dinner tonight and I have to say I love the fact that it didn't call for cream.
Used only half of one lb. box of Penne Rigate but used the full recipe of sauce.

I did use a little less than 1/4 cup fat free cream and 1/2 cup skim milk.
Hated to open a can/carton of chicken broth so used a salt free packet of chicken broth w/3/4 cup water. Worked out great!

I threw in some chopped baked spiral ham and left over broccoli while the sauce was thickening. Would rather use frozen small peas but didn't have them.
Added just pinch of dried Thyme, Rosemary and Basil.

This is a wonderful recipe.Follow it as is and add whatever protein, vegetables and spices you like.
Will make often and certainly for guests. Will double the sauce tho'.

CORRECTION: Forgot....I used Kraft Italian Classic mix of Mozzarella and Parmesan cheeses. Used same amt. as in original recipe..

attributes.source_text: Made this for dinner tonight

reviews.review_text: This was fantastic!!! We made a few adjustments just because we had the ingredients to hand: 1) when making the sauce we added a splash of white wine first, let the alcohol cook off and then added the stock and milk. 2) We added spinach at the last minute of cooking the sauce just to wilt it slightly. 2) We fried off some pancetta cubes until crispy and we then added the drained pasta and the sauce to the pan, mixing it all together. We then added some reserved pasta water (just a tad) to the finished dish and mixed it to emulsify the sauce slightly. It was so delicious and tasted very creamy and indulgent (and no cream in it - just skimmed milk!). One of my favourite recipes ever!!!!!!!!!!!!

attributes.source_text: indulgent

reviews.review_text: Tried this recipe last night. I made the sauce as posted with the exception of a couple of shakes of cayenne for a little kick. I also took the advice of some reviews and found that exactly two cups of penne with the sauce was a perfect fit. I also added about a cup of broccoli florets that I had blanched, just dropped them into the sauce right before I added it to the pasta. Wouldn't have changed a thing, this was so good! DH said he liked it but three helpings proved his point. Oh, I used real butter, canned broth, and skim milk. I will never lose this recipe, very versatile. I'm going to add chicken next. This is a definite go to I'll use over and over. Thanks so much!

attributes.source_text: a couple of shakes of cayenne for a little kick
DH said he liked it but three helpings proved his point

reviews.review_text: This was great and very simple to make! I ended up using about 3/4 of a pound of pasta (used up some partial boxes) and it was the perfect amount for the sauce. Like other reviews, I would double up on the sauce if making an entire pound. I added an extra garlic clove, sautéed a jalapeño, and threw in strips of a roasted poblano pepper at the end to make it a bit more substantial for a main dish. I also used fresh parsley. It needs a little something "more" so I just threw in some different spices I had on hand to punch up the flavor. Still its a great alternative to the sodium-laden Lipton's Pasta Sides, etc. I'll make this again!

attributes.source_text: to make it a bit more substantial for a main dish

reviews.review_text:
Made this last night, and served with sauteed garlicky spinach ,and garlic bread. ONLY change made was 1 extra garlic clove ( we love garlic here ) and a few red pepper flakes. Will DEFINETLY make again, possibly with broccoli, and sliced italian bread and butter. The possibilities are endless. Also had to double everything. We are all big eaters here, and we all bring our lunch to work with us. Just add a little butter, or olive oil to leftovers and reheat. Wonderful, all my co-workers were oohing and aahing over the aroma.
Excuse me for saying so, but to all the reviewers who claim this was bland, I don't remember seeing this presented as a "spicy" dish. If it was presented as a "spicy" dish I would agree. It was what it was presented as, creamy and delicious. If you want spicy, make your changes as wanted, as I did, but don't give a great recipe a poor rating because it was bland. It was actually exactly what I was looking for, not a tomato sauce and not an alfredo sauce. Take the recipe for what it was presented as. For my 12 hour day, it was "creamy and delicious" short on time and easy. Thank you Karen, for this wonderful recipe, which is going into my new ( Christmas Gift) family album of recipes. Happy New Year to you and yours. ( By the way, am making again for New Years Eve buffet)

attributes.source_text: I don't remember seeing this presented as a "spicy" dish

reviews.review_text: I should have read all the reviews before starting this.  We found it to be very bland as well, even though I added Coconut Milk in place of regular milk since we're lactose intolerant.  We added some vegan cheese and it was better, but not "there".  Needs spices to get this to taste good. I served it with chicken, garlic sauteed mushrooms and squash, over elbow macaroni and it was just OK as a base recipe.<br/><br/>Oh, and there's NO way that this is 6 servings. I didn't double anything and it was barely enough for 2 of us, with a little left over, and we were careful with our servings.  It might be enough for 3 servings.

Great recipe, definitely 5 star. If you are using 1 pound of pasta, I agree with so many of the other reviews-double the sauce! I doubled it, but only used 3 tablespoons of flour, otherwise it gets too thick. I was worried it looked thin in the saucepan, but when I tossed it with the penne it coated the noodles beautifully and the pasta soaks up that sauce! My family loved it and my 7 yr old son gave it one of his "Favorite Recipe" stickers- LOL. It is as easy to make as the boxed mixes, but tastes so much better.I did use fresh parsley and added in some spices as suggested by others: crushed red pepper flakes (a pinch), 3/4 teaspoon sea salt, fresh ground black pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon Italian seasoning. I think the Italian seasoning gave it the spark it needed. I served it with Crispy Balsamic Baked Chicken Breasts (from this site , another favorite) and a vegetable blend of broccoli, cauliflower, carrots, zucchini, and yellow squash. What a keeper, thanks so much!

attributes.source_text: My family loved it
my 7 yr old son gave it one of his "Favorite Recipe" stickers

reviews.review_text:
This is an excellent dish that lends itself to many additions. I followed others remarks and added more than twice the amount of cheese in the recipe. I did not have any fresh Parmesan cheese to grate, but will be sure to use the fresh cheese next time. I also put a bit of Pecorino Romano Cheese in place of some of the Parmesan cheese. It adds a nice "tang" to the sauce!

I also added bit more garlic to my families "taste". 

Next time I am going to add some Sun Dried Tomatoes and some grilled chicken strips to the dish. 

Easy, quick and delicious! This recipe makes you feel like a real chef!

attributes.source_text: It adds a nice "tang" to the sauce!
I also added bit more garlic to my families "taste".

reviews.review_text:
This is a very yummy, quick dinner to make.  

I followed the recipe almost to the 'T'.  i've made this recipe about three or four times now.  

The only changes I made was to the parmesan cheese.  I used parmigiano-reggiano instead of parmesan cheese.  I also added extra fresh grated cheese on top of the entire dish to finish it off.  

I made this Sunday night and had only Parmesan cheese, so I used 1/2 cup cheese instead of a 1/3. I also baked some chicken breasts seasoned with Italian Seasoning and cut it up and put it on top of the pasta and topped it with cheese.

All in all this is a GREAT recipe, THANKS!!!

attributes.source_text: quick dinner to make

reviews.review_text: I was looking for some sauce to use with refrigerated tortelloni and this one turned out to be perfect. Several people said that it seemed to lack something, and others said that they added more garlic. Here's what I did: I roasted a whole head of garlic (cut off the top of the bulb, drizzle about 1 Tbsp of olive oil over exposed cloves, then bake @375 degrees for 30 min.).  I used half of the roasted garlic cloves for the sauce (you can omit step 2) and the other half I mixed with some softened butter.  Warm, crusty sourdough bread with garlic butter was a perfect compliment to the pasta dish.  Also, I used chicken bouillon and water in place of the chicken broth, and the sauce did not need any additional salt.  Next time, I think I will try adding some rosemary or perhaps some fresh basil for a different twist.  Although the recipe says it serves 6-8, when we used the sauce pretty generously, it only served two adults and two small children.

This certainly gets points for the creaminess of the sauce! But since I am a picky eater, I'll have to work on the seasonings to get the taste just right! I used jarred minced garlic & I don't think I used enough; I'll up it to 1 tsp next time-maybe even more. I added 1/4 tsp garlic salt & 1/8 tsp onion powder & will probably double those next time. I will probably leave out the parsely because I thought it distracted from the garlic taste! I loved the cheese taste & I also added some marinated chicken to make this a main dish. Oh, and I only used 4 oz pasta & it was plenty (cut the rest of the recipe in half). Thank you for sharing!

attributes.source_text: gets points for the creaminess of the sauce
distracted from the garlic taste
I loved the cheese taste
to make this a main dish

reviews.review_text:
Very good! I actually used rotini, because its what I had. It was very good though! I think this would be great with a can of tuna added also, like a tuna helper- but better! I added peas into the sauce, juice and all, and that really gave it something! Thanks for a wonderful recipe! Ill make it over and over. Update- I've made this alot! It is good with tuna, it is good with chicken, its good with broccoli too. Its very versatile
 I always always double the sauce though because i like alot of sauce and i sometimes make it thicker with more flour at the begginning. Dont be afraid to go heavy with the sea salt with this dish, and i put more cheese as well and use all organic ingredients, raw milk and homemade stock- i think it makes a quality difference. Ive also use whole wheat pasta most of the time. Still good, but this white roux is better with regular white pasta

Great starter recipe! I am somewhat challenged when it comes to measuring ingredients or using the exact recipe...<br/><br/>I used Garlic powder because it was too much work to find my garlic (with my Mom in the kitchen, everything is arranged where I can't find most things), then I forgot I did not have broth, so I just used water and 1 chicken bouillon. I also added peas because I thought it needed something green, and chopped 2 slices of deli ham. It is AWESOME! I uploaded a photo, but I don't know where it went ;) <br/><br/>Thanks, Karen!

Karen, this was very good! I did however... only used about half the pasta (9-oz. to be exact) so the pasta was nice and creamy. I cooked the pasta with 1 tsp of salt added to the boiling water, and along with a bit of vegetable oil. I used a low sodium chicken broth, 2% milk, used only 1 tsp of dried parsley flakes, an 1/8 tsp each of black pepper and red pepper flakes, plus added 1/4 tsp of dried Italian seasoning. Next time I will add some diced yellow onion when I add the minced garlic. I look forward to preparing this dish often. Thanx for the recipe Karen. It's a keeper!!

attributes.source_text: so the pasta was nice and creamy

reviews.review_text: I enjoyed substituting ingredients to make this recipe vegan.  I made the following substitutions: brown rice noodles, veggie broth, brown rice flour, roasted broccoli/red pepper/red onion, earth balance in place of butter, almond milk with a little extra added so the sauce wasn't so thick, nutritional yeast in place of cheese.  It was pretty good with using this recipe as a foundation, but I think I might cave for some vegan parmesan cheese next time, so it's more of a creamy white sauce instead of a creamy yellow sauce (looked like fancy mac n cheese), and see how the taste changes.

This recipe isn't bad.  My first thought was that it was on the bland side, but I have just gone back for a second taste and found it to be improved.  I followed the recipe exactly, but doubled the garlic, used fresh parsley instead of flakes and added small slices of maple back bacon.  Nice consistency and better than I expected.  Even with the extra garlic and bacon though, this is a very mild sauce.  Probably good for those occasions when you need something that will satisfy a wide range of tastes.   Would make again.

attributes.source_text: this is a very mild sauce

reviews.review_text: This was a super easy recipe, just wish I had planned ahead instead of dashing around the kitchen in a mad dash to get the ingredients at the right time. It is a great base and it is one I will definitely be using again. I doubled the amount of garlic, added italian seasoning. Next time I will double the sauce recipe as suggested in other reviews, so that there is an extra creamy sauce left on the noodles. Also, this recipe we added our broccoli, because it just felt like it needed something added to it. But overall, great recipe!

This was really good!  I took some advice from other reviews and added mushroom and chicken to make it a meal.  I also added a bunch of extra garlic, since we are huge garlic lovers.  I loved this because it was like having alfredo sauce, but better for you and less dairy.  I have a slight lactose intolerance issue, so less dairy with a similar taste is perfect for me!  We'll definitely be making this again, since we always have these ingredients on hand.  Next time, I might add some red pepper flake or cayenne to give it a little extra kick.  Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: I also added a bunch of extra garlic, since we are huge garlic lovers
it was like having alfredo sauce, but better for you

reviews.review_text: I signed up to food.com just to write how awesome this recipe is! The results were almosy identical to my favorite restaurants Alfredo dish only better and cheaper! I used vegetable stock instead of chicken and honestly it's so amazing. Also, i saved some of the pastas water and added it to the cream mixture - I heard this adds a soup texture and since I don't want the pasta to be so thick it dries up fast, so the pasta water really helped! So great, so easy, best recipe I've tried so far!! Will make again for sure !!!

items.label: Kittencal's Famous Greek Salad
items.name: Kittencal's Famous Greek Salad
items.description: Be prepared for the best Greek salad on the planet! --- plan ahead the dressing needs at least 2 or more hours to blend the flavors, I sometimes add in 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese to the dressing for a more cheesy dressing, all amounts may be adjusted to taste ----  to marinade the salad allow to sit at room temperature before serving, see bottom of instructions --- you will find this and many more of my recipes posted here http://kittencalskitchen.com/2009/04/13/kittens-famous-greek-salad/  ---also see my recipe #359292
instructions: For the dressing; in a processor or use a wire whisk process/whisk the olive oil with lemon juice, 2 teaspoons dried oregano, garlic, dried, basil, red wine vinegar, salt and sugar until smooth (add in more oregano and lemon juice if needed).
Season with black pepper.
Chill in fridge for a couple of hours before using to blend flavors.
Place the salad ingredients in a large bowl.
Pour dressing over; toss to combine.
If desired allow the salad to sit at room temperature for 20 minutes before serving, or you can refrigerate for 1 hour (tossing a few time during sitting time).

reviews.review_text: Perfection! We've had Greek salads at many restaurants and our favourite is a little Mom & Pop Greek diner but it's expensive to feed a large family. I followed this recipe, exactly as written. I buy hearts of romaine when it's on sale as it's easily rinsed and has a better flavour. For 5 people, I used 1Â½ hearts of romaine, half a green pepper, 2 Roma tomatoes, half a red onion, half an English cucumber, full amount of blue cheese & olives. I chopped the green pepper & onion only so our 10 year old wouldn't get a large piece and she had seconds. For the dressing, I used the full amount of oregano & lemon & 3/4 cup of good extra virgin olive oil, as recommended by Kittencal. I reserved half the dressing to use later in the  week, with the remaining veggies. Served with souvlaki, tzatsiki & mushroom rice. This is my second keeper from Kittencal. Many thanks!

attributes.source_text: our 10 year old wouldn't get a large piece and she had seconds

reviews.review_text: By far the best greek salad I've ever had.  However, I could not imagine using an entire cup of oil.  I did not use 3/4 cup, or even 1/4 cup.  I only used 1 tablespoon.  Also, since I wanted to keep the calories down, I added fewer olives and less cheese.  This reduced the fat even further.  I added maybe half a carrot for extra vitamin A and some quartered artichoke hearts because I like them.  No changes at all, otherwise.  Also, I was unclear whether I was supposed to add all of the dressing to the salad.  I did, but it seemed excessive so I poured off most of it.  As per Scotch Bob, I did marinate most of the veggies in the fridge with the dressing before putting everything over the lettuce and adding olives and cheese.  I did include some parmesan cheese.  I was not concerned about it's being authentic Greek or not.  I would definitely make this again.

I brought this to a cook out today, and it was thoroughly enjoyed.  I was asked to share the recipe, too!  I did make a few minor changes just as a matter of personal taste - nothing at all wrong here with the recipe.  I cut the olive oil down to 1/3 cup and the salt to 1 teaspoon.  I put in a full tablespoon of basil, but this was only because I didn't realize I misread the recipe until after I dumped it in.  It turned out fine because we love basil, and so I'll probably continue to make it the same way.  I used grape tomatoes vs. regular in the salad and added a can of artichoke hearts since I had a taste for them (turned out that many others were snatching them out of the salad, so it was a good addition!).  I only used 1/2 an onion since mine seemed really strong.  Finally, after reading some reviews of other recipes, I went with solid feta that I cubed rather than the crumbled type (the cheese didn't disintegrate and become "lost" in the salad this way).  The dressing is amazing and so I plan to keep a bottle made up in the fridge regularly!  I have to say that I probably wouldn't have made this if it weren't for the reviews.  The ingredient list seemed rather ordinary to me, but believe me the end result is anything but!  I will make this often.  Thanks for such a great recipe.

attributes.source_text: I brought this to a cook out today

reviews.review_text:
The first time I made this recipe it was a 3 star recipe for me.
I just changed the directions it a bit and it was a five star recipe!! Here's what I did:
I mixed the basil, oregano, pepper, vinegar and oil and poured over the onions and let them sit for 1-2 hours. And sprinkled the sugar and salt on the tomatoes and let them sit for a few mins before tossing them into the salad. I mixed everything together (along with the onions, and their oil/vinegar). It was one of the best greek salad i ever had!!
Thank you kittencal for a fabulous recipe!

attributes.source_text: one of the best greek salad i ever had

reviews.review_text: The recipe doesn't need another 5 star rating -- but it's so wonderful that I can't let you NOT know how much we enjoyed it.  You've done it again!  I made the dressing about 6 hours ahead of time to make sure all the flavors had time to blend with one another.  I followed your directions exactly as written and this turned out just great.  I did let the cut up Romaine sit in a bowl of ice water for several minutes prior to mixing it with the remaining ingredients --and did the same with the sliced red onion.  Do you have any idea how long the dressing stays fresh in the refrigerator?  This is a salad that I could fix for my husband and I several nights a week!!!

I followed the recipe to the letter.  I thought it was quite good, but it didn't "knock my socks off."  I am still looking for the perfect Greek salad that I had in Greece.  Maybe Arbequina olive oil (Italian, mild & fruity--my usual choice for salads) is too mild for this recipe. I think I'll try it again with a Greek OO.  Or maybe it's my distaste for sugar, which I don't normally use, I'm very sensitive to the taste, I thought it could have been omitted entirely. I'll try it again without sugar.
I absolutely agree with other reviewers to marinate the red onion & cucumber for a good hour at room temp. before adding the remaining ingredients. That's a must for me...

attributes.source_text: the perfect Greek salad that I had in Greece

reviews.review_text: Perfect Greek salad but it was too much dressing for the amount of ingredients and there was a pool of dressing in the bottom of the serving dish and I did follow the directions to add before serving. I have now made this a number of times, once even adding gluten free pasta to make it more of a meal! I used a good flavour organic olive oil, fresh organic lemon, organic mountain oregano from Greece, organic fresh garlic clove, organic apple cider vinegar in place of red wine vinegar for religious reasons, sea salt, to taste, a little more organic cane sugar because if my change of vinegar, romaine lettuce hearts, I left out the onion, no bell pepper, plus the rest of the ingredients. I will make this dressing and salad or modified as I try to avoid cheese again!

attributes.source_text: Perfect Greek salad

reviews.review_text: Oh, WOW! Quite probably the best salad I have ever had, Greek or otherwise. My roomie declared this to be better than all of the Greek salads he's ever had, even from the best Greek restaurants. I used the upper amount of lemon juice, the full 1 cup of oilive oil, and because I realized too late that I was out of basil I upped the oregano just a little bit more to compensate. I also left out the olives, since my fiance hates them (and I dislike them anyway), but made them available "on the side" for our guests. I also used halved grape tomatoes instead of Romas, as we prefer their smaller size and better flavor. This is a new staple in my house. Thanks for sharing!

My roomie declared this to be better than all of the Greek salads he's ever had

reviews.review_text: I printed this recipe a long time ago, not sure if we would like such bold flavors.  Well, I made this last night and wow was it sensational.  Hubby and I couldn't get enough of it.  DH is a thousand island man only, so I wasn't sure how he would feel about this salad but he loved it.  Even took the left overs with him for lunch today.  The feta cheese in this is great, I love the sharp taste with the dressing and the rest of the ingredients.  I only wish I wouldn't have waited so long to try.  Thank you soooo much for posting, we will be making this often...Stephanie

reviews.review_text:
Awesome!!  I have made this before, but, for some reason, (apologies in advance) I never gave a review (must have been when I had visitors from Aussie last year for my son's wedding) but, after having a reprieve in the weather today (we hit 19 plus celcius - bring out the suntan lotion) I made this.. I wish you could have seen hubbies delight in savouring this lip smacking refreshing salad.  
Thank you so much for sharing this recipe - a definite must again this summer.. roll on 
P.S. The dressing is to die for..  I didn't add the sugar in the dressing.

attributes.source_text: refreshing salad
hubbies delight in savouring this

reviews.review_text: This dressing was really good and a nice change of pace from the Italian dressing I usually make.  I was out of red wine vinegar, so I used white wine vinegar.  I think I would have liked it better with the red.  I used 4 tablespoons of vinegar, as I like it on the tangy side.  It was a tad bitter, so I added first one teaspoon of sugar, tasted it, and added the second teaspoon.  It gave the dressing a nice flavor.  I just realized that I accidentally omitted the garlic and I could kick myself!  I can't believe I overlooked it, as my husband and I are garlic fanatics.  Oh well...will be a welcome addition next time.  Will definitely make this again.  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: I like it on the tangy side

reviews.review_text: This was my first attempt at making a greek salad...and will not look any further for a new recipe!!  It was great.  I, too, was a little frightened by the ingredients...thought it would be way too olive oily...but it seemed perfect.  I did make a few adjustments.  I only added 1/2 an onion as mine was a bit potent.  Also left out the olives...not a big fan.  My husband added his grilled chicken...absolutely delicious!!!  I think we used sun dried tomato feta...which was good...but probably will go just plain feta next time.  Also added about 1/2 cup shredded parmesan to the actual salad.  The whole thing was a great meal and I have already passed on the recipe!  Thanks Kittencal...absolutely fabulous!

attributes.source_text: making a greek salad

reviews.review_text: Another good recipe, Kittencal! I used 3/4 cup olive oil (it was plenty), 3 T of lemon juice, 4 tsps dried oregano, increased red wine vinegar to 3 T., added 1/4 cup parmesan cheese as suggested in recipe notes. Omitted the green pepper, added 1/2 cup marinated artichoke hearts; I used chunk feta which I cut into cubes instead of crumbled (Sundried Tomato Basil flavor). Got rave reviews from friends who have requested the recipe. Makes plenty so I will be adding some grilled chicken to the leftovers.

attributes.source_text: Got rave reviews from friends who have requested the recipe

reviews.review_text: This IS "The Best" Greek salad according to my family. Sure beats the heck out of my old Greek salad recipe. I left out the sugar because we like the tartness of the dressing. When the salad ingredients were gone, my son scooped his bread around the bowl to get the last of the delicious dressing. I will be making your salad for a potluck we are having at a campground this weekend and I know it will be just as big a hit there as it was at home. Thanks Kittencal for a truly delightful salad that will be a welcomed addition to our meal rotation.

attributes.source_text: This IS "The Best" Greek salad according to my family

reviews.review_text: I have made so many greek salad dressings and have finally found THE ONE with this recipe!  The only thing I adjusted with the dressing was to add a 3 more tablespoons of red wine vinegar because our tastes lean towards more of a "tang", but that is strictly our preference. The food processor emulsifies it perfectly and it dresses the greens beautifully. I used kalamata olives and added fresh chopped mint leaves to the salad as well. This is better than restaurant quality and I know we will be making this again and again! Thanks KC!

attributes.source_text: greek salad dressings

reviews.review_text: This greek salad is to die for!! Until now, I've tried in vain to find a recipe that duplicates the experience of the dressing on the greek salad at my favorite greek restaurant, and finally I've found it! I like things tart, so I did not add the sugar, but added a little extra parmesan. For the salad, I omitted the romaine and added extra cucumbers. It was a perfect addition to what turned out to be a Greek themed dinner -- rack of lamb, greek potatoes (#87782) and 24k carrots (#152441). Thanks for another great recipe, KITTENCAL! :)

attributes.source_text: This greek salad is to die for

reviews.review_text: I was looking for a new salad recipe and having never tried greek salad, the five star rating and great reviews convinced me to give this a try. The salad dressing recipe is wonderful; just full of flavor. The sturdy, rough leaves of the romaine lettuce holds the dressing on so well so every bite packs a punch. The feta cheese adds a great tanginess and the olives just brings it all together. Of course the other veggies do their part, too, to make this salad exceptional. Just a perfect recipe that I will make again and again.

reviews.review_text: Everything Kittencal posts is the best and this is no exception. When I do a search for a recipe and see hers, it is always the one I choose.  This was the perfect Greek Salad....just what I was looking for!  We are garlic freaks, so the 2 TBL. was perfect.  However, it was way too garlicky for my kids....who enjoy garlic and spice.  So you may want to adjust the garlic levels or start off with 1 TBL and then add more if you want.  We brought this to a cookout and it was devoured and the recipe was requested over and over again.  YUM!
