items.label: Bev's Spaghetti Sauce
items.name: Bev's Spaghetti Sauce
items.description: This is a recipe I have developed over a number of years. This is the only spaghetti sauce my family will request! Very easy to make. I hope your family enjoys it as much as mine does!
instructions: Brown the ground beef, onion and garlic in olive oil with bay leaves, oregano, basil, Italian Seasoning, salt and pepper.
Add tomato paste, tomato sauce and diced tomatoes.
Stir well and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Use sauce to top your cooked spaghetti.
Top with sauteed mushroom.
Pass the Parmesan.

reviews.review_text: I made this for the first time yesterday, and everyone loved it. I doubled the recipe, and it was enough for dinner, leftovers, and a couple more meals in the future (froze the sauce). I always change things a bit, as sauce simmers, so I tasted this sauce and ended up adding in the equivalent, for a single recipe, of 1/2 cup of red wine, 1/2 cup of grated parmesan. I added in a couple extra cloves of garlic while sauteing the onions. I also added in the "secret ingredient" that pioneer woman recommends - one jar of pre-made sauce. yeah. I know. It's kinda crazy. But the spices are already there, etc, and it adds a secret oomph to the sauce that gives it another depth of flavor. Since it only makes up about 1/6th of the total volume of the sauce, it doesn't overpower the actual sauce flavor, just adds something extra. I used plain Prego, my family's favorite jar sauce. (don't hate me!)

attributes.source_text: enough for dinner

reviews.review_text: After years of research for a "go to" marinara spaghetti sauce, I finally found my go to recipe with Bev's Spaghetti sauce. Whenever I make this, everyone always comments how yummy, robust and tasty the sauce is. This sauce also freezes well. Here are some tweaks and/or tips: - Make the sauce a day ahead (the flavors will meld and taste even better the next day) - I did not use ground beef. I placed some olive oil in my dutch oven, browned (semi cooked) the hot italian sausage links. I removed the links and then used a pack of pork neckbones (which you can usually find (or request) in your local grocery store) and browned the neckbones in the italian sausage link "grease" and removed the pork neckbones so that I can go on to the next step (browning the onion, garlic etc). If you like pork and want to add another dimension to the sauce, I highly recommend browned pork neckbones. If not, I would recommend hot italian sausage links. - I love garlic and minced about 7 large garlic cloves (instead of using 2 cloves) - I used Contadina tomato sauce and San Marzano diced tomatoes. - After I browned the garlic, onion, etc and placed the tomato paste, tomato sauce and diced tomatoes, I then placed all the meat (sausage links and pork neckbones) into the sauce and as soon as the pot came to a simmer, I covered the pot and simmered for 2 hours. Super yummy spaghetti sauce!!!!

attributes.source_text: everyone always comments how yummy, robust and tasty the sauce is

reviews.review_text: I have not made spaghetti sauce in over 25 years! What happened with that? This recipe has changed that, & it is so EASY to prepare!!! Like most cooks, I did make a few changes: Turkey Italian Sausage links. Split the links before cooking & scrapped out the sausage. Then cooked the loose meat along with the onions & spices. DH never even realized it was not manly beef! LOTS more garlic (good for the heart). May have been as much or more than 12 cloves, which was NOT too much for us!!! (I promise we will brush our teeth & gargle before leaving home!) 2 onions (thought to double the recipe, until I saw how much it was going to make & did not want to dirty another pan) I think I will stay with the 2 onions next time, too. Mexican oregano...yummy!!! The canned tomatoes had green chilies (all I had). Only a smidgeon of olive oil, used to give the mushrooms a bit of that flavor, along with garlic salt & a bit of spray butter, too. The mushrooms were fantastic on top of the sauce & spaghetti!!! I had never done it that way, had always incorporated the mushrooms. Not any more, the woodsy flavor of the mushrooms just sparkled within the sauce in my mouth!!! Brilliant idea, Bev! Whole wheat pasta, (which we are finally getting used to). Just a tiny bit of parmesan cheese on top, more for looks than anything. Speaking of on top...this recipe is OVER the top!!! We can hardly wait until tomorrow for leftovers! Given that I did make some changes, perhaps I should not rate with stars. However, it turned out so well that I want to award 5 stars to Bev for another simple, terrific recipe!!! Dan'l you have the right idea, Bev is a keeper!

The only things I did a bit different were added 1 extra garlic clove and about 2 Tbsp. sugar to the sauce. I also couldn't resist adding my mushrooms to that wonderful meat mixture cooking on my stove. A perfect combination of spices and a sauce I couldn't stay out of the entire time it simmered! I also kept the cover tilted to let some steam out for about 45 mins to let some of the liquid cook off as it was pretty soupy.  I think this as a result condensed the salt so it was super salty.  I'll definitely not add the tsp of salt and get low sodium cans if possible.  This was an error on my part.  I added canned mushrooms instead as this is what I had on hand and 2 tsp of sugar to cut the acidity.  I also would add green peppers next time just to add some more flavor. I didn't simmer the sauce for 90 minutes, only about 30 and it was perfect! I will definitely be making this again. Thanks for sharing, Bev!

 It turned out beautifully! Generally I just take a jar of store-bought sauce and amp way up by adding lots of extras so this was my first time trying a spaghetti sauce from scratch so to speak. items.label: Oreo Balls
items.name: Oreo Balls
items.description:
My sister's co-worker brought these to a party and they were quite a hit. I don't know where the recipe came from originally.

"Bark" is an artificial chocolate or vanilla candy coating/confectioner's coating used to make a treat called almond bark and can be found at most grocery stores near the chocolate chips. 

You can use chocolate chips and white chocolate chips if you don't have almond bark, but I have found that almond bark melts better and is easier to work with.
instructions: Using a blender or hand held mixer, mix Oreos and cream cheese together.
Roll into walnut size balls.
Chill for an hour.
Melt approximately 3/4 package of white almond bark.
Stick a toothpick in an Oreo ball and dip it in the melted white almond bark.
Allow to harden on wax paper.
Takes about 15 minute.
While waiting, melt about 1/4 package of chocolate almond bark.
When Oreo balls are no longer sticky to the touch, decorate with drizzles of chocolate and white almond bark.
I just use a sandwich bag with a tiny hole cut in one corner to drizzle the almond bark.

reviews.review_text:
Absolutely wonderful. Helpful hints- 1) use a food processor to make the cookie crumbs 2) I used a kitchen aid blender to blend the cream cheese and Oreo crumbs together. As far as dipping there's many ways so I won't go into much detail there.

I make these all the time year round. They're an absolute smash at all kinds of events. Yes they are a little time consuming but totally worth it. I'll just put on my black under armor sweatshirt and sweatpants and go to town and can have an adequate amount made in seemingly no time at all. Oh wear black because sometimes they can get a tad messy if you use the regular oreos.

Overall if you have an hour and a refrigerator go for it. I sometimes add the chocolate drizzle but not always. You can go for the healthier alternatives but I usually go for the regular old ingredients, I think they taste better that way but that's just my opinion.

Nov. 25, 2006- I made several desserts for Thanksgiving, but these were the first to disappear (and fast). The guest raved over them. They looked so professional they thought I had bought them. I dipped some in white almond bark and when I ran out, I used melted white choc chips. I drizzled all of them in semi sweet choc. Easy, Messy, and Worth It!!! Definite Keeper!!! Thank you New Nana!!! Edited to add Nov. 30, 2006- I will be adding these to my Christmas Trays and I will be drizzling in red and green. I am sure they will be a beautiful addition. I will also be packaging them in some small bowls, saran wrapped with a bow. for gift giving. Then Easter, I will drizzle them in pastels. Valentines Day- red....they sound like a KEEPER, don't they!? 
Edited to add December 20, 2006
The red and green icing didn't work, but Christmas sprinkles did and so easy! I took the to work an my many co-workers devoured them, overly complimented me and said they should adorn the window of a specialty shop. There has not been one person that has tried these that did not like them. I will try to not rate these again :). I just get too excited when I come across a "Lifer"! :)

attributes.source_text: I made several desserts
for Thanksgiving
The guest raved over them
adding these to my Christmas Trays
my many co-workers devoured them

reviews.review_text: Well! These were sure the hit of our family picnic today! I've never had more compliments/recipe requests on a recipe in my life! I had quite a time crushing the Oreos to coffee ground size because my blender wasn't working with me much, but I was determined not to let any lumps slip by and put in the extra time to get it done right. It was certainly worth it too! I had purchased white almond bark for the white ones, not noticing that it was vanilla flavored. I really didn't like those ones at all and threw them out, then made that half of my second batch with white chocolate chips. Those turned out very tasty and the chocolate ones were just unbelievable! Yum! Lastly, I used DebS lovely picture as a reference  (since the blue seems to really add to the Oreo theme somehow) and added a few drops of food coloring to some of the white chocolate chip drizzled ones. It was a beautiful presentation and a special little treat! Thank you for the recipe and thanks also for everyone's suggestions and comments to assist!

attributes.source_text: the hit of our family picnic today
the hit of our family picnic today

reviews.review_text:
Absolutely delicious!  I made these for the first time this Christmas, with rave reviews.  Some of my friends were speechless, and my aunt said they were "to die for".  My uncle couldn't believe I made them because they looked so professional after drizzling with chocolate, etc. Everyone wanted the recipe!  

I was having a hard time finding almond bark- when I finally did find chocolate almond bark, it had the almonds in it, so I didn't think it'd work as well (and it was $4.99/8oz).  I couldn't find white almond bark.  So I used Wilton melting chocolate instead since I had it around anyway for other goodies I was making.  

At first I wasn't sure if I was making them right, because the oreo mixture was pretty mushed- but I did find it easier to keep the balls in the freezer for a while before dipping them into the melting chocolate. I also made them smaller since they were rich, as suggested by a few other reviewers; plus dipping them in the chocolate adds to the size.  I got about 50+ balls from one recipe. However, I am sure that no one would complain if they were bigger! 

Making the mixture is incredible easy using a food processor- I made sure my cream cheese was very soft. Forming the balls is easy if you use a small cookie scooper that helps pop them out, since it's rather sticky. If you're looking for perfect circles, your hands will get a bit messy when rolling themm in your hands (but I would suggest chilling them beforehand). The only real time consuming part was dipping them in the chocolate one by one. I found that using two toothpicks helped.

Absolutely wonderful- I am going to make these "oreo truffles" many many more times.  And I am sure I will keep sneaking them myself :)

attributes.source_text: I made these for the first time this Christmas
Some of my friends were speechless
my aunt said they were "to die for"
My uncle couldn't believe I made them
I also made them smaller since they were rich

reviews.review_text: I have made these delicious balls numerous times since first discovering the recipe back in October. First batch chocolate drizzled with white, next white drizzled with chocolate(this combo uses up the leftover bark from the first batch perfectly). Next batch was EYEBALLS! Yes, I said eyeballs. Decorated for a Halloween party by dipping in white bark and using blue and black tubes of cakefrosting for the iris and pupil. And finishing it off with red gel for blood vessels. I can't tell you how unerving it was to have a whole tray of bloodshot eyeballs looking back at you. Sure didn't stop anyone from eating them tho, especially Clint Eastwood and Shrek. And most recently about six batches made for Christmas by dipping in wite and drizzling with red and/or green candy melts. Green used on the mint oreo balls and red on the plain oreo balls. Both colors used together if there was only one flavor being made for that occassion. Everyone remarked that they were beautiful and looked like I paid big bucks and bought them at a candy store. This is a phenomenal recipe that deserves more than five stars!!

attributes.source_text: Decorated for a Halloween party
Decorated for a Halloween party
about six batches made for Christmas

reviews.review_text:
Sorry to disagree with so many people, but ratings are subjective, right? 
These are not all that, IMHO. 
I followed the recipe exactly except for decorating the dipped balls. Glad I saved the white bark. 
I did make the balls a bit smaller counting on the richness noted by so many other raters. 
A blender is almost impossible to work with in this recipe, but the handmixer worked great (started with ground up Oreos which I did accomplish in the blender - pulsing in small batches). The inside texture of the finished product is very nice, smooth and tastes ok. ..just NOT all that. Also this is a pretty expensive recipe. Just add up the individual ingredients for the tallyâ€¦.
I would rather spend my time, money and calories in rolling up balls of REAL chocolate truffles and use my Oreos in that fabulous Cookies and Cream cake recipe. Bigger payoff for time involved and taste.

attributes.source_text: The inside texture of the finished product is very nice, smooth

reviews.review_text: This recipe was very helpful, however I changed a few things. I prefer using chocolate chips and white chocolate chips instead of the almond bark. It just tastes more like real chocolate that way. Also, contrary to the other reviews I used a hand mixer to finish blending it and it worked fabulously! There were no chunks of cookies at all. I did crush the cookies very well by hand first but the mixer did a good job of finishing turning the cookies into crumbs and mixing in the cream cheese. My last change was that instead of using toothpicks and dipping my balls I use a spoon and pour the chocolate over them, rounding it around the bottom as I went along because I don't like having little holes at the top of my treats.

I love how versitle this recipe is. I used 1/2 cream cheese and 1/2 peanut butter for my middles -they were a little softer set but that is ok because they are fine in the fridge- and real white chocolate for the coating (mixed with a tsp of canola oil which makes the chocolate smooth/easy to dip and gives a great shine). I then drizzled with melted peanut butter chips. YUMMY! My kids want me to dip them in peanut butter chips next time which I will try too!
I used a candy dipping utensil (looks like a big loop with a handle) and mine came out very professional looking. Of course they got eaten so fast it didn't matter anyway lol.
Worth noting, double stuff do not work very well for these centers, too much cream. You can get away with it but it will be really gooey inside.

attributes.source_text: they were a little softer set
makes the chocolate smooth
My kids want me to dip them in peanut butter chips next time

reviews.review_text: This recipe was on the internet submitted by wyndel from Mississippi about 7 years ago.  I made it by putting the cookies in a plastic gallon storage bag & used the rolling pin.  It was a little messy but it worked. I have candy tools that I use to dip the balls and it is easy & quick.  they can be bought at Michaels or Hobby Lobby in the cake decorating section. I have also removed the filling & rolled the cookies in the bag first. Then I put the cream cheese & icing together first then added to the cookie crumbs.  When you dip your balls put then on waxed paper on a cookie sheet.  Immediately put in refrig for about 5 mins.  Then you can serve then at room temp to serve later.  Store in refrig or freezer. lola103

I use a food processor to grind up the cookies, and add the cream cheese a quarter at a time and get a perfect "dough" to roll into balls.  I also add either rum or whatever I feel like at the time to either the cookie mix or the chocolate, depending on who I am serving.  The last time I made these I dipped them in dark chocolate and then into toffee bits that I had broken down in the processor. Everyone thought I had spent a fortune on expensive chocolates at some specialty store.  Excellent, easy, delicious recipe.  I use the cheap off brand oreo type cookies and lowfat cream cheese and then splurge on the liquor and topping.  Never fails to be the first consumed and then GONE! wherever I serve them.

These are so rich and good! I didn't use a blender though, the recipe I found said to use a food processor to chop up the oreo's but I don't have one, so I used a hand chopper and chopped them until they were nothing but crumbs. Then I used my hands (as called for in the recipe I used) to mash in the cream cheese. It worked great. I used a bag of vanilla candy melts I had left over and then instead of doing the whole melt dark chocolate and drizzle thing I just sprinkled some mini chocolate chips on top. It gave it that great contrast of color but was much easier! Anyway you do it though, these are soooo good!! Try with mint oreo's and mint chocolate chips for coating...my hubby LOVES them that way!!

attributes.source_text: These are so rich and good!
my hubby LOVES them that way!!

reviews.review_text: The easiest way to crush the Oreos put in a ziplock bag and either roll them with a rolling pin. Or if you have young kids and want to keep them entertained and focused and “help” put in a zip lock bag, give them plastic whiffleball batts and let them at it. They can crush those things within an inch of their Oreo loving life. I used to do this when my kids sew small ( they are now in college) and they still want me to make this every Christmas and they beat the Oreos with wiffle ball bats. They put them away and save them for this purpose only. Lol. Got a call from one of them and said mom, having a study break and getting frustrated, can we make a batch of dirty snowballs. That is code for, get the whiffleball bat ready, cause I need to beat some Oreos. Lol

attributes.source_text: they still want me to make this every Christmas
they still want me to make this every Christmas

reviews.review_text: I actually haven't made these yet but my future daughter in law made them for turkey day and they were wonderful! I didn't think the were to rich maybe that's because she did the same recipe but added 1Tbs. of creamy peanut butter and 1Tbs powder sugar. After dipping them in white chocolate she dusted them with some of the oreo crumbs. She did some with just a drizzle no dipping. My husband who hasn't be eating sweets much just loved them. He thought they were made with brownies. They were a big hit and went fast. I have seen a lot of variations for this recipe. You can try adding flavorings like orange, mint etc. which I plan on trying this x-mas as well as an orange ball made with vanilla wafers that I found on this site. when I do review on it to follow. also people are saying they are expensive to make. I usually get my oreo's for 2 for 5 bucks or 2.99 which isn't bad. they also have a store brand with Chocolate centers which would be interesting to try. Yummy Stuff!!!

attributes.source_text: made them for turkey day
My husband who hasn't be eating sweets much just loved them

reviews.review_text:
These were wonderful.  Decadent.  Indulgent.  *****  


But I gotta help you learn from my mistakes:  *****  

First, do not put the cookies in an old stand mixer and turn the dial on.  Cookies and crumbs everywhere!  I recommend using a blender ... or mixing the cookies and cream cheese a bit first. *****  

Second, these are rich, and they're a bit spendy to make (about $5 with sale-priced ingredients:  $1 -- cream cheese; $2 -- generic oreos; $2 -- chocolate bark)  So, don't plan these for snack when you're feeding a crowd of kids.  Somehow, kids don't get slowed down by the richness of a snack!

*****  

However, these are so good that I am going to make these as part of the treat baskets that I make my neighbors this Christmas.

attributes.source_text: Decadent.
Indulgent.
these are rich

reviews.review_text:
These are really good.  I used a 1 inch melon baller with the spring to make the balls. The cookie sheet filled up quickly and I just gave each a quick roll to smooth them out.  I used 2 forks to dip them in the chocolate. One fork to get them covered and the second fork to slide them off on to the wax paper to keep the tops smooth. The size is perfect, it made over 60 balls.  I just used chocolate chips and parafin wax since I could not find the almond bark. I was going to top them with cookie crumbs but I forgot to save some. I will try that next time.   I did add crushed peppermint to the top of a few, but the kids said they taste better without the mints.   
I will make these year round!

These are simply wonderful and easy to make.  It took a while for the food processor to finely crush all of the Oreo's (yes, I crushed them beforehand) - and then even longer to evenly distribute the cream cheese - but it came out as a mushy, chocolatey dough.  They were easy to roll - the oils from the cream cheese made it easy to not make a total mess while rolling them into balls.  The dipping is always a mess - but well worth it.  Thank you for this wonderful recipe.  -  I might add that these NEED TO BE REFRIGERATED!  I made them last night and then put them in the fridge - then this morning I had to try one and they were even better than the night before.  Thanks again for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: a mushy, chocolatey dough
a mushy, chocolatey dough

reviews.review_text: I enjoy trying some new recipes every year for the holidays & this was a HUGE hit with everyone! My 9-year-old grandson smashed the Oreos, (which were first placed in a heavy-duty, freezer-type, zip close bag), with the smooth side of a meat mallet. He easily mixed them with a hand-held mixer in a deep, narrow bowl, then we both shaped them into balls and chilled them AGAIN, before dipping. He was so proud of his accomplishment! We used reduced-fat Oreos and fat-free cream cheese & they were delicious! We just placed them on parchment, (instead of waxed paper) and had no 'sticking' problems, at all. This is definitely a keeper and will be on our 'must-do' recipe list every Christmas! Thanks, New Nana! Lucas & Pat

attributes.source_text: for the holidays
My 9-year-old grandson smashed the Oreos
every Christmas

reviews.review_text:
Good recipe. I have personal taste testers (children next door) I got mixed reviews. The ones who liked it said it was "Fantastic", "Amazing".
My son really liked these.

**UPDATE**
This has been the most requested desert recipe in my home.
I use the food processor to grind up the cookies, then put them in the bowl & use the hand mixer to mix it well. I add a teaspoon of pure vanilla extract. I will not buy Oreo brand unless it's on sale & was bugged to make these again so I tried it with Wegman's brand of Oreo. They were just as good as the Official Brand cookie.
UPDATE: I now grind up extra oreo cookies (without the cream center) and roll the Oreo Ball to coat them.

attributes.source_text: My son really liked these
the most requested desert recipe in my home

items.label: Ww 0 Point Weight Watchers Cabbage Soup
items.name: Ww 0 Point Weight Watchers Cabbage Soup
keywords: c("Onions", "Vegetable", "Low Protein", "Low Cholesterol", "Healthy", "Free Of...", "Savory", "< 60 Mins", "Beginner Cook", "Stove Top", "Easy", "Inexpensive")
items.description: Make and share this Ww 0 Point Weight Watchers Cabbage Soup recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Spray pot with non stick cooking spray saute onions carrots and garlic for 5 minutes.
Add broth, Tomato paste, cabbage, green beans, basil, oregano and Salt & Pepper to taste.
Simmer for a about 5-10 minutes until all vegetables are tender then add the zucchini and simmer for another 5 or so minutes.
I have tried different variations. Leaving out green beans. Adding chopped green onions in addition to the yellow onion.
All very good. You can customize it a bit.

reviews.review_text:
Preparation Notes:

1.	I could not find fat-free beef broth, but I did find and use 99% fat free beef broth
2.	I used a tablespoon of Extra Virgin Olive Oil to satuee the onions (I donâ€™t care for cooking spray)
3.	Instead of using fresh carrots, green beans and zucchini, I used frozen vegetables.
4.	Instead of dried basil and oregano, I use fresh herbs.
5.	If you add more vegetables than the recipe calls for, then you will need more beef-broth


Here is my modified recipe:
(keep in mind that I doubled the recipe)

8 	cups, 99% fat-free beef broth (two large cans)
3	garlic cloves, minced
1/3	small can tomato paste (adjust to your preference of a â€œtomato-eeâ€� taste
2/3	small head of cabbage, chopped
1	small yellow onion
1	small bag of frozen, crinkle cut carrots (Kroger Brand)
1	small bag of frozen green beans (Kroger Brand)
1	small bag of mixed vegetables, including carrots, lima beans, zucchini, and cauliflower (Kroger Brand)
2	tablespoon, fresh chopped basil
2	tablespoon, fresh chopped oregano
	Salt & pepper to taste

I followed the preparation directions, except I let the soup simmer for about two hours â€“ I have no idea how they could have cooked this recipe (especially with fresh vegetables) for only 10-15 minutes!

i started Weight Watchers a few weeks ago, and with that being said, I downloaded the niffty app on my iphone to calculate points. After being on this website looking at the different Weight Watchers recipes, and calculating the points for each item....I found that everything that is posted on this website to be completely incorrect to Weight Watchers standards. This soup is actually "1" point per serving, although it is just "1" point, it is not considered a FREE food, and the more you eat of this, the more the points go UP. I also found a cupcake recipe on here that said it was only "1" point, did the math and it came out to be "8" points!!!! My point is, do the math, make sure the point value is correct for those of you who are serious about this program. i am sure not every recipe is incorrect, but 75% of the ones I found, were :(

This is a recipe you can play with.I do not saute veggies,I just throw everything into the soup pot and let the flavors simmer.You can fudge with ingredients and amounts as desired.I did not have zucchini on hand and omitted  tomato paste as I used leftover tomato ingredients.I did increase beef bouillion broth to 5 cups,actually 10 cups as I doubled.I have made beef cabbage soup by adding leftover roast beef and some leftover gravy. I have also made a spicy cabbage soup (i used half a head of cabbage)using leftover carnita pork #25621 and by adding 2tsp. fuego spice which is 1/4 cup paprika,2 tsp cayanne pepper,2 tsp white pepper,2tblsp oregano,chile powder,garlic powder,salt,pepper.yields one cup,store in airtight container for future mexican meals..Also I keep a freezer bag in my freezer that is a catch all for all leftover tomato sauce,tomatoes-canned and fresh leftovers.I had about 2 cups I tossed in the soup.Also added 3/4 cup celery and 2 cups carrots and a drained can of green beans..Nice spicy cabbage soup..I always double this recipe...

attributes.source_text: Nice spicy cabbage soup

reviews.review_text: What a GREAT soup!!  I decided to "go big or go home", and make a HUUUGE pot so i could eat it at home when i got hungry, and more importantly, to be able to take some to work all week...so i used 2 32oz. cartons of beef broth.  I basically doubled everything...used 1/2 a head of cabbage, 4 carrots, 1 zucchini, green onions, 1/2 a large onion, 1 can green beans, 2 stalks of celery, garlic, and fresh parsley...i basically just started throwing whatever i could find into the pot...BEYOND YUMMY!  i doubled up on the oregano and basil, also added a little thyme. That is truly the beauty of this recipe...you can play with it and make it your own. It really is VERY filling too...after i let it all simmer for about an hour, i had about a cup and a half...FULL!  this is going to be the NEW staple of my diet!!  Swimsuit here i come!!!  thank you for a GREAT recipe dageret!!  :-)

Well, I'm just going to sound like an echo of the last 169 reviews of this recipe... but, OMG!  This is SO good!  I set out to make this exactly as directed (using beef broth)... fresh green beans and all, but my 3 year old distracted me just as I was opening the tomato paste and guess what?  Yep, the whole can went into the soup!  I didn't read any reviews prior to eating the entire batch myself, but I see now that others have used more tomato paste also.  I can't believe that I didn't miss meat or pasta in this soup because the flavor was so wonderful.  Even my toddler ate it!  Unfortunately, none of it made it's way to the freezer, but I'm getting set to make another batch & will double it this time to make sure there are lots of servings to vacuum pack & freeze.  Thanks so much for posting this recipe, dageret!

attributes.source_text: Even my toddler ate it!

reviews.review_text: Sorry but this just was not great. I added more vegetables and a bit more spice but it was bland. We don't like spicy btw. I used an organic beef vegetable broth, organic garlic, organic tomato paste, organic green cabbage, organic yellow onion, grated organic carrots, organic yellow beans instead if green, no zucchini as I had none on hand but added half an organic green pepper, fresh organic green peas in the pod, dried basil, organic fresh marjoram in place of oregano in a greater amount, a dash of cayenne pepper powder, sea salt & freshly ground black pepper. This may be a bit better the second day but I don't think we will finish it! DD1 (6 years old) loves soup but said this was only ok. I made a similar recipe before which had more flavour if I want this type of soup I will look for my review.

This soup has been around for years!  I taught Weight Watchers for 20 years and have been wildely endorsing this soup that long too!  For WW Point followers, be aware that if you add starchy vegetables, you no longer have a 0 Point recipe. This recipe has a lot of "wiggle" room. I substitute one box of frozen chopped spinach to replace the cabbage and I also use home made chicken or turkey broth (very low sodium that way). I also like to play with the seasonings.  I'll use fresh herbs from the garden when in season or I might try using hot sauce or pepper flakes to give it some heat.  Also, try adding leftover chicken or shrimp but be sure to figure the points if you're following WW  Points.  This is a truly delicious, versatile and healthy dish!

After making this again yesterday, I'm now revising my previous review from 2 stars to 4.  I think the reason I didn't like it the first time I made it is that I had followed the instructions and cooked my garlic much too long..I suppose it burned, which gave the entire soup a bad taste.  This time I sauteed onion and carrots in extra virgin olive oil for about 5 minutes, THEN added the garlic and cooked only til the garlic was fragrant.  Otherwise, I followed the recipe using the beef broth and it turned out to be quite good, as well as quick, easy and very nutritious.   And the next day, it was even tastier.   I'm so glad I gave this soup another chance...I'll definitely be making it regularly.

I experimented a bit.  Omitted the green beans and the zucchini and I was out of basil, so I skipped that too.  I only used 2 cups of the beef broth and used a full 6 ounce can of tomato paste, then added a can of corn and a can of pinto beans.  After everything was put together, I let it simmer for about an hour on the stove.  It turned out really nice.  The corn I loved, nice little bursts of sweetness.  And the beans added the heartiness that I typically find lacking in most soups.  While I'm sure my changes changed the nutritional value a bit, the fiber from the beans and the negligible calories from the corn...probably didn't up the points more than one or two at most, if that.  Still very healthy and quite yummy.

attributes.source_text: nice little bursts of sweetness

reviews.review_text: I just made an 8qt batch of this.  Always love this soup.  I always put in yellow squash & zucchini, kale, carrots, green onion, cabbage, and diced tomato's.   But this time, instead of regular diced tomato's I used Hunt's Fire Roasted Tomatoes with garlic.  Also, I wanted to try a different broth.  I used the Mazola Tomato Bouillon with Chicken Flavor.  I have made this soup many times and have always used either beef or chicken bouillon.  With the Tomato & Chicken Bouillon,, this was by far the best batch yet!!!!  My 13 y/o tried it and tho I had my doubts about him eating it, the bowl was done in no time flat!  He said he really liked it, veggies and all!  Wanted to know if there would be some for tomorrow!

attributes.source_text: My 13 y/o tried it and tho I had my doubts about him eating it, the bowl was done in no time flat
He said he really liked it, veggies and all

reviews.review_text: You know, i was going to only give this four stars b/c it's not my favorite thing in the world, but then i thought about it, and then decided to go for five because it's probably the best zero point thing i've tasted. I doubled the recipe for a potluck and i think it'll go over pretty well, especially with my vegetarian friends (i used garden vegetable broth and it tastes fine, i bet the beef would be even better though). i had to replace the green beans with peas, not being able to find my green beans (although i found them later, of course) and it taste fine, but the biggest addition i did was adding some Sriracha! I put 1/2 teaspoon in at first but then added another 1/4, and wow it really adds to it! It gave it just enough of a kick to make it more interesting and it helps flavor it even more. Also, this was very easy to prepare, and that's saying a lot, because i'm usually a disastrous cook. So, it deserves five stars, definitely.

attributes.source_text: I doubled the recipe for a potluck
especially with my vegetarian friends
It gave it just enough of a kick to make it more interesting

reviews.review_text: This soup really suprised me. I've never liked a soup without meat, but this was really good. Until I realized how much salt was in even the lower sodium chicken broth! I've recently developed high blood pressure so this soup ended up not to be as healthy for me as everyone else. I will look for no sodium chicken for next time. I used 3 cloves of garlic, 1/4 t red pepper, 1 C fresh shrooms, a can of tomotoes instead of paste, and omitted the green beans. I keep trying beef broth in soups and just don't like the flavor so I probably will stick with chicken. When I make it again for my husband he wants me to ad a pound of Italian sausage. As good as it tasted, even after 2 bowls throughout the day we just didn't feel satisfied. Guess we just needed some meat. This is an excellent soup I will be trying different varieties of. Thanks for a great tasting healthy soup. - Omitting the sodium for me of course!

This is good for vegetable soup... I think I was expecting something else after reading all the reviews. I messed with the recipe (I always do, can't help it) and it came out pretty good. I added 1 can diced tomatoes, used whole can of tomato paste, used veggie broth, 1/2 red onion, 16oz frozen bag of corn, can of each pinto beans and kidney beans (drained and rinsed), added extra basil and oregano, red pepper flake, 5-6 shakes of tabasco sauce, 1/2 cup red wine, 2 bay leaves, 1 cup spicy V8 juice, added thyme and sage.... put it all in my crock pot on high for 1 hour then on low for 2 hours... came out pretty good. I'll keep messing with this one, thanks for posting!

I'll be honest - I expected this soup to be really healthy but nowhere close to yummy.  I was so wrong!  I'm detoxing, and this is a great, healthy detox meal!  I doubled the recipe, using the following ingredients: one cup sliced carots (equal to three carrots), one cup diced celery (equal to two-thirds of a large rib), four cups of green cabbage (equal to half a large head) and a can of white kidney beans.  I skipped the tomato paste as I'm not eating nightshades.  I made an Italian-style sofrito by sauting ALL the vegetables in olive oil with the herbs and three bay leaves until they were soft.  Then, I added the broth, brought it all to a boil and simmered for about forty-five minutes.  The result is a delicous, sweet soup that you'd have to be crazy not to love!

attributes.source_text: a delicous, sweet soup

reviews.review_text: Loved this dageret, I followed the direction exactly (except for Zucchini as I had none) and it was great for lunch, then I decided to try it for a base for dinner and added a potatoe with some left over port - still healthy and low in fat and it was great.  Served it with my sage rolls and it made for a hearty, warm and satisfying dinner.  I can imagine a lot of things could be added, but I like it just as written for when those HUNGRIES strike.  Update: August, 2015.  Continue to use this just as written, though I do double it then freeze in batches to handle those times when hunger strikes or just a a lovely fall dinner with a slice of home made bread and a class of red wine - Yum and not bad on the calorie side

attributes.source_text: it was great for lunch
it made for a hearty, warm and satisfying dinner

reviews.review_text: WOW! That's what I can say about this soup. I made this while my hubby made dinner tonight so I could put it in the fridge for lunch throughout the week.  I sat down right after dinner, and after putting the soup into containers and putting in the fridge, and started reading these reviews.  I really didn't think that I would like this soup because the beef broth didn't appeal to me but I was sooo wrong.  After reading the reviews I couldn't wait to try the soup.  I had just eaten dinner and so I was not hungry at all, but if I hadn't stopped myself I probly could have eaten the entire bowl.  I added extra garlic and did not use the green beans because I didnt have any. Thanks for a great recipe.

attributes.source_text: for lunch throughout the week

reviews.review_text: Very good soup. Filling and full of healthy stuff. I tripled the batch for eating for the week. I used a mix of chicken and beef broth because that's what I had. The beef made it so rich and nice. I use Vidalias because they are really good right now. I also used the entire can of tomato paste, but at triple the batch, it seemed about right. I did find the zucchini to be a little mushy compared to the cabbage being harder. I think I'd add that a little bit later next time. You really can make this soup to be your own. I added mushrooms and rosemary to mine and I think it would be really great with some garbanzo beans. Awesome soup that I'll be eating all week! Thanks! :)

attributes.source_text: The beef made it so rich and nice

reviews.review_text: I make this soup quite often - at least once a week. I add double the broth as well as a lot more cabbage than it calls for, and 2 cans of diced tomatoes. I do not add the carrots or green beans as I am not a big fan. I add at least triple the garlic as well as about a of half of a block of low fat cream cheese just to give it texture. I saute the onion and garlic and then saute the zucchini with it once the onion is finish. I let the soup simmer for 1 to 1.5 hours and as it is finishing, I add about half a teaspoon of cayenne to give it a kick. items.label: Turkey Meatloaf
items.name: Turkey Meatloaf
items.description: This recipe came from a package of ground turkey. It is by far the best turkey meatloaf I have ever tasted.
instructions: Melt butter in a skillet.
Cook onion and garlic in melted butter for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Place mixture in a large bowl to cool for 5 minutes.
Combine turkey, bread crumbs, egg, 1/4 cup of the katchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper with onion mixture.
Press meatloaf into an 8x4-inch loaf pan.
Spread remaining catsup on top.
Bake in a 350 degree oven for 50-55 minutes.
(Internal temperature should reach 165 degrees.) Remove from oven and let stand 5 minutes before serving.

reviews.review_text: This is by far the BEST recipe! I did change it up a bit based on the reviews and I've gotta say it turned out amazingly. My recipe was as folllows: <br/>o	2 tablespoons butter ( or margarine) <br/>o	3/4 cup red onion, chopped<br/>o	1/4 cup shredded carrots<br/>o	2 celery stalks <br/>o	3 cloves garlic, minced <br/>o	1.3 lbs ground turkey (pre-seasoned if available at store) <br/>o	1/2 cup seasoned breadcrumbs (add extra 1/4 cup if mixture is super moist)  <br/>o	1 egg ( or 1/4 cup egg substitute) <br/>o	3/4 cup ketchup & 1/4 cup Sweet Baby Ray?s BBQ Sauce (blend together)<br/>o	1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce<br/>o	3/4 tablespoon red pepper flakes (if you like spicy) <br/>o	3/4 teaspoon salt <br/>o	1/2 teaspoon black pepper <br/>Sautee the veggies together.  I cooked mine in a cupcake pan which is perfect for parties or freezing afterwards. You only need to cook for 35-40 min on 350. Check internal temp to ensure its 165 degrees. Enjoy!

I made this tonight pretty much as written.  I relied on my eyesight for most of the measurements.  I even dragged a rarely used loaf pan out of the basement, just for clarity for all of you who are on the fence about this.<br/><br/>With no reservations, I say "Go For It"!  It is perfectly delicious as written here.  I make a lot of meatloaves with ground beef/pork combo.  And this held it's own!<br/><br/>My advice is that you will want more than five minutes for a resting period once you take it out of the oven.  More  like 20 minutes, minimum, in the pan.  And at least 10 minutes out of the pan.  Or some variation of that.  <br/><br/>But make it!  It is easy, healthy, cheap and delicious comfort food!  You won't regret it!

I think this by far is the best turkey meatloaf recipe ever.  I had been using another turkey meatloaf recipe for years. One day I started getting my ingredients together to make turkey meatloaf and I realized I was missing one key ingredient and since I was short on money I had to look for another option so I came across this recipe and tried it. Thank God I did because it was so moist and flavorful I couldn't believe it. I made my meatloaf almost exactly as told except I omited the Worcestershire sauce (I didn't have any on hand) and I used red onions (that was the only thing I had) and I used 1/4 cup of catsup (I thought it said 1/4 instead of 3/4..lol) and it came out very well. This recipe is definitely a keeper. My sister and bf had some for lunch the next morning and said it was very tasty.

reviews.review_text:
Though this recipe hardly needs another rave review, I thought I'd put my two cents in anyway.  My family usually loves meatloaf, though I find traditional (beef) meatloaves too heavy and dense.  This was perfect for all of us: light, traditionally flavored and easy to make.  My mother, who didn't know it was turkey, was convinced it was veal or a combo of veal and pork.

The changes I made to the recipe: olive oil in place of butter; added three stalks of chopped celery to the onion; mixed the salt and pepper (less of each) in with the veg mixture; added about 1-2 tsps of italian seasoning; used three slices of whole wheat toast, chopped finely, in place of breadcrumbs; used only about 2 Tbsps of catsup on top. 

I did have some trouble getting the loaf out of the pan - it's just that tender! - but the taste made up for the poor presentation.  Next time, I will just make it "freeform" on a baking sheet.  It also took about 75 minutes to cook.

reviews.review_text: If you are looking for a delicious turkey meatloaf recipe, this is it! It was so delicious and so easy to make. Also, substituting a few ingredients to fit your taste seems to work well with this recipe. When I made it I used Garden Herb Triscuits instead of Saltines. I added finely chopped celery and green peppers when sauteing the onions. (I try to sneak more veggies into recipes whenever possible). Also, I added a splash of soy sauce to the ketchup topping to give it a more spirited taste and made some extra. At 375 for about 25 mins, the loaf was perfectly moist but once sliced I added a few spoons of the soy sauce ketchup mixture (heated) for good measure. My husband and I ate almost the entire loaf in one sitting! We could not stop eating it. I have not commented on any other recipe sites but I had to on this one, because this is the best turkey meatloaf recipe I have found anywhere. Thanks!

reviews.review_text: I made this for dinner last night, with the help of my four year old. He was easily able to follow the recipe and help with every step except the sharp knife and hot oven parts, and the final result was delicious. We used mostly Panko (the last in the box), and made up the rest with crushed Ritz crackers, as desperate times call for creativity. We made the loaf in the shape of a snowman, and used less than 1/4 cup of catsup lightly smeared on the top. I made a sauce to serve with it for the adults, of catsup, worcestershire, port wine, a couple drops of chili oil, and adobo seasoning. I was really grateful to find a recipe that didn't call for processed foods, yet was still quick and easy for a weeknight dinner. My husband said he wasn't expecting to like a turkey meatloaf, but found it moist and delicious, and my son yelled "I love turkey meatloaf!" Caramelizing the onions and garlic is a huge help. We served with rice and salad, and after making those, I still had time while it was in the oven to tidy up the kitchen and set the table, including candle-light. Definitely recommend this one.

reviews.review_text: I made a few changes, but otherwise followed the recipe. I used Italian seasoned bread crumbs, and I skipped the salt as the Worcestershire sauce & ketchup would add plenty of their own. I also added 1/2 cup of finely shredded cheddar cheese (Reduced fat), a trick I learned from a PA Dutch restaurant I worked in (gently mix in after all other ingredients have been mixed in). It was the 'secret ingredient in their meatloaf. Cheese also adds salt. Divided among 8 mini-loaves in an Ecko mini-loaf pan. Extras will go in the freezer. Recipe is a keeper. Steaming cubed Russets in the Tiger rice-cooker, to make mashed to go with. Coleslaw is ready in the fridge.

Finally a Turkey Meatloaf I love! This one I will keep I have tried so many recipes searched online and this is the BEST! Even my picky 2 year old ate it! I added 1/2 cup chopped fresh mushroom, 1/2 diced green peppers, shredded/chopped 1/2 carrot because thats all I had and sauted it with the onion garlic mix in olive oil. Made my own bread crumbs a little over 1/2 cup  maybe alot more (toasted sliced whole wheat bread & throw in processor). I left out the black pepper. Also a little splash of soy sauce just because I felt like it. I did use ketchup I figure its ok because I used an organic ketchup. reviews.review_text: This is a great recipe.  There are so many with a variety of ingredients, but this one is very simple.  Sauteing the garlic and onion mean everything.  If you're not going to do that, it's pointless.  Because I'm opting for turkey instead of ground beef, I take the more healthful options and use olive oil to saute and use egg substitute.  I've also found I like it with a little less Worcestershire sauce.  I also use Heinz Hot & Spicy ketchup.  It gives it a little kick without being overpowering.  If you think it might be too much, try using it only in or on the meatloaf and use regular with the other.  Either way, given the basic recipe, it's awesome goodness.

items.description: I made my daughter's wedding cake using this recipe. It turned out fantastic. The texture is just perfect for a wedding cake -- not too fluffy so it breaks from the weight, but also not overly dense. The flavor, texture and moistness were just right. I made two batches of the batter for a three-tiered wedding cake using 14", 10" and 6" pans that were 3-inches deep. I had enough extra batter for a 9" layer (not a deep pan).  This recipe was originally created by Rebecca Sutterby.
instructions: Place all dry ingredients in a large mixing bowl and stir together with a wire whisk.
Add the remaining ingredients and beat on medium speed for 2 minutes.
Pour into greased and floured cake pans, filling each pan a little over half full.
Lightly tap cake pans on counter to bring air bubbles to top.
Bake in preheated 325° F oven until cake tests done.
Baking time varies according to the size and depth of pans being used.
I used Wilton's Bake Even Strips on my cake pans to ensure a level-topped cake which required absolutely no trimming-- I highly recommend these, or good quality professional baking pans.

reviews.review_text: Most EXCELLENT recipe, for sure! **********ALERT********* I have read a few comments about the cake not rising in the center. I don't know if this has anything to do with that, but please note that the recipe calls for 18 ounce boxes of cake mix. These no longer exist. These days they are 15.25 ounces. You might consider buying a 3rd box and taking what you need from it and combining that with each box so that you end up with total of 36 ounces of cake mix. Also, I believe you MUST use All Purpose flour. I used the whites of 6 extra large eggs and 2 yolks from those extra large eggs. I divided between two 9x13 pans and utilized parchment paper. I added about 2 cups chopped walnuts to one of the mixtures. I baked both pans (one at a time) at 335 for 50 minutes. After cooling, I covered and placed them in refrigerator. Next day, I sliced them in half HORIZONTALLY to make 4 layers. I used the Italian Buttercream recipe on this website and spread a thin layer of frosting between each cake layer starting with nut cake on bottom, then frosting, plain cake layer, frosting, nut cake, frosting, plain layer. Frost sides, top and decorate. This is, honestly, the MOST delicious cake I have ever eaten!!!

This is by far THE BEST cake recipe I have ever had the privilege of trying and eating!!!!  All I can say is PHENOMENAL!  It is so moist - you won't believe it!  I have used this recipe with white cake mix, yellow cake mix and chocolate cake mix!   They have all turned out perfectly!  One thing I would note now is that the cake companies have changed their packaging making the amount of cake smaller.  Therefore, if you use a cake mix that is 15.25 ounces - just reduce the serving to 34 and this will change your recipe to accommodate the smaller packaging!  When making the chocolate at the 34 serving size - change the following:  put in 1  and 1/3 cup flour and  1/3 cup cocoa powder.  I use Devils Food - which is the best!  Also - I bake at 340 degrees (all kinds) and start out at 35 minutes and check and then add time in 10 minute increments.  You will need to do this dependent upon the size cake you are baking.  Also, I cut a piece of parchment paper the size of the bottom of my pan.  I spray the bottom with vegetable spray, then lay the parchment paper down so it sticks.  Then I spray the top of the paper and the sides of the pan.  DO NOT FLOUR YOUR PANS!  I also use the Wilton Baking strips and my cakes turn out perfectly every single time!  Even heart shaped cakes!!!  I have never been this excited about a cake recipe - and neither has my family and friends!  Hands down.........this is the best!  Happy Baking!

I, like many other reviewers have not been a fan of white cake or boxed mixes.  I wanted to try this for the volume of batter I needed to make a cupcake cake for a bridal shower.  I made adjustments based on what I had in the house and the cupcakes turned out beautifully.  I used Aldi's white cake mix, which happens to have pudding in the mix.  Using my kitchen scale, I added approximately 5 tbsp AP flour to make the 18 oz.  I measured out 3/4 cup egg whites from carton and used half milk, half water.  I didn't have enough sour cream in the house so I subbed all FF Greek yogurt. I also decreased the sugar to 1-1/2 cups.
The cupcakes took about 20-22 minutes in my oven at 350.  They are nice and white and perfectly domed.  They pull away easily from the liners and the crumb is somewhat dense but they are quite light to taste.  I used the almond flavor and it does taste very much like wedding cake.
I'm sold on this method and will be trying the flavor variations.  If you don't like this recipe then you must be doing something wrong.  The recipe seems to be very forgiving with the adjustments made. 
I was able to get 4 dozen nice sized cupcakes by filling the cups 2/3 full.

reviews.review_text: This is an amazing cake. I was very fortunate to find this recipe. My sister got married on July 30, 2016. We lost our mother 2 years ago and I wanted to do something special for her and volunteered to make her wedding cake. I love to bake so I did a lot of research and settled on this recipe. I wanted the cake to be perfect. In my research I learned that I could start making my cakes 2 weeks ahead if it's a moist cake and freeze it. This recipe makes a large batter, enough for 2 layers of a 12" cake. In my hast I put in the whole eggs (it turned out fine, the yokes make it richer). Over a 2 week period I was able to makeup 3 batters, my largest layer was 12"s and I made smaller layers as well. I allowed the cakes to cool, then I wrapped them. I put them in the refrigerator for 1 day and then moved them to the freezer. The night before I started layering and putting on icing (I should have taken off the brown coating). I made a white butter cream icing for high temperatures and I put a lemon curd filling between the layers. This is the best cake ever! It was a big hit, it's very moist and flavorful. I have gotten several calls for information about the recipe. This was my first wedding cake, and I would do it again. It was a perfect solution for a tight budget. I definitely recommend anyone to try it, just pace yourself. Thank you food.com for this amazing recipe. Brenda

reviews.review_text:
I wanted to make a cake for my husband for Valentines day. The store did not have white cake, so I used Betty Crocker yellow. I cut the recipe exactly in half, since this was only for our family.

I miss the 'Champagne' cake I can get in Bakersfield from Smith's bakery where I'm from, so I took inspiration from that. I don't have a ton of equipment, but I made up for that with the use of parchment paper. LOL!

I baked one round and one square cake and lined the pans with parchment. Cut the round in half, arrange the square cake so it looks like a diamond then put each 1/2 circle on the two top sides, making the heart shape. My long thin bread knife took care of any leveling, but honestly it was minimal. I didn't have a pan quite large enough for this...but two things made it easy for me to house the cake once together...the bottom of my roasting pan and a small countertop chopping block (in case you are like me and need ideas to enable your cooking!!).

Once the cake was together, I frosted it with Wilton's Whipped Icing Mix (because I prefer the Whipped topping over buttercreme). I then sprinkled a little plain cocoa powder over the cake for both color and flavor (I just shook it through my mesh collander), then shaved some Wilton's red melting chips with my cheese grater and sprinkled them on top (I use a Salad Shooter so this took less than a minute and a half to shave all of it).

I have posted a picture of this. I do not typically make 'pretty' food...usually just good tasting and baking is particularly difficult for me...following directions and all. This recipe was EASY to work with and was VERY tasty!!! I appreciate the use of the box mix approach because the ingredients are all pre-measured and there are plenty of other things I can make from scratch so this very pretty, very very tasty cake was also quite simple and straightforward with just a little patience and a couple hours of my morning. Thank you!

Perfect white cake!  I baked this cake for my son's 7th birthday and it tasted delicious and moist.  I made (3) 8" circles and 24 cupcakes.   I made one circle cake chocolate by adding 1/2 c dark cocoa; melted 1 square unsweetened chocolate, and about 2 T milk to the white batter (just for that batter for the one 8" cake).  Make this the day before a party.  It will freeze if you must, but you will sacrifice a bit of the moistness.  It'll still be good, but not as good.  I made this on a Wednesday for a Sunday party.  Our samples of the cupcakes prior to freezing on Wednesday -- incredible.  After thawing, still good but not as incredible.  So...it's a "sure thing" recipe...everyone will love it.  Just try not to make it too far in advance if you can help it.  

This was fun....I stacked my 3 circle cakes -- white, chocolate, white.  It looked JUST like a hamburger!  I covered it in frosting for my son's birthday, but I think I'll make a novelty cake for a Superbowl party by doing it again and not covering the outside in frosting, just have red (ketchup) frosting and yellow (mustard) frosting inbetween the layers and oozing out the sides.  The cake is great without frosting, so it won't be lacking!

reviews.review_text:
Thanks to Jill (and Chrissie) for your positive and adventurous attitude in letting Aunt Laura and I make your wedding cake. It was alot of fun!  And thanks to Donna M. for this great recipe --  it's very tasty, has a beautiful texture, and is easy to make -- far superior to the other recipes we tested.  For icing we used the "Extra Special Buttercream Icing" that Donna M recommended, and it was also very nice.  
Advice:  Make only 1/2 recipe ("20 servings") at a time -- a full recipe doesn't fit in a regular size mixing bowl!  1/2 recipe makes approx 8 cups batter.  (We made a 5-tier double-layer cake [2" deep pans with diameters 6", 8", 10", 12" and 14" --see pic] for which we multiplied the basic recipe x5 [to"200-250" servings] for the shopping list.)  Baking times vary by pan size/depth from approx 30 minutes to an hour.  Caution: Big cakes are very heavy! -- If you're going to make a big one, learn how to stack tiers with dowel rods.  Other advice:  Use the "bake-even strips" as Donna recommends -- it's amazing the difference they make.  And for larger diameter pans (12" and larger) get/use the core heating accessory.

This is now my "go to" recipe for cakes.  I have a culinary background, and just never liked the way true homemade cakes turned out.  The texture has just never been exactly how I liked it. I always make it with French Vanilla Duncan Hines cake mix, vanilla, and almond, but this time I'm using Princess Emulsion (sticking with the French Vanilla cake mix).  I am doing a 10, 8, 6 wedding cake.  One recipe makes two 10" layers, one 6" layer, and a jumbo cupcake (for taste testing, of course).  I use the batter measurements from the Wilton website, so a 10" layer is 6 cups of batter and the 6" layer is 2 1/4 cups, with a smidge leftover (for the cupcake).  I rarely separate the eggs to just use egg whites, so I put 6 whole eggs in the recipe. It makes it extra rich.  I know the yolks tend to alter the true white color, but with the French Vanilla cake mix, it's already slightly off white, so using whole eggs doesn't make a difference.

reviews.review_text: Decided to use this recipe for a father's day cake and I am so happy I did! Everyone loved it. The cake was dense enough to keep its shape, and still so moist and flavorful!! I also added chopped pistachios on the top of the cake and smeared cherry preserves between the layers. It was excellent!!! The recipe is huge. I used two 9" baking pans, set the oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit, baked both on the same rack for about 40 minutes. This worked for me and may not for everyone, best to keep on eye on the cakes yourself! My pans baked the cake faster than normal, darker pans. I used the rest of the batter to fill two more 9" baking pans. Once completely cooled, I stored those 2 in my fridge, wrapped in saran wrap and placed each inside a large zip bloc bag. About 5 days later, I used the leftover cakes to make cake pops! The cake was still so tasty and moist. Perfect recipe if I do say so myself.

items.name: Dutch Apple Pie
items.description: Make and share this Dutch Apple Pie recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Fit pie crust into pie plate.
In a large bowl, mix sliced apples, lemon juice, both sugars,flour, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Pile into crust.
Prepare topping:
In a medium bowl, with a pastry blender or a fork, mix flour, both sugars, and butter until coarsely crumbled.
Sprinkle evenly over apples.
Bake at 375°F for 50 minutes.

reviews.review_text: This recipe is great. My husband absolutely loved it! I used the instructions almost to the letter and it came out perfect. I had NO soggy bottom or excess liquid. TIPS: 1) I used a frozen Marie Callendar's pie crust for convenience. No need to defrost. Just use right from the freezer and load it up. Also, I baked the pie on the BOTTOM RACK in the oven and NOT with convection. Just regular bake. This helps the bottom crust cook better, as the pie is closest to the heat element in your oven. It also avoids the top from browning too fast as it is farthest from the top heating element. I didn't need to tent my pie with foil at all the whole cooking time. The top crumb mixture still came out perfectly crispy and not burnt. 2) I used 5 apples: 3 Granny Smith, plus 1 Fuji, plus 1 Honey Crisp. This helps break up the tartness of the apples. I may add another apple in the future, as the mixture did shrink a little after cooking, but not a big deal. 3) I did not change the sugar amount and did not find it too sweet. 4) But, I did do what other reviewers suggested and after I sliced my apples, I combined them with the sugar mixture and let them sit for 15-20 minutes. I then carefully removed the apples from the bowl and discarded the excess liquid on the bottom of the bowl. 5) I cooked my pie for 10 extra minutes than suggested (60 minutes). My apples were not too crisp nor overcooked, just perfect.

reviews.review_text: This is a great starter recipe which is why I gave it 4 stars. And like any baker, I have since mastered my own way of baking the pie and have altered it to my tastes. I also like to experiment w/recipes as you can see. The changes I made are as follows:  6-7 cups of apples as I prefer deep dish pies, 1 Tsp of cinnamon if not more to taste, 1/2 Tsp of nutmeg or more to taste (The more spice the better in my opinion!) 3-4 Tbsp of flour depending upon how watery the apples are after mixing in the sugar (The amount of sugar used in the recipe was perfect for me!) Topping: (Came out less doughy this way and more crumbly.) 1 cup of brown sugar, 1 cup flour, and 1/3 cup of butter like the recipe calls for. For those of you interested in the easiest bottom crust ever, use this recipe by Mr. Food:  (Make the bottom crust right into a pie pan. It's pure genius!) 1-1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 Tbsp sugar, 1 Tsp salt, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, 2 Tbsp cold milk. Sift the flour, sugar, and salt into a 9-inch pie plate. Whisk the oil and milk separately and pour evenly over the mixture. (I made this w/pre-sifted flour to prevent sifting.) Using a fork, mix until completely dampened. Press the dough evenly over the bottom of the pan, then up the sides and over the rim. (I used my hands to press the dough once it was moist, then made slight indentations on the bottom of the pie plate w/a fork to ensure dough would cook evenly.) Next, pour the filling into the unbaked pie crust. Lastly, I changed the cooking time to 400 degrees to start for about 10-15 minutes to brown the top of the pie, then turned the oven down to 350 for another 60 minutes. (I prefer to bake pies longer b/c I don't like crunchy or firm apples.) In the past I have also covered the pie for the first 60 minutes baking it again at 350, uncovered it, then increased the oven temp to 400 for the last 10-15 minutes. (Works just as well!)

attributes.source_text: Came out less doughy this way and more crumbly.

reviews.review_text: I'll add another 5-star review for sure, this was awesome. I used 5 x Golden Delicious apples and that was just right for a 9-inch pie (I also pre-baked the crust for 15 mins and let it cool before adding the apples). Oh, and thanks to the other reviewers, I let the apples sit in the mixing bowl with the sugars and the flour and all that stuff for about 20 mins - and then removed them with a slotted spoon to put them into the pie shell, since there was a lot of liquid left in the bottom of the bowl, it's true. So, that meant it all held together well and wasn't wet/soggy at all - in fact, it cut into nice even slices, which made it easy to serve. I didn't adjust the sugar and i didn't think it was too sweet at all - but - I have a feeling it depends on the apples you use? (Mine were pretty tart) - so maybe taste one of the apples first, and then decide? I also added 1/2 tsp of cinnamon to the topping and baked it in a fan-assisted oven at 350 degrees (instead of 375) - but other than that I followed the recipe exactly and it was perfect, yum.

reviews.review_text:
Holy YUM! Perfect and amazing pie. I used all granny smith apples and doubled the recipe to make 2 pies  - one to cook "now" and one to freeze for later. Cooked the first one as written, from start to finish. for the "freezer" pie, I followed all directions up to baking - instead of baking, I wrapped the unbaked pie in 3-4 layers of plastic wrap, placed in a gallon-sized freezer bag, and froze for 2 weeks. When I was ready too cook the frozen unbaked pie: 
1) I baked the pie covered with tinfoil on 400 degrees for about 30 minutes. 2) After that, I removed the tinfoil and reduced the temp to 375 for another 30 minutes, 
3) then reduced the temp to 350 for another 30 minutes or so. 
Turned out wonderfully. I will ABSOLUTELY make this pie again. Served with ice cream = Heaven! (And, I'm not even a huge "fruit dessert person" - typically a chocolate gal).

Ok guys i need some help/advice!!!  I made this for thanksgiving and while the flavors are outstandingly delicious and i will definitely make it again i went wrong somewhere because it was super liquidy sopping wet inside when i cut into it!  I followed the recipe exactly with the exception of letting the apples (macintosh) soak in water while i peeled and cut them so they wouldnt turn brown and then let them sit with sugar on them for a while to help get some liquid out.  I got maybe 1/3 cup out!  I made the pie the night before, when i took it out of the oven it had bubbled over once right at the end of the baking time.  It seemed like the inside was nice and syrupy and delicious.  I put it on a cooling rack and let it sit on the counter for a while.  I noticed it looked like clearish liquid was starting to pool on top so after a few hours i put it in the fridge.  I then took it out and brought it over to my moms for thansgiving dinner.  At this point it still looked amazing, but when i would tip it slightly i could see there was watery liquid in there and when we cut into it it was like a bath tub in there ??  the flavor was still amazing...but what did i do wrong?? But this pie, OMG! You%u2019d think all that other stuff was awful compared to this pie. So far I%u2019ve made four of them in the last three weeks (Its apples season). Talk about people dropping everything the moment word spreads I%u2019ve brought pie. I%u2019ve been offered money to bake them for Christmas dinners. In case I wasn%u2019t clear, this pie is awesome!

Talk about easy, have no fear of being able to get great results, with very little effort.

Usually I like to make my own pastry and crusts but I was in a hurry the first time and just used a pillsbury refrigerated pie crust. They come two to a box and with eight apples you%u2019re all set to make two complete pies. People went so crazy over this with the store bought crust why make it more complicated and mess with perfection.

I mostly use Rome apples which hold up well, and the flavor develops when baked. The first time I made the exact recipe. While everyone went crazy I felt it was a little sweet for my taste, and in the subsequent pies I cut the granulated sugar for ? to ? cup in the pie and left the topping as is. I was happy with the result and everyone else agreed it was better with the sugar reduction, which lets more of the %u201Capple%u201D come through.
