reviews.review_text: Will definitely be using this recipe again!! I tweaked this a little based on reviews of it being too runny. I used granny smith apples. I sliced the apples into a bowl and then covered with the white sugar and let them sit for 30 minutes. At that point I drained the juice that had formed out of the bowl. I learned this trick last year and it is a life saver. Then i mixed the rest of the ingredients in the bowl. I did use a frozen pie crust but did not have issues like others have said. I think the draining really helps. The pie is very slightly tart but not at all too tart. We had a party last night and everyone loved it! Also we did not have nutmeg so I just did a tablespoon of cinnamon.

attributes.source_text: The pie is very slightly tart but not at all too tart
We had a party last night

reviews.review_text: WOW...WHAT A PIE!  After reviewing over 30 Apple pie recipes this one caught my eye.  The results were fantastic! I had never made apple pie before from scratch...so it was very pleasing to find a recipe that was both simple and delicious...it is so simple in fact you shoud call it "No Fuss Dutch Apple Pie."  My family enjoyed it so much they asked me to bake another one the same day.  I used Granny Smith apples and reduced the nutmeg to 1/8 tsp. the second time around....this was more to our particular taste. No more store bought....this pie will be out favorite thanksgiving dessert from now on.  Thank you so much for sharing this incredible recipe!

attributes.source_text: My family enjoyed it so much

reviews.review_text: My bff made this pie for her family and told me how great it was so I had to try it. I now see why her kids love this pie so much. This is the first apple pie I made from scratch and it was incredible. I made it exactly as written except I reduced the granulated sugar to 1/4 cup as recommended by others. I had to make the topping twice because the first time I blended it too much with a fork (because I didn't have a pastry blender) and the crumbs turned into dough but it was fun doing it all over again. Right before I put it in the oven I sprinkled some cinnamon on top. My family couldn't believe I made it. My apple pie is this years new addition to the Thanksgiving table. Thanks for sharing.

This was by far the best apple pie I've made!  I've never had any luck in the past with them; either the crust didn't cook or the apples were too crispy or the whole pie was just too "watery".  This one came out perfect.  And for my husband to tell me that then it must be!  He's not one to mix words when I ask his opinion on dishes!!  I will definitely recommend this to all my friends and family.  The only changes I made to this recipe was that I used 5 large apples (which was actually around 6-7 cups) and I used 1 teaspoon Cinnamon and 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg.  Other than that everything was the same.  Great recipe and well worth the time to make!!

attributes.source_text: for my husband to tell me that then it must be

reviews.review_text:
Been married 42-1/2 years and have made MANY apple pies. My husband said this is his all-time favorite. I served it to guests here from China who attended their daughter's wedding in my best friend's backyard. They told us that this recipe could truly be served in a 5-star hotel in China! They were amazed and couldn't stop telling us how wonderful it was. They had never tasted anything like it! It's truly a KEEPER and I will now only make this version. No changes were made to the recipe. It's outstandingly easy to prepare. I used thinly sliced Granny Smith apples so that they would "cook down" and not be crunchy.
!

attributes.source_text: My husband said this is his all-time favorite
I served it to guests here from China

reviews.review_text: Great recipe! I made a few tweaks for my own taste and I really liked the results. I blind baked the crust for 20 minutes at 325 F. I also briefly cooked the apple mixture in a pot to form a loose caramel. I only cooked the pie for about 40 minutes because of this precooking. I nearly doubled the cinnamon and added a little fresh orange juice (cinnamon is very dry, so I needed a bit more liquid), some extra lemon juice, a bit of vanilla extract, a splash of whiskey, and some ground cardamom. Like I said, these changes were about personal taste, so the only real issue I have with this recipe is that the apple:crust recipe is too low.

items.label: Edna's Apple Crumble (Aka. Apple Crisp)
items.name: Edna's Apple Crumble (Aka. Apple Crisp)
items.description: A simple and easy to make but oh so yummy recipe. Known as Apple crumble in the UK and Apple Crisp in the US
instructions: Put apples in an 8 or 9 inch square baking dish.
Combine the rest of the ingredients in a separate bowl and mix.
Spread crumble mixture over apples and bake for 35 minutes in a 375ºF degree oven.
For an added treat top off with a little English custard.

reviews.review_text: I was seeking something similar to a recipe I once found in a cookbook at my mom's place. This was it, precisely how I remembered it. I used Becel non-hydrogenated half-fat margarine, though I used to use butter; I've noticed no difference. Placing the margarine in the microwave for about 6 or 7 seconds seemed to make it the best consistency for mixing. Any more and it doesn't seem to bake right, but any less, and the mixing is slightly more difficult. I find that a deeper pan that's less wide works best if you like apples; they will still soften beneath. Unlike most reviewers, I prefer the apple part, untainted, with the crisp for an additional flavor. The only thing I altered is that I didn't use nutmeg - none in the house and again - I used to and I haven't noticed a difference... and I imagine I added more cinnamon, as I don't measure it. I think next time I might throw some flax seeds into the topping mix or add some berries with the apples.

attributes.source_text: they will still soften beneath

reviews.review_text: Made this exactly as  posted including the English custard on top, very good - this is the first time I've ever "made" a crumble but not the first I've ever "eaten" one and with all the apples from the orchard decided it was time to make my own.  This was so good with the flavor of the tart apples and the crunchy topping, YUM; the only thing I had a problem with and I'm pretty sure it was me - is that parts of the topping was still dry, thinking I should have added more butter to it or something.  But the flavors, oh my!!  Used recipe#483829 for the cream which was a new experience (in a good way) for me - thinking it'd also be so good with a scoop of vanilla ice cream

attributes.source_text: the flavor of the tart apples
the crunchy topping

reviews.review_text:
I loved this recipe. It was so simple yet so delicious. My apples were gigantic Grannies.  I increased flour and oatmeal (used whole wheat flour) by 50%. I did not increase the butter however. My butter was hard so I just chopped it into the oatmeal, much as though making a pie crust. I more than doubled the cinnamon, sprinkling some on the apples themselves. If you don't have Granny apples and you like their tartness, sprinkle a little lemon juice on your apples. (That's what my Mom always did.) 
I loved this. It brought back memories of watching my Mom prepare this and eating the long stripes of apple peel, (a real treat in those days!)
 Bought the ripple ice cream as suggested by someone. Goes perfectly with this although it would even be good plain. A real keeper!

WOW!  Made this for a co-worker's birthday & it was gone before I had a chance to have any (luckily though, I snuck a small bite from the edge when it came out of the oven ... I had to make sure the apples were done!)  When I went to measure the ingredients, I found that I only had dark brown sugar -- which worked out fine.  Baked this in a deep dish stoneware pie plate and it came out perfectly.  The only addition I made was to melt another 3T of butter & stirred in about 1/4 tsp vanilla & drizzled it over the top when it came out of the oven.  Next time I may add some nuts under the topping (so they don't burn).  Thanks for posting!  -M =)

attributes.source_text: Made this for a co-worker's birthday
Made this for a co-worker's birthday & it was gone before I had a chance to have any

reviews.review_text: This was absolutely FANTASTIC! I didn't have granny smith apples on hand but I did have 3 large Heraldson apples so I just used those and, to my surprise, I think I liked the heraldson better! (I had previously only used Heraldson's for other baking, not in a crisp)I cut the Nutmeg down to 1/2 Tsp. (which turned out to be just right for us) because I thought 3/4 would be too overpowering, baked it at 350' for 30 minutes. Served it hot from the oven with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. My mouth watered the whole time it was baking and my house smelled so wounderful. It was PERFECT! This took no time at all to throw together. This was exactly what I was looking for, Thank You!

Delicious except that mine crust was too brown after 35 minutes. To salvage the apple crisp, I scraped off a part of the crumb topping (fortunately I had doubled the crumb topping after reading other reviews). The lower layer was ok. I know that it would have been perfect had I taken it out of the oven at 25 minutes as the house smelled perfect at that time. I shall definitely make it again and wont be distracted with doing other stuff around the house as i was this time. 6 granny smiths were perfect - I like that your recipe doesnt call for sugar on the apples like other apple crumble recipes. I find that too sweet. I will review again after I next make this. Thanks 1Steve

attributes.source_text: I like that your recipe doesnt call for sugar on the apples

reviews.review_text: Yummy!  I did tweak it a little which is why I gave it a four instead of a five.  First I knew we'd need a bigger batch since my family and I are gluttons so I doubled the apple portion so it would fill a 9x13 size pan.  I also tossed the apples in a little vanilla and white sugar.  We love the apple crisp topping so I tripled that.  I added a couple dashes of salt to the topping and ended up adding two sticks of butter.  It came out picture perfect.  It tasted just like I wanted it too and my family loved it.  Vanilla ice cream on top is a must of course ;)

attributes.source_text: my family loved it

reviews.review_text: I used Penzey's extra fancy Vietnamese cassia cinnamon because it is more flavorful than the grocery kind. Also, I used half the amount of nutmeg, a pinch of salt, fresh lemon juice and zest. Lastly, I always add vanilla flavoring to my desserts even when it's not called for in a recipe because it enhances flaovr just like salt does to desserts. I learned that in culinary school and it does make a difference. I would suggest using Granny Smith apples for this recipe or a mix of them with another apple. You can also use peaches in place of the apples. I have also used frozen apples which worked out very well. When I am doubling, tripling and even quadruling this, I do use the frozen to save time.

I doubled up on the recipe since I was making a smaller one for my in-laws using a smaller dish.  Next time I will triple since we like the crumble on top.  I will add more oats and as other reviewers mentioned more cinnamon!! I ate this on coffee ice cream but really liked it by itself a couple of days later.  Yes it lasted a couple of days because I'm watching my weight.  The kids loved it too. Got a call from my in-laws and they both loved it and said next time I make it again, they'll take another plate. LOL TY 1Steve it's a keeper.

attributes.source_text: The kids loved it too
Got a call from my in-laws and they both loved it

reviews.review_text: This was really delicious, and simple to make! This was my first time maing Apple Crips, and I was worried the topping would be soggy (which I can not stand), but it was perfect. It was even tasty second day, after a night in the fridge - I just warmed it up in the oven. I did not have nutmeg, so I used a little more cinnamon, and did not make any other changes. Also, I baked it for about 45-50 min or even more (wanted topping to get real crisp). It was very good, but apples fell apart, it was almost like an apple sauce on the bottom (still delicious). Next time I will try to only bake for 35 min as suggested in the recipe.  Thank you for the great recipe!

attributes.source_text: wanted topping to get real crisp

reviews.review_text: Sorry, this just didn't work for me. I used 4 apples instead of 3, but the crumb topping I made as written. It wasn't crumb like in the mixing bowel, but I decided to just roll with it...which was my mistake.  At the 30 minute mark I checked on it and there was no crumb mix on top to speak of. It looked just like sugar and flour dumped on top. I added small cold chunks of butter on top and cooked another 10 min which really helped. As written though, the crumb topping is no good. Sorry...I really wanted this to be amazing

Review with minor tweaks... This is absolutely delicious!! I made the topping as written and it turns out a lovely dark golden brown and has a dense and crunchy texture- yum! For the apple filling, I sprinkled about 1 1/2 Tbl flour, 1/2 tsp each nutmeg and cinnamon and a dash or 2 of salt and tossed it all together. I added the flour to thicken the juices a little. I think the additional spices boosted the flavor over the top. This is so good that my husband asked for it twice this week. Thanks for sharing this :)

attributes.source_text: has a dense and crunchy texture

reviews.review_text: As a tried-and-true New Englander (literally family in every New England State lol) Apple Crisp cravings are genetic and normally induced by beautiful Fall weather. All that aside this recipe is simply amazing. I used fresh picked organic Rome apples which are amazing in Connecticut this year. I contemplated cutting down the sugar, but I left it in the end. Thank God! The crumb mixture bled into the crevices the cored apples created which was amazing. My fiancÃ© and I had it for desert and then thought it was prudent to have it for breakfast as well. I know this was long winded, but seriously, thank you for the recipe it made my taste buds tingle and brought back awesome childhood memories.

reviews.review_text: This is a fun recipe. Next time I will  cut out the nutmeg, its overpowering even in small doses ( I barely added just a dash). It would have been much better with just cinnamon. Also, I used 3 green apples and one really sweet red apple. When I got bites of the red apple I could really taste the sweetness, and it was delightful. Thanks for a great recipe! I was skeptical about the "crumble" before baking it, but it really melted down and was the perfect topping. Many Thanks!!

attributes.source_text: I could really taste the sweetness, and it was delightful

reviews.review_text: Wow wow wow!!!  I also doubled this recipe and put it in a 9x13pan.  At first it seemed like too much "crisp" but in the end it was great.  I did have to grate some frozen butter on top of the whole dish midway through cooking though because the crumble was dry and the butter did not distribute evenly.  I sprinkled some cinnamon on top of the apples before putting the crisp on as well.  I thought it was really good warm out of the oven, but it was ten times better cold out of the fridge the next day.  Delicious and easy.

I have made this twice and the topping is excellent, however..Next time I make this I think I will add a bit of sugar and cinnamon with the apples, I felt the apples lacked something.  I used spy apples the first time and the suggested granny smith apples this time.  Some nuts in the topping would be good too..but I reitterate the topping is excellent as is and there is plenty, no need to increase amount of topping as I have with other recipes.  Good with vanilla ice cream! Enjoy!

items.label: Awesome Baked Ham
items.name: Awesome Baked Ham
items.description: I love this recipe because it is so easy and it calls for hardly any ingredients, and I always have these ingredients in my pantry. This recipe came from a good friend's mother, who was always asked to bake the ham for get-togethers and family dinners. Now I get those requests. People who ordinarily aren't too fond of ham rave over this one. After I carve, I spoon a little of the glaze over the meat in the platter - yummmm!
instructions: In a medium size mixing bowl, mix yellow mustard and brown sugar until you have a thick\
Take all wrappers off of ham and trim away excess fat.
Line baking pan (I spray with Pam in case some of the brown sugar mixture escapes, clean up is easier) with Aluminum foil.
Place ham on foil and spread brown sugar/mustard paste on top.
Fold and seal foil.
Do not open again until ham is done.
Bake at 350° for 4 hours.
Let set for about 1 hr then carve.
One of the best tasting hams you will ever have!

reviews.review_text: I'm going to risk sounding like an idiot. I bought a pre-cooked ham (without a bone) prior to finding this recipe. Looking at the cooking time I didn't think my ham would really work so I took it back. The grocery store didn't sell "raw" hams which is what I thought I was looking for. (I don't cook a lot of ham.) The butcher suggested a pre-cooked spiral sliced bone-in ham. It did have a longer cooking time on its directions although it was only about 2 hours (it was half a ham...not 15 pounds). I cooked it for 2-3 hours at 325 (ham directions said 300 and this recipe said 350 so I compromised). It was still cold in the middle. I bumped it back up to 350 for about another hour and that was better. The end result was fabulous. So, for anyone who really hasn't dealt much with hams... I'm guessing the pre-cooked, no bone ham would have been fine with a shorter cooking time. The spiral sliced bone-in ham was fantastic as I spread each slice with the sauce before going in the oven. Anyway, I will do this recipe again. The ham/sauce is wonderful. Thank you!

One thing I would suggest when preparing this is to allow a few more minutes prep time to coat the ham in the paste.  I found it to be a little annoying because it would not stick to the meat.  I ended up smearing most of it around the sides on the top hoping it would 'melt' down to the bare spots.  Thankfully it worked, but did take longer than I thought it would.  I was on a pretty strict schedule for preparing/cooking everything because my guests wanted the food ready when they got there (good thing I prepared the paste the night before).  I just took it out after 3.5 hours (12 lb ham) and will let it sit for about 40 minutes because I don't have enough time for it to sit for an hour.  I wrapped it in foil but there were still juices but no big deal.  This is the very first Ham I have ever made (first Holiday meal as well) and I was so worried I would botch it much like the turkey fiasco in National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation.  I stole a quick piece to test it and was very pleasantly surprised!  I prefer ham to turkey and this was by far the best ham I have EVER had!  Very moist and just a hint of sweetness.  I have a HUGE family (grandma had 15 kids) and for over 20 years I thought her ham was the best.  Sorry Grams...this one might be better!

reviews.review_text: We really enjoyed this recipe!  I was worried since I have some non-mustard lovers in the house but after the brown sugar gets mixed with it, the mustard is less predominant.  Add to that the released ham juices while it cooks and it just morphs into a wonderfully deliciously flavored sauce and steam that infuses nicely into the ham.  It was not dry and really was loved by everyone in my home.  The foil method was nice.  I took 4 long sheets of foil, crimping two together longways.  I then laid the double width food sections in a cross fashion in my baking pan.  I put a little sauce down in the center, added the ham, poured on the remaining sauce and then sealed up the first set up foil and then the second.  My pan came out sparkling clean, not a drop escaped.  Thanks for a great recipe Boopster!  I look forward to making it again.

attributes.source_text: the mustard is less predominant
It was not dry

reviews.review_text: OMG!!!  Until I tried this recipe, I wasn't wild about baked ham.  Besides pizza, it would probably be one of the last things I'd really ever have a craving for.  However, hams were on sale, and I remember my mom used to bake a ham, then use the remaining bone to put in a pot of red beans, which being from Louisiana, red beans and rice is a traditional weekly meal, and one of my favorites.  I had a 9 lb. half ham, so I adjusted the recipe accordingly.  The only addition I made was to put some ground cloves into the brown sugar/mustard paste, then right before it was done, I opened the foil, decorated it with pineapple and cherries, and returned it to the oven, uncovered, and under the broiler for about 5 minutes more, to try to caramelize it a little.  Boopster, I will NEVER bake a ham any other way from now on!  Because of your recipe, I love baked ham!!  It was so moist and juicy, and just deeeeeeeeeelicious!  Thank you very much for sharing! :)

attributes.source_text: It was so moist and juicy
It was so moist and juicy

reviews.review_text: i just made this for christmas dinner, and it was a hit!  i halved the recipe and added a dash or two of ground cloves.  i only ended up using about 2/3rds of the glaze, and saved the rest to use as a sauce after i added about a 1/2 tbs of extra mustard (i used a combination of plain yellow and spicy brown) and about a 1/2 tbs of freshly squeezed orange juice.  i reheated in the microwave just before serving, and that nearly outshined the ham, itself!  mine, personally DID come about a tidge dry, but that was my fault on account of i l lost track of time. i aimed for two hours, but i believe it ended up baking for around two and a half.  i will definitely try this again, only next time i'll be sure to use all of the glaze and make extra for serving.  thank you so much for such an easy holiday dish!

reviews.review_text: I had my doubts about mixing mustard with brown sugar, but glad I decided to go for it. This recipe is definitely a keeper!! I used a fully-cooked 7.2 lb. ham and took others' advice to lower the temp to 325 F. I cut the recipe in half for my smaller-sized ham. I lined my pan with foil and then rubbed the thick paste all over the ham. I put the ham flat-side down on a second sheet of foil and then wrapped it up, crimping all the edges of the foil to avoid leakage. I then cooked it for 2 hours 20 minutes, then let it sit for an hour before serving. I happened to be in the kitchen near the ham when our son-in-law returned for seconds and he said, "I usually don't like ham, but this one is quite good!" Then, other family chimed in and said, "Yes, this is a really good ham!" My husband and son said it was the best they had ever had. I would have to agree. The ham was moist, tender and very delicious. I am definitely using this recipe to cook ham from now on!

reviews.review_text: As the recipe says "One of the best tasting hams you will ever have".  I used a semi-boneless 1/2 ham that weighed 9 lbs and made the paste with 1/2 lb brown sugar and 1/4 cup of yellow mustard.  It made a nice thick paste to coat it with.  I wrapped it in the foil using two sheets (one going in each way) in a foil roasting pan (no worry about clean-up).  I then placed the roasting pan on a flat pizza pan and cooked it at 350 degrees for 3 hours and let it sit for 1 hour.  It was so moist and tender, it just melted in your mouth.  I poured off the gravy and poured it into a gravy boat on the side after spooning a small amount over the meat on the platter.  I will probably never make ham any other way again.  We all just kept going back for "just one more piece".  Thanks Boopster for making my Christmas dinner a booming success.

attributes.source_text: It was so moist and tender

reviews.review_text: Awesome ham! Having promised ham for Saturday, almost panicked when planning my holiday shopping list this morning  -  having missed reviewing I  had to search for my copy of your Awesome Baked Ham. That is not going to happen again! Although with 202 reviews there is not much I can add that hasn't already been said. Review being added  right  now to assure the recipe is just a click away! Have used the mustard and brown sugar when baking ham over the years -  great having the recipe on paper. Health issues here have me cutting back on the brown sugar and it does work for me. Both the yellow and the honey dijon mustard made for great tasting ham. The foil (I double wrap) combined with the mustard/brown sugar makes this recipe outstanding - the combination results in juicy great tasting ham and makes slicing a snap! Plans are to serve with Dotty2's recipe#413380 which compliments this recipe so well. Thank you for sharing.

attributes.source_text: results in juicy great tasting ham

reviews.review_text: this was so extra good!  after trimming the fat, i scored the ham and applied the mustard first and the brown sugar second (instead of mixing into a paste).  i wrapped the ham twice in heavy duty aluminum foil after reading some of the reviews about the juices leaking out.  two hours into cooking i removed the outer layer of foil, as the internal temp wasn't where i thought it should be.  i opened the foil a bit to expose the ham for browning.  this was a 7-1/2 pound ham, and i only had to leave the ham in the oven for about three hours before the temp reached 160-170 degrees.  this was by far the easiest ham i've ever made, and the juice is amazing.  thanks so much for this recipe - i loved it!!

Boy, how I hate to give this another 5 stars, haha!  I am pretty new at cooking and this was my very first ham.  I was a little scared because it wasn't my mothers traditional pineapple juice marinade, but I tried it anyway.  I swear, they should make a candle that smells like this ham slow baking in the oven!  It is wonderful.  I made a 7 lb. ham for our family just to piece on throughout the week...and I am on my second plate right now.  I may have overcooked mine a little, but that was just a first-timers mistake!  LOVE IT!!!!!  Oh, the only change I made...
I basted every 15 minutes and 10 before taking it out of the oven I used about 1/4 cup brown sugar and crumbled it over the top.  I put it back in the oven uncovered to get that burnt sugar taste...
AMAZING!

reviews.review_text:
This is an OLD recipe that my grandmother and mother used to prepare their hams for baking. And of course it's the only way I've ever fixed my baked hams. The combination of brown sugar and mustard will make a wonderful glaze without being overly sweet. Unless I'm baking a spiral cut ham, I always score the top of the ham (only about 1/4 inch deep and about an inch apart) to hold the glaze in place while the ham is baking. My mother use to poke a whole clove in each cross cut but I'm not a big clove fan and you certainly don't want to forget to remove all of them and accidently bite into a clove....Uggg!! Although I have always baked the ham in foil, I'm sure a Reynolds self basting bag would shorten the baking time and allow for even more moistness.
Anyway, I was happy to see my grandmothers baked ham recipe on this site and would highly recommend it to anyone who wants a flavorable, moist baked ham for any occaision..

attributes.source_text: without being overly sweet
a flavorable, moist baked ham

reviews.review_text: Okay. So I am a vegetarian, and cooked dinner on Christmas for 15 carnivores. I chose this recipe because of the ease (hard for me to tweak meat recipes since I don't taste them!), timing (stuck it in the oven at my house, left it to cook and went to my mother's house to cook everything else in her oven, ran back to my house to change into party clothes, pick up the ham and go back to mom's, and when everything else was ready, opened the foil and cut the ham. As per ALL of the carnivores, it was amazing, moist and PERFECT. the only caveat: if you think this will feed 25 people you are crazy, as the amount of people going for seconds (& 3rds) may surprise you. I know this is probably a strange review, but as a non-meat eater, cooking meat can be a dicey prospect and this joins a very short list of recipes that I can make and KNOW people will love it.

reviews.review_text: I'll add another 5-star review along with the hundreds of others. I had a 14 lb bone-in pre-cooked ham that I wanted to come out moist and tasty. I can not tolerate sweet, sweet glazes and this one looked promising. I used about 1 cup of brown sugar, the listed amount of yellow mustard and then I threw in about 2 tsp (approximate, I didn't measure) of horseradish (regular, not hot) and several dashes of worcestershire sauce as I wanted to lean away from super sweet. I baked it as directed but only went 3 hours and let sit for about 20 minutes. It smelled great baking. I put down 2 layers of foil in the bottom of the pan in case it leaked (it didn't). The ham tasted PERFECT and was super MOIST! I will use this recipe to bake ALL my future hams. Like the title says "AWESOME"!

reviews.review_text: This is by far the best and easiest baked ham recipe I have ever tried!  The hardest part for me was to not peak as the smell in my house was incredible.  My DH, who is not a ham lover, enjoyed it immensely and asked for ham sandwiches the next day for lunch!  I halved the brown sugar but used the 1/2 c mustard and althought the paste was a bit thinner it was easier to put on the ham.  My ham was about 8 lbs and I still cooked it for the full four hours and let it sit for an hour before carving.  I served it with scalloped potatoes and a green salad.  I will never make ham any other way again!!  Thanks for a great recipe!!

reviews.review_text: 5 stars plus about 20 more for us. I have never made a ham like this, bone-in, not precut and not ready to serve. items.label: Pumpkin Spice Bread
items.name: Pumpkin Spice Bread
items.description: Hooray for fall! We love this pumpkin bread recipe--especially when the slices are slathered with a generous spread of cream cheese. Makes two loaves, so freeze the other one, or heck--eat it. This bread goes fast.
instructions: Heat oven to 350.
in a large mixing bowl, combine pumpkin, sugar, water, vegetable oil and eggs.
Beat until well mixed.
Measure the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, salt, baking powder, nutmeg and cloves into a separate bowl and stir until combined.
Slowly add the dry ingredients to the pumpkin mixture, beating until smooth.
Grease two 9 x 5 inch loaf pans and dust with flour.
Evenly divide the batter between the two pans.
Bake for 60-70 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool for 10-15 minutes, then remove from pans by inverting onto a rack and tapping the bottoms.
Slice and serve plain, buttered, or with cream cheese.
Note: Cream cheese is the ONLY thing to put on this bread because--it is so so so yummy!

reviews.review_text: Wow.  I made this for tonight's dessert, and I have a feeling I'm going to end up eating half of it before then.  It's probably a good thing that I only made half the recipe, or I'd have a major tummy ache on my hands.  Great spread with cream cheese, and probably would be nice with PB too.  Changes I made: for starters, I used pumpkin that I had harvested in the fall and frozen, which is about as close as you can get to fresh pumpkin in June.  As some other people suggested, I used less sugar.  Since half a recipe calls for 1 1/2 c, I used 1/2 c white sugar and 1/2 c brown sugar (which I highly recommend).  Instead of 1/2 c vegetable oil, I used 1/4 c veg oil and 1/4 c unsweetened applesauce.  And as some else also suggested, I used unsweetened cider instead of water.  I also threw in 1/2 t ginger and a splash of vanilla extract.  I bet this would be great to serve at an autumn dinner party, along with chili and a nice salad, and maybe some roasted autumn veggies.

attributes.source_text: I made this for tonight's dessert

reviews.review_text: Very good. I doubled the recipe, since I had lots of pumpkin to use. I used fresh (cooked) pumpkin, and since it is moister than canned, I used more pumpkin and less water, and that worked well. We don't like waiting for loaves to cook for breakfast, so I made 2 dozen mini-muffins (took about 20 min to bake), then 6 mega-muffins, then 2 loaves, then another 2 dozen mini-muffins. Now my freezer is ready for company!--Update: I had to upgrade this recipe to 5 stars after tasting it NOT fresh from the oven. Give it half a day, or more, and you will be in love. I ate these as muffins right after my daughter was born (at home!), and they were sheer heaven, especially with chocolate chips and pecans. My freezer is now well-stocked again. This last time I was short on pumpkin so used homemade applesauce to get my 4 cups puree.

reviews.review_text:
I have made this recipe probably 50 times since I came across it.... and I just LOVE IT. In fact, everyone loves it. The only thing I do differently-- to make it "my own"-- is that I add slightly more of each spice to make it more "spicy" and add a bit of ginger-- seriously, the ginger gives it the perfect kick that it needs. I also like to serve it with Pumpkin Spice Cream Cheese Spread (
Recipe #328442).

One more note-- I have doubled, tripled, even quadrupled this recipe with no problems!

A couple updates on my review: I continue to make this recipe every year at Halloween, Thanksgiving and Christmas and I get requests from EVERYONE. I have to make about 40 loaves at one time. That all said-- I recently was totally not paying attention and added only HALF the called-for liquids and the bread still came out great-- a bit dry, but still totally edible.

To make this into Chocolate Pumpkin Spice Bread (which is really good): add 5 tbsp cocoa, 1/4 cup extra sugar and 1/2 cup chocolate chips (optionally).

To make it more nutritious, I reduced the oil by 1/4 c, replaced 1 c all-purpose with white whole wheat flour, used 1/2 c egg beaters for 2 of the eggs, and reduced the sugar by 1/2 c.  It was still sweet, soft, and delicious, and I'm about to get another slice right now (before my son demolishes it all).  Previous review on Mar 25, 2006:  Terrific pumpkin bread! My 9-year-old son said it's the "best bread ever". I've made this twice now. This time I had only about 2 cups of granulated sugar, so I used about a cup of light brown sugar and it worked just fine. Couldn't find my bottle of ground cloves so I used ground allspice instead. Tasty bread, great texture, and the cook time was right on at 60 minutes in nonstick aluminum loaf pans.

items.label: Szechuan Noodles With Spicy Beef Sauce
items.name: Szechuan Noodles With Spicy Beef Sauce
items.description: Tired of using ground beef the same old way? Try this spicy dish! Feel free to double the sauce if you like it really saucy! Update: the hoisin sauce is quite sweet, so you might start off with just a little and work your way up!
instructions: Brown ground beef in a large skillet, stirring until it crumbles; drain and keep warm.
Pour sesame oil in pan and heat till hot. Saute onion and next 4 ingredients  hot sesame oil until tender.
Combine cornstarch and beef broth, whisking until smooth.
Stir broth mixture, hoisin sauce, and soy sauce into onion mixture.
Bring to a boil, stirring constantly; boil, stirring constantly, 1 minute.
Stir in ground beef.
Toss with hot cooked pasta, and sprinkle with sliced green onions.
Yield: 4 servings.

reviews.review_text: Great base!  I have never made a dish such as this one with ground beef.  I used 92% lean beef, so I did everything in one pan (I'm big on dumping in ingredients & using few dishes).<br/><br/>Some people complain about changing recipes, but I love to--based on my tastes & what I have on hand.  I really liked this recipe & read through reviews to see what others had added.<br/><br/>Mine tasted great--in addition to the onions, garlic, ginger, Hoisin sauce, sesame oil, soy sauce & beef broth, I added chopped carrots and celery (done in the food processor), some toasted slivered almonds, a can of julienned bamboo shoots, some fish sauce, and some Mae Ploy sweet chili sauce (I left out the red pepper flakes this time to be kind to my stomach).  I served it over boiled rice noodles.  This combo no doubt crossed a bunch of time zones, but I treated it as I would fried rice or jambalaya--used what I happen to have.<br/><br/>Thanks so much to the poster!

We ABSOLUTELY LOVED IT! It was such a different thing to do with hamburger. And it was simple and quick. I would totally do it with a sliced beef, such as flank, or round steak. I didn't have any fresh ginger, and could not find it in the grocery store, so I used the ground ginger I have. I used alot more garlic, like 2 tablespoons, cause we love garlic (well, I do, because Husband said "I know you put more garlic then required!"), I used minced garlic from the jar. I also used about 2 tablespoons of dry crushed red pepper flakes, because we like heat.. Instead of vermicelli pasta, I used whole wheat spaghetti. I cooked my onion, garlic and red pepper flakes with my hamburger. Lastly, as others mentioned, the directions did not say where to add the sesame oil? So I added it after I tossed everything into the hamburger, and added the pasta last. This was a quick no hassle meal. The kind I like to do on a Saturday  if we do not order out. Thank you for sharing!

reviews.review_text: My husband really liked this, and I thought it was pretty nice as well. I ended up using the full amount of hoison sauce despite being apprehensive about the sweetness (because my husband can't stand sweet taste + meat... but this was fine) - the crushed red pepper is crucial to balance it. After sauteeing the onions etc in step 2, I added in about a third of a cabbage (maybe 2 cups shredded) and about a cup of sliced white button mushrooms. And sauteed both of those with the onion mix until soft and "wilted". Then I proceeded with the recipe, adding the broth etc. I loved the extra veggies for crunch, nutrition, and stretching the meal... they also weren't visible so picky eaters probably wouldn't notice. I'll probably add more mushrooms next time, and maybe thinly sliced carrots. broccoli might work too. thanks for a versatile, easy meal!

I came across this recipe while searching for a simple weeknight ground beef meal. The idea sounded interesting but a little bland, so I gave it my own twist.

I used coconut oil rather than sesame oil to saute the onion, garlic and ginger, and used chili-garlic sauce in place of the dried red pepper. I halved the amount of hoisin sauce and made up the difference with oyster sauce. I used a bag of fresh Asian stir-fry veggies, nuked for 3 minutes and then added to the skillet with the ground beef in step 6.

Served it all over cellophane noodles. 

This was an excellent dinner that my family enjoyed and, with the addition of the colorful vegetables, it looked great on the plate. I give the original recipe four stars because I feel like it is a fantastic foundation recipe, just waiting to be built upon.

reviews.review_text:
Very torn about this review. When I review a recipe, I usually divide it in half and make it the original post and then add my changes. So here is the review.

First, I really didn't like the texture of the ground beef. I asked my butcher to take a round steak and rough grind it. It gave me a more steak like texture and that made a huge difference for me in the overall taste.

Second, I didn't find too much red pepper, it was fine for me.

Third, I did add broccoli because it was just to one dimensional for me, it need some texture and different flavors. I did use fresh broccoli and some fine match stick sliced carrots, just for a little crunch. I think that helped.

Overall the flavor was good, I used a good szechuan noodle but the sauce was not bad.

As one poster mentioned, it reminded them of an Asian Sloppy Joe over noodles. I agree in a way. That is why I think the carrots and broccoli and the meat texture really changed the texture, but not necessarily the flavor. I purchased my ground sirloin right at the regular grocery store. I just asked the butcher to rough grind it for me, or you can do it yourself at home. I think it really helped the overall recipe.

I will try it again with a few changes. 3 stars for the texture and presentation; but 4 for the overall flavor
Thx, Kim

I added half a can of chopped water chestnuts and some frozen peas. You could add so many different veggies and it be wonderful! GREAT recipe!! Thanks for posting!

reviews.review_text: This was so good! Normally, nothing is spicy for me, but this was! (A good thing!) I used 1 teaspoon crushed red pepper, and substituted the fresh ginger with a proportional amount of ground ginger (dried). I think that I had a cup's worth of beef broth (1/4 cup more didn't make a difference). I was bummed that I couldn't find hoisin sauce anywhere, but was happy to find that others used oyster sauce (I used a little less than 1/3 cup). Also, I used about 1 teaspoon of sesame oil. Ooh I just loved the results! I can't wait to get my hands on some hoisin sauce and see how that tastes! This dish was super easy to prepare, and was done in no time at all. Thanks for posting! I will be making this again and again!

attributes.source_text: Normally, nothing is spicy for me, but this was! (A good thing!)

reviews.review_text: Sharon, this is just the best!  I made this two nights ago for DH and me and we both enjoyed it immensely!  The sauce was wonderful, tho I may double it next time...and there will very soon be a next time, for sure!  I didn't have vermicelli so I used linguini, but everything else I did as instructed.  The pasta didn't make any difference in the taste at all.  My son is a vegan and DIL a vegetarian, so I will sub the beef for TVP crumbles and soak them in veggie broth, but follow your recipe exactly with only these two exceptions.  It can't be anything but a 5 star aas well, even with those changes, I am sure.  Now I am looking forward to their visit so that I can make the veggie version of your recipe!  Thank you so much for the wonderful recipe.

attributes.source_text: I made this two nights ago for DH and me and we both enjoyed it immensely

reviews.review_text: Cheap to make and Oh so good and flabourable.  I did serve over rice once I found out I didn't have the vermicelli noodles in the pantry - but the DH was disappointed there wasn't left overs as he felt the mince with the rice would be great in toasties and he wants to try it with the noodles and the big one was it had a spicy bite which even the DM devoured.  After making though and the reason ours may have been so spicy was that I used dried crushed chillies [1 teaspoon] (home grown and I know they are hot) but that is also what we usually buy here in Australia (my awareness now is that crushed red peppers are dried red capsicum/bell peppers) but would recommend the chillie option if you like spice and hot.  Thank you Sharon123 for a great recipe, made for Potluck Tag.

attributes.source_text: it had a spicy bite
he felt the mince with the rice would be great in toasties
which even the DM devoured
made for Potluck Tag

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe as is. I have not cooked with hoisin sauce before so I was a tad skeptical. Before I added the beef & noodles I made my husband taste the sauce. If it was not good I was going to make something else and I did not want to waste noodles & beef. He said it was awesome and kept tasting it. I was shocked because I did not think it would be as good as it was! If you want something new... OMG!! TRY THIS RECIPE! That hoisin sauce is going to become my new dipping sauce. Now I need to find spicy sesame oil and try it with oyster sauce as recommended by other reviews. My picky eater husband commented that he wants this in our rotation!! Thanks for the great recipe!

attributes.source_text: He said it was awesome and kept tasting it
My picky eater husband commented that he wants this in our rotation

reviews.review_text: Delicious! This recipe is perfect for busy weeknight chefs or chefs on a budget! It is quick to put together and is really delicious. It is one of those recipes that  further your meat without sacrifice to the flavor - nor does it leave you feeling that it is a budget meal. This will be made again and again in our household. The Asian spices and condiments are a wonderful addition to the ground meat and noodles... who would have thought?! I did not have cornstarch so I subbed a Tablespoon of flour and this worked well and did not interfere with the taste of the recipe. The heat was perfect for us at 1 1/2 teaspoons. BTW, I had to make this recipe after seeing peacefulnightdove's photo! Thank you so much Sharon.

attributes.source_text: perfect for busy weeknight chefs
The Asian spices and condiments are a wonderful addition
The heat was perfect for us at 1 1/2 teaspoons

reviews.review_text:
Really great recipe. I made a few change but not to overall ingredients. I doubled the sauce as others suggested but used 1 lb of meat. I browned the meat, onions, garlic and ginger together and added mushrooms and green pepper after some browning. Steamed some broccoli and carrots and added them in right at the end.
After cooking, I tasted and realized I had forgotten the crushed red pepper ( a definite must or it will be very bland) so I added about 2 tsp; it was perfectly spicy for me but perhaps a bit much if you don't like spicy food.  I served it with rice but just because it was the easiest thing to make.
Over all, a great recipe - I loved the hot and spicy flavour!

attributes.source_text: it was perfectly spicy for me

reviews.review_text: I needed a fast meal that used numerous ingredients in my fridge (headed on vacation and I hate waste). I decided on this recipe because I had veggies, ground beef, and lots of asian ingredients. I did as others said and did half oyster and half Hoision sauce. I added onion, yellow peppers, and zucchini as my veggies. I did not use crushed red pepper at all. I instead used 5 thai chili peppers that I keep on hand in my freezer. My husband is Korean so spice is a must for us. I was so surprised at how delicious this turned out! I used spagetti noodles, but next time I will plan ahead and buy Lo mein noodles from the asian market. For a quick meal this is a keeper.

attributes.source_text: spice is a must for us

reviews.review_text: All I can say is.... YUM! It is ten a.m. and I just ate my leftovers for breakfast. (I usually never eat leftovers so that is saying a lot!) I also don't usually care for ground beef. I thought the use of ground beef in an asian meal was unique but very delicious. Everything was wonderful about this meal! Because I had a closer to a pound and a half of beef and we like things saucy I did double the sauce. It worked out perfectly. I didn't think it was too hot at all but, that is because I LOVE spicy and have a huge tolerance. So next time (for my daughters sake) I will cut down on the crushed red pepper when doubling the batch and have some extra for myself on the side. So delish!

attributes.source_text: I just ate my leftovers for breakfast
the use of ground beef in an asian meal
I didn't think it was too hot at all

reviews.review_text: We loved this quick, tasty dish! It is slightly sweet from the hoisin, a little spicy, and has the perfect amount of sauce for our tastes. I used ground turkey instead of ground beef and whole wheat spaghetti noodles instead of vermicelli. I also added some shredded napa cabbage and thinly julienned red pepper for a little more nutrition.  I also was not sure when to add the sesame oil since it is not mentioned in the instructions, but tossed the cooked noodles in the sesame oil before adding it to the pan and tossing everything together. This was a fantastic, quick an easy one dish meal that everyone in the family enjoyed. Thank you for a definite keeper!

attributes.source_text: slightly sweet from the hoisin
a little spicy
everyone in the family enjoyed

items.label: Best Beef Stroganoff
items.name: Best Beef Stroganoff
items.description: My mom made this beef stroganoff weekly when I was younger. I don't have the same metabolism I did then, but it's still the best $%#&* beef stroganoff I have ever had. I just want to thank everyone for all the wonderful reviews and ideas, I too now add a splash of Worcestershire sauce! Thanks again!
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in butter over medium heat.
Stir in ground beef and brown stir in flour, salt, mushrooms, and pepper cook 5 minutes, then stir in soup.  Simmer uncovered 10 minutes.
Stir in sour cream until heated. Serve over noodles.

reviews.review_text:
I lost my favorite stroganoff recipe so I needed a new one and this looked simple enough. Overall I thought is was pretty good and it was super easy to make. I have never used ground meat before but tried ground turkey. I used 2TBS of butter to saute the onion. The mixture was really thick, so I didn't add the flour. I used about 1/4 C sour cream. I would have liked a slightly looser gravy. I usually make stroganoff with thin slices of sirloin so there ends up being more gravy for the noodles, the ground meat doesn't leave any extra. I would prob saute the mushrooms before adding them to the mix, that's what my old recipe did. And I think it could use some broth. 

*The recipe didn't say what size the cans of mushrooms should be. I ended up using 4 small cans and I think it could have used more.

I made the recipe for dinner last night, but since I am on WW, I made a few adaptations to make it a little more waist-line friendly. First of all, I used turkey instead of beef. Secondly, I used greek yogurt instead of sour cream. Thirdly, I used margerine instead of butter. Finally, I lower cal, 98% fat free cream of mushroom soup.
I followed the instructions as provided (except I did double the garlic), but per other reviewers' instructions, I used worcestershire sauce (probably a couple of tbsp worth, i didn't really measure) and some beef broth (probably 1/2 c, once again, didn't measure) too. This turned out well. My husband loved it! I liked it, but discovered I don't really like cream of mushroom soup (not reflected in the review b/c that's not the recipe's fault)..I'm not sure what I'll use next time, maybe cream of chicken like one other reviewer did.  Overall, however, this was a good recipe and one we will be adding to our dinner rotation. For those of you on WW, with my substitutions, I calculated the points value on the recipe to be 7pts for 1/8 of the pot (this include the egg noodles). Thank you for sharing this delicious recipe.

attributes.source_text: I made the recipe for dinner last night
My husband loved it!

reviews.review_text: This was very yummy!! I read the other review before I made this so I only used 1/2 the sour cream at first and tasted it, then added more. Every time I added more sour cream it got better and I used what the recipe called for. I did make some small adjustments. I left out the canned mushrooms because I forgot to get some...lol. But I did add about 1/4 cup of beef broth because the mixture was very think. At the end I added about 2Tbsp. of worcestershire sauce. I only used 1/2 bag of noodles because I like a higher meat mixture to noodles. But next time I will double the mixture recipe. My DH usually complains when I make beef stroganoff due to the fact that they always serve this in the chow hall when he has to eat there. But he actually said that this was VERY good! THANKS!!! Will be making this again soon!

attributes.source_text: he actually said that this was VERY good!

reviews.review_text:
Edit 5/27/08: If you haven't tried with the addition of Worchester and beef buillon, you are missing out! Try it!

I prepared as followed, but tasted before adding sour crm..it was ok. I took Misty G's suggestion of adding Worchester. Since I halved the recipe I just added a "few splashes". That helped. I then took the restof her suggestion of adding beef broth. I concentrated it a bit and added until I was happy with the result...probably added 1/2 cup at least. That took it from ok to really good! I put about 1 teaspoon of flour, although I don't think it needed it. I finished up by adding a dash or two of paprika. So thanks to Misty G for taking this recipe from about a 2 1/2 to a 4! Hubby went back for more and even the 17mo. old ate it :)

attributes.source_text: Hubby went back for more
even the 17mo. old ate it

reviews.review_text: Here's my tweek. Followed Jimmy801 pretty much. Here are my changes to his and it's an OMG meal. I used 1-1/3 cup sour cream (hear me out Jimmy801, it's not overpowering at the end, but gives it moisture) 3 cloves garlic 2 Tbl Worcestershire sauce (it contains anchovies if you didn't know already) About 1/2 tsp pepper Half an 8 oz pkg fresh mushrooms I'm vegetarian so I used a 13.7 oz pkg of ground beef-less from either Gardein or Morningstar. I used the red onion as well. Cooked frozen peas and carrots from another suggestion. Now, the ingredient that set it out of this world awesome!!! Sherry. I know some folks don't like or drink alcohol but it you cook it down well with the onions/mushrooms/garlic there is no alcohol left but that wonderful flavor remains. I probably used about 1 cup but add it a little at a time until you get the flavor you like. If at the end it is still a little thick like mine turned out I added about 1/2 cup milk. My husband is still eating spoonfuls without the noodles. I hope some is left for another meal my dear. Highly recommend and will make over and over. Such a keeper. Thanks Jimmy801 and Bri22. Looks just like the pic.

attributes.source_text: gives it moisture
My husband is still eating spoonfuls without the noodles

reviews.review_text: My stroganoff hating DH hated this... but I absolutely loved it. I omitted the beef and use vegetarian worchestershire (since I'm vegetarian) and instead of the canned mushrooms, I toss in a bunch of largely chopped fresh mushrooms and saute them along with the onion and garlic (I've tried both button and portobella, both were great). I haven't eaten stroganoff since I was a kid and this was way better then I had then :)   I've made this many times but for some reason have never rated it. Tonight, I found out I was missing the sour cream so I replaced it with 0% fat greek yogurt and it was still awesome! I make this recipe whenever I need some good comfort food. The brand of mushroom soup really does matter in this, Annie's is my personal favorite. Thanks!

Made this for dinner tonight because my family loves stroganoff, it sounded quick and easy, and the use of hamburger makes it a little cheaper than the version we usually use.  It had a good creaminess and flavor, but my husband said he likes the flavor of the crockpot version I make with thinly sliced steak better and we decided in the future we'll probably stick to the other recipe I'd been using when we want stroganoff.  I omitted the salt but took others' suggestions of adding worcestershire sauce and also added 1/4 cup water (forgot to pick up beef broth at the store) because it was a little thick.  If i made it again I would probably use more worcestershire sauce and beef broth instead of water.  I mixed the sauce with the noodles for serving because my family likes the noodles coated.  We all did enjoy it and my picky two year old had seconds!  Thank you for posting this variation!

attributes.source_text: Made this for dinner tonight
It had a good creaminess
my picky two year old had seconds

reviews.review_text: This was a wonderful base recipe for Stroganoff. I did add a few items and change one or two things. I used Top Round cut into cubes which I browned with the onion, garlic, as well as a minced cerrano pepper (we like a little heat). I seasoned the meat with a little salt, pepper, and paprika before browning. I also used fresh button mushrooms (i think next time I will either slice some crimini's or use chantrels). This is an easy dish to make, and tastes extraordinary. If you want to put a little spin on it you can also serve over rice, which I did the first time I made it, and it is really nice. Serve with either fresh green beans or maybe asparagus if it is in season. Great recipe. Thank you.

AMAZING!! I thought there would never be a stroganoff recipe I loved more than my mom's. Then I had this. It was extraordinary! I took the advice of someone else's comment and added 1/4 cup of beef broth.  I've made this twice, now and both times everyone told me how good it was. I had to give my mother in law the recipe after my brother in law ate it because he loved it so much.
The first time I made it with two 2oz. cans of the mushrooms and I decided the second time to cut it back to the one can of mushrooms and I think that was plenty.
The second time I made it with Recipe #83125.
Thanks for this great keeper! I know I'll be making this often!

attributes.source_text: my brother in law ate it because he loved it so much

reviews.review_text:
Fantastic, even with the low fat modifications I made.  I used the leanest ground beef I can find (sometime you can get even leaner than the 93% lean), fat free sour cream, and Smart Beat Trans Fat Free Spread.  That is the best tasting low fat butter there is.  Most low fat butters have more than twice the fat, and the other butters that are as low in fat taste like an abomination.

I also added more salt at the end and used three times the garlic. 

Thanks Bri, and don't let your metabolism prevent you from enjoying the foods you love.  I'm sure the full fat version is better, but if you give my modifications a try (it must be Smart Beat Trans Fat Free) it may come close.

I gave this 4 stars for easy to make. It was very tasty but not the stroganoff I'm used to. I did like this dish only thing I changed was I didn't have canned mushrooms so subbed fresh. I just have to say this -- most of the reviews are other peoples recipes, they didn't follow yours. "I addded this, I did this, I didn't add this. I wish folks would just follow the recipe. It seems as they're submitting their own instead of making this dish. Thanks for an easy recipe for stroganoff Bri22, I did like it! Thanks

This was absolutely delicious, and so simple!!!  I left out the mushrooms even though I would have loved them because my fiance won't touch anything with mushrooms, but it was still so yummy.  I also lightened it up a bit.  I used 3 tablespoons of light butter, 93% lean ground beef, 98% fat free cream of mushroom soup, and light sour cream.  You would never, ever know there weren't full fat ingredients in it!!  When I'm feeling like indulging a little more, maybe I'll try it with full fat ingredients to see if it's that much better :-)   Thanks so much for posting this!!

I originally made this recipe for my fiance and I and it was great!!! A few weeks later we were visiting at my mother's house and I made it for dinner as well since it was such a big hit before.  She said it was THE BEST beef stronganoff she's ever had! I had to give her the recipe before we left town. No joke when it says serves six to eight, it does make a lot.  Instead of using canned mushrooms I used a large amount of fresh because I love mushrooms on just about anything. Other than that I followed the recipe exactly. Thanks for such a great recipe! I will be using it a great deal in the future!!!

attributes.source_text: I originally made this recipe for my fiance and I and it was great
She said it was THE BEST beef stronganoff she's ever had
I made it for dinner as well

reviews.review_text: Wonderful easy comfort food!  It was delicious!  DH and I normally do not like stroganoff using ground beef, we prefer stew beef.  However, this made me realize that I just had not found the right recipe!  This may replace our verson using stew beef!  This is so quick and easy.  I was concerned about not draining the ground beef, especially since I was using 80/20% ground beef.  However, NOT draining the beef and the butter are definitely key factors in the flavor obtained. I would also like to try fresh mushrooms, even an exotic blend next time!  Wonderful and definitely a keeper!  Thanks Bri22!

Very good.  I used Turkish natural yogurt instead of the sour cream and omitted the butter & just sauteed the ground beef & onions together.
Thanks for posting, will make again!
**Made this again, it was even better than I remembered so I turned my review from a 4 star to a 5 star** This time I took a previous reviewers remarks to heart and added about a 1/4 c beef broth.  Again, I used plain yogurt instead of sour cream.  Next time I will try it with diced sirloin.  I can definitely now say this is the best *$#@*$ stroganoff we have ever had :)

This was great! Perfect for a snowy afternoon... and my husband RAVED about it. I did read through all 311 reviews of this dish prior to cooking, so I followed some advice and made a couple of changes (I used fresh mushrooms, which I sauteed along with the onions and garlic, and I used 1/3 cup of sour cream instead of the full cup). Other than that, I followed the recipe with success. I served over whole wheat egg noodles and sprinkled with a bit of parsley. This is a very RICH dish, so it's not something I would make often, but it sure was delicious for a mid-November treat.

attributes.source_text: my husband RAVED about it
This is a very RICH dish

reviews.review_text:
This was really good! 

I work late so my husband has to cook and I knew this would be an easy one for him. I came home to him freaking out b/c he thought he ruined dinner. Long story short..he only forgot to add the sour cream. 

It was really delicious and very rich. I might use half as much sour cream and some milk to thin it out to be a little less rich. 

The worchestire sauce really does make it just perfect.

Oh I think it would also be yummy to use baby bella mushrooms instead of canned but I love how easy this recipe is (nearly husband proof) with the canned ingredients. 

Thanks Bri!

attributes.source_text: very rich

reviews.review_text: ABSOLUTELY LOVE THIS RECIPE BUT MADE SOME CHANGES! This is so so good and now I'm hooked. I did make a few changes but nothing durastic! For the sour cream, I only added about 1/3 cup instead of 1 because I didn't want it to be too powerful. I did add 2 cloves of garlic because we are garlic lovers! I added enough salt and pepper so my liking so that can vary. :) I loved the idea to add Worcestershire sauce to the meat! It added a little something and made the meat not too dry. I would 100% recommend this recipe! This was a really easy dinner to make!

attributes.source_text: made the meat not too dry
a really easy dinner to make

reviews.review_text: I can't believe I forgot to review this recipe.  I've been making this for over a year.  My husband loves it when I make this.  As a matter of fact he requests it often.  I enjoy cooking from scratch and with lots of garlic thus unknowingly I incorporated many suggestions already posted.  I use 2-3 garlic cloves depending on the size, half an onion, freshly sliced mushrooms, and instead of sour cream I use plain yogurt (gotta cut the calories where possible).  Also instead of using all the butter to sautee the onions I use a bit less than one tbsp of butter and about the same amount of olive oil.  Like others I also add a cup of milk to make it a bit more runny since we don't like this as thick.  The base for the recipe is delicious.  Say goodbye to that boxed stuff!

attributes.source_text: My husband loves it when I make this

items.description: Make and share this Perfect Chocolate Brownies recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Grease a 9x13\
squares.
I have read all the great reviews and learned from them, thank you all. Now I line my pan with buttered alumunin foil or parchment paper. This works very well.

reviews.review_text: These were great brownies!As you say, after trying several brownie recipes,* FINALLY* one that I was pleased with the result!! I found them to be better on the second day,and they do kind of remind me of those two bite brownies at the grocery store! Mine were starting to get a little dark around the edges at about 28 mins.(which is when i took them out of the oven) so I wonder if I may have slightly overbaked,I think I will watch them more closely next time and may only bake about 25 mins. If they are any moister, I will be extremely impressed!! I really liked the fact that these were all mixed up right in one pot and using all ingredients that you have on hand, no trips to the grocery store for special chocolate such as the baking squares which i do not buy on a regular basis, usually only when i need them for something specific. These were so quick & easy to make and they still taste great! Thanks!

I just finished putting away the remaining brownies, and all I have to say is that these were perfect.  The top was a thin, flaky, crispy layer of chocolate, with chewy goodness underneath.  I was tempted to bake the brownies a little longer than 30 minutes because I was afraid they were not done, but after letting them sit for about 40 minutes, it was obvious that would have been a mistake.  They were perfect at 30 minutes and then cooling and solidifying a little.  
I usually watch what I eat pretty closely, but these made me want to sit down and eat the whole pan.  My husband, who usually leaves me alone in the kitchen, actually ran to the stove to pull these out of the oven when the timer went off.  Five stars aren't enough!  Thank you for a great recipe :)

attributes.source_text: a thin, flaky, crispy layer of chocolate

a thin, flaky, crispy layer
chewy goodness underneath

reviews.review_text: Hi Virginia...I made your brownies today, after reading all the great reviews, I just had to see what all this fuss was about, and now i know...well, what more can I add that has not already been said...these are actually the best brownies that I have ever made...this is what a brownie should taste like...moist, soft, and with a rich chocolate flavor...made them exactly as stated... I added 1 cup chocolate chips, and 2 Tbsp Kahlua (that I had left over from Christmas, with the vanilla)... baked it on the middle rack, so they would not get too over done on the bottom...they turned out wonderful, so good that they really don't even need any frosting, but we my DH and my son love frosting so I will add it on the brownies. Thank you so much for posting such a wonderful recipe, I will be making these again very soon. :-)

attributes.source_text: with a rich chocolate flavor
moist, soft, and with a rich chocolate flavor
moist, soft, and with a rich chocolate flavor

reviews.review_text: I came across my previous review for this recipe recently, which just said "Mmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm..." Now I don't know what I was thinking just leaving a review like that or if I even tried these, so I figured I owed it to both you and myself to give these a go, if I didnt' before.  These are wonderful- I halved the recipe and cooked in an 8x8 pan, which still worked perfectly.  I actually forgot the nuts, which I wish I hadn't done- but next time (and there will be a next time!) I'll remember!  These are moist, chocolately, perfect chocolate brownies.  I liked how these just used the one pot and came together very quickly and easily. I wanted to line the pan with aluminum foil or parchement, but I'm unfortunately out of both, so I just oiled the pan well, but man these guys still stuck.  Oh well- you can bet I will be picking every little stuck-on bit out of the pan and savoring it.  These are delicous!  Thank you for posting- I will definitely make again.

attributes.source_text: These are moist, chocolately, perfect chocolate brownies
These are moist, chocolately, perfect chocolate brownies

reviews.review_text: I really like these brownies, the walnuts gave a wonderful flavour and I also added a few semi-sweet chocolate chips which worked really well, so I'll add more next time.  I used copha as shortening just because I had it on hand.  I found the brownies a little too sweet for my taste, so I would reduce the sugar to 2 cups next time.  The texture of the brownies turned out mostly fudgy & chewy however I found the edges were a bit hard but that could be because of my fan forced oven, so I may have to reduce the temperature a little next time.  The thing I liked about this recipe was that I had all the ingredients on hand, and that the recipe was so easy and quick to prepare.  I'll make these again!

attributes.source_text: mostly fudgy & chewy
mostly fudgy & chewy

reviews.review_text: First my changes = I subbed equal parts unsalted butter + coconut oil for the shortening. I used only 2 cups sugar based on other reviews about them being too sweet. RESULTS = I thought they were great. The perfect balance of sweet & chocolate (admittedly they weren't terribly sweet, but that's how I like my "sweets"). My husband who is a sugar-aholic thought they weren't sweet enough (although that hasn't stopped him from eating them all day!) I should have taken the advice of other reviewers who said to take them out of the oven a tad earlier, for that bit of under-doneness I like in a brownie. Not sure how they'll fare tomorrow since I just made them today, but plan on putting them in a tupperware like container to insure freshness hopefully.

With 154 ratings, I don't know what I could add except to say that I had my heart set on making these today and I found out that I only had 1/2 cup shortening, only 3 eggs and only 1 3/4 cup sugar. (I need to get to the store!) I made them anyway and  baked them for 28 minutes and the texture is just perfect.  Very fudge-y!  I am pretty sure they will be gone before the evening is over.
If you are worried about them sticking to the pan, I recommend that you whip up a batch of Kittencal's Pan release, Better than Pam Spray (Professional Pan Coating) #78579.  It is amazing and economical.
Thanks, KCShell

attributes.source_text: Very fudge-y!

reviews.review_text:
its simply..awesome:D fudgy..slightly gooey texture and super choclatey.. :DD
DO ADD ALL THE SUGAR! hahaa.i thought of putting 1cup less but changed my mind after tasting the cocoa-butter mixture XD
i used about half a block of butter instead of shortening and i didnt add nuts. i halfed the mixture into two 7x7" pans and put toblerone choc chunks into one of them and about 1/2cup choc chips in the other. everyone preferred the toblerone one XD maybe cos i added too much choc chips in one of the tins and its was a bit too sweet and sticky. putting baking paper in the tin before pouring the mixture helps alot.  fyi, im a 15yr old UBER NOOB cook and it was my first time baking brownies and i did it all by myself(not lying k! xD). so yea, this recipe rocks :D :D

attributes.source_text: slightly gooey texture
super choclatey

reviews.review_text: I was looking for a recipe to use up some ingredients in my pantry and came across this one.  After combining the melted shortening and chocolate I was a little concerned that the mixture would be too thick after adding the flour as the eggs were the only "liquid."  I needn't have worried.  The batter turned out perfectly.  I used an 8" x 8" pan so the brownies would be a little thicker and adjusted the cooking time accordingly.  These turned out fantastic -- not dry or cake-like, but chewy and fudgy -- just the way we like them.  Thanks for sharing this recipe -- I already have requests to make it again!

attributes.source_text: not dry or cake-like
but chewy and fudgy
but chewy and fudgy

reviews.review_text: After reading the astounding 240 reviews of this recipe I just had to try it out as I am trying to move toward more homebaked goodies and foods on a consistent basis.    I am a true chocoholic and this recipe will not disappoint even the most finicky of chocolatiers and will delight the taste buds of all who use it.  To all you novice bakers, you can substitute butter or margarine for the required shortening.  If you choose to use salted butter or other substitute that includes salt, you can cut the amount of salt required in the recipe to half.  I used unsalted butter and then used the full amount suggested in the recipe.  I also used a cup or 2 sticks of unsalted butter.  Whether you use shortening, butter; salted or unsalted, or margarine each will have it's own unique flavor.  Depending on your sensitivity to taste this will make a difference.  It is best to use what you regularly cook with and use as table spreads for your toast and waffles.  Using shortening as your cream base if you are used to butter or margarine on a daily basis will have a funny flavor not that it is a wrong flavor just different.  Too much salt can sometimes have a bitter taste and if you reduce the amount of sugar or other ingredients you may have to reduce the amount of cocoa too. When making modifications to any recipe just be careful you have enough time to make corrections or start all over again if it is needed and don't need to be greeting guests or walking out the door with a first class presentation just hours away.  You know what the old expression says, "If it ain't broke don't fix it!"  Sometimes recipes will not allow for substitutions and I am still trying to figure out why that is or if it is chefs choice.   I also added a quarter cup of semi-sweet Toll House morsels to my batter.  I consider my cooking to be at the intermediate level bordering to advanced on rare occasions and am in no way an expert on the subject. Mom was a great teacher and I have improved over the years too.    Like so many others who commented on this wonderful recipe, I could not wait til they cooled either....OUCH!  Great going Virginia!

reviews.review_text: I made these for my SO on 11/23/10.I sort of followed the recipe as it was written( READ: messed up :) big time ) I didn't read the recipe right and put the cocoa and sugar in the same bowl, luckly I was able to get out most of the sugar. Even mixing the batter by wooden spoon is simple because you are adding in only portions at a time.  I omitted the nuts as I will be offering these to my son who doesn't like nuts in his brownies (I love them and would have added walnuts - next batch, I will!).  Brownies were ready and baked in exactly 30 minutes.  I will keep this recipe in my Make Again Collection!  Thank you for sharing this recipe with us, Virginia!

reviews.review_text: I've been making these brownies once a week for the last 2 months, and have been tweaking the recipe slightly every time. They have been coming out amazing! I minus a 1/4 cup of sugar, add an extra egg yolk, add an extra 1/2 teaspoon of baking powder, add 8 squares of bakers chocolate to the Crisco while it's melting, and mix 1 tablespoon of instant coffee with the Crisco/cocoa mixture. I also add an extra 5 minutes to the baking time, as well as an extra 5 degrees to the oven temp. Any time my wife is craving chocolate, I make these brownies. We are both in LOVE with these!!!

reviews.review_text: I'm not sure you need another 5-star review, but you're getting one from me.  I needed a recipe that uses cocoa powder.  So many use baker's chocolate or chocolate chips.  This was the perfect chocolate brownie.  Took me right back to my childhood.  Crispy edges and super moist inside.  I had to halve the recipe due to a shortage of sugar, so I used a 8" round cake pan.  Baked just as long.  All gone before they even had a chance to cool off.  My husband is amazed I could make something that good with ingredients from the cupboard.  My secret: Barry Callebaut cocoa powder--and a great recipe!

reviews.review_text: OMG!! YUM YUM YUM. I made this a few weeks ago when my cousin and her family came up to visit. It was a cold and rainy day and all us girls wanted to do was eat and I remembered that I had saved this recipe and never cooked it. I know the recipe says to completely cool the brownies but we couldn't wait to eat it. We wanted it warm anyway and we served it with vanilla ice cream, canned whipped cream and hot fudge sauce. We faught over the last piece that was left and I'm glad that I was lucky enough to get it as I was the chef for the 10 days they were here. Will most definately be making it again and soon hopefully.

Oh wow! So, so good! Flakey on top, chewy in the middle, crunchy or crusty on the edge, the perfect brownie. I only had 1 stick of butter so I melted that with 1/2 cup Crisco. Now I must say that I'm a butter lover and was VERY hesitant adding shorting (crisco) but it came out absolutely amazing and I will cherish this recipe as my one and only scratch brownie recipe from now on. That's how good this was people. Don't read any more reviews. just give it a try you will not be upset. Or actually maybe you will because this is so good you are likely to eat the whole pan yourself. Lol. Anyhow, happy baking!
