items.label: Easy and Tasty Barbecue Chicken Sandwiches in the Crock Pot
items.name: Easy and Tasty Barbecue Chicken Sandwiches in the Crock Pot
items.description: This is almost too easy to be called a recipe, but I had to share it anyway. I came up with it one night when I wanted a nice meal but wasn't feeling too motivated. I love Crock-Pot cooking!
instructions: Remove all visible fat from the chicken and toss it in the crock pot.
Place the onion slices on top of the chicken.
Pour the barbecue sauce over top.
You may not need the entire jar, just enough to cover the chicken.
Cook it on LOW for 8 hours or until the chicken is nice and tender.
Shred the chicken with a fork and knife; scoop the mixture onto the bottom buns and top it with the top buns.
Or, if you're like my dad, you might prefer leaving the breasts whole and eating it that way.
Voila!
An easy weeknight meal that doesn't heat up your kitchen in the summertime!
I love this with potato chips and a carrot and raisin salad.

reviews.review_text: Tasty recipe!  I used 4 boneless chicken breasts, and a 16 oz. container of K.C. Masterpiece jerk chicken sauce.  I have a newer model crock pot, so my crock pot recipes always cook much more quickly than directed.  I cooked on low for 4 hours, stirring once an hour so the sauce remained on top of the chicken.  I then removed the chicken, shredded it with a knife and fork, and returned to the crock pot so it could simmer in the sauce on low for another hour and a half.  Total cooking time was 5 and a half hours.  I served it on baked Pillsbury Southern biscuits, which I would not recommend, as they are too small.  Opt for the hamburger buns instead, and you may want to toast them so they don't get mushy from the chicken mixture.  I thought the 16 oz. jar of sauce resulted in a recipe a tad too tangy.  Thus, next time, I'll use just enough sauce to cover the chicken, then once the chicken is shredded, I'll add more sauce as needed.  Thanks for this great and easy recipe!!

It was around 4:15 and I realized that I needed to make dinner, but didn't want to stand over the stove forever - I'm 5 months pregnant :) - so I found this recipe and got it in the crockpot as fast as I could. First I thawed 3 chicken breasts in the microwave, sauteed some onions, and threw those both along with about 1/2 a bottle of Sweet Baby Ray's in the Crockpot set on High. I came back to the computer to read reviews about cooking time, and saw someone say they cut up the chicken to cook it faster (duh! why didn't i think of that?) so I went back to the pot and cut up the chicken into chunks. I let the chicken cook for almost 2 hours, and heard the lid bubbling so i opened it and was able to shred the chicken easily- and it was done! I added just a bit more bbq and the hubby and I ate it up on leftover hot dog buns. I thought it was really good and moist, he said it was "delicious" and I was so happy to be able to cook up yummy bbq chicken in such a short amount of time. I will definitely DEFINITELY make this again!! :) Thanks for the recipe! **Update- I have made this MANY times and it is always, always delicious. The last time I made it I added grape jelly, which is a secret ingredient (well, not anymore) that a chef my husband works with adds to bbq sauce. It was the BEST.**

attributes.source_text: the hubby and I ate it up
it was really good and moist

reviews.review_text: I pinched a nerve in my neck last night - so the last thing I wanted to do was cook. I saw this recipe and figured it would be easy enough. I put three large frozen boneless, skinless chicken breasts in the slowcooker, and sprinkled onion salt over them (I needed to go shopping and didn`t have onions). I used a 500ml bottle of Diana`s Rib & Chicken sauce. I cooked it on high for four hours. I shredded the chicken using two meat forks. Even though they were fully cooked, I left them in for another hour on low just to soak up more flavour. I toasted a few sesame buns in some butter in a frying pan and loaded the meat on. They were really good - DH added pickles to his, but I`m more of a purest. I served it with spicy fries and corn. The sides of the chicken got a bit crispy from touching the sides of the crockpot - which we liked since it seemed more like bbq. I think it would have been even better with some creamy coleslaw on top, and baked beans on the side. DH gave this a rating of 8 out of 10. Thanks for sharing this with us!!

reviews.review_text: A keeper for sure!  I used 10 skinless bone in chicken thighs (it was cheaper to feed a crowd that way) I used a small bottle of Sweet Baby Rays and also poured about a cup of Diet Coke on the bottom.  I did it on high for about 6 hours and I came home and it was all falling apart and perfect!  It looked VERY VERY watery and I thought UGH I need to strain it some but it actually just soaked all up into the meat once I shredded it more.  And by using bone in I used tongs to just pick up the bone, no fighting it, and the meat shredded itself.  I used a meat fork and just stirred and it did the rest of the shredding work.  We served on Texas toast with cheddar cheese and mac and cheese on the side (I needed soft food b/c I had a tooth pulled and this was PERFECTLY soft and I could chew it on the first day!!!)  Thanks for a super great recipe...I'm going to make this again and again!!!

reviews.review_text:
Update: This recipe has become a household staple, and in the course of preparing it, I discovered Crock Pot Liners.  I've now found that I can take two crock pot liners, and in one liner bag I can make this BBQ recipe, and in the other bag I can make Crock Pot Chicken Taco Meat (Recipe 4957) and cook them in the same large crock pot.  If cooked on high, it only takes me about 4 to 5 hours, and I stop to switch the bags around half way through the cooking so the chicken breasts cook evenly.  Within 5 hours I have two delicious and easy meals, great for entertaining. 

Oh man...I know, this is too simple to be a recipe, but I'll be keeping this one! Wonderful, delicious chicken. I was worried when I opened the crock pot, removed the onions and saw how much liquid was in the bottom...it was very runny. But, once the chicken was shredded and mixed back in, it was perfect. The chicken soaked up all of the BBQ, and tasted fantastic.

attributes.source_text: great for entertaining

reviews.review_text: This is an easy and great crock pot recipe. Perfect for a pot luck and great for the football season. However, I gave mine a little twist. I like to season my chicken by adding your favorite seasonings. But with the Barbeque sauce, not much is really needed though. So I just added salt and pepper to each side of the chicken. After seasoning, applying the onions on top, I squeezed a full lime in a bowl. This way you can take out any pull seeds. And last but not least, I poured a whole bottle of Barbeque sauce. We all have our favorite, so chose what you like best. But what I did was add a quarter cup of coke. I prefer the glass bottle that is from Mexico, as the coke is better. Stir together well and pour over the chicken in the crock pot. It will retain the juices more and thicken a little bit. Excellent over toasted buns with some sliced deli pepper rings and even better on Texas toast. Serve with a side of country potato salad, Cole slaw and some Tim's Cascade Chips. Now ready to eat!!

reviews.review_text:
Thanks so much for posting this!!!! My neighbors moved away and gave me their crock pot. I had never cooked anything in one before and my family didn't use one growing up so I'm pretty clueless when it comes to the way of the crock pot. 

This is the first recipe I've ever tried in it and it was delicious!!!! I used 6 large boneless skinless chicken breast halves, half a bottle of craft bbq sauce and half a bottle of Jrader Joe's bbq sauce. I didn't have an onion on hand so I just used a few dashes of onion powder. 

I cooked it for 4 hours, shreading the chicken after 2. The chicken turned out extremely tender and wonderful. The taste of the sauce wasn't as good as I had hoped, but that's not the fault of the recipe. Next time I'll stick with KC Masterpiece (it's what I usually use). Maybe I'll add a little garlic and cayenne pepper as well for some kick. 

This recipe is definitely a keeper. My bf ate two of these sandwiches in the blink of an eye and brought a bun and more filling for lunch at work. YUM!

attributes.source_text: The chicken turned out extremely tender
My bf ate two of these sandwiches in the blink of an eye

reviews.review_text: This is a very good idea, and I'm sure that when you do it correctly, it is amazing and easy!  I, however, forgot the first rule of crockpot cooking, which is...make sure that the crockpot is at least half full.  I used 1 1/2 pounds of chicken and the whole bottle of BBQ sauce...and it only covered the bottom of the crockpot, but I wasn't thinking because I was tired (worked nights) and went to bed.  I woke up because my apartment smelled like burning.  The sauce was stuck to the edges of the crockpot and was turning black.  I quickly rescued as much chicken as I could, and it was very tender and amazing and fell apart after only six hours on low!  I just have to find a way to add more sauce to it, since all the sauce burned and now I don't have any left. I'll finish cooking it on the stove.  So in conlusion, good recipe! just be careful if you have a big crockpot.

attributes.source_text: it was very tender

reviews.review_text: Oh.. my.. goodness! This is SOOOOO amazingly good and absolutely NO work. I just put in about 1 lb frozen chicken with a whole bottle of Stubb's Smokey Mesquite BBQ sauce (I've found it's the most low calorie bbq sauce! ;)) and omitted the onion. Turned on the crock pot and went about my day. The last hour of cooking I removed the breasts, shredded them, and put them back in the sauce in the crock pot on the WARM setting so they could absorb all that sauce. I also added some Chipotle Tabasco sauce, salt & pepper. I went and worked out, came back and put some shredded chicken on top of salad greens for a nice healthy, low-carb option. I topped it with a litte bit of sour cream & salsa mixed together as a dressing. The whole time I ate that salad I was getting almost giddy with delight that something so easy could be so healthy and so yummy. Thank you SO much for sharing - this will become a staple in our house!

I had good intentions of following the recipe exactly, but one thing always leads to another!  I had 4 bone-in skinless breasts so I used those.  I put a little water and liquid smoke in the crockpot and cooked them on low for 7 hours.  I cooled and shredded them, then put in the frig for the next day.  I put the chicken back into the crockpot to reheat with a bottle of Sweet Baby Rays (yummm) BBQ sauce and heated on low for 2-3 hours.  Anyway, it tasted great and I will use your recipe again.  It would be great for a crowd of folks with the crockpot doing most of the work.  Paired it with slaw, corn on the cob and homegrown tomatoes.  Thanks, Kree, for the original recipe that got me to get out the crockpot in the first place.

I had one boneless skinless breast and 3 with skin and bone in.  I put it in the crock pot on low at 7:15 am this morning and had frozen sliced onions which I added with a smidgen of salt and pepper and topped with Stubbs Mesquite BBQ sauce.  Just got home now at 5:30 and took everything out of the slow cooker, shredded the boneless breast and the skin came right off the other 3 breasts, shredded those too and strained the sauce and put the chicken back into the slow cooker, added the rest of the BBQ sauce and it's now on low for another 20 mns or so.  My husband just came in and commented how good it smelled in the house.  I gave him a taste of the chicken and he said it was so good it made him weak in the knees!  Thank you so much for sharing this recipe, it's a keeper!

reviews.review_text: Well, here's rating #281, and no wonder - this recipe has it all.  Ease of preparation, great flavor (depends on your barbecue sauce, so use a good one that you like) and enjoyed by the whole family.  I made my own hamburger buns from my recipe#445540 and it went very well.  I used a bottled sauce that I tweaked to our liking, cooked the onions with the chicken in the crock pot, and served with jalapeno slices and cheese.  Don't do what I did, thinking it didn't have enough water I added a 1/4 cup to the pot when I started and it watered it down WAY to much as it cooked, had to drain it off and add more sauce.  The recipe is right on as to how to fix this very comforting, fast dish.  Made for Comfort Foods in the photo forum.

reviews.review_text: I gave this 3 stars. I first want to say I think it was the bbq sauce we used. I used jack daniels and we had never tried it before. I also used frozen chicken breasts so I think this may have been why my sauce remand thin. I didn't have time to cook this the full 8 hrs so I cooked it on low for 6 hrs then on high for 1 hour to thicken up the sauce. Once I shredded the chicken the sauce seemed to thicken. I also didn't have a sweet onion so I used a regular onion. I wasn't crazy over the onions as they never got fully cooked. Overall I will make this again with a homemade bbq sauce as I really think that was the problem and then rerate it. Thanks for posting a good recipe. Christine (internetnut)

I am back to work after having a baby, so Quick & Easy recipes are at the top of my list right now. I thought this recipe would make a serviceable, but not exciting, dinner.
Wrong. I used chicken that was still mostly frozen (had placed in fridge overnight from freezer), a store-brand bottle of BBQ sauce to which I added some black pepper, garlic & chili powder, and a mix of red & white onion slices.
Heavenly! The onion kind of "melted" into the meat/sauce, it was so tender it fell off the fork while I was trying to shred it, & DH and I enjoyed it on toasted whole-wheat buns.
I'll make this again & again.

reviews.review_text: Since me and my husband haven't been married that long yet, I was a little nervous when he wanted me to invite his family over for a meal. I never cooked for that many people before (there were 7 of us). I had soup in my freezer and I thought some kind of sandwich would go well with that. reviews.review_text: These were fabulous!  I love pulled pork sandwiches (but not the fat!) and was so happy to see that this was a perfect substitute.  I used 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts, and 1 bottle of Stubbs BBQ sauce, and of course 1 onion.  This cooked for 5 hours, and then I shredded the chicken (just mixed it around with a fork) and let it sit for another hour or so.  I served this on hamburger buns with my favorite coleslaw (Recipe ## 359978), corn on the cob, sweet potato casserole, and fresh homemade iced tea, followed by my fried cheesecake bites (Recipe # 234317).  It was a fantastic meal!!  Thanks for a keeper!

Fantastic! This is probably the easiest and best recipe I've found yet! If it didn't turn out great, you did something wrong. Make sure you use a small (2 quart) crockpot, 2 pounds of chicken,
low temp setting all the way through, and one full bottle of sauce (Sweet Baby Ray's is the best). I'm the typical male cook, and while I love great taste, I'm always interested in how easy something is to make and how many ingredients it has. This is so simple to do and all you have to add is some ready made deli slaw or broccoli salad plus chips and you have a fabulous meal. Bravo to whoever came up with this one!

I was a little skeptical about trying this out because it looked too easy -- I couldn't believe it could be as good as all the reviews raved. Well, I'm a believer now. It's THAT GOOD. I used about 2 bone-in, skinless chicken breasts and half a bottle of Bulls Eye barbeque sauce. I shredded the chicken during the last 30 minutes of cooking so that it would soak up all the sauce. YUMMY! Unbelievably fall-off-the-bone-tender. And the taste -- it tasted like I'd been slaving away in the kitchen all day. Definitely a keeper! We'll be making this regularly. Thanks for the recipe!!

reviews.review_text: Wonderful and what a time saver!!! Just throw it in the crock pot and forget about it...no need to stir it or anything. I checked on it after about 3 hrs and the chicken (I used 4 Lrg breasts) were cooked. I then shredded it w/2 forks and tasted it. I decided to spice it up a notch and added some crushed red peppers since my Honey and I like things spicy. I threw in some salt and added a little bit of ground Ginger. The 2 of us almost devoured all of it but left just enough for his lunch at work the next day. Oh and Sweet Baby Rays is definitely the way to go on this one! Thank you for posting, we're already planning to make it for next weekends BBQ!!!

This makes wonderful, tasty, flavorful BBQ sandwiches!  It is so easy, you won't believe it - perfect for a weekday meal, for entertaining (because you do not have to cook, while guests are there), and the recipe could easily be adjusted for a large crowd.  The only things that I did differently was sprinkle the chicken breasts with garlic salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper; add a few dahses of hot sauce to the BBQ sauce; and throw in some diced green chiles for the last 1/2 hour of cooking time(I, too, shredded the meat during the last 1/2 of cooking time, so that the meat could soak up the sauce and flavors). Served it with BBQ beans and corn, which was perfect with it.  Wonderful, simple recipe - thanks for sharing a great idea!

items.label: Restaurant Teriyaki Sauce
items.name: Restaurant Teriyaki Sauce
items.description: You know the nice, sweet, thick Teriyaki sauce you get from your favorite takeout joint? Now you can have it at home.
instructions: Mix all but cornstarch and 1/4c water in a sauce pan and begin heating.
Mix cornstarch and cold water in a cup and dissolve.
After sauce is simmering, add cornstarch and water mixture, whisking well until sauce thickens.
Heat until sauce thickens to desired thickness.
Add water to thin if you over-thick it :).

reviews.review_text: I agree with Rob. Never thicken marinade for basting. NEVER recycle used marinade. (See Salmonella or other bacterial food poisoning on WebMD). Do this recipe a day ahead (up to the thickening part). I use half for marinade, and save half for later. The flavors “get to know each other” in the refrigerator overnight. Again, Honolulu Rob, pineapple juice and/or crushed pineapple is an excellent addition, as is anise and bay leaf. To thicken, put cornstarch in a very small bowl, add Cold water. Wash your hands, even if you did it before cooking, LOL, and mix with your fingertip. You can smooth out any lumps against the side of the (bowl, ramekin or shot glass). After trying this cornstarch-water trick, you’ll never use a whisk again. We love ginger, so use grated fresh ginger with a very tiny spoon as garnish on the finished product. Oftentimes, I mix it with crushed pineapple and other veggies (in whichever recipe I’m using) to make a “salsa”. Lots of complimentary flavors. A little fresh ginger goes a Long way!

Phenomenal! I wanted to find a good recipe that my sister could have -- she has Celiac disease and can't have gluten, so readily available bottled sauce isn't something we can use. This was just wonderful. Before I added the slurry I had her taste the sauce and she said it tasted just like what she remembered from the restaurants. Five stars and two thumbs up!

A quick tip to those who said their sauce was too watery: a slurry (any type of starch mixed with water) needs to be made with cold to cool -- NEVER HOT -- water and added to SIMMERING liquid. It's okay to bring your liquid to a boil, but you need to lower it again until it's gently boiling with LITTLE waves. You can't just add cornstarch (or any starch) into a hot liquid, it won't bind it, and the liquid can't be too hot or it breaks the starch down and, again, it does nothing.

attributes.source_text: my sister could have

reviews.review_text: Well....This gets the one star for being as thick as I'd hoped it'd be. It doesn't taste like much of anything, let alone Teriyaki. I followed the recipe exactly, and ended up with a bland but thick sauce/glaze. The recipe I usually use for a more liquid marinade is 1 cup of water, 1 cup soy sauce and 3/4 cup of sugar (you can use more or less per your own tastes), eyeballing the amount of ginger, garlic and pineapple juice. This is the recipe my father returned from Japan with, but I'm pretty sure there are as many variations to making a Teriyaki sauce as there are stars in the sky and it can really depend on what you're looking for in terms of flavor. I was disappointed with the recipe as written and added more soy sauce until I was pleased with the flavor. I didn't know that for thickening a sauce you have to add Corn Starch to cold water in order to get it to work, so I threw on an extra star for the woman who wrote that tidbit in her review, because that was totally helpful and deserved a star all on it's own. But I won't be bothering with this recipe ever again.

attributes.source_text: as thick as I'd hoped it'd be
a bland but thick sauce/glaze

reviews.review_text: Delicious. I doubled the recipe. Though I hesitated, I did end up doubling the cornstarch too, to get the right consistency -- this wasn't too thick for us, despite other reviews. Outstanding over rice. Used jarred minced garlic instead of ground. I eyeballed the brown sugar and I think I added a good bit less than was called for, but it was perfect for us. I will definitely make this again. ***UPDATE*** I make it by the bucketful and freeze for later use!  I keep a mason jar of it in the fridge for super-quick, delicious packed lunches at work; just make some rice, toss some precooked chicken on it and spoon teriyaki over top. It thickens in the fridge but thins out again when reheated.  We LOVE this stuff!!! I'm planning to make some homemade frozen "TV Dinners" with it, too, I think they'll do well.

attributes.source_text: this wasn't too thick for us
super-quick, delicious packed lunches at work
It thickens in the fridge
thins out again when reheated

reviews.review_text: I just made this for chicken drumsticks, and it was great! I added a little fresh garlic and sesame seeds, and didn't thicken it much, and then poured it over half baked drumsticks, and let it thicken and flavor the chicken. Great dinner! Tonight, I'm making it again, but, adding a little crushed red pepper, and marinading a tri-tip in it. Thank you! - had the tri-tip and I'd recommend it to EVERYONE!  don't thicken the sauce first.  I marinated it overnight, cooked it at 350 in a dutch oven until desired temp, took the lid off to brown, poured off the marinade to thicken on the stove, and it was a hit!  Thanks again for the wonderful sauce!!

attributes.source_text: Great dinner!

reviews.review_text:
Recipe is good but slightly vague and needs to give more detail. It is important to use Japanese Soy sauce as other types like Chinese soy can be quite salty. Definitely substitute the powdered garlic for fresh as this makes it more traditional and tastes better. If marinating, as one review previously said, do so with out adding the cornstarch to the rest of the ingredients. Once marinated, drain off the liquid and cook/add cornstarch then to make a sauce. It is important to note as one review before believed that the sauce is gluten free, that soy sauce contains a lot of starch(wheat) as those most cornstarch now too to stop caking occurring.
J.D

I made a stir fry and added this sauce when the dish was almost done. Actually when I tasted the cooked sauce by itself, it had a pungent taste and aroma and was going to throw it out. Pretty sure it was the honey. However the weirdest thing happened. . . when I added the prepared sauce to my chicken stir fry and continued stirring until the dish was cooked, the end result was very good. IMO the sauce is better for adding in and mixing with the stir fry rather than using it for dipping. I guess you can call this sauce, a double cooked sauce. Goes to show what a difference a sauce makes once you incorporate it in your dish. I think next time I will leave out the honey and add more brown sugar instead. Thanks for posting, Juniper

I was looking for a teriyaki recipe for my brothers birthday because he loves nothing more the some teriyaki cover meat....So what I did was follow this recipe but accidently skip the 1 cup of water in the x's6 batch I made.I dont know dumb mistake I just looked and thought it was the water that you mix with the startch. But let me tell you it is still amazing taste exactly like a local spot called bottlenecks that I absolutely love! What im doing now with it is marinading chicken and steak cubes for kabobs 1 cup each Im gonna let it sit for 24 hrs then with the rest Im using it for basting on the grill and then adding some toasted sesame seeds to the last bit for dipping!

attributes.source_text: it is still amazing taste exactly like a local spot called bottlenecks that I absolutely love

reviews.review_text: Was looking for a quick and easy recipe for chicken teriyaki dinner.  This was perfect.  I usually like to make things a little more in depth, i.e. fresh garlic and ginger but I was in a rush.  I simply cooked up some onions and peppers, set them aside and then began cooking the chicken in a little soy sauce and oil after marinating in soy sauce for 15 minutes.  I drained off the marinade after cooking for about 4 minutes, added my veggies and the teriyaki sauce and turned up the heat until it thickened.  Super quick, super easy.  Thanks for sharing!

attributes.source_text: for chicken teriyaki dinner
chicken teriyaki dinner

reviews.review_text: I am super sad to say this but.... I seriously question the reviews on here.. Some are funny saying they used corn meal, extra garlic and ginger, that's nasty. I've been cooking for 20 yrs now. This sauce is super easy (Thank You) but I thought it was gross! Bitter aftertaste. I was mad that I had to dump it. So I made it again but WITHOUT the ginger or garlic (which I love) and it was crazy good. Save the seasonings for your food and keep your sauce simple. I made Teriyaki Meatballs(w/ginger & garlic powder in the meat) and sauted Broccoli and Onions. I poured the sauce at the end of cooking. Served with steamed jasmine rice.

I wanted a teriyaki sauce to make teriyaki chicken sushi nori rolls. It was amazing. So super easy and SO tasty. I didnt use the cornflour or the last 1/4 cup of cold water. I poured it over the chicken when it was ready (still thin and watery) and let it simmer down. It became thick and sticky, and absolutely perfect. No issues making it gluten free... just need a gluten free soy sauce (Fountain is great). Everything else is already GF. I didnt have garlic powder so I used 1tsp garlic from a jar. I'll definitely make this sauce again, I've already written it in to my favourites recipe book!

attributes.source_text: a teriyaki sauce to make teriyaki chicken sushi nori rolls
It became thick and sticky
It became thick and sticky

reviews.review_text: Simply Amazing!!  Look No Further! This IS the RECIPE YOU WANT!! Delicious, full of flavor, and most of all EASY!! I'm made Teryiaki Chicken and Sticky Rice last night for Dinner, when I realized I was all out of any type of Stir-Fry/Teriyaki Sauce. So, I went to Google, and BOOM! I had all the ingredients I needed. I whipped it up together within mins. (even doubling the recipe)<br/><br/>Next time I make this, (And their WILL be a next time.) I'm going to substitude some water for Pineapple Sauce, for more of a tropical feel. :-)

attributes.source_text: last night for Dinner

reviews.review_text: This is wonderful teriyaki sauce.  Very easy and tasty.  I like that it doesn't have a lot of artificial ingredients.  Like one other reviewer, I use Bragg's Liquid Aminos and have for a long time ~ like them much better than regular soy sauce.  I also made this a little different than posted ~ I combined everything except the cornstarch and cold water and poured it over browned boneless skinless chicken thighs and simmered them for about 20 minutes and then thickened the sauce.  Served with rice and sugar snap peas.  Thanks for posting this Juniper!  Made for Zaar Chef Alphabet Soup.

attributes.source_text: This is wonderful teriyaki sauce

reviews.review_text: Today I had such a craving for teriyaki chicken but had no teriyaki sauce so I went searching and found this recipe! So easy to make and tastes amazing! One hint I would give to the inexperienced cook is to pour the slurry in when the sauce is just hot not boiling or simmering and then stir, stir, stir and gradually bring the mixture up to a low simmering bubble and at that point cook it for exactly 5 minutes and it'll turn out perfect every single time! Thick enough to coat but not so thick that it's gooey. Hope this helps!

attributes.source_text: I had such a craving for teriyaki chicken
Thick enough to coat

reviews.review_text: My husband wanted to make Teriyaki glazed chicken wings - well all bottled teriyaki sauce I've ever bought from the store have never measured up, so I searched for a homemade recipe.  My husband scoffed - but I continued... Found this recipe, went to the store to buy the couple of ingredients that I didn't have on hand... He bought 2 bottled sauces - and guess who is in love with THIS sauce?!?  It is truly "restaurant quality" as the title states...  Love, love, LOVE it!  It is insanely simple and super delish and will be my go to from now...

attributes.source_text: guess who is in love with THIS sauce?!?

reviews.review_text: If ever a recipe here deserves 5 stars it is this one!  I never knew it was so easy to make your own teriyaki sauce.  It is 10 times better than the sauce you get in a bottle.  I can't believe that something so simple can turn out so delicious.  I cut my chicken into bite sized pieces and cooked them in a skillet until done.  Then I added the sauce and let it simmer together for 5-6 minutes.  It was sooo good.  My 7 year old just went on and on about how good the chicken was.  I'll definitely use this recipe again and again!

attributes.source_text: My 7 year old just went on and on about how good the chicken was

reviews.review_text: This was fantastic! It is very versatile. I have now made this a number of times and always make a double batch to make sure I have left overs. (Although I do agree with the other post that you will need more than a single batch for a meal). I thicken it with flour instead of cornstarch (3 1/2 tbsp flour to the same amount of water) and the texture stays the same for when I go back to my leftovers. I have used this for homemade stir fry, beef and broccoli, chicken and broccoli, chicken rice bowls... you get the idea. I have adjusted for my family by using 1 tsp garlic powder (instead of 1/4 tsp), 3/4 tsp ginger (instead of 1/2 tsp), and I add 3/4 tsp onion powder. My husband and son both agree this is a keeper. I will never go back to store bought again. Thank you for the recipe!

attributes.source_text: My husband and son both agree this is a keeper
My husband and son both agree this is a keeper

reviews.review_text: Great sauce, and it's SO easy to make which is wonderful!  I followed the recipe exactly (except I added an extra 1/4 tsp. garlic powder and probably should have done the same for the ginger powder for extra flavor).  Though, I will say that it was a bit too sweet for me, I would lower the brown sugar to 4 TBSP. instead of the whole 5.  Also, I added it after I made the sauce, but 1/2 tsp of cayenne pepper gave it a great spicy kick.  But I will DEFINIETLY make this again with or without alterations!

attributes.source_text: gave it a great spicy kick

reviews.review_text: This recipe is really good and flavorful and I generally have everything on hand. This is the second time making it and I made a couple change this time. I used 1/2 cp Orange juice to five it a tropical flavor. You could also use pineapple juice that would be good! I added a touch of sesame oil and some sesame seeds. I used the conrstarch and it did what it was supposed to do..thicken the sauce. If you have trouble with your leftovers pop them in the microwave for 30 seconds then give them a quick whisk and they are perfect again!

attributes.source_text: to five it a tropical flavor
thicken the sauce

items.label: 4 Minute Spicy Garlic Shrimp
items.name: 4 Minute Spicy Garlic Shrimp
items.description: Recipe is originally from the Food Network courtesy of Rachael Ray, but I tweaked it to fit our tastes. Very quick & easy shrimp recipe that's done on the stovetop. If your tastes desire spicy & garlic, then this recipe is just for you.
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium high heat.
Add olive oil, garlic, red pepper flakes, and shrimp.
Season with grill seasoning or salt & pepper.
Cook shrimp 3 minutes or until just pink.
Toss with lemon zest, juice, & chopped parsley.
Remove shrimp to a serving platter, leaving the garlic cloves in the pan.

reviews.review_text: This is a no fail recipe. Look at all the substitutions - you really can't go wrong. I rarely ever cook, in part because I'm the youngest in this family, and I'm just a little shy since everyone else in my family is naturally gifted. For the past week my mother's been out of town. I was starving and wanted to have a little something before I went grocery shopping and stumbled upon this! MY GOD. This recipe is so basic, you can guesstimate the measurements, play around with the seasoning and this will still come out amazing. SPLOGS - that is the acronym I'll be using to remember this 10 minute recipe (that's shrimp, parsley, lemon, olive oil, garlic, and seasoning). YUM!

Very tasty and easy to make.  I didn't have any Jumbo shrimp so I used a bag of frozen 50-60 count medium white shrimp.  I defrosted them in cold water and removed the shells and de-veined them.  I went ahead and removed the tails because it was taking much too long to try to keep the tails intact while removing the rest of the shells and legs on such small shrimp.  I also substituted 1/2 tsp of Old Bay seasoning for the 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes because I can't eat things with too much red pepper.  I also substituted Chef Paul Prudhomme's Meat Magic Seasoning for the Steak Seasoning and it turned out great!  My husband loved it too.  I served the shrimp over a bed of fettuccine noodles with tomato basil marinara and had caramelized baby Brussels sprouts on the side.  I will definitely make this again!

attributes.source_text: My husband loved it too

reviews.review_text: Used a pound of smaller shrimp. Should have doubled the sauce but since I didn't know how much 12 jumbo shrimp weighed, I wasn't sure what to do but I will know next time. The taste was great. I used the batch of the smaller shrimp like Red Lobster's shrimp scampi and tossed them onto Caesar salad. YUMMY! If you like spicy, add more red pepper. If using frozen cooked shrimp, defrost and dry the shrimp first and then the sauce comes out great. If you don't it will be watery.<br/><br/>Update:  Made this again with JUMBO shrimp but didn't use the Montreal Seasoning and used extra lemon, then I made Kittencal's Caesar salad dressing recipe to make  Shrimp Scampi-Caesar Salad and it was amazing.

Just perfect!  Amazing how something so simple and quick could taste so delicious.  The seasoning added in this recipe completely accented the shrimp while still allowing you to taste the great taste of quality shrimp.  I didn't use jumbo shrimp...probably more medium sized.  I also didn't use Montreal Seasoning since the store didn't carry it but they made their own version of the Montreal Seasoning and it was wonderful!  Can't believe I haven't tried the seasoning before.  I eyeballed the zest and juice, increased the garlic (of course!) and the crushed red pepper.  Even my 4 year old liked it but told me it made his lips burn!  haha  I did think it had a nice kick.  I will definitely make this again.  I served this tonight with butter/parmesan pasta and balsamic cauliflower.  Wonderful.

attributes.source_text: I did think it had a nice kick
Even my 4 year old liked it

reviews.review_text: This was super easy and had such a great flavor that even the four year old had extra helpings! Instead of jumbo shrimp, I used a pound of medium shrimp...same amount, more individual shrimp to divide among everyone. I had a sample packet of KC Masterpiece steak seasoning, which worked well for this. We had it with Linguini with Creamy Spinach #76652, which balanced nicely with the garlic shrimp. I think next time we'll have to increase the recipe because everyone was left wanting more...and since it's a high-protein dinner that the kids will eat and that I can make so quickly, I know we'll be having it quite a bit. Thanks so much for posting!

attributes.source_text: even the four year old had extra helpings
a high-protein dinner that the kids will eat
it's a high-protein dinner

reviews.review_text: Not sure I need to write a review on this recipe with large list of all the others.... but I prepared this last night to top our caesar salad and by unanimous hands this was a 5 star recipe.  I used Old Bay seasoning to replace the pepper flakes (as suggested by others) and it made the shrimp a bit too salty... No big deal, next time I will just as less or half peppers and 1/8 tstp seasoning.  These are wonderful cold but my boys preferred them warm from the pan.  Thank you, this will be etched into my cookbook. :)

attributes.source_text: my boys preferred them warm from the pan

reviews.review_text: Om, nom, nom. SO good. Had some frozen, cooked shrimp that needed to be used and they worked perfectly in this recipe. Didn't have any Montreal seasoning so I substituted another seasoning mix that I had on hand and use often.  I had about 24 shrimp so I doubled the ingredients, and since the shrimp were already cooked I just cooked them long enough to warm them through, then removed them. I then simmered the sauce for a few minutes on the stovetop so it could thicken up, and added the shrimp back to it. Served it with a side of brown rice. Delicious. We'll definitely be making this again. Thanks!

I'm not going to select any stars because I don't want to lower your overall rating -- but this was just not the dish for us.  I love hot stuff -- but it was a little too hot for me.  I think I'll just stick to Shrimp Scampi.  I KNOW this has to be a great recipe -- as evidenced by all the stars it has received.  So on behalf of all of those folks, thanks for posting a recipe that has been so very popular.  I'll search around for some of your other recipes to try.  Happy cooking.  Bobbie

This was soooo easy to make and even more easier to eat! The Montreal steak spice an was awesome addition and actually gave off some heat of it's own. I planned on serving this for dinner which included a 4 and 2 year old and even with the heat they gobbled it up! (I did minus the pepper flakes though) I also used the frozen shrimp which I thawed out. I used way more garlic though as we are a garlic loving family, and I threw in some chopped mushrooms about half way through so they weren't soggy but were still cooked and seasoned. GREAT recipe! I served with Lois' So Yummy Baked Potato Salad and Lisa Hayward's Breaded Porkchops. My dinner was a hit that night!

attributes.source_text: actually gave off some heat of it's own
I planned on serving this for dinner
a 4 and 2 year old and even with the heat they gobbled it up
so they weren't soggy

reviews.review_text: I ended up increasing this recipe to make 3 pounds of shrimp for a small party.  I did 3 batches total.  By the time I was putting the second batch on the serving platter on the buffet the first batch was almost gone.  Same was true with the third.  Then they were wiping out the bowl with bread!  I think the lemon zest is really what made the dish so outstanding and different than other similar dishes posted here.  GREAT DISH, went over very very well with my crowd and I'll be making it again.

attributes.source_text: for a small party

reviews.review_text: This shrimp was soooooo wonderful. We savored every last bite and can't wait to make it again. It's like a low-fat shrimp scampi, but there is nothing low-fat about the taste. I used only 1/2 the oil and had 12 jumbo shrimp from costco. Very spicy, just how we like it...but don't let that keep you from trying it, just leave out the red pepper flakes. I did not have lemon zest, so I just skipped it and I used dried parsley because it's what I had. Thank you for an instant FAVORITE!  I am editing this to note that I smashed and then chopped the garlic, I just couldn't see not eating that yummy garlic!!  And...we are having it again tonight!

attributes.source_text: Very spicy, just how we like it

reviews.review_text: This was great -- easy, quick and tasty! I used the Montreal Seasoning "25% Less Sodium" variety and it was still quite flavorful. I tripled all of the ingredients and used a little extra garlic; we just loved the flavor of the shrimp. As per another reviewer's suggestion I served it over Angel Hair Pasta in Garlic Sauce (#29172) but without the Parmesan Cheese. The dish went nicely with steamed broccoli and red bell pepper. This recipe was terrific -- thanks for posting!

All the reviewshave already said it for this recipe - quick easy & TASTY - Can't improve on something this good thanks Chippie for a recipe that will be repeated over &  over again
25 Jan 09 Made & enjoyed again. Didn't have Montreal steak spice so I used a hot spic mixture Mmmm
19 July 09 This time I used Jumbo Prawns so large that you only needed two per serving. Fabulous - Too bad that the photo really didn't capture how good they were - Great recipe

attributes.source_text: hot spic mixture Mmmm

reviews.review_text: i've been wanting to learn how to cook shrimp for a while now, but finally got the courage to do so with this super simple recipe.  I made this for our valentine dinner, along with steak, twice baked potatoes and veggies. YUM!!  My husband was blown away by how great it looked and tasted.    I made the recipe exactly as directed too - perfection!  Note: we've also have made this without garlic (we were out) and it's still good, but not quite the same.  Not perfection in my opinion, so make sure you have garlic!!

attributes.source_text: I made this for our valentine dinner
I made this for our valentine dinner
My husband was blown away by how great it looked and tasted

reviews.review_text: This recipe is amazing! It won over my picky family...we've actually had it twice this week by my husband's request! I have to say, it's a little frustrating to read through reviews because it seems as though everyone spins it to their taste or what they have on hand. While that's great, it doesn't help those who want to know what people think of the recipe as is. I prepared the shrimp exactly as the recipe directed and it turned out wonderfully!

attributes.source_text: It won over my picky family
by my husband's request

reviews.review_text:
Oh My Goosh what a wondeful recipe. I doubled the recipe and used 6 cloves of garlic. Ate the whole batch myself.
Do not omit the steak seasoning. I forgot and was trying to talk myself into a 4 from 3 star. Reread the recipe and discovered I didn't put in the steak seasoning. I immediately tossed the shrimp with the seasoning . What a world of difference it made.
The lemon juice and zest complimented the garlic perfectly. 
Thanks for the wonderful recipe.

attributes.source_text: The lemon juice and zest complimented the garlic perfectly
The lemon juice and zest complimented the garlic perfectly

items.label: Crock Pot Chicken, Gravy and Stuffing
items.name: Crock Pot Chicken, Gravy and Stuffing
items.description: Make and share this Crock Pot Chicken, Gravy and Stuffing recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper and place chicken breasts in crock pot. Pour Chicken broth over breasts.
Put one slice of Swiss  cheese on each breast. Combine both cans of soup and milk.
Cover  chicken breasts with soup mixture. Sprinkle stuffing mix over all.
Drizzle melted butter on top.
Cook on low  for 6 hours or high for 3.

reviews.review_text: I made this almost as written.  Only thing I changed was add some garlic powder along with the salt and pepper on both sides of the chicken.  I always add garlic powder to chicken otherwise the meat lacks some flavor.  I added cheese (completely covering the chicken) next so that when I poured in the chicken broth (14 oz. low sodium,upped from a cup) it wouldn't wash all the seasoning off the chicken.  I upped the milk to 1/3 cup and the stuffing (Betty Crocker Cornbread Stuffing - my favorite) to 4 cups.  I cut the butter down to about 1/3.  So other than increasing some of the amounts and adding some garlic powder, I followed the recipe exactly.  I made most of these adjustments from other reviewers suggestions.  It turned out great.  It had a wonderful gravy which was good over mashed potatoes.  Served with mixed vegetables.  I will be making this again and again.  My family told me to make sure I saved that one.  Thanks for sharing.

attributes.source_text: My family told me to make sure I saved that one

reviews.review_text: I have been wanting to try this recipe and the other day I thought to myself, Self.. you need to make this!  But I had already ran out of time for the crock pot, SO I cooked it in the oven instead ( after pan cooking the chicken in chicken broth to almost doneness ). I used two boxed stuffings and just mixed the seasoning packets with the milk/soup/broth combo.  I cut each breast in half, layed them flat, put slices of swiss over them, covered them with the breadcrumbs, then poured the liquid mixture over it all and popped that bad boy in the oven.  Oh my goodness!  The swiss cheese is something I would have never thought of and it gave it the most delicious flavor. Thank You Thank You Lusil for this wonderful recipe.  Next Time I am going to plan ahead to make it in the crock pot... but this is wonderful from the oven as well!!!!!

Wonderful, hearty recipe! I wanted to make it a truly one-pot meal so I added a layer of veggies under the chicken. I chopped carrots, parsnips, potatoes and half a large onion into big chunks, put them in the bottom of the crock pot and then sprinkled them with a little salt, pepper, garlic powder and onion powder. I  then added the chicken breasts and seasoned them the same way. I poured the chicken stock around the edges of the chicken so the seasoning wasn't disturbed. Then I layered about a cup or so of shredded Swiss cheese on top of the chicken (didn't have slices) and then the soups (I used the low sodium version). I ended up topping it off 2 cups of cubed PF stuffing mix and 2 cups of PF cornbread stuffing and drizzled it all with 1/2  cup of melted butter.  I cooked it on low for 6 hours and we came home to a wonderful feast! Not only was it a complete, delicious meal but clean-up was a snap! I had lined my crock-pot with a roasting bag so there was nothing to scrub or even rinse off afterward. A total win! Thanks for a wonderful recipe.

OK, I won't bring down the rating for this recipe since everyone seems to love it.  But this was a disaster.  It is not necessarily the fault of the recipe, but I made this in my 6-qt crockpot which runs very hot.  I followed the recipe exactly, did not change anything.  When I got home from work, the entire recipe was stuck to the bottom.  And the stuffing was black.  I did not consider this edible.  My husband insisted on sampling it.  I scraped a spoonful for him and he said that it was ok, just overdone.  So I tried some, and it was extremely salty.  Of course, the liquid had reduced so much that I guess that shouldn't be surprising.  I had only cooked it for 6 hours.  So just be careful, if you have a hot crockpot, you may need to cook it much less.  I may attempt this again, but only if I will be around to keep an eye on it.

Comfort food that is so easy and DELICIOUS! I have made this many times now and all have been great but my fav changes are to sprinkle poultry seasoning and pepper on the chicken, omit the cheese, and use cornbread instead of the bread stuffing mix. To my crumbled cornbread, I add chopped onion, celery, bell pepper, mushrooms, parsley, sage-just like you would make your stuffing but I bet Stove Top Cornbread mix would be great, too. I also like to add veggies like baby carrots, peas, green beans, kernel corn for all-in-one meal. This is also great w/ pork chops and you can add some sour cream to change it up a bit. In my crock pot I love to use the liners and my chicken is fully cooked in 3 hours on low. And of course, serve w/ cranberry sauce! Thank you, Anne, for a great recipe!!!

it was 3pm and i was wanting some chicken and stuffing. being pregnany and super lazy this recipe was exactly what i was looking for. this turned out really good and talk about tasty! this one would get 5*s from us w/ a few adjustments. i used frozen chicken breasts, just put them in the pot right out of the freezer. i used Recipe #57287 instead of the canned soup, just dumped it in hot on top of the frozen chicken, broth, and cheese. I used cheddar/jack cheese as we didn't have any swiss and couldn't even tell it was in there so next time i'll probably leave it out all together.  I used my own dried bread cubes and next time i'll double up the stuffing as others did so there will be more of it.  it was also a bit salty for us, next time i won't use any extra salt at all. i cooked it 3 hrs on high in my old crock pot and it came out great. i have to say i'd be hesitant about cooking it for 6 hrs on low, mainly because it seems like the stuffing would turn to mush. but i usually forget to put the crock pot on till later anyway so the 3hr cook time was perfect for us. i'm tempted to try this sometime w/ biscuits on top instead of the stuffing, hummm.... but this will definitely be a regular in this house, thanks for a keeper! :)

This is definately 5 star!!! I made this last night with a few changes. First I didn't have swiss cheese so I used mozzerella cheese. I couldn't find the pepperidge farb herb stuffing so I used pepperidge farm cornbread stuffing. Oh and I used 5 chicken breasts instead of four just because of our family size, and used 3 cups of stuffing. It turned out awesome!! I also did as someone else mentioned and used some poultry seasoning on the chicken. 
My son who is 2 now is extremely picky. I made this with mashed potatoes and gave him his taters and chicken and he ate ALL of his supper....which is VERY rare for him!!
It's gone under favorites now and we will definately have this again!!

attributes.source_text: he ate ALL of his supper

reviews.review_text: A real winner. Made exactly as stated w/ only one substitution no butter on hand so melted 1/4 cup Smart Balance spread. Worked just fine. I used perhaps a bit more cheese, my slices were approx 4x4 so I used two per breast and overlapped them a bit. Plugged her in at 10am and we ate at 5:30. The chicken was VERY tender. Wonderful on a rainy night. Next time I will add the 3rd cup of stuffing as others have suggested. Thanks for a great and so simple meal. Update: I made this again using Pepperidge Farm stuffing and it came out very mushy. Previously I had used a crouton like stuffing from Mrs. Cubison which held together nicely. The PF was too crushed to begin with for such a long cooking time. Update: Made again for the third time. This time I used healthy request soups and reduced fat swiss cheese. The result was great!

attributes.source_text: The chicken was VERY tender

reviews.review_text: I added onions and baby carrots under the boneless chicken- chicken breasts were frozen- and I added about 1/4 cup of white wine to the stock, reducing the soup to just one can. I used Pepperidge Farm sage stuffing mix, but as the other testers stated, I would add more dry stuffing mix on the top next time, to soak up more of the juices on top. I cooked it on high for 4 hours.Tasted wonderful, chicken  was falling apart tender and no dryness from being frozen. I added mashed potatoes on the side, and it was a great tasting, roast chicken dinner that was so easy. I love that you can use frozen boneless chicken and it turns out great! Sometimes I forget to thaw the chicken overnight in the fridge, and I am left in the morning scrambling before work, with out the main ingredient for my slowcooker easy dinner! This solves the problem and it's really good!  Great cold weather dinner too!

attributes.source_text: no dryness from being frozen
a great tasting, roast chicken dinner

reviews.review_text: I made this last night.   My husband is not a fan of chicken or stuffing, but I wanted to see if he would at least try this.  He raved about it.  I was shocked.  He even took leftovers to work to eat at lunch today.  My two daughters, one who is picky, didn't want any of it, until I convinced her to try it.  Then she ate the whole plate.  My other daughter only ate the chicken because she doesn't care for stuffing...but don't go by her, she's a typical teenager! It was delicious.  There was a lot of liquid, soup and such, compared to the stuffing I think I may add a bit more stuffing next time.  Also I didn't have the 6-8 hrs. to cook this, so I took the suggestion of another reviewer and used frozen chicken and cooked it on high for 3.5 hrs.  I think that may be why my swiss cheese melted into my soup.  It gave the soup a cheesey delicious flavor though.  Next time I will use thawed chicken and use the 6-8 hrs on low and see what is different. My crockpot is round and it is quite big but I still had to stack a little of the chicken on top of each other, that may be another reason why things slid off into the soup. Anyway, if I can get a non-chicken eater and my picky wickys to eat this and like it, I will definitely make it again.

Very easy and tasted wonderful with mashed potatoes and asparagus. The gravy tasted very homemade and not like "canned soup"! I can't wait to make this in the crock pot. reviews.review_text: This is our favorite "new" recipe! Comfort food! Unfortunately I changed it so much it is really different but you get the same type results.  I use 6 small boneless chicken breast in crockpot, 3 to 4 98% fat free condensed cans cream of chicken soup over top of chicken and then sprinkle one package of low sodium chicken flavored stuffing on top.  No broth, no butter, no milk, no cheese.  FANTASTIC! I only changed it because I wanted less fat. Thanks for a great recipe for me to tweak to our liking!  I like to use frozen chicken breasts and cook on high for two hours and then low for two hours.

Comfort food at its best; and so easy!!  I didn't have the PF herb stuffing, but did have bread cubes.  I wanted to try this recipe without having to run out to the store, so I let them out to get somewhat hard and stale.  Added tarragon, rosemary, sage, poultry seasoning, parsely and onion powder and used this instead. Otherwise, made as posted except used three chicken breasts and just 1 can cream of mushroom.  Because I used the bread cubes, the stuffing was a bit "mushy", but the flavor was delicious! Served it with peas and carrots. This tasted like a Thanksgiving meal without any of the hard work! Thanks for a wonderful recipe.

items.label: Roast "Sticky" Chicken
items.name: Roast "Sticky" Chicken
items.description: Beautiful and delicious, this incredibly moist roasted Chicken puts Kenny Roger's Roasters, Boston Market, and other rotisserie style chickens to shame! Please don't let the word "overnight" mislead you; for actual hands-on preparation, this is  a Quick-N-Easy way to impress Sunday dinner guests!
instructions: (Day 1) Blend all spices together and set aside.
Remove neck and giblets from chicken cavity, rinse well inside and out, and pat dry with paper towels.
Rub with spice mixture, both inside and out, then stuff cavity with onions.
Wrap in a resealable\
plastic bag (I just use a new, unscented, white kitchen can liner.), tie closed, and refrigerate overnight.
(Day 2) Remove from plastic bag and place in a shallow baking pan.
Roast uncovered in a 250 F oven 5 hours.
(This is not an error, I repeat, 250 F for 5 hours!) If the chicken contains a pop-up thermometer, ignore it.
This recipe is SAFE.
According to the United States Department of Agriculture Food Safety and Inspection Service, a whole chicken should reach an internal temperature of 180 F.
For more info check out their\
campign Web site! http://www.fsis.usda.gov/thermy/index.htm
Baste with drippings every 30 minutes after the first hour.
(I admit I'm not consistent on this point, but it still comes out wonderful!) Let rest for 10 minutes before carving.

reviews.review_text:
Call me chicken but couldn't do it at 250' 
My grocer had wonderful 5# roasters on sale, your recipe looked yummy and so many reviews WOW. I followed but roasted it in a Reynolds® Oven Bag @ 325' for 21/4hrs 170' internal temp. TURNED OUT WONDERFULLY. 

Did check http://www.fsis.usda.gov/thermy/index.htm 
This is what I found
The minimum oven temperature to use when cooking chicken is 325 degrees F. Using a food thermometer is the only sure way of knowing if your food has reached a high enough temperature to destroy foodborne bacteria. All poultry should reach a safe minimum internal temperature of 165 degrees F as measured with a food thermometer. A whole chicken must reach a minimum internal temperature of 165 F throughout the bird. Check the internal temperature in the innermost part of the thigh and wing and the thickest part of the breast. For reasons of personal preference, consumers may choose to cook poultry to higher temperatures. For approximate cooking times for chicken, go to: Focus on: Chicken <http://www.fsis.usda.gov/fact_sheets/Chicken_Food_Safety_Focus/index.asp>.

I originally got this recipe from another recipe site and have made it many times.  In fact, I won't make a whole chicken hardly any other way!

The changes that I made were that I only used 2 teaspoons of salt instead of 4 and I used 1 C. of onion instead of the 2 large onions.  I cut them into large pieces and then stuffed them inside.  I also put this in the crockpot for about 8 hours on low.  Who wants their oven going for so long when it's hot outside?  It was falling off the bone tender when I cut it.

I agree with everyone else that this is quite a messy recipe, but it's to be expected since it's a rub.  I also agree with another reviewer in that you shouldn't use a trash bag to cover your chicken.  I used two clear plastic food storage bags.

This recipe is a definite keeper.

reviews.review_text: Really delicious!  I used the rub as written and found the combination to be fine for our family, kids and all.  I read the various opinions on the slow-cooking method this recipe calls for and the concerns. For my own info, I looked up the government website and found a section on 'slow cooking' for chicken. http://www.fsis.usda.gov/Fact_Sheets/Focus_On_Slow_Cooker_Safety/index.asp   It states: "The direct heat from the pot, lengthy cooking and steam created within the tightly-covered container combine to destroy bacteria and make the slow cooker a safe process for cooking foods."  So with that, I felt more comfortable using my Necco Roaster which has a cover.  Turned out great!  I would suggest that those cooking in the ovven use a roasting pan with a lid as well to be safe.  Pam :-)

reviews.review_text: Holy Moly! Best roast chicken ever! I changed up the cooking method to 350 degrees for three hours instead of the 250 for five. I have immune issues, so I didn't really want to take a chance. I also made this at the last minute, so an overnight marination wasn't possible, I just slapped on the rub and into the oven it went. I added smashed garlic to the cavity along with the onions. The bird roasted beautifully and held up during the resting period and carving, but the carcass collapsed after the meat was removed (A sure sign of quality roast chicken!). I used the pan drippings and caramelized onion that fell out of the bird during roasting to make a gravy. I just added 3 tbsp of flour, cooked it for three minutes, added 2 cups of water and brought it to a boil until it thickened. The result was a gorgeous, thick chicken and onion gravy that really complimented the meat. I served it with herb stuffing and steamed green, yellow wax beans, and carrots and corn muffins. This made a fabulous Easter dinner. This recipe will now be my standard roast chicken recipe. Thank you very much for sharing this winner!

reviews.review_text: WOWZA!  We just finished dinner, and this chicken was a HIT!  I made the spice rub exactly as the recipe stated, and the only change I made was to stuff the chicken with an onion and a lemon.  I let the chicken marinate in a poultry baking bag overnight, and pulled it out of the fridge about half an hour before I started to bake it.  I always bring meat to room temperature for even cooking.  I lined my baking dish with raw potatoes and carrots tossed in a little olive oil, salt, and black pepper to make a one dish meal.  I put the chicken on top of the veggies and cooked it as the recipe stated.   I let it rest (very important step) for about 10 minutes before carving.   There are 2 of us, and half of the chicken is now gone!  I loved the carrots that cooked with the chicken too: next time I might just add all carrots since they were really tasty.  DH said this was a keeper, and he really doesn't care one way or another about roasted chicken.  I can't wait to make a chicken sandwich tomorrow out of the leftovers!  Next time I think I am going to make 2 chickens, since I can already think of dozen of things to do with the leftovers.   Thank you for sharing a great recipe!  This is truly a keeper!!

reviews.review_text: Yum. Yum. YUM! Five star fabulousness! I was expecting a huge mess with all the "messy" reviews, but it wasn't so bad. I skipped the bag and seasoned my 6lb bird right in my 9x13 glass pan. I stuffed one quartered onion, 5 cloves of sliced garlic inside, 2 whole sprigs of fresh rosemary, covered it with plastic wrap, and stuck it in the fridge. When I was ready to roast it, all I had to do was take the plastic wrap off, and stick it right in the oven. I added a 1/2 cup white wine and 1/2 cup chicken broth and a few pats of butter. I sliced potatoes and added them the last four hours... they weren't quite done with one hour to go, so I raised the temp to 350. Everything was unbelievable PERFECT. Made gravy with the drippings, homemade rolls, green beans, and wild rice. The kids could hardly stop eating it, and my very picky hubby was impressed! I'm going to turn the leftovers into a yummy chicken and wild rice soup. Can't wait to try this method with a turkey!!!

After marinating it with the spice mixture (exactly as listed) for two days in a food grade plastic bag - the mix was rubbed both under and on top of the skin -and stuffing it with sliced onions (removed before inverting it onto the beer can/holder), I cooked it on our gas grill, keeping it at an average temperature of about 375 degrees for close to two hours, till golden brown and the juices ran clear. Using the beer can method made it unnecessary to baste, and when I carved it, the meat was incredibly moist and tender - absolutely wonderful. Love the spice mix, it adds so much flavor without being overwhelming.

items.label: Uncle Bill's Microwave Potato Chips
items.name: Uncle Bill's Microwave Potato Chips
items.description: These potato chips are very easy to make in the microwave. Also, they are healthier for you as they are not cooked in any oils. This method has intrigued so many people that have tasted them and then made them for themselves. The younger people just love them.
instructions: If potatoes are old, peel and slice thin, less than 1/16\
in thickness (paper thin), slicing across the potato.
Place potato slices in a bowl, sprinkle with some salt (if desired) cover with cold water and let sit for 10 minutes.
Remove potato slices in batches onto paper toweling and pat dry.
If you have a microwave bacon tray, rub the tray with a vegetable oil, then place the sliced potatoes flat on the tray in a single layer.
Sprinkle with your choice of herbs or spices or just leave them plain.
Cover with a microwaveable, round heavy plastic cover.
Microwave on HIGH (full power) for 5 to 5 1/2 minutes or until they curl slightly and are a very light brown in color.
Cooking time could vary slightly, depending on the wattage of your microwave and the thickness of the slices.  The thinner the slices, the quicker they cook and the tastier they are.
You do not have to turn the sliced potatoes over.
If you do not have a bacon tray, use a microwave safe casserole dish.
Rub the inside of the dish with some olive oil for the first batch of potato chips.
I do not know why, but I find that if you do not rub oil the first time, some chips will tend to stick to the dish.
After the first batch is done, you do not have to rub the dish again.
Continue to microwave the remainder of sliced potatoes as noted above.
If using a bacon tray, after the first batch is cooked, you can reduce the microwaving time to 4 1/2 minutes and even less as you continue to microwave each batch.

NOTE:  You can also use PARCHMENT PAPER to microwave the potato slices.  Lightly spray or rub the parchment paper with some vegetable oil or a Pam spray. Place your potato slices on the parchment paper, then sprinkle them with whatever you like and then place another piece of parchment paper on top.  This will help microwave the  potatoes more evenly and they should turn out nice and crisp.  Microwaving time should be between 5 and 6 minutes.
ADDITIONAL IDEAS, suggested by Deb K:
Granulated garlic powder with parsley.
Cracked black pepper, grated parmesan and sea salt sprinkled after removing from microwave.
Another, after removing chips from microwave, sprinkle with grated cheddar cheese, zap for a few seconds to melt the cheese, then add a dab of sour cream.
A great dip is Robert Rothschild Farm Dips:
Emerald Isle Onion Dill and Horseradish Dip.

reviews.review_text: Thank you so much Uncle Bill, you had the timing just right on these!  You weren't kidding when you said there is no need to turn the potato slices.  I was playing around w/how best to use my microwave for crispy potatoes.  My first batch, I used a microwave safe plate, and sprayed it w/Pam, laid one layer of slices, sprayed slices w/Pam, and sprinkled Seasoned Salt.  I microwaved on high for 4mins and then turned slices, sprinkled again w/seasoned salt and micro'd again for 2mins, and kept repeating the 2mins on each side for what seemed like forever.  So I got impatient and though they were completely cooked thru and prob ready to cool off, I tossed em under the broiler for 3mins each side.  They were less like potato chips and more like crispy baked fries; but your method worked amazingly simple.  I micro'd the second batch for 7mins, no need to spray Pam again, either.  7mins was a bit long, I prob should have started w/5 and worked forward (I got one burnt chip), but the rest browning up PERFECT and I was surprised at how good they tasted.  Thanks for posting a better way to make homemade chips! :)  I'm eating them for breakfast, lol.  Oh well, at least they are healthy!

reviews.review_text: Uncle Bill, these are wonderful! My brother wanted something for an evening snack this evening and he insisted on getting potatoes! That split second I decided I would try out this recipe. I did and I'm so glad I did that. I used 3 medium-sized potatoes(peeled and thinly sliced), 1/4 tsp. black pepper and 1/2 tsp. salt. I mixed it all nicely together in a microwave bowl and microwaved these chips on HIGH power level for 7 minutes 29 seconds to be precise! Please note that I did not apply any oil to my bowl and these chips were wonderful - they did not stick to the bowl, though I admit, they did stick to each other, but that was fine, really. They scooped out beautifully and I served them to bro with some tomato ketchup on the side. He was really delighted when I told him that these are no oil French fries! He was really thrilled on hearing that. Thank you so much for posting this recipe. No more of the French fries on the stove with oil and the mess of draining the excess oil on kitchen paper napkins. We'll go with this recipe hereafter! A thousand thanks!

attributes.source_text: something for an evening snack
He was really delighted

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe today along with a batch of â€œoven-friedâ€� chips. While the oven chips were good, this microwave recipe is perfect as I got uniformly brown crisps chips. My entire family (which includes a 3 year old and a 6 year old) loved them! I used my pizza stone (as noted by an earlier reviewer) and cooked the chips uncovered (this helped me monitor them too). There was a little olive oil on the stone from my oven-fry trial other than that I did not add any additional oil. I used my food processor to slice the potatoes which gave me uniformly thin/even chips. I kept it simple this time using only sea salt for flavor. Cooking Time: The first batch cooked approximately 15 minutes.  I canâ€™t be exact because I started with 7 minutes and kept restarting the time until the chips turned brown and were crunchy. Reading earlier posts and seeing pictures helped, so did taste tasting. (If they are soft, they have not finished cooking and the thicker the slice the longer it will take)  My second batch only needed 9 minutes.  I plan to try this with other â€œchip-ableâ€� vegetables as we are on a quest to find healthy AND tasty snacks.
