reviews.review_text: These are just great!  I have made these a few times now, although with different results.  The first time I followed the recipe and the rolls were too dark on top, a little doughy, and they didn't rise much.  The second time I thought I would try whole wheat flour, and that was just a flop because they didn't rise at all, so they were small dense lumps!  The third time I was able to perfect the recipe.  I stuck with the bread flour but let them rise 1-2 hours and then followed the other reviews and lowered the oven temp to 350 degrees and baked for 15 minutes.  Thanks for the recipe, it will be a huge hit at Thanksgiving this year!

Made these yesterday for Hamburger Night at our house.. and all I can say is, "WOW!"  They.  Are.  Awesome!  I followed many of the tips given by other reviewers and turned out a batch of 16 fragrant, fluffy, soft, buttery rolls that were not only easy but fun to make.<br/><br/>I shaped the rolls and baked 16 of them for our dinner.  I then froze the remaining 12 on a cookie sheet and then wrapped each dough ball individually in plastic wrap and put them in a zip-lock bag.  This way I can just pop one or two - or the whole bagful - into the oven for baking in a snap.<br/><br/>We loved these rolls... and I especially liked the technique one reviewer gave for how to form the rolls.  They came out beautifully shaped and baked like a dream.<br/><br/>I am new to homemade bread-making, and this was my first attempt at making rolls.  I won't need another recipe... This is it!

reviews.review_text: I made this twice in two days.  The first time I used half regular flour, did 2 one hour rises and baked at 350-- the rolls were very good but a little too "biscuit-like".  Today I used only regular (all purpose) flour, and I cut the egg to 1.  They were GREAT!!  I don't use a bread machine, but I did keep track, and I used just a little less than 4 cups of flour... probably just a tablespoon or two less.  Next time, I'm going to put half the butter in at the beginning, then I'm going to cube or coarsely grate the other 1/4 cup and incorporate it (cold) into the dough just before forming the rolls, hoping I'll get even flakier rolls.

I ABSOLUTELY LOVE THIS RECIPE! I don't heat the milk, and it works just fine for me. Sometimes its cold, right out of the fridge. I have even used powdered milk. My machine calls for wet ingredients first, then dry. I put margarine, eggs (fresh eggs) salt, sugar in first. Then I add the flour, put a little dent in flour and add 1 Tablespoon of yeast. 375 is too hot for my oven. 350 degrees is plenty and I cook them for about 15 minutes until they are golden brown on top. I've made these for dozens of family events, public events, potlucks, and EVERYONE has loved them. I do NOT turn them and knead or do anything to them! I take them from the machine and put them right into the pan. Take a piece of dough and shape a ball, then make an "O" with your them and pointer finger. I press the dough through that hole and press the back of ball together to make a beautiful roll. Learned this from my mother. Then, put in a greased 13 x 9 pan and spray the tops as well. You can also make the clover type rolls, by making three small balls and pressing them carefully into muffin tins. I have also made fry bread with this recipe. Roll out dough and fry. I have also made bread sticks. Just add garlic salt instead of salt. Then shape how you wish, and brush butter on top. I accidentally figured out how to make hamburger buns tonight. I didn't put enough flour so the dough was very sticky and hard to work with. I did it anyway and shaped my "rolls" the best I could. After they rose I put them in the oven and they had sort of "melted" is what I call it, to form hamburger buns.. They were AMAZING.. Needless to say, this recipe is easy to use, (my first bread machine recipe) and very versatile. Just follow your directions on your bread machine and have fun with this!! :) Thanks for posting Jean, this will ALWAYS be a family favorite!

reviews.review_text: I must agree with all the commenters, this is a wonderful recipe. I was completely out of milk, buttermilk and heavy cream; all of which are staples in my fridge. So, I improvised with adding a touch of water to sour cream. I then proofed the yeast in the sour cream with a pinch of sugar. My husband, who doesn't normally like soft white breads truly loved these rolls. I mixed garlic powder in melted butter and slathered it on right before they went into the oven. You won't regret making these rolls. Almost foolproof. Try using sour cream,plain yogurt or buttermilk instead of milk.

items.name: General Tso's Chicken
items.description: Wow! This is even better than the BEST I have had in my fave Chinese restaurant. To make the meal go quickly prep everything the day or night before and store in the fridge. To make this easy to understand I have changed the terms to cornstarch slurry and sauce. The first is used to coat the chicken for frying, the second to coat the fried chicken. HTH I use a grater with small holes for the garlic or you can just zip all the sauce ingredients up in a blender or food processor. Enjoy! NOTE: I really appreciate all the reviews this recipe has received. I know that when making this it seems strange and like it just is not going to work. Trust that it will work even though the method and the way that the cornstarch slurry acts before cooking are so different. I was the same way the first time I made this. It does result in crispy pieces of chicken that are so like you find in a restaurant. The heat here is pretty much a balanced amount because some like it hot and some do not. Taste and add more heat as desired. Thanks again for trying this recipe. I hope that you have the great results that I have had time and again. Here is info, pics and heat levels of different chilies. http://www.foodsubs.com/Chilefre.html
instructions: Place sauce ingredients in a quart jar with a lid and shake to mix. If you make this ahead of time just refrigerate until needed, shaking it again when you are ready to use it. This also keeps your dirty dishes down.

Mix cornstarch slurry in a large bowl- the mixture will be strange but trust me it works. It will be VERY thick almost paste like. Add ALL the chicken pieces and stir to coat. Using a fork remove ONE chicken piece at a time and let the excess mixture drip off. YES even though the mixture has a weird consistency it will not stick like paste and the excess will drip off. Add chicken to the hot (350 degree) oil and fry until crispy. Only cook 7 or 8 chicken pieces at a time. You do not want to lower the temp of the oil by cooking too many at a time. You can use a simple cooking or candy thermometer to judge the temp of the oil.
Drain on paper towels. Want them extra crispy? Put them on a rack over a sheet pan. Keep warm- I just put them in the oven with the oven off. Repeating until all chicken is fried.

In a separate wok or large skillet add a small amount of oil and heat to 400 degrees. Again, a candy thermometer works great. (Want less dishes?  You can just drain the oil after you fry all the chicken, leave a small amount (about a tsp) in the pan and use the same pan if you like.)
Add green onions and hot peppers and stir fry about 30 seconds.
Stir (or shake jar) sauce mixture, and then add to pan with onions and peppers, cook until thick. Some reviews didn't kniw what \

meant. Thick like the same sauce you get at a restaurant.you want it to just coat the chicken. If it gets too thick, add a little water or other liquid. The thickness of the sauce should be similar to what you get when ordering this at a restaurant.
Add chicken to sauce in wok and heat just until the chicken is hot enough for you. It may not even need a minute if you kept the chicken warm. The quicker you serve it the crispier the chicken stays.

Don't be scared by any negative reviews. It's not rocket science though if you have never cooked with a cornstarch slurry it may feel like an experiment. Trust yourself! You've got this! If you have any doubts reread the recipe and get everything in order before you start to cook. I promise you will thank yourself and maybe even me! Enjoy!
Oh it's great served over rice!

reviews.review_text:
We were actually very impressed with this recipe, given the questionable comments of some who have previously tried it and disliked it. Here are my suggestions: First, it WILL take you longer than 40 minutes to make this if it's your first time. My husband and I both worked at this and it took us about an hour and a half total...

Make the sauce ahead, that would help! For the sauce, I would recommend using brown sugar in the sauce instead of regular white sugar, and I would decrease the cornstarch a bit to 1/3 a cup because it did turn out thicker than it should have with 1/2 cup starch. I also added about a tablespoon of fresh ginger which is actually a very important flavor in this dish.

As for the slurry, it is the most bizarre thing I've ever cooked with, but if you put all the chicken in it at once (NOT piece by piece) it just works and magically coats the chicken, even though you think it won't. Then leave it in there until you're literally dropping it into the oil to cook. We used a deep fryer to cook our chicken. First we put it in at 350 until it was nice and brown. It will not be that crispy at first, that's why the second fry is so important. Once they were all done cooking at 350, instead of putting chicken in a pan of 400 degree oil, we kicked up the heat on our deep fryer to 400 and put them back in for a second fry. It was just easier for us to keep track of the temp that way. Then we kept warm in our toaster oven until we were ready to put them in the sauce. They were definitely a lot crisper after the second time frying!

Lastly, I would not add the chicken to the sauce until you are practically ready to plate it. It will decrease the chance of it losing crispiness. We put our chicken in the thickened sauce right before plating it, gave it a minute over heat to make it bubble and it came out WONDERFUL. We will definitely make this again with these few modifications.

attributes.source_text: a very important flavor in this dish
They were definitely a lot crisper after the second time frying

reviews.review_text: I’m British & though we have loads of Chinese Takeaways, we do not have a meal called ‘General Tso’s’. I googled it when I first heard of it, so I know the history but had no pre-conceived idea of restaurant taste, how it’s served & therefore expectation. I don’t know what the original terms were referred to in the description but surely the terms batter & sauce are easy to understand? The only difference is that soy sauce is used instead of milk as Chinese people don’t use dairy products. I didn’t find the batter a slurry consistency either (like a clay/coal mixture running off a mountain?), it was a ‘cement’ consistency as someone mentioned, more a volcanic lava consistency, but other than that did not behave in any strange way. Thermometers seem very new-fangled & high-tech to me, I was taught that if a fresh bread cube browned in 1 minute, that the oil was hot enough. The appearance, swell & shimmer of oil when hot enough is like telling when the tide is about to start coming in, it is something you learn & gives you confidence with experience that is much better than when said gadget has gone west & you can also pass this on to children. (Like sell-by-dates, I didn’t have these in greengrocers or butchers). I like the fact that you bothered to explain that too many pieces lower oil temperature, not many recipes mention that & people make the mistake of adding more pieces because a pan is big, the pieces should continue to lightly sizzle. The picture showed a thick sauce as commented on; I made mine a little thinner by adding 100ml water; I served with steamed broccoli as shown mixed with fried beansprouts & cauliflower with a sauce of rice wine, ginger, garlic as well as boiled/fried rice to accompany. I have given 4 stars because I could taste the cornflour, this may be because my oil was not hot enough, as despite my knowledge about bread cubes, I am a wimp about hot oil – but they did fry nicely; I also put them under the grill to keep warm which dried them out. We have similar battered pieces in Britain called sweet & sour; whichever sauce is used, do not add until serving as otherwise any batter will go soggy. I think they are fine reheated under grill or in oven but a microwave probably won’t bring back the crispiness (and DO NOT add sauce to any pieces that you want to reheat later!). Maybe Chinese people don’t use Western cornflour/cornstarch? Maybe rice flour? I will try rice flour but next time I will try Chapatti flour – I know it’s Indian but it’s a very, very fine grain (wholemeal) – I shall use a bit less than the cornflour. I will add the ginger & cashews like another poster too. I thoroughly enjoyed this, thank you. ?

I just made this, and I really can't believe I actually made something that tastes like food you'd get from a Chinese restaurant! It was absolutely delicious. I made the sauce last night, and I used 14 restaurant packets of soy sauce to make 1/2 cup, and I substituted Dole Pine-Orange Banana juice for the wine, and I totally omitted the chicken broth (on accident, I just now realized that while writing this!). I only used 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts, and I'm not sure how many lbs that would be, maybe around 1 lb? I used 8 restaurant soy sauce packets for the 1/4 cup of soy sauce. The cornstarch batter is really weird! I originally used 7 packets of soy sauce, and it was tough to get it to coat the chicken pieces, but adding another packet was perfect. I used some crushed red pepper instead of the dried chilies. I served it with rice and Birds Eye Steamfresh veggies (the kind that you just throw the whole bag in the microwave), broccoli, carrots, sugar snap peas, and water chestnuts blend. It was an immensely delicious meal for two, and we had enough leftovers that we'll make another meal of it. I can't believe I totally forgot the chicken broth. I thought it was delicious without it though, because it would have been REALLY runny sauce with all that extra liquid, though you probably would have needed it for all the chicken the recipe calls for. I didn't have that much coating left over, because at first I was using it too thick, and it made coating puddles around the chicken. Didn't hurt it though, it was still tasty! It does take quite some time to make, but I think it's well worth it!

attributes.source_text: tastes like food you'd get from a Chinese restaurant

reviews.review_text: I have made this recipe twice, first time following directions exactly (having never made general tso before) I found i had to adjust the Slurry to get it usable. First the Slurry : It was to hard to work with but i added an extra egg a a pinch more of corn starch to get it to the right consistency. with the addition of another egg it smoothed the Slurry out and i could manage to actually coat the chicken bits for frying. it the extra egg makes it to liquid just add a small amount of cornstarch until the consistency is right. I then made everything else as they listed in the recipe. The outcome tasted nothing like the local Chinese place, but it was ok. I thought it tasted to strongly of Soy Sauce as did my family, but it wasn't wasted. I knew this recipe had potential, so i decided to give it another go. This time making adjustments.<br/><br/>I had to add the egg to the slurry again. I adjusted the sauce recipe (thanks Anderspt02 for your informative review) adding Orange Juice and Ginger. Only I cut the Soy Sauce in half as well as the water and used Orange Juice to sub. We like it spicy at my house so I also added a bit Sambal Oelek . While the second try did not taste like the Chinese place it was better then the first go round. I will definitely make this again with the adjustments. I have a wonderful flavor and my family enjoyed it (I have a finicky child)

attributes.source_text: my family enjoyed it

reviews.review_text:
Thank you for this recipe! I'm glad you made mention of the slurry consistency, otherwise it would have been very confusing. (If you have ever mixed corstarch and water to create a fun putty as a science experiment with kids, it's exactly the same consistency. The putty seems to flow when it's treated gently and is very tough and resistent when you try to mix it hard or poke it or punch it.)

Like another reviewer I added the juice of an orange, but I did this as an afterthought after tasting the finished sauce. We find our restaurants' versions have a fruity taste, even when ordering General Tso's instead of Orange Chicken, though they are very similar. The additional liquid and the late addition didn't compromise the sauce at all.

Because of poor planning on my part and sensitive palates, I didn't add chilies, rather I added a small amount (1/4 t.) of Vietnamese Chili Garlic sauce in with the scallions. If you do this be careful of popping and splattering as you add it. I also neglected to buy a can of chicken broth and substituted boullion with water, though I'm sure boosting the sodium content, so next time I will be better prepared.

I topped half of a platter with the chicken and the other half with steamed broccoli, served with steamed rice and some sliced oranges and my whole family loved it down to the smallest kid (3 years old). What we appreciate most is that this saved us our entertainment budget for the month which would have surely been fully spent had we gone out for a Chinese restaurant meal.

If you have the luxury of 2 hands in the kitchen this is a breeze. One person can mind the fryer while the other prepares the sauce and steams the broccoli, cuts oranges and (next time) brews a nice pot of Chinese tea!

Next time we'll add some sesame oil with the sauce's fry oil and toss the finished chicken with toasted sesame seeds for a little variety. Or we'll toss in some orange peel in the fryer to add to the sauce while it comes together for orange chicken. Thanks for opening up the possibility for us to do these favorites at home.

attributes.source_text: my whole family loved it
down to the smallest kid (3 years old)
have a fruity taste

reviews.review_text: I was excited to try this recipe since we've been craving General Tso's Chicken for some time now and haven't been able to find a restaurant that makes it quite as well as they do in our hometown.  I followed the instructions exact, absolutely no changes were made.  Now, I've been cooking for many years and although I'm no 5 star chef, I'd like to think I know my way pretty well around the kitchen.  I agree with others who say that the prep & cook times are way off.  It took me somewhere in between 1-2 hours total.  I went through all the necessary steps though I fried it in a deep fryer.  I would strongly advise against this.  The "slurry" coating leaked through the bottom of the basket which caused the pieces of chicken to "fuse" to it.  It was a pain trying to get all of the pieces off, though I eventually did and lost a bit of breading on the bottom due to it.  The breading was not crispy at all this way as it is from the restaurants, the best way to describe it is that it had more of a thicker McD's chicken nugget texture to it.  Maybe it would've been crunchier had I have pan fried them.  I was not impressed with the "sauce" at all, either.  It was very thick and gooey as it cooked, so I thinned it down with water as was suggested.  Though as it sat for a bit, it gained a more gelatinous consistency rather than a sauce.  Maybe this could be avoided by omitting the cornstarch in the "sauce," it was just far too much to begin with IMO & it was very overpowering in the overall taste of the sauce as well.  It's safe to say that I will not be trying this recipe again.  As a matter of fact, I have a pizza in the oven as I'm writing this since the family is still hungry!

Maybe I did something wrong here but my dish turned out terribly. It ended up like a gooey black mess and just tasted like Soy.

First of all "20 min prep" needs to be updated to 1-2 hours of prep + another hour of cooking. Granted I am not a pro chef but this was probably the most time consuming / complicated recipe I have made, and it also creates a rediculous amount of dishes to clean up afterwords.

The recipe is not too clear in my opinion. Is it assuming that we have a deep fryer? How do I know if my oil is 400 degrees or not? I have no idea if I was under or over cooking the meal. "cook until thick" I am not sure what that means, ours ended up like a sticky pudding consistency. I thought it needed to cook more but my wife thought it was too thick already, so we left it as it was.

I gave the recipe 2 stars because the coated chicken pieces were excellent and I plan to make those again using a different sauce. I do have a problem with the slurry mix though. Surely there is a typo there, there is more cornstarch than liquid and yet in step 2 of the instructions it sounds as though it should be a sauce that is dripping off the chicken. It was literally a hard sticky paste and was very difficult to coat the chicken with. I will follow other peoples ideas to simple coat the chicken in egg and soy and shake in a bag of cornstarch.

My recipe looked nothing at all like the picture here so I am sure I did something wrong. Unfortunately the amount of work involved in this recipe negates the desire to try again to do it right. I would recommend this recipe only for experienced cooks.

This is an absolutely wonderful recipe!!! So happy I found it. I did make a few changes though...

1. In order to make this dish a little healthier, I skipped frying the chicken. I just seasoned with salt and pepper and cooked in a small amount of olive oil until crispy. Once the sauce was on it, I did not miss the fried part of it and you really could not tell a difference.

2. Sauce: I added fresh ginger and orange juice instead of water. Both added another set of great flavors.

3. I briefly steamed some fresh broccoli and red peppers and added them into the sauce with the chicken.

I will definitley be making this again!

And to all the negative reviews, don't pay attention. People need to use some of their own decision making in the kitchen instead of relying on a recipe to tell them EXACTLY what to do and EXACTLY how long to do something...when the chicken is crispy and cooked, it's done! When the sauce is as thick as you'd like it, take it off the heat :)

attributes.source_text: cooked in a small amount of olive oil until crispy

reviews.review_text: My fifteen year old daughter is into anything Chinese/Japenese.  My husband also LOVES General Tsos Chicken and it is always what he orders from our local restaurant.  My daughter had an anime convention coming up this weekend and in addition to going in full costume, she informed me she wanted "real" Chinese food.  So...I went out and bought a Wok and googled this recipe.  My daughter did most of the steps because she wanted to do it herself with the exception of frying the chicken.  The only problem we had was when we went to the mix the sauce in a jar the cornstarch clumped up at the bottem and we couldn't get it to mix.  We started over with the sauce but this time I didn't add the cornstarch.  Instead I measured it in a bowl and stirred in the water to mix it.  While the sauce was simmering I gradually mixed it in until the sauce thickened.   This recipe was such a hit!! My husband said it tasted just like the restaurant if not better.  He took some for lunch today leftover.  I had to make another batch tonight for my daughter to take to all of her friends going to the convention!!  Then to top it off, there was about a plate full left in the fridge that my husband just finished eating COLD.  When I asked him why he didn't warm it up, he said "that is the sign of awesome Chinese..when you can eat it cold and it still tastes good!"

attributes.source_text: My husband said it tasted just like the restaurant if not better

reviews.review_text:
I did not cook this recipe. My husband was the one that cooked this recipe. He is a wonderful cook and usually does not need a recipe. But he did not even know where to start with General Tso's Chicken. He did not follow your directions exactly of course because he has his own way of doing things. We did not have the vinegar in the recipe so we substituted the exact amount with malt vinegar instead. My husband added about half of a green bell pepper to the onion mixture. He also added quite a bit of extra garlic since we love garlic. We did not have the onions that the recipe asked for so we just added the onion that we had on hand (I am not sure how much my husband added but he added less because it was a stronger onion). And he used chili powder instead of the 8 chilis. He did not want to make it very spicy because we also fed this meal to our 1 and 2 year old kids. Well, your recipe was a big hit. My husand is very picky about what he likes (it has to taste real good---with lots of flavor). For him to say a recipe is really good means it is truly a really good recipe. He did say he would like to make it spicier (so we will have to make it one day when we can make something else for the kids). We both do love spicy foods. Since he liked it so much he has saved your recipe.

Again this was the best recipe. My husband loves General Tso's Chicken when we go out and eat Chinese. He said this tastes almost exactly like it does in the restaurant.

Thanks for your recipe,
Pamela

attributes.source_text: your recipe was a big hit
we also fed this meal to our 1 and 2 year old kids

reviews.review_text:
I loved the texture of the chicken. I do not often fry food, but I was in the mood to make something that I love from Chinese restaurants. The slurry made an awesome batter. I did add an extra egg because mine was too dry. I tried the chicken because they were so beautiful after I fried them. They were great chicken nuggets. The soy sauce added just the right amount of salt to season the chicken. I also used the the regular sodium Kikkoman soy sauce not the low sodium. The Asian culture use soy sauce in place of salt. It is how they salt their food. Unless you have hypertension or renal problems eat and enjoy your salt. I also used boneless skinless chicken thighs. I love dark meat, and I think it has a better taste.

The sauce was great. I did add extra garlic. Also, in conjunction with the green onions I put in two green peppers that were in bite size pieces and a yellow onion chopped into bite size pieces. I also like a little more heat. I put in one large Jalapeno sliced. I think it could have used a few more, but I wanted to make sure it would not be too spicy. I did not know how hot the chillies that I put in would make it. I loved this. I also forgot to say, I used one of Julia Childs tips, and it worked perfectly. for my white wine I used vermouth. My mother hates wine in her food, and she had no idea. Vermouth has a great flavor and is perfect for cooking.

attributes.source_text: just the right amount of salt to season the chicken
I did add extra garlic
I also like a little more heat
I wanted to make sure it would not be too spicy

reviews.review_text: To review the food itself - It's AMAZING! I'm not a fan of takeout General Tso chicken. It's the texture. It's too gummy. This recipe is delicious. I was making it strictly for my boyfriend and ended up loving it. The process.... dear lord thats another story. This is NOT a quick fix. And I know my way around a kitchen and love making adventurous new meals that take some time. It's not this recipe at all, it's simply this dish that's tedious in itself. It takes time to cut up all the chicken and to fry that many pieces. The cornstarch slurry does work. You will think there's no way in hell that its going to but it does! It's a slow going process though. I found that I had to roll the bowl around slowly to really coat the chicken. Then pulling out the individual pieces to fry them is a bit challenging since the slurry likes to hold them in one big sticky glob. Overall the recipe is pretty dead on. The cook/prep time is way off. It took my boyfriend and I around 2 hours our first time making. Definitely get everything ready before you start frying. It's long and tedious but a delicious outcome. I say it's a special occasion meal. Stick to takeout. Way too much work and time involved to make very often.

attributes.source_text: I say it's a special occasion meal

reviews.review_text: Mediocre recipe at best. I made sure to make it like the recipe said so i could judge it fairly, and I was disappointed. First off, it took me a lot longer than 40 min to prep and cook total time. No stars deducted for that though, working in a professional kitchen it wasn't too surprising to see that it took longer than someone said it would. The second I looked at the slurry mixture amounts, I knew it wouldn't work, but again, keeping true to the recipe I did it anyway, and surprise, it turned into a giant block of cornstarch. I really hope that was just a typo. I did end up adding water to the slurry in order to make it actual slurry consistency. Now the biggest disappointment, the sauce. It has great consistency, but that's about it. Pretty flat flavor. Was hoping for something sweet and spicy and all i got was soy sauce. I ended up adding Siracha after I tried it according to the recipe. That made it better, but still was meh. Chicken was fine, but honestly next time, I'd probably made it with the batter i normally make fried chicken with. I give this two stars because I didn't think it was bad enough for one. As the recipe stands, if this beats your local asian restaurant, I'm sorry.

Dove into this head first on a weeknight, was a good amount of work so some prepping would be smart, however it was a huge hit! I wouldn't call the Slurry a Slurry, it's more of a coating for the chicken pieces, being made with Cornstarch it's not a breading or a batter. I think next time I'm going to try a different method, like putting the chicken in the bowl, then coating with cornstarch then adding the egg & soy sauce, or I may do the cornstarch last, I haven't decided yet, but getting that sticky stuff to coat the chicken was do-able just a lot of work! I also don't have a wok, so I just used a pan on the stove, but I think next time I will use my large electric skillet so I can do it all at once, that was very time consuming. Also after we ate & were cleaning up, I found the chicken broth ... oops! So I will say it was good even without it! I will use it next time, & yes there WILL be a next time, to decide if it's better! LOL

attributes.source_text: on a weeknight

reviews.review_text: I registered JUST to rate this recipe because it's absolutely amazing. I have to eat gluten free, and with some tamari swapped out for normal soy sauce, this whole recipe is gluten free, which is just the most amazing thing ever. A few thoughts: 1. The effort of frying is definitely worth it, and we use a combination of coconut oil and olive oil and vegetable oil, but I'm sure it would be delicious with non-fried chicken, too. 2. Steamed broccoli is where it's at. 3. We didn't find the original recipe spicy at all, so we've been adding more peppers, and toasting some Szechuan peppercorns with the scallions. 4. Anyone who doesn't like this, simply does not have a soul. It doesn't leave you gross-Chinese-food-feeling, and did I mention how easy it is to make gluten free? The ONE complaint that we have, is that we always have trouble re-heating leftovers. We've tried adding water, doing it in the microwave, on the stove top, and nothing seems to work. The chicken gets heated, but the sauce generally stays pretty clumpy. Anyone had any luck with reheating tricks?

My husband enjoyed this recipe, I on the other hand wasn't a huge fan.  I LOVE, LOVE, LOVE the slurry and also loved how the sauce came together over heat.  I did a few things differently than what the recipe called for, and also next time I will do a few things differently.  I followed the slurry recipe to a "T" and it was perfect.  I mixed the slurry in my food processor, then transferred it to a gallon zip lock bag.  Cut up chicken thighs and added them to the slurry.  Made the sauce to a "T" as well, which  I wasn't a big fan of.  I thought it had too much vinegar.  I thought it would be too much when I was making it, but went with it anyway.  Next time I'll skip the vinegar, keep the wine and add some fresh ginger for a more complex flavor.  I also added dark brown sugar vs. white sugar.  I pan fried the chicken and it was PERFECT!  I will use the "slurry" recipe for future recipes such as Sweet & Sour Chicken, or Sesame Chicken.  Overall I will make it again, with a few changes.  Thanks for the great recipe!

attributes.source_text: My husband enjoyed this recipe

reviews.review_text: I have made this several times and it comes out great every time. I make this for family and guests, and people just love it. Besides the fantastic taste, this recipe is excellent for entertaining because of its wonderful visual appeal. I serve the chicken on a large platter alongside steamed broccoli and egg rolls (fried in the same oil right after the chicken), ringed with orange wedges, with rice served separately in rice bowls. It's hard to imagine a more beautiful presentation. As far as the recipe itself, go ahead and substitute to taste, but I make it exactly as written and I consider it pretty close to perfect. Now, about the slurry -- it works great as written. When you first mix it,  it forms a brick. But have faith. When you add the chicken pieces and stir, something magical happens (at least I can't explain it). The slurry loosens up and coats the chicken perfectly. Thanks for this wonderful recipe.

attributes.source_text: I make this for family and guests
I make this for family and guests
this recipe is excellent for entertaining

reviews.review_text: OMG! This was absolutely great!! Although I tweaked the recipe a bit, this could not have come out better. I read the reviews before trying the recipe and decided what to do and not do dependent upon others responses.  My #2 son (19 yo) enjoyed helping with the meal. He loves trying to cook different things and bragging about his cooking.  We also cooked chicken fried rice to go along with this recipe.  The sauce on the General Tso Chicken topped off everything perfectly. I switched the sugar to brown sugar (added more to taste the way we are used to getting at the restaurants where we dine), which worked perfectly. Thanks to the help of my son, which made this fun and less trying for me.  All my sons (4) really enjoyed this. They were amazed. Think we'll do this at least once a month. Any more good recipes, please send my way.  Thanks a million.  Oh, forgot to take a picture and didn't think about it until half way finished with the meal.  Sorry!! Will remember next time.  :-)

attributes.source_text: All my sons (4) really enjoyed this

reviews.review_text: Great and easy to make! I followed the recipe as is and it was great. I had no problem with coating the chicken with the egg, cornstarach, soy mixture.  The chicken alone, without the sauce was great.  The sauce thickened perfectly and tasted great.  All the stores in my town (and there are 3 major stores) were out of dried chilies, which was so odd!! But, I had some type of chili sauce from a Chinese grocery, and I used that for some heat.  I made this for company.  So, I made and fried the chicken in advance and had the sauce made and set aside in a jar.  When they arrived, I put the chicken in the oven and heated for a few minutes- then turned on the wok, added the onions and chili paste to some peanut oil- added the sauce and it thickened up beautifully.  I then added the heated chicken and served with rice and steamed broccoli.  It was great!  I did use low sodium soy sauce and low sodium chicken broth.

attributes.source_text: I made this for company
The sauce thickened perfectly
I used that for some heat

reviews.review_text: My husband and I made this last night and were thrilled with the results.  We followed the recipe with only a few small changes.  For the sauce we added a bit more grated garlic and included a few teaspoons of grated ginger as well.  We also added about a teaspoon of cayenne to the sauce mixture, omitting the dried chiles.  We're fans of spice, so we also added some red pepper flakes to the wok when frying the green onions.  Heat is definitely something that can easily be adjusted to taste for this recipe.  I read the reviews before beginning and kept in mind suggestions lessening the amount of cornstarch in both the slurry and sauce.  We used the amount listed in the recipe, however, and would do it again.  Although the slurry is quite thick and gooey, it made a fantastic fried coating for the chicken.  The sauce was thick, but what I'd expect General Tso's sauce to be.    We thought it was just right.    We served the chicken with steamed broccoli and white rice.  Delicious!

attributes.source_text: The sauce was thick
the slurry is quite thick and gooey

items.label: Steak Marinade
items.name: Steak Marinade
items.description: This is a variation of a recipe I got from a book that came with my BBQ.  I used strip loin steaks and it was fantastic.  You don't need any steak sauce to go with it.  The taste from the marinade is delicious!
instructions: Mix all ingredients together and place steaks into freezer bag with marinade, preferably overnight.
The original recipe used balsamic vinegar.Seems I never had that on hand so  I just used white and listed that in the recipe, but balsamic is definitely better.

reviews.review_text: this was AMAZING! i made a few changes..i tripled the recipe and used about 7 pepper steaks. i also used one tablespoon less vinegar because i find that it usually overpowers marinades...i added onion powder, salt and 2 pinches of dry mustard to the marinade. i threw it all in the food processor and then poured it into a freezer bag with the steaks. i marinated the steaks for 7 hours and then placed them, with extra marinade poured on them, in the oven at 450 degrees for 9 minutes on each side to cook it to medium rare. i actually cut the steaks into bite sized pieces and placed them atop a salad of lettuce, tomatoes and cucumbers, drizzling the marinade over the steak salad. it was DELICIOUS!! i would say though that if you are not a mustard fan this is probably not for you....that was a very notable flavor in this dish. thanks for posting! i will definitely make this again!

attributes.source_text: that was a very notable flavor in this dish

reviews.review_text: Awesome marinade for steaks!!!  I didn't have the time to marinate it overnight.  I mixed all the ingredients together (using the balsamic vinegar) in a ziploc baggie.  I also added some horseradish and garlic powder (along with the minced garlic).  I tenderized my steak with a tenderized that looks like a bunch of nails so that the marinade would be able to soak into the steak.  I put the steak in the baggie and let it marinate for about 3 hours.  I grilled the steak to a nice medium rare.  The results were fabulous!  I had a juicy, tender, flavorful steak that would rival any restaurant.  I normally use steak sauce and horseradish with my steak, but this steak didn't need anything.  Thanks for sharing such a great recipe.  I will be using this often in the future.

attributes.source_text: juicy, tender, flavorful steak
juicy, tender, flavorful steak

reviews.review_text: I was nervous about using anything on my 4 beautiful ribeyes. We don't eat a lot of red meat but I bought the steaks on sale for a special meal (and they were still a big bite in my food budget!) This recipe had so many good reviews and the ingredients were in my pantry. So I did a 'Zaar meal with grilled ribeyes, Mean Chef's french fries, and a green salad. This was as good as any meal we've had in a steak house! The recipe made the right amount to have the meat well-coated but not swimming in liquid. I threw in some diced onions and doubled the garlic. Refrigerated everything in a zip-lock bag for 6 hrs. Grilled the steaks on a hot grill about 5 minutes a side to medium weIl. The meat was exceptionally tender and nicely seasoned without being overwhelmed by the marinade. The meat wasn't overly salty, didn't need any other seasoning or sauce. It was a beautiful meal and impressed my guests. I can't imagine doing my steak any other way from now on. Thanks LuuvBunny!!

attributes.source_text: impressed my guests
The meat was exceptionally tender
nicely seasoned without being overwhelmed by the marinade
The meat wasn't overly salty

reviews.review_text: Awesome marinade.  I just served this to my family and they loved it.  I only had an hour to marinade the steaks so I can't wait to taste a steak marinaded over night.  I served a salad with the steak and used Recipe #43522 for the dressing.  The two went great together.  To add to the meal I made up a recipe for some onions.  I put some EVOO in a pan with garlic powder (didn't have fresh), salt, and pepper.  I let the flavors mix over medium heat and then added some Balsamic Vinegar.  I let that reduce and the added a sliced Videlia onion.  I cooked till tender and served them over the steak.  Talk about GOOD, man this was fantastic.  The sweetness of the Videlia onion went so well with the steak.  The whole meal was great.  I will most assuredly use this recipe again and try to marinate longer.  Thanks so much for this wonderful recipe.  Folks, you really need to try this one!

attributes.source_text: I just served this to my family and they loved it

reviews.review_text: OMG The Very Best Indoor Steak EVER!!! You should be walking around like a proud peacock knowing you introduced such a wonderful marinade to all your fellow zaarities. I only was able to marinade for about 2 hours, then preheated a cast iron grill skillet on medium high heat for 10 minutes. Cooked, without disurbing any of the marinade from the steak, for 6 minutes on each side to produce a just well done steak. Very juicy and tender was my T bone. Thanks so much for posting. Will be a do again soon! UPDATE: I have used this recipe sooo many times now, I buy any kind of steak on sale and use this, I crave this taste. This recipe is enjoyed 2 to 3 times a week... I can say that I enjoy this cooked inside more than I do grilled.  Oh and have discovered with many times of cooking and different marinade times... that one hour marinating is as good as 24 hours, taste wise.

attributes.source_text: Very juicy and tender was my T bone
Very juicy and tender was my T bone

reviews.review_text: This marinade is fantastic! It doesn't change the steak's flavor, it just enhances the natural flavor, tenderizes, and creates a beautiful carmalization on the outside. I was a little skeptical that this would taste good since it smells kind of gross uncooked, but boy, was I wrong! I am doing a south beach diet, and always have to choke steak down since I'm growing so tired of it, but this marinade made me look forward to meal time again! The first time I used the marinade I just let the meat sit in the marinade. Then, I wondered if I could get even more of that tenderness and flavor if I pierced the steak all over before marinading it. Since I love steak medium rare, this was a mistake. The inner part of the steak cooked too fast and it turned out well-done. I won't do that again! Thank you so much for sharing this!

attributes.source_text: it just enhances the natural flavor
tenderizes
even more of that tenderness
creates a beautiful carmalization on the outside

reviews.review_text: A few weeks ag I bought a few steaks to grill.  The butcher was out of the ones I wanted and subbed a more expensive steak for the sale one.  Well, it was inedible after it was grilled.  I threw the others in the freezer in disgust.  I decided to use them and get it over with.  I marinated them in this for 24 hours after stabbing them a bunch of times with a fork.  DH said that they were way better than the previous steaks and wouldn't believe me when I told him they were the same ones.  The flavor was great besides that they made shoe leather tender enough to chew.  I used balsamic vinegar and vegan  worcestershire sauce (allergy reasons).  Thanks, I didn't have to throw away these steaks.

attributes.source_text: DH said that they were way better than the previous steaks
tender enough to chew

reviews.review_text:
This marinade tasted great on my NY steaks.   The flavors were totally compatible with beef without being overpowering.  It's an easy to fix recipe that doesn't use any weird ingredients or require chopping (if you use a garlic press, as I did.)

I really should have followed the advice to marinate 24 hours, but forgot to make it until the morning of the day I planned to eat the steaks.  I could tell that it had tenderized a thin layer on the outside, but the steaks were kind of tough so could have used a longer marinate time.

This recipe does not make very much marinade.  It was barely enough for my 2 steaks.  If you have more steaks, I recommend that you double or even triple the quantity.

attributes.source_text: without being overpowering
it had tenderized a thin layer on the outside

reviews.review_text: this is something like the marinade my mom uses, however being new to cooking, i didn't know much about steaks and just bought what looked like a nice hefty piece of meat which when i came home and did research on the net, it turned out was a rather tough piece, but i took heart from all the reviews on how this marinade miraculously tenderized the meat so i marinaded it for almost 24 hours. unfortunately, however the meat did not get tender at all, and my husband and i left more than half of our steaks and chose to fill up on the potato gratin instead. I don't really think that this can be considered the fault of the recipe, however all the reviews led me to believe that i would have a nice tender steak regardless of my meat and in that sense i was disappointed.

Awesome recipe. I doubled the recipe because I had two giant Chuck steaks that I bought on sale. As most people know Chuck steaks isn't the greatest, it's also kinda tuff. I marinaded the steak for 6 hour in the fridge and 1 1/2 out side of the fridge before grilling. The only thing I changed was the garlic amount and I used white vinegar because that's what I had. I added 6 cloves since my family loves garlic. It turned out great! So flavorful and tender for the type of steak. I will definitely use the again in the future. Thank you for this recipe

attributes.source_text: tender for the type of steak

reviews.review_text:
I will not "rate" this, as I'll never try it.  I am baffled every day as to WHY one would take a great steak and obliterate the flavor or the meat?....:::GRRRR:::
If you are going to take a "chuck" and bastardize the meat, so be it.  But, for the life of me, I CANNOT understand WHY anyone would ruin good cuts of meat with a marinade.....?  If you want to smear a good butter/garlic mix over it after it's cooked. Cool!  But, please, please, don't ruin good meat with sauces, concoctions, dry mixes.  Just go to your local Rylands, or whatever is near you.  Let them ruin it, then you can substantiate the price!

I used this marinade to flavor and tenderize less than ideal cuts of steak, and it was pretty good. I didn't want to heat up the house with the broiler, so I just pan fried in cast iron. Served these with sauteed mushrooms and sweet onions, a couple lashings of gravy, and mashed potato. While my less than ideal steaks still weren't crazy tender, it was definitely an improvement, and I'll try this again with meat. If I'd done these longer, I think it would have been even better, but I only had 8 hours. Thanks for sharing.

Excellent, simple marinade, especially for those who like to doctor up their recipes.  I used it on a cheap London broil, and I added 1/3 can of beer (makes the meat extra tender), cayenne pepper, and a pinch of salt.  I also upped the original ingredients to balance with the beer. Within 4 hours, the steak was practically falling apart in the bag.  After a quick broil, it was the best $3 steak I'd ever had! It definitely tops those $20+ restaurant steaks that the cooks never seem to season right.

attributes.source_text: makes the meat extra tender
the steak was practically falling apart in the bag

reviews.review_text: This is a really tasty marinade, the only one I have used repeatedly since I discovered it here.  I like to leave it overnight to really let it soak in (flipping the bag or container and swishing the marinade around every couple of hours or so), but don't leave it any longer than that for quality steaks like ribeyes/ prime rib steaks it can make them almost mushy if left for more than 24 hours.  (dinner plans changed and I had these marinading for a couple/ few days)

Okay, I'm not much of a red meat eater, but my husband loves a good steak, so I found this for him (or so I thought!).  I ended up sharing his sirloin because it was sooooo good. TENDER?!! YES....it almost melted in my mouth...it probably would have if I had marinaded it longer than 5 hours!  No steak sauce needed even for those "addicted" to the stuff!!  My husband said he would definately serve to guests!  I made no changes to the recipe..it's a "keeper" just the way it is!  Thanks for posting.

attributes.source_text: my husband loves a good steak
My husband said he would definately serve to guests
TENDER?!! YES
it almost melted in my mouth

reviews.review_text:
I tried this thinking that it would make a nice marinade but believing we would still want steak sauce or some kind of condiment, as we always do (my husband puts horseradish on all red meat).  It was so good we both agreed it needed nothing.  Thanks!

As an aside, I tasted the marinade before putting it on the meat and thought the mustard flavor was too strong, but I stuck with the recipe and the mustard blended right in when the meat was cooked.  Delicious!

attributes.source_text: the mustard blended right in when the meat was cooked

reviews.review_text: Flavor, flavor, flavor. I used balsamic vinegar,  Dijon mustard, Tamari soy sauce, 4 cloves of garlic, and 1/4 teaspoon finely ground black pepper. I tenderized  2 top sirloin steaks with a Jaccard Meat Tenderizer (tool)  and  tossed all into a zip lock bag for about 2 hours, turning  and "smushing"  every 30 minutes. Cooked on my grill pan over med-high heat for 3 minutes per side. Perfection. I always have these ingredients on hand so I know I will use this often. Out of the 146 steak marinade recipes that came up in my search, I picked a winner! Thanks LuuvBunny!

Excellent marinade! Puts a great flavor on the steaks. Going to use it again today for about the 4th time. Trying to get a quick bbq in before we get more snow tonight in Newfoundland! I added a bit of lemon juice last time because I had half a lemon sitting there waiting to be used and it added to the flavor nicely. I am so over store bought marinades and their immense amounts of salt  and whatever sketchy ingredients they put in to make it work so fast! This is now my go to marinade!

I have mixed reviews on this recipe.  My husband thought it was great, I thought it was okay.  I marinated 2 Rib Steaks for over 18 hours.  I think cooking time may be the determining factor. My steak was cooked Well Done, my Husband's Medium-Well.  For mine, the edges tasted great, but the main part of the steak didn't have any special flavour to me and it was a little tough.  My husband's steak had great flavour throughout and was very tender.  My husband insists I make this again, I guess I will have it Medium-Well next time ;)

attributes.source_text: My husband thought it was great
was very tender

items.label: Caramelized Baked Chicken Legs/Wings
items.name: Caramelized Baked Chicken Legs/Wings
keywords: c("Chicken Thigh & Leg", "Chicken", "Poultry", "Meat", "Toddler Friendly", "Kid Friendly", "Brunch", "Oven", "< 4 Hours", "Easy", "Inexpensive")
items.description:
Delicious! Yummy  caramelized legs, kids love these! So quick and easy and no marinating required. Just prepare the sauce, pour over the chicken and pop in the oven!  I actually like this with wings better ;-)
 

VERY IMPORTANT TO LEAVE IT IN THE OVEN UNTIL IT HAS CARAMELIZED TO AVOID DISAPPOINTMENT. 

Thank you to everyone for their positive reviews!

Try adding Sambal Oelek as Chef  #27416 has suggested in his review. What a great idea ;-)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit or 180 degrees Celsius.
Place chicken in a 9x13 inch baking dish. Mix together the oil, soy sauce, ketchup, honey, garlic, salt and pepper.
Pour over the chicken.
Bake in preheated oven for one hour, or until sauce is caramelized.
Could also use wings or pork ribs.

reviews.review_text: This recipe is great. It's going on my "Keepers"  list. Thanks for posting it!<br/>What I love about it it:<br/>-It's so flavorful. The soy tenderized the chicken nicely. Before serving, I skimmed off the fat from the pan sauce and poured remaining glaze over chicken. <br/>-The ingredients are usually right on hand.<br/>-It's quick, easy and rather inexpensive.<br/>-Can be multiplied up for a crowd in a foil pan. It's pretty enough for a party! <br/>-Can be made with skinless, boneless chicken breasts and thighs. (I'd recommend this)<br/>-For another layer of interest, it can be "fired up" with a teaspoon or more of crushed red pepper (which I added, because my husband is addicted to cayenne. Lol)<br/>Get you some cornbread!

attributes.source_text: The soy tenderized the chicken nicely

reviews.review_text:
I was looking for something different to do with the chicken legs I had, and this recipe sounded very good.  I usually am not a fan of soy sauce so I was a bit reluctant at first, but figured I would try it anyway.  They turned out to be absolutely wonderful, and the best part is that this is a recipe that you can make out of stuff that is almost always in your pantry anyway.  No running to the store for an ingredient you don't have.  

They were great as is, but if I had to change anything, it would be to marinate them for several hours, or even overnight to give a more intense flavor throughout the piece of chicken.  Another thing I might try next time is adding a dash or cayenne pepper, just to give it a bit of a kick, which I like. 

Awesome recipe, will definitely make these again.

You definitely deserve 5 stars for ease on this recipe!  The taste was very good, but a bit on the sweet side to me.  But then again it could have been my measuring of the honey.  Next time and there will be a next time I will add just a bit less honey.  Also, I deskinned my legs as we are tyring to stay away from the "BAD" stuff (fat) and flipped them probably 4 times in the cooking cycle just to make sure they didn't stick.  Had no problems whatsoever.  Oh and I thought I'd be proactive towards the cleaning portion of the dish and lined it with some foil for easy clean which would have worked well if I didn't slice a whole in it with the tongs!   LOL.  Very good way to easily make some chicken legs and I 100% recommend :o)

Just to add my two cents....my hubby LOVED these! He said they would also make fabulous wings!
I had 4 1/2 lb pack of chicken legs and doubled the sauce (using low-sodium soy sauce). Marinated them in a very large zip top bag in the fridge for several hours prior to baking. I lined a jelly roll pan with parchment paper for easy clean up (no additional spraying required). I only placed the legs (not all the extra sauce) on the paper lined pan. I brushed the legs w/a coating of sauce & turned every 20 minutes or so and meanwhile reduced the remaining sauce in a small pan on the stovetop which worked out very well. Thanks for the post! We will be making this one again, the house smelled soooo good!

attributes.source_text: my hubby LOVED these

reviews.review_text: Great recipe!  I was looking for a fairly simple recipe.  I searched for baked chicken.  This was easy and VERY scrumptious.  I made it exactly like the recipe said.  I didn't know though if it was supposed to be baked covered or uncovered.  Since it didn't specify I did it uncovered.  I was a little worried that it would be dry baking that long.  I decided to flip the chicken several times during the baking time.  It tasted fabulous!  My sauce was a little thin, but the chicken I had on hand was injected with a water solution, so I'm sure that contributed to the sauce being thin.  We spooned it over the chicken and baked potatoes.  Yum!   fyi- for those of us on Farenheit the degrees should be 350.  I had to find a celcius to farenheit converter.  Next time I'll try it with butcher-shop chicken to see if the sauce is still thin.  Either way, it is absolutely wonderful.  Thanks for sharing the recipe.

I used chicken wings (1 oz short of 5 lbs worth - 18 wings in total including tips - ) so I upped the sauce as follows taking into account dietary needs - 3 1/3 T olive oil, 3/4 cup soy sauce (low sodium), 3 1/3 T tomatoe sauce (ketchup). 1/2 cup honey and 5 teaspoons of minced garlic.  I poured this over the wings and let them marinate for a few hours and cooked as directed (they were well crowded in the pan) and baked them for 1 hour at 175C fan forced oven and turned them over about half way through the cooking time.  Delicious with the sauce drizzled over the rice and steamed vegetables.  Of the 18 cooked we ended up with 5 left over and it is a bun fight between the DM and me as to who gets them for lunch tomorrow - so maybe if will have to be a snack for each of us.  Thank you djmastermum for a great recipe (which I will be trying with a quartered chicken) , made for Aussie/Kiwi Swap #37 February 2010.

attributes.source_text: it is a bun fight between the DM and me as to who gets them for lunch tomorrow
who gets them for lunch tomorrow
maybe if will have to be a snack for each of us

reviews.review_text: Oh. My. Goodness. I decided to make this chicken after reading the raving reviews and am SO glad that I did! I followed the recipe exactly, using chicken wings (skin on) instead of drumsticks. I basted the chicken every 15 minutes and flipped the wings half way through cooking (about 30 minutes in) and then increased the oven temp from 350 F to 375 F for the last 15 minutes to caramelize the chicken nicely. My boyfriend LOVED it. No leftovers. I paired the wings with green beans sauteed in butter and fresh garlic (http://www.food.com/recipe/garlic-green-beans-261583), and white rice. We poured the chicken glaze onto the rice for some added flavour and it was yummy! I highly recommend this dish.

attributes.source_text: My boyfriend LOVED it

reviews.review_text: Hi Darlene. There should have been more space between the 1 and the 2/3. What was meant was one and two thirds (1 2/3) tablespoons. Common mistake:) When you see the /, like in 2/3, and it's 2 or less, the first number, the 1, is supposed to be a whole tablespoon because there are 3 teaspoons in a tablespoon. One wouldn't say 3/3 tablespoons, so when they are talking tablespoons, the first number before the / would be either a 1 or a 2, never higher:) One wouldn't also say 1/3 of a tablespoon as that would be a teaspoon. Hope that helped you. Are you a new cook? It takes time to learn everything, so don't fret:)

I just made this for the first time yesterday.  I doubled the recipe with the addition of two heaping teaspoons of Sambal Oelek (thanks William "Uncle Bill" Anatooskin for this suggestion!) and also turned the wings twice during cooking, basting each time.  I also turned up the heat for the last 10 minutes plus another 10 minutes in order to caramelize the sauce.  The sauce was so delicious that we were spooning it out for dipping and the wings taste even better right out of the refrigerator today!  I only gave four stars because the sauce is very thin.  I think I may try adding cornstarch to the sauce or dredging the wings in flour next time to see if that helps thicken things up. I may also add a bit more Sambal Oelek to up the heat.  This one is definitely worth saving!

Wow, this chicken was very good! Made our house smell wonderful. I used all legs. Next time I will probably poke holes and marinate to let the sauce sink through more thoroughly. But my oh my, that sauce was delicious! After about each bite we would drag the chicken through the sauce and eat. Couldn't get enough! (Edited to say I've made this recipe close to 7 times now, and counting :) and always cook about 1hr 25 minutes with a 2-4 hour marinade if I have the time, but even without people want the recipe. I also always use the 4.5 lb pack of legs, about 5 cloves garlic, 3/4 cup soy sauce and 1 cup honey).  I highly recommend. Very simple and yummay. Keep Jesus!

We Loved this chicken! After reading the many posts, I decided to OMIT the olive oil in the ingredients and only use enough to coat the bottom of the pan to prevent sticking. I feared the oil could cause the sauce/glaze to "slip" off the chicken, causing no flavor to soak into the meat. I also baked the chicken at 400 degrees F. for 30 minutes, leaving the chicken in the oven, turned the temperature down to 350 degrees F. baking for 20-30 minutes more. I found it advantageous to baste the chicken every 10 minutes as the sauce is thin but did create a yummy sweet/sour flavor when done. This is a keeper!

attributes.source_text: did create a yummy sweet/sour flavor when done

reviews.review_text: so good! i've rated this b4- but i just roasted a turkey with this sauce and it came out so yummy- melt-in-ur-mouth!! i usually use only 1/2 the sauce when using on chx or ribs, and save the rest for another day.....but on turkey just brush some on about once every hour of cooking. last hour or two- throw a piece of foil loosely over top to preventing it from getting too dark. i was busy and baked turkey good 5 1/2 hrs- and it was just falling off the bone. my kids do not like garlic- but love this sauce. i do recommend using low-sodium soy sc. since this has so much in it...it still tastes the same- and i never add additional salt- just lots of pepper :) happy eating!!

attributes.source_text: melt-in-ur-mouth
my kids do not like garlic- but love this sauce

reviews.review_text: This recipe shouldn't be complete without instructions for cleaning up the pan! LOL!  We had these for dinner last night and they are stupendous!  I used 10 legs, baked at 400 for about 1 1/2 hours turning every 20 min.  They carmelized very nicely and were extremely delicious.  I, too, had quite a bit of sauce in the pan (more like goo), but served the legs with tater tots, so scooped it out and tossed it.  (Then soaked the pan in soapy water for an hour!) DH suggested lining the pan with foil first, as I've noticed others had done.  Why, oh why didn't I read all the reviews first?  Anyway, it was a great meal that will be repeated at our house.  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: We had these for dinner last night

reviews.review_text: This was very disappointing and it's mostly my fault.   The recipe said you could use this on ribs as well so I couldn't wait to try this with country style spare ribs.    The sauce was AMAZINGLY DELICIOUS even though I only had 1/2 cup of honey.  Then  I made the mistake of pouring it over ribs.  I baked the ribs at 400 degrees for 30 min. then turned the heat down to 350 and baked another hour.  Yuk!  The ribs were dry, the sauce was thin, and the pork changed that wonderful flavor that the sauce had before I poured it over the meat.   Take it from me, don't use pork.  I'm making this again this weekend for my son's birthday party - but this time I'll use chicken wings instead.

Hello DjMastermum;
This recipe is so easy to make and turns out absolutely fantastic.  I used chicken legs with back attached and the only addition to your recipe was 1 teaspoon of Sambal Oelek.
I baked the legs at 350 F for 52 minutes, then turned the heat up to 375 F for 8 minutes.  They caramalized to perfection.
We had a visitor just as the chicken was finished and even though he had his dinner, he wanted to try the chicken.  Well, talk about devouring the chicken and for a moment I thought he was going to eat the bones.
Smackin his lips, and wanted the recipe immediately.
Thank you so much for a real yummy, yummy chicken recipe.
"Uncle Bill"

attributes.source_text: he wanted to try the chicken

reviews.review_text: This recipe made me sign up so I could join in all the fun.  My 5 year old left the TV in her room to come out and find out what that yummy smell was.  She gave this 100 stars.  It is quite delicious!  I tweeked it a little bit.  Here's what I did:  I made 5lbs of drumsticks so I doubled the sauce (and it was too much but half would not have been enough either so I have saved it and will use it on pork chops later) and added ALOT more garlic- we are Italian and love our garlic, I added about a 1/2 tablespoon of onion powder plus 2 tablespoons of apple cider vinegar.  I marinated these little cuties right in the roasting pan for about 6 or 7 hours and then baked them right in the sauce.  They took alot longer than an hour.  Mine took a little over 2 hours to get the skin the way we like it and to get the glaze to carmelize.  Towards the end, I tasted the sauce and thought they just didn't have the flavor I was looking for.  They were sweet but that's it.  So I squirted a bunch of lemon juice over them, basted them to mix it in a little and finished baking them.  They were fabulous!  My husband said "I can't stop eating these, they're addictive."  Next time, I'll used more cider vinegar and lemon to give them a little more zing.  What's nice is that you can easily adjust the recipe to your liking.  They are really good!  As a matter of fact, the leftovers are calling out to me from the kitchen right now!  I think I'll go have one (or 3).  Yum!!!!!

attributes.source_text: My 5 year old left the TV in her room to come out and find out what that yummy smell was
My husband said "I can't stop eating these, they're addictive."

reviews.review_text: I prepared this tonight for my three children, one of their friends who is sleeping over and my husband.  For the first time in YEARS it was completely quiet at the dinner table!  It was one of those busy days when I had chicken thawed but had not decided how I was going to cook it. I ran across this recipe and decided to try it because of the rating and reviews. I concur with every other reviewer that this is a winner. I amped up the garlic (we love garlic), let it marinate for about 2 hours, and basted consistently while in the oven.  Simple ingredients, quick prep, and a "crowd pleaser" in my household.

attributes.source_text: my three children
one of their friends who is sleeping over
my husband
a "crowd pleaser" in my household
I amped up the garlic

reviews.review_text: Very good taste... I also was a little wary about the ketchup... I like it but just don't usually cook with it!  I loved the way the garlic infuses the whole dish...don't leave it out!!!  I did marinate the legs in a ziplock bag for 2 hours before baking... I baked them for close to 70 minutes and the sauce still didn't caramelize, but was starting to thicken.  I went ahead and served the sauce over some rice since the chicken was already done. The legs were beautifully colored and the smell was heavenly!  We loved this easy dish to throw in the oven when you don't want to spend a lot of time in the kitchen...

attributes.source_text: I loved the way the garlic infuses the whole dish

reviews.review_text: Oh my...my preschooler was afraid to try this...he made the funniest face and I got him to try it..and one BITE and he says, MOMMY THIS IS DELICIOUS! He ate three! My husband got home and tried them, and said "you can make these ANY time!" They smelled delicious. Im a vegetarian, so I can't vouch, but the preschooler and husband L-O-V-E-D them. Im going to make them again tonight (2 weeks later). My husband told me that he had never really been a chicken leg guy, since no one knows how to make them properly, but THIS recipe is amazing......Thanks so much for a great recipe.
