items.label: Classic Potato Salad
items.name: Classic Potato Salad
items.description: Make and share this Classic Potato Salad recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Boil peeled potatoes in salted water until done. Cool to room temperature.
Place diced potatoes in large bowl.
Mix mayonnaise, cider vinegar, sugar, mustard, salt, garlic powder, and pepper in another bowl.
Add to potatoes.
Add celery and onions and mix well.
Stir in eggs.
Sprinkle a little paprika on top.

reviews.review_text: This potato recipe is really good.  It's exactly as my mother makes it.  And she's 94 !!<br/>I use Yukon Gold potatoes, that I microwave for 6 minutes at a time, flip them, another 6 min. flip them again.  Usually by the 3rd or 4th flip they're done.  I keep the skins on until they're cool to handle, then peel and cube.<br/>For the dressing, I combine Best foods ( or Hellman's) Light mayo, honey mustard, Old Bay seasoning, lots of dill weed, Johnny's Seasoning salt ( like Lawry's), Montreal Steak seasoning for the pepper part and a dash of teriyaki sauce ( I use Soy Yeh).  Combine and alter to your taste.  I don't know proportions because I take some of this and some of that, a squirt of this...on and on.<br/>I also chop up some celery ribs, a whole onion and a few garlic cloves and sauté them briefly in some olive oil and chicken stock...just to add some flavor.<br/>Combine well and then chill.  Preferably overnight.  This isn't at it's best when it's really fresh, just made.  The flavors have to mingle.<br/>I tried adding bacon once, and thought, nah, not worth it, so there you go.  It's really easier than it sounds.

A great potato salad recipe that will also work when you want to add other ingredients.

This is my first time making potato salad. Bummed because I overcooked my potatoes. I could tell when I started dicing them because they were falling a apart a little. I let the potatoes cool before dicing them. I also didn't know what a "medium" potato was. My potatoes were a little smaller than a baseball. I used the red potatos that I had in the house already. I mixed all the ingredients in a separate mixing bowl. I added just a little dill, diced scallions with the red onions, dijon mustard instead of yellow. Smoked paprika instead of plain. 1/2 cup of buttemilk and 1 cup of mayonaise. (personal preference). I only had 2 hard boiled eggs....I would definitely add more the next time. I really liked the taste but unhappy because it was mushy because of the overcooked potatoes. I would definitely use this as a "staple" recipe and would make again. IMPORTANT: Definitely ADD SALT when boiling the potatoes. The potato itself will have more flavor. Leave a few slices of the eggs to decorate the top. TASTES SO MUCH BETTER THE NEXT DAY....try making it a day before your event.

I stumbled across this recipe years ago, made it, really enjoyed it, saved the page to my bookmarks and made it over the years. About 3 years ago, that laptop experienced many problems...cracked screen, dead battery, charger wouldn't make a good connection and computer would shut off immediately after turning on. I got a new laptop and searched and searched for this recipe again but could never find it. I would try other recipes, but they were never as good as this one. I finally broke down and spent a bunch of time and a moderate amount of money to get the old laptop working long enough to find this recipe again. I agree with a previous reviewer, it doesn't seem that much different than thousands of other potato salad recipes, but to me, it's the best by a mile. MizzNezz, if you ever see this...Thank you!

My husband and I married because we both hate mayo. My husband however loves old fashioned potato salad even though it has mayo because it's paired with yellow mustard. I thought after 28 years of marriage it high-time I made my hubby real potato salad. Do you remember the scene in "A Christmas Story" where Ralphie's teacher is passing back the classes essays about what they wanted for Christmas? The scene shows Ralphie daydreaming about his teacher dancing enthusiastically across the chalk board writing Ralphie's essay grade as an A++++++++++++++++++++++++++. I say this is a well done recipe, A+. We've made it twice and the 2nd time I doubled the recipe. It was a massive hit with people fighting for the last dab in the bowl. My one tweak: we didn't have celery and only a partial onion.....so I used what onion I had and added green onoions minced, as well as, minced fresh parsley. This recipe is a keeper!

attributes.source_text: My husband however loves old fashioned potato salad

reviews.review_text: Raw vegetables such as celery and onions do little else but make your stomach and gut uncomfortably gassy being why adding them isn't worth the extra trouble, expense or gas discomfort.<br/><br/>One teaspoon of Celery Salt adds just the right amount of seasoning and flavor as you'll soon discover for yourself.<br/><br/>If you're an onion lover you can add a few shakes of onion power or salt. Some others instead prefer a few shakes of Lowry's Garlic Salt.<br/><br/>The dried seasonings are vastly superior tasting, less expensive and reduce preparation time dramatically.<br/><br/>The secret to GREAT COOKING is making the best tasting recipes, using the least possible number of ingredients, for the least expensive cost, in the least possible time and least possible amount of clean up.

My husband LOVES potato salad but he just never could get the recipe correct when attempting to make it himself. I can tolerate eating the premade store bought kind but my husband absolutely hates it! I was feeling ambitious one day and decided to take a crack at making it. The recipe was suprisingly easy to make and I was VERY impressed with myself for it turning out perfect the first time. YAY! I followed the recipe pretty much exactly with just two changes. First, I did NOT use the cider vinegar. Only because when I was at the store I had thought we had some at home. Turns out we didnt and I was too lazy to go back out. Second, I added in 1/3 cup of sweet relish. Just for personal preference. Based on a previous review, I salted the water the potatoes were boiling in too. For those who have a difficult time making hard boiled eggs, I find it easiest to cover them in salted water, bring them to a boil for 5 minutes, then turn the heat down to a simmer for 10. afterwards, soak them immediately in ice water to cool them down. Should be perfect. definately keeping this recipe on hand! I would make it daily if I could. The whole bowl was licked clean within 24 hours. my husband and I LOVE this!

attributes.source_text: My husband LOVES potato salad
my husband and I LOVE this

reviews.review_text: Add me to the list of 5-Star reviews for this recipe. It is fantastic. One thing I typically never put in  potato salad was garlic powder, but I think that and the cider vinegar are what really make the flavors come together in this recipe. That, and the proportions of each ingredient are spot on. The dressing is tangy enough to hold up to the potatoes and eggs for a nice balance. I would recommend putting the paprika on just before you're about to serve it, as you'll need to stir it up every hour or so while it's chilling to keep everything coated evenly. It also helps to mash up some of the potatoes and stir that into the dressing to give it more of a paste-like consistency, it will coat the chunks of potato better.

reviews.review_text: I made this yesterday for a dinner with friends.  Other reviewers mentioned that while it looks like a classic recipe, not different from others, I agree with those who said this one somehow just tastes BETTER.  It's got a nice zip without being too tangy.  I used a full 2 pound bag of baby reds and quartered or cut into six pieces, depending on their sizes.  I omitted the celery. There was plenty of "sauce" for all the salad, in spite of the increase in potato.  I normally like to make this type of salad a day in advance so the flavors have a chance to blend, but was unable to do so this time.  Our guests remarked how much they liked it and I passed along the recipe.  Overall, a big hit!  I enthusiastically recommend this recipe.  Enjoy!

I was having family over for a cookout and wanted something special. Success! I knew it was great the night I made it when I sampled it! Then the next day I enjoyed watching the potato salad eaters go back for seconds!<br/>One change I made though (only because I realized too late that I was out of garlic powder), I halved the salt and replaced the garlic powder with garlic salt. I also thought 5 eggs sounded like too much, so I only put in 3. Well, this potato salad was so tasty and the compliments so many, that I will make this from now on. I now have a worthy contribution to take to potlucks at work and family gatherings.

I'm seriously considering keeping this my own little secret and not giving out the recipe. I did not use celery, as I didn't have any on hand. I had planned to use pickle relish, per the other reviews, and that is how I am used to having it. But I tasted the "sauce" mixture and it was PERFECT without the addition of the pickles. I forgot to add paprika, and since it was already so delicious, I didn't bother adding it. I prepared this on a Friday evening for Sunday dinner. It was still perfectly delicious on Tuesday. Thank you so much for sharing this recipe.

Delicious. I have found my go to potato salad recipe for sure!

reviews.review_text: I have made potato salad before.  I've had other's potato salad before.  I get it.  So I thought.  But I decided to try this recipe based on the reviews, and lack of relish in the recipe.  I don't know whether it was the cooling of the potatoes before adding the dressing, or the bit of garlic, but this turned out far superior to any potato salad I have had.  I, the apathetic potato salad eater, not only went back for seconds, but licked the serving spoon while putting it away.  It's creamy and flavorful.  So good.  Definitely my go-to recipe now!  Thanks for posting!

Miss Nezz does it again!  This is exactly as it says - a classic!  I usually add sweet relish, just because I like pickles in potato salad, but I followed the recipe exactly and everyone thinks it is fantastic.  I think it would also be great with a pickle relish, but it already has a little crunch, so that works for me.  All the reviews and all the pictures can't even show the 'exactly perfect' blend of flavors.  You are one of my favorite Chefs on Zaar and now food.com.  If I need a really, really good recipe, I just go to what Mizz Nezz does, she has never steered me wrong.

attributes.source_text: it already has a little crunch

reviews.review_text: Very good indeed. I followed the recipe as written with the exception of using just one boiled egg and adding some finely chopped green pepper. Too, I made a little discovery. When I've made potato salad in the past, I think I've not waited until the boiled potatoes were completely cool, or at room temperature resulting in a kind of "mashed" potato salad - edible, but not especially attractive. This time, I got busy with something, and came back a couple of hours later. By then the potatoes had completely cooled and had firmed up nicely and didn't stick together when I added all the other ingredients.

It's been many years since I've made potato salad but, growing up in Amish country it's something I grew up with. For some reason I started to crave potato salad while thinking of what to make to accompany a steak on the grill on a beautiful summer day. So happy I found this recipe using mayo as a base; my mother always used Miracle Whip which I find too sweet. The garlic powder was a surprise but in it went. So glad I found and made this recipe as both husband and I really enjoyed the flavor profile. It's definitely a keeper and I suspect we'll have home made potato salad more often.

I am pretty picky when it comes to potato salad and have tasted other versions of my memory's favorite and have been sadly disappointed.

This recipe ROCKS! It is clearly the best potato salad I have tasted.
I did add 1/3 cup of Sweet Dill Relish - which for me has always been a key ingredient.
It tasted exactly like I have always remembered a potato salad should taste.

I will be making this recipe often!
Thank you for posting this wonderful anytime food!

Roger Baran

We have had some hot weather here in NH and I wanted to make something that would be quick and easy to grab for dinner, so I made this along with a pasta salad.   I have to admit that I had 3 helpings of this in a 24 hr. period and decided I better give some away before I ate the whole darn dish of it :)  It is a wonderful potato salad.  I was a little apprehensive about putting in garlic powder, as I had never had it in a potato salad, but along with all the other ingredients it made for one very tasty one!  I look forward to making this again and again, but may cut back  on the mayonnaise  just a tad, as it was a little on the runny side (it may have been due to the size of my potatoes.  Maybe they weren't medium potatoes??)  and I like mine kind of sticking together.  This was very flavorful and really delicious ,and I enjoyed it very much.  My cousin and friend thank you, as they loved it too!  Thanks for sharing this classic with us MizzNezz!  Linda

items.name: Olive Garden Pasta E Fagioli Soup in a Crock Pot (Copycat)
items.description: Make and share this Olive Garden Pasta E Fagioli Soup in a Crock Pot (Copycat) recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Brown beef in a skillet.
Drain fat from beef and add to crock pot with everything except pasta.
Cook on low 7-8 hours or high 4-5 hours.
During last 30 min on high or 1 hour on low, add pasta.

reviews.review_text: Delicious!  Even better the second day.  Made this yesterday for DH and myself and had plenty of leftovers for today as well.  Actually still have some!  Like another reviewer I also used Prego Traditional Sauce.  After pouring it into the soup pot I filled the jar half full of water and added that as well as it seemed to not have enough liquid for my taste.  That turned out to be a good decision.  The recipe didn't call for it but I added 4 cloves of fresh garlic minced when I sauteed the ground beef and the veggies together.  I let the beef brown a bit first before adding the garlic so it wouldn't burn and get that bitter taste.  I didn't have plain oregano so I used the Italian seasoning I had on hand and that worked fine.  I had fresh parsley left over from another recipe so I used that instead of dried.  By today when we took it out of the fridge to warm it up the pasta had absorbed most of the liquid so we added a small can of spaghetti sauce, some more water, and some more Italian seasoning.  That worked out perfect.  It tasted even better than last night!  The pasta had absorbed more of the flavor too.  I didn't cook this in a slow cooker, but just let it simmer on the stove until all the veggies were tender.  It is a very savory soup and would be especially comforting in cold weather.  We will be having this again!

attributes.source_text: It is a very savory soup
until all the veggies were tender

reviews.review_text: This soup is REALLY good!  Seriously! The ironic thing is, i picked out a soup to make that i knew wasn't really up my fiances alley because i wanted to take it to work for lunch for the next week, so i wanted to be sure there was plenty...no joke, he at THREE BOWLS!  He just kept saying over and over, "Man, this stuff is GOOD!"  I stuck to the recipe pretty closely...didn't make it in the crockpot because i started making it around 6pm, but it was still outstanding. i took the suggestion of another poster and sautee'd the onion, carrots, celery and garlic together...i then added a pound and a half of ground beef and sauteed that with the veggies (plus some salt and pepper).  When the beef is browned, i drained the fat and added a jar of Newman's Own Marinara sauce, (1) 14oz can of diced tomatoes with juice, 1 box of beef stock (plus one can also later on when the soup reduced during cooking), 2 Tbsp Dried Parsley, 2 Tbsp Oregano, 1 can drained Kidney Beans, 1 can drained White Beans, 1 Tbsp Franks Hot Sauce and about 2 Tbsp of Tomato Paste.  I simmered all of that for about an hour. I cooked the pasta separately, then added it to the finished soup.  I boiled 1 cup of dry salad macaroni pasta...but honestly, i think that's too much.  I made the mistake of just dumping all the cooked pasta in the soup instead of adding it a little at a time.  Next time I will just make a half cup of the dry pasta.  This is really a GREAT recipe and it DOES taste just like the Olive Gardens.  I'm definitely making this one again.. THANK YOU!

attributes.source_text: he at THREE BOWLS!
take it to work for lunch
it DOES taste just like the Olive Gardens

reviews.review_text: I have never reviewed a recipe before, but after making this one, following the recipe to a T... I absolutely MUST share my opinion. I am an avid fan of Olive Garden and frequent the establishment often, and this soup is almost always part of my meal. But fellow viewers, this does not taste anything at all like the copycat! I usually use Todd Wilbur's recipe from his Top Secret Recipes book, which indeed, is the exact copycat, but I wanted to do it in a crock pot this time, so found this recipe. This is missing some key ingredients and totally lacking the tang in OG's version. And where is the garlic?! I ended up adding basil, vinegar, V-8, more hot sauce, garlic, obviously, and the ditali pasta (which OG uses), and of course topped it with freshly grated parmesan like in the restaurant.... yet it still didn't taste like the "original". This recipe is more stew-like than a soup. Also note this recipe is gauged for a HUGE crock pot. Only half of it would fit in mine... "which I thought was a 5 quart". I still think it is! Five stars for the really good stab at this copycat, but it definitely is lacking in flavor.

I've never had Olive Garden's version, and we didn't follow the recipe exactly, but this was really tasty (it would be even better with some romano or parmesan but we can't have dairy anymore). We did this on the stovetop as a bit of a last minute meal and used home-canned carrots to speed up the cooking time. We used three 14.5oz cans of italian diced tomatoes, great northerns instead of white kidney, a 32oz box of beef broth, not enough oregano because we ran out mid-recipe, and small shells. We skipped the tabasco and the spaghetti sauce which resulted in a more stew-like consistency rather than soup. This was really yummy. REALLY YUMMY. It's going into our soup rotation!  Thank you @ravensmith for expanding my family's options for dairy-free ground beef recipes.

Update ~ Feb 14, 2012. Made it again for Valentines Day dinner! Again, made it on stovetop, simmering soup for about 2, 2 1/2 hours. Added pasta (elbow), al dente, about the last 1/2 hour. It was a big hit again. Family came over to eat. Served it with cornbread. Oh, one last thing, When my meat was almost done browning, I added all my veggies and seasonings to the meat until the meat was done. Drained and transfer all to my deep pot, added the rest of the ingredients (except pasta), tomatoes, broth, tomatoe sauce.
Wow!! This was soooooo good! I made the Pasta E Fagioli Soup today. It was all on ths stove ready to go at 3pm, and we were eating by 530pm. My husband and I each had 2 bowls! I followed the recipe exactly, and took the suggestions of others and cooked my pasta (elbow macaroni) on stove top, then put in with the soup right before serving. I seasoned my ground beef with seasoning salt, pepper, and garlic powder, then used the seasoings in the recipe ingredients. This Soup was fantastic! I've never had soup with pasta. We loved it and will serve again. I served with multi-grain french bread!
Thank you for sharing!!

attributes.source_text: Made it again for Valentines Day dinner

reviews.review_text: I have made a few recipes from Recipezaar for me and my wife to date.  This is the recipe that made me sign up and leave my very first review.  I love the Pasta e Fagioli soup at Olive Garden.  This is just as good. My brother-in-law who has never been to Olive Garden happened to be over when I made it and he loved it. I think this recipe is a little more hearty than the Olive Gardens but that's ok with me. I used two pounds of extra lean ground beef. I could not find beef stock so I used beef broth instead.  I could not find white kidney beans so I used northern beans.  I finally found white kidney beans and beef stock for the next time I make it. Next time I will cook the pasta seperately as other reviews have suggested as they were just to soggy in the crockpot. Still an absolutely superb recipe.

attributes.source_text: My brother-in-law who has never been to Olive Garden happened to be over when I made it and he loved it

reviews.review_text: My family loves this soup - I make the whole recipe on the stove because my crockpot is too small - and freeze half for another time. I sauté the aromatic vegetables, along with some about 3 cloves of minced garlic, then remove from the stockpot, then I cook the ground beef (sometimes I use a pound of ground beef plus a pound of chicken Italian sausage) until cooked through, and drain. Then I add the veg and everything else but the pasta (I use Penzey's Tuscan Sunset seasoning rather than just oregano and parsley), and simmer it for about 1 1/2 to 2 hours. I make the ditalini separately, about 3/4 oz per serving, and ladle the soup over the pasta. We top it with freshly grated Parmesan, and it's a meal all by itself. Thank you so much for this recipe - it's a winter staple for us.

attributes.source_text: My family loves this soup
it's a winter staple for us

reviews.review_text:
A great recipe, I made a couple changes...

-Added 1/3 cup of fresh diced parsley as indicated by some other recipes
-Used ground turkey instead, and browned it in the same stock pot, in 2TBSP olive oil
-Used Beef bouillon instead of stock (small difference)
-Instead of crock pot, I brought it to a boil and simmered for 1 hour.
-Skipped the pasta and the hot sauce. I hear the hot sauce is really important so may try it next time!

These changes weren't really because I found anything wrong with the recipe, but out of necessity and preference, and I wanted to let you know everything came out great as such.

This recipe was excellent!  I will definitely make this again and again!  I did make a few small changes, though.  First, I used some ground pork with the ground beef and sauteed about 4 minced garlic cloves with the meat.  I also sauteed the carrots, onions and celery for about 10 minutes in a small amt. of olive oil before adding them to the crock pot.  In addition I used 1 35oz can of crushed tomatoes and 1 14 oz can of petite diced tomatoes instead of the 2 large cans of diced tomatoes.  I used lots of fresh parsely and omitted the tabasco sauce.  Finally, I  cooked the pasta separately and added it to each bowl upon serving so it wouldn't make the soup starchy.  My family loved it!

attributes.source_text: My family loved it!

reviews.review_text: I made this in different batches with slight modifications to each.  Bottom line, I am Latina and love flavor.  This particular recipe is quite BLAND if followed exactly as written.<br/><br/>#1).  Where is the garlic?  Like any Italian dish, garlic is in the core and essence of the dish.  I minced 4-5 cloves and voila!<br/><br/>#2).  Salt.  It needed it.  I added some beef bouillon (Knorr brand) and a tad of sea salt and voila!<br/><br/>#3). Spices.  I found that adding a few cumin seeds, 2 bay leaves and some thyme and rosemary really made the soup pop and taste like the real deal.<br/><br/>#4).  Beans.  There is nearly not enough beans which are the "meat" of this soup.  I found that cutting down to ONE lb of beef to 4 cans of beans was perfect.  Also TWO lbs to about 4-5 beans was best.  Otherwise, you will end up with a HUGE pot of broth/meat/veggies and beans very skimpy. <br/><br/>Lastly, I made some jalapeño cornbread, salad and topped the soup with fresh Romano/Regianno and it truly is an AMAZING soup!  Enjoy!

This was a great success in our house!  I used a roaster-sized crockpot, and the recipe made a huge amount.  I used a 28 oz. can of crushed tomatoes instead of the two cans of diced tomatoes.  I couldn't find white kidney beans at my local store, so I used canned navy beans instead.  Just before the end of the cooking time, I added cooked pasta in the shape of animals. (More appealing for the kids!) Although I chopped the carrots quite small, they were still a little crunchy after cooking for 8 hours.  Next time, I'll probably cook them a bit before adding to the other ingredients. I love using my crockpot, and this recipe is definitely one that will be filed away for future use!

This was great!  I did not have any parsley so I just left that out. I added some minced garlic in the hamburger meat as I browned it. Also, instead of the diced tomatoes I added 1 (28 ounce) can of crushed tomatoes. I also added 2 tbsp of 
Worchestshire sauce and 2 tsp of chipoltle flavored tabasco sauce. I could not find white kidney beans so I added northern beans instead. Instead of adding 3 tsp of oregano I added half oregano and half italian seasoning and lots of black pepper. For the spaghetti sauce I added one can of Hunts Garlic and Herb Spaghetti sauce. For the pasta I used very small shell pasta. Wonderful, everyone loved it. My husband said it was much better than Olive Garden's.  My 13 year old had 3 bowls!

attributes.source_text: My husband said it was much better than Olive Garden's
My 13 year old had 3 bowls!

reviews.review_text: I liked this recipe but I felt it needed more spice. I added  1 tsp thyme and a little more oregano. I made the mistake of using low sodium beef broth only to have to add more salt after tasting. I did add the pasta and now wish I had not. It soaked up the broth AND I HAD TO add more beef broth and I added some tomato juice, about I cup of each.  After heating it up the second time the pasta had again soaked up the broth and it was more like goulash than soup.<br/>I will go back to Olive Garden to check it out but I think they must add the pasta just before serving or maybe make smaller BATCHES AND ADD IT TO THE SOUP and serve it soon. The pasta just keeps growing and growing the longer it sits in the soup.

This was delicious!! My fiance absolutely loved it. I changed the recipe around a little bit because I decided to make this at about 5pm at night so I didnt have time to use a crock pot. I sauteed onion, garlic, carrots, and celery for about 10 min then added the ground beef and cooked until brown. Then added one can of kidney beans, one can of great northern beans (both drained and rinsed), two cans of diced tomatoes(undrained), jar spaghetti sauce, can beef stock, 1 T oregano, 1 1/2 T parsley, 1 t pepper, 1 t salt, and a pinch of ground red pepper. Mixed that all together and let simmer for almost an hour. I then added noodles that had been semi cooked. The noodles will finish cooking in the soup. My fiance is a huge fan of Olive gardens soup and he said this tasted just like it!!

attributes.source_text: My fiance absolutely loved it
My fiance is a huge fan of Olive gardens soup and he said this tasted just like it

reviews.review_text: Excellent.  I don't eat at OG much and usually don't get this soup, so I can't compare this to that.  But as a fagioli soup, this was very very good.  5 stars for easyness, preparation, clean-up, cook-time and taste.  I didn't do the crock-pot as I didn't want to wait 7 or 8 hours so I did it on the stovetop and cooked for a couple hours.  PERFECTO!!  I also didn't use beef broth as I was trying to use up what I had in my cupboards, which was Chicken Broth.  Regardless, it still tasted GREAT.  Like other reviewers, I will cook up my pasta separately and add to the soup.  It tasted so good while cooking that I ate a bowl without the pasta b/c I didn't want to wait anymore.  YUMMY!   Thanks for a great tasting recipe!

Wonderful!  I halved the recipe for just 4 adults.  I used Recipe #266734 for the spaghetti sauce.  I ended up adding 2 cans of beef consume and it worked out great!  I aslo added 2 tsp of vinegar and about a tbl of worcestershire.  I seasoned as I went along with extra pepper and garlic salt.  Oh, and what I think made it really special was using little cheese filled tortalinis for the pasta - delish!  I cooked the soup in my crockpot for 5 hours on high.  The veggies were perfect.  Cooked the pasta separately and added to the bowls.  I made Recipe #104628 to go with it and it was a perfect combo!  Thanks, will definately make again.

OUTSTANDING! This does taste very similar to Olive Garden's pasta e fagioli!! I made this recipe for my husband and I, and it is a HUGE batch of pasta e fagioli!  I made the recipe as is, except for 2 things. I chose not to put the tobasco sauce in, as i am not a huge "spicy" fan, and people who ate it thought it still had some spice in it!  (recipe is perfect without it!) Then, Instead of throwing pasta into crockpot to cook it, i pre cooked it on the stove, and added it in to the dish after rinsing it in cool water (to slow the cooking of the pasta).  Overall i Give this 5 stars, because you cant have just one bowl!!

reviews.review_text: It was truly a hit with our family ... I did cut the celery down to 2 stalks as my husband has this thing about celery and I saute the celery and carrots in my chicken burger toward the end of its browning so they were perfectly done when the soup was .. loved it! Also, I  served our whole grain pasta by dishing it up in the bowl and then adding the soup ... we loved it this way and have no wish to try it any other way. Absolutely fabulous my son-in-law, and husband thought it was wonderful, my daughter didn't think she was going to like it, she is an extremely picky eater and she loved it! Will definitely be making it again!

items.label: Southwestern Baked Spaghetti
items.name: Southwestern Baked Spaghetti
items.description: This is an easy, yet very tasty spaghetti casserole, which reminds me of the spaghetti they used to serve us in elementary school. I loved their spaghetti! I normally only brought my lunch, but not on spaghetti day!
instructions: Cook spaghetti per package direcions.
Combine milk and egg, mix well.
Combine drained spaghetti, milk and egg; mix well.
Pour spaghetti mixture into a buttered 9X13 inch casserole dish.
Brown ground beef with onion, bell pepper and garlic in a large skillet; drain.
Return drained meat back into the skillet and add seasonings; Cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in tomato sauce and cook for 2 more minutes.
Spread meat mixture over spaghetti.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 425°F for 10 minutes or until cheese melts and is bubbly.
Remove from oven and let stand for 10 minutes.

reviews.review_text: I've never had "baked" spaghetti before. This was good. I didn't have regular spaghetti, so I used vermicelli (which only took 5 minutes to cook) and it worked well with the recipe. When I mixed the egg, milk and spaghetti together, I also stirred in 1-1/2 Tablespoons of butter, (til the butter melted) then I stirred in 1/4 cup of Kraft's Grated Parmesan Cheese. I did use abit more of the ground beef, (1-1/4 lbs.) plus I added another (8 oz.) can of tomato sauce. I doubled the spices, as suggested by others, but with the oregano, I only added 3/4 tsp of dried oregano, plus I added 3/4 tsp of dried basil. I didn't add a whole (chopped) green bell pepper, just used half a bell pepper. I took others suggestion in doubling the amount of shredded cheese, but wish I didn't, as I thought it was too much cheese. Next time I will add either a 1/2 cup (or) 3/4 cup of each, but not a cup each. Also, I did not have Monterey Jack Cheese, so I used Mozzarella, which tasted great along with the Cheddar. I did bake this as the written, (10 minutes in a 425 degree oven) and when I let it set for the 10 minutes, I covered the casserole, so it would stay hot. One more thing, before assembling casserole in baking pan, I did spray it with a no-stick canola cooking spray. Thank you Kim D for the recipe!

Made this for lunch and it was a hit! For the noodles, I left out the milk and added some spicy brown mustard in with the egg. I reduced ground beef to half a pound, and sub'd homemade spaghetti sauce instead of tomato sauce.  Also, used all cheddar (we're out of monterey jack) to top. I cooked and assembled everything last night, covered with foil, and stored in the fridge. Then, for lunchtime, I popped it in the oven for about 25 minutes at 350, just to heat it through and melt the cheese. I also topped mine with some sour cream -- delicious!  Thanks for posting, Kim D!

attributes.source_text: Made this for lunch

reviews.review_text: This was very easy to put together and came out really tasty!  I did have to make a few substitutions:  used flax pasta (good way to use up those 'healthier' pastas - you don't even notice it with this recipe), Boca soy crumbles instead of the ground beef, and 1 can of sliced black olives instead of the bell pepper.  I also subbed the monterey jack for pepper jack cheese since that is what I had.  The spices are pretty subtle so I might increase those a bit next time, but it was still very yummy!  I would suggest whisking the egg before adding it to the noodles.   Thanks for a great recipe that is easy and delicious!

attributes.source_text: The spices are pretty subtle

reviews.review_text: This was scrumptious!  I used a lot of garlic, cumin and chili powder, omitted the peppers and tossed the meat mixture with the spaghetti before topping with cheese and baking.  I'm basically incapable of doing anything other than digesting, now... I ate far to much!  If I'd been cooking for myself alone, I would have put jalapeno slices on top of the cheese before baking, and I probably would have added some diced ones to the meat mixture, too.  As it was, I satisfied my need for heat with a dash or two of Tabasco on my serving, but it was very tasty without, too.  Great comfort food!

attributes.source_text: I used a lot of garlic

reviews.review_text: After so many wonderful reviews, I was hoping my family and I would like this baked spaghetti more than we did. It was simple and easy to put together, and I liked that it used common ingredients. I made it exactly as directed. We just didn't find the resulting flavors something we cared for- it was like a taco type casserole with spaghetti--I guess my tastebuds wanted it to go one way or the other. It was not anything specific that was wrong or needed to be changed. It had very mild flavors and is not a bad recipe, nothing wrong per se, just not to our tastes. Thank you for sharing though.

Funny....I am a school nurse and still occationally eat the lunch from the school cafeteria and I do love their spaghetti with meat sauce.  When I read your description I knew I had to try this recipe and it did not disappoint!  I added 1/2 green and 1/2 red bell peppers and I was an ounce short of tomato sauce (used one 15 oz. can instead of two 8oz. cans) so I added a little ketchup to make up the difference.  The sweetness of the ketchup added a nice flavor.  I think will add a little more tomato sauce next time because it was a little dry after baking.  Thanks Kim D. for posting and I have added this to my regular meal rotation at my families request.

attributes.source_text: The sweetness of the ketchup added a nice flavor
at my families request

reviews.review_text: I screwed up royaly when I first made this dish. I doubled the pasta/egg/milk portions, and kept the meat-sauce portions as it stated. Oh Lord! I thought, "Here's some food destined for the trash can." :( Baked it anyway and it turned out FABULOUS!!! Turns out that my family is far more pasta oriented than sauce oriented and the 1:2 ratio was perfect for us! So, I've made it twice since then and we LOVE IT!!!! Read all the reviews: added fresh mushrooms; a can of Mexican Corn; chopped jalapenos; and a Prego spaghetti sauce. Left out the listed spices which my family doesn't like. This freezes so superbly that I over-make this, just to freeze it. I'd give this recipe 10 stars if I could!!

attributes.source_text: my family is far more pasta oriented than sauce oriented

reviews.review_text: This is one great dish! Putting a Mexican spin on it, I used chorizo, which is easier to get 'round here, instead of the ground beef and used asadero cheese for the same reason. I served this with garlic bread and by meal's end, myself and the five grown men I served were filled-up and pleased. I was a bit hesitant about adding the egg (I have a bit of an egg aversion), but believe it helped keep the spaghetti from drying out during the baking process. The cheesy topping has always been my favorite part of baked spaghetti dishes, so I upped the cheese to 1 1/2 cups. Thank you, Kim D., for a recipe I will certainly come back to!

attributes.source_text: Putting a Mexican spin on it
the five grown men I served were filled-up and pleased
helped keep the spaghetti from drying out
The cheesy topping has always been my favorite part

reviews.review_text: Overall we liked the recipe.  Tried to stay true to the ingredients.  That being said there was some blandness to overcome.  I think it would be easy to do by doubling the spices.  I might also try to add some diced tomatoes and some chopped mushrooms as other reviewers have suggested.  Maybe even a tablespoon of diced green chilis.  Finally to add a little flavor to the noodle part of the dish, I would add some grated parmesan when mixing the egg/milk with the  noodles.  Thanks Kim D for providing an easy recipe.  Oh I almost forgot, I think this would freeze well, but put the shredded cheese in a separate container to add closer to the end of the cooking time.

I made this recipie and my husband gave it six stars cuz he said five wouldn't do this spaghetti justice!Let me say this is the best spaghetti I have ever made or eaten in my adult life!I doubled the chili powder and the oregano.And I bought a whole bag of chedder and a whole bag of the jack cheese and mixed half in with the spaghetti noodles and the rest on the top.Other than that I followed this one to a T and it turned out delicious like nothing I have ever tasted before!Thanx for this great recipie though I better watch out because I ate nearly half the pan myself!!

attributes.source_text: my husband gave it six stars

reviews.review_text: This recipe was very easy to make and it was de-licious!  Instead of the ground beef I used ground turkey instead.  It was still fabulous! It was so good I'm making it for the potluck that I will be going to. I made the full serving for 6 even tho its just me.  I divided it up into six servings froze it and I had a ready to made dinner for the week. The only thing I had to do  was to  add a side dish or salad. . The next time when I make it I will throw in some mushrooms and maybe some olives.  For a person like me who HATE to cook this was perfect!

attributes.source_text: a ready to made dinner for the week

reviews.review_text: I made this for the first time tonight and it's pretty good. I only gave it 4 stars because as written. I think although it's a very easy and fast meal to make, it's a little bland unless you put your own flavor on it. I used a package of 93% lean ground turkey instead of beef because that's what I had (next time I may try very lean ground beef to see how I like the difference) so I had a little more meaty topping. I also added a can of petite diced tomatoes and about 1/3 cup water to help make up for the sauce I might need since my meet ratio was a little more than 16 ounces. I added a dash more black pepper, more chopped garlic and about 1 tsp. of Mexican blend spice in addition to what the regular spices were. I would consider adding crushed red peppers or a spicier chile powder next time (however my little one probably wouldn't eat it if it was spicier!). I also added about 1/2 cup more monterey jack cheese to the top since we like cheese. All in all, I like this recipe and will make it again, but I may tweak the seasoning a little more and add in a little bit more noodles if I use the turkey again (since it's more meat). I would also continue to use diced tomatoes, but I will probably use a flavored one that has peppers or is fire roasted. Yum!

I followed the recipe as closely as possible except for the changes below. I realized that I didn't have enough tomato sauce so I made my own with tomato paste, water, and 2 generous pinches of sugar (to curb the acidity).  I also used ground turkey for the meat and added a little more cheese over the top and let it brown just a bit under the broiler (just a family preference).  I read how someone thought the sauce was too soupy - it wasn't -and that the pasta was bland so I made sure to boil it in salted water (don't always do this).  This is a great recipe for a weeknight because it comes together pretty fast and I only had to wash one pot (I browned my meat in the same pot after boiling the pasta) and most importantly it's tasty!  I will make again and look forward to some of the additions other have mentioned and maybe adding just a little bit more of the spices..thanks for bringing back a much better version of a childhood memory!!

attributes.source_text: This is a great recipe for a weeknight

reviews.review_text: Yum!!!  My BF wanted spaghetti for dinner but I was tired of the same old thing... when I read the description, I knew I just had to try this one!  I also loved the spaghetti they served when I was in elementary school (many moons ago!)  I did scale it down to 3 servings, since it was only the 2 of us... but now I wish I had made the full recipe.  I really loved it and my BF ate it happily, but said he would rather he spaghetti and meatballs...  He is not one for change!!!  I made it just as written (except for the fact that I cut it in half) and I thought it was perfect.  Not too saucy, not dry at all and just the right amount of seasonings... Just delicious, easy to throw together and takes only 10 minutes to bake since all the ingredients are hot to begin with.  I served it with Recipe #18914 I had stashed away in the fridge since I could bake both at basically the same temperature for the same time.  Thanks for a keeper from my childhood!!!

attributes.source_text: My BF wanted spaghetti for dinner
my BF ate it happily

reviews.review_text:
This recipe I think has all the right ingredients, however I think it needs to be put together a bit differently.

When they spaghetti came out, the milk was runny still (even after overcooking it for an extra ten minutes) and there was hardly enough meat to satisfy my tonsils.

I would recommend: Use a bit less noodles. Use a bit more Tomato Sauce, but instead of "laying" the meat over the top, you could mix it together and it would be much better.

My only real complaint, (Since this recipe is VERY tasty) is that the noodles and the meat sauce didn't jive. I think they need to be mixed together, rather than separate. Some of you may like this, but I had a few complaints.

Great recipe overall!

This was pretty tasty.  Made it for dinner last night with only a couple of changes.  I didn't have cumin so I increased the chili powder to 1.5 tsp.  I also used 2 cups of Mild Cheddar & Monterey Jack with Jalapenos blend shredded cheese.  Finally, to avoid the dryness that some previous reviewers mentioned, I added an undrained 14.5oz can of diced tomatoes (the tomatoes added a nice extra element to the texture).  In the future, I would probably at least partially drain the diced tomatoes because it added slightly too much extra liquid, but it wasn't runny and I certainly didn't have any problems with dry pasta.  I layered 1 cup of the cheese on top of the spaghetti mixture, topped that with the meat mixture, and then followed with the second cup of cheese on top.  Had leftovers for lunch and put some sour cream on top and that made it even better.  Thanks for posting, my family enjoyed it!

attributes.source_text: Made it for dinner last night

items.label: Potato Salad
items.name: Potato Salad
items.description: I make this all summer long. We have to have this anytime we grill or BBQ which is often. Never, never any left-over.
instructions: Cook potatoes in boiling water to cover 40 minutes or until tender; drain and cool.
Peel potatoes and cut into 1 inch pieces.
Chop egg whites.
In a large bowl, stir together potato, egg whites, 1/2 t. salt and green onions.
Using a fork, mash the yolks in a small bowl; add in remaining 1/2 t. salt, mayo, pickle relish, mustard, pepper, and celery seed; stirring until well blended.
Gently stir yolk mixture into potato mixture; adjust seasoning to taste with salt and pepper.
Cover and chill 2 hours (it is even better if you can chill this overnight and serve the next day).

reviews.review_text: This is a great recipe ... I've made this same potato salad for years, with a few minor variations, and it is always the one dish that is asked for at every gathering. I make the "dressing" ahead of time (even the day before, if I'm pressed for time), adding both the mashed hard-boiled egg yolks and diced egg whites into the dressing. I also gently toss 1/2 lb. (cooked) crispy crumbled bacon with the potatoes just before adding the dressing; this helps keep the bacon crispy for a longer period of time. I use chopped dill pickles, rather than sweet, and diced celery for a bit more texture. And, I hope it is okay to mention a brand name here because I only use Hellmann's mayo; other brands just don't give this dish the same great flavor we're used to. Enjoy!

attributes.source_text: crispy crumbled bacon
this helps keep the bacon crispy for a longer period of time
it is always the one dish that is asked for at every gathering

reviews.review_text: LOVE this potato salad recipe!!  I live in northern Malaysia where the people LOVE spicy hot in EVERYTHING so I thought I'd try adding 3 small green thai chilis to this recipe and WOW...this one is a winner for sure.  If you don't like spicy don't add em in but if you do, try putting just 1-2 chilies sliced up in this salad.  I made this exactly as the recipe said the first time and then started experimenting the 2nd and 3rd times.  I also, as some other reviewers did, thought it just a smidge bland 1st time around so added 2 tsp of cider vinegar to the dressing before adding it to the other ingredients ever since.  Thanks for this very basic, but great, potato salad recipe!!  Oh almost forgot...I ran out of celery seeds from making this so often so this last time I just chopped up and added 1/2 c celery... WONDERFUL!!

We made this to the "T" for Memorial Day weekend, but had to doctor it a lot.  I wanted to give it a 5 based on all the other reviews, but for us, it wasn't ok as written...it turned out dry and very bland for us.  (Used Hellman's Light, and I do think the mayo one uses makes a huge difference...maybe with something else, it would have been perfect.)   We added:  1 cup sour cream, 1 very finely chopped med onion, 1/2 cup of chopped celery + salt, sugar and mustard to taste.  In the end, we made a delicious salad, but I think I could have gotten there without this recipe, so I'll say that this one is a good start!  I do disagree with Chef #837995 who says that this is too sweet...I didn't think I liked sweetened potato salad, in fact, most store bought is too sweet for us, but as written, it didn't even taste a bit sweet to me...the only sweet addition, as written, is 2 T pickle relish (unless you use a sweetened mayo/salad dressing brand).   I liked the combination of mayo with light sour cream (Reduced Fat Breakstone is awesome.)  The celery seed is good in there, I ended up adding in a bit more of that, too.   Thank you!

reviews.review_text: I guess July 4th was Nurse Di day in our home. To compliment the steak kabobs we bar-b-qued I made these mushroom skewers, her potato salad and her rainbow pasta salad. The mushroom skewers were gone before I could even serve the meal, the only reason I had  potato salad and rainbow pasta salad left was because I doubled the recipes so we would have some leftovers during the week. I did make the mushroom skewers with margarine in lieu of butter since I keep kosher and could not baste them with butter when serving with a meat meal. Obviously, the margarine made no difference, I tripled the mushroom recipe and THERE WAS NOTHING LEFT. Thanks Nurse Di!!!

reviews.review_text: Yet another FABULOUS recipe from Nurse Di!! I loved this potato salad! I made pretty much exactly as directed and it was creamy and had just the perfect flavour! Though I love my Mom's potato salad and I usually follow her method, (which is just a throw together and not a specific recipe)I may be abandoning it for this one, as I found it easier to have specific amounts, that produced the desired flavour & consistency,without having to add a little more salt here, a little more pepper there, another spoonful of miracle whip....( which sometimes leads me to overdo it!) This comes out JUST the way I like it in the end, with no second guessing! I did make extra hard boiled egg, which I sliced to arrange over top of the salad once in the serving bowl, and I topped it all off with a sprinkling of paprika. Next time I'm going to try it with  a can of peas and some grated carrot added in, which we always include in our potato salad. Though I must say I thoroughly enjoyed this as is, and no additions are really needed,the taste is right on, but I do like the added colour that the peas and carrots give. My sister tried this and the next time she made potato salad she called me for the recipe! (she uses Mom's method normally too....you may have turned us into traitors!!!!!! LOL!!) Thank you so much for a delicious (and easy!) recipe! :)

Now i really just don't like potato sald at all, therefore i have never made it. Though beeing i have a goop as beeing a great cook, i didn't want to let everyone down, so i went on a search for a recipe that looked good, i came across this one and saw it had good reviews so i gave it a go! I like the idea of the egg yolks being mashed and also using green onions...they were not as strong as regular onions. I think this was better the next day when even more thoroughly chilled. Out of the four of us who had it, 2 people thought it was awesome and 2 people thought is was very good but like my regular recipe better (creatures of habit!), so I guess a 4.5 would be my rating, but rounding up to a 5 ;)!  Thanks for sharing!

I've never been a fan of making potato salad, but this one is a keeper!  First, make sure you don't overcook the potatoes!  This seems to be the problem I've had in the past.  Followed the recipe and ingredients nearly exact except I used horseradish prepared mustard (Webers) which gave this a nice kick!  I also added 6 slices of finely chopped cooked bacon!  I made it again today and pre-peeled and diced the potatoes.  It seemed to go more quickly this way because they cook and cooler faster!  We're really enjoying this simple and tasty recipe!

reviews.review_text: This was a very good recipe. It makes a metric ton, so be sure to have a really large bowl on hand for mixing it all up. While this is a great traditional standby, I may add a little more mustard, or perhaps some cider vinegar to the next batch in order to make it a little more tangy. Also, I followed the recipe exactly, but next time I'd quarter or dice the potatoes prior to boiling, in order to shorten the boiling time and make it easier to dress. (Slicing up soft potatoes makes them even mushier.) Thank you for the recipe!

I will say this is a good potato salad recipe. However, I thought the dressing was a bit too mild. However, if kids or timid taste buds are on your guest list, then this is the one for you. Mind you, I will enjoy eating this (it's a lot like egg salad, which I love, with potatoes in it.) However, next time, I'll try something with a bigger hit to the tongue or modify this. reviews.review_text: Great salad.  I made it the night before serving it.  As mentioned by a reviewer, I doubled the sauce, so that I can you use the secound half to re-moist the salad before serving the following day.  One lesson I did learn while making this recipe, never through potatoes into boiling water.  Fill the pot with cold water, and throw in the potatoes, do NOT wait for the water to get hot. If you do, potatoes come out mushy and messy.  Most people know this, but figured, I would throw it in for all those beginner cooks like myself.

I love this recipe... however, if you don't already know this, the key to a really exceptional potato salad is to dice up whole pickles or pickle spears in place of the relish. You'll never go back once you do this. It makes an unbelievable difference! Anyway, other than that the only changes I make to this recipe are to use dried onion flakes instead of the green onions (my stomach doesn't tolerate raw onions for some reason) and double the mustard. I also try to peel and dice the potatoes beforehand when I remember.

This was really good.  I used new red potatoes, steamed with the skin on.  Once cooled, I chopped into big chunks.  I mixed the dressing and put it in the fridge for the flavours to blend, then added it to the potatoes, eggs and green onions.  I accidently poured in too much celery seed, but it didn't harm the recipe at all.  In fact, it gave better flavour.  We had leftovers tonight and it's even better the next day.  I don't make potato salad often, but with this AZ desert heat, I will definitely be making this again!  Thanks Nurse Di!

The only change I really made was peeling & dicing the potatoes before cooking. 
I made sure to chill the salad overnight & serve the next day (small family gathering) for better results.

The texture was great! Creamy dressing, and the potatoes held their shape well, but overall flavor (even with the celery seeds) was a bit "plain" for my tastes. My brother & husband said it tasted pretty good.

4 stars, because I would make this one again (for Office Potluck/Family Cookout/BBQ, as it makes a lot of salad). Maybe Miracle Whip instead of Mayo next time for more tangyness???

items.description: This chicken recipe is so easy, I hesitated in posting it. But I couldn't find it posted here, and it's so good, I thought I'd share it. It's my favorite way to bake chicken because it's moist and tender every time and the flavor is delicious!
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Spray a shallow baking dish with non-stick cooking spray.
Rinse chicken breast under cool running water.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Place chicken in dish.
Brush the melted butter over the chicken, using all the butter.
Sprinkle with seasoned salt.
Bake for 50-60 minutes or until cooked through.
~NOTE~Chicken takes only 50 minutes in my oven.
Don't over cook, as they might turn out tough.

reviews.review_text: I needed something simple, something quick.  I didn't have alot of other ingredients here at the house and I didn't want to make a special trip to the market.  I found Kim's recipe.  I thought, "Wow, how simple, but I bet it will be so bland."  OMG, the smell while it cooked was hypnotizing.  I didn't use the same seasoning.  I used McCormick CA Style Garlic Salt  w/ parsley and Lawry's seasoned pepper. If I hadn't of tasted the chicken myself, I wouldn't of believed how delicious it is.  It's so easy and so tasty.  At this point, I don't know when I will make chicken any other way.  And I'm having to rethink buying boneless, skinless breasts because cooked this way, the skin is yummy!  Thanks so much!

Ok,have been unsuccessful at baking chicken for the last 30 years,always too dry,too bland,just not quite right.I know this recipe sounds too easy and simple to produce a sumptuous (sic?) chicken breast,but it really does.I do them 50 minutes,even the huge mac daddy over fed fat chicken breasts,and they are always perfectly done.I do let them rest for 15 minutes or so after I take them out,then take it all off the bone and slice up.I toss it all back into the yummy drippings and toss around to coat,then serve.My VERY picky husband and children always eat lots when I serve this.This will forever be my go to chicken dish!!

I made this last night.........and EASY ?   Wow. I didn't think I could get this much flavor and crispy skin from such a simple recipe.  
I had frozen a cut-up chicken and made two breasts and a thigh (there are only 3 of us).  I did find that even tho I left them in the ove for 45 min. , I think I could have taken them out at about 35 min.

I can't think of any reason to work harder with complicated recipes,when this turned out so great.

reviews.review_text: Due to procrastination on my part, I was left with nothing thawed for Sunday dinner for DH and myself. All I had were two chicken hind quarters left from a 10 lb. bag I'd bought the day before. I had it earmarked for soup but I thought "What the heck." I brined them for an hour, using a quart of water w/ 1/4 cup of kosher salt dissolved in it. I lined a samll baking pan with foil and wrapped a small baking rack as well. I followed the recipe as written only using less butter of course, and it was a combination af real butter and I Can't Believe It's Not Butter. The seasoning I used was just a generic season-all blend. I made sure to pat dry the pieces really well before hand. A previous review stated that brined chicken wouldn't come out crispy, but that wasn't true in my case. 45 minutes in the oven, uncovered, with a five minute rest worked really well. The chicken was moist and the skin was wonderfully crispy! Such a delightful result from two lower class cuts of chicken! Served it with warm buttered french bread, canned corn, and tossed salad. Great quality from low budget fare. Wonderful, simple recipe I'll use again and again! Five stars!

the skin was wonderfully crispy

Who knew something so easy could be so good?? I used 6 chicken breasts to 1 cube of butter, and instead of the seasoned salt I used salt, pepper, rosemary and sage. Even the refrigerated leftovers were tender and juicy!
10/07/2012 UPDATE: This is now my go-to for chicken breasts! I get the boneless, skinless chicken breasts in a bag and just throw them into a casserole dish - still frozen! - and top them with the melted butter (sometimes I substitute the butter with olive oil). Then I top them with whatever seasonings tickle my fancy that day and bake at 450 degrees in the convection oven for about 30-40 minutes, depending on the size of the chicken breasts. They come out tender and juicy and delicious!

The skin was brown and crispy and with the BBQ sauce it tasted almost as good as grilled.  It was very tender and moist inside too. items.label: Wholly Guacamole
items.name: Wholly Guacamole
items.description: This is a true Tex-Mex recipe concocted by a distant relative stationed at the Alamo nearly 160 years ago. According to family lore, he was out looking for some good tomatoes when Santa Ana attacked the now famous Texas landmark. Luckily, our relative kept this recipe in the lining of his coon-skin cap, and both he and his avocado dip lived to fight another day. Years later, near death from an infected Chihuahua bite, he looked deep into his son's eyes, and with his last breath, uttered the familiar phrase "Remember... the...guacamole."
instructions: Cut avocados in half, remove pit, and spoon avocado into a mixing bowl.
Add minced garlic and squeeze the juice from one-half of the lime into the bowl of avocado.
Mash the ingredients together to desired consistency using the back of a large spoon or a potato masher (some like the avocado chunky, some like it smoother).
Fold in diced tomato and diced onion, a couple pinches of salt, and the juice from the remaining lime half (Also add cilantro or peppers at this time).
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for 30-45 minutes.
Uncover and taste.
Add salt as needed.
If you don't give the resulting guacamole at least 4 stars, then you ain't making it right.
NOTE: The purpose of the lime is to allow any leftover guacamole to retain its \
color as it sits in the fridge.

Some folks use lemon, but it's been my experience that if you accidentally add too much lemon, it seriously affects the guacamole's flavor; if you happen to add too much lime, the guacamole just gets a little more tangy.
If you find the leftover guacamole has darkened, simply stir it before eating and use more fresh lime juice next time.
Wholly guacamole may be used as a topper with tacos, enchiladas, fajitas, etc.
However, some say it is at its best with a bowl of warm tortilla chips and an ice cold beer.

reviews.review_text:
Wholly Guacamole...this was good stuff!!!  This will be my "go to" guacamole recipe from now on.  My family had this for a Cinco de Mayo/Supermoon party this year and it was a hit.  Like another reviewer said, they were sold on trying this by the story that went with it.  Loved it!!  I read somewhere that if you put the avocado pit in with the guacamole that it also helps it from turning brown along with the plastic wrap trick on laying it right on the dip.  I put a couple in and the next day it was still beautifully green.  Thanks for sharing a great recipe!!
UPDATE March 4, 2016: I found a new way to keep it fresh and green looking. When ready to store, forget the pit and plastic wrap technique. Instead, push down guacamole to get all the air out and smooth top. Add about 1/2" of LUKEWARM water and close with a tight fitting lid. Sounds weird but it works. On the 3rd day it was still green. Do this every time you get out and use.

attributes.source_text: My family had this for a Cinco de Mayo/Supermoon party this year and it was a hit

reviews.review_text: I've made this many times, but I'm just now getting around to rating it.  This is the absolute best guacamole I have ever made.  I love good guacamole and I try it at every Mexican restaurant I go to.  Sadly, most restaurants don't know how to make very good guac.  Everyone loves it when I make it.  Once I found this recipe my search was over.  I would give it 10 stars if I could.  And I disagree with Carla.  I like the chef and his story.  Nothing like a good hand-me-down family story to accompany a good handed down family recipe.  Thanks for sharing your family with the rest of us!

Very very very good!!!  OK, I kind of cheated and didn't let it sit 30-45 minutes, but I think it sat long enough, because it was AWESOME! My sister gave me 4 humongus avocados from a friend's tree in West Palm Beach.  Each of these, I kid you not, was almost as big as my head. They were gorgeous and needed an excellent recipe to do them justice.  I used only 2 for my recipe since I am assuming that the recipe was referring to Haas avocados which are quite a bit smaller- I also used green onions instead of the white and added a bit of oregano.  This guacamole was as good as any that I have had in authentic Mexican restaurants.  I have never made guacamole this good! Shows you what great ingredients and an amazing recipe can do! Thanks Mark!!!! :o)

A true winner.  "I HATE AVOCADOS AND I HATE GUACAMOLE" are the words of the better half.  Even after having him try "my" version of guacamole, he states "It's good, but I just don't like avocados".  Well that all changed tonight when he could not keep his chips out of the guacamole bowl! This is a Godsend because of the health benefits of avocado, so, I thank you in advance for his reduced high cholesterol to come.  A MUST TRY! Side note- I added all of the optional ingredients, and I think that made all of the difference.

attributes.source_text: he could not keep his chips out of the guacamole bowl

reviews.review_text: I made this AGES ago.  I can't believe I have not rated it.  This is seriously great guacamole.  It is as good as any guacamole I have had in Mexican restaurants.  And we have a LOT of great Mexican food here in Texas.  I have a good friend who is Mexican, and she says the ONLY onions you should use when making guacamole or salsa are WHITE onions, not yellow ones.  So, just a tip for you.  One time I made this and realized I had no fresh chilies, so I used some sliced pickled ones and it was really good, too!  Don't leave out the cilantro....definitely not as good.  Thanks for the recipe!

This was such a fantastic guacamole !!! I love your intro for this recipe....I had cut this recipe in half because it was just the two of us to go along with Recipe #60316  Cheese Spinach Quesadillas....Such a great flavor...and so easy and fast to put together. I made it in the morning for lunch and it kept it's nice green color. I would of added the cilantro but it was on special at the grocery store this week and there was none to be had....I could definitely see myself sitting and just eating a bowl of this stuff myself !!!! Thanks so much for sharing Mark....we loved it.

attributes.source_text: I made it in the morning for lunch

reviews.review_text: I would so love to give this 5 stars but it is missing a few fine points to make it truly outstanding. Everything in the recipe as stated is great, but it still needs a few helpers included to put it on top. Cumin, you need to add maybe 1/2 t in this, more or less to taste. Also maybe a pinch or more of cayenne. I know the jalapeños will add heat but the cayenne gives it a more rounded heat and dimension. As stated this recipe is a solid 4 stars but can be improved with the additions I stated above. Thanks for submitting a good recipe!

(First time -- 4 stars) This is a nice guacamole recipe.  I made it according to the recipe, including cilantro (I think that should be required) and excluding peppers.  It was yummy and easy to make.  I served it as a taco topping or as a dip for tortilla chips.

(Second time -- 5 stars) I made this a second time including the jalapenos and 1 T chopped black olives.  Wow!  Those jalapenos made a great difference.  Took it to a pot luck with chips and overheard nice comments like, 'This is all I'm going to eat tonight'.

So...if you make this, be sure to include the jalapenos and cilantro.  (And adding some chopped black olives are pretty good too.)  Also, don't be shy with the salt.

attributes.source_text: Took it to a pot luck

reviews.review_text: We were going to a poolside BBQ and I had picked up some store bought guacamole to go with our fajitas.  My husband stared at it in horror and anounced "You can't take that!" "These are native Floridians honey, they don't even know what guacamole is," I replied.  Well the guacamole purist had his way and we made homemade guacamole, using this recipe.  It was great guacamole and everyone loved it!  I would recommend this recipe to anyone who likes avocados, it is perfect for the afficiando and beginner taste buds.

attributes.source_text: We were going to a poolside BBQ

reviews.review_text: This is THE BEST guacamole I have EVER tasted!!!  If I could give 10 stars, I would.  I made it chunky and it is SO MUCH BETTER than the restaurants!!  You can't have guacamole without cilantro and jalapeno!  I made my own chips and it was PERFECT with my fajitas!!!  I always put the pits in the guac to keep it from turning brown.  You can also put plastic inside the bowl directly on top of the guac and up the sides of the bowl, but the pit(s) is so much easier.  THANKS FOR THE RECIPE!!!!

reviews.review_text: Hmmm.....What do I like better, the description or the recipe?  It's a toss up...they're both 5 stars! hehe  We absolutely LOVED this guacamole, Mark!  I have always made guac with lemon, but this time tried it with lime, and you are totally right that it's better.  I did add that little jalapeño--and I am glad I did!  I love food that bites back a little.  I think you have converted me to my plain old guac recipe to your family treasure, Mr. Hendricks!  Light a candle for the ancestors for me!  :)

attributes.source_text: I love food that bites back a little

reviews.review_text: This was excellent!  I made this for a football fajita party and it was a huge hit.  Usually I can take or leave guacamole but I've never had it prepared this way and I loved it!  I used lime juice rather than limes and just kept adding till it tasted good.  Rather than cut a tomato I used a can of diced tomatoes.  I used about 3/4 of a large white onion and added cilantro (fresh) as well as some cayenne pepper and cumin. items.label: Amazing Chicken Marinade
items.name: Amazing Chicken Marinade
items.description: This recipe came from Allrecipes (Ruth Crickmer). My whole family loved it even though it cooked too fast. The original recipe said 'high heat' on the grill, which my husband did. It ended up cooking 8 minutes total, charred but not burnt tasting, and very juicy and flavorful. We'll turn down the heat next time for texture, but this is a keeper in our home!
instructions: In a large, non-reactive container, whisk together ingredients beginning with cider vinegar through salt.
Then whisk in olive oil and pepper.
Place chicken in the mixture.
Cover and marinate chicken in the fridge 8 hours or overnight.
Remove chicken from marinade just before you turn on your grill or broiler to let come up a few degrees.
Discard marinade.
Lightly oil your grill or broiler pan.
Grill or broil about 10 minutes per side.

reviews.review_text: I was so pleased with how this turned out! I only had 4 chicken breasts, and had to marinate them in my old pyrex pie plate since I was out of ziploc freezer bags (what I usually marinate in), but I could have easily fit 2 or 3 more chicken breasts in (there's plenty of marinade) and after tasting these tonight at dinner, I wish I had had more chicken to marinate! Delicious! I marinated my chicken overnight, and I did use more garlic than the recipe calls for. Also, in my quest to use up a bottle of key lime juice, I used 2 tbsp of that in lieu of the lemon and lime juice called for in the recipe. These grilled up nicely, without too much charring (not the recipe's fault -- our bbq is on its last legs). I'll be using this marinade all summer!

attributes.source_text: I did use more garlic than the recipe calls for

reviews.review_text: The first time I made this, I may of cooked it too high and it burnt the marinade on the chicken so I did not rate it.  So not giving in, I tried it again as all these votes could not be wrong.  The only thing I did different was to cook the chicken breast in the pan with the marinade not too high at all.  As I was not well prepared, I could only marinade the chicken for approx three and half hours but truly, it came out just fantastic.  The marinade reduced as it was cooking so it became a beautiful sauce accompaniment to the chicken as well.  I had only planned on eating half of my half breast but devoured it all.  It was worth every kilojoule!  Thanks GinnyP It's a keeper here as well.

I've made this marinade for company three different times now, substituting Splenda brown sugar mixture, and it has always received raze reviews and requests for the recipe.  I've marinated the chicken overnight each time (basically for about 24 hours) and it has been awesome.  I've doubled the amount of garlic as well, because we all love garlic.  While very fragrant in the marinade, the garlic flavour has not overwhelmed the other flavours when cooked.  I start the chicken baebecuing on medium heat, and then turn it down to low part way through, and it has worked very well.  High heat would simply charcoal the meat (at least on my BBQ).  I've also found that this quantity of marinade will do at least 10-12 breasts easily.  Great recipe, thanks for posting Ginny!

reviews.review_text: This recipe was absolutely fantastic. As many have said before, it really doesn't need another 5-star rating, but I felt I'd also throw my 2-cents in. Not being one for chicken breast, but dieting, I needed something to make this chicken much better than the dry white meat it is. I didn't have the required type of mustard that the recipe called for, so I used French's yellow mustard, like others suggested. I also had no lime juice, so 3 tablespoons of lemon juice was what I used for the citrus. I only marinated it for 8 hours and cooked it on the grill. It came out juicy, flavorful, and delicious. DH also loved it, eating the entire chicken breast in just a few minutes, even burning his tongue slightly in the process (whoops!). This marinade lived up to it's name, even with substitutes! Wow. Simple. I will be making this recipe again!

DH also loved it

reviews.review_text:
Delicious.  Wasn't sure what to expect but was pleasantly surprised.  Will definately be making again.. and then have my sister try it! 

I reduced the recipe by 1/6th to try.

My ingredient changes were to use splenda brown sugar substitute, whole grain dijon mustard, garlic granuals, bottled lime juice, and omitting the lemon juice and the oil.

Chopped up a boneless skinless chicken breast into 3/4" cubes.  

Put chicken in a small plastic sandwich bag, add marinade ingredients, smush chicken & marinade together to mix.

Stored in freezer for a few weeks,  unthawed, kept in fridge for 12 hours.  Panfried with no oil.

Ok, I did *major* improvisation on this recipe, and it still turned out, so it definitely deserves all its stars!  I used White wine vinegar instead, normal mustard instead of seeded.  I didn't have lime, so I increased the lemon, then placed some lemon slices on top of the chicken while it marinated.  No fresh garlic, but powder seemed to do it.  Like I said, I'm amazed that it turned out!  The only thing I found was that it needs to be grilled at a relatively low heat because the sugar in the marinade burns quickly.  Other than that, it was great and the chicken turned out moist, juicy and flavourful.   Definitely a keeper!

attributes.source_text: the chicken turned out moist
juicy

reviews.review_text: Mark, I have to admit to ignorance, but I am not sure what coarse grain mustard is so I used regular ole French's mustard.  Other than that, followed your ingredient list exactly and blended it all together in my blender because I was too lazy to mince the garlic.  This made plenty of marinade for 10 thighs which we grilled outdoors after about 6 hrs. marinating time.  You are right!  This is a wonderful marinade for chicken.  I left the skin on the thighs for grilling because I believe it helps keep the meat moist. The combination of this marinade and grilling gives the chicken a finger-lickin' good flavor!  We will be using this recipe often.

reviews.review_text: I know I'm the bad one here, but I didn't care much for this recipe. I marinaded the chicken overnight per instructions and grilled the chicken on the pit. Anytime you use sugar in a marinade you have to be careful because the sugar can and will burn easily. I didn't have any issues with this, but you need to watch your chicken. Taste? Well....there was no flavor from the marinade inside the chicken. I've had just as good results (if not better) soaking the chicken in simple Italian dressing with some added spices. Unfortunately, this recipe won't be going into my recipe box.

This marinade is fantastic and so easy to make. I have everything on hand (I just used bottled lime and lemon juice, and it turned out fine). I marinated chicken tenderloins overnight (about 19 hours, total) and fried them off in a pan on the stovetop. I served them over a salad for a light dinner and it was delicious. I used dijon mustard instead of coarse grain (because it sounded good) and mixed everything up in a gallon size zipper bag (because I'm lazy and didn't want to wash another bowl. I cna't wait to try this out on the grill--I'm sure it will be even better!

reviews.review_text: `Sorry Yooper, This recipe really didn't produce the results I was looking for. I think I may be looking for a recipe that is unobtainable for boneless, skinless breasts -one that will produce a crisy, brown, but still moist breast of chicken. Made your full recipe of sauce so have plenty left over which I have stored in a jar. I may try it on pork chops or perhaps some cut of bone in chicken in the near future(before I think the sauce is getting a little too old to use and have to throw it out. However, Many thanks for taking the time to post your recipe.

This is a sweet chicken marinade so if you are not ok with that, then stay away! Ok, So I didn't have all of the called for ingredients on hand so I had to substitute a bit. I used 2 tb of spicy brown mustard. Left out the lime juice because I didnt' have a lime or lime juice, had to use 1 ts of minced garlic as I didn't have fresh , 1 ts of salt, 2 tsp of lemon juice from a jar. I marinated for about 6 hours then drained the marinade off and baked the thin sliced chicken breasts in the oven on 375 for 15 minutes.  I think next time I will just saute it in a pan to get it a little crisyp but either way it was very tasty!

reviews.review_text: I'll see this recipe pop up constantly but never got around to using it; so I was SUPER excited when I finally had the time to try this, and let me tell you, this was just SO delicious. I had skinless chicken thighs (bone in) and marinated them for over 24 hours, and the chicken ended up so moist and full of flavour! And the sauce was to die for! I think next time, I'd reserve the marinade after putting the chicken in the oven, then cook it on the stove top to help reduce it a bit more and get a nice, thicker consistency. Also I think the only other minor thing I'd do next time is to maybe reduce the brown sugar just a tad, but other than that, this was perfect! Thank you!

Not that this needs another review: but it was great! Here's a few of my tips and subs:
1. Replace lime juice for lemon juice. 
2. I included some freshly chopped herbs - oregano, tarragon and thyme. 
3. I wasn't in the mood for grilling, so dumped my chicken breasts (having marinated for 6 hours) into a baking dish with the marinade, covered with foil and baked for 1 hr at 180 degrees celcius. 
Delicious! I was worried that the marinade would be too acidic and would make the chicken too mushy, but it was just right! This is a regular "company" dish, served with steamed veg or salad and potato bake. 
Thanks Ginny!

reviews.review_text: The marinade itself is perfect. Don't change anything. Marinade all day or overnight. I haven't come across anything better and neither has anyone I've cooked it for or shared it with. Every time someone tells me ahead of time that they already have a chicken marinade and will never change, I laugh inside. They always switch to this one once they have tried it. I recommend using boneless skinless chicken thighs because boneless chicken breasts tend to dry out when grilled. Cook extra so that the next day you can heat up a thigh to make a chicken sandwich for lunch. Use a nice bun, leaf lettuce, and a tablespoon or so of freshly made pico de gallo on top. Nothing else. Give it a try. You will be amazed how well these flavors combine. Unless you hate cilantro and pico de gallo in general, you will be hooked.
