The egg white makes for a really nice crust
the olive oil gives the bottom a nice crunch

reviews.review_text: I made the dough in the bread machine by first warming the water and butter in the microwave for a minute then I added the dry ingrediants and put the yeast on top.  Even though I accidently put both tablespoons of butter in the dough it still came out good.  I used 2 3/4 cups of flour and only 2 teaspoons of the sugar. Shaped the loaves and let them rise and then used an egg wash (beaten egg yolk with a smidge of water to loosen)  then just sprinkled with sea salt.  I also put a pan of water on the bottom rack to help with the crust.  Not sure if it made a difference or not. A keeper for sure. Thanks.

I love this recipe! My 2nd batch of this delicious bread just came out of the oven. I made the 1st batch following the recipe verbatim using my kitchenaid mixer w/ dough hook and it ended up a little flat (shape-wise but the flavor was phenomenal) so i tried it again with my food processor w/ dough blade, and used the full 2 1/2 cups of flour, and didn't let it rise as long (about 20 min) after forming the loaves, and it turned out amazing! I did brush the bread with eggwhites the 2nd time around and sprinkled some kosher salt on about 15 minutes into the cooking of the bread. 10 Stars! Thank you hunter for an easy yet delicious recipe! :)

I will give this about 3.5 stars to 3.75.  Some things I noticed with the recipe is it did not address making the crust "Crispy". So to adapt to do that I boiled some water and placed it in a pan below the baking bread and spritzed the top of the bread at the beginning and 2 more times at 5 minute intervals.  It crisp the bread but it still needed a bit more TLC.  the bread  already baked completely, so I spritzed a little olive oil and placed it below the broiler briefly to get the color I desired.  Immediately after removing it from the oven, I brushed it with butter and salt.<br/><br/>Be aware that this is a delicate dough when it is rising.  Once you touch it, the rise deflates, so handle with care.  When mixing use the two cups of flour until mixed well and add additional flour as needed.  I did not need to use the other 1/2 cup as my achieved the proper texture with only 2 cups.  Remember not all flours measure in volume the same versus weight.<br/><br/>It was a very good bread, but I would probably add additional rosemary both in and on the bread, maybe another tablespoon total.  In addition, (Macaroni Grill does not add this) I think adding a very fine crushed garlic mixed with olive oil just before putting it under a broiler will take this up a level.  I LOVE the bread at Macaroni Grill and will say this is close, but not quite.  Excellent attempt at a recreation recipe.  I will update this again as this recipe is a good one to start perfecting to achieve the results of the Macaroni Grill.

attributes.source_text: It crisp the bread
this is a delicate dough when it is rising

reviews.review_text: We love Macaroni Grill, esp. the bread.  So this recipe was greatly appreciated.  I followed the directions AND some of the suggestions posted in the reviews.  Followed the ingredients list but needed about 3 cups of flour.  Used my BM, the dough cycle.  Used fresh rosemary, chopped it up fine.  Brushed the loaves with egg white during the baking, got a nice crisp top. Put chopped fresh rosemary and sea salt on the top too.  Most important:  it has to be eaten right after baking, out of this world.  Dip in olive oil/balsamic vinegar combo.  Oh...to die for.  This is a keeper, to be repeated many times!!

attributes.source_text: got a nice crisp top

reviews.review_text: This was my first time baking bread and I was glad to find that it wasn’t as difficult as I thought it would be. This recipe was delicious. We try to go as healthy as we can so after reading a few reviews it was made with 50/50 whole wheat and AP flour. I also subbed EVOO for the butter. Finally, I sprinkled garlic powder & kosher salt on top, We thought it was great. It was almost too easy. I will be making this again (at least once the exact way it is provided); and probably can get a little more creative with the flavors. Thanks. ps, they looked as beautiful as they were delicious but I had an issue uploading.

Yum! I've tried many different bread recipes but this one was one of the best I've made. I have a rosemary bush in my garden so anytime I see a recipe that calls for it I don't hesitate. I used my kitchen aid to mix up the dough. If you're using a stand mixer you made need a little extra flour to keep it from climbing the hook. I used maybe an extra 1/4-1/2 a cup beyond the 2 1/2 specified in the recipe and my dough didn't become tough at all. It also baked up in about 17 minutes to a lovely golden brown. I did put a pan of water in the oven to help with the crust.

I agree with so many of the other reviewers -- this was fabulous!  The dough was so easy to work with -- I used my Kitchenaid with the dough hook.  I could have probably added another tablespoon or two of flour -- the dough was very soft.  But once it was baked, it was just so soft and fluffy.  I only used the one tablespoon of rosemary -- I didn't sprinkle any additional on the tops of the loaves.  After brushing the butter on the top of the loaves, I sprinkled a fair amount of very course kosher salt on the loaves.  We really enjoyed this bread -- and look forward to making it many more times in the future.

attributes.source_text: it was just so soft and fluffy
it was just so soft and fluffy

reviews.review_text:
I can be fairly critical of "copycat" recipes if I know what the real thing tastes like and it doesn't match. I LOVE Macaroni Grill's bread, and this to me tastes almost exactly like it! The only thing I did differently was that I used Herbes de Provence instead of just rosemary, because after making the dough I discovered I was out of rosemary! 

It just came out of the oven about 10 minutes ago and one loaf is gone already between me and four boys. I don't fancy myself as being the best breadmaker, but this recipe sure made me feel like I was! Thank you so much! I will make this again, and again, and again!!!

attributes.source_text: one loaf is gone already between me and four boys

reviews.review_text: This did taste very much like the bread at Macaroni Grill. The only thing I thought was different for me was the texture. My loaves rose very nicely while proofing, but didn't bake up very high in the oven. The texture was a little crumbly too, so I don't know if I did something wrong at the end or not. I did brush the tops with egg wash before baking and that did make a nice crust on the top. I will try this recipe again, and even though it didn't turn out the exact way I wanted, it was great to dip in the sauce from the Carmela's Chicken Rigatoni recipe I made to go with it!!

attributes.source_text: that did make a nice crust on the top

reviews.review_text: This was a very easy recipe to put together. I didn't have any rosemary on hand, so I used dried italian seasoning which was still delicious and still tasted somewhat like Macaroni Grill's bread.My bread did not brown a whole lot, but I kind of liked it that way. I rubbed butter on the top after baking because I like a soft crust on bread like this. I baked it on a sheet pan that had been lightly coated with olive oil, which crisped the bottom crust a bit and gave it a wonderful extra note of flavor. I'd recommend that. This will definitely be made over and over again! Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: I like a soft crust on bread like this
which crisped the bottom crust a bit

reviews.review_text: Awesome Bread! I did add a tsp of olive oil, 1 tbsp garlic powder and 1 tsp onion powder to the recipe as well as increasing the salt by 1/2tsp or so. Came out wonderful. I did the egg wash with one loaf. looks a lot like the picture! beautiful. I tried the water bath on the other, didnt make my bread crispy though. As others have said the dough was pretty sticky. I refrained from adding addl flour because I was using all purpose flour and didnt want the bread to become too dense. It was perfect. I used dried rosemary and 1 tbsp was plenty I think. Delicious. Will be using this basic ingredient list for other breads as well.

I made the dough in the bread machine and then shaped, allowed a 2nd rise and baked in the oven.  Sprinkled the top with the extra Rosemary and sea salt and it turned out great.  I love the flavor of the Rosemary and  the salt gave it an extra flavor that we enjoyed.  Next time though I think I'll use the egg wash instead of the extra butter as I like the shine I get from that.  As an update:  Continue to use this awesome recipe, my family likes it served with a dipping sauce of olive oil and balsamic vinegar with Italian herbs.  Never a piece left over

attributes.source_text: I love the flavor of the Rosemary
the salt gave it an extra flavor that we enjoyed
my family likes it

items.label: Taco Seasoning Mix
items.name: Taco Seasoning Mix
items.description: Make and share this Taco Seasoning Mix recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a small bowl and blend well.
Spoon mixture onto a 6-inch square of aluminum foil and fold to make airtight. Label as Taco Seasoning Mix.
Store in a cool, dry place and use within 6 months.
Makes 1 package (about 2 T) of mix.
Using the above recipe as a guide you can increase the amounts to make any number of packages.
Taco Filling: Brown 1 lb lean ground beef in a medium skillet over medium-high heat; drain the excess grease. Add 1/2 cup water and the seasoning mix.
Reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Makes filling for 8 to 10 tacos.
Hope this is what you are looking for.

reviews.review_text: I was browning ground beef for nachos and it ended up that I didn't have a packet of taco seasoning. I remembered I had this in my cookbook and decided to give it a whirl. I had everything except for the cumin, so I still went ahead with it. I added the entire mixture to my browned meat with about 1/2 cup of water. It worked PERFECTLY! While enjoying our nachos I asked hubby if the meat tasted o.k.....he said he thought I used the packaged stuff! So, if you are in need of this and do not want/or can't run out to the store, check your spice cupboard first! I will use this a lot Barb! Thanks!

attributes.source_text: he said he thought I used the packaged stuff

reviews.review_text: I love Mexican foods, but it don't particularly like me!!!  I am quite sensitive to chili peppers these days and wanted to come up with a spice mix that could work for me.  I cut the chili powder down to 3/4 tsp..the crushed red pepper to 1/4 tsp and the salt to 1/2 tsp...I upped the oregano, garlic and cumin a smidgen to get a little more of a  omph!!  I used this in #84030  and it was still quite flavourful!   I would not have been able to eat the dish I was making if I used commercial taco seasoning, so this was quite the guilty pleasure!!! My stomach says "thanks"!!

Browned my meat, went to the cupboard...no taco seasoning. I was not going to pile the kids in the car for a trip to the store. I knew 'Zaar would have the answer. I always buy the McCormick taco seasoning. Not aymore. You get in the habit of buying all of these prepackaged itmes and you just don't need to. This had an excellent flavor. Husband even commented that it tasted fresher than usual. I omitted the corn starch and added a 1/2 t. of paprika. My method: I brown my hamburger, add the spices, then 1-2 T. apple cider vinegar, then a cup of water, then cook it down. Flavor seems to be stronger and more infused in the meat that way. Low cost, no fillers or preservatives. Thank you  very much!

attributes.source_text: it tasted fresher than usual
Husband even commented that it tasted fresher than usual

reviews.review_text:
I cleaned out my kitchen in Jan. and was in the midst of cooking when I realized I did not have taco seasoning! Thanks for coming to the rescue, I also used fresh minced garlic on nights when I was using the batch right away. I've probably made this 3 or 4 times now, and I go a little light on the red pepper! :)
Update - I wrote my review in May '08, and tonight I realized, I really use this alot. I cut back a bit on the red pepper flakes and am a little generous with the cumin, per my taste preferences but I can't go back to prepacked seasonings...I love this one :)

This is exactly what I was looking for! My wife and I tried it last night and were very impressed. As other reviewers have said, we'll never buy taco seasoning again! The nice thing about this recipe too is the ability to adjust how hot it is, based on how much of the "hotter" spices you want to put in! Very nice. I didn't have the onion or the garlic, so I just used onion powder and garlic powder. Still tasted great!!! The only thing I would change is the amount of salt. Next time I think I'll put half the amount, but that's just my preference! Thanks for this recipe!

attributes.source_text: the ability to adjust how hot it is

reviews.review_text: I was making tacos tonight and had browned the beef. I took out the taco dinner kit when I realized it was taco shells only. I immediately thought of the 'zaar, so I began searching and found this recipe with excellent reviews. I followed the recipe except for the cornstarch (didn't have any) and I was very pleased. My children liked these tacos than what I previously make, so I have to assume it was the recipe for taco seasoning. This recipe was a hit and helped me out in a pinch. I will use this recipe instead of using store bought seasoning. Thanks for the recipe.

attributes.source_text: My children liked these tacos than what I previously make

reviews.review_text: Excellent. I love this recipe. This puts all those packaged mixes to shame. The flavor is so perfect. For my family, I always double this recipe and use all of it immediately. I have used this seasoning on 1 lb of ground beef and on recipes that call for 1 1/2 lbs. to 2 lbs. of ground beef. The most recent recipe I used this seasoning recipe with is recipe 33919 on this site. Wow, what a great blend of flavors. This is so easy to make and chances are you have these ingredients on hand. Give it a try, you will not be disappointed.

We've been using this for a while now.  (Sorry it took so long!)  It's wonderful!  WAY better than any brand of packaged seasoning.  I make it exactly as written and it's perfect.  I make a triple batch and store it in a spice jar.  There is only 2 of us, so when I need taco seasoning for a recipe that's not tacos, (like Taco Avocado Wraps by looneytunesfan) I don't always need a whole envelope.  I love that I can now measure out exactly what I need. Not only is this more convenient, but tastier too!

At our house we subtitute ground turkey a lot for ground beef.  I had some ground turkey I was going to use for chow mein but then decided it was more efficient to make tacos, to go with the fresh salsa I made. I thought I would check out 'Zaar for a seasoning mix. This was excellent!  I did have to double it since I was working with ground turkey.  Thanks for posting! It saved me the trouble of experimenting when I needed something fast and a sure thing!

Who would have know with a few ingredients that I most always have on hand I could make the seasoning to whip up a great taco salad?  The only thing that I changed in this was to use Hot Shot Seasoning instead of the Crushed Red Pepper and it turned out wonderfully.  I doubled the batch as I made 2 pounds of hamburger and wanted there to be plenty of spice.  I agree that this tastes pretty similar to Ortega brand taco seasoning and I too will be using this often.  Thank you for a great spice to add to my cupboard Opal Fitzgerald!

attributes.source_text: wanted there to be plenty of spice

reviews.review_text:
This is so good! I've just finished off yet another pan of tacos!
I do it slightly differently:
Dry onion flakes, garlic powder, cumin seeds, no cornstarch (boyfriend's allergic). Also, I have really spicy chili powder, so I don't do the flakes. (Also sometimes use one small onion and some cloves of garlic instead of dry)
I do the meat as you say, then stir in a can of refried beans and some cheese - fantastic dinner! We've started eating it with Mexican Crema.
Anyway. My mouth is currently singing your praises yet again. Thank you.

attributes.source_text: fantastic dinner

reviews.review_text: Excellent taco meat mix! Even better than the store-bought packet! I mixed up the spices in a small bowl and set it aside then I browned and drained 1 lb. of  meat, added the spices (the whole recipe) and about 1/2 cup water and cooked and stirred until the liquid was evaporated. I also added a few tablespoons of tomato puree which added another layer of tomato flavor but it wasn't necessary - this taco seasoning blend stands very nicely on it's own! Thanks Barbara!

attributes.source_text: added another layer of tomato flavor

reviews.review_text: We had a snack party planned at work for New Years Eve day.  I planned on having Taco Dip.  I had worked the night before and was going to make it before I went to work.  Upon checking in the morning i found that I had no Taco Mix.  Off to Recipezaar I went.  Found your recipe and I was saved.  Very easy and delicious I had many compliments for something that could have ended up kind of bland without Taco Seasoning.  Thanks so much for the emergency care.

attributes.source_text: a snack party planned at work for New Years Eve day
a snack party planned at work

reviews.review_text: This was wonderful!  I went to my sister's for tacos last night, and she told me she forgot to buy taco seasoning.  She said she would just wing it, but I knew there had to be an actual recipe on zaar.  I loved that I had all of the ingredients, and it took about a minute to mix it up.  I used about 1/8 tsp red pepper flakes as we don't like things too spicy.  It tasted exactly like the packaged versions, but it was better because I knew what was in it.  Thank you!

attributes.source_text: we don't like things too spicy

reviews.review_text: I was surprised how bland this was after reading a lot of 5 star reviews.  I was very disappointed with this after following the recipe.  I had to add other spices to kick it up.  I personally think that 1 tsp. of chili powder for a pound of meat is simply not enough.  (To me) for a pound of meat, you need at least 3 Tbsp. of chili powder, and sometimes that's not even enough, depending on if you use ground beef or turkey.

For some stupid reason i picked up a box of Taco Shells, not the dinner!  My son is a Taco fan, so when I told him i didn't have the seasoning package, he was crushed.  I knew Recipezaar would have a recipe and after looking thru them all decided on yours. Opal this was so good.  After we had dinner and I saw how much everyone loved, I won't go back to Taco Dinners again!  I made a big batch and have it stored in a airtight container.  Thanks so much!

attributes.source_text: My son is a Taco fan
After we had dinner

items.label: My No Roll Pie Crust
items.name: My No Roll Pie Crust
items.description: The only pie crust I will use anymore. Its flaky and slightly sugary and oh so easy to do. Note: due to some major discrepencies please use a good quality oil, preferably a vegetable and a good name brand like Mazola, it may not seem like it will make a difference but in the end it will, also use new oil not something that has been sitting around for a while.
instructions: Mix dry ingredients together with a fork in a pie pan.
Make a well in the center and add the oil and milk.
Mix with a fork til it makes a ball.
Flatten and press into the pan in pie crust shape and flute the edge.
Bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes until golden.
One crust pie, excellent for cream pies and crumb topped baked pies.

reviews.review_text: THANK YOU Laurie! I am extremely pleased with this easy to make pie crust recipe! used it to make Yummy Crunchy Caramel Apple Pie #31128 and plan to use it for mushroom quiche and also Recipe #33454. As one reviewer suggested, I put 2 tbsp of milk into a 1/2 cup measure and then fill the rest with oil. I did the same using Leisure oil. It seemed a bit crumbly, so I splashed on a bit more milk into the crumbly dough so it would hold together  Didn't pre-bake, but brushed the crust with beaten egg white to remain crisp before I added the apples. Made a second pie crust but it was a much smaller pie plate, so used half the dough to make a crumb topping. Mixed in about 1/4 cup quick oats, 1/3 cup of brown sugar and 2 tbsps of butter - then whizzed in the processor till crumbly. 6 granny smith apples were perfect for filling the 1" x 9" pie dish I have. To make a double pie crust I would prefer to make the recipe twice instead of just doubling the ingredients.

attributes.source_text: brushed the crust with beaten egg white to remain crisp

reviews.review_text: I thought this was very good!  I used to be able to roll out crusts quite easily but have had a hard time doing it in recent years.  I also hate the mess it makes.  So, this is a great idea!  I was almost out of oil and had to melt shortening for two thirds of it.  I don't know if that is why it came out greasier than I wanted it, but I just added a few tablespoonfuls more of flour and it came out fine.  I made a large pumpkin pie in a five quart rectangular Anchor Hocking pan, for a dinner with my kids and grandkids, and it was a hit!  I did double the recipe, as I don't think one would have easily spread across that large of a pan.  I had a little left over, though, which I will make into a small tart or something.  I will be hanging onto this recipe!

attributes.source_text: for a dinner with my kids and grandkids, and it was a hit
for a dinner with my kids and grandkids, and it was a hit
for a dinner with my kids and grandkids

reviews.review_text: This was absolutely HEAVENLY! It was perfectly flaky and purely delicious. I just love that it has oil instead of shortening and it's so simple! I made a blueberry pie today and this is one of the few pie crust recipes that didn't require shortening- I choose not to keep it in my house as it isn't healthy. My only issue was figuring out the top part of the crust but I rolled it between a piece of folded piece of parchment paper and it worked out alright. I've never made pie before but when I tasted it, my first thought was 'I have to rate this, right now.' I ended up eating like 3 slices just to get to the crust hehe :)

attributes.source_text: perfectly flaky

reviews.review_text: I made this pie crust based on the reviews. Boy was I disappointed! I was expecting a flaky crust as described but the crust just crumbled. It tasted salty and greasy. I followed this recipe completely and used top brand ingredients so it could not have been an error on my part. Maybe I should have used melted butter in place of the oil. I made this crust for a chess pie and I had to throw the entire pie away. I am not sure what type of pie would benifit from this crust but i can't imagine it tasting good with any type of sweet pie. If you are looking for a flaky crust you should go elsewhere. Yes, it is easy, but not very good.

I made this crust to go with my quiche recipe and it was really good! I used brand name oil that was open for less than a month. I could definitely see how some people could say it was too oily, but I liked the way it complimented the veggies in my dish. The oil makes the crust different than say using shortening or butter, but it was still flakey and the flavor was good. It was pretty easy to pat into the dish as well. I used a spoon and my finger tips to do it. I will use this again, thanks for sharing! Oh, and the only change I made was using soy milk instead of cows, made no difference taste wise.

attributes.source_text: it was still flakey

reviews.review_text:
This is a perfect crust for people who don't like to make them.  There is almost no possibility of messing it up.
It is actually quiet nice as a "pot pie" crust.  I made two, one for the top and one for the bottom.  It isn't too sweet.  It is easy to get to the thickness desired.
I made it into the little pans like you get a store bought pot-pie in and it made five bottoms and three tops, so it would have made four complete pot-pie crusts but I did roll it between plastic wrap to get it thin.
This crust is great for pies and pot pies.
The climate may make a difference in the amount of liquid needed.

attributes.source_text: It isn't too sweet
I did roll it between plastic wrap to get it thin

reviews.review_text: Awesome!  I needed a quick and easy recipe and this is just fabulous!  Have always avoided making the crust myself because you always hear how hard it is.  But this was really easy and it tastes great (except I want to add less salt next time).  I live in Japan, where you can't find ready-made crusts, and am using this recipe to teach Japanese people how to make an American pumpkin pie. Used it raw and filled it with Libby's filling (#101104).  It came out perfect, with a nice crispy texture and subtle flavors.  So this recipe has now gone global, if it hasn't already  ;)  Thanks for the fabulous and easy recipe.

attributes.source_text: how to make an American pumpkin pie
with a nice crispy texture
subtle flavors

reviews.review_text: I love this recipe! It is quick and easy and so hard to mess up. I have been using this recipe for years now, with great success. I will say I use it most often with savory dishes, I simply leave out the sugar and it tastes great. It has worked with pot pies and quiches. I also found it tasted great when cooked with alternative milks like almond milk, so perfect for vegan pot pies. For the top crust I always went rustic and just formed the dough in my hands and dropped it on top. It doesn't look perfect, but still tasted fantastic. Overall a very handy recipe to have on hand for a quick easy meal, or dessert.

attributes.source_text: I use it most often with savory dishes
for a quick easy meal, or dessert

reviews.review_text: I used this recipe for my vanilla creme pie and although the crust worked great for this type of pie,the texture was not was what I was expecting. It was more crumbly than a regular crust. I followed the recipe perfectly so idk what I did wrong. Next time I'm going to make it with butter and add more flour and cut the butter mix it together and spread in the pan. I like my crust thick and with yummy crust. My crust barely reach the edge so I was not able to flute anything. But it was good a substitution. For a graham cracker crust it's perfect! I'd try recipe as is for a cheesecake and use my variation for other pies like blueberry and apple.

I am not sure if I have left a review for this yet or not...if so,i dont mind leaving another one - this is the easiest pie crust I have ever made! I usually dread making pie crusts,i'd rather buy them then deal with the hassle....I will make this one everytime I make a pie,soooooo simple to make and sooooo easy to work with! My father in law is a very picky eater,he is very picky on how things taste but yet likes things simple too,he doesnt like most of the newer foods  - he made a point to tell me that this was the best pie crust he had ever eaten.Thanks for sharing!!! 5 stars all the way!

attributes.source_text: he made a point to tell me that this was the best pie crust he had ever eaten

reviews.review_text:
Finally an easy, yet tasty, pie crust! I do not like to use shortening and am always trying to find recipes that use other oil alternatives.  I am so glad I tried this one. 
Extremely easy, shaped into the crust just fine, tastes good and flaky, too! I used half sunflower oil and half peanut. I made 2 of them, one for a pecan pie and one for a pumpkin pie.
I do, however, like the flavor of the vinegar crusts as well, just don't like the shortening required in those.  Perhaps next time I will reduce the milk and add some white vinegar and see what happens. 
Thanks so much for posting, Laurie!

attributes.source_text: tastes good and flaky

reviews.review_text:
I've attempted this recipe once again. My first time making this it came out far too dry and cracked, not to mention salty. So I looked through a lot of the reviews on here, to see what may have been the problem and made the following corrections. 

First, because my first attempt was too salty, I only added half the recommended amount of salt (so a total of 1/2 a teaspoon of salt). Second, because my first attempt was WAY too dry, I added about 1 additional tablespoon of milk (so a TOTAL of 3 tablespoons of milk, give or take a bit). And lastly, I added about 1/4 vanilla to the milk to give it a bit more flavor. 

These changes wonderfully corrected the problems I had - and the crust came out PERFECT! My dad, mom, sister, and significant other all loved it and said the crust is what made my pie stand out from all the rest. Thank you for this recipe, and I hope my review can help some of you who may have had the same problems that I did.

P.S. My reasoning for four stars instead of 5 is the fact that I had to alter key ingreidients or otherwise the pie crust came out pretty badly (cracking everywhere/in half, extremely hard to mold, and just plain falling apart).

attributes.source_text: My dad, mom, sister, and significant other all loved it
My dad, mom, sister, and significant other all loved it
My dad, mom, sister, and significant other all loved it
My dad, mom, sister, and significant other all loved it

reviews.review_text: Just today I came across an old favorite recipe of mine that I thought I had lost forever.  It's a cranberry walnut pie.  Now, mind you, I have never made my own crust for anything -  I must admit I buy them (Oh the shame!) and I had none in the house.  Then I remembered I had your recipe saved in my cookbook and I gave it a spin - WOW!  I will never buy pie crusts again!  I love how it is sweet and yet a little salty all at the same time.  When I was mixing it up it didn't ball up for me so I added another teaspoon or so of milk and it came right together.  Perfect!

attributes.source_text: it is sweet and yet a little salty all at the same time
it is sweet and yet a little salty all at the same time

reviews.review_text: Not too bad of a crust and I have never seen anything easier to make. Now I'll be making more pot pies for dinner. A QUICK TIP: to make this even easier, take a piece of Saran Wrap and place it on top of the dough pressing through the plastic wrap to even it out and work it up the sides of the pie plate. When you're done simply throw away the plastic wrap and no messy hands to clean up, plus it presses even faster against the plastic.  I used to hate to have to go to all the work of making a crust, chilling, rolling, etc this recipe makes things a snap.

attributes.source_text: making more pot pies for dinner

reviews.review_text: I am currently residing in Giessin, Germany, and was wanting to make a chicken pot pie. Unfortunately they don't sell frozen crusts in stores here, or even rolling pins for that matter! So looking for something that might fill the void, I stumbled upon this recipe for a no roll pie crust and was saved! Not only was it easy, but was also simply delicious! I only added a pinch of sugar instead of the 2 tsp, and it was the perfect compliment to the creamy texture of the pot pie filling. Thank you Laurie... I am planning on making a homemade apple pie tomorrow night using your crust!

I thought this was so easy and the taste was pretty good.  It was nice to have a homemade crust come together so easily without all the rolling and chilling. However, we did miss the buttery flavor and flaky texture of a traditional pie crust.  I used this for my Thanksgiving pumpkin pie and I did not pre-bake this crust, which really turned out nicely after having baked for a little over an hour.  It had nice color and was a little dense and crumbly when eaten. Overall, I would make this again when I'm in a pinch or would like a homemade crust without doing a lot of work.  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: I used this for my Thanksgiving pumpkin pie
crumbly when eaten

reviews.review_text: This crust definitely takes a bit of practice and some getting used to, but I love this recipe. It can take a bit of time to get the dough to fully come together; I find that it needs more milk and/or oil than called for, otherwise it's really crumbly and cracks easily if it's too dry. The texture of the dough seems weird when handling, but after baking, it's wonderful. I always cut down the amount of salt (and usually the sugar) because I find it too salty otherwise. I've used this crust for pot pies and pumpkin pies and it's pretty versatile. And no rolling! Love that! Thanks!

items.label: Simple Vanilla Cupcakes
items.name: Simple Vanilla Cupcakes
items.description: Easy and simple but can be made individual with a slight twist or a special icing. For a nice twist, can add frozen fruit just before it goes into the oven and it will burst into flavor and color.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375f or 190c; line muffin cups with papers.
Cream butter and sugar till light and fluffy (make sure the butter is room temp so the mixture doesn't clump) . Beat in eggs one at a time.
Add flour (mixed with baking powder and salt) alternating with milk beat well; stir in vanilla.
Divide evenly among pans and bake for 18 minutes. Let cool in pans and enjoy! :).

reviews.review_text: Hello everyone, I could like to ask for a wee bit of help if anyone wouldn't mind. You see, today is my mom's birthday and as a birthday present (since I have no money) I wanted to bake her some cupcakes and well, we do not have any cake mix so I was going to try making some from scratch. But the problem is we don't seem to have any baking power (or baking soda) from what I see. Does anyone know what else I could try? Or maybe some cookies or something? I just want to do something special for her. If anyone has any advice that'd be great. I'm sorry if this isn't the proper place to write this too.

This recipe is so bad I put forth effort to sign up to this site to warn others only to find out I had an account and had to run through the forgot password. Anyway I pulled together the ingredients before I read the reviews and tweaks. I should have listened to the warnings but I was already committed as the ingredients were already measured. I should have sucked it up and taken a few minutes to make buttermilk. Or I should have just used any other recipe than this one. The come out VERY dense, VERY bland (I added amaretto too), VERY dry. They were great for breakfast as a muffin with honey and butter.

attributes.source_text: They were great for breakfast

reviews.review_text: I thought they were pretty good, though I added a touch more milk than the one cup the recipe called for. (Next time I will add even more, and perhaps a touch of canola oil too...) The cupcakes weren't as light and fluffy as a cake mix, but this is one of the better vanilla cupcake recipes I've tried so far. I'll make them again for sure. I used the 3/4 c of sugar and they weren't too sweet, which is perfect because I plan to use buttercream icing on them tomorrow. Again, this recipe isn't perfect but it's simple to make and the cupcakes are good.

attributes.source_text: one of the better vanilla cupcake recipes I've tried so far
they weren't too sweet, which is perfect

reviews.review_text: In Directions. Step 1. the Oven temperature says 375F or 150c. The conversion should be to 190C. Those who have cooked using Fahrenheit have probably made lovely cupcakes, those using 150C will have under cooked, flat, pale, heavy little pancakes! We started at 150C before I realised 10 mins in that the conversion must be out as they weren't rising! I will try again another time using the correct conversion. Please edit the recipe so other's who use Celsius don't have the same fate!

My daughter wanted to make these today for big brother's birthday + it's a snow day...and they're fabulous! We followed the recipe exactly b/c we're not comfy making changes with baking (other than dropping in chocolate chips or adding sprinkles). The first batch was in for 16 minutes after reading a review to NOT bake them for the full 18 minutes (second batch is baking now). They're a nice golden color but not brown, and they rose nicely (we live at 6500' so we were concerned about them baking into flat balls of nothingness). We waited 30-ish minutes to ice them and are learning how to pipe frosting with a baggie! Very proud of the results: light and fluffy, but a touch cakey (does that make sense?!) We hope you enjoy making these as much as we did :) We will definitely be baking these again!

reviews.review_text: I thought this was a great cupcake.  Super-easy to make and they came out with a good flavour and texture.  I added some chocolate chips to the batter then iced them with orange frosting (the butter cream recipe from the icing sugar bag with grated orange rind and orange extract and a squeeze of lemon added).  Glad to have the heads up about adding the baking powder and salt to the flour or I may have missed them.

Our daughter (@ 3y/o) is showing signs of becoming a budding chief ??.  So today, I knew I wouldn't get my list checked off unless I made the cupcakes she was begging to make.  This recipe was GREAT!  It works with ingredients you have in the cabinet!  I followed the suggestion of decreasing the time by 2-3 mins and added a full cup of sugar and I added a full 12oz can of milk.  The kids love them!!!

My whole family including myself loved the cupcakes and we all thought they were the best ones we have ever had. They were super fluffy and delicious. Instead of 3/4 cups of sugar I added 1 1/2 cups of sugar. I also put a tablespoon of some honey. I also made some butter cream frosting to go on top. I will be using this recipe forever.

We followed the directions exactly and I can honestly say this is a legit cornbread recipe. They taste like cornbread, crumble like cornbread and would be a solid recipe if that's what we were actually trying to make. I don't recommend this recipe at all. We will stick to the box next time. :(

I made these just now, and they turned out perfectly. They have nice, raised tops and just the right amount of sweetness. I frosted them with homemade buttercream frosting that took me all of 2 minutes to make. Husband loves them, and I'm pretty impressed myself. I'm not a professional baker, so I don't have a piping bag or anything like that, but they turned out great (for an amateur/casual hobbyist).

reviews.review_text:
Perfect Recipe!
It's just the way I like them, easy & simple & tasty!
Before I even opened the oven, the fresh, DELICIOUS smells perfumed the kitchen. After the timer went up, I took them out and let them cool on the table. I locked the door of the kitchen and, SECRETLY, decorated them.
Da da! It's done! The rich, golden-yellow colour and the white cream linings on the cupcakes were AWESOME. The peaches and small chunks of strawberry on top made it even more SCRUMPTIOUS! items.label: Moist and Delicious Banana Bread
items.name: Moist and Delicious Banana Bread
items.description: This is the best banana bread I have ever had.  I buy really ripe bananas just so I can make this :-)  Got the recipe years ago from my friend Rachel.  We used to beg her to make this for us in college!  I think the moistness is due to the 1/2 cup of oil - I didn't say it was the healthiest banana bread around, but it is worth the extra time on the treadmill!
instructions: Combine the oil, eggs, sugar, milk, vanilla, and mashed bananas.
Add the baking soda and flour.
Combine well for 2-3 minutes.
Pour into a greased loaf pan and bake in a preheated 325 degree F oven for 1 hour and 20 minutes.

reviews.review_text: Great recipe after some tweaking. I only used 1 cup of sugar. I added 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon poweder. I also used 3 and a half bananas. Smash the bananas first and let them sit for a couple minutes at least. I don't know why but it makes them taste better and bake better.I beat the eggs separately before adding them. I also put the vanilla in with the eggs. I mixed the oil and sugar first before adding the other ingredients. Then followed the rest of the directions. After mixing everything I added 1/2 cup chopped walnuts. I baked for 1 hour first at 325° then an additional 12 minutes. I pulled the bread and let it rest on a cooling rack until it was room temperature before serving. This came out great! I'm still searching for the perfect Banana Bread recipe but this came pretty close!

Really simple and easy to follow recipe. I checked out the comments before I started and replaced 1.5cups of sugar with about 1 cup brown sugar. The sweetness was perfect for me. It's not too sweet. I also added 1/2 cup of frozen raspberries. I rolled the fruit in flour (to absorb moisture) straight from the freezer before adding it into the batter. Quick tip per a baking with frozen fruit guide I read - drop the fruit into the batter AFTER the batter has been poured into your pan/ mould and push the fruit into the batter. I poured half my batter in first, dropped some fruit, then the other half and pushed the rest of the fruit into it. This way the fruit won't sink to the bottom. I also changed the baking time to 1hr instead of 1h20m and left it in the oven for a few minutes after switching the oven off and then let it cool in the pan outside for a bit as well. Overall, super moist, super soft, just the right amount of sweet and little bursts of tartness. Perfect! Thanks for your recipe. I would make this again for sure.

attributes.source_text: The sweetness was perfect for me
It's not too sweet
just the right amount of sweet

reviews.review_text: I was specifically looking for a recipe that used oil and found this one. I've never made a cake using oil and I'm no baking expert by far, so I was scared. I also had to convert the oven temp from degrees to celsius (because for now we're living/working outside the US) so I was REALLY scared! I also read the reviews and tweaks submitted, and I decided to give it a try. It came out perfect even though I accidentally added 1/2 c milk instead of the 1/4 c that the recipe called for (and it was whipping cream, not milk). It rose normally and was moist. In addition to the accidental extra cream, I also substituted brown sugar and reduced the amount to about a cup, added chopped walnuts and a little cinnamon. Oh and I also used olive oil (YIKES I didn't even consider the flavor it may impart until after I added it) and to me, it didn't make the cake taste funky or odd at all. The ONLY issue I have with the recipe is the mild banana flavor. I personally like more banana, but I am not complaining. I would definitely use this recipe again and I'd add one more banana. With all the suggestions, tweaks and spins submitted, this recipe is a keeper.

attributes.source_text: It rose normally and was moist

reviews.review_text: Excellent recipe. I actually enjoyed it better the next day after storing in saran wrap and aluminum foil overnight. I may cut the sugar to one cup next time, but I will ask my daughter for her opinion first. I have made dozens of banana breads before. This is definitely my favorite. I put aluminum foil on my bread the last 15 min of baking. Also, my oven is electric, so I baked it about 5 to 10 min less than recipe states. I will definitely be making this again. Very moist and delicious!! I just made again today July 25th, 18. I had a paper to write for school tonight so I did not start baking the banana bread until after midnight. Needless to say, by time the bread came out, I wanted to wrap it and go to sleep. Unfortunately, I flipped the banana bread out of the pan immediately and it broke. Next time I will wait a half hour due to the moisture of the bread. Next time I will let it cool off in pan on cooling grid for a full half hour. Absolutely delicious recipe!!

attributes.source_text: Very moist and delicious!!

reviews.review_text: I baked a loaf of this today and it's basically finished! I made an account just for this recipe! If I could give it 100 stars I would!!! This tasted amazing!!!!!!!  It was supper moist, just as it said. Its was easy and pretty quick if you have all your things together before you begin as when you're baking any other thing. The only thing was I took it out when it still had about 9 mins, because it was pretty brown, it was perfect! This was my first time baking banana bread ever. I wont even bother to try much less look at another banana bread recipe it would be a waste! This ones a keeper! Thanks for sharing!!!!

attributes.source_text: It was supper moist

reviews.review_text: I cook a ton, and always get good comments, but I am not a baker! This is the first time I've ever made banana bread (or any kind of sweet bread). I made this recipe because it looked so simple, and it was. My bf cannot have nuts so I substituted 1/2 cup of chocolate chips for the nuts and after reading comments I didn't feel bad about changing sugar to 2/3 cup of brown, especially since I was adding sweetness with the choco chips. It turned out pretty good! I only had 2 1/2 ripe bananas and you definitely need at least three. One thing I was not prepared for was the MONSTER loaf this makes! I followed baking directions exactly and it turned out just right.

Someone wrote this recipe is not healthy , but delicious. NOT TRUE!!! You can make this a healthy recipe by a few tweaks. First, instead of using regular milk use ALMOND MILK, instead of regular sugar use LAKANTO MONK FRUIT SWEETNER (can get online if not in stores has the same consistency as sugar has ZERO CALORIES), use organic eggs, instead of regular flour use OATMEAL FLOUR (just pour oats in blender and blend will get oat flour that easy), instead of oil , I did indulge in one stick of butter NOT margarine (margarine is NOT good for you) Ingredients in butter were clean , only cream, water, salt. FULL FAT is good for you or you can use olive oil. Anyhow, this turned out delicious. Try it!! :) :)

This has become the baking dish that has put me on the map. I've made this dozens of times and every time I do and bring it to work, even the most introverted of people who rarely speak throughout the day come to find me to not only comment on the banana bread but to also ask for the recipe. For some reason I've found that men rave over this recipe more than women. I DO NOT tweak the recipe (I don't add Walnuts bc I'm allergic). So when people ask and wonder what makes is EXTREMELY moist and delicious, I credit it to the heavy load of sugar. I strongly encourage you to try it out as is - but this is definitely more of a dessert BB vs. a breakfast BB. The only thing that I do tweak is that I combine all the wet ingredients first and then I add my mashed bananas after to not over mix. I also mix by hand vs. an electric mixer - no idea if that makes a difference, but I'm paranoid that if I ever make it differently than how I have been, that it won't turn out as good :)

reviews.review_text: Would have given 5 stars except for sugar ( too much) and baking time ( too long) If you like a very moist, naturally ( not overly ) sweet banana bread, here's what worked for me: 1) use over ripe ( spotted) bananas 2) substitute /2 cup dark brown sugar for the white sugar 3) substitute non fat lemon yogurt for the milk 4) use olive oil as the vegetable oil 5)add 1/4 cup fresh raspberries for extra zip 6) If you use a convection oven, preheat to 325 degrees and bake for about 50 minutes ( when the top looks done, it's ready)

reviews.review_text: I make this recipe ALL THE TIME.   I actually make extra to freeze and use for kid lunches.  I use a 8X8 round pan and check at 35 mins. (335 degrees)   I use  one cup of whole wheat flour, and 3/4 cup of white flour the result is a deeper richer taste.   When I freeze I let my circle cakes air dry, cut in half moons, then add a piece of paper towel, then wrap in plastic wrap.  I then put into a ziplock bag and into the freezer.  -- as good as the day it was made.  For extra special I use a white store bought icing and add a bit of cream cheese (sec. in microwave)   Fabulous recipe.

reviews.review_text: I made it into 18 individual muffins rather than the loaf, cooked them for 23 minutes in total at 160c in a fan oven turning the tray round after 11 minutes. They came out a lovely golden colour, they taste amazing. The only odd thing was they became really sticky on the surface after cooking, not sure if this is due to the amount of banana per cake but it didn't ruin the cake just need to wipe your hands after! Will definitely make it again! Just read about the reviews saying it's too sweet. I love the sweetness, I also used brown instead of white sugar :-)

Ive substituted the sugar with apple sauce before and it tasted fine. I also use coconut oil instead of cooking oil, theres no difference in my opinion. If this recipe isn't doing anything for you, you probably forgot to add sugar or missed another ingredient. (happens to all of us lol) Cheers!

items.description: Make and share this Italian Wedding Soup recipe from Food.com.
instructions: In medium bowl combine, meat, egg,bread crumbs, parmesan cheese, basil& onion powder; shape into 3/4\

reviews.review_text: I'm having trouble with this review as I feel it's mainly personal taste that goes with it.  I've never had Italian Wedding soup so really have nothing to compare it to, but wanted to try it as I've heard so much about it.  It was simple and easy and DH said he liked it but it just didn't have that much flavor for me, kind of bland - but like I said I feel it's probably personal taste and maybe what this type of soup is supposed to be.  I used homemade chicken stock and then made 2 changes that I don't think would make a lot of differance but then again maybe it did.  After doing the meatballs put everything in the crockpot for 4 hours on low and second - couldn't find orzo pasta in my little town so used pearl pasta.  Other than that followed the directions.  Served with a fresh garden salad and a glass of white wine and it did make for a nice light dinner.  Thanks for posting.

it did make for a nice light dinner

reviews.review_text:
I made this last week and loved it and had to make another batch but this time I doubled the recipe with the exception of the orzo. I like a brothy soup and I felt that the orzo kind of took over the soup so when I made the second batch I doubled everything except I used 1/2 cup of orzo. I also tweaked the meatball recipe by adding fresh chopped garlic and instead of onion powder fresh chopped onion.
I didn't cook my meatballs prior (as some reviewers said they had). I felt that by allowing the meatballs to cook in the soup (as the recipe suggests) it would also add a good amount of flavor. I also opted for spinach instead of escarole. The soup is delicious and super easy!

attributes.source_text: I like a brothy soup

reviews.review_text: This recipe was delicious.  I Love soup and was so pleased to find a great one to add to my "usuals".  I don't typically make any changes to recipes on this site as I feel that you can't truly know if the recipe works if you do not make it the way it's written.  This time though I did go half ground beef and half italian sausage for my meatballs as I do it that way for spaghetti and any other meatballs I make.  My large family Loved it and I ate the leftovers each day until it was gone. As with most soups, the leftovers were just as great if not better! Just remembered, I did use Chicken Bullion granules with water instead of chicken broth as I almost always do this in place of broth as it's more economical for the large bunch I feed and I always have a large jar on hand.  It was still delicious and I if real broth made it any better I'd be amazed as it was perfect :)

attributes.source_text: My large family Loved it

reviews.review_text: Simple, fast, delicious.  I used three hot italian sausages instead of meatballs, took the skin off them and ripped them into little pieces.  Used acini de pepe pasta instead of orzo just because it appealed to me more in the store, and used spinach as escarole was nowhere to be found.  I added basil and garlic salt to about a litre of chicken broth.  Forgot to buy carrots, so we did without...DH refused to put the parmesan cheese on his (I'm not really sure why, didn't think it needed it or something) and he still raved and raved about it.  Using the hot sausage really gives this some kick, it'll be perfect for a cool fall day, that's for sure.  This was on the table in less than 45 minutes, which is pretty incredible for homemade soup.  You've given me new incentive to make up a big batch of homemade chicken broth so I can make this often throughout the winter!

attributes.source_text: Using the hot sausage really gives this some kick
he still raved and raved about it

reviews.review_text: This was really easy to make!  I think chopped fresh kale would lend a nice full bodied flavor too so I will try this at some point with that substitution.  This soup is very visually appealing!  I didn't have chicken broth and thinking of the ground beef in the recipe, I used the beef broth and veggie broth I already had.  I think chicken broth is the only way to go here (as stated) because the beef broth was a little overpowering. Not a negative, just thinking maybe someone else might sub out this ingredient with less than desirable results, too.   I had to brown the meatballs a little in a pan first because they were literally falling apart in the soup when I just put them in raw. That added a lot of time to the prep which already took me 15 minutes not counting browning the meatballs first to help with cohesiveness. I think browning the meatballs added more flavor to the soup too. In the end, we were eating 50 minutes after I began the soup.  We paired this with bruschetta and fresh cherry tomatoes.  Thank you for your recipe! We did enjoy it!

Oh My, What else can I say that hasn't been said? This is my first attempt at wedding soup and this recipe is fantastic. I think I will have to say that this is my new favorite soup! One that I will be making again and again. I couldn't find orzo at the store (what a sin!), so I used fideo instead and it worked beautifully. I also browned the meatballs before putting in the broth, just because I like the look of browned meatballs better (just a appearance thing for me, that's all). I also added a bit of garlic powder to the meat mixture and used spinach instead of kale. But other than that, those were the only changes I made. Thank you Evangelia, for this yummy soup. Hugs, Susie

I don't like soup. My family does, so I'm trying to learn how to make these. I had to make a few alterations, but this was a great dish - even I enjoyed it!
I doubled the recipe, and used turkey instead of beef. Added almost all of the egg(s), but the "dough" was too sticky. Would have added crumbs but was too lazy. Next time will not double the egg. Also added a t of salt instead of parm because of Kashrut restrictions - a bit too much - and used about 4 cups of veg stock since I didn't have enough chicken stock on hand. Quick and delicious. Next time might add a little of another veg just to pump up the nutritional value, and make the meatballs TINY for my little girl and my own taste.

Absolutely delightful! This is so easy to throw together. I used frozen meatballs (not thawed) that I just threw in when the recipe says to put the meatballs in. I also used 2 packages of frozen spinach (10 oz each), that I put in when the recipe said to put the spinach in. I used 3 cans of roasted garlic chicken broth. I added a bit more carrots than what it called for, and added various Italian seasonings, too. I just let it cook on high until it boiled again, which did take a while due to all the frozen things, and then turned it to medium until the orzo was al dente. Delicious meal, and so quick to throw together, I'll definitely make it again. It's even delicious as leftovers!

attributes.source_text: until the orzo was al dente

reviews.review_text: Making this recipe exactly as written provides a delicious pot of soup. So much so, it is a favorite and I make it often. However, with the passage of time I have just realized that I haven't reviewed it and have tweaked it a bit. Meatballs: I add 1/4 tsp. garlic powder & 1 Tablespoon minced fresh parsley or half a Tbl. dried. They are always tender and never dry. Broth: I do add 1/3 C diced onion to the carrots and sweat both before continuing with the rest of the instructions. I also add a 14.5 oz can of tomatoes or fresh tomatoes from my garden along with some fresh basil. Things I have discovered: The soup tastes better the next day. I usually make a double batch of the meatballs I can use them for soup, pasta and sauce, an appetizer, with my favorite sauce. Now I want to try them on homemade pizza. Thank you Likeit Loveit. Little did you know that you posted a "Gem" and a keeper for us.

reviews.review_text: Love the recipe, but of course, I had to add garlic and a little white wine to the mix. the "prep time" of 5 minutes is nuts... unless a little fairy has chopped your veggies, beaten your eggs and rolled your meatballs for you... but I'm sure that was just to get it to the top of the sort when folks are looking for a short "time to make". Made a batch for 15 for our partners... they loved it. One mistake though... if making ahead, DO NOT add the pasta in ahead... do it just before serving. I should have known better but I was very tired when I made it. I also took Christina1's advice and added fresh sage. All in all a good call.

We added fresh garlic to the meatballs (which we browned) and also to the broth, as well as adding around 3 cups of baby spinach.  My cook husband thought it was awesome also.  Funny story - I combed the internet for almost an hour looking for the recipe for this soup that sounded the best (and one that I, no cook here, thought I could handle).  I finally found this one after looking at many and went to buy the ingredients.  Much to my surprise, this was the EXACT recipe I found on my box of Ronzoni orzo.  Must have been fated! I did brown them before adding to the soup.  I did use escarole (never used it, and wanted to say that I've used it).  I was asked MANY times over to share the recipe.  I made up everything the night before, execept adding the orzo.  At work the next day, I let the soup get nice and hot, and then about an hour before serving time, I added the orzo pasta. (I used my Nesco roaster to heat in order to be able to control the temperature better. Thank you so much for posting this delicious soup.

Since he's usually tolerant of my usual vegetarian meals I decided to reward him with this soup. I was at first hesitant about putting the raw meatballs into the soup, without browning them.  However, the fat in the meat imparts so much flavor into the soup, that I think if I browned them first, it would seal in the juices.  I have passed this recipe on to other friends who have also raved about it.  I had never used orzo before so I was surprised that the recipe only called for 1/2 cup.  Thankfully, I cooked the soup as written (as opposed to adding more), and discovered that orzo certainly expands!

reviews.review_text: This soup, when prepared as instructed, is amazing. For those of you unsatisfied with the flavor, but who decided to pre-cook your meatballs, that's the reason. The meat adds a crisp, succulent flavor when cooked in the broth. It adds all the flavor of the soup via the seasonings in the meat along with the fat. Sure, it's not as healthy with all that yummy fat floating on top, but it sure is wonderful. <br/><br/>This soup was a big hit for the family I cook for 5 days a week, and they have requested it monthly. I served it with cheddar garlic biscuits, and a light salad. Well done, LikeItLoveIt.

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe yesterday for a client and it turned out yummy! So good that I am making it for my husband and myself tonight!  I did make a few changes - I kind of combined two recipes where I made my own stock at the beginning by simmering chicken stock with carrots, herbs, celery and onions.  And, I added fresh chopped sage and lemon juice to the meatballs and sauteed them in a dry frying pan just until they were browned to give them a more pleasing color. Then I added them to the broth with the spinach (used frozen chopped) and orzo (I just love orzo).  I also added crushed tomatoes, fresh minced garlic, lemon juice and parmesan cheese at the very end and simmered for another 5 minutes or so.  Made garlic parmesan toast to go along with it.  I love the recipe - and am so glad I found it!

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe yesterday and it was AMAZING!!!  My fussy 11 year-old couldn't get enough.  At the direction of my niece, who is an amazing cook, I stirred a few raw eggs with parmesan cheese at the end.  This was the perfect finishing touch.  I also used orzo, but I would recommend that you keep it separate from the broth until right before you are ready to serve.  Otherwise, the pasta will absorb too much of the broth and get really big.  Next time I would like to try using ground turkey (instead of beef), rice, and low-sodium chicken bouillon. items.label: Brussels Sprouts in Garlic Butter
items.name: Brussels Sprouts in Garlic Butter
items.description: This is a recipe from Joy of Cooking... totally changed my mind about Brussels Sprouts! It's imperative that you use fresh sprouts, the texture would be way off with the frozen ones.
instructions: Melt butter and olive oil in a medium skillet (over medium-high heat) until butter is foamy.
Reduce heat to medium, add smashed garlic and cook until lightly browned.
Remove garlic and discard.
Add sprouts cut side down, cover, and cook without stirring on medium-low heat 10-15 minutes or until tender when pierced with a knife.
The cut side of the sprouts should get nice and browned, with a nutty, buttery flavor enhanced by garlic.
Top with freshly grated parmesan and salt& pepper to taste.

reviews.review_text: Just wanted to clarify one reviewer's question about smashing the garlic with a knife vs. using a garlic press. Since garlic burns very easily, you want large pieces of garlic in this dish that are less likely to burn. To smash garlic: Take a peeled garlic clove and place it on a cutting board. Lay the broad flat side of a chef's knife on the clove, then press down carefully on the knife with the heel of your hand until the clove gives, leaving you with a somewhat flattened, smashed clove of garlic. This is a good option whenever you want the flavor of garlic without the actual garlic, as the flavor will easily and quickly permeate the dish, and the large pieces are easy to remove. Or, as other reviewers have said, leave it in if you enjoy garlic! Thanks for all the kind reviews, I'm glad you all enjoy this recipe as much as I do!

This is a great way of cooking brussels sprouts. It's delicious! I usually roast them in the oven after a quick sear on the cut side in the pan with butter and olive oil, but leaving them in the pan to cook slowly definitely worked just fine! I had 1 lb brussels sprouts, so I decided to cook them all. As a result, I increased olive oil and butter to 2 tablespoons. I also used minced garlic and left it in the pan for the whole time. Sprinkled freshly ground pepper and salt when the brussels sprouts were cooking. I did have to cook them a little longer than the recipe states, but they came out great! Parmesan cheese was definitely an essential touch for this recipe! Thanks for posting! I will make this again.

reviews.review_text: Tracy says, "It's imperative that you use fresh sprouts, the texture would be way off with the frozen ones." I have cooked these 5 or 6 times with frozen and they turn out so scrumptious I haven't bothered with fresh. I plop 1/2 a one pound bag ( right about 15 sprouts) in a Pyrex measuring cup, cover with water and one minute in the microwave does the trick. Once thawed I spread them out on a paper towel for a bit to dry. Slice in half and back onto a paper towel cut side down to draw out some more moisture. Even with frozen sprouts these rival the ones my family still talks about that I ordered at an upscale Italian restaurant years ago. Fresh, frozen... just make 'em. Thanks Tracy.

Just one major problem, I now have to get 2 large griddles for my stove top.
We had these the other night with lamb chops as per previous suggestion (geoval2) the polite war was on as to who would get the rest, we gave up the ghost and bought more, that night, and had them for snacks, they have always been one of our favorites,
but they are top of the line now. And yes leave some garlic in if you are not wusses and grated and curled parmesan are wonderful also
and please use good butter, even with the garlic some funky supermarkets butter detracts, by adding its own off taste,(i gave the recipe to a non purist and had to,  figuratively slap her accross the head,....philistine..)
you know this could replace chocolate....the new addiction..

I've made this recipe 3 or 4 times now and just love the way the outer leaves get nice and brown, and the inner part stays a little bit crispy.  I used 20 sprouts and couldn't fit them all in the pan cut side down, so I did it that way with as many as would fit, then just threw the rest of them in on top.  They eventually all got browned and I left the garlic in the pan - love it when it gets all carmelized!  At the end of the night, there were only about 6 halves left - and brussel sprouts are one of those things that not everyone likes!.  Thanks for posting this great recipe!

I grated fresh parmesan cheese after it had cooked 15 minutes, turned off the burner, and left it in the pan with the lid on for about 2 more minutes. And although the parmesan is listed as optional, imo it is the difference between a 4 and 5 star recipe; unless you're vegan or dairy-intolerant, make sure you include the parmesan! I used sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper and added a bit of extra butter at the end. Even people who are sure they don't like brussels would do well to try this recipe. items.label: Oreo Truffles
items.name: Oreo Truffles
items.description: Make and share this Oreo Truffles recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Using a food processor, grind cookies to a fine powder.  With a mixer, blend cookie powder, cream cheese and vanilla extract until thoroughly mixed (there should be no white traces of cream cheese).
Roll into small balls and place on wax-lined cookie sheet.  Refrigerate for 45 minutes.

Line two cookie sheets with wax paper.  In double-boiler, melt milk chocolate.  Dip balls and coat thoroughly.  With slotted spoon, lift balls out of chocolate and let excess chocolate drip off.  Place on wax-paper-lined cookie sheet.
In separate double boiler, melt white chocolate.  Using a fork, drizzle white chocolate over balls.  Let cool.
Store in airtight container, in refrigerator.

Note:  When I am exceedingly lazy (most often the case these days), I forego the chocolate 'dip' and merely roll my truffles into various mixtures - chopped nuts, chocolate sprinkles, vari-coloured candy sprinkles, cocoa powder, chocolate shavings, coloured sugars -- still pretty -- less work.

reviews.review_text: These always win rave reviews!  My original recipe for these (from a friend) calls for twice the amount of cream cheese here.  I compromised and used 12 oz. of Neufchatel cheese for the first batch, which I used regular Oreos for.  After chilling for half an hour or so, it was the perfect rolling consistency.  I used my small melon-baller to scoop the balls and that seemed to make the perfect bite-size.  For the second batch I made, I used mint Oreos, which only seem to come in the double stuffed.  So I used just 8 oz. of the Neufchatel cheese, and the consistency matched the other batch pretty well.  Each batch made 4 1/2 to 5 dozen small truffles.  I dipped half of them in white chocolate and half in milk chocolate.  Just divine!  Thanks for posting this recipe!

First time i read the ingredients for this 'truffle' I noticed there was no cake mix or icing required. I was kind of put off by mixing cookies and cream cheese together, honestly thought I'd end up with a cheesy ball of cookie crumbs and that sounded unappealing. Im in the process of making these right now and though it seems to be a pretty popular recipe floating on Pinterest I'll wait to make my mind up when I actually have a finished product and have tasted it for myself. a little reminder to add to the directions listed- after removing balls from refrigerator/freezer let sit a min. dipping cold balls into hot melted chocolate can cause the choco shell to crack or not give the results expected.

I brought these truffles to a new year's eve party and my friends all commented on what an amazing cook I am. Little did they know that these truffles are so easy my teenage sons could do it (in other words, it's very simple, with few steps and almost impossible to mess up ;-) ). Really, the recipe is a snap and they taste like a million bucks. You could not find a tastier treat anywhere! I substituted marscapone for half of the cream cheese, because I dislike that sour taste that cream cheese sometimes imparts to these things. Also, in my shopping frenzy I forgot the white chocolate, so I sprinkled some decorative dots on the candies, which worked just fine. This dessert is already in my recipe book and I will pull it out again whenever I have an excuse to do so.

One reviewer lamented on the time it took to dip in chocolate - I dropped 4 -6 balls at a time into the pot and rolled them around right there. It was pretty quick. Best to use 2 spoons - things like tongs will mar the chocolate coating.

reviews.review_text: My co-workers give this 5 stars. I made them last night and brought them into work today. items.label: Caramelized Butternut Squash
items.name: Caramelized Butternut Squash
items.description: This is a delicious butternut squash recipe from Ina Garten / The Barefoot Contessa. We really enjoy this during the holidays. It is best when the squash is cut in medium to large chunks so that the outside gets a maple-flavored crust, and the inside stays soft and delicious.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Cut off the ends of each butternut squash and discard.
Peel the squash and cut in half lengthwise.
Using a spoon, remove the seeds.
Cut the squash into 1 1/4\
cubes (large and uniform is best), and place them on a baking sheet.
Add the melted butter, brown sugar, salt and pepper.
With clean hands, toss all of the ingredients together and spread out in a single layer on the baking sheet.
Roast for 45 minutes to 55 minutes, until the squash is tender and the glaze begins to caramelize.
Turn the squash while roasting a few times with a spatula to be sure it browns evenly.
Adjust seasonings if needed.
Serve hot.
Enjoy!

reviews.review_text: I can't count how many times I've made this after getting the recipe from Ina. I get the precut squash that's available in all the grocery stores I go to. I cut the pieces smaller to ensure everything gets cooked through. I line the tray with parchment paper so nothing sticks. I don't think I've ever measured, I just drizzle oil and throw in a handful of sugar and mix. I used to make the old Black Eye Pea restaurant recipe, which is mashed with some butter and brown sugar..or something like that. After finding this recipe I don't make it any other way. I meant butter not oil!

How could I not try this after seeing such a beautiful picture of this featured on the home page?  I am so glad I did!  In 31 years of marriage I had never made this squash...I can tell you now that it will be a regular veggie at my house as we all loved it.  I actually peeled mine with a veggie peeler after cutting and removing the seeds, then melted the butter and other ingredients in my 8 cup glass measuring bowl in the microwave, then added the squash and tossed and turned onto the baking sheet.  Easy to do, easy clean up, and so so yummy!  Thank you so much for posting...you've made us Butternut Squash lovers!!

I have never peeled or chopped a butternut squash. Usually just cut half lengthwise and bake with butter and salt and pepper. <br/>I only had one squash but still used 6 tablespoons margarine, 1 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon pepper and the quarter cup dark brown sugar. <br/>I also only baked it for 25 minutes at 400 because the butter and sugar were absorbed and the squash was tender.<br/>It had too much pepper, my fault...otherwise very tasty. A bit more labor intensive than I'm used to. I might try again and adjust the seasoning. <br/>Thanks for the recipe.

reviews.review_text: I created an account just so I could rate and review this :) ... I have organic vegetables delivered every Friday and I'm always looking for new ways of making things I probably would never try otherwise. I'm not a huge butternut squash fan, but now ... I gotta say ... I'm a FANATIC.  This stuff is amazingly good. Better than candy!  I used a dark cookie sheet (to get a darker reaction in the squash/carmelization), and a sprinkle of cinnamon.  Unbelievable!  The pepper and the salt really round out the flavors nicely. Don't need to do anything other than follow the exact instructions in this recipe ... I made this for dinner tonight and loved it. I didn't have a problem pealing the squash, so didn't heat or boil it to soften.
I made 1/2 the recipe (had only 1 squash) and it made a whole large sheet pan full.I used 4 T. of butter and it was plenty. The only thing different from the recipe was adding a handful of walnuts to the mix. My DH is not the greatest fan of butternut squash but the walnuts really gave it a nutttier and mellower taste. (He ate all of his serving, so guess he was happy with it.)
I really loved it, so will make this again.

items.label: Beef Patties in Onion Gravy
items.name: Beef Patties in Onion Gravy
items.description: Good "stand-by" meat-and-potatoes meal. This goes over big with husband and kids. Easy, quick, and tasty comfort food.
instructions: Combine all patty ingredients;mix thouroughly with your hands and shape into 4 patties.
Spray a non-stick skillet, and brown patties on both sides.
Add dry onion soup mix and 1 1/2 cup water.
Cover pan tightly and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove patties to a plate.
In a gravy shaker or jar, combine 1/2 cup water with 2 tbs. flour.
Stir flour and water into onion gravy.
Stir constantly with a whisk until it comes to a boil.
Boil 1 minute.
Return patties to pan.
Serve with mashed potatoes or hot cooked noodles.

reviews.review_text: This recipe is CRAZY good! (salt = "hangover").<br/><br/>I served this with rice and asparagus. I know my husband likes a meal when he waggles his fork at me while he's eating and there was a LOT of waggling going on!<br/><br/>The only thing I will do differently the next time is double or triple the recipe in order to freeze some.<br/><br/>Kudos for a great recipe and thank you for posting it.

Because I just cant leave well enough alone I made a few changes. (next time I will use the reduced salt crackers or maybe bacon dippers crackers to lesson the salt taste) I put all the soup mix along with one and a half cups of water in a mason jar and shook it until well blended, let it sit overnight in the cupboard letting the dehydrated onions soften, then shook again just before pouring into the pan.

Had plenty of left over gravy, served with mashed potatoes and corn. was delishhhh, thank you!

Hi papergoddess - this was the ultimate in comfort food! It was very tasty and I added caramelized onions to the pattie as well as the gravy! I also sauteed mushrooms(about a cup)for the gravy and did like ms_bold did an used beef broth instead of water! Yummy, yummy, & yummy! I served it with parslied egg noodles & string beans! It was awesome! It would also go well with a rice dish(since that is what the Cubans here at the home, always ask for!) Thanks ever so much for posting this delicious dish, Diane :)

I used 1.5 pounds of ground beef(I can never find a package with just a pound!)...so I increased eggs to two & used a whole envelope of dry onion soup mix.  I still used 1/2 an envelope for the gravy & threw the remaining half into some mashed potatoes.  I also topped the patties with big slices of sweet valdalia onions like the pictures show.  Was very yummy and DH really liked it.  I think it was a little too greasy for my stomach though, so I'll just use a little less gravy next time.  Drats!

attributes.source_text: DH really liked it

reviews.review_text: This recipe is versatile, easy to prepare and a real family pleaser!  I was all set to makes this when I discovered I didn't have onion soup mix but I did have beefy mushroom dry soup mix so I substituted that for the onion.  The meat patties were moist and delicious and the gravy was fantastic with the mushrooms. I served this with fluffy white rice and my dh and ds both had seconds.   I can't wait to make this again and this time I will use onion soup mix to see which one we like the best.  Thanks for a great recipe.

attributes.source_text: a real family pleaser
The meat patties were moist
the gravy was fantastic with the mushrooms
my dh and ds both had seconds
my dh and ds both had seconds

reviews.review_text: Incredibly simple to make, Great for the bachelor who has no time or ability to cook. Yet so good it can impress the ladies. I went to the store with an modestly stocked kitchen and got the ingrediants for 7 bucks. When was the last time you fed 4 people for 7 bucks? I give it 2 thumbs way up. My local store didn't have plain dry breadcrumbs so I spiced it up a bit with italian seasoned crumbs... In the words of Borat.. Nice. I served it with a side of potatoes and some mixed veggies.

Fantastic and lip smacking good comfort food! This recipe definitely lives up to it's reputation. I used ground turkey and my store only had Onion Mushroom soup mix. It was so yummy, flavorful, and easy. I served it over hot noodles with honey glazed carrots. Mmmmmmmm! I can't wait to make it again with mashed potatoes. This is a delicious and easy weekday meal and I also would be happy to serve it to my friends and family. Thank you Papergoddess for sharing this recipe. I got a "wow" from my hubby! :)

attributes.source_text: I got a "wow" from my hubby!

reviews.review_text: Definately a keeper. I really liked the texture of these patties, they are firm but tender. I was "scared" there might be too much of an intese overwhelming soup mix flavor but it was perfect! I did double the sauce portion. I also used the Lipton beef onion version soup mix becasue that's what I had on hand. I also added a good sprinkle of garlic powder to the gravy.  I served this over mashed potatoes....SO yummy, filling, hearty and so easy to throw together on a weeknight. Excellent.
