reviews.review_text: I brought these appetizers to a party and made everyone happy.  Here is the system I used to stuff:  After cutting off the stem, I used a very small melon baller to remove the seeds--worked great.  Then I used the tip of a small knife to fill the jalapeno boats.  I made a pile of shredded cheddar and pressed the cream cheese side of the jalapeno into it--the cheese adhered well.   I started on the bottom of the jalapeno when I wrapped the bacon, stretching it around the jalapeno several times, trying to end the wrap on the bottom, too.  If the bacon ended on the bottom, I didn't bother with any toothpicks,  if it didn't end up on the bottom, I secured with a toothpick.  Baking on a rack ensures that the bottoms are crispy, too.   Great recipe.  Takes a little time to put together, but well worth it.

reviews.review_text: I wish I could give this recipe 50 stars!!  I absolutely LOVE these poppers!  I especially love how easy these are to make!  Many times I've tried an appetizer that turns out to be very cumbersome to put together, especially the "stuffed" kind, but these are super easy and look fantastic.  They've definitely got some spice to them (of course), but if you prefer less spice, just use bigger peppers, since they have more cream cheese to balance it out.  It worked out perfect for my husband and me, as I love super spicy and he likes a little less, so he took the bigger, less spicy peppers, and we were both happy.  I would also recommend lining your baking sheet with foil.  I made it the first time without, and last night made them again with it lined and the cleanup was much easier.  I could easily eat the entire batch myself!  These will definitely be something I will crave often.  Thanks for an awesome recipe, Stephanie!! UPDATE: I made this last night, but just wasn't in the mood to stuff the peppers, so I decided to make it in dip form!  Lo and behold, it worked!  I very coarsely chopped the peppers and roasted them for five minutes or so.  Fried the bacon on the stovetop (used turkey bacon and it tasted great, although nothing is ever quite the same as the real thing), then mixed it all together.  Baked in the oven at the same temp until hot and gooey, about ten minutes.  ATE IT WITH A SPOON, which just seemed so wrong, but it tasted exactly the same and had the same amounts of everything, so I did my best to get over my feeling like a pig!  I posted a pic.  Would be great with tortilla chips!

reviews.review_text: It takes a little longer but well worth the effort.Do not cut the pepper in half and leave stem on peppers and slice one side so you can open it up and clean it out.  Mix 16 oz cream cheese 3.5 oz of sun dried tomatoes and chopped onion to your liking. Stuff peppers thoroughly and wrap with a whole piece of bacon and pin them with tooth picks. I cook them indirect on charcoal ( no flare ups ) until bacon is almost done and then finish them off on top rack of gas grill on low heat. This allows the pepper to cook more and become soft it's also a little more pleasant on the taste buds. I think they are even better the next day at room temp. I leave the stem on so you have something to hold while you eat them. I buy one pound of bacon for 15-20 poppers

I took other reviewers' advice and partially pre-cooked the bacon prior to wrapping. Even with this, they still took longer than 15 minutes to get the bacon to cook all the way, more like 20 minutes. However, with the pre-cooking, I had no problems with the peppers burning at all. Because I had thoroughly de-veined and de-seeded the jalapenos, the peppers were quite mild when cooked. They were very well-liked by everyone who tried them. Next time, I may make half of them "hotter" by leaving in a few seeds or a bit of the vein. Overall, a big success, and I will definitely be making them again. Thanks for sharing.

reviews.review_text: These peppers rock. I made them last weekend for a movie night with friends and they were inhaled! I made them again tonight just for me and Dugan as an entree. Last weekend I filled them to the rim with cream cheese and then put shredded cheddar on top and wrapped with bacon. THe excess cheddar cheese bubbled over and most of it was lost. But they were delicious, anyway. Tonight, I half filled them with cream cheese and using my finger I formed a "well" and then filled the well with shredded cheddar til it came to the top of the rim (but level instead of heaping)of the cut peppers. I had no spillage or leakage of any cheese and they were not only delicious but beautiful. I also used a variety of peppers. Red jalapeno, green jalapeno, and banana peppers. They were all delicious. I prefered the green and Dugan preferred the red. But if you have picky guests consider the banana peppers, also. They have ZERO heat but are also outstanding and delicious. I would happily pay money for these in a restaurant. One other point... be sure to use regular or thin sliced bacon. The first time I used thick cut (because that was what I had) and it took some time under the broiler to crispen. But that only validates my point. Which is... you can't screw these up... they are wonderful and Dugan wants me to tell you that this is the best recipe I have force fed him from 'Zaar. And I have made him eat alot of recipes from 'zaar. He loves you!

reviews.review_text: Wow! I did love this Stephanie. If I could give it more stars I would. This really hit the spot! My pictures my look a bit drab, but these were delicious! I followed the recipe exactly, however reduced the recipe as I wasn’t having a party to only 4 peppers, halved, for the 2 of us. DH doesn’t like peppers so I also used hollowed out mushrooms and prepared them exactly the same. Fantastic for both of us! I cannot find jalapeno poppers anywhere in the UK and was looking to make them myself. This recipe was even better than store-bought as it doesn’t have all the calories of the bread crumbs and the deep frying. Bacon isn’t the same here as it is in the states, but I used what is called ‘streaky bacon’ for this. Thanks for this recipe. It will certainly be used often.

Yum! I left the stem on, so we could have a handle to hold onto while we ate them.  My favorite tool, a grapefruit spoon, was used to remove the seeds and membrane.  I found that if you angel the center of the bacon over the center top of the pepper that the ends can easily be tucked under the pepper and put on the baking sheet. Don't be afraid to stretch that bacon around the pepper.  These were not spicy hot at all.  I was surprised, even though I know the heat came from the seeds and membrane.   DH knowing these were  jalapenos, ate 2 of them after I had told him they were not hot.  He does not do spicy foods at all!   I'll be making these again, thank you so much for posting this recipe.  Made for *Zaar Chef Alphabet Soup 2008* game

I tried these on a group of 20 people as a test for a larger party, and they were the favorite recipe of the 9 things I served. They really are good, and the bacon-lovers in the crowd were blown away! I did have to raise the oven to 475 to get the bacon crisp enough. Next time I'll either precook the bacon a little or start them out at the higher temperature. Thanks for a recipe that is wonderful, easy and different.
March, 2010:  I served these for the third time and they are consistently a hit.  Precooking the bacon about halfway really is essential.  They can be made at least one day in advance and held in the fridge, which I consider a big plus.  If anyone is afraid the peppers will be too spicy, fear not.  The cream cheese seems to calm the peppers and even people who don't care much for spicy foods often like these!   KK

reviews.review_text: We have made these for cookouts for years.  We usually use homegrown jalapenos and put them on the grill! So good!!   The seeds are what really creates the heat, so remove them AND RINSE if you can't stand spice and they will only be a mild flavor.  If you like heat, you can leave a few of the seeds.  I like to mix my cheese and if you do cook them in the oven make sure that you use a rack so that they are not swimming in grease.  Like some have said, these do take a few minutes to prepare, so allot for that.  You have to scrape all of them out.  Also, the seeds burn my hands afterwords, and it's definitely not good if you rub your eyes, so I tend to use a pair of gloves when I am removing the seeds.

OMG!! YUMMY!! ADDICTING!! Can I give it 10 stars?? I have made this for every possible occasion in the last 3 weeks I could think of! Really yummy with maple flavored bacon too. My SIL (sister-in-law) made them on the grill one night- she skewered them and cooked them- yummy too! 
The only change is- serve them when they are hot- not cool (unless you like room temp. bacon????) You can save a few calories by placing them on a paper towel once cooked but before serving (to soak up some of the bacon fat). items.description: Mom got this recipe from somewhere a long time ago and passed it on to me. Just multiply the amounts according to how much fish that you have to fry.
instructions: Sift dry ingredients.
Add water and mix well.
Use to coat fish or chicken filets.
Cover the fish completely.
Deep fry until a nice golden brown.

reviews.review_text:
I rated this recipe with 5 stars, not because it tasted like LJS ( I altered it so I couldn't say how close it would've been.) although, the texture of it, once cooked was so close, if not spot on, but because it was incredibly easy to make, it coated the fish perfectly, and the cracklin's that were produced with the leftover batter were out of this world delicious.
After reading several reviews, I opted to alter the recipe slightly. I doubled the recipe and added another teaspoon of salt, about 1/2 teaspoon of garlic powder and the zest from half of a medium-large lemon, using a rasp type zester. I also used half water and half whole buttermilk.
As I am typing, my better half is moaning with delight while continually uttering, "Oh, that was good!" We put our plates up about 30 minutes ago and he's been back for more of those cracklin's twice already.
I'm thinking of all the things I'll be using this batter for, altering the seasonings for various things.

attributes.source_text: my better half is moaning with delight while continually uttering, "Oh, that was good!"

reviews.review_text:
I just want to add my comment to all the others.  This is a really great recipe.  I've never been able to successfully fry anything with batter before, but this recipe came out perfect!  
I don't have a sifter but I just used a mesh strainer and it worked just as well.  I also added seasoning salt, cajun spice seasoning and black pepper and sifted it all together with the flour.  
I don't have a deep fryer so I just used a large deep frying pan and filled it 1/4 way, turning the fish half way through.  The batter stayed on the fish throughout the whole cooking process and it came out light and delicious.  Thank you, Mysterygirl!  This is going to be a favorite way for me to serve fish from now on.

attributes.source_text: it came out light and delicious

reviews.review_text: Looking at the ingredients list I am surprised that anyone would think it’s going to taste like LJS. Other than batter ingredients there’s only salt. Lol... what did you expect from salted batter, Long John Silvers? The value of this recipe is the quality of batter, not the taste. I’ve made this many times since reading it way back when. Sometimes I use beer, sometimes not. I have my own spice list for this recipe which makes it taste great to us. All of you long time cooks and lifetime LJS fans should have known after reading the ingredients list this recipe wasn’t going to taste like LJS, yet the batter is really, really close and works every time. Figure out your own seasonings and sprinkle on some malt vinegar if that’s your thing. You’ll be happy.

attributes.source_text: salted batter

reviews.review_text: I don't use a thermometer but test the fat and browning was too slow.  Now I add 1 tsp sugar.  Problem solved.  I've done lg catfish fillets, cod, oysters, shrimp, scallops, onion rings, and the only thing that didn't work well was mushrooms.  I rinse in cold water and pat dry with paper towels B4 dipping in the batter.  It's nice and thick and really sticks well, then fries up super crispy.  To drain, I use a cookie rack suspended on a jelly roll pan lined with newspapers, maybe a layer of paper towels on top to look better.  Can use over and over that session and saves on paper towels.

attributes.source_text: fries up super crispy

reviews.review_text:
I know, this recipe doesn't really need an 86th review, but I can't help it- I am so impressed!  My fish turned out beautifully, didn't stick to the pan, was tasty and light and made a beautiful dinner.
I made the batter about 45 minutes in advance as a few other reviewers suggested, but my whiting filets were breaking apart because the batter was so thick and wasn't coating evenl. So I added about 1/3 cup of water, which made it the perfect consistency.  I ended up having enough batter to fry up about 10 fish filets, 25 shrimp, and 20 mushrooms.
I did double the amount of salt, and then lightly salted everything as soon as I set it to drain, which seemed to make it the perfect level of seasoning for my family.
DH claims it's really similar to LJS (and he is a fanatic)- he wants me to try it on chicken breast next.
This is my new stndard- thanks so much!

attributes.source_text: was tasty and light
made a beautiful dinner
the perfect level of seasoning for my family
the perfect level of seasoning for my family
DH claims it's really similar to LJS

reviews.review_text: I used this to make Chicken Fried Steak fingers and Onion rings. I mostly followed the recipe. Instead of water, I used Beer.,I added Tex Joy BBQ seasoning and garlic powder in place of salt. I also preseasoned the beef and let sit overnight with the Texjoy, garlic, and msg. I also let the onion rings soak in 3 cans of Regular Budwiser ( I'm not a lite beer kinda guy. ( I don't like unleaded) for 2 hours then patted them dry on paper towels. Best wet dredge I've ever used!!! I will use it again and I'm gonna pass it around to friends and family on social media.

First, when this recipe was first posted LJS was running commercials saying they were using Pollock. Lately those commercials have been saying Haddock. You might want to look at those types of fish if you want the LJS taste. My review is based on whether it tastes like LJS. I see a lot of people criticizing others for basing their reviews on that. Isn't that the point? This is pretty much just a variation of most Fish and Chips recipes you find. It does not taste like LJS. It was somewhat bland. That's not to say it's not a good fish recipe, but it's not LJS. Anyone who's ever had LJS knows it has a somewhat odd taste to it. This doesn't have that. It takes like a standard Fish and Chips recipe. I did it no dredging, cornstarch dredging, flour dredging, and season flour dredging. None gave me the taste or consistency of LJS. That might be hard to pull off. The consistency of of LJS is almost like a fillet. I don't mean fish that was filet but actually more like a processed fish filet or a boneless chicken breast. If you've ever had LJS fish and chicken, the consistency is about like a McDonald's chicken nuggets. It might be hard to get the exact consistency unless you use some type of fish streak. But whatever that odd taste that LJS fish planks have, this does not have it.

A few mentioned it here, and I totally agree. It tastes okay, but not like LJS batter. There could be here a reason that it seems most recipes miss. The flavor of anything fried, has a lot to do with what type of oil they fry it in. People seem to rave about the egg rolls that I make, and the real reason is that I fry them in Wesson Corn Oil. Many people try to be healthy and fry everything in oils such as olive oil, which is a totally different flavor. Unless we know what LJS uses to fry their battered foods, we have no hope of duplicating the flavor

I do not see the LJS connection, but it has been a long time since I have eaten there. However, this is an excellent recipe for battering probably anything! I tried it on shrimp first and fish the second time. Both times was great. The food was well coated and crispy with very little effort on my part. My only change was substituting the salt for 1/2 tsp seasoning salt. I do want to play with flavor a bit so I will likely try some different spices again in the near future. Thanks a lot for an easy batter with common ingredients. I will NEVER buy tempura mix again!

attributes.source_text: The food was well coated and crispy

reviews.review_text: A great coating but not quite like LJS's. I had trouble with it being a bit soggy but I used tilapia which is probably a wetter fish than cod, which is what I think LJS's uses. We also had someone stop in right as I was done deep frying it and so I had to 'hold' it in the oven for about 10 minutes which also could have contributed to it getting soggy. I think it would taste more authentic with more salt. It was very good though and we all enjoyed supper. I served it with Favorite Hushpuppies and Sweet, Creamy Coleslaw. Thanks for sharing!

Good news and bad news.  The good news is, this is one of the best recipes I have come across here on 'Zaar. Everyone raved about the fish supper.  I used your batter with Tilapia.

Now for the bad news. For the past few years, our family has been going on an hour's drive to this wonderful fish restaurant every chance we go,it was our get away. 
It's pretty obvious we just found his recipe,if not a better one.  I guess we'll have to find ourselves an out of the way Italian place so we can go on our jaunts again, 'cause we've all agreed there's no more fish runs.

This recipe is so FREAKIN' AWESOME!! It was a little flat/bland for our taste, but that's why you make a recipe as is first, and doctor it the second time! I do agree that it needs more salt and something else, just not sure what. But DANG! This fried up so beautifully!! The batter stuck to the fish (like everybody said it would) and was so light (non-dense) it was really great!! I was so proud of myself when I showed my husband how good it looked!! 8~) I don't eat fried stuff very often, but I am looking forward to the day when I can make it again. Thanks so much for the recipe!!

attributes.source_text: was so light (non-dense) it was really great

reviews.review_text: I actually spoke with someone who worked at a LJS and with the exception of MSG which most won't use anyway, she said they also use a small amount of paprika and very HOT water in the batter. It's never cold. I have never seen a cornstarch batter that was prepared with HOT water since it would make the CS lump. BUT, I use flavored seltzer water (lime) and it's ICE cold. The batter comes out so crisp and doesn't pull away from the food, and the slight hint of lime it gets really gives it something!

attributes.source_text: The batter comes out so crisp
the slight hint of lime it gets really gives it something

reviews.review_text: Ok, I've made hundreds of recipes from this site, and have relied heavily on reviews before making anything. After searching for a LJS copy cat recipe, I decided on this one based on reviews. Only a couple did not think it was like LJS, all the rest raved. Trust me....it is nothing like LJS, and even as a recipe in its own right, I don't recommend. I added garlic, and extra salt, from other recommendations, but other than that followed exactly. A waste of good chicken strips in my opinion. Keep looking, not going to fix that LJS craving!

Simply stated--Amazing. My grandmother has been using beer batter for the halibut that my dad brings home on occassion and she was complaining about having to keep a can of beer around just so she would be ready whe he brought home fish. She asked me to look for a recipe that didn't need beer and this is the one I gave her to try. We all loved it. It stayed wonderfully crispy and tasted GREAT!! I have never been to Long John Silver's myself, but my grandpa said it was just like he remembered. Thanks for posting the recipe!!

attributes.source_text: It stayed wonderfully crispy
my grandpa said it was just like he remembered

reviews.review_text:
I think this is bit crunchier than Long John's but just as good. It is definitely less salty- which I love.  This is going to be my standard batter. I used this to deep fry some chicken tenderloins. They were delicious! 
Edited 3-1-07: I have made this dozens of times since my first review and just wanted to add that I now sift the dry ingredients 2 or 3 times and it makes the end product much lighter. (similar to a tempura batter) This is the only recipe I will ever use because it is ridiculously simple and delicious.

attributes.source_text: bit crunchier than Long John's
makes the end product much lighter

reviews.review_text: This is a great "starter" batter recipe - the batter stays on during frying, is not too thick and crisps up wonderfully. That said, it's a bit on the bland side for our taste. I used this recipe exactly as-is the first time I made it, and while it was good, it was also lacking. The second time through I added garlic salt, onion salt, paprika, a bit of chili powder, and some lemon zest. That certainly zinged it up nicely. Like I said, great starter recipe, but also one that allows you to get creative with your own flavors and spices - don't be afraid to make it yours.

attributes.source_text: is not too thick
crisps up wonderfully

reviews.review_text: Based on some reviews, we increased the salt to 1/2 tsp per batch and added in about a heaping teaspoon of garlic powder.  Although it doesn't taste like LJS to me, it is an excellent, light, and crispy batter -- better than LJS!!  We also used it to make onion rings (using sweet white onions), and -- I'm not exaggerating here -- those onion rings were probably better than I've ever had in any restaurant in my entire life.  I don't know why, but while the fish was very good, the onion rings were out of this world!  Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: it is an excellent, light, and crispy batter
it is an excellent, light, and crispy batter

items.label: Oatmeal Cottage Cheese Pancakes
items.name: Oatmeal Cottage Cheese Pancakes
items.description: These are wonderful and are almost too healthy to be true. Lots of calcium, protein, fiber, etc. I usually eat them without any topping and just keep popping them in my mouth! Yum. But a good jam will do them nicely as well.
instructions: Blend all ingredients in blender.
Spray skillet with cooking spray and cook just like\
pancakes, a few small ones at a time.
Top with your favorite pancake topping!

reviews.review_text: I'm not sure if I should even rate this recipe because technically I did not make it...but, I will anyways because I feel it may be helpful.  I chose to make this because I can not eat gluten and am often looking for healthier options than gluten free mixes which are packed with white flours and sugar.  Unfortunately I could not find gluten free oats (my store was out), and so I used gluten free oat flour instead thinking that it would be comparable cause its just ground up oats anyways.  I had to add more cottage cheese because 1/2 cup of oats is less when ground than 1/2 up of pre-ground oats, either way these turned out totally uneatable and I had to doctor the mix with GF pancake mix so as to not waste the batter completely.  So I don't know if the sub out of oat flour is mainly to blame or the recipe itself, I understand that my thinking that I could sub one for another may have been naive but it seemed like a good idea at the time.  So long story short don't use oat flour. I will try again with oats and see if it makes a difference.

I was skeptical, but the glowing reviews about kids eating these had me pulling out the blender this morning...and I'm so glad I did!
I used 2 eggs as another reviewer mentioned (worked fine & was easier this morning), I also added just a Tbs of my cinnamon/sugar mix as recommended by some others.  Since my DD loves blueberries, and I had some in the freezer, I went ahead & tossed about 1/4 cup of them (frozen) into the blender w/the mixture.  I don't know if this added moisture helped, but I had no problems with the sticking & as long as I cooked them long enough, no mushy centers either.   
My kiddos ate these up!  4 y/o, who is giving us lots of food battles lately, ate up 4 with just the smallest pool of pure maple syrup on her plate, my 1 y/o ate 3 plain & I decided I liked mine with just a little bit of jam (although I'll have to try raw honey next time because I think that would be great but I'm currently out).
Will def. make these again because my 4 y/o said she would absolutely eat them again!
I highly recommend giving this one a try!  Thanks for sharing - I certainly would have never put this together on my own.

attributes.source_text: My kiddos ate these up!
4 y/o, who is giving us lots of food battles lately, ate up 4
my 1 y/o ate 3 plain
my 4 y/o said she would absolutely eat them again
no mushy centers either

reviews.review_text: I have a whole new respect for cottage cheese!  I had read some of the reviews and agree that extra flavor is needed.  I used fat-free cottage cheese and added 2 T. flaxseed, 2 tsp of Splenda, 1/4 t. cinnamon, and 1/4 t. maple extract.  While I thought the flavor was really good as it was, I think it needs a little something more before I'll be able to sell my family on it.  I may try adding a bit more maple extract next time.  I love pancakes and follow the WW core plan so this is an EXCELLENT way for me to have one of my favorites with no guilt!  Oh, I used a little bit of Log Cabin Sugar Free maple syrup on top, but cinnamon apples or other fruit would also be great.  Really loved 'em but can't quite give it 5 stars due to the fact that I added some extra flavor.  Thanks for posting!  I will be making these again!

Since this said it only made one serving, I quadrupled it for me and my 5 children.  I used 2 c oatmeal, a 16 oz container of cottage cheese, 8 whole eggs (figuring 2 eggs would replace 4 egg whites), 1 tbsp vanilla, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, sprinkle of nutmeg, 4 tsp baking powder, and 4 tbsp pure maple syrup.  These changes were all based on other reviews I read.  I then used my stick blender to blend it all up. I did end up adding a handful of mini-chocolate chips for my kids.  They all really liked the pancakes.  Thanks for the recipe.  Oh, and quadrupling the recipe was more than enough so I would say that a single recipe of this would serve 2-3 people and not one as the recipe states.

attributes.source_text: They all really liked the pancakes

reviews.review_text: I've been dying to try these but finally got around to it this morning for breakfast.  First, the texture is very different from a regular pancake, but this of course is to be expected; there is simply no way to duplicate the texture with completely different ingredients.  The taste by itself was similar to plain oatmeal, which I don't particularly care for, so the second round of cakes got a sprinkling of cinnamon on the them before flipping.  This we really enjoyed!  Added a bit of butter and syrup as if they were run-of-the-mill pancakes, and these were a sure winner.  My 2-yr-old ate an entire one herself with no toppings at all, just the cinnamon!  I will add fresh blueberries next time and I can't imagine how yummy they will be.  Add all of that to how easy these were to make, and you've got yourself a nice five star recipe.  THANKS for sharing!!

attributes.source_text: this morning for breakfast
My 2-yr-old ate an entire one herself with no toppings at all

reviews.review_text: So glad I came across this recipe. It's a rainy day today and my kiddos requested pancakes for lunch. I happen to see this recipe and had to give it a try. It's sure to be a new staple for us. Like another reviewer, I also used two whole eggs instead of just whites. I added in a bit of cinnamon and about 1 tsp agave. This made 7 small pancakes, which was a good amount for two small children, but I'd definitely double if making breakfast for our family. They do almost taste more like french toast. I had old-fashioned oats. I used my immersion blender to mix this well, I was worried my daughter would see chunks of cottage cheese and turn up her nose. But all was well blended and yummy.

attributes.source_text: my kiddos requested pancakes for lunch
my kiddos requested pancakes for lunch
a good amount for two small children

reviews.review_text: These pancakes are great healthy  and quite tasty substitutes for those with a pancake craving, but not so desirous of all the super-high carb-count in traditional pancakes. For those on a "Zone" diet (or "way of life") program, these make excellent Zone snacks or meals, depending on how many are eaten at a given meal. I agree with the suggestions many others have posted about adding a bit of Splenda, cinnamon -- and I also added a few drops of maple extract and almond extract instead of vanilla (because I am a huge maple fan!).  Maple extract is a great way for those with a maple weakness (such as myself) to get that tasty maple flavor without the excess carbohydrates. I tweaked the number of egg whites, because I only had extra-large eggs, so I just added three egg whites, which seemed plenty. I also decided to do a mix of half-rolled oats and half steel-cut oats, as steel cut oats are much higher in fiber and recommended for those following the Zone diet -- and they also add a bit of texture to the final pancake, which I like. I too added psyllium husks (thanks for the recommendation!) and wee dash of baking soda. Next time I make them, I'm going to try added a few sliced peaches or apples to the blender for some "fruit cottage cheese" pancakes and see how that works. I had a bit of trouble the first batch on the griddle, as I think the pan was too hot and I didn't have enough coating on the pan. So, careful of that -- because the batter is basically just egg and cottage cheese, it will cook quickly, and they're a bit hard to flip. I reckon one of those silicon spatulas would be handy for these. Great recipe, though ... I love them! They're so easy to make -- and perfect for refrigerating for a quick brekkie on the go. Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: that tasty maple flavor
these make excellent Zone snacks
perfect for refrigerating for a quick brekkie on the go

reviews.review_text: I have never been more excited by a recipe in my life! These taste exactly like silver dollar pancakes, but are made from 100% healthy ingredients! I am blown away! Even better, they're packed with protein so no worrying about crashing mid-morning, as you would from regular pancakes. I make mine exactly how the recipe describes - maybe with a little extra vanilla, and they come out exactly how I like my pancakes - not too thick. I top them with either real Vermont maple syrup or pumpkin butter. Oh, and so I'm not wasting whole eggs, I use the egg whites that come in a carton. Perfection! I make this for breakfast every morning. I can't wait to share this recipe with everyone!

attributes.source_text: not too thick
I make this for breakfast every morning

reviews.review_text: Gorgeous little pancakes - turned out beautifully. (My friends were seriously suspicious until they came out of the pan, when they were gobbled up!) We doubled the recipe for 3 of us (the double batch made 10 2.5" pancakes) with a little bit of sugar and some mixed spice thrown in. It's a fine line between too-sticky-to-flip and starting to char, (takes about 1 minute per side) but they were quite nice when slightly well done. Ours weren't really sweet enough to eat on their own, but they went very nicely with strawberry jam. You do need to blend the ingredients - we tried by hand to save washing up and it's impossible to get the curds to mix in even with a lot of elbow grease!

attributes.source_text: My friends were seriously suspicious until they came out of the pan, when they were gobbled up!

reviews.review_text: So easy, so versitile, so delicious! I used 1/4 cup for each pancake and ended up with 4 regular-sized pancakes. I subbed brandy extract for vanilla and sprinkled quite a bit of cinnamon in the batter (I'm a cinnamon freak). I ALMOST didn't see the *blender* part. Good thing I did otherwise I'd have lumpy pancakes. I used my mini cuisinart (it's so cute!) and wizzed it together. The result: a light, fluffy, smooth, tasty pancake that provides protein, fiber, and flavor. To top it, I used equal parts pureed granny smiths and sugar-free maple syrup (and some more cinnamon ;) Yum! Yum! And I even used FAT FREE cottage cheese! This is a recipe that CANNOT be screwed up!

attributes.source_text: a light, fluffy, smooth, tasty pancake
a light, fluffy, smooth, tasty pancake
a light, fluffy, smooth, tasty pancake

reviews.review_text:
As I was making these, I wondered how they would even be edible; the ingredients seemed so wierd. But they were great! The texture is not at all like a regular pancake, they are eggy, and nutty tasting. I might omit the vanilla next time (I felt that it didn't add much, just a vanilla scent), and add some fruit, such as ripe bananas. 
   I love the fact that these are healthy, and freeze well. You could even have these for dinner instead of rolls, with the right meal. 
   I do suggest making them like the instructions say, as silver dollar pancakes, I made my first batch larger, and the taste wasn't as good as when they were thinner.
I enjoyed mine with homeade apple butter. Thanks!

attributes.source_text: they are eggy
nutty tasting

reviews.review_text:
I took the basic recipe and adapted it to fit my weight-loss plan (Lean for Life) by adding another 1/4 of oatmeal and using 2 whole eggs, rather than the four egg whites.  I also added 6 packets of Splenda (major sweet tooth)and about 1/2 teaspoon of cardamom, my current spice of choice.  They were wonderful! In fact,I immediately made another batch, double this time, so I could put them in the freezer and microwave them if I need a quick breakfast. For the Lean for Life plan, one-third of the recipe as I made it counts as one grain portion and one protein portion.  

Thanks for posting!  It's not so easy to come by quick, healthy recipes.

attributes.source_text: if I need a quick breakfast

reviews.review_text:
I was skeptical, but all the positive reviews convinced me to give these a try.  And I'm so glad I did!  My pancake-loving family loved them, and I liked them much better than regular pancakes!  They taste like a mix between crepes and pancakes.

I did modify the recipe slightly.  The first batch was too runny, so I added extra oatmeal.  I used two whole eggs, fat free cottage cheese, and added a generous pinch of salt and a few shakes of cinnamon.  I also put in two droppers of liquid stevia (a natural sweetener).

I love it--a *healthy* pancake recipe with no sugar or refined flour, and a nice serving of protein to boot.  Thanks for a great recipe.

attributes.source_text: My pancake-loving family loved them

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe twice.  Once with cottage cheese and once with ricotta cheese.  They were both very good, and I am not sure if one was better than the other.  I found that if I put the eggs into the blender first, it makes for an easier mixing;whereas, if I put the oatmeal in first, it tends to clump and is harder to mix.  I also used 2 whole eggs, rather than the egg whites as called for in the recipe.  DH and I both liked these healthy pancakes, and we will be looking forward to eating them again.  We used sugar free pancake syrup.  As most people have commented, this is certainly a healthy and nutritious breakfast.  Thanks for posting, Bramble!

attributes.source_text: DH and I both liked these healthy pancakes
this is certainly a healthy and nutritious breakfast

reviews.review_text: Well, I'll have to admit that after reading all the rave reviews I was expecting something more than these bland, rubbery little discs.  I followed the recipe, just substituting two whole eggs instead of the four egg whites, as most of the reviewers recommend.  They certainly are filling, like lead in the stomach.  I suspect the attraction of this recipe might be for those who, like myself, are on high protein diets, like the Dukan diet, and are just craving something that remotely resembles bread - almost anything will do, including these yukky "pancakes."  I give the recipe an "A" for effort, but I won't be making them again.

I loved these! I eat a pretty high protein diet, and to be honest, my expectations were not too high. I was eating a protein powder pancake recipe; to put it simply, they were just edible. These were actually really enjoyable! My boyfriend pretty much eats whatever he likes, and he liked them, also. I did use two eggs instead of the whites, fat free cottage cheese, added 1/2 tsp of cinnamon, a littttle extra vanilla, one tsp of stevia, and it all blended nicely. They have an almost buttery taste just on their own. I was very satisfied with this recipe and will definitely make again(as I hate cottage cheese any other way, haha).

attributes.source_text: They have an almost buttery taste just on their own
he liked them, also

reviews.review_text: Don't go in expecting these to really be like pancakes, but they are very good considering how healthy they are.  I used steel cut oats, two whole eggs, low fat cottage cheese and added a tsp of sugar, crushed walnuts and a tsp of cinnamon.  I also used some syrup on them.  My two year old gobbled them up.  I liked them, too.  I will keep experimenting with the recipe to make it even more healthy.  Maybe some roasted ground flax seed, a banana, etc.   Thanks so much for this recipe.  I cannot handle wheat gluten but I seem to handle oats ok, so this is a great gluten free meal, too, as long as you can find gluten free oats.

attributes.source_text: My two year old gobbled them up

reviews.review_text:
I made these for brunch for my mom and I. She couln't believe there was no flour or wheat of any kind in these. They are so easy and really delicious. I added diced apple and cinnamon and served them with whipped cream -- perfect. I dont know where you came up with this, but its a lovely recipe.
9/21/07 I feel the need to  solidify my glowing review -- I made the batter last night and kept it in the fridge and made them before work this morning and they were PERFECT. I used 2 whole eggs, added apples again, and chocolate chips and sugar and I'd say theye were still pretty darn healthy. I ate them with applesauce and I feel ready to take on the day. Thnaks Bramble!

attributes.source_text: I made these for brunch
for my mom and I. She couln't believe there was no flour or wheat of any kind in these

reviews.review_text: These are very good, very healthy pancakes. The first time I made them I followed the recipe to a T and my only thought was that they needed a bit of sugar or something, so the second time I added a few spoons of granular splenda and, out of sheer laziness, used two whole eggs instead of 4 whites. They were just as yummy, if not better. I could go either way with the whole eggs/egg whites, but I think the sugar/sweetner is a must. The flavour is lacking slightly otherwise. All in all a really good, healthy recipe though. It's so nice to be able to have pancakes even though I'm on a diet! AND the BF liked them too, which is a small miracle.

attributes.source_text: the BF liked them too

items.label: Grilled Cheese, Diner Style
items.name: Grilled Cheese, Diner Style
items.description: The mayonnaise in place of the butter makes the bread toast evenly and gives a similar yet different crispiness. This is how they made it on the grill at a diner I used to frequent, the kind where the grill is behind the counter and you can watch.  CAUTION: using low fat or no fat mayo or even miracle whip will change the outcome of the final product, the first 2 contain water and the second sugar that does not act in the same manor as an oil or fat sub.
instructions: Heat a small skillet to medium.
Using a butter knife, spread half of mayonnaise onto one slice of the bread, place mayo side down in the skillet.
Top with cheese.
Spread remaining mayonnaise onto second slice of bread and place mayonnaise side up on top of cheese.
Cook 3 minutes, or until bread is toasty brown, turn and repeat.
Note: Miracle Whip does not work for this, as the sugar in it tends to burn.

reviews.review_text: Well Dawnab, my comment stands: Once again, making Grilled Cheese Sandwiches this way has never been easier!! I wish I could rate this recipe 5-stars twice, once for me and once for Ma (my Grandmother)because she loved the taste and was shocked that I grilled the bread in the skillet with mayo instead of butter!  I had to post again because my Grandmother told me to ALWAYS make her breakfast sandwiches this way from now on.  After frying up some bacon & eggs for Ma, I spread the mayo thin on the bread (to me, that's the key to perfect browning)and while the bread was grilling in the skillet I added the bacon & eggs, topped with a slice of Cheddar Cheese, topped with the other slice of bread lighlty coated with mayo on the other side and flipped the sandwich over.  Needless to say, My Grandmother loved it!!  We both concur, No wierd taste from the mayo and the cheese melted perfectly.  Once again, Thanks for a new spin on an old classic.

attributes.source_text: she loved the taste
make her breakfast sandwiches this way
My Grandmother loved it
the cheese melted perfectly

reviews.review_text: God I love this site!  It's recipes like this that give the tricks of the trade that the average cook would never have figured out.  I'm not the best grilled cheese maker (I'm the person who always cooked on a super high setting causing the bread to burn but the cheese not to melt) but have been trying to be patient since my kids really like them for lunch.  I came across this and had to give it a try.  WOW!  PERFECTLY crisp on the outside and ooey gooey on the inside.  The bread was so perfectly crisp that I was even able to slice the sandwich with a triangle shaped sandwich cutter (the kids like it that way) without all the filling coming out.  As I pushed through the bread I just heard the perfect crunch as it pushed right through.  It was great!  Will ALWAYS make mine like this from now on.  I used low-fat Hellman's and it worked perfectly!  Thank you for this one!  Excellent tip for us novice grilled cheese makers!

attributes.source_text: my kids really like them for lunch
my kids really like them for lunch
PERFECTLY crisp on the outside
ooey gooey on the inside

I just heard the perfect crunch

reviews.review_text: Well, I'm anti-American (cheese that is), but the mayo trick is great!  I have been struggling with some of the basic "things mom used to make" since I've been on my own like grilled cheese and french toast and stew... things you would think so basic, but darn! it's hard to get it as good as mom's.  I used Ezekiel spouted bread and fancy-schmancy drunken goat cheese (a goat cheese that has been cured in wine and soooooo good) that I had been trying to save for too long and really needed to use up.  The mayo (I used Organic from Trader Joe's) was just like all the other reviewers said- not greasy, but crisp, no mayo flavor, it browned very well and with a good rich flavor without being oily.  Thanks Dawn- I'll be making those basics better than mom yet!

attributes.source_text: not greasy

reviews.review_text: I was surprised about the mayonnaise. The Sandwich was beautiful and evenly browned and very tasty. This will be my new way to make grilled cheese for now on. I just want to add that when my dad made us grilled cheese sandwiches growing up, as soon as he removed the sandwich from skillet he would open the sandwich while the cheese was still warm and sprinkle Worcestershire sauce in the middle. That is how my siblings and I eat our sandwiches and that's how all my dad's grandchildren eat the sandwich's as well. Once you eat it like that it's hard to go back. I didn't think grilled cheese could get any better, but the mayo has now made it one heck of a sandwich. Thank you for sharing that tip Dawnab!

reviews.review_text: I have been making grilled cheese sandwiches this way for years.  My "big kids" still request these all the time! I have made them for other kids that were visting my kids and, since I shooed everyone out of the kitchen before I did it, nobody knew!  I'd get comments like "That was the best grilled cheese sandwich I ever had!"...But I didn't let them in on my secret!  Mayonnaise makes the bread more "crispy" than butter or margarine.  I also use cheddar, MJ or Provelone cheese rather than American slices, which, to me, are alot more disgusting than mayo!  The secret is to spread the mayo thinly all the way to the edges of the bread.  It makes the crust taste almost like pie crust.  I believe mayo cooks faster than butter/marg so I turn the stove down a little bit (just under medium) and watch carefully so that the bread doesn't burn. Also, before I put any mayo on the bread, I usually pop the assembled sandwich in the microwave for 20-30 seconds (depending on how thick the cheese is) to start the cheese melting before I put it into the frying pan. This guarantees a nice melty grilled cheese sandwich. After the cheese is warm I put mayo on the first side of the sandwich and don't spread it on the second side until the sandwich is in the pan. If I'm making it just for myself, I sprinkle a tiny bit of salt, pepper and maybe garlic powder on each side before spreading the mayo.  The mayo trick works well on Quesadillas, too (using flour tortillas), but go easy on the mayo!

reviews.review_text: Mayo in general creeps me out but on the outside of a grilled cheese? EEK. I thought poor Dawn had to be mistaken.  LOL  But I was intrigued and had to try it.  The mayo (I used Best Foods brand) works PERFECTLY for a grilled cheese -- it turns a gorgeous brown and it doesn't leave behind a mayo flavor.  The added benefit is the easy spreadability of mayo as butter is often too hard and will tear your poor little pieces of bread.  With this recipe you don't have to wait for butter to soften -- you can have a grilled cheese right freaking NOW.  This is how I will make a grilled cheese from now on.  Thanks Dawn! :)

I wish I could give this 10 stars !!!! Oh my gosh what a wonderful grilled cheese. I would have loved to had taken a picture. It grilled up so nice and golden brown. Using the mayo was a millions times better than the butter. I will never cook grilled cheese the other way again. I used Dukes brand mayo, and I placed one slice of fat free cheese and one slice of fat free swiss. Next time I make it I will add some garlic salt/parsley seasoning just to zest it up more. I think it is IMP for people to know not ever to use fat free or low fat mayo, because that is made up of mostly water. Maybe you can make a note of that in the recipe :) Thanks for a totally wonderul grilled cheese.

i used to hate mayo, but im learning it has its uses, and this is one of them, i dont spread it on thick, just a thin even layer and it always browns evenly and nicely, leaving not even the littlest bit of mayo flavor behind (at least not one i can detect) id like to try useing the mayo on a sandwich made in the sandwich maker also, thanks for posting

*note*

i recently tried this useing the sandwich maker... and it didnt turn out so well lol, i guess ill just have to stick to the frying pan when i use mayo

Well DUH!!!  I can't believe that I didn't think of this before...lol!!!  My sweet DH was always the one to make these for me because I could never get them to turn out right.  I can make the most difficult meal, but have a hard time with the most basic comfort food... He saw me make this with JUST cheese and nothing else and knew he was going to be beat out of first place and even admitted that he was!  These are great and easy!  I am THRILLED that my daughter will have a mommy that knows how to make a grilled cheese sammich!!  Thank you for sharing!!!

My toddler said this was the yummiest grilled cheese ever!  Quick to yield a super golden, crispy exterior and a moist interior with perfectly melted cheese on our griddle.  Also had a somewhat less greasy finger feel than our usual butter version, as it seems the mayo absorbed into the bread better than butter.  Ours had a yummy mayo flavor, but we didn't mind as we make our own fresh mayo (thanks to our chickens for great eggs!)  A great way to make crispy, golden grilled cheese.

I made another batch for my husband and I using a curry mayo that gave a nice layer of flavor to an otherwise ordinary sandwich.  Thanks again for the mayo tip!

items.label: Strawberries & Cream Bread (Strawberry or Blueberry)
items.name: Strawberries & Cream Bread (Strawberry or Blueberry)
items.description: A wonderful recipe using fresh strawberries from Netherhill Strawberry Farm in Australia. This recipe also yields a tried and true (and reviewed) great Blueberry & Cream Bread.
instructions: Combine flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and cinnamon; set aside.
In small bowl, beat butter until creamy.  Gradually add sugar, beat 1 minute or until light and airy. Add brown sugar. Beat in eggs, one at a time. Beat in sour cream and vanilla.
Stir into flour mixture only until dry ingredients are moistened.
Fold in strawberries and nuts.
Pour into a greased 8 x 4 inch loaf pan.
Bake at 350°F for 60 to 65 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.
Let stand 10 minutes in pan.
Turn out on rack to cool.

reviews.review_text:
Mmmmmm...very nice! I had to make a few changes as I didnt have all the ingredients on hand. I used Low fat butter and low fat cream cheese. I used about 1 1/2 cup strawberries and only 1 egg. No nuts.I tossed the berries in cornflour to prevent sinking (just in case!) I also only added the 3/4 cup sugar and I'm so glad I didnt add more! It was plenty sweet for us. My strawberries were not very sweet either but the sugar quantity in the cake was more than enough...its just right with some low fat whipped cream on the side. I will make this with less sugar next time though so we can have it with strawberry butter. I baked it in a round spring form pan and it only needed 45 mins..probably because of the low fat ingredients so if anyone decides to try a low fat version, keep in mind that it'll take less time to bake. We all love this bread/cake and will certainly be making it again and again! Thank you for posting this one. Highly recommended.
UPDATE: I made this today without any eggs at all (for a friend who doesn't eat eggs) and it came out tasting super! I was thrilled! I added 2 tablespoons of oil, 1.5 tablespoons of baking powder ( plus whats already called for in the recipe)and 1 tablespoon vinegar. I also used extra light cream cheese (as I always do) so needed about 1/8 to 1/4 cup milk to get the mixture to the right consistancy.

attributes.source_text: It was plenty sweet for us

reviews.review_text: SO GOOD!!!!  Can't stress enough how much we loved this.  I chopped more strawberries than called for and of course couldn't waste them, so I added more that the recipe called for.  I also read other reviews where some said to add more sugar and since my fresh strawberries were not the sweetest, I added some extra sugar (also threw in a couple extra walnuts).  When I first tasted it warm out of the oven, got rave reviews, but wasn't crazy about it-even was slightly disappointed because of all the rave reviews.  But when I tried it the next day at room temperature it was one of the most delicious things I have tasted in a long time.  I guess flavors had time to meld.  All I can say is that it disappeared when I went to take a shower and not a CRUMB was to be found!  Will keep this in my permanent file and already getting requests to make again.  Can't wait to try the blueberry...THANK YOU!!!!

i used this recipe twice, making cupcakes instead of the loaf. i made 18 cupcakes with the serving amount given on this recipe...i cooked the cupcakes for about 17 minutes total (though i checked them at the 15 minute mark with a toothpick) on 350. i didnt change any ingredients in this recipe (unusual for me but it is just so perfect the way it is!)...the only change i made was to actually place the strawberries in a food processor and chop them up into tiny pieces (just a personal preference..i dont like any fruit pieces larger than a tiny sliver in my desserts)...otherwise i left it as is..these are the best cupcakes i have ever had..perfect for a summer bbq or just to have on the dining room table for the nibblers of the house to grab....this is a recipe i will be using for years to come! thank you for posting!

reviews.review_text: This Strawberry Bread is SO easy to make – such easy-to-follow instructions – and is every bit as delicious as it looks in Melody’s and Varsha’s excellent photographs.  And it really was fun to make.  I carefully perused all the reviews and followed several of the excellent suggestions made there.  This is obviously SUCH a versatile recipe: great!  I served it with ncmysteryshopper’s Decadent Strawberry Butter Recipe #121467.  WOW!  A taste sensation!  Rather than add extra strawberries as several reviewers had suggested, I made this bread with 3/4 cup of strawberries and 3/4 cup of raspberries (I love the slightly more tart flavour of raspberries) and I added 1/2 cup of chopped almonds instead of the optional walnuts.  Since I was adding almonds, I followed another reviewer’s suggestion and used almond essence instead of vanilla essence.  I followed Varsha’s suggestion of making this in a spring form pan; it made getting the bread out of the pan such a breeze!  Next time, I’m going to use Greek yoghurt in place of the sour cream.  This bread has a scrumptious blend of flavours and a lovely light texture, and those berries, WOW; and the Decadent Strawberry Butter, WOW!  I know that I’ll enjoy making slight variations probably every time I make it.  One thing’s for sure, next time I make this, I’ll be - at least - doubling the recipe!  And putting some in the freezer sounds like an excellent idea.  I think I’ll make the ones for the freezer in muffin pans: easy then to take out a few at a time.  And that way, they’d be great for picnics or for take to work lunches, and children’s lunchboxes.  Everyone absolutely loved this bread; and I’m really looking forward to sharing it with others.  Thank you so much for sharing it!  Another Zaar World Tour super-find!

reviews.review_text:
This was very, very good. Light and fluffy and perhaps this would have been a five star if not for my substitutions.

I subbed half oat flour for the flour and the other half was whole wheat.

I added more cinnamon as per my tastes

I used slightly more blueberries, all of which were frozen

I used half brown sugar and half demarra sugar

I omitted the nuts.

I used a hand mixer for everything except the final addition of blueberries.

Like I said, this was REALLY REALLY good but not a five star for me. Perhaps white flour would have done that.

Also, even though I sprayed my cake pan with butter flavored Pam, it still came out as a HUGE mess. Perhaps it was still way too hot to try and take out of the pan. I was bummed about that though.

Also, because of near freezing cold conditions where I was working all of the ingredients were cold except the butter.

All in all, I would have liked to have seen more flavor in this bread. The blueberries and the sugar were the stars of this dish. Perhaps it could use an addition of citrus?

I also opted to add the brown sugar to balance out the tartness from the cranberries and replaced 1/4 of sugar with Splenda. The result was nicely dense and moist, between bread and muffin in texture. I also baked these in 3 mini-loaf pans for 45 minutes on 350 convection, thinking that I would freeze one or two because the family is not much on sweets but was surprised. Then again this is not as rich as a cake with frosting plus it has fruit and yogurt. I think I"ll be making this often and I can't wait until strawberries come in season.  I hope this will come out well with frozen cranberries because I still have half a pound that I had leftover from everything. Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

reviews.review_text: This is an okay recipe eaten warm or a couple hours later, but if you wait until the next day, you will be rewarded!  I used half vanilla/half almond extract, increased the strawberries to 2c, and used finely chopped (almost ground) almonds.  Since I made two batches, I made muffins and an 8x8 pan.  I think the muffins are a bit tastier, but maybe it's because they were scooped first and got more strawberries, not sure.  This is great plain, with butter, or with more strawberries on top for a decadent strawberry shortcake!  I was also making a double batch of banana bread (muffins & an 8x8 pan), so combined what was left of both batters and baked a loaf of strawberry-banana bread!

This is fantastic.  I have to tell you, I am normally very disappointed when I put strawberries "in" something.  I love strawberries so much that I just like to eat them plain...why mess with perfection!  However, this is now the ONLY way I would consider cooking/baking using strawberries as an ingredient (except for jam)  I made a few minor changes..I used subbed yogurt for the sour cream; I accidently used too much baking soda; and rather than making one loaf, I made 4 mini-loaves.  I made the mini-loaves to freeze for later so we wouldn't be gluttons...Oh, well....2 are already gone before making it to the freezer. I upped the cinnamon to a full teaspoon and instead of butter I used 1/2 cup of applesauce and 1/2 cup of oil. I'm not wild about nuts in my bread so I decided to leave them out. Since I doubled the recipe I used 1 1/2 cups of sugar and 1/2 cup of brown sugar.I still felt it wasn't quite sweet enough but that's probably because my strawberries were not very sweet.I think it would be good with a brown sugar topping and next time I'll add even more strawberries.I can't wait to make this bread again!

Might try it as muffins next time, or even in a cake pan and drizzle a little glaze over it after.  Wonderful recipe!  Thank you so much!

items.label: Baklava Salmon (Salmon With Honey, Butter, Walnuts, and Mustard)
items.name: Baklava Salmon (Salmon With Honey, Butter, Walnuts, and Mustard)
items.description: One of my friends deemed this "Baklava Salmon" and the name stuck. The salmon & mustard go well with the honey, butter, and walnuts. We usually serve this with rice and steamed carrots or broccoli.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°; Line shallow roasting pan with non-stick aluminum foil, or spray with non-stick pan spray.
In small bowl, blend butter, mustard, and honey, set aside. In another bowl, mix together bread crumbs, nuts, and parsley.
Place salmon fillets on prepared pan, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and brush with honey-mustard mixture. Sprinkle tops with crumb/nut mixture; if any remains, press into sides of salmon.
Bake salmon 12-15 minutes in preheated oven, or until it flakes easily with a fork. Serve with lime or lemon wedge.

reviews.review_text: DELISH!  All my guests loved it, and I can't wait to serve again.  After reading a handful of the reviews, I varied the quantities slightly, and next time I will vary a bit more.  For 2 lbs of fish (a double recipe), I will double the crumbs and the mustard.  But, I will use only 2T butter and 2 T honey, in all.  This is because my salmon could only hold less liquid on top (and also for health reasons.)  (Tips - do not heat the honey with the butter, as this will make it too liquidy to stay on.  If you can use an instant-read thermometer, cook the fish until just 140.)  Instead of individual pieces, I did a whole side of salmon, and served it with a green (brown) rice and roasted cauliflower.  It also occurs to me that this would be a fabulous recipe to serve on Rosh Hashanah, where honey often figures into the meal (for a sweet year.)  Thanks for sharing, Tiger Jo; this was fabulous.

reviews.review_text: Really really easy way to prepare salmon... we are trying to eat more fish but I just hate "plain" baked fish... I was a little skeptical at first, since the ingredients seemed like they would not taste good combined... BUT I was wrong.  Somehow, all the ingredients combined just transformed a plain filet of salmon into something spectacular!  I halved the recipe for 2 servings and all the ingredients accordingly... I seemed to have a lot of the butter mixture leftover however... but the crumb mixture was perfect to top off both filets.  It smelled so good while baking and the tops browned to a golden brown and was delightfully crispy.  I think I overcooked it just slightly, but I will watch it more carefully next time... Thanks for a keeper for life!!!

attributes.source_text: was delightfully crispy

reviews.review_text:
We tried to grill salmon before but usually turned out rather tough.  However, the butter and honey really preserve the tenderness of the fish.  

Sometimes I used bought chopped mixed nuts, dried herbs like sage, rosemary instead.  They all turned out very nice.

There are 2 tips I think it may be useful.  I lay the fish with skin facing down so the scales become quite crispy afterwards.  Besides, I mix the salt and pepper in the butter, mustard and honey mixture so the fish pieces can be seasoned more evenly. 

Salmon fillet can be quite expensive, so we often use trimmings which is a fraction of the price.  Unfortunately, after buying the trimmings a number of times, the owner knows there is the market and has increased the price a bit. 8-(

I thought an alternative method of preparation would be to coat the bottom of the baking pan with a thin layer of the HM sauce, place the salmon in it, pour the rest of the HM sauce over that, and then distribute the bread crumbs over the top of all that.  Definitely not as attractive, but faster, and no leftover HM sauce.

reviews.review_text: I LOVE this recipe. Even my father, who doesn't love salmon, thought this was great. I doubled the recipe and used three different mustards (honey dijon, white whine dijon, and stone-ground dijon). I used clover honey as well. I also used Panko breadcrumbs, for extra crunchiness. At my mother's request, this is what I prepared for Mother's Day today. I supplemented it with a salad that included walnuts, chopped apricots, cranberries, mixed greens spinach, tomatoes and cucumbers, as well as fresh french bread and fresh corn on the cob. Altogether a delicious meal! I also cooked a little longer than specified, about 25 minutes, because I doubled the amount of salmon.

reviews.review_text: Made this with Pecans, Dried Parsley, Whole grain nut bread toasted and then pulverized. I pulverized the entire group above with my motar and pestle. Added Trader Joes whole grain mustard and Agave syrup since I didn't have honey. Baked at 400 in toaster over for about 22 min or so because the fish was slightly icy still. Served with Pressure Cooker Quinoa and Lima beans with the left over sauce and crumb mixture added to the liquid in the pressure cooker. For "oil" in the pressure cooker (for the lima beans) I added 1 tsp bacon drippings. Boyfriend says this is a keeper and wants it again, soon.

reviews.review_text: Are you a believer in Love At First Bite?? I wasn't but now I am! I am not a fan of fish, but I know that if cooked right (like Pecan Crusted Grouper from one of my fav restaurants) I eat it up. I have been on a mission to unravel only the best of the best recipes for fish - in order to incorporate it into my diet. And this one, so far, TOPS the list. For those of you non-believers out there, you need to try this one.... you surely will fall in love. I myself, used honey butter in stead of regular butter (and still added honey), and in addition to the bread crumbs I used wheat germ, for just a slight bit more additional nutrients. 1/8 cup Wheat Germ & 1/8 cup bread crumbs. Dijon mustard, Pecans and a Lemon were the rest of my choices. TigerJo, you should have kept this recipe a secret, but boy am I glad you didn't!

What a wonderfully different way to prepare salmon!!! I had about half of the butter mixture leftover so I think I could easily cut all that in half. The flavors so complement the salmon and nothing overpowers...just beautiful. The lemon squeezed on top makes everythign just "pop". I do think next time I will try adding some garlic...I kept thinking I was getting a slight "DeJoghne" flavor and I think that might be an interesting twist. This will be made when I need to impress and do not have a lot of time as so much of this can be prepped ahead and put together at last minute.

reviews.review_text:
This was just fabulous!  I used all of the ingredients except the lime/lemon at the end, but I did make changes to suit the size of the piece of salmon I had, and to make it a bit lighter in fat and calories: 12 oz piece cut in 3 servings, 2 T butter, 2 T grainy mustard, 1 T honey, 2 T dry bread crumbs, 2 T walnuts, 
2 t dried parsley.  I served with couscous made with chicken stock, dried basil, garlic, and onion, with tomatoes and balsamic vinegar served on top, as well as asparagus spears on the side.  Thanks, TigerJo14, for such a great dish!

Just a wonderful recipe.  Salmon intimidates me, since it often comes out "fishy," so I run salmon under cold water for about two minutes before cooking or seasoning it, and then pat dry.  As for the recipe, I made as is, only using regular table salt, omitting any lemon or lime, which I thought would have overpowered the honey mustard taste, and using slivered almonds instead of walnuts or pecans.  I served with steamed broccoli and cheesy baked garlic bread.   I baked for 15 minutes, and the salmon was EXCELLENT...I would not have baked it a minute less or more!!  Thanks for posting this great salmon recipe!

reviews.review_text: So good! And different than any other salmon recipe that we've tried. I used half olive oil and half margarine instead of butter.  I also didn't have any walnuts, (my hubby isn't a huge fan), so we used almonds and they were great! I dipped the entire fillet in the sauce and then into panko. Next time, I will just put the nuts on top instead of mixing them with the panko, the two textures just didn't mesh well. I sprinkled them lightly with olive oil and then baked like normal. My hubby couldn't get enough!

items.label: Traditional Irish Shepherd's Pie
items.name: Traditional Irish Shepherd's Pie
items.description: Posting this per a request.  I've said it once and I'll say it again there is nothing Irish about Corned Beef and Cabbage, but Shepherd's Pie has always been and still is a staple of traditional Irish cooking.  This is a really easy, but tasty recipe that the whole family will enjoy.  It's nutritionally sound with all the major food groups represented.  The British use lamb in their Shepherd's Pie, but we've always used beef.  Do whatever you prefer or even try turkey if you're watching fat content.  This sauce is lovely and rich and should go well with any meat.  You can use fresh or leftover mashed potato.  I usually use 3 tbsp of ketchup instead of the 2tbsp of tomato paste as I like the hint of sweetness, but traditionally the paste would be more sound! You can also make individual pies which are always a hit with the kids.  This freezes beautifully too, so make two and save one! Just let it defrost and glaze with the egg and pop into the oven as directed.  Enjoy! :)
instructions: Pre-heat oven to 200C/400°F.
Saute carrots in the olive oil until starting to get tender.
Add in the onions and saute for a minute or two then add the meat.
Season with black pepper and thyme.
Cook until browned then drain fat.
Add the butter and peas.
Sprinkle with flour and stir through.
Add tomato paste, wine and Worcestershire sauce.
Let this reduce slightly then add the chicken stock. Allow to reduce down until you have a thick meaty gravy. Season to your taste.
Remove from heat. Grease an oven proof dish** (9x13 works for me, as does an oval baker) with butter and add the sauce.
Spoon or pipe the mashed potatoes over top. Brush with egg and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese if using.
Bake for about 20 minutes or until the potato is nice and browned on top.
Serve as is or with some crusty bread to mop up that yummy sauce!

reviews.review_text: With regard to the following comment:<br/><br/>"I've said it once and I'll say it again there is nothing Irish about Corned Beef and Cabbage..."<br/><br/>This is incorrect. Both corned beef and cabbage are some of the most traditional ingredients in Irish cooking for hundreds of years. There are several texts and entries in historical documents that confirm this - if you had done an internet search it wouldn't have only taken you a few minutes to see this. I see that your profile says you are from Michigan not Ireland - I will give you the benefit of the doubt as you may be from Ireland originally but I am from Ireland and have lived here all my life so I know what I am talking about. If you are from Ireland and your family didn't eat corned beef and cabbage then you are one of the few. <br/><br/>I should also add that this recipe isn't "traditional" for a few reasons but in particular because olive oil is a relatively recent addition to most Irish kitchens nor does red wine feature in "traditional" Irish cooking. I point this out to show you that people in glass houses shouldn't throw stones. <br/><br/>* A note for people who identify themselves as "Irish Americans". I appreciate the desire to identify with your ancestry but you will find actual Irish people do not consider someone as being Irish if their great great grandfather's dog was Irish [Irish humour]. If you are born in America or any other country and have spent all your life there then you are from that county and not Irish. You are only Irish if you were born in Ireland or if you spent the majority of your life, in particular your childhood, in Ireland. I don't say this to be mean or hurtful but because it is something that is extremely irritating to Irish people and it's about time someone told you.

This is pretty darn close to my inherited recipe (I used this once when I couldn't find my copy) and turned out pretty well with what modifications I could remember (I doubled the recipe, used a can of tomato sauce instead of paste, and a bottle of Irish red lager). I did want to note, however, that both shepherd's pie made with ground beef and corned beef come from Irish immigration history. Lamb was/is common and cheaper in Ireland, but when the immigrants came over they found beef was the staple. They adapted their shepherd's pie recipe accordingly, then took a lesson from the Jewish community when they bought the shoulder cuts (typically the toughest, least appealing and, most importantly, cheapest!), mixed some spices and made corned beef. While it's not a dish from back home, it's still an acceptable Irish-American dish, and it is flat out amazing when cooked properly.

attributes.source_text: come from Irish immigration history

reviews.review_text: This was excellent!  I would like to mention first that if you don't use ground lamb and use beef instead this is called "Cottage Pie". I used 1.25 pounds of ground beef sirloin so a bit more meat than the recipe called for.  We made our own potatoes (about 7 cups mashed) and I always boil with garlic cloves in the water so I can mash right in with the potatoes, and used milk, butter and sea salt and mashed to a fluffy consistency.  I really think the mash potatoes can make or break this recipe so be sure to put the time in to customizing them the way you like.  Next time I will add a little more peas too.  I would also recommend going up to the larger size baking dish as I used the 9x13 and had some overflow of juices into the oven and things got a little smoky - this could have been avoided if I have just used the 15x10x2 pan instead.  This made about 12 -- 1.5 cup servings.  Thanks for the great recipe!  Delish!

reviews.review_text: Hubby has been asking for Shepherd's Pie for a couple weeks. Rather than my usual throw together, I decided to consult my Food.com peeps. Am I ever glad I did. This was amazing!!! Followed the recipe almost exactly, with the exception of using dried thyme and Sherry. For those concerned about not having red or white on hand, I have found that using Sherry for either is a great alternative. You can pick up a big bottle in any liquor store for about $6.  For those concerned about the prep time, try using instant potatoes. They have changed so much over the last few years and honestly you cannot tell the difference. Our favorite is Idahoan Four Cheese. Remember too that Shepherd's Pie is one of those dishes that can be made earlier in the day and just tossed in the oven when you are ready. A chilled dish just takes a bit longer to heat.

Just made this for Christmas dinner 2012, and it was great!!! This is just the sort of dish I love to find at British pubs, but usually the pub version is too pricey to indulge in on a routine basis, so it's so nice to be able to make this at home. This recipe is going straight into my family collection.

I think what makes this recipe sing are the red wine/tomato paste/broth combo and chopping the veggies fine and mixing them in with the meat so that all the flavors blend seamlessly in every bite.

I used the Costco premade mashed potatoes and canned LeSeuer petite peas. Ground the carrots and onions to grate consistency in the Vitamix. (World's greatest kitchen appliance, BTW, but I digress ;) Dried thyme was just fine (and much faster for those of us who hate picking those pesky thyme leaves off their branches). Time to make will depend on how many shortcuts you take, of course, but this isn't a dish to make when you're in a hurry.

Very versatile recipe, and I'm already thinking about ways to play with it for next time. I might add button mushrooms, celery, and garlic. Might also try it with stout instead of red wine. The meat mixture alone (minus the mashed potatoes, or with rice mixed into the meat) would be a tasty filling for stuffed cabbage.

reviews.review_text: This is a great recipe for Shepherd's pie! I did change a couple things though. After cooking the carrots and adding the onion, I added about 7 large white mushrooms chopped and 1/2 C water. I upped the beef to 1 1/2 lbs and did not drain also 1 C cabernet and Worcestershire sauce but no peas or tomato paste. I also doubled the flour and used 1 can of Campbell's beef broth instead of chicken. I let this reduce for about 35 mins, allowing the contents to brown on the bottom and scraping them up with a wooden spoon every few minutes. It really added to the rich meaty flavor! For the potatoes I used instant since I didn't have potatoes on hand. A good way to get the potatoes to brown on top is to use a fork and make a cross hatch pattern on top. Keep an eye on it after 20 mins and let the whole top get some color!

attributes.source_text: It really added to the rich meaty flavor!
