reviews.review_text: This recipe was very easy to follow and it turned out great!  I had never made Shepherd's Pie before tonight, and I was hosting a small dinner party.  I wasn't worried because the ingredients and cooking methods were pretty basic.  Anybody could make this pie!  I followed most of the recipe, but improvised a little.  I added a large clove of garlic while sauteing the onion, and didn't use any corn, just carrots and frozen peas.  I also substituted dried thyme for fresh thyme, and added buttermilk to my mash potato mixture for a little added flavor.  I added some finely shredded Irish cheddar to 20 minutes into the baking of the pie.  I served it with a big leafy spinach salad.  I didn't need any bread because there really wasn't a lot of extra gravy, since I  reduced the gravy while sauteing the beef in the ban.

Overall, we liked this recipe a lot, but there just wasn't enough flavor. I used exactly the amount of ingredients the recipe calls for, but my husband and I thought it was more on the bland side. I think adding twice the Worcestershire would probably take care of the flavor imbalance. I did, however, use dried thyme as my local store does not carry fresh, so perhaps I needed to add more thyme, but that's a different flavor and that seemed fine to me. Also, I didn't like adding my homemade, fluffy mashed potatoes to the top to have it baked for 20 minutes...made the potatoes lose their fluffiness. I am definitely going to make this again, but I will try it with double the Worcestershire and putting the mashed potatoes on top after the rest of the dish has baked for 20 minutes.
Update: Made this a second time last night and it turned out PERFECT! I doubled the amount of Worcestershire sauce (4 tbsp instead of 2), added a little bit more chicken stock, maybe 1/4 cup. Added more thyme...I did use dried thyme instead of fresh. I also did not dice the carrots up "fine" as stated in the recipe. I sliced the carrots into thin round slices instead of dicing to give the dish a bit more texture and I didn't break the beef up as fine. Also did not put the mashed potatoes on top in the oven, instead, I cooked the mixture at 375 for 20 minutes, which gave it a nice caramalized texture on top and I served the mashed potatoes separate from the mixture. We mixed it all up on our plates of course...just something about putting mashed potatoes in the oven that makes them not as fluffy and creamy. I saw someone say they put cheese on their mashed potatoes and that sounds like a nice twist I might try next time. Definitely bumped this recipe up to 5 stars now!

I worked in food service for several years and am very well-versed in cooking and always get compliments on my cooking, I have made numerous Shepherd's Pie recipes, I have come up with my own recipes, I have had Shepherd's Pie at many, many restaurants all over. I thought this one sounded a little...different, but I'm always willing to try something once. With all of that said, this was absolutely AWFUL!!! No recipe should ever call for an entire glass of wine - not only that, but technically, how much is one glass even? It also calls for thyme, which I think could be left out - it's too potent of an ingredient and this recipe, just like the wine, calls for WAY too much. All of my ingredients were purchased the day I made it, the meat was fresh from a local meat market and I checked dates on all other ingredients. I can't even describe the taste, but it is disgusting - it tastes like it was made weeks ago and has gone bad, right after preparing and baking it. I think if the wine and thyme were completely left out, it would be a huge improvement and I'd be willing to try it without those things. It also wouldn't hurt to eliminate tomato paste altogether. There's no need for tomato paste in a meat, vegetable, and potato dish since it's not an Italian meal. This was supposed to be a meal that I could feed off from for a few days and heat up when I get hungry. Now I have to throw this whole thing out, waste ingredients and money, and make something else.

I decided to make this on a night I was sick with a really bad cold (comfort food!).  Anyway, because I was sick, I took some shortcuts.  Unfortunately, it also means my taste buds were shot but my husband assures me it was awesome!!  LOL  From what I could tell, it was tasty but I'm glad I froze half for another night.  I used Frances Coppola Cabernet as my wine.  My husband told me the mixture was too "wine-y" before we put it in the oven---even after I simmered it for an extra long time---but I hoped the baking would reduce that; he said it did.  Here are the shortcuts I made:  I used pre-cooked ground beef that I had in the freezer, 1 16-oz bag of frozen peas and carrots, 2 tablespoons of dried minced onions, omitted the olive oil (since I didn't have anything to saute), used a couple good shakes of dried thyme, used 2 containers of Country Crock pre-made potatoes (which normally I'm totally against even buying) with a can of drained diced potatoes mixed in (again, normally I'd think "eew" but we really like lumpy potatoes [don't judge] and it totally worked!).  This recipe gets a 4 from me today, since my husband like it so much and since what I COULD taste seemed to be pretty great; I feel like I might have to upgrade it to a full-on 5 when I try the other half.  I'm definitely looking forward to making this with my own homemade lumpy potatoes :-)

reviews.review_text: I must say...this recipe is HIGHLY recommended to all.  I am a very particular about recipes; but THIS ONE IS A KEEPER.  I used all the ingredients mentioned in the recipe as well as followed all of the instructions.  The only thing that I did different, not on purpose, was use White Zinfandel wine, instead of red wine (I didn't have any red wine and didn't feel like driving down the mountain to get it when I had everything else cooking--lol).  Unless you like that kind of wine, don't use it.  When I buy more red wine, I will try it--so I could decided which one is best.  Also, it really makes a difference when you season your potatoes and get them into a semi-creamy texture with butter and canned milk.  Whip on HIGH with hand mixer.  Just a thought, if you haven't tried it that way.  : )

Absolutely phenomenal.  I'm not a big fan of stewy dishes but the flavor of this one was incredible, and the quantity of ingredients is minimal to achieve what it does rather well.  My better half said this is her new favorite recipe that I make so I thought I'd create an account and weigh in on the topic.  As many have indicated you don't have to make homemade mashed potatoes to make this thing work.  Just buy a box of the powdered ones, but use more than you think you will need.  That speeds up the process immensely because you can just nuke 7-8 portions worth out in one fell swoop.  Very good recipe and I will be making this a lot more often since it was so well received.  Otherwise I made it as instructed.

attributes.source_text: My better half said this is her new favorite recipe

reviews.review_text: I love this recipe!  I had a friend from Ireland once make Shepherds Pie for dinner and thought it was so good.  This is the first recipe I have come across that tasted like hers.  I have made it a couple of times now.  I follow the recipe except most of the time I don't use any stock.  The first time the only red wine I had was Marsala.  I was concerned that it might be too sweet but really liked how it came out and use it every time.  This recipe is time consuming but like someone else suggest using carrots already shredded really helps.  I don't like instant mashed potatoes but sometimes buy some already made at deli.  I always use ground lamb which is more authentic than beef.  It shocks me that some people think it's bland.  Mine is anything but.  This is quickly becoming one of my favorite recipes to make.

So, this is the first review I've ever submitted for an online recipe, and I've been using online recipes for years.  I was moved to write a review, though, because this recipe is JUST THAT GOOD! Very Easy to make, and ridiculously delicious. I try not to make substitutions the first time I try a recipe, but I did so for the red wine as we are a non-alcohol family. The substitution was simple: 1.5 Tbsp. of Balsamic vinegar to 1 cup of beef broth. I stock a variety of flavor-infused balsamic vinegars, but for this just used an aged balsamic.  The result was a deep, acidic flavor with all of the tartness one expects from a red wine.  I was also out of peas, but we hardly noticed.  I chopped the carrot and onion coarsely (so the carrot hater could pick them out; likewise, the onion hater), and, as other reviewers have noted, focused on a potato layer to match the richness of the meat layer by using real butter, cream, pink Himalayan sea salt, garlic powder, and plenty of fresh ground pepper.  The gravy, however, is the star of this dish, and lends a rich and hearty body to a classic winter dish. Our experience was reminiscent of the titular scene in the wonderful kids' movie, Ratatouille. Minus the mouse.  (I hope.)  Much like the movie, this was an instant family favorite. YUM!

reviews.review_text: This is a staple recipe in our kitchen.  There is something about true comfort food and this one nails it.  I've had lots of Shepherd's Pie across the pond, and this one doesn't disappoint.  The first time I made it exactly like the recipe, but often I like to switch things up as well.  My favorite version now is to substitute Guinness (the can not the bottle) for the wine, to re-hydrate 1/8 cup finely chopped porcini mushrooms in beef stock, and add a cup chopped baby bella's.  I always also always make a double batch as it's just too darned good the next day, and the day after that, and....  My spouse is also a triple portion guy on Pie night, no need for any side dishes here!

reviews.review_text: I'd never had, nor had I ever made a Sheperd's Pie before, and this was very good!  I got nothing but compliments at our annual St. Patty's Day shindig.  I doubled the recipe for the most part, only used about a cup and a half of wine, but 3 cups of beef stock.  I used Merlot, because it's what I had and that added a distinct flavor.  Next time I will try it with Cabernet to compare.  I also cheated and used 3 packages of Idahoan instant potatoes since I was short on time.  Oh, and I didn't use the egg and cheese on top, a neighbor can't have dairy.  He was on his own with the potatoes however.  ;-)   Thanks, I will be making this every year now!!

This recipe is EXCELLENT!  And the cup of red wine makes it DIVINE!  I used ground bison for the meat, and for the veggies, I used a mixture of fresh and canned/frozen veggies.  I think I also used ketchup in place of tomato paste (that's what I had on hand).  After adding the red wine and letting cook down, if it's too liquidy, sprinkle a little more flour over everything and stir to mix well.  I made fresh mashed potatos (made extra to be sure there was enough).  Sprinkled with grated cheese on hand....I don't like it to be covered in a whole layer of cheese, that's so not necessary!  ENJOY!!  This rivals any pub shepherd's pie!! (Especially with the red wine added!!!)  My husband and I LOVED this!!  Going to make it again tonight!!

attributes.source_text: My husband and I LOVED this

reviews.review_text: This recipe is awesome! I searched for a traditional Irish dish to use for the St. Patrick's Day potluck at the office and this one looked yummy and had great reviews, so I gave it a shot. I followed the recipe to a "t" and it went over so well! Everyone loved it and it was gone in no time! I even made a separate small one for my husband because he couldn't resist the smell while I was cooking! I used the ground beef because I couldn't find lamb at my grocery store, so next time I will try lamb to see how it tastes. I used fresh mashed potatoes (with a little milk, butter, salt, pepper, and Parmesan) and I always leave some small chunks of potato intact and that seemed to go over well, too. I highly recommend this dish! Thanks for sharing the recipe!

reviews.review_text: This was my first time making shepherd's pie and it turned out great. items.name: Big Thicket Chicken and Dumplings
items.description: If you love good, old-fashioned, down home chicken and dumplings, this is the real thing! Note that this dumpling recipe makes "a bunch of dumplin's" because around here, most folks want more dumplin's than chicken. (prep time includes cooling time for cooked chicken.)
instructions: Place whole chicken and water into large pot or dutch oven.
Add poultry seasoning, garlic powder& pepper.
Bring to boil and reduce heat to medium.
Cook chicken for about 1 hour or until tender.
When done, carefully remove chicken from pot; set aside to cool.
Remove 2 cups of stock and set aside to cool.
Add celery, onion, carrot and bouillon cubes to remaining stock and continue to cook on simmer.
While chicken is cooling, prepare dumplings.
Into large mixing bowl, combine flour, baking powder, poultry seasoning and salt.
Add margarine and combine until mixture is coarse and crumbly.
(use a hand mixer) Add eggs and cooled chicken stock (be sure your stock has cooled to\
) then stir by hand to form a dough.
Turn out onto floured surface and knead slightly until smooth.
You may need to divide dough in half and only roll out half at a time.
Roll out to approximately 1/8-inch thickness.
Using a sharp knife or pizza cutter, cut dough in vertical strips about an inch wide.
Then repeat the process, cutting horizontal strips, which will give you little square dumplings.
Return chicken stock to a boil; drop dumplings in, a few at a time, as quickly as possible.
Cook about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent dumplings from sticking to bottom of pan.
When done, remove from heat and cover pan.
Remove skin and debone cooled chicken.
Cut into bite size pieces then fold into hot dumplings & broth.
This recipe will serve a family of 4 two main course meals.
Leftovers can be frozen.

reviews.review_text: No time to read the over 200 reviews, so I hope I am contributing something new here...  For the broth/soup I started with my leftover Thanksgiving turkey carcass that I had cooked for the broth.  Most of that I froze for later because it made 6 gallons or so.  I used about 2 gallons for this recipe.  I used all the remaining turkey meat from the bones and added chopped carrots and onions and seasonings to my tastes (I used some sage, rosemary, and basil, but the original recipe or whatever you like would be fine too).  For the dumplings, I forgot at the last minute that I was out of eggs, so used Ener-G egg replacer, and it worked fine.  I was also in a hurry and had no time to roll out the dumplings, so dropped them by teaspoofuls into the broth.  They cooked up fine!  I suspect the texture is a bit different done this way, but the dish was still delicious and my husband loved it.  The kids, unfortunately, refused to even try it!  This is the first time I have made such a dish and it looked very strange to them--too mushy looking I think.  More for us though.  I plan to try again rolling out the dough, but will probably half the dumplings.  I cannot imaging how they all could fit in only 1 gallon of soup.

attributes.source_text: my husband loved it

reviews.review_text: This was my first attempt at two things: Making homemade dumplings and using a whole chicken. Both turned out perfect!!! This recipe is a little time consuming, but I made it for OAMC, so while the chicken was boiling I made other recipes. I used a small vidalia onion instead of green onions, and I let the vegetables simmer in the stock for about 30 minutes while I made the dumplings (I like them to be really soft, and subtle-flavored in this type of recipe). I should have listened to some other reviews and only made half the dough, but I LOVE dumplings, so I made the whole recipe. After putting half of the dumplings in, I realized that my pot wasn't going to hold the rest so I decided to freeze the dough for a future recipe. Another thing I liked about this recipe is that is doesn't use cream or milk to make it thick. The flour from the dumplings were enough to really thicken up the stock and make it creamy. I was a little nervous when I first started dropping in the dumplings because I was thinking "how is this going to get creamy?", but after fifteen minutes of cooking, I realized my worry was misplaced and it really got nice. This made a large amount, and I definitely was able to freeze about four containers for future dinners (there's only two of us). I'll probably serve this with soft rolls and possibly a side of corn. Overall, a beautiful recipe! Thank you!! EDIT: I recently made this recipe again, but this time doing the "drop" method by pinching off about a tablespoon of dough and dropping it in.  With this, I was able to use ALL of the dumpling dough, to my BF's happiness!  With that, I have to put in about two tablesppons of flour to the stock to thicken it up, but it works great!!  This is now an absolute favorite recipe!!

reviews.review_text:
This is soooo GOOD! I changed so many things..I can not rate this properly. (I used what I had on hand).  But, I will tell you what I did. ;) First I read all the reviews. A must!
Chicken Substitutions: 4 Leg quarters. Ingredient substitutions: 1 tsp dried minced garlic, Pinch pepper flakes, 1/8th tsp celery seed, 1/4 large onion, Frozen green bean and carrot mix (3 large hand fulls added with one hour remaining in cooking time), I packet of poultry gravy mix **extra: added I bay leaf.

Halved the dumpling mix. added the egg to the stock and mixed the egg in with a fork, added to flour mixture mixed well. Sprinkled with a bit more flour (1/4 c) and mixed until just not  wet looking...but not OVER mixing. 
Placed the de-boned cut up chicken back into the pot..returning pot to a boil. Reduced heat to soft boil, dropped large tsp fulls of dough into stock. Cooked 15-20 minutes. Covered. Stirred gently about 2 times.

At first I was afraid to make the dumplings because my husband is not a lover of soggy bread/dough...I too have never been a fan of the Dumpling part either...But this was not the case with this. We both absolutely loved it! I had never made Chicken and Dumplings...As a child, my mother used to make it..and I just dreaded it. She was a great cook..but not with dumplings! LOL This recipe..the dumplings have this awesome flavor. This recipe is so versatile you can add or take away anything you like to adjust it to your own taste! Great recipe! And It was really easy to do. Thanks for giving me a new staple recipe, I will definitely pass on to my children. ~sandesnow

attributes.source_text: We both absolutely loved it

reviews.review_text: I can't believe I forgot to rate this the last time I made it. We really like this recipe. We are true Southerners and wanted a dumplin' recipe to match! (Using canned biscuits just wouldn't work!) I especially love the big, thick dumplings. ***I wanted to note some healthy changes I made for my family. A recent reviewer pointed out that this recipe is not low-calorie. That may be, but it can be made with far fewer calories, without sacrificing the great taste. Use a lean chicken and be sure to remove all fat and skin, use whole wheat flour instead of white, and use Smart Balance butter instead of shortening. For this to work you'll need to add more liquid into your dumpling dough - I use almost double. Try adding a bit at a time, until feels and looks right. If you want to get really picky you can use four egg whites instead of two eggs, or one egg and two egg whites. Once these changes are made, you are left with a healthy, tasty comfort food. Enjoy.

reviews.review_text: This review is for the dumpling part of the recipe only. I usually make chicken and noodles with more of a bread type dumpling, but I wanted to try something different this time for the noodle/dumpling thing.  They were easy to make and tasted delicious.  They also filled my need to have both since these are much like a chewy noodle without being dry like a bread like dumpling can be.  I used a little garlic and onion powder instead of poultry seasoning.  This recipe makes a huge amount of dumplings.  Next time I think I will halve the recipe since it is only my daughter and I.  Tip:  Do not make these too far in advance unless you can leave them in a single layer on the counter until you need them.  If you try to stack them, they will stick together and become a solid mass once again.  You will need to re-roll and cut them again.  Even heavily flouring them did not prevent this from happening.  However, the heavy flour will help thicken your broth nicely.  Thank you for a different dumpling (then what I am used to) that I plan to use again.  I love the texture.

reviews.review_text:
After all of the great reviews, I honestly was disappointed with the result.  My dish, while it had flavor, lacked depth which left a kinda flat feeling in my mouth.  My family liked it, but didn't get real excited.  

On the broth, I think part of this may have been my fault - my only change here - I used 4 chicken breasts instead of a whole chicken which might have been more flavorful.  Next time, I think I will use thighs and legs like my Grandma used to and brown them in a little butter and evoo first, before adding the water. I will also use a bigger pot so that I don't have to worry about boiling off some liquid to make room for the chicken and dumplings. I ended up having to add a can of broth at the end because my result was too thick.

The dumplings (why I chose this recipe) reminded me of what my Grandma used to make minus the poultry seasoning.  I used garlic and onion powder instead along with a few tablespoons of the chicken fat (replacing a little of the margarine) that  I skimmed off the broth for flavor.   Just note that your flour may not need all 2 cups of stock.  Mine didn't, but my daughter wasn't listening so the result was a gloppy mess.  After lots more flour (almost a cup) we saved the dumplings.  Yes, it really makes a whole lot and no, I shouldn't have cooked them all.

Thanks for the recipe, I will use it again with a few changes and a sprinkling of chili powder on top!!

reviews.review_text:
just to add to my previous review, once i posted it a friends daughter came up for a bowl and she inhaled it.  LOL she did not even sit down to eat, she stood in the kitchen and ate so fast that she never got to the chair. i did change the broth a little by browning the chicken pieces and deglazing the pot with water and using the roast chicken seasoning that comes in a grinder spice jar instead of regular poultry seasoning. This gave extra flavor.  Some things i will try next time are making it a thicker stew,as well as using more onions and deglazing with white wine. Probably removing the dumplings after cooking to thicken/change the base and then readding them.  I think that they need the lighter broth to cook in. 

However just as it, its a flavorful deep chicken stock. Best way i can describe it is the perfect combination between homemade chicken soup and stew with dumplings.

items.description: Make and share this Crepes recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Combine flour, milk, eggs, and oil.
Add salt.
Heat a lightly greased 6 inch skillet; remove from heat.
Spoon in 2 Tbsp batter; lift and tilt skillet to spread evenly.
Return to heat; brown on one side only.
To remove, invert pan over paper toweling.
Repeat with remaining batter.
Fill with your favorite filling.
Here's a few we like: Any flavor fruit jam, sweetened fresh peaches, cream cheese and pineapple, ham and maple syrup.
Endless ideas.

reviews.review_text: Good basic recipe. I just placed all ingredients in a blender to mix, and just poured about 2 Tbsp in my 6 inch crepe pan. I was cooking them only for me, so I only made three crepes, then placed the mixer jar in the fridge. The next morning I was able to use the left over mix again for more crepes.  The ingredients did separate, but I just pulsed it on the blender for a few seconds and it was as good as new, it tasted great. So it can be made the day before if you are looking for an easy breakfast.  For fillings I tried : dulce de leche, nutella and strawberries,  nutella and banana, cinammon and sugar, maple syrup. I will likely add some creme anglaise next time, and maybe try some savory type of filling like left over chicken and asparagus with some kind of white sauce like hollandaise sauce. Thanks for sharing.

attributes.source_text: if you are looking for an easy breakfast

reviews.review_text:
This recipe was great! This is my husband's favorite breakfast food, so I took a chance (okay..HUGE risk..) by making these this morning for our 7 year anniversary. First time in 7 years I've made them right! (Either that or he's just being nice because it's our anniversary :p ) The only tips I have:

1. Oil in the pan does NOT work well. Causes separation between batter making it difficult to spread in pan effectively. Pam worked much better.

2. If you have trouble getting the crepe out of the pan, let it cool down a bit. I found this out by accident when almost giving up on making them & walked away with one it the pan on a back burner. Viola! ever since

3. Start with a high heat pan...then bring it down to a low/very low med. The batter will spread more evenly, cook more even, prevent crisp edges and allow you to remove them much easier!

Thanks again for making it a great anniversary morning! (FYI, our filling was 1/2 C. low fat vanilla yogurt mixed with 2 tbs. homeade berry jam...yuuuumy)

Saw this in the new reviews this a.m. & decided ..hmmm think I'll make a batch..
my mom-in-law taught me how many many many years ago & I used to do it from memory BUT..
and it has been too many years since I've made them..
these are as close to her's as you can get..the only difference I can think of is we had to let ours sit awhile..(the batter that is)
these made WONDERFUL crepes had mine with a little homemade jam and a sprinkle of powdered sugar..
so MizzNezz I want to thank you for the wonderful recipe..
and it is funny how fast the tilting & moving of the pan came back to me..
I did NOT change 1 thing and won't...

Perfect Crepes!!!!!!!!!!  I think crepes are easier to make than pancakes!!  I do have a French non-stick skillet and I applied a thin coating of oil with a paper towel to my skillet in between lots of the crepes.  You can hardly screw these up unless you just went in the other room and left them in the pan to burn.  They don't stick and they pop right out when they are supposed to.  I wrapped these in classic style and I decorated and filled these with recipe#122352 that I had already made.  This is such a great recipe, I loved honoring my idol Julia by making some crepes on a Saturday afternoon!!!  Thanks for this wonderful recipe!!!

To make this easier, I just used a can of evaporated milk. Maybe it's because we use Lactaid milk that the evaporated works so much better for us for recipes... I always keep several cans in the pantry. I also sweeten up the recipe with either honey or agave (warmed up to make sure it blends easily). I throw all ingredients in a Nutribullet and am pleasantly surprised that I don't need to sacrifice the first crepe to the "crepe gods"! So often chefs will say that crepe batter needs to stand or cool for 10 minutes before using... not this recipe! I just zap it and use! I will make several and throw fresh fruit and granola with either whipped cream or yogurt in it for a quick breakfast on the go for my daughter and me. THANK YOU for a fabulous recipe! This is perfect and will keep in the bullet for 2 days as batter :)

reviews.review_text: Can't miss w/ crepes.  I make so many variations of this.  Instead of white flour I often add 1/3 c of whole wheat per cup of milk for a little more nourishment.  I also add seasonings like cinnamon and nutmeg to the crepe.  Great for desserts, breakfast and supper.  Today, i acually added some Italian seasoning and additional chopped Rosemary.  I stuffed it with sauted chopped onion, minced garlic, chopped fresh spinach, and tomatoes, seasoned with a little more Italian seasonings.  I added the hard guyere grated cheese, rolled and served with a dollop of creme fraiche and sprinkling of fresh parsely.

attributes.source_text: Great for desserts
breakfast
supper

reviews.review_text: I was once brave and tried crepes in a popular breakfast restaurant.  They did not turn out to be as wonderful as I thought they would.  I vowed to learn to make them at home.  Little did I know, there is nothing to learn!  I chose this recipe because I only had two eggs and the others called for more.  They turned out wonderful. I have a Pampered Chef small saute pan that is the perfect size for making crepes.  One problem -- crepes with strawberries and whipped cream are now my husbands favorite and most requested breakfast!!

attributes.source_text: crepes with strawberries and whipped cream are now my husbands favorite and most requested breakfast
my husbands favorite and most requested breakfast

reviews.review_text: Wow!! So quick & easy!! My husband was SO happy!!! We filled them with strawberries, blackberries, whipped cream & sweetened cream cheese (1/4 c. sugar mixed with 8 oz. cream cheese), and they were wonderful!! We felt like we were back at a little French cafe where we once ate!!  Edited to add that we continue to make this on a regular basis, especially when I want to treat my DH on the weekends!  We have also tried lite cream cheese in the sweetened cream cheese, and can't tell a difference!  Thank you for one of our favorite recipes!!

attributes.source_text: My husband was SO happy
when I want to treat my DH on the weekends

reviews.review_text:
Miss Nez!!! I can not believe I made a crepe! Thank you so much for sharing this recipe. I just had my very first crepe in Paris in October 2010, and this morning, you provided me the opportunity to share that experience with my children! Yummy yummy nutella-covered thank yous from the Paterson family!
I followed the recipe exactly. It was so easy, and worked so perfectly despite my nerves that somehow, someway I was going to mess it up. It just couldn't be as easy as you make it sound...could it? Yes!

attributes.source_text: you provided me the opportunity to share that experience with my children

reviews.review_text: We tried this recipe out because we were worried our Swedish foreign exchange student was feeling a little homesick during the holidays.  Everyone loved the crepes, and our exchange student said they were even better than what she ate in Sweden! The kids kept coming back for more! Since there were six of us trying them out, we would have given them 6 stars if we could! We laid out fresh peaches, bananas, powdered sugar, whipped cream, and boysenberry preserves and let the kids pick their own combos. Everything we came up with was delicious.

attributes.source_text: our exchange student said they were even better than what she ate in Sweden
The kids kept coming back for more

reviews.review_text: I awoke to the smell of pancakes but to surprise my 11 year old daughter had ventured off to make crepes- something I love but never tried to make.  The crepes came out lovely and couldn't have been easier to make.  So I say if an 11 year old can make these you can also be a success at making these delicious crepes. We spread a teaspoon of apricot preserves then loaded strawberries and raspberries in them and topped with whipped cream.  This will go in the family recipe book of keepers.  THANK YOU so much.

These were great! This is the first time I made crepes. We usually go to an amazing creperie in town, so I was hesitant to give it a go but I'm happy I did. I did add about a teaspoon of spoon of sugar, a sprinkle of cinnamon and a dash of nutmeg and about a teaspoon of vanilla. We only cooked one side like the directions said and it worked out great. Tilting the pan to get the batter to spread evenly is key. When these were done we flipped them out onto the paper towel and then filled them with strawberries and Nutella!

items.label: Crock Pot Chops That Will Make You Eat Til You Pop!
items.name: Crock Pot Chops That Will Make You Eat Til You Pop!
items.description: These have to be, hands down, the BEST meal I have EVER made in a crock pot. I borrowed a friend's crock pot one weekend and made this for my honey. Low and behold, I got a crock pot for my next birthday along with a request for this recipe to be the first thing I made. I really wish I know where I got the recipe from because I would LOVE to give credit for it. I beg of you, do yourself a favor and try this. You will NOT regret it. Let me know what you think!!
instructions: Salt and pepper pork chops if desired.
Add all ingredients except water and cornstarch to the crock pot.
Cook on low for 5 1/2 hours.
Mix cornstarch and water together and stir into crock pot.
Cook 30 minutes more.
Serve over rice.

reviews.review_text: I noticed you said you don't know where you got this recipe. I have been making this dish for years and it's one of my favorites and a favorite of anyone I make it for. I found it in the "Taste of Home (february/March 1998 edition)magazine" They had a special on crockpot cooking. Anyway this recipe won grand prize. Me personally I change it a little I prefer to cut the chops up into bite size bits. I don't care for celery so I leave that out. I also add the green pepper about 30 min to an hour (depending on how fast your crock pot cooks) before serving. Also for the last 30 min I cook on high (after adding the cornstarch).I find it makes the veggies less mushy. Salt and pepper to taste. I usually double the recipe because it seems to be a favorite. Then I serve over rice for a one dish meal. I think the rice tones down the sauce/meat mixture because it does have quite a bit of flavor.

attributes.source_text: I serve over rice for a one dish meal

reviews.review_text:
As a girl who actually burned (rather, turned into 'pork jerky') my last round of crockpot pork chops - on low! - I was a little worried about trying the technique again despite the glowing reviews on this recipe.

The meal turned out pretty well, and as others have said, it yielded a lot of sauce, but it was good sauce, so who cares if you get too much?  Very easy to make.  On the second night of this dish, I reheated the pork chops in the sauce on the stovetop, and the chops kind of shredded apart, so I just chopped up the bigger pieces and served it on toasted hamburger buns, kind of like pulled pork sandwiches.  They were really good too!  

I think I'd describe these as sweet & sour pork chops.

attributes.source_text: I think I'd describe these as sweet & sour pork chops

reviews.review_text: Wow.  You have some very mixed reviews here, I was a little tentative about this recipe, but it turns out that my worry was in vain.  Very satisfying!!!  Pork was too expensive, but petite sirlions were on sale so I used those.  I covered the steaks with kosher salt and fresh cracked pepper than seared 'em in a little olive oil.  I then dumped everything in the crockpot turned it on high and left it for 3 hours then low for the last hour- perfect!  This was exactly what I look for in crockpot fare- easy, tastey, and with pleanty of left overs.  Added bonus- only 8 WW points.  Add a half cup of rice and a salad with low fat dressing and you have a very filling, yummy dinner for only 10 or 11 points. Great stuff!

attributes.source_text: a very filling, yummy dinner

reviews.review_text: I have been looking at this recipe, (which is the same as Kari's ,in the top 100),for awhile now and have been wanting to try this for quite some time, so maybe I set my expectations way too high. While I liked it, I was not as wowed by it as I wanted to be. The meat did come out excellent, fork tender, and the sauce is tasty, I know a lot of her reviewers said the sauce was too sweet & stuff, I did not think so, but this did kind of remind me of a swiss steak or something and all the while I kept thinking I would prefer it with beef. My husband was kind of the same, he liked it but did not rave. I served it over rice which was good, but I think if I were to make again I would try with mashed potatoes instead(maybe that was it!?):)

attributes.source_text: The meat did come out excellent, fork tender
My husband was kind of the same, he liked it but did not rave

reviews.review_text: We loved this dish.  There were a couple of things I did different due to necessity.  When I decided on the recipe...it was too late to make in my slowcooker...so I used my Guardian Service Roaster on top of the stove.  Like one of the other reviewers I browned the porksteaks first, after I seasoned them with salt and lots of black pepper since several other reviewers said it was a little bland.  I also substituted carrots for the green pepper like another reviewer and added an extra can of stewed tomatoes since my DH loves them.  By the time the meat was tender, about 1 1/2 hour later, much of the liquid was cooked away having reduced to an almost concentrated amount.  I added a couple of cups of water removed the meat while thickening.  Removed the bones from the meat which left nice good sized pieces and blended them in the sauce/vegetable mixture.  I served it over rice and it was wonderful.  My DH said, this is kind of like a Sweet n Sour dish...but with more flavor and a little kick of spice.  Needless to say it was a hit and I will be making this again.  Really easy!  Thanks JustMarried for sharing!

attributes.source_text: My DH said, this is kind of like a Sweet n Sour dish
By the time the meat was tender
a little kick of spice

reviews.review_text: I followed the recipe exactly as said. The taste is definitely unique and got mixed reviews in my family :), I believe I liked it more then my husband and although it's a keeper, it will not be made often in my family. The sauce had just the right "thickness" for the  rice and you could actually cook a couple more pork chops in it (6 instead of 4).  The rice makes this dish even better! It's got a sweet and sour taste and if you want to kick it up a notch, a few drops of tobasco sauce wouldn't hurt this recipe :-). I salted my plate and I loved it even more (sweet/salt).  If my husband would have approved of this recipe like I did, I would have rated it a four star, I'll definitely recommend to my mother which I believe she will like as well :-).  Thank you for the good recipe!  P.s. I cooked mine on high for the same amount of time, the veges were tender, no problems for me.

attributes.source_text: The sauce had just the right "thickness"
It's got a sweet and sour taste
sweet/salt
the veges were tender

reviews.review_text: Another 5 star rating for this one!  I put this in the crockpot this morning, exactly as the recipe was written.  When I got home, I added the cornstarch and water to let it thicken while I made the rice.  I decided I wanted steamed broccoli with this dish so when my rice was about halfway finished, I lay the fresh broccoli spears on the rice, covered it, and the broccoli steamed to a perfect crisp-tender while the rice on the bottom of the pot finished cooking slowly.  The broccoli doesn't flavor the rice this way and it makes life so much simpler with just that one covered pot to clean.  This dish reminds me of Chinese sweet and sour and Southern barbeque all at the same time.

attributes.source_text: This dish reminds me of Chinese sweet and sour
Southern barbeque

reviews.review_text: My husband loved it this recipe.  I love reading the other reviews so that I can try them out when making a recipe.  I browned my pork in a frying pan first, along with my veggies before putting in the crock-pot.  I also added carrots and my veggies were a nice texture, not to mushy and not too crunchy, just the perfect texture for me since I had recently had gastric bypass 7 months prior so this dish was perfect over mashed potatoes and the pork was nice and tender for me to eat.  I however cooked mine on low for 7 hours, since I do crockpot cooking while I am at work, allowing my family to have a nice, hot, homecooked meal when we all get home.  This is a keeper.  I even printed the recipe for my mom so that she can make it and keep the recipe to make for future dinners.

attributes.source_text: My husband loved it this recipe
the pork was nice and tender

reviews.review_text:
This is so good! I couldn't find the thick cut chops, so I used regular boneless and the chops were done in 4 hours on low. Very tender! I removed them from the sauce, stirred in the cornstarch and water and cooked on high for 30 minutes as directed. The sauce did thicken to just the right consistency for me. I don't care for sweet and sour sauces, but thought I'd give this a try anyway. Too my pleasant surprise it wasn't too sweet at all. Perfect blend of flavors here! I served with egg noodles and brussel sprouts. Thanks for a great recipe!

Okay, I copied and pasted my initial review in the above paragraph. I've made this again and I have to change my rating to five stars (I'm pretty stingy with those...lol). This time, I served it with mashed potatoes and green beans. It was so, so good! Thanks again!

attributes.source_text: Very tender!
it wasn't too sweet at all

reviews.review_text: I modified this slightly, and used it to try to salvage severely freezer burned country style ribs. With the intent to feed it all to the chickens if need be! I had almost a crockpot full of ribs, cut in half, then added about 3/4 can of lemon-lime soda (didn't have any other)and used chicken boullion (didn't have beef). I also didn't have any ketchup left since I used it up making BBQ sauce, so I used the BBQ sauce in place of ketchup. After 8 hrs. in the crockpot I removed any bones and quite a bit of fat, the meat fell apart into chunks! I doubled the cornstarch mixture and actually thickened it on the stove. It was really quite good!

attributes.source_text: the meat fell apart into chunks

reviews.review_text: WONDERFUL; it was differant from the pork chop recipes I usually use, much better and flavorful.  Kind of reminds me of Salisbury Steak but better.  Pork was very moist and tender and the best part was how it cooks without me being there to watch it.  I really liked the idea of using the corn starch to thicken at the end & had lots of sauce left over (only did 2 chops) and froze that to use as a gravy at a later date.  The only two changes I made was pre-browning & sauting the meat & vegies as I'd seen on other post, and instead of 1 large green pepper, used 1/2 green and 1/2 sweet red pepper. Veggies & meat where perfect when done.  Served over steamed white rice with hot dinner rolls & a bottle of our favorite red wine - YUM!   Thanks for great recipe, it's a keeper and will be used again.  Next time I'll serve hot sour dough bread with it.

attributes.source_text: Pork was very moist and tender
Pork was very moist and tender

reviews.review_text: We loved this recipe.  I bought pre-prepped chopped onions & peppers, threw them in with the rest of the stuff, and this was quite possibly the easiest dinner I've ever made... and it was incredibly tasty with tender pork.  It is a definite keeper.  I think people must be looking for some kind of 5-star restaurant gourmet stuff when they rank this low.  I don't know, but the simplicity to taste ratio is unbeatable here.  :)   I didn't use the celery.  I also cooked it for 5 hours then put in the cornstarch for another 30.  My crock pot is fast, and I miscalculated dinnertime.  (I am very bad about not reading ahead... thought it was to be done in 5.5 lol)

attributes.source_text: the easiest dinner I've ever made
tender pork

reviews.review_text:
I just finished eating this meal and thought it was delicious. I do not understand the one star ratings. Based on the ingredients, I thought I knew what to expect, but it was even better. The chops were tender, the sauce delicious, the vegetables perfect, not crunchy and not mushy.
I ate it over rice with a side of peas, my personal favorite with any rice and sauce. Do to some of the ratings, I almost used only one tablespoon of brown sugar, but because I believe in making the recipe the first time as written, I used two and was glad I did. I thought it was a great balance of sweet and sour. I loved this recipe. Thank you Malriah. This is a keeper.
Think I will also try this with chicken.

attributes.source_text: The chops were tender
a great balance of sweet and sour

reviews.review_text: I don't know how this recipe is rated like it is, could it be an internet hoax?  My wife and co-workers found this recipe out here where her co-worker has had good luck.  I registered as a user to warn others about this catastrophe.  It's basically a non-BBQer's weak attempt at BBQ.  With ketchup, the cider was too much and the cornstarch was a thickening shortcut instead of reducing the sauce down.  You'd really be better off buying your favorite BBQ sauce, sautee some veggies and throw them all in crockpot together with some chops.  Don't waste your time and ingredients - I really can't comprehend the good reviews.

As last I tried this recipe. It is a great combination of ingredients.  A fantastic crockpot recipe!!!! I particularly liked the combination of the cider vinegar and the brown sugar. Although, I only used one scant tablespoon of brown sugar and this still gave the meal a delicious sweet and sour taste.  I found that the vegetables were cooked to perfection and were soft and the meat just fell off the bone.  I think that this is an economical meal as we had 3 adult serving, 3 containers of left overs for our lunches the next day and a small container of the sauce is in the freezer to pour over hot rice for maybe one or two people.   We will definitely cooking this recipe again.

attributes.source_text: gave the meal a delicious sweet and sour taste
were soft

reviews.review_text: I enjoyed this recipe, easy to put together and very tasty.  I followed just as written, except added 1 clove chopped garlic, 1 diced carrot, and added seasoning salt and pepper to veggi mixture.  I put everything together in crockpot night before and put on low when I left for work.  Checked at lunch time, 5 hrs later and was not ready.  So I left on low til after work 4.5 hrs longer and meat was falling apart tender.  I enjoyed the sauce over rice.  Very flavorful, the worcestershire give it a little kick.  I will keep and make again.  I like that I had everything on had in my pantry, but combination was different than I had done it crockpot in the past.

attributes.source_text: the worcestershire give it a little kick
meat was falling apart tender

reviews.review_text: These were soooo good!  This was my first try at crockpot cooking and it turned out great.  My DH has been haunted by bad crockpot recipes from his childhood, and now he's been converted!  I made it just as described, except for one hour, I turned it up to high, then back to low.  The cornstarch really didn't thicken the sauce that much, but it still tasted great.  It's a tad bit sweet, so next time I think I'll cut down on the ketchup and brown sugar.  For you Atkins, low-carb types: I served it over grated cauliflower (so it would look like rice) and it turned out wonderfully.  Thanks for a fabulous recipe!

attributes.source_text: My DH has been haunted by bad crockpot recipes from his childhood, and now he's been converted!

reviews.review_text:
I am with reviewer Marcia Smith on this one. It was not bad but I don't think it deserves the highest rating 
on the site. I tried it and followed the recipe faithfully and was quite disappointed. I tasted as I thought it would ...sweet and
somewhat ho-hum. The best that can be said for it is that it is easy and for those with weak teeth, the chops are tender.
I would far rather marinate a  boneless pork steak and grill it. I have given it one star and am not sure it deservs that.
I prefer to give good reviews but this recipe has been so over-rated that I felt I should help to correct the balance.

attributes.source_text: the chops are tender

reviews.review_text:
I'll have to hop on the bandwagon with this one!! This recipe is outstanding!! I doubled the recipe, as I used 8 boneless pork chops. Threw it all in the crockpot and went swimming for the day...came home to lots of yummy smells!! I only had a 28 oz. can of diced tomatoes on hand, so I used them, and I also cut the veggies into a bit bigger chunks. The pork just fell apart when you tried to take it out of the sauce. YUMMY!! We ate this over cooked egg noodles b/c my family's not wild about rice. Lots of yummy sauce to sop up with the noodles. Thank you for posting this...definitely a keeper:) 
~Manda

attributes.source_text: The pork just fell apart when you tried to take it out of the sauce

reviews.review_text: I made this last night and my family loved it! They were very impressed. They told me it's one of the best meals they've ever had, and they definitely want to have this again. I, on the other hand, did not enjoy it as much. The pork was very tender, which was good, but I thought the sauce was unpleasant. It was almost a sweet and sour sauce, only (in my opinion) not sweet enough or sour enough to actually be a sweet and sour sauce! I had trouble choking it down, and I didn't finish my serving. I'm giving this recipe 4 stars, however, because of my family's reaction. They think it's awesome. I guess it's a personal taste thing.

attributes.source_text: my family loved it
The pork was very tender

items.label: Jumbo Shrimp Parmesan
items.name: Jumbo Shrimp Parmesan
items.description: I made these for dinner tonight and they are scrumptious! Can be made ahead up to and including the breading stage and refrigerated. Then drizzle with butter and bake. Found on the Global Gourmet website.
instructions: Preheat oven to 475 degrees.
Peel and devein shrimp, leaving tails intact.
Mix together olive oil, garlic and salt and pepper in a bowl.
Add shrimp and toss lightly to coat.
Refrigerate 30 minutes to an hour.
In shallow bowl, combine bread crumbs and Parmesan cheese.
Place each shrimp in bread crumb mixture and turn them to lightly coat both sides.
Arrange shrimp so that they aren't touching each other in a ungreased 9 x 13 pan.
Drizzle with melted butter.
Place pan on the center rack of oven and bake for 10 minutes or until done.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

reviews.review_text: I prepared this for my DH as I don't eat shrimp.  I used 12 41-60 count shrimp amd marinated them in 1 Tblsp olive oil, 1/2 tsp lemon juice, 1 fresh clove minced garlic and some fresh ground black pepper for about 2-3 hours.  I used about 1/4 cup breadcrumbs (Quick bread crumbs for Casseroles recipe #57875 which I had in the freezer - great recipe!) and 1/4 cup parmesan cheese.  I baked them 10 minutes.  My DH loved them.  Said the flavor was outstanding!  They were pretty easy to prepare, especially since I did the first part of the prep earlier in the day.  Thanks for sharing your recipe Marie!

attributes.source_text: My DH loved them

reviews.review_text:
These were a hit with my two shrimp eaters. (I'm not one of them, but they smelled yummy!!!)

I used 31-40 shrimp, used garlic powder and cut the garlic in half, as my fiance' is half vampire, and only let the shrimp marinade about 45 minutes. 

I placed the shrimp on a baking pan lined with parchment paper. I baked the shrimp for 12 minutes, which, according to the fiance' was perfect. (I personally would have broiled for a bit to brown them up.) I omitted the butter as was suggested by so many reviewers, and was very glad I did. The oil in the marinade negates the need for the butter, imo.
There was way too much breading. Next time I will double the recipe, but not the breading! 
I served it with spaghetti and homemade marinara sauce and salad. 
This is a lovely and elegant meal that is surprising in its simplicity.

attributes.source_text: These were a hit with my two shrimp eaters
according to the fiance' was perfect

reviews.review_text: I was sitting on the fence between a 3 or 4 rating for this recipe and gave the recipe the benefit of the doubt in the event it was my doing that caused my shrimp to be soggy and not crispy like others commented they achieved.  I added extra garlic and used italian bread crumbs since that's all I had on hand.  I also used smaller sized shrimp since it was all I had and another reviewed said hers turned out great in a smaller size.  This was definitely tasty...but the sogginess kind of took away from it for me.  The fresh lemon at the end is a definite must and probably was the determining factor in giving this 4 stars.  I may attempt this again after reading all reviews to see what I can do differently to avoid the soggy breading.  Still a good recipe.  Thanks for posting.

Omigosh, marie, these are soooo fine!!!

I had a small problem with the cooking time, but it wasn't the fault of the recipe.  The only seriously big shrimp my market had today was the size they classify as "colossal".  (1.02 lbs., and I only got 8 shrimp.)

I allowed an extra 2 minutes for the size....but had to stick them back in the oven for almost 3 minutes more.  (Those suckers were huge!!)  Served with lots of lemon wedges, as suggested, and a very spicy cocktail sauce on the side.  

This had to be the best 10-minute meal I ever fixed!

UMMMM! These were SOOOOO GOOD!! Turned out perfect! I used 1LB of jumbo shrimp, Panko breadcrumbs, and added a few dashes of hot sauce.. but not enough because they were not spicy. Also in the marinade, I sprinkled about 1/2 tbsp dry basil. We didn't even use cocktail sauce, cause they were so good they didnt need ANYTHING. Oh, one more thing, I did as one of the reivewers said.. I put oven on BROIL, and timer for 10 minutes, and after 5 minutes, i turned the shrimp over. I will do 2lbs SHRIMP next time, because we COULD NOT GET ENOUGH! 
Thanks for sharing...

Ok, cute story time....  I have a 13 yr. old daughter, who for the most part, has an aversion to seafood. Consequently, I don't make it all that often. I made this recipe tonight, mostly because it is Good Friday, (no meat) and I thought she would not be home, as she was putting in service hours at the fish-fry at church. (for her Confirmation) Well, the way it worked out, she came home, just as I was serving dinner. I insisted that she try these little guys, because after tasting them myself, I was convinced she would love them! Well, she was reluctant to say the least, but after she ate the first one, she grabbed 4 more off my plate, and ran! I laughed SO hard! Needless to say, these were a hit! I made them exactly as directed, except I doubled the recipe, and I used PANKO bread crumbs. I believe this is the answer to the recent reviews mentioning "soggy" crust. I baked for 10 minutes, then broiled for about 3. FANTASTIC! A must, must try recipe for anyone who likes shrimp. (and clearly those who have never tried it!) Company-worthy for sure. Delectable!  Thanks  for posting this recipe!

attributes.source_text: mostly because it is Good Friday
she grabbed 4 more off my plate, and ran

reviews.review_text:
EXCELLENT!  The easiest and tastiest shrimp I've ever had that were not fried! I did marinate fresh local shrimp about 6 hours, which may have made them so very tender. 

The only problem I had was getting enough of the bread crumb mixture to stick to the shrimp. (I had almost 1/3-1/2 of crumb mixture left) I did add 1/2 teaspoon fresh ground pepper, 1/2 teaspoon Cajun seasoning, and 1/4 teaspoon seasoned salt to the (Panko) bread crumb mixture.

A delightful alternative to fried shrimp!  I will be making these again and again!  Thanks for a great recipe.

attributes.source_text: which may have made them so very tender

reviews.review_text: Yummy!  I didn't make enough!!  I only made 4 large (not jumbo) shrimp for each of us, and both of us wished we had more.  :)  I marinated my shrimp for about an hour.  Forgot to drizzle with butter for the first few minutes of cooking, freaked out because they looked really dry when I finally DID drizzle them, but they turned out delicious anyway.  :)  Skipped the lemon as I didn't have any on hand.  Served with Recipe #12365 tossed with mini pasta shells and a salad for a great meal.  Thanks so much for sharing this awesome, simple recipe!  We will be making these again for sure.

YUMMY!  These shrimp were simple and great!  The only change was to use some cajun seasoning instead of just salt and pepper.  I served them with a long grain and wild rice and a couple of vegetables, and we loved them for dinner.  I doubled the recipe since I had a 2 lb bag of frozen shrimp.  The next night I made pasta, Aglio e Olio: spaghetti with EVOO, crushed red pepper, and garlic, and added some mushrooms.  At the last minute, I threw in the leftover shrimp to warm and tossed them into the pasta.   We couldn't decide if we liked them better plain the night before, or in the pasta made with the leftovers!  GREAT RECIPE!!!

attributes.source_text: we loved them for dinner

reviews.review_text: The recipe said go light on the batter, and I totally agree.  I got a few shimp all battered up to see how they would compare, and since we drizzle butter on them, it makes them too soggy, and the cooking time increases. I noticed that cooking the shrimp long enough to get the bread crumbs really golden makes a big difference in flavor. Yumm!  Also, I used store brand shredded parmesan, and the parmesan could not be tasted.  Guess next time I gotta go for the expensive stuff! I REALLY enjoyed this recipe. I actually didn't change anything and I usually do! Thank you.

I used panko bread crumbs and parmesan that I grated in my good processor which I think detracted from how much better they would have been because the bread crumbs and the parmesan were not fine crumbs they were quite large which made sticking to the shrimp difficult. Next time I'd either process them smaller or use regular bread crumbs and grated parmesan reggiano from the store.

FANTASTIC FLAVOR! UPDATE: I just made these again tonight and used finer, homemade, bread crumbs... they worked great and I love the flavor.

These are absolutly wonderful tasting. I especially liked the coating- nice and light. I doubled the recipe and added 2 minutes to the cooking time to compensate for multiple trays at different levels in the oven. Prepared the recipe as written with the following exceptions. I used Panko breadcrumbs, 1/8 cup freshly grated parmesan cheese, and 1/8 cup freshly grated romano cheese. I did use a cooking spray on the baking pans and omitted drizzling 2 tablespoons of butter. Thanks you for the recipe I will make these again and again.

attributes.source_text: nice and light

reviews.review_text: Oh my gosh...so tasty. I did not have jumbo shrimp, so I used medium shrimp. Needless to say I am sure the bigger shrimp is easier to work with. My husband and I do not like having to pull tails off the shrimp, so I usually do that before I cook them. Other than that I followed the recipe and it was tasty. My oven made the bottoms of the shrimp a little too cooked, so I think next time I will put them on for a minute or two less. Oh, and instead of drizzling butter, I used spray butter instead. Made it very easy to cover the pan. Thanks for posting.

Made for 12 people last night using 20ct prawns.  For the breading, I used regular panko, garlic herb panko, parmesan cheese, and some potato flakes for some extra crunch.  I sprayed with a butter spray rather than drizzling with butter.  The baked up perfectly in 10 min.  I served with a few different sauces... pineapple habanero, champagne grapefruit cardamom mustard, remolaude, and cocktail sauce.  I had rave reviews from everyone!!  I will definitely make again and will also be trying this recipe with fish.

attributes.source_text: some potato flakes for some extra crunch

reviews.review_text: My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed this delicious recipe. I basically followed the recipe but I had to make a substitution and use shredded Parmesan. I made fresh bread crumbs and just threw the shredded Parmesan into the processor with the bread so it would have a texture similar to the grated. I butterflied our shrimp because they were really jumbo. Lightly battered as directed and put them on a foil lined and lightly oiled pan before drizzling with the butter. I baked them about 13-14 minutes. I will be making this one again and again!

attributes.source_text: My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed this delicious recipe

reviews.review_text: This was very good and so easy that my nine year old enjoyed helping.  Prep time is mostly the marinating time for the shrimp.  It really only took about five minutes total prep time for this dish.  I served mine with Pasta and garlic alfredo sauce and brussel sprouts.  I drizzled the butter on the shrimp with a teaspoon, but a medicine dropper would be good to use too, because they do  not need but a few drops on top of each shrimp for them to turn out nice and golden/crispy. Very good and thank you for posting.

attributes.source_text: nice and golden/crispy

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe exactly as written with one deviation; I used Panko Breadcrumbs instead of regular breadcrumbs. These were very good and I will make them again. The shrimp were very juicy and tender on the inside; crunchy and flavorful on the outside. I did find that 1TBS of butter would have been more than enough for this dish, and thus, 4 stars because the shrimp was a bit oily on the bottom side.   The next time that I make this recipe I will cut the butter by half. VERY good recipe- thank you!

Also, to get these crispy may I suggest broiling them on LOW for approximately 10 minutes and make sure you flip them at least once.  The breading on ours turned out nice and crunchy, so if you are looking for a crispy version of this recipe, try the broiler.  Thanks Marie for a great recipe and these would also work great as an appetizer!

Company was coming over and I found out *very* last minute that one guest has not been able to eat crab so I had to switch to something  from shrimp stuffed with crab meat. I paired these with a spinach salad and garlic bread.  Wonderful!

items.label: Creamy Potato Salad
items.name: Creamy Potato Salad
items.description: Have you ever posted a recipe and just love reading the reviews for it?  This is my signature potato salad.  Whenever there is a pot luck function at work, I am TOLD that I have to bring the potato salad.  No one else is allowed to and I am never given a choice.  Thank you everyone who ever tried this potato salad and for leaving such glowing reviews for it.  You all have made me look so good.  I personally can not stand eggs or raw onions, so I leave them out but I know most people don't think a potato salad is complete without them.  Thanks again for so many wonderful reviews. (psssst....check out my recipe #123107 as well.  It shares the dressing with this recipe but tastes much much different because of the different ingredients) Please see Recipe #242966 for bacon bit tips.
instructions: Cook potatoes in boiling, salted water until tender.
Drain well.
Peel and cube potatoes.
Transfer to a large bowl.
Add celery, onion, sweet relish and bacon bits.
Combine mayo, sugar, celery seed, vinegar, mustard, and salt.
Add mayo mixture to potatoes.
Toss lightly to coat potato mixture.
Carefully fold in the chopped eggs.
Cover and chill thoroughly.

Bacon bit tip:  Partially freeze your package of bacon.  Use a sharp knife and cut the frozen bacon into long strips about 1/4 inch wide.  Turn the bacon and cut the strips into pieces also about 1/4 in wide.  You now have perfect raw bacon pieces to fast fry.  No need to separate.  They will separate during cooking.  Perfect bacon bits.

reviews.review_text: Absolutely love this recipe! When I made it the first time I didn’t have any relish so I used some Bread and butter pickles that I had left in the jar. This time when I made it I run out of that so I use dill pickles chopped up and both times it’s absolutely delicious. The first time I used turkey bacon, Made nice and crisp. The second time I used maple bacon which I chopped up while it was still frozen and fried it like that. Came out beautifully. I also added three eggs instead of two. And I didn’t have any celery seed so I used 2 teaspoons of celery salt instead and left out the salt. I added a touch of Cayenne pepper, caraway seed, oregano, and thyme. It was a hit with my whole family. So I just made it again and I can hardly wait to eat it!

attributes.source_text: It was a hit with my whole family

reviews.review_text: OML - Who in their right mind would NOT give  this 5 stars?? I actually didn't have all the ingredients on hand, so... instead of bacon used garlic sausage, instead of celery - used red capsicum!  I also used 3 eggs instead of 2 and didn't add the salt or celery!... I have 9 mammoth potatoes so used 2 cups mayonaise and 3 teaspoons mustard. Whilst I found 1/3 cup sweet relish, think I will need to exhaust that of making my own sweet relish as this is unequivocally my 'go to' potato salad... thanks so much for sharing this recipe. I will be making this for a group of 12 and I think hands down this will be a recipe I will be sharing.

attributes.source_text: potato salad

reviews.review_text:
Fantastic potato salad! I brought this to a picnic and was nervous as it was the first potato salad I had made. Everyone loved it and the entire batch (2.6 pounds of potatoes!) was eaten up by 10 not super hungry people. Success!!

Here are the changes I made:
1) I used 2.6 pounds of baby potatoes. I believe they were the waxy Yukon Golds
2) Didn't have bacon and therefore used 160g of pancetta. As it was not extremely fatty, I fried the pancetta and tossed the boiled and cut potatoes into the fat. Perhaps this gave it that incredible flavor
3) Didn't have sweet pickle relish and therefore chopped up 1/3 cup pickle gherkins and several teaspoon full of capers and added a large tablespoon of honey
4) Used white vinegar in place of apple cider as I didn't have any on hand
5) Omitted the eggs because I forgot to buy them

I didn't make extra dressing even though I had an extra .6 pound of potatoes and it still came out fantastic. It tasted okay right after I made it but it tasted amazing several hours later when the flavours matured. Served it the next day and it was still incredible. Worth trying this recipe!

attributes.source_text: I brought this to a picnic

reviews.review_text: YUM!! This was hands down the best potato salad we've ever had (and believe me, we've made and/or purchased many various kinds in the past!). What really threw me was what simple ingredients were involved. My husband and I lean towards more exotic ingredients and are spice-aholics, and at first glance I really thought this potato salad would be just ho-hum, but WOW were we pleasantly suprised! My husband now says that we will never "buy" potato salad again -- he only wants this one, and I agree. The only change I'll make next time is to cut down a bit on the salt amount. 1.5 tsp was a bit too salty for me, but perhaps that's because I highly salted the water I boiled the potatoes in? Next time, I'll use 1/2 the amount of salt and see how that works. THANKS for sharing such a spectacular recipe!!!

attributes.source_text: My husband now says that we will never "buy" potato salad again -- he only wants this one

reviews.review_text: I took this to a 4th of July (well, 3rd of July) event. Potato salad is about the only thing I make without measuring, by taste, the way my mother and grandmother made theirs. After seeing all the great reviews I decided to try some of the ingredients in this recipe. I never thought to add bacon to potato salad. It adds great flavor. I used about 10 small-medium potatoes, 12 oz. of bacon, a whole onion, and kind of guessed on the celery... maybe 3-4 stalks. I subbed dill pickles for the relish and kind of guessed on that amount as well. I love hard-boiled eggs in my p. salad so I probably used close to a dozen. I stuck with the mayo and other ingredient measurements although left out the celery seeds b/c I didn't have any. I threw in some pepper and paprika as well. A friend attending the event said it was the best potato salad she's ever had. Everyone really enjoyed it and gave it great compliments. I think I may have just changed our family potato salad "recipe". Thanks!

attributes.source_text: I took this to a 4th of July (well, 3rd of July) event
A friend attending the event said it was the best potato salad she's ever had

reviews.review_text: I love potato salad and this one was great -- simple enough to go with almost anything but fancy enough to take to a party. I used whole-grain mustard and skipped the eggs but otherwise followed the directions. I only needed about 1 cup mayonnaise and it was plenty creamy enough for me. If you wanted to make this lower-fat, I'm sure you could sub in a little bit of yogurt for the mayo, maybe 1/4 cup. I wasn't sure what kind of relish to use and know the kinds we get in the UK are different to the U.S. so I used a sweet onion relish made by Branstons. I think it's this that gives the salad its "special touch". Even my husband, who normally only likes potato salad done the way his mom did it, had a bowl and enjoyed it.

attributes.source_text: it was plenty creamy enough for me
fancy enough to take to a party

reviews.review_text: What a wonderful and flexible recipe.  I made so many modifications that I'm reluctant to leave a star rating -- I used this recipe as inspiration rather than instructions!  I omitted the celery, halved the celery seeds, omitted the eggs, subbed onion powder instead of chopped onion, tripled the sugar and mustard, and added a bit of garlic, a teaspoon of no-salt seasoning, a half teaspoon of cayenne pepper, and a half teaspoon of regular black pepper.  Still tasted great, though a bit too mustardy and sweet (I wasn't reading the amounts and put in quite a bit too much)!  Served with BBQ Pork Steak and went over great.  Thanks, Karen!  I'll try this again sometime -- PROPERLY -- and give a star rating.

Another happy reviewer, Karen!!  :)  I made this the night before and kept sneaking back to the kitchen for "test bites" while it was still warm!!  It was great cold, too!  I discovered after starting the recipe that I was low on mayo, so I ended up substituting ranch dressing for about 1/2 cup of the mayo, and while it may have changed the taste slightly, it was a decent sub.  I also didn't have celery, but think it would add a perfect crunch & will definitely make sure I use it next time.  Wonderful combination of flavors, Karen - thanks!!  I took it to my parents' house for the 4th of July and realized when I got home that my mom had NOT packed up the leftovers to send home with us...they loved it, too!!  :)

reviews.review_text: I don't like potato salad.  That said, I got thinking, maybe it is because I never had good potato salad.  A quick search and I found this 5 star recipe.  I figured I would like potato salad if  I found a good recipe and made for it myself.    I made exactly as written.  Excellent potato salad.  This has a nice depth of flavor.  Many people who make potato salad mix a bit of mayo with some potatoes and a couple other things and think that is all that is needed (i.e. my sister- yuck- you really are not the great cook you think you are).  This is great.  Better than I expected- and I expected a lot given the 5 star review out of 200+ reviewers.

attributes.source_text: This has a nice depth of flavor

reviews.review_text: This is a great recipe Karen! I did change it up a little bit.. and even with using what I had on hand the potato salad didn't suffer.. I didn't have any red onion and didn't want the harshness of the yellow I had so I steamed some shallots and let them cool off and tossed them in.  I used my homemade mayo and mustard as well as my own put up relish. I used regular vinegar, was had on hand and cut down on the pepper, personal family preference. I did add two more eggs after reading Rayna's addition. I used young celery from my garden as well. This was a show stopped at today's cookout. People loved it.. thanks again for posting a great recipe...

attributes.source_text: This was a show stopped at today's cookout

reviews.review_text: I personally hate potato salad, I've never liked and never will.  That being said, everyone in my family loves it, so I usually have to suffer through making it anyway with the same old, bland recipe everyone uses.  This is actually the first recipe I've tried from the site, and I was nervous because I couldn't taste it and test whether or not it was descent.  Anyway I made it, set it out at lunch, and the response was overwhelming!  My mother (who considers herself a potato salad aficianado) said it was the best she'd ever eaten!  Everytime my grandmother would take a bite, she'd make this "mmm" sound.  This was a home run recipe and I'll definately be making it again!  Thanks for the great recipe!

reviews.review_text: Absolutely 5 stars wonderful!  I omit the celery seed (personal preference), and often use sweet pickle juice instead of the cider vinegar, but otherwise follow the ingredient list.  I like to add the dressing to the still warm potato cubes because I think that they absorb more flavour that way.  Also, for any doubters (such as myself the first time making this) the salt amount is spot on...I feared that the dressing was too salty on its own, but potatoes apparently need that quantity, and after it has all melded together it is perfect.  Honourable mention goes to the method of preparing the bacon bits...great idea!

I never liked potato salad...until NOW!!!  Everytime in the past when I had potato salad, it was either too crunchy or too mushy...too dry or way too mayonaisey... I guess my picky palette was trying to tell me I needed to make some homemade!  I scaled this down to 3-4 servings for the two us to have with some hamburgers on the grill. I did not boil the potatoes, but instead used some leftover baked potatoes I had in the fridge.  I just peeled and cubed them.  I'm not too fond of raw onions either, so I just put in the tiniest bit, very finely chopped.  I liked the color they gave to the salad.  I used a half and half mix of mayo and miracle whip dressing and did add in the egg. I really liked this salad.  It was a great refreshing compliment to our grilled hamburgers.  Thanks for a potato salad I will be making from now on!

attributes.source_text: a great refreshing compliment

reviews.review_text: Yum, YUM!  Thanks Karen!  I just put this together and it was awesome AND I'll bet it will be even better onoce it sits in the fridge and gets cold and the flavors blend some.  I'm one of those that needs the onion and eggs in my potato salad -- so I added them.  But I don't think I added as much onion as you had indicated.  I like a "hint" of onion -- nothing that would overwhelm all the other wonderful flavors in the salad.  I have your Macaroni Salad marked as well and will be trying it soon (123107).  I'm going through my recipe files now and deleting all references to other potato salads!!!!  Thanks, Bobbie

attributes.source_text: I like a "hint" of onion

reviews.review_text: Karen, this was a good potato salad, but somehow it still needed more flavor. I did notice that the salad kept well in the fridge for 3 days (meaning it didn't get watery or runny like most potato salads do). The bacon was a nice touch, but I did make a few changes though. I only used 1/2 c. sliced celery, 1/4 c. chopped red onions, 1/4 c. relish, 1 tsp. celery seed, and 1/4 tsp. salt. I noticed my prep time was exactly 1 hour, not 45 minutes. Karen, I'm sorry I wasn't able to give this recipe more than 3 stars, (I hope you won't hold that against me) but I am pleased to see others here enjoyed your salad. Thanks for the recipe Karen!!

reviews.review_text: Well Karen, you have another 5 stars for your yummy potato salad. Made it for a summer party and it was a hit. One woman said it was the best she ever had. It was delicious!<br/>I used everything in the recipe but used about 1/8 cup of real bacon bits because I didn't have bacon strips and I did cut back a bit on the onion and celery. Left everything else the same. <br/>I mixed 1/2 of the dressing in the night before and added the rest in the morning. Topped with a little paprika to make it look pretty. Sooo good! Thank you

reviews.review_text: Really good!  I don't normally like a "sweet" potato salad as that's not what I had growing up, but since I liked the Creamy Macaroni Salad so much I decided to try this too.  Very good.  I scaled it down for about 3 servings just based on the potatoes I had leftover and did everything per recipe except for the eggs and bacon, simply because I didn't have them.  I will definitely review again when I make it as written because I'm sure they both contribute alot.  I did add fresh parsley and fresh ground black pepper.  Thank you!

Awesome flavor - the whole family loved it! I doubled the recipe using 5 lbs. of potatoes.  Boiled them whole, skin on, then cooled them on counter...then put them in fridge overnight.  The next morning, I peeled and cubed and added the doubled ingredients. (Cutting them into cubes when they are cold helps them keep their shape, not getting so mushy) After tasting, I added 1 more tsp. of mustard, because of our taste. 
I also diced the onions and the celery very fine - again for our taste.
The family loved it! Thanks for the great recipe!
