items.label: Macaroni Salad
items.name: Macaroni Salad
items.description: I was hesitant about posting this recipe - it's the macaroni salad I grew up with, and pretty basic. But it is so darned good that I decided to go ahead.
instructions: Combine dressing ingredients.
Stir into remaining ingredients.
Cover and chill.

reviews.review_text: I want to thank the other reviewers who cautioned that the flavor might be 'too much' if you follow the recipe as-is and instead should consider cutting down on the vinegar and mustard. I actually did half vinegar, half mustard, and half sugar and the flavor is good that way! I also added shredded carrots for extra color/flavor. For anyone wondering if you can make this in advance versus day-of, I suggest you try what I did because it worked well. I made the macaroni noodles and cut up all the veggies and put that in a bowl, and then I mixed up the dressing in a separate bowl, and then refrigerated both bowls separately over night to chill. In the morning I mixed them together and let them chill together for an hour or two before the event. It was a lot less hassle on the day-of but still tasted freshly made!

Totally refreshing and even better left over. Thanks for sharing! Update: Just made for the third time. Perfect as is but started adding fresh dill and it is amazing. Note: I have found that I get the best texture by mixing the wet ingredients with the seasonings and then stirring in the macaroni. As it sits I finely dice the veggies then stir them in. I have added the veggies before the macaroni, and it comes out fine. But adding the pasta in first, it coats with the mayo base much better and turns out creamier. <br/><br/>I am once again making this salad. It has become my go to recipe. I have always doubled the recipe since day one. At first because we were having people over for a bbq, but now I only double it because we just love this left over. Mmmmmmm, mmmmmmm.

attributes.source_text: Totally refreshing
turns out creamier
we were having people over for a bbq

reviews.review_text: This is a terrific Macaroni Salad.  Very similar to what I grew up on.  I was worried after my first couple taste-tests that it might be too "mustardy" but after chilling in the fridge for several hours it all came together.  I only made three small changes.  I didn't have any green pepper but had just bought a bag of small multi-colored peppers so I used one small red and one small yellow.  Together they came to a perfect 1/2 cup.  I left out the other half cup of peppers.  The last change was to add about a Tablespoon of Green Olive brine because I just couldn't resist.  The only thing I will do next time is to actually add some diced Green Olives to complete the flavor I enjoy and maybe add a bit more pepper.   Really enjoyed this one tonight.  Thanks for sharing.

I made one with the vinegar as directed in the instructions. I made another substitution of pickle juice as suggested in some of the reviews. I actually prefer the vinegar. It has more of a kick to it than the pickle juice which is just sour. Also, I ended up adding about 1/2 tsp of sugar more and more black pepper. I used the cracked black pepper which gives it more of an aroma. I have never used mustard before so when I went to the store I was contemplating on whether I should buy expensive or cheap mustard. I ended up buying the cheap little bottle which tasted fine when everything was mixed. It was not an overpowering flavor. I would also mix the sauce into a large bowl since the pasta will take up alot of room. I had to transfer my sauce into a large bowl after failed attempts into the small and medium bowl. After mixing I realized it wasn't as creamy as I'd like for it to be so I made more and now it's perfect. I can't wait to taste it tomorrow when it's actually been chilled! I'm really glad I picked out this recipe. Today was a test run. I'm definitely going to be make this for family gatherings.

attributes.source_text: It has more of a kick to it
gives it more of an aroma
It was not an overpowering flavor
now it's perfect

reviews.review_text: This recipe is spot on. I always had  trouble getting the amount of  each ingredient right, and my salads always seemed to be not just right to me.  This recipe was more than perfect.  I followed it exactly using rice vinegar. I just added a couple Tbs. of chopped pimento because I had it to use up.<br/>It is such a colorful salad too.  I am so glad I tried it, and am looking forward to making it many more times for home and for when I need to take a covered dish to pot-luck dinners.<br/>Thanks so much for posting it. Now if I can find the perfect potato salad just as good I'd be happy!

Simple and basic, yes, but simply and basically delicious too.  I followed it to the letter (NOT).  I used 12 oz of 3-color farfalle, since that was on hand, and tossed in a little extra of the chopped peppers (red and yellow.  I also did not toss in all the dressing, since it would have been a bit too much for my taste.  I also added an extra tsp or so of sugar, since I really like sweet salads.  I consider those minor substitutions to be following it very well, do I recommend that better behaved cooks do their best to take evelyn's directions to heart.  Thanks again for another wonderful recipe, Evelyn!

Seriously this is the recipe I have been looking for! Made this morning for Father's Day BBQ and frankly ate some for breakfast. I cooked a pound of ditalini pasta (very small salad type macaroni) and the drained rinsed and laid it out on paper towels in a sheet pan to dry off a bit while I mixed dressing. I then used 1/2 of the pasta with the dressing but added more pasta to the mix. I don't like my salad very "saucy" so just added more cooked macaroni until I got the consistency I liked. I had a tiny bit of chopped red onion that had been soaked that was left from another recipe so I dropped that in - less than a tablespoon. I added more red pepper than green because we are not fans of green but other than that no substitutes this round. None were needed! Next time I might pop in a small can of sliced olives as we like that in our region with Santa Maria Style BBQ. The mom of my childhood best friend used to make a macaroni salad that I craved and his is as close to that recipe as I have ever found so thanks for that. Definitely going to bring this to Fourth of July party so I can watch everyone swoon ????????

attributes.source_text: Made this morning for Father's Day BBQ
Made this morning for Father's Day BBQ
frankly ate some for breakfast

reviews.review_text: I forgot about this recipe! I made this a few times years ago, and was only reminded when a friend asked me for this recipe today. I have saved this recipe, and I'm making sure I give it the rating it deserves. I love this recipe because it's not rich like most macaroni salad recipes are. I add shredded cheddar cheese and hard boiled eggs, but it's good without as well. Again, you know it's a good dish when friends continue to ask you for the recipe years after you've made it.

I gave this a 5 stars because it has all the ingredients for a basic recipe. Personally, the dressing wasn't to my liking...way too strong and salty. Adjusted by cutting vinegar and mustard in half and added a pinch or two more sugar. I also added two chopped hard boiled eggs. After sitting up in fridge it dried up a bit so I added a little more mayo, vinegar and sugar. My family likes more pepper than I, so they seasoned to taste. great basic recipe that can be modified according to your liking.

I looked at a lot of macaroni salad recipes, and many had so many ingredients, I thought the fundamental flavor of macaroni salad would be overpowered - (one had hard-boiled eggs.....I'm sorry, I like a good hard-boiled egg as much as the next guy, but in macaroni salad?????????). Then I saw this recipe.  Wow, is it good!  Served it tonight for dinner as a side to BLTs.  Funny to see Julie 80113's potluck comment.  I said the very same thing to my husband tonight...."I'm making this for the next neighborhood potluck.  This recipe is wonderful.  Thank you for sharing. P.S. Can't wait to have it tomorrow, the 2nd day.  I hear it gets better!

attributes.source_text: Served it tonight for dinner
as a side to BLTs

reviews.review_text: This is my favorite favorite macaroni salad. Everybody wants me to make this when we have a family gathering. My husband is allergic to onion and my brother is allergic to green pepper so I took those out and added yellow and orange peppers with the red. I like a lot of veggies and less macaroni so I also add small diced carrots, small cubes of cheese, hard boiled eggs and diced chicken tenders. I made it once and then doubled the recipe because there wasn't any left over because people just kept eating it until it was gone. It doesn't matter what you put in this, it's delicious. The dressing is outstanding. I usually make more of the dressing and then add more the next day and it's just as good as it was when I first made it. I can eat this for days, and never get sick of it.

attributes.source_text: when we have a family gathering

reviews.review_text: Great.as written. However, When I double it, which is almost always, I do not fully double the salt. I add more to the dressing only if it needs it. Sometimes it does, but mostly it is just right. going a tad scant on the double batch.My last batch of celery was salty...Hmmm I know celery is higher in sodium, But I never had celery that actually tasted really salty.... strange . One tip I saw on line is to mix the sugar and vinegar first, Then add into mayo. It seems to blend better. I made it mostly as directed...and actually measured..(rare for me) 1 medium to med/lg bell pepper is appx 3/4C. I did use the whole thing. Like another reviewer, I add in tomatoes( a handful of grape tomatoes, cut in half, or more. ) Plus diced carrot.and about a half of a cucumber ir so to a doubke batch. My mom likes to add in celery seed ...Whole, not ground, about 1. to 2 t or so( for a double batch) So i do add that into both my macaroni and potato salads. Definateky a keeper. Glad you decided to post it. The dressing is perfect. This us what i grew up on too. My hubby likes hard boiled egg in his. So I always cooked and sliced some hard boiled eggs ,Then arraged them in a circle aroud the outside edge. It looks nice and gives him and others a choice. . I personally avoid them . UPDATE: Barilla Protein Plus is a GREAT choice for the noodles. Definately worth the extra price..makes carb eating so much better balanced and more diabetuc friendly.

attributes.source_text: My hubby likes hard boiled egg in his

reviews.review_text: I've made this so many times--it's one of my favorites!  Normally, I make this with Hellman's mayo with olive oil.  For the green onion, I just add some chopped up Vidalia onion (yummy).  I usually leave out the celery (personal preference), but try to add lots of bell peppers (fresh is best but frozen, if drained fully of water, is good too).  The last time I made it, I put in some chopped up hard-boiled egg (leftover from Easter), and yep, still oh-so-delicious!  Thanks, Evelyn!

This is my first review!!  I was looking for a basic macaroni salad recipe, so I could add my own touches.  Oh my gosh it's exactly what I was looking for.  I  used what I had on hand, apple cider vinegar instead of vinegar.  Used only red pepper, and finely chopped red onion instead of green onion.  Because my kids like it, I added shredded cheese.  Dressing is just right flavor wise, and not so much it's swimming in dressing.  Rave reviews from the family!!!

attributes.source_text: Because my kids like it
Rave reviews from the family

reviews.review_text: LOVE IT. My picky kids LOVE this. My 9 year old made another batch herself because she liked it so much and we had enough ingredients left from the first one. I agree with other posters- it is better the second day. I made it just like the recipe says, except that I used Vegan mayo for mine because I am allergic to dairy and eggs. My kids ate the real kind and mine and could not tell the difference in taste. I am picky about my salads but this lived up to its reviews!

attributes.source_text: My picky kids LOVE this
My kids ate the real kind and mine and could not tell the difference in taste

reviews.review_text: This one's a definite keeper in my house.  It may be a basic salad, but that's what made it easy to put together this afternoon for an impromptu picnic with our grandchildren -- all of the ingredients were right there in my kitchen!  When I first tasted it I thought the vinegar had made it a little tart for my taste, but by the time everything else was ready and we got to our picnic spot the flavors had blended and mellowed and it was delicious!

attributes.source_text: an impromptu picnic with our grandchildren
for an impromptu picnic
the flavors had blended and mellowed

reviews.review_text: I always think it's the add-ins/changes the flavor to not have a flat taste. I really don't like macaroni salad when it doesn't have flavor. What about using grilled or roasted red/green/yellow/orange peppers/onions. I have some and will test with your recipe. I just had the most delicious macaroni salad and I know there was a distinct flavor I could not identify. I didn't have time to check with the Kitchen but I will when I'm there on my next visit.

I made this with a few differences..they are - no green peppers (didn't have any), maybe a 1/4 cup of frozen red peppers sliced up (thawed out), and since I didn't have green onion I used maybe a 1/4 cup of white onion finally minced. I was worried that the mustard flavor would be overpowering, but it wasn't. I actually really enjoyed it. UPDATE: I tried it the following day, I needed to add more Mayo...but I didn't care much for the flavor. Weird.

attributes.source_text: I was worried that the mustard flavor would be overpowering, but it wasn't

reviews.review_text: I was craving a macaroni salad that was like my mom makes for pot lucks, well, I was hesitant about finding one on here that tasted as good.  Sure enough, this was it!  I was so happy to find this recipe and will make it often.  The first bite told me this is a keeper!  I didn't have any green peppers but I did put in the red peppers.  No green onions but put in white onions.  Everything else was as the recipe said.  Awesome and thank you so much!

If you are looking for a basic Macaroni Salad recipe than this is a good one.  I really liked this one,  DD and DH only rated this a 3 however.  DD would've liked it if it was only the dressing and pasta, not a fan of peppers, onions or celery (kids!!)  DH would have added bacon, eggs, olives, cheese etc.  It's hard to please everyone in our house.  Myself.... I liked this one alot.  I had seconds and will be picking at the leftovers everytime I peek in the fridge.

items.label: Pork Tenderloin
items.name: Pork Tenderloin
keywords: c("Meat", "Very Low Carbs", "High Protein", "Free Of...", "High In...", "Oven")
items.description: Make and share this Pork Tenderloin recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Mix garlic, salt, pepper & thyme in small bowl.
Rub mixture over tenderloin and wrap in plastic.   Refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat olive oil over med. high heat. and brown pork on all sides, approximately 7 minute total.
Remove pork and place in a 9x13x2 pan.
Add enough water to come up to bottom edge of pork (about a half inch). I rinse my frying pan and scrape blackened bits for water.
Cover with foil and bake at 350 for approximately 45 to 50 minutes.
Boil the drippings and add a little cornstarch mixed with water to it for gravy. Season with salt & pepper. Good with mashed potatoes.

reviews.review_text: This recipe was very good.  I did not weigh the meat so I don't know but it was two pieces of pork tenderloin.  I used extra garlic and marinated for actually over 24 hours. I brushed off the majority of the garlic before browning to prevent burning of the garlic.  I browned the meat in a cast iron skillet and didn't remove. I added chicken broth to the skillet then covered in foil and baked for the recommended time and made the gravy with the cornstarch/water.  Oh wow the gravy was so good and I highly recommend using chicken broth and I didn't need to add any salt or pepper to the gravy since the meat had been marinating for over 24 hours - adding extra would have made it too salty and that's saying a lot for a salt addict!!! I made it with roasted brussel sprouts and noodles, but would have made potatoes, just ran out last night making prime rib lol!!!  I will make this again for sure.

attributes.source_text: I used extra garlic

reviews.review_text: I made this for dinner today and we all loved it.  I ended up leaving the pork in the rub for about a day and a half.  I did use garlic powder instead of fresh because I was worried it would burn during the searing process.  I used poultry seasoning instead of thyme because I was out.  My package of pork tenderloin had 2 tenderloins in it, and weighed 2.63 lbs, so I doubled the rub.  I put them in a 9X13 pan after searing and they were done in 35 minutes.  They probably could have come out 5-7 minutes earlier.  Next time I think I might add a little lemon pepper to the rub.  When making the gravy I added about a ts of chicken base because it was a little bland.  The pork was so tender and flavorful that it really didn't need the gravy.   I will definitely make this again.  Thanks for posting.

attributes.source_text: I made this for dinner today
The pork was so tender

reviews.review_text: OK. This recipe is awesome, easy, quick and adaptable, how much more can you ask for?!  I browned the meat in my large fry pan and since my pans can go into the oven at 350 degrees all I did was cover the fry pan with foil after adding the water. Voila less dishes! My  tenderloin, when I unwrapped it from the original wrapper, was in two pieces, so I put some of the seasoning between the two pieces and tied them together then sealed in the plastic wrap.  Loved the garlic/spices in the center. So next time I might just cut a tenderloin in half and do it the same way.  Try this recipe it's a great "basic" thats dress-up-able for company and yet also easy to throw together with microwave baked potatoes and veggie.  Thank You for posting!

attributes.source_text: Loved the garlic/spices in the center
Loved the garlic/spices in the center

reviews.review_text: This was excellent. I used a 2-2.5# tenderloin. Used 2 garlic cloves, 1 1/2 tsp. sea salt, 1/2 tsp. pepper, fresh rosemary and thyme, then mixed with olive oil to make a paste.  Then rubbed over roast.Omitted browning.  Left in fridge for a few hours then baked for 1 hr and 15 min. I did turn the temp. up to 375 deg. to brown for 10 min.  Did use the water in the pan.  Was very moist and a wonderful flavor.  Then on 4/19/03, I used the same idea minus the thyme, added extra fresh rosemary and put under the skin of a whole chicken, about 5#.  Left in fridge for a few hours then baked at 375 deg. for about 2 hrs.  It could of come out an 1/2 hr earlier, I think.  Was very moist and again, great flavor.  Thanks for sharing this recipe.  Definitely a keeper.

attributes.source_text: Was very moist
Was very moist

reviews.review_text: I was looking for an easy recipe for pork tenderloin that I could serve with the kielbasa and sauerkraut that I cook in my crock pot. I didn't want any unusual ingredients, just a basic roast. This fit the bill perfectly! Used garlic powder, pepper, salt, and onion powder for the marinade. Left out the thyme as it is not one of our favorite spices. Marinated about half an hour, but next time I intend to marinate longer. I didn't brown first as I was runnning late--- just removed cover 10 min. before done; however, I think it would be better to brown the roast before putting it into the oven. Served this topped with sauerkraut and some kielbasa on the side. Delicious!

This is really good!  I have tried so many recipes from this site for pork tenderloin, and they usually don't measure up to the ratings for me.  This one was so simple, I did not expect much, but it'll be my "go to" recipe from now on.  I let mine marinade for about 5 hrs. before cooking and the flavor was terrific and the meat was very tender.  It only took about 28 minutes to cook and I let it rest for 10 minutes while I made a salad.  The only other thing that I did differently, was to use a tenderizer tool that pokes holes in it that I use when I marinade meat.  Thanks Jjortkka!

attributes.source_text: the meat was very tender

reviews.review_text:
Excellent simple blend of flavors.  I did, however, have to make some adjustments . You see I thought I was defrosting a pork tenderloin but it was reall pork snitzel pieces. So I seasoned them according to your recipe, rolled them, wrapped them in plastic wrap and left them in the fridge for 8 hrs. Then I browned them on both sides, rolled them, held by a tooth pick added 4 sliced mushrooms to the pan and 1/4 cup vermouth
Covered the pan turned the heat to low for 20 minutes and they were delicious. Thanks 12 March 10
Made again with tenderloin - followed the recipe, doubled the garlic, wrapped in the fridge for 11 hours. Tender delicious easy recipe

attributes.source_text: Tender delicious easy recipe

reviews.review_text: I followed the recipe as stated, except I marinated it for about 7 hours.  I browned it just slightly in a cast iron skillet, until the garlic began to really brown up. I would have liked more color on the roast, but worried the garlic would turn bitter.  Then I just covered the skillet in foil and popped it in the oven for about 45 minutes.  I brought the roast out and continued to have it covered for several minutes.  I moved it to a serving platter and made the sauce.  My family was very pleased and considered this a definite do again meal!

attributes.source_text: My family was very pleased

reviews.review_text:
I made this tonight and it was wonderful.  I didn't have any thyme, but did add some onions to the pan as it cooked in the oven.  I also added 1 tbsp of Better Than Boullion Beef flavor (didn't have pork flavor) when I added water to the pan to get the good bits off the bottom after browning the meat.  Very easy to make.

I served it with glazed carrots and mashed potatos (with added scallions and fresh parsley).  Yum!  My family loved it.  Thanks for the recipe!  This site has quickly become my favorite site for finding recipes!

attributes.source_text: My family loved it

reviews.review_text:
This was amazing!! Ours marinaded the recommended 5 hours. We used a 4lb loin, so we had to adjust everything up some. And we doubled the garlic, because we love it so much. We didn't really have a skillet big enough to brown it in, so I did the best I could with what I had. But, I think that if it was browned better it would have been amazing!

The one thing I may change for next time is maybe use a smidge less thyme. It seemed a little thyme heavy to me, but just a touch.

Thanks for posting! We'll definitely be using this again!

I made this for dinner the other night and it was wonderful! I let it marinade for the full 24 hours. I did a few things differently; used black pepper instead of white because I didn't have any, baked for 35 minutes and let it stand for 10 minutes covered with foil and put the tenderloin on a rack in the pan. I wouldn't change a thing. Even my son, who doesn't usually like pork ate it in record time and didn't complain! This is the only way I'll make pork tenderloin from now on. Thanks for posting!

reviews.review_text: This was my first time making pork tenderloin, and it turned out very well!! I did not marinate it (Oops! I forgot!), but it still turned out great. I cooked the pork as the directions state, but made my own sauce. I deglazed the pan that I browned the pork in with about 2 tablespoons of brandy, then I added some of the drippings from the pan the pork cooked in, some heavy cream, apple cider, and a little mustard. It was very good! Served with polenta and roasted green beans. Delicious! Thank you!

The first time I made this, I used the seasonings from this recipe and cooked the pork on the grill.  I was pleasantly surprised at how good it was, having tried many different (and more exotic) pork tenderloin recipes.  We made it again last night, cooking it as the recipe directed.  Next time I'll cook it on the grill again as the flavors seemed more complex and I wasn't crazy about the 'boiled/steamed' texture of the meat from baking it in a covered pan with water.  I love the simplicity of the seasoning, although I added a little cayenne or chipotle pepper for complexity and heat.

attributes.source_text: the flavors seemed more complex

reviews.review_text: I'm not much of a Thanksgiving turkey eater, so this was our Thanksgiving meal!  Everyone enjoyed it very much and were very impressed!  I bought a 2 pound Tenderloin, so i put it in for about 5 minutes longer than said.. there was no need for that, and next time I'll check on it earlier than I did this time because I'm sure it could have been more moist than it was.  But in the end, the only one that really criticized it was me!  It was indeed a successful substitute and I will make it again!

attributes.source_text: this was our Thanksgiving meal

reviews.review_text: I like pork tenderloin a lot and am always looking for a great way to make it. I've made this a few times now and each time it's great - very tender and moist. My DH and DS (2 years old) like it too - DS always eats two helpings of it! I never remember to marinade it so I always just rub the marinade on it right before I sear it. Works great! I used chicken broth tonight in place of the water and I think it gave it a pretty good flavor. I also had a tenderloin that was 1.75 lbs and baked it for 45 minutes and then let it rest for about 15 minutes. Turned out perfectly cooked. I only gave it 4 stars becasue the gravy is rather bland to me. I served with rice and asparagus and crescent rolls. Thanks for a great recipe.

reviews.review_text: I'm making this for the third time now. I love this simple recipe! Thank you for posting it. 4-6 hrs. "marinating" time works for flavor and I preferred it as a dry rub to the time I accidently made it a marinade with the oil (but you really can't go wrong.) I used the suggestion of baking for 35 minutes but leaving the foil on for 10 minutes and this was perfect for my oven. I love the flavor (I use fresh thyme and extra garlic) Great sandwich material too with a crusty sourdough bread and good mustard. Yummy!

items.label: Slow-Cooker Beef Short Ribs
items.name: Slow-Cooker Beef Short Ribs
items.description: You won't believe how good these ribs are!!! I think we could have these every other night with no complaints! They're YUMMY!!!!
instructions: Put flour, salt and pepper in a bag.
Add ribs and shake to coat.
Brown ribs in butter in a lg skillet.
Put in slow cooker.
In same skillet, combine remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil, stirring.
Pour over ribs.
Cover and cook on low for 9 hours.

reviews.review_text:
I found this recipe after making an impulse buy of bone-in short ribs late this afternoon. Being new here, I decided to try a recipe rather than use one of my own. This recipe looked interesting, but there was not enough time to cook them in a slow-cooker so I made them in the oven: 350 degrees for 1 1/2 hours.

I made a few modifications to the recipe (besides using the oven and bone-in short ribs) which I shall definitely do again. First, I do not have a sweet tooth, so I drastically cut the amount of brown sugar. I decided to gradually add brown sugar to the rest of the mixture so I started with just under 1/4 cup brown sugar (packed a 1/4 cup measure to about 1/3" from the top). I liked the taste of the sauce with this amount so I stopped adding more.

The other modifications I made were:

1. Instead of 3/4 cup wine vinegar, I used 1/2 cup wine vinegar and 1/4 cup cider vinegar.

2. The recipe calls for 1 cup beef broth. I used an entire can of double strength Beef Broth, 10 1/2 ounces.

For preparation:

1. I browned the short ribs in vegetable oil. Using short ribs with bones, there is more fat in them (than in the original recipe) and I wanted to discard the fat before continuing with the sauce.

2. I put the ribs in a Pyrex dish large enough for the ribs to sit beneath the rim and stuck them in the preheated, 350 oven while making the sauce.

3. I poured all the fat/oil out of the browning pan, but left all the brown flour. To this I added 2 Tbs. butter and sauteed the chopped onion a bit while measuring then adding the other ingredients. The brown sugar was added last.

4. When the sauce was done, I took the ribs out of the oven, covered them with sauce, then tightly sealed the dish with tin foil.

5. After one hour I removed the ribs from the oven, removed all fat on the surface, turned the ribs over, then put them back in the oven for another 1/2 hour.

I will definitely make these again. I'm pretty sure the short ribs would have been done in 1 1/4 hours, but I was disorganized and had forgotten to start cooking anything to go with them.

Oh, I could not get all the sauce in the baking dish I used. I probably have about a cup left. I intend to marinate chicken pieces in the left over sauce then cook them on the grill this weekend.

attributes.source_text: I do not have a sweet tooth, so I drastically cut the amount of brown sugar

reviews.review_text: Okay, you know a recipe is good when everything possible goes wrong and it STILL turns out great. Was very excited when I woke up this morning to make these ribs -- my first attempt at ribs ever. As I was browning them, I realized I had forgotten to buy beef broth, and no onions. Then noticed I did not have enough red wine vinegar. Ran around the kitchen in a panic for a minute, then decided to improvise. Used beef bouillon granules instead of broth, used 1/4 cup white wine vinegar and 1/2 cup red wine vinegar, and decided to buy an onion at the store and add it later. Great! Got them browned and in the crockpot, and off I went. Returned home 2 hours later, onion in hand, to realize the crock pot was at room temp. What the....??? Check power source, check controls. Yep, it died on me! Scrambled in a panic, not wanting to waste these fine ribs. Dumped everything in a pyrex dish, added the onion, covered it and popped it in the oven at 250 for 5 hours. The house smelled heavenly all day and I could not wait to dig in. When I finally did they were SO worth all the hassle and the wait. These ribs were fall-off-the-bone tender, and the flavor was amazing. I served the gravy over mashed potatoes and even my picky preschooler inhaled it and asked for more. These ribs are a winner and will definitely be served again in my house. Hopefully with a working crockpot next time. Thanks MizzNezz!

attributes.source_text: These ribs were fall-off-the-bone tender
even my picky preschooler inhaled it and asked for more

reviews.review_text: Oh my!  DELICIOUS!  DH and I devoured the entire crock pot full in ONE sitting!  I did make some modifications based on other reviewers suggestions, preference, or necessity due to not having on hand what the recipe called for exactly and those are as follows:  Used white whole wheat seasoned flour that I already had on hand (#426791) and omitted the additional salt and pepper. Used olive oil rather than butter for browning.  Used 1 small onion, 1 green bell pepper and 1 red bell pepper b/c the peppers needed to be used before they spoiled....think I will add some celery next time too if I have it.  I substituted the broth for 1 cup of sodium free beef flavored Herbox. I reduced the red wine vinegar to 1/2 cup and then added 1/4 cup of apple cider vinegar.  I too, reduced the brown sugar to 1/4 cup of packed homemade light brown sugar (made with 1/2 cup of evaporated cane sugar and 1/2 Tb mild flavored molasses) and used the other 1/4 cup for making chili sauce (#52689) from scratch b/c I didn't have any.  I preheated the crock pot and cooked on high for 2 hours and low for 5 hours, however it was slightly too long as the beef really was falling apart more than we would normally like, so I will likely reduce that to 1 hour high and 5 hours low next time. I also thickened the sauce during the last 30 minutes or so of cooking time by adding approx 1/2 cup of a corn starch slurry.  Served over garlic mashed potatoes and a fresh green salad.  Simply one of the most delicious meals EVER!  Thank you so much for posting!

attributes.source_text: DH and I devoured the entire crock pot full in ONE sitting

reviews.review_text: I thought this recipe was really good.  I don't think you could mess this recipe up if you tried.  I didn't get this started until about 12:30 pm and wanted to have it for supper by 5 or 6 so I floured & browned probably 1-1/2 lbs of very lean boneless beef short ribs in the butter & a little olive oil (only added the olive oil because I browned them in my Fagor Multi-Cooker and the brown setting gets pretty hot and I didn't want the butter to burn). I removed the meat just to bring the sauce to a boil and then added the ribs back to my pot.  I used a little less of the brown sugar, didn't have chili sauce, so I just did 3 big squirts of catsup and used extra chili powder (I think, I didn't measure, just sprinkled generously).  I used all the red wine vinegar I had on hand which was probably 1/4 - 1/2 cup.  Since I was short on time, I used the high pressure setting for 10 min., then switched over to slow cooker on high for about 4 hours.  It smelled so good cooking.  I thickened the sauce and served it over rice.  The meat was tender and the sauce was great.  See what I mean, you just can't mess this recipe up!  Will definitely use this again and for other meats too.

attributes.source_text: The meat was tender

reviews.review_text: Unbelievable! This is one of the tastiest dishes I've eaten in a long time. As I was pressed for time I decided to cook the recipe on my stove-top and allowed almost 4 hours to completion. I also substituted apple cider vinegar instead of the red wine vinegar simply because I was out of it - I also used garlic chili sauce in place of the chili sauce and increased the amount of garlic to 4 finely chopped fresh cloves. The smell while it was cooking was out of this world and if you don't have the time for using a slow cooker, don't panic, it turns out fabulous on the stove top. After browning the ribs on all sides, I put the ribs aside and added all of the other ingredients into the pan making sure to scrape up all of the rib braising morsels. I then put the ribs back into the pan, covered and reduced the heat to medium low and let it do it's thing. I checked them every 30 minutes and turned them each time. I served small dishes of the sauce with the ribs - I think I must have added a little more chili sauce than the recipe called for as it was pretty spicy but I hope I make that same mistake again because I wouldn't change a thing...delicious, delicious, delicious - this is a better than even a 10 star dish. Thanks so much for sharing!  I added this later as I wanted to share that I used the leftover sauce on chicken.  I browned chicken thighs and poured the left over rib sauce over them and let them simmer for about an hour - delicious!

attributes.source_text: it was pretty spicy but I hope I make that same mistake again

reviews.review_text:
I have never made beef shortribs before so I picked this recipe because of all great reviews.
All I have to say it was delicious as all of her recipes are as I have tried!
I read the reviews first & doubled the sauce but cut the red wine vinegar in 1/2 as I don't usually cook with it.
I bought a pkg. of ribs at Costco which had 4 boneless ribs in it without much fat at all.
I started it yesterday evening, cooked it 4 hours cooled it & put it in the fridge overnight.
Took it out late this morning scraped off a tiny bit of fat & put it back in the crockpot, cooked for 4 more hours, until fork tender.I turned the crockpot to high & the sauce got nice & thick.
The sauce was wonderful, very tasty, lick you plate clean!
I made mashed potatoes with ribs since I think that go best with it.
I only use olive oil (no butter) to brown the ribs.
Thanks for posting such a great recipe, the only one I'll use.

attributes.source_text: until fork tender
the sauce got nice & thick

reviews.review_text: I adapted this recipe somewhat; I live alone and have a 2.5 quart crock pot. I downsized the quantities of the ingredients to fit the size of the crock pot, all to taste. I omitted the chili sauce and garlic and substituted a bit of tomato sauce and added a generous amount of an oriental Chili Puree with Garlic, all other ingredients per the recipe. I had to use bone-in short ribs as I could not find boneless. I also omitted the butter in an attempt to reduce the some of the fat mentioned by other reviewers. I added a bit of olive oil to a non-stick pan to brown the short ribs. I drained and blotted the ribs with paper towel and drained the fat from the pan before proceeding with the recipe. In the end It was still very fatty, tasty but fatty. I skimmed the excess fat. I enjoyed this but I doubt I would make this again due to the amount of fat although I might try a different cut of meat.

Make that 5 stars ! I believe you now that these are GOOD !
I had just a couple of changes.....I didn't have red wine vinegar and used apple cider instead. I used chopped garlic in chili oil for a little spice.
When I sauted the onions, I added some chopped mushrooms and green peppers..(would also be good with some spicer peppers.) I don't think any of my changes altered the recipe though, and we loved it.
I agree that this sauce is perfect for chicken or pork too, (in fact an old boot would taste good in this sauce..LOL.)
This is a recipe I will keep close by to use a lot. Oh, forgot that I did mine in the oven,tightly covered for about 3 hrs, and they were perfect.I served it over noodles. THANK YOU for this one.
I am going to try browning the ribs on the stove first to eliminate some of the grease as they are cooking in the oven or crockpot. After seeing this suggestion in the reviews it seems it will eliminating some of the grease that I have to remove at the end. Donna

attributes.source_text: for a little spice

reviews.review_text: Wow!  So happy to have found this receipe - thanks MizzNess for posting - the ribs were amazing.  <br/><br/>I made only a few minor changes:<br/><br/>I used Sriracha Hot Chili Sauce.  Since my family members are divided between liking spicy and not so spicy I left out the additional chili powder.   I forgot to add the minced garlic.  I didn't miss it but I'm sure it would be nice to have included it.  Either way works...<br/><br/>After browning the floured ribs in the skillet with butter, I moved the ribs to the crock and sauteed the onions a little before adding the remaining ingredients.  After it started to boil I added about 1 Tbs corn starch to a small cup mixed in with a little warm water & then added that to the boiling mixture to thicken up the sauce just a bit.  Boiled for a few minutes then poured on top of the ribs.  Cooked on high for 1 hour then on low for 7 more hours.<br/><br/>Served the ribs over brown rice with a side of steamed fresh broccoli and carrots.  Delicious!

I would give this more stars if I could. I tend to drink wine while I cook...so needless to say, having a recipe like this, that I can start in the morning and go about my day, and just do my dinner-drinking when I start making the sides at night, makes this recipe a blessing! It’s delicious EVERY time (even When I’m halfway through making it and realize I don’t have enough garlic, or only have balsamic rather than red wine vinegar etc). This is something that is SUCH a crowd pleaser, tasting impossibly fancy, but is easier to make than an omelet! The fact that it makes the house smell incredible all day is an added blessing! I’ve made it for Christmas dinner before, and even last night, in the midst of this Coronavirus Pandemic of 2020. (My local store was out of all chicken and pork, so I stocked up on beef.) Pairs well with cheesy garlic/shallot mushrooms and/or cauliflower dish. Can’t wait to make again!

attributes.source_text: SUCH a crowd pleaser
I’ve made it for Christmas dinner before
I’ve made it for Christmas dinner before

reviews.review_text: I made this yesterday and .....oh boy! Delicious! I used a little less brown sugar than what was called for and a little less vinegar also..due to reading those suggestions in some of the reviews. At about 8 hours on low, I removed the ribs from the pot and the meat fell off of the bones. I got rid of any remaining fat on the meat. I poured the sauce into a glass measuring bowl and ladled the fat off of the top and used paper towels to absorb the rest off of the top. I put the sauce in a pot and added a cornstarch and water mix and brought it to a boil to thicken it. I put the defatted meat back in the crockpot and then poured the thickened sauce over it and kept it on warm until it was time to eat. I have to say, it was so delicious that I was like a crack addict while removing the fat from the meat, I kept eating little pieces...couldn't seem to stop myself! My husband, son, and I all had 2 helpings! Served over Texmati brown rice and had roasted green beans on the side. Next time, I will cut off as much fat as I can before cooking. Other than that.....I will repeat it just the way it is. Love, love, love!!

attributes.source_text: the meat fell off of the bones

reviews.review_text: Followed recipe w/exception of no chili sauce or powder and no catsup. Added instead Hoisin garlic glaze & marinade by Soy Vay, teriyaki w/pineapple sauce by Giant Eagle, (I didn't measure but if I had to guess it was about 1/4 cup, each)  and added a few squirts of spicy brown mustard, along w/red wine vinegar, brown sugar, and only 1 T. worchetersire sauce and used about 12 garlic cloves chopped fine.  Browned meat with butter and flour and all sides for about 15 mins in a thick stainless steel pan, and added a whole sliced sweet onion.  Stirred up the liquid and did not heat it just poured it over meat and cooked for 2-1/2 hours at 325. It was simply delicious.  Meat had a great flavor  but towards end the sauce got very oily & I took meat out of sauce immediately.  I didn't use the sauce for gravy, but the meat itself had the best taste ever. Thanks for recipe.

Awsome flavor! But I too found that the long cook time was a bit excessive and turned out an extremely dry final product. I can accept that my crock pot might have lost its calibration due to age. However, all of my other recipes seem to turn out just fine. Perhaps you might add a heads-up or warning in your recipe about the problem with older crockpots before people commit to this expensive mistake? Now if I can just figure out another way to correctly cook this recipe without drying the meat out. It was tasty but way too dry to enjoy. Lastly, I agree with Linda A. about the length of prep time. I work in a commercial kitchen and can truthfully say that a 10 minute prep time is really pushing it. Realistically I would say 25-30 minutes prep which includes browning the meat. I will continue to follow your recipes as they are tasty! Now to have another look at my crock pot before I destroy something else. Thanks for your insite!

I decided to try this recipe when I got my first ever Crock Pot yesterday.  This recipe was really delicious.  Though I am not experienced with slow cooking, I found this easy to prepare and absolutely delicious.  

Now about the sauce!  I thought it was delicious.  Like most reviewers, I loved it.  While it was cooking I started to read more reviews and saw a few people thought the sauce was too thin/ watery/ oily and not thick enough.  I imagine this is how this dish is supposed to be.  It is more of a juice in my opinion than a gravy and is meant to be poured over the meat and rice or whatever else you decide to serve it with.  The flavor was amazing and there was no overwhelming flavors from any of the ingredients in my opinion.  They blended well to create a rich, warm taste that paired perfectly with the boneless short ribs.  I also did not see an overwhelming amount of oil like some reviewers.  

I want to add that I followed this recipe exactly and it cooked for the full 9 hours.  I did not substitute any ingredients and followed the amount needed.

attributes.source_text: create a rich, warm taste

reviews.review_text:
This was AMAZING! Seriously...tender, flavorful, mouth watering, easy to make, absolutely wonderful!
While at the grocery store last night I saw a sale for $1.99/lb Boneless Beef Short Ribs. I had never bought these before, but figured for $5 I would give them a try. I googled looking for a crock pot recipe and came across this one. I just happened to have all the ingredients it called for. I started at 8:30 am and and by 5:30 I was excited to "sample" a bite. WOW! Perfection! I made some mashed potatoes to go with it.

I will admit, I first thought the ribs looked strange siting in the juice (as I wasn't sure what they were suppose to look like) but after pulling them out of the crock pot I knew I would be making this again in the near future.
Thank you so much for this recipe!!!

attributes.source_text: tender

reviews.review_text: Great recipe,  will use it many times again, but,  reserve the right to alter according to my devious mind. :)     Another way to go in the same vein:  and this applies not only to short ribs, but pork ribs and beef back ribs etc.   This idea was given to me by my good friend Rich. Give it a try you will be pleasantly surprised.     Take whatever ribs that float your boat, put them in the slow-cooker.  cover them with you favorite BBQ sauce (mine > Sweet Baby Ray's) (I also make up a Mexican style salsa)   and turn the cooker on "WARM"....yup I<br/>said "warm" and depending on the size of the meat,  cook for 24-36 hours...  check every couple of hours after 24 and you can ascertain if they're done.    I serve them with grilled corn, <br/>smoke BBQ beans etc.     Enjoy !       Uncle Don

This is a recipe for people who don't actually like the flavor of meat. It is waaaayyyyy too many flavors mixed together with just an overpowering result that makes it pointless to have spent the money on decent meat. If you actually like the taste of beef, move along. This is the equivalent of going to a nice restaurant, ordering a $50 filet, and then asking the waiter to bring A1. Cooking ribs for 9 hours is also just completely excessive. Of course the meat is tender after you basically boil it off the bone. That's easy enough to do, but doesn't make for a good recipe. Definitely won't ever mix up all of this nonsense again. I can only imagine that this "recipe" came about because somebody just decided to mix up a little bit of every kind of sauce or ingredient in the fridge one day. It leaves an absolutely horrific after taste.

Delicious as fully expected from a MizzNezz recipe ;)!  I purchased only 1.5 lbs of ribs as I cooked only for me.  I prepared the sauce as directed using minced onions because I thought I had an onion, but not so (senior moment).  I cooked on high for 1 hour, then on low for 4 hours and mine were done to perfection.  I will say there is a flavor in the sauce that I cannot put my finger on, but I didn't care for it.  I would guess it may be the red wine vinegar since that is the only ingredient that I have not used very much and am not that familiar with in a sauce.   However, it was still very good and will definitely make again, perhaps not using red wine vinegar just to see if I am correct about the flavor.   Thanks for the keeper MizzNezz!

This came out sooo good! I have a few tweaks based on what I had available in my pantry. I used bone-in ribs and I needed a bit more liquid to make sure they were submerged in the slow cooker, so I added about 1/2 to 3/4 cup of red wine to the sauce mixture. I omitted the brown sugar and supplemented with about 1/2 cup of honey instead. I omitted the chilli powder because I didn't want it to be too spicy. Just the chilli sauce gave it a nice dose of mild-medium heat that rounded everything out beautifully. My ribs were done in 4 hours on low because my slowcooker runs hot. I knew they were done because the meat slid right off the bone. Even with minor adjustments, this came out amazing. I can't wait to make it again!

attributes.source_text: gave it a nice dose of mild-medium heat
the meat slid right off the bone

reviews.review_text: With all due respect to those of you who had issues with this recipe, I don't think you have knowledge of some basics of braising in a crock pot. The author, obviously, created this for those that do. This recipe is fantastic.  I made it last night and doubled the quantitys for a crowd.  I had nothing but rave reviews. First of all, when you braise beef in a crock pot or even a double oven in a stove, you need to skim off the fat before you serve it.Otherwise it will be totally "greasy".  Second, 9 hours at low in a crock pot is totally appropriate when you work and want to come home for your dinner.  However, if you do it in a crock put on high or even in a dutch oven in your stove at 325 degrees you can cut the cooking time in half.  I love short ribs and this is the best recipe I have found.

items.label: Slow Cook Down Home Pork Chops and Gravy
items.name: Slow Cook Down Home Pork Chops and Gravy
items.description: I don't even like Pork, but was tricked into tasting this dish when I was told it was chicken. WOW! The meat was sooo tender and juicy; so tender in fact, that it was literally falling apart! It was like nothing I'd ever tasted before! Definitely not like my mother's hard, crusty pork chops! lol! This recipes goes hand in hand w/ some mashed potatoes. Just pour the leftover gravy on the taters' and enjoy!
instructions: Combine 1st four ingredients in a shallow dish.
Dredge chops in flour mixture and set aside.
Combine what is left of the flour mixture w/ the chicken broth and pour into your crock pot.
Pour oil into a large skillet and cook the chops in hot oil until browned on both sides.
Place chops in crock pot and cook covered on High for about 2 to 5 hours or until tender.
Serve w/ hot rice and/or mashed potatoes.
++If the gravy becomes too thick just add a little water. If you accidentally add too much water then add a little more flour.
Season w/ salt and pepper too your taste.

reviews.review_text:
This was a fantastic base recipe for pork chops and gravy that can be suited to your own tastes. As for me, I used 5 teaspoons of yellow mustard (didn't have dry) and increased flour to 3/4 cup. Also, I used a teaspoon of locally obtained seasoning mix that included salt paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, and black pepper. After browning chops, I made a roux w/ green onions and remainder of the flour, mustard, seasoning mixture. I used about 48 oz of chicken stock slowly mixed into the roux which was then poured over the chops in the crock pot. I cooked on high for two hours and all was done but not quite falling off the bone yet. Then cooked on low for another two hours. Also mixed in a tablespoon of cornstarch for thickening and added a cup of mushrooms. Finally, I tasted and re-adjust seasonings as needed before serving.

Read more at: http://www.food.com/recipe/slow-cook-down-home-pork-chops-and-gravy-45940?oc=linkback

Wow! This turned out awesome!  I needed a dinner where it could be done in a few hours without me sitting there watching it and this fit the bill!  I did not have any condensed chicken broth, so I used regular chicken broth.  I also ended up using double the amount of flour, mustard, salt and garlic powder to cover all of my chops which I cut off the bone since I had bone-in center cut chops. I ran out of flour mixture right in the middle of breading!  I would recommend making sure all the chops are covered in the gravy while they cook as those chops were the most tender.  I also used a whole container of chicken broth, (you know the broth that comes in the resealable containers).  I mixed in about 3/4 cups of flour and about another tsp of mustard, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp pepper and about a tablespoon of chicken buillion granules for the gravy.  My chops took 3 hours on high in my oval Rival crock pot and they were very tender.  I made sure to whisk the gravy really well to incorporate the breading that came off and adjust the gravy thickness after the chops were done and out of the crock pot.  If you need the gravy thicker, one cup cold water or broth mixed with one tablespoon of flour and bring to a boil in a saucepan or pour in the crock pot on high and let cook for 15 minutes or so until it thickens.  Use more or less flour/water mixture to get the thickness you desire.  These were moist and tender and this extra broth made enough gravy for all the mashed potatoes I made to go with these.  Very flavorful.  Very easy!  Took me ten minutes to prepare and throw in the crock pot and that was it!  I would definitely recommend.  I would also make sure to use boneless pork chops also, because in my past experience, the bone breaks down in the gravy and you get crunch bits in your gravy, yuck!  You can always cut the chop off the bone like I did and that worked great!  Just make sure you have lean chops or the dish will be too greasy! You gotta try this!  Thanks for posting buttercup!

I needed a dinner

reviews.review_text: A great recipe!  I was very thankful to find a recipe like this that did not use 'Cream Of..."  I read the reviews first and planned accordingly.  For my purposes I didn't need a crockpot.  I seasoned the chops and and browned them in an oven proof skillet.  Then I sauteed mushrooms, onions and garlic, added the stock and some flour mixed with dried mustard and water.  I was only making 3 x 1" thick chops but used the full amount of gravy ingredients.  It went in to the oven at 350 for 1 1/2 hours with a pan of brussel sprouts, carrots and cauliflower put in to roast for the last 40 minutes.  I found it very flavourful and suspect that those who didn't may not have used the concentrated broth.  It would make a huge difference substituting regular broth imo.  Anyway - it was a fabulous meal with lots of gravy left to pour over the mashed potatoes.  This will be a regular item here!

This was good. I did a couple things differently - added some different spices to the flour mix, including some thyme and paprika. I also whisked the flour into the broth, in the same pan I fried the chops. That helped thicken things a little and I had no clumping.  As for the broth, I used the Knorr liquid chicken stock bubbles (no idea what their name is!)and instead of adding 3.5 cups of boiling water to it, I only added about 12oz water. Once it was bubbling in the crock pot, I thought perhaps there wasn't enough liquid and I added about a half bottle of beer. My husband LOVED this and there was a nice amount of gravy. I gave it 4 stars because it was a touch bland, but if I make it again, I will doctor it up more. I also cooked it on high for 2 hours, then switched it to low for 2 hours and it was fall off the bone tender. Thank you for this recipe!

attributes.source_text: My husband LOVED this
fall off the bone tender

reviews.review_text:
I would have given this 4.5 if I could have. I am stingy with 5's :-). I made this mostly according to the recipe. I used boneless pork sirloin chops. I probably added proportionately slightly more dry mustard because I know I like that as a flavoring. I left out the salt, knowing it is easier to add later than to take out. I used Better Than Bouillon brand chicken bouillon (that is my go-to brand for all bouillons). I also added 3 red potatoes cut into 1 inch chunks. Aside from those minor changes, I followed the recipe pretty closely. After about 2 hours in the crock, I tasted the gravy, and thought it needed a bit more flavor, so I shook in some Nature's Seasoning blend and mixed it up a bit. After another 45 minutes, I couldn't wait any longer, so I cut off a third of one of the chops and pulled out a few potato chunks to have a little "before meal snack." It was very good! I did sprinkle a bit of pepper on it too, but that's all. And I am really the type to often "dress up" a recipe more than that. The pork was nice and moist. It wasn't yet "fall apart tender" but had a very nice texture. I put the lid back on and will let it cook another hour and then turn it off.

Very nice, easy, yummy dish :-)

P.S. Mine came out a light color like chicken gravy, not brown like in the picture, but I don't care about the color. It tasted very good.

attributes.source_text: The pork was nice and moist

reviews.review_text: Gibblet had popped his in the oven at 350 F; I followed his lead and popped mine in a 170 C oven for an hour, then decreased to 150 C for one and a half more hours.  The pork was so tender I had to take care in moving the chops!  Sadly though, I have to agree with Laura70 - this one was a no-go for my family and me either.  The meat and gravy both turned out bland even by my standards, which are very much on the light side.  The first word that came up in my mind was actually "boring"; it seemed to lack depth of any sort of flavor.  Even my SO's brother, who dropped by the house on a whim and grabbed a small chunk of meat that had come off of a chop stopped after that piece, and it's a shock to ever see him restrain himself when there's meat on the dinner table.  This is a guy who typically clears every available piece of meat on the table before dinner is over.  Everyone ended up gobbling up and praising the Recipe #114556 on end and more or less ignoring the main dish - and here in Norway, meat is always the main deal.  That was a strange sight to behold.

attributes.source_text: The pork was so tender I had to take care in moving the chops!

reviews.review_text: I rarely make pork, but on impulse, I bought some chops because they looked fresh and delicious.  Trouble is, once I got them home, I had no idea what to do with them!  I didn't even know slow cooking was an option until I saw this recipe, and the excellent reviews persuaded me.  I'm so glad they did!  I used adobo seasoning (the kind with pepper) instead of the salt and garlic powder, and I used a touch more dry mustard than is called for... I was looking for tangy, and boy, did this ever deliver!  So good, so good... I reached in to stir it up when it seemed done and the spoon went right through the chops.  Tonight I served this with rice and a spinach salad, but I bet this would make incredible, messily delicious sandwiches, too, on a thick and crusty baguette.  I definitely will make this again--I'm astonished that I was able to make something so great with what I already had on hand.  Never would have thought of it myself!

attributes.source_text: I was looking for tangy, and boy, did this ever deliver!
the spoon went right through the chops

reviews.review_text:
I made 12 chops,,,,used a 32 ounce carton of chicken broth. I also used some seasoned salt, pepper, paprika and about 1/2 t. of italian seasoning.
After placing chops on top of gravy broth I sliced half an onion on top. I added about 1 cup of water ( I was out of broth),,,,,,, to prevent the gravy becoming too thick. I also added 1/4 c. worcestershire sauce. Stirring gently occasionally helped . I slowly steamed cubed potatoes in the pan the chops had browned in. I added 2 T. butter and 1/2 c. water , then served the meat and gravy on top.There were no lumpsin the gravy and the taste was WOW!!! I can't wait to experiment with more meats.Thank you for this recipe!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

My husband is usually a "nice" guy when it comes to me trying new recipes. But THIS time? He was more than nice--- he ate a few bites and was like, "YUM! Definitely make this one again!" So that says a lot! The flavors were great, I served this over mashed taters--- I made this with 4 large bone-in chops--- the "Gravy" only covered one of them in the pot, and I was worried how they would cook. I readjusted halfway through, and they were awesome. The breading fell off in clumps though- wish there was a way to make it stick better. But excellent none the less!
(UPDATE:  I made this in my oven the other night and I liked it WAYYY more... followed all the same steps except cooked it in a foil-covered 9x13 dish in a 350 degree oven for 2.5 hours...  the breading stuck a lot better b/c they weren't all stacked on top of each other and the gravy only covered the bottom half of each chop.  YUM!  this is a keeper!)  (my photo is of the Oven version, FYI)

attributes.source_text: He was more than nice--- he ate a few bites and was like, "YUM! Definitely make this one again!"

reviews.review_text: The first time I made this, my family and I were not too impressed.  Like some other reviewers, we felt the dish was a little too bland.  Adding a bit of sage really helped.  I almost didn't bother trying this again, but I needed a quick and easy crockpot dish the other day--one that wouldn't require all day to cook, and so I gave this one another shot.  I made it exactly as the recipe call for (just as I did the first time--before I ended up adding the sage, that is), but for some reason, the dish turned out much more flavorful the second time around.  Maybe the quality or particular cut of the pork chops is the reason?  I don't know.  At any rate, this came together quickly and easily when I needed a crockpot meal to be ready in 3 hours, and it was so much better the second time I tried it that I'm sure I'll make it again.

I made this for dinner tonight with a few changes based on what I had on hand.  I had 1 lb of pork loin, I cut it into bite sized pieces and coated in 1/4 cup of flour, 1/2 ts of mustard powder, and a little salt, then browned it in a frying pan.  I removed the pork, added 2 tb of butter 1 clove of fresh garlic and scraped up the browned bits, added 2 Tb of flour and cooked it for a minute.  Then I added about 11 oz of reduced ham stock, and 1 ts of dry mustard to make a gravy.  I added the pork back in, covered it, and baked at 350 for 1 hour.  The gravy seemed a little too thick so I added 1/2 cup of milk (next time I might add another 1/4 cup), then tossed with egg noodles.  We all liked this, my son (who right now only really wants to eat sandwiches), even asked for seconds.  The meat was so tender and the gravy was delicious!   Thanks so much for posting!

attributes.source_text: I made this for dinner tonight
my son (who right now only really wants to eat sandwiches), even asked for seconds
The meat was so tender

reviews.review_text: These pork chops were delicious!  However, after reading the reviews, I did make some alterations.  Fist of all, I seasoned my chops before browning.  Secondly, I did not have condensed chicken broth, so I used cream of chicken soup and chicken broth.  I doubled the amounts and used a 26 ounce can of cream of chicken and 1 1/2 small cans of chicken broth.  It made a lot of gravy, but it was well worth it!! I also added a little Kitchen Bouquet to give it a nice brown color.  The chops were so tasty and so tender. I cooked them on high for 3 hours and warm for 1 additional hour.  My husband and I had gone to a basketball game and had not planned on eating them that night, but they smelled so good that I cooked up some mashed potatoes and we performed a taste test.  My husband performed 2 1/2 taste tests!! They were delicious!

attributes.source_text: so tender
My husband performed 2 1/2 taste tests!!

reviews.review_text: I pretty much made this as described, except I used 8 chops and quadrupled the gravy (we love gravy).  I think the condensed broth adds flavor, although I might try using the low salt version next time.  My slow cooker is ... well ... slow, so I like to add hot liquids whenever possible to give it a jump start.  I think that worked well with this recipe.  After browning the chops, I browned the rest of the flour in the drippings and added the broth to the pan.  No lumps, and you get a nice color from the browned bits in the pan.  I was careful not to let it get too thick, since it thickens a bit more in the slow cooker.  This is the second time I'm making this, and it's a huge hit with mashed potatoes and fresh green beans.  Comfort food at its best!

I actually made a recipe very similar to this tonight that I found on Pinterest: ( http://www.mydailymoment.com/recipes/slow-cooked_pork_chops.php ).This recipe called for condensed chicken and rice soup (which I thought was a little strange but was shockingly delicious!) and no addition of flour to the broth. My daughter said this was her favorite dish ever and "Don't lose this recipe, mom!"  It's a definite keeper... I'm thinking about experimenting with some different condensed soups for different flavors... maybe onion soup! Yum! Thanks for this easy go-to pork chop recipe... it's a winner! UPDATE: I made this recipe with condensed  french onion soup and it was pretty good but my daughter thinks it was better with the chicken and rice soup.

attributes.source_text: My daughter said this was her favorite dish ever

reviews.review_text: This is a BIG Sunday dinner good as we say here in the south.  Afer frying up the pork chops, I added mushrroms and some sliced onions to the pan and got up all the good ole brown bits and thru those into the crockpot, and then made the gravy in the same pan (as per directions...I may have used a little more flour and chicken stock), threw it all in the crockpot, cooked it on high for 4 hrs, then turned it down on low for the last hour.  I iddn't need to thickened it any further and it was great,  The pork chops (and mine were rather large pork chops that were on sale) were tender and jucy.  Family said that this one is a "keeper" and needs to be repeated.   Was winner here!

were tender and jucy

reviews.review_text: My s/o claimed that this was the asbolute best thing I have ever made (now, I don't know how reasonable that is.... he says that with every outstanding dish I make.). But both of us could not stop raving, and I couldn't stop being thankful of how EASY it was... I had been running all day and got home late, but was able to have the pork chops ready in 2.5 hours on High... items.name: Amazing Chicken Tortilla Soup!
keywords: c("Chicken", "Poultry", "Meat", "Mexican", "Lactose Free", "Low Cholesterol", "Egg Free", "Healthy", "Kid Friendly", "Free Of...", "Spicy", "Beginner Cook", "< 4 Hours", "Easy")
items.description: This recipe has been a huge hit with everyone who has ever tried it. We make it almost weekly, and the leftovers are eaten immediately. It is also very healthy! It is a little spicy, so if you don't have too much of a tolerance for spicy foods, you may choose to leave out the seeds of the jalapeño. If you love spicy, like we do, extra cayenne pepper adds even more zing. Enjoy!
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, jalapeño and green pepper with olive oil in a large pot until soft.
Add all the rest of the ingredients to the large pot and bring to a boil.
After about 15 minutes, remove the chicken breasts and shred.
(Two forks work well to pull the chicken apart!).
Return shredded chicken to the pot and simmer an additional 45 minutes.
Serve, topped with crushed tortilla chips if desired.

reviews.review_text: WOW!!!... amazing is right!!!  I changed it up a bit because, I can't seem to be able to just leave a good recipe alone! I tend to like my meats browned rather than just boiled so, I pan fried the chicken breast (I added a couple more breasts), until browned than added it to the soup with the drippings from the pan. I followed someone elses suggestion and mashed a can of cannellini beans to thicken the soup. In addition, because I like color, I added a can of black beans, some red and yellow peppers in addition to the green, about three stalks of celery an extra garlic clove and another jalapeno pepper for spice. I omitted the 1/2 cup of water or wine and added another can of chicken broth. Because of all of my additions, I added a few more dashes of the three spices.  Simmered for about an hour and served with some homemade tortilla strips and a sprinkle of cheese... it was truly AMAZING!!!  With the extra jalapeno pepper, I was afraid it may be too spicy but, it wasn't at all... I may even add more next time.  I was thinking that a sprinkle of cilantro may be a nice touch too!!!  This will be an all time favorite in our household from now on!!!  Enjoy!!!

My husband said this is the best soup he has ever ate.  That is a huge compliment.  The only variations I made were boiling a whole chicken and used that as my stock plus one small can of chicken stock.  I shredded the whole chicken so you got chicken with every bite.  I also omitted the the wine and added green onions along with the regular onion and added about a 1/4 cup of chopped fresh cilantro.  Also added 1 extra Tsp. of cumin to give it an extra smokey flavor plus 1 cup of sharp cheddar cheese and 1 can of black beans (mashed 1/2 can).  To give it a thicker texture I took 1/4 cup of the soup and mix with 1 Tsp of flour and added that to the soup as it cooked down.  Garnished with cilantro, cheese, sour cream, tortilla chips, and green onions.  JUST PERFECT!!!!!!

Goya Sazon, 1 tsp. paprika, and 2 zucchini (thick sliced), used tomato paste in place of sauce, added ground chipotle, made homemade tortilla strips, garnished with avocado, sour cream, colby jack cheese. I did add more chili powder and cuminos to adjust to our taste---however, I did not use fiesta/southwest corn because I could not find any at the grocery store. items.name: Chicken Scaloppine With Lemon Glaze  (Low Fat and Delicious!)
items.description: This is a wonderful lower-fat restaurant-quality dish that is easy to make, I also like to add in a few tablespoons of capers and cook with the lemon glaze if you are a lover of capers then add them in as it really adds to the flavour of this dish ---  this lemon sauce is not a heavy creamy sauce which is what makes this dish lower in fat, it is more like a glaze that soaks into the chicken, and I would strongly suggest to double or even triple the glaze I most always do, and please be certain to use only dry breadcrumbs as fresh will not stick to the chicken as well --- this is *very* good!
instructions: In a small bowl or shallow dish whisk together mustard and eggs; set aside.
Combine the dry bread crumbs with poultry seasoning, garlic powder and seasoning salt; spread on a piece of waxed paper.
Dip the breasts firstly in egg/mustard mixture (shake off any excess egg) then coat well with the crumb mixture, pressing downs with hands to adhear the crumbs to the breast.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add in the chicken and cook for about 5 minutes on each side, or until it is no longer pink inside; remove and transfer to a plate to keep warm.
For the glaze; in the same skillet add in the broth, lemon juice and 1/4 teaspoon salt (or to taste, if using capers add in now) bring to a boil scraping any brown bits from the pan.
Add in lemon slices and parsley; mix to combine for about 1 minute.
Spoon the glaze/sauce over chicken.
Delicious!

Rare as it is that I give a 5-star review but this is one of them and my wife and children agree.  The only thing I would change, and it should not affect the rating, is to double the sauce.  The sauce is enough to "glaze" the dish and the breading seems to soak most of it up, but that may be a preference to the author.  I did use panko bread crumbs and it worked out great.  One other suggestion I'd make is once you pound out the breasts, two breasts take up the entire pan.

As for the flavor, it was excellent and I did not find the lemon too strong at all.  The texture is crisp and the chicken was juicy.  I may add sauteed mushrooms next time. Great recipe.

reviews.review_text: WOW. Just, Wow. I made this with vegetarian chik'n (Quorn brand, it's almost exactly like chicken in taste and texture) and it was delicious! I made some changes besides that: I used an egg white instead of a whole egg (to cut calories and cholesterol), I didn't have poultry seasoning so I used some other spices instead (same ones in the store bought mix), and instead of chicken broth I used veggie. The glaze was WAYYY too salty, so I added some water and sugar to balance the flavor along with some cornstarch dissolved in water. I will DEFINITELY be making this again and sharing this recipe with my vegetarian friends. Thanks, KittenCal!!

Simply wonderful. Easy to make, easy to eat. I didn't add capers, but I can see how they would add to the taste. I really enjoyed the dijon mustard addition, but ended up throwing out 85% of the mustard/egg mixture- it just wasn't needed. I would probably use one egg, 1 T of dijon next time. Fresh lemon juice was a great addition- I am so glad I didn't use bottled. Was a teensy bit salty, probably my fault, as my poultry seasoning is a little salty on its own. I also added 1/2 tsp of cornstarch to the broth mixture (which I doubled as per another reviewer) just to make it a little bit thicker. Really really nice little dinner. Thanks for sharing.

attributes.source_text: Really really nice little dinner

reviews.review_text: OMG - my roomate's mother (back in college) made this and I never knew this is what she made until tonight.  I've been searching for this recipe for 15 years.. lol    WE LOVED THIS!  So easy, and so delicious - and it looks like it takes so much time to make.  I'll definitely use this for entertaining.  The kids liked the chicken, but not the sauce, so I will leave it off a piece or two for next time.   I doubled the sauce recipe as well and it was just enough. I actually bought the thinly sliced chicken breasts from the grocery store and was able to eliminate the pounding.  Thanks for another fabulous recipe Kittencal - I can always count on yours to be the best! :)

attributes.source_text: The kids liked the chicken

reviews.review_text: I had a feeling that this was going to be an awesome choice for dinner tonight with all of the 5 star reviews and I wasn't disappointed! I halved this recipe for just my husband and me but tripled the sauce (added cornstarch) which was delicious on its own but next time I'll try the capers. The dijon mustard added outstanding flavor to the breading mix and did a great job of helping the crumbs to adhere. For those of us looking to jazz up boring chicken breasts without using a ton of butter or oil this recipe is a lifesaver. I'm adding this recipe to my permanent collection--thanks so much for posting! :)

attributes.source_text: an awesome choice for dinner tonight

reviews.review_text: Wowza!  This was a hit at our house tonight...we both devoured so much of this that we didn't even need a side to go with it!  I followed the directions exactly, using just one egg, which was plenty.  The only thing I will change next time I make it (which will be soon!) is add the salt in to the breadcrumb mix, skip the chicken broth, and just squeeze some fresh lemon on top during frying.  I think this will be better for our personal taste, as we like it a bit more lemony, and it may help to keep the chicken more crispy.  Thanks for the AWESOME recipe!  Will be a regular in our house, as it is very healthy, flavorful, and just yummy!

Another winner!!!  Made this for our dinner cutting down on the chicken and using chicken tenderloins pounded down and left the sauce at the same amount.  I did use some panko crumbs with the breadcrumbs and added some capers.  (I breaded the chicken and like PaulaG I let them sit for about 15 minutes).  The chicken turned out to be so tender and DH loved this dish.  Definately an easy and quick dish on a hot summer night.  Served with fresh stirfry of broccoli, cauliflower, mushroooms and onions.  Wonderful.  Thank you for posting.  Going into my Favorites of 2013.

reviews.review_text: Tonight was a Kittencal night at our house.  I made this, along with the Sweet & Spicy Sweet Potato Bake.  Not sure if it was a good pairing, but each dish is really good!  I found my pan to be a little dry after sauteeing the chicken on each side, so I added the juice of half a lemon, a couple of splashes of chardonnay, and a few splashes of chicken broth as well, and let the chicken simmer in that for just a couple of extra minutes.  Had to throw in some more capers, too, because we love them.  DH was mmm'ing over this one at first bite.  DeLISH!  Thanks, Kittencal!

reviews.review_text: FANTASTIC! Made this chicken last night for 7 of my family & friends & it was a huge hit!  Everyone called today still raving & asking the recipe. At first tasting the lemon glaze I thought yikes its so tart it may be too much but it was perfect.  I used all natural chicken breasts & they cut with a spoon they were so tender.  The mustard adds taste texture & holds the bread crumbs (used Italian more added flavor). Also used capers which adds depth to the dish. Beware I made quite a bit extra chicken thinking I would have leftovers for the week...not so people were pigging out...so be sure to make more than you think you might need!
