items.label: Tortellini Tomato Spinach Soup
items.name: Tortellini Tomato Spinach Soup
items.description: Make and share this Tortellini Tomato Spinach Soup recipe from Food.com.
instructions: In a soup pot, heat olive oil over medium high heat.
Saute the onion and garlic, stirring often until onions are translucent, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Add broth and tomatoes, turn heat up to high, and bring to a boil.
Add the tortellini and cook according to package instructions.
When tortellini is almost done, add spinach and taste, adjusting seasonings with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately.
Garnish each serving with a sprinkling of Parmesan.

reviews.review_text: I made this once as written. After a search for a real good recipes to do. And with resulted in other similar recipes, I decided I wanted to create something unique a great base recipe and easy to modify depending on your tastes.. It may be a stretch to call my creation, but the result was a meal the whole family will liked. MY was Not better, not worse, just different ! I've will added this to my recipe book "AS IS" and with my additions TOO. I have two way to do it!! THANK YOU!! I can do the happy food dance!! NOW !! I can't leave anything alone! THANK YOU!! ALWAYS READ THE RECIPE IN FULL BEFORE YOU START, then read the reviews. I can do the happy food dance!! NOW !! You get good Tips and Hints or two, to Note there. There are some great chefs here on Zaar, and she's one of the best! See Chicken Spinach Tortellini Soup or Chicken Soup for more tip's.

attributes.source_text: the result was a meal the whole family will liked

reviews.review_text: I decided to use this recipe because of the great reviews and because I was looking for a recipe that would use up my tomatoes and fresh spinach.  I did not have tortellini, so I used chicken instead and a 1/2 cup of rice that I added with the broth. I know this changes the recipe, but it also shows the versatility it has when you just don't have certain ingredients on hand.  I also upped the amount of garlic cloves because my boyfriend and I love garlic :)  The soup was fantastic topped with fresh mozzarella cheese.  I will definitely try it with cheese tortellini next time.  I also used fresh tomatoes because I did not have canned.  Thanks for a great one :)

(1/20/2009)This wonderfully flavorful soup can be put together in a matter of minutes.  I made as directed using 6 cups of reduced sodium chicken broth, about 1 cup of chopped onion, 1 (29 0z) can of whole tomatoes and   sausage with cheese fresh tortellini which added a lot of flavor.  This is a great recipe if you have little time to spend preparing supper.  I served with a crispy crust French bread with butter.  Thank you for posting, spatchcock! (Updated 2/13/2012) I continue making this soup.  Now I am using all organic vegetable broth and replacing the tortellini with mini spinach tortellini filled with sun-dried tomato. Super-good!!

attributes.source_text: preparing supper

reviews.review_text: I absolutely loved it!! I changed only a few things to tweak....I changed out the spinach for kale, and only because it's better for you. I added a half stick of butter when I had the olive oil, onions and garlic sauteing, I used the three cheese tortellini, which the entire family loved. And I added more parmesan cheese than the recipe called for. I also added carrots and chopped red potatoes( I didn't want them going to waste) it ultimately turned out to be a super fantastic veggie/tortellini soup!!! I will most definitely be making this again!! Very fast and easy to make!! Great idea when your putting up Christmas lights! :)

reviews.review_text: I make this often, and it always gets rave reviews! My version only had 6 ingredients (sans onion, pepper, & salt) but I will try that nex time around. Here's the beauty, use fresh frozen or dried tortellini. Use fresh or frozen spinach. I use a large can of Chicken broth, and diced italian seasoned tomatoes. No matter what you do, you can't screw it up! The best way to serve is with freshly grated parm on top! This step makes all the difference. I am sure Kraft is ok.....but if you go with the shredded, you will make huge points. Company just loves this, and we serve it all the time for quick winter meals!

for quick winter meals

reviews.review_text: great soup. I didn't realize when I read it that its basically the same soup I've been making with my home made turkey broth (from the Thanksgiving bird) but with the addition of tomato. I used petite diced tomatoes, drained, and cooked them up with the garlic. I did not use the onion, simply 'cause I am too lazy to chop them today. I used my home made broth with is quite flavorful to begin with as it was made with a grilled bird (has a slight smoky flavor). I used 2 9 oz pkgs of cheese and roasted garlic tortellini. I did not use the olive oil to cook with but I enjoy a drizzle over my bowl of soup. The rest of the fam used cheese.

attributes.source_text: has a slight smoky flavor

reviews.review_text: This was great!! I am not feeling well and neither are my two young boys. This warmed us right up and at least got some good liquid into my kids who aren't drinking much right now.  I added 2 cloves of garlic, 6 cups of chicken stock, oregano, thyme, paprika, and a bit of chipotle powder for a little kick. I also added 16oz of tortellini instead of just 8oz. I omitted the cheese b/c frankly I forgot about it. My 2 year old slurped it out of his bowl and ate the entire thing. My 4 year old ate a little bit but more of his grilled cheese sandwich.  I also left out the spinach b/c I didn't have any.  I will definitely make this again. I could even eat this without the tortellini, the broth is that good.

reviews.review_text: My husband made this for dinner a few nights ago.  It is cheap, healthy, easy, and DELICIOUS.  We used fresh whole wheat three cheese tortellini with a side of crusty rosemary olive oil bread.  I noticed that many people reduced the spinach, and that surprised me.  The high spinach content makes this soup stand out from the others that I've tried in the past, and it is healthier.  (Come on people!)  We have already made it again using ravioli, which also works nicely, though I prefer the texture of the tortellini better.  I add a dash of red pepper flakes for a quick, and the parmesan is not a must, but a luxury that can be afforded.

reviews.review_text: This is a amazing soup, and one of my boys' favorite dinners!!! I use more onion (a cup?) and 2-3 cloves garlic, plus italian seasoning. To save a step I throw the frozen package of chopped spinach into the pot when I add the broth and tomatoes, so no need to defrost or chop. I let the soup simmer away until we are 15 minutes away from eating, and then add the tortelli and cook until done. I've never added the paresan, don't think it needs it.  The tricky thing about this soup is that it is not one you can make and keep warm on the stove to feed family members eating in multiple 'shifts.' After the tortellini is cooked al dente, it continues to swell up and soften and absorb a lot of the broth. Those eating after sports practices and evening meetings get more of a 'stew'. Still tastes great, though! I like to serve with warm crusty sourdough bread.

attributes.source_text: one of my boys' favorite dinners

reviews.review_text: The only things I changed were to use a whole onion instead of 1/2 cup, and to use diced tomatoes instead of whole. I used frozen spinach, but I think it would be better with fresh spinach. My tortelloni were cheese-stuffed so I did not add any parmesan. I like how quick and easy this soup is to make... I'd give it an extra 1/2 star for that if possible. I'll probably make it again as I often have these ingredients on hand. I bought a big bag of cheese-stuffed Tortelloni at Costco and this is something nice to do with some of them without using a rich, fattening sauce. Thanks for the recipe!

I made this for dinner tonight using cheese tortellini. I also used a bag of fresh spinach.  It was a little smaller than what the recipe called for but it seemed to be perfect.  The fresh grated parm. at the end was a must for us.  It really made the soup.  I had a Italian seasoning grinder on the table that some of us added to the soup as well.  No one in my picky family gave this anything lower than four stars.  Wow! That doesn't happen often!  I served this with Bada Big Betty's Tuscan Portabella Melt (193692)  These two wonderful recipes compliment each other well.  Made for a delicious meal!

reviews.review_text: DH always buys the refrigerated tortellini when it comes on sale, and I really wanted to try something different and healthier than our normal combo of pesto and either cream or bechamel sauce with the tortellini. This was awesome! My market only had fresh Thai basil, so I subbed with jarred pesto. Kept most things the same, but added Garlic salt w/ parsley, dried basil, dried oregano, dried Provence herbs, 1 Tbsp tomato paste, used 1 chicken stock cube and 1 Kallo Tomato with herbs stock cube for the 6 cups broth. Used fresh spinach.

This was the 3rd soup recipe I've tried from Food and been over joyed with them all. the first was Tuscan Potato Soup  then Butternut Squash Soup, This time I read the reviews before heading to the store. I used 3 & 3 on the stock both chicken and veg., I used 2 cans of Muir Glen diced tomato's (fire roasted), 3 cloves of garlic and a hole onion (Small) garnished with parm. and fresh basil, served with Itl. herb French bread with garlic butter. It was a home run, even my picky partner had 2 helpings.  most soup are better day 2 and I'll be having leftovers for lunch tomorrow.

reviews.review_text: Very tasty and super quick to prepare.  I used olive oil cooking spray instead of the tablespoon of oil to cut back on as much fat as possible and it worked well.  I also used a 28 oz can of tomatoes (with basil) to give a little more of a zing, and only 4 cups of chicken broth.  Omitted the parm cheese at the end as well.  I cooked the tortellini only 3/4ths done added the spinach and immediately packed 5 servings into containers for ready to go lunches and dinners.  The pasta did not overcook, and I still had soup instead of stew.  Will make again!

reviews.review_text: This was the easiest soup I have ever made, and very quick (I found myself almost over-simmering it to try to get some dishes done!). I used dry cheese tortellini which was only an 8 oz. package, chicken broth, and fresh spinach. We topped the soup with mozzerella cheese because I was out of parmesan, but that was a bit too bland. I used diced tomatoes because the stores here have stopped selling small cans of whole tomatoes. I had to stretch to get 5 servings out of this - it seems to be more like 4 servings, and I would serve bread with it next time.

When I was done making this dinner, I said to myself, "Am I really done already?" It was so quick & easy! I used Cheese Ravioli because that's what I had in the house. But next time I will go w/ the suggested tortellini. Nevertheless, this meal was fantastic. Had a great flavor. When I first served it to my husband he groaned "What's this?" but then he promptly ate all his soup and finished it off by slurping the last juices from the bowl. I think the presentation doesn't do the meal justice! I also  added fresh basil, oregano and parsley to my creation.

reviews.review_text: I've had fun playing around with different ingredients to this recipe. Tonight, I browned ground hot italian sausage first, then sauted onions, garlic and red pepper. Once soft, I added 1/2 cup of red wine. Then added 6 cups of broth plus 1 can of tomato puree. I used roasted diced tomatoes and also added roasted eggplant and 2 tbsp of red pepper flakes before adding the tortellini and fresh spinich. It was such a delicious hearty soup. I have had fun changing this up each time and it always comes out great!

reviews.review_text: This soup was excellent  I made it to accommodate another pasta dish I was making my boyfriend and I ended up giving him the pasta and eating the rest of the soup!!! I only changed a couple things other than that it was PERFECT! I added a little less spinach than what they called for I felt like that was too much than I did one  can of halved tomatoes  and than one can of diced tomatoes I love tomatoes and I also added about 1/2 cup to 1 cup of tomato juice instead of just vegetable broth. I also added italian seasonings and fresh basil! I hope you enjoy it as much as we did!

reviews.review_text: This is a great soup!  I didn't have any canned broth, so I made my own veggie broth by boiling an onion, celery, baby carrots, and salt and pepper, then straining out the veggies.  I never made broth before, so I was scared I was going to ruin the recipe, but it was wonderful!  I also added a little bit of basil and oregano.  I think fresh spinach is the best to use. I've used frozen spinach in soups before, and I'm not a fan of the texture, it gets slimy.  This is a very light and healthy and fresh tasting soup.  I will be making it again!

reviews.review_text: This is sooooo good.  Would be great as is I'm sure, but I always have to toy with recipes...so here goes: I reduced the chicken broth to make it a bit thicker and added italian stewed tomatoes to beef up the flavor.  If you buy the already chopped frozen spinach, you can add it right in at the end and no need to defrost.  I also used frozen tortellini and brought the broth/onions/garlic to a boil to cook the pasta (before I added the cooked spinach). What a wonderfully hearty, tasty quick soup. items.label: Uncle Bill's Green Split Pea With Hambone Soup
items.name: Uncle Bill's Green Split Pea With Hambone Soup
items.description: Make and share this Uncle Bill's Green Split Pea With Hambone Soup recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Rinse peas well in cold water and add to a large cooking pot.
Measure 8 cups of water and add to cooking pot.
Bring to boil, remove from heat, cover and let sit for 1 hour.
Return to stove and bring back to boil.
Add ham bone, carrots, onions, celery, bay leaf, beef bouillon, salt, peppercorns and dried thyme.
Reduce heat to simmer, cover and cook for about 1 to 1 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Remove ham bone and cut off any remaining ham, cut into bite size pieces and return to soup.
Discard ham bone.
If there are big pieces of ham in the soup, remove, cut into bite size pieces and return to soup.
Remove bay leaf and discard.
Adjust seasonings to taste.
If you desire a smooth soup, then puree' in batches in a food processor or blender.
Or eat the soup without puree'ing.
If soup is too thick, add more water to your desired consistency.
Beef broth or chicken broth may be added, just reduce the water by the amounts used.
Smoked ham hocks are excellent to use instead of a ham bone.
If there is not enough ham on the ham bone, then add additional ham of your choice.
You may also use about 1/4 teaspoon of Liquid Hickory Smoke, to get a smokey flavor.
You may also use whole peas, but it will take a bit longer to cook these peas so that they are tender.

reviews.review_text: I've made this many times over the years with variations of ingredients/seasonings and it has always turned out wonderfully. Very hard to make a mistake unless you forget it and let it burn like I did once. I often use my large slowcooker with a lining to make this. The peas do not need soaking ever as the packaging will tell you. I dump the peas that have been sorted for rocks and rinsed right into the slowcooker with whatever liquid you prefer, water, broth, etc along with onion and garlic and seasonings. Set it for low for 6 hours and then let it switch to warm for two more adding frozen carrots if you want.. You can stir it periodically and if it isn't as thick as you like, remove the lid during the warm hours and it will thicken right up. Add more liquid if too thick for your tastes. Super easy and the liner makes clean up a breeze!

attributes.source_text: if it isn't as thick as you like

reviews.review_text: So far this is turning out pretty good.  It still has a little bit more to go on the stove.  There is a little story behind this.  When I was a little girl I had a baby sitter that would always feed us "Split Pea" soup, but it  was like just mashed up peas, and when I was little I could not stand peas.  Growing up, I never wanted any part of the yuckie green soup that I remembered from my child hood.  Well, when I was on my luch break one of my co-workers was eating a soup that looked great, and sure enough it was Split Pea soup, not like I remembered though.  She let me try some and it was delicious, who would of thunk.  So, I decided that I wanted to try and make it, and here I am making it.  Thank you for helping come over one of my fears of PEAS!! Mt only down fall with this is that I am not sure how it is sopose to taste, so far its pretty yummy.

...for years I'd been using the Fontier Soup kit for split peas. Last year, something about the spices changed (maybe it was my palette) but I couldn't stand the taste. Fast forward to this year and the left over ham bone from Christmas Eve. I knew I wanted my split pea soup but I was hesitant because it's suppose to taste a certain way...and what if the recipe I make doesn't...the search started... I had found a recipe on another website that looked promising. I printed it and started to gather the ingredients when I realize that THAT recipe didn't call for a ham bone. Now, I know I could have just followed the recipe anyway, added the ham bone and hoped for the best...but...this is the meal I look forward to every year (my husband is not crazy about split pea soup so it's me against the entire soup pot) and I didn't want to mess this up. After additional searching, found this recipe...it seemed SO EASY...and the reviews were...SO GREAT!!! Now, I did change it up a bit...I took the advise of another reviewer and sauteed the onions, carrots, celery...and two minced garlic cloves in a little olive oil before I added the water. I also used two teaspoons of "Better Than Bouillon Beef" cause I already had that at home AND I used two bay leaves instead of one (just cause my grandmother always used two). THANK YOU WILLIAM UNCLE BILL!!!! THIS is how I remember my grandmother's split pea soup tasting. I'd never imagine to use beef broth instead of chicken but man, it really adds to the flavor. I'm so so happy to have found your recipe. it's already been printed and added to my recipe book. HAPPY NEW YEAR!!

5 stars all the way around the table!  I have always prided myself in my split pea soup (our ingredients are near identical) but this method will now replace mine.  I am convinced that soaking the dried peas in the hot water for 1 hour (w/o seasonings) makes a HUGE difference. This soup is much smoother in consistency than any other split pea soup I have had or made.  I used chicken broth, more thyme as pinches can vary, no beef bouillon cuz I forgot, and a smoked butt. I have always used a stick blender at the end, that said, this soup blended up smoother, no kidding! My husband could not stop praising this soup. I'm so glad we have some leftover for lunch today. YUM!  My recipe is now out the window and this recipe is replacing it. Thanks for sharing this gem, Uncle Bill!

reviews.review_text: Wow. I love split pea soup, but this is just the best--with some minor tweaks. I used only ten cups of liquid-half water, half chicken stock and it was still a little bit much. Also, I used just a pinch of salt, since the stock had some. My husband just finished his third bowl and can't stop raving about it. (And I thought my previous recipe was pretty good--this is GREAT!) reviews.review_text: Used 8 cups low sodium chicken broth (therefore omitted salt and bouillon).  Added 4 hamhocks for flavor...After about 1/5 hours, removed hocks and poured soup in to blender and set to purree for about 20-30 seconds.  Then back in pot.  Then realized there was absolutely no meat on the hocs.  Sent DH to the HoneyBaked Ham store and they actually sold a ham bone with a few slices on it (they say they can't keep them in stock - who knew?)  Chopped up the ham (removing the crust) about 4 good slices and simmered about 1 hr more - the longer the simmer, thicker it gets.  If you are eating that day, this will be fine.  Leave thinner if you are refrigerating and eating the next day.  DH loved it as did I - great flavor, simple filling delicious.  Any time I see it's an Uncle Bill recipe, I know we will be savouring every bite.  Thanks!

reviews.review_text: DH requested Split Pea Soup and I decided to give this recipe a try.  I didn't have any ham bones in the freezer so I bought 2 smoked ham hocks and used a ham steak for the chunked meat (hocks gross me out so I used for flavor only.) Following the advice of others I used 5 cups of water and 5 cups chicken stock and upped the thyme to 1/4 tsp. After the 1st step of having the beans sit for 1 hour, I simmered for 2 hours and the texture was perfect the soup was thick but not globby, no blending needed and there was still chunks of carrot.  Next time I make I will make sure to use low sodium broth and possibly lose the additional salt. It was a bit on the salty side the way I made it but easily fixed.  Great soup - the family loved it!  Thanks for posting Uncle Bill.

reviews.review_text:
This is a great recipie. I can't imagine using 12 cups of liquid though. I only used 8 cups and it's still a little to watery for my liking. I agree with those who suggested using two bags of beans. I intend to add a second bag of beans to this batch then i'm sure it will be perfect. I used a ham bone but it was pretty clean so I cut up part of a ham steak as well. I also added garlic to this and only used chicken stock for the liquid. It's a great recipie. Perfect amount of veggies and seasoning. Thanks so much.

I have to say this gets better each day.  We had leftovers for lunch and my 3 year old asked for seconds.  I changed my vote from 4 to 5 and i'd go higher if I could.

We had leftovers for lunch

reviews.review_text: WOW!!!  Superb!!  I can't believe how flavorful this is and how low in fat!!!!!  My husband is one of those guys that "thinks" he hates something even though he hasn't tried it in 20 years.  He scoffed at my making this..and I was making it for myself...took one taste and went crazy for this!  I wish I would have doubled the recipe now!  I bought pork hocks from the grocery store since I buy boneless hams...I followed the rest of the recipe just as stated and it was THE BEST!!!!!!  I didn't puree anything because I love the large bits of pea.  The consistency was perfect with the stated 8 cups of water and I diced up some cooked ham I'd made the night before to add.  Froze most of it and will thaw to eat daily for lunch.  Just LOVED it!  Thanks Uncle Bill!

attributes.source_text: will thaw to eat daily for lunch
I love the large bits of pea

reviews.review_text: I made this soup a couple of days ago as I had a ham bone left after having friends over for dinner. I have made pea soup a few times, but my husband and I are in California for the winter and forgot the recipe at home. So, I looked up this one, and am so glad I did. This is the best pea soup I have ever made, I chopped all the vegtables up in a chopper and added the drippings that I had from cooking the ham. I added 10 cups of water plus the drippings, also added some garlic. As I said this was perfect and it was so good as the weather here in Palm Springs has cooled off this week with the storms coming so it was a real treat. We had some for dinner tonight with my homemade bread and it was a perfect dinner. Will definatley make this again.

attributes.source_text: We had some for dinner tonight
it was a perfect dinner

reviews.review_text: This soup is fantastic! And for all those who thought that there was too much water, I would have loved to have been there the next day when they went to reheat it for another serving - it thickens up so much you can hold the pot upside down and it would stay - LOL.. I always, always make pea soup the day before I want to serve it, exactly for that reason. This recipe was about the same as the one I've always used, but the addition of thyme and bay were new to me and added so much more flavor.. this is the one I will always use from now on. I used smoked hocks this time, for I generally only have a ham bone like once a year.. anyhow, thanks for posting this!

attributes.source_text: it thickens up so much you can hold the pot upside down and it would stay

reviews.review_text: I used 2 bay leaves, 1 lb bag of baby carrots (remember to cut them up), 2 chicken bouillon cubes, 2 pinches thyme, water and liquid smoke (used the extra spices because mine are old). No salt added. Very good. Also added extra diced ham because there was not enough on the ham bone. Cooked for 9 hours in crockpot on low.  It was not done, so I turned it on high for 3 hours. At 1 hour, it was done enough for me, at 3 hours, it was done enough for dh. Total crock pot time: 12 hours. Used the 4 qt crock. Next time, use the 6 quart to make sure there is enough room to add things like more ham and not boil over.

I like lighter broths. When I first mixed the ingredients, it didn't look like there was enough liquid so I added 3 cups of water. Even having done that, I wish I hadn't used the salt. I used low sodium chicken broth (1 can) and sodium free chicken bouillon, and still feel the ham would have been enough to flavor the soup. That being said, the soup is outrageous. I reserved the last of our ham and cubed it, and added it at the end. I did not use the boiled-for-an-hour ham that was on the bone. Makes a nice dog treat, does nothing for me. Pureed the whole soup to a drinkable consistency. Could have sold it in a restaurant, with homemade, buttery croutons on top. My first try, too! Thanks.

attributes.source_text: Pureed the whole soup to a drinkable consistency

reviews.review_text: This is one of the best-tasting soups I've ever made.  I used some chicken broth, as you mentioned -- about 6 cups low-sodium broth and 2 cups water.  I didn't have to adjust any of the seasonings or proportions in the recipe -- I can always count on Uncle Bill to post a recipe that is a 10-star; I never make one and then think I will tweak it next time.  They're always perfect just as written. I pureed half of the soup in the blender; this made a nice and thick soup with still some texture. The three of us finished this in one night, with some crusty rolls.  I can't wait to make it again, it's SO good.  Thanks for sharing your recipe.

attributes.source_text: this made a nice and thick soup

reviews.review_text:
Revision "So, I am making it AGAIN today....I am changing my rating to a 5....My father in law really put a wrench in the rating and it really does deserve 5 stars!!!!!!!!!!"

All I can say is YUM! This was a really easy soup to make and was really delicious. I followed the directions exactly as suggested. I served it for my in laws and my father in law is not a fan of split pea soup in general. He gave it 3.5 stars! I thought that was pretty good for someone who actually doesn't like the stuff at all! I will definitely make this again next year after the thanksgiving ham is left over. It was wonderful. I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 because that was the average was from all of the four raters who ate it!

attributes.source_text: I served it for my in laws
He gave it 3.5 stars

reviews.review_text: A good recipe and definitely worth a try if anyone has any doubts.  However, cooked as directed, either the amount of water was too much or the amount of split peas was too little, because I wound up with a watery soup and had to double the cooking time (uncovered) to achieve the right thickness.  I would also edit the recipe and include more specific direction for the amount of ham to be added, instead of suggesting the ham bone scraps.  Each ham bone can be different, so without specifics, each pot of soup can also be different, making it difficult to get the desired result from each person using this recipe.

Made 12 cups of water and a lb of split peas (about 2 cups).  Great flavor, the split peas were mostly broken down by the end of the cooking time and the consistency was thin with a split pea remnants on the bottom of the pot.  I like my soup a little thicker so I raised the pot up to a rolling boil for about 10 minutes and stirred with a metal spoon most of the time.  This caused the split peas to disintegrate and stay in suspension, giving me a soup with the consistency of a cream of mushroom type soup.  More to my likening.

I will definitely be making this again.  Thanx Uncle Bill

attributes.source_text: the consistency was thin
the consistency of a cream of mushroom type soup

reviews.review_text: Uncle Bill we loved this. It's getting cooler is Qld, Aust now and this was perfect. I grated my carrot and used bacon hocks which my butcher cut up into smaller pieces for me.  I also used the full 12 cups of water and I'm glad I did. It ended up simmering on the stove all afternoon which meant that I didn't need to puree as the split peas and veggies were so very soft - yum. I took the lid off and turned it up slightly higher allowing the soup to reduce down. Both my 2 and 4 year olds loved this. Served with Kittencals Delicious Cheesy Parmesan Garlic Bread Recipe #105726. Thanks for sharing a wonderful recipe :)

attributes.source_text: the split peas and veggies were so very soft
Both my 2 and 4 year olds loved this

reviews.review_text:
Oh, Uncle Bill, this was just perfect for the cold weather we've been having.  My partner rated it better than her mother's split pea soup, and  she doesn't say that very often at all.  
As usual, wonderfully clear instructions and this came together so well.  
A couple of changes were made - subbed bacon bones for the ham bone, and I used 2 cups of beef stock and 10 cups of water in place of the bouillon cubes since we find they add too much salt for our taste.  
Thank you so much for recommending this recipe - it was exactly what we were looking for and we''ll be making this often.

attributes.source_text: perfect for the cold weather we've been having
My partner rated it better than her mother's split pea soup

items.label: Greek-Style Turkey Burgers
items.name: Greek-Style Turkey Burgers
items.description: The best turkey burgers i have ever tried .... I freeze left-overs, and heat in the microwave later ...
instructions: Combine all the ingredients in a large bowl.
Form into 4 patties, then grill.
I have served this on regular burger buns with tomatoes and mayo, and on pita with tahini, tomatoes and lettuce.

reviews.review_text: Oh Wow! I made this exactly as posted, and it was fabulous.  I ate this on Arnold Select Sandwich Thins, something new I found at the grocery store.  I can't stand the pita bread at the grocery store, and didn't have time to run to the greek market for fresh!  These sandwich thins were a cross between a pita and a hamburger bun, perfect for this burger!  Next time I'll throw some cucumbers and sliced onions on the bun with the burger.  And mix up some tzatziki sauce to use instead of the mayo.  Thanks so much for posting this recipe.  I loved it!  I made this for Zaar Chef Alphabet Soup Tag!

Wow! This was so awesome! I wasn't expecting this to taste as wonderful as it did. I'd give it more than 5 stars. I didn't even use the full cup of Feta. I bought the smaller one at the store by mistake. I can only imagine it with more!!! I made my patties four hours before cooking so the flavors would meld a bit. I served them on pita, with lettuce, tomato and topped them with Egyptian Garlic Yogurt Cucumber Salad Recipe #200504 . I even love this without sauce. I made two with black olives for me and two without. The burgers without olives were still great but think the black olives gave it extra great flavor. I'm thrilled, what a great way to make ground turkey taste good. I'll be making this very often. THANK YOU!

WOW !   I love Greek food and wondered at first about turkey and greek?    But you made a believer out of me.  Our guests loved the burgers along with a greek salad.   A few other posters complained about the consist not holding up and falling apart.  Suggest use a little less olive oil and put the patties in the fridge for 30 minutes before grilling and make sure the grill is seasoned and the grates are not sticky and you will be fine.   Man oh man were they good.  This is my go to recipe from now on.   Thanks najwa!    13 years later and your recipe is still going strong.  Be proud you are headed to the recipe hall of fame!

attributes.source_text: I love Greek food
Our guests loved the burgers

reviews.review_text: My boyfriend and I just taste tested these (we're now waiting on sweet potato wedges to bake before making the patties). DE-LI-CIOUS! We followed the recipe exactly, using ground turkey breast because the store was out of the other. It's so flavorful and tastes just like something we'd find at our favorite Mediterranean restaurant. I give this recipe infinite stars. We will be serving it in pita pockets with lettuce, tomato and plain yogurt (i'd love to try it with tzatziki). I wanted to do baked zucchini fries on the side but the zucchinis are so small right now, I went with baked sweet potato wedges.

attributes.source_text: tastes just like something we'd find at our favorite Mediterranean restaurant
My boyfriend and I just taste tested these

reviews.review_text: Used 1 1/4 lbs. of 93% turkey and adjusted all seasonings proportionately except for the feta (about 4 oz.) and olives.  This resulted in nice, big patties that made you feel like you were indulging yourself, but still only weighed in at about 265 relatively low fat calories each.  I was a little concerned about grilling these since they were so tender in consistency, but I slid them off the plate onto the grill and they didn't stick one bit!  Ate with whole wheat buns, a slice of onion and homemade tzatziki with a side of simple salad with more tzatziki on top.  Delicious taste reminiscent of gyro meat, juicy and tender.  Microwaved for a minute the next day and still juice and tender!  My favorite turkey burger!

attributes.source_text: reminiscent of gyro meat
juicy and tender
juicy and tender
still juice and tender

reviews.review_text: This was the BEST burger of any type of meat I have EVER had! I used the pre-packaged 85/15 Turkey. I included the Basil. The burgers rested in the fridge for about an hour before pan-frying in olive oil and 1/2 tbs butter. I lightly salted the exterior only of the turkey burger. To Serve: I brushed Whole Grain White buns with olive oil and sprinkled with toasted Italian Seasoning left on the pan after baking some waffle fries, then toasted buns in oven. I served with tomato, red onion, mayo, tahini & bread n butter pickles. It was SO good!

I didn't have Feta cheese, but I had everything else, so I substituted shredded parmesan (bagged) in place of Feta and all I can say is THANK YOU! These were great! Very moist and delicious! I grilled them for about 11 minutes...6 minutes Side A and 5 minutes Side B (be sure and oil your grill well because they stick a little too-possibly because I used parmesan?) I served them on the new Oro Wheat Sandwich Thins with grilled onions and ketchup/mayo.  Anyway, they were thick and beautiful!  I was going to submit a photo, but I was hungry and...hey don't judge me! :-)

attributes.source_text: Very moist
they were thick

reviews.review_text: AWESOME and EASY! I'm not normally a fan of turkey burgers because most seem so bland but this recipe has changed my mind. I really enjoyed making and eating this! I do regret not having any feta on hand but loathed to run out to the grocery store. Otherwise I did make as is with the exception of adding some olive oil to the mix as well as slathering some on before cooking on my cast iron grill pan. I served inside half pitas with tzatziki sauce, tomatoes, lettuce and cucumbers. Thanks for a great recipe najwa! This will be going into my "favorites".

I have been planning on making these burgers after I got some lean turkey on sale.  I followed the recipe except I omitted the olives.  I was worried that my BF who is not a huge olive fan would not like them.  I served these on the 40 minute buns (Recipe #183081) and Tzatziki (Recipe #287845).  This recipe deserves the fantastic reviews and I encourage others to make these burgers.  I did cook them in an electric skillet as my grill seems to always break my burgers apart.
Thank you for posting.

Lovely burgers! I'm not crazy about ground poultry, but I know it's supposed to be healthier than MOO, so I tried it and was pleasantly surprised!  This was so packed full of flavor, my tastebuds had a party! I made mine with kalamata olives and served the burgers on onion rolls with the delicious Recipe #59336 to dip/spread.  Unfortunately, I didn't have lettuce or tomato, but honestly, with this much flavor and texture, coupled with the Recipe #59336, you really don't need them. I can imagine it on pitas with the veggies and tzatzki... mmmm.  Thanks for the great recipe, najwa!

Yum, Yum, Yum.  My DH is very into turkey burgers, so I'm trying to find variations to make a normally bland choice of ground meat stand out.  I used 3oz pre-crumbled feta and about 1/4 cup chopped kalamata olives and next time I might add more of the olives.  I used the Pasta Sprinkle herb mix from Penzeys instead of parsley and basil and subbed in garlic salt for the onion, garlic and pepper.  Yum, Yum!  Served on toasted wheat buns with broccoli salad on the side...Will definitely use again!

4 out of 5 because I didn't follow the recipe to the T.

I didn't have any italian seasoning on hand and didn't use the olives. I did substitute fresh parsley and onion for the dried/powdered variety.  Also, I squeezed a little lemon juice, added some of the zest and 1 garlice clove (that I grated on a microplane - I love that microplane!).  I pan fried it in olive oil.  Served it with some tzatziki in a pita with more feta, fresh parsley, lettuce and tomatoes.  Delish!

I loved theese burgers, I skipped the bun, and ate two! I didnt have onion powder so I added some chopped green onions. I also ommited the parsley because I didnt have any. I used lowfat feta cheese, and for half the turkey I used ground white turkey to lower fat grams pretty well! I did not grill theese. If you do grill them, make sure to use foil or you will loose half your yummy burger in the coals!!!
 I rate theese excellent, and I will make them again, only next time I will make more, so there are leftovers for lunch!

Made these for a BBQ on Saturday and they turned out nicely! Used manzanilla olives stuffed with garlic instead of kalamata (husband doesn't like those for some reason). I made 2lbs of ground turkey for a total of 8 patties. The comments I received were all of praise and suggestions for next time: 1 tsp of salt for bring out the flavor of the turkey, a tbsp of olive oil to give it a little fat (so it doesn't stick to the grill), and grated parmesan/romano cheese to accent the feta. With all these ideas, I can't wait to make these again. :D

attributes.source_text: Made these for a BBQ on Saturday

reviews.review_text: Mmmm! We made these last night and they were great! Instead of onion powder we used finely chopped onion which added a bit of fresh flavor along with the fresh parsley we used instead of parsley flakes. Also, since it was rainy, we pan-fried rather than grilled. They were wonderful! I would have maybe added even a bit more feta if I had more, but then again I'm a real cheese fan. We ate them on whole-wheat buns brushed with olive oil and toasted in the oven. They go very well with dijon mustard I found and are quite easy. mmmm....

A yummy burger! I used 1/2 lb lean ground turkey & since I'm watching my calories-only 2 tbsp tomato basic garlic feta cheese. It worked out fine! Since my cheese was already seasoned, I cut the spices down a bit: 1/2 tsp italian seas, 1/4 tsp oregano, 1/4 tsp onion powder & 1/8 tsp garlic powder. Next time I might try some garlic salt instead of garlic powder. I left out the parsely, basil & olives since I'm just not an olive fan although I've tried to be. :-) Flavorful & filling!

These burgers are outstanding. Tonight is the 4th time I have served them and I have now added them to "family favorites." They are healthy and delish. I have served them on buns, toasted English muffins and tonight in Pita Pockets. We loved the pockets. I have served with tzatzki and fresh sliced onion. We enjoyed the burgers both ways. It is easy to eat healthy with burgers as good as these. The only change I made to the original recipe....I use Greek Oregano and fresh dill. Yum

WOW we had these for dinner last night and hubby even loved them.  What gandmothers won't do for their kids.  My Granddaughter won't eat 'cow' so we all have been looking for something that she will eat and won't be left out during family picnics.  I did make some adjustments.  Left out the olives - yuk!!!  I also reduced the basil to 1/2 teaspoon (it was optional anyway).  It was raining last night, so pan-fried in cast iron with a little EVOO.  This is a keeper recipe  :-D

attributes.source_text: we had these for dinner last night
hubby even loved them

reviews.review_text: My husband and I love Greek food especially after living next door to our Greek landlord when we were in Germany (yeah, I know).  I had 1/2 lb of ground turkey and 1/2 lb of ground pork in my freezer I needed to use which really helped the flavor and the consistency (turkey tends to crumble).  I only added 1/2 c of feta and it still had great flavor.  I served it with Tzatziki (recipe #310246) which was a perfect compliment to the flavor of the burger.  Delicious!

attributes.source_text: My husband and I love Greek food

reviews.review_text: DH didn't sound too thrilled when he asked what was for lunch and I told him greek turkey burgers. I had made greek burgers using a different zaar recipe.  He said they were ok but probably don't make them again.  He isn't a big fan of ground turkey but he was surprised by these. I used a combo of green and black olives.  He said they were so much better than the ones he had before.  I made a greek pasta salad to go with it. A great summer meal!  Thanks so much!

attributes.source_text: what was for lunch
greek turkey burgers
he was surprised by these
He said they were so much better than the ones he had before

items.label: Biscuits
items.name: Biscuits
items.description: Make and share this Biscuits recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Preheat oven to 425 F Mix first 4 ingredients together in a bowl.
Cut in butter with a pastry blender or a fork, or two knives, until crumbly.
Add milk.
Stir until it forms a ball.
Add a bit more milk if necessary to make a soft dough.
Roll or pat to 1 inch thick. (I usually pat the dough).
Cut into circles with a biscuit cutter or a floured glass.
Arrange on a greased baking sheet.
Bake in 425 F for about 10- 12 minutes or until risen and nicely browned. (in my oven it usually takes 15 minutes).
This is supposed to make 12, but I almost always only get 11 biscuits, with the size of the glass that I use.

Variations: Try adding some fresh or dried herbs. Some good pairings are basil and oregano, or parsley and fresh ground black pepper, or thyme and garlic, or add some grated sharp or old cheddar cheese.

reviews.review_text: Excellent biscuits!  I've made them twice now and they've turned out soft and moist each time.  I use butter, not margarine, and reduce the sugar to 1 tbsp because I like to serve them with SOS.  The first time I made them, the dough was perfect and I patted them into a rectangle and cut them into squares.  The second time I made them, the dough was stickier, so I patted them into biscuit shapes and dropped them on a cookie sheet.  They were perfect both times.  I found it helps to wet my hands when patting out the dough.  Thanks for a biscuit recipe that doesn't call for shortening!

attributes.source_text: they've turned out soft and moist each time
they've turned out soft and moist each time

reviews.review_text: These were the best biscuits I have ever made.  I was interested since I had never had biscuits with that much sugar in them and also made with butter.  They just had a hint of sweetness and were the most moist biscuits I have ever eaten.  I usually find that most biscuits are a little dry...but not these.  My dough was on the sticky side...but I didn't want to ruin the texture so instead of adding flour and rolling the dough to cut them out...I simply took a handfull of dough and patted it with my palm onto the cooky sheet.  I would not make them in any other way...they made 9 nice large biscuits puffs.  Terrific recipe!!!

attributes.source_text: They just had a hint of sweetness
were the most moist biscuits I have ever eaten

reviews.review_text: I am a baking novice, but now that I am a mom I have been trying to learn by baking at least one new thing a week (emphasis on 'trying') that doesn't come from a box.  I needed biscuits for a chicken casserole and, uh-oh, i was out of bisquick...what to do?!  I found this recipe, and these turned out delicious...even using margarine (all that I had on hand)! I also just shaped the dough in my hands instead of cutting out, like some other reviewers, because I was short on time.  This will be my go-to biscuit recipe from now on. (i'll save the bisquick for the waffles :)

For the time involved in making these, they were 5 star biscuits!  Simple stock items is all that is required to make them.  I rolled them out and used a mid sized cup to cut them and I ended up with 9 biscuits. They went well with the gravy and other breakfast items and my dish was empty when breakfast was over.  They were a hit with the grandkids and adult kids alike.  The grandkids always enjoy watching home made items coming out of grandma's kitchen.  So thank you for a tasty and simple recipe.  I wouldn't say these were the most amazing biscuits I have ever made, but for time and difficulty level, I'd say they are 5 star! ;)

attributes.source_text: other breakfast items
They were a hit with the grandkids
adult kids alike

reviews.review_text:
I just made some as a trial run for tomorrow night, when I have company coming.

I have *never* been happy with biscuits I've made before, they've always been too dry or floury or something.

These were fabulous.  And so easy!  I used the food processor and did NOT roll out the dough, just kind of scooped handfuls and baked on silicone baking sheets.   I will never roll out biscuit dough again after doing it this way.  They looked better too, imo.

Tomorrow night I think I may add some grated cheddar to them and drizzle garlic butter on top, so that they'll be like the ones at Red Lobster.  Yum!

What a great recipe to have tucked away.  These are definately better than store bought although I'm not known for my patience and patted the dough down too much.  Next time, I'll be sure to leave the dough at a full inch.  These tasted great though.  Served with a Sunday morning breakfast and were enjoyed by my family.  I did get 12 out of the recipe but I think it was because my dough was too thin.  I also put a little melted butter on the top so they would brown up nicely.  Thanks for the recipe, I'll be using it often.

attributes.source_text: Served with a Sunday morning breakfast
were enjoyed by my family

reviews.review_text: Very good biscuit. I used bread flour, omitted the salt (was using salted butter) and I  cut the sugar back to 1T and 1 tsp because I was making then for sausage gravy. I didn't roll out either, just patted the dough into an 8x8 baking dish. Came out with very fluffy, very light biscuits. Baked them half way, then pulled them out and brushed butter on the top and let it drizzle down the sides. Were so good that we didn't even want the gravy with them! Been looking for a good biscuit to go with sausage gravy. This one is it.

attributes.source_text: very fluffy, very light biscuits
very fluffy, very light biscuits

reviews.review_text: Finally a biscuit recipe I can call a keeper.  We love Pillsbury Country Biscuits but I was looking for a homemade version and this is definitely it.  I tried this recipe for the first time but only added 1 Tbsp sugar and instead of butter or margarine, I used grapeseed oil.  Increased the milk to 7/8 cup.  So easy to make.  All ingredients on hand.  Made 14 biscuits and down in 12 minutes.  No kneading required.  No mixers.  Can't ask for a simpler recipe.  Clean up was a breeze.  Thanks for sharing your recipe.

Oh my goodness. This was my first time making home made biscuits.I was always too afraid. Thought they were just way too hard.You have to roll them out and cut them. Needing space I do not have. But these were awesome. I just patted them in my hand like patties. Made them a bit large but they were grrreat! I will have to quadruple the recipe next time. No one in my family believed they were homemade. They all thought they were from a box mix. Yeah like something this good could be mass manufactured. Thanx for sharing.

Quick, easy, tasty, and sans shortening!  Omitted sugar and added 1 tbsp. honey with milk.  Mixed and shaped biscuits using only a butter knife and a spatula; hands off = minimized heating of dough and dough wastage.  Stated amounts were perfect; no adjustments needed.  A major hit at dinner; breadbasket was empty in no time.  BF's bro was over for dinner.  He's my best measure of success, because he's so picky and is very obvious in how much or how little he likes anything.  After getting his 5th chicken leg and more home fries, he asked for the breadbasket yet again.  When we showed him the empty basket, he said he wouldn't eat without more biscuit, pushed his plate away, and crossed his arms emphatically. ^_^  I split the biscuit I'd been slowly savoring with him since everyone else had devoured every biscuit they'd picked up.  Next time: only 1/2" tbsp. honey, more cheese, savory seasonings, a butter or egg wash, and more savory ingredients, e.g. sauteed onions, bacon...  I'm thinking biscuit pockets tossed in the freezer for variety alongside the pizza dough and pie dough pockets I make, which my BF loves to take to work and reheat in the toaster oven.  I'll try increasing the milk and decreasing the butter,  since this will be a regular rotation recipe.  PS: For sausage sandwich-size biscuits, this recipe makes 4 biscuit sandwiches.

attributes.source_text: A major hit at dinner
he's so picky and is very obvious in how much or how little he likes anything

reviews.review_text:
Woot!!!!  These were perfect!!!!  I've tried so many times to make biscuits from scratch in the past and I failed miserably. 
I was a bit hesitant to make these because I'm a poor student and I was pretty much using the VERY LAST of all my ingredients.  I had about 3 cups of flour, a few tablespoons of sugar, a bunch of salt, a stick and a half of butter, and some EXPIRED baking powder.
I was hungry and craving biscuits, though, so I took the risk.  I'm SOOO happy I did.  These were great!  Thank you SO much!!!

Just right! Technique-wise, I improvised. I feel compelled to share how (in case there are others like me). I have no rolling pin;  I have no biscuit cutter. So, I patted the dough into a spring-form pan and baked for 15 minutes. Once baked, I popped off the round edge off the pan, slid the uni-biscuit onto the cutting board, and sliced it into squares. There was no compromise on taste, even my Southern-bred husband approved, though he did seem a bit suspicious about the shape at first.

attributes.source_text: even my Southern-bred husband approved

reviews.review_text:
Super easy to make and SOOOO Moist! =) 
I was craving Biscuits but had no buttermilk and started searching for a recipe. When I went to make them I realized I only had 1/2 cup of milk. So even with 1/2 cup milk and 1/4 cup vanilla soy milk the recipe was still amazing. 
Also, I just patted the dough down with my hands and used a glass to cut them so as not to overwork the dough. One of the Best Biscuits I have tasted. They were gone in minutes!

attributes.source_text: SOOOO Moist

reviews.review_text: Never made biscuits before and picked this recipe for its great reviews and simplicity. Turned out awesome! Better than any biscuit I've ever had, everyone else thought the same and raved about them. Patted the dough out on a silicone baking sheet and cut into squares with a blunt knife, pulled them apart to separate and they baked up beautifully without having to dirty the counter or grease the baking sheet. They rose so high, made a great fluffy biscuit.

attributes.source_text: made a great fluffy biscuit

reviews.review_text:
My 19 year old son wanted to make biscuits and gravy for breakfast one morning. He asked me if I had a good recipe for biscuits. I have several, but since he had never made biscuits, I wanted to try and find a simple recipe for him. These were so light and delicious!
I plan to trash all of my biscuit recipes, as I have found a new one.
My son is planning to get married next spring. I plan to put this recipe in a new cook book that I am preparing for his fiance and himself.

items.label: Bev's Macaroni and Cheese
items.name: Bev's Macaroni and Cheese
items.description: This is the recipe I have been using for Macaroni and Cheese since the beginning of time! Truly a classic and a staple on our family table. I hope you enjoy it as much as we do. A great side dish to be served with my Meatloaf Barbecue Style!
instructions: Melt butter in medium saucepan.
Stir in flour, salt, mustard and pepper until smooth.
Remove from heat and gradually stir in milk until smooth.
Stirring constantly, cook over medium heat until thickened (about 10 minutes).
Remove from heat.
Stir in 1 1/2 cups cheese until melted.
Combine cheese mixture with macaroni in greased 2 quart casserole.
Sprinkle remaining cheese on top.
Bake in 375 degree oven for 25 minutes or until lightly browned.
Makes 6 servings.

reviews.review_text: Original review 18 Feb 08: I had one person to impress with this recipe: a very picky 9 year old boy. He went back for thirds. As long as he was happy, that's all that mattered. My work is finished. (I added bread crumbs to the top because I love bread crumbs on my mac 'n' cheese.) Prepped the casserole one day in advance although I don't think next time I would do that. For quicker preparation a food processor was very handy for grating the cheese because I doubled the recipe. Thanks for posting. cg Update, after reading through some of the reviews again I found it necessary to say that if you use a whisk to stir the flour and milk together it will break up any lumps. Use a whisk also to stir the cheese into the milk. I forgot to mention in my initial review that I decreased the salt by half, used white pepper instead of black, added a splash of Worcestershire sauce to the milk/cheese mixture (because that's what my Mom did.) Use a sharp cheese. What else? As close to my Mom's macaroni and cheese that I have no doubt they are the same recipe. thanks

attributes.source_text: a very picky 9 year old boy. He went back for thirds

reviews.review_text: !! I didn't realize I never reviewed this!!!  Bev, we love, love, love your Mac and Cheese... I had a really hard time finding a decent mac & cheese recipe on 'Zaar that didn't contain Velveeta (yuck!) and I really struck gold with this one.  We make this all the time- sometimes adding little extras like minced salami, onions, red bell peppers, etcetera but its always fabulous.  One recommendation I would make, though- mix less cheese into the sauce and put more on top.  The sauce kind of steals the distinct cheesy flavor (this is true and we even use extra sharp cheddar) and the browned cheesy crust is so tasty, besides.  Thank you so much for posting a recipe for mac and cheese that uses ACTUAL cheese and tastes GREAT.

attributes.source_text: the distinct cheesy flavor

reviews.review_text: I think this is my highest rated recipe EVER! Wow--- reading the ingredients, you wouldn't think you would get a super creamy mac and cheese, but this IS IT! This is my second time making mac and cheese- the first was a disaster (horrible recipe) but THIS is a keeper!!! I made it two nights in a row! (I halved it and DH and I ate the whole thing). It doesn't re-heat too well, but it's so easy to make I didn't mind making up another batch the next day! I will be passing this on to all my friends and family! (oh, and I used skim milk in mine... the key is to WAIT and really let it thicken!)  **EDIT:  You HAVE to make this with SHARP cheddar--- i used mild the other day and it did not taste NEARLY as good as when I made it with Sharp!

attributes.source_text: super creamy mac and cheese
DH and I ate the whole thing

reviews.review_text: Bev, I chose this recipe in a hurry for a side dish -- I have my own Mac and Cheese recipe but yours is BETTER! It's simpler than mine too. If folks follow your recipe to the letter, they will come out with a fine batch of super-tasting macaroni and cheese. I did make VERY slight changes to suit out tastes, but not many. I used all the cheese listed, in the sauce, and sprinked the top with additional cheese, about 1 1/2  cups. The next time, I will add about 3/4 cup of grated Parmesan to the sauce just to gild the lily. Since I also doubled the recipe, I did bake it longer (about twice as long) but I just left it in until it was pretty much lightly browned all across the top. At the table, I used the salt shaker a little but my wife said that it was perfectly salted as it was. This is DELICIOUS macaroni and cheese, Bev -- the best I've ever eaten, no kidding. I'm going to be going over the rest of your recipes with a magnifying glass -- anyone who can come up with this one is bound to have plenty more great recipes. Thank you so much for posting! pat.

reviews.review_text: This isn't a bad recipe by any means. I put it all together about like what was said. I also threw some extra cheese on the top at the end like some recommended. Immediately when my mom had her first bite, she noticed that it tasted very familiar. We were suprised to find that it tasted exactly like Stouffer's frozen macaroni and cheese. Maybe it was the sharp cheese I used (Happy Farms sharp cheddar from Aldi). Perhaps if I ever make it again, I will use a really nice, exotic extra sharp cheddar that is much tangier than others. You can't go wrong with the recipe, but with all the trouble I went through to make it, it's easier to buy Stouffer's.

This has lately gotten so many reveiws that I just couldn't keep myself from trying it at last.  It is good!  It is very, very good!  I will for sure make this again, as all the elements for "comfort" are there.  I think (and according to my upbringing) I'll use evaorated milk for extra richness.  I loved the recipe as is, and used 2% milk.....I usually only by 1%, but the store was out.  I think if you are going to indulge in such a recipe "indulgence" should be part of the recipe....thus, my "whole evaporated" milk leaning.  All that said, it's a great recipe, and I don't see why anyone could not LOVE this simple indulgence.  I'll just tweak it with my own prefs!  Thanks for sharing!

This is divine! I've never made macaroni and cheese from scratch and this is so delicious! I followed the recipe for the sauce exactly except for adding a little more cheese in the sauce then it calls for (because we like extra-cheesy food). It was perfect - lightly tangy and very flavorful. I think the dry mustard really makes it taste so good (although it doesn't taste like mustard at all). I used mild cheddar cheese and skim milk and I can't say enough about how good it came out. The only gray area for me was the measurement of the macaroni. I believe it should read 8 ounces dry macaroni (then cook it) rather than 8 ounces of cooked macaroni. And actually it made so much sauce that I was able to use a whole 12 ounce package of rotini pasta. Super good - a real keeper. I'll make this over and over again! Thanks, Bev!

attributes.source_text: lightly tangy

reviews.review_text:
Holy Schneikes! Wow was this simple - and AWESOME!!!!!!!  I think you need to rename this recipe: "Perfect Mac and Cheese"!  Let me tell you something..... this almost never made it into the oven!  I started eating it right out of the pan while I was cooking it on the stove top!

 I like my mac & cheese a bit spicy so I always mix in some "Franks's Red Hot" or "Tabasco" sauce. I did taste this before adding putting it into the oven and adding the hot sauce and it was creamy, and gooey, and soooo yummy. Mmmmmmmm.  Also, hope you don't get angry, but I cut up some chicken hot dogs for protein and mixed that in.  Thanks for sharing this Bev!

reviews.review_text: If I could give more stars I would. Wonderful recipe, everyone loved it. It reminded me of Souffers, which is a compliment. Its the mustard that gives it that great flavor. I toyed with the idea of topping this with breadcrumbs or ritz cracker crumb but never got around to it which is fine, 'cause it doesn't need it. I left it under the broiler for a few minutes to brown the top really well and it was great. I also doubled the recipe and put it into a large round casserole. Next time I will use a more shallow one 'cause we fought over the top crust :-) Thanks for posting this great recipe.

My flour and butter stayed clumped up even after I added the milk, so I solved it by putting the milk mixture in a blender.

After I finished baking the macaroni and cheese, I let it cool on the table, then in the freezer to firm into a block.  I cut the block in-half, and wrapped each one in plastic wrap to store in the freezer for later.

A few days later I thawed one of the blocks and had some.  IMO it's similar to Stouffer's M&C, but better texture.  I used New York extra sharp cheddar.

I'm excited, because I'm confidant I can make macaroni and cheese anytime I want, and "nail it" every time.

I had a major craving for mac & cheese and didn't have the time to make my own family recipe (it take a long time) so I thought I'd try this one out for size. Similar to what another reviewer stated, the macaroni measurement is far is too low. I ended up boiling over 16 oz. of pasta for this recipe only to find out that it was so salty, I couldn't bear to eat it. items.label: Caramelized Chicken Wings
items.name: Caramelized Chicken Wings
items.description: Make and share this Caramelized Chicken Wings recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Place chicken in a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Mix the oil, soy sauce, ketchup, honey, garlic, salt and pepper and pour over the chicken.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for one hour or until sauce is caramelized.

reviews.review_text: I rate this recipe a 5 for the chicken, but a 10+ on pork chops with a variation in the cooking method.  I doubled the sauce and used approximately 1/2 cup on four frozen (previously seasoned) porkchops.  Because they were already seasoned, I omitted the salt and pepper from the recipe.  I placed the frozen pork chops in a skillet on med-high with some chicken broth (not quite covering the chops).  I allowed the chops to simmer until they thawed and began to cook through.  Then, I poured the sauce over the cops and increased the temperature.  I watched them closely, so as not to allow them to burn (due to the honey and ketchup).  I flipped the chops, so that they could carmelize and brown on both sides.  My husband could hardly wait for them to come out of the skillet...he devoured two in a matter of minutes.  Thank you so much for this delicious and different way to cook chicken & pork chops.  I will definitely make them again!!

attributes.source_text: My husband could hardly wait for them to come out of the skillet

reviews.review_text: Fantastic recipe! My husband and so enjoyed the chicken! Unfortunately I only had 2 lbs. of chicken on hand to use in this recipe, and after my husband and I ate the 2 lbs., I wished I'd of had the 3 lbs. of chicken. When I was mixing the ingredients, I used a low sodium soy sauce which I purchased at Festival Foods. The brand was Essential Everyday, and it only had 580 mg of sodium in it. I didn't add any salt, but I did use 2 cloves of garlic (minced). I did lightly grease the baking pan, before adding the chicken and the sauce, and I baked the chicken for 30 minutes, then flipped it over, and continued baking for another 30 minutes. And it was perfectly done and caramelized within the hour. I would bake as per the instructions, but just be sure to turn the chicken over after the first 30 minutes of baking. By the way I wanted to mention, while the chicken was baking away in the oven, my whole house smelled absolutely wonderful, kind'a like Chicken Teriyaki. I will definitely be making this chicken again! Thank you Theresa/Thunderbird for sharing this recipe. It's definitely a keeper!!

attributes.source_text: My husband and so enjoyed the chicken

reviews.review_text: After preparing this recipe many times and following the directions precisely, I've decided to re-rate it with four stars, rather than five. The sauce tastes great and the ease of preparation is good. However, following the recipe directions as written results in the wings "floating" in so much rendered fat that the marinade is completely diluted and the wings are almost "stewed." Thickening and cramelization just don't occur. So, I now put the wings in the oven for about 15 minutes and at the end of that time period, I drain off all the accumulated fat. I then add the sauce, making sure not to "drown" the wings. I turn the wings as they continue to cook and sometimes even adjust the oven to broil for the last few minutes to get the caramelization and sticky texture I want. I dress the wings with some chopped green onion and a few sesame seeds before serving.

attributes.source_text: to get the caramelization and sticky texture I want

reviews.review_text:
The only reason I haven't given 5 stars is because I adapted the receipe as per other peoples recommendations ....it turned out absolutely amazing but I can't see how the original recipe could have warranted 5 stars.
I used 2lb wings as thats allp had in the freezer, half cup sugar & half cup honey, dark soy sauce, 2 cloves garlic and sprinkled some sesame seeds on once out of the oven. As per another reviewers suggestion I used dark soy sauce as I don't like things too salty - this was perfect and any more salty I would not have been able to bear. I also cooked the wings for about 20 min before adding the sauce, to avoid the fat swimming issues that other reviewers had. 40 min after adding the sauce it just wasn't thickening and I was getting a bit bored and hungry to say the least, so I mixed a paste with some cornflour and a little water and mixed that into the sauce (having put the wings in a bowl momentarily) ....added the wings back in and returned to the oven for another 10min on 200 degrees c. On returning to the oven I Found the sauce had thickened and caramelised into a lovely thick jam like consistency and then stirred the wings around in this with a large slotted spoon to get them all coated in it. Then sprinkled on the sesame seeds. I would recommend leaving them for at least 5-10 min before putting anywhere near your mouth as the sauce is scorching and takes a while to cool due to the hot sugar. They were a fantastic hit with my boyfriend and am now planning to try next time with ribs. They are even more yummy when cold and would be great for a picnic or having in your lunch box, providing there's any left (make sure you pack loads of baby wipes though for cleaning yourself up!).

reviews.review_text:
I doubled this recipe...except for the soy sauce and honey. I used 3/4 of a cup of soy sauce and whatever honey I had left. I marinated them in the refrigerator for a couple of hours before cooking them, since I got home a couple of hours before hubby and wanted to have dinner done before he got home. I haven't tried them baked yet, but the sauce was good. A little too salty, but not terrible enough to not eat. I'm serving this with fries, since hubby got a choice of rice or fries. I'd have prefered rice, but that's what I get for giving an option. I'll let you know what we think.

ETA: Oh, my awesomeness! These were amazing. I should have listened to the other reviewers who baked them first then added the sauce. I ended dumping the sauce off into a bowl and basted them while they baked at 450* for another fifteen minutes while I waited for my fries to cook. They turned out very good this way. Maybe even better then baking them first.

My husband loved these, but I thought they were missing a zing of something.  I think I'll go with granulated garlic next time to see if that's it.  I cheated a bit to not heat up the house so much by pre-cooking my wings in the crock pot, then I poured the glaze over and cooked it on in about 20 minutes in the oven with convection and finishing up with broiler, turning once to coat as the sauce thickened.  I love how this sauce thickened and coated everything, and liked it more after it sat a bit as far as flavor.  I'll definitely try it again, even tho the carb count kept me from eating many, which my husband had no complaints over, either.  ;-)  Thanks for sharing.

I love how this sauce thickened

reviews.review_text: I have been craving wings lately and have a stash in the freezer that I bought when they went on sale...  I used a little over 2 lbs of wings so I cut down all the ingredients just slightly...  I know from experience that the kind of soy sauce I prefer ( a good mushroom soy) is saltier than your usual run of the mill... so I used only about of 1/4 of the called for amount.  I also drastically cut back on the honey...  I could hardly wait for them to come out of the oven!!!  They smelled so good.  I had them with some jasmine rice and it was just perfect.  They were so sticky, gooey, and lick your finger delicious!  Thanks for sharing!!!

reviews.review_text: Do not let the smell of this dish cooking put you off!!!!  Its actually very tasty!!!  I made this recipe exactly as directed and I have to say, the smell of it cooking really put me off.  But i'm so glad I gave it a chance because it really was good.  I also had a lot of extra sauce like other reviewers but a lot of the sauce did caramelize on the wings.  These wings had a good, sweet flavor which I like. The only thing I did not like about the taste of these wings is that it left a bit of an unpleasant aftertaste.  This may have just been my tastebuds though.  Other than that these wings were great!  Thanks for posting!

reviews.review_text: Delicious wings! After reading some of the reviews, I made the following adjustments...I used 1/3 cup brown sugar and 1/3 cup honey and 1/4 cup low sodium soy sauce and 1/4 cup regular soy sauce and about 1/2 teaspoon crushed red pepper. It had just the right salty/sweet/heat combination for our tastes. I baked the wings without the sauce for about 30 minutes then poured off the fat. While they were baking I heated the sauce at a low simmer on the stove for about 15 minutes to blend the flavors and thicken it a bit. Added sauce to chicken and tossed to cover the wings then back in the oven for about 45 minutes, turning every 10-15 minutes.They were perfect! Definitely a go-to appetizer from now on!

attributes.source_text: just the right salty/sweet/heat combination
just the right salty/sweet/heat combination

reviews.review_text: This was a great recipe! I seasoned my wings with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and some adobo seasoning and let marinate for about 3 hours. I threw all the sauce ingredients (plus about a tbsp of sesame seeds, and an additional tbsp of garlic) in a saucepan and brought to a boil, then turned down to a simmer.  After marinating, I cooked the wings at the stated temp. for about 30 minutes, drained off the fat, and poured the thickened sauce over the wings. After thoroughly coating each wing, I cooked for another 15 minutes. I then broiled for another few minutes. They were awesome!

These were really good!! I hate to review a recipe when I changed some of the ingredients, but to one their own right? After reading a lot of the reviews I had discovered that they were really salty and I am not a salt lover. So instead of using soy sauce I used dark soy sauce (which I have recently fallen in love with) it's a lot sweeter and not nearly as salty, I had to go to a specialty Asian market here. It made a phenomenal difference; I also split the honey with brown sugar (half cup of each) and doubled the garlic. They were really easy and really really delicious!! I highly recommend these with the dark soy sauce!!

I finally tried this recipe today and I could not believe the reaction from my kids and husband. They all said, "this is so good!". Picky eaters like them never say anything good except for ice cream or cookies. This chicken wings recipe is a keeper. 
since I didn't have wings, I used the thigh part.  I also made some changes to the sauce, I put paprika and garlic salt on top of the chicken first which gave more favor to the chicken. Then I added the rest of the thick sauce on top of that. I think if you use the wings, you should not use this method, it might be too salty.
The taste of my chicken reminds me of the delicious BBQ pork that I had in some good chinese restaurants. I might use the same sauce to make pork next time and see if it will turn out to be as good as the restaurant's BBQ pork.

reviews.review_text: This was a good recipe.  Following the reviews I baked the chicken for about 20 min without sauce at ~175C, drained the fat then added the sauce.  I then increased the oven to 190C and flipped the chicken about every 10 min for an hr until the sauce began to caramelize.  I did use the oven's broil option for the last 15 min to see if that would help the process.  My only changes to the sauce were to use 4 cloves of garlic and a bit of cayenne pepper.  The chicken came out tender and I thought the pepper added a nice balance to the honey.

While they were browning... I thickened the sauce in a saucepan with cornstarch and after thickening, poured about 3/4 over the chicken wings.  The remaining 1/4 of sauce, I served over mashed potatoes for my family and not only did my husband eat about 1/2 of them, my 1 year old ate more than I've ever seen her eat!  This is a keeper!  My family requested I make these once a week now!

I made this with wings, thighs and bone in breasts. All of them were good, wings were the best.
I halved the soy sauce and honey as I kept having too much sauce left over.
I also pre-cooked the meat to render some of the fat. The wings didn't need it but the thighs and breasts did.
Since I am cooking for a 3yr old as well I didn't add any heat, but this is a great starting point to add cayenne, serranos or what ever for some kick.
I like more garlic so I tripled that as well.
Thanks for sharing. This is a keeper.

My family was hesitant to try this recipe as we have another wing recipe that has proven tried & true in our household.  I went ahead & tried it since I was intrigued by all the reviews & boy was I glad I did!  They were quite simple & tasty!  My husband & children raved about them.  I did try the pre-cook method to rid the wings of the excess fat however, I thought that they had lost some of their moisture.  Next time I will omit that recommendation.  Thanks again for a great & easy recipe, can't wait 'till football season rolls around again!
