reviews.review_text: This roast was tender and delicious.  I must add that I made a few changes, and it was wonderful.  I started with a 3.5 pound roast, so I cut the recipe in half.  I didn't have a can of the cream of mushroom soup on hand so I used my Condensed Cream Soup Substitute recipe using beef broth.  Also, in place of the water I used a mixture of beef broth and red wine (a pot roast isn't a pot roast with out a little red wine.)  I also added carrots, celery, and fresh minced garlic, and served with mashed potatoes.  Excellent!!!  Thanks kcdelong!!!!

attributes.source_text: This roast was tender

items.label: Thick Chocolate Pudding
items.name: Thick Chocolate Pudding
items.description: This is the perfect chocolate pudding. It has a rich chocolate flavor, great texture and is not high in fat. I can't count the number of times I have made this. I hope you enjoy it as much as we do.
instructions: In a 2-qt. microwave-safe bowl, combine the first four ingredients.
Stir in milk until smooth.
Microwave, uncovered on high for 3 minutes; stir.
Microwave 4-6 minutes longer or until thickened, stirring after each minute.
Stir in vanilla.
Pour into individual serving dishes; cool.
Refrigerate.
Garnish with whipped topping if desired.

reviews.review_text:
Finially !!! My frustrating days of trying to use soymilk with commercial packet mixes and never having them set properly are over... This is quick & easy to prepare. I tried it with regular low fat milk, plain soymilk and chocolate soymilk. The one with choc soymilk was voted the best of the bunch by a very slim margin but everyone agreed that all three versions were streets ahead of the boxed supermarket brands. I cooked this up both in the microwave and on the stovetop...  and with both, once the thickening process started it went very quickly indeed so don't think you can leave it unattended... or do a little multi-tasking while you make this, you won't have time :) I'd say that my microwave did it in 5 minutes and on my stovetop in 7 but amazingly it went faster on the stovetop (opening and closing the door to the microwave took up more time!) A smooth, chocolat-y, mega quick, super easy, idiot proof recipe that uses pantry cupboard staples and is totally economical as well. What more do we need? Please see my rating system: a very well deserved 5 stars.
Many many Thanks !

attributes.source_text: A smooth, chocolat-y, mega quick, super easy, idiot proof recipe
A smooth, chocolat-y, mega quick, super easy, idiot proof recipe

reviews.review_text: I made these yesterday and they turned out very well. I used the microwave method. I put all the dry goods into a sifter and sifted them into a 2 1/2 quart CorningWare pot. I added the whole milk and did the 3 minute first heat cycle. I used a vented microwave cover just in case of bubbling up. I then did the 1 minute cycles with a stir in between each. After only 2 it seemed pretty thick but I went ahead a gave it the 4 cycles called for and it did seem to maybe get a bit thicker. It does not yield as much pudding as I expected but was quite good. I put it into five 4oz. ramekins. Served them that evening for dessert with whipped cream on top. EZ to prepare and I had none of the problems as reported by some reviews. Thinking of trying almond extract instead of vanilla next time. Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: Served them that evening for dessert
it seemed pretty thick

reviews.review_text:
Ok, a summary of things people have done:
adding instant coffee; adding some chocolate chips; stirring in a large tbsp of PB until blended;
changing up for other types of milk, including almond and soy; varying the amount of vanilla; subbing splenda and sucanant etc for sugar; cooking on stove -- bring milk to warm and then whisk in all of the other ingredients that have been pre-mixed together; make sure and cook to a full boil with cornstarch to remove the starch taste; adding coconut, roasted nuts, serve with whipped cream on top,.... Lots of variation to have with this great recipe. Prepackage it so it is ready for kids to do instead of purchased packages. ENJOY!!

I don't normally leave negative reviews, but I'm making an exception in this case.  I followed this recipe to the LETTER last night.  I am accustomed to making pie fillings and puddings in the microwave- have been doing this for years.  (The only way to do it, IMO.)  I was skeptical about the recipe not including eggs, but with as many great reviews that it recieved, I thought it would be okay to try it.  BUT, I see now what the addition of eggs does for a pudding.  That smoothy, creamy texture and rich flavor was totally lacking in this recipe.  It pretty much tasted like chocolatey cornstarch "glop".  Today, after sitting in the fridge overnight, the texture is almost like gelatin!  Bleh.  I am very disappointed in this recipe and next time I need a chocolate fix, will RUN back to my old recipe.  (BTW- For those afraid of using eggs due to having egg "lumps", a simple run through a strainer before cooking can easily catch those lumps.  The eggs have it!) Sorry. :(  Two thumbs down.

Wow!! I couldn't believe this pudding was homemade- it was SOOO finger lickin good! We don't get boxed puddings here and I was getting worried about when I would run out of them since I only have a few boxes left. I'd been looking for a recipe for a while now and well this recipe even beat the boxed kind! I've now been making this one rather than the boxed stuff and continuously look for ways to have this.  The first time I made it, the consistency seemed perfect to me but the taste was just okay since it wasnt chocolately enough for me like the boxed kind.  I made it again and increased the cocoa and sugar content and wow was it good!! I simply fell in love with this pudding! I can't thank you enough for posting this recipe Chris! This is truely a 10 star recipe considering the few ingredients, ease of this recipe and most of all its delicious taste.  It goes in my all-time favourites folder! thank you thank you thank you!!!

I am sorry that I have to rate this so low.  I tried multiple times to make this in the microwave.  When it first comes it it is very thick (Just what I wanted), but as it cooled it became more and more runny.  By the end it was more like a chocolate milk in consistency.  When I asked on the Q & A forum what might be happening (I tried to make it twice by then), they thought I was over cooking it.  So the next couple of times I worked on adjusting the time and/or the power setting.  Still when it first came out it was a perfect thickness, but as it cooled it went back to that chocolate milk consistency.  I do have to say, I loved the flavor.  It was chocolatey and not sweet.  Again I am sorry, but thanks for sharing.  The hundred   reviews that were positive can't be wrong.  Just didn't work for me.

attributes.source_text: it is very thick (Just what I wanted)
It was chocolatey
not sweet

reviews.review_text: This is really good. The first time I made it, I cooked it on the stove (for the first time making real pudding), and ended up cooking it far too long (rubbery, really quite disgusting). Since then, I have made it several times in the microwave, with great results. Make sure you watch it, though, because 3 minutes is just a little too long for my microwave (it starts to bubble over). 2 1/2 minutes, stirring it, and then putting it back in for another 30 seconds works well for me. I have followed the recipe precisely, and also made it with slightly less sugar- it's good both ways, depending on personal preference. I like it both warm and cold. Great recipe- thanks!!

Simple and delicious. It has all the delectable chocolate taste without all the guilt! My BF and I were craving some pudding but were out of the boxed kind so I threw this together. It was so easy. I used a 4 c Pyrex cup to cook it in so the clean up was a cinch. Make sure you stir after every minute during the second stage of cooking to prevent overflow! Thanks!  Edited 08.29.07 : Just wanted to say I made this with 10 oz of soy milk and 6 oz of skim milk and it still turned out so delicious.  For all the reviewers who said the texture was off or that is was clumpy... make sure you use a whisk during the 2nd phase of cooking and to whisk the pudding after every minute to ensure that it is smooth and the "crust" does not harden on top.  I only have to cook my pudding another 4 minutes after the initial 3 minutes until the texture is just right... We love this as a light dessert with some homemade whipped cream a couple of times a week!!!

attributes.source_text: all the delectable chocolate taste
to ensure that it is smooth
We love this as a light dessert

reviews.review_text: I had a little bit of trouble with this and the microwave- One minute it was still quite liquidy and the next it was pretty set.  I'm not sure if this caused this, but I ended up with a few little cornstarchy (yet chocolatey, so I assume it did ) bits in the pudding.  I think that personally, I'd rather make this stovetop to better monitor the level of setness.  I thought the flavor was pretty good.  The texture seemed a little too cornstarch-thickened to me.  BF thought it was okay.  Now, the really weird thing.  I made this yesterday, and I just went to get some out of the frige- and it seems the cornstarch has pretty much given up- its lost a lot of its solidity.  Weird.  Not bad, but not really my thing, I guess.

attributes.source_text: yet chocolatey

reviews.review_text: This is yummilicious! I can't believe how quick this got ready. I needed a few very good chocolate dessert recipes as I am off to a birthday party in a while, and I wanted to surprise the birthday girl{who turns 9 today} with a few chocolate homemade recipes. I picked this and I am so glad I did. This has come out superb! It tastes excellent and has a great texture. It was ready in 7 minutes!! I set this in a tray and then I used Smartie chocolates{colourful gems} to write "ABI" on place them on top of this pudding. So now, there is the birthday girl's name over her pudding! She's going to love this! Thank you so much for making me make this by posting it!

attributes.source_text: I am off to a birthday party in a while
I needed a few very good chocolate dessert recipes

reviews.review_text: I was looking for something to satisfy my chocolate craving - QUICK.  This certainly did the trick.  I'm trying to eat healthy so I cut it down to 2 tbsp of sugar (I only made 2 servings though - halved the rest of the ingredients).  Surprisingly it ended up tasting just right.  The only problem was that I didn't sieve the cocoa or cornstarch so it ended up being slightly lumpy.  I couldn't really taste the vanilla so I might add more (but then again I love vanilla) the next time round.  I need to find more ways to serve this because I'm not much a fan of pudding by itself.  A friend of mine served her pudding sandwiched with plain graham crackers and more pudding and chocolate sauce over the top, sprinkled with chopped peanuts.  Oh that whole sweet-savoury combination - YUM :)

attributes.source_text: satisfy my chocolate craving

reviews.review_text: As if this recipe needed another 5 star review! This was a hit in our house. I doubled the recipe as I used the pudding to make a pie. I poured the pudding into a chocolate pie crust, layered it with bananas, and spread white chocolate shavings on top. Also to make this recipe nearly sugar-free I used 20 packets of Equal to sweeten the pudding instead of sugar. If you do decide to use artificial sweetener, make sure to stir it into the pudding AFTER cooking. This recipe is so easy that I'll never use the packaged version again. Thanks for posting!

I make this chocolate pudding all the time! It's a quick, easy, and healthy, and it can be easily adapted—I've used Silk coconut milk, stevia, and thrown in a handful of semisweet chocolate chips, and it turns out great! I make it on the stovetop and constantly whisk to ensure a smooth and creamy consistency. Basically, give it a good beating to break up all the cocoa and cornstarch lumps. When I want an extra decadent treat, I'll add banana slices, fresh whipped cream, walnuts, or chocolate chips—or all of the above!

attributes.source_text: ensure a smooth and creamy consistency
ensure a smooth and creamy consistency
an extra decadent treat

reviews.review_text:
Wow Chris! What a delicious burst of chocolate heaven! I wasn't quite sure when I was assembling the ingredients... what a surprize was in store! I always have these ingredients in the house and yet I am always fretting when guests are coming over. What dessert should I make? Never again will I feel stumped. Chris from Kansas you have rescued me! I was tense for the last 5 minutes as the pudding was rising too high and almost over the brim. It is cooling right now, but I have had many generous licks already. Thanks a ton

I can't believe how wonderful this is!  I was just amazed at how incredibly easy it was to make and how fast it was done.  I'm not a fan of boxed instant pudding and this is a gazillion times better in every single way.  I was in desperate need of a chocolate fix and used Dutch processed Cocoa and it's just  absolutely excellent!  my son and I both had a serving of it when it was hot and I just had a bowl straight from the fridge and when the flavors have time to blend and cool it's even a little better.  Mixed with some canned cherries and whipped cream.. the perfect chocolate fix!

Thank you so much Chris for posting this super easy recipe!!

attributes.source_text: the perfect chocolate fix

reviews.review_text: This is a simple, tasty pudding recipe.  Way better than any box pudding mix and way easier than a stovetop variety.  I made the recipe as written with my only change being I sifted my dry ingredients before adding the milk.  I also used a whisk to do my stirring.  I had no problem with the texture as others have mentioned.  I love the idea of trying different extracts like almond, raspberry, or mint.  I also want to try making a pie.  What a nice last minute dessert idea for entertaining or a potluck.  The texture reminds me of the snack pak pudding cups that are so pricy.  I will definitely make this again & again.

attributes.source_text: nice last minute dessert idea
for entertaining or a potluck

reviews.review_text: I too must be off the mark with this one (Sorry!).  I followed the directions too the T and this is just WAY off the mark for me.  The taste is not on, I agree it's a little bitter and the texture is just weird, it reminds me more of Flubber!  If I didn't know this was pudding, I don't think I'd actually try it.  I may just chuck this one and try something else for supper, don't even know if I can serve this one to my family.  I guess my idea of the "perfect chocolate pudding" differs.  A lot of people seem to love this one, and I am obviously in the minority here.

I made this last night and am anxious to have it again for dessert later today. I used splenda instead of sugar, and next time I will be more careful about measure the cocoa as my pudding turned out EXTREMELY cocoa-y flavored. I might even try sifting my measurements next time. I think adding cool-whip will help cut the rich flavor. Anyways, the texture was was creamy and yummy. As many reviews stated, I did add a little extra splenda and I think it needed it. Over all, pretty great recipe, anxious to try again with a few tweaks.

the texture was was creamy and yummy

reviews.review_text: This was so rich, chocolatey, smooth & creamy!  It was absolutely delicious.  I followed the recipe exactly except I added a little Benefiber before microwaving (I try to add it in whenever I can).  I whisked it like crazy after every minute and it was done after 8 mins total (3 first, then 5).  Since my hubby and I tasted the spoon after I took it out of the microwave, we couldn't wait for it to cool down.  We spooned some over some ice cream like another user recommended.  Hoo Boy!  Good bye Smuckers microwave hot fudge.  We're using this from now on.  Not only is it terrific warm, it's even better cold.  Creamy, cool, smooth, rich, decadent, this recipe is all of these.  This is a simple, quick, wonderfully delicious pudding.  Thanks so much for sharing Chris!

items.label: White Chocolate Chip Cranberry Oatmeal Cookies
items.name: White Chocolate Chip Cranberry Oatmeal Cookies
items.description: I originally made these at the request of my old chorus director John Kelleher, who also worked at Seattle area Starbucks (I think he'd had the combo in a cookie there, once). I was surprised but very pleased they came out so tasty! These days, these are pretty much the only cookies which are requested and I make on a fairly regular basis.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In a large bowl using an electric mixer combine the sugar, brown sugar and butter; mix well to cream together.
Add in egg and vanilla extract and mix until combined.
Add the cinnamon, baking soda, salt and flour and mix well.
Fold in the oatmeal, dried cranberries and white chocolate chips- making sure that all ingredients are uniformly distributed.
Roll dough into 1-inch balls and place 3 inches apart onto a greased cookie sheet and bake at 375° for 10-12 minutes, just until the edges are lightly golden.
Remove from oven and let cool for 2-3 minutes on the cookie sheet, then transfer cookies to cooling rack.

reviews.review_text: UPDATE 2: I make these every Xmas... I read that cookies put in fridge bake better - and due to timing left in fridge overnight. When I baked them cold - they STUCK to the pan - so need to use parchment if you are going to cool the dough. They were not flat - did not spread and were thicker and chewier due to the cold dough. (which we like). UPDATE: I've made these about 8 times now - and use all the sugar all the time... I've begun to soak and plump my craisins too-- thanks for that suggestion! Everyone LOVES these cookies!!! I used my cookie scooper and had no trouble with flattening cookies or too plump cookies. I got 28 cookies and 12 minutes was a good time - except after the cookie sheets were hot - the second round in the oven (last few cookies) got a bit overdone - probably should reduce a minute or two if using the cookie sheets a second time... UPDATE to the UPDATE - Turn down the oven a bit and cook them a bit longer so the butter doesn't melt and spread out and make flat / ugly cookies....

attributes.source_text: I make these every Xmas
were thicker and chewier due to the cold dough
were thicker and chewier due to the cold dough

reviews.review_text: I did what others said to do, soaked the cranberries in warm water for 10 mins and drain, added additional egg yolk (although did not add extra baking soda), reduced the white suger to 1/2 cup.  I made them twice as big as recipe and squished the dough balls flat.  Baked on convection bake for 8 mins. on 375 deg.  I also added 1/2 cup of pecans (because I love nuts in my cookies).  Next time I would add 5.5 oz vs. 6 oz of white chocolate b/c it would be exactly half of the 11 oz bag of Ghiradelli and I could make 2 batches from 1 bag. If you make these, you will want to double the batch, they are very yummy!

THis is an excellent cookie, but I found it tricky.  I reduced the sugar as suggested by others, and flattened them before I baked them on parchment paper on my old, reliable, thin cookie sheets.  I made 2 cookie trays and the lowest cookie tray had burned cookies, and both trays "browned" too much.  My oven is pretty accurate-- so I figure either 375 is too hot, or Jules uses an airbake cookie sheet.  Anyway, I had some dough left, so I reduced the oven to 350 degrees, and kept the "round shape" for the remaining 6 cookies.  Those cookies were perfect!  Thank you.  My husband loves them...but has asked that I add more cranberries when I make these again.   Which I will.

attributes.source_text: My husband loves them

reviews.review_text: While hanging out with some girlfriends, we found this recipe, read the amazing reviews, and got very excited! Unfortunately, upon browsing our pantry, we discovered a lack of oats. Not to be deterred from making these highly anticipated cookies, we took a trip to Ralphs. (On the way, we decided to stop by Blockbuster and make it a girls night in!....by the way, would not recommend Science of Sleep.) It was well worth it, because they were very good! Howvever, due to our very high expectations we were a little disappointed about quantities and consistencies. There wasn't enough dough for all the white chocolate chips and cranberries. We even had leftovers in the bowl! (However, they did make a good trailmix to eat while the cookies were baking!) Also, when they cooked, they didn't really flatten out so they were still in ball-form and they didn't hold together too well because of the extra chocolate chips and cranberries. Will definitely make again, but will use less white chocolate chips and cranberries and make our cookies bigger. Other family members sure enjoyed! Also, we added some pecans to a few for an extra flair!

attributes.source_text: Other family members sure enjoyed!

reviews.review_text: I really was not a fan of these cookies. I'm giving one star for the combination of white chocolate and cranberry (delicious, I will take that combo elsewhere), and one star for looking so fantastic (just enough spread, nice and thick, perfect colour). However, for me that is where the good ends. I found these WAY too sweet, and too crunchy (which is personal preference really, but I just like my cookies soft and slightly chewy). I used whole wheat flour which may have impacted the texture, but I always do for other cookies with no problem, so this just didn't work for me. Also, beneath the over sweetness and white chocolate these seemed almost... bland. Weird. Needless to say, I will NOT be making these again (though it appears from the other reviews I am nearly alone in this). Thanks anyway.

attributes.source_text: nice and thick

reviews.review_text: Wish I'd read the reviews BEFORE I started these! I agree with several previous posts that these are a tad sweet and would back the sugar down a little. I made a double batch (cuz I just knew 3 dozen wouldn't cut it for my crowd!) and found it very difficult to work in the oats, chips, and craisins, along with a cup of chopped walnuts. It was hard to work with the dough and not have it break apart. I didn't soak my cranberries, altho I think that would have helped too. I did find 375 to be too hot and backed it down to 350 for 11 minutes, and I tried rolled and dropped. I liked the results with rolling a little better - a moister, thicker cookie. All that being said, they are delicious and with a few changes, I would make them again.

attributes.source_text: a moister, thicker cookie
a moister, thicker cookie

reviews.review_text: OMG!!!! These are probably the best cookies I have ever made and certainly the best I've ever eaten. I love the thin, chewy texture. That is always something I look for when I search for a recipe. The only thing I did different from the original recipe was to simmer, yes simmer, my cranberries in dark rum! I put my dried cranberries in a small sauce pan, then added just enough rum so they would simmer. Of course be careful, low flame since alcohol is flammable. I just did it real low, about 10 minutes. This cooks off the alcohol and you are left with the flavor. It actually absorbed all the rum. I tripled the recipe because I like to make large cookies and I wanted to send some with my daughter and her boyfriend. These look like they came from a bakery, seriously! I can't say enough about them. But I do think that the oatmeal cookie dough "base" would be perfect for anything you wanted to do. Raisins, Chocolate chips or all nuts...Even used as a base for Monster Cookies would be amazing. Biggest challenge with these will be not eating the whole batch myself! I will be adding these to my freezer cookie line up. I just flash-freeze scoops of dough, then place them in freezer bags. That way you can make as many as you need...great if a sweet tooth hits and you don't wanna make a big batch

attributes.source_text: I love the thin, chewy texture
I love the thin, chewy texture
you are left with the flavor

reviews.review_text: I made two batches...the second one was so much better and they were not as dry as the first batch. I made them slightly different but wasn't much of a change. I soaked the dried cranberries in very hot water. I put them in a bowl, microwaved some eater in a mug for a bout a minute and poured it on the cranberry bowl. Let them soak for about 20 minutes and this made the cookies taste so Much better! I also added a tablespoon of olive oil into the mix to make them softer since my first batch of cookies turned hard after cooling. and last change I did was lower the temp to 350 and cooked for about 11-12 minutes just as the edges were brown. My dad said these were a bit too sweet so maybe I will use 1/2 cup of white sugar instead of 3/4. Made 3 dozen an they are all gone!

attributes.source_text: they were not as dry as the first batch
to make them softer

reviews.review_text: I always find myself tasting the "dough" first and it was delicious and the baked version are superb too!!! Did add 3/4 cup small pecan pieces (finely chopped) and maybe 2 tsp low fat milk, divided flour with white and whole wheat and add 1 Tablespoon Ground Flax Seed.  They're in oven right now and smell great and the buzzer has sounded. While putting on wire rack couldn't resist Julesong thank you so much for posting. I made these for work for "Fun Friday" - payday, now just have to stop sampling so I'll have some to bring to work.  I feel less guilty consuming these!!! Justmez2

attributes.source_text: I made these for work for "Fun Friday"

reviews.review_text: Oh, my .... these were the best oatmeal cookies I have ever had.  Really.  No exaggeration.  The flavor was superb, the texture was great ... these were really excellent.  I thought about trying to make them lower fat/calorie, but decided not to .... why ruin perfection?  This is definitely a case of keeping the recipe as is, eating a little less, and enjoying it a lot more.  Thanks so much for posting this!  NOTE:  After reading other reviews, I wanted to note that my cookies DID flatten and spread out, and so the 3" safety zone was a good thing.  The cookies were crisp, not soft -- which is EXACTLY what I wanted.

attributes.source_text: The cookies were crisp, not soft

reviews.review_text: I didn't read everyone's review before making these cookies and although they were very tasty, there is room for improvement.  I had a hard time "folding in" the chips, oatmeal, and cranberries as I thought the dough was a little dry.  I may not have allowed my butter to soften enough because it was late and I was in a rush to make these as my family was craving something sweet after dinner.  I am going to give this recipe 4 stars.  I prefer chewy, soft cookies and as the rest mentioned, soaking the cranberries, and adding an additional egg may allow for that.  Overall, they were still very tasty and if the batch makes 36 cookies, I was left with a dozen so we did eat a few.  I also didn't roll them into balls, I just used by cookie scooper.

attributes.source_text: my family was craving something sweet after dinner

reviews.review_text: I read the reviews and decided to make some changes for my first attempt. I added about a 1/4 cup of apple sauce, an extra egg, and about a 1/4 cup of instant vanilla pudding since some complained they were hard cookies. I used Craisins instead of cranberries and soaked them prior.  I also added about 1/4 cup more flour to compensate for the apple sauce and egg. I cooked them at the described time and temp, 375 for 12 minutes. The cookies turned out perfect. They flattened just enough and are still soft and a little cakey. I also added macadamia nuts. They are delicious

attributes.source_text: are still soft
a little cakey

reviews.review_text: I can see why it gets 5 stars. The flavour is very good - and it is a super moreish cookie. However, i gave it 4 stars because of the tweaks it needs. I followed and agreed with a) reducing the white sugar to 1/2 cup, b) soaking the cranberries in alcohol of choice and warm water for 15 minutes or more, and c) reducing the oven temp to 350F for a 10-12 min bake. However, I added an extra egg yolk and found it made the cookie texture very cake-like. I personally would omit this tweak in future, even though it didn't stop me from reaching for another... and another...

I love these cookies! I made 3 batches of these to take to a potluck and they were the first thing gone. Everyone kept saying they were some of the best cookies ever. I used a little less white chips --probably about 4 oz. -- as I thought their flavor overpowered everything else. And I used egg beaters since I didn't have any eggs. My cookies did not really spread, so I just pushed down on the tops a little before I baked them. I only had to bake about 8 minutes then removed them when they didn't look done. This way after cooling they were perfectly soft. GREAT recipe!

attributes.source_text: to take to a potluck
after cooling they were perfectly soft

reviews.review_text: I just made these incredible cookies this morning. I read all the reviews and decided to make the recipe as it stands with 2 small changes. I substituted the old fashioned rolled oats (which counters the sugar content nicely) and I used the added soaking, draining method on the cranberries. I made a double batch, one as presented and the other half I added macadamia nuts chopped. Both were very successful. I did also slightly flatten the dough before baking. Wonderful results. Thank you for sharing this recipe!

These were one of three cookies I made for my MIL's birthday, and they were a hit. When I made these cookies, I had tripled the cookie dough ingredients, but when I added the dried cranberries, I added about 8 ounces, which is about (2) 3/4 cups each, and I added (1) 12 ounce bag of the white chocolate chips, plus a 1/4 cup of the chips as well. I baked these cookies on my Pampered Chef Stoneware for 13-14 minutes.  In tripling the recipe, this made about 8-1/2 dozen cookies. Thank you Jules, for this really yummy cookie recipe!

attributes.source_text: for my MIL's birthday
they were a hit

reviews.review_text: I made these to take camping last weekend and they were gone on the first day.  Everyone raved how great they were and I didn't think the hubbs would eat them because they were oatmeal but he wants these from now on and even asked for me to make some so he could take to work.  Thanks for a great recipe this is a big keeper!<br/>Update: these are my go to cookies for all occasions and the most asked for cookie I make.  Even when over baked and crunchy they are wonderful coffee dunking cookies - know this from experience!

reviews.review_text: I made these for the first time today.  I doubled the recipe and I did not use the electric mixer --maybe I should have!!   The mixture was quite thick when I was done.  I will add that extra egg yolk next time as someone recommended.  I found that the cookies were a bit dry but they still tasted good.  I used my cookie dough scoop and baked them in regular size muffin tins like I usually do.  They came out thick and chewy and friends seem to like them.  Will definitely make these again.  Thank you for sharing this recipe with all of us.

items.label: Chicken Cordon Bleu Casserole
items.name: Chicken Cordon Bleu Casserole
keywords: c("Chicken Breast", "Chicken", "Pork", "Poultry", "Cheese", "Meat", "Very Low Carbs", "High Protein", "High In...", "< 60 Mins", "Oven", "Easy")
items.description: My family loved this recipe. All the flavors of the real deal, only quicker to put on the table. It would be a lovely brunch dish too.
instructions: Dip chicken in egg and milk mixture, then toss with bread crumbs, coating well.
Brown in a little oil until golden.
Place chicken in a baking dish, add cheese and ham.
Mix soup with 1 cup of milk and pour over all.
Bake at 350°F for 30-35 minutes, or until tender and bubbly.

reviews.review_text: My DH is not a big chicken fan, but I had a large pkg from the warehouse that needed to be eaten. I put two large skinless boneless breasts and about 1/2 of a LARGE ham steak w/bone on the foreman grill (diced both after grilling). I Did not bread the chicken thinking I would do a corn flake crust on top, but I ended up not having any and didn't want saltines. I had about 1/4 bag of tater tots I chopped up on top and dotted w/butter. After 30 mins I put the broiler on for 5 mins to crisp up the top. DH said it was VERY VERY good and we will have it again. Oh, I also only used 4-6 oz of swiss, grated on top but under the tots - a little over half of the block.

attributes.source_text: DH said it was VERY VERY good

reviews.review_text: Wonderful recipe that my whole family enjoyed. Here are some thoughts and tips I have: Some reviewers suggested using frozen breaded chicken nuggets or popcorn chicken. While that idea appeals to me as does anything to do with a fast put together but tasty meal, I have to say I breaded my own chicken and browned it according to the directions. A little bit of labor but well worth it because you control the quality of the breading on your chicken. I used 1 cup of seasoned bread crumbs, 1 cup crushed french fried onions and 1 tsp Paula Deen's House Seasoning and fried it up in 1/4 cup of vegetable oil and 2 tbsp butter. I took note of the comments on the runny sauce and added 1 tbsp of flour to the canned cream of chicken. It all came together beautifully! Thanks for sharing.

attributes.source_text: my whole family enjoyed

reviews.review_text: Delicious!  Even DH, who is not overly fond of Swiss Cheese, enjoyed it and said it's a keeper.  He said he actually liked it better than traditional Cordon Bleu because the cheesy sauce coated each and every bite.  I used some leftover ham that had been in the deep freeze and wasn't quite worthy of sandwiches and sandwich sliced Swiss that I diced myself.  I mixed the soup and milk, added the ham and stirred in the cheese pieces to keep them from clumping together.  Put the chicken in the bottom of the baking dish and dumped the the soup and ham mixture over top.  I also added another step.  Whenever I use a breading on moist meat or veggies I always dredge in flour first.  This gives the wet mixture something to "grip" and makes for a better final coating.  I used WW Flour with a dash of salt and pepper.  Salad and Garlic Toast completed this yummy meal.  Thanks for sharing!

attributes.source_text: Even DH, who is not overly fond of Swiss Cheese, enjoyed it
the cheesy sauce coated each and every bite

reviews.review_text:
I had to make a few changes to this recipe but I'm sure it didn't make any difference because of how delicious this turned out. I used cream of celery soup and the swiss cheese and ham were sliced- not in chunks- so I cut them into small pieces and mixed together before sprinkling over the chicken.
After reading the reviews that said the chicken was a little bland, I added some paprika for color and garlic powder for taste to the milk/egg mixture.
I also added some brown mustard to the milk/soup mixture.
If there had been a pattern on the plates I used, my husband would have licked it off. We eat a lot of chicken and he said he hoped I never lost this recipe because it deserves more than 5 stars.
One of the things I really like about this recipe is it's flexibility. A different soup- chives or green onions added or broccoli. Whatever you might have on hand. That's what can make a good recipe in my opinion.

attributes.source_text: my husband would have licked it off

reviews.review_text: I made this to serve with broccoli, but would add a green salad, too, the next time.  I cooked the chicken in a little water first, then cubed it.  I added the other things layered over it and skipped the egg.  I added garlic powder and parsley, then put breadcrumbs on top.  I used cream of celery soup and 1% milk, as that was all I had.  We don't really like "cream of" soups, but this was ok with it.  I prefer a real white sauce, but this was faster.  The ham and cheese added the right amount of saltiness.  I would make this again and try it exactly as written to see which I prefer.

attributes.source_text: The ham and cheese added the right amount of saltiness

reviews.review_text: Both my fiance and I absolutely LOVED this!!  I only had a 6-oz block of Swiss on hand, but I felt like there was plenty in the cooked dish.  Also, instead of using the chemical-y canned condensed soups, I've started making my own (Recipe No. 25653); for this casserole, I substituted 1/2 cup of the water (called for in 25653) with white wine and it was an AWESOME addition!  The only reason this gets 4 stars instead of 5 is because 1) it didn't specify the quantity of bread crumbs required; I think I used about 1 cup, and 2) it doesn't call for white wine, which I think is a must-have!  This casserole makes more than my fiance and I can (ok, SHOULD) eat in a single meal so next time I'll try freezing half; I've done some research and I think it will hold up fine, even with the homemade soup.  Will definitely, DEFINITELY repeat this recipe!!  Thank you :-)

attributes.source_text: Both my fiance and I absolutely LOVED this

reviews.review_text: i have made this twice now and i have to say it is very good. i cut up the raw chicken and put it into the pan then sprinkled bread crumbs over the top and broiled on high for about 10 minutes, until brown. then i added the ham, cheese and soup and cooked as dierected. this method turns out so good and much easier than frying. i do have to say tho the dish seems a bit bland. the first time i made it i used montreal chicken which i didnt like. this time i didnt add anything except for salt and pepper and i think it does need a little something for a kick, i will have to try something else next time. i also used white wine instead of milk and i will be doing that everytime, it was good. thanks for a unique recipe, we will be eating this on a regular rotation.

After reading reviews I decided to add about 4 T or to taste of French's Dijon mustard with chardonnay. I also baked my chicken, but coated it with mayo and parm cheese and Progresso Italian flavored panko breadcrumbs and added the same kind of breadcrumbs to the top. I decided to bake the cheese, ham and soup mixture til the cheese melted, then mixed in the chicken and sprinkled the breadcrumbs on top and baked for another 10 min. I was pleased with the outcome, as was my husband (picky eater)! I made mashed potatoes AND egg noodles. Next time it will be a salad or green veggie. It was rich and heavy-ish with the potatoes for us. Thank you for submitting this recipe.

attributes.source_text: as was my husband (picky eater)
my husband (picky eater)
It was rich and heavy-ish

reviews.review_text:
Everything about this recipe said it should have been outstanding. Unfortunately, on my first try it wasn't. It was dry, and the cheese cubes didn't melt well - they just ended up as slightly soft but still chewy blobs. So, I tried again, with some changes.
Instead of cubing the cheese and using the soup/milk I made a double batch of cheesy whitesauce ("Recipe# 111645"), with shredded swiss instead of cheddar. I think that would have been fine right there, but for personal taste I added a layer of sauteed sliced mushrooms before pouring on the cheese sauce.

I'll confess that I'm surprised I liked this casserole. I made it for my husband to eat while I'm working late a couple of nights this week. I took some in my lunch today and really enjoyed it. I'm normally not a chicken casserole fan, I think because the chicken pieces always seem, well, slimy to me. But since the chicken in this dish was breaded, it really helped with the "sliminess factor" I perceive. My husband really liked this too and it was fairly easy to put together. I like the suggestion to add broccoli. I'll try that next time. Thanks for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: My husband really liked this too

reviews.review_text: Wow!!!!!  This is so good.  It really does taste just like the real thing, only better because its alot less work.  I used panko breadcrumbs to coat the chicken and I probably used a little more ham then  called for but it was fabulous.  I didn't think it turned runny at all like some of the other reviewers.  DS#2 looked at me and said "Mom, you are the best cook ever"  That right there made this dish 100 stars in my books.  Thank you so much for sharing this yummy recipe with us, I know I will be making it again soon.

attributes.source_text: I didn't think it turned runny at all
DS#2 looked at me and said "Mom, you are the best cook ever"

reviews.review_text: I really enjoyed making this recipe.  Few ingredients, easy steps and on the table to eat in less than an hour!  The bonus is that it actually tastes like the original recipe which takes much longer to prepare.  I used the 98% fat free cream of chicken soup and 2% milk which helped to lower the total fat content but didn't compromise the wonderful taste.  The sauce was exquisite and the chicken was fork tender.  I served it  over noodles.  Thanks Miss Annie!  It's a keeper!!

reviews.review_text: This was delicious! I tried to lighten it up a bit by using reduced fat swiss cheese and healthy request cream of chicken soup and it still came out so decadent tasting. I halved the recipe since I was only making it for two, and I used the other half of the cream of chicken to mix in with hot egg noodles and served the casserole over them. So simple yet so delicious! I probably won't make it all that often since it's pretty unhealthy but it's a fantastic comfort food meal for every now and then :-)

reviews.review_text: I made this for my employer and husband, and have looked for the recipe for over a year to make it again! I make a few changes (just can't help myself). I used crushed Ritz crackers mixed with garlic and onion powders to bread the chicken in nugget sizes. They were so crisp and tasty, I should have made more, because i kept snacking on them as i fried them up in batches! I did use diced ham, but shredded cheese, and it melted nicely. To the sauce, I added a splash of Chardonnay and a dollop of Dijon mustard, and it took it to the next level. A lot of reviews say to serve with noodles, rice, or mashed potatoes, but it is a very rich dish. I paired it with roasted broccoli and crusty French bread, and two delicate appetites and two ridiculously BIG appetites were satisfied, with some leftovers to spare.

items.label: Moist & Delicious Banana Nut Bread
items.name: Moist & Delicious Banana Nut Bread
keywords: c("Breads", "Tropical Fruits", "Fruit", "Nuts", "< 30 Mins", "For Large Groups", "< 4 Hours", "Easy")
items.description: I got this recipe when I was 12 and have used it for the past 33 years and haven't found one better!  My son used it when he was 12 at the California State Fair and won a first place ribbon with it.  It is just simply delicious & moist.  I either make a loaf or put it into muffin cups & make muffins for my kids to grab in the morning on their way to school.  Using margarine makes the muffins come out in a better form, but the butter has a better flavor, so I usually use 1/2 of each to get the best of both worlds.
instructions: Cream butter & sugar.  Add vanilla & eggs.  Combine dry ingredients, add alternately with bananas & milk. Add nuts if desired. Grease & flour 1 bread pan (2-3 smaller pans) or pour into muffin cups.  For loaf bake at 350 for 45-60 minute  Muffins 350 for 20-25min.  Enjoy!

*Note- I usually use a smaller bread pan to make the 2 loaves, or use a larger one and just make 1 big loaf, but it will need to bake longer.  I adjusted the time because people had been saying it was over baking, now people are saying it's under baked.  I would use the old fashion test of a tooth pick at 45 min, then at 1 hour -- up to 1 hour & 30 min if needed.  Hope that helps!

reviews.review_text: I made this bread last weekend,I made it by adding an extra half of the ingredients ie.3 cups of flour, 3 eggs etc. I also added about 1 cup of a mix of Walmart brand Dried Berries and Golden Raisins and 1 cup of walnuts,and I added approx. 1 tablespoon each of ground ginger and cinnamon...and instead of all white sugar I used one and a half cups of brown sugar and half a cup of white sugar. These ingredients made two 9 by 5 inch loaves which took approximately one and a half hours to bake..I served slices warm with warm custard ( Birds Custard Powder available in the British section of the international food aisle of most stores or from Amazon ,made as directed) This is without doubt,the best banana and fruit bread I've ever made....and it freezes very well!

I made this the first time without realizing I had no white sugar. well only a 1/4 cup and the rest was made up with brown sugar. I baked it in a deep 9 inch round cake pan because I had stopped baking for so many years I had thrown out my loaf pans. ( yeah it was over 20 years. closer to 30). It took a really long time to get done but I checked it faithfully and did not burn it :) HOLY cow!! all the neighbors loved it and so did my son ( who i was making this for to begin with) and it disappeared in less than 36 hours. This is now my go to recipe to save all those bananas that almost went to waste !!! THANKS!!!

attributes.source_text: all the neighbors loved it
so did my son

reviews.review_text: Amazingly Delicious!!! And... I used alternative ingredients. I am trying to stay away from enriched flours and white granulated sugar. So with the this being my first try at this recipe I split the ingredients with healthier choices. Instead of 2 cups of all purpose flour I substituted one cup of Almond flour and instead of 1 1/4 of Sugar, I used one cup of Truvia baking blend and 1/4 cup of sugar. All other ingredients were as directed. It came out so delicious... I plan to try the full amount of alternative ingredients next try. Keep you posted on what difference this makes, if any. Thanks for the recipe. I can’t stop eating it.

My bananas came to about 1-1/2 cups so I just used it all. I also used a full cup of chopped walnuts, added about 2 heaping tsp. of cinnamon and a few shakes of nutmeg. I also didn't have vanilla, so I used about a couple tablespoons of Vermont Maple Syrup. I made it into one large loaf, it is spectacular, truly moist, and made a beautiful bread. I probably cooked for about an hour at 350 and turned down to 325 and put foil loosely over the top for the last 15 minutes in order to have it cook through without browning any more. Perfect!

attributes.source_text: truly moist

reviews.review_text: Very, very good banana nut bread. I felt like making it even though I didn’t have all the ingredients and had to substitute. I only had cake flour and just 1-3/4 cups of that, so I used about 1/4 cup of Pioneer baking mix. I ran out of butter yesterday and I don’t really like margarine, so I used mostly coconut oil (solid) with just a bit of margarine for butter flavor, I misread the directions and used 1-1/2 c of sugar and I added about 1/2 tsp cinnamon just because. With all of these substitutions and missteps, it’s the best banana nut bread I’ve ever tasted. It has a nice crunchy top, too. I did have walnuts (surprise) and they are a nice touch. I made 2 loaves. It might have all fit in one pan, but having 2 loaves means it lasts longer. ??

attributes.source_text: It has a nice crunchy top

reviews.review_text: I usually just buy store bought banana nut bread or a mix. I have a lot of time on my hands. I had 3 ripe bananas, headed to my local grocery store and purchased walnuts, vanilla bean extract, eggs and almond milk. My kitchen smelled like my Home Economics class room from high school. The aroma of the banana nut bread baking was so good. This morning I cut me a slice and had with my coffee. OMG, this is the best tasting, moist tasting banana nut bread. I made one large loaf and one small loaf. I am definately going to make my own banana nut bread from now on.

items.description: I searched and searched for a banana bread recipe with the texture that I wanted and couldn't find one.   One day I decided to modify my Recipe #14187 to see if I could make up my own recipe.   My family loved it and it was exactly what I was looking for so here it is.   I hope you like it as much as we do.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F.
Mix oil, eggs and mashed bananas.
Combine remaining ingredients and add to banana mixture.
grease and flour pans,place on baking sheet.
Bake in a 2/ 9 x 5 x 3 inch pan 0r 4 mini loaves [mini's will take about 45 minutes] for 1 hour or until bread tests done.

reviews.review_text: The only reason why this recipe has no stars is because it doesn't deserve any stars at all for me.  This was by far the worst, most frustrating recipe I have made from Zaar so far.  The flavor of the batter was great, but the directions as to what size and how many loaf pans to bake the bread in were too vague.  I baked the bread in 1 standard 9X5X3 loaf pan, very well loobed with shortening, for an hour and a half, and the batter never set on the inside.  I had doubts when I saw the batter filled the pan right to the top; fortunately, I placed a parchment-lined sheet pan under the bread to catch all the batter that ran over the sides.  I still have to clean the oven rack, and the bread pan itself is soaking so I can clean the outside .  If the author of this recipe would care to write me  and provide clearer baking instructions, I would love to try this recipe again as I had high hopes for it, but for now, this recipe is a disaster.  I am no baking novice, but I don't understand how this recipe earned such high marks.

I want to start out saying I was determined to make this recipe!!  I used 1/2 cup strawberry lite applesauce (sweetened with splenda; for some reason I was out of the regular lite) plus 1 tbsp Enova oil instead of the 2/3 cup oil, 2 eggs worth egg beaters, 1 cup half whole wheat half enriched white mix flour, little less than 1 cup splenda instead of sugar, 1 box fat free sugar free banana cream pudding (again for some reason I was out of vanilla), salt substitute, and a little baking powder since splenda seems to flatten a lot of my recipes.  And I mazola sprayed my loaf pan just in case.  This was absolutely delicious!  It is truly the most moist banana bread me and husband has ever had.  Thank you for the recipe... next time I will use regular applesauce, but it was still good.  Thank you for the wonderful recipe.

attributes.source_text: the most moist banana bread
me and husband has ever had

reviews.review_text:
If your store only has a large size of banana pudding use about half cup of pudding. I added 1 cup of coarsely chopped walnuts. After reading about it being a little "wet" in the center I added 1/4 cup of flour. I used 1/4 cup of apple sauce and 1/4 cup of oil. I used the apple sauce as a substitute for oil and it worked. 
Each batch made 4 mini loaves. I cooked them in the blue silicone loaf pans. It came out ok. I made 3 batches and 1 or 2 loaves had a little sticking problem. All the oithers were fine. Finished product was very moist. I'm going to give away to friends and neighbors this holiday season. Thanks to everybody who gave input in tweaking this recipe. QUESTION - This recipe doesn't use baking powder only baking soda. Why is that? Did anybody try adding baking powder? Result?

attributes.source_text: Finished product was very moist

reviews.review_text: I am in search of the perfect banana bread.  I have tried 4 recipes so far.  This was very good and moist.  I halfed the recipe as I only wanted one loaf.  I accidentally forget to half the baking soda and it can out perfect.  I have read many reviews of this recipe of all the failures (i.e. cake fell in the middle).  I think the problem might be mysterygirl forget to double the amout of baking soda.  In all four banana bread recipes I have tried, they have called for 1 tsp  of baking soda for one loaf.  I did have to bake it for 1:20 minutes.  I ran a knife around the edge to remove and it can right out. Other than the baking soda, I used slightly less oil , regular vanilla pudding were the only changes.  Mine came out much darker than the picture.

reviews.review_text: I made a double batch cause I had quite a few bananas to use up and so I baked in a large, non-stick bundt pan, which I didn't grease (if you read other reviews you'll understand why I mention this).  I did make 3 slight (?) changes in that I added 2 tsps of vanilla extract and a tsp of baking powder and reduced the sugar to 1 1/2 cups (for the double batch).  The cake rose up high, and it took exactly 1 hour and 40 minutes to bake - but don't forget this was a double batch.  It did not burn, but it did get rather dark.  This always happens to my cakes in this non-stick pans.  At first it wouldn't budge and I thought it would be stuck in the pan, but a sharp tap on my counter with the pan turned upside-down brought the cake out perfectly!  Smelled great.  Couldn't wait to cut in.  Interesting exterior...not really cakey, more like a 'shell'.  When you cut in, the whole cake kind of sinks in until the knife cuts through the shell-like exterior, which is a bit chewy, but good.  Inside, fluffy, not dense at all.  Good banana flavour.  Even with reduced sugar, I still found it a tad too sweet - could be our Greek vanilla pudding is sweeter than yours - anyway, I'll cut back a bit more next time.  All around, very nice bread for all the time.

reviews.review_text:
Now I see what "too moist" means. This was delicious. I didn't have vanilla so I used choc pudding, then thought, hey, why not some choc chips too? I started with 3 dying bananas; now I have this way-decadent banana-chocolate cake. I'll try it again; maybe bake it 90 min. instead of 80, add flour, use vanilla pudding mix, and maybe sub some of the flour for whole wheat. I also used applesauce instead of oil; I have been doing that for awhile and my stuff always comes out identical. I sprayed with non-stick spray, and let it cool in the pan, and only a few choc chips stuck to the pan. Yes, they were yummy!
Update: I cut out one sixth of the sugar, and it was still very good. I tripled the recipe, added a bunch of healthy stuff (chia, ground flax, quinoa flakes, substituted one sixth whole wheat flour, chopped walnuts), and it is still so delicious. Mini muffins for ravenous kids for breakfast, mini muffins w choc chips for me for later and to share with others, and 2 loaves still baking for the freezer.

reviews.review_text: This has been my standby for years. The only reason I have not reviewed it before is the sheer amount of positive input it has received, but perhaps on more can't hurt. This is a very moist, dense luscious bread. I can't abide a dry bread and this one has no chance of becoming so. I have tried it in all different varieties and tweaked things here and there but I always come back to the original. Yes, it does occasionally come out to wet in the middle but I get around this by using mini loafs or one those cool novelty pans with sticks or tiny bite sized squares they have for brownies now adays. They are always perfect and then I can just bag them up for lunches or snacks. This recipe freezes wonderfully and only gets better the longer you let it sit. Perfect!

items.label: Kittencal's Extreme Chocolate Brownies
items.name: Kittencal's Extreme Chocolate Brownies
items.description: if your looking for an everyday run-of-the-mill cake-style brownie then pass this by, this is a a moist chewy extreme chocolate bakery-style brownie that takes little time to make and tastes even better the next day, it's everything a good brownie should be!  --- I have even made these using half brown sugar and half white sugar, the amount of sugar listed will give you a sweet brownie you may reduce the sugar by 1/4 cup or more if desired or if you have a sweet tooth use amount stated --- add in a couple of tablespoons of coffee-flavored liqueur in place of the vanilla if desired -- according to a reviewer oil may be used in place of the butter successfully --- these brownies freeze very well,  they are so simple to make just mix everything by hand, they bake out so rich and sinful! --- see recipe#89207
instructions: Set oven to 325 degrees F.
Grease a 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
In a heavy saucepan, bring butter, sugar and water to a boil, stirring constantly until the butter is melted and sugar is dissolved (about 3 minutes).
Remove from the heat, with a wooden spoon, stir in 2 cups chocolate chips until melted; cool slightly, beat in vanilla.
In a mixing bowl,whisk eggs, gradually add in the chocolate mixture, beating with a wooden spoon until completely mixed.
Mix together flour, baking soda and salt; add to the egg/chocolate mixture; mix well to combine.
Stir in the remaining chocolate chips.
Spread into prepared baking pan.
Bake for 35-40 minutes (don't over bake).
Cut into squares.
Note: If desired, chopped walnuts may be added.

reviews.review_text: TL:DR Do not use Nestle semi-sweet chocolate chips in this recipe!! I have made this recipe at least a dozen times and let me just say it is ah-ma-zing! The following has nothing to do with the recipe but it is a warning to other bakers. I normally use Ghirardelli semi-sweet chocolate chips and have never had a problem making these. Today, I only had Nestle semi-sweet chocolate chips. I followed the recipe the same as I always do but when I added the chocolate chips to the sugar mixture the whole thing clumped up and turned crumbly. I assumed it was too hot for the chocolate chips so I decided to try it again. This time I melted the chocolate chips in the microwave and let the sugar mixture cool for a few minutes before I mixed them together. The same result but to a lesser degree. I have come to the conclusion to never use Nestle for this recipe. I probably won't be using Nestle at all in the future.

AMAZING! Kept well sitting out for a couple days, too. Our goto brownie recipe! My only caveat is that the edges cook WELL before the center. I read on here this may be because of the chocolate chips. I will need to try with melting them all, next time, to see if that helps. Keep an eye on 'em in the oven and if anyone has any suggestions for a more even cooking, please let me know. (I DID try to cover them while cooking, but it didn't help.)<br/><br/>Edited to add: I've made these several times since. Here are my thoughts:<br/><br/>1. Don't over cook or cook until they look "done." If you do that, it will end up like a very dry cake with all of your chocolate chips on the bottom somewhat dry and slightly burned.<br/><br/>2. Instead, cook the brownies in a LARGE pan (they really rise from all those eggs!) until they no longer shake like jelly in the middle when you shake the pan. Once it's firm enough not to shake, leave them in another minute or two and then take them out! THEY WILL NOT LOOK DONE! But, once they cool, they will firm up into very fudgy ooey gooey brownies that are absolutely heavenly.<br/><br/>3. Enjoy!

reviews.review_text:
These were great, and this is my first review and first time making brownies. Infact I have my second lot in the oven now!!!!

A few things went wrong for me,but my fault. I find it difficult to convert some measurements into Australian ones, so maybe I ended up with some variations, especially in the `cup` listings.
I also completely overlooked the instruction of halving the chocolate, so mine were all melted chocolate, no pieces. Mind you, this did not detract from the yumminess factor here!!!
My main problem was that the chocolate seized up following the instructions of putting into the butter, sugar and water mixture. And thats a lot of chocolate to ruin. I continued with the recipe anyway, and it turned out yummy enough that I got no complaints. It didnt cook all the way through, but that may have been because I stuffed up the chocolate and it cxhanged the texture??? Anyway, the second time I melted the choc by itself in the microwave and so far all is good.
I also added walnuts which was a big hit and made it a bit more grown up.....and of course added some more calories!!!!!

I can see this dessert served on a white plate warmed slightly with cream on the side.It is worthy of serving to guests thats for sure! 

I like how this recipe is pretty forgiving, and easy. Well done for posting it!

reviews.review_text:
Having discovered Kittencal's recipes and being SO delighted with the results, I will now commence working my way through all of them - well maybe not ALL!!! I urge you all to try them!!
Anyway, I had a brownie 'cook-off' today with my daughter and her friend (both 16 and brownie addicts) as the final arbitors!!  I have al;ways used BC mix ones - doctored with extra chocolate chunks but feel guilty to call them homemade if all i did was assemble them :-( So I was looking for the ulitmate replacement. 
This recipe came out tops from 3 other recipes and I then tweaked it a bit further to suit their demanding tastes. I kept the same amount of sugar but then replaced 2 tablespoons of the flour with 2 tablespoons of best cocoa powder and added a teaspoon of instant coffee granules. It just added that extra dark chocolatey bitterness - which meant they could carry off the sweetness from the sugar. I can't recommend these highly enough!

reviews.review_text: I made this for a Christmas Eve party, and I *liked* them but didn't *love* them, hence the four stars.  The recipe was great and I made it exactly as stated (baked the first batch for 35 mins and the second batch for 32 minutes to try to get them a little more moist) - but they came out more like little chocolate cakes than brownies - which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but just not what I wanted!  I guess the four eggs should have been a clue!  Anyway, one interesting thing, as a few others have said here, they were about 1000 times better the next day and the day after that - so keep that in mind - much less cakey and much denser and richer.  Still, I have always used the RZ recipe for "Whatever Floats Your Boat" brownies (no. 32204) and will stick with that one for thinner, more gooey brownies, but if your prefer a chocolate-cake brownie, then do use this Extreme version - but make it the day before serving for sure.  I didn't get any oooh and ahhs on Christmas Eve, but by the end of Christmas day these were all gone!!

Once again, thank you Kittencal for a great recipe. I like this recipe but it did turn out a little "cakey" for me, but it could have been because I substituted two things! I didn't have vanilla, so I used molasses, then I ran out of pure butter so I used butter AND vegetable oil. So, I think if I followed it to a "T" it would be great! I NEEDED chocolate.  I was desperate.  But it couldn't be just any chocolate; it had to have the right texture as well.  So, there was only one answer: BROWNIES!

I didn't have chocolate chips, so I used premium chocolate bars.  400 grams of dark chocolate for the batter, then I broke one bar of white chocolate and one bar of milk chocolate into chunks to mix in place of the second addition of chips.

Also, instead of plain vanilla, I used something we have here that is a mixture of Vanilla and Orange Flower extract.  It gave a wonderful little "extra" zing.

My oven tends to bake hot; so I did reduce the baking time by about 5 minutes.  Underbaked brownies are better than overbaked any day.

These were just about the perfect brownie.  I froze half (I'm not crazy; I wasn't going to keep ALL of them available at one time!), and put the rest in an airtight tin.

A quick, delicious recipe to be sure. I 'll be making it again when my hips recover from this batch.

items.description: This is how my Granny made sweet tea and it is some kind of sweet. Know that and beware. Pa-Paw used to down 2-3 glasses after working in the garden all day. Back off the sugar if you can't handle it. This one is for true southerners only ;)
instructions: In a large glass measuring cup, place the tea bags and add the baking soda.
Pour the boiling water over the tea bags.
Cover and steep for 15 minutes.
Take out the tea bags and do not squeeze them.
Pour the tea mixture into a 2-quart pitcher; add the sugar.
Stir until the sugar is dissolved.
Add in the cold water.
Let cool; chill in the refrigerator and serve over ice.

reviews.review_text:
The fact that I'm willing to drink this cracks me up because tea is something COMPLETELY different (and holy) to me (I order it direct from a farm in Japan or from importers here who specialize in top-grade tea--bags are anathema).
This was yummy--more along the lines of soda (without the bubbles) than tea! I went with 1.5 cups of sugar and used Lipton because we have no Luzianne in NYC and I refuse to pay to have it shipped. I also like the fact that it's so beautifully transparent. My tiny deviation consisted of dunking the brewed tea bags in the cold water in order to get as much as I could from them without squeezing. We have access to Meyer lemons here, which provide a perfect (albeit Yankee, I assume) complement.
I recently learned of a new, one-for-one sugar substitute called Whey Low that I intend to use in the future in order to avoid having my pancreas charge me with attempted murder. It's guaranteed to taste MUCH better than Splenda, exactly like sugar (from which it's made), and is safe for diabetics. I'm now looking forward to making this recipe with a safer GRI. Thanks SO much for posting!

I was a bit concerned about using this recipe today for two reasons. One I purchased tea specifically for this recipe and still managed to buy an herbal tea. Must have seemed like a good idea at the time but as I pulled it out of my cabinet I realized I wanted a more traditional flavor, which this recipe implies. 

And two I've switched from sugar to agave nectar, which although it takes less to sweeten an item, I've found that it takes a LOT of product when making liquids so I feared I wouldn't be able to get it sweet enough. Both due to the loads of calories and the cost of agave nectar.

Long story short neither was an issue. I'm waiting for it to chill but as it stands it's very sweet without having used a full bottle of agave:) And the herbal tea is a nice touch although next time I will go with traditional.

reviews.review_text: I Doubled the recipe, used 12 Tea bags (I bought the cheap ones), steeped for 1 Hour (I forgot about it lol), used 3/4 cup Sugar, juice of 1 fresh Lemon, and added a 1/2 inch chunk of peeled, fresh Ginger and it was perfect for me. I usually follow a recipe the first time I make something but I knew that was way too much sugar for me, and I doubled the amount of tea and water. I hate when people say they made it but they've changed pretty much everything in the original recipe but that's exactly what I've done here. :-( Please forgive me, I'm trying to replace soda with sweet tea, I'm attempting to avoid corn syrup and Aspartame and I need something caffeinated to replace soda. :-)

Growing up in Alabama but with a mom that doesnt drink sweet tea, I had to learn how to make southern sweet tea for my husband. Definitely start with less sugar and add if needed! My MIL makes hers with 2 cups and it's just too sweet for my husband and I. We go through tea really fast, so I reduced the amount of tea bags because I was going through them like crazy. I use 3 tea bags and let the tea steep for longer. After steeping and letting it set for a few hours, I warmed the tea back up so it would dissolve the sugar easier. I use about 1 cup - 1 1/4 cups of sugar and this is PLENTY sweet for us. Then I let the tea bags hang out in the tea pitcher for a few hours before discarding them. Not sure if it's the baking soda or what but this is the smoothest tea I've ever had and my husband really loves it so it's a winner in our house!

Just got back from visiting my sister in the south and I have to admit that when I get home I miss the sweet tea almost as much as I miss visiting with my sister. 
I have tried to make sweet tea several times before, but it always has a bitterness to it and doesn't seem to taste like the sweet tea in the Low Country.
I have to admit that I almost turned away from this recipe at first because the baking soda was an odd ingredient, but after seeing the reviews I decided I probably couldn't go wrong, and I was right.
I doubled the recipe and only used 2 cups of sugar in the whole thing and it was sweet enough for me. And I have to admit that the baking soda does actually make it smooth, so interesting.
Thanks for sharing your granny's recipe, I am so glad that I can now make delicious southern sweet tea anytime I want while I'm at home in California. :)

which really does cut down on the bitterness

reviews.review_text: I joined this web site just to comment on this recipe. I made 1 gallon of Lipton's Blackberry tea using 14 tea bags, 3 cups of sugar and steeped it for 18 minutes. I did not squeeze the bags though I did allow the excess water time to drip out and it turned out great. I agree its a bit sweet though it did not over power the good clean tea taste. I forgot to use the baking soda of which I think is to help it not be cloudy. Thanx for the recipe, it will always be the recipe I use from now on.

attributes.source_text: the good clean tea taste

reviews.review_text: I'm afraid I just didn't care much for this iced tea. It wasn't the sweetness--it was that all I could taste was sugar. It was too weak for my taste. I made a 1.5 batch, using 9 bags of Red Rose tea and just under 3 cups of sugar. I think I'll stick with my old, quick, brewed iced tea recipe, which is stronger-tasting. This was quite easy to make, and if you like a sweet, not so strong iced tea, I think this would suit very well. Sorry it didn't work out, but thanks for posting anyway, ratherbeswimmin'--I'm glad I tried it! Made for Comfort Cafe.

attributes.source_text: if you like a sweet, not so strong iced tea
if you like a sweet, not so strong iced tea

reviews.review_text: This is the smoothest ice tea ever, no bitter Taste with the tea after it has steeped. I did however read the reviews with the taste of sugar. This is a treat following the given amount. It's sweet tea! But we drink ice tea everyday and I start with 1/3 cup of sugar that is good to the taste for drinking it all the time. It's a matter of preference . Thank you for the baking soda addition would not have known this to cut the bitterness that sometime overstepped tea can give.

attributes.source_text: This is the smoothest ice tea ever
no bitter Taste with the tea after it has steeped

reviews.review_text: When it says sweet, oh man, they're not kidding.  It was sweet, brown water.  And I'm from the south and like it super sweet, but this was just too much even for me.  I could taste no tea flavor at all....not even a little.  So, I tried it again.  I doubled the tea bags so that you could actually TASTE tea and cut the sugar back to 1 cup.  Then when I served it, I served it with lemon wedges to further cut back on the ubersweetness.  Second batch was definitely better than the first.

The folks I had for dinner (we are expats working in Bahamas) were all from VA and NC. I knew I had to make good sweet tea for them.  They gulped down two pitchers-full of this stuff; even my DH, who doesn't usually drink that much, said it was superb. I didn't add quite the amt. of sugar called for, and it was plenty sweet. But thanks so much because I was iced-tea challenged up this point. I made one of the ladies promise she wouldn't spill the beans that I actually had to use a recipe to make this  !! But I was so happy; thanks for a great recipe.

attributes.source_text: The folks I had for dinner
even my DH, who doesn't usually drink that much, said it was superb
it was plenty sweet

reviews.review_text: Excellent! I used two family size teabags and it made a strong looking tea, but it had no bitter/strong taste to it at all. Really delicious! I only used 3/4 C. sugar and it was just right for our taste. I must confess, I made this for my daughter who loves sweet tea, but after tasting it myself, I ended up drinking 4 glasses!!! I am also going to make this again without sugar for my husband who doesn't care for sweet tea but lives on unsweetened tea. I'm curious to see if it taste any different than the reg. way we brew it.  Thanks for this yummy version...it's a keeper!

attributes.source_text: it had no bitter/strong taste to it at all
it had no bitter/strong taste to it at all
my daughter who loves sweet tea
my daughter who loves sweet tea

reviews.review_text:
Thank you for sharing this simple recipe. My husband loves sweet tea and after his tea maker broke he was lost for a while. I tried sun tea- but it was too weak for him. Regular tea recipes weren't sweet enough (my hubby puts sugar on his frosted flakes if that tells you anything!) When I tested this out on him he loved it. Now I make this 2-3 times a week for him and he's happy.

6/4/10 Edited to Add: I still make this for my hubby soon as it gets close to summer time. I make it by the gallon so I only have to make it every-other day.

attributes.source_text: My husband loves sweet tea
