items.label: Fried Rice
items.name: Fried Rice
items.description: Make and share this Fried Rice recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Melt 1 tablespoon butter in skillet or wok.
Scramble eggs in butter, breaking up the cooked eggs into small pieces.
Set aside.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in skillet or wok.
Saute onions and/or green peppers in butter for 3 minutes.
Combine eggs, onions, rice, and meat.
Stir in soy sauce until color of rice is uniform.
Stir in peas.
Heat only until warm.

reviews.review_text: You know I"ve been making this for over a year now and realized I haven't reviewed this awsum, amazing, wonderful rice recipe! We LOVE LOVE LOVE it, thank you so much! I do 3 things different: 1)  I use a 50-50 combination of peanut oil and sesame oil instead of butter, 2) I add a clove of fresh minced garlic to it, 3) I fry the rice by itself for 10-15 mins or so till some is lightly browned before I lastly put in the other ingredients and soy sauce to brown it. Usually I make without meat, but it's still wonderful with! And of course I always make it inthe wok. Another tip: I put our leftover rice from meals in the freezer, then thaw it out when I want to make this recipe. Works like a charm and we aren't wasting it!  I cannot thank you enough for this recipe.

What a great way to use up little bits of leftover ingredients!  I was looking for a recipe that would use up a small amount of leftover meat and rice and this fit the bill perfectly.  This was very quick, easy, inexpensive, and tasty.  This was indeed nothing like Asian style fried rice - this has a completely different taste.  My family enjoyed this very much and we will make this again.  The only changes I would make would be to decrease the amount of butter - I halved the butter and still felt I could have used nonstick butter flavor spray instead.  I also thought the amount of soy sauce made this a little bit too salty - I would either reduce the amount or use lower sodium soy sauce.  I suspect that the author perhaps eyeballs his soy sauce as he adds it to the rice - he instructs you to add soy sauce until the rice turns brown (so maybe he guessed approximately 1/4 cup and it is actually less?)  Anyway, I still thought is was a very good family dish.

attributes.source_text: My family enjoyed this very much

reviews.review_text:
Very nice recipe indeed.  I did however, improvise... (pardon) I added to the onions (1.2 red onion) 1tbl freshly grated garlic, half yellow and red bell pepper. 
I did too.. (gosh so sorry) added 1 cup freshly sliced mushrooms. 
The secret of this recipe, in my opinion, is to layer the onions, and in my case, the garlic and bell peppers then layer the rice, the scrambled egg and then veges and cover and let it steam on a low heat.  Outstanding taste indeed.  I did "cheat" and added 1 cup of "stir fry veges" to the mix for colour and variety instead of just peas.. just of personal perference...  I also didn't add the soy sauce to the whole dish, I allowed my guests to add their own quantity of soy when dishing up.  
Really outstanding.. thank you very  much... it was a pleasure to make ... I served this with a barbecued thick pork cutlet. 
Mmmmmm , very good.

attributes.source_text: I allowed my guests to add their own quantity of soy when dishing up

reviews.review_text: I had rice leftover and also some chicken leftover from bourbon chicken, so I diced up the chicken into smaller pieces.  I also used some peas & carrots (frozen), reheated first of course.  I took the advice and did not use that much soy sauce, I just splashed some in.  Then I remembered that I had a tiny bit of "Veri Veri Teriyaki" sauce too leftover and not enough to really do much with, so I sprinkled in about 2 tbsp of that too.  I added a bit of chopped scallions.  Better than most Fried Rice I'd had at a lot of restaurants.  Great way to use up some leftovers too!  Will make this again.  Thanks!

I never really liked fried rice because I always thought it had little or no flavor (therefore purpose for existence). I made this because of all the reviews. After following the recipe, I thought - huh - tasted just like 'fried rice'. Then I thought to add garlic per other reviewers. Let me tell you, THAT changed EVERYTHING! For some reason, for me adding the garlic just totally TRANSFORMED this dish into something else entirely. I swear, I've never tasted fried rice I've liked until NOW for the first time! BTW I did only use 1 T butter and did use 1 tsp sesame oil and green onions, no grn pepper, did do carrots. :p

attributes.source_text: adding the garlic just totally TRANSFORMED this dish

reviews.review_text: This is almost exactly how I have made my fried rice for years. It is my favorite way to use leftover pork.  I use a little oil instead of butter, and sautee my eggs in one giant "omlet" across the bottom of skillet, flip them out and dice, I then add fresh garlic, onion and rice to the pan along with a dash of ginger and my leftover meat, and soy to taste.  I add frozen peas or peas/carrots right at the end of cooking!! My family LOVES this!!  It is so veratile - you can add whatever you have.  I agree chilled rice works best, but I use freshly cooked rice all the time with the same results!!! Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: My family LOVES this!!

reviews.review_text: This is an Excellent rice recipe!  Next time we'll make it with more veggies, cooked until they are nicely sautéed in butter til veggies are still crisp, will use more eggs, and will use pork next time (we used chicken last time). I Love the versatility of this recipe with all the optional ingredients.  We added carrots and celery, and I add whatever veggies I have on hand and it always turns out great. We don't think it's too salty, we used regular soy sauce and just added barely enough so that it was evenly colored.  This is a definite hit at our house! I don’t care if it’s “authentic” fried rice or not, I just know we love it!  Thank-you Robbie for the Awesome recipe.

attributes.source_text: We don't think it's too salty

reviews.review_text: Made to go along w/ Chinese Chicken and Broccoli Chinese Chicken and Broccoli. I stole a bit from another recipe that made too much, and used a good slosh of sesame oil to saute the onions in instead of more butter. I used green peas but no peppers or meat. I cooked long grain white rice in my rice cooker, using just a smidge less water to make sure that the rice wouldn't be gooey, and it came out just over the line of un-done thankfully. All in all, the recipe was quick, tastey, and easy to customize.

I served this tasty fried rice w/Kittencal’s Easy Japanese Chicken Wings recipe #152964 & it was a match made in heaven! I halved the recipe for only 2 of us, added diced mushrooms, further reduced the soy sauce in half & left out the optional peas & peppers (just didn’t have any). This was good stuff & the “bare bones” of this recipe (w/reduction of the soy sauce amt) make it perfect to create a 1-dish meal of meat or shrimp fried rice expanded to include baby corn, snow peas, mushrooms, bamboo shoots, bean sprouts & water chestnuts. I can't wait to try it! Thx for posting this.

The first time I made this I made it as directed and the flavor was just okay, but it was easy and it had the best texture of any fried rice we'd tried, so I tried it again adjusting a bit to suit our tastes. This time I stir-fryed the pork in the wok before starting the recipe. I beat a couple of drops sesame oil into the eggs, added 1/4 cup mushrooms with the green pepper and onion and used half butter and half olive oil instead of just the butter. Perfect for us. Thanks for sharing.

While searching for a  fried rice recipe, I came upon yours and when I noticed the many reviews I knew right then and there that I need look no further.  This recipe is so easy to make and the appearance and taste is absolutely awesome. I made it with chicken and  the only thing I did differently was to add a can of peas & carrots as opposed to just peas.  I will definitely be bragging about your fried rice recipe to my co-workers.  Thanks a bunch Robbie for sharing it.

Loved it. Per some of the other reviews, I subbed green onions and left out the green pepper as my family doesn't like it. Also per some of the reviews, I added only 1/8 cup of soy sauce at first and tasted the dish. I ended up adding it all and thought it was amazing.  Next time I will probably add some carrots as well, as I like to have both a green and orange veggie in each meal. My husband loved it and we finished it all! UPDATE: served it with Recipe #313537 - a real winning combo.

attributes.source_text: My husband loved it

reviews.review_text: Could use a little less soy sauce.  Maybe closer to 1/6 cup?  I know it's a small difference but soy sauce has a very strong flavor.  Being part Asian, I had some kimchee in my refrigerator so I just cut it up and used 3/4 cup of that instead of the onions, peppers and peas.  Being a college student, I only have inexpensive foods handy so instead of pork, shrimp or chicken I used 1/2 cup of bologna instead.  The result was an incredibly economical and yet delicious meal.  Next time I'll opt for cooking spray instead of butter to make it a little more healthy.

I have always been a failure with fried rice.  But I have finally found the secret is to use cold leftover rice :)  I fixed this with some leftover pork roast, all green onion and no peppers.  I really like this and could see adding some grated carrot for color. This was served as a side with Recipe #135753 and broccoli that i tossed with braggs amino acids, rice vinegar, ginger and sesame seeds.  Yummy meal and this rice was perfect!  thank you for posting :)

attributes.source_text: This was served as a side

reviews.review_text: What a fantastic recipe!  I completely forgot about it being a Friday during Lent and was in a panic trying to figure out what to make for dinner.  This recipe is completely made with every day pantry items.  I made it with shrimp, skipped the green peppers and used a rice-orzo concoction that my family prefers.  I used egg whites only.  My entire family loved this recipe.  I doubled it to use as an entree, and it is a good thing I did!  Thank you so very much for a recipe that is delicious and easy to prepare!

attributes.source_text: My entire family loved this recipe
what to make for dinner
to use as an entree

reviews.review_text: This was very very yummy!  I changed it just a bit, leaving the meat out, the green peppers and peas out (although the peas will go back in the next time) and I used green onions instead of white onion.  I think I am going to add shrimp next time.  My DH, who was babysat for years when he was grade school age by an older Asian woman (who made him fried rice and eggrolls homemade all the time) said this really reminded him of her rice.  Good job!  Thanks for the recipe!

attributes.source_text: My DH, who was babysat for years when he was grade school age by an older Asian woman (who made him fried rice and eggrolls homemade all the time) said this really reminded him of her rice

reviews.review_text: This was really easy to make especially since I made the rice the day before. I didnt use green peppers like the recipe suggested but I did use peas and chicken. I used less soy sauce than it calls for because I don't like soy sauce. I really didn't like the flavor of this at all, probably because of the soy sauce in it, and it definitely did not taste like the fried rice you would get in a restaurant. My husband added more soy sauce to his and he thought it was an okay dish.

items.label: Fresh Peach Cobbler
items.name: Fresh Peach Cobbler
items.description: Make and share this Fresh Peach Cobbler recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Mix peach slices with 3/4 cup sugar, set aside.
Pour butter in 8 inch square baking dish.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, nutmeg and remaining sugar.
Stir in milk, until just combined.
Pour over butter.
Top with peaches.
Bake at 375* for 45 minutes.

reviews.review_text:
This was good! I made a few adjustments using brown sugar and 1/2 teas. cinnamon in the peach mixture, and granulated sugar in the flour mixture. Out of milk, I substituted half & half and water. And lastly, I used 4 peaches instead of 2. 
I must add, that this recipe had me a bit nervous (especially steps 2-5). Oddly enough, I usually make cobblers with a homemade pie crust (cooking crust first, cooling, then adding peach filling). So, imagine my surprise when I pulled this cobbler from my oven:)
I'm aware that cobblers don't have pie crust...I just always preferred the crispy flaky texture in fruit filled desserts. Nevertheless, I will be making this again. Delicious & Simple!!! Thank you MizzNess:)

I had to play with this recipe quite a bit, but we were very happy with the outcome. First, I had to double the recipe since I didn't have an 8x8 pan :) I used 2 small nectarines, 1 big purple plum and 3 small red plums. I did NOT double the sugar in the fruit, using only 3/4 c. I added nutmeg into the fruit, and a cup of pecans as well.  The nuts didn't spread evenly, so next time I'll sprinkle them on top.
I had to leave this in the oven for an extra 10 minutes, and should have left it in even longer. I also suspect my baking powder is dead. Regardless, this was a delicious way to present stone fruit, and we'll do this again soon

This was delicious! Like a few other reviewers, I doubled the amount of peaches and added a tsp of cinnamon.  The bottom was a little too soggy, but that could have been the extra peaches. I also cut back the sugar to 1/4 cup on the peaches, which were very ripe and used the full 3/4 cup in the other part of the recipe.  The peaches wept a fair amount of liquid, which I added as well (next time I don't think I will). My baking time was also closer to 40 minutes (the top on the cobbler was dark brown at that point).  This recipe is also best served warm otherwise the peaches make the crust soggy.  This was a very simple recipe and would probably be excellent with many kinds of fresh fruit.  I think I'll try apples next time!

My BF's mother just gifted us with a ton of fresh SC peaches and while I love eating them as is...  they are startingto go bad...  this recipe saved these beauties from the garbage can.  While reading the other reviews, I decided to increase the amount of peaches...  I think I ended up using about 8 small peaches.  I really like a lot of fruit as opposed to dough.  I only used 1 cup of sugar (divided) and it was just the right amount of sweetness for us.  I didn't know if I was supposed to add in the juices from the peaches, so I only added in a few Tbs to keep it from being too juicy.  We both loved this topped off with some homemade vanilla ice cream...  Just delicious! Thanks for sharing!!!

attributes.source_text: it was just the right amount of sweetness for us

reviews.review_text:
I made this recipe twice this week. First one with fresh peaches and it was excellent. I also decide to try with plums and it came out great, the only thing I would suggest with plums is to add a 1/3 of a cup of flower in addition to sugar (when you put plums and sugar together while preping the other other ingrediens. I must say in our house it is a winer. I know I will be making this over and over again even during the week after I get home from work (late after 6pm), because all ingredients are always in my pantry and you can make this recipe in no time. Truly wonderful dessert.
Barbara

attributes.source_text: Truly wonderful dessert

reviews.review_text: This cobbler is delicious but it requires some modifications, which is why I've rated it 4 stars. First of all, 2 peaches is nowhere near enough fruit. I like my cobbler to have a lot of fruit, so I tripled the amount of peaches. The first time I made this, I only used peaches and found that it really needed something more tart to balance out the flavors. The second time I made it, I added fresh blackberries and it was exactly what it needed. This recipe also has a little too much sugar, so I cut it back slightly. The butter is also a little more than is needed, so I cut this back as well. I added some lemon juice to the peach mixture and also put half granulated sugar and half brown sugar. When I made it the first time around, I used the nutmeg but I wasn't all that fond of it. The second time around I added cinnamon to the peach mixture as well as the batter and it turned out PERFECTLY! :)

I've made this twice now and it's just delicious.  The first time I used the full amount of butter and about half the sugar.  We loved it, but it just seemed like an excessive amount of butter.  The second time I used only about 2 tablespoons of butter, and sprinkled only a little bit of sugar on my peaches (they were really ripe and very sweet).  I still used about half the amount of sugar in the dough and also added a bit of cinnamon too.  It turned out just wonderful even with my changes.  I used 5 peaches, but I think I could've thrown even 2 or 3 more and it would've been fine.

I guess I'm the odd man out.  I really didn't enjoy this.  The butter on the bottom made a huge mess.  As the cake began to bubble, it was spilling butter over the edge in the over and landing on the burner and the whole house smelled like smoking, burning butter.  The edges of the cake also had this flavor.  This also wasn't very cobble like.  It was very spongy, sticky and cakey.  I usually enjoy cakey stuff, but this just wasn't what I was going for.  My daughter took a couple bites and my husband ate half his serving, but no really enjoyed it.  So sorry to not post a good review but this was just odd for us.

OMG! This was SO good!  The crust was light and fluffy!  The peaches tasted devine!  It was so easy to make that I can't believe it came out so well!  I took another reviewer's advice and used brown sugar to mix into the peaches and white sugar for the crust part.  I used 3 large peaches instead of 2 and it might have even used the 4 like everyone else was saying.  I omitted the nutmeg due to personal preference and since I made this in a glass dish, it cooked much faster and I took it out for fear of burning after 40 minutes.  But this is a keeper!!  Thanks for sharing!

attributes.source_text: The crust was light and fluffy
The crust was light and fluffy

reviews.review_text: I needed a LOT of peaches because I used a 9x13, which made a thin cobbler - I like them that way because I like my dough "crunchy" rather than "cakey". I ended up putting the nutmeg on the peach mixture and mixing a tsp of vanilla into the crust. Despite using about 15 small peaches, I would have liked more fruit and next time I will use more for the bigger size pan. The ease of prep (other than peeling/slicing all those peaches!) was easy and the taste was divine. Thanks so much for posting, I know I will use this again!

attributes.source_text: which made a thin cobbler - I like them that way
I like my dough "crunchy" rather than "cakey"

reviews.review_text: MizzNezz, I have made this so many times, I thought that I had already rated it, but I guess I didn't, well not like you need another 5 star, but I just had to get my 2 cents in anyway lol!...well, there's not much more that I can add to this huge heap of 5 star reviews, just that as all of your other recipes, this is definately another winner...very easy to make, wonderful served with ice cream, I used 6 smaller fresh peaches, and that seemed to work just right for me. Thank you so much for sharing MizzNezz, we thoroughly enjoyed it!....Kitten:)

I had been wanting to make this for awhile & fro some reason never did. Friday afternoon I remembered that i had to bring desert to girls night. Well what better. time. I thought I had all the simple ingredients on hand & starting making it & then realized all I had was skim milk. This was still DELICIOUS. The only thing different was I topped it with a combo of brown sugar & crushed glazed pecans. Few tabs of butter & wha la. Topped with vanilla ice cream & it was gone. I should have tripled the recipe. Thank you . It's a keeper for sure.

attributes.source_text: I had to bring desert to girls night

reviews.review_text: I really liked this  ... I was going to make a peach cobbler that called for bisquick instead I added flour so I had to find a recipe I could adapt to what I had already mixed up. This recipe worked great. I had already drained and put 1 1/2 quarts of peaches in the bottom of my 8x8. I made a few other change. I used cinnamon instead of nutmeg, added 1 cup sugar to the batter and sprinkled sugar on top of the peaches and added blueberries. I also had already melted the butter and stired it into the batter. Anyway you slice it this made for a great breakfast - Thanks

attributes.source_text: this made for a great breakfast

reviews.review_text: This cobbler is fabulous!! I made a few changes though and it turned out exactly like the cobbler my grandma used to make before she passed. For the peach mixture I mixed in dark brown sugar instead of the regular sugar (and added a teaspoon of vanilla), I added cinnamon- both in the flour mixture and sprinkled a bit on top. The last 10 minutes of baking I drizzled a mxiture of butter and brown sugar and it made a sort of candy coating that topped this cobbler off perfectly! Thanks so much for the recipe..I won't be needing any other cobbler recipes from here on out :-)

I think you are bent upon collecting all the stars in the Universe. So please let me contribute 5 more to your kitty. I made this today to take to my nephews birthday and I had a sneak(y) preview. It tasted YUM!! First time that I have made a cobbler. Not the last but!!! We do not get very large peaches in India so I was confused as to how large large was. I went ahead and used 9 but it did seem the dish could take some more. So on Sunday when I make it again I am planning to use 12. Thank you MissNezz you are a star yourself. :) Fay

attributes.source_text: to take to my nephews birthday

reviews.review_text: DELICIOUS and worth another 5 stars!  It was very, very easy and my family loved it! I used 1-1/2 times the batter recipe, used 6 medium peaches, only 1/4 cup butter, and used a 7x11-inch 2-quart casserole and baked about 1 hour because I had increased the recipe.  The cobbler crust/dough was very nice and light  and the peaches were perfectly done.   I did add 1/2 tsp. cinnamon, but otherwise followed  the recipe as given.   I will be using this for many different types of fruit cobblers as the seasons change.  Thanks for a wonderful recipe.

attributes.source_text: my family loved it
The cobbler crust/dough was very nice and light

reviews.review_text: Chef Bev was nice enough to let me have some of this cobbler that she prepared last evening.  This was truly an out of body peach cobbler experience!  To attain maximum flavor absorption I would have smeared it all over myself as I ate it except I didn't want to waste it.  This is the way peach cobbler is supposed to be!  The breading was not at all mushy or flavorless like most cobblers and it didn't mask the sweetness of the peach flavor.  I suggest you try this cobbler first-time without the ice-cream so you don't disturb the flavor.  This one's a keeper!  Hooray for Inez!!!

attributes.source_text: out of body peach cobbler experience
The breading was not at all mushy
the sweetness of the peach flavor

reviews.review_text: This was wonderful.  I had actually found some really sweet, ripe peaches and went looking for a great recipe...found one!!  I made only one change and that was the amount of peaches.  I used 6 good size ripe ones.  I did not change the batter amount or anything else.  It was perfect.  I did add some Watkins Vanilla Nut extract to the peaches and sugar.  We won't know what it tastes like as leftovers as there aren't any.  Easy prep and great taste.  DH says he still prefers the crunchy pie crust type crust for a cobbler but had 2 servings of this one!

attributes.source_text: really sweet, ripe peaches
DH says he still prefers the crunchy pie crust type crust for a cobbler but had 2 servings of this one!

reviews.review_text: We have made this several times. The first time we made it with 4 peaches, it was too much bread for me but my husband loved it. The next time we made it with 4 large apples so we doubled the cake portion, definately too much bread. The third time we made it with 8 peaches, it still was not yielding the type of consistency that I like, a nice juicy peach cobbler but the method is so simple and the taste so divine that I was determined to make it work. Yesterday we made it with 12 peaches, using a 9x13 baking dish. We mixed 12 peaches and 1 1/2 cups of sugar and let it sit for hours. It was so much juice it spilled out of the pan as it was baking. I need a bigger pan. I was baking it for a potluck and it wasnt pretty but my sister said to bring it anyway. It was the first dessert to go. If you are looking for a juicer cobbler with the simpliest method around this one is it. My best friend usually gift homemade cobblers for my birthday with the fancy lattice work now I can make one on my own whenever we want without having to make pie crust. I bake a lot and try a lot of recipes, I have to admit this one is my favorite, in simplicity and taste. I love that it celebrates the freshness of the peaches and not cover them up with the addition of too much nutmeg and cinnamon. Ratings on as written I will still give it a 5, it tasted great and was definitely easy to make. Aside from increasing the peaches and the sugar for the increased amount of peaches, I leave everything else the same.

attributes.source_text: a nice juicy peach cobbler
my husband loved it
I was baking it for a potluck
It was the first dessert to go

reviews.review_text: This recipe is Foolproof!!!! No matter how many peaches you put in, the results will equal the best tasting cobbler.  I used 6 medium to large sized peaches and kept the batter the same.  I added 1/2 tsp. cinnamon but otherwise did not change a thing.  This recipe is just as good cold as it is warm.  Top with fresh whipped cream and you have a truly great tasting dessert. I like how quick this recipe is to make.  Thanks for the great recipe.  I will also make this with my own canned peaches and will keep the taste of summer alive.

attributes.source_text: a truly great tasting dessert

items.label: Chocolate Cream Pie
items.name: Chocolate Cream Pie
items.description: This pie is so rich. It is so quick and easy. It is also enjoyed quick and easy. You must try this for your next Chocolate Pie. I HAVE to make it EVERY Thanksgiving, especially for son Kevin and son-in-law Dwain. My sister-in-law, Sherry, entered it in their 1996 church cookbook, "Give Us This Day Our Daily Bread", Wise County, Texas.
instructions: Mix water and cornstarch and cocoa until smooth.
Sir in Eagle Brand milk and egg yolks.
Cook until thick in saucepan or microwave.

reviews.review_text:
I am giving this recipe a five star for the pie filling and the review and advice from Dr.JenLeddy (thank you for your recommendations).

First I made my crust (no store bought for this girl). I decided on an Oreo cookie crust.
Ingredients:
20 - 30 Oreo cookies
4 - 6 Tbsp unsalted butter
Directions:
- Melt your butter (start with the lesser amount and add more if needed)
- Crush your cookies as fine as you can (a zip lock bag and rolling pin worked fine for me.)
- Pour your grounds into your pie pan (I use a porcelain or glass pan)
- Add butter and with your HANDS mix thoroughly until the cookies are lightly coated enough to be spread evenly along the bottom and sides of the pan (too much butter can make the crust harden until it is like trying to eat cement). Add cookies and melted butter as needed.
- Place crust in pan uncovered in freezer until you are ready to use.

Now with my filling, I followed the basic layout of the recipe but used the advice from fellow users. This is what I did, using a small whisk the entire time for mixing. I wanted it perfectly smooth because nobody likes a lumpy pudding or pie.

Ingredients:
1 2/3 C. water
4 Tbsp cornstarch
6 Tbsp cocoa powder
1 can sweetened condensed milk (14 oz)
2 eggs
2 Tbsp salted butter
1 tsp vanilla
Directions:
- Mix water, cornstarch, and cocoa in pan until smooth (stir constantly otherwise the cornstarch will thicken too fast)
- Begin heating on medium/low until light bubbles appear
- Add condensed milk and stir
- Lightly beat the eggs and begin to tempur, then add to mixture over heat and whisk until smooth
- Add your butter and vanilla and whisk until thick
- Remove from heat, whisk until SMOOTH and let it cool, stirring occasionally
- Pour into pie shell, cover in plastic wrap (against the filling itself to prevent skin from forming) and refrigerate (overnight/24 hours gave me the consistency and firmness that I was looking for

I then topped my pie with homemade whipped cream. A semi-sweet whipped cream because of all of the sweetness from the crust and filling.

Whipped Topping
Ingredients:
1 pint heavy cream
3/4 C. confectioners sugar
Directions:
- Whisk together heavy cream and sugar until desired consistency and firmness

I then crumbled some additional Oreos on top of my pie for added fatty deliciousness and decorative flare. This is an incredibly rich pie, but absolutely delicious. I would recommend anyone try it. It's quick, easy and unbelievably tasty. If you're wary of food comas, do not try this pie. My husband and my little boy both loved it, which is always the highest praise in my kitchen. Hopefully you will try and enjoy!


Remember, it's your kitchen!: Never apologize! No excuses--no explanations!

reviews.review_text: I have to admit I was very skeptical of this recipe at first.  I have made many cream pies, but never a chocolate cream, only because there is too much variation with what type of chocolate to use(semi-sweet, cocoa powder, baker's chocolate, etc...) in every recipe.  Most cream pies, use a vanilla based pudding and you add the actual flavors to it (bananas, coconut...).  Then I became worried as I was making it because the recipe calls for water. No where in the recipe is there "cream" or a milk product.  Also, I have never had a cream pie call for sweetened condensed milk; that is yet another mystery of this recipe.  So, while it was cooking on the stove I was kicking myself for not using milk/cream instead of water.  Even after I got done cooking it and the pudding was still warm, I couldn't decide if it was good.  I had to pour it in the pie shell and hope for the best, after it set up.  Truthfully, it came out tasting pretty good!  The only reason I gave it 4 stars, is the lack of "cream" in the recipe; can you really call it a cream pie, if there is no cream?  I decided to go with a graham cracker crust and whip cream instead of meringue.  I would definitely make this again.  It was fast and easy as the introduction states.

This was my first attempt at a homemade chocolate cream pie.  I used my own pie crust recipe and baked it until it was a perfect toasted golden brown.  For the filling, I used about 3 1/2 tablespoons of cornstarch, which I then mixed with 5 1/2 tablespoons of Ghirardhelli Cocoa.  I stirred in a small amount of water to moisten and remove lumps, then the rest of the water...except I tossed the last 1/4 cup and replaced it with coffee I had brewed earlier that day.  Then I put this mixture on the stove with the eggs and condensed milk.  It took a while for me to thicken, but probably because I kept the heat lower and was using a diffuser (so as not to scorch the bottom), and also continuously stirred it to make sure there was no lumps or scorching.     Once thickened, I stirred in the vanilla, I set this to the side, continuously stirring, so that it could cool.  It wasn't cooling fast enough, so I put the whole bottom of the pot in a bowl of ice water.  After 5 minutes, it was cool enough to poor into the pie crust.  I let it set in the fridge for about 1 hour, and then covered with fresh whipped cream, and served about an hour after that.  Everything was delicious, although, I noticed that I put too much whipped cream, because it overwhelmed the amount of chocolate custard.  Next time I may double this chocolate filling so as to make a really spectacular tall pie.  Loved the depth of the chocolate filling and it was perfectly chocolate, not overly sweet.  Tasted very gourmet, very impressive!  Will definitely keep this recipe for its simplicity and deliciousness!

instructions: Cut the mushrooms into slices.

reviews.review_text: I always make things from scratch but for some reason thought cream of mushroom was always a hassle, so I'd either switch up for bechamel or use store bought soup. <br/>Now that I made this for the first time, I've totally changed my mind<br/>It is CRIMINAL to buy the canned stuff when this soup is so, so, so, so easy to make, so much more cleaner tasting (and by cleaner i mean: doesn't have the dingy taste of preservatives, isn't overly salted, and doesn't taste processed to the point that it doesn't taste like mushrooms anymore). <br/>My tips:<br/>1) make sure to dice the onions very very finely. Use white, use butter (makes things taste smooth and creamy), and don't go over board. <br/>2) crush the garlic and then chop it up.<br/>3) I mixed brown mushrooms with white, white gives taste, brown tops keep their shape and color better through the cooking process<br/>4) doesn't need crazy long time to be prepared. literally wait for the flour to absorb the broth (about 1/3 of the liquid will evaporate/be absorbed) and add the cream, let it boil for a bit on high heat, and turn the heat off. the rest of the soup will fall into place while it's cooling down. <br/>5) used 18% table cream if that matters.

reviews.review_text: Great and simple recipe! I've always loved cream of mushroom soup. Most people just use the canned version as an addition to other recipes, but I've always liked to eat it as-is. That is, until I tried this recipe. It was simple and easy enough that I could see me making this on any given day.<br/><br/>I stuck strictly to the recipe as it is printed here (because I always do that with a new recipe when making it for the first time). I thought the ingredients/proportions were spot on. The recipe truly only makes about 4 servings. My 'tweaks' were as follows: I chopped the mushrooms up so they were more dispersed throughout the soup; I added just a bit of the chicken broth to the mushrooms/garlic/onions to give the mushrooms more liquid to imbue their flavor to, then I put a lid on it and let it cook for awhile to get the mushroom flavor fully embedded in the juice. I recommend starting the roux separately while the mushrooms are simmering. I melted 2 Tbsp. butter with 2 Tbsp. flour and stirred that continuously until it was slightly golden. I gradually added the rest of the chicken broth. Adding it very slowly keeps the mixture smooth, lump-free and thick. After about 10-15 minutes simmering the mushrooms, I poured that mixture into the roux and stirred that all together. <br/><br/>Following the directions, I mixed the 1 Tbsp. of flour with just a small amount of the light cream (to keep the flour from lumping up). Then added the rest of the cream and the seasonings; then put that all into the soup mixture. I let it heat for another 5 minutes. It was awesome! I put leftovers into the refrigerator and it was even better the next day!  I could definitely see me using this in recipes that call for cream of mushroom soup. I imagine it will take any other recipe up a notch or two and will impress the heck out of my friends and family at the next potluck dinner.

If I could give this 6 stars I would! I've never had cream of mushroom soup before aside from the canned variety and only in recipes. But today I had fresh mushrooms that needed to be used, searched the site and came across this recipe. The nutmeg intrigued me because it is a key ingredient in my favorite homemade potato soup. So, I gave this a whirl and I can't say enough about how delicious it is. I only had red onion on hand but I chopped it super fine and it cooked up beautifully. I also made my own broth using Better Than Boullion brand chicken base. Now if only I could figure out a condensed version of it to use in some of my recipes! Thanks so much for posting! Will make again and again.

I did cook the soup longer than time given to bring out more of the mushroom taste and to blend flavors.  The nutmeg addition was a wonderful idea and complemented the mushroom flavor.  The only problem I had with the recipe was the quantity given is 6.  The two of us used this as a main dish with dinner rolls and it was just enough for the two of us.  However, that could be because we are piggies!  I will definitely make this again, but will add more mushrooms, since we are mushroom freaks.  I also may heat the butter/flour roux in a small saucepan, then stir in the chicken broth until lumps go away before adding it to the sauteed mushroom mixture.  This may reduce lumping and whisking time.  However, this a very good recipe as written and I will definitely make it again.

I rough cut 4-6 cups of assorted mushrooms and puree once the 1/2 & 1/2 is added.. I finely chop 2 more cups and sauté until browned then add to the finished soup for chunks of mushroom. This has become a huge family favourite but I wouldn't have tried it without this simple recipe.

attributes.source_text: I make it in fall and winter
I make it in fall and winter

reviews.review_text: FABULOUS!!!  I just made this.  I used heavy cream b/c that is what I had.  I also fished out all the mushrooms and put them in the mini food processor and chopped them up fine b/c I was afraid my kids would freak if they found a big old mushroom in their green bean casserole!  I think portioned it out in 2-4 oz portions and froze it for future cooking use.  And with the remaining 1 oz in the pan, well...that lone dinner roll in the freezer got thawed and mopped it up and jumped in my mouth and it was sooooo yummy!  Oh, I left out the nutmeg b/c I'm not sure about nutmeg with my nut allergic kids.  Not really sure if that is a nut or not.

Loved this!!! And easy too. Thanks for bringing a favorite cooking ingredient back to my kitchen. The canned stuff contains MSG or is really runny. I used drained canned mushrooms and chopped them in a hand chopper. I also replaced 1/2 cup of chicken broth with the liquid from the can to kick up the mushroom flavor. I also used evaporated goat's milk which is good for lactose intolerant people but has a slightly different flavor than regular evap milk. It also cooks down into a condensed soup VERY easily if you simmer on low for about 1-2 hours just remember to keep a close eye on it and stir often. GREAT RECIPE!

attributes.source_text: to kick up the mushroom flavor

reviews.review_text: While this recipe is a good starting point, I felt there were a few adjustments necessary for my taste. First of all, a single recipe would not yield six servings. I doubled everything to get eight small servings or six larger ones. Also, because I think beef broth goes better w/mushrooms, I used that instead of the chicken. Spice-wise, I used half the salt, a few 'shakes' of nutmeg, rather than 1/4 tsp called for and added a couple generous 'shakes' of cayenne. I chose to use cream in my soup, as I'm making small servings. The soup is excellent and I will happily serve it to guests tomorrow! It is a very simple recipe. I will serve it w/a sprinkle of chopped chives. Thank you for posting the original recipe.

I tripled this recipe so we'd have enough to share with extended family & it was amazing... I used baby portobello mushrooms chopped in quarters - I followed the recipe pretty much as listed for the basic ingredients & instructions, but at the end I partially blended the soup with an infusion blender for an extra mushroomy taste to the broth, making sure to leave lots of mushroom pieces to enjoy with each bite. I also had chicken breast that needed to be used up, so I diced it up fine & added it in with a little rice which made the soup a perfect meal on it's own - very hearty, easy & delicious!

attributes.source_text: for an extra mushroomy taste to the broth

reviews.review_text: This was an awesome recipe for the base of the soup. I altered it by making the following changes: 16 ounces of mushrooms, most chopped in large slices with some minced. 2 1/2 tablespoons onions chopped. 2 garlic cloves. 3 tablespoons butter. 3 - 4 tablespoons flour (separated). 2 2/3 cups chicken broth. 1 12oz can evaporated milk. About a teaspoon salt, about 3/4 teaspoon pepper, about 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg (seasoned to taste). Added a teaspoon of corn starch. Added a pinch of Spanish saffron. Added a dash of parsley. Added about an hour of heating on low low heat to blend the flavors with regular stirring.

instructions: Preheat oven to 375 degrees.

The chocolate chocolate chip cookies wasn't too over powering chocolatey which was great, it means being able to eat heaps at one go washed down with a glass of cold milk.  The butterscotch gave a great buttery taste which was also wonderful.  I did cut down on the sugar for the butterscotch a little.  It still tasted great..and sweet enough for my family.
I might add white chocolate bits mixed with butterscotch chips next time, think the combination might be quite good.

Easy to make; I added a "heavy" teaspoon of almond extract, along with the vanilla (due to the white chocolate pudding flavor); made over 6 dozen cookies of a substantial size for teenagers.  I can hardly wait for tomorrow because they were excellent right out of the oven ... I divided the dough into halves with one having chocolate chips and the other butterscotch chips ... they are both fantastic!  Make sure you use parchment paper and they come out lovely ...  Will make again and again!

I had 4 guests this week and have already gone through 3 batches, each one a bit different. reviews.review_text:
My favorite cookies are the ones I find at Subway; when fresh, they can't be beat.  Well, make these cookies and let them sit for 24 hours, and you wind up with Subway cookies!

I made them once, and based on reviews, I knew I'd done something wrong ; they were quite hard and crunchy.  Figures, my crunchy-cookie-lovin' husband thought they were pretty good.  I realized I'd shorted the amount of butter needed, so I promptly made another batch.  Now, I'm all for soft cookies, but these are way too soft at first.  When removing them from the cookie sheet, I had to be very careful because they were practically the consistency of uncooked batter!  Once they cooled a bit, they did firm up, but they were still too soft for me.  Now, the next morning, they were UNREAL!  That's when they hit Yowza status, as in "Yowza, this is good stuff!"

My first batch, I used chocolate pudding and chocolate chips; besides being too hard because I messed up, it was a tad too much chocolate for my taste.  The next batch, I used butterscotch pudding and chocolate chips... very tasty, indeed!  Next go-round, I'll be trying chocolate pudding with white chocolate chunks, as that's really my favorite flavor of cookie.

One tip for people planning to make this recipe... if you like a thinner cookie, definitely spread out the batter, as these are not cookies that really flatten and spread out while baking.  They do a little, but if you put the dough in balls on the sheet, your cookies will be fairly thick.

So, to sum up, this is one heck of a cookie recipe, and I appreciate you sharing it!  Definitely going into my recipe binder, and I'll be making these cookies for years to come.  Wonderful that you can switch things up by using different puddings and chips.  The possibilites are endless!  This is a recipe I'll be sharing with anyone who cares to listen to the blabbering fool you all know as Rushed 4 Time!

attributes.source_text: my crunchy-cookie-lovin' husband thought they were pretty good

items.label: Fish Tacos
items.name: Fish Tacos
items.description: We got the best fish tacos in a little fishing village in Mexico. I have tried to recreate them as best as possible
instructions: Combine sour cream, mayonnaise, cilantro and 2 tablespoons seasoning mix in small bowl.
Combine fish, vegetable oil, lemon juice and remaining seasoning mix in medium bowl; pour into large skillet.
Cook, stirring constantly, over medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes or until cod flakes easily when tested with a fork.
Fill taco shells with fish mixture.
Top with toppings.

reviews.review_text: MmmmmmARVELOUS!  What a terrific flavor these have. I used Lawry's taco seasoning (love their Baja marinade on fish, too!) and everything else as written except I forgot the lime juice which really ticked me off because I LOVE limes, particularly on tacos.  Won't forget next time as I reminded myself in the "My Notes" section. My husband is one of those who claims cilantro tastes like soap (huh?), but he ADORED this sauce. I even put a ton of it in, too, because I was feeling the need to spoil myself and I'm a big fan of cilantro. I used NZ orange roughy and corn tortillas.  Oh, and added avocado to one of my two tacos.  Major Yummage all the way around.  Your recreation is a success - thanks for a real treasure, Tish!

attributes.source_text: he ADORED this sauce

reviews.review_text:
I joined this site to tell you all how AMAZING this recipe is! I've been using this site for meal planning. Last night I did not feel like cooking. I knew I had frozen cod filets, they had been breaded but not cooked. I was hoping to find an easy way to cook them. This dish did just that with amazing results.

I just let the fish soak up the chili oil a bit. Then, cooked them as usual. WOW. This is a keeper. The fish went like hoecakes, so I'm using some chicken instead tonight. I made homemade tortillas, used lettuce instead if cabbage, and used the taco seasoning off this site since I don't handle MSG well.

This recipe is so good, it's sick!!!  My husband was appalled at the idea of "fish" tacos.  Needless to say we were both completely blown away with this recipe.  I'm from Chicago which has an excellent Mexican food neighborhood where I always went to get my steak taco's.  I'll never need a beef/steak taco again after eating this.  Insanely deelish!  I used more cilantro and  probably a lot more taco seasoning since I didn't have a way to measure it.  I used halibut as the white fish and olive oil in place of the vegetable oil.  I ate this on corn tortillas and my husband ate it on flour tortillas.  I used the cabbage and taco sauce and made my own pico de gallo to serve on this as well.  I also added a bit of mashed avocado.  Out of this freaking world!  My husband agreed.  Thank you so much for this one!  Just FAB!

attributes.source_text: My husband agreed

reviews.review_text:
I was looking for a healthier way to use cod then fried and found this recipe.  I'm glad that I did!  They were fabulous.  My wife loves fish and she was happy when I told her we were having fish for dinner.  When I told her that I was making fish tacos, she frowned and said that she wanted fish with rice.  Well, she loved the tacos and even ate seconds!  My 9 year old and 7 year old ate them too, and the only kind of fish they will eat is fish sticks.

I made two minor changes to the recipe.  I added a few drops of Tabasco Chipotle to the sauce and sliced avocados inside the tacos.  I also used low fat sour cream and mayo.  Give them a try for a different, healthy way to eat cod.

reviews.review_text: My husband and I just had these for dinner, and they were so delicious.  I made quite a few alterations, only because I had another idea in mind for dinner and didn't look up this recipe until I had already started another recipe.  So, here's what I did:  I made a mango salsa which included 1 chopped mango, 1 chopped tomato, about 1/4 cup chopped cilantro, a couple tablespoons of red onion minced, the juice of 1 lime, and a tsp or two of cumin.  To this I added about 1/4-1/2 cup of mayo and the 2 Tbs. taco seasoning.  Then I tossed the cubed fish (I used orange roughy) with the rest of the taco seasoning and 1 Tbs. veg. oil and the juice of a lime.  **The taco seasoning I used was called Nueva Cocina Chipotle Taco, and it had lots of dried raisins and other delicious and unusual items in it.  The combo was incredible!  We only added some shredded spinach to top these--so, so yummy!  We will definitely have these again :)

This is a great recipe that I modified just a little.  I'm so excited to find a good fish taco recipe, and hooray!  it's EASY!

After my 5 year old and I tasted the "dressing", it was a little too spicy for him, and a little too sour cream for me (not a big sc fan).  So I added 1/2 cup mayo, and more cilantro.  This was the perfect "less sour creamy" and "less spicy" to satisfy me and the rest of my family.

I used Mahi-Mahi, and only a pound.  I have plenty of leftover sauce to make again soon.  I cut the fish into 1/2" pieces since I knew my kids would like it better that way. 

Also, I garnished with fresh avacado, and I will also garnish with fresh cilantro next time.

Just great,  thanks a bunch!

Also worth noting is that Costco has this recipe in the May 2015 Costco Connection magazine (the only difference is the there is no taco seasoning added to fish... so this recipe is better, but everything else is the same!).

My only suggestion is to kick up the heat a bit. I used garlic and chili infused oil, but still needed something.  Topped with green cabbage, cheese, avocado, red onion and the sour cream sauce. Overall, it had great flavor and super fast meal to prepare. This was the first time I had ever made fish tacos and my daughter devoured them!! I followed the suggestions to use 1 T of oil, light sour cream, and  I used 2 T of light mayo for the taco sauce. I also added a Chipolte pepper in adobe sauce to the fish liquid.
