reviews.review_text: A friend gave us a whole bunch of cod, and we weren't sure how we were going to use it all up, since it's just DH and me.  Well, now we know.  This is a great recipe!!  Very easy to put together, and the flavors in the sour cream/mayo topping work very well together.  I used a chicken taco seasoning mix and fresh lime juice, instead of lemon.  Rather than taco shells or flour tortillas, I  pan fried some corn tortillas.  What I really liked about this dish is that the fish is sauteed, rather than deep fried.  Thanks for a real keeper, Tish!!

These were very flavorful!  I used Tilapia filets, did everything else the same. We found that adding some creamy italian dressing to the coleslaw made a nice lightly sweet and creamy addition.

One tip that my sister taught me worked well too... put a piece of foil, cut slits in center with knife,  on top of skillet the last couple of minutes of cooking fish, makes a great shelf to heat the tortillas on!!! Or use a seperate skillet with just water on simmer... heats the tortillas like a charm!

Really, really delicious!  I used almost 1/2 cup low fat sour cream and only about 1/3 cup mayo.  I also used low sodium taco seasoning.  The sauce turned out great - I had about twice what I needed, so I could have halved the recipe.  I used  a 12 oz bag of frozen tilapia, which tasted a bit "fishy" to me, but it was probably just my particular batch.  I never thought taco seasoning of fish would be good, but it really was.  My husbad added cheese to his, but I found cheese totally unnecessary.

I made this for my family's Taco Tuesday.  Everyone rated it between 3 and 5 stars, so a 4 star average.  To have a recipe that was eaten by all is a rarity indeed. My family did choose shredded lettuce over the shredded cabbage. I also offered other topping so everyone could top with what they like. The only complaint was that DD said she liked the sauce better before I added the cilantro.  Next time I will leave a little out for her before I add the cilantro for the rest of us.  Great way to switch it up and have something a little different than traditional tacos

Awesome!
Thanks for a perfect recipe!
I love fish tacos, but have never made them at home. I wanted to add them to our Family Cinco de mayo feast since my hubby no longer eats meat (only seafood). 
I copied the recipe as written (except I tripled it!). Everyone loved it (except I must admit, my family is silly, and only my in laws and I would try it as tacos...everyone else ate the fish and sauce with rice) oh well...it was loved by all though! 
The leftover sauce was great to dip tortilla chips in!!!

attributes.source_text: Family Cinco de mayo feast
only my in laws and I would try it as tacos

items.label: Baja Black Beans, Corn and Rice
items.name: Baja Black Beans, Corn and Rice
items.description: A south of the border blend of textures and flavors. serve hot as a main dish or a side dish with grilled meat or chicken.
instructions: Cook brown rice.
In a medium bowl, combine black beans, corn, tomatoes, onion, cilantro, jalapeno, lime juice, oil, salt, pepper and hot sauce.
To serve, Place a scoop of hot rice in a bowl or on a plate, top with a generous scoop of the black bean mixture.
Stir together before eating.

reviews.review_text: When I first tasted this I thought it needed a little boost so I added a tsp of whole cumin seed and it was delicious. I used a pint of grape tomatoes for the tomatoes. They looked really pretty halved and they always are very flavorful. To make it extra quick I used minute rice brown rice which was already cooked in the little single serving packages. I dropped the rice in boiling water to make it taste unpackaged and then cooled it in cold water. It probably took a total of three minutes for the rice. Then, I added cooked shrimp, an avocado, and topped it with sour cream which turned this into a delicious cold main dish (for lunch) that we enjoyed immensely. It was so good I'm thinking about putting this on our restaurant menu. Thanks!

attributes.source_text: for lunch

reviews.review_text:
I loved this. However, i like things on the spicy side, so I added 1/2 pablano pepper, chopped, 1/2 anehiem pepper, chopped, smoked paprika, ground chipote peppers, ground ancho chilli peppers and topped it with chunks of avocado. I also did not add the tomatos until serving time
to individaul bowls. (they tend to make their own juice) I also roasated my tomatos, jaleopena
pepper, garlic and corn. When reheating the rice i added some of the diced tomatos with it..then added the black bean/corn mixture with some avocado on top. will definately make this again!! =)

attributes.source_text: i like things on the spicy side

reviews.review_text: We made this without rice, served cold as a kind of a salsa with tortilla chips for Thanksgiving supper.  I made way too much for our small family, but it was a huge hit.  My Mom didn't even ask -- she just took about a third of what was left as leftovers for her and Dad!  (It's a custom to share leftovers, but we USUALLY say PLEASE, Mom!)  Didn't have fresh cilantro, so used about 1 1/2 or 2 Tbsp. dry cilantro, also added 1 heaping Tbsp. cumin.  Used the juice of one-half of a small fresh lime.  Didn't add hot sauce or jalapeno at all, cuz my family's chicken, but substituted about 1/2 of a large green bell pepper for color.  This was super-tasty.  However you make this, you're gonna love it!!!!

attributes.source_text: for Thanksgiving supper
My Mom didn't even ask -- she just took about a third of what was left as leftovers

reviews.review_text: i used instant rice cooked in broth for i am a lazy monkey. i also skipped the cilantro as i'm firmly in the "hate" camp but i added half a green bell pepper instead which was very nice. used frozen corn and halved the whole recipe. if i remember correctly i added a little sour cream and shredded cheddar and minced the jalapeno in my garlic grinder. used powdered chipotle pepper as i was out of tabasco. it didn't turn out as spicy as i thought it would. next time i might add more jalapeno. course that may just be that mine happened to be a milder one. i added some garlic powder as well, i think. this was a lovely blend of spicy, sweet, and satisfying. definitely baja, not mexican, which is a nice change. i was going to put this in lettuce wraps but forgot all about it. next time i guess. will certainly make again. i'm looking for more ways to make beans tasty since i hate them but they're SO good for me. may try adding some shredded veggie chicken next time. leftover guacamole might be nice in this too.

attributes.source_text: a lovely blend of spicy, sweet, and satisfying
a lovely blend of spicy, sweet, and satisfying
definitely baja, not mexican, which is a nice change

reviews.review_text: Okay, I make new recipes from 'zaar constantly. Rarely do I repeat one on a regular basis, even if I love it, because I like to try new things constantly. Each time I make a recipe, I ask Alan, my husband, how many stars he would give it. He has never given five stars (and we're often in agreement on this, although I often add points for ease of the recipe, etc. whereas he wouldn't do that), mainly because he considers that to be a "perfect" recipe, and one that he could and would eat over and over again. Finally...we've got a five star recipe with this one! I was a bit skeptical when I realized we'd be putting a cold "salad" on hot rice, but I had no cause for worry...this was fantastic! I prefer it with extra hot sauce, but Alan loved his as is. The leftovers heated up great also, which is a huge plus for me. I did use a can of diced tomatoes, but only because I didn't have any fresh on hand. I LOVE that this is healthy, easy to make, tasted delicious, can be a main course with grilled chicken or a side dish as is, has great presentation, and makes great leftovers for lunch or another dinner. We actually piled some of the leftovers in baked potatoes with salsa...yum! Barb, you're simply the best!! Thanks so much for sharing this recipe...it will become the first one ever to be made weekly at our house!

attributes.source_text: Alan loved his as is
can be a main course with grilled chicken
or a side dish as is
makes great leftovers for lunch or another dinner
makes great leftovers for lunch or another dinner

reviews.review_text: Not that we needed another review here, but... I found this via the "low-fat" theme so I thought it could also be pointed out that, between the beans and the rice, this meal provides a complete protein, so it's a good vegetarian meal that goes beyond just omitting meat. I also went with some cheddar (between rice and other mixture). I made the cold part a day ahead and kept it in the fridge, but added the tomatoes when I took it out of the fridge a while before serving. I also used chipotles rather than jalapeno because that was what I had. It all turned out wonderfully, refreshing, with interesting flavors and textures, and healthy, too!

attributes.source_text: refreshing

reviews.review_text:
Barb,
 This was Oh So Goooood.
it Tasted Somewhat like the Southwestern Rice dish at Taco Belle That I love so much.I won't buy fresh tomatoes at the store during the winter,so I drained a can of Diced tomatoes with green chilies and used that,so then I eliminated the Jalapeno,because the tomatoes are already HOT.I also cooked a couple of diced up chicken breasts with some cumin.I put the chicken on top after all else was assembled.There was a little left over after my husband got finished,(he had 2 big helpings)and he said "Don't throw that out I'll have some more later" I really think he too liked it.Ha
Thanks for a GREAT recipe.
Darlene Summers

attributes.source_text: the tomatoes are already HOT
he had 2 big helpings
he said "Don't throw that out I'll have some more later"

reviews.review_text: Excellent dish Barb!!  We were invited out last minute to a friends house who was serving enchilladas.  My FIL was visiting and is Vegan so I knew I needed to bring a dish that would work well for him also.  This one fit the bill perfectly and tasted so....good!  The tomatoes at the store were terrible so I bought canned, diced tomatoes w/green chilis and drained it well.  Everything else was as is, except I used 1/2 of a jalapeno pepper and I mixed everything together rather than just topping the rice.  We ate it at room temperature but think it would be great hot or cold too.  This recipe goes in the keeper file! Thanks. :)

This is a really nice, refreshing dish. I put together everything and let it sit for an hour or two to let the flavours blend together; then I cooked the rice in the rice cooker and added the bean mixture just as the rice was done cooking to let it all heat up. The only thing I did differently was leave out the onions and jalapenos, and used lemon juice instead of lime. It was spicy on its own, but not so spicy when mixed with rice, so I'll probably up the spice next time. I'd love to use this with just about everything! Thanks!

attributes.source_text: really nice, refreshing dish
It was spicy on its own

reviews.review_text: Delicious!!! I'm sure it is great as written, but I changed a few things. I took this to work for a large group so I didn't want to make it TOO hot. I used Rotel tomatoes with green chilies in them, and left out the jalapenos. This gave it some heat, but wasn't overly hot. It also saved me time by not having to chop the tomatoes and jalapeno called for. I increased the lime juice by 50%. I used a little less rice than called for (I doubled the entire recipe, however). My coworkers really enjoyed this, and when there are 30 something dishes to choose from, and people really like yours, that has to mean something! Thanks!

attributes.source_text: My coworkers really enjoyed this
This gave it some heat
wasn't overly hot

reviews.review_text: I made this for a summer potluck. Because it had to travel a bit, I served it cold, and all mixed together. There was a lot of food, and amid all the chaos, I think I only heard one compliment (a favorable one). I made this exactly as written. Even using Roma (small-medium) tomatoes, this yields a lot more than "6 servings" in my estimation. Half the dish disappeared at the potluck, so I took the rest home and ate it over several days. It's pretty nice, and fresh, and a bit on the simple side. I noted that the seasonings (lime juice, hot sauce, salt and pepper) are pretty minimal, and this dish just relies on the basic rice and vegetable flavors. This isn't anything extra-special, but it's pretty nice.

attributes.source_text: I made this for a summer potluck
a summer potluck
pretty nice, and fresh

reviews.review_text: Amazing flavors and healthy! I did use garlic salt instead of regular, 2 ears of fresh white corn instead of canned, and more fresh ground black pepper than the recipe called for because I love fresh ground black pepper. No hot sauce because my jalapeno was already really spicy, but I would have used hot sauce otherwise. I forgot the olive oil at first and it was great. Added the olive oil and it was still great. Served it over brown rice and red quinoa. I will be eating this a lot this summer! Thanks!!!

attributes.source_text: my jalapeno was already really spicy

reviews.review_text: I included all ingredients this recipe called for except I used cooked frozen corn and extra hot sauce, and the results were great!  The textures were good too, a nice combination of soft beans and crunchy corn and onion.  At first I thought it might need more lime juice but 2 tbsps. were just right.  I tried this as a cold dish and hot (reheated in the microwave at work) and loved the way it tasted both ways.  High in fiber too.  BTW, six servings seemed a bit low to me; you might be left with lots of tasty leftovers.  Thanks Barb.

attributes.source_text: a nice combination of soft beans
crunchy corn and onion

reviews.review_text: I love this!  I halved the recipe and it still made an enormous amount (for a family of 3).  I served it with tacos and burritos and it made a lovely side dish.  I put some in my burrito as Heather suggested too, it was delicious!  After dinner, I mixed the rice in with the bean mixture.  This is just as good cold as a rice salad or quasi salsa.  I am eating it with tortilla chips for lunch, crunching while I type.  Thanks for an easy, fresh, side dish.  Thank you, Barb, for posting such a versitile recipe.  Sue

attributes.source_text: it made a lovely side dish
I am eating it with tortilla chips for lunch
an easy, fresh, side dish
crunching while I type

reviews.review_text: This is fantastic!  I didn't realize at first that this is a cold topping over hot rice - in my haste I just assumed it was all hot.  I hesitated, but absolutely love it.  I mixed the leftovers together and will have a Mexican rice salad for lunch tomorrow.  The changes I made were to use a drained can of petite diced tomatoes, 1 cup of frozen corn instead of the canned, and threw some chopped avocado on top.  A new staple in our house, especially for summer. Thanks Barb!

attributes.source_text: a cold topping over hot rice
especially for summer

reviews.review_text: This became one of my favorite recipes the first time I made it.  I make it constantly.  So healthy and flavorful - I'm never tempted to add cheese or sour cream.   I stick to the recipe as written, adding only a clove of minced garlic (because I just love it), and am generous with the hot sauce and lime juice to balance out the onion flavor.  I find the brown rice is quite tasty if I add a little butter and garlic powder (in addition to generously salting the water).  Awesome recipe.

For us this was a good base recipe that can be enhanced with addtl ingrediants to suit personal preference.  Also noticed it was much better on second day so recommend that it be made day before so the flavors can settle.  We also added about 1/4  cup sala; small can diced green chiles; and 2 tblsp Mt. Olive diced jalapeno peppers.  In our opinion, it needed a little extra boost.  Can be served warm or cold but we preferred a little warm.  Will make again. Thanks.

This was excellent.  My first time trying brown basmati rice and the beans and corn were wonderful with it.  I used frozen corn instead of canned and used tomatoes fresh from the garden.  I also used banana pepper instead of jalapenos because I was serving it to children.  We had it as our main course and it was plenty filling.  I think this would be an excellent potluck dish for summer cookouts.  And I also ate some of the beans with homemade baked corn chips.  Very yummy!

attributes.source_text: We had it as our main course

reviews.review_text: Love this recipe! The only change I made was to use only half the tomatoes.  DH and I ate this over the brown rice the first time, then used the leftovers and some grilled tilapia for fish tacos. Yum!  The black bean mixture is very versatile too.  It would make an excellent topping for grilled chicken, or a great side for all kinds of tex-mex dishes.  It is also really easy to adjust this to suit your taste.  With the tacos I added more lime juice and some habanero sauce.

items.label: Weight Watchers Parmesan Chicken Cutlets
items.name: Weight Watchers Parmesan Chicken Cutlets
items.description: Make and share this Weight Watchers Parmesan Chicken Cutlets recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
In resealable plastic bag, combine cheese, crumbs and all seasonings; shake well.
Transfer mixture to plate; dip each chicken breast in cheese mixture, turning to coat all sides.
Arrange on nonstick baking sheet.
Bake until chicken is cooked through, 20-25 minutes.

reviews.review_text: If somebody needs a 59th rave review to tell them this chicken is good and they should try it then let me be that 59th reviewer!  Firstly, I am always looking to cut fat and calories so I loved that there was no oil involved with this coating and it still clung perfectly to the chicken.  Like a previous reviewer, I did the shake and bake method of just putting the chicken in the bag with the coating and shaking everything up.  The whole dish came together in less than 2 minutes this way and without any mess.  I was impressed that the bottom of the chicken didn't go soggy at all such has happened to me with oven baked coated chicken in the past.   I think so many different types of seasoning could be used with this method.  I could see mixing it up with some spicy seasoning in the future.  Made for PAC Fall 2008.

attributes.source_text: the bottom of the chicken didn't go soggy at all

reviews.review_text: I used chicken breast tenders. 1.33 pounds of chicken had 12 tenders in it. I didn't measure the breading ingredients very carefully. Just kid of eyeballed it into the bag and roughly doubled the quantity. I made a grilling pan for my BBQ out of 2 layers of tinfoil and put the chicken in that to cook. I just put the tenders, one at a time, into the bag with the breading. The breading didn't stick a lot. Just a very light coating. I sprinkled some of the extra breading over the top of the chicken after it was in my makeshift pan. Cooked for about 15 minutes on a very hot grill, indirect. Came out juicy, done and flavorful. The entire familiy enjoyed. Will make again. I like cooking it out on the grill in hot summer weather. Thanks!

attributes.source_text: Came out juicy, done and flavorful
The entire familiy enjoyed

reviews.review_text: I liked this... I did have a few minor points to sort out though. I made this exactly as directed but needed a longer cooking time because my were still uncooked in the middle  after 25 minutes... mine took closer to 40 minutes to be done.(...and yes, my oven was preheated).The flavour was ok, but for my tastes I think I'd like to add some real garlic (minced) and a heap more fresh herbs next time because I thought that the flavours needed a bit of omph. I was delighted though that the breadcrumb mix seemed to stick quite well to the chicken and that this is a relatively no-hassle recipe. Best of all is the calorie count and that makes healthy eating even easier. Please see my rating system: a lovely 4 stars for an easy recipe that can be so easily kicked up a notch with extra herbs if you like a more herby flavour. Thanks !

Great recipe. The only change I made was i preheated my Power XL Air Fryer Grill with my grill pan inside to 400 degrees F for 5 minutes. Gave two sprays of oil to the chicken after it had been dipped and then air fried them on my grill pan for 10 minutes; flipped them over, one more spray of oil and then did another 8 minutes. Wow - they came out so moist and with great grill marks. Also roasted 2 red potatoes that I cut up in a small cast iron pan with butter, garlic and onions and cooked on the shelf above the chicken. Lastly served a green salad on the side. Thanks for sharing this recipe.

attributes.source_text: they came out so moist

reviews.review_text: Well I didn't realize how popular this recipe is, until I tagged it in PRMR Tag Game and went to review it!!!!  I made this for my lunch, so scaled it back for one.  I wasn't serving this with pasta, so I did add some marinara sauce and then topped it with some mozzarella, which I know would up the points/calories, but it was so good.  I too, used fresh shredded parmesan in place of the grated Kraft kind.  I had this with some carrot sticks, as I knew I was also going to meet my DS at the movie theater and knew I would be eating buttered popcorn and this would help keep my calories to where they should be.  Thanks for sharing a great lo-cal recipe Lainey!!!

attributes.source_text: I made this for my lunch

reviews.review_text:
*Original Post 03/18/08*
I've made these a few times now, and I could've sworn I'd written a review!  

Everytime I've made these I've followed the directions to a T.  The only slight change is using 4 C's grated parm instead of Kraft "powdered" parm.  Either way, it's awesome.

However, I can say the best way is making these to go with Cabarnet Marinara and pasta.  YUM-O!  Definitely a keeper recipe no matter how you make it!

*EDIT 03/23/09* 
I've also learned if I add a sprinkle of McCormick Parmesan Herb seasoning to both sides before baking, the flavor is even more enhanced.  Not too sure how it changes the nutritional value, but thought I'd add in my extra tip :)

It wasn't clear (at least to me) whether you were supposed to cover the chicken or not when you put it in the oven.  I was scared about it drying out, so I covered with foil for the first 15 minutes, and uncovered for the last 10.  Not sure if that changed anything, because I'm a horrible cook, but this turned out wonderfully with everyone at the table loving it.  I used parmesan cheese shreds and instead of melting, they just turned hard.  I wasn't a fan but since it got such rave reviews, I'm giving this five stars as the parmesan cheese is most likely my fault.

Having read all the reviews, I was ready to wish I had put more spices in it, but I always try to make a recipe as closely as I can the first time so the rating will be accurate.  Anyway, I soldiered on and followed the recipe exactly as written except I used chicken tenders.  

The chicken turned out wonderfully.  I don't think it needed any more spices.  I wonder if the folks thinking it was bland were using fresh parm or the stuff in the green can.  That may make all the difference.  The green can hasn't been in my house in years.  Anyway, I really really enjoyed this.  Made it with a parm & herb risotto (so much for the low cal) as a side dish.  This recipe will definitely be a regular in our household.  Thanks for sharing.

Cutlets were moist, tender and flavorful. A keeper recipe. I rubbed a drop of olive oil all over each cutlet before adding coating. It made a huge difference in getting the coating to adhere to the chicken. I used a little less freshly grated Parmesan cheese, a little more Panko breadcrumbs, 2 tsp. Italian seasoning, 1 tsp. rosemary and a dash of Jane's Mixed-up Salt. You can adjust the seasoning flavor profile to your tastes - that is one of the things I love about this recipe. I baked 40 minutes at 350 degrees (because I needed the oven at 350 for my side dish) then put under the broiler to crisp up both sides for 5 minutes; turning half way through. Yum!

attributes.source_text: Cutlets were moist
tender

reviews.review_text: So funny to find this recipe. I have been making various versions of this recipe for years. I just came up with it myself. Great minds think alike. I butterfly open the breast, put it in a gallon size zip lock bag, and pound it out with the flat side of a meat mallet to about a 1/2 inch thick. It cooks quicker and more evenly while still staying very moist. You will need to spread the breading out on a plate and dip the cutlets in it. It will be much easier. <br/>I started out using a thin layer of mayo to hold crumbs on. Tried fat free mayo to cut calories, but it doesn't crisp up. Olive oil mayo seems to work best. It has the same caloric values as low fat mayo, but it utilizes a healthier fat. <br/>  For those who find the original recipe lacking enough flavor, more Italian seasoning can be added to the bread crumbs. I have tried several other seasonings, paprika, lemon pepper, cilantro, coriander,  Mrs. Dash (several varieties,) creole seasoning (my favorite.) Most often I add pepper, garlic and onion powders. Put these seasonings on over the mayo and before the breading. This has been a favorite for my family for years. Make this recipe your own. Enjoy.

attributes.source_text: while still staying very moist
This has been a favorite for my family for years

reviews.review_text: Fabulous! I took a frozen skinless boneless out of the fridge, started running some cold water over it, and threw everything else together into a ziplock bag. I did increase the spices a tad for extra flavor. Within a few minutes the chicken was mostly thawed, I dried it off and tossed it into the bag to coat. My chicken took about 27 minutes to cook (but then it was still slightly frozen in the center when I started). It was juicy and had tons of flavor. Definitely not just for dieters.

attributes.source_text: It was juicy

reviews.review_text: This was very good. I did make a few changes. I cut my chicken into short strips. I put salt, pepper, garlic, and a little paprika on the chicken before I put the bread crumbs on them. I only had plain breadcrumbs so I added some Italian seasoning to it about 1 tsp I would say. (I don't measure I eye ball) Then I added salt, pepper, garlic, a little onion powder, and paprika to my crumbs. I did try to shake my chicken in the bag with the crumbs, but since I used freshly grated Parmesan, it didn't work. So I did have to pour the crumbs on a plate and that worked so much better. The chicken came out moist and very good! My husband doesn't care for chicken a whole lot, but I got a thumbs up on these. Thank you so much for posting! :)

attributes.source_text: The chicken came out moist
My husband doesn't care for chicken a whole lot, but I got a thumbs up on these

reviews.review_text: This recipe was very simple and is a great, healthy alternative to products such as Shake & Bake. Both my husband and I really enjoyed this. It was super easy, and it was ingredients we had on hand. My only complaint is that I felt it was a little dry. I think next time I will probably turn the chicken once during cooking to distribute the juices better, if that doesn't work, I may end up covering it through part of the cooking process. Due to ease of make, and great taste, I will definitely make this again. It's a great quick and easy main course!

attributes.source_text: Both my husband and I really enjoyed this
It's a great quick and easy main course

reviews.review_text: These were yummy nummy, and it was so easy to make them! Since I had to divide a 2 lb. package of chicken in half, I ended up cutting my own strips. I mixed everything in the bag rather than dirtying an extra plate. The tenders were finished in 25-28 minutes, and we all enjoyed them. I served this with au gratin potatoes and mixed vegetables. I would double the recipe next time because we didn't have enough for everyone once I'd trimmed the fat off the chicken.

My fiance and I are trying to lose some weight before the wedding in the fall so I've been looking for some lower fat recipes so we're not eating the same stuff all the time so I came across this recipe this afternoon and decided this would be what we were going to do for dinner tonight since I have all the stuff on hand.....anyway I have to say it is simply delicious, my fiance gave it rave reviews and told me I need to make this again no question. So a big 5 stars if I could give it 10 I would

attributes.source_text: what we were going to do for dinner tonight
my fiance gave it rave reviews

reviews.review_text: Simple, easy to make, with ingredients I have in my kitchen all the time. Who knew that grated parm, when used in moderation, was fairly low calorie? Tasty, easy, and delicious. Thanks for an easy way to make chicken in my oven (I'm sick of grilled chicken!!!)  UPDATE:  This is now my go-to recipe for chicken--- whether for on a salad, with alfredo, with marinara, for sandwiches--- it's great all ways (and delicious cold!)  Irregardless of whether I'm dieting or not, this is my favorite recipe and SOOO easy with minimal ingredients (that I always have in the house!)

My husband recently joined WW so I fixed this tonight to go with broccoli and corn on the cob with V8 juice.  We both thought it is good and was very moist.  I did brush a little olive oil on the pan because I did not use a nonstick baking sheet.  Thanks for the recipe.<br/><br/>07/20/13  I forgot to add that I turned them over after 10 minutes baking and used a spatula to pick up what fell off and placed what fell off on top.

attributes.source_text: was very moist

reviews.review_text: This was excellent.  I used this to put on top of recipe #294654 for a complete one plate meal.  The two went so well together.  For rating purposes, I tried this recipe separate from the other and we loved it.  I cut my chicken into strips and then doubled the breading because there were more pieces to cover.  Because we like a little spice, I used 1/2 paprika and 1/2 cayenne pepper to give it a little zip.  I'll be making this again.  Thanks Lainey

attributes.source_text: to give it a little zip

reviews.review_text: What a flavorful and delicious chicken recipe! I used 2 Tbsp Matzo Meal and Italian seasoning and that worked fine. Otherwise followed the recipe exactly. I had no trouble with the mixture sticking to the chicken breasts as I wet them down and them put them in the plastic bag and shook it up. The coating stuck just fine! These were easy, delicious and so very healthy. I will be making them on a regular basis. Thanks for this great recipe, Lainey!

yum-so simple, and so delicious!  these are so moist - baking works much better than when i used to try a recipe and pan-fry the chicken.  i used breasts, but cut them up into smaller portions so they would cook faster, as well as so that I pass them off as "chicken nuggets" for my toddler, who won't eat chicken without "toppings".  i made a big batch to keep in the fridge to use for salads and wraps throughout the week.  thanks for sharing!

attributes.source_text: these are so moist

items.label: The Ultimate Strawberry Shortcake
items.name: The Ultimate Strawberry Shortcake
items.description: Make and share this The Ultimate Strawberry Shortcake recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Wash, stem, and cut strawberries in half.
Add sugar; toss to mix well.
Chill.
Beat cream cheese and powdered sugar well.
Fold in whipped topping and cake cubes.
Spread cake into an ungreased 13x9 dish.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours.
Cut cake into squares; top with strawberries.

reviews.review_text: I wish I could give this recipe 10 stars instead of 5. It was a big hit at the party. But I did a few changes since I am a cake decorator and I like my cakes to be clean when I cut them. First I used 2 boxes of angel food cake and I baked them separately in the same pan so I could layer my cake. So I started with the first angel cake, then I put the cream cheese, sugar & whipped topping filling. Since I did not want the chilled strawberries on top of the cake, I added it to the cream filling. I did put a bit more strawberries than the recipe ask for. I then topped everything with the second angel cake. To finish the cake, I covered it with butter cream icing so I could decorate it. It looked really nice (like a normal cake) and it was easy to cut since it was like an angel cake with a strawberry filling in the middle.

attributes.source_text: It was a big hit at the party

reviews.review_text: My favorite strawberry shortcake is still ''the one Mom always made.'' Clean and cut the berries at least in half; cut larger berries more. Macerate the berries with something close to 1/2 cup sugar to 1 cup cut berries, or more, long enough to dissolve all or most of the sugar. Stir occasionally. This yields a lot of that luscious syrup. Just before serving, bake fresh, old-fashioned lard and baking soda biscuits until lightly browned with a crunchy crust. Have things ready to assemble the individual servings as soon as the biscuits come out of the oven. For each serving, cut a biscuit in half and generously butter each half. Place the bottom half into the dish and top generously with strawberries and syrup. Add the top half of the biscuit and add more strawberries and syrup on top. Pour a reasonably generous amount or cream over the whole thing and eat before the biscuits get cold and lose their crunch. Please, don't tell my cardiologist that I posted this!

attributes.source_text: with a crunchy crust
lose their crunch

reviews.review_text:
Tried the shortcake tonight for a potluck. It went together very easy--especially after I decided it would be easier to gently break the angel food into small chunks instead of cutting into cubes--I think it came out the same in the end. I envisioned it being cake height, but in actuality it was only about an inch high and a bit difficult to serve in intact squares. As was mentioned in another review, served up in spoonfuls after failed attempt at squares. The flavor was very good though--everyone loved it.
 UPDATE: Made the a second time this week.  Tried to be even more gentle when folding in the cake pieces.  I put it in a 8" trifle-style bowl and I was happier with the results.

attributes.source_text: for a potluck

reviews.review_text:
Luscious.

After reading every (yes every 171  of them!) reviews this is what I did.  I pretty much stayed to the recipe; my changes were minor.  I only found a 12 oz angel food cake so there was less cake to cream mixture which worked out just fine.  I added another 2 cups of strawberries and kept the same amount of sugar; my strawberries were local and extremely sweet.  I thought the amount of strawberries was just about perfect; it could have used maybe even a cup more.  I used the creamy cool whip.  I ripped my cake up in large chunks.  When I make it again I'll add a few more strawberries & keep everything else the same.

This was a delicious recipe.  I had put this one in my cookbook many months ago, and finally decided to make it for my husband's retirement party.  I made a test run following the recipe exactly.  For the party I did the following:

First:I cut up the angel food cake into very small squares using kitchen scissors. 

second:  I put the "cake" mixture into individual metal cupcake liners. (which is why I need the pieces of angel food cake to be small)

third:  I froze the "cake" portion for a week.  On day of the party I took them out of the freezer about 2 hours before serving them and spooned the strawberries on top.  

They defrosted beautifully and everyone loved them.

attributes.source_text: make it for my husband's retirement party

reviews.review_text: This strawberry shortcake was an easy to prepare dessert, and a great crowd pleaser!  I used an electric hand mixer to combine the cream cheese & powdered sugar, which is easier to do when the cream cheese is at room temperature.  I haven't come across frozen whipped topping in Australia, so I just whipped up 300ml thickened cream, and combined 1/3 of the cream with the cream cheese/sugar mixture, then then this was combined, folded in the remainder of the cream.  Combining these ingredients first made it fairly easy to fold in the cubes of cake.  I haven't come across prepared angel food cake either, so I used a prepared madeira cake which gave the cake a slight citrus tang.  I also used 500g, or 2 punnets of strawberries, and didn't mix these with sugar as I thought the cake was sweet enough.  I agree with previous reviewers that the cake worked well with the additional strawberries.  Thanks for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: an easy to prepare dessert
gave the cake a slight citrus tang
I thought the cake was sweet enough

reviews.review_text: Great dessert! Tastes wonderful and is so easy. Have made it a few and it’s been a hit EVERY time (even with superbowl fans)  I have changed the assembly method slightly.  I, too serve it in a trifle bowl.  I was having lousy luck cutting my anglefood cake into cubes and mixing it into the cream.  Now I cut the anglefood cake in half lengthwise, and have a perfect round base to start layering the trifle.  Next I do the strawberries and then the cream.  Repeat the layers and end with fresh, whole strawberries.  From the side, the layers look great.  Nice and neat (because I’m not usually a “neat” dessert maker!)  ~B

attributes.source_text: Great dessert!
even with superbowl fans

reviews.review_text:
Yum!  I had a craving for Strawberry Shortcake and this totally fit the bill.

The only change I made was to use a whole big container of strawberries (can't think of the size off the top of my head, but I do know it was bigger than a quart) and instead of cutting them in half, cut them in quarters so the sugar can break them up a bit better.

I paired this with #24041 which might seem strange, but after the spices in the mexican dish, strawberry shortcake was just the refreshing kind of dish we wanted afterwards.  I'll be making this again. Thanks so much for sharing, I'm really loving your recipes!

attributes.source_text: strawberry shortcake was just the refreshing kind of dish we wanted afterwards

reviews.review_text:
Oooh so rich! It was so yummy! The only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 2 was because it was too rich for my family but the recipe itself is great. I did do a couple things different in the preperation but kept all the ingreidants the same. 
I baked the cake according to the box directions in a loaf pan. And added an extra 2 tbl sp of flour to the mix for high altitude. After the cake cooled I cut it into 3/4 " slices. It held together great! Then layered 2-3 pieces of cake and cream cheese mixture then topped with strawberry mixture and cool whip. It looked so pretty and didn't require the 2 hour fridge time.

attributes.source_text: Oooh so rich!

reviews.review_text: Made this for Fourth of July party - what a HUGE HIT!!  I basically kept the recipe the same but made a few changes from the comments - used 12 oz of creamy cool whip in the recipe instead of 8 and let the cake sit overnight.  Put the strawberry/syrup on the cake about two hours before serving and then topped with more cool whip and then made the famous flag design on top with sliced strawberries and blueberries.  It turned out great and was so incredibly light and delicious!!  Everyone had seconds!!  Next time I will try the low fat or no fat version to see how it turns out!!  Thanks for such a great recipe - a new tradition in my family!

attributes.source_text: Made this for Fourth of July party
Fourth of July party
so incredibly light

reviews.review_text: Very good.  I increased the amount of strawberries and whipped topping.  I added some of the strawberries and some blueberries to the cake and cream mixture.  I put 8 oz of whipped topping on top of that and let it chill, then I put the sweetened strawberries on top in the middle and put sweetened blueberries around the outside.  I took it to a church supper and was afraid the strawberries would not be evenly divided if i just let people put their own on top.  Anyway, I loved it and so did everyone who had a piece of it.  Thanks for this goody.  I will make it again.

attributes.source_text: I took it to a church supper

reviews.review_text: I made this dessert for 4th of July,(which was very simple to make.) Everyone had filled up on barbeque, chips, and all appetizers you can think of until they probably were sick to their stomaches. My mother-in-law brought out one of her desserts and sat it on the table.  Once I saw hers I remembered mine was chilled in the fridge, so I brought mine out and oh did everyone get up so quick that by the time everyone was seated I looked at my dish empty and scraped.  My poor motherinlaw's dessert was sitting there untouched.  I did not taste it but everyone one had cream on their face.  So I take it that it was 5 stars.

attributes.source_text: I made this dessert
for 4th of July

reviews.review_text: This was soooooo good and soooo easy.  I had to take a dish to a picnic this past weekend so I threw this one together.  Normally, I hate angelfood instead of the bisquick biscuits...but THIS...was awesome.  I took the advise of others and used 1 1/3 blocks of cream cheese, about 1 & 1/3 cups of powdered sugar and a whole tub plus a big spoonful of coolwhip.  I also used 2 9 oz. angel foodcakes and just tore them up.  After I took it out of the fridge, I spead the rest of the cool whip on top and then cup into squares.  It was perfect.  Thanks for the GREAT recipie.  This one is a keeper.

attributes.source_text: I had to take a dish to a picnic this past weekend

reviews.review_text: Wow, there's no kidding about the title of this recipe-this is the BEST strawberry shortcake my husband and I have ever had! Because of some of the prior comments on presentation, I also left the angel food cake whole (instead of cutting it into cubes) and spread the topping over it. The end result was lovely and made for such a delicious dessert! The cream cheese/powdered sugar/Cool Whip topping is unbelievable and it pairs so well with the sweet strawberries and light-as-air cake. I can't wait to make this one again-I'm sure it'll be on a pretty regular rotation around here! =)  Thank you for the terrific recipe!

attributes.source_text: my husband and I have ever had
made for such a delicious dessert
pairs so well with the sweet strawberries
light-as-air cake

reviews.review_text: Incredibly Delicous!  Even after reading all 100 reviews, I only made one small change.  I used 3lbs of strawberries and 1/4 cup of sugar with them.  They were already ripe and sweet, so hence my change.  Mizz Nezz, this was such a nice change from the same old biscuits of traditional strawberry shortcake.  The angel foodcake/cream cheesecake mixture was a little sweet and maybe in the future, I would try to adjust that a little, just a personal preference.  However,  this is delicious as is.  Thank you so much for sharing this recipe with all of us.  It's a winner and I recommend that everyone try it!  Tweeky

The name says it all! This IS the ultimate strawberry shortcake. I make mine as a trifle the night before, though I do wait to add the strawberries and yummy syrup til a few hours before serving. I also like to reserve some of the strawberries so that once it's dipped you can add your own. Always a hit! Oh, and for those of you who live near an Amish community or are able to find and purchase an Amish made vanilla angel food cake, I highly recommend it. You will turn something that is already amazing into a royal treat :) Thanks for another wonderful recipe MizzNezz!

I thought this was pretty good.  I made it as stated combining cubes of angel food with the cream cheese filling.  I used light cream cheese and cool whip.  Friends and DH really liked it.  I thought the consistency was a little odd.  I wanted to layer it, but I cooked my AF cake in a round pan, and served in 9x13 so I had to cut it up.  It wasn't very pretty and the juicy strawberries started to make it look nasty very quickly.  Next time I will layer incredients, probably keeping the cake whole and add some vanilla to the cream cheese mixture.  I thought it needed a little something.  

Thanks for posting.

attributes.source_text: Friends and DH really liked it
Friends and DH really liked it

reviews.review_text: Great recipe! I didn't like how tall it was (about an inch high) once you spread it in the pan) and my husband said the cake mixture  reminded him of someone chewing it up and spitting it out. So the next time I just made a regular buttered pound cake (the light & fluffy boxed kind) I baked it in a regular cake pan. When it was cooled I spread the layer of cream cheese mixture on top and topped with the fresh strawberries. It came out much prettier and neater. This is the best strawberry shortcake recipe by far. The flavors are excellent.

I made this tonight for an evening coffee snack - it was a huge hit!  This recipe is very easy to prepare - although I think it takes a bit longer than 20 minutes.  I used "light" cream cheese and "light" whipped topping - it worked very well.  I took some of the others suggestions and added more strawberries - I also decreased the sugar by about 2 tablespoons.  I did let mine sit for 6 hours and it seemed to be very easy to serve in squares.  A definite keeper and I will definitely make this very light and tasty desert again and again!!

attributes.source_text: for an evening coffee snack
for an evening coffee snack
very light and tasty desert

items.label: Libby's Famous Pumpkin Pie
items.name: Libby's Famous Pumpkin Pie
items.description: Well, after looking for this recipe on here and not having any luck, I decided to find it and post it. In my opinion, this is the best pumpkin pie. Make your own graham cracker crust or buy an already prepared one.
instructions: Note: Substitute 1-3/4 teaspoons pumpkin pie spice instead of cinnamon, ginger, and cloves; the taste will be slightly different.
Preheat oven to 425 degrees Fahrenheit.
Mix sugar, salt, cinnamon, ginger, and cloves in small bowl.
Beat eggs in large bowl.
Stir in pumpkin and sugar-spice mixture.
Gradually stir in evaporated milk.
Pour mixture into pie shell.
Bake at 425 degrees Fahrenheit for 15 minutes.
Reduce temperature to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
Bake for 40 to 50 minutes or until knife inserted near center comes out clean.
Cool on wire rack for 2 hours.
Serve immediately or refrigerate.
Top with whipped cream before serving for best results!
Do not overcook; overcooking leads to pie cracking in the middle.

Try to bake the day you will serve the pie. Cooking in advance can make the crust soggy. If you have to bake a day before serving, pop the pie in the oven for 5 to 10 minutes and it should bring the crust back to life!

reviews.review_text: This is the BEST pumpkin pie! I always make 2, but I just tweak it a little bit: For two, non deep-dish 9" pies, I double the recipe. For the cinnamon, ginger, and cloves, I substitute an equal amount of pumpkin pie spice. The last change I make is to use one 12 oz. can of evaporated milk and one 14 oz. can of Eagle Brand sweetened condensed milk, instead of two cans of evaporated in the doubled recipe. The crust I use is homemade, and it makes 2 9" pie crusts (Recipe #401353). I always make them the day before, I don't bother blind baking the crusts (though it probably wouldn't hurt), and I bake them on 375 degrees F the entire time for about 35-40 minutes (or until a knife inserted in the center comes out clean). I have found that if the temp. is 425 to start, the crusts brown too quickly (for us). This is the only recipe we enjoy around the holidays. Thanks for posting it!!

attributes.source_text: This is the only recipe we enjoy around the holidays

reviews.review_text: I live in Ingland so I coudn't find the pumpkin puree, but I replaced it with half a kilo of sweet potato...I guess that changing the main ingredient defeats the full purpose of baking a pumpkin pie :-).  Put it came out really well.  I also followed some advise about adding just half of the evaporated milk to make it more consistent, which is a good idea but I would suggest that if you do that probably just leave it in the oven for no more than 35 mins after reducing the temperature because it otherwise you take the risk of getting the edges a little bit burned.

yum! i think this is similar to the one i usually use that is on the "one pie" pumpkin can, but I can't find "one pie" brand stuff here so I found  this which seems pretty close.
Followed the recipe pretty much... i made my own crust, basic flaky pie crust. Oh, and i did use pumpkin pie spice, and yes, i would like to use all the individual ones but i'm in college and am therefore too cheap to buy all the different spices. But I'm going home for thanksgiving so i'll definitely make this recipe with the real spices while i'm there. 
great recipe!! thanks!

Classic and easy pumpkin pie.  I use premade pie crust, and I take a second premade pie crust to make cut outs with cookie cutters to decorate the top of the pumpkin pie.  I brush the cut out pie crust with egg wash, sprinkle with sugar and bake the cut outs in the 425 degree oven along with the pie, on a cookie sheet...watch them carefully and pull them out when golden brown.  Once the pumpkin pie is cooled, place the baked cut outs on top of your pumpkin pie for an extra special decorative touch!

I made this as a much lower fat and PARVE (NON DAIRY) version since I had to serve it with a fleishig dinner, and it was absolutely DELICIOUS! Instead of the evaporated milk, I used 6 ounces of parve/non dairy rice milk and 6 ounces of parve/non dairy whipping cream (usually found in the freezer section in the Jewish section). The whipping cream should be refrigerator-thawed when used. It was so amazing, i would never consider making this dairy fuller fat version! I have never eaten pumpkin, but decided to try this recipe since my friend told me about it. I had a feeling someone already posted it here on zaar! I had enough to fill a Graham cracker parve crust as well as additional to put in a ramikin (corning white) which was not greased. I cookde it only 40min once I brought the temp down to 350, and was wary as it looked undone, but after the resting time it was denser. I ate it out of the ramikin without even properly swallowing - it was SO SO good. Highly recommended recipe!

attributes.source_text: after the resting time it was denser

reviews.review_text: It's a classic!  I add 1 1/2 capfulls of vanilla extract, & substitute 1/4 cup of the white sugar with dark brown sugar. Most importantly in my book, is that I do not use the whole can of evaporated milk - I use about 80% or 10 ounces instead of 12.  This keeps the crust & the center from being too wet.  The pie baked up beautifully & firm  - consistent baking throughout the pie. Also, I use the spice mixture, not the premade pumpkin pie spice.  Next time though, I think I will add a bit of nutmeg to the spices. Yum!

attributes.source_text: The pie baked up beautifully & firm
keeps the crust & the center from being too wet

reviews.review_text:
This is my first attempt at Pumpkin pie, as I don't eat it but my son and husband does.
I did cheat and use a frozen pie crust, next time I'll try from scratch. It did take a little longer too cook maybe because of the frozen crust?  I had to use the pumpkin pie spice (bad me), but I thought I have ground cloves and of course I didn't (next time will try using listed ingredients).

My son LOVED it, he ate 1/2 the pie himself (thankfully not in one sitting)!  I tried it and it was good, it wasn't heavy like some of the other pies I've tried. It was fluffy and I liked the texture.
And of course my son piled on the cool whip. 

I will make this again, and take a picture!!

Thanx, this is a keeper!

**update 10.18 made this again and my sister LOVED it, forgot to take the picture again. 

Thanksgiving is coming up and I'm sure people will want my homemade pie over my aunt's store bought one any day!!!***

attributes.source_text: My son LOVED it
it wasn't heavy like some of the other pies I've tried
It was fluffy
my sister LOVED it

reviews.review_text: This was better than any store-bought pumpkin pie I've ever had. It was so easy to make that I really doubt I'll ever buy a store-bought one again. Also, I liked that it cost less than $4 to make it. I didn't use ground cloves since they were expensive ($9.99). I just used extra cinnamon and ginger to make up for it. I also didn't use whipped cream because I thought it was good enough without it. I had to bake mine for 15 mins plus the full 50 mins. Thanks so much for sharing this excellent recipe!

I'm a young chef, but I've been cooking since I was tall enough to flip the grilled cheese.  This recipe really can't be beat, except literally. No seriously,  Whip the mixture for a few minutes, (It's easier with the whip attachment on a standing mixer.) until it gets a little lighter in color, before you pore it into the pie crust.  This is a family secret passed down to my sister and I, now that we've taken over the generational cooking. You'll have the creamiest pumpkin pie ever!  Guaranteed!

attributes.source_text: You'll have the creamiest pumpkin pie ever!

reviews.review_text: This was the first pie that I ever made and I love pumpkin pie. I followed the directions exactly, except for the part which called for a can of 100% pumpkin puree. When I went to the grocery store, they only had one brand of pumpkin puree, E.D. Smiths and it was in a giant can. I had to figure out 15 ounces in metric. I ended up with just a little more filling than could fit in the pie shell. I think next time I might ad a 1/4 more spices to it.

I have made this pie for years (and never a soggy crust)but like others I find brown sugar the best and the spice mixture, not the pumpkin pie spice, to much all-spice in it I think. I have had my recipe for years and I thought it was a Libby recipe but mine calls for 1 egg and 1 tbsp flour and 1/2 tsp nutmeg, the rest the same. Maybe it’s the ED Smith recipe, who new but it great anyway. I notice some reviews say that they have made it for other because they don’t care for pumpkin, well try 2 cups of purée carrots really really yummy. Thanks for posting, it’s definitely the best pumpkin pie recipe. You also might like to try setting aside some of you pumpkin pie mixture and folding it into you whipped topping, very good!

attributes.source_text: never a soggy crust

reviews.review_text: Oh my goodness this was so good!  If I had known how easy it was to make a pumpkin pie, I wouldn't have wasted all that money on Mrs. Smith.  The only changes I made were to increase the ginger and cinnamon by 1/4 tsp and the cloves I made as a heaping 1/4 tsp instead of just 1/4 tsp.  Used my mixer to make the batter smooth. The only downside was the crust was too overcooked. (Hence the 4 stars).  I would either buy those crust "protectors" or do as one reviewer did and just bake at 375 degrees F. the whole time.  Next time I might add a splash of vanilla extract.

attributes.source_text: Used my mixer to make the batter smooth

reviews.review_text: I had some pumpkin left from our Thanksgiving pie that needed to be used so I made this pie but I made it less calorie-dense to give our bodies a break after the holidays.  I used skim evaporated milk, I sprayed a glass pie plate and omitted the pie crust, and I replaced 1/4 cup of sugar with sugar substitute.  It still turned out really well.  I grabbed a small piece while it was still warm and that has convinced me that I should make this often as a quick and guilt-free dessert.

attributes.source_text: a quick and guilt-free dessert

reviews.review_text: OH MY GOODNESS! I can say it loud and say it proud - this was delicious. Never had pumpkin pie before so this was my first attempt. Mine made two 8 inch pies - they weren't very deep. When I told Dad what was for pudding he was like NOO!!!!!!!!!! (aka a vegtable). But I wanted pumkin for halloween and it was the only way. He LOVED it, so did mum and she rated it higher than houstons in the us. Thanks for posting - will be making for years to come. Happy cooking. Miss Pixie x x x :D

Note to Canadians - my can of pumpkin puree was not the same size as what this called for.  It was 13 oz.  So I had to use part of another can.  I couldn't find Libby brand.  Also, mine took 50 minutes to bake and it made one thick pie.  It was delicious!  Oh and I cooked mine the evening before and it wasn't soggy at all!

The spices aren't overpowering, it's got a really nice balance of flavours: a bit creamy yet light and still full of flavour. I've made it with a no-roll pie crust (51537) and it works wonderfully. (I never use ready-whip topping though) The other day I made this without the pie shell- I simply cooked it in a baking dish, and it was perfect! I don't like pie shells very much, and since everyone in my family was so alienated by the appearance of the final product, I got to have it all for myself! So awesome! Overall, this is definately a tried and true recipe!

reviews.review_text: Hosted a 4-H Food Project meeting at my home earlier today--featuring "Fall Produce"...and baked up six pies (yes, the kids did all the work!).  We pitted this recipe against HeatherFeather's Recipe #105977 and did a taste test.   Wish I could declare one a clear-cut winner, but we ended up with a tie!  This pie WAS smoother and more dense.   We used a regular flour & shortening pie crust  which was light & flakey (that's a COMPLIMENT!!!)  :rofl:  Thanks KatieMom84 for a great recipe!
