items.label: Chicken Pesto
items.name: Chicken Pesto
items.description: This was my daughter's favorite dish (along with some of her friends). She enjoyed it so much that we had to make it a weekly recipe.
instructions: Prepare pesto sauce according to package direction.
Heat oven to 350 degrees.
Spray rectangular dish (9 by 12 inch) with no-stick spray.
Moisten chicken with water, shake off excess, and coat complete with bread crumbs.
Place chicken in baking dish.
Spread pesto sauce evenly over chicken breasts.
Cover each breast with ½ slice of provolone cheese.
Spread mushrooms over cheese.
Bake in oven for 45- 50 minutes.
Serve with pasta.

reviews.review_text:
What an easy, tasty dish!
I did make a couple of minor changes due to the ingredients that I had on hand. I thought I had Knorr Pesto, but I really had Knorr Creamy Pesto in the pantry. So I prepared the creamy packet. I had frest mushrooms, so I sauteed them while the sauce was cooking. Also, I decided to pound the breasts to about 1/4" for even cooking. I dipped the breasts into the crumbs, then spread the creamy pesto on them. Then I placed the mushrooms followed by the provolone slices. I thought that by putting on the mushrooms -- then the cheese last -- this would keep the mushrooms in place better so they couldn't slide off. Anyway, thanks so much for sharing this great recipe. We really enjoyed it, and I will be making this again.

--Marla

Totally awesome!  I just could NOT resist a huge bunch of fresh basil at the Farmer's Market last weekend.  With no real plans for it, it sadly sat in my fridge until last night when my menu plan had gone awry and I was searching for something to make for dinner.

I found another awesome 'Zaar recipe for fresh Pesto (recipe #49909) and whipped that up (instead of using the packaged Pesto mix called for).  I pretty much followed the recipe as written, with the exceptions of only using 2 breasts (it's all I had and I WISH I'd have made more) and I used fresh mushrooms and shredded mozzarella (instead of the provolone).

My husband said it was one of the best things I'd made EVER.  And we WILL be making it again.  Thank you SO much for posting.

attributes.source_text: My husband said it was one of the best things I'd made EVER
searching for something to make for dinner

reviews.review_text: This was the best. I did make a few changes because I am low carbs: I used turkey cutlets, what I had on hand. I dipped the turkey in egg substitute and then into a mixture of 1/2c parmesan cheese and 1/4c bread crumbs. I then sauteed the turkey in a nonstick skillet sprayed with nonstick cooking spray and a little oil. Fryed until crisp then spread the pesto on top (I had sauteed some onions and mushrooms) added them next and then put the provolone cheese on top. Put the patties under the broiler for a few minutes for the cheese to bubble. The taste was unbelievable. I will try next with spaghetti sauce or maybe salsa, the possibilities are endless. Turkey cutlett that are ususally dry and need a sauce are now moist and great tasting. Thanks for a great recipe that I will make again and again.

attributes.source_text: Fryed until crisp
are now moist

reviews.review_text: Just not that great at all... Another reviewer made the comment: "this recipe is only as good as the pesto you use." I'd have to agree. I took a couple of extra steps to try to bring this to life as I was already a bit weary up front, but I also felt silly questioning numerous 5 star reviews. I haven't found any recipe where canned mushrooms work better than fresh mushrooms, so I substituted fresh mushrooms which turned out well. I also butterflied the chicken to help the flavor penetrate throughout the breast. In the end, the chicken was cooked to perfection as far as temperature was concerned, but the overall flavor was really overpowering, and not in a great way (this coming from someone who typically enjoys pungents foods). I supposed making your own pesto would make things a lot better, but that would also defeat the purpose of a simple meal wouldn't it? Another reviewer suggested adding foil for the first thirty minutes. If you don't want the provolone overcooked, I'd advise doing so...

This was a hit. I used my homemade pesto and fresh mushrooms. OMG was it good. Next time I may butterfly the breasts, as mine seemed too thick when I took them out of the oven. My son said the chicken was awesome. It was moist and flavorful. I served it with vermicelli and mescalin salad with balsamic dressing. May 25, 2005: I made this again and used fresh breadcrumbs (a darkly-toasted bagle) which seemed to "stick" better. I used Thai basil for the pesto and the dish was better than the first time. I love this stuff. May 2008: I made it differently this time. I didn't bread the chix instead I laid a rectangle of puff pastry on top. I added ALL of the toppings after I baked the chix by itself for 12 minutes. It was excellent. Thanks for such a versatile recipe!

attributes.source_text: My son said the chicken was awesome
It was moist

reviews.review_text: Recipe was pretty easy to put together. I halved the recipe for our family and put it in an 8x8 pan. My cheese was pretty brown by the end, I would maybe put on tin foil next time and take off the last 10 minutes. We ate this with some wheat penne. Since there was some of the pesto sauce left over from halving the recipe, I decided to just add the last of it to the pasta, kind of have a pesto theme. I followed someone's suggestion and put the mushrooms on underneath the cheese, so they wouldn't go all over the place. I also used fresh mushrooms. I also used full slices of cheese, just a family preference. I didn't bread the chicken with the breadcrumbs and it was still wondrful. I forgot that it was going to take 45 minutes to cook though. That was the only bummer part. The next time I made it I only put it in for 30-35 minutes. This meal was excellent! We will do it again. The pesto pasta made the whole meal a bit much on the side of pesto, but was still good. For not that much money, this is a pretty fancy meal. Thanks for the recipe, Maine-iac!

Another winner on RECIPEZAAR.. There is no other place I go for recipes, and if I do it's because I saw something on foodnetwork. Anyway, this recipe was sooooo delicious.. The only change I made was when I put the cheese on. I waited til there was about 20 minutes left.. However next time I think I will put it on when there is about 10 minutes to go.. It's just that I prefer my cheese bubbly, not golden brown and bubbly, which is the way it was.. It was fine though, I just know to do it differently next time. To go with my Chicken Pesto, I made linguini and tossed it with pesto and grated parmsean cheese.. I can't wait to try this dish out on family and friends.. Thanks soooo much for sharing!

THANK YOU for sharing this FANTASTIC recipe!! I used the tips from the top 3 most helpful reviews, and added a couple things myself. I used defrosted frozen chicken tenders, dipped them in melted butter and then breaded with panko that I seasoned with Italian seasonings and salt. I baked for half the time (allowing panko to get crunchy), then topped with store-bought pesto, chopped tomatoes and sautéed mushrooms (so worth the several minutes it takes to sautee fresh mushrooms in butter, adding salt and pepper). Then I topped with 1/2 slice of provolone, and finished baking. I served with broccoli as well as fettucine tossed in remaining pesto sauce. This dish is relatively easy and full of flavor. A new family favorite!

attributes.source_text: allowing panko to get crunchy
A new family favorite!

reviews.review_text:
I made this for our Mother's Day dinner. I did coat my chicken with flour, egg wash, and seasoned bread crumbs and sauteed til almost done, and baked with the sauce. I added freshly sauteed mushrooms on half of chicken pieces. I really thought the mushrooms made it special, but not everyone in my family appreciates mushrooms the way I do! I did use Knorr packet of pesto sauce. Even though my chicken didn't need to bake long to cook through, I covered it with foil so it would stay "melty." I served this with my Giardiniera Lasagna  recipe #117371, which complemented each other nicely. This is a great chicken dish for company.

Roxygirl in Colo.

attributes.source_text: I made this for our Mother's Day dinner
I made this for our Mother's Day dinner
This is a great chicken dish for company

reviews.review_text: OH MY GOSH, this was SO good! I figured w/ such high ratings that it would be but I guess I was skeptical b/c it seemed too easy to make!  It is fantastic. I followed directions but used spray butter instead of water before coating with breadcrumbs (I used Italian-style). I also used Classico brand pesto in a jar (my ghetto walmart did not carry the Knorr sauce packet and this was all I could find).  I also used sliced fresh mushrooms and put the cheese on top.  I kept covered with foil until last 10 minutes. So good! This recipe will definitely take varsity status in my recipe rotations!

We LOVED this!!!! At first I thought I made it wrong, I doubled the sauce and made the packets according to the "sauce directions".) It was soupy, but I just went ahead and used it. I topped the crumb-coated chicken with fresh, sliced mushrooms, then poured half the sauce over all the breasts, and baked them. When there was 15 minutes left, I topped them each with a mountain of shredded 5-Blend Italian white cheese!! They were KILLER!!!!!!!! I served them over linguini tossed in the other half of the pesto sauce! YUM!!! We had this with Bergy's Easy Olive Garden Bread Sticks and tossed salad! What a feast!!! Thanks so much!!! A DEFINATE keeper!!! :)

My husband and I loved this dish!  I made it pretty much as directed except for the substitution of roasted red pepper slices for the sliced mushrooms, since I don't like mushrooms.  The roasted red pepper added more color as well as flavor to the dish.  I also put the red pepper on the chicken first, and then topped them with the provolone slices.  (I figured the melted cheese would keep the pepper from sliding off the chicken.)  We've had this a couple of times, with different brands of pesto sauce each time, and while the versions tasted slightly different, they were both delicious.  I imagine with homemade pesto it would be out of this world!

attributes.source_text: My husband and I loved this dish

reviews.review_text: This was a wonderful dish! I made pesto sauce from a pkg, which took no time at all. I am not a low carb dieter, but I do believe in portion control, so maybe this will help someone else. For the coating, I used 2 tbsp seasoned breadcrumbs + 1 tbsp grate parm cheese. I then coated one chick breast with it (just me for dinner), and even had some coating leftover! I then topped the chicken with about 4 spoonfuls of sauce (just enough to cover) & sprinkled 1/4 cup part skim mozz cheese on top. The cheese browned wonderfully & the chicken tasted great. (I skipped the mushrooms cuz I don't like them) A keeper!

attributes.source_text: just me for dinner

reviews.review_text: So good!  I used a refrigerated jarred pesto sauce, added tomatoes, artichokes, used fresh mushrooms instead of canned, and served over pasta.  Yum! I will definitely make this again!  Even my chicken-hater husband loved it!  Next time, I will probably cut the chicken breasts into smaller pieces, sautee the mushrooms (I just threw them in raw) and maybe sautee some onions with the mushrooms.  I was very pleased that I was able to make a chicken dish that I would be happy with if I ordered it at a restaurant--I have had trouble with drying chicken out.  Not this one--moist and delicious!

attributes.source_text: Even my chicken-hater husband loved it!
moist and delicious!

reviews.review_text: What a hit!  Too easy to be so good, and the presentation is amazing!  I always slice my chicken really thin and then I breaded the fillets.  I sprinkled them with olive oil and baked them for about 15 min. at 350 degrees.  Then I added the pesto, fresh sliced crimini mushrooms, and the chesse.  I cooked it for maybe 10 more minutes.  I threw it all under the broiler just to make the cheese extra bubbly and to give it that great golden color.  Everyone loved it, even my two and three year olds!  My husband wouldn't let me fix anything the next day, he just wanted leftovers!  Thank you Maine-iac!

attributes.source_text: even my two and three year olds
My husband wouldn't let me fix anything the next day, he just wanted leftovers
to make the cheese extra bubbly

reviews.review_text:
i sauted the mushrooms first, then put them on the chix then the cheese so the mushrooms would stay put. i also wrapped the dish with foil. i couldnt find any pesto mix, just the stuff in the jar so i just put half of it in. we ate the chicken pesto alone, but next time we will put it on noodles so it can soak up some of the pesto. very easy to make. will make again.
also tried this with a creamy pesto mix. cut chix in cubes and put the mix in with the chix. put it on noodles, delicious! pesto mix is cheaper than the stuff in the jar. it was 5.99 a for tiny jar here!

Fabulous dish!  I made this for some friends to discuss an upcoming trip to Italy.  Everyone raved and thought it was as good as one of our monthly "gourmet club" meals.  I did not use breadcrumbs (forgot about them).  I also used fresh mushrooms instead of the canned.  I used an organic pesto sauce mix and made extra to spoon over the cheese and spinich tortellini that we served.   We also served it with a salad w/ homemade oil and vinegar dressing, tuscan bread and fresh fruit.  Delicious!  Thanks for the great recipe.  Definitely will be making again!

attributes.source_text: I made this for some friends

reviews.review_text: YUMMY!  It's incredible how tender & juicy & flavorful the chicken is - we don't use mushrooms but quartered grape tomatoes instead - it is beautiful with the red & green & amazing taste as well.  I didn't think it'd work with just breading the chicken w/ breadcrumbs & not browning before baking but it does.   Soooo good - we've made at least 9 or 10 times & is always great.  Gave friend recipe & she makes all the time too.  I use the packet of pesto sauce since I think the jar might make too oily.  The packet makes the sauce really thin as well (thinner than the jarred stuff) which is why I think the chicken is so tender....so much liquid to bake it in.  Thanks for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: how tender & juicy & flavorful the chicken is
how tender & juicy & flavorful the chicken is
The packet makes the sauce really thin as well
which is why I think the chicken is so tender

reviews.review_text: This recipe is excellent!!! Extremely tasty and full of flavor.  I made this for my mom when she came over for dinner.  She travels every week for her job so needless to say she eats out quite a bit, so when she said that it tasted better than any pesto chicken she has ever had at a restaurant, I was proud.  The presentation is very impressive with very little work.  I used Delallo jarred pesto sauce from Italy instead of getting a package which made preparing even quicker.  I to will be making this on a regular basis.  Thank you for such a tasty recipe!!!

attributes.source_text: I made this for my mom when she came over for dinner
she came over for dinner

reviews.review_text: This was absolutely delicious, scrumptious, wonderful and any other adjective you can think of that can convey to you just how fantastic this recipe is. My DH took his first bite, looked at me and said, "Wow, I didn't know that I liked Pesto so much!" He's told me about 10 times in the last few minutes how good dinner tasted, how it's now one of his top 3 favorites and (this one's the best) how dinner looked and tasted like we went out to an expensive restaurant. He's in the kitchen now, happily doing the dishes while singing praises to me. Does it get better? While I'm a good cook, I'm not creative in being able to alter recipes (yet) so I heavily rely on reading the reviews to find out what other people have done to tweak a recipe. That's what's so great about Recipezaar, it's such a great springboard to inspire cooks like me. So here's what I did to make this a winning dinner. I bought a jar of Classico prepared pasta. I also bought 8 oz of fresh mushrooms, sliced them and sauteed them in margarine. I also dipped the chicken breasts in melted margarine before coating with Italian style breadcrumbs. I used three large chicken breasts which I split in half so they weren't so thick. I ended up with 6 pieces which was almost too much for my baking dish. I don't know how you could ever fit 8 chicken breasts in a 9x12 dish. Anyway, I then spooned the pesto sauce over the chicken, then the entire 8 oz of sauteed mushrooms and topped it off with provolone cheese so the chicken was totally covered. I covered the dish lightly with tinfoil for the first 20 minutes like other people have stated. I uncovered the chicken and cooked it another 20 minutes. The chicken was perfect. I wouldn't change a thing for the next time I make this.

attributes.source_text: My DH took his first bite, looked at me and said, "Wow, I didn't know that I liked Pesto so much!"
I didn't know that I liked Pesto so much!
how good dinner tasted

items.label: The Best Chicken Tortilla Soup
items.name: The Best Chicken Tortilla Soup
items.description: I'm in love with this soup!! A very good friend of mine made this for me recently and I fell in love. I'm very picky about my Tortilla Soup and this by far the best ever. She makes hers in the crock pot and I have to agree, that it's easy and tastes just wonderful!! Whatever you do, DO NOT skip the garnishes! They are the icing on the cake! UPDATE April 2010:  Obviously I've made this so many times I never even look at the recipe anymore!  But I wanted to add some variations that I play around with that are great.  Like many reviewers black beans and corn are great additions.  Sometimes I add them to the leftovers (if there are any :-) so that is feels like something new the next day!  I have also made it several times with shredded pork which turns it into a pork carnitas type of soup.  If you like it on the spicy and smoke side buy a can of chipotle peppers in adobo sauce and mince up one or two and add it.  And lastly, a little swizzle of half and half or heavy cream just minutes before serving makes it a creamy tortilla soup that is wonderful and it is also a good way to tone down the heat if it got away from you...
instructions: Throw everything except the garnishes in your crock pot and let it cook on high for 5-6 hours.
Dress with garnishes and give it a squeeze of lime (a must:-) and you're good to go!
Enjoy!
If you are not using a crock pot, saute the garlic and onion in 2 tablespoons olive oil before adding the remaining ingredients.
Simmer for at least an hour so that the flavors mix together.

reviews.review_text: I've been on the lookout for a good tortilla soup recipe - this is the one!  I modified the recipe slightly based on my preferences and what I had on had.  I made it in the slow cooker, but did sauté the onion and garlic before putting them in (I feel this gives better flavour).  For the chicken meat, I roasted bone-in thighs.  I probably used a bit more onion than called for (one large), and as I didn't have any fresh tomatoes, I added extra diced tomatoes.  I had just bought several jalapeño peppers, so used 2 large (and no Anaheim).  Oh yes - also added canned black beans and corn based on input from other reviewers.  Used more cilantro than called for (half a bunch).  Served with Tex Mex grated cheese, crumbled tortilla chips, fresh lime, sour cream, and avocado.  Guest worthy!

Really good stuff! 
My modifications: I omitted the chipotle because I didn't think mine needed more heat (I used 1 fresh hot green peppers, 3 sweet green peppers and pickled jalapeno in the soup).  I also increased the onion and garlic, added two grated carrots, some diced celery root, some pinto beans and oregano to add some heft (this will serve 5 as a main course, I'm thinking).  If I had some masa harina, I would mix that with a little olive oil and add it to the soup to thicken it up, too.  
None of these are criticisms, mind you--it is a wonderful, fragrant and tasty soup as is.  Just mentioning how I noodled around with it.  It is definitely the best that I've made from scratch!  Thanks for posting!!!

attributes.source_text: it is a wonderful, fragrant and tasty soup as is
this will serve 5 as a main course

reviews.review_text: As expected-this was pretty awesome!  Absolutely restaurant quality, if not better!  I followed the recipe for the most part, but used 2 lbs boneless skinless breasts (not sure how many cups that made, but it was plenty of chicken) cooked and shredded, 2 jalapenos instead of one, a bit extra chili powder, 4 garlic cloves vs. two, and a splash more tobasco than called for.  This definitely made it too spicy for most-but perfect for us!  I agree that the garnishes cannot be skimped on!!  I added sour cream to my garnish selection and I think you NEED this, especially if you want to cut down on the spice level!  Even if you don't-just use it!!  Threw it all in the crock pot on high for 6 hours and it was the best treat to come home to after a late afternoon , very chilly, baseball game!  Mmmmmmm..........

attributes.source_text: This definitely made it too spicy for most-but perfect for us!

reviews.review_text:
Fantastic! I regularly make homemade chicken stock for matzo ball soup. I save the soup chicken for another use, such as chicken salad, etc. I used my leftover soup chicken in place of the rotisserie chicken and it was delicious. We can't deal with a lot of heat, so I will back the jalepeno down to 1/2 (I used no anaheim chilies) and only a teaspoon of the chipotle hot sauce. Thank you Jill4man for a wonderful recipe!

--------

Used this recipe to make Turkey Tortilla Soup with Thanksgiving leftover turkey. For T-day gravy, I make my own stock using turkey giblets, neck and lots of veggies. Used some of my leftover turkey stock in place of the chix broth. Delish!

attributes.source_text: with Thanksgiving leftover turkey

reviews.review_text: I had never heard of Tortilla Soup until Jill4man was a featured cook recently. This recipe was so popular with other Zaarees, that I had to try it. I was worried about all the 'heat' that went into this, but was so wrong. We all loved it -- even the French exchange student who doesn't like 'spicy'. I made the recipe as written -- except that we don't have chipotle peppers or chipotle Tabasco in Australia. I used regular Tabasco, and added sour cream as a garnish. I can imagine throwing in some chopped kalamata olives, too. I guess it's sounding even more like a taco in a bowl. Either way, it's divine. Thanks for sharing.

attributes.source_text: even the French exchange student who doesn't like 'spicy'

reviews.review_text:
Very good recipe - although I had to make some changes based on availability and making the recipe easier. Normally I follow recipes to a "T", but the absurd high price of tomatoes (3x what they were a few weeks ago - no kidding) caused me alter the recipe slightly.

Instead of the 15oz can of diced tomatoes, 3-4 tomatoes (diced), and 2 anaheim peppers, I used a 28oz can of diced tomatoes, 1 can of Rotel, and 1 can of diced green chilies. It was cheaper and I think it stayed within the parameters of what the recipe tried to accomplish.

The soup was very good, and with no added fat pretty healthy to boot. Using the rotisserie chicken is a great idea, as you can usually find them for $5 - $6 around here - which is about what you'd pay for a whole frozen chicken. Plus you'll probably have some extra chicken meat left over to boot!

I may try the black beans in the soup next time as well like some other reviewers have suggested. This is definitely a keeper though.

I found this to be a good tortilla soup recipe that tastes better the second day. The photo, however, makes the soup look a clearer red than it turns out to be if you give the tortilla chips a fine to a bit under medium cruch and if you cruble the cheddar cheese rather than shred it in strips. The chips will melt into the soup and so will the cheese, so it won't look or be as clear with tomato-chicken broth. Rather than fool with reconsituting chipotle pepper or rebuying it and using it dry, I used 1/2 tsp. adobo sauce (homemade from an online encyclopedia recipe). That worked fine. I left out the anaheim chilies and used canned sliced green peppers in place of the 1 jalapeno pepper. The dish will taste hot enough but not overpoweringly so if you do these things and use only 1 tsp. Tobasco sauce and 1/2 tbsp. chili powder. I imagine this dish will taste a good deal hotter if you use the amounts for all the hot foods/spices called for. If you are a person who prefers a redder, clearer tortilla soup, find a recipe that uses tortilla strips and shred the cheese using the biggest shredder size. Bon appetit!

attributes.source_text: The dish will taste hot enough
but not overpoweringly so

reviews.review_text:
Yummers.. Not a fan of tomato based soups but this is really tasty and satisfying. I can never leave a recipe alone-so here is what I did.
  Sauteed fine chopped onion,anaheim chilies, 3-4 tomatillos and crushed garlic and added to soup. Added 1/2 c.canned corn,omitted the fresh red tomatoes and and jalepenos. Wanting to make the soup a bit more creamy but not thick I mixed some Wondra thickner and 1/3 c.heavy cream with a bit of the warm broth and added to soup. That made it just a little more special. I also added some Chicken broth base powder as I did not have enough canned broth and extra tomatoe sauce just make sure you add enough water to compensate for the concentrated chicken powder.Next time I will have cilantro.And the toppings are a must.I did this on the stove for a quick dinner, it was fantastic, but crocking it would be even better. mimsy

attributes.source_text: Wanting to make the soup a bit more creamy
for a quick dinner

reviews.review_text: Wonderful, fragrant, delicious! My go to. I dont remember when I first made this soup recipe but its one of the best Ive ever tasted and it can be tweaked to your tastes on that particular day. And it really is simple, I love that she shared this with us! I followed some tweaks mentioned regarding the enchilada sauce and it is very good. Im a doubler or tripler of sauces at times even though its just the 2 of us at home, but this is a great leftover meal so I enjoy it for days and make a lot of it. I finally "made" the tortilla strips by cutting up and baking corn tortillas with oil & cumin and it made it so much better usually I throw in tortilla chips. This is just one of those recipes that will go down as a favorite and people really enjoy thanks for sharing!! I also read somewhere whether here or another site about spooning the soup on top of the tortilla chips, avocado, cheese (i vary between using several different mexican cheeses depending on what i have) and lime juice and believe it really does taste wonderful with the garnishes at the bottom of the warm soup yum so good making it again today. Have i said how happy i am she shared this with us?

attributes.source_text: Wonderful, fragrant, delicious!

reviews.review_text:
This is absolutely to-die-for and will be a regular with me for life!  I had never even heard of Tortilla Soup (not seen in the UK, at least not that I've seen) but I came across the recipe when looking for new inspiration for my crockpot, which I use nearly every night...I've made this twice now, simply throwing it all in the crock and leaving all day on low (start off on high), exactly as stated in the recipe and it is absolutely delicious, we were fighting over seconds at the crock!  As Jill4man states and other reviewers have said, it is the garnishes that really make it - we thought it would be weird to put advocado on top of a soup, so wrong, it was exceptional.

**the only thing I would add is that it is more than a soup, it is definitely a meal in a bowl and certainly a perfect Monday-night supper to use up Sunday's roast chicken leftovers** 

~thank you for taking the time to post this recipe I for one am delighted!~

attributes.source_text: a perfect Monday-night supper

reviews.review_text:
Excellent soup! DH wanted to know if there was more before he finished his first bowl-and everyone went back for seconds!

Made it a day ahead of time on the stovetop. Used extra chicken, full can of tomato sauce and an extra jalapeno. Was worried at first that it might be too spicy. But the flavors really came together and it was perfect. As good as the best I've had in any restaurant and better than most! 

The toppings really put this soup well...over the top! The lime was an excellent addition to the flavor. We also used sour cream along w/the avacado, cilantro and a blend of cheddar and montery jack cheese. And by the time I got to the bottom of the bowl it was creamy and...well...simply fantastic.

Served it with quesadillas, but didn't really need to. With the extra chicken the soup was really a meal in and of itself.

Thanks Jill4man for sharing!

attributes.source_text: DH wanted to know if there was more before he finished his first bowl
it was creamy

reviews.review_text: Oh, my goodness! I just made this soup with my left over chicken from Yesterday,from the recipe I found on this site for the deli rotisserie chicken, which was delicious... Oh, this soup is a real winner! I am so glad I have leftovers for tomorrow.. think of it, three meals from one little rotisserie chicken. I tasted it as it cooked during the day, and I loved it from the very first bite that I sneaked.I put the trimmings on it, except I forgot the lime on the first bowl. but wow, what a difference when I added it to the next two bowls. (thats right, I had 3 bowls of the stuff)I could live without all the fixings, but the lime juice is a must do... don't neglect to use that. the other stuff gives it appeal, and sorta gives it EYE APPEAL,like a restaurant would do. The lime gives it TASTE appeal...its a winner.

the lime juice is a must do

reviews.review_text: This is an exceptional dish!  I really enjoyed it.  I omitted the cilantro, because I am very picky about how it tastes.  I decided the first time I made it I would taste it without it, and then the next time I made it I would try it with the cilantro.  See how it changes it up.  I didnt use crushed tortilla chips, I crisped up some cut up tortillas.  The only problem with that is that the tortillas will go soft after a while.  But, lol, my family ate it so fast that they never got that way.  The lime and avocado are a must.  I was worried about the heat too, so I didn't use the chipolte peppers.  My store was out of stock of the chipolte tabsco sauce, GO FIGURE, so I used a chipolte pepper marinade from mccormick.  I used just a little bit.  It was good.  Thanks Jill for the wonderful recipe.

attributes.source_text: my family ate it so fast

reviews.review_text: Terrific!  I made this for Super Bowl Sunday -- well, for us it's Puppy Bowl Sunday.  I made it exactly as written, except that I squeezed two limes into the soup right before serving, rather than garnishing with lime wedges.  I used three different kinds of chili powder, including a teaspoon of chipotle chili powder.  Loved the fact it was very flavorful without being too hot -- my husband stopped at the halfway point of dinner and said, "You know, this is really delicious."  I used chili & lime tortilla chips on top, and thought it made a big difference.  This is a definite keeper -- thanks so much for posting it!

attributes.source_text: I made this for Super Bowl Sunday
without being too hot
my husband stopped at the halfway point of dinner and said, "You know, this is really delicious."

reviews.review_text: Great flavors in this spicy soup!  I used a rotisserie chicken and shredded just the breast meat and I doubled the chicken broth (I like my soup a little runny).  Plus I blended all the peppers, tomatoes, onions and jalapenos in a blender before I cooked it so that my son would eat it!  (What he doesn't know is there, won't hurt him!) I saved the one can diced tomatoes back to give the soup some texture. I think next time I'll add a bit less peppers as it was a touch too spicy for him (I loved it) and add some veggies like squash and zucchini into the blender before I blend! He won't even taste them and it'll give him some extra veggies!!)  Will also add more chicken broth!  Wonderful soup as is though and I highly recommend it! And I've tried TONS of tortilla soup recipes!

attributes.source_text: Great flavors in this spicy soup
I like my soup a little runny

reviews.review_text:
Dear Jill4man,
Thank you for inviting us into your kitchen to taste your fabulous "The Best Chicken Tortilla Soup."  Although I was no doubt many miles from you when we had this, I felt like we were having lunch together!  DH and I love Tortilla Soup, and the quest for the best recipe stops here.  I used an 8 oz. can of tomato sauce, but followed the recipe completely other than that.  We had powdered chipotle peppers, so we did add it.  It was "bright" but not too spicy to be enjoyable.  There is a deep rich flavor to it that I was looking for.  And the garnishes are indeed "the icing!"  I can't thank you enough for this treat.  I know we will make it again and again.

attributes.source_text: DH and I love Tortilla Soup
It was "bright"
not too spicy to be enjoyable
deep rich flavor

reviews.review_text: Don't have a slow cooker so I cooked it on the stove for a couple hours. Skipped the fresh tomatoes, it's February and they taste like cardboard, even here in California. Used a couple Anaheim chiles and a Poblano as well. This was the best tortilla soup recipe I've tried and it comes reasonably close to the best I've had in a restaurant. What I don't understand about this recipe (and didn't follow) is using Tabasco, there are plenty of Mexican alternatives available almost anywhere (I prefer Tapatio, although I only added it after cooking) and cheddar cheese. Far better with Monterey Jack, which has a very different effect, or even real Mexican cheese if you can get it.

We loved this really versatile soup recipe. Even my daughter who is picky about tomatoes had no problem gobbling down a bowl and taking leftovers for her lunch today. I did have to tone down the heat a bit as some members of my family can't digest spicy food, so I used a can of diced tomatoes with green chilies as my only peppers. I did serve jalapenos on the side to go into the soup for those who wanted heat (like me!). This soup is easy and absolutely delicious. As stated, the lime is REALLY an important little garnish. And besides the jalapeno and suggested garnish we also had sour cream.

attributes.source_text: Even my daughter who is picky about tomatoes had no problem gobbling down a bowl
my daughter who is picky about tomatoes had no problem gobbling down a bowl

items.label: The Very Best Salisbury Steak
items.name: The Very Best Salisbury Steak
items.description: This is our favorite salisbury steak recipe. I always make enough extra sauce to serve over potatoes. Tastes like it took all day to cook.
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together 1/3 cup condensed French onion soup with ground beef, bread crumbs, egg, salt and black pepper.
Shape into 6 oval patties.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown both sides of patties.
Pour off excess fat.
In a small bowl, blend flour and remaining soup until smooth.
Mix in ketchup, water, Worcestershire sauce and mustard powder.
Pour over meat in skillet.
Cover, and cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.

reviews.review_text: I made this tonight and we all loved it. I did, however, make a few changes. First of all, I sauteed some fresh mushrooms in the pan first, removed to a paper towel covered plate and set aside, then browned the beef patties. When making the patties, I had to get a little creative. The recipe does not say which size egg. Since the medium egg is the standard for cooking and baking, I used that as a yard stick. However, I only had jumbo eggs. Since two medium can roughly equal one jumbo,, I separated the yolk from the egg and only used half of the white, reserving the other half for a facial mask for tonight....put it in the fridge and get it cold...great for those bags under the eyes. I seared the patties and removed them to the plate with the mushroom. Scraping up the fond on the bottom of the pan (the brown goodies), I added the flour, stirred until the flour was cooked, then proceeded with the sauce. Because of the review which said it was too sweet, I used half of the catsup and replaced it with water. Next time, I think I'll glaze the pan with red wine first and proceed with the recipe. That is, replacing the additional water with wine - about 1/8 of a cup. I returned the mushrooms and patties to the skillet, covered and simmered per directions. We served it with buttered egg noodles and a nice, fresh salad to cut the richness. Soooo good.

attributes.source_text: to cut the richness

reviews.review_text: Great recipe!  As with all recipes I tweaked it a bit according to personal preference.  Keeping in mind that I never measure anything, here's my take on it:  Instead of french onion soup, I use a dry packet of Knorr's onion soup mix.  I combine 1/2 with the meat mixture (which otherwise is the same as this recipe) and reserve 1/2 for the sauce.  For the sauce I use a tetra pak of beef broth to which I add onions, mushrooms, worchestershire & ketchup to taste, and the remaining onion soup mix.  To thicken I use a flour & oil rue.  Awesome over mashed potatoes!!!

I made this tonight and it was so yummy :)  I did make some changes out of need i only had a packet of french onion soup and chicken broth so i kinda made due with what i had and i added half the soup packet to the 1st step then  a little broth to make up and i didnt have bread crumbs or bread so i used a little bit of oatmeal and for the sauce i made a roux sauce on the stove then added chicken broth and the rest of the soup packet and then added the rest of the ingredients.... this was sooo yummy and i was able to get 10 patty's out of my recipe :) happy eating  we will be making this again and again and again :)

I was desperate for something new that I could make without going to the market. This was exceptional! I made the patties according to the recipe, they were a little loose and didnt need the extra 20 in the sauce.... Browning in my cast iron cooked them through, they ended up tender and delicious. I didn't have any Worcestershire or ground mustard and I'm not a fan of ketchup. So I made the sauce with the soup and flour, did a little squirt of mustard, maybe 2-3 table spoons of ketchup (figured it needed it) added a little A1 in place of the Worcestershire. But it still needed a

attributes.source_text: they ended up tender

reviews.review_text: This is a recipe that truly lives up to its name. Mind you, I haven't had this dish since seeing its dreadful announcement at the college cafeteria, but it will now become a standard at our house, I can tell. My kids all devoured 2 patties each (good thing I doubled the recipe), and my husband--well, let's just say there wasn't much after he got through with it! After reading all the reviews, I didn't think I'd really be impressed with such a simple recipe, but it's a winner! Note: I used dry french onion soup mix (no msg)--and I think the soup is what takes this over the top.

attributes.source_text: My kids all devoured 2 patties each
my husband--well, let's just say there wasn't much after he got through with it!

reviews.review_text: So, my adaption for this solid foundation recipe is the following: -After pre-cooking the patties, I put them in the warming drawer, then add garlic and olive oil 1 TBP each to the pan, then add 1/2 c. sliced green onion and 3 chopped large Portobello mushrooms. Saute for 5 minutes then deglaze with 1/4 c. Masala wine. Only then do I add the sauce but no water in the mixture, the wine does the trick. Proceed with returning patties to pan, cover with sauce, cover pan and simmer 20 minutes. My family can't get enough of this rich yummy sauce.

attributes.source_text: this rich yummy sauce
My family can't get enough of this rich yummy sauce

reviews.review_text: 5-Stars!! So simple and Easy! Tasted wonderful! I was really impressed! I read a bunch of reviews and saw many people say they made more gravy so I did change things slightly.<br/>I used 2lbs of Beef, <br/>2 cans of French Onion Soup, <br/>1/2c of the soup in the beef,<br/>2tbsp of ketchup. <br/><br/>It came out absolutely perfect. I was surprised that beef patties could taste so moist and tender and delicious!! This is such a keeper!! <br/>I usually take pictures of all recipes I make...but I was so excited I forgot haha. Next time!

attributes.source_text: beef patties could taste so moist
moist and tender

reviews.review_text:
I followed the recipe to the letter first try and found that the soup, even though condensed, made the mixture far too sloppy and salty. Its not a hard recipe to make and I thought Id give it another go. I left out the soup mix full stop, and it was much better. The flavouring stand well as they are, the onion soup is not really needed.

I made gravy from scratch using stock and Bisto powder, it took less than ten minutes and tasted fine. I would make this recipe occasionally as its a good standby when funds are low. I served it with creamed potatoes, fresh green beans and oven roasted tomatoes.

Since I don't use canned or packaged soups, I caramelized onions & added beef stock.  Since caramelized onions contain sugar & vinegar, the ketchup isn't really needed except perhaps for color.  I used about 1Tb. ketchup, 1-1/2 Tbs Worcestershire, a splash of red wine, and the mustard.  Also added a few Tbs. fresh minced onion & minced parsley to the meat. Served with garlic mashed potatoes & sauteed asparagus. My husband almost never finishes his plate, he had two helpings. Fantastic stuff!

attributes.source_text: My husband almost never finishes his plate, he had two helpings

reviews.review_text: As soon as I added the french onion soup to the ground beef, it smelled "salisbury-ish" and I knew it would be a winner. I didn't think it was salty at all- in fact I added a little to both the meat and gravy. If you are going to be serving this with mashed potatoes, double or even triple the gravy!! When I went to stir it, a good portion had already dried up even though it was covered. We would have loved some more for our potatoes, but next time I'll be sure to make plenty. This is an enjoyable, economical, comfort food recipe.

attributes.source_text: I didn't think it was salty at all

reviews.review_text: We liked this recipe for Salisbury steak the best. It has more flavor than the others in my cookbook and its just as easy. Highly recommended, but one change I made after making it many times is I use stuffing mix, dry, from the box instead of the breadcrumbs.  It makes the patties more moist and gives it even more flavor.  I use the chicken flavored stuffing mix but you could also use the cornbread mix if you prefer.  Really good with sauteed mushrooms and sauteed onions added to the sauce in the final stages.

attributes.source_text: It makes the patties more moist

reviews.review_text: I made a few changes to this recipe.  I wanted double the gravy, so I used 20 oz. of beef broth in place of french onion soup (beef broth was what was on hand).  Because I doubled the liquid I need to make a cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce, which was made up of 1 tbsp. cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp. water.  I added onion powder to the steaks, but those were the only changes I made.  I loved the zesty tang of the gravy because of the added ketchup and mustard.  We loved the recipe served with peas and homemade mac n cheese.

attributes.source_text: I loved the zesty tang of the gravy
the zesty tang of the gravy

reviews.review_text: This came out way better than I thought it would! Such amazing flavor! Very impressed with this recipe! Definitely a keeper that I will make again very soon. I suggest that everyone who likes extra gravy to use a large 18oz can of Progresso onion soup in this recipe to make for extra gravy to serve over the meat and potatoes, rice or egg noodles!!!! Delicious! Also the 2lbs of meat made 8 large and thick meat patties. (The picture only shows 6, but it made 8, this was taken after feeding my boyfriend :)

attributes.source_text: 8 large and thick meat patties

reviews.review_text: This was WONDERFUL! I wanted to lighten it up a little, so I used half ground turkey and half ground beef. Didn't have plain bread crumbs, so I had to use Italian seasoned (extra seasoning can't hurt!). I also sauteed mushrooms in the pan while cooking the burgers. My husband doesn't like the texture of onions, so I used my emulsifier to blend the onions, flour, ketchup, Worcestershire and mustard...plus I added some beef broth to make more gravy. My picky family loved it! This is a keeper that will be made over and over again!

attributes.source_text: My picky family loved it

reviews.review_text: 5 stars are not enough for this recipe! It is so easy and requires very little prep time. Exactly the type of recipe I need for quintuplets, (YES, QUINTS!) and a hungry husband. My husband was very uncertain about having salisbury steak, he remembers it as tasteless rubber being served in the grade school cafeteria. Needless to say, this recipe blew him out of the water. The recipe is very easy to double, and I served it over medium egg noodles. The quints ask for it every week, that's the only downside of it!

attributes.source_text: this recipe blew him out of the water
The quints ask for it every week

reviews.review_text: The sauce for this dish is just wonderful!!  It tasted so yummy over mashed potatoes.  I made everything as is but next time plan to add garlic to the meat and maybe some other spices - it seems a bit bland but the sauce really shined so I will be carefull not to add to much of anything that could possibly clash with the sauce.  Oops, I guess it wasn't completely "as is", I did add a small can of mushrooms as some others did.  This a nice easy, comfort food dinner and I'm sure I'll be making it again.

attributes.source_text: comfort food dinner

reviews.review_text: I'd really rather go 4 1/2 stars but since that's not an option, I'll go ahead and give it the full 5.  The meat patties were awesome and I will absolutely make them that way again - very moist, good flavor and a very nice, even texture.  I didn't hate the sauce, but it wasn't really what I was expecting.  I had to use cornstarch since I didn't know I was out of white flour till I went to make this - still thickened nicely.  The sauce was tasty, it just isn't what I'd qualify as "salisbury steak" and was a bit sweet from the ketchup - maybe would be better with plain tomato sauce instead of ketchup?  I doubled the sauce amounts and it seemed to be just about the perfect amount.  I did half ground beef and half ground turkey.  My 9 year old had 3 servings!

attributes.source_text: very moist
a very nice, even texture
My 9 year old had 3 servings!

reviews.review_text: So I made this last night for the first time. Loved it, however, I forgot to add our beloved mushrooms that my husband, son and I love. Query as to when I should add them... when I add the sauce or do them in a separate pan? Last issue, was that I didn't want to lower the heat too much and have the burgers come out uncooked and I ended up following the directions to a "T", but then ended up burning the bottoms in the end because maybe I didn't lower the heat enough even though the recipe didn't say anything about that? Looking to make this again soon since I have a lot of mushrooms in my fridge to use up! Any one want to help me with a suggestion? Thank you!!!! :)

Made this recipe today and everything turned out fine...except except the sauce/gravy. Against my better judgement, I used the exact measurement of ketchup that this recipe calls for and you could clearly taste the sweetness of the ketchup in the sauce/gravy which didnt go over well for me or my guest. The expectation was that the gravy would have a beefy flavor & color, so when the slightly orange tinged gravy tasted somewhat sweet it wasnt well recieved. The Salisbury Steaks were very good though. This recipe is similar to my Grandmother's (Ma) recipe minus the can of Campbell's Condensed French Onion Soup, Mustard Powder & the Ketchup. 

Based on a previous review, I used 2 tsp of Worcestershire sauce which gave the sauce a good flavor without tanginess and I didnt have any mustard powder on hand, so I didn't use it. However, once the ketchup hit the mix, the sauce lost it's savory, beefy onion flavor & added a level of sweet that I did not like. I made it anyway because I didnt want to waste the ingredients. Good base recipe though. Next time I WILL NOT use the MSG laden can of Campbell's French Onion Soup nor will I use Ketchup. Next time I'll use a homemade onion soup mix that I make with a non-MSG powdered beef base, dehydrated onions and spices then add that to beef stock & rice flour.

items.label: Utterly Deadly Southern Pecan Pie
items.name: Utterly Deadly Southern Pecan Pie
items.description: The secret to this rich pie is cooking the sugar and corn syrup first. It is definitely not diet food!  I bake this pie for 45 minutes according to my oven but you may need to bake longer.
instructions: In saucepan boil sugar and corn syrup together for 2 to 3 minutes; set aside to cool slightly.
In large bowl beat eggs lightly and very slowly pour the syrup mixture into the eggs, stirring constantly.
At this point I like to strain the mixture to make sure it's smooth and lump free.
Stir in butter, vanilla, and pecans and pour into crust.
Bake in a 350°F oven for about 45 to 60 minutes or until set.

reviews.review_text: First time making a pecan pie. I have only made pies a handful of times in my life so I still have a lot to learn. I wish the directions we more specific for people like me who are beginners. For example, just saying stir in a 1/4 cup of butter into the mixture. Does it need melting or do you just put in 1/4 cup block straight from the fridge? And saying to slightly cool the syrup/sugar mixture before adding it to the eggs - perhaps give some science behind the need to cool the mixture (so it doesn't cook the eggs) and not allowing it to cool too much so it doesn't mix. I did appreciate the tip on straining the mixture because I did have lumps of cooked egg. It took at least 75minutes to bake, but it didn't spill over like in other reviews. After I put the pie in the oven, I found the Tweaks tab which would have been very helpful as there were suggestions to brown the butter and to add the eggs to the syrup, not the other way around. The pie looks lovely and I will know how it tastes tomorrow at work.

The most amazing pecan pie EVER! I made this about a month before Thanksgiving, and on Thanksgiving we had a store bought pecan pie that dulled in comparison. Normally I take a big slice, and this time I could only have two bites of the store bought pie!! After making this recipe, I will never be able to look at any other pecan pie, homemade or store bought, the same! It is so so simple to make, and absolutely delicious. I made this for my boyfriend and his roommates and it was gone in a day, and I've been getting requests to make it ever since! <br/><br/>I followed the steps exactly, but I added the butter to the sugar/corn syrup mix after removing it off the heat so it could melt easier. Then I followed the rest of the steps exactly. At first I only baked it for 30 minutes because it looked ready and the pie crust was starting to brown and I didn't want it to burn. I took it out and realized about an hour later that it definitely needed more time in the oven. I was hesitant about putting it back in the oven after it had sat out for so long, but put it back anyway. After an additional 20-25 minutes in the oven, it turned out perfectly! I definitely recommend leaving it the oven for the recommended time, and next time I will reduce the temperature of my boyfriend's oven because I think it is not completely accurate. Not sure if using a glass pie pan had an affect on the quick browning of the pie crust or not, or if the rack being set one higher than the center position of the oven had to do with it. Regardless, this recipe is amazing and DEFINITELY recommended!

attributes.source_text: I made this for my boyfriend and his roommates and it was gone in a day
I made this for my boyfriend and his roommates and it was gone in a day

reviews.review_text: Hi I made this pie for our Christmas Eve celebration, and I am here to say thus was the absolute BEST pecan pie I’ve ever made or had! I used half and half on the corn syrup, and toasted the pecans prior adding them to the pie. I boiled the corn syrup and sugar let cool then added 2 tablespoons of bourbon to the mix while it was cooling. Followed the rest of the recipe as worded. Be sure to temper the eggs with a small amount of the hot sugar syrup as to not scramble the eggs! Then add the rest accordingly. The only other thing I suggest is cooking this pie st 375 degrees rather than 350. I also cooked it a bit longer than an hour maybe an hour and fifteen. This pie sets up beautifully and is perfect if you are a pecan pie lover!

attributes.source_text: I made this pie for our Christmas Eve celebration

reviews.review_text: I had a few questions regarding the directions for making this pie and I don't know that my interpretation worked out successfully. I heated the sugar and syrup and allowed to boil for the 3 minutes. Then I added the butter to this in order to melt it in the hot sugar. I then added the egg and vanilla to the sugar and butter mixture. I thnk that I didn't allow the sugar/butter to cool long enough because the eggs began to cook a little which made the straining difficult and I think was the main reason my pie was so soupy...not enough egg made it through the strainer. After cooking for an hour and ten my pecans in the middle were starting to burn but I was still a syrupy mess on the outter rim and inside the pie. So, I served pecan syrup with ice cream at my dinner party! The taste of the filling was better than any pecan pie I have made before so I will defintiely be giving this recipe another shot. I will probably not bother with the straining in the future.

attributes.source_text: at my dinner party

reviews.review_text: My sister had a pie bar around her KrispyKreme tower at her wedding reception and I was asked to contribute 2 pecan pies.  I don't even love pecan pie, but met many people I didn't know because they wanted to let me know that they thought the pie was divine.  Leftovers of every single pie on the bar, except for the pecan pie, and it was also the very first gone before some were even tried. Had a feeling it might go that way though, because I ended up making FOUR 'test runs' before the wedding, including a chocolate one with 1/2 cup cocoa, and they were all history by day's end.  *Instead of vanilla (except in the case of the chocolate pecan pie I made), I used a teaspoon of maple flavoring and a tablespoon of bourbon and I baked all the pies for about 55mins.

attributes.source_text: at her wedding reception

reviews.review_text: If I could give this 10 stars, it would be an 11!! Made this and my family all loved it. My husband  loved it and he only loves his mom's pecan pie :) So that is an accomplishment. I used vanilla bean paste from Sur la Table instead of vanilla extract and that was good. I also melted the butter in the hot sugar/syrup mixture. I strained it after adding to the eggs and glad I did. There were some chunks of sugar that had not melted. My only fault was I filled the pie too full and it overflowed into my oven. So be careful not too fill to the top. It made a mess on the edges of the pie plate too and didn't look too pretty, but it tasted delicious so I guess it is ok :)

attributes.source_text: my family all loved it

reviews.review_text: Oh my! This is the best pecan pie recipe that I have ever made. I followed the recipe exactly as written. It made a beautiful presentation and was delicious. I loved the idea of cooking the sugar and syrup on top of the stove before putting in the pie plate. Being in a hurry, I added the butter to the sugar/syrup mixture as it was cooling. Cooking the mixture before putting in the oven prevents extra time in the oven and over baking the crust. No need to strain. I was worried that the pie would be too sweet using 1 cup of sugar, but it was not at all. I used a glass, 9 inch more shallow pie plate, and the filling filled the plate nicely. The gooey filling was just perfect.

attributes.source_text: The gooey filling was just perfect

reviews.review_text: The first time I made this, I knew I'd found the missing link in my pecan pies: Cooking the sugars. Basically, you're making a soft candy, which makes it stand up better.  Then I had to play with it.  Since my pie pans are deep-dish, and I make two at once, I increased the eggs to 10, the corn syrup to four cups, the vanilla to 4 tsp and added another generous half-cup of chopped pecans.<br/><br/>For those who like a bit bolder flavor, replace a half-cup of the dark corn syrup (for TWO pies) with unsulphured molasses.  YUM!

Our New Old Holiday Favorite! Pecan pie can be intimidating, especially when you're charged with making it by your ailing father whose favorite dessert of all time is pecan pie. So many things can go wrong! I made this recipe for Thanksgiving, and it was glorious! I followed the recipe to the letter, only changing up the crust to an unbaked roll-out one instead because the store was sold out of the unbaked crust in the tin shell. The pie set up perfectly! I agree with a previous review that the secret here is boiling the sugar and corn syrup together. It makes for the perfect pecan pie!

reviews.review_text: This pie definately had the flavor you want in a Pecan Pie. It was delicious. My only advice is this: Make sure you boil the syrup and sugar for a good 3 minutes. Start the timer when it STARTS boiling. I made 2 pies. Same amount of everything, I even baked then at the same time, however 1 pie was a little runny while the other was nice and firm. The runny pie was just as delicious as the other pie though! I just didnt boil the 2nd pie's sugar and syrup as long. SO good and will be a holiday staple in our house for years to come. Thanks!

reviews.review_text: I've never made a pecan pie before so I don't really have anything to compare to besides store-bought pies, but this was good and I was quite pleased with the results! It was easy to make and it cooked up nicely, with the filling setting perfectly - it wasn't runny at all! I cooked it probably about ten minutes longer because I wasn't sure if the filling had set or not, and then I was afraid that I'd overcooked the pie, but it ended up being just right. I used 2 cups of pecan pieces as others suggested, but I think I'll scale down to one and a half cups next time because there was almost too much filling for the crust to handle and we like the gooey part better anyway. I also used both light and dark corn syrups as suggested, but I'll probably just use light next time because we didn't really care for the flavor of the dark. Everyone really liked this though, especially served warm. Thanks for the recipe!

reviews.review_text: Pecan pie is my husband's very favorite pie.  When Thanksgiving rolled around this year, I couldn't find my recipe box so turned to the computer recipes hoping for something that was equal to the pecan pies I have baked for 43 years for him. reviews.review_text: This was excellent, and way better than many pecan pies that end up starchy and tasting like wallpaper paste. Ewwww. Some tips: use the best pecans you can find, it makes a big difference. Buy whole pecans and chop them up (or not, I don't) - whole pecans are often better grade than the ones that got crushed in processing or don't look good and are sold as "chopped pecans". Some changes I made, strictly for my own preferences: I cut the sugar by about 1/3 (like it a bit less sweet than many folks), doubled the vanilla (love vanilla), and added 2 Tbsp. of bourbon (can also use rum). As I say, just some personal prefs, but I know that the recipe exactly as written would also be pretty awesome.

This was my first time making Pecan Pie and it turned out great! I told all my guests they had to give me feed back because I was no expert and a friend who considers himself a connoisseur of pecan pie said this was excellent! It was easy to make and it set up perfectly. My mixture looked very smooth so I did not strain it. The cooktime had me worried. I went 20 minutes over but think I could have gone 15 and been fine, I just didn't want a runny center. I left my pecans whole because it looks nicer but I can see where it would be easier to slice if the pecans are chopped. Very happy I picked this recipe to be my 1st - everyone loved it.

reviews.review_text: Absolutely wonderful taste!  I followed the directions to the T.  I made two of them and took them to my Thanksgiving family gathering.  The problem I had was that they were not completely done -still runny.  I had made them the day before, so they had been in the frige overnight.  My sister, who had made Pecan Pie before told me that you have to always cook Pecan Pies longer than what the recipe calls for.  I imagine another 10 minutes would have helped.  The taste, however, even runny, was unbelievably great, so we still enjoyed them.  I will definitely make this my Pecan Pie recipe for always.
