items.label: Rice Pudding
items.name: Rice Pudding
keywords: c("Lunch/Snacks", "Medium Grain Rice", "Rice", "Low Protein", "Low Cholesterol", "Healthy", "Kid Friendly", "< 60 Mins", "Stove Top", "Easy")
items.description: Make and share this Rice Pudding recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Bring rice, water and salt to a boil over med-high heat.
Simmer covered until water has been absorbed (approximately 15 minutes).
Stir in milk and sugar and cook uncovered over medium heat for 30-40 minutes, stirring frequently--especially towards the end of cooking.
The pudding is done when the rice and milk have amalgamated into a thick porridge-like consistency.
DO NOT OVERCOOK or the pudding will be solid instead of creamy once cooled.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla.
Turn into a bowl or cups.
You can sprinkle cinnamon on the top if you like.
COVER with plastic wrap directly on surface \
you don't want a skin.
COOL.

reviews.review_text: EXCELLENT! My daughters said this was the best rice pudding they've ever eaten. I did, however, make some changes. Here goes. I used short grain brown rice and whole, raw milk from the farm. Instead of white sugar, I used coconut sugar. Using short grain brown rice, it never really thickened up the way it should do with white rice. So, I added a shy tablespoon of non-GMO corn starch with 1/3 cup milk. That worked well to thicken it up perfectly. We still added the 1/2 tsp vanilla and 5 shakes of cinnamon. DELISH! Thanks so much for the recipe that will now go into our PERMANENT FAMILY FAVORITES!

attributes.source_text: My daughters said this was the best rice pudding they've ever eaten

reviews.review_text:
Amazing! I ended up using 1 cup rice and added a 1/3 cup of coconut milk (leftover from making curry for dinner). I also added raisins towards the last 10 mins, which helped to plump them up. I served this warm, with cinnamon sprinkled on top. 
I also kept this on the stove at a low heat and only stirred occasionally (because I was eating my curry dinner). I also omit the vanilla extract because I did not have any left (but I'm sure it would have been a little better with it, but still tasted wonderful without it). I also added 3/4 cup sugar as recommended from other reviewers. 
My mom suggested that I add more rice next time because she wants her rice pudding to have more rice, but I think it's fine as is. But if you add another 1/2 cup to the recipe, it would probably still come out just as creamy.
thank you for sharing an easy recipe!

This is soooooooo good.The only change I made (based on other reviews) was to increase sugar to 3/4 c and added 1 tsp vanilla instead of 1/2 tsp, which I added along with the milk and sugar. I didn't set my timer until the milk/rice came up to a soft simmer. Then I set the timer for 30 min. I probably added about another min while I was trying to decide whether or not to take it off the heat, because it seemed quite soupy. I took it off, and now it's cooling in the pan on the stove, and it has thickened up beautifully. I know because I can't keep my spoon out of it. Thanks for a great recipe

attributes.source_text: it has thickened up beautifully

reviews.review_text: I have had Rice Pudding twice before and thought it was about time I made it at home. I took the suggestions of other reviewers and used 3/4 cup raisins, 1/4 tsp cinnamon and about 8 grinds of fresh nutmeg. Rice Pudding, to me should have a very delicate taste and I think I used a very heavy hand to it! So next time I make it (and I will) I will use 1/2 cup sugar (you don't need it any sweeter unless you have an extreme sweet tooth), 2 cups of half and half, 2 cups of 1% milk... leave out the cinnamon and maybe use 3 - 4 grinds of fresh nutmeg just to give a hint of the taste. The way it was presented to me before was one had raw brown sugar sprinkled over it and the second presentation was with a wonderful rhubarb compote. Both were equally tasty. Thanks Cheryl for posting!!

Great recipe! I just made a few changes: I used brown rice instead of white to make it a bit healthier and also used low fat (1%) milk instead of whole.  I also took out the salt since some of my family members really do not like to have salt in their sweet dishes. Also, I just cooked the whole dessert with a cinnamon stick in it so I didn't have to sprinkle it on top later; the flavor was already infused in the pudding. Next time, I will use a little bit less sugar since it was a bit sweet for me, but this recipe itself is really a great basic guide to making rice pudding. Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: the flavor was already infused in the pudding

reviews.review_text: I changed the recipe slighty just so I wouldn't have to go to the store and it was still yummy.  I used brown rice, which made absorbing the water longer (45-50 min, follow the instructions on the package).  Then I put in unwhipped whipping cream (1 cup) and 3 cups 1% milk.  I had to increase the cooking time to closer to an hour instead of 30-40 min.  We cooled it for about an hour or so and ate it kind of warm and it was soooo delicious.  The next day, after it had been in the fridge, it was still really good, but the rice was a little more grainy than white rice.

I am the Poster Child for "Not Reading Directions" ... so ... I put everything but the vanilla into the pot all at once (in my defense, though, I was previously reading a recipe where everything went in all at once). I must say this is one of those times where the mistake came out awesome! I doubled the recipe and made a huge ol' pot! I added 1 tsp almond extract and 2 tsps vanilla at the end (yes, I know that's triple, not double! LOL - I love vanilla!). I grated some fresh nutmeg onto my bowl and am currently chowing down! YUM!!!

Delicious!! My father used to make this (we called it Rice Cream) when I was a kid and I never learned how to make it. This is just like what he used to make!! The only changes I made were similar to others.. I've tried it twice so far and the first time I used 3/4 cup of sugar (brown and white mixed) and 1tsp vanilla and sultanas. Second one I used the same vanilla amount and sultanas, plus 1/2 cup of sugar and 1/2 to 1tsp of molasses (you could use treacle or maple syrup I suppose)... was fantastic!

This took well over an hour to prepare, which I thought was overlong--but then this was my first attempt at rice pudding, so maybe the long cook time is normal.  I loved the consistency and the creaminess (I used 1% milk)and I liked that the recipe doesn't require eggs.  I increased the sugar to a little less than 3/4 cup and added 1/2 cup raisins with the milk.  I think a good variation might be to add 1/2 chocolate chips to melt in.  I plan to try that next time.

attributes.source_text: I loved the consistency and the creaminess

reviews.review_text: I made a quarter of a recipe because I only wanted enough for myself. I cooked for 25 minutes, which must have been too long because I did end up with solid pudding once it had cooled down. I guess that I should have reduced the cooking time even more since I was making a smaller recipe. However, I will probably try this again with a shorter cooking time because I really did love the flavour of this and it's exactly what I want in a rice pudding (no eggs, etc.). The only other change I made was to use skim milk.

I made this with brown rice and skim milk, plus I cut the sugar to 1/4 cup and added 1/4 cup of craisins.  It took longer to cook than I the recipe said probably because of my changes but it was delicious and my husband loved it.  I thought it was great too.  I love rice pudding and while this was pretty time consuming because I had to stand at the stove because I was afraid the milk would burn the end product was very nice.  I added a teaspoon of cinnamon with the milk plus a touch of grated nutmeg.

attributes.source_text: my husband loved it

reviews.review_text: Made this today as I was hungry for rice pudding - I added about a teaspoon of butter to the rice when cooking to keep it from bubbling up.  I used SuperSkim milk (tastes like whole but no fat), added raisins and cinnamon when I added the milk and didn't measure the vanilla (so I probably used more than 1/2 teaspoon).  The amount of sugar was perfect - it is plenty sweet enough for me.  Next time I may stop cooking it when it is a little runnier - mine thickened up a little too thick.  Great low fat dessert.

attributes.source_text: it is plenty sweet enough for me
Great low fat dessert

reviews.review_text: Oh my, my, this was a little bowl of heaven!  I also used already cooked rice (to use it up) and I halved the recipe.  I added a really generous helping of raisins, cooked it on med-low heat and it still took the full 40 minutes to really come together.  It was all worth it in the end though, that's for sure!  I can't decide if it's better warm or cold, it's just perfect either way!  Thanks for an amazing comfort food.  Shh...I think this turned out even better than my mom's:).

Such a sweet treat! I measured out the rice, water, and milk, but eyed the other ingredients, and it turned out wonderfully. I also added a few dashes of nutmeg, and while I'm not fond of raisins, some of my siblings like to put them in their rice pudding. I usually make rice pudding the fast, lazy way-- adding cold milk, sugar and cinnamon to cooked rice and eating it straight-- but I felt like putting in the time, and it was well worth the extra effort! A perfect dish for a cold winter night.

attributes.source_text: Such a sweet treat!
A perfect dish for a cold winter night

reviews.review_text: Yum! My first rice pudding and it turned out great. I boiled the rice, salt & water for about 15min uncovered until it was thick and the water was gone. I added 4 C milk & 3/4 cup sugar and stirred at a boil for 30 min and turned off the heat and added 1 tsp vanilla and a shake of cinnamon. It was too sweet for me so I'll reduce sugar next time and maybe lessen the vanilla but my boyfriend and son loved it how I made it. Thanks for the recipe Cheryl.

attributes.source_text: my boyfriend and son loved it
my boyfriend and son loved it

reviews.review_text: YUM YUM YUM...this is OUTRAGEOUS!!  I have been craving rice pudding, but in the past my rice puddings have tasted so eggy.  This was perfect, my only complaint was that staring at it didn't make it cook any faster!! (LOL!)  I used 1 can of evaporated milk and the rest was 2%, also, I accidently added the vanilla & a few sprinkles of cinnamon when I added the milk, but I don't think it mattered...ate a bowl while still hot!  Did I mention...YUM??

Best rice pudding recipe ever!!! My goal was to find a recipe that was as good as Kozy Shack (which is all natural & very delicious). This recipe, (with some adjustments I made) surpassed my goal! The 1st time I made it, I added one egg beaten with a little heavy cream at the same time as I added 4 cups of whole milk & I stirred in a pat of butter at the end too. I cooked it for about 30 minutes & I took it off the heat when it was still a little more liquidy than I thought it should be because the recipe warns not to overcook in big letters & I got scared LOL. It was very delish the 1st time, just not quite as thick as I like it, but it was still nice & pudding-y. The sweetness was perfect with 1/2 cup sugar too. The 2nd time I made it, I used 1 cup rice instead of 3/4 (so it took more water to cook the rice), I used mostly 2% milk with a little whole milk (cuz that's what I had on hand) & I used 2 eggs beaten with about 1/4 cup of heavy cream. I used 3/4 c sugar this time since I increased the rice & heavy cream. I also added the butter at the beginning when I was cooking the rice, instead of stirring it in at the end to help the flavor cook into the rice more. Oh & I doubled the vanilla too. I also cooked it for longer by not starting to time the 30 min. until the milk & everything started simmering. Well it was absolute perfection the 2nd time! I always sprinkle cinnamon on the top. After it chills in the fridge, it is the most delicious--even better than Kozy Shack! I use medium grain white rice, called Calrose to make this, which makes a creamier pudding than long grain rice. This is definitely my go to rice pudding recipe with the adjustments I made! I think adding eggs makes it tastier, but it’s still good without them.

attributes.source_text: The sweetness was perfect
makes a creamier pudding

reviews.review_text: This is a very good rice pudding!  At first I thought it was just o.k. But I did use 1% milk so if that was the case it's not fair to give a bad rating if you didn't follow the recipe the way it was written. My DH said it was good though.  I thought it needed more suger. But after letting it sit overnight in the fridge..OMG!! Amazing!! It was perfect, creamy, and the flavors all came together..no need for any more suger.  Can't wait for him to try it now!  We will be having this again for dessert tonight !!! Thx for posting!

attributes.source_text: My DH said it was good though
It was perfect, creamy
We will be having this again for dessert tonight

reviews.review_text: So easy to put to together, my fiance liked it.  I had  some leftover rice from another meal, so I used that instead of cooking it fresh.  I  added the milk, sugar, and leftover rice, let it cook about 25 minutes, then added cinnamon, vanilla, and some raisins, because he likes it with raisins.  It cooled in the pan about 20 min before it was refrigerated, just to make sure it would thicken up.  Will save make again, he liked it, I did not taste it as I am not a rice pudding fan, but worth the effort for those who like this.

attributes.source_text: my fiance liked it
he liked it

items.label: Hummus
items.name: Hummus
items.description: Make and share this Hummus recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Drain beans and reserve the liquid when you do so.
Blend beans, along with the other ingredients and 1/4 cup of the liquid.
Process until the mixture is smooth.
Add liquid until the desired consistency is reached.
Adjust seasonings alongwith more cumin, lemon juice, salt and pepper.

reviews.review_text: I can make this in under 10 minutes now, including licking out the blender. I like to use ground white pepper to avoid little black specks and prefer copying expensive gourmet hummus flavors such as sundried tomato and artichoke heart. If you gave up eating sundried tomatoes during the recession as I did, you may not have tried an innovation I bought recently (and which works great in this hummus recipe). They are neither the crispy sort nor the soaked-in-oil sort, but rather a soft dried sliced tomato in a pouch. Try using five slices to start. I bought mine at Sprouts (a New Mexico healthy grocery), but the gal in the check-out line at Trader Joe's said they carry something similar. Yum.

attributes.source_text: sundried tomato and artichoke heart
sundried tomato and artichoke heart

reviews.review_text: I used to use a hummus recipe that let people know you had some garlic hummus for hours after just tasting it (we're talking like 5 cloves of garlic minced.. raw).  This is a wonderful recipe that makes things much more mild and pleasant!  These are the general ingredients, so it is the proportions that matter.  I took the advice of others and sauteed the garlic and cumin in a little evoo.  I halved the recipe, but still used 1/4 cup of reserved chick pea liquid to make it very smooth.  This is delicious and definitely recommended for all.  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: makes things much more mild and pleasant
to make it very smooth

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe before I read the other comments!!!!  People found three garlic not enough???  I found it a bit on the heavy side!!  I love garlic, but I find too much raw garlic burns my lips and does a number on the gut!!  I wonder if roasted garlic would suit me better??  Comments, anyone??  I thought the 1/2 cup tahini made the dish!!   Next time, I would cut the garlic down to 2 and thin the hummus out with about 3 T water...then this would become a 5 star dish for me!!!  Loved this with veggies and as a sandwich spread!!  Kudos on the posting!!

My brother raves about hummus, but it wasn't until I wanted to make a batch for my students that I wanted to try it! This was perfect. I served a little dallop for each brave taste-tester in a mini pita cut in half (from Whole Foods Market). I did have quite a bit more leftover, and so ate it by myself. I found I prefer it on flat pretzels. I'm getting ready to make 1/2 a batch for a party and I wouldn't mind leftovers at all! Great recipe!! Update - made it again this year and a parent (who owns a restaurant) called to tell me their daughter said it was the best she'd ever had...and she's had a lot! :)

Update 2012 - I made this for my neighbor...I had the beans in the blender when I realized I only had key lime juice. Not a bad substitution. We'll see what she thinks :)

attributes.source_text: I wanted to make a batch for my students
their daughter said it was the best she'd ever had
I made this for my neighbor

reviews.review_text: I LOVE this recipe. It's one of my favorites. I make it at least once or twice a month. After scooping my finished hummus into a container, I use a spoon to form a little crater in it and then pour good quality olive oil into the crater and over the top of it, and sprinkle a little more salt. Mmmmmmm. So delicious!! I like to make it for potlucks and serve it with fresh cut up Japanese cucumbers, red bell peppers, celery and baby tomato. It's always a huge hit! Healthy, visually appealing, and so delicious.

attributes.source_text: I like to make it for potlucks

reviews.review_text:
Very tasty!  We'd only had the boxed version (yuck) once before a trip to a middle eastern restaurant in Detroit over Christmas break.  This recipe was very good, especially after it set in the refrigerator for a couple of days.  We used the bottled lemon juice instead of freshly-squeezed and had to add an extra tablespoon to get the right level of tart.  Beyond that, we followed the recipe exactly.

Next time we might add a touch of cayenne - or just make as-is.  I didn't think I'd like hummus after trying the box mix, but this is a keeper.

attributes.source_text: to get the right level of tart

reviews.review_text: I've tried and been left disappointed by many hummus recipes on the web. This one tastes just like the one I enjoy at my favorite Lebanese restaurant. The ingredients are well balanced and has fewer calories without the oil. I serve the hummus topped with a little bit of ground cumin, a dash red pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil.  Make sure though you use pressed garlic. I used minced the first time I made it and it overpowered the other flavors. This tastes best after refrigerating it for a day.

attributes.source_text: tastes just like the one I enjoy at my favorite Lebanese restaurant

reviews.review_text: Wonderful.  Great way to SAVE $$$! Even using tahini, it costs only a 1/3 of store made.  And I am able to adjust the flavors and experiment with spices. I've made it with peanut butter and while it was good, it doesn't quite hit the spot like tahini.  Making 1/2 recipe, I used 1 can beans, 3 TBSP lemon juice, 2 garlic cloves, 1/2 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp chipotle lime seasoning and 1 tsp red pepper oil - and 6 TBSP of the reserved liquid from the beans. Perfect - with a little bite. Enjoy and have fun mixing it up to suit your taste!

attributes.source_text: with a little bite

reviews.review_text: I thought this recipe was good; however, I found there to be too much tahini for my liking. I wish I had started off by putting less, because I found the taste to be overwhelming in the finished product. I also thought it was missing flavor, so I added more garlic (an additional 2 cloves) more lemon juice (about 3 tablespoons), and some cilantro to kick it up. I also had to add much more chick pea water than suggested. To one batch, I added siracha sauce, which was a pleasant kick. I was hoping for something that would blow Sabra out of the water. Perhaps I will try this again with half the tahini and then go from there, because this recipe has potential.

Thank you!  I am currently living in China and was excited when I found imported canned garbanzo beans.  That meant I needed to find a good hummus recipe--and I'm so glad I did.  I had to use sesame seeds (tahini is definitely not available here) and thought that it was a great tip from another reviewer.  I did add a bit of olive oil, but otherwise left the recipe alone.  It was the perfect hummus.  My five year old son loves it too, and he never liked hummus from stores or restaurants back home.

attributes.source_text: My five year old son loves it too

reviews.review_text: I do believe this is the most fantastic hummus I've ever tasted! I used less tahini than called for, though I'm not sure how much. I used whatever was left in my jar, but it didn't look like a full 1/2 cup left. I like a little less tahini in mine anyway, so it all worked out. I also roasted a head of garlic like some others and used that because I love garlic. I added quite a bit of bean juice because I like my hummus very smooth, and whipped it all up in my blender. Thanks for sharing!

attributes.source_text: I like my hummus very smooth

reviews.review_text: This is a good base recipe that I think I will keep tweaking until it tastes like my favorite store bought stuff.  Instead of raw garlic I added roasted garlic but think I will add some of each next time since I needed more of a sharpness to it.  This was my first time making hummus successfully though and I thank you greatly for that.  I did half the recipe and it still made a good amount.  Can't wait to play around with it some more :)

This was amazingly simple and delicious!
I did tweaked the recipe by adding only two cloves of garlic,( figuring I could add more later). a teaspoon of olive oil, some niÃ§oise olives and
2 tablespoons of the niÃ§oise olive juice. Added the juice from one lemon. Mixed between adding each ingredient like another review suggested and this was so creamy and smooth 
it can easily be used as a sandwich spread with grilled veggies on a crusty roll.

attributes.source_text: this was so creamy
and smooth

reviews.review_text: I’m giving this 4 stars because it’s a lovely hummus base. I found it a little bland as is, but added more lemon juice, more cumin, more garlic (initial garlic was fresh, added about another clove’s worth of jarred), a little chili powder, some cayenne, some parsley, and lots of salt and pepper - then I thought it was fantastic! As others did, I used olive oil to thin it out rather than the liquid from the beans. I don’t care for the flavor of that liquid. Thank you for the basic recipe, though. I can tell that it will be versatile!

I have made this several times. The recipe is quite delicious. A good, basic hummus. I have found that adding a little olive oil evens out the consistency. Makes it almost silky. And, if the tahini is a bit too much for your tastes, just cut it back a bit. I was craving hummus today, and found a PERFECT recipe at Mixing Bowl. It was absolutely amazing. Check it out if you want to try a little something new -- it's called "Spicy Hummus." ENJOY!

attributes.source_text: Makes it almost silky

reviews.review_text: A variation of this recipe was passed down to me from my Lebanese-Canadian mother.  Instead of thinning it out with water we use a good quality light extra virgin olive oil, it gives the hummus a smooth, creamier texture.  I use 1 tablespoon of tahini to one can of chick peas otherwise the tahini flavour is too overpowering, and no cumin, just lots of lemon juice and minced garlic does the trick, and then garnish with a sprinkle of paprika and a sprig of parsley!

attributes.source_text: it gives the hummus a smooth, creamier texture
it gives the hummus a smooth, creamier texture

items.label: Deviled Eggs
items.name: Deviled Eggs
items.description: This recipe was my Mother's and she taught me to make them. My sons and their families always request these eggs for all family get-together dinners.
instructions: Peel shells off cooled hard-boiled eggs; slice into halves lengthwise.
Remove yolks from whites and place in a small round bowl.
Mash yolks with a fork into fine pieces.
Add 2 heaping tablespoons Mayonnaise, yellow mustard, diced gherkins and finely chopped jalapeno (seeds removed), and salt and black pepper to taste.
Stir mixture until creamy.
Spoon mixture into a zip-lock sandwich bag; seal bag and snip off one corner of the bag.
Squeeze mixture out of corner of bag into egg white halves.
Sprinkle tops of filled deviled eggs with paprika.
Chill in refrigerator 1 to 2 hours or until cold before serving.

reviews.review_text: My favorites! An excellent basic deviled egg. You can add bacon, shrimp, chives, crabmeat and pimento but I don't cause to me, these are perfection! Except with Hellmann's mayo and 1 1/2 T sweet relish, 1/8 t salt. Here are some great tips on cooking and peeling eggs that I found in Southern Living: Place eggs in a single layer in saucepan; add water to depth of 3 inches. Bring to a boil; cover, remove from heat and let stand 15 minutes. Pour off water. Add about 1 inch cold water and several ice cubes to the still warm eggs in the saucepan. Cover pot and shake vigorously so the eggs will crack all over. Peel under cold running water, starting at the large end, the air pocket there will give you something to grip. Thanks, Nurslinda, these are awesome!

House Rule:  There shall be NO Miracle Whip in my house.  The Miraculous thing about Miracle Whip is that anyone buys it.  For vile taste, it is unsurpassed.<br/>I made Deviled Eggs last night, just winging it.  Did the egg thing and took the yolks to a bowl.  Mashed them.  Added Hellman's Mayonaisse, just a bit.  Added celery salt, McCormick's Salt-Free Spices, Herbs de Provence, a bit of Paprika and some dark Chili Powder.  Also Cayenne to taste and a good helping of Turmeric powder.  Mixed thoroughly.  Added some more mayonaisse to moisten.  Mixed.  Took a spoon and scooped the yolk mix into the whites' cavities.  Patted down with finger to remove spaces.  This is necessary to get the maximum amount of this mix back into the whites.  The reason is that it is so delicious that you don't want to waste any space on air.  Sprinkled a bit of dark chili powder (my paprika was so old it was black and tasteless) on top and served.  Also, with the Turmeric added, these were also healthy and allegedly will prevent cancer.  Best of all possible worlds!

Thanks for posting this great recipe = ) This is my standard too, except for the jalapenos..... Dukes MAYO here... no miracle whip for us. My sisters and brothers in law always ask for Jane to make the deviled eggs! lol The one thing i do differently to make the filling fluffy is use my food processor. Pulse the dry yolks until crumbly after cooling to room temperature. (Never use boiled eggs from the refrigerator, or you can get lumps in your finished product.) Then add the rest of your ingredients and pulse until creamy. Put the yolk mixture in a Zippy and cut off a corner to fill the whites. Garnish with olives or crumbled bacon and paprika. Sit back and watch them disappear! lol

attributes.source_text: to make the filling fluffy
pulse until creamy
My sisters and brothers in law always ask for Jane to make the deviled eggs
My sisters and brothers in law always ask for Jane to make the deviled eggs

reviews.review_text: Delicious deviled eggs. Made the recipe exactly as written. It is very close to my own deviled egg recipe except I usually add 1 teaspoon horseradish to give the eggs a little zing, and I use a little more Miracle Whip. I use an empty egg carton (lined with plastic wrap if it is cardboard carton) to transport my deviled eggs to a party then transfer them to a lettuce-lined serving plate. Thanks for posting. Made these again and cut the cooked eggs in half the way they stand in the egg carton; they fit better in the egg carton for transporting.

attributes.source_text: transport my deviled eggs to a party

reviews.review_text: This is a very basic deviled egg recipe, if you pronounced it delicious after altering it to suit your taste you are not reviewing it as written.  Myself I would add a few drops of Franks hot sauce and use powdered dry mustard.  The basic recipe as given would make a perfectly passable egg. Miracle Whip haters you are not the authority on what the rest of the world likes, it and Mayo are both in my fridge, there is a use for both. Mixed in some applications the Whip adds a zing and Mayo tones the Whip's unique flavor. Actually I like bread with nothing but Miracle Whip now and then.

My grandmother taught me her recipe.  We use Hellman's real mayo in our house.  Its way less sweet and has no HFCS.  Next we are purists and take no shortcuts like this recipe does.  First of all, you get a quality gherkin instead of relish.  My favorie is the German imported gherkins from World Market.  You do the basic prep the same exept you chop up the gherkins to tiny pieces.  Mix the cooked yoke with mayo, mustard, and the gherkins.  Sprinkle with some paprika.  Cut a large olive in two and place a half on the top.  Now its a gourmet egg.

NurseLinda,
Thanks for posting. I had to change a couple ingredients only because I'm the type that if I am out I want grab that one thing at grocery store. So I used Ranch Dressing and Chipotle Mayo, didn't have sweet relish so I used dill spears and olives chopped up fine. But everything else I used. Will get mayo next store visit and dill and sweet relish, my substitutions were okay have a feeling the "original" will even be better.

These were really good. They did seem to have a lot of relish, but I like relish so I am not complaining! I just made them for myself, but I think if I were to make them for guests I would reduce the amount of relish to 1 1/2 tbsp. I didn't have paprika so I left it out and it didn't seem to make a difference except for that they didn't look as pretty. If you need a certain number of deviled eggs you may want to add a few extra in when you boil because 2 of my eggs broke open while they were boiling.

This is how my mom taught me to make deviled eggs as a kid! We always made them with our leftover colored Easter eggs. I haven't made them in years, so I looked on Recipezaar for a reminder on how to do it, and I'm glad I found this recipe. Mom never actually measured the ingredients, it was a squirt of mustard, a blob of relish, etc. It's ok to get all fancy with them if you want, but this is the canonical recipe, as far as I'm concerned.

Had an abundance of eggs to use up and a taste for deviled eggs we hadn't had for a while.  These really hit the spot, lovely and easy! I used 1 tablespoon of red hot pepper relish and 1 tablespoon of regular sweet pickle relish, nice combination and it gave them a little bite. Love the idea of pushing the mix through a corner of a plastic bag, worked perfectly.
Thanks for sharing a good one we will probably make again!!

attributes.source_text: it gave them a little bite

reviews.review_text: I doubled the recipe to serve at a birthday bbq supper, none leftover. The only thing I wondered about is it says 3 tbsps. miracle whip in the recipe and 2 tbsps. in the directions? I did not catch it in the directions until afterwards, which I re-read cause I did wonder if the filling could have been just a little firmer than it was. So, for that reason I will try going with the two tbsps. next time. The taste was right on though and they were enjoyed, Thanks!

attributes.source_text: to serve at a birthday bbq supper
to serve at a birthday bbq supper
to serve at a birthday bbq supper

reviews.review_text: Made these devilishly good morsels of wonderfulness for a St Patty's potluck; yes, I added 4-5 drops of green food coloring and the crowd was *wild* about them!! As for the delectable taste, because I doubled the recipe, I actually used 2 Tbs low-fat sourcream and 2 Tbs (regular) mayonnaise. I had neither the jalapeno (tragedy for a NM native!) nor any gherkins, but used 2Tbs dill pickle relish. Great substitute! Added no salt or pepper---garnished with a very small amount of chopped parsley to go with the St. Patrick's theme. Indeed, this recipe is a keeper!

attributes.source_text: for a St Patty's potluck
for a St Patty's potluck

reviews.review_text: This is my 'secret' family recipe that everyone loves and people beg me to make!  My mom taught me this recipe years ago and I've tweaked it a little bit. 1. I use two types of mustard - yellow and either spicy brown or dijon, whatever I have on hand, and I use equal amounts of each.  2. I also add just a little bit of sugar - about a teaspoon if I'm making 12 whole eggs.  I get rave reviews on these.  My boyfriend's boss used to sign him up for deviled eggs every time they had a pot luck so I would make them :)

attributes.source_text: every time they had a pot luck

reviews.review_text: When I first saw this recipe I was a bit turned off because of the relish, and my family had never had Deviled Eggs made that way. I decided to give it a try though, as it was my first time making Deviled Eggs. I upped the recipe for 32 eggs, because I was making them for a family get together. I was so pleased to see that everyone had finished all of my Deviled Eggs and my Aunt's were not even a fourth gone! They are really sweet and have a great zing to them, that's not too strong. I myself added a bit more mustard, because I couldn't taste it enough for my preference. I will definatly be making these again. Thanks so much for the recipe!

attributes.source_text: I was making them for a family get together
They are really sweet

items.description: This recipe is very easy to put together and takes practically no time to make. Try other flavors of cake mixes if you like. When I make them, I use 2 cups (total) of peanut butter chips and chocolate chips mixed together. Very easy to whip up at halftime!
instructions: Combine cake mix, oil and eggs in a bowl and mix well.
Stir in chips and nuts, if using.
Drop by teaspoons on ungreased cookie sheet and bake at 350 degrees for 8-10 minutes.
Upon removing from oven, let the cookies stand on sheet for two minutes, then cool on racks.

reviews.review_text: My 15 YO son made these cookies for an after school snack today with a chocolate cake mix, chocolate chips, and butterscotch chips.  Our oven is so small that baking traditional round cookies takes a really long time because we can put in only one cookie sheet at a time.  Therefore, we always make bar cookies. DS prepared the batter as directed and then proceeded as we bake bar cookies: 1. Spray a 9 X 13 metal baking pan with vegetable cooking spray. 2. Pour prepared batter into greased pan. 3. Bake 20 minutes. 4. Let cool in pan for 10 minutes. 5. Cut into square--we got 32 cookies. Other DS has requested strawberry cake mix cookies for the near future. Thanks for a great recipe.

attributes.source_text: for an after school snack

reviews.review_text: After spending all these years looking for a perfect cookie recipe I never would have thought that I will find one from boxed cake mix!  The cookies wore soft, and delicious!  I made two batches one of chocolate with white chips and one of with butter caked mix and regular chocolate chips, each one received rave revues.  When I first mixed them I was a little concerned about the outcome as the batter seemed very greasy, but the baked beautifully although I did shorten the baking time just a bit.  Even people that are in the catering business wore raving about how good they wore!  Everyone was asking for the recipe but I just could not bring myself to tell anyone how easy they are to make!  I would give this cookie 10 stars if I could!

attributes.source_text: The cookies wore soft

reviews.review_text: What a blast from the past. Many years ago, I was in the Panama Canal Zone working at a hospital and needed to come up with a batch of cookies. All I had was a box of Devil's Food cake mix, mini choc chips and some walnuts. I added 2 eggs, 1/4 c oil and 1/4 cup water. Saw that it was the right texture. Added 1 c mini chips and 1/2 c finely chopped nuts. I always bake my cookies on parchment paper and easily remove them from the hot pan after they come out of the oven by slipping them onto the counter so they don't over cook. It was an easy treat with simple ingredients. Thanks for reminding me of an old memory.

THANK YOU BOTH, LORAC & LINDA!!! I never would have tried a cake-mix cookie on my own, but after reading Lorac's thread about the killer chocolate-orange combo, I had to give it a shot. These were wonderful! I used orange cake mix, and (as I was out of chips) 2 cut-up Ritt milk chocolate bars. Heavenly tasting, wonderfully textured, and not a single person I served them to suspected they came from a box. A real winner, especially considering how easily and quickly they came together! Thank you very much! UPDATE: I've made these yet again. Half a batch the chocolate-orange, and the other half a devil's food with white chocolate chunks & almond bits. Mmm. I even made a few of the cookies yin-yang style and they looked superb and were really just the best of both worlds. Thanks again, you've made some quite happy people here! (posted 5/20/2002)UPDATE AGAIN!!  Made a fresh batch with spice cake mix and cinnamon chips.  What a great and different cookie!  I think these would do smashingly as a holiday 'gift' cookie with a little bit of cream cheese icing on top.

attributes.source_text: the killer chocolate-orange combo

reviews.review_text: I've made this quite a few times with various cake mixes and add-ins, as other reviewers have done. But my favorite way is to make ice cream sandwiches! I double the recipe and pour into two 9x13 greased pans. When cool, I remove them from the pans and put plastic wrap in one of the pans (with some extending over the top on all 4 sides) and the put one back in the pan over the plastic wrap (for easy removal later). I then cut ice cream into 1/2 inch slices (ice cream from the rectangle boxes with the sides pulled down) and put the slices over the cake I placed back into the pan.. I then take the second cake and put on top of the ice cream layer. Then place plastic wrap over all of it. Freeze until the ice cream is frozen. Remove from the pan and cut into rectangles similar to ice cream bars you buy from the store. Wrap each in plastic wrap  and put into freezer bag. Place back into the freezer. We love these ice cream sandwiches. I even made one as a cake for a graduation cake for my son's friend. He loved it! Try it, you'll love it! I give this recipe 5 stars, but it's worth more. ;) I forgot to say that I made these into Snicherdoodles by rolling balls of dough into sugar and cinnamon. Very good!

items.name: World's Best Cinnamon Raisin Bread (Not Bread Machine)
keywords: c("Breads", "Breakfast", "Grains", "Toddler Friendly", "Healthy", "Kid Friendly", "Winter", "Brunch", "For Large Groups", "Oven", "< 4 Hours")
items.description: This is the best Cinnamon Raisin Bread I've ever had! It really has a great consistency and smells WONDERFUL while baking. I made this for the first time about a year ago and since it makes 3 loaves, I gave one to my neighbor. Now she asks for it constantly and since it is so fun to make, I oblige her, plus I get to keep the other 2 loaves!
instructions: Warm the milk in a small sauce pan on the stove until it just starts to bubble, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat.
Let cool until lukewarm, about 120-125 degrees.

Dissolve yeast in warm water and set aside until yeast is frothy, about 10 minutes or so (make sure your water is at the correct temperature or the yeast won't activate.) Then mix in eggs, sugar, butter salt and raisins (stir in the cooled milk slowly so you don't cook the eggs.) Add the flour gradually to make a stiff dough.
Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for a few minutes until smooth.
Place in a large, buttered, mixing bowl and turn to grease the surface of the dough.

Cover with a warm, damp cloth and let rise (I like to let my bread rise in the oven with the light on. It has just the right amount of heat and keeps the bread out of drafts.) Allow to rise until doubled, usually about 1 1/2 hours.
Roll out on a lightly floured surface into a large rectangle 1/2 inch thick.
Moisten the dough with 2 tablespoons milk and rub all over the dough with your hands.
Mix together 1 cup of sugar and 3 tablespoons cinnamon and sprinkle mixture evenly on top of the moistened dough.
Roll up tightly (the long way).
The roll should be about 3 inches in diameter.
Cut into thirds, and tuck under ends and pinch bottom together.
Place loaves into well greased (you can use Crisco or butter for this) 9 x 5 inch pans and lightly grease tops of loaves.
Let rise in warm place, uncovered, again for about an hour.
Bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes or until loaves are lightly browned and sound hollow when tapped.
Remove from oven and let cool on rack.
Take melted butter and spread over tops of loaves.
After about 20 minutes, lay loaves on their sides and remove from pans.
Allow to cool before slicing.

reviews.review_text: Read the directions all the way through before attempting. The directions are somewhat ambiguous. The recipe doesn't say when to ad the yeast. It says to ad yeast to warm water and set aside. Then it says to ad in the sugar eggs, salt, etc. Well the recipe calls to ad sugar at 2 different places in the recipe 1/2cup and 1 cup...I mixed the 1 cup of sugar into the dough, when actually it should have been the 1/2 cup of sugar... Hope it doesn't matter too much...the dough after mixing was quite runny. I added a little bit more flour to stiffen it up. The dough is rising now. I hope it turns out...???? This my first attempt at bread making. I've heard that the most accurate way of measuring ingredients is to weigh them. I weighed my flour at 127g per cup. That may be why I gad to ad more flour. Important ingredients like flour should be measured by weight not by volume as in a measuring cup because it can be compacted so much...after readjng the tweaks section, I'm not the only person who had to ad more flour to the recipe...and the recipe seems to be lretty flexible about the ingredients and which is good...

I made this bread today, and it is amazing! I read all the reviews, and I did make some additions based on the helpful suggestions of others: I added 1 Tablespoon of sugar to the water that the yeast was proofing in, and I also added 1/4 c. white sugar, 1 Tablespoon cinnamon, and 1/2 tsp. salt to the dough. I also added 2 cups of raisins to the overall recipe (so there are 3 c. TOTAL), and put half of them (1 1/2 c.) in the dough, and half of them in the filling. I was a little worried that the chunks of softened butter would screw up the dough, but they were fine, and it didn't matter that they were all chunky before I put the flour in. I guess the kneading took care of them. It took me about 9 cups of flour to have a dough that was manageable. I also changed the filling a bit. I used 2/3 c. brown sugar (packed), 2/3 c. white sugar, 1/4 c. cinnamon, and I mixed it all together and sprinkled 1/3 of it in each loaf with the remaining raisins. The baking temperature was right on, and my loaves were done in 30 minutes. I'm sorry I messed with your recipe so much, but thanks so much for posting it! I am SO glad I took the time to try it and for all the others who have tried it and made the suggestions that made mine such a success. Thank you Lydia. :)

Absolutely scrumptious- this cinnamon raisin bread turned out beautifully! After comparing a number of different recipes, I decided to give this one a try and I couldn't have been happier with the results. The loaves were fluffy, moist, and flavorful, and an intoxicating aroma filled my home not only during the baking process, but also every time a slice hit the toaster this week. I did make a few minor adjustments that I think made a positive difference to the final product: I added 1 T of sugar to my water/yeast mixture to help it proof. I increased the salt an extra 1/2 tsp (totaling 1 1/2 tsp) and increased the raisins an extra 2 cups (totaling 3 cups- I wanted to have 1 cup per loaf. At first, I was worried it would be too much, but in the end it turned out just right! Be on the lookout for extra moist raisins specially made for baking- I found them at my supermarket and they worked out great- if you can't find them, you can always plump your raisins in hot water for a few minutes before you add them!) Instead of 2 T of milk to wash the dough, I did 1 T milk + 1 T melted butter. I'd also recommend separating your dough into 3 parts before you start rolling- it made it so much easier to handle, and allowed me to form each loaf with a nice tight swirl. Just sprinkle about 1/3 cup of the cinnamon sugar mixture in each loaf to make sure it comes out evenly distributed. Lastly, my loaves were  perfectly golden and ready to come out at 35 minutes (10 minutes shy of the 45 minutes in the stated recipe.) I hope these suggestions help! Lydia, thank you so much for this fantastic recipe- my family simply loved it!

reviews.review_text: I made this bread as have many others. A lot of respondents have noted they altered the recipe following recommendations of others. I only made minor alterations: adding 1 Tbsp sugar to the water & yeast while it proofed and increasing the raisins & soaking those raisins in the hot water to plump slightly (I used the "plumping water" in the bread so didn't loose any of the sweetness of the raisins by dumping that soaking water down the drain). I did not need an additional cup of flour (many commented needing 9 cups). A slightly "wet" dough is okay because those raisins will absorb some of that moisture. I think many who have not worked with yeast before need to understand that bread is a living thing....you need to learn your particular conditions & ingredients. What works in July may need adjusting in December...heat, humidity, moisture content in flour & other ingredients play a HUGE factor in what your bread does, both while it is being prepared & when it proofs (raises). Additionally, I did not used butter to make the cinnamon-sugar mixture "stick" before rolling. I'm making bread, not cinnamon rolls. I grew up with a less sweet bread when I had cinnamon raisin bread & found this dough to be just sweet enough. It's a good recipe, just tweaked the prep method slightly. Will be using this to make bread pudding very soon. Thanks so much for a sturdy, well behaved dough recipe! I'll use this again repeatedly. I agree with other comments, my dough did raise fast (less than the 90 minutes). I did allow the 2nd raise to be longer (about 2 hours or so). I did not butter it prior to baking. In my oven, 35 minutes was sufficient (again, know your conditions & adjust accordingly). I brushed with melted butter out of the oven. Three beautiful golden loaves (one of which never got cool) with a beautiful dense crumb...some space in the swirl, but I'm okay with that. Will definitely make this again.

attributes.source_text: found this dough to be just sweet enough

reviews.review_text:
Very, very good! Mom was giddy for it while it was baking. We didn't put the loaves into loaf pans, but I will do that next time. Minor adjustments: I needed to add about another 3/4c-1c flour because the dough was just too sticky to work with. Added 2 additional cups of raisins, a teaspoon of vanilla to the egg, and added an instant mocha coffee mix (about 3 tbsp, heaping) to the cinnamon-sugar mix. Will probably increase the vanilla to 2 tsp next time. I should probably also not let this rise overnight. We ended up with monster loaves that were crawling off the cookie sheets I let them rise on. All in all, DELISH.

edit: my mom had some church friends over and served the bread; they loved it so much they asked to take some home! Also, fixed the rating! Thanks to Kat's Mom for letting me know the stars were missing.  <3

reviews.review_text: This bread is bland. I have made it multiple times, given it to many different people (since 1 batch makes 3 loaves, that is easy to do), and everyone's reaction has been, "thanks, that's nice" but it has not ever gotten the kinds of raves that the other bread I make a lot (a sourdough wheat) gets. It is not hard to make, which is a plus. And you should definitely use the full amount of cinnamon and sugar indicated.l<br/><br/>That said, it DOES make Excellent french toast once it has gotten a few days past its prime! (Yes, the sign of a not great bread - you have enough left over for french toast, ha ha.) Since it is (for all intents and purposes) a very plain white bread with some cinnamon/sugar/raisins in the middle of it, it's just right for french toast.

** Baked in my Instant Omni Plus ** I'm a beginner bread baker and my dough always comes out heavy and dense. After reading the reviews, I changed my tactic and added flour until the dough became less sticky- but it still didn't form into a ball in my stand mixer. In my case it was still 7 cups of flour. I had a plan for my 3 loafs, one plain for sandwiches. One regular-sized loaf and 3 mini loafs to give to neighbors. I made the dough per the directions EXCEPT, I kept the raisins out of the dough while being mixed in my stand mixer. Once the dough was done mixing, I made 3 portions and put my plain dough into the loaf pan for its first rise. With the remainder of the dough I added raisins, 2 tablespoons of sugar, 2 teaspoons of cinnamon and a few good shakes of nutmeg and kneaded by hand. Then followed the rest of the directions by rolling out in a rectangle, adding cinnamon sugar mixture and rolling up, etc... By now, you might be wondering, what happened to making ALL the dough go through it's first rise?? ... Well, ROOKIE mistake, I FORGOT... no worries, I Googled it and it said that some breads don't need to rise twice. Psshhhh, it's fine!! (haha I hoped!). I popped them in my Instant Omni Plus - proof feature- and those babies did rise, just like they were supposed to! The plain one did rise faster than the ones with all the sugar in it and the plain one got to rise twice vs the cinnamon ones just got one rise (haha Rookie!!). I baked it in my Instant Omni Plus - Baked - 350 degree for 20 minutes, the tops colored a lot faster than I'd like but I waited until the internal temp was 190 in all spots (some spots where higher). Next time I think I'll decrease the temp to 325 and go for a longer bake time. The result was very nice crusted bread on all sides and a super fluffy, soft springy-to-the-touch inside. Beautiful and very delicious!! The plain one actually tastes like store bought sandwich bread!! And what about the cinnamon ones that only got to rise once?? Well, they actually turned out perfect and I might just omit the 2nd rise for this recipe in the future. Just know that if you're short on time, it will be fine if it only rises once! This recipe is a definite keeper and will go into rotation!!

reviews.review_text:
WOW! This bread definitely lives up to its title! I made it last night and my husband was still raving about it as he was leaving for work this morning. Don't let the long list of directions scare you off-it's really pretty simple if you just take it step-by-step and follow the directions.

I had read that the stickier your dough, the fluffier and moister it will be once baked. I didn't use all 8 cups (about 7 instead) and the dough was still a bit sticky but elastic and in one piece. Loved the tip about letting the bread rise in the oven with the light on- worked perfectly in my old, cold kitchen! How have I not known about this before?? Also, when you roll your rectangle up, I found mine to be approximately 24 inches long (in addition to 3 inches thick) if that helps. I also didn't use the whole cup of sugar, only about 1/2 cup, and we found it to be be plenty sweet.

This is a fantastic recipe and I can't wait to try it, as one reviewer suggested, in bread pudding! Yum!!!

reviews.review_text: Below this is my original review but I wanted to update my review: I've now made this bread at least 25 times, and I've sent others to this site to bake this bread. I really appreciate this recipe being so consistent and want to say thanks to Lydia for posting it. I've been baking bread since I was very young with my Grandma and I'm a very picky baker. I love this bread. I've made some changes-added more salt to bring out the flavors more, increased the flour to make it easier to handle, added more raisins but all in all this recipe is terrific and the texture of the bread is wonderful. I'm off to bake 3 more loaves-always give one away too:-) Thanks again Lydia!!! Ive made this bread 3x's & I"m wondering if anyone else has had this problem with it. First time it turned out nice. 2nd&3rd times,following recipe exactly the same way as the 1st time, I've had to add 1-1.5cups more flour to it to even be able to handle it. I've been baking bread since I was 8 and do it for a living. Is this a recipe that is affected by the vagaries of weather? I just can't figure it out. It has been sooo sticky the last 2 times I've been unable to get it to form a ball cleaning the sides of my KA commercial mixer. Can't figure out why theres been such discrep- ancies between batches. I'm a real stickler for following directions the first couple times I bake a recipe so I get a feel for what it's sposed to be like. Anyone baked this and had the same thing happen? I do like the flavor and when it rises-wow-it heads for the roof of my oven!TIA.

After reading most of the reviews, i felt encouraged to try this recipe.  This recipe was easy to make.  Instead of adding flour gradually, i poured the liquid mix into the flour (8cups)and knead the dough in the bowl, adding a little bit of flour while kneading it.  My dough did not seem to rise (maybe because i let it rise for only 1hour).  I shaped it into loafs and they seem to rise a little bit in the pan.  I was surprised when they came out of the oven in perfect shape.  I don't know if dough rises during baking but mine did.  The bread was soft and delicious.  Two minutes after the breads came out of the oven, my husband and my four young children sliced and ate them.  Thank you Linda for sharing this recipe.  It's a keeper.  A BIG "Thank You" to all of you who  shared your experience with this recipe. If there weren't many of you, i would have missed this delicious treat.

reviews.review_text: I've had an obsession lately with Macdonald's raisin toast so figured I needed to try and make my own, if for no other reason than to save money. I'm new to bread making, but this recipe is so easy and has so many great reviews I figured I'd give it a go. I most definitely need to improve my bread making skills (I haven't yet got the perfect consistency, I think I'm either over proofing or under kneading?) but other than that, this bread is AMAZING. I've made multiple loaves, eaten way too much of it myself and given some away. It is completely delicious on its own, but I've also used it for french toast and to make bread and butter pudding for a family gathering. Rave reviews all round. Will be making this very regularly! I made a few changes after doing my first try - I used more raisins, and added cinnamon to the dough itself for extra flavour. I used melted butter instead of milk to rub over the dough, and also used much less sugar in the filling, as I didn't think it needed so much.

This is by far the best I have seen yet. I have been making 3 loaves at a time and my boys (husband and son) eat everything! I did modify the instructions a little. I add a little bit of sugar into the water for yeast to feed on. Then, I use less flour then the recipe calls, usually untill the dough is still soft and slightly sticky, not hard. I then grease my hands with oil and form the dough into a ball. I let it rise for 1.5 hours in the oven with the light on then knead it and put back in the bowl and stick in the fridge overnight (making sure I knead it one more time before I go to bed, usually in a few hours, otherwise it will run away). The next  morning I take it out, let it stand at room temperature a little (30 min or so) and then form into the loaves. Also, I did not put raisins in the dough until today, I used to put it on top of the sugar/cinnamon mix. I also use butter instead of milk to coat the rolled dough. I usually leave one loaf and slice and freeze the rest. Even defrosted the bread is great. I also formed some of it into buns for easier handling onthe go, it made really great raisin buns, I just added a little more sugar in the dough, since there was no inner layer of cinnamon/sugar.

reviews.review_text: This is an excellent recipe, and very easy to make!  As an experienced bread maker, it takes just about 9 cups of flour to make this bread not sticky and easier to handle.  Using a stand mixer with a dough hook is key.  Incorporate the 8 cups of flour gradually, adding just enough remaining flour until dough is no longer sticky.  Once it's rolled out, use 2 tablespoons softtened butter or margarine--do not use milk, as this makes the dough sticky.  Spread the cinnamon-sugar mixture to about 1/2 inch of the dough's edge.   I opted not to use raisins in this recipe, as a lot of people don't care for them--but think I will do this for my family.  I made 7 loaves for a craft festival (okay, so we ate one of them!) this weekend, and every one sold!    This recipe is even easier to make than my grandmother's century-old raisin bread recipe, and one that I will make often!

attributes.source_text: I made 7 loaves for a craft festival

reviews.review_text: We made this raisin bread exactly by the recipe the day before Christmas to have Christmas morning. It came out very good and reminded me of the bread my grandma use to make. Some people think this recipe isn't sweet enough. This isn't a cinnamon roll. :) Good raisin bread really isn't suppose to be super sweet, but to each their own. Everyone in my family thought it had a good flavor along with just the right amount of sweetness. It's good buttered and toasted or to make french toast. We gave two of the loaves to friends and they wanted the recipe. Just some tips. We used metal loaf pans and the three loaves only took 35 minutes to cook. Make sure your water and milk is warm enough to activate the yeast. Cover the bowl of dough with a warm damp cloth. When you roll it up into the one long roll, make sure you roll it tight and even. Otherwise, your loaves will rise at different levels. We had one loaf that rose uneven. It still tasted good, but it didn't look as uniform as the other two loaves. I plan on making some more loaves at the request from some neighbors.

reviews.review_text: I tried this recipe, and I have to agree with the "world's best" part.  This recipe is awesome!  I followed it exactly, except I always add a little sugar with my yeast and warm water...I feel that this helps activate the yeast better.  I've also been using my microwave to proof the dough (just make sure you're family knows so they don't turn it on!).  I placed my dough in a greased pot as well as a cup of boiling water in the microwave and repeated this step once the dough was in my bread pans.  The microwave keeps the drafts out and the water provides heat as well as steam to speed up the proofing process.  The result?  3 beautiful, glorious, golden brown loaves, and a deliciously scented home!  The bread has a lovely crust, good texture, and a sweet, yeasty taste.  I'll definitely be using this recipe again, but next time...I'm adding more raisins!

reviews.review_text: I hate to be negative when obviously so many people loved this bread, however I found the recipe to be dissappointing.  Perhaps it was because I tried to use about half whole wheat pastry flour, a cup of fresh ground whole wheat flour, a few Tbsp. of gluten flour (to compensate for the lack of gluten in the whole wheat flour) and white flour for the remainder.  We omitted the raisins, but other than that, followed the recipe exactly - even checking the temperature of the yeast mixture and the cooled milk.  The dough was very heavy and dense, and took forever to rise. The cinnamon/sugar mix for sure needs to be increased -  maybe doubled - and I think I'll stick with brown sugar for this purpose. My good ol' whole wheat bread recipe that I generally use when I make cinnamon bread always puffs way up, only has to rise once and is more flavorful than this recipe was.  After all the work and time that went into this bread, my hubby and kids were not impressed.  In our opinion, it was not sweet enough (and we're not sugar-holics), nor particularily flavorful, and did not rise very much.  I am willing to acknowledge that perhaps the wheat flour threw things all off.  I have made, literally, hundreds of loaves of bread in my relatively short lifetime, but I'm afraid I will not try to experiment with this one any further.

Wow! I have to say this is awesome. BUT...  first... I have to mention that I used JUMBO eggs....  so then needed to add more flour. My dough was really sticky and I really wondered if I'd made a mistake. Well....    this bread turned out really well...   I mean.. GREAT....  I added some almond extract and vanilla to the dough...  and the extra sugar/ brown sugar and more salt as others have suggested. ... Plus... I doubled the raisins. It's really a great recipe. Thanks so much Lydia Holton. I started another batch this morning only using two jumbo eggs and using Craisins.  UPDATE: The two jumbo eggs and Craisins turned out wonderful. Oh ... can't wait to try other variations! Maybe some orange zest and nuts? ... or how about strawberry preserves in the filling with a streusel topping?

items.label: Kittencal's Easy No-Fail Make Anytime Turkey Gravy
items.name: Kittencal's Easy No-Fail Make Anytime Turkey Gravy
items.description:
I have been using this recipe for many years, my family loves this gravy and I have served it to dinner guests over the holidays and always receive rave reviews! --- you don't need to make this gravy using all pan drippings, if you do not have 4 cups of drippings you may mix with chicken broth to make the 4 cups, or it may be made with only chicken broth, please see note on the bottom of the recipe--- this may be made slightly ahead and kept uncovered on top of the stove until ready to serve, just whisk before using If you have any left over this gravy freezes very well or you may reduce all ingredients down to half and for a thinner gravy reduce flour by 1 tablespoon  --- also see my recipe#314890
for more of my recipes visit www.kittencalskitchen.com
instructions: Drain the pan drippings for the roasted turkey through a fine strainer.
Let sit and then remove any fat from the top of the drippings.
Add in chicken broth or water to make 4 cups if necessary.
In a medium saucepan, melt margarine or butter.
Add in lots of black pepper.
Add in 1/2 cup flour plus 3 tablespoons; constantly whisk for about 3 minutes over low heat.
Slowly add in the 4 cups turkey broth/drippings; whisk constantly over medium-low heat until bubbly and thickened (about 3 minutes).
Use right away or keep warm over lowest heat setting, whisk again before serving.

**OPTIONS**  to make this gravy using all chicken broth prepare as directed using 4 cups low sodium chicken broth and 1 tablespoon chicken boullion powder ---- or you may add in low sodium chicken broth omitting bouillon powder to pan drippings to make up 4 cups.

reviews.review_text:
Kittencal, I have used a few of your recipes over the years for my western restaurant in Tianjin China, need to have something different once and a while and I don't mind looking at other chefs ideas, especially yours.

I am getting ready to do a Thanksgiving feast at one of our international schools for 250 people. Of course I have my own recipe for turkey gravy but thought I would give yours a try, let me tell you, yours is my new mine now.

I will be making 20 turkeys so drippings are no problem. I will boil giblets, chop and add to gravy, and as another review mentioned, also use giblet water with drippings. Other than that no changes. I roasted a small turkey today and made your gravy for it, so I know 250 people are going to be very pleased in the near future, thanks.

attributes.source_text: I am getting ready to do a Thanksgiving feast

reviews.review_text: Excellent base for gravy.  I doubled this recipe.  I wanted to prepare my gravy the day before Thanksgiving so I had no turkey drippings since I hadn't cooked my turkey yet.  I had purchased some turkey gizzards for my stuffing, trimmed them and boiled them in some water.  I took the trimmings (throw away pieces) and fried them in some butter for some turkey flavor.  I added them to the broth and let simmer to help bring out the turkey flavor.  Then I proceeded to make the gravy.  I used 4 cups of organic no msg chicken stock and 4 cups of the water that I used to boil my gizzards in to make the gravy.  I removed the trimmings and gizzards before adding the broth to the rue.  Used a ton of white pepper and then took two gizzards and a laddle full of gravy and pureed them in the blender.  I then added that back to the gravy.  Added a bit of salt, but not much, and some more pepper until I got it to my liking.  It was seriously the best gravy I've ever made.  Will be making this again!!  Thanks!

reviews.review_text: Best.  Gravy.  Ever.  I used Kittencal's turkey recipe (sorry, I didn't copy and paste the recipe#).  It was my first time making the turkey.  It is her turkey recipe with step-by-step instructions for beginers if that helps.  Anywhooo...I made this gravy from the turkey and it was AWESOME.  I could eat this gravy by itself.  OK...I will admit to all of you I had to "taste test" it several times before everyone arrived because I became instantly addicted.  Don't tell anyone...but my Mom can't make gravy without lumps so she has given up.  I had no lumps in my gravy on my very first try thanks to Kittencal.  This lady is one GREAT cook.  Bless your heart, Kittencal!

reviews.review_text: WOW...this is a great and easy recipe.  The thought of making gravy can bring on an anxiety attack!    I'm glad I chose this recipe.  I did not use butter as the turkey drippings measured out perfectly 4 cups plus 1/2 cup of fat.  I carefully skimmed off the fat and used that instead of the butter.  I added the neck meat and the little dripping crumbs too, I like "dirty" gravy, yummy to get a little tidbit of meat here and there.  I added about a tsp of salt.  I will definitely make this anytime, using butter next time.  My guests and husband were raving over this gravy and poured it over everything except the green bean casserole.  Thank you kittencal, this recipe is a keeper and my little secret!!

reviews.review_text: Believe it or not, I'm in my 50s and don't think I've cooked a turkey more than once in my whole life.  Today I decided re-create Thanksgiving and prepared roast turkey, stuffing, mashed potatoes & gravy and green bean casserole (yes, in a heat wave of almost 90 degrees here in Southern California but I didn't know that when I bought the turkey last week!) and this gravy turned out delicious and it was so easy!  It was a hit with my friends who shared the meal, and I will definitely make this again.  My friend helped and he was so pleased to learn how to make homemade gravy today and will never, ever have to open a can again!

reviews.review_text: I have been making this same recipe since I learned to make gravy in 1975 when I was 15. It's my mothers recipe to a T, Kittencal! I think it tastes delicious as the recipe stands, but I have always made mine even better by using 1/2 butter- skip the margarine, everything always tastes better with butter- and 1/2 turkey fat- from the pan drippings- for the roux (the flour/fat mixture for all you new cooks out there). I also use the potato water (saved from boiling the potatoes for mashed) and the giblet water (from cooking the giblets). These 2 waters give the gravy a richer flavor. And, of course the giblets are star of my gravy. They are what gives the gravy its ultimate richness. If you are using turkey drippings you may not need much salt but with stock or broth you may want to salt, add bouillon and add a little Bell's Seasoning (the best poultry seasoning out there). I absolutely love this gravy and always get rave reviews.

attributes.source_text: These 2 waters give the gravy a richer flavor

reviews.review_text: Thanks Kittencal you saved the day. This recipe is going to be my staple from now on.  My oldest daughter had done the holiday grocery shopping and had bought by mistake a precooked turkey. I had never had one before so had no idea how much pan drippings I was going to get off it so I printed out your recipe since you gave instructions for chicken broth to be used also.  Well turned out to have enough drippings but used your recipe anyways and it is truely fantastic. Loved it :)

Even though I've always made tasty gravy, when I was poking around in your recipes I ran across this recipe.  Of course, I just had to test run it as it was just my small family for Thanksgiving.  BINGO, money, winner, ringer, choice, etc.!!!  I had approximately 1-1/2 cups of drippings, added "free range" organic chicken stock to recipe's directions, and it was out of this world delicious ~ thest best gravy I've ever put out in my kitchen!  Your recipes are becoming a household name around these parts, I will never make gravy any other way, and I want to thank you once again for sharing your time and talent!!!

reviews.review_text: I made recipe #39044 and had 4 cups of lovely stock left in the crock pot which I originally was going to use for soup. The weather changed and I decided to make recipe #77608 but wanted gravy over it. I went directly to Kitten's recipes to see if she had a turkey gravy recipe because I knew it would be great as are all the recipes I've tried of her's. I wasn't wrong! It was fantastic on the croquettes. Very good directions made this easy to make and the results were delicious. The remaining gravy is in the freezer to use for another meal.

A fool-proof recipe that delivers a HECK of a bang!    I added 1/4 cup of water and the water mixed with the drippings the turkey breast made in the crockpot got me about 2 cups of drippings.  I offset the remaining amount of gravy with chicken stock.  I used A TON of fresh ground black pepper and followed the rest of the recipe to the letter.  I'll admit, I did have to add a bit of Wondra to thicken this to my liking,  Excellent flavor and consistency.  This is my go-to gravy recipe for chicken and turkey.

This gravy is very easy to make and delicous! I have made it twice now since making a Turkey on Sunday. I am freezing half of the second batch, the first batch is already gone! I have never followed a recipe to make my gravy, I have always just whished things together. Never again! I am going to follow this recipe whenever I need a gravy. I did have to use 1 cup of water in my second batch but it turned out just as great as the first. Thanks for sharing this wonderful recipe.

This is the first time I've ever made gravy and I was happy with how simple it was with so much flavor! I changed the 5 cup serving to 2 1/2 cups and only used chicken broth instead of pan drippings or chicken bouillon. I also added some garlic powder when I added the pepper. It took longer than 3 minutes to thicken, but once it started to thicken, it was done. I will use this recipe again and again and again. Thank you for posting! Everyone loved it with their turkey dinner.

attributes.source_text: with their turkey dinner

reviews.review_text: My 1st home made scratch gravy!!! Ingredients: 1c turkey drippings, 1/3c cold water, 1/3c butter and tub marjorine, crushed black pepper, sea salt to taste, approx 1/2c corn starch. Boiled low heat and as directed. Buttery taste came through, light on seasoning however--Added more to taste. Kittencal, I love you!!! First home-made gravy ever! You are my go to recipe preference. Compared to mother figure's stories of "lumpy first gravies", this was a creamy start!!! Some flavor especially when paired with well seasoned meat, however, light on seasonings. Appearance of white gravy like offerings at some restaurants--my guess contributed to use of cornstarch. Yummy first try--all thanks to Kittencal!!! Now I can add gravy to my list of kitchen skills with this recipe by my side.

attributes.source_text: Buttery taste came through
this was a creamy start

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe on 6/14/09 with the drippings from Recipe#104965. And I did make a mistake with this recipe, I only made half :).The recipe was sort of made as written, I used 1 cup of drippings. And then added 1/2 cup chicken broth and the rest water.Proceeded with the rest of the recipe as it was written. And have to tell you, this is some of the best gravy. I will make this recipe anytime turkey gravy is needed. Thanks for posting and, " Keep Smiling :) "

Thank You!!! Five Stars! Great Gravy!

I made this gravy today, and it was so good! I'll definitely make homemade gravy every year now that I know how. Your step-by-step directions were great, and I followed them exactly, only adding extra black pepper after tasting, as my family loves pepper. This is my go-to recipe now, everyone loved it, and complimented me on my homemade gravy.

Thanks again for hlelping make our Thanksgiving meal a spectacular one.

attributes.source_text: make our Thanksgiving meal a spectacular one

reviews.review_text: I couldn't have asked for a more perfect turkey gravy! This was my first year cooking the entire thanksgiving dinner. I can make great beef gravy, but it's a putzy process so I needed a quick and easy turkey gravy recipe. This was AWESOME! My mother-in-law kept asking what was in it and kept insisting that there MUST have been more spices than that... the only thing I added  was some granulated garlic powder to taste (I did use all turkey drippings and no water or broth so that probably helped with the full flavor). PERFECT. I will never use another gravy recipe again.

attributes.source_text: cooking the entire thanksgiving dinner
My mother-in-law kept asking what was in it

reviews.review_text: I was nervouse making gravy for the first time, instead of pouring it out of a can, but it was very simple and delicious. I made it with Kittencal's Classic Whole Roasted Turkey (for beginners) and it was perfect. It had a great flavor, made more than enough for dinner, leftovers and the rest I poured on top of some french fries. I froze the leftover stock so I can make it easily, all the time. It was my first gravy recipe, and I don't plan on trying any more.

attributes.source_text: made more than enough for dinner

reviews.review_text: I am always stressed about my gravy for Thanksgiving. So I thought I would make this ahead of time just in case it is a flop, I can always run to the store!!  But, this is WONDERFUL!  It is a great gravy and is a perfect base.  I love poultry seasoning so I added about 1 1/2 tablespoons to the gravy while it was cooking and WOW oh WOW!  I could just eat the gravy! Thanks Kittencal again for another great helper recipe!  You are making me feel like I am a good cook!!

This Christmas is the first time in about 20 years that my branch of the family was called upon to make and bring the turkey to the big meal at my inlaws' house (my mother in law or sister in law usually do the meats and I do the bread/sides, etc.)  My adult daughter had brined and set up the turkey in a roasting pan so all I had to do was stick it in the oven after she left for work.  While it was roasting I made yeast rolls, stuffing and side dishes, and was REALLY getting nervous about having to make gravy to feed all these people.  Naturally, I turned to Recipezaar and was so relieved to find a No-Fail Turkey Gravy recipe from a chef whose recipes I have used many times before!  I skimmed the fat from the pan drippings and added enough canned chicken broth to make the 4 cups.  Followed the directions and it turned out PERFECT.  My only comment would be that on an electric cooktop like mine I had to up the heat a little bit to get it to thicken, but once it did, I tasted it and it was delicious (no "raw flour" taste at all). Transferred to a small crock pot to keep warm until it can be transported to the inlaws' house in a  couple of hours.  I am sure it will be a hit!  THANK you for saving me again with a terrific recipe!  ~ Zew

attributes.source_text: This Christmas is the first time in about 20 years

items.description: Make and share this Grandma's Soft Sugar Cookies recipe from Food.com.

Drop by heaping teaspoon approx 3\

reviews.review_text: I LOVE these cookies!!! Usually i dread making cookies,but these were easy and came out great! I didnt have vanilla so I used honey instead, which is frowned upon,i know...but this time it was ok,since one of the previous comments said to up the sugar,which I wanted to do,because i like sweet cookies...in the end I made a few as is(with the honey sub) and then I added,mixed spice, a bit of ginger and some cinnamon to the remaining dough,can anyone say YUM...thank you so much for this easy recipe!

After u try this i guess IT will be good . also my sis made a lot of homemade cupcakes and cakes!!!!! There really great i substituted the butter witdch oil! And i changed the sugar amount to 1CUP and the vanilla to 1TB!! But it still turned out great!!!!!!! (:(:(:(:(:(:(:(:(:(:(:(:(:(:(:(:(: And it was the easiest cookie recipe i ever !!
