items.label: Thick, Soft, and Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies
items.name: Thick, Soft, and Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies
keywords: c("Chocolate Chip Cookies", "Dessert", "Cookie & Brownie", "< 30 Mins", "For Large Groups")
items.description:
I moved out of the house in 1992 but my dad still insist I make his chocolate chip cookies for him. After much searching these are the ones we deemed "best". Soft and chewy but with a lightly crisp outer layer. If you don't want the crispness, substitute more butter for the shortening. 

I have found that you need to follow the directions *exactly* to get the best cookies. Not using real butter or all brown sugar, not beating the eggs in one at a time, not baking them at a higher temp than the "traditional" recipe, all make a difference in the end result. 

I have also found that Land o' Lake butter makes a better cookie than some generic brand butter. Don't let the butter sit out too long. It needs to soften but if it sits until the moisture starts to separate from the butter, it is too soft and it will affect the resulting cookies. If that happens, refrigerate the dough for about an hour to help them not spread as much. It also helps to use the mixer on the dough in between batches going into the oven. It helps keep the dough from starting to separate if it is a warm day. 

Another thing I've learned is you have to make sure there is plenty of circulation in your oven. When I moved, my cookies started turning out flat again. I finally realized that my oven was smaller at the new house and when I switched to smaller cookie sheets, my cookies turned out perfectly!
instructions: Mix flour, baking soda, and salt in a small bowl.
In a separate bowl, beat butter and shortening until creamy.
Add sugar and vanilla and beat with a mixer on medium speed until well blended.
Beat in eggs, one at a time, mixing well.
Add flour mixture, and beat slowly to incorporate, then beat to blend well.
Stir in chocolate chips and nuts.
Drop batter in 2-tablespoon portions about 2 inches apart on baking sheets.
Bake in a 375°F preheated oven until edges of cookies are brown but an area about 1 inch wide in the center is still pale, about 10 minutes.
If using 2 pans in 1 oven, switch positions at half-time.
Let cookies cool on pan about 5 minutes, then transfer to racks with a spatula.
Serve warm or cool.

reviews.review_text: I had to leave a review. I live in Colorado at over 6,000 feet, so the first time I made these they came out completely flat. For anyone having this problem, here is what I did the second time around with adjusments, and OMG these are the BEST cookies I've ever made. They turned out even better looking than in the photo above! Okay, so, these adjustments are for anyone living above 6,000 feet, but I got them from my brand of flour 's website (kingarthurflour.com), and they have adjustments for lower altitudes as well. Again, here's what I did that turned out perfectly for me (everything is the same except for measurements, so just follow recipe except change the measurements to what I list below): I let my sweet cream butter (salted butter) come to soft, room temperature (took an hour or two). I creamed them briefly, as per the instructions. I used all butter, not shortening. I baked at 400 degrees, and I didn't bake until brown...more like a slight tan! Lol For the flour, I did 2 1/2 cups + 3 tbs and 1/4 tsp of Salt since I use salted butter, 1/2 tsp of Baking Powder. For the vanilla, I did same as recipe for Vanilla, but the sugar I did 1 cup and 6 1/2 tbs of Brown sugar. Everything else I followed, except I put my dough in the freezer for 30-45 minutes before baking. I will make these forever! SO GOOD!!!

So I am an avid baker and cookie snob. Well, I'll *eat* pretty much any cookie, but as for what I actually think about them, I'm a snob. I almost gave these four stars, but only because mine did not come out thick at all - though the crispy edges and chewy middle were definitely as advertised and after all, that's what makes a perfect cookie. Then I got to thinking that everyone - the author and the reviewers - said not to change anything or they might not come out right, and I did, so that's no one's fault buy my own. And as the aforementioned avid baker and cookie snob, as well as an insane perfectionist, I need to tell you that the one and only reason I changed the recipe is because I didn't realize I was low on butter and brown sugar until I was already bowl-committed. (Did you catch that? Like pot-committed in poker? Man, I'm hilarious.) Anyway, the only things I did differently were use 1 tablespoon of margarine because I didn't have quite enough butter, and 1/4 cup of white sugar because I didn't have quite enough brown sugar. Everything else - to a T. Butter room temperature but not soft, chilled the dough because it's wicked not here and kept it in the fridge between batches. I even weighed out the flour and sifted it. (On that note, I consider 120g a cup, but have heard some people say that say it's 125g per cup, so it's possible that being 12.5g short on flour was an issue.) Anyway, see what I mean? I'm full-on anal-retentive. Anyway, ten minutes at 375 was perfect. I now have an oven thermometer after realizing my oven ran about 75 degrees hot - and somehow I still never burned anything. Weird? I thought so. So if yours burned, check your oven temp! To the people who said their cookies were "missing something", I think it might be love. Try loving the dough. Really thinking happy thoughts for it. And if that doesn't work, I sprinkled a tiny bit of smoked salt on mine when they first came out of the oven and we're still a little tacky and Oh. My. God. Sounds weird, but it's amazing. I will definitely make these again, maybe add a little bit more flour and make sure everything else is right on and see if they're thicker. Thank you, Marg!

reviews.review_text: This is a great cookie recipe. I made two batches, one with refined coconut oil since there was no shortening, the second with butter only. The first batch spread out too much, I think it was due to not using quite enough flour. I'm fairly new at cookies, and did not want to mess them up, went light on the flour. Being new at baking cookies, I appreciated the detailed instructions of the recipe, it seems they make all the difference. The oven temp and time was spot on for my oven. The cookies maintained crispness on the outside, with softness on the inside after cooling and the flavor is good. I don't think they will last very long around here, its likely that we will prefer the butter batch, though. These need to travel across country, so I added a bit of glycerin to keep them soft. They're traveling literally to the other side of the country, and my relative specifically requested soft cookies. The trick is to reduce butter or shortening the same amount as the glycerin added. Reduce butter first, put in mixing bowl, add glycerin to the butter about 1 or 1 1/4 tsp. for these. The second batch seemed thicker, so right now that batter is chilling overnight. I'm looking forward to sharing these. Four stars since I tweaked it, it would have come out better exact. It's good to know we don't have to be so careful about the flour as we thought. Thank you for sharing this recipe! It's going to be our new favorite. These are what I think of when thinking of chocolate chip cookies!

reviews.review_text: I have tried several different recipes for chocolate chip cookies. They're all good. I stumbled on this one a couple of weeks ago and made a batch. They were eaten that same day. Since then I have put two batches in the freezer and two rolls of the dough in the fridge. This is a great recipe. It is so easy to slice a few and bake them for a treat. If you are pressed for time and need something to send with kids for their lunch box, they will love them. I experimented with some of the dough and pressed it into a 8x8 pan and baked them. While still warm I cut into squares and put a scoop of vanilla ice cream on top of each square. Terrific. This will easily be my "go to" recipe for chocolate chip cookies. Thank you very much Marg.

reviews.review_text:
Great cookies. I used cashews and swirled chips. I noticed you said Land O' Lakes butter worked better than generic butter. If you look at the packaging of the butter, you will see a small shield printed on it. the letters in the shield are the grading of the butter. Land o' Lakes is always grade AA. If you purchase any brand of butter that is grade AA, the results should be the same.
Also another reviewer noted that she was making substitutions to make non-dairy cookies. She then went on to say she will add even more chocolate chips next time. "Milk chocolate chips."

This is a wonderful recipe. I'm not sure why but many of my cookies did not escape the spread. I only had 4 or 5 that stayed nice and thick. I had ones that spread and ones that stayed thick on the same pan and while using a scoop for uniformity. Who knows how that could be, but they were equally delicious either way. I will keep trying this recipe to get the picture perfect cookie. In the meantime, I'll be happily enjoying them flat or thick. They have that crispy outside and chewy on the inside goodness. I won't ever need another chocolate chip cookie recipe. This is it for me. Thank you Marg. The only thing better would be for you to come to my house and bake them too.

reviews.review_text: So I read the reviews about the cake flavor to the cookies. There is a cake flavor to them but delicious. I started by putting 3/4 crisco and 1/2 butter than I added another 1/8 crisco to the mix. Addres 1/2 cup more flour. Cooked them for 12 mins at 375. They stay as balls for the complete cook time. At the end of 12 mins I took a spoon on the tray in the oven and pushed the cookies down while hot in the over so they hold together then remove them from the over and used a spatula to remove the cookies from the hot tray. They are very crumbly when first removed hot but once cooled they hold together great. Love the taste and texture. Very Yummy cookies will make them again.

reviews.review_text: These cookies are great as is. I rolled mine up into about the size of a golf ball. MAKE SURE you do not leave them in the shape of a ball when they cook or they will be big thick lumps. Smoosh them down flat into a cookie shape/thickness you desire and they will not spread/rise much further. Everyone loved these. Thoroughly mix the sugar in. Very easy and simple recipe *Err on the side of caution and use less shortening than more if you're wary about it. These cookies can get very flat with too much.Doing half white sugar and half brown would be good too

This is the first time I made a soft chocolate chip cookie.  Usually when I make them they are more crisp and crunchy.  These were very good.  Nice and soft and chewy.  I like these much better than the thinner crispy chocolate chip cookies.  I had 1/2 a cup of white chocolate chips that I wanted to use up, so I used the 1/2 cup of white chocolate chips and 1 cup of the semi-sweet chocolate chips.  I also added a cup of chopped pecans.  These cookies were excellent.  I will be making my chocolate chip cookies this way from now on.  Thanks for sharing such a wonderful recipe, Marg.

reviews.review_text: I have been looking for a soft chocolate chip recipe for ages. Most I found and tried were a big disappointment. They would come out flat, others still too crispy. This recipe is great. Made them for the first time last night and we all enjoyed them. I actually made the dough up and refrigerated it a couple hours only because I wanted to serve the cookies warm. I also used a small cookie scoop. My son is allergic to nuts, so I just added some mini candy coated chololate (M&M's) to the batter and they not only tasted awesome, but the M&M's looked festive. Try this recipe, you won't be disappointed.

reviews.review_text: My best friend of over 48 years makes THE BEST CHOCOLATE CHIP cookies EVER!!!! But I couldn't ask her for the recipe. I have two adult sons, and every year for their birthdays and for Christmas, all they ever wanted was my best friend's chocolate chip cookies. I went on a search for a chocolate chip cookie recipe so that I could make these cookies for my sons. After trying five recipes, I found this one and IT IS THE BOMB!!!! Definitely worthy of my best friend and approved by my boys! I think the shortening was definitely the the big difference here! We absolutely LOVE these cookies!!

reviews.review_text:
I was torn when trying to decide on a CCC (chocolate chip cookie) recipe from this site.  I like my cookies with an ever-so-slight crunch on the outside and soft n' chewy on the inside - NOT cakey or puffy.  I am a CCC afficcionado and to me, next day taste and texture matters just as much as when it comes out of the oven.

I'm very pleased to report that this cookie holds up to both of those tests:  Out of the oven they are warm and gooey, slight crust outside chewy inside.  If they are wrapped well (like in a tupperware w/lid) the next day they maintain their softness and chew.

A major factor that affects cookies is cook time.  If you take it out when it "looks done", it's overdone.  It might be soft that day, but next day it will be crunchier than you wanted. 

I take the cookies out when the very edges have a slight hint of light golden brown and the middle still has that raw dough look and leave the cookies on the hot cookie sheet for a few moments where they'll finish up baking and be absolutely perfect, then move to a cooling rack.   

Another thing about overbaking (even slighly): any chocolate chips on the bottom of the cookie resting on the baking sheet will get more a burned chocolate flavor which isn't that yummy, so if a crispy cookie is your goal it's best to alter the ratios of brown to white sugar to make a crispy cookie instead of letting a soft cookie recipe cook longer to achieve a crispy texture.  Remember, more brown sugar = softer cookie, more white/granulated sugar=crisper cookie.

For this particular recipe (and most others I come across), I found 8 was the magic minute.  Any more than 8 minutes and they got too crunchy for my liking, which was especially noticeable on Day 2 when eating left over cookies.  Of course the bigger your cookie the more time it needs to bake.  

And finally, the reason for only 4 stars:  Although the texture and softness was perfect, the flavor of the dough was kind of lacking in my opinion.  I followed the recipe exactly except for adding a little more vanilla and excluding the nuts.  Eating a bite of cookie without chocolate chips left me feeling kind of disappointed.  I consider this recipe to be a good or even great base for texture/chewiness, but would definitely alter it slightly to find a better tasting cookie dough recipe.  It wasn't bad or unpleasant, just kind of blah tasting.  But thanks for the great base recipe!

items.label: Thick and Creamy New England Clam Chowder
items.name: Thick and Creamy New England Clam Chowder
items.description: This is the BEST chowder I've ever had. I've had chowder at Legal Seafoods in Boston, which I have to say is good, but mine is BETTER! If you like thick chowder, you'll love this one!!
instructions: Add bacon to sauce pan and cook on medium low heat until crispy.
Add onion and cook until translucent.
Add clam juice from both cans.
Add potatoes.
Cook and cover until potatoes are fork tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Stir occasionally so potatoes won't stick.
Add clams, soup, cream, milk, and dill weed.
Stir together.
Add butter and let melt into the chowder.
Cook for about 30-45 minutes or until thickened.
Stir occasionally.

reviews.review_text:
FAB recipe!  Just finished making and eating it and really enjoyed it.  I am in the UK but I used to live in the US, and NECC is one of those dishes that you do not see in the UK.  Notes for anyone in the UK that wants to make this...first of all I was making it for two so halved everything, with the following notes..
Baby clams: Could not find these ANYWHERE then all of a sudden Tesco has started stockin them - they are by John West and you find them in the canned fish section, I used 1 x 280g can.  Celery soup - I used 1 x 295g Campbells Celery Soup, diluted as directed on the can.  Chop the potatoes small - about half the size of a sugar cube.  You may need to add more liquid at stage 5, I put in some of the prepared celery soup to add to the clam juice from the can.  Dill Weed is called tarragon in the UK (also by the way heavy cream means double cream in the UK) - I used dried tarragan which tasted fine, I also put in a teaspoon of dried thyme as I have seen this in most other NECC recipes.  I forgot to put the butter in because I was so eager to eat it!  I will def make this again and again, thanks teen!

I have made this recipe more times than I can remember and it is a consistent family favorite. I have made a few changes for our use and continue to vary the ingredients depending on what my whim is at the time. I add fresh minced garlic to the bacon when I add the onions, typically 0.5 to 0.75 teaspoons depending on the garlic (twice that for double pot). I use canned clams and juice, but stick to fresh for veggies or additional seafood. I often add some shrimp or cod to cook in the chowder during the last stage. In addition to the dill weed, I add 1.0 to 1.5 teaspoons of Bay seasoning. I have used a variety of "cream of" soups and often mix them - the current family favorite is a can of mushroom and a can of potato, but celery combined with cream of broccoli is also good. This last batch also got a fresh ear of corn (microwave in husk 3 minutes, cut off cob) and that looks like a permanent addition. I typically use whole milk and occasionally use all heavy cream, but that is too rich for some folks. Celery, carrots, other compatible veggies may make it into a batch just depending on what is in the kitchen. I try to never full boil the chowder - soft small bubbles and lower heat (yeah, I'm lame and I probably stir too often) for 60-90 minutes makes a perfect consistency. My guys like the Pillsbury Cresent Rounds with the chowder, but any warm, fresh bread works. I assume the chowder would keep for 4-5 days properly strored, but we'll never know since any size batch disappears in less than 48 hours. Love it. p.s. I use the same process (bacon, onions, garlic, then potatoes and chicken stock or broth) to make a base for a fantastic creamy chicken chowder with fresh vegetables and rice. You can figure out how yourself, but cream of chicken is obvious and we prefer grilled chicken (couple lbs breast and/or dark, cut into small cubes). This recipe can be pushed toward barbeque, teriyaki, or other chicken flavor and can be spiced up or down for heat. FYI.

attributes.source_text: it is a consistent family favorite

reviews.review_text: I'm giving this five  stars only because I can't give it 4.9.  I made quite a few modifications to the recipe based on all the other reviews. I used seven slices of bacon. I should've diced it a bit finer. I also used two stalks of celery and omitted the cream of celery soup. In its place I used some Better Than Boullion Clam Base and a couple cups of water. I used a sweet onion and four Yukon Gold potatoes. I cut the dill in half and my bf thought it was still a tad too strong. I also added a dash of Worcestershire sauce and a little Old Bay seasoning. I stuck with the cream and I'm glad I did. I also added the clams in the last ten minutes of cooking. Thanks Teen and all of you wonderful reviewers who had so many terrific suggestions. I'm not a fan of clam chowder, but this was edible in my book and my bf absolutely loved it...and that was the important thing since I made it for his birthday dinner. I guess I'll be making this again!

reviews.review_text:
YUMMM!  Did as another reviewer suggested, and boiled the potatoes separately and added to crockpot with rest of ingredients.  Had 2 cans MINCED clams with juice, but don't think that changed anything.  Used 2 cups Half and Half instead of milk and heavy cream (had some to be used). Put all on LOW in the crockpot for about 1 hour.
 Prepared it Sunday and put (cooled) in fridge overnight -- good for melding of flavors.  Heated about 1/2 of contents of pot in a casserole, covered with foil, in the oven at 300 degrees.  After all had heated and melted some, added some 1% milk and about 1/2 cup Golden Sherry, and replaced in oven at 350 degres for anout 20 minutes, while "tube biscuits" heated, and topped with pepper.  WAS WONDERFUL !! Thought I had plenty for 3 meals (for 2)-- now not sure we will make more than 1 more meal !!  Really enjoyed it, teen - Thanks !

attributes.source_text: Really enjoyed it, teen - Thanks !

reviews.review_text: My kid recently informed me that she loves clam chowder. A friend's mom made it for her and she came home raving about it. So tonight she had a craving for it and I thought "why not." This caught my eye, I had just a little bacon in the fridge, we made a quick trip to the store and wahhlaaa! It turned out deliciously. I will say I always amend recipes just a tad and this was no different. I used 3 strips of bacon, half a large onion and 4 cans of chopped clams. Additionally I only had 4 potatoes. So I rendered the bacon, threw in the onions (with 2 T butter), once they were translucent I drained all 4 cans of clams and added the clam juice to the potatoes. I also added one cup of water since it just didn't seem like enough liquid. Simmered that for 10 minutes until the potatoes were tender and then added the celery soup, clams, 1 cup half-n-half and pepper. I only just heated it through and served it and my little family declared it a success! My daughter loves it and was overjoyed that I learned a new recipe and made it for her! Even hubby approved and that is rare indeed for a soup! Thanks for an easy, delicious, adaptable recipe! It has gone into the family recipe album!!!

my little family declared it a success

reviews.review_text: I will agree that this is the best recipe for clam chowder that I've ever made. Like others have said, I too was skeptical when I saw that you needed to add canned soup to the chowder. But everytime I make it, it gets scraped down to the bottom of the pot. Always a big hit. And like others I tweaked it a bit. I doubled the recipe and used a whole 51oz can of clams (less a couple of spoonfulls that I had to eat) and all of the clam juice that came in the can. I used most of the juice to have enough liquid to cook the potatoes, about half, and then added the rest when I added the heavy cream and milk. The only seasonings I added was a pinch of salt and pepper. There's no need to make and add a roux or a flour and water slurry to thicken it. The cream of celery soup does a fine job. But if you like it thicker by all means add something. Made another double recipe an hour ago and having a couple of friends come over. There shouldn't be any left when they leave.

I like to cook from scratch too, but I thought it made a lot of sense to use cream of celery soup as a base for this clam chowder. I bought fresh minced clams (in their juice) and used half and half. After I browned 4 slices of Oscar Mayer bacon and a whole vidalia onion (chopped); I added two cans of cream of celery soup, two cans of half and half and all of the clam juice to make a broth. Separately, I boiled potatoes, and acknowledging the other reviews, I only peeled and cut up two potatoes so as not to make it too potato-ey. I reserved the fresh minced clams until the end so that they would not get overcooked and rubbery (thanks for that tip too!). The stock seemed a little thin, so I added two tablespoons of Idahoan instant buttery potato, sprinkling it in the broth and letting it dissolve. It thickened the broth and the taste was wonderful--flavor from the soup stock, half and half and clam juice--plus richness from the instant potatoes. I added half a stick of butter to the bacon when it was cooked before I put the onions in too. Now, the chowder is just simmering under a boil--stirring so it doesn't stick to the bottom of the Le Creuset pot--adding the clams last and letting them heat through for flavor but not overcooking them is the last step. Coarse pepper ground on top. I bought two pumpernickel bagels at the farmer's market and will toast them and spread cream cheese on top to go with this hearty chowder for our supper by the New England coast. Thanks for all the tips and observations as you can see they helped me to fine-tune this recipe. It is DELICIOUS, just the right consistency and flavor.

reviews.review_text:
I am from the Great Plains, so I admit that I am not a Clam Chowder expert. My only exposure to clam chowder was while visting in Maine and New Hampshire during the winter one year. The chowder I enjoyed the most was thick, creamy and had a fair amount of potatoes. So that is why I started with this recipe. I read other reviews and incorporated some of their suggestions.

I doubled the amount of canned clams. I was concerned that the extra amount of clam juice would make the soup to thin, but that was not the case. It really brought out a nice clam flavor.

I added two stalks of chopped celery to add little more texture variation. I also added a couple of cloves of garlic.

But the thing I added that really topped off my variation was 8oz of cream cheese. Of course, I'm sure that clam chowder purists abhore the idea of canned cream of celery soup, canned clams and cream cheese, but it works really, really well. I have made numerous fans by sharing my recipe variation.

attributes.source_text: It really brought out a nice clam flavor

reviews.review_text: Let me start by saying that this Clam Chowder was a hit for Christmas Eve dinner! It was my choice that I carry on the Family tradition of having Clam Chowder (and cheese bread) for Christmas Eve dinner this year. You see... the Matriarch of our family passed away this year at the age of 96 years old. She has prepared Clam Chowder every year at Christmas for a long,long time. So with the Holiday's fast approaching I set out to find the perfect recipe for chowder and found it with this one.It was very thick & creamy and unbelievably easy to prepare. It took all of one hour for me to put together. I did not veer from the recipe provided and used Yukon Gold potatoes instead of russets. Of three pots of soup there this one was devoured quite fast ! I only got one bowl out of it ! Guess that says it all ......Oh yeah.....I upped the amount to 10 servings and it filled up a healthy sized 8 quart pot. Thanks for helping keep our holiday tradition going Teen. The Gregory Family

reviews.review_text: Seriously tasty! This is the first recipe I came across to make my 1st batch of clam chowder ever! I lucked out...definitely a keeper for a base recipe. I did make a few modifications based on other reviews: 4 cans of chopped clams, 2 cans cream of celery & 1 can cream of mushroom, 1/2 teaspoon of dill & 1/2 teaspoon of thyme, 1/3 teaspoon parsley, substituted 1 cup fat-free 1/2 & 1/2 (instead of heavy cream) along with 1 cup 1% milk, turkey bacon, and added 1/8 cup each finely chopped celery & carrot, & 1 clove minced garlic to sautee with onions. Also, adding about 4 oz of clam juice really gives it that clam chowder authentic flavor...otherwise it tastes more like potato chowder with clams. Has become a family favorite...would dare to say better than restaurant quality!

attributes.source_text: Has become a family favorite

reviews.review_text: FANTASTIC CHOWDER!!! I hesitated somewhat to try this recipe because of the use of canned soup (total scratch cook here). However, because of the amazing reviews, I gave it a try - oh thank heavens I did! Hands down this is the best I have ever made, and probably had at any restaurant (chefs/restauranteurs in the family)! Also shocked how something this good could be that easy to make - other recipes require much more time, ingredients, etc. Only changes/additions:  Sauteed a diced rib of celery w/ the onions; used 1/2 & 1/2 because that is what I had on hand; added more dill - preference; and added the clams about 5 minutes before the end of cooking (experienced them becoming tough/chewy if overcooked). After I tasted this, I ended up taking 1/2 to another chowder lover (ex-chef) - rave reviews, and felt the same as I in that it is one of the best he's ever tasted. Thank you Teen for sharing this awesome recipe!

attributes.source_text: taking 1/2 to another chowder lover (ex-chef) - rave reviews

reviews.review_text: I have to say this recipe was easy to follow and is probably the best tasting chowder I have ever had.  I live in Washington State and we get lots of fresh razor clams.  I used gold potatoes because of their buttery flavor.  Good razor clams have the same flavor...buttery and yummy.  The celery soup give it a great base flavor and as you add everything together it really blends well.  I did not add butter to the soup, but put a dollop in my serving bowl.  It has all those natural buttery flavors with the gold potatoes and fresh razor clams.  I followed the recipe and cooked the potatoes in the onions, bacon and clam juice.  I just kept stirring them and there was plenty of liquid to cook them.  I used a Pampered Chef dill mix that I had..just enough for flavor.  I baked fresh Garlic Artisan bread to have with it and the meal was really delicious.  I highly recommend this recipe!

attributes.source_text: It has all those natural buttery flavors

reviews.review_text: This was wonderful.  I did make a few tweaks based on previous comments and my own, personal, tastes.  I used eight slices of bacon.  Instead of the onion, I substituted shallots, and I cut up about a rib and a half of celery.  In addition to the two cans of baby clams, I used two cans of minced clams.  The extra juice covered the potatoes perfectly, but the end product should simmer longer to thicken as a result.  Finally, I threw in a few dashes of Worcestershire and omitted the dill.  Finally, I believe it results in more servings than stated.  My four year old lapped it right up, asked for more, and I've got enough leftover for my family of three to have two more meals.

attributes.source_text: My four year old lapped it right up, asked for more

reviews.review_text: Super Clam Chowder! I read some of the reviews about the excess celery taste and remembered that I was confused about the way the recipe called out ingredients.  Was it two 21 oz. cans of celery soup, or 21oz total?  Campbell's has two sizes of soup- 10.75oz and 26 oz, so I just figured the chef was talking about two of the smaller cans for an approx total of 21 oz total.  Same issue with the cans of clams.  Clams come in 6.5 oz cans normally, not 10oz (at least here in FL).  But- you can never have too many clams in clam chowder (GRIN).<br/>Recipe came out great this way.<br/><br/>Thanks to the chef for a great recipe!

I am not a fan of any seafood but my husband loves clams especially chowder so I decided to try this recipe ... HE LOVED IT !!!! I did what others did ... put my twist on it , it says 6-7 potatoes ( I used 2 BIG ones) I did not use bacon (in clam chowder--- I think not) instead I used butter(a couple of tablespoons) put the onion & celery when done (took the pan off of the burner) put the clam juice (maybe a little extra) then the potatoes, when done add the clams, cream (8oz.) and about 3/4 cup milk & the soup (used 1 can of cream of potato soup & 1 can cream of celery soup) just keep checking on it ---- smells so good, next time I'm going to double the recipe and freeze some for when my husbands in the mood (for chowder)

attributes.source_text: HE LOVED IT

reviews.review_text: This is a great recipe--and while I usually don't like using canned soup, I am glad I tried this! I did make a couple of changes based on other reviews: I did not add the bacon (I didn't miss it at all) and used a couple Tbs of butter instead. I also used 1 10 oz can of baby clams, 1 6.5 oz can of chopped clams, and 1 6.5 oz can of minced clams. I cut back to two Russet potatoes (plenty!), minced two ribs of celery that I cooked with the onion, and then used cream of potato soup. I also added some parsley, subbed some thyme for the dill, and added 1/2 Tbs of sherry. It tasted great and I will definitely make this again!

I wanted so badly to love this recipe based on the scores of reviews I read, but sadly I did not. First I should say that I am not crazy about the taste of seafood, though most people reading this probably are. I do love a good clam chowder, however, (just not too "fishy" tasting, to my taste). I followed the recipe except used one can cream of celery and one can cream of potato soup. Came out a little too fishy for my taste. If I were to do it again - and I am not sure it's worth it to me, I would not add the reserved clam juice, just the clams. I bet then it would be pretty good. Love that people love it; it is great to find a recipe that is a gem.

I made a half batch of this for my DH. Since I don't like clam chowder this review is based on his opinion. I think I must have used larger potatoes than intended because I used three and he said that it was a little bland as I made it and it needed salt and pepper. I think I'll make this again and add salt, pepper, double the clams (he said the clam flavor wasn't very strong) and use fewer potatoes. There wasn't enough clam juice to boil the potatoes so I had to add water, and I think that is where the blandness came from. Unfortunately, I couldn't taste as I went so I'll have to use trial and error, but I think this one is one that I'll be able to modify to work for him. Thanks for the recipe!

attributes.source_text: this review is based on his opinion

reviews.review_text:
You are so right on the money with this winner!  It IS the BEST clam chowder I have ever tasted!
My friend had a hankering for homemade clam chowder, so I surprised her by whipping up a batch of this last Sunday.  We both had 3 bowls of this addicting chowder!  It was easy and the flavors married beautifully, especially the dill. The only change I will make is next time I make this, after browning and crisping the bacon in the pan...I will remove it and add it back in at the last minute.  The bacon kind got soft after simmering in the broth for the rest of the cooking time!  I must confess, I have never made homemade clam chowder before, but with the ease of this recipe...I will make it any time I have a craving!  Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: My friend had a hankering for homemade clam chowder, so I surprised her by whipping up a batch of this last Sunday.

reviews.review_text: Served this for company ... even the one who "doesn't like clam chowder" gave it a thumbs up! DH who rarely gives anything a five star did so on this one and told me to "keep that recipe." I did make a couple of changes but nothing that would affect the overall recipe ... I used chopped clams instead of baby clams. I always drain and rinse the clams to get rid of any "grit" so I didn't have the reserved clam juice so I used an 8 oz bottle of clam juice plus 1 cup of water to cook the potatoes in. I also used 1/2 and 1/2 instead of heavy cream and milk. Next time I will use a full package of bacon but that's just personal preference.

items.label: Kittencal's Famous Coleslaw
items.name: Kittencal's Famous Coleslaw
items.description: This is the most delicious coleslaw that you will ever have! I make this for weddings, large socials and in the summer for BBQ's and parties, and there is never anything left it all goes and everyone wants the recipe --- plan ahead the coleslaw needs to be refrigerated for the stated time to blend the flavors, this coleslaw will intensify in flavor with chilling time --- this is not a thick heavy dressing like some other coleslaw recipes it's the perfect texture and flavor and what makes this coleslaw stand out from all others is the fresh lemon juice so please use only fresh I have used bottled in the past and it is just not the same --- the dressing amount will yield enough for two 16-ounce packages prepared coleslaw mix or 1 head of green cabbage --- for one 16-ounce package prepared coleslaw mix use the dressing amounts posted on bottom of recipe and add in 3 or more large of chopped green onions.   For more Kittencal's recipes, visit my recipe site www.recipezazz.com
instructions: In a food processor chop the cabbage into small pieces (should look like about the size of confetti) or shred the cabbage.
Transfer to a large mixing bowl.
With a fine shredder, shred the peeled carrots; add to the cabbage in the bowl.
Chop the green onion finely; add to the cabbage/carrot mixture along with the celery seed.
Mix the three veggies all together with a wooden spoon.

To make the dressing: in a medium glass bowl whisk together all the dressing ingredients starting with the lower amounts then adding in and adjusting to suit taste but using 1/3 cup plus 2 tablespoons sugar.
Pour over the veggies in the bowl, and mix well to combine.
Store covered in the refrigerator for at least 8 hours or overnight (overnight is better) to blend flavors.

FOR ONE 16-OUNCE PACKAGE COLESLAW MIX use the following amounts; 1/2 cup mayonnaise/ 2-1/2 tablespoons milk/ 2-1/2 tablespoons buttermilk/ 1-1/2 tablespoons vinegar/ 1-1/2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice/ 3-1/2 tablespoons sugar/ 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder/ 1/2 teaspoon seasoned salt, or to taste.

reviews.review_text: Kittencal is the chef of the week at our house since this is the 3rd recipe of hers I've used this week.  This coleslaw lived up to her high standards!!!  The only reason I say it was near perfect (not the recipe but by my own doing), is because I used sour milk in place of the buttermilk and 2% milk in place of the half and half. (I had used up all the half and half in her Spinach Parmesan Rice bake earlier this week).  My taste buds can only imagine how wonderful this recipe would be done the right way! I halved this and wished I hadn't after my 1 & 1/2 year old granddaughter and I sat in the kitchen and "taste tested"...almost too late I realized that this dish might not make it to supper.  Thanks for sharing Kittencal..you are a super cook!

attributes.source_text: my 1 & 1/2 year old granddaughter and I sat in the kitchen and "taste tested"

reviews.review_text: Another home run for Kittencal!  This was excellent!  I'm not even much of a coleslaw fan but we were having guests over for a BBQ and I was already making a pasta salad but figured I should make another salad and opted for this one.  PERFECT!  I used pre-shredded cabbage and pre-shredded carrots.  I didn't put them in the food processor because I prefer larger pieces of carrot and cabbage in my coleslaw.  The only changes I made were to use low fat mayo and to cut the sugar a bit.  It was excellent from the second I mixed it together.  I let it chill for only about 5-6 hours and it was devoured.  Thank you for another perfect recipe.  This will be my only coleslaw recipe from now on.  UPDATE:  It's been 3 days since I made this coleslaw.  Tasted it today and tastes as good, if not better, than the day I made it.  It holds up well in the event you actually have leftovers.

attributes.source_text: we were having guests over for a BBQ
we were having guests over for a BBQ

reviews.review_text: Beyond tasty Kitten and a thorough delight to fix for this afternoon at the farm. It is warmish here, even though the mid/west part of the U.S. has snow...however; we ambled on out in the bright sun, listen to the birds making nests, and had a burger accompanied by this delicious, cool, refreshing outrageously good coleslaw. I easily halved this recipe and made the dressing in the morning with ingredients I had on hand. I let that sit in the fridge for about an hour or so, and then thinly sliced the cabbage, (I also used red cabbage too) carrots, and in place of green onion, I had a red onion.  The buttermilk is such a great addition to this and I did use "Hellman's" mayonnaise. Had fresh lemon which I used the juice and some bright apples and spinach for extra pow. Thank you, Kittencal! Another winner!

attributes.source_text: this delicious, cool, refreshing outrageously good coleslaw

reviews.review_text: I have made this a couple of times. I cut the sugar back to 1/4 cup, and that works for my tastes. If I follow the recipe to the letter, it really does taste like KFC coleslaw. This stuff is really addictive. I never seem to have buttermilk, so I use regular or Greek yogurt instead. I always add heavy cream instead of milk (yum). I've also just made the dressing and used it on other salads and roasted veggies. Thanks for the recipe. All your meals come out good. I start hunting for your name as soon as the search gives me the top recipes for what I want to make.

Knock out of the park coleslaw!! This is by far the best I've tasted in 57 year lifetime! I had to make my own buttermilk so used cream and vinegar to do that...It was thickish but lavish!
I chopped the cabbage in very small pieces using my Swissmar Borner V-1001 slicer and knife. I used rice vinegar instead of white. I used sea salt instead of seasoned salt, and added a little more carrot- squeezing out the liquid. The slaw was not runny at all even after sitting for two days!
I ended up using the smallest amount of sugar and the other ingredients for the dressing which the recipe said to start out with the least and increase to personal taste. It was dead on perfect and three people ate an entire batch in two days.

reviews.review_text: Finally, coleslaw that I really like. I loved the finer texture of the slaw and I love anything with lemon juice in it...the only thing I altered in this recipe was that I used heavy cream, as a prior reviewer noted her dressing could have been thicker. I think I would have liked it equally with the lighter cream or milk. No one flavor overpowered the cabbage, which I really appreciated. Usually American coleslaw can have too much celery seed in it, or its bland and is cut too large. This is my forever coleslaw recipe. I could have eaten a huge bowl all by myself. Thanks, Kittencal!

reviews.review_text: I wish I could give this more than 5 stars. I have always HATED coleslaw! Too sweet,too much mayo, soggy. I tried this recipe because I wanted to make fish tacos,never had, and I needed coleslaw. I immediately got on and looked to see if Kittencal had a recipe. I didn't even bother looking at any others. This was delicious!!! used flour tortillas,fried cod pieces, coleslaw,and homemade tartar sauce. Now one of my favorite dishes! I did omit the seeds after the first batch because I thought they took away from the other flavors. I also added about 1/4 cup of orange bell pepper. It went with this recipe so well. When adding the bell pepper do not use more than a third cup of sugar. Thanx for another keeper. Now I gotta go make some coleslaw for fish tacos tonight!

I just made this about half an hour ago - waiting for all the flavors to marry - unfortunately, I misread white vinegar - thought it said white wine vinegar which I didn't have (duh me), so I substituted rice vinegar - this may have contributed to the sweetness, because it seems pretty sweet and I didn't even use all the sugar called for. Used plain greek yogurt instead of buttermilk, also used a little cream in the milk. Other than more sweetness than I'd prefer, it is delicious!! My husband and family will love it. Can't wait to make it for the next potluck! Thanks!

I put it in a plastic container and turned it every few hours, then let it sit overnight. The volume decreases, but the veggies stay crispy. It was so good even I loved it. items.label: Best Apple Cake
items.name: Best Apple Cake
items.description: This is my DH favorite cake, I have tried many apple cakes over the years and this is a winner!! So moist and dense, with a caramel taste, cannot say enough, just try it and see.
instructions: In a large bowl combine flour, sugar, soda and salt. Make a well in the center and set aside.
In a medium bowl combine eggs, oil, apple juice and vanilla. Stir in apples and nuts. Add the egg mixture to dry ingredients, just until moistened.
Spread batter in a greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake at 350°F for 45-50 minutes.
In a small saucepan combine the brown sugar, butter and cream.
Cook and stir till bubbly and all of the sugar is dissolved. Cool slightly. Drizzle warm sauce over cake, when it has cooled for 5 minutes, so it can seep into the cake, keeping it moist.

reviews.review_text: This is a very good cake.  I appreciate the advice of other posters to use apple sauce in place of half the oil, and to reduce the sugar in the cake by half a cup.  I did both, and the cake was marvellous.  I was spooked, however, by the posters that said they had cooled the sauce too long.  I barely cooled it at all and the result was to have it run off the top of the cake instead of soaking in, and pool at the side of the cake pan.  I spent a good deal of time spooning it back onto the top of the cake.  The idea to poke holes all over the cake with a tooth pick before adding the sauce was a good one.  Making double the sauce was also not a good idea.  I was making two cakes, one for the group I attended, and one for family.  I doubled the sauce thinking it would all go on the first cake,  and it was way too much.  I then kept the excess sauce on a warm spot on the stove, stirring from time to time, and used it over the second cake, about an hour later.  It was just the right amount, and worked much better in not running off the cake.  Has anyone tried this as a bundt cake?

Like most others, I love this recipe(with some adjustments)! I've made this a couple times and think I've mastered my alterations. I reduced the oil to 1/2 cup(no replacement with applesauce) and the sugar to 1 2/3 cup.  I also added 2 t cinnamon and 1 t pumpkin pie spice.  I omit the nuts, just as a personal preference.  The glaze topping was delicious!! I poked many holes with a toothpick all over the cake. Before topping the cake, I allowed the glaze and cake to cool about 5 minutes, spread about half of the glaze on, and then waited another 15 minutes before adding the rest.  As written, this is probably a 2-3 star recipe.  With my adjustments, I rate this a 5!  So, I'll average it out for the official rating. :)

Very good! I made a few adjustments which resulted in possibly more pudding like than intended, like sticky date pudding, I used; chopped dates, 1/2 cup less sugar but still so sweet, apple and lemon blend juice, grated pink lady apples, 1 tsp cinnamon + 1/2 tsp nutmeg + 1/4 tsp ground ginger, fine cake flour and a mixture of peanut and grapeseed oils (needed to finish off the grapeseed and was only 1/2 cup). I used raw sugar which has more molasses content than caster/white sugar therefor adding to the caramel content. I also used my own vanilla which is made from a lot of v/beans crammed into a small bottle and filled with scotch or vodka, I top it up with either one when it gets low. I haven't made any topping or sauce, but I think even a ginger mascarpone whip would be nice.....

attributes.source_text: but still so sweet

reviews.review_text: WOW! That sums it up. This was a huge hit with my family! We all loved it. Can't say enough about it! I did make some adjustments though. I did take the advice from others and used 1/2 c applesauce and 1/2 c oil. I also omitted the nuts (personal preference)in the batter. I also added 1/2 t. of ground cinnamon to the batter. I wasn't really sure if the apples should be packed or not, but I did pack them down. Next time I make this cake I will add more cinnamon (1 t.) I doubled the sauce, and took the advice from others and poked holes with a toothpick on the top. I put half of the sauce over the cake, let it cool a bit, then put the rest on it. I then topped it with chopped pecans. YUMMO! Thanks for submitting this keeper recipe, I too have to agree .....BEST APPLE CAKE!

Excellent, thank you for sharing...oh and I did not have apple juice I used OJ and it worked great...thank you!!! Definitely a keeper.

UPDATE...MAY 10, 2008
Just adding here have made this again in a bundt pan, this time using exact ingredients, and my cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg as stated above, just needed a little longer cook time, just watch and test with a tooth pick. reviews.review_text: I made the 6 serving version of this cake except without the walnuts because I wanted a less dense cake and used two small/med eggs instead of 1 1/2 large. I also used Granny Smith apples, a pinch of cardamom and cinnamon, a 1/4 tsp of lime juice, and a tbsp or so of vanilla sugar. The resulting cake was moist and not too dense, a bit like a muffin/bread in texture, and tender from all that sugar. My first taste after cooling an hour, I thought the cake was too sweet and wanted more apple and tartness, but like many have mentioned, this cake tastes better after it's cooled completely or the next day. The buttery flavor of the glaze and the sweetness of the cake mellows out. Next time I think I'll chop the apples less fine, add half a tsp of lime and leave out the cinnamon. Nonetheless, the cake disappeared pretty quickly when usually my family aren't too big on sweets and cakes. I loved how this was quick and easy, no need to use a mixer or fuss with a frosting. I used a 9 inch springform and baked for 30 minutes with the convection on in my oven.

reviews.review_text: Already so as always I ended up with tons more apples then I could use in desperate search for new and tasty recipes that helped me use some of these apples.  I found this cake and had to try it. I made mine as directed with the exception of nuts which I didnt have on hand, used bundt pan and rather then whipping cream I used heavy cream.  The cake is definitively very dense.  It is not light and fluffy like most cakes but the taste is by all means not too sweet or over powerful.  The recipe is very easy and straight forward to follow through with and the aroma while it bakes is nevertheless worth the time.  The cake baked up to a wonderful golden color and got tons of oohs and aah from my guys when it came out of the oven.  I made the sauce at the same time I baked the cake and let it sit in worm spot on the stove while the cake finished baking and cooled.  One batch of the sauce was more then enough for the cake, we used the left over sauce over ice cream.  None of us thought the cake was over sweet or that it was missing anything.  Fabules cake, super easy to make and it looks like it took forever to make... in my opinion its a winner and a keeper.  Thanks Rose for awesome recipe.

I made two 8X8 inch cakes, one went to a friend and the other we kept. They baked for 45 minutes and  only took a few minutes to whip up.

Very good and tasty, I am going to make it again tomorrow!

Next time I'll try the glaze. Overall it had great flavor. A nice dense cake, and feels like autumn.

items.label: Top Rated Classic Meatloaf
items.name: Top Rated Classic Meatloaf
items.description: My family enjoyed the slightly spicy taste of this meatloaf. This recipe, submitted by a local DJ, was in our local paper.
instructions: Preheat oven 325 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large mixing bowl, combine ground beef, cracker crumbs, salt, pepper, egg, onion and tomato sauce.
Mix lightly.
Shape into a loaf and place in a baking dish.
In a small mixing bowl, combine the ketchup, brown sugar, water, mustard and vinegar.
Brush the loaf with this mixture.
Place meat loaf in oven and bake 1 hour and 15 minutes, basting occasionally with sauce.

reviews.review_text:
I was originally planning on making meatloaf in a muffin tin, but I ended up doing this one instead.

First off, I used storebought dry breadcrumbs instead of cracker crumbs, however, I looked at the ingredients on them, and I won't be buying them again.  I also followed suggestions and cooked the onion in olive oil until translucent beforehand.  

My final change is even more fun, and I think it worked spectacularly.  I was planning on using less water in the sauce like suggested, but as I was starting to put it together, I spied the apple cider. So, I ended up with 1/2 cup of apple cider instead of water and brown sugar in the sauce, and it made the loaf smell so good while cooking.

I baked the meatloaf on a broiler pan, but there was very little grease, but I don't really remember what type of ground beef I bought.  I basted the meatloaf probably four times during the cooking, and I used a meat thermometer to help determine when it was done.  I had divided the meat into two loaves since they were easier to handle, and with that, the cooking time seemed to be just slightly shortened.

The meatloaf turned out very, very tasty. I couldn't help but nibble some of it before I cooled it and put it away for lunches the next day.  It was, of course, very tasty the next day as well.

I think that next time, I wil substitue some of the crumbs with rolled oats, since it is healthier.  I also might experiment with some TVP, but you really can't go wrong with this, at least if you make a few adjustments if desired.

attributes.source_text: put it away for lunches the next day

reviews.review_text:
Thank you so much for the recipe. As often seen, I had to use what was on hand....so i changed some things. No ketchup, so used tomato soup. Used less than half of a cup of the soup for the meat mixture, adding a little bit of skim milk to make it thinner. I also added about 2 T. minced garlic in the mix. I used 2/3 cups crushed crackers and 1/4 cup potato chips. Reduced the salt. I also used green onions, cause that's all I had.
 For the sauce, i used the rest of the can of tomato soup, mostly plain mustard, with a little honey mustard added. Also added a couple of T. hot picante sauce. Being the garlic lover I am, I also added about a T. of minced garlic to the sauce.Did not have a basting brush, so just spooned more sauce over it about every 20 mins. Was just told, "Best I've ever had". Thank you for the basics.....

This is a great recipe!!  I followed some of the reviews, I didn't add water to the topping and used Italian Panko instead of bread crumbs or crackers. items.label: Baked Tilapia With Lots of Spice
items.name: Baked Tilapia With Lots of Spice
items.description: This is a fabulous recipe for oven fried tilapia slightly adapted from Paul Prudhomme's wonderful "Fork In The Road" lower fat cookbook. I served this for dinner with family and it got rave reviews. Even my picky 5 year old eater enjoyed it. The ingredient list here is long, but is mostly spices. Please don't be put off, this is wonderful stuff and once you get the spice mixture combined, quite easy to make.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees.
In a small bowl combine the spices from the salt through the Italian seasoning and set it aside.
In a shallow container mix the bread crumbs, dried parsley, and green onions.
Measure 4 tsp of the spice mix and sprinkle that all over the 4 fish fillets.
Add the remaining spice mix to the bread crumbs, mixing well.  Add the olive oil to the bread crumb mix, blending it in with your hands.
Dredge the fish in the breadcrumbs, coating well.
Shake off any excess breadcrumbs.
Place the fish on a baking pan that has been sprayed with non-stick spray.
Bake for 6 minutes.
Turn over and bake for 4 minutes.
Turn over again and bake until flaky, about 4 more minutes.
Serve immediately.

reviews.review_text: This was a very easy alternative to fried fish.  I had read the reviews prior to cooking this and made one small change.  I completely omitted the salt, as it would be easy to salt at the table if need be.  The taste was phenomenal without salt, so that is how I will make it from now on.  I have a hard time eating fish, as I just don't normally like the taste of it, but with this recipe I will be able to start rotating it into our diet more often.  Even my 1O, 8 and 4 year old children loved it.  My 8 year old daughter wanted more, but alas there wasn't any leftover.  Thank you for a great new way to eat fish ladypit!

A 12 oz package of fresh-frozen Tilapia was on sale, so I since the recipe uses 16oz worth of fish, I used the entire package.  Other than the amt of fish, I followed the recipe exactly. This was good Tilapia, esp for someone like me who is so picky about fish.  Bf and I each had 2 1/2 fillets (5 fillets in a 12 oz package) and he said "Mm, spicy, yum," on his first taste. items.name: German Apple Cake
items.description: This moist flavorful cake is an old standby for potlucks and picnics. My sister gave me the recipe after she got tired of making it for me so often.
instructions: In large bowl, beat eggs and oil until smooth.
Add next 6 ingredients and mix well.
Fold in apples.
Pour into greased 9 by 13 pan.
Bake at 350F degrees for 50-55 minutes.

reviews.review_text: Yummy. Wonderful moist cake chock full of apples with a slightly crispy topping. I used a potato peeler to peel the apples (five medium), an egg slicer to slice the apples, then chopped the slices with a knife. To prepare the baking pan I used Pan Release Pan Release which I keep on hand all the time. You can use a silicone pastry brush, a piece of wax paper, or a plastic sandwich bag over your hand to spread this excellent pan greasing mixture. My KitchenAid made short work of the batter then I used a wooden spoon to fold in the apples because the batter was stiff. I topped the barely warm cake with a glaze of about 1 cup icing sugar, a dash of almond extract, and enough milk to make a glaze consistency. To top it off, a sprinkle of sifted icing sugar made for a pretty presentation (some icing sugar in an empty spice bottle with a shaker top is handy). Add a dollop of whipped cream then a hint of sifted cinnamon on top of each serving. A scoop of ice cream would be nice too. This goodie is going in my excellent file to make again and again. Thanks.

reviews.review_text: This is FANTASTIC and EASY!!! I used four leftover medium apples--of a variety my husband wanted to try for snacking but didn't care for the texture--and it came to four cups. I also weighed my flour and sugar because I wanted to see, based on reviews stating the batter was super thick, if it made a difference. The batter was still super thick (however, in the process I learned that the way I've sifted flour for years, moderate tablespoons added to the measuring cup, tapped slightly and then cut and leveled with a butter knife was off by an increased two ounces from what should correctly be 4oz--four oz of flour=1cup). <br/><br/>I baked for 30 minutes, pulled it out because the cake was overly brown, but tested with a toothpick. The toothpick came out wet, but not creamy. Still, I was unsure if it was because of the apples or the cake needed to bake some more. I turned down the oven to 250 and baked for 10 more minutes. The result was what appeared to be an overly cooked, dried out cake, but after about 15 minutes I cut a piece out and sampled it. My, my, my, it was moist and delicious on the inside and the overbaked crust turned out to be flaky and good! Thanks MizzNezz--this is a winner!

reviews.review_text: Made the cake taking into consideration all of the reviewers who said to cut back on the sugar. I went with Luis's suggestions and sautéed the apples (probably used closer to five cups of apples) in a little bit of butter and some brown sugar and let it cool a bit. I think it made it easier to fold into the batter and it also enhanced the apple flavor in the finished product. I used 1 1/2 c sugar and, again, took Luis's advice and upped the cinnamon and added fresh grated nutmeg and powdered ginger. I used butter spray in a 9 X 13 pan and lined it with parchment paper and sprayed it again. Smoothed the batter evenly into the pan and sprinkled some turbinado sugar on top, baked for 45 minutes, turned the oven off and left it in for another 5 minutes. Came out perfect, looked like a blondie bar with apples - texture somewhere between a bar and a cake. Perfect for an afternoon coffee break but Ive been slicing off pieces as it sits on the counter and it keeps getting better - and at this rate its going to be an all day coffee break. Great way to use up apples, easy to throw together with the cuisinart mixer and the only work is preparing the apples. Maybe some chopped walnuts or pecans added the next time I make the recipe.

attributes.source_text: enhanced the apple flavor in the finished product
upped the cinnamon
Perfect for an afternoon coffee break

reviews.review_text: Fantastic! I hate to review a recipe that I've altered but the basics here are SO wonderful! I used half the sugar since we prefer less sweet...lol but then I added back by using the topping from recipe #136589. I spotted about a half a mini bottle of grand marnier in the fridge from another recipe so added that to the cake batter/dough too. Baked in two 9" cake pans and just stacked them (my 9 x 13 is MIA) and with the remaining heavy cream from the other recipe I whipped it with a touch of powdered sugar and a smidge of vanilla pudding mix to stabilize it for a pretty garnish and a contrast in texture.  I used Granny Smith apples that were rather large and 3 was more than enough! The "batter" is very dense so don't let that throw you! This is quick, easy and very, very good! Will make again without any hesitation.

attributes.source_text: I used half the sugar since we prefer less sweet

reviews.review_text:
I wanted my cake to have that beautiful crusty top like in God's Sugarcookie's photo, so I did NOT cut down on sugar, plus I turned up the heat at the very end. I only had time to peel half the apples and that worked fine. The peel softened and the flavor was still great.  I baked it in two 9 inch pie pans (again judging by the photo).  I left cinnamon as the only spice, and got compliments on that simplicity of spice. I had to use red delicious apples so I upped the vanilla and added lemon juice since I prefer a more tart flavorful apple. The cake was extremely easy to put together as promised (I first beat the eggs with the sugar then added the oil and other ingredients, to ensure an easy way to beat the eggs smooth quickly). Thanks, Mizz Nezz, you are one of the reasons Recipezaar is my favorite site.

Since this cake is so well reviewed, I wanted to also tell readers to check out charmed's Recipe #90984 for German apple cake. If you follow my shortcuts there, you get a really amazing and quick apple cake, too, that is a great change of pace from this one.

attributes.source_text: that beautiful crusty top
The peel softened
I left cinnamon as the only spice, and got compliments on that simplicity of spice

reviews.review_text:
I have made this cake twice now. The first time, based on reviews, I cut the sugar and oil by half but otherwise followed the recipe. The cake came out pretty good, though it wasn't overly thrilling. 

The second time I made it, I still cut the sugar down to 1 cup and cut the oil, though this time I only reduced it to 1/2 cup. I reduced the amount of apples from 4 cups to 3 cups, chopped them finer than I had before, and rather than adding each as a separate ingredient I tossed the apple pieces in the cup of sugar and teaspoons of cinnamon and let them sit while I prepared everything else. I felt like the apples needed to be better integrated as an ingredient, and coating them in the sugar and cinnamon before adding to the batter definitely helped. As another reviewer mentioned doing, I also sprinkled a bit of cinnamon and sugar on the top of the cake before sticking it in the oven. If I make it again, I'll go back to the 4 cups of apples but definitely put the sugar/cinnamon on first. This second version was a great improvement over round one.

Finally, I suggest checking it around the 40 minute mark, don't just throw it in the oven for 55 and call it a day. 40 min was plenty for mine.

Oh my...so delicious, and so very easy. This is one of those recipes that TASTES like it was a lot of effort, and only you will know how easy it was. The changes I made were simply personal preference: I doubled the vanilla, added a pinch of nutmeg along with the cinnamon, used one cup white and 1/2 cup brown sugar, and I ground Whole Foods Winter Baking spices over the top before baking. It has brown sugar, lemon zest, orange zest, whole cloves, cinnamon and a bunch of other yummy things, and comes in its own convenient grinder. It forms a nice little crust on top.

This cake smelled heavenly while baking, and my husband paid me the ultimate compliment: it rivals his beloved grandmother's sacred apple cake recipe! We will be making this very often. Many thanks!!!

attributes.source_text: It forms a nice little crust on top
my husband paid me the ultimate compliment

reviews.review_text: I haven't made this yet, but I'm planning to this week and it looks AMAZING. I was wondering if anyone had any tips to maybe a lite frosting? I know I can't use just anything, and it'd be pretty hard to match. If I can find a good frosting to go with it, then I'm going to be putting it on top of a kids' birthday cake. There's more that goes with this, but to keep it short, it needs to be something that kids might like, but something that I can also make from scratch. ANY SUGGESTIONS will help. Thank you! (It's the end of September now, and I'm making the kids' cake towards the end of October. I'll check back!)

I thought this cake was wonderful! It was so simple to make. As others have said, the most difficult part is peeling the apples. After that, it takes 5 minutes to prepare everything. Also as others have said, the dough was incredibly thick and difficult to stir prior to the addition of the apples. I only added 1 cup of sugar instead of the instructed 2 cups and I thought the cake was the perfect amount of sweetness. The only other change I made was that I baked the cake for only about 40 minutes, as opposed to the recommended 50-55 minutes. When I checked on the cake it looked golden brown so I took it out and it was perfectly moist. I highly recommend this recipe!

attributes.source_text: it was perfectly moist
the perfect amount of sweetness

reviews.review_text: Fantastic recipe!  I've been asked for this recipe by sooo many people since I started making this cake.  It's easy and delicious.   I've tweaked the recipe a little bit to make it my own.  Firstly, I halved the sugar (per other reviewers suggestions) and it's quite sweet enough with half the sugar (I use fair trade brown granulated sugar).  Secondly, I replaced cinnamon with mixed cake spice - gives the cake a very festive flavour that reminds me of Christmas.  Thirdly, I add a cup of sultanas that I've soaked in orange juice (or brandy, port or Cointreau if you're feeling very festive :) ).  This cake has now become a firm favourite among my family and friends.  Thanks for sharing.

attributes.source_text: it's quite sweet enough with half the sugar
gives the cake a very festive flavour
a firm favourite among my family and friends
a firm favourite among my family and friends

reviews.review_text:
Oh, soooo good. I love how this turned out with a crispy shell on top and a super moist cake underneath. I cut my apples into large chunks (like picture #7) and I'm really glad I did. It makes for a great third texture to the cake! I used a mixture of Gala and Stayman apples, and otherwise followed the recipe exactly.
I'm definitely going to be making this one again. I'd give it 20 stars if I could!
UPDATE 11/11 - I went to make this again after reading about how much I loved it the first time! I didn't mention in my first review that the batter is VERY stiff - more like dough than batter. I didn't use my KitchenAid mixer but mixed it by hand and could barely stir it. There is no pouring it into the pan - it has to be spread and gently moved around into the corners. It looks beautiful this time around and I can't wait to eat it!
12/11 - what a versatile recipe! I made this again today w/ 1c of sugar and 1/2c oil plus 1/4c water. It was fluffier and slightly more dry, and still amazingly good!

attributes.source_text: with a crispy shell on top
a super moist cake underneath
I cut my apples into large chunks
It was fluffier

reviews.review_text: I made this cake for the very first time, and it was delicious! I am glad I read the reviews beforehand...definitely cut the sugar to 1 1/2 cups and the bake time to 45 minutes (next time I might even bake for 35-40 minutes to preserve some of the moisture). I also added 1/2 teaspoon each of allspice and nutmeg and I am glad I did, it gives the cake a wonderful flavor! I cannot stress enough that the batter is VERY thick, and it must be pressed into a greased pan. Also the consistency after baking is a bit bread-like, but still very good! I am sending this recipe to friends who requested it! Four stars only because the original recipe requires some changes, but still a winner!

The bad news - I can't stop eating it. The good news - it' delicious AND easy. Who knew that was possible. I made a few changes. I added 1/2 cup of oil and 1/4 cup of apple sauce to make it a bit more on the healthy side. Also, due to my 4-year-old's diabetes, I wanted her to be able to eat this without it taking her sugar through the roof - so I substituted the 2 cups of sugar that it called for, for one cup Splenda, and 1 cup of regular sugar. DELICIOUS. I'm on my way to make it again because I'm taking it to a get-together tonight. Thank you for sharing this wonderful recipe. However, my hips do not thank you. ;-)

attributes.source_text: I'm taking it to a get-together tonight

reviews.review_text: This really was fantastic. Has anyone tried to make muffins with it? I'd like tips on how to bake them in cupcake tins. I did, and everyone went crazy for them, but they're so moist they were hard to lift from the pan when the were hot. Maybe I didn't bake them long enough, because they didn't want to stand proud. The result was a very homemade-looking muffin that everyone went completely crazy for. I've never had luck with paper muffin liners -- they either stick to the pan or to the muffin -- but I wonder if I should try them on this recipe. Anyway, technique suggestions welcomed, because I'm baking for a huge crowd next week. I know there are apple muffin recipes on this site, but this recipe was SO good I don't want to try another.

attributes.source_text: they're so moist

reviews.review_text:
I love this cake!! Have made it twice already and it is always a big hit!! "Batter" is more like a crumble. So don't be surprised when it looks like a bunch of little peas. I too have an apple peeler/ corer/slicer as another reviewer mentioned. Does the apples in about three minutes!! So easy!! 
It's so funny that I just realized that in the picture shown of the cake there is an icing on it!!??  I don't see any recipe for an icing or hadn't noticed if anyone mentioned anything about an icing? Would love to know!! Looks good with a bit of icing too!! Anyone?

This was delicious, fast and easy to make with common pantry ingredients.  Per other reviewers, I half the sugar to 1 cup and added 1/2 teaspoon of nutmeg.  I did not peel the apples.  Used the apple slicer/corer that cut into 8 pieces and then I just chopped them into smaller ones. I had some turbinado sugar and cinnamon on hand for cinnamon toast and sprinkled some of that on top before putting into the oven.  I had the whole thing prepared by the time the oven warmed up.  Very thick batter, denser than quick bread.  I baked for 38 minutes and it was ready.  Would make a good coffee cake.  Thank you.

attributes.source_text: Very thick batter
denser than quick bread

reviews.review_text: This is sooo good! It is so cool how the batter changes when you add the apples. If I hadn't read the previous reviewer saying that the "batter was very dry and hard to handle" I would have thought I did something wrong. I was amazed how the apples change the texture from a dough to a cake batter. Before I added the apples I thought "no way am I going to be able to fold in the apples"...lol Don't fret it really does work out. The combination of the spice and apples is delicious. Really I would give this more than a five star if possible.  It is just about the easiest cake I have ever made and so delicious.I will be making this over and over.

Great cake, and so easy!! I halved the recipe with great results, cutting down the baking time to about 25-30 minutes. Also, by halving it the recipe still called for a whole cup of sugar, and based on other reviews, I only used a half cup and a little brown sugar. It turned out exactly the right sweetness, and nobody knew I had halved it! I might add a couple more spices next time like nutmeg, allspice, ect. though my mom said she loved the spices. When I told her it only had cinnamon she was like, "Woah!" I got 8 medium sized pieces (see my picture) out of the half recipe. Thank you!

attributes.source_text: exactly the right sweetness
my mom said she loved the spices
she loved the spices
it only had cinnamon

reviews.review_text:
I have made this on several occasions, and it has ALWAYS been a huge hit!!!
i have made it according to the ingredients listed, it was wonderful, i have made it with Splenda brown sugar baking blend, it was wonderful, i have made it with 1/2 white sugar & 1/2 splenda (1 cup of each), and it was wonderful. i like the fact that i can make this with Splenda, and be able to have my diabetic friends and family enjoy this cake with the rest of us. no one can tell when i substitute with the Splenda either!!  EVERYONE absolutely LOVES it when i make this, i can't thank you enough for this awesome and easy recipe!!!
