items.label: Angel Food Cake - Homemade
items.name: Angel Food Cake - Homemade
items.description: This is a MUST if you have never tried a homemade Angel Food Cake. I never liked Angel Food Cakes until the neighbor lady invited me over for coffee shortly after I was married. That was almost 15 years ago, and my children and husband always ask for this for special occasions. Thank you Artie, for being a wonderful friend and for the recipe!
instructions: Note: For those not use to making angel food cakes Don't get any yoke in the whites, if you do throw out and start over.  I always separate the egg in a glass first.  Then if no yoke pour into measuring container.
DO NOT GREASE PAN.
I always use a two piece angelfood cake pan.
Heat oven to 375°.
Sift the cake flour and 3/4 cup + 2 Tbsp sugar separately; set aside.
Combine the extracts in a small bowl; set aside.
Beat egg whites, cream of tartar and salt until it forms peaks.
Add the other 3/4 cup of sugar slowly, then beat on high until stiff peaks form.
If you have a mixing guard for your mixer bowl now would be a good time to attach it.
Beating on LOW, add flour mixture and extracts slowly.
Make sure you fold in the sides and bottom of your mixing bowl.
(You can fold in flour mixture by hand but this way is faster.) Spoon into an angel food cake pan.
Move a knife through batter to remove air pockets.
Bake 30-35 minutes or until top springs back when touched lightly with finger.
Invert pan onto a tin funnel to cool completely.
To remove the cake from your pan run a knife around the rim of the cake pan just to get the 'crust' away from the pan.
Then firmly spank the sides of your pan.
You could use a knife but this sometime tears the sides of the cake.
Invert onto your serve plate then take the knife to the now top which was the bottom of your pan and gently cut cake away from the  pan insert.
No need to cut around the center tube as you just give the cake a gently but firm tap or downward shake on to the plate.
Or you can pick up plate while holding onto the pan insert with your thumbs and firmly strike the bottom of the plate onto a folded towel.  (Just give it a slam down on the towel/table).

reviews.review_text: This is the simplest and most effective AFC recipe I've found. Thanks for sharing! My observations and suggestions: No fat! No greasing the pan, not even a drop of yoke in the whites, no wooden spoons (contain natural oil), no plastic or latex bowls or utensils (oil adheres), wash hands before and during prep (especially if a yoke breaks). The reasons many AFC'so fail are due to one or more of the following: an introduction of oil, not beating the whites long enough (beyond a medium peak), not sifting ingredients, use of a non-stick pan (the batter must stick so that it can climb as it bakes), and, not handling the beaten whites gingerly. For this recipe I heeded caution and I did reduce the sugar by just 2 T. The sweetness turned out perfectly for me though following the recipe precisely would have been fine too. My oven is precise, so I reduced baking temp to 350 and baked for 40 mins. which turned out perfectly. I sifted my ingredients twice. I also used extra fine granulated sugar (carried by most grocery stores near the brown and powdered sugar section). Finally, folded in the final ingredients, using a large stainless steel spoon, then I spooned the batter into my fluted pan rather than poured. The cake turned out beautifully, and we ate it both plain and with a strawberry sauce. Next time I am going to make it with caramel flavoring, as another reviewer suggested.

attributes.source_text: The sweetness turned out perfectly for me

reviews.review_text: I did a small 8-portion first as I'd never baked this or had it ever anywhere. I think I'd vaguely heard of it but I've never seen it on sale here in the UK either. I didn't know there was such a thing as an angel cake tin either! I thought I'd try it anyway as was curious about the 'angel food' texture so I've got one now. It was fine so I made the larger 16-slice today for the Easter weekend. I like Derf's idea of fruit/cream in the tunnel so will do that. I will make icing to cover but haven't decided on conventional or Mascarpone yet or fruit choice, it will be chosen tomorrow; I don't fancy whipped cream, it will be served with cream & custard anyway. I am not really a fan of plain cake & don't go into raptures even when it is this airy so I don't know if I will make it again unless baking with grandchildren. 2 tips, a buttered flat palette knife helped to loosen the cake from the pan, yes, a few brown bits came off, just a few. and there are lots of gadgets on the market for egg white/egg separation. I ALWAYS crack my eggs into a bowl/cup first before using anywhere (I hate the 2 gelatinous streaks attached to the yolks which I spoon out) so that is easiest before adding to the separator - you don't get shell bits in your food either. I used the unused yolks fried with tomatoes/mushrooms for brunch.

attributes.source_text: even when it is this airy
for the Easter weekend

reviews.review_text: This recipe worked for me (used my own farm eggs that were about a week old).  I'll try it a couple of more times to see if I can get consistent results.<br/><br/>Remember, the reason you do not grease the pan is so that the cake can "grab" the sides to climb (rise).  My guess is that people are using a non-stick pan or spraying them with a bit of oil and that is the reason the cake falls.<br/><br/>UPDATED 05-21-2014:  I have used this recipe many times and each time it has worked out perfectly!!!   I've changed up the flavorings and have used caramel extract which is my new favorite!

attributes.source_text: have used caramel extract which is my new favorite

reviews.review_text: This recipe does make a delicious cake but the instructions are not very clear. Basically you use 1.5 cups of sugar total. -Half you add to the cake flour and sift/combine to have your bowl of dry ingredients. -Then you beat 12 egg whites until peak forms, then slowly add the other 3/4 cup sugar while you continue to beat until stiff peaks form. -Then you slowly fold or beat (on low) in your dry ingredients. I think I've made 7 of these and 6 have been really good. One I messed up but that's part of the fun. Oh ya and little home-whipped cream and macerated strawberries really set it off! I made a 1 minute time lapse of me making one recently, check it out: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V6l4s4nIv1Q

This is truly a heavenly angel food cake and the one I will always use to delight my guests. It is the best angel food cake I have ever had and came out perfectly when followed correctly. In addition to measuring accurately and precisely following all directions, i.e., eggs at room temperature, no yolks, using knife to remove air pockets in cake before baking, I would add a few tips: It is important to use the correct cake pan. I purchased the Nordicware Classic Angel Food Cake Pan from Williams Sonoma. I can’t say that I would have the same cake without it. This pan should not be greased or sprayed since angel food cake needs to “climb up” the sides of the pan and will not fall out of the pan when it is later flipped to cool. I also highly recommend watching Martha Stewart’s video (“Martha Bakes” on removing angel food cake from pan) for great tips. If you don’t have time to wait for eggs to be room temperature, place the egg whites in a in a bowl within a warm water bowl to speed up the process; just make sure your water is not too warm or you will cook your eggs!). I also prefer using brown, organic eggs. When preparing the ingredients in advance I put the sugar/flour mixture in one bowl and then the separate sugar (3/4 cup) in another bowl. Each of these went through my sifter 3x . When baking the cake, try to wait as long as possible without opening the oven door or moving the cake since if you do this too early it may collapse. Angel food cake is very tricky and you can do everything right, but one little thing wrong can mess it up! I did not use a convection oven setting and my cake took about 35 minutes to bake, but every oven will be a little different and you will need to check towards the end. I baked my cake at night, inverted the pan, let it cool over night and removed it in the morning. I would make sure your cake completely cools before you remove it. I love serving this cake with fresh strawberries and homemade whipped cream. Thank you so much for sharing this wonderful recipe!

attributes.source_text: to delight my guests

reviews.review_text:
Absolutely amazing cake!!! Thank you, Charlotte, for the easy and excellent step by step instructions!!!  I've always loved Angel Food and had never made it...
I chose this recipe because of all the 5* ratings, and they were dead on!
In case it's helpful, for 12 large egg whites I used what other websites suggested as equivalent and measured 1 1/2 cups egg whites and actually only used 9 eggs. Evidently eggs here (in Argentina) are bigger :) ?
Since we don't have cake flour down here, I looked up the equivalent to 1 cup minus 2 tbsp flour, and weighed 110 grams of flour and then added 2 tbsp cornstarch.
I cut the cake in half and filled it with whipped cream and strawberries, and frosted it with light pink Italian Meringue made with a recipe adapted from ?Mastering the Art of French Cooking? by Julia Child that was printed in the New York Times and posted in the internet by MARIAN BURROS.  To cut all the sweetness of the meringue I served the slices with a side of sliced strawberries and blueberries.
Everyone at my friend's birthday party raved about this marvelous cake.  Again, Charlotte, thank you for such an excellent recipe!

I was looking for a recipe to use to enter in the county fair. I made this once and found out the things that I needed to do differently. The first time I made it I put the flour and sugar in my sifter and ran it through once. The flour was clumping when I was adding it, so the second time I sifted it 3 times to make sure it was all mixed together well. I also mixed it in by hand which takes a little longer but it works better. So when I made it the second time and entered it in the fair I not only got a blue ribbon, but I also got "Best of Show"! Fabulous cake!

OMG, Angel Food Cake is my all time favorite cake and NOW I can make it from scratch! Thanks so much. Much better than store bought. Most of the time I will make it plain or serve with fruit but I made it for Easter and iced it with recipe #22181 . As a kid this was my favorite way to have Angel Food Cake (and still is) ymmmm.
*******************************************
7/08 I made the cake again for the umpteen time but my internet was down so I tried to remember all the ingredients, etc.  I forgot to add the sugar to the eggwhite at first and when I did, the whole recipe dropped and I thought I had a liquid mess.  I cooked it in two round cake pans and although it wasn't light and fluffy, like normal... it was still delicious... good as strawberry shortcake base.  I just love this recipe... even when I mess it up!  :-)

attributes.source_text: I made it for Easter

reviews.review_text:
Yum,yum....yum!  Just bought a angel food cake pan and saw this recipe had the most stars, so I decide it use it, now I know why!!
I was planning on using the liquid white eggs in the carton, even bought an extra one so I'd have enough to equal the 12 eggs but I read the carton before hand an it said not to use for angel food cakes because of pasturization.  So, I only had 10 eggs and used the carton stuff to make up the 2 I was missing.  Also sub'd all but 1/2 cup of baking sugar with Slenda.  Added 1 tsp. fresh lemon juice.  It didn't get as tall as the picture but came out tasting great...I would definately make it again. Serving it with fresh California strawberries. Thanks so much for the recipe.

Fantastic tasting cake!  I don't own an angel food cake pan-so I used a bundt and a medium loaf pan (after reading some of the reviews, I was nervous about the cake spilling over the bundt).  I reduced the time to 20 minutes, and everything came out nicely.  

I made the mistake of not reading the directions completely, so I tried to remove the cakes without allowing them to cool fully.  I ripped one of the cakes, but was able to piece it back together, and with some chocolate glaze and strawberries, you'd never know!

i have this angel food cake, but one thing, if you really want to "WOW" it, get a pint of cream, and whip it, but add also just a few drops of peppermint in it... now that's a wow!!! and it tastes Devine!!!! i also cut the middle of the angel food cake, and layer it with the cream mixture, then add the rest of the mixture on top and the sides. THEN! i take fresh or store bought strawberries, or whatever you want, cut them in halves and add them here and there to the top of the cake. Then i shave chocolate hard pieces to the top here and there. It really doesn't take much time to do! And you'll have a lot of compliments ;o)

This was my first attempt at angel food cake and it was a hit. I used 2 tsp lemon extract instead of the vanilla and almond. I also made 4 mini angel food cakes instead of one big one, and baked for 25 minutes. I served mine with a raspberry whipped cream made by adding 1/4 strained raspberry puree to fresh whipped cream.

This recipe was really good, really pillowy and soft, and really easy to follow. I might cut back on the sugar a little bit because it was quite sweet for my taste, but it was still very good. I will definitely be using it again!

attributes.source_text: really pillowy and soft
really pillowy and soft

reviews.review_text: by far the best!!!!  my boyfriend LOVES angel food cake and has been begging me to make him a homemade one for over a year.  i made this one and will NEVER go back to using boxed cake mix again. i added slightly more almond extract and more vanilla extract to mine and it was so moist and light and delicious. the cake was gone that evening and there are 5 people in his house hold. people kept sneaking extra slices.. my boyfriend even got up 3 times in the night just to have another piece =) i frosted mine with sweetened whipped cream and topped with fresh berries (rasberries, blueberries, strawberries and blackberries) YUM.. this is a staple for sure

my boyfriend even got up 3 times in the night just to have another piece

light and delicious

reviews.review_text: This recipe is PERFECT. I've repeated this recipe four times and it's improved with every try. This past try ended up being a perfect bake and it was just so gorgeous and delicious. I followed the recipe exactly except that I fold in the flour mixture instead of beating it. This seems to really improve the volume, even though it takes more time. Also, it's a BIT too sweet for me and I'm still figuring out where to remove some of that sugar. Still, amazing amazing cake. This will definitely be at Thanksgiving this year!

attributes.source_text: This will definitely be at Thanksgiving this year

reviews.review_text: I'm hoping someone may comment or message an idea as to what I may have done wrong. Like a few people, I ended up with a squished cake. It was much smaller than it should be, probably at least half size tall. It tasted fine, though it did burn a little on one side. I was always taught by my family to use a paper bag for non stick at the bottom of the pan. At other recommendations, I also tried to do 350 instead of 375 for 40-45 mins instead of 30-35 mins, though I watched it closely. So any recommendations on how to make it rise properly?

items.label: Chewy Double Chocolate Chip Cookies
items.name: Chewy Double Chocolate Chip Cookies
items.description: I got this recipe from my best friend, and we sat down and ate quite a few. You can not stop at one, they are very chocolaty and additive. YUMMY!
instructions: Cream together the butter, sugar, then add the eggs and vanilla.
Blend in the cocoa and add baking soda, salt and blend well.
Add the flour into the creamed mixture and fold in the chocolate chips.
Bake at 350° for 8-9 minutes.

reviews.review_text:
I have named these my mmmm Good, Got Milk cookies.  These are truely one of the best cookies I have tried.  Here are the changes I made to the recipe.

1.  Substituted 1 cup Crisco + 3 Tbl water + 1/4 cup butter for margarine.  This eliminated the problem others talked about with the cookies being too oily.  I also cooked on parchment paper.

2. Used 1 cup sugar and 1 cup brown sugar per others suggestion.

3. Used hershey's premium dark cocoa.

4.  Used 1 cup white chocolate chips and 1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips per others suggestion.

5.  Make sure to really blend well in step 3 so the eggs actually fluff up the batter some. And don't blend much when adding the flour or your cookies will be tough.

I made larger cookies (slightly over flowing #50 scoop) and baked for 14 minutes.

They came out soft and chewy and oh so delicious. THANK YOU Tweety Grams for a terrific recipe!

attributes.source_text: They came out soft and chewy
They came out soft and chewy

reviews.review_text: Made these last night. The recipe is similar to the Tollhouse chocolate chip recipe except for the addition of cocoa and there's the problem. Although the flavor was good the cookies were too dry. Whenever you add cocoa powder to a recipe, you need to reduce the amount of flour by the amount of cocoa powder you'll be using. So the flour used should be 1-1/4 cups flour and 3/4 cups cocoa powder. The result will be a moister and chewier cookie. I also used 3/4 cups granulated sugar and 3/4 cups brown sugar instead of 2 cups granulated sugar. I also divided the dough in two and rolled it into two long logs in plastic wrap and chilled the dough for a couple of hours until it was firm enough to slice. Chilling will help to keep the cookies from spreading too much and slicing a log is less of a hassle than scooping out 1 tablespoon of dough for each cookie.

I accidentally made these cookies with 3/4 cup of butter instead of 1 1/4 cups!! I'd  like to say this was a rookie mistake, but I'm a seasoned baker and bake at least once a week. It was a rushed mistake I guess. Anyhow, I've tasted these cookies warm and cooled and they taste very good. I'm curious to know though, how they would taste had I used the appropriate amount of butter. I will definitely make them again (using the correct amount of butter). Like other reviewers, I used 1 cup of regular sugar and 1 cup of brown sugar and I used 1/2 cup of white chips and 1 1/2 cups of semi-sweet chocolate chips.  I'm sure peanut butter chips would taste good too.  I love chewy, gooey chocolate chip cookies and these were just that!  Great recipe!

attributes.source_text: I love chewy, gooey chocolate chip cookies and these were just that
I love chewy, gooey chocolate chip cookies and these were just that

reviews.review_text: I changed the amount to 6 cookies and actually got 12 cookies. I used a tablespoon to drop them on an ungreased cookie sheet. I also sub'd with half brown/white sugar. I didn't use egg either. I used an egg replacement (1Tb ground flaxseed & 3Tb water, simmered 3 min, cooled. Equals 1 egg.) I used 3Tb butter and 2Tb oil. Baked for about 12 min. They were perfect. I'd suggest not flattening them. Just drop by tablespoonful. Update: I made these with oil instead and they still came out great! Another update: Used only 1/2C oil and all brown sugar. Still came out great! One thing though DO NOT pack the brown sugar because it will be too sweet. Can't go wrong with this recipe.

Yum!!!  I did double the recipe, and I'm glad I did.  I was concerned that 5 sticks of butter was going to make them greasy, but they weren't.  The batter was pretty thick and it did make so much that my Kitchenaid stand mixer found it kind of tough to mix, but we made it.  I can't stand crunchy, overbaked cookies, so I took out my first several sheets right at 8 minutes, and then let them sit for 5 minutes or so before moving them to the cooling rack.  I didn't taste one until all I had left was my last sheet, and I decided then to leave that last sheet in for 9 minutes.  I think those were better.  They were still pretty doughy at 8 minutes.  These are very sweet, but I wouldn't change a thing!  I got 6 dozen 2 inch cookies.  I liked the looks of the ones I flattened a bit better than ones I didn't.  Fantastic cookies, and I'm excited to have a new cookie to add to my collection.

attributes.source_text: These are very sweet, but I wouldn't change a thing!

reviews.review_text: Has anybody referred to these as "chocolate heaven" yet??? I started my Christmas baking today, and added this to the lineup because I'm pregnant and had a huge craving for chocolate. These deserve way more than 5 stars - they're everything I was hoping for and more. Great chewy texture, very chocolatey. I halved the recipe this time around (believe me, I'm definitely going to be making some more!!!) but kept the full amount of vanilla in. I used 1/2 white sugar and 1/2 brown sugar per other users' suggestions. I didn't have any problems with spreading. Baked for 8 1/2 minutes and got approximately 40 (2.5 inch) cookies out of the half bath I did. Thanks sooooooooooooooo much for posting this!!!!

attributes.source_text: I started my Christmas baking today
Great chewy texture
very chocolatey

reviews.review_text: We enjoyed these so much!  Deep chocolate flavor and really nice texture.  I had no margarine and was leery of using that much butter, so I used shortening, and it did just fine.  That is the only adjustment I made ... usually I try not to change ingredients on the first-run of a recipe.  I wondered myself about using that much white sugar and contemplated doing half and half, white and brown sugars - I wimped out and now wish I had done it for the chewiness, which is fine now, but maybe could be better.  Loved that the recipe called for 2 tsp. of vanilla!  I ALWAYS do that when 1 tsp. is called for, and so do most bakers that I know, so here's an honest recipe, for sure.  Oh, one thing I did was mix the cocoa with the sugar and shortening to eliminate the chance of the cocoa clumping.  And I mixed the salt and soda with the flour which is pretty standard in cookiedom.  I have made chocolate chip cookies for fifty-seven years ... these are my first chocolate chocolate chips, and I will make it often, I know.  I really like the recipe, and I recommend it highly as is, but I still plan to fiddle with it!

attributes.source_text: Deep chocolate flavor

reviews.review_text: I found this recipe a few years ago, and it is still my go-to for chocolate cookies. I use butter, and I sub half the sugar with brown sugar, but I don't change quantities of anything. A spoonful of fresh-mixed dough on a cookie sheet baked to a nice puffy dome of a cookie in 9 minutes at 350 (it flattens a bit after cooling, of course). I don't understand how people are ending up with flat/runny cookies. It must be in the mixing process. Be sure to whip together room temp butter & sugar a few minutes until fluffy before adding the eggs one at a time. I can't imagine what else the problem could be. These cookies are excellent!

attributes.source_text: baked to a nice puffy dome of a cookie

reviews.review_text: We try to consider health issues when attempting a recipe. I halved the recipe and replaced margarine, cocoa, sugar, and chips with real butter, Stevia/Truvia, carob powder, and carob chips. I expected these would flatten but to my surprise...no. So before they finished, I pressed them down with a spoon. They also came out a tad dry so I put a few drops of safflower oil on each one and let the heat of the oven moisten them. You could also use a touch of coconut oil. These are healthy oils. Stevia is a natural sweetener and lets you use half the amount of sugar in any recipe. These came out soft, chewy, and delicious. This became a calorie- and sugar-reduced, and caffeine free treat.

attributes.source_text: These came out soft, chewy, and delicious
These came out soft, chewy, and delicious

reviews.review_text: Ehhh. These are ok. 3.5 stars. The recipe definitely needs to be tweaked. The dough was dry and there were way too many chocolate chips. As others have mentioned, do 1/2 & 1/2 with the sugars. Issues: -Less flour. 2 C. is too much. Maybe 1 1/4? (plus the 3/4 C cocoa powder might be enough dry ingredients). -Less chocolate chips. I found that 2 C is too much; they didn't stick in the dough at all and I ended up removing many chips. You want an equal dough to chip ratio. -My cookies didn't flatten; I had to hand-press them prior to putting them in the oven. They cracked on top too. They were crisp on the outside and chewy, which was good.

These are Delicious cookies, moist and chewy. To those that had flat cookies make sure that you have fresh baking soda. items.label: Kittencal's Famous Caesar Salad
items.name: Kittencal's Famous Caesar Salad
items.description: I developed this dressing years ago, and I can honestly say that you won't be able to keep your spoon out of the fridge for a taste, it is *that* good! --- although I do think the dressing is better with the anchovy it can certainly be made without them. In a pinch I have even substituted buttermilk for the half and half cream, just use about the same amount --- this dressing gets stronger with refrigeration time so a small amount of fresh garlic goes a long way! ---- usually one recipe without doubling is perfect for one large romaine lettuce, if you are serving a large crowd of people you might want to double -- salad dressing will not work for this use *only* mayonnaise, I find Hellman's brand mayonnaise works the best and for the  perfect companion to this salad see my recipe#125034-------------LOWER-FAT OPTION use reduced fat mayonnaise and fat-free half and half or low-fat milk --- also see my recipe#66596
instructions: In a small 2-cup mini food processor, process/mince the anchovy fillets and garlic together until finely minced (do this together and firstly, otherwise it will not get minced properly with the other ingredients).
Add in the remaining ingredients, and process for 30 seconds, or more until well mixed.
Adjust seasonings to taste.
Thin with buttermilk (or milk) for a thinner consistency if desired.
Store in fridge, covered in a glass container for 3 or more hours before using (the flavors become stronger when left in the fridge for a longer time).
Toss desired amount of dressing with Romaine lettuce and croutons.
Sprinkle with more grated Parmesan cheese if desired.

reviews.review_text: When I was looking for a Caesar dressing recipe, your's was the first to come up so, naturally, I looked no further. It is wonderful. I grated the Parm myself so to others who grate their Parmesan and end up with a fluffy cheese, make sure to pack it into the cup when measuring or else the end product will be weaker than intended.<br/><br/>I cooked this recipe http://www.food.com/recipe/4-minute-spicy-garlic-shrimp-107997 to go with my salad (minus the Montreal Seasoning) and the combination was a Ten Star Meal for sure.<br/><br/>Great recipe, once again. I made this again with Fish Sauce instead of anchovies. Used a teaspoon of yellow mustard and a splash of white wine vinegar instead of dijon. It was still so so so so good. I could just eat it with a spoon... .or on my shoe... it's THAT GOOD.

Dear Kittencal, I love your recipes but I must say some of them are too decadent for me. I have to avoid butter and cream for health reasons. Here I used another recipe #36134 for croutons (it had olive oil instead of butter) and in your dressing I used only milk (no half-and-half) plus 1/2 cup of mayo instead of 1. I didn't thin the dressing. In the end I found it was still a bit too creamy/too much (I don't like my salads dripping of dressing) but I guess this is due to the fact that the lettuce was maybe smaller than the one you used. The taste was awesome though and my DH took two helpings more. I will be making this again for sure! Thanks for posting, for a long time I've been eating caesar salad only in restaurants and wondering what the taste of a home made ceasar salad would be!

attributes.source_text: my DH took two helpings more

reviews.review_text: Love, love, love this recipe!  This makes possibly the best Caesar dressing I've ever had.  I put grilled chicken in this, and my 13 year old son had three helpings (he would've had more, but we ran out of lettuce!).  The only word of caution I would say is to stick with the recipe as far as garlic goes -- the second time I made this, I thought I'd add more garlic because my family are such garlic lovers, but if you let this sit for an hour or more (as you should) the garlic becomes very intense.  Even as a serious garlic lover, I'd have to say that anything more than what is written here is probably too much.  Other than that, I used about 1-2 tbs of anchovy paste, and it was wonderful.  After loving at least 10 of her recipes, it's about time that I say that Kittencal is my go-to recipe guru.  She has yet to steer me wrong.

attributes.source_text: my 13 year old son had three helpings

reviews.review_text: I cannot believe I have not reviewed this yet...  ooops... I wanted a grilled chicken caesar salad for dinner and ALWAYS use this dressing.  No other dressing even comes close... restaurant or bottled!  My BF claims he "hates" anchovies but does not complain one bit as he devours his salad and then proceeds to lick any remaining dressing stuck to the bowl!!!  I use 2-3 anchovy fillets, 2-3 large garlic cloves, 2% organic milk, freshly grated parmesan, fresh lemon juice ( as if there were any other!!!) stone ground mustard, and organic worcestershire.  I do thin it out with a bit of milk because it is quick thick... but soooooooooo delicious.  It does get stronger as it sits in the fridge, but it usually does not last more than 2 days around here!!!  Thanks for a keeper for life!!!

reviews.review_text: Wow!  I am speechless!  This was so amazingly delicious.  It couldn't have been any easier to prepare, it made a considerable amount, and it tasted unbelievable! I placed three, large leaves of romaine lettuce leaves (with the very bottom broken off) on a salad plate.  I then tossed a few croutons over the leaves.  I drizzled the dressing over this and shredded fresh parmesan cheese on top.  At the table, I cracked fresh pepper over the salads of those who wanted it.  Everyone was raving about the dressing!  Several even dared to lick their forks!  As I left, I told my parents that I put the remainder of the dressing in the refrigerator.  My dad actually said, "Great!  Thanks, that's fantastic!" items.label: Potato Kielbasa Skillet
items.name: Potato Kielbasa Skillet
items.description: Make and share this Potato Kielbasa Skillet recipe from Food.com.
instructions: In dutch oven, brown potatoes, kielbasa, onion and peppers in oil.
Add seasonings and water.
Bring to a boil.
Cover tightly and cook for 20 minutes on low, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and put cheese on top.
Simmer until cheese is melted.

reviews.review_text: 1.5 cups = 12 oz. Beer comes in a 12 oz bottle. Coincidence? I think not. I used beer instead of water and it was definitely what the kielbasa was asking for. I like my recipes a little more precise... a large potato can vary tremendously depending on the type you're using. I decided to use 3 lbs, which was only 3 large russet potatoes. I think the potato/kielbasa ratio was pretty good with this measure, although I might have liked just a touch more kielbasa. All the kielbasa in my grocery store came in 12 oz packages, not 16 oz. So I had to dip into a second package to get 1 lb... very annoying. There was a bit too much liquid... I may have to take a few hits off my beer before I poor it in! I used olive oil instead of vegetable oil, cheddar instead of American and I got 6 servings, not 4. Oh yeah, the recipe doesn't specify, but the oregano and basil measures are for dried herbs; use a tablespoon each if you use fresh.

I'm only giving 3 stars for this because although it was tasty, it wasn't an overwhelming hit, AND the recipe directions are not very good.  For one thing, the time to make - 28 minutes is a complete fallacy.  The recipe says to add all the ingredients and brown the potatoes - it doesn't give any clue of how long it will take, but I can tell you that I sautéed the potatoes for over 10 minutes, and they still were not brown.  At this point, I was up to 15-20 minutes of prep (all the chopping) and cook time.  I added the other ingredients (I used chicken stock as some other reviewers suggested, unfortunately, I did not read the review that said the recipe had too much liquid, and I added a hole can - 14oz - of stock).  It then took another 5 minutes to bring to a boil.  I set the timer for 5 minutes so I could uncover and stir.  When I checked after 5 minutes, now down to low, it didn't seem like the potatoes would cook.  After 10 minutes,  turned the heat back up.  When the 20 minutes were done, the potatoes had finally softened (I used red bliss), but, there was a lot of liquid left so I left the lid off and let it simmer another 10 minutes.  If you are keeping track, we are up to 55 minutes.  I finally added the cheese, and that seemed to make the liquid into more of a sauce, and the result was pretty good - very tasty, it reminded me of sausage and peppers that I make, and I ended up sopping up some of the gravy with bread - so very carb heavy meal.  I wish I could figure out a good vegetable to have with it (besides a salad).

attributes.source_text: the potatoes had finally softened

reviews.review_text: I used real stuffed polish sausage that I got at my grocery store (not Kielbassa), and this recipe just didn't work for me.  Perhaps if the sausage was removed from the casing it would have been better, but I felt like I was chewing elastic bands.  Was it supposed to be a stew?  Maybe it should be finished in the oven, uncovered, to let the broth reduce?  I love cheese of all kinds, but this was an indignity to cheddar!  It curdled when left to simmer.  I used slightly less water, fresh basil, a bit of beef boullion and red pepper flakes, but nothing could help this loser.  Now I have to send my husband to work with it, since I didn't have a back-up plan :(  Sorry for the bad review.

This is very good. I used a can of chicken broth in place of the water, figuring if it was too watery when the time was up I would just drain the extra broth off. No need to drain, it cooked down to a thickend sauce so that when I added the cheese it made almost a thick cheese sauce. I didn't have any kielbasa so I used Mild Italian Sausage links. They worked great, gave a nice flavor. I am going to try this same recipe with other meats, maybe chicken or beef. I think it will be very easy to tweak. Thanks MizzNezz for another keeper!

reviews.review_text: An amazing recipe!! It's hard to find new options for Kielbasa--we used the turkey variety. I used about 2 cups diced potatoes--the recipe calls for a lot more but that seemed like too much for my husband's tastes. I also skipped the green pepper (he doesn't like them) & added some garlic powder into the seasoning mix. I used a low fat Mexican cheese, and my potatoes were cooked in about 15 min--probably since I reduced the amount. I sure liked the one skillet convenience & my husband ate it right up. Thanks so much for sharing!

Absolutely wonderful combination of flavors! I did alter recipe somewhat - omitted green peppers (they don't like our tummies)and cut back on the cheese (used all I had in fridge). My potatoes created enough water I didn't need to add any but this was just wonderful. I served with steamed carrots, corn bread and blackberry cobbler for dessert. Thanks for posting - we'll be making this again and again!!

1/5/08 I have made this several times since my original edit. This last time I did make with the green peppers - they add incredible flavor (even if we do suffer a little after)! I added 1 cup pale wheat beer and OMG! This has quickly become an often requested supper dish that I am more than glad to make upon request. Thank you again for an awesome recipe!!

reviews.review_text: Made this last night and it smelled wonderful - hubby couldn't wait to try.  We loved it with one exception, I only had Velveeta and it made the dish way to rich and thick.  Next time I won't use the cheese at all, or leave it on the side for each person to choose because we felt it really didn't need it. I did blanch the Kielbasa in hot water to remove some of the fat so it wouldn't be greasy then added it after the veggies softened. This will be a dish I can use while camping this summer. Give it a try, you'll enjoy.

I had a weird mix of ingredients to use up and nothing was enough to make much with.  This recipe used up the 1 potato, 2 kielbasa, 1/2 onion & 1/2 green pepper that were all begging to be eaten!  I was amazed when I found it.  Even more so when we ate it this morning for breakfast.  I scaled down the recipe to compensate for the ingredient amounts and it was just feeding two of us anyway.  The only ingredient change I made was to use a 4-cheese Mexican blend instead of American.  It was so delicious!  DH, myself & even our toddler loved the flavor.  I wouldn't change a thing & I would make it for dinner or breakfast, anytime!  :)  Thanks for sharing, MizzNezz!

reviews.review_text: I really hate giving bad reviews but this meal was not liked very much by myself or my family. I made it expecting what was in the picture and wound up with some kind of soupy mush of half-boiled/half-mashed potatoes, kielbasa and chopped vegetables. I followed the instructions up until I realized that the water was not going to evaporate. After that, I removed the lid and let it cook for the rest of the time (9 minutes), stirring occasionally to cook all of the potatoes. I wound up ladling out some of the soupy stuff so it would evaporate and I ended up with potatoes that turned (almost) to mush. We also found it pretty bland and we all doused it with ketchup to eat it. I really wish I would have taken a picture of the look that was exchanged between my son and husband when I sat the plates in front of them. The first thing out of my husband's mouth was, "That doesn't look like the picture on the recipe card." And he is completely right. Many people try a recipe based on the picture. I really wish the picture that is posted as the main photo would be taken to illustrate a recipe that isn't altered so much that it winds up looking nothing like the way it is supposed to turn out. Overall, the picture difference was bad but I would have had the same review of this recipe if the picture would have matched whatever I wound up with. I will definitely NOT be making this again. I will also post a picture of what mine looked like since I've seen quite a few reviews describing something similar to what I had.

Yummy. ... winged it using a round Polish sausage... I cooked ths onion, capsicum, sausage and herbs plus salt and pepper altogether first and softened the potatoes in the microwave (just to speed up the cooking) once the potatoes were done warming up I added them to the pan and browned them off a little before adding just 1 cup of water. I added tasty cheddar cheese at the end. .. was beautiful. I served with fresh crisp corn on the cob with a bit of butter. I'm pretty sure my neighbours were jealous with the awesome smells coming from my kitchen. ;) can't wait to make it for friends and family.

Personally, I don't think this had much flavor. It wasn't quite as tasty as I thought it would be. After reading some of the reviews, I sautéed the peppers and onions in a little olive oil before adding the potatoes and kielbasa. I only added three potatoes. I added a cup of water and only boiled it for about 10 minutes and then the potatoes seemed super soft, so I pulled it off the burner. I used shredded Swiss cheese instead of American. It was a filling dish, but I was a little disappointed!

attributes.source_text: the potatoes seemed super soft

reviews.review_text: This was really good.  I cut the recipe in half, and had enough for 2 adults and a toddler for dinner.  I also cut down on the liquid at the end, using just under a half cup water with chicken boullion added, also cutting down on the salt.  I do think you need the liquid, it helped to deglaze my cast iron dutch oven and all the stuck cruchy bits were added to the potato/sausage mix.  My yukon potatoes were a bit soft, so next time I will cut down on the liquid even more.  A great recipe overall, will make it again!

attributes.source_text: for 2 adults and a toddler for dinner

reviews.review_text: Definately a yummy recipe.  I do wish there was a more specific measurement on the potatoes, as they can really vary in size.  I used 3 large russets and that seemed like plenty to me.  Also when it was finished there was still a lot of water in the bottom of the skillet which I drained off.  Next time I will use less.  I left the skins on the potatoes, subbed in a Mediterranean Herb Chedder that we had and served with fried eggs and toast for a breakfasty type supper.

attributes.source_text: for a breakfasty type supper
a breakfasty type supper

reviews.review_text: My wife and I loved this.  I changed a few little things up...I sauteed the onion and pepper in olive oil and then added potatoes and kielbasa.  I transferred to a large pot (I have no dutch oven) and browned the potatoes a little.  I added a little less water, probably a cup, and covered the pot to steam the potatoes.  Then I cooked all the excess water away and it was really good.  I used colby jack on top because I love that cheese.  This is a keeper!  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: My wife and I loved this

reviews.review_text: This was a perfectly nice, easy, tasty meal that came together in the amount of time promised.  Looking for gourmet?  Keep looking, but if you want a stick to your ribs tasty, fast meal this checks all of the boxes.  I read the reviews and reduced the liquid - I used used chicken stock.  As a cheese lover I didn't really understand the comments about leaving out the cheese but frankly it would taste just fine without.  Definitely a keeper recipe for rushed evenings.

attributes.source_text: for rushed evenings

reviews.review_text: MizzNezz I love this recipe.  Easy dinner fixings on a week night.  I left the skins on the potatoes, sliced slivers of sweet red peppers along with green peppers.  Just as the potatoes started to brown, I added the spices and water.  Covered and let simmer.   Was not soupy nor like a stew as others posted.  It was a one pot- plate meal.  Next time instead of water, I may try adding some of my homemade stewed tomatoes to change it up.  Thank you for posting, my family loved it.   I will make again.

attributes.source_text: Easy dinner fixings
on a week night
my family loved it

items.label: Easy Banana Muffins
items.name: Easy Banana Muffins
items.description: Make and share this Easy Banana Muffins recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Mash bananas, add sugar and the slightly beaten egg.
Stir in melted butter.
Stir in dry ingredients.
Spoon into medium size muffin pan (I use the paper muffin cups inside pan).
Bake 20 minutes at 350F degrees - 375F degrees.

reviews.review_text: Great, simple recipe with excellent results!  I had 4 black bananas, so I used all of them and added a smidge more flour and a little more leavening.  I added some chopped walnuts, dates, and the zest of one orange as well.  But, even without those additions, it's a great basic recipe that is so fast to put together.  I had one bowl and the cup that I melted the butter in to wash, you can't beat that!!  I beat the egg in the bottom of the mixing bowl and then put the bananas in and mashed them, that way I didn't have to dirty anything else to beat the egg.  Used muffin liners and they detached easily.  These were a big hit w/ the kids and the grown ups for breakfast this morning!

attributes.source_text: a big hit w/ the kids
and the grown ups
for breakfast this morning

reviews.review_text:
wow, these are very good and oh so easy.
I used 3/4 cup white flour and 3/4 cup whole wheat flour and  1/2 a cup of unpacked brown sugar.  
I might try making them with even less sugar next time. but they were not too sweet with the brown sugar.
I baked them in my convection oven at 350 for 13minutes and they came out perfect.
I did however only get 11 muffins, so I wil have to double the receipe next time as I know these wont last long.
This recipe is a keeper, thanx!

attributes.source_text: they were not too sweet with the brown sugar

reviews.review_text: Absolutely DELICIOUS, DELICATE & MOIST! I've made lots of banana muffin recipes - many add vanilla, but these are perfect just the way they are! I had only one fresh banana and 2 frozen, thawed bananas and the muffins turned out wonderfully - I also made 6 giant muffins instead of 12 medium which are nice for breakfast - they do take a few minutes extra to bake - I'd say approximately 25-30 minutes. I did not have any walnuts on hand but honestly these little gems are so delicious "as is" - this recipe is a keeper - Thank You so much michelle baker!

attributes.source_text: DELICATE
MOIST
which are nice for breakfast

reviews.review_text: Perfect! I was looking for a muffin that wasn't crumbly because my 3 youngest kids still make a big mess when they eat.  This was great - moist and held together just right.  I also liked the fact that this recipe went by number of bananas not cups of mashed bananas - I never know how many cups of frozen bananas I have but I can glance in the freezer and see the number (I just toss them in there whole when they start to get too brown).  These muffins tasted fabulous!  I didn't have any muffin liners so I just greased the muffin tins and they came out just fine. I followed the recipe exactly except I used all whole wheat flour instead of white and added a teaspoon of vanilla and a half teaspoon of cinnamon.  I'd highly recommend you double this recipe if you have kids, the muffins will be gone before you know it!

attributes.source_text: a muffin that wasn't crumbly
my 3 youngest kids still make a big mess when they eat
moist and held together just right
held together just right

reviews.review_text: Thank you for a new awsome recipe for those over-ripe bananas that I often have. For my Hubby and me, it's a keeper. What I liked was that it really easy to make. What I liked the most was their texture and "Great Taste". I did add 1/2 Cup of chopped walnuts and sprinkled a little cinnamin sugar on the to before I put them in the oven. I would like to add chocolate chips in the next batch. There will be a lot of more batches for this recipe. Has anyone ever froze these? If I can, it would be great to have them handy. .

attributes.source_text: For my Hubby and me, it's a keeper

reviews.review_text: These were so easy to make.  I am new to baking and have failed many times but these muffins were so easy to make.  I did like a lot of other people said and substituted 1/2 cup of oats for 1/2 cup of flour and they are super moist and delicious.  I cooked mine at 350 degrees for 20 minutes.  I probably should have cooked them for an extra 2-3 minutes but they are still great!  If you are looking for a sweeter muffin I would definitely add chocolate chips.

attributes.source_text: they are super moist

reviews.review_text: Easiest recipe for a muffin i have ever come across! My 5 yr old daughter and i made a pie pan muffin that will be cut into sqaures for a gift as well as some for the house, we added in a half cup of chocolate chips and omgsh it smelled awesome while cooking. Cooked on 350 for about 25 minutes, used a toothpick at the 15 min mark to test. Have it cooling in pan on the counter by the open window. Cant wait to try a piece!

I made these the other day. They were very good with very few changes. I only got eleven muffins out of the recipe, but they were a nice size with a good dome. I was worried about the amount of baking soda making the muffins taste soapy or bitter, but I left the amount at 1 tsp. and they tasted fine. I used 4 Tbs. butter and about 1 & 1/2 Tbs. Fage 0% plain yogurt. No nuts (my daughter doesn't like them). I did use the 1/2 tsp. salt (recipe says optional), but I think necessary. 1/2 cup shredded sweetened coconut, 1/2 cup combination milk chocolate and dark chocolate chips (it's what I had in the house). I love a recipe that is easy to prepare and tastes really good.

OMG These muffins turned out great. I used four bananas that were really ripe (mine were small) and I also used half brown sugar. I opted not to use the nuts or chocolate and my muffins turned out delicious. I baked them so my family could eat them tomorrow but I tried one tonight after they cooled and want to eat the whole batch. My three year old is up with me and he keeps going over to the table asking for another muffin. I'm gonna have to watch him because I know he'll help himself when he thinks I'm not looking. Great Recipe. Once my family tries them, I'll have to update my review. I know they'll love them. This is definitely a keeper and has such great flavor. I will make these again. Thanks two times because I was craving something sweet and savory.

attributes.source_text: I was craving something sweet
My three year old is up with me and he keeps going over to the table asking for another muffin

reviews.review_text: Very easy recipe with great results! I made a few small modifications - I used 1 cup all-purpose flour & 1/2 cup whole grain oat flour. I added 2 Tbsp of ground flax seed. I did not use salt or chocolate chips, but I did use 1/2 cup of chopped walnuts.  I also sprinkled the tops with cinnamon sugar mix before baking.  Easy enough to make before my daughter even got out of bed - warm muffins for breakfast, yum! Baked at 375 for 20 min.

attributes.source_text: warm muffins for breakfast

reviews.review_text: I made these to use up some wrinkly bananas - was impressed with the ratings, but didn't have very high expectations. The simplicity of the recipe is fab - I didn't even take out the hand mixer, just  a good old fashioned wooden spoon and bowl! Cooked at 375 for about 25 mins, and have the yummiest muffins! Even my toddler gobbled them down, and she is the fussiest in our family! Will for sure become a staple in our house - thanks so much!

attributes.source_text: Even my toddler gobbled them down

reviews.review_text:
these are GREAT..

my little eldery neighbor lady called me at noon...
"honey, I have 2 big really ripe bananna can you use them for something?????"

so in search of a easy banana muffin recipe

in less than a hour I had retreaved her 2 banannas
did a search..
whipped these up popped in the oven
and baked delivered 3 to her  (the one that called me)
4 to my other eldery neighbors( a married couple)
and shared my 5 with myself and my daughter..I have 1 left for later as we (my daughter & I) ate 2 each
I know the recipe calls for 3 banannas BUT I had 2 only...
the taste was still wonderful...
everything else I followed to a T...
it really does make a nice big well rounded muffin...
can't wait to use this recipe again
with the 3 banannas called for..
if 2 taste this good can only imagine how great 3 would be in it..
but if you only have 2 banannas...
never fear..try this one and you will be VERY pleased

attributes.source_text: delivered 3 to her
4 to my other eldery neighbors

reviews.review_text: Wow, I'm impressed! This was super easy to make and tasty. One bowl, quick to mix up, minimal ingredients. The muffins came out of the pan clean without papers (just a bit of cooking spray) and are light, moist & delicious. My go-to banana bread recipe is much heavier than this muffin recipe. But these are lighter in texture and just the right balance of flavors (sweet enough but not too sweet, banana isn't too strong). I will definitely make these again!

attributes.source_text: sweet enough but not too sweet
sweet enough but not too sweet
banana isn't too strong

reviews.review_text: I agree a very easy and fast muffin but also a very moist and tender muffin.  These were mixed up in a flash and popped into the oven to bake while I was getting ready for work.  I did use a combination of Splenda and white sugar along with 1/2 cup chopped pecans.  I left off the chocolate chips but plan on making them with mini-chocolate chips in the future.  Thanks for sharing this delicious recipe.

attributes.source_text: a very moist and tender muffin
a very moist and tender muffin

reviews.review_text: I originally made these for my muffin obsessed three year old son. He loved them! So did everyone who tried them. My VERY picky five year old son even liked them! He liked them so much that I'm currently making them right now for him to take to school as a 'special treat' for his classmates because its his birthday tomorrow. Probably the first kid ever to ask for muffins instead of cookies or cupcakes, but these were the treat he asked for!

attributes.source_text: my muffin obsessed three year old son. He loved them!
My VERY picky five year old son even liked them!
because its his birthday tomorrow

reviews.review_text: Well Happy Easter morning, it certainly was for my sleeping family to wake up to this wonderful muffins under their nose, not one of them woke up in a bad mood!  This was way too easy.  My 16 yr old who only cooks hamburger helper offered to make another batch.  After I smelled the first batch baking, I started a second batch, they just don't know it yet.  Thank you for such a lovely pre-feast muffin.

attributes.source_text: Happy Easter morning
my sleeping family to wake up to this wonderful muffins under their nose

reviews.review_text: I actually have to buy bananas that I know will brown up a bit in a few days because my very picky 3 year old loves them and I have to make them on a weekly basis. :) Easy breakfast for the 6 year old before school and for hubby to eat on his way to work. Sometimes I throw in an additional banana, but other than that the only thing changed is that I bake at 350 for 22 minutes to get a nice brown top.

attributes.source_text: my very picky 3 year old loves them
Easy breakfast for the 6 year old before school
for hubby to eat on his way to work
Easy breakfast for the 6 year old before school

reviews.review_text: These are some pretty delicious, extremely easy banana muffins. I didn't add nuts or chocolate hoping to focus on an intense banana flavor. I would recommend that if you won't be using some pretty outstanding bananas to add the nuts or chocolate to help boost the flavor a bit. However, if you're looking for a nice, not too sweet, mild banana flavored muffin to go with a nice cup of tea - here's your recipe.

attributes.source_text: intense banana flavor
not too sweet
mild banana flavored muffin

reviews.review_text: Good, easy starter base recipe but very unimpressive without any tweaks because the truth is, it could use another banana and some vanilla. [Notice that EVERY FIVE STAR REVIEW DID NOT MAKE IT AS IS!] I ended up making it as written for some muffins then tweaking the rest of the batter. The muffins with some brown sugar substituted in, extra banana, vanilla, & dark choc chips were miles better than the original.

items.label: Charlie's Famous Chicken Salad With Grapes
items.name: Charlie's Famous Chicken Salad With Grapes
items.description: A really great guy I used to work with would make this and bring in to share. We all loved it so much and would beg for more! Sounds strange with the grapes, but it's so good! Allow time for salad to chill.
instructions: Combine all ingredients; chill.
Serve with just about anything- crackers, chips, rolls, bread or bagel.

reviews.review_text: I used this as a base because I wanted to make chicken salad but was out of celery so I decided to make it with grapes instead. I had never made a chicken salad in my life so this was my first venture. I do like to cook I am just not a fan of chicken salad so I never made it. I didn’t follow this recipe to a tee but it was just what I needed to create my own without screwing it up on my first attempt. So I did not use the Worcestershire sauce. I also didn’t use the celery as I didn’t have any. I used chicken but instead of chunked, I shredded it but shredded it chunky not super fine shreds, 1/2 a red onion minced, My grapes were large so I sliced them in three slices not just halved, I used a about a cup but I eyeballed it. I used chopped walnuts, real mayo, not Miracle Whip, A tablespoon of sweet pickle relish, and a 1/2 teas. curry. Just enough mayo for everything to stick together and voila! I actually have a chicken salad I love! If you like a Miracle Whip, and I do, you can use it I’m sure, but I prefer to just put it on my toast or bread rather than make the whole salad with it. If you don’t have the sweet pickle relish you might want to try the MIracle Whip instead but I thought it would be too overpowering with both. Also, it’s really easy to over power with the curry. It can overwhelm and I was going for just a hint. I didn’t measure but it was close the 1/2 a teas, or less. You can always add more so start tiny. Hope you like my rendition and thanks to this poster for giving me the base! Nice!

attributes.source_text: I was going for just a hint

reviews.review_text: I usually do not eat miracle whip but the rest of my family loves it so I took a chance on this recipe. I used the optional cup of chopped pecans in the ingredient list (love pecans.) When I was done putting all of the ingredients together it looked good to me, but I knew my hubby would want the meat to be the main player and it seemed lost amongst the other ingredients in the bowl. I doubled the amount of chicken called for in the recipe and then also doubled the dressing ingredients (miracle whip, salt, and worcestshire sauce) so the salad would not be dry. I served it on croissants and did not tell my husband there were grapes in it (so he wouldn't complain before even trying it.) My entire family absolutely LOVED this recipe. I have never had a chicken salad sandwich from a restaurant that is this good! I will be bringing this to our next family function, for sure! Thanks sooo much!!

attributes.source_text: My entire family absolutely LOVED this recipe

reviews.review_text: This recipe is fab! I was looking for a recipe to use up the remaining chicken from a Sunday roast, but it also had to be relatively low in calories and tasty. Boy did this recipe deliver! The first time I made it, I followed the recipe exactly, apart from the miracle whip as I couldn't find it over this side of the pond (England), so I substituted lighter than light Mayo instead. The second time round (as the first only lasted a few days...oops :op ) I added a couple of tablespoons of some mixed seeds - just as good as the first time! Thanks so much for posting this recipe, its now become a firm favorite for lunch time at work!

attributes.source_text: a firm favorite for lunch time at work

reviews.review_text: This is a new staple at our house! We make it all the time. This recipe also travels great...we make the chicken salad ahead, chill and keep in a cooler, then assemble with bread when we are ready to eat. It's wonderful and easy for travel or great picnicing. I've also made 100 sandwiches for a big gathering, went over great with teens and adults. The only changes I maKe are using real mayo, red grapes only, and sometimes i sub slivered almonds for a healthier choice and instead of celery we might put in celery seed.  It's also good with a pinch of tarragon. Thank you for such a yummy recipe!

attributes.source_text: great picnicing
for a big gathering
went over great with teens and adults
went over great with teens and adults

reviews.review_text:
Awesome and Thank You.  I used cashews since I had them on hand.  I remember this recipe from a deli in CT (or close to it).  I found a need to add a bit more salt and some pepper, but that is for my taste.  Again awesome, I doubled the recipe and stored some in vacuum bags so that it last through the week.  Was so sick of the commercial sandwiches at work, what a nice change, will have some on crackers and a nice sandwich for lunch.  Thanks again for sharing.  The Worcestershire sauce was a great addition, just enough with over powering the salad.  
Very satisfied.

attributes.source_text: a nice sandwich for lunch

reviews.review_text: Great recipe.  The following tips are not meant to detract from original recipe, it was great, just a few tweeks for me personally. I left onions out due to personal taste as they seem to overpower delicate tastes for me but a little onion powder and pepper gives a little flavor without overpowering.  I will cut back on salt next time, I had rotisserie chicken seasoning on my boneless skinless chicken breasts that I baked, and didn't figure the salt in the chicken breasts adding to overall the saltiness.  So use caution if using heavily salted rotisserie chicken or maybe add to taste at the end.  I have previously been a strictly mayo user, but had bought miracle whip for another recipe and was looking to use it up.  This will keep me buying miracle whip, I think that is what adds that little extra tanginess.  Also worcester sauce really added a zip and I loved the recipe!  Thanks.

attributes.source_text: that little extra tanginess

reviews.review_text: I have tried this recipe 3 different times.  The first time I made it with some chicken breasts I cooked in stock, and I followed the recipe exactly.  I found that the celery and onion were overwhelming.  The next time I made it, I used canned chicken.  NOT GOOD.  I would not recommend the canned chicken.  The third time I made it, I shredded leftover whole chicken, left out the celery, and cut down on the onion significantly.  It was perfect.  If you find you are leery about the amount of onion or celery, I would definitely recommend that you trust your instinct.

Too easy and so delicious!! Due to laziness, I used a store bought rotisserie chicken and just shredded it with my hands. I bought the grapes, but did not put them in as I wasn't sure if my boyfriend would like it with them. (But I did make a couple spoonfuls for myself with the grapes on the side and it was just as with and without them.) I am sometimes hesitant to use nuts, but the taste of the walnuts I chose to use were not overpowering. It was just right. I am living overseas and they do not have miracle whip so just used lite mayo. I added the salt, but I would suggest trying it without it first and then adding to taste. So easy and so good. Thank you for the recipe!

Very good recipe! Used real mayo cuz that's what I had on hand...and also snipped 2 green onions instead of regular onions cuz I just don't like to crunch down on raw onion. Besides those adjustments, followed recipe as written and let it sit in fridge overnight before eating. It was incredible and everyone loved it. Even 5 & 6 year old niece & nephew! Not sure if anyone else made their own chicken....but for those looking to do this, I had great success with putting 2 frozen chicken breasts in small crockpot with 4 cups of chicken stock & let cook for 3 hours, then cube. Very tasty & easy!

Hi Sherri. Awesome recipe! I've tried it with many different fruits... apples, raisins, Craisins and red seedless grapes. All are wonderful. I do, however, cut the celery down to 1/4 c (just because I don't care for it) and only use about 1/3 c of diced onion (because I like to leave it sit overnight, and then the onion really takes over). I also add just a pinch of mustard (because that's how I've been making it for 40  years. I too love "Miracle Whip"!!! Thanks so much for dressing up a classic go-to sandwich (croisants rock!). P.S. I skip the nuts altogether... they don't work welll with false teeth! LOL. :-)

Yummylicious and easy!  Thanks to another reviewer, I substituted the Miracle Whip w/ 1 C. of real mayo, 1 tsp. lemon juice, and 1/2 tsp. sugar.  I poached three chicken breasts on the stove after brining them for 1 hour in 2 C. of water and 1-1/2 Tbsp. of salt in the refrigerator.  Be sure to thoroughly rinse them b/4 poaching.  This makes them nice and tender.  I omitted the onion and salt (personal preference).  Everything else is the same except that  I added 1/2 tsp. dill, too.  Tasted just like the chicken salad at a tea room here in St. Louis!

attributes.source_text: This makes them nice and tender.

reviews.review_text: I absolutely do not like mayonnaise. I was desperate to find a recipe that used miracle whip (sometimes the ration of mayonnaise to miracle whip are not 1:1). This recipe is so excellent! not just because it uses mayonnaise but because it is delicious!! It is the perfect combination of sweet and salty. My husband dislikes "cold" meals, but he had no problem devouring this entree! I also like the crunch from the walnuts, pecans, and celery. Disclaimer: I did take the lazy route. Instead of using diced "fresh" cooked chicken, I totally used canned chicken breast. Therefore, I omitted the salt in the recipe since I knew canned meat is salted plenty. This recipe was super amazing! This will be a summer staple!

attributes.source_text: the perfect combination of sweet and salty
I also like the crunch from the walnuts, pecans, and celery
he had no problem devouring this entree

reviews.review_text: I used the Kraft squeezable mayo, and added a little bit of lime & some pepper. This was overall really good, I think the chicken needed a little something so next time I will lightly season it. I got crazy with red grapes, they are a nice touch. I omitted celery;although, it does have a nice crunch. I wanted to find something as good as Mccalister's and I think I just did! I'm letting all the ingredients settle overnight and putting them on a croissant w/ lettuce & tomato slices :) this is delish!

This was my first time ever making chicken salad, but I knew I wanted it to taste like my mother-n-law's and this recipe looked like it would. I'm not a fan of Miracle Whip so I used real mayo and used half white and half red seedless grapes and added Craisons. It was wonderful, and the whole family loved it. Next time I think I'll mix the mayo and Miracle Whip half and half to see if I can get it just a smidge more tangy. Thanks so much for the recipe Sherri :o)

attributes.source_text: the whole family loved it

reviews.review_text: Made last week and my husband loved it. Was in a grocery store today, and their honey almond chicken salad was $9.99 per pound!!! And, not as good as this one - and this place has great salads. I bought some boneless skinless breasts for $1.99 per pound, and for a whole lot less have a better salad. Last time, I also added glazed slivered almonds to the recipe. I used recipe 15362 for Glazed Nuts. This time, since I didn't have Miracle Whip, I added about a tablespoon of honey.  Delicious.   Served on some pretzel rolls with arugula. Thanks for a great recipe.

attributes.source_text: my husband loved it

reviews.review_text: Excellent chicken salad!  I made the recipe exactly as posted the first time, then with mayonnaise and a touch of lemon juice the second: both were equally good (it's just that we don't generally have Miracle Whip in the house).  This recipe is easy, quick, and delicious whether served as a sandwich filling, as a stuffing for tomatoes or green peppers, or even on its own with toast or crackers.  A definite 'do again' for us, and an outstanding use for leftover baked chicken breast!

I made some alterations to this recipe but after searching through all the chicken salad recipes posted this one was closest to what we like.  I subbed slivered almonds for the nuts, left out the worcestershire sauce, used real mayo and added 2 teaspoons of Penzey's Balti seasoning.  We loved the cool sweetness of the grapes, crunch of the nuts and the low heat of the Balti.  Worked very well on big buns for a picnic while camping by the lake.  I will make this again.  It is very adaptable to personal tastes.

attributes.source_text: the cool sweetness of the grapes
crunch of the nuts
the low heat of the Balti
for a picnic while camping by the lake

reviews.review_text: This was delicious! I boiled 3 chicken breasts for 20 mins, then chopped them up in my food processor. I only used 1/2 cup of pecans and I probably won't use them next time. The pecans were good, but at $2 per half cup I'd rather just leave them out. Or if I have the extra money to spend maybe I'll add dried cranberries instead of the pecans. Either way, I'll definitely be making this again. Don't leave out the grapes. The grapes are what makes this recipe so great. Thanks for sharing this great recipe!

I used this recipe for an appetizer at a skin care party I held at my home...it was a hit! I used canned chicken instead of cooked chicken for convenience and I used fat free Miracle Whip and both red and green grapes. I served it inside a loaf of Hawaiian bread that I dug out the middle of to place the salad in. It was awesome! No one ever noticed I had used fat-free anything! I had to include the recipe when I delivered everyone's skin care orders!

attributes.source_text: for an appetizer
at a skin care party I held at my home

reviews.review_text: Delicious! I used a mix of pecans and walnuts and they were delicious in this recipe. I also added a few dried cranberries as I had a few on hand. This was exactly what I wanted, and so easy to make! I didn't have any celery on hand, so I finely chopped some baby carrots and used them instead. They added nice crunch and some sweetness. I ate mine with pretzels for lunch, but I would have loved to eat it as a sandwich on a croissant. Thanks for sharing this recipe!

attributes.source_text: some sweetness
They added nice crunch
I ate mine with pretzels for lunch

items.label: Zesty Oven Baked Fries
items.name: Zesty Oven Baked Fries
items.description: Make and share this Zesty Oven Baked Fries recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Heat oven to 450°.
Spray a baking sheet with cooking spray.
Combine all dry ingredients and combine with potatoes, tossing to coat.
Drizzle with oil, tossing again to coat.
Arrange potatoes in a single layer on baking sheet and bake for 35 minutes or until golden brown.

reviews.review_text: Marie -- Another great recipe.  I made these tonight and we thoroughly enjoyed them.  It was a bit of challenge -- I had two other things that I was baking in the oven -- so I had to do some juggling.  Even though these turned out so good -- I know if I hadn't had the other two dishes in the oven at the same time -- they would have even been better.  I did what others did -- put all the dry ingredients along with oil (I used olive oil) into a plastic bag, added the potatoes and coated them that way.  It was a breeze.  We'll be enjoying your potatoes a lot in the future.  Thanks for sharing.

I made these last night after going back on WW'ers. I used Reduced Fat Parmesan Cheese instead of the regular Parmesan Cheese. It's kind of hard to find, but they just started carrying it at our local Walmart. These fries were very tasty and they honestly come out like they are fried. Be careful not to cut the potatoes too thin. I was trying to mimic fast food fries but didn't account for the fact that they shrink up when they cook, so some of them were too hard. My daughter said some of them were a cross between a french fry and a potato chip. haha! So I'll cut them a little larger next time. They DEFINITELY curbed my french fry craving, and I suppose if you don't want your french fries "zesty", you could just use a little more salt and none of the extra spices. Another note, I used the bagged potatoes that aren't "large". I used four regular sized potatoes instead of the two large. For you WW'ers out there, for a regular sized potato, it came out to 3 points total for each potato. You're serving will be about the size of a medium fry at McDonalds. 3 points for a medium fry - excellent deal! :)

attributes.source_text: My daughter said some of them were a cross between a french fry and a potato chip

reviews.review_text: I've made these fries twice now and forgot to review the first time. I put all of the spices in a big ziploc bag and shake the fries that way-then pour the oil in the bag and "squeeze" gently until coated. Another reviewer insisted that the baking time was too long, but it seemed about right to me. Maybe it depends on thickness of your fries and the 'personality' of your oven.  I used a french fry cutter and baked for 30 minutes. Just have to keep an eye on them. One more thing...I also did the LIGHTEST dusting of cayenne pepper over my fries before baking because I like alot of zest on my fries! Thanks for an outstanding recipe!

I made this and it's the first time I've made fries of any kind...and I made it for a new guy haha! Well, he loved it. The only thing is, I cut the potatoes to be similar in size as MacDonald's fries...and that was not too smart. The fries needed a little more time to get crispy, but the smallness/thinness of the fries made it not an option.... they would've burned instead of becoming crispy. So I suggest cutting the fries bigger, more like the fine restaurant's version of fries. Also....I tried it with Sweet Potatoes...it was pretty good, too!
One more thing, I added a sprig of fresh Rosemary, and a little bit of dried basil from my garden. It added a wonderful flavor to the fries for sure!

attributes.source_text: he loved it

reviews.review_text: We loved these! After I cut the potatoes I put them in a bowl of cold water and let them soak for an hour, then I carefully took them out not to disturb the starchy residue at the bottom of the bowl, dried them a bit on paper towels  I was using more potatoes and didn't want them to stick together which can happen if the starch is on them. Then I  followed the recipe using peanut oil because of the high temp.  My kids thought they were great.

attributes.source_text: My kids thought they were great

reviews.review_text: We had these tonight with hotdogs - instead of popping in frozen fries, we decided we wanted something more healthy to go along with the un-healthy (hotdogs) and I decided upon these.  Hubby said "Everytime we have something that goes with fries, you need to make these ones!!"  After reading other reviews, I used olive oil and left the potatoes unpeeled.  I, also, doubled the recipe... even though we're 2 people, hubby eats large dinners.  My potatoes stuck to the pan a bit - but probably my fault. I don't think I sprayed enough cooking spray near the edges, I used more in the middle.  I figured the olive oil would keep them from sticking, but next time I'll just make sure I use a wee more coooking spray all over the baking sheet. Regardless, these were fantastic!! So much more healthier than frozen or fried fries. Great flavor that stayed ON the potatoes. Mine took 20 minutes so I'm glad I checked them earlier - mine were quite thin, could be why.  I dipped mine in ketchup and hot sauce, hubby dipped his in ketchup and mayo (hey, he's Dutch! lol).  Thanks for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: Hubby said "Everytime we have something that goes with fries, you need to make these ones!!"

reviews.review_text: What can I say, I found another Zaar 5 star recipe.  Made as directed, except I didn't peel mine.  Set the oven timer for 17 minutes because I was going to turn them.  I was glad I did because mine were cooked perfectly.  They were cut like shoestring fries. Next time (as soon as I'm done leaving the review) I am going to cut them a little thicker like steak fries.  These were very good and without all the fat and mess of deep frying and the oil slick taste of frozen.  Thanks for sharing such and easy and delicious recipe.

These are FANTASTIC!!  I was shocked that they were not only as good  as, but better than most fries that are fried in oil and grease - and that cost much more than just buying a couple of potatoes.  The flavor is great.  My husband said they look and taste like a restaurant's fries.  I served them with bbq pork sandwiches, and they were fantastic.  I did line my pan with foil to make cleanup easier, but that's the only thing I changed.  Thanks so much for this recipe.  I think I'll make them again today for me for lunch!

attributes.source_text: My husband said they look and taste like a restaurant's fries

reviews.review_text: Thanks very much for this recipe.  I haven't eaten any regular fries for ages because they are high fat and this satisfied the craving.  As per other reviewers' suggestions I didn't peel the potatoes and used olive oil.  However, I cut the potatoes about half as thick as shown in the photos, and in the same cooking time they ended up nicely crispy on top, which I thought was perfect.  I think you could experiment with other types of seasonings too, including add more salt, etc.

Just right! They were a little spicy but not too much. 

My adaptions: I did four potatoes for two adults and four kids. I didn't peel the potatoes, I just cut off the ends and squared off the sides which removed a lot of the peel but not all. I also mixed the oil and spices in a plastic bag and tossed the potatoes around until they were all coated. 

The only change I recommend is turning them about halfway through baking.

Otherwise, this is a good standard five-star recipe. Thanks!

Maybe I over-seasoned? I used garlic salt instead of garlic powder & salt-to save time. My potatoes were cut kind of thin & I baked them for about 30 min till crispy-the way my man likes them :-). Thanks SO much!
