items.label: Black Bean and Tortilla Bake
items.name: Black Bean and Tortilla Bake
items.description: Make and share this Black Bean and Tortilla Bake recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350* F.
Spray a large skillet with cooking spray.
Add garlic, onions, tomato, green onion, cumin, and chili powder.
Cook on medium heat until onion is tender.
Add tomato sauce and cook 5 minutes more.
Stir in beans, cilantro, salt and pepper.
Spray a 9 inch square baking dish with cooking spray.
Layer 4 tortillas, 1/3 cheese, and 1/3 of the bean mixture; repeat 2 more times.
Top with reserved 2 tablespoons of cheese.
Bake 20 minutes, covered, then 10 minutes uncovered or until bubbly.

reviews.review_text:
I was cooking for myself and feeling experimental, so I halved the amounts and used whatever I had in the kitchen. Luckily, almost all of the ingredients were around. I didn't have cilantro, but was fine with excluding it, as it can sometimes overpower some of the other flavors/spices. I used a chunky pasta sauce that was sort of like a combination of chopped tomatoes and pure tomato sauce. I also substituted onion powder for actual onions. This is a great recipe to experiment with. If you want to add salsa, go for it. If you want to double an ingredient, it won't ruin the overall flavor.

If you're going for spicy, definitely add a lot more in. I wasn't going for spicy, so I enjoyed the taste per instructions. I'd also suggest baking then broiling for 5-10 minutes towards the end.

attributes.source_text: I wasn't going for spicy, so I enjoyed the taste per instructions

reviews.review_text: Delish! I made a few small changes - canned diced tomatoes (drained), switched the amounts of cumin & chili (I find cumin can be overpowering), parsley not cilantro, and whole wheat flour instead of corn tortillas. I do not have a 9x9 baking dish so used an 11x7; my layers were a bit thin as a result, so next time I'd probably use an 8x8 instead. Rather than spray the dish, I spread a bit of tomato juice from the canned tomatoes over the bottom. As I mixed this up yesterday, I got a phone call with an invite for dinner out, so I finished assembling the dish then stuck in the fridge overnight. Pulled out today 45 min. before baking, then added an extra 10 min to the covered bake time - worked great! This was tasty with a little sour cream on top. Thanks for sharing!

Awesome!  My boys even asked for seconds, instead of their usual pattern of leaving the table and then asking for snacks 20 minutes later.  I used Mission Carb-balance tortillas b/c I have a diabetic son, and they fit perfectly in my 8 x 8 baking dish.  With these tortillas I used only 2 per layer, and 1 on top.  I kept the filling within the tortilla circles and so served pie-shaped servings.  One boy asked if it was a quiche based on the presentation!  I used a drained can of diced tomatoes in lieu of fresh tomatoes, and used 1 cup of chopped green onions (including white parts) instead of 1/2 cup green and 1/2 cup regular onions.  I did this b/c I hate buying a bunch of green onions and having 1/2 go bad, while the white onions in my fridge last for weeks.    I picked this recipe in part b/c I wanted to use up cilantro I had used in 1 recipe the preceding week that was not going to last much longer.

In any case, this recipe was a huge hit and my husband implored me to serve it once a month.  (I'm always trying new recipes and he hates one-hit wonders that he never sees again.)

my husband implored me to serve it once a month

reviews.review_text:
A vegetarian winner and already on request for repeats! I did modify it quite a bit after reading some reviews, as follows:

-Can of tomatoes w/ juices substituted for the tomato sauce and chopped tomato (it's winter, tomatoes are nasty in the supermarket right now)
-2 cans of black beans used instead of one
-Splash of salsa added in the bean mixture, and another in the bottom of the pan before layering
-Onions and spices doubled to keep the proportions right b/c of the extra beans
-My 9x9 pan needed 3 tortillas per layer, not 4; so we only used 9.
-I baked uncovered for first 20 minutes, then stirred the top layer a bit with a spoon before adding the last bit of cheese and putting it back in the oven for the last 10 minutes. (Kept it from drying out on top without me having to fashion a foil cover.)

Doubling the beans filled the pan nicely and kept this from being skimpy. There's four of us, and we have leftovers for tomorrow despite everyone eating their fill.

We're serving a toddler, so we kept the spices as described, but heat lovers might think about adding a can of green chilis or some serious salsa/pepper sauce to up the ante a bit. It's good as is, though! Thanks for sharing, spatchcock!

attributes.source_text: We're serving a toddler

reviews.review_text: Fabulous recipe - Being in Australia I found dried 'Black Turkey Beans' in my health food shop. To use these black beans in this recipe I followed ketchupqueen's advice "You can soak beans overnight in cool water, or bring to a boil, boil for 20 minutes, turn off heat but leave the cover on, and soak for at least 2-4 hours. If you have hard water, you should add a tsp. of baking soda". Other than that I followed the recipe exactally except to subsitute the fresh tomatoes and sauce for a tin of tomatoes. Thanks you meow! for introducing us to black beans and for posting a recipe that I will use often.

This is a very filling dish!  I used 1/2 tsp chili powder and 1 tsp cumin, which was just perfect for my kids' palate.  I added a can of drained and rinsed corn to the filling, and used a mix of mozzarella and jack cheese (about 2 cups).  The corn stretched the filling just enough so that the edges of the tortillas were covered and stayed moist.  I only used about 6 small corn tortillas, tearing them to fit in the casserole dish.  I added some Taco Bell sauce to my portion and my husband spiced his up with Tabasco, since I had to keep the spice level down for the kids' sake.  My husband really enjoyed it, and didn't miss the meat (especially since I used so much cheese!)

attributes.source_text: just perfect for my kids' palate

reviews.review_text:
I didn't make the recipe exactly as described; I used more garlic ('coz we love it!!), no green onion (just increased the other onion), tinned tomatoes instead of the tomatoes & tomato sauce, my own spice & herb blend (similar to chili powder, although I used some chipotle paste rather than cayenne pepper or whatever) instead of the chili & cumin, borlotti instead of black beans (as that was the closest I had), no coriander leaves as I'd run out, and full fat cheddar. Oh yes, and a little bit of cocoa powder as I always add it to anything chili-ish! I fried the onions for a few minutes with some cumin seeds before adding anything else, but otherwise followed most of the recipe approximately as written.

I also layered it differently to the instructions as I had a round container which was a fraction smaller than the tortillas so I just pressed a tortilla into the bottom, spread a layer of the mixture on & sprinkled with cheese, repeating until it was all used up. Consequently it ended up being a bit more like a pie, as the edges of the tortillas formed a sort of crust!

I served it with creme fraiche & a guacamole-inspired avocado & cherry tomato salad.

It was delicious, and my 7 year old son was especially impressed, despite the fact that he thought it was a bit too spicy at first (by the end he was licking his plate!!). If you're not sure whether it'll be a bit spicy for your kids, I can recommend serving it with creme fraiche or sour cream as it really cuts through the spice (I always serve yoghurt with curry for the same reason).

Definitely one to make again, and I think the recipe is very adaptable (it would be hard to go very wrong with this recipe as a rough guide!).

attributes.source_text: my 7 year old son was especially impressed

reviews.review_text: Great recipe - we loved it!! After reading other reviews, I added a small can of corn, a can of sliced black olives, and a small can of green chiles. I keep fresh roasted poblanos in the freezer for dishes that are "worthy" of them, and this one definitely is, so I'll use them next time. I also used a whole onion (no green onions), and instead of the fresh tomato and tomato sauce, I added a can of Rotel and a 10 oz. can of tomato puree. I used maybe half again as much cheese as called for, combining sharp cheddar and jack. It was a perfect consistency. This will definitely go in my favorites file!

This dish tastes fantastic - really flavorful and incredibly healthy because it's high in fiber, vitamin C and low in fat.  I agree with other reviewers in that I would also decrease the number of servings to 4 instead of 6.  My only problem was that it was drier than I expected.  That may have been my fault, as my tortillas were frozen so I put them in the oven to defrost and they may have become too dry.  So to increase the moisture I added about 1/4 cup of V-8 juice I had in the refrigerator, but it was still too dry.  Next time I try this recipe I will add more tomatoes or tomato sauce.  Still deserves 5 stars though because of the intense taste and good nutrition.

reviews.review_text: I tried this recipe last night.  Overall it is a good basic recipe but I will need to tweak the spices to suit my taste next time (something seemed to be missing to me).  The method itself worked well as the casserole held together nicely and was even better the next day (just had some leftovers for lunch).  It is like a Southwestern lasagna. I am gluten-free and could only find small soft taco size corn tortillas so I used a 11" x 7" glass dish and only needed two tortillas per layer.  It still made plenty - would feed at least 4 people for dinner.  The pan was the perfect size - I had just the right amount of bean mixture.  I subbed another 8 oz can of tomato sauce and a little water for the diced tomatoes (total of two cans and about 1/4 cup water) because I am not a fan of tomato chunks.  Next time I may try adding some salsa for more flavor.  I had leftover black beans from another recipe already in the fridge so I used about 1 1/2 cans in total.  I think adding some meat substitute crumbles or if you eat meat, ground turkey, would also make the filling more substantial.  I garnished mine with a dollup of sour cream and some cubed avocado.

items.label: Flourless Peanut Butter Cookies
items.name: Flourless Peanut Butter Cookies
keywords: c("Lunch/Snacks", "Cookie & Brownie", "Lactose Free", "Free Of...", "< 30 Mins", "For Large Groups", "Oven", "Easy")
items.description: This flourless peanut butter cookie recipe is excellent and so easy to make. Your kids will love it and you will too!  Because this recipe contains no flour, the true taste of the peanut butter comes through loud and clear!  I hope you will enjoy these cookies as much as I do!
instructions: Preheat oven to 350* and grease cookie sheets.
Beat together peanut butter and sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer until smooth.
Add beaten egg and baking soda to peanut butter mixture and beat until well combined.
Roll 1 teaspoon of dough into a ball and place on cookie sheet.
Place dough balls one inch apart on cookie sheet and flatten with tines of fork making a cross pattern.
Bake until puffed and a golden pale, about 10 minutes.
Cool cookies on baking sheet about 2 minutes and then transfer with spatula to rack to cool.
May be kept in air tight container at room temperature for 5 days.
Makes about 2 dozen cookies.

reviews.review_text:
alright.  nj "newbie" here.  known for my devotion for peanut butter, could not keep this recipe in my cookbook for too long without giving it a try.

first - that silly cross pattern with the fork
tip:  continually rinse off your fork with warm water ever 2 cookies or so, or it will stick and lose that wonderful pattern in a mush of pulled up dough

second - i made my cookies enormous (i only rolled 18).  
tip:  trust me, the WILL expand.  they don't look like it, but they do.  make real spoonfuls, not shovelfuls. 

third - if you are crazy and want enormous cookies, reduce the oven to 300.
tip:  plan an activity to do, these will take longer to cook.  the smell of peanut butter will taunt you.  if you don't keep yourself busy you will be glaring at the oven for 15+ minutes trying to cook them faster with your soul, and it didn't work for me.

fourth - good news!
tip:  the cookies will harden when out of the oven, so you can be slightly impatient and take them out a little early to maintain a soft chewy cookie!  yay!  (maybe the soul glare worked?)

fifth - additions
i agree with other reviews, these cookies would rock even more with other goodies in them like peanut butter chips or oatmeal - i'm going to try that next!

attributes.source_text: maintain a soft chewy cookie
maintain a soft chewy cookie

reviews.review_text: I love this recipe.  As the only member of my family that HAS to be gluten free, I'm always on the lookout for recipes that work for the gluten eating members of my family as well as myself.  This one hits the mark.  These cookies are easy to make, I always have the ingredients on hand and they taste good too.  My family likes bigger cookies so I usually double the recipe which makes about 3 dozen 3 inch cookies.  I've also used 1/2 white sugar and 1/2 brown sugar (1 cup of each) when doubling the recipe with no problem.  I learned this out of necessity whenever I had already dumped the peanut butter in the bowl before checking to see if I had enough sugar! Still turned out great.  Now I just use whatever I have on hand.  One more compliment for this recipe, this is the CHEAPEST gluten free dessert I've ever made and it didn't need any "special" ingredients.  Love, Love LOVE it!

attributes.source_text: work for the gluten eating members of my family as well as myself

reviews.review_text: HOW!! HOW did I go 46 years without knowing I could make DELICIOUS Cookies in my home WITHOUT Any Flour!!?? Are You Kiddin' Me!?? Ok, 1st of all, peanut butter cookies..not usually my thing..but, I'm desperate and in NEED of something sweet. 2nd, OMG!! I'm IN LOVE! Ok..so..being the experimenting cook that I am, I'd love to share my few tweaks to this WONDERFULLY EASY recipe. I added about a 1/2 tsp. of vanilla extract. I used Roasted Honey Nut peanut butter and 1 Envelope of Instant Banana oatmeal. B/C of the extra sugar in my added ingredients, I only used 1/2 cup of sugar. (DIDN'T Miss the other half at all!!) 3rd, DID NOT Realize HOW BIG these little dough balls expanded during the baking process!! :o AND they cook REALLY Fast, gotta keep a close eye on them. I definitely should've used a timer. 4thly...can't tell you how many I was able to make b/c some were giant, some were petite..most..WERE GONE by the second batch I put in to bake. :-) THANK YOU SO MUCH for making it so easy to satisfy my BIG Sweet Tooth, and SO Quickly!! 5 STARS BABY!!

attributes.source_text: in NEED of something sweet

reviews.review_text: Ok Bev, I know I have already reviewed these yummies, but today I whipped up a batch and folded in some Tollhouse Swirls (little PB & coc swirled chips, very cute!), they were very good, well worth trying. The chocolate and pb chips were just subtle enough to give the a little something without taking away from the simplicity of the cookie. I have shared this recipe with ALL of the moms from playgroup, I kindof regret that move because before when I showed up with perfect pb cookies, they all thought I was supermom! Now they know the truth, I just had 4 ingridients and an hour!LOL! But they were gratefull, when I told them the cookies did not have flour, they all clucked sympathetically, "no sleep huh?" and proceeded to tell me of all the things they have forgotten! But boy these are a hit!

attributes.source_text: just subtle enough to give the a little something

reviews.review_text:
just made these, but of course, I made adjustments to make them organic and vegan.
I used organic(no sugar,no salt) chunky peanut butter. Instead of the egg, I used 1/4 cup of silken tofu that I blended until it was smooth. I also added 1/2 tsp. baking powder and used organic palm sugar(low glycemic index)- I decreased the sugar to less than 3/4 cup and the sweetness was perfect. I also added 1/4 tsp. of salt to balance out the sweetness.
These just baked for 12 minutes and were soft when they came out the oven but as they cooled, they hardened a bit, but still remained soft/chewy and slight crispy edges. Out of the oven, I sprinkled a bit of organic cane sugar and a very small amount of pink Himalayan sea salt. They tasted great and looked great, not to mention, high in protein.

reviews.review_text: This is a suprisingly good recipe with a few changes. I used 1/2 cup brown sugar and 1/4 cup white sugar and put in 1 tsp vanilla extract, and 1/2 tsp of baking soda. It also wouldn't hurt to add a pinch of salt in too. If you still have a few bits of brown sugar that aren't combined correctly, don't stress it because those will carmelize into chewy bits. It is important not to overcook these cookies, but to cook them just until they are starting to brown and crack a little. Don't wait until there are big cracks running through the cookies in the middle. Let them sit for quite some time, and they should turn out nice and chewy. These are very good and satisfying when you are hungry and will likely be a big hit at parties, but they are cloyingly sweet and almost inedible if you are not hungry. But you shouldn't be eating when you're not hungry anyway ;)

reviews.review_text: Thank you for posting.  This is the second time I've made these, and I agree with the other posters that these are the easiest PB cookies you can make with a light texture and good flavor.  I *do* like a traditional cookie better, but when the cupboards are bare this is a great way to still be able to bake up cookies without a trip to the store.  A word of caution or advise:  the first time I made these they did not turn out AT ALL.  My problem was that I was really worried about getting these mixed well, that I ended up overmixing them, which resulted in a crumbly dough with the oil (from the PB) weeping out - and totally inedible cookies.  When you mix, keep an eye on the dough.  As soon as the dough pulls together and actually looks like cookie dough - stop mixing.  More isn't better!

attributes.source_text: with a light texture

reviews.review_text: I am celiac and have tried baking with a lot of gluten/wheat free alternatives flours. First when I saw this recipe though I’ll try it the evening for me this was a stretch. My daughter who always says I make my own creation tried these cookies and said mom physic good in now these cookies are great your best cookies yet. I told her I found the recipe on the cycle genius kitchen and it has no flour in them. I have made them three times since finding the recipe it is so simple, quick, easy on the ingredients, and I always have peanut butter because that is something that I love. Thank you genius kitten for such a wonderful recipe. I am going to make again today and hopefully I will be able to take a picture. The others did not last long enough so that I could get one. The only tweak/cons to this recipe is I did not get as many as stated in the recipe. That might have been too to me making a larger cookies. ??

attributes.source_text: My daughter who always says I make my own creation tried these cookies and said mom physic good in now these cookies are great your best cookies yet

reviews.review_text: I made the mistake of using natural peanut butter when I prepared this recipe. I didn't realize it hadn't been stirred properly before and that the pb at the bottom of the jar was very dry. When I was finished mixing the dough up, it was basically crumbs. I could form it into a ball, but when I tried to press down on it with a fork, it crumbled. I decided to add another egg and some oil to moisten it. I finally got them to hold together, but in the finished cookieI can taste that I probably put in too much oil. Fortunately, everyone else things they are good. :) I decided not to rate the recipe with any stars since I messed it up and altered it so much. I would have to make them again correctly to give an honest opinion.

This is a great flourless cookie! You are right when you said that the peanut butter taste will come loud and clear coz' it certainly does! Just for fun I lessened the sugar a wee bit and added a tsp. or two of vanilla... hehe... yummy!!! The bag of oatmeal was still unopened and I can't open it without grandma's permission so I'll try these with oatmeal nextime. I used a toaster to bake my cookies (oven's broken) and I baked perfection at around 6-7 minutes, while flipping the pan at 3 minutes to get an even bake. The temp. different in the toaster and it's harder to bake there. I noticed that my cookies always get yummier after sitting in the cookies jar over night... wonder why??? :)

attributes.source_text: the peanut butter taste will come loud and clear

reviews.review_text: What a surprise! I did this all by hand and they came out so tasty. I had to experiment a bit with what size to use in my little toaster oven and how long to cook etc. I made two little changes. I used brown sugar instead of white sugar cause I like molasses..and thought it might make them a little chewier. I also added a big splash of imitation vanilla flavor (didn't have extract) which I think really balanced out everything, As a result, I had to drop the temp to 325 to avoid any burning in..as I said..my little toaster oven. These are MY kind of cookie. Crunchy and chewy and very peanutbuttery! Plus? To keep myself from chowing down on the whole batch..I shared them with my pups! When you think about all the extra work we go through to make traditional recipes I realized that adding butter means you have to add flour..and as a result it makes it less intense. I used generic peanut butter and brown sugar as well. So you don't need anything fancy. One little caveat is that they ARE a dark cookie.

attributes.source_text: very peanutbuttery

Plenty sweet. I added about a 1/3 cup of flax meal, just on general principles. I dipped my fork in water then sugar to make the criss-cross pattern, ended up with a nice glaze on the cookies. Halfway thru baking I planted a Kiss on each cookie. My cookies are small; only baked them about 10 minutes total. In the time it's taken me to type this comment, my kids have consumed almost the entire first batch! I think this recipe's a hit.

I thought they might not be sweet enough, but they were delicious. Even our sugar-loving, peanut-butter-cookie-hating, 8 year old niece loved them! Another bonus of the simplicity is that kids can help too. Thank you, we will be making them regularly!

Bev, thank you for this recipe!
I had never made any recipes "flour-less" before, and when I saw this one, I had to try it.
The cookies were amazing.  They turned out so moist and chewy.
I added the vanilla, rolled them in my palm, and dipped the fork in sugar.

reviews.review_text: This is a really good recipe, but they were far too sweet for me. IMHO, you only need the full cup of sugar if you're using unsweetened natural peanut butter. I used Skippy, which is already sweetened, and combined with the recipe's sugar was just too much. I cut the amount in half, added a tablespoon of butter pecan extract, and 1/3 cup of chopped pecans that I had on hand (peanuts would obviously work too for a more authentic peanut butter cookie). Once I took them out of the oven, they barely had time to cool before I was shoving one into my mouth. Amazing!!!

These cookies are delightful.  I was initially concerned about whether reduced fat natural peanut butter would work in this recipe and decided to take a chance.  I was glad that I did, because it worked beautifully. I also scaled back on the sugar without a problem.  I used a tablespoon "ice cream" scoop sprayed with non stick instead of rolling the cookies into balls and found that this made for even portioning for cookies of equal size. The 10 minute baking time worked perfectly.  My yield was 24 cookies.  Thank you Bev for sharing the recipe.

I'm not nuts about peanut butter but decided to give this a go since it's crazy easy to make. I gave some to my boyfriend and mom to take to work.. wow! Absolutely EVERYBODY loved the cookies and they want more! I've just bought a jar of peanut butter to make a batch specially for my aunt who's addicted to peanuts :) Thank you so much for sharing this recipe, what a hit! (Btw, I made no modifications to the recipe and the cookies came out perfectly. I made sure I used sugarless/unsweetened peanut butter so they weren't too sweet at all. items.label: Korean Roast Chicken Thighs
items.name: Korean Roast Chicken Thighs
items.description: Not sure where I found this recipe, but make it monthly for my family. I have used vegetable oil in place of the sesame oil and it still tastes great.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
Place chicken skin side down in a large baking dish.
Combine the remaining ingredients in a bowl and then pour on top of the chicken.
Bake uncovered for 45 minutes.
Turn the chicken over in the dish and bake for another 15 minutes.

reviews.review_text: I've had this recipe saved for awhile in my cookbooks, and decided this was the night to make it. I read some of reviews (there is a LOT!), so I adjusted the recipe. I used half of the sesame oil, half of the honey (because I don't like overly sweet meat), and cut the soy sauce with a little water so it wouldn't be too salty. I used fresh ginger, more garlic, and put it under the broiler to crisp up the skin some. I used bone in chicken thighs, which I let marinate for an hour or so in the sauce before putting it in the oven. I toasted sesame seeds to adorn it along with chopped green onions, and served it with rice and green beans. It was wonderful! So, am I rating a recipe that's not true as written, even though I used all of the ingredients,  or just listening to others who have tried it? I think we can all use our own tweaks, and if they turn out, great! So, thank you all of the past posters for your tips! I will make this recipe over and over because it was so good, and we loved it. Thank you for sharing.

This was really good. I took out a package of bone-in, skin on chicken thighs out of the freezer, there were five pieces in the bag. I let them thaw over night, mixed up the sauce ingredients in the morning, with a few changes, didn't have honey, so I used brown sugar, sprinkled some hot pepper flakes for zing, and I did not use three tablespoons of sesame oil. I would NEVER use three tablespoons of sesame oil in anything. It would be totally overwhelming.  I used just one tablespoon.I don't normally have such a strong opinion but I made the mistake once, in a marinade for grilled salmon. I couldn't go near sesame oil for two years. I poured the sauce ingredients into the bag with the chicken and left it all day in the fridge. Baked as directed, turning twice, once every twenty minutes, ending with skin side up, and turned the broiler on the last five minutes or so to crisp up the skin as another reviewer suggest. Served with white rice. They were excellent! Moist and tender and not too salty at all. Thanks so much! I love fast and simple, these were great!

attributes.source_text: not too salty at all
Moist and tender
Moist and tender

reviews.review_text: I followed the directions exactly. Tasted the sauce when turning the chicken over and didn't care much for it.  I think it was just a matter of personal taste.  I poured the sauce into a pan, added about 3 or 4 tablespoons of brown sugar (ran out of honey or would have added that). Thickened it with cornstarch and poured it back over the chicken. Not too sweet, just right for us. Put them back in the oven for the last 15 or 20 min. It was out of this world!!!  Tasted like something from a good restaurant.  Served over plain white rice.  It looked exactly like Charmie777's photo!  I thought maybe I should be giving this only 4 starts since I had to tweak it a bit, but it was so wonderously delicious I had to give it 5 stars.  Without your recipe, Petunia, we wouldn't have had such an outstanding meal. I will be making this again and again. Many thanks for posting this great recipe, Petunia.

attributes.source_text: Not too sweet, just right for us

reviews.review_text: This was very easy and simple to make, and tasted delicious. I didn't have sesame oil or green onions, so I used vegetable oil and regular white onions. I also used more ginger and garlic, but I think I could have used even more of both. The chicken was moist and delicious, and not too salty at all. I did what another reviewer suggested, and put the oven on "broil" for the last ten minutes, after flipping the chicken thighs skin side up. The skin did indeed crisp, but it also burned a little bit. No biggie at all. It tasted good and looked even better. Phenomenal, easy, quick recipe. Serving suggestion: I served this with rice and garlic kale. We spooned the juices from the baking dish onto the rice and mixed it in. It was a little greasy but it tasted great, and the kale lightened it up, and could also be mixed up with the rice. No one needed to season their food further, which almost never happens. I only left off a star because I've had better, but this was truly a great recipe.

I followed the recipe to a tee, except a used skinless/boneless chicken thighs because that's all I had (and it still turned out super moist and tender!) and I added a bit more garlic, ginger and pepper because we tend to like a lot of flavor in our recipes.   I used a light soy sauce which I think was nice because it didn't overpower the rest of the flavors, but I think I would like to try it with a heavier soy sauce and see which one we like better.  I can't imagine this recipe without the sesame oil because the sesame oil really is the star ingrediant in my mind that helps create the unique flavor of this dish!  Family vote was that this is something they would like to have again so thanks for posting!

reviews.review_text: This was really good!  I think I'd like just a bit more of a spicy bite to the sauce, so I'll add either chili flakes or chile garlic sauce next time.  I cooked 2 thighs, but made half of the sauce and served it over jasmine rice.  Additionally, I minced the white part of the green onions, but kept the green parts to garnish the completed dish, giving a fresh crunch to it. This was fully cooked after 45 minutes, I checked the temp after 20 minutes and flipped the pieces over at that point to finish cooking. The flavors of sesame, honey and soy were very nicely balanced I wouldn't change anything about the ingredients except to change the ginger to fresh- I always prefer fresh ingredients when I can get them.  Very nice- I may try using this as a marinade, and cooking the chicken on the grill.  Thanks for a wonderful dinner; I'm already looking forward to the leftovers for lunch tomorrow.

reviews.review_text: Made this tonight and it was pretty good. However, 1) chicken thighs are extremely fatty so there was a half inch layer of fat in my pan. Next time I'll use skin-on, bone-in chicken breast and adjust the cooking time; 2) The skin was tasty but the flavor didn't penetrate into the meat...I'll marinate overnight next time; 3) I tweaked the recipe a little because we like spicy food so I added a whole large jalapeno (part of it chopped and part of it I left in rings) and yet it wasn't spicy...at all. I think next time I'll use a serrano OR as another reviewer did, I'll throw some sriracha in there :) Good recipe to use as a springboard. Unlike another reviewer, I did use the 3 T. of sesame oil and barely tasted it. I also used 1/4 t. fresh ginger (available in tubes at the Japanese market I frequent) but I didn't taste that either so next time I'll use 1 T. (I like ginger), oh, and I used tons of fresh chopped garlic. Served with jasmine rice and almond broccoli.

YUMMMM! Made this as written without any alterations to ingredients.  I did marinate for an hour in a ziploc bag before putting in a PAM sprayed baking dish.  Everyone walking in the door wanted to know what was for dinner because it smelled so good.  The chicken was moist and wonderfully flavored.  Although the chicken was really good on its own, after removing the chicken from the baking dish I emptied the rest of the sauce into a saute pan, added a couple tablespoons of brown sugar and reduced the sauce by half.  The sauce really made this dish out of this world.  Just a bit of extra sauce on each chicken thigh to go with the steamed rice and it was absolutely amazing.  Fantastic quick, easy and delicious recipe!

reviews.review_text: This is a great recipe!  I thawed what I thought were thighs, nope, 3 very fat boneless skinless chicken breasts.  They were a little icy still, so I made the sauce minus 1 tablespoon of the sesame oil (personal pref only) and let the breasts sit in it  and marinade until completely thawed.  I was a little worried about the breast meat drying out, so cut the cooking time back to 45 min total.  Even with my tinkering, these were the moistest, most tender chicken breasts!!  Even reheating one the next night in micro, it was still moist and tender.  DH kept muttering to himself how good it was, as well as any man can mutter with a mouth full of food.  This is a do again and again and again.  I'm thinking this would be awesome on pork too.   Oh, I did use the jarred ginger instead of ground.  It was great.  Served with basmati rice and cucumbers/onion salad.  TY so much for this recipe.

I only did 4 pieces of chicken so that I could use the sauce over the brown rice and broccoli florets (took picture prior to adding extra sauce and those items were in frozen section at trader joe's). Prior to cooking, I didn't marinate it, and it was still flavorful. My concern was that the chicken will come out too dry, but it came out perfect. The mix for the marinade is genius, I will be trying it on other kinds of meat too. The only issue about the marinade , is the soy sauce, when adding it you have too be aware that some sauce sauces are a little saltier than others, even when you eat at different restaurants. Nevertheless, it is not a jab at the recipe , because it is incredible, very flavorful, and not at all complicated. :)

Marinated overnight as others suggested. Even though I cut back on the low sodium soy sauce it was still too salty for me. Next time even less. Also would use brown sugar instead of honey as not sweet enough or maybe a combination of both. Would also use fresh ginger instead of a combo of fresh and powdered. Covered it with foil for the first 20 minutes, then did 20 minute intervals uncovered and spooned sauce over chicken each time when turning. Toasted sesame seeds to put on it after thickening the sauce and pouring it back over it. Finished off with chopped green onions. The smell it emits while cooking was driving us crazy! This is a keeper!!!

Used a couple lbs of boneless skinless breasts cut into strips, marinated it all for 3 hours before baking 45 mins at 350, flipping halfway through. Used only 1 T of sesame oil which was plenty, also used fresh ginger.. After cooking chicken, poured the liquids in a saucepan with cornstarch/water mix and cooked to thicken up. Served chicken over rice with side of asparagus and sauce over the whole thing with spicy chinese mustard on the side. Was delicious, can't imagine it would be as good if it wasn't marinated or if the sauce wasn't cooked though. Will make again!

I have been trying new recipes since I got married 1 1/2 years ago and this one blew them all out of the water!! I marinated it for 4 hours and reduced the sauce added the pan drippings and served it over the rice and chicken. The whole family loved it clean plates around the table. It was awesome if you like Asian food of any kind this is sweet salty sticky and delicious!!! A MUST try!

items.label: Iced Coffee
items.name: Iced Coffee
items.description: I love coffee. (you're shocked, I can tell) I like to keep a pitcher of this in my fridge, especially during the summer.
instructions: Combine brewed coffee and sweetened condensed milk in a large pitcher.
Refrigerate until chilled.
Serve over ice.
TIP- Use leftover coffee to make coffee ice cubes with.
Then you have the chill without getting watered down.

reviews.review_text: I was trying to convince my friend that she did not need to spend $30 a week at Starbucks (she likes some kind of caramel crazy drink), so I made this recipe.  I made the coffee ice cubes with a leftover pot of coffee, used only 3/4 of  a can of SCM initially to stir in, and brought  the rest of the SCM to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it became a caramel color.  I let it cool, then drizzled some inside the glass, filled the glass halfway with the iced coffee, added a little more caramel, filled up the glass, then topped with some whipped cream and another drizzle of the caramel.  I thought she was going to pass out- she drank almost 3 glasses of it, then took the rest home with her!  LOL.  This is a fantastic recipe- thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: she drank almost 3 glasses of it, then took the rest home with her

reviews.review_text:
I'm really sorry that I have to rate this so low. I thought about it a long time, because I love Recipezaar and my fellow Recipezaarians, but I figure it's best to be honest.

I used a quality SCM (eagle brand) and about 9-10 cups of coffee. It was just too devastatingly sweet - even for my wife, who loves Starbucks iced coffee. After we tried about half of the original batch, I added another 5 cups of fresh coffee, effectively halving the amount of SCM - it was still too sweet for me, although Kelly said the sweet was about right at that point. But what was still a problem for both of us was the heavy caramel notes that the SCM brought - really overpowering the coffee.

I don't think I'd use this recipe unless I cut the amount of SCM to 1/4 can, and had a *really* strong brew that would work well with the caramel notes (like a dark roasted Kona).

attributes.source_text: Kelly said the sweet was about right at that point

reviews.review_text: Excellent! Sorry Starbucks this Seattle girl is going to have to diss you for this. I remember when the first Starbucks opened at The Pike Place Market here in Seattle. It was so quaint, but they have out grown their britches and I'm so happy to have found this recipe. Who'd have thought 2 simple ingredients could taste so good. Thanks CoffeeMom!! UPDATE 5/4: I have made this 4 times in the the past week and I have found that the Mexican brand of sweetened condensed milk is sweeter than the American. My coffee maker brews "12 cups" which is actually 64 ounces or, 8 cups. I use about 3/4 - 1 cup of fine ground french roast coffee to brew one whole pot (and it is strong). If I find that it is too strong, I dilute it with plain condensed milk (not water!!). It is sooo creamy!! I have fooled my Frappuccino guzzling DH.  he, he, he...

reviews.review_text: I didn't realize there were some many reviews on this recipe, but after making it, I just had to add mine..I am an ice coffee nut, no matter what time of year...After having a little snafu with my coffee maker this morning (it died) I was having such a craving for this that I went to Duncan Donuts and bought 3 large black coffee's and then came home and made it with the sweetend condensed milk...I also make the ice cube to go with it....This was so good, I will be making it  alot more...am going out to buy a new coffee maker  so I will be prepared the next time I make it which I know will be soon...Thanks again for a great and easy recipe...

I am editing my review of this iced coffee. The last time I posted my review, was back in July of 2005. However, last Summer I started making this delicious coffee, but making it with FOLGER'S GOURMET CHOCOLATE TRUFFLE GROUND COFFEE, and boy is that ever good. While using this coffee, I found I didn't need to add coffee flavored iced cubes, but rather just added regular ice cubes to my drink. Whenever I make this iced coffee, (using the Chocolate Truffle Ground Coffee) this is how I make it. I use 6-1/3 cups of water, and 6 tablespoons of the ground coffee. One more thing I wanted to add...I have also made this iced coffee, but using a FAT FREE SWEETENED CONDENSED MILK, and that tastes just as good as the regular canned sweetened condensed milk. By the way, this was the review I posted back in July of 2005: CoffeeMom, this coffee was 
"superb". I definately will be making this again. For those who thought this was too sweet, add a few ice cubes to your glass. And for those who think the ice cubes will weak'n the flavor of the coffee, add coffee flavored ice cubes to your drink. It will be less sweet, but still have that wonderful coffee flavor. "Thank-you" CoffeeMom for the great recipe.

attributes.source_text: wonderful coffee flavor

reviews.review_text: With 98 previous reviews, you certainly do not need mine to verify that this is good, but I have to tell you how fantastic this is and how long I've searched for a good recipe for iced coffee.  I'm from Arizona, but spend the summer on Cape Cod in Massachusetts where there are two Dunkin Donuts on every street corner.  I'm totally hooked on DD's iced coffee and when I go home in the Fall, I miss it sooooo much.  Now I can make something equally delicious and it's so easy!  Thanks CoffeeMom - you've made my day!  Georgeann

CoffeeMom, this stuff is better than a vitamin B12 shot for me!  Seriously! I'm working outdoors in the heat everyday till noon.  I come home feeling like a limp noodle. After a shower, change of clothes and a bite to eat I get soooo sleepy. Well, not anymore!!  I made your iced coffee recipe using one of my favorite flavored coffees.  I made the coffee ice cubes too! Now, after lunch, a frosty glass of iced coffee is my dessert and it really "picks me up" so I'm good to go for the rest of the afternoon.  Thank you so much for posting this super recipe!

a frosty glass of iced coffee

reviews.review_text: I have made this recipe twice in as many days. My fiance and I adore it. We were always splurging on the bottled Starbucks Frappuccinos and now we don't have to! Although if I were giving this a rating based on "resisting drinking the whole batch in one go" and "how it affects my waistline" I'd have to give it 1 star LOL!<br/><br/>We make it with 8 cups strong coffee and the coffee ice cubes. Some of our friends have said it's too sweet, but I just add extra ice cubes to their glasses and don't hear another word on it. <br/><br/>Our next attempt will have us using flavored coffee (Creme Caramel) to see how it turns out.<br/><br/>THANK YOU COFFEE MOM!

reviews.review_text:

The 2nd pitcher, I use regular coffee and regular sweetened condensed milk.  The 3rd pitcher, I used Chocolate coffee and fat free sweetened condensed milk.
All 3 were terrific, but since I am watching my weight, I will stick with using fat free sweetened condensed milk.  I can't tell a difference between the two.  This is definitely my new favorite summer drink.

reviews.review_text: if i could i would come and thank you personally!!!!  delicious and to make it the perfect recipe; simple and cheap.  i have found a superb iced organic coffee, called "froid" which i loved but could not justify buying each day at 3 dollars for a small bottle.  i tried other iced coffee recipes but none were creamy; they were good but too watery even if i used coffee ice cubes.  today i bought organic coffee beans, sweetened condensed milk (couldnt find organic) and just made a pitcher. this makes it affordable, delicious and when i find the organic s.c.milk; the perfect daytime pickme up refresher. thank you so much for sharing.

I did find the ratio a bit too sweet and probably increased the coffee by half again, but then again I'm not big into dessert-things so that may just be me. I was a bad girl, lol, and used the full-fat, regular s.c. milk since that's what I had on hand; next time I will try a lower fat one and see if there is a way to make this guilty pleasure a little less guilty (so that I can have it more often, of course!) reviews.review_text: This was really good.  I used some leftover flavored coffee from my shop to make this.  I made it with a Hazelnut Cream flavored coffee, and it was great.   Then I got to thinking, hmmmmm this would be good with other flavored coffees.  So, to date, I have tried it with, besides the Hazelnut Cream, I've used French Caramel Cream, and a Butternut Rum flavored coffee.   I do like the idea of adding a little vanilla also.  I have a flavored coffee at work called French Vanilla Nut, I bet that would be good with extra vanilla added.  WOW!  The possibilities are endless........................... I was looking for a way to use roughly half of a leftover 300ml can of sweetened condensed milk I had from a pie I'd baked. I dont like my coffee very sweet so I brewed 6 cups of strong coffee and added the leftover condensed milk (about 150ml) and a few squirts of hershey chocolate syrup. To my surprise I was drinking the best cup of iced coffee I've ever had! Will definitely keep this in my fridge on a regular basis and I will never buy a single iced coffee ever again! Does this recipe really need another great review??? Oh why not...This is AWESOME!!! I love coffee and I just had to try this. I loved it! I used fat-free sweetened condensed milk just to cut back a little on the fat and calories and it was still wounderful. I used the leftover coffee to make coffee ice cubes (which was a great tip) So I can keep my yummy treat nice and cold. I think the cubes would be great in coffee smoothies too. Starbucks has lost my business! Everybody here loves this stuff. I made it using Folgers 100% Columbian coffee and generic SCM. The first time I made it, I used 8cups of coffee and it was pretty sweet, so the next time I used 10cups and it was perfect. It turns out fairly thick and creamy, therefore I saw no need to freeze coffee-ice-cubes, because regular ones don't seem to dilute it enough to matter, and believe me, I do not like watery coffee, so I would notice this. items.description: Someone gave me this recipe a few years back and it's become a household favorite. You can use mild, medium or hot salsa depending on your taste. I usually serve it with Spanish rice and Mexican-style canned corn. Very easy and quick!
instructions: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Place chicken breasts in a lightly greased 9x13 inch baking dish.
Sprinkle taco seasoning on both sides of chicken breasts, and pour salsa over all.
Bake at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) for 25 to 35 minutes, or until chicken is tender and juicy and its juices run clear.
Sprinkle chicken evenly with cheese, and continue baking for an additional 3 to 5 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Top with sour cream if desired, and serve.

reviews.review_text: There are some recipes that are little gems - and this is one of them! My version: 11 boneless skinless thighs - I coated them in President's Choice (Canadian Superstore brand) low salt taco mix in the blue package - baked them without the salsa first at 450 F for 20 minutes then poured the salsa over and baked further 20 minutes. Served with dollop of sour cream and green onions - on top of Uncle Ben's Natural Select Spanish rice - excellent weekday meal - thank you so much!

I used the taco seasoning #38756 which was perfect for the coating, and good-quality mild salsa to pour over chicken. I rubbed the chicken breast with a taco seasoning (not a mix) and then sprinkled with pepper and cilantro.  I seared the chicken in a little bit of olive oil on both sides.  Then added 1/4 cup of salsa and 1/4 cup of water and simmered for 15 min.  Then I added the rest of the salsa and simmered for about 10 more minutes.  I sprinkled with cheese the last 3 minutes.  I served it over brown rice with sour cream and guacomole.

items.description: Make and share this Chili's Salsa recipe from Food.com.
instructions: In food processor place jalapenos and onions.
Process for just a few seconds.
Add both cans of tomatoes, salt, sugar, and cumin.
Process all ingredients until well blended but do not puree.
Place in covered container and chill.
A couple of hours of chilling will help blend and enrich the flavor.
Serve with your favorite thin corn tortilla chips.

reviews.review_text: We're addicted to Chili's salsa and always bring home an extra bag of chips and bowl of salsa. I've been making this recipe for years. Because I normally cook for 2, and this recipe makes a lot of salsa, I had to modify it slightly. I use 1 (14oz) can of whole peeled tomatoes, plus ¼ diced fresh jalapeño (about 1 tablespoon), scale the remaining ingredients by half (using granulated garlic instead of garlic salt), then blend it until the consistency is right. I add about ½ teaspoon lime juice at the end to brighten it. The taste is so close to Chili's my family says it's spot on! I always buy a bunch of jalapeños at a time and dice them. It's amazing how well they freeze in a ziplock bag and how long they last. I love having them always at hand. I toss them frozen into chili con carne, pico de gallo, tortilla soup, anyplace I want a hit of fruit and heat.

attributes.source_text: my family says it's spot on

reviews.review_text: I've been making this recipe regularly for about 2 yrs now. To make it easy on myself, I open my cans of tomatoes and put the juice only in the blender, to that I add a 1/4 cup white vinegar, 1/4 cup Lime Juice.  I just toss in about half an onion (the blender will chop it), 1/4 of a bunch of Cilantro (stems and all), a clove or two of garlic.  For heat I use a fresh jalapeno, but the secret here is to fry it in a pan with a little oil. Keep turning until the skin becomes bubbly all over.  The heat will release the capsicum.  Usually you will only need half of the jalapeno.  Blend it all up with out the tomatoes.  Taste it, it is very strong at this point, make any adjustments to taste, I usually add more salt.  Toss in the tomatoes and a couple of pulses...You're done. The flavors really come together after a day in the fridge.

This is extremely close to Chili's salsa. This is a "no cooking" salsa but is fresh salsa so that might explain some of the low ratings. The first time I made it I followed the recipe and used canned tomatoes and thought it was good. I also added some black pepper and it gave it some extra flavor. Make sure you chill it well before serving.
2nd time I made it, I used fresh tomatoes (blanched and peeled the skin) from the garden instead of the can of whole tomatoes. Used fresh jalapenos and cilantro. Much better the 2nd time with the fresh homegrown tomatoes (this is key to a better flavor for those who didn't like.). Tomatoes from your garden or vine ripened tomatoes are key to a better flavor for those who didn't like it. Canned tomatoes (in my opinion) are better for cooking.

attributes.source_text: is fresh salsa

reviews.review_text: this salsa is good but not like chili's enough for me to give up the search for the actual recipe.  First of all there is something missing.... I can not put my finger on it but the chilis version has a kind of tangy flavor... not sure what the ingredient is though.  Then there is the cumin.  Cumin is so strong half a teaspoon completely overpowered my salsa.  I would add a dash and taste it until you get it to where you like it.  It ended up making the salsa taste a bit like it had too much chili powder in it.  This is on the right track. I made it again without the cumin completely and added a fresh garlic clove and a tiny bit of lime juice and extra jalapenos and it was very good.

I made this as part of the dips for my daughter's birthday party.  I only had a 28 oz can of tomatoes so I doubled the recipe.  I found out AFTER I had mixed the tomatoes and the 2 cans of rotel that I only had fresh jalapenos (and only 2 at that) so I used them and added some cayenne pepper.  I also used a whole onion.  The salsa was very good, but I know had I had either the canned (or more fresh) jalapenos it would have been great that is why I am giving it 5 stars.  I will make this again but next time make sure I have all of the ingredients!!  Thanks for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: for my daughter's birthday party

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe with some homemade tortilla chips.  For a canned tomato salsa, this was very good!  I do recommend to get a brand name tomato versus your generic or store brand kind.  It makes a difference.  I used hunts brand for the whole tomatoes and a generic for the chopped.  When I started making this I tasted it and it was very good!  But when I went to add in the chopped tomatoes I could tell it weaken the flavor a bit by using an off brand.  Next time I may use all whole tomatoes, since the whole keeps in more flavor than the already chopped.  Otherwise it was really good, and even better the next day.  This is very versatile to make your own.  Add more jalapeno for spicier, or even fresh cilantro would be good in this.  Ive never had this at Chili's so I dont know how authentic it is.  But its a great, easy, and fast salsa to make.  Everyone loved it!

It's Super Bowl Sunday and we are just having a family party so I'm just throwing stuff together. I just made it and it's sitting in the fridge. I had to try it right away though and it was good. I'm sure it will only get better as it chills. Even though I ate Chili's Chips and Salsa along with their top shelf margarita :) (and I LOVED it) all the time in college it's been awhile since I've had it so I don't remember what it was like. Update: Made it again (Aug. 2006) with tomatoes from the garden instead of the can of whole tomatoes. Much better. Will be making again and again.

reviews.review_text: Oh wow, this was so good. I was skeptical at first....For me, salsa is all about the fresh ingredients. I was nervous using all canned stuff. I was wrong! I doubled the amount of jalepenos and added a large handful of cilantro and this was to die for. It did not last long in my house, and it does taste even better the next day. I am making some more tonight. It stays fresher a lot longer than fresh salsa too! It doesn't break down as much. This is something I think I will ALWAYS have in my fridge from now on. It is EXCELLENT! Thanks for sharing!

I've been working on my salsa skills for the past year. Usually I use fresh ingredients, or I cook the ingredients. It never even occurred to me to use canned tomatoes until I looked up this recipe. I am obsessed with Chili's salsa, so I decided to give this recipe a try. I used the suggestions and added fresh garlic and lime juice. I added about four fresh jalapenos without the seeds, so mine ended up pretty spicy. It got rave reviews from the family. I personally loved the consistency. I think the taste and consistency were close to Chili's version and it was the easiest recipe to make. I am saving this recipe and I will continue to play with it. It's a keeper.

attributes.source_text: mine ended up pretty spicy
It got rave reviews from the family

reviews.review_text: This is great, the texture is perfect, because I don't like chunky salsa. I added fresh garlic, a fresh jalepeno pepper (which made it quite hot), fresh cilantro and some parsley. I didn't have garlic salt, so i used garlic powder, and added just a little kosher salt. It wasn't too garlicky with the fresh garlic and the powder. I also put some pepper in it. I will defintely make this again, and it was really close Chili' Salsa, now if I could just find chips, like the thin, and crispy ones they serve!

attributes.source_text: which made it quite hot
It wasn't too garlicky with the fresh garlic and the powder

reviews.review_text: Wow!! Good stuff!! Hard to believe canned tomatoes can make this good tasting salsa. I did use shimmerchk suggestion and added garlic, cilantro and lime juice. I also didn't have canned jalapenos and used fresh ones. Three as a matter of fact, 'cause mine don't seem very hot for some reason. We love salsa and when I can't get fresh tomatoes this is my next best choice. Also love the fact this is SO EASY to make. The hardest part is waiting for it to meld. Thanks for posting this keeper.

I love this salsa.  I have been making for several months now, and I'm just now getting around to writing a review.  I just made some today.  I made it for my family members, who are Mexican food lovers, and they LOVED it.  I took the advice of another reviewer, and I add cilantro, lime, and minced garlic.  The nice thing about this recipe is you can adjust the ingredients to your taste.  Make sure when you buy the diced tomatoes, though, that they're not Italian!  Been there, done that.  And it's hard to mask those flavors.   Great recipe!  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: I made it for my family members, who are Mexican food lovers, and they LOVED it

reviews.review_text: Although I don't know that I've ever had Chili's salsa -- so I don't know how good of a clone this is -- I do know it tastes very much like other restaurant salsas that I love. The salsa is very flavorful with just a hint of sweetness. It was surprisingly fresh tasting, despite the use of canned tomatoes. I did use fresh jalapeno, not canned, and added extra since I like it hot. I also added some fresh cilantro that I needed to use up. This recipe has gone into my "favorites" file.

attributes.source_text: with just a hint of sweetness
It was surprisingly fresh tasting

reviews.review_text: I was seriously EXTREMELY leery about making this one!!  I've made salsas before but never with these ingredients.  I've never used canned anything to make a "fresh" salsa...but this was GOOD!  Probably one of the best salsa recipes that I have tried.  I made it EXACTLY as indicated...  I even included the sugar.  It's such a small amount that all it really does is slightly cut through the acidity.  You can't even tell there's sugar in it!  Delicious!  I will be making this on a weekly basis!

attributes.source_text: You can't even tell there's sugar in it!

reviews.review_text: So this salsa is wonderful for sure! The only thing that I decided to do differently then the recipe is to add a whole fresh jalapino rather then the canned kind, and it really tasted wonderful. As a person who does not like cilantro, this salsa has a great refreshing taste and I you can really make it as mild or hot as you want it based on how much jalapinos you add. I am a college student so I am always looking for things to snack on or take for group dinners and this is pretty cost effective and delicious, making it the perfect option!

reviews.review_text: This was good, truly you are right, don't use pickled jalapeno's. My second batch (the right way, was good tasting, had a nice consistency, not exactly chili's and not hot enough for my sweet little family, maybe next time I will also lessen the cumin and up the garlic salt, thanks for a good one! Update tweaked it and now we love it. I put in 2 jalapenos, 1/2 belle pepper, 1 clove garlic, and left out the cumin and sugar, then I stuck it in the blender and froze it. Thanks again.

items.label: All-Purpose Stir-Fry Sauce (Brown Garlic Sauce)
items.name: All-Purpose Stir-Fry Sauce (Brown Garlic Sauce)
items.description: Adapted from Martin Yan's Chinese Cooking for Dummies. This is my favorite stir-fry sauce. It makes enough for two meals. Having extra on hand makes for a quick meal. My son will actually eat vegetables he can dip in the sauce! WARNING about the amount of soy sauce. When I used Kikkoman soy sauce, I found this sauce far too salty. I now use Angostura, which is much lower in salt. When adding soy sauce, start with less than half the amount and slowly add more to taste. Using vegetable broth makes this vegetarian. Yield: 1 3/4 cups (couldn't get that amount entered)
instructions: In a bowl, combine soy sauce, broth, rice wine, sugar, sesame oil and white pepper. (See note in intro about the soy sauce).
Dissolve the cornstarch in 1/4 cup water.
Heat a pan over high heat; add the cooking oil, swirling to coat; add the garlic and ginger; cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 15 seconds.
Add the soy sauce mixture; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cornstarch solution and cook, stirring, until the sauce boils and thickens.

reviews.review_text: I made garlic chicken with the garlic sauce, it was the best I've ever had! Never ordering takeout again! I paired with a simple fried rice recipe, wish I knew how to find the recipe number for you. Only thing I tweaked was, I cut the soy sauce in half, used mirin instead of rice wine and added an extra tablespoon of garlic. For the chicken I cut up breasts in about 2-3 inch strips, then dredged lightly in flour. I find cutting them in strips or chunks is easiest because you only steaming for 10-15 minutes. Add 1-2 tbsp Of butter, 1 tbsp Of oil to a frying pan. Fry for about 1-2 minutes on one side. Flip chicken, cover with tinfoil or lid and shut burner off. Let steam for 10-15 minutes. Do not open lid! Chicken will be so moist you can barely pick it up with a fork! Then I add the garlic sauce recipe to the chicken, heat for a maybe a minute or so just to get sauce warm again. Amazing recipe!! Definitely must try!!

attributes.source_text: I made garlic chicken with the garlic sauce
Chicken will be so moist you can barely pick it up with a fork

reviews.review_text: Wow!  This sauce is amazing! It smelled incredible cooking.  I used low sodium chicken broth and low sodium soy sauce.  I ended up adding a little salt because it wasn't salty enough.  Next time I will use regular chicken broth.  I cooked the sauce, and kept it on very low on the stove top while I made the stir-fry.  I put a little oil in a stir fry pan, added chicken strips and cooked until no longer pink.  I threw in fresh broccoli florets and cooked about a minute, until it was bright green.  Then I added fresh snow peas, red pepper strips and fresh mushrooms.  I poured the sauce over and stir fried it all together for approximately 2 minutes.  Served over white rice.  Served mandarin oranges on the side.  It was a delicious meal!  Thanks for a great recipe that will definitely be made again and again.  For those of you who don't know (because I didn't know until today), rice wine is different than rice vinegar and rice wine vinegar.  Rice wine is also called sake.  I found rice flavored Oriental cooking wine in the Asian section of our supermarket.

Great recipe! Definitely a keeper! I had a bunch of vegetables I was needing to use up, along with some leftover chuck steak and chicken, so I threw it all to together! It's been in the 90's and I honestly was not looking forward to having stir-fry for dinner, but for the sake of using up food so it did not get wasted. . .I did. :o) This recipe did not disappoint! In fact, it made dinner thoroughly enjoyable! The good news is there is leftovers for tonight! I used low-sodium soy sauce, tweaked the recipe slightly, as I did not have just Rice Wine, but had on hand Rice Vinegar which I used. I added about an extra tablespoon of sugar, and added about 2 tablespoons of Hoisin sauce. I used TruRoots rice from Cosco which is a combination of Quinoa, wild rice, red rice, and brown rice. Not usually a fan of those types of rice, but this is truly my favorite rice anymore. For vegetables, I used what I had on hand; bok choy, broccoli, mushrooms, green pepper, carrots, onions, yellow crookneck squash, and green beans (with those I steamed slightly before adding).

attributes.source_text: it made dinner thoroughly enjoyable

reviews.review_text: I've been looking for a long time for a quick and easy recipe for actual Garlic Sauce for a few years now and landed here.. I'm surprised how much it made.. mind you.. I cook food from the far east all the time.. so I tend to have some more exotic ingredients in the house on the regular.. For example I added black vinegar and white vinegar to it, and quality soy instead of that burned pitch black junk they sell in most common grocers.. I recommend something like Mushroom soy or Pearl River or Swan River Bridge soy. Pearl River Bridge is sweeter than Swan River Bridge, and the usual Mushroom Soy can be a bit salty, so go easier on it. I'm very pleased with the recipe and the quantity.. It's nice to have enough left over for several subsequent meals. I also used a tablespoon of Master Brand Korean Fermented Bean Paste and some garlic chili paste, since I love my spicy food. Next time I will also cut back on the sugar so it won't be more of almost teriyaki sweet. I cut back by 1/2T. on the soy. I also might do a bit more garlic and ginger since I like such sauces to be a bit lemony and strong. Thank you very much..

Making it tonight for my daughter to compliment a pan fried whole red snapper (Yum!). Wanted to comment on the salt issues - other than the soy sauce, the chicken broth (or stock) you use can add a large quantity of salt, especially canned broth or (yikes) broth from chicken base. The person who commented on using water to cut the soy sauce in half makes sense as it also dilutes the salt from the broth. Combining all these salty ingredients you will need to be careful and start with half quantities - increasing the amount to taste. Also remember - you are reducing this sauce a bit when it boils - this will further concentrate the salt. Can't wait to try it!

Used the sauce as a base for chicken and broccoli stir fry tonight and both kids loved it! Did make some additions/substitutions due to what was on hand and personal preferences. Added a couple tablespoons of rice vinegar in place of the wine. Used a combination of brown sugar and honey in place of the regular sugar and some onion and garlic powder (didn't measure just added to taste). Didn't have fresh broccoli so used frozen which had been thawed. After browning the chicken I dumped the broccoli over the top along with the sauce and a few sliced green onions and cooked for about 5 minutes, adjusted the seasonings and served over rice. (149)

attributes.source_text: both kids loved it

reviews.review_text: I had to make a beef stir-fry tonight, for certain reasons: I had the right veggies, and husband didn't feel like steak-in-a-pan; he's not really a steak man. And the two sirloin steaks were shouting from the fridge and about to attack me, they'd been there so long. (Vacuum-sealed, thank heavens!) I thought I'd cobble together an orangey-soy sauce, then saw my one single orange had gone bad. To the computer and Zaar for inspiration, but how to find a sauce and not a whole recipe??? I found this one. It's been my decision from some time ago to give 5 stars only to recipes which, to my (yes, subjective!!) taste, cannot be improved upon (nasty witch, me!). This sauce, especially for the beef, cannot be improved upon. It's a great sauce, and if anyone thinks it might be too salty, NO, it is not. It is dead right. I had all the ingredients except for the rice wine, so I used a very dry sherry. Didn't seem to affect the sauce negatively. It was also quick to make, and then I just had to stir-fry the rest of the stuff in batches. Thanks, Connie!!!

attributes.source_text: if anyone thinks it might be too salty, NO, it is not

reviews.review_text:
Delicious! My family said it tasted like something straight out of a restaurant. It beats my original (lazy) way of making stirfry, which involved simply combining soy sauce and stir-fry sauce.I substituted the rice wine for orange juice and it gave it a sweet, tangy taste. Sprinkle some red pepper flakes in, and creates the perfect balance of sweet and spicy. I used GROUND ginger and black pepper instead of white. Finally, because I was very conscious of the amount of soy sauce, I used less than 1/3 cup of Kikkoman soy sauce, and added more as necessary.

I definitely will try this recipe again. In fact, I JUST ate some (added it to a shrimp, chicken, onion, broccoli, and red, green, and yellow pepper stirfry and pour the rest over a homemade shrimp fried rice) and I'm already thinking about demolishing my leftovers. Thanks Connie!

reviews.review_text: I do not consider myself that good at making "chinese" food but this is quite good.  I did not have rice wine and used about 3 tablespoons of rice wine vinegar.  I used less oil in the stir fry and one T of each sesame seed oil and veggie (canola oil).  I have some nifty dried ginger (Penzey's) that I haul out for occasions like this.  Soaked it in water and then cut it up with a kitchen scissors.  I also think I can get two meals out of one sauce recipe.  I stir fried chicken, sugar snap peas, green beans, onions, carrots and some green pepper and served it with brown rice.  Yum.  Can't wait to share this with my DS.  I think he will like it also.

reviews.review_text: OMG!!! It came out excellent!!! Thank you everyone for all of your suggested tweaks! I took the advice of so many others who warned that the recipe is too salty, so I used 1/3 cup of reduced sodium soy sauce and then I added a little more but it was still a little bland, so then I added two packets of regular soy sauce (from Chinese takeout) and that did the trick. I also substituted low fat reduced sodium beef broth instead of chicken broth. I didn't have rice wine, so I substituted Marsala wine...and I only used 2 Tblsns of sugar. As someone else said, the cornstarch mixture was too much for this recipe, so I added it little by little and ended up using about 1/2 of it and It came out perfect...tasted just like a Chinese takeout dish! My friend and I were amazed at how authentic it tasted! This recipe is a winner!!! I used it to make Fried Tofu with Steamed Vegetables. It was awesome!

attributes.source_text: tasted just like a Chinese takeout dish

reviews.review_text: This sauce is VERY similar to the one used at my local Chinese restaurant. It's absolutely delicious. I agree with the other reviewers about decreasing the amount of soy sauce used. I used only 1/2 a cup of low sodium soy sauce and instead added another 1/3 cup of unsalted beef broth and it was perfect--anything more would have been too salty. I also substituted mirin for rice wine and flour for corn starch. I used only 2 TBSP of sugar and 1 TBSP of cooking oil--more than that really isn't necessary. Everything yieled about 1.5 cups of a super amazing garlic sauce that I liberally sprea over four large bowls of beef and broccoli. Yum!

reviews.review_text: Wow, just what I was looking for! I did read some reviews and used low sodium soy sauce (which is the only one I keep in stock). Already had all ingredients in my pantry. Only change I made is ommiting the cooking oil. That is due to me only having crushed garlic and crushed ginger. It can burn too easily. Just heated up the sauce with the crushed garlic/ginger, then added the non-gmo corn starch/water mix. Perfect balance for tonights meal of seared steak bites with rice, asparagas and juliennne carrots. I tasted the sauce, fantastic! I know my husband is going to be thrilled with this beef bowl tonight!
