reviews.review_text: I made this soup tonight and slightly tweaked it after reading people's reviews and it came out excellent. I used the chicken boullion, celery, onion, and red pepper (though I added a lil more than called for). I also upped the cumin and added an extra 1/2 teaspoon. I also added 1/4 teaspoon of cayenne and it gave it a smooth kick. I omitted the lemon juice and cornstarch (as I didn't have any) and just added a mixture of flour and water. I let it simmer a lil bit longer to really extract flavors from it and it tastes very very good.

attributes.source_text: it gave it a smooth kick

reviews.review_text: I'm a huge fan of this recipe, it's a hit at my house even with super picky eaters. I make the recipe vegetarian by using vegetable bouillon cubes. I always omit celery as I'm not a huge fan and the cornstarch at the end. I have made it both with water and vegetable stock but I prefer vegetable stock as it makes the soup more flavorful. Only issue is the first time I made the recipe It ended far too salty. So I would omit the 1/2 a table spoon of salt and I go as far as to use reduced sodium beans, but the latter is optional. This is a wonderful recipe and I'm always asked to prepare it regularly.

attributes.source_text: it's a hit at my house even with super picky eaters

reviews.review_text: I made the soup yesterday! It was the best. I did make a few revisions. I wanted to give it a little more spice so I sauteed 3 chorizo sausage links and chopped those and added to simmer with the bean soup. I also followed someone's suggestion of adding 1/2 jar of salsa. I added chix stock instead of the bouillon cubes and didn't need the cornstarch. I didn't want as much sodium so I drained 1 can of beans and semi-drained the other can. I didn't add any salt. It was restaurant quality! Will make again. Thanks for the recipe! Super easy and quick!! Tastes better the next day!

attributes.source_text: I wanted to give it a little more spice

reviews.review_text: This is phenomenal! I too changed it to fit what I had in my fridge (no red pepper, added carrots and a half a tomato), but kept the seasonings the same. (oops, and now that I look at it, I left out the cornstarch!) It's so good. We don't have a Panera around, so I can't compare it, but I don't care how it compares because it's great! It's vegan! It's wonderful. Thank you! ***ALSO - I meant to say this - there are about 100 fewer calories per serving than the nutrition info indicates because it's calculating for dried beans. Super low-cal and VERY filling. Awesome!***

Thank you so much for posting this recipe. I didn't have any celery on hand, and frankly I don't think it's needed. I probably won't add it for next time either. I'll probably end up mincing up some red pepper and freezing it for future recipes, this was so quick and easy... I adored it.

UPDATE: I just went to Panera cause we were out and needed something. Got their black bean soup and my toddler spit it out (loves mine!), and my husband declared that mine (this recipe) is sooooo much better. And it is! This recipe blows Panera's out of the water!

attributes.source_text: my husband declared that mine (this recipe) is sooooo much better

reviews.review_text: This is sooo good. I love black bean soup especially panera's and kick'n chicken's but this is great, not to mention also super quick and easy! I followed another reviewer and used the bird's eye seasoning blend, awesome I hate cutting veggies. I also used my homemade veggie broth and a little bit of better than boullion's veggie boullion, like 3 to tsp of cumin and 1 tsp of garlic. I also only used 1 can of beans since I'm the only one eating it. I also forgot about the chili powder. It's amazing that the lemon juice isn't noticed at all. Again it's just really good and even better with sour cream!

items.label: Beef Tips
items.name: Beef Tips
items.description: Make and share this Beef Tips recipe from Food.com.
instructions: In a large skillet, heat oil over high heat.
Saute the onion until translucent.
Add stew meat and cook on high heat until meat is browned on all sides (3-5 minutes). Pour 2 cups water, soy sauce, and worcestershire sauce into the skillet.
Stir in garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Bring to boil and reduce heat.
Cover and simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Then combine the gravy mix with 1 cup of water, mix thoroughly and stir into the meat. Bring to boil, stirring frequently until it slightly thickens.
Serve over egg noodles.

reviews.review_text: After I started making this recipe, and while it was simmering, I read through all the reviews and I ended up making the Beef Tips the following way... I used 1 cup of diced onion, and after I sautéed them and added the stew meat, I kept stirring the pot for the entire 3 minutes, so the meat and onions wouldn't stick to it. I did add the teaspoon of salt, but next time I'll either reduce it to a 1/4 tsp., or omit it all together. I only added 1/2 a teaspoon of black pepper, but next time I'll be sure to just add a 1/4 teaspoon. I did use the garlic powder which the recipe called for, and I used a regular soy sauce, but next time I may just use a less sodium soy sauce (such as Walmart's Great Value brand), as it has far less sodium than the other store brands. I simmered the meat (in the water) for exactly 1-1/2 hours, as that's all the time it took to tenderize the meat. To make sure the liquid had thickened up nicely, I only used a 1/2 cup of water (along with 2 tablespoons of cornstarch), and the packet of gravy mix. That was the trick to make sure the liquid had thickened into a nice gravy. Also, next time I think I'll use a less sodium gravy mix, the McCormick brand. My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed this recipe, but the only one regret I had, I wish I had more stew meat in the freezer, so I could make this again. The next time I happen to make Beef Tips, I will definitely be using this recipe, and along with the adjustments I made to the recipe.

attributes.source_text: all the time it took to tenderize the meat
My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed this recipe

reviews.review_text: I tried to do this in the crockpot with not so great results. I adjusted the recipe for 3 pounds of stew meat, since that's what I had, and I did sub red wine for part of the soy and Worcestershire as recommended by some other reviews. I also used frozen chopped onions instead of fresh and added a large can of sliced mushrooms, drained. I followed the rest of the recipe from there, except the last cup of water (2 cups with the adjusted recipe), which I left out since you need less liquid when cooking with the slow cooker. Unfortunately, there was still too much liquid. Even after adding 2 packages of gravy mix and a cornstarch slurry, the sauce never thickened up. But, the good thing was it still tasted really great! My husband gave it a 4 as it was and I would give it a 4 for flavor myself. I do want to try this again on the stove so I can see how the gravy thickens up the right way before I give this one official stars. But if it tastes as good on the cook top as it did in the crockpot, plus it has real gravy, I'm betting it'll be a 5 star recipe. Thanks so much!

attributes.source_text: My husband gave it a 4

reviews.review_text: I would fill the page with stars for this if I could!  Yummy Yummy Good!!  I made mine in the crock pot so I switched it up a little but the structure was all yours!  Here's what I did...  First I halved the recipe to 3 servings (still quite a bit for my small family)  I put S&P & garlic seasoning on the meat and rubbed it in real good then covered and let sit in the fridge for about an hour to absorb the flavors.  Then I seared the meat and put the meat in the crockpot.  I placed the onion on top of the meat.  Then I deglazed the pan with balsamic vinager to get all the yummy bits up.  To that I added the worchester sauce, soy, and a little garlic powder, stired it to mix and poured over the onion and meat.  Covered it all up and let it cook on low for about 7 hours then I pulled out a ladel of the juices and mixed in some powdered gravy mix, wisked it together and added back to the pot for the last hour.  When it was all done my family could not say enough good things.  Thank you SOO much for this wonderful dinner that I just shared with my family.  (^_^)

attributes.source_text: my family could not say enough good things
this wonderful dinner that I just shared with my family

reviews.review_text: You know how you read a recipe and you think, "I have all that stuff, this'll be great!" and then it turns out you have none of it after you started?  Well that's what I did.  I'm posting this to show substitutions that worked for me.  Didn't have any brown gravy mix so I coated the meat in flour, pepper and thyme before browning and used a can of beef broth instead of water.  Didn't have soy sauce so I used full amount of Worcester sauce and added some balsamic vinegar. To top it all off, once I got it brown I realised that what I had thought was beef had been labeled wrong in our freezer and was actually pork.  I don't know how it still turned out great but I have to tell you it was phenomenal.  I didn't cook it for the full amount of time because I was worried about the flavors overly condensing resulting in too much salt.  This want over big.  Loved it!

Yummy!!! We really enjoyed this recipe. After reading the suggestions of many of the other reviewers I omitted the additional salt all together. I used 1/8th of a cup of reduced sodium soy sauce and 1/8th of a cup or Worceshire sauce. I used a cup of water and 1 1/2 cups of beef broth and added about 12 oz of sliced mushrooms. I didn't add the additional cup of water the recipe called for but, just ladled out some of the broth from the cooking process into a measuring cup and then added two gravy packets to the broth, whisked the mixture and then added it to the rest of the mixture, this provided a ideal gravy to the dish. 
I think next time I will reduce the Worcestershire sauce to 2 Tbs and increase the beef broth...I personally didn't care for the tang that the worcestershire sauce brought to the dish. Thank you for sharing this dish, this will definately be added to the rotation. :)

Dana, I've made beef tips for years but decided on a whim to try your recipe.  This is the way I will make it from now on!  Awesome. A friend was cleaning out her freezer and gave me the meat which was from beef she had processed at the locker.  She had told me that what she gave me was tough and older and to do what I wanted with it.  Well I took her tough old stew meat, browned it and made the sauce then threw it all in the crockpot on low over night and all day.  When I got home from work I took took off the lid, turned it to high, made the gravy and stirred it in, letting it boil.  We had it over buttered noodles and I was quick enough to make a small portion for my friend.  She loved it and asked for the recipe.  Bet she wishes she would of kept the meat!  I only wish I could of gotten a picture of it.  Thanks for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: She loved it and asked for the recipe

reviews.review_text: I thought that this was OK.  I substituted 1 cup of the water with 1 cup merlot, and used 2 large cloves of fresh garlic.  My only complaint was that I thought it tasted extremely salty, and I had omitted the salt and used reduced sodium soy sauce.  I also had some weird tasting meat (I think it was a bad cut, I don't blame the recipe for that).  I think that next time I will reduce the soy and worcestershire sauces to 2 TB as one of the reviewers did, and fill it out with red wine, then use water for everything else.  I am giving this 4 stars because my stepson absolutely loved this and gobbled it up, which is very much a rarity, as he is a PICKY eater.  So any recipe that he likes is worth at least 4 stars in my book.  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: my stepson absolutely loved this and gobbled it up
he is a PICKY eater

reviews.review_text:
Hey Dana..similar to what I always cook..except I don't use soy sauce, but I'd put beef in flour before putting in hot oil to brown some, I also put worcestershire sauce in with beef..then add ingredients..I also use 2-3 tsp. of parsley, 1-2 tsp. celery salt, 2 beef bouillion cubes (or 2 tsp beef bouillion powder), 1 tsp. poultry seasoning, 1 tsp.garlic salt, and about 1 tsp or 1 1/2 tsp of liquid steak seasoning. Sometimes for my boyfriend, I'd put some cut-up carrots and a small can of mushrooms in.
Good...and yours is good but you might want to think about reducing your soy sauce. 
Thanks!

I agree, Excellent! The meat was very tender and the taste was fantastic! I made a few adjustment because I was only cooking for two and didn't have all the exact ingredients. I used 1 pound beef stew meat that I cut into smaller chunks which I browned in olive oil with fresh garlic. As other reviewers suggested I lowered the soy and worchestershire sauce to 1tbsp each and added no salt (I forgot the black pepper), and for remaining the liquid I used 2 tbsp red wine and added 1/2 pound of fresh sliced mushrooms. I made the mistake of cutting the brown gravy mix in half, too so the end result was too runny, though. (My bad!) Thanks again for a new addition to my cookbook!!

attributes.source_text: The meat was very tender

reviews.review_text: You can find my adjustments in a lengthy explanation within the "tweak" category. I was being modest when I said I've made this about 22 times. The first two times, I followed the recipe exactly. Long story short (minus some extra ingredients): 1 tsp. of brown gravy powder (not a whole packet), get rid of the garlic (which I otherwise love), splash of balsamic, less salt, thicken slightly with a Tbs. cornstarch mixed in a bit of water before added at end, and double the sauce (or halve the amount of meat). Stew instructions included. Oh, and I forgot to mention in that section that it's way better served over homemade mashed potatoes or next to homemade scalloped/cheddar potatoes. I have mastered this dish and thank the author greatly for inspiring my own version. That whole packet of brown gravy though? Just... no. No, no, no, no, no. That's the only reason I knocked off a star. Just... how could you?

This was very similar to the beef tips that my family has been making for as long as I can remember. We really enjoyed it. I wanted to add the mushrooms and wine so next time I will try that. I did use fresh garlic and sauteed it with the onions and added celery since I wanted to use it before having to toss it out. I used low sodium soy and didn't feel that it was too salty, although I did not add the additional salt, however, I do always salt and pepper my meat and lightly flour before browning.  I think the gravy package may be what is contributing too much salt for some people depending on the brand you buy.  Thanks for this easy, tasty and filling post!

attributes.source_text: didn't feel that it was too salty

reviews.review_text: This was great! When I was little, beef tips in gravy served over warm egg noodles was my absolute favorite, so I was so pumped to find this recipe! I read all the reviews (yes, all 52!) and went ahead and made a few changes- I used 2 tablespoons of soy sauce and 2 tablespoons of worcestershire sauce, a little more than 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and I omitted the 1 teaspoon of salt. (I was very paranoid it would be too salty, because so many people said it was.) I omitted the vegetable oil and used olive oil flavored cooking spray. Also, I used a little more than 2 pounds of beef loin sirloin steak- Since it wasn't beef stew meat, it didn't take as long to cook. I used a large sweet vidalia onion. Overall, this made a wonderful beef tips in gravy. I will be making this again!

MY DH devoured this!!! He LOVED IT!!!  I did make some changes.  I used 1.25 lbs of stew beef because there's only 2 of us, and I didn't use the onion because I'm not fond of them.  On the last step, instead of adding 1 cup of water to the gravy mix, I just sprikled the gravy in the liquid that was already there, it made a perfect consistancy (I saw some people complain the liquid was too thin, mine thickened up nicely this way).  The flavor was *wonderful* - the "gravy' this made was absolutely delicious.  However, as many reviewers said, it WAS too salty for me... and I even omitted the teaspoon of salt (do NOT add that!!).  Maybe next time I'll try a reduced sodium soy sauce and use a little less.  Other than that, it really was a great tasting meal... very tender meat (I simmered 2 hours).  We had it over egg noodles!

I made the recipe as is, based upon a couple of suggestions- I lessened the amount of salt, and I substituted 1/2 cup of Merlot for 1/2 cup of water, so ended up with 1.5 c water. Complete perfection, served with mashed potatoes. As it's just the 2 of us, we have enough left over for three lunches, with gravy in the freezer to enjoy over noodles or a steak some other day. items.label: Ranch Chicken Thighs
items.name: Ranch Chicken Thighs
items.description:
Needed a quick & easy weeknight meal. This is adapted from an old Taste of Home magazine. The chicken is tasty & juicy, with a nice crunchy crust. You won't miss the skin!  
ETA -- some say this is too bland.  The ranch dressing is not enough seasoning.  I do add season salt to taste (Nature's Seasonings) to the bread crumb mixture for more flavor.  Hopefully as a cook, you will know what to add to suit you and your family's taste.
instructions: In a shallow bowl, combine crumbs, Parmesan cheese, cornmeal, Italian seasoning, and seasoned salt.
Dip chicken into salad dressing, then coat with crumb mixture.
Place chicken in a greased 13x9 baking dish.
Bake, uncovered, at 375 degrees for 45 minutes or until juices run clear.

reviews.review_text:
I doubled the recipe because DH eats a lot.  I cooked them for about 1hour and 15 minutes.  They weren't crispy when they were done but when reheated in the oven the next day, they were.  Also, when they came out of the oven, they were floating in chicken fat.

Also, I had to use a lot more dressing and crumb mixture.  Even when I got to 6 thighs, I had added more to the coating dishes as there wasn't enough so I probably used 3x what was called for.

These were tasty but I have far better chicken thigh recipes to make this again.

attributes.source_text: when reheated in the oven the next day, they were

reviews.review_text: I don't know about the one person who didn't like this... I think it's great. I've made it with the skin off, bone in & boneless skinless and i've done it with breasts.. (advise cutting them in half) I've done it with blue chhese, with ranch & with chunky garlic ceasar.. I think I added extra seasonong, because I am so used to breading & baking that I just always add paprika & cracked black pepper. Don't shoot the poster if you like things spicier, just add more spice. It's a good recipe. One less dish than the flour egg & crumb as the dressing is the first 2 steps. Thank-you Kiwi...Oh, right, you're from Kentucky, not New Zealand ...thanks KeyWee. Good dish..delish!

Wow! I am so impressed that such a simple and quick recipe can taste so good! I followed your directions exactly. I used Panko breadcrumbs as that is all I had, (and I used a Recipezaar recipe of Italian herb mix I got on the website, but can't remember what number). I don't even eat Ranch on my salads, and as someone of Italian heritage, it was against my nature to couple the Italian seasoning with it, but I have to confess, it was delicious. I plan on making this for my next large group gathering -- that's how tasty, easy and inexpensive this recipe is! Thanks!

This was fabulous! We all loved it. I used boneless, skinless thighs, but adhered to the cooking time in the recipe, and it was right on, very moist inside and crunchy on the outside. I'll lightly salt and pepper the chicken before dipping in the dressing next time, and I used Panko because I just prefer it. Even our daughter raved about it, stuck as she is on ranch dressing, and hates that we eat so much chicken at our house. And the possibilities! We're thinking bleu cheese, Green Goddess, and on and on! What a keeper, thanks so much for sharing this!

I dusted the chicken with flour first since I was using a low fat dressing and I was afraid it would be thinner than regular.  My chicken wasn't done in 45 minutes.  I turned the oven to 400 degrees for another 20 minutes.  I don't know if it was because I used a low fat dressing but it tasted sort of sour to us.  I would try this again using Italian dressing.  While the flavor was disappointing the chicken was very moist and the coating very crunchy.  I'm sorry we didn't like it more but I think it was just our personal taste and not the recipe.

Seasoned salt, pepper, smoked paprika, onion powder.<br/>And baked at the same temp/time the recipe called for.<br/>Great recipe and best of all no frying ! Thanks.

reviews.review_text: Wow, Keywee! What a super chicken recipe! I loved it but, more importantly, my WIFE loved it too. items.label: Thai Chicken Breasts
items.name: Thai Chicken Breasts
items.description: This recipe actually calls for Breasts, but I used thighs and they were moist and lucious! Goes well with steamed Basamati Rice.
instructions: combine the gingerrot, garlic and red pepper flakes in a cup and set aside.
Mix flour with salt and pepper to taste and dredge chicken pieces in this.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet.
Saute the chicken until browned on both sides and cooked through.
Remove the chicken and put in a warm dish, set aside in low oven to keep warm.
Add the ginger-garlic mixture to the skillet and saute until lightly browned.
Add the soy sauce, brown sugar, vinegar and fish sauce (if using).
Bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer, stirring frequently, until the sauce reduces and thickens.
Pour the sauce over the chicken pieces in the warm serving dish and keep warm until ready to serve.
Trim and shred the sugar snap peas diagonally.
Just prior to serving sprinkle the top of the chicken with the shredded snap peas.

reviews.review_text:
Very good!
I did add just a bit more red pepper, not much, but I like spicy. However, the overall taste didn't change at all.  I though it was very good.  Followed exact except for the garnish of the peas. I love them sauteed, so I used them as a side dish sauteed in sesame oil and garnish the chicken with fresh cilantro since I had a ton in my herb box.  It was very good with the chicken.
I used fish sauce in mine because I had some on hand, but anchovy paste, which I also had would of worked well too.  

I though it was excellent. And the peas would of been great as a garnish, I just love them sauteed, but they would of been very good as your recipe states.

On my list and will certainly make again.  Would be excellent with thighs as well. Nice recipe thx

I am joining the rest of the reviewers with a 5 star rating.  Excellent dish.  I did use boneless, skinless chicken thighs, well trimmed of visible fat.  After browning, I drained off all the fat and then added a small amount of olive oil to saute the ginger, garlic and red pepper flakes.  I used fish sauce as I had some in the frig.  I did not have sugar snap peas so just chopped some green onions and sprinled on the top.  Served with brown rice and broccoli.  Thanks for posting MarieAlice.
PS  I forgot to mention that I used the Spenda Brown Sugar blend and it worked fine.  My husband is prediabetic so I am always looking for ways to reduce carbs and calories.

What more can I say about this recipe that hasn't already been said! It is quick, easy and absolutely delicious. I only used 2 breasts but kept the amount of sauce the same which was perfect. I used  a little less then the 1/8 tsp. of red pepper flakes and believe it or not it was a bit too spicy for me! I am sensitive to hot spices but I never thought that amount would be too much. For me I would tone it down even more next time... my husband thought it was zingy. He also loved this dish and doesnt usually say too much about my cooking. I will definitely be making it regularly. The one other change I made was to use Splenda brown sugar and reduced it to a little more then a 1/4 cup and it was fine... might even reduce further the next time.

I skipped the whole flouring step b/c DH and I were in a hurry and it was still outstanding! I also used low sodium soy sauce and I really can't say enough about how good this is. Don't let the fish sauce scare you away! I'm not a big seafood/fish person, but the fish sauce is a MUST. This would probably still be good w/o, but you wouldn't have that little something different that makes this unique and gives it that "Thai" flavor. I've already given this recipe to a friend and was super tempted to make this the night after we first tried it. This is SO in the rotation now! Thanks MarieAlice! GREAT recipe!

reviews.review_text: Very good. I took advice from other reviewers and cut up the chicken breast into bite-sized pieces and doubled the sauce. Also, I find that chicken breast can get dry and tough when fried, so I changed the cooking procedure to this recipe by first sauteing the chicken pieces and then adding the remaining ingredients directly into the frying pan with the chicken still in the pan. I boiled down the sauce and stirred the chicken in the sauce frequently. That worked out well, as the chicken pieces absorbed some of the sauce and were fork-tender when done. My kids and husband asked me to make this recipe again. There is something missing to this sauce, though--maybe pineapple or orange juice? I'll be making this again and will find out. I served this meal with white rice and black beans (the Goya recipe on the back of the Goya black beans can; it's the best black bean recipe). I will use this recipe often!

Altered the recipe a bit: I chose to mix all the ingredients as a marinade for the chicken, let it sit in a gallon bag for about 10-15 mins, and then added it all to a skillet. 
Used fish sauce (patis) and replaced the white wine vinegar with rice wine vinegar. Also added a few drops of sesame seed oil to the mixture as it adds a nice slight smoky flavor. This is so delicious and easy to throw together for dinner!

I gathered that although rice vinegar was fine it did not have the acidity of ww vinegar. instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F Line a rimmed baking sheet with Reynolds Wrap® Foil. Spray lightly with non-stick spray or use non-stick Reynolds Wrap® Foil.

items.label: Buttered Egg Noodles (Best Ever)
items.name: Buttered Egg Noodles (Best Ever)
items.description: Make and share this Buttered Egg Noodles (Best Ever) recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Bring water, 2 boullion cubes and 1/2 stick of butter to boil using med to high heat.
Add egg noodles.
Cook until noodles are desired texture.
(About 6-8 minutes) During last minute of cooking add remaining 1/2 stick of butter.
(You may add additional butter if desired. Also you may use 1 can of chicken broth instead of bullion. I suggest using bullion).

reviews.review_text: Uh, helloooo!! This was AMAZING! I did add about 2 cups of water as I could immediately tell the 1 1/2 cups would not be enough to cover the noodles. I then added about a spoonful of butter and one more bullion cube. I saw that it didn't need any butter at the end, it was just too goood! For those thinking about making this it's basically one of those recipes you just figure out as you go.  The amount of water, butter and even bullion is totally up to you.  More noddles, more of the other ingredients!  But if you make close to 8 oz then 2 1/2-3 1/2 cups of water should do the job.  Thanks so much for sharing! This is a keeper!!!

Obviously, this doesn't need another review, but what the hey...  These noddled were groovy.  My new word for 2008...lol!  It was such an innovative way to make buttered noodles, and the fam loved them.  I, too, only used 1/2 stick butter (total), used a little extra water, and at the end added cracked black pepper and garlic powder.  Remember folks....stir, stir, stir....have to keep those noddles moving while they're cooking.  I think maybe next time I'll try a butter substitute just to make it a bit healthier.  This is now saved in my "tried and true" folder.  Thanks so much for a winner!

attributes.source_text: an innovative way to make buttered noodles
the fam loved them

reviews.review_text:
These worked so well for us! Not only do they taste wonderful but I have a tiny kitchen and not having to drain the noodles was a huge help for me.  I didn't use Wyler's chicken cubes, I used a teaspoon of Watkin's in some homemade broth and I didn't add as much butter as the recipe called for, only about half.  I'll definitely be making noodles this way again....it's so easy and delicious!  Thanks David!
****update on 8/27/06**** since my husband's heart 'incident', I've had to change our cooking habits.  I made this favorite recipe of ours a bit differently and it worked!  I used sodium-free, Herb Ox chicken boullion, Earth Balance 'Buttery Sticks' (which are no cholesterol, non-dairy) and for the noodles, I used 'No Yolks' egg noodles.  This was still terrific and I'm so glad we can still enjoy this recipe!  Thanks again David Ball :)

I just saw chefhopeful's review this a.m.
and decided to try this even though I knew it wouldn't work..thought the amount of water would be way off..
was very glad I was wrong..the amounts were RIGHT ON!!!
I did stay right there and stir quite frequently as another reviewer stated since the amount of water IS SO SMALL

noodles..thanks for posting this it is a real winner

reviews.review_text: YUMMY!  These were delicous.  Instead of real butter I mostly used light margarine.  It turned out great!  I addded lots of salt, pepper, and parsley to flavor it nicely.  At the end of cooking I did add 2 tbs. of real butter along with the light margarine.  This needs to be frequently stirred since the water doesnt completely cover.  Also covering your pot while it boils will give an extra hand on steaming those top noodles that arent under the water.  After the 6-8 minutes it was perfectly cooked and all the liquid was sucked right up into those noodles.  Im glad I found this recipe!  I will be making it all the time!

Very good, very easy!  I did make a 12 oz bag, so I upped the water to 2 1/4 cups and did 3 cubes, and 1/2 stick butter.  I kept covered on medium and stirred often, but had to add about 1 cup more water! I did not add more butter.  Served with brocolli and grilled chops.  The kids loved them.  So much better than the packaged mixes.  Thanks for sharing.  I do think a whole stick (which would be 1/2 cup) butter would be way too much, so one cup (2 sticks???) would be excessive. reviews.review_text: I gave this recipe 4 stars. My family really liked these noodles. My 3 & 5 yrs old newphews woofed them right down and asked for seconds. The only problem I had with the recipe was the sauce never thickened with 8oz of noodles, so after they cooked I removed them added 8oz more of noodles and 1/4 cup more water and cooked the noodles until tender and poured the sauce over all the noodles. Next time I will start with the 16oz of noodles. Overall these were so good and we will have these again for sure. Thank you so much for posting a yummy recipe. Christine (internetnut)

reviews.review_text: Speedy and simple, this is a real keeper for homestyle dinners. I doubled the recipe except for the butter, kept that about 3/4 - 1 stick, and found it to be a good balance; still a bit greasy but good flavor. I kept the pan covered when I wasn't stirring (do stir often!)to try and keep as much moisture in as possible but still needed to add about 1/3 c extra water near the end to get the noodles to our desired consistency (perhaps due to less butter?). With the sodium in the boullion cubes, we definitely didn't need any salt at the table, lol. I think this could be a good basis for one pot dinners...add in frozen peas and cooked chicken, or use beef boullion and add in mushrooms and cooked ground beef, etc. I served this with Super Simple Crockpot Chicken and Gravy #98380 and they work well together. This will definitely go in our menu rotation...thanks! :o)

Thank you, gonna make some more of these asap!

Next time, I would decrease the amount of butter and use unsalted butter (or use a low-sodium chicken broth instead of the bouillon cubes) and I have no doubt it will be a 5-Star recipe for us! This was such a simple and easy recipe to make that I was surprised at how good the noodles tasted.  Given that the recipe calls for 1/2 cup butter I was surprised that it wasn't greasy. items.label: Best Cream of Broccoli Soup
items.name: Best Cream of Broccoli Soup
items.description: This recipe is thick and flavorful. Simple, delicious, and quick to make. Hope that you enjoy it as much as my family does. I have added chicken to this soup, very good
instructions: Melt 2 tablespoons butter in medium sized stock pot, and sauté onion, garlic and celery until tender.
Add broccoli and broth; cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Purée soup  (I use a hand blender) or mash with potato masher.
Return to heat.
In small saucepan, over medium heat melt 3 tablespoons butter, stir in flour and add milk.
Stir until thick and bubbly, add to soup.
Add cheese; stir until melted.
Season with pepper and serve.

reviews.review_text: Clearly, this recipe does not need another 5* review, but I couldn't resist. I had some broccoli & cream that I needed to use up, and selected this recipe. I omitted the celery (didn't have any), used a head of broccoli without measuring, used part cream and the rest whole milk, and used Gouda and a small handful of Parmesan (actually Grana Padano, which is just as delicious & cheaper). Followed the method in accordance with the recipe. This is terrific! I loved the delicious broccoli taste, and do not agree with those who said the soup needed additional flavor - I feel that other spices would disguise the taste of the broccoli, which was not my intent. For me, this was a WOW! recipe that I will be making again frequently.

attributes.source_text: I loved the delicious broccoli taste

reviews.review_text:
Loved it! But in fairness, I changed it ...I used 1/2 cup 1% milk and 1 1/2 cups of pureed cauliflower (my own favority sneaky trick on my kids) instead of the 2 cups of milk, I cut the broth in 1./2 (due to many reviews about the thinness of the soup) and pureed 1 cup of brocolli and put the rest in chunky to compensate with heavier liquid. Also, I cut the velvetta and used fresh chunk mozzerella with a sprinkle of fresh parmesan crumble. That was a taste-based change - We opt more for the Italian cheeses than the cheddars and such. Plus, I like to keep this a white soup base (again, that is a child-based negotiation).

Nutmeg!!

Yummy!!! Thank you for sharing and inspiring.

This was easy, healthy and delicious - thanks! 
I strayed a little from the recipe, just to use what I had on hand. I used vegetable stock instead of chicken broth, used more garlic than the recipe suggested, and used grated cheddar cheese, about 150g, instead of Velveeta (I'm in Australia; I have to admit I don't know what Velveeta is!). 
It was delicous and ridiculously quick. I seasoned with a little salt and pepper as I went but the great thing about this recipe is that the broccoli flavour gets to shine. 
I didn't have a blender, so used a potato masher. This made for a chunkier soup, but the chunks were tasty, so that was fine! 
The celery is important for a more complex flavour, as is the roux, I think - it gives a good flavour base without the heaviness of cream. 
I'll be making this again - thanks!!

reviews.review_text: Excellent soup!  I didn't care for the other popular cream of broccoli soup recipe on this site, so when I received more broccoli from my food co-op, I decided to try this recipe and I'm so glad I did!  I sauteed the veggies in homemade vegetable broth instead of butter, skipped the flour and butter altogether, added about 1/4 cup of raw cashews (blended in my VitaMix--really makes soups like this creamy), used almond milk and used about 1 1/2 cups of sharp cheddar cheese in place of the velveeta.  I just realized I forgot to add the pepper and it's still delicious!  Normally I'm not a big fan of broccoli, but this makes it easy to like.  Thanks for the great recipe!

reviews.review_text: This definitely gets 5 stars from me for ease and taste!  I did change it up a little.  I didn't have celery, so I completely omitted that from the recipe--still tasted great!  I also used red onion because that is all I had on hand at the time.  I left the broccoli fairly chunky for some texture.  I did use 1/2 cup of evaporated milk.  I also used only the 1/2 cup of velveeta that the recipe calls for.  It turned out GREAT. items.label: The Ultimate Salmon Fillets
items.name: The Ultimate Salmon Fillets
items.description: Living on the west coast, we have eaten a great deal of salmon. This is ABSOLUTELY the best way we have found to cook it. It is so moist and the flavor is fantastic! Many reviewers have said that they think the cheese, especially the cheddar is unnecessary, and I have to admit that I omit the cheddar cheese myself. The flavour is a little too strong and it is extra fat that is not needed. I do like the sprinkling of parmesan with the paprika because it looks so nice when it is broiled. Using light mayonnaise and light sour cream or yogurt tastes just as good as the full fat versions and cuts down fat and calories even more. Thanks for all the great reviews!
instructions: Preheat oven to 450 degrees.
If frozen, partially thaw fillets and cut into serving size pieces.
Place in a greased baking dish.
Combine sour cream or yogurt, mustard, onion, dill, and mayonnaise.
Season with salt and pepper.
Spread mixture over fish.
Bake 20 minutes per inch of thickness of fish if frozen or 10-12 minutes if thawed.
When just done, sprinkle with the cheeses and a dash of paprika.
Broil 1 minute or until the cheese is bubbly and flecked with brown.
Serve with lemon wedges.

reviews.review_text: I made this one for lunch, picked up a nice never frozen salmon fillet weighing in a little over a pound.  I didn't have dill and used thyme, the fat free mayo and sour cream as well as a stone ground mustard, topping it with sliced vidalia green onion.  I also didn't broil it as it was done in 15 minutes.  It was absolutely fabulous!  I never would buy salmon because I thought I didn't like it...but guess what?  Now, I LOVE it, and remember how good it is for us too!  Thanks for a simple great recipe, dill would've probably been better but I had no complaints, only compliments.

attributes.source_text: I made this one for lunch

reviews.review_text:
This has GOT to be my new favorite way of making salmon! While my hubbie has never been a big fish eater (would much rather go for steak and taters) this is a 5 star in his book! I left the onions out and used stone ground mustard (more for taste and just to use what I had in the fridge). 

I didn't use as much cheese as called for, I didn't want to smother the flavor of the sour cream coating. One discovery, that mix of sour cream with the other ingredients makes a MEAN chip (in my case chili cheez-it) dip.

If doing in a toaster oven I found that I needed to bake just a bit longer (added 10 min to the unfrozen time).

This is a KEEPER!

attributes.source_text: this is a 5 star in his book

reviews.review_text: Wow!  I bought a huge 2.6 lb salmon steak and didn't really know what I wanted to do with it.  I found your recipe and knew that was the ticket.  I put the steak in a 13x9 glass dish, tripled the recipe (I used Dijon mustard) and poured it on top.  Baked it for 25 minutes (it was fresh, not frozen and about 1 and 1/2 inches thick) and sprinkled the shredded cheese on top, broiled it for 2 minutes and WOW.  I just ate one serving with a salad and put the other 4 servings in the fridge for later.  It was delicious and moist beyond belief!

attributes.source_text: moist beyond belief

reviews.review_text: Used the highliner 4 in a bag salmon fillets and cooked from frozen, approx 25 minutes. Served with basmati rice, a bag of japanese veg mix and red lobster cheese biscuits (Recipe #11571). The biscuit recipe is good but I always have left over garlic butter so this time I used the remaining garlic butter from the biscuit recipe to toss and coat the veg mix theb topped  with toasted almonds. Additionally, for broiling I layered 1/2 cup crushed pecans/walnuts, 2 green onions and then the cheese. This was very good! Thank you for posting it.

This was absolutely delicious! We did not expect it to be so good - typically liking our fish prepared without creamy sauces. But this was a wonderful recipe I will serve again proudly! Super easy, too! I made 1 1/2 lbs of salmon fillet to serve 3 adults and one toddler and we each would have gladly eaten the entire thing ourselves - it was that good! Very much a comfort food kind of feeling to it. Yes, we omitted the cheddar - feel it would have upset the perfect balance of flavors in the sauce and fish. We used the parmesan and paprika and browned under broiler for final minute or two. The dill was important, don't skip it,  and I used sour cream and Hellmans (Best Foods) mayo. A good spicy brown or dijon mustard works best. The tiny bits of diced onion were noticed and appreciated in the sauce, too. Definitely will make this again!

attributes.source_text: Very much a comfort food kind of feeling to it

reviews.review_text: This is an absolutely wonderful recipe. We had this for lunch today with a pilaf and roasted asparagus. I'm not normally a big fan of salmon (hubby is) but even I loved this, it was so mild and not in the least bit "fishy". Based on what I had, I used - honey dijon mustard, shallots, light mayo and lowfat sour cream. I used about a third of the sauce for 12oz of fish (0.74lb) and I thought it was plenty. Baked for 13 min with parmesan and paprika on top for the last 3. Left out the cheddar and it didn't really need salt. But I do think a sprinkling of a good salt like alderwood smoked sea salt would be a nice touch with the paprika. Thanks Paja for a wonderful recipe!

reviews.review_text: I don't care for fish, especially salmon, but this recipe gave me reason to keep up my Omega-3's. I used fresh salmon, made the "sauce" following  defined ingredients, except, I used (leftover) buttermilk ranch dressing (3) tablespoons, instead of the mayonnaise. Since  the dressing already had dill and seasonings in it, this worked out perfectly. I sure did use the parm cheese and cheddar cheese. Broiled at the last minute, terrific! This made a salmon lover (at least liker) out of me. My DH loved it too! Thanks, Paja!

attributes.source_text: My DH loved it too!

I was terrified of making something like this, but I went for it, followed your recipe to a tea, just doubled the amount of sauce because I was using 5 prepackaged individual salmon fillets. These were AMAZING!! Prepped everything early, and then covered them with tin foil until the guests arrived. Popped them in the oven, and skipped the cheese and the last broil. I can't WAIT to make these again, for us and for my family. Loved it, loved it, loved it!

One change to the recipe I made was I used ground mustard (1 tsp) instead of prepared mustard, because I was out of wet mustard and the second change I made to the recipe was cooking the fish at 425-degrees so I could cook potatoes in the oven with the fish--ofcourse we also had to cook the fish for close to an hour (our fish was 3-inches thick). When I cook fish I want to taste the fish, not a myriad of jarred accompaniments.  :s  It made an otherwise light and delicious supper heavy and stodgy.  Furthermore the recipe as it stands overcooks the salmon.  Salmon should be cooked just until the center is done, or if fresh, it should be slightly undercooked.  Would not make again.  Sorry. :(

I also think that this is the best way to make salmon.  I omitted the cheese and broiling as well because it is perfect without it.  Thank you so much for this one. reviews.review_text: Looking for yet another salmon recipe (Don't care for salmon) because the wife insists that we need the Omega Oils, less red meat, blah,blah,blah.  And then I came upon this one.  Sour cream, mayo, cheese, dill, what's not to like?  I bathed my fillet in lemon juice while I mixed up the rest of the stuff.  Couldn't have been easier.  Before spreading on the sauce I massaged in some Salmon rub we bought from our trip to Alaska.  Didn't use the cheddar but DID use the Parmesan.   Excellent.  I will now have my omega 3's on a regular basis!!

We love salmon and trying different ways of preparing it...  I used 4 4oz filets and thought the amount of sauce this recipes makes was overkill for this much salmon, IMO.  We like to taste the fish itself and let the sauce enhance it.  The sauce was delicious... but just a little too rich for us.  I will make half the amount of sauce next time and spread on a thinner layer.  We didn't bother with the cheddar...  the fish was delicious without...  Thanks for sharing...

Thanks for the great versatile recipe. I bet you could even use this on chicken breast and it would taste good.. :)

items.label: Alfredo Sauce
items.name: Alfredo Sauce
items.description:
This is my son's favorite meal. I make it with shrimp for him for his birthday every year. GREAT for company because it is so easy and yet taste wonderful! I cook this in the microwave, but I'm sure you could do it on the stove too. Times are what work in my microwave. Please use your own good judgment on times to use in your microwave. (In my quest to eat healthier, I now make it with light butter, light cream and reduced fat Parmesan cheese. It still tastes wonderful, but there isn't any guilt!)
PLEASE NOTE! This is an "authentic" Alfredo sauce recipe! Real Alfredo sauce *only* contains butter, cream, Parmesan cheese and pepper. It will be thin and there is no garlic in it! If you want a thicker sauce or one with garlic like modern restaurants serve, please look elsewhere! Recipe #52892 and Recipe #8596 are two good places to start.
instructions: Place butter in microwave safe pot and heat on high for 30 seconds or until melted.
Add cream and warm on high for approximately 1 minute.
Add Parmesan cheese and warm until cheese melts.
Add salt and pepper to taste. (If serving with shrimp, you might not need much salt.).
Pour over 4 servings of warm noodles (I use angel hair) and toss to coat. Serve immediately.

Notes: I serve it with cubed, grilled or broiled chicken breast mixed in with the noodles or shrimp. Add a green salad and you have a complete meal. I have used margarine and canned Parmesan cheese and it worked fine.

reviews.review_text: I'm giving this one 5 stars because my boyfriend who grew up on genuine Italian food LOVED it!  I can't say I was as impressed as he was but I know that was my own fault.  I couldn't find the cheese I had set out (my kitchen is under construction, give me a break) so I started using the "shake cheese" style parmesan and guestimating amounts.  I finally was able to find the real stuff and finished off with that.  Pretty sure that was my problem.  I also added a couple tsp. of dried hot pepper powder because it went with the rest of my meal but left out the salt.  It was easy and fast and pretty tasty.  I'll make it again and make sure to keep track of the cheese. :) Thanks!

attributes.source_text: my boyfriend who grew up on genuine Italian food LOVED it

reviews.review_text: Create a thick sauce without using flour or cornstarch. Instructions are from a site referring to Alfredo's original recipe. 1. Don't use cheap cheese, Parmigiano Reggiano is a good option for flavor. 2.Melt the butter in a sauce pan low heat to prevent separation. If it does, start over. 3.Slowly whisk in the cream and let simmer for about 1 -3 minute until mixture starts to thicken. The real thickening will occur with the addition of the cheese. 4.Add drained pasts to creamy, buttery mixture. 5. Remove from heat before adding the parmigiano to the Alfredo cream mixture and toss. Sauce will quickly thicken over time so wait at least 1 min before deciding to add more cheese to thicken. For thinner or thicker sauce adjust with amount of cheese but every time I follow these instructions the sauce is thick and sticks to the pasta. A pinch of fresh ground nutmeg gives subtle flavor.

I mixed in season chicken pieces & broccoli florets served over twisted noodles, Yummy!!!  My son (12) wanted to bottle the sauce & sell it at school! Well, better than one most kids are selling!  Thanks for the recipe! Oh and I added about 1/4 cup more heavy cream.

I did cook this on the stove & also added a little garlic and a cornflour mixed with water to thicken it.  I used it in a recipe to make shrimp & scallop crepes which were superb.  There is a little sauce left which I think will be wonderful with some pasta.  This was so easy and delicious.  Think it will be my new basic white sauce.   Thank you so much for a great recipe

I have never made this before as I know DH won't like it, he won't eat anything with cream or parmesan, he is so missing out this was fantastic, so quick and easy to make and I am ashamed to say that I ate it all myself, not all at the one sitting mind you, and yes it reheats very well. I had it with king prawn and some red and green peppers chopped very fine with riginette pasta it's a flat ribbon pasta with rippled edges to catch all that lovley sauce. When I have the girls round for lunch I am going to make this for them they will go nuts for it. Thanks for a great recipe Marg, next time I will get a picture.

Excellent, excellent recipe Marg!!  This recipe is so easy to make and yields a thick, rich, delicious sauce.  Sauteed 2 teaspoons Crushed Garlic in the butter then added 1 1/4 cups Heavy Cream, 1 cup Grated Parm/Romano and 1/2 teaspoon Course Ground Black Pepper.  Grilled a boneless/skinless chicken breast on the George Foreman Grill, sliced it into strips, topped it on hot Angel Hair pasta tossed with EVOO then topped with the sauce.  DELICIOUS!!  (Tip: If the sauce is a little thin for your taste, just add more Parmesan Cheese or a tad bit of Shredded Italian Blend Cheese to thicken.)

reviews.review_text: I made this last night, and we really enjoyed it.  I had no idea 'real' alfredo sauce was so incredibly easy!  I used margerine, whipping cream, and unfortunately had to use the 'fake' parmesan cheese.  The flavor was excellent, and the sauce wasn't too heavy, but my 'cheese' never melted and made the sauce extremely grainy.  I served it with fettucinni and broiled chicken breast with a side of broccoli and garlic bread.  Would have been perfect if not for the sauce texture!  We will definitely be making this again, with REAL parmesan cheese, and at that time I hope to upgrade my rating to a 5!  Thanks for posting!

items.label: Steven's World Famous To-Die-For Sour Cream Chicken
items.name: Steven's World Famous To-Die-For Sour Cream Chicken
items.description: I've modified my grandmother's recipe for the 21st Century. I can't have a dinner party and not asked to make this simple dish. Enjoy!
instructions: Clean chicken and pour sour cream over it and let marinate for about an hour in the refrigerator.
Meanwhile, take crackers and crush into medium course crumbs, mix in Parmesan cheese and Tarragon/ Marjoram.
Melt half of the butter and pour on the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish.
Dredge chicken in the cracker mixture and set in baking dish.
Repeat until complete.
Melt rest of butter and pour on top of chicken.
Bake@ 350 for 35-45 minutes or until golden brown.

reviews.review_text:
This was very good and moist.  I didn't add the tarragon because we don't have any and my husband doesn't like unfamiliar spices that well, plus on advice of others we used only 1 stick of butter and 2 rows of Ritz crackers and slightly more sour cream because I was afraid it would be too dry.  I did have to cook it about 20 minutes longer than it said, I baked it on one side, then turned all the pieces over and browned the other side. 
There's 3 of us, and I used 3 chicken breasts and had it with the fried rice on this site.  That was Way too much for us, we have about half of it left, so next time I'd only use 2 chicken breasts at most for 3 adults with a healthy appetite.  Good, but I don't think we'll have it often, because as my 2nd recipe from this site it's the #1 recipe, and I expected something Really Special.
I do love all of the options on this site though, it's more user-friendly and has more options than Epicurious, cooking.com and allrecipes.com, in my opinion.

Ok...I read ALL the reviews...here's what I did: I used 6 chicken tenderloins, didn't scrape off any sour cream when I dredged them, my crumb mixture was: 1 1/2 sleeves of ritz crackers,1/2 cup parm,1 tsp tarragon,three pinches of white pepper. I melted 1 stick of margarine, used about 4 tbls on the bottom of the dish, then the dredged chick, sprinkled the rest of the bread crumbs on top, followed by almost all of the rest of the melted butter,( I used the leftover melted butter for my green beans, no potato, so I wasn't "over saturated fatting us"...you don't miss it with the bread crumb mixture!)... then spinkled garlic powder over that, baked for 50 mins...OH MY GOD!!! this was simply awesome!! Who knew that chicken could cut like butter???? The flavor was just perfect!!!..my kids (11 & 16yrs) want to know why there isn't more??? gotta go, makin' another batch and printing this out for all my friends to try!!!

Then I added the leftover ranch dip we had (ranch salad dressing and sour cream) and poured it on top, combined some crushed Townhouse crackers with some parsley and parm cheese and 3 Tbs melted butter.  I stuck the whole thing in the oven for 10 minutes, then broiled it for about 4 minutes to really crisp up the crackers.  
This was fantastic- I ended up making the recipe the way it is written  about a week later, and Dh preferred the ranch flavor, so I will be doing that from now on.  Thanks so much for posting!

reviews.review_text: I did not make the recipe as it was posted due to the reviews so it's hard to rate it correctly. I payed attention to the reviews and make adjustments accordingly and it came out really really good. My DH didn't even use ketchup or hot sauce like he does on everything because he said he didn't want to ruin the flavor. I read complaints about the fat content, so I marinated it in fatfree yogurt instead of sourcream, and I greased the pan with a little bit of oil instead of all that butter, then I only drizzled about 1/4 cup butter over the chicken instead of 1/2. I also read reviews that the crackers were too sweet, so I used half Ritz crackers, half bread crumbs. As for the spices, I replaced the 2 TBS terragon with Garlic Salt and Italian Seasoning/ Oregano, salt/pepper, and a touch of Cayenne pepper. I think we should use the herbs we like here. It Was Really Great. Thank you Steven for the recipe and thank you everyone for the reviews.  This is how you perfect a recipe for yourself!

reviews.review_text:
Outstanding recipe.  I made the following changes: I used less than one half the butter and decided to use Progresso Italian Bread Crumbs.
Since I was using flavored breadcrumbs I didn't use additional spices.  However, I used Locatelli Cheese which is a type of Romano/Parmesan Cheese. Also, I didn't cut the Chicken Breasts.  Baked at 350 for 1 hour.  Excellent taste, flavor, easy to prepare.  I definitely would make this recipe again and I might even try the Ritz Crackers next time. 

Another thought, you could add Provolone Cheese on top of the Chicken when it's almost done add a little Marina Sauce and you have Chicken Parmesan with a side of Angle Hair Pasta, Antipasto Salad, nice Red Wine.  Great Gourmet Dinner!

This was good although the fat content is rather scary.  I tried to cut down on some of the fat content.  I only used 1/4 cup of butter, 1/8 for the bottom and 1/8  for the top and think that if I ever made this again I would forgo it completely as it isn't necessary to the dish.  I also used low fat sour cream.  I added garlic powder, pepper and onion powder to the ritz cracker mix as well as I thought it may be bland otherwise.  As I said, I would make this again with even more modifications and perhaps try with a thicker yogurt next time.  It is a promising base that makes the chicken super moist.  Thanks for posting.

attributes.source_text: makes the chicken super moist

reviews.review_text: This recipie sounds similar to Poppy Seed chicken, which is not only SO easy to make, it's delicious! you stew the chicken in a small amount of water, shred it. I use low or no fat sour cream, a can of cream of chicken soup and mix those together. Pour it over the chredded chicken. Mix melted margarine with about a roll of crushed ritz crackers and top the chicken mixture. Sprinkle about 2 T of poppy seeds over that and bake at 350 for about a half hour, or until it's bubbling. no real need to add salt and pepper as the crackers and poppy seeds have enough flavoring. This is hands down my boyfriends favorite meal. enjoy it!

attributes.source_text: my boyfriends favorite meal

reviews.review_text:
Maybe not 'to die for', but very tasty. I used 1 cup crushed chicken-in-a-biscuit crackers mixed with 1 cup Italian breadcrumbs for the breading. I wasn't entirely sure if this recipe was calling for fresh or dried herbs and I noticed that some people said the flavor was too strong so I went with 2 tablespoons of fresh chopped marjoram (thinking they used dried and it came out stronger). I did cut the butter down to 1/2 cup and it was still too much. It kept the breading a little soggy. At any rate, it was easy; the chicken was moist and tender and the overall flavor was good. Thanks.
â€” Update -
Tried this again with ritz and tarragon instead of chicken-in-a-biscuit and marjoram and added 1 1/2 tsp garlic salt, 1/2 tsp each cayenne pepper and thyme to the mix as well. Definately liked the marjoram better, no real preference on the crackers. I used turkey this time which worked fine and cut the butter down to 2 tbsp which made it still soggy on the bottom, but crisper on top.

attributes.source_text: the chicken was moist
the chicken was moist and tender
but crisper on top

reviews.review_text: All those reviews. So many different opinions. I read them and decided on my game plan.I cut the chicken in strips as per the recipe. I cut the butter down to 1/2 cup. Half in the bottom of the pan, and half sprinkled over the chicken. I used the ritz crackers, but only 1-1/2 sleeves. I used the tarragon, because we really do like it, but here again I cut the amount in half. I added 1 t salt, 1/2 t pepper,1/2 t cayenne pepper and 1/2 t thyme to the crumbs.  The baking time is pretty close, I baked it 50 minutes, and it was just right. We really liked this and will make it again.

I haven't tried this exact recipe, but I make something close to it. In the sour cream you need to add worcestershire sauce, enough to turn it a beige color, maybe 2 tble. spoons, and some lemon juice, about 1 tbl. You will first dip breast into butter, coating well, then dip it into sour cream mixture, then roll in ritz crumbs or bread crumbs, pour remaining butter over each breast, it shouldn't be much.
No need for the parmesan cheese nor the tarragon. 
The breast are so moist. I have found that the frozen boneless skinless breast are the most tender.

attributes.source_text: The breast are so moist
the most tender

reviews.review_text:
I read all the reviews before attempting this dish. I added tobasco sauce to the sour cream, marinated it for two hours, sprinkled it with garlic salt before rolling in Ritz and I used the roasted vegetable flavor Ritz. Also, I cut the amount of butter in half and it was plenty. 
That said, this recipe was rated a "keeper" by DH, my 9 year old DD said it was great(and she came back and ate it cold for snack) my 8 year old Ds said it was good, and my 7 year old DD said she didn't like the taste. I thought it was good but next time I will spice it up a bit more and maybe try the Chicken in a biscuit crackers.
All in all, we will be making this recipe again.

reviews.review_text: Very tasty, and easy. The chicken pieces were moist, the coating was flavorful, with the tarragon giving a unique exotic touch. The one cup of butter almost made me pass this by, but I'm glad I didn't - DH & DS make this a keeper. As another reviewer suggested, I only used 2T butter, nonfat s. cream, & whole wheat Ritz - these worked out great. One thing - I used less than half of the crumb mixture & of course had to toss it since it had come in contact with raw meat. One and a half rolls (5-6 oz.) would have been plenty. But then you may want to reduce the parm. cheese & tarragon to reflect this change.

attributes.source_text: The chicken pieces were moist
DH & DS make this a keeper

reviews.review_text: You have to give 5 stars to a recipe that you really go astray on and it still is super!  I thought I had gotten chicken out, instead I had thick pork chops.  Being short on time I thought, heck with it.  This should work on those too.  It did and it was darn good.  Juicy!!  I just pasted on the sour cream let em sit for an hour.  I used Ritz crackers the vegetable kind.  Did them in the oven for about the same amount of time turning them half way through.  Turned out great.  The coating was not real real crispy but browned nicely.  Thanks Steven, add pork chops to die for!

attributes.source_text: Juicy!!

reviews.review_text: The whole family loved this juicy & tender dish!  I let 3 lbs. of chicken tenderloins & sour cream marinate in a ziploc bag for an hour.  I only had 2 rolls of the Ritz crackers...I crushed those & added some Italian seasoned bread crumbs & grilled chicken seasoning.  I didn't have Parmesan cheese, so I used mozzarella.  To cut down on prep time, I layered the bottom with 1/2 cup of butter and a few crumbs.  I then layed the chicken on top of that, followed by the mozzarella, bread crumbs & butter.  I cooked this for 45 minutes and it came out perfect!

attributes.source_text: The whole family loved this
juicy & tender dish
juicy & tender dish

reviews.review_text: I give this recipe ten stars for taste and maybe 3 for texture of breading. The chicken was amazingly tender and moist ( I used tenders which always dry out) but the underside of the breading was soggy. I halved the butter and even though I drained the pan twice, there was still to much. Take my advice, grease your pan well and use maybe a 1/2 of stick total butter. I don't favor the spices used so I left those out and in place added a teaspoon of garlic powder to my crumbs along with a good dose of pepper. I will definitely make this again with less butter, Thanks!

attributes.source_text: The chicken was amazingly tender
amazingly tender and moist

items.label: Blueberry Pie
items.name: Blueberry Pie
items.description: I love the taste of mouth watering Fresh Blueberry Pie! Yum! This blueberry pie is probably the best I have ever tasted. I hope you will enjoy it, too! I do not use the refrigerated pie crust when making this pie, I use recipe #26205.   A NOTE to those who have made this pie before, I have increased the amount of flour in the ingredients list from 1/3 cup to 1/2 cup.
instructions: SPRINKLE berries with lemon juice; set aside.
FIT half of pastry in a 9-inch pieplate according to package directions.
COMBINE 1 cup sugar and next 3 ingredients; add to berries, stirring well.
Pour into pastry shell, and dot with butter.
UNFOLD remaining pastry on a lightly floured surface; roll gently with rolling pin to remove creases in pastry.
Place pastry over filling; seal and crimp edges.
Cut slits in top of crust to allow steam to escape.
Brush top of pastry with beaten egg, and sprinkle with 1 teaspoon sugar BAKE at 400° for 35 minutes or until golden.
Cover edges with aluminum foil to prevent overbrowning, if necessary.
Serve with vanilla ice cream, if desired.

reviews.review_text: I just realized I didn't rate this recipe yet. I had never made a blueberry pie before because I really "didn't" like it but my sons do. I've made it 3 times now and I'm a convert. This one is so easy to make that even I can do it. I did the unthinkable and used premade frozen crusts that come in their own tinfoil pans. This turned out to be a good thing. I took the advise of others and coated the bottom crust with the beaten egg and added 2 tablespoons of corn starch to the dry ingredients and berries. The cooking time I increased as well to 50 min. After 30 minutes I used the tinfoil plate to cover the pie to keep it from getting to brown instead of tinfoil around the edges. That worked so well as the crust came out nice and brown and not crumbly with the pie well cooked. For the best results let it cool then chill in the refridgerater before cutting. Awesome recipe Bev :>)

attributes.source_text: not crumbly

reviews.review_text: - Margarine? That's vegetable oil on a pie. Ick.<br/>- Someone didn't think lemon juice was appropriate. The acid (of lemon) and pectin (of fruit) react with sugar and will thicken (set).<br/>- Tapioca flour is better than all-purpose. It's grain free (for you non gluten folks), is smoother in texture and binds better.<br/>- I've never understood the infatuation with (read: overuse of) cinnamon. It can compete with the blueberry flavor. Maybe a teeny hint. Nutmeg is a softer complement.<br/>- Egg yolk vs. whole egg for glazing crust.<br/>- Make your own flaky crust and make sure you have a little bit of vinegar in it. You can also swap some water with blueberry, apple or orange juice. Certain liquors can be used as well.<br/>- 35 minutes is definitely not long enough. You need the blueberry mixture to get hot enough for the pectin, etc. to set. Cook at the bottom of the oven to avoid burning the crust too early.

Okay, so I had never made a "real" pie before, but blueberries are super cheap right now so I decided to go for it.  First of all, I was really surprised at how easy it was to make!  I bought the "unroll and bake" pie crust and brushed the bottom crust with egg white (per another reviewers suggestion), mixed up and added the filling, threw the top crust on, and tada!!  A beautifully browned and delicious pie came out of my oven just thirty-five minutes later!  I did add the extra flour per other reviewers suggestions, and my filling wasn't runny after sitting on the counter a couple of hours.  The one thing I didn't do correctly was to "mix well" before putting in the filling.  I thought I had mixed it up enough but I had some flour/sugar mixture in the bottom of my bowl at the end after pouring in the berries, which I poured right on top of the blueberries - big mistake!!  Next time I'll just mix it better or discard any extra since the very middle of my pie has a sort of gritty texture and is too sugary - right where I added the extra mix.  So our first bite of this pie was good but not great, that is until we got toward the outer edge of it and man, was it good then!  Just fresh blueberry flavor and not a lot of glaze like you get with many fruit pies.  As I was glancing over the recipe again yesterday I realized for the first time who posted the recipe, and I said to my husband "Well, of course this will be good...it's a BEV recipe"!  Anything I've ever tried of hers has always been great, and this pie definitely doesn't disappoint.  Thanks a million, Bev!

attributes.source_text: Just fresh blueberry flavor

reviews.review_text: Read here to make a perfect pie using frozen blueberries: We used the full five cups of blueberries thawed, thoroughly drained, and squeezed a bit in a colander.  To the flour mix we added one tsp of cornstarch.  In place of sugar, we used splenda (cup for cup) to save calories.  We tried previous reviewers methods of brushing egg wash on the bottom crust before putting in the filling; this worked well. My husband rolled the top crust out, cut it into seven 1 1/4" wide strips and did a basketweave pattern on top.  (We saw this method on Alton Brown's Good Eats Blueberry episode.)  We dotted the margarine in between the slats of the top crust, and brushed on an egg wash of one beaten egg with approx. 1 tbsp water.  It looked like a Martha Stewart pie.  Alton says to let it cool a long time--at least two hours--so that it will hold up.  Ours cut and held together perfectly, but we let it cool overnight.  We ate it for breakfast this morning warmed up with lowfat vanilla frozen yogurt on top.  It was easy, delicious, lower calorie than most pies, and a perfect spring/summer dish.  The frozen blueberries were much more cost effective, and I doubt anyone would guess that they were not fresh.  Thank you for sharing!

attributes.source_text: Ours cut and held together perfectly
We ate it for breakfast this morning
a perfect spring/summer dish
a perfect spring/summer dish

reviews.review_text: This recipe + modifications from reviews yielded the best blueberry pie I’ve ever made. I brushed the bottom and top crust with beaten egg, only used 3/4 c of sugar (brown sugar), added 1 Tbsp cornstarch to the filling, crushed up about 1/3 of the berries and combined/shook the filling in a ziplock bag to ensure everything was well combined. I ditched the cinnamon (personal preference) and added lemon zest. Finally I baked this for 35 minutes at 410, then an additional half hour at 375 (eventually covered). I think it’s actuslly pretty hard to overcook a pie like this as long as you make sure not to burn the crust. Don’t be afraid to let it go until the filling is fully bubbling over the sides. It was the perfect amount of sweetness, filling congealed beautifully and cut into complete slices, and the bottom crust stayed crispy. To die for!

attributes.source_text: It was the perfect amount of sweetness
filling congealed beautifully
the bottom crust stayed crispy

reviews.review_text: This was the first time I made a Blueberry  pie.  I made it for my dad for Father's Day (since it is his favorite). I used fresh blueberries and the pillsbury crust.  I read the reviews before and added a Tsp of Cornstarch to the Flour Mix.  I also did the egg wash on the bottom crust and top crust.  After I had all the berries added to the flour mix, I did squish them a little bit so it was still almost all whole berries, but some of the squished berries mixed well to make a great filling.  I saw that Alton Brown squished about half his berries first so I tried squishing some of mine.  I would probably make this pie exactly the same again.  My dad sent me a text message on Father's Day evening thanking me for the wonderful pie and said he had devoured a fourth of the pie before he had even realized what had happened.  :-)  Also, the vanilla ice cream is a must in my opinion. :-)

[Oops - somehow, the page hadn't finished loading and this review mistakenly went under another blueberry pie recipe. Here is my review, meant for THIS recipe: ] Perfect for the 4th of July. Five stars because even though it was the tiniest bit runny, the excellent flavor overcame everything else. Used the crust recommended, and overall this pie turned out excellent! I baked it for 50 minutes exactly on 400 (and it could've gone a bit longer, to be honest). Used foil around the edges the entire time (forgetting that I had an edge cover, ha) and made a foil tent for the top at about 30 minutes, as it was getting brown already. Turned out yummier than I'd imagined. Next time I will let it cook longer, cool longer, and yes, add a bit of corn starch for good measure. Either way, taste is excellent and my son - who doesn't love fruit pies - was licking his plate!

reviews.review_text: Bev, I truely wish I could give your pie recipe more than 5 stars Bev. I made this tonight but increased the fresh lemon juice by a tablespoon, and used frozen blueberries that I had in my freezer left from last season, although I am not really one to use frozen berries for pies, and from my previous experiences of "runny" fruit middles using frozen berries, I added in some quick tapioca, and that seemed to work wonderful! I am so pleased with the finished pie, the middle held together beautifully, and had a fantastic flavour. I used my butter pie crust recipe#66926 for the bottom, and used a crumb topping for the top... thank you very much for an outstanding pie recipe Bev! I will now go ahead and make many more using your recipe and frozen berries....Kitten:)

attributes.source_text: the middle held together beautifully

reviews.review_text: This was my first time making (or eating) a blueberry pie. My husband had requested it, after seeing blueberry pie on TV, so I tried this recipe, and it came out great. <br/><br/>I forgot the butter, so when I checked the pie at ~30 minutes, I brushed some melted butter on the top of the lattice crust (aiming to get some blobs in the lattice holes), before popping it back in the oven. After reading some of the reviews, I decided to let it bake a little longer (about 50 minutes).<br/><br/>It was *almost* too sweet, but that is probably because I'm not used to eating a lot of sugar. The sweetness was mellowed out perfectly by the vanilla ice cream. I might use slightly less sugar next time, but other than that, this pie was perfect. My husband was 100% pleased.

attributes.source_text: My husband was 100% pleased
The sweetness was mellowed out perfectly by the vanilla ice cream

reviews.review_text: This was the best tasting blueberry pie recipe. I loved the little hint of cinnamon. I did make my own crust, did add a teaspoon of vanilla and a Tblsp. of cornstarch as some said it was a bit runny. I also squished some of the blueberries with the back of a large spoon when stirring the flour mixture in. I used 1/2 cup flour. I followed the rest of the recipe as written. You do have to make sure to stir until you see a syrupy sauce so mix well! I baked it for about 30 minutes with only the edges covered and then I tented some foil on top and removed the edge rim off and baked another 20 minutes. I made sure to let the pie rest a few hours before cutting and serving. It was well set and not runny at all. I served it with caramel vanilla gelato. OMG! It was the best blueberry pie! Thanks for the recipe and I will be making this again soon!

attributes.source_text: I loved the little hint of cinnamon

reviews.review_text: Bev, If I could give this ten stars I would!I certainly hope that more people will try this recipe-it is sooooo good.:)Believe it or not ive never made a blueberry pie--so that intimidation factor was working against me--but this was such a hit.I made a few minor changes based on the reviews but thats all-used Pillsbury refrigerated pie crusts and did alter the cook time added about ten extra mins. The sugar on the top crust was the perfect compliment to your perfect pie filling.!Blueberries are on sale right now and your pie is being made over and over and shared with lots of happy souls--one devoured it for breakfast--said pie that good needs no ice cream and should be consumed immediately!!!Thanks ever so much for making my first blueberry pie a huge success!PeggyLynn

reviews.review_text: I made this pie as written except I substituted turbinado sugar to sprinkle on top as I thought the larger grains would look prettier.  I thought the pie was a little bit too sweet, but it could be because my berries were exceptionally sweet.  Next time I will reduce the amount of sugar to 1/2 Cup.  I baked my pie for 40 minutes and the berries were still a little firm, maybe because there were so many in there.  Next time I will bake for another ten minutes or more, maybe 55 minutes.  Love the egg brush and sugar on top, that really gives it a nice finishing touch.  We enjoyed the pie and there will be a next time.  I've already purchased some blueberries for it.  Thank you.

This recipe is great, but I did make some changes. As others suggested, I reduced the sugar to 3/4 cups and in turn reduced the flour to 1/3 cup. I did NOT use the cinnamon because I hate the warm spice it imparts, taking away from the fresh and fruity lemon- blueberry combo. I did add a teaspoon of vanilla extract though to enhance the flavors. I have no doubt that this filling would be amazing in any pie or pastry shell. As I result, I used Dufour Puffed Pastry and made 6 large turnovers. Rolled out the dough, scooped in the filling, sealed them, placed them in the freezer for 20 minutes, brushed them with egg white and placed them in a cookie sheet in a preheated 475 degree oven for 10 minutes. Reduced the heat to 375 and continued cooking another 15-20. Let them cool for 30 minutes (they do gel up nicely). Served with vanilla ice cream. Superb!

reviews.review_text:
Excellent.  My family loves this so much I am going to have to start making two at a time.  

I use a 8" pie plate and I've found that reducing the blueberries to 4 cups and mashing half of them makes a thicker filling so the pie more compact and easier to work with.  You may want to reduce the sugar to compensate for less berries.  I also reduce butter by at least half.

I use pie crust 13619 with half butter, half shortening.  The crust actually takes slightly longer to make than the pie itself, but I think it's worth it.

attributes.source_text: My family loves this so much

reviews.review_text: My local grocery store had a sale on blueberries, so I thought I would try this blueberry pie recipe.  After reading some of the other reviews, I too increased the flour to a 1/2 cup.  I also added 1 tsp lemon zest and a 1/4 tsp of nutmeg.  The aroma when I took the pie out of the oven was mouthwatering.  It was hard waiting for the pie to cool down so that I could have a piece.  It was worth the wait -- the pie was delicious. I took a couple of pieces over to my mother and father-in law because blueberry pie is their favorite.  They too agreed that this pie was delicious.  Thanks for sharing such a good and easy recipe.

attributes.source_text: I took a couple of pieces over to my mother and father-in law because blueberry pie is their favorite

reviews.review_text: Very good recipe! I have made it several times and tweaked the recipe a little bit. No drastic tweaks but instead of 5 cups blueberry I use 4 cups blueberry and 1 cup raspberry. Also, I make my own crust and I butter my pie pan and sprinkle cinnamon and sugar in the raw on the butter. Lastly, I brush the egg wash on the top of the pie but make sure not to use it all and pour in the juice left in the bowl from mixing the blueberries, raspberries, lime etc. And brush that around the rim of the crust then sprinkle a generous amount of sugar in the raw on the wash and juice mixture follwed by a light sprinkle of cinnamon. It creates a sweet berry flavored crispy/crunch on the thick part of the crust. My niece and nephew never eat the thick outer part of the crust on a regular pie, but they love this crust and eat every bite.
