reviews.review_text: I followed the recipe exactly.  The butter substitution idea that some reviewers suggested sounded tasty but shortening blends so nicely and adds nice texture so I went with shortening.  The texture of my cake is wonderful - not dry at all. I baked it at 340 degrees because my oven bakes hot.  I'm sure my oven setting contributed to my nicely evenly baked cake. I also rotated my 3 pans during the baking time to ensure even baking. (I made a double recipe - 3 nine inch pans & one 8 inch - I baked the 8 inch separately).  My complaint about this cake is the flavor. It's kind of blah. I also think it's not sweet enough. (I'm talking only about the cake recipe - I didn't use the icing recipe).  I think the flavor was lacking but I'm not sure how to improve it. So overall, it's an ok recipe.  Nice texture, easy to prepare and a beautiful looking cake but as far as flavor - you can probably find a better red velvet recipe (Or maybe I SHOULD have used butter instead of shortening!). By the way, I HAVE used this icing recipe on several occasions and it's always to rave reviews.  Old fashioned recipe with wonderful flavor, not too sweet with a whipped cream like texture. It's a great icing recipe.

attributes.source_text: not dry at all

reviews.review_text: To everyone who says this cake isn't good: try this, in the batter, i switched out the shortening with butter, which was way better for taste, and i mixed the cocoa into the dry ingredient mix to lighten the brown color. and i only used the food coloring last, and only enough for desired color. for the icing, instead of 3T of flour i do 1 1/2 T flour and 1 1/2 T corn starch into the milk, then i mix it up, then i strain it for lumps. then i heat it gradually in the microwave, checking it every so often and whisking until its thick and very hot. then i put in the sugar, mix it, and again strain it. then cool. when whipping flavoring and butter into it, i use a butter vanilla emulsion rather than straight vanilla. it gives it a much better flavor. and i use half the amount of butter and half shortening to hold the icing on the cake. if you do these things, it works so much better. everyone who as eaten this cake raves over it if you do it the way i did. i am a baker at a shop, and just made a wedding cake with this recipe.

This cake was delicious and offered a dramatic presentation, with the dark red cake and the white frosting. Being the first time out with this recipe, I followed the instructions to the letter. A few call outs:

1. The cake came out perfectly moist and dense. For reviewers saying that it was too dry, try adjusting the temperature of your oven and/or cook time. Different ovens cook at different temperatures, and I've burnt a cake more than once by being too literal with the instructions.

2. The flour frosting was amazing - liked whipped cream, but doesn't melt. Next time, I plan to increase the amounts called for in the recipe. I used two 8-inch diameter layers for the cake, and didn't have enough frosting. I had to make a second batch.

3. I would definitely recommend using 2 oz. of red dye. It yields a rich, dark red color for the cake. One ounce of dye made the cake look bright red - sort of like a clown nose or a fire truck. Some of the charm and sophistication that should come with this cake was lost.

attributes.source_text: The cake came out perfectly moist and dense
The cake came out perfectly moist and dense

reviews.review_text: It's the all-time classic Red-Velvet Cake recipe. Look no further this is it!!! Made this cake with Kittencal's Best Cream Cheese Icing cream cheese icing as another reviewer did and the cake turned out absolutely perfect. The only change I made was to use butter instead of the shortening. I baked the cake in three 8"X1" pans and each layer took around 15-20 minutes to cook. The only thing I would change next time (besides using butter) is to make 1.5 times the recipe as the amount of batter is a little low and so did not fill my pans properly and the layers came out a little thin. But still tasted excellent thought!!!! Next time I will make 2 times the recipe and use the extra batter to make a few cupcakes and then crumble the cupcakes up to decorate the sides of the cake!!!! Excellent recipe and this will be the recipe I keep forever! Thanks for Sharing!!

I made this for my anniversary because I wanted to try something that would have a "wow" factor.  That said, I prefer the red velvet cake made with oil.  To me, this cake lacked moistness (and it wasn't overcooked).  It was much better at room temperature than cold.  The icing was a trick - I made two batches of the milk/flour mixture before I was able to get *most* of the lumps out - even adding the milk gradually while using an electric mixer I was unable to get all the lumps out so I settled for getting it mainly lump free.  When heating the flour/milk, start with your burner on very low and when it clings to the surface of your whisk or spoon then its thick enough.  At least that was thick enough for me.  The icing did have a nice smooth texture, but, I think for red velvet I prefer the cream cheese and confectioners sugar icing.  Glad I tried it, but, I won't be making it again.

attributes.source_text: I made this for my anniversary
The icing did have a nice smooth texture

reviews.review_text: My Gramma used to make this cake for my father when he was a child and then when I came along I was able to experience the magic that this cake creates... But some how her recipe was lost, so thank God you have the same exact one that she made, so I went and was able to make it and it was just the same as when she was alive, it warmed my heart and brought tears to my eyes and also so many loving memories back!! I am getting married and we have decided to have this as our wedding cake, to celebrate with all of our loved ones and give them a piece of the joy that it has brought me through out my life with my gram... I will admit, I have to scrap my first try, because if you  don't mix and do everything right, it does come out a little off (meaning dry and over bearing of cocoa and food coloring), but it was such a great experience I really didn't mind. So to all that are going to make this... just take  your time and double check and when it comes out and you can enjoy, now you know how a little piece of heaven taste!! Thanks again, you really have made my life a little brighter!! :)

I wonder if the reason so many people say the cake is dry, is because those are the people who substituted butter instead of using shortening? I used butter-flavor shortening, then threw in a few Tbs of butter for good measure, too. Or maybe they think it's dry because they don't use the frosting as recommended? The frosting is very wet/moist...as a matter of fact, after icing all 4 layers of the cake, it seemed rather unstable as it was so tall and the frosting so loose, so I refrigerated the completed masterpiece overnight before serving, and no complaints of dryness. Perhaps some of the moistness comes from using the right frosting? (I made a double batch of the frosting and used all but about 1/4 cup of it!). Frosting is daunting, but I just did it....probably wasn't perfect (I think maybe a little lumpy), but the lady I made it for was the one who gave me the recipe and she said it tasted even better than when she made it! So, maybe it doesn't have to be perfect!

The cake is delicious. It's not difficult at all to make and not time consuming. I used 1/2 cup of butter instead of shortening and one ounce of red food coloring instead of 2 at the suggestion of other viewers. The cake was very moist. Do not overbake it.

NOW for the frosting. It tasted a lot like Dream Whip Whipped Topping ( it is a powder you mix with milk) and I didn't care for it. My mom made it a lot when I was growing up. My family didn't like the Frosting either. Because of the milk in the frosting, I refrigerated the cake because I was afraid it would spoil. And it seemed the icing became heavy instead of light and fluffy like when I first made it. It's also time consuming. If you do decide to make the icing, double it. I used 1 1/2 times the recipe, but I really stretched it to cover all 3 layers and the sides.

My family said that next time I make this, they want me to use buttercream icing. That's why I rated this 4 stars - because of the frosting.

attributes.source_text: The cake was very moist.

reviews.review_text: Made this for my granddaughters 15th birthday...she said it was the best red velvet cake she had ever had. I was worried about the icing but my husband encouraged me to use the original instead of subbing in a cream cheese icing. I only got two 9 in layers that I cut in half so the finished product was 4 layers. I used an entire batch of icing in the layers alone and about 1 and 1/2 batches of icing to ice the cake...as I did decorate it with my own butter cream roses in red and a white shell border, it was phenomenal!! Of 15-20 people, just a die hard butter cream fan was not absolutely thrilled with this cake, even one of my 2 1/2 year old grandsons passed on the triple chocolate cake served side by side (their brother turned 13 just a few days before so there were two cakes) and opted for the  red velvet. I will make this again, and again, and again!! The cream cheese icing was not missed, and in this case is highly overrated!

attributes.source_text: Made this for my granddaughters 15th birthday
she said it was the best red velvet cake she had ever had
one of my 2 1/2 year old grandsons passed on the triple chocolate cake served side by side

reviews.review_text: A friend requested a Red Velvet Cake for his graduation present and I made this one.  Had no problems with the recipe as written.  Was reluctant to add 2 OZ red food coloring - but I did and the cake was really really dark red.  Others have said 1 OZ does the trick.  Next time will try only 1 OZ. For the frosting:  I whisked (which I think is key) the flour into the milk one TBL at a time - then  I cooked it - stirring constantly for about 4 minutes till it got really really thick and sludge like...  Initially I was scared of the frosting (!) given all of the reviews - but when I mixed the cooled milk/flour sludge with the butter/sugar which had been running for about 8 minutes in my mixer, the frosting came together very very nicely and was excellent.  Actually recommended this frosting to a friend for a different desert!  All in all - the graduation crew said it was a perfect red velvet cake!  Thanks much!

attributes.source_text: for his graduation present
the graduation crew said it was a perfect red velvet cake

items.label: Cabbage for Those Who Dislike Cabbage
items.name: Cabbage for Those Who Dislike Cabbage
items.description: This is so much nicer than plain steamed or boiled cabbage. Try it on the cabbage haters in your family and see if it converts them.
instructions: In a large skillet, heat butter and oil over medium heat; add cabbage, garlic and brown sugar to pan.
Sauté until the cabbage is limp, about 5 minutes or so.
Reduce heat to medium-low and stir in vinegar.
Cook, stirring very often, for approximately 20 minutes; taste and if cabbage is too crunchy for you, continue to cook for a few more minutes.
Add salt and pepper to taste and serve.

reviews.review_text: This recipe was exactly what I was looking for!  I really liked it, although the rest of the family was more neutral.  (It was also possible they were OD-ing on cabbage last week from other things.)  I did add the onions, as many had suggested.  This is really cool:  My 6 y/o said "Why does it look like noodles?"  And, it did, as I had shredded the cabbage into long shreds.  Ever since he said that, when I eat it, I felt like I was eating buttered noodles, to the point where I am convinced this could be a great low-carb pasta substitute for certain sauces.  I'll have to work on a recipe...  Anyway, I also had leftovers, so I heated up some sliced smoked sausage (hot dogs would do nicely here) in a frying pan, then added a large pile of the cabbage, and when hot, added some scrambled eggs.  Delish plain or with mustard.  Thanks, Lennie ~ I do expect to make this again.

5 star all the way! - This recipe is so simple and the end result is so good . I got everthing ready i in the morning so it only took me minutes to prepare, I only cooked the cabbage for about 8 minutes (I like it crunchy) added the vinegar after 4 minutes.Instructions are clear and easy to follow . Thank you Lennie for a great recipe. P.S. there is a bit left over and that will be going into my "clean the Fridge: fried rice - Can't wait
Added note:   I made this again last night for about the 6th time! with a difference  I chopped up a large onion and sauted it it the butter/oil until it was really golden brown then followed the recipe except I used Balsamic vinegar - either way the original recipe or last nights variation this is an excellent veggie dish Thanks again Lennie

attributes.source_text: I like it crunchy

reviews.review_text: As one who rarely uses cabbage even though I like it, this was really good! I made this with half green and half purple cabbage to give it nice color.  LIke the others suggested, I doubled the sauce ingredients, mixed the brown sugar with the melted butter and oil, and added the vinegar (I used balsamic) after the cabbage had sauteed for a few minutes.  Instead of canola oil, I used sesame oil, which gave a nice flavor!  I served this with corned beef brisket and the sweet/tangy taste was a nice compliment to offset the saltiness of the corned beef.  Also, one thing i noticed is the cabbage reduces ALOT in size after sauteéing for 20 minutes.  My big wearever skillet was full when I started and it reduced to about 1/4 in the skillet when it was fully cooked.  I shred 1/2 each of an average sized green and purple cabbage into larger than bite size pieces and it was enough for the two of us with no leftovers.  Will definitely make this again with the different variations of red wine vinegar and/or onions.  I thought I'd try it also with red cooking wine sometime as well to see how that tastes.  If I do, I'll let you know! Definitely a keeper and a great excuse to make cabbage more often!

attributes.source_text: the sweet/tangy taste was a nice compliment
the sweet/tangy taste was a nice compliment

reviews.review_text:
After trying coleslaw once, I thought I would hate cabbage for life. Right now, I'm on a fat-flush diet (for the first time in my life). At first, I was disappointed to find that cabbage is high on the list of items to eat to attack belly fat. And THEN I found a Chinese Egg Rolls recipe (I used turkey meat) and now THIS recipe. My mouth was watering before this recipe finished cooking!

I followed the recipe, except no salt, and then made some substitutions and additions, for personal taste. First, I took another reviewer's advice and added a whole yellow onion, thinly sliced. I had part of a cole-slaw package leftover from the egg rolls that I used with a whole head of shredded green cabbage. I substituted olive oil for the canola, and ended up with about 1/4 cup olive oil, couldn't resist a second tbsp of butter, and 4-5 cloves of garlic in the pan. I also substituted Balsamic Vinegar for the red wine vinegar. I usually use a lot of spices, but on a whim, I was generous with Greek Seasoning as the only seasoning. Also, personally, I like my food spicy, so I added some thin slices of yellow hot peppers. Finally, I didn't want the package of crab meat I had on hand to go to waste, so in the last 2 or 3 minutes of cooking, added that, too. (I threw in the hot peppers at the same time as the crab.) Once the crab and peppers were thrown in, I added a small splash of lemon juice in the last minute of cooking.

I could hardly wait to eat by the time this was ready. I ate 2 servings of this with half a serving of Turkey Cutlets With Balsamic-Brown Sugar Sauce. I was in absolute heaven. Could have had an orgasm. lol Thanks, Lennie, for this recipe! My diet is now something I am really really enjoying!! (Imagine that.)

I didn't use salt as I don't cook with it & left out the sugar as British people don't add this to vegetable & salad dishes. The vinegar gave a lovely piquant flavour. The 2nd time, I added caramelised onions as one reviewer suggested. I think a gr8 dish with cold cuts & boiled potato or crinkle-cut chips (fries) & salad as well as more traditionally with gravy. I don't know any 'cabbage-haters', it's a typical British veg. I do recall a couple at school canteen dinners being sent back to their seats with no pudding for not eating it. I think the problem was that it was over-cooked & all those smelly sulphide aromas would come out. The frying here only has a little oil & the oil/vinegar cancels out those aromas, which don't really appear as it's cooked quick - or at least, I did, I added some water & it doesn't need 20mins. However, a whole head of cabbage if wilted like this would not serve 6 in my house unless lots of other veg were with it - definitely not 8 people. I'm making it again soon.

attributes.source_text: The vinegar gave a lovely piquant flavour

reviews.review_text:
In theory, this is an excellent recipe. I have cooked similar dishes before which I have enjoyed, but they weren't from recipes.

The problem was the cooking time & the type of cabbage I used (savoy, which does cook quicker than other types); I read the other reviews & decided to cook it for 5 minutes less than instructed, then noticed a few minutes before this that it looked a bit soggy & overcooked so turned off the heat. Since I'd expected it to take 15 mins I had to wait for the other dishes to cook & the standing time made it even worse. Luckily I really like cabbage, so I didn't find it totally inedible, but my son (who normally eats cabbage) really disliked it!

I'd like to try this again but with the cooking time reduced to perhaps 3-4 mins sauteing & 5-10 mins in vinegar. And perhaps use a thicker variety of cabbage next time!

It's not that I don't like cabbage, but I don't normally seek it out, and I've never made it before.  However, thought I'd try it for a change, and this saute sounded like just the thing!  I had a small head of cabbage, so I filled the dish out with sliced onion, bell pepper, celery and carrots, and a diced jalapeno pepper for a little background kick.  Based on several of the reviews, I used balsamic vinegar and increased the amount to about 2 or 3 tblspns.  Left the veggies pretty crunchy and drizzled just a bit of sesame oil over it at the end.  It was a big hit, and everyone loved it!  I never would have thought about using brown sugar and vinegar, and was pleasantly surprised at how well the flavors went together.  Excellent dish!  Thanks for posting.

attributes.source_text: Left the veggies pretty crunchy

reviews.review_text: The taste of this was pretty similar to the way my MIL taught me how to make cabbage, but I must say I really enjoyed the method of making this much more.  Because my husband likes bacon in his cabbage, I cooked and crumbled about 3 slices of bacon and added it to the mix.  Also, I used bacon grease instead of the oil and had to substitute cider vinegar for the red wine vinegar since it's what I had on hand.  Next time I want to try other reviewers' suggestion about adding some onion in while it cooks too.  20 minutes equaled perfect texture for us.  Easy to do and had great results.  Thanks for posting...we'll be using this method again and again!!!

Hungarians love cabbage, it's just part of our blood.  However I usually make it WITH something, corned beef, stuffed, cabbage and dumplings, etc.  I got the urge however to just try it by itself with a smoked sausage and this was the recipe I decided on.  I did modify it by frying two strips of bacon and using the render with butter instead of canola oil, added about 1/3 sliced sweet onion, and added the crisped bacon in at the very end.  Delicious.

What a  great way to cook cabbage. I agree, it could make a convert out of a cabbage hater. We all like cabbage and we loved it cooked this way. I cut down on the fat by about half and omitted the garlic, since one of the other dishes we were having was quite galicky. I added more than one tablespoon of vinegar, because it didn't seem very tangy with just one. At the end, I took off the lid and raised the heat a bit. This lightly caremalized the edges of the cabbage, and, I think added to the sweetness. Thanks for a great recipe, Lennie!

attributes.source_text: added to the sweetness

reviews.review_text: Dee-lish!  I've made this several times now for my husband and I and for extended family and it has been enjoyed by all who have tried it.  I took one reviewer's advice and added onion (cooking it in the butter for a wee while before adding the cabbage) and I think that makes a great recipe even better.  Once or twice I have used balsamic vinegar instead of the red wine vinegar and I think I prefer that, plus I (at least) doubled the amount of the vinegar.  Thanks, Lennie, for a fabulously useful cabbage recipe.

attributes.source_text: for my husband and I
for extended family

reviews.review_text: Very Very good!!! Lennie. Will be making it again and again and again..... Did use the sliced onion which caramalised very nicely. And used sunflower oil and plain vinegar (do not have balsamic or red wine)and all of us absolutely went bonkers!! The taste was very different from what we are used to. I made it both ways (cooked longer and shorter) and must say I prefer the crunch. I make cabbage in many ways and thanks for adding to my arsenal!!

attributes.source_text: The taste was very different from what we are used to
I prefer the crunch

reviews.review_text: This was really good.  I don't hate cabbage, but this was a nice way of preparing it.  I took LaceLady's suggestion of adding onions, and that was nice, but they didn't really come out tasting like carmelized onions, in my opinion.  I prepared it according to the amounts given, except that I used balsamic vinegar.  I didn't think it needed anything more than that, but I did also have the onions in there.  The family liked it too, so I'll make this again.  Thanks.

attributes.source_text: The family liked it too

reviews.review_text: I tasted as I stirred, and,like the others, thought the dish needed more flavor. I had already doubled the brown sugar and the balsamic vinegar,but still, it needed something. I crushed nearly 1/2 tsp dried tarragon and sprinkled ground ginger on it. It added the flavor I was looking for, but next time I won't double the sugar. I thought it was too sweet. DH gobbled it up and kept saying how delicious it was, and he is not too fond of cabbage..he ate the remainer that was in the pan and asked me to make it again!I had a small head of cabbage because DH dislikes cabbage!I used onions instead of garlic.

attributes.source_text: DH gobbled it up and kept saying how delicious it was

reviews.review_text: I'm biased because I like cabbage, but I think that only means that I'm harder to impress with a cabbage dish.  This dish was excellent.  I loved the combination of the vinegar, brown sugar, and of course, cabbage.  I didn't have red wine vine vinegar, so I used apple cider vinegar with a splash of balsamic.  I also sauteed a large onion beforehand & added it after step 2.  I also added a stalk of celery & sauteed it with the cabbage--yum (next time I will use two stalks).  I will either cut down the butter or leave it out altogether next time.  Thanks for a great and easy recipe!

If you already like cabbage, then the measurements are good.  I like cabbage and thought it was a very nice dish, but I can see why someone would think it is bland.  Cabbage IS bland.  If you have a crew that truly dislikes cabbage, then you should double the sugar and balsamic vinegar to give it more flavor.  I also carmelized the onions before adding the cabbage, and it didn't take 20 minutes to cook the cabbage.  The cabbage was the right "crunchiness" for me after about 10-15 minutes.

attributes.source_text: The cabbage was the right "crunchiness" for me

reviews.review_text: Well, Lennie, I really enjoyed this enough for 5 stars, but I love cabbage. My husband said it was "okay", but he hates cabbage. So, I arrived at 4 stars. Because I know he doesnt like cabbage, I decided to half the recipe, and I used a bag of the pre-shredded coleslaw. This worked out really well- he ate a little bit and I ate the rest and wanted more after that. I will definitely be making again- I could eat a half-batch by myself. Thank You!!

Wow, was this good.  I sauted some sliced onion in the butter/brown sugar before I added the cabbage.  I also used garlic powder instead of the cloves.  I like garlic only in small amounts.  I tried to get my cabbage hating DH to try it, but he woudn't.  My DD came in and found the leftovers in the pan and quickly finished it off exclaiming how good it was.  I will definitely make this again even though DH won't even try it.

attributes.source_text: My DD came in and found the leftovers in the pan and quickly finished it off exclaiming how good it was

items.label: Cucumber Salad
items.name: Cucumber Salad
items.description:
This is a REFRESHING, tangy Salad--low in fat. If you want it creamy and not so low in fat, just add 2 tablespoons mayonnaise.
 Be sure to slice the cucumbers and onions very very thin!
 Serve as salad or top open faced sandwiches with it!
instructions: Mix cucumbers and onions together.
Mix rest of ingredients together in a closed bowl and give a shake.
Add to cucumbers, chill till very cold & serve.

reviews.review_text: This was a great break from my usual cucumber salad recipe and I'll certainly be keeping it in my recipe box! The dill and red onion were a departure from my 'old standby' and they made this a really nice and refreshing salad even if I sliced my cukes thinner than I normally like! I used (1/2 t) dried dill since that's all I had and used cider vinegar the first time. The vinegar was a little strong so I think I'll try white vinegar next time. Thanks for a great recipe and another way to use up the mountains of cucumbers coming out of my garden!

attributes.source_text: a really nice and refreshing salad

reviews.review_text: My mother used to make this and I just love it! I made a few variations. I added the following: diced carrots, diced zucchini, one chopped tomato (seeds removed). I cut the dill back to a 'dash.' I went with the vinegar and sour cream. Lots of (course) pepper (my husband loves it!) No lemon juice or sugar. Turned out excellent after chilled! As a reviewer suggested, you must squeeze the water out of the cucumbers (which I forgot to do!) but it wasn't that bad.

attributes.source_text: my husband loves it!

reviews.review_text: I made this for a picnic we had on Saturday afternoon. I made sure to follow the directions exactly b/c I don't like to experiment with a recipe the first time I make it. I liked the flavor, and it seemed to go pretty quickly at the picnic. We only had a tiny bit of leftovers which were eaten the next day. It was a tiny bit more watery than i would like, but I think that could be fixed by not letting it sit too long before serving it. Thanks for posting this great & refreshing recipe. Oh, and I also added the mayo, and would probably never go without adding it, it gave it a great flavor & creaminess.

attributes.source_text: I made this for a picnic we had on Saturday afternoon
this great & refreshing recipe
it gave it a great flavor & creaminess

reviews.review_text: I loved this recipe, although I didn't see the necessity for sugar. It tasted great without. What I also like about such recipes as this one is how many different ways one can vary it. CrÃ¨me Fraiche, mayonnaise or yoghurt instead of sour cream. Replace vinegar or lemon juice for lime juice and if you don't like dill use basil,alone or in combination with garlic, instead. My sister made this a couple of nights ago and served it with celery sticks and julienned carrots. Delicious!!!

I made this cucumber salad with creamy Greek yoghurt rather than sour cream (personal taste preference and NOT exactly low fat!) and lemon juice rather than vinegar.  Otherwise I followed the recipe exactly.  Really delicious!  I’ve had this recipe saved with the intention of making it for some time, and finally made it to serve with Kaarin’s Kusherie (Egyptian Rice and Lentils) Recipe #134402, for the 2005 Zaar World Tour.  I’ll be making it again during the summer.  Loved it!  Thanks for another great recipe, Rita!

WHAT A LUNCH!!!! Boy, did this hit the spot! I made it as suggested with two minor changes....used 1/4 tsp sugar and only had dried dill; added 1/2 tsp full. I had some fresh pumpernickel bread which I first topped with a thick slice of beef tomato and then the salad. Ate it open-faced (one slice)along with some ice-cold grapes. Just a great late Sunday afternoon lunch. Oh, I used fresh lemon juice also. BTW.....did I already say that this was GREAT?

attributes.source_text: WHAT A LUNCH!!!!
Just a great late Sunday afternoon lunch

reviews.review_text: This has been a delicious standby in my family for years.  We go the creamy route, but eliminate the fat by using a tablespoon or two of fat free mayo or miracle whip.  Also, we are not huge dill fans, so I have always used mint instead of dill.  The mint seems to give it an even more summery taste.  On the off chance you do have any leftover, be prepared to be making a snack run to the fridge every couple minutes to snag a cuke out of the bowl.  At least, that's what I do!

attributes.source_text: We go the creamy route
The mint seems to give it an even more summery taste

reviews.review_text: I've never been much of a fan of cucumber salad but I needed to use up some cucumbers before they went bad so I made this. It was pretty good, and I like that it is very low in fat so I can eat as much as I want without feeling guilty. I don't like raw onions so I used celery instead. I had to double the sauce, but it wasn't a problem since I had plenty of vinegar, sour cream and sugar. I used dried dill instead of fresh and it worked fine.

This was a nice side for Recipe #186193. Made half a batch using up some regular and seedless cucumbers I had in the fridge. My hubby really enjoyed this and requested that I add more dill next time. I used vinegar and lemon juice...I just couldn't decide! Since I was not also eating this, I cut back on the onion. Don't need to be kissing Mr. Onion Breath later on this evening! ha ha. Made for my Babes for ZWT4. Thanks for sharing!

attributes.source_text: This was a nice side
My hubby really enjoyed this

reviews.review_text: What a fantastic cucumber recipe this is! I doubled the recipe and served this to guests along with a salmon dinner on Sunday, this is so light and refreshing and a wonderful change from a regular salad, not to mention a great way to use up cucumbers from my summer crop!  The only adjustment I made was I increased the sugar slightly. I know I will make this again soon, thank you for sharing this great cucumber recipe Rita we loved it!...Kitten:)

attributes.source_text: served this to guests
this is so light and refreshing
this is so light and refreshing

reviews.review_text: This is an excellent cucumber salad!!!  The dressing was perfect.  I often don't like sour cream dressings unless they contain salad dressing or mayo but this was delish.  I loved the dill with the cucumbers and the little bit of vinegar was tasty but not overpowering.  I added a couple of thinly sliced radishes to this salad, as I wanted to use them up.  They were a great addition.  I will for sure make this salad again and again.  Wonderful!!!

attributes.source_text: I loved the dill with the cucumbers
the little bit of vinegar was tasty
but not overpowering

reviews.review_text: This was definitely a nice and refreshing side dish!!  I used one cucumber peeled and one with skin on (since the recipe didn't specify) and next time I'll peel all cucumbers.  I used fresh lemon juice and 1/4 teaspoon of sugar.  While I enjoyed the flavor, I did think it needed a bit more punch just before serving so I added some Garli Garni to it until I got the flavour I wanted.  Delicious.  Will make again.

attributes.source_text: a nice and refreshing side dish
nice and refreshing

reviews.review_text: I made this very simple salad tonight to share with my neighbor.  He loved it...and...we both decided that the lemon juice and onions made our taste buds come alive!  I made this recipe as posted with a few changes.  I used half as much dill, I used nonfat sour cream and I added 1/2 c. frozen/thawed peas to make this salad a little bit sweeter.  Thank you for posting this and adding to my collection of fabulous recipes.  Sincerely, Sherry

attributes.source_text: He loved it
the lemon juice and onions made our taste buds come alive
the lemon juice and onions made our taste buds come alive

reviews.review_text: With a quick taste on my fingertip, I was in a time warp: sitting at my Oma's kitchen table in Germany having her cucumber salad. I almost cried. Thank you for a delicious dressing! I used plain Greek yogurt and only cucumber as my red onion had seen its better days, and, well, I thought I was growing dill but apparently not (still don't know what that plant is! LOL!), so I used dried dill. Yummy! Thank you so much, Rita!

I crave this light and tasty salad..hot day this is a cooler. I used a Julienne Vegetable Peeler and made cucumber " noodles" (see my photo) this was my only change. Next time after I julienne the cucumber into noodles..do this in the am. Ill put in a strainer in fridge to drain a till I make salad for dinner. Other than this..love love love this!<br/>Thank you!

attributes.source_text: light and tasty salad

reviews.review_text: A company-worthy dish.  I took your advice and added the mayonnaise, otherwise following the recipe as is.  I think I would've preferred the onion diced--will keep in mind for next time.  I agree that a fair amount of ground pepper compliments the sugar in this salad quite well.  Served this as a refreshing appetizer before a hearty bowl of pasta and meatballs.  Thank you for posting.

attributes.source_text: Served this as a refreshing appetizer
a refreshing appetizer
compliments the sugar in this salad quite well

reviews.review_text: I used a mandoline to slice the onion and cucumber very thinly. I wanted to see whether we liked the vinegar/sour cream combo or the lemon juice/yogurt combo better, so I divided the cukes and onions in half and made half with one and half wth the other. They were both really good but I think we preferred the vinegar/sour cream combo more. Thanks for a great recipe. *Made for ZWT 4*

items.label: Simple Caribbean Jerk Chicken
items.name: Simple Caribbean Jerk Chicken
items.description: I like jerk chicken but often don't have all the exotic ingredients. This simplifies the mix by using dry italian dressing. Yummy on the Grill!
instructions: Mix all ingredients except chicken in bowl.
Pour over chicken.
Cover and marinate 1 hour or over night in fridge.
GRILL it!
Enjoy!

reviews.review_text: UPDATE, Jan 24/'08: Made them last night (using chicken thighs again) but didn't cook them on the grill, this time I used a skillet pan (much to cold outside to grill) and they came out perfectly. I (mistakenly) added two teaspoons  of cinnamon (never try to carry on a conversation while preparing a recipe) and decided to also add some sugar (about 1 tsp) this time which added a nice sweetness to the sauce. They were delicious!  I made this recipe last night on the grill, using chicken thighs. I've never had Jerk chicken before so I can't vouch for the authenticity of the flavors but this recipe was delicious. I didn't have any ground red pepper so I substituted that with red pepper flakes. I only marinated them for an hour but they were tasty and very moist. I'll definitely be making these again.

attributes.source_text: they were tasty and very moist
added a nice sweetness to the sauce

reviews.review_text: I canNOT believe how good this is!!  I literally just took it off the grill a few minutes ago and snuck a couple of bites of chicken.  This is one of the easiest recipes I've used!  There was a sale at the store on cut up chicken, so I got to experiment all at one time with 'hindquarters' with the bone in (thighs and drumsticks), and I deboned and removed the skin from the breast pieces, it's all good! I never use Italian dressing packets, I'm going to the store tomorrow to stock up so I always have them on hand specifically for this recipe!  I will make again and again.

This was definitely outstanding!! I've had this in my "chicken" cookbook for awhile, and just got around to trying it tonight. I was a bit nervous because the ingredients sounded all a bit "weird" together (like italian salad dressing mix with cinnamon, etc)..  but WOW did these flavors blend PERFECT together.  I followed recipe EXACTLY as stated.  I marinated mine for a bit over 9 hours (started it after I fed our toddler breakfast, and started cooking when husband came home from work)..  kind of cold here now, so I used my foreman grill (and I used thin cutlets).. cooked for about 7 minutes.  YUM! I will most certainly serve this again and again!

Excellent recipe!!!  I used chicken tenders for the sake of shaving off marinating time (1-1/2 to 2 hrs.), and they turned out beautifully.  Served them to my 8 & 4 yr. olds, as well as the neighbors' family, and received rave reviewes.  Chicken was pared with a simple romaine salad (cucumbers, tomatoes, carrots & radish), tossed with Buttermilk Ranch Dressing.  Today, I thinly sliced the chicken left-overs (originally made 2 batches - all but 3 pieces were left), and served them on top of salad for lunch.  Will try with pork chops next, w/ grilled pineapple slices.  Thanks for sharing this quick, flavorful, and most excellent recipe!  In the box of family favorites :)

attributes.source_text: Served them to my 8 & 4 yr. olds
as well as the neighbors' family, and received rave reviewes
served them on top of salad for lunch

reviews.review_text: I made as written, stupendous, though I used skinless fillets as I don't like bones. I also tried 'Gary in AZ' ideas, with lime, beer & (my UK equivalent of) Smokey Joe sauce. It shouldn't have been called 'Jerk', it's like saying I had a Texan Chilli last night but used Basil instead of chilli powder. I call it Italian-inspired (maybe, but it does have Soy Sauce - which is neither Caribbean nor Italian) BBQ chicken. (I used a branded Italian herb mix, I wasn't sure if by seasoning, you meant this or a powder; I've found powders contain a lot of salt so I use herb mixes, more tasty anyway). It's just the name people don't like, it's a lovely recipe though.

This was absolutely delicious and very easy. The marinade is so thick and has a wonderful flavor when grilled.  We had just come back from the Bahamas and I was looking to replicate the Jerk Chicken Wraps they served at our resort.  Using your recipe, I grilled boneless breasts (cooked in 10 minutes), sliced them thinly, then put them into flour tortillas with cheddar cheese, wrapped them in foil and put them in the oven for 5 minutes or so to melt the cheese.  They were delicious!  Even my picky 7 yr. old loved them!  I didn't have crushed red pepper, so I used McCormick Grill Mates Monterey Steak seasoning (has red pepper in it) as a rub over the marinated chicken just before grilling.  Great recipe!

Yum!  I've been wanting to make this for a while, and we finally had it tonight!  I love that I had all the ingredients on hand.  I only had about 4 hrs to marinate the chicken (used boneless skinless breasts) but it still turned out very flavorful.  Not as spicy as some jerk I have tried before - possibly because I used red pepper flakes instead of ground?  I'll correct that next time and hopefully up the "oomph".  :)  I served with buttered white rice and the pineapple mango salsa from Recipe #67080.  Thanks for sharing this easy recipe!

This recipe was quick, easy and full of flavor I couldn't believe it! I read some of the other reviews and made a few changes. I prepared this recipe using boneless chicken breasts. First I litely seasoned the chicken with salt and pepper (My family is from the south and we don't like bland food...lol). Next I combined the rest of the ingredients but instead of using 1 teaspoon of cinnamon I used 1/2 as most suggested that the cinnamon took over the flavor. My boyfriend was in a rush to eat so I let it marinate for I hour then baked it in the oven on 350 degrees for 30 minutes and it was DELICIOUS. My boyfriend loved it and even asked for seconds. Thanks for this recipe and all the helpful reviews. Next I'll try this recipe on wings:)

attributes.source_text: My boyfriend loved it

reviews.review_text: My parents came over for dinner tonight, and I decided to try this out on them - everybody loved it except my 1 year old son (a little to spicy for him, I think). I couldn't find dry Italian dressing mix at the local grocery store, so I used 2 Tbsp of the mix from Italian Dressing Seasoning Dry Mix instead. I used two cut up whole chickens and trippled the marinade, leaving the chicken to marinate overnight. Like I said, everybody loved it. My parents both had seconds and my husband packed some of the leftovers for work tomorrow. I cut up the rest of the leftovers to use for sandwiches for the kids and I tomorrow for lunch, too.

attributes.source_text: My parents both had seconds
my husband packed some of the leftovers for work tomorrow
came over for dinner tonight

reviews.review_text:
Taken from Southern Mama's review because we feel the same way- 
"I have to say we didn't care for this too much. It was a very simple recipe but we didn't care for the flavor. It was not a bad flavor, just not something we like." **** Adding to the quote- We also didn't like the texture of our chicken. I had doubled the recipe and cooked half in the oven after marinating for probably 2 hours and then cooked the other half on the grill after 24 hrs. I thought the grilled would be better, but it wasn't. So sorry, I really had high hopes due to the ratings.

We made this for dinner last night along with the Yo Ho Ho and a Bottle of Rum Caribbean Salsa, and I have to say it doesn't get much easier than this...  I added a little extra ground red pepper to give it that island flair.  I'd also recommend sprinkling in a tablespoon or so of pre-mixed jerk seasoning and a few drops of scotch bonnet pepper sauce if you have either at your disposal to make it a little more authentic.  Great recipe for summer and highly recommend with Recipe #161366 on the side.

attributes.source_text: We made this for dinner last night
Great recipe for summer

reviews.review_text: This is not Caribbean or Jamaican Jerk.  I live in Jamaica, the real home of Jerk. You can't use Italian seasoning, put it on the grill it and call it Caribbean or Jamaican Jerk.  Jamaican jerk has its own unique flavour, spices and seasonings that are authentic because of the type of soil in which the spices and seasonings are grown here ( rich bauxite soil)  such as thyme, scotch bonnet pepper, escallion, ginger, pimento berries, etc.  and it MUST be jerked over pimento wood because that wood gives it a special flavor.  Anything else than that is pure fake....not jerk...perhaps BBQ chicken, possibly but definitely not jerk in the true sense.

This chicken was awesome! DH loved it and he is hard to impress! I brined my chicken first and then stabbed with a knife and marinated for 24 hours, so that made it extra juicy. Then DH grilled it to perfection while I made roasted veggies to go with it. It tasted just like my favorite restaurant grilled chicken. I used an italian seasoning mix recipe I found here and since I only did 2 chicken breasts I scaled the seasonings back a little. Didn't have red pepper so I used Tony Chachere's since it has red peper in it. Very sweet and salty and super flavorful!

attributes.source_text: Very sweet and salty
Very sweet and salty
so that made it extra juicy
DH loved it

reviews.review_text: Made this yesterday and it was delicious!  I saw this and decided to make it for supper, but didn't have long and my chicken breasts were still frozen.  So I mixed together the marinating ingredients and put the frozen chicken into it.  I kept flipping them over every 10 minutes or so.  They marinated for about an hour.  Then I popped them into a hot oven, still in the marinade, on the top shelf.  (about 400*)  I then cooked them for about 40 minutes, turning them frequently.  They were lucious and tender.  We really enjoyed them!

attributes.source_text: decided to make it for supper
They were lucious and tender

reviews.review_text: This chicken is so very good!  I didn't have thyme, so instead I added some italian spices.  I absolutely loved the cinnamon flavor and couldn't imagine decreasing it.  I was only making two large chicken breasts, but kept the amount of everything else the same and it made a nice drizzle for the rice I served under it (easy garlic rice #71739) and can't wait to make this again.  I cooked the chicken in the oven, uncovered, at 400 degrees for 40 minutes.  Half way through I basted the chicken with the leftover marinade.  Super tasty.

attributes.source_text: I absolutely loved the cinnamon flavor

reviews.review_text: This was delicious!  I did not have time to marinate, just spooned the jerk mix over the pieces of chicken (thighs and breasts) and roasted them in the oven for about 45 minutes. The only thing I would do differently next time is to decrease the cinnamon, as it seemed to dominant the flavor.  The chicken was moist, tender and very flavorful.  I can't wait to marinate and grill the chicken next time.  I will definitely grill some extra tenders and try the tortilla suggestion of one of the other reviewers!  Thanks princess buttercup!

attributes.source_text: The chicken was moist
tender

reviews.review_text: This is something I serve my family at least every 2-6 weeks.  I forgot to rate it, and can't believe it!  I hosted a BBQ on Memorial Day and this was everyone's favorite item! I marinated boneless skinless thighs for 24 hours, and then let the meat rest, and sliced it into strips. Then I served it with fresh lime wedges to squeeze over top of it, all wrapped up nicely in a warm flour tortilla.  I always serve it with a nice green salad!  I loved the review of putting it with Alfredo sauce, and cant wait to try that next.  Yummy!

attributes.source_text: I serve my family
I hosted a BBQ
on Memorial Day

reviews.review_text: Wow!  I haven't tried a chicken recipe with such great results in a long time!  I used 5 nice-sized boneless, skinless chicken breasts and the amount of marinade was just right.  I also only used 1/16 teaspoon of red pepper since I didn't want to make it too spicy for my kids.  It was the perfect amount for them.  For the adult preference, I would probably use 1/8 teaspoon red pepper.  If you like it really spicy, go for the full amount.  I will definitely be making this recipe again soon!

attributes.source_text: It was the perfect amount for them

reviews.review_text:
I am going to give this a 4. The basic recipe is really good. REALLY GOOD! But...

What I did the second time was this. I substituted the cinnamon with allspice. I also used Chipotle Chile spice.  Since the mix was a bit thick before, I squeezed in a half a lime, and added between 1/8th, & 1/4 cup of beer. I wanted something that flowed a bit better so I could baste while grilling. I also grilled on a little Smokey Joe. Now, this still ain't a "jerk", like the jerk said. But whoa!

items.label: Simple Tomato Sandwich
items.name: Simple Tomato Sandwich
items.description: I am only posting such a simple recipe because I actually somehow lived 29 years of life before my husband introduced me to the Tomato Sandwich. If you've only used tomatoes as an accessory in your sandwiches, and not as the Featured Ingredient, you are truly missing summer as it was meant to be tasted. Note: after many years, I have solidly converted to mayo for this sandwich, with fresh ground black pepper too.  (Oct 2012)
instructions: Toast bread.
Slice tomato.
When bread is adequately toasted, liberally spread both sides with Miracle Whip (or butter one side with Miracle Whip on the other).
Lay tomato slices on one side of bread.
Salt tomato to taste.
Slap that baby together and savor summer at its best!

reviews.review_text: I don't have a vegetable garden of my own, but I picked up a few tomatoes at an Amish farm stand recently with this sandwich on my mind. It's one of the best things about summer. I agree with the consensus, this sandwich is all about the tomato, and a supermarket-bought variety, even those pretty ones, won't do. I also prefer white bread for this one - I don't want to be tasting delicious bread here - and I use mayo, just because I was raised eating tomatoes with mayo rather than MW. If you've made it this far without trying one, you should - you'll never drive past a farm stand again, unless you're lucky enough to have a garden full of tomatoes at home.

attributes.source_text: It's one of the best things about summer

reviews.review_text: There is definitely something special about the simple tomato sandwich. I remember being introduced in my childhood while over at my neighbours house for lunch. I came across this recipe and decided to revive the old favourite and tried it as written. It is absolutely important to use home grown or the best quality tomatoes you can find in the store that are still on the vine. I used the miracle whip option but I must say I wasn't impressed. I'm not really a mayo fan either (personal taste). For me, I like my tomato sandwich on fresh, untoasted buttered bread and a bit of salt and freshly ground pepper. I'm not giving stars as my preference is too different from the original recipe, but thanks for reminding me of an old favourite!

smellicious is so right.  The proper way to make a mater sandwich is to go out into the garden just before lunch and pick a big, red juicy one that's nice and warm from the sun, reach into the middle of the loaf of white bread and grab the softest pieces, slather DUKES mayonnaise thickly onto both pieces of bread, slice the mater and load it onto the prepared bread.  Sprinkle mater with plenty of black pepper, place other piece of mayo laden bread on top.  Let the sandwich sit for a few seconds to allow the mayo to kinda soak into the bread and release the tomato juices.  Fix yourself a big glass of sweet ice tea, grab some paper towels and go out on the back steps and eat the sandwich.  It's not made right if the bread doesn't stick to the top of your mouth (wash down with sweet tea), or mater/mayo juices don't run down your arms...that's what the paper towels are for.  Enjoy!

I grew up eating these regularly.  Of course, it's at its best during the summer when fresh tomatoes are abundant.  However, during the winter I sometimes still have to have a "fix", and will break down and use Roma tomatoes.  I agree with an earlier poster that Duke's mayo is the best for these sandwiches....but, I only use Duke's for anything anyway.  I do put a good deal of fresh ground pepper on mine too.  Though I never buy white bread, I still think these were so good with white bread so fresh it stuck to the roof of your mouth when you bit into the sandwich.  YUMMY!!..a life-long favorite of mine!  I do ocassionally make a small loaf of white bread just to recall the original delight of these treats.  Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: it's at its best during the summer
during the winter I sometimes still have to have a "fix"

reviews.review_text:
Sweet simplicity.
As of this review I'm 43 years old. This is my first ever tomato sandwich. I can't believe what I've been missing out on!!! It makes me want to cry! LOL
I used soft, white bread as it was all I had. The tomato came from a farmers market just this afternoon and was room temp. I used regular mayonnaise , Miracle Whip isn't a favorite .. 
A TINY sprinkling of salt ... and oh my gosh ... within , literally, about 3 minutes , I was back in the kitchen making another one.
My husband is 47 ... today he also  had his very first tomato sandwich. His comments mirror mine. LOL  We don't want summer to end, now that we've tasted this fabulous sandwich!!!
I did see a different one, but it called for onion and I didn't want onion gunking up my tomato taste ... so very glad I saw this one!!
Thanks so much for posting!!
Thanks so much for posting!!

attributes.source_text: His comments mirror mine.

reviews.review_text:
Thanks annelouise for bringing back memories of summer's simplicity!!  My grandparents have always had a garden in thier backyard and tomatoes were always abundant!  I now carry the torch of tending the garden and I plant Beefsteak tomatoes.  

I pick em' fresh from the garden, give em' a good rinsing then I toast Brownberry Health Nut Bread (which is such a hearty wheat bread and has pieces of walnuts in it), smooth on the Miracle Whip and sprinkle salt and course ground black pepper on both sides of the sliced Beefsteak Tomatoes & make me a big, fat Tomato sandwich!!

Just whip up some flavored ice tea (I like Tazo Passion, Wild Sweet Orange & China Green Tea Tips mixed together), and all I can say is Whoooooooo Baby!!  

Makes me hate summer only comes once a year in Michigan and only lasts about four months!! I movin' down South!! ;^}

Not something I would expect from a gourmet chef's restaurant, but any recipe that has me eating it less than 5 minutes after seeing the recipe deserves way more than 5 stars (and 3 sandwiches at that)! Everyone has their personal favorite bread (I prefer squishy, white bread like Wonder), but don't usually toast mine unless making a blt or club). Warm tomatoes are a law and I would only use home-grown garden tomatoes (or bought ones if the bought ones were heirloom type). I go with mayo and no salt for me- just sopping up the tomato juices from the slices onto the bread before adding the mayo. I learned this recipe from my dad, who was a depresson-era child, but kept his love for the simple things always. Sometims simple is best, and at that here's 5 more stars for your collection!

These are delicious sandwiches! I've been making them for years with toasted bakery style white bread, spread with butter and Miracle Whip Salad Dressing on both sides (decadent), with our garden fresh tomatoes or in the winter I use the store-bought tomatoes on the vine! For seasoning, I sprinkle the tomatoes with a little kosher salt and freshly ground pepper. In the summer I make a meal out of these sandwiches and recipe #147254. Hot buttered corn on the cob and toasted tomato sandwiches are great together. Thanks for posting. :) Burnice

AMEN!!!!  This sandwich has been a staple in my family growing up and my dad's family as well.  Every summer, towards the end of August, my dad's huge Mennonite family rents a lakeside Bible Camp for the weekend for a giant family gathering and all the aunts who grow tomatoes bring them by the boxful.  The standard breakfast at these gatherings is toast'n'tomatoes.  (One year, we had the gathering in June and the biggest complaint was the lack of tomatoes for breakfast!!)  Try toasted bread with just butter and a thin slice of sharp cheddar cheese -- and don't forget the pepper!

attributes.source_text: The standard breakfast at these gatherings is toast'n'tomatoes.
for a giant family gathering

reviews.review_text:
Last summer when times were HARD --on unemployment --a friend gave us some home grown tomatoes.  I made sandwiches for the family for lunch and there was not enough meat for everyone.  I had a "simple tomato sandwich" with an added slice of cheese.  My dd wanted a bite of mine.  The next day, she asked if she could have one of those special sandwiches like we had yesterday!  I knew it was special, but I didn't know that her tastes were developed enough to appreciate it!

I grew up on these darlings --mon adds thinly sliced cukes -- not me!

attributes.source_text: for the family for lunch
she asked if she could have one of those special sandwiches like we had yesterday

reviews.review_text: A reviewer is so right!! The ones in the store do taste like plastic.  The best kind of tomato for a TRUE FLAVOR OUT OF HEAVEN is a homegrown one that is full vine ripe!  My father always had a big garden and I grew up eating plain old tomato sandwiches - bread, sliced tomato, mayo, salt and pepper.  But I never toast my bread.  The softness of the bread  helps in the flavor.  In our area in the southeastern USA tomatoes are in season in the month of July.  We go to a "pick-your-own" garden patch where four varities are grown.  You just can't beat the flavor of a tomato sandwich with lots of black pepper.  Annlouise, thanks for a memory.

I ate tomato sandwiches as a kid, Its right up there with a BLT!!! I lean more towards the mayo(Hellmans) and not the light kind either than anything else.I know it was probably my grandmother that got me started on 'em. I think they came about while you were eating BLT'S and you ran out of bacon. White bakery bread was usually the bread of choice too !! It feels good to know there are other people out there who love the simple things in life just like I do .

I'd forgotten just how much I LOVE tomato sandwiches!  I was always the oddball growing up when my mom made BLT's because I would just eat a lettuce and tomato sandwich and leave off the bacon.  I haven't had my tomato/lettuce sandwich in years and then stumbled across this recipe.  I didn't add lettuce this time (but love it with lettuce as well) and followed the recipe exactly except I added pepper along with the salt.  PURE heaven!  I had the freshest garden-ripe tomatoes and ate it on whole wheat bread, lightly toasted.  YUM!!!  Thanks for reminding me of an old favorite!

Well, what can I say?  It does what it says on the tin.  I have a glut of toms right now and wanted a snack after my lunch salad (all from my garden as well) has worn off and I was a bit peckish.  This hit the spot!  As has been said, this must be done with good (preferably your own grown) fresh tomatoes.  We don't have Miracle Whip, so I used Helmann's extra light mayo on a bit of ciabata I had in the bread bin.  Really tasty!!

attributes.source_text: wanted a snack

reviews.review_text: Are you my daughter in law? I remember when my son introduced her to tomato sandwiches for the first time. She was 29 at the time and I had a garden full of heirloom tomatoes. We like ours with garden fresh tomatoes, especially the beefsteak types like brandywine, black seaman, or kellog's breakfast. Then add mayo, salt and pepper and enjoy a slice of heaven. We like ours open faced. Saves a bit on calories.

The best sandwich in the world--maybe even the universe!!!  My brothers and I used to have tomato sandwiches all the time when we were kids.  Our dad would bring home beefsteak tomatoes he bought from a little mom and pop store that was located near a tomato field--so the tomatoes were really incredible!  A single slice from one of those huge tomatoes, on whole grain bread, with a little mayo...and we had the perfect lunch!  Thanks for posting this wonderful recipe annlouise!!!

attributes.source_text: we had the perfect lunch

reviews.review_text: I make a pimento cheese filling and keep a bowl of it in the fridge throughout the summer to make an open face (only 1 slice of bread--reduces the carbs without reducing anything else) cheese tomato sandwich. I spread the pimento cheese on one side of the bread. Put Into toaster oven and broil (425) until cheese is bubbly. Put thick slice of tomato, salt and pepper on tomato and enjoy!! absolutely delicious.

attributes.source_text: throughout the summer

reviews.review_text: Simple, yes, but just about the best thing EVER! I've been doing this for years. I agree, junky grocery store tomatoes are just tasteless and awful once you've had a big, homegrown, juicy tomato. Tomatoes burst with flavor! I especially love pretty much any heirloom variety...on a sandwich, with sea salt, fresh cracked peppercorn medley and real Hellman's mayo (Miracle Whip is an abomination!!!)

attributes.source_text: big, homegrown, juicy tomato

reviews.review_text: The taste of this sandwich brings back memories of summertime growing up.  My mom would pick fresh tomatoes from our garden and make us fresh tomato sandwiches for lunch, or sometimes just a yummy snack!  They're the best thing ever!  I agree that homemade bread is the best choice, but I like just plain ol' white, and I don't toast it.  It's SO GOOD!!  Thanks for posting this great recipe and bringing back fond memories.

On hot summer days when the tomatoes are at the peak of perfection nothing beats a tomato sandwich. My first taste of this was at a friend's house and she always bought Dukes mayonnaise so every summer I get a small jar of Dukes just for this. They are best when eaten while still wet from the lake or pool :-) For the Vegans, I knew someone who ate these with mustard and loved every bite just as much. I also sometimes put a thin slice of vadalia onion on this if in season and when out of mayo butter is good too. I don't miss the heat but I do miss summer's bounty.

attributes.source_text: On hot summer days

items.label: Cheesy Ham and Potato Soup
items.name: Cheesy Ham and Potato Soup
items.description: Comfort soup at its finest!  I usually make this to use up leftover ham.  This is easy to adapt with other ingredients.  I don't put celery in mine.  I have added garlic sometimes as well.
instructions: Combine potatoes, celery, carrots, onion, ham, and water/broth in stockpot and bring to boil.
Then cook over medium heat until potatoes are tender.
Stir in the chicken bouillon, salt (if using), and pepper.
In separate saucepan, melt butter over medium-low heat.  Whisk in flour and cook stirring constantly until thick.
Slowly stir in milk as not to allow lumps to form and all milk is added.  Turn up to medium heat. Continue to stir until thick (4-5 minutes).
Add in cheese and stir until melted.
Stir the cheese mixture into the stockpot and cook until heated through.  (I also will break up some of the potatoes for thickness.  It gets thicker as it cools and next day).

reviews.review_text: WOWOWOW  Love this soup.  I made a couple of slight changes....Started with 1/2 lb pepper cracked amish bacon and the 1 1/2 cups left over ham cooking in pot with a bit of olive oil.  After the bacon sweated a bit - I took the ham / bacon mixture out.  I then added all of the veggies (plus lots of extra of each) and got the brown bits off the bottom of the pan.  Added the water and followed the recipe....except used whole milk instead of 1/2 and 1/2 and used 2 C light cheese.  I ended up needing about 3/4 C more milk b/c of all of the veggies.  The soup was still quite thick and excellent.  YUM.  Thanks  UPDATE:  just made this again - added a ham hock to the broth as the potatoes cooked - and the flavor is great.  Added a couple carrots to the veg too!  Used the immersion blender to puree a bit as well.  Sooooo goood!

attributes.source_text: The soup was still quite thick

reviews.review_text: This soup is wonderful provides whole meal. Changes to simplify:No peeling veggies: I used 2 cups of dehydrated potato slices I had in a box of hamburger helper I had on hand after I let them soak 10-15 min in boiling water, and then I added 2 cups of frozen hash browns. (Im going to use frozen hashbrowns from now on in cassarole dishes they are quick and delicious)  I also increased onions to 1/2 cup.  I did use the 1/2 and 1/2.  The soup was asolutely delicious, and the nice thing about it is uses small amounts of ingredients left from other dinners like holiday ham you might be getting tired of and small amounts of veggies on hand left from other recipes

So. Freaking. Good. This is the ultimate in comfort food! Like others I made this with leftover Christmas ham. The real bonus was using a mixture of gourmet cheeses that we had received in a gift basket. What a treat. I didn't measure my veggies. I used: 4 fist sized potatoes-peeled; 2 stalks celery; 3 good sized carrots; and one medium Vidalia onion. One 32 oz. box of salt free organic chicken stock. And finally about 4 - 5 oz. of really good cheese. I used: Edam, Brick, Cheddar with onion and even a bit of Cheddar spread. Really looking forward to today's leftovers! Happy New Year!

Great, savoury soup! Made 1/2 recipe, skipped the celery, skimped on the cheese a bit since I was using strong, old Gouda; used bouillion cubes instead of granules - substitution charts say 1 ts of granules equals 1 bouillion cube, and this was certainly not true for me! I used 2 cubes for 1/2 recipe, and I think 1 cube plus a sprinkling of salt would be just right; and I like my salt, I assure you! 1/2 recipe also made more like 3 servings for me. Still, the soup turned out simply delectable: smooth, chunky, savoury, creamy - all tasty things in one! Thank you for a lovely recipe SweetsLady - this will be repeated!

reviews.review_text: MMMM MMM GOOD!!  In cleaning out my freezer yesterday, found some chunked up ham leftover from the past Christmas.  It was in a foodsaver bag, so I knew it was still good, but I also knew I would be having more ham soon, so I needed to use it up.  I thawed it out and went in search of finding something to do with it.  Found this recipe and followed it almost exactly, except I only used 1 T. of bouillon, 4 T. butter and melted up some velveeta instead of shredded cheese.  Great way to use up some stuff in my fridge.  Makes for a yummy lunch.  Thanks for the recipe!

reviews.review_text: This was great. I made a few changes. First of all, mashed potatoes are always my last leftover from Thanksgiving, after getting carried away I'm done with carbs until christmas, I also used some cauliflower, just because it was sitting around. most importantly, I had bought leeks intending a potato leek soup, but found this recipe first, they made a great sub for the onion. I used the last of my turkey stock from the holiday, and now have a clean fridge and a happy tummy. I'll be cooking a ham next week just because I want the leftover for another round of this.

Amazingly good and I will make this again and again!  I doubled the recipe, left the peel on 3/4 of my potatoes, used 6 cups chicken broth plus 1/2 cup water, added NO salt (easier to add to taste after it's done than fix an oversalted dish), 2 cups milk & 2 cups FF 1/2 & 1/2. items.label: Quick Cinnamon Rolls - No Yeast
items.name: Quick Cinnamon Rolls - No Yeast
items.description: These wonderful cinnamon rolls are on the table in an hour -  no waiting for hours or overnight. They are simple and quick to put together.
instructions: For the filling, in a small bowl combine softened butter, brown sugar and cinnamon to form a crumbly mixture.
Sprinkle 1/2 of the mixture over the bottom of a 9x9 pan.
In a large bowl mix together flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Cut in softened butter (sometimes your hands are the best tools).
Stir in milk to form a soft dough.
Roll out dough on a lightly floured surface into a rectangle about 1/4 inch thick.
Spread the remaining filling on the rolled out dough.
Roll up the rectangle,  with a sharp knife slice into 18 small rolls (12 if you want them a little bigger).
Bake for 20-25 min at 400°F.
For glaze, combine powdered sugar and milk in a small bowl and stir until smooth.
Once rolls are finished, drizzle on glaze and serve warm.

reviews.review_text: Thanks for posting this! I wanted something that had NO yeast- I hate rising and kneading etc. I halved the recipe and got 8. I would only make 1/2 the filling mix in the future- I found spreading it on the bottom of the pan just wasted it; it didn't stick to the rolls or anything. I was able to work with the dough just fine- not too sticky, or too sweet . After sitting out for an hour or two they get very crisp, so I'm thinking of perhaps adding an egg or trying a moister recipe to make future leftovers more appetizing. Perhaps I will also lower the cooking temperature and time. I'd recommend packing them very closely together when they cook, so they don't fall over lopsided. Be sure to grease the pan bottom and sides. And here's the best tip ever- instead of a knife, which squishes down the dough, use a thread to cut the rolls! Slide it underneath, cross it on top, and give it a swift pull. It's like magic!

attributes.source_text: not too sticky

reviews.review_text:
Okay, so I read all the reviews and tried a bunch of different ways. Here is my two cents:

1. Leave the dough recipe as is. Adding an egg will make it stickier than necessary.

2. Love the filling recipe, but I added chopped walnuts to it. I also used it solely in the rolls, not at the bottom like the original recipe said to because if you do, it'll caramelize at the bottom into an ooey gooey mess.

When you are cutting them cut them about 1.5 to 2 inches thick. They will spread out horizontally but not height wise (unless you add yeast) so the height you cut them at will be about what they stay.

3. Bake it at 300 instead of 400...gets the dough gooeyer (is that a word??) It will take longer but WORTH it. Bake it only under the tops start to firm and if you stick a toothpick it comes out clean.

4. Bake them in a spring form pan (about 7-8 per pan, leaving room to spread out). Trust me on this one, that way you just pop the outer pan off when they are done and serve!

5. As you are letting them cool take a knife and gently slip it around the corners of the spring form pan and each other, so they pull apart nicely.

6. Once cool, add about 4 tbsp melted butter on top of the rolls to get them nice and buttery soft. Then put on the icing, pop the spring form pan, and serve!

TRUST ME. I baked these until I got a batch I liked and this is what worked. Love how quick this is though. No waiting on them to rise or messing with yeast. My whole family approved of them!

reviews.review_text: Here's my innovation:  Use parchment paper in the pan.  A piece of parchment paper that comes over the sides of the pan.  After baking, pull the whole piece of parchment up out of the pan and nothing sticks to the pan, and the rolls are easy to remove for serving.  <br/><br/>I've made this twice.  The first time, I didn't think there was enough filling, so I doubled it, spread a thick layer of it.  It was way too sugary.  <br/><br/>The second time I made it with only the amount of filling called for, and it was MUCH better.  I also added raisins and pecans.  <br/><br/>Both times I left off the glaze.  Both times I didn't bother putting sugar on the bottom of the pan.  Both times I cooked it 350 degrees for 24 minutes.  I felt a lower temp would make the rolls softer, and they were soft and delicious.  Both times I made the dough exactly as the recipe specified and it was perfect amount of moisture, easy to roll out (and I hate rolling out dough).<br/><br/>Next time I might try only making 2/3 of the amount of filling to make it even less sweet, but that is just my preference.

attributes.source_text: they were soft and delicious

reviews.review_text: This recipe was perfect for us in a pinch!!! Thanks for posting Hannah34! We forgot to buy Pillsbury Cinnamon Rolls for my husbands Christmas-Day-tradition:( and after going to three small stores on Christmas Eve and not finding any we gave up. :( But, on Christmas day we were still had a hankering so we went online to look up a scratch recipe which did not require yeast. This sufficed perfectly! They were irresistible and my husband did not have to go without his favorite treat on Christmas! (RE: recipe revisions- do not add eggs as someone stated, dough is perfect without. Use wax paper on countertop and have some extra flour on hand for your rolling pin/hands and paper to cut down on stickiness, the liquid to powerdered sugar is grossly overestimated...to get the thick consistency on icing put entire amount of powdered sugar into bowl THEN a dab a tiny bit at a time the milk- you will find that you will not use all of the milk or you will use lots more sugar to make lots more icing-which is not a bad thing;) ENJOY!!!! (Oh, and YUUUMMMMM!) P.S. Taking them out early might be necc depending on what type of pan...I found the cooking time to be just about perfect - though wait for them to cool down just a bit before removing from pan...they will stay together better.

reviews.review_text: This is a very decent recipe if you're pressed for time and lacking in yeast. FYI- they come out more like a sweet biscuit than a sticky bun, so adjust your expectations accordingly. I can attest that an egg is -not- necessary, but I didn't try it with one so it may not hurt. The dough was a bit sticky so either flour the rolling surface or use parchment to save yourself some headache. Also, add more powdered sugar to the glaze to make it less runny. Pro tip-- Unless you're weighing out the flour, always use a spoon to fill, tap, and level off your measuring cup. If you use the measuring cup itself to scoop up the flour for recipes, you're compacting it and your baked goods will be inconsistent. The more you know! *cue star and rainbow flying thru space*

reviews.review_text: Great recipe when you realize you don't have yeast or eggs and no stores are open to get any. I changed it up a bit. Instead of mixing the butter, cinnamon, and brown sugar, I spread softened butter over the rolled dough, then sprinkled the brown sugar and then cinnamon all over. I did the same to the pan before placing the rolls in it. I totally agree with dancejennie...put more powdered sugar in the mixture for the icing. I still prefer the old-fashioned, yeast cinnamon rolls, but this is a good alternative. No problem with the dough being too sticky or hard to roll. The dough was soft and rolled easily. Perhaps those that found it too sticky put a bit too much milk in it or didn't use enough flour on the rolling board, the rolling pin, or their hands (when removing from the bowl). I'll use this again when I forget I am out of yeast.

reviews.review_text:
Hello...

I just made these buns today...it was a new thing to put the filling on the bottom as well as inside...but, I tried it, and it was good.
I did not get the amount of buns from my roll as the author did...I got ten small ones in a square metal pan.
I decided not to use the icing...I thot it would be too sweet and for me, it would have been.

I used wholewheat flour and brown sugar for everything.
I cannot understand putting an egg in the recipe...have not heard of this be4, and I am glad the author did not do that.

When I took the pan to the butcher board, I put a plate on top and then flipped the thing over, so that the sugar mix on the bottom of the pan was seen on the buns.
It covered the whole bun with brown sugar mix, so you could not see the coil; but, I liked it that way better, it looked prettier.

The magic was in the tasting...they looked liked cinnamon buns I have made in the past...very simple w/o yeast, but, after the second biteinto it, I was hooked!

The flavor is perfect, the salt with the sweet...all you need is a big slather of hard butter and it's feasting time.
I could not just have one...
These are really good...not fancy...but, they taste great...a different version of the cinnamon bun, which the store sells you, that you pull apart...I guess it has it's place, but, these are fine for me.

I have printed out the recipe and thankyou to the author of them.

It was plenty sweet enough w/o icing, and I had run out of icing sugar, anyways.

Next time I make these, I will try Indian White Flour bread, which is part wholewheat and I cut them wider so they are bigger buns to munch on.

Last of all, I found the dough very pliable, soft and fairly co-operative.

Kudos to the Author.

Layna
Vancouver, Canada.

reviews.review_text: This is an awesome no-yeast recipe.  I don't feel like it was any easier to make this than a yeast cinnamon roll, just a lot faster without needed time to rise.  The roll tastes a bit like a cross between a pie crust and a southern style biscuit.  The filling melts into the bottom (but there is plenty left on the rolls!), so I found no need to put half of it in the bottom of the pan.  Delicious, but since I use my bread machine to make yeast dough for cinnamon rolls while I crochet or do something else, I would honestly choose the yeast version next time, and just make them the night before and bake them in the morning to enjoy.  But, for a quick, "gotta have cinnamon rolls NOW!" recipe, this is definitely it.

reviews.review_text: These made an excellent Xmas morning treat--very tasty, very easy; the sugary bottom layer made them more fun and surprisingly didn't stick to the pan (perhaps thanks to the high butter content). Would be helpful if the author provided general dimensions to aim for when rolling out the dough, as rectangles can run the gamut. As an example, for 9 one-inch high rolls, you'd roll it so one side is 9" long--and make sure that 9" edge is the one you roll with (I.e., every part of that rectangular edge should be in the middle of the spiral, and every part of the opposing 9" side should be on the outside of the spiral).
