she loved it

reviews.review_text: I used just a pound of hamburger meat and cut down on everything else accordingly. It was good, I just should have added a little more salt. I sauteed the onions with garlic, butter, Worcester sauce, some liquid smoke and a little soy sauce. That's just because my fiance doesn't like raw onions. It added a lot of flavor, but I'll put extra onion powder in it next time for a stronger onion flavor. I cooked them in a non-stick pan with some oil and made brown gravy to go with. It's good but it didn't have much of a Salisbury steak flavor to me. My fiance however loved it.

attributes.source_text: My fiance however loved it

reviews.review_text:
I liked this dish. 
I used regular mushroom soup so added a bit of tomato paste to change the color as I really don't like the color of the mushroom soup. I also added 1/2 tsp Worcestershire sauce to bring out  bit of the steak flavor. 
I cooked the patties in the Foreman grill to help drain the fat, the resulting patties were very tender and delicious.
Served with fresh mashed potatoes (Recipe #230695). I was afraid my family wouldn't appreciate it as they usually dont go for this sort of meal but they liked it. Very good and satisfying meal. Thank you.

attributes.source_text: the resulting patties were very tender
they liked it

reviews.review_text: LOVE these NurseDi!  So easy, yet so good.  Real comfort food.  Made at my dh's request, he loves salisbury steak, and this one seemed easy enough.  It was!  I also doubled up on the soup for the sauce--used the remaining soup from the first can plus one more can, and about 2/3 of a can of water.   Next time, I think I'll try white wine. And I did the trick with the bread slices underneath--that was a great tip! Served with egg noodles and green peas, my dh was in heaven.  Thanks, Di--great, easy recipe!

attributes.source_text: Real comfort food
my dh was in heaven

reviews.review_text: Have a can or jar of extra gravy around for this recipe, in no way does it make enough for mashed potatoes or noodles. I transferred my patties to a pie plate after the first 40 mins. to get them out of the grease, then combined the rest of the soup,water & a can of gravy a dumped on top then baked the additional time. I thought the taste was OK but nothing really special enough to make twice.(I used garlic powder) I really enjoy Nurse Di's recipes but not this one too much.

Wow, I like another reviewer, had never made salisbury steak before but something made me look for the recipe today. Sounded easy and based on the reviews, thought perhaps my kids would like it too.  Everyone loved it.  My DH and DD want me to do it again soon. The only thing I had to do different (other than as others did, cook the patties on the Foreman grill for 5 mins. first) was to substitute dry onion flakes for the onion. Thanks for a great, economical dinner option.

items.label: New York Cheesecake
items.name: New York Cheesecake
items.description: What a delicious way to end a meal! There's nothing better than a great piece of New York Cheesecake!
instructions: For crust, combine graham cracker crumbs and melted butter.
Stir until well combined.
Press onto bottom and about 2-1/2 inches up the sides of a 9x3-inch springform pan.
Mix cream cheese, sugar, flour, and vanilla.
Beat with an electric mixer until fluffy.
Add eggs and egg yolks, beating on low speed just until combined.
Stir in whipping cream and lemon peel.
Pour into pan.
Place pan in a shallow baking pan in the oven. (Does not mention anything about a water bath)
Bake in a 325 degree F oven about 1-1/2 hours or until center appears nearly set when shaken.
Cool 15 minutes.
Loosen crust from sides of pan.
Cool 30 minutes more; remove sides of pan.
Cool completely.
Chill 4 to 24 hours.
If desired, garnish with fresh berries.

reviews.review_text:
I was so nervous about attempting to make an authentic cheesecake..but I found this recipe and decided to try my hand at it based upon other reviews.  Well, I wasn't sorry...this recipe made a delicious cheesecake that my husband said was better than any cheesecake he had every eaten...and that was without any toppings.  I did use the water bath and I used a spring-form cake lined with foil to avoid the batter leaking into the water bath. 
The thing I will do differently next time is to double the graham cracker crust mix and add a little more butter because I did not have enough crust mixture to go up as high as the cheesecake batter went, and in the end..it was spread thinner than I personally care for...maybe the extra butter will help hold the mix together better.  I did not loosen the crust from the sides of the pan after cooking, instead I put the springform pan in the fridge overnight after it had cooled a couple of hours on the counter.  It unmolded perfectly and was beautiful the next day.  Did I mention the texture?  Heavenly.  You don't have to look anywhere else for a great cheesecake recipe..or for one that is easier to make! Thank you for posting, Bev.

attributes.source_text: my husband said was better than any cheesecake he had every eaten

reviews.review_text: I made this cheesecake for Christmas dinner and two days prior.  It turned out beautifully with no cracks, silky and delicious!  I baked it at 325 in my gas range and in a water bath for an additional 10 minutes.  When completed, I allowed the cake to cool in the oven with the door slightly ajar for the first 15 minutes and then closed. It sat in the oven for about 5 hours and then was left on the counter for 1 more hour before placing in the refrigerator to chill completely before wrapping.  I couldn't have expected a more lovely result.  I also lined the sides of the springfoam pan with parchment paper about 1-1/2 inches higher than the 3 inch sides.  I kept the paper on until I was ready to serve the cheesecake.  Easy to remove and helped with the wrapping of the cheesecake while in the refrigerator.  I will only use this recipe for cheesecake from now on.

attributes.source_text: I made this cheesecake for Christmas dinner
for Christmas dinner
silky and delicious

reviews.review_text: WOW.. this was my very first time making a cheesecake.  Hubby wanted cheesecake for his b-day so I went in search and found this recipe.  I must say that I've been intimidated with the thoughts of making a cheesecake in regards to whether or not to use a water bath & how long to cook it, but after some research I found that the reason why this recipe does not call for a water bath is because of the flour.  Cheesecakes with cornstarch or flour added to the batter do not crack as easily from overbaking. The starch molecules will actually get in between the egg proteins preventing them from over-coagulating. No over-coagulating, no cracks!!  So I did as the recipe stated & only put it in a pan therefore no cracks.  The only things I did differently was to not add the lemon because I had none & after it was done baking I left it in the oven to cool.  PERFECTION!!

attributes.source_text: for his b-day

reviews.review_text: First time making cheesecake, and it was delicious. I followed recipe with a few minor changes thanks to reviewers. I made sure ingredients were all room temp and 15 second softened my cream cheese in microwave. I Lined the pan with round parchment. I added 4 tbsp of sugar to crust, put pan with crust, in freezer while I made the filling. I used all but about a cup of the filling in my pan. Filled to about 1 inch below rim. I baked in a water bath at 325 for 1 hr 40 min. Turned off oven heat, cracked open door, and left in Oven for 1 hr. Removed from water bath and placed back in oven for 2 more hours. Then put on counter to cool until bottom of pan was cool to touch. Covered pan with foil and cooled overnight. Removed from pan in morning. It came out perfect. No cracks, just a nice toasty brown top. Very easy to make and directions were simple to follow. Perfect for making a day or two ahead. First time was a bit time consuming but next time should be a bit faster.

I had never made a cheesecake before this one. I was SO scared but it turned out really fine!!!!! I think I used a little bit less of cheese when I converted it from ounces to my country's unit, but it turned out really fine. I let it cool in the oven around half an hour, then another half hour outside, then four hours in the fridge, because I was so scared it was going to break when I unmolded it - but it didn't! I had to turn the pan upside down (since it wasn't one of the ones that has removable ring) and then the cake upside down again, and even then it didn't break. It did have a few cracks but they were almost unnoticeable and I covered the cake with strawberries and jam so even less. I will definitely cook it again!!!

Does it taste good? Yes! I followed this recipe as stated and the top cracked around the edge and when I took it out of the form, the top around the edges just fell off. The crust was very crumbly to the point it would not really hold together well. There was so much extra filling, but not realizing it at the time, I just poured it all in and it went way above the crust to the top of the pan making it hard to move. When it baked it rose about 3 to 4 inches over the top making it very difficult to remove from the form as the cheesecake now stuck to the top. My suggestions are to use a water bath, use a 10 inch pan versus a 9 inch, and use parchment paper on the bottom. The other option is to tweak the recipe ingredients so there is less filling, but that might change the quality.

This was my first attempt at cheesecake!  I used homemade graham crackers, farm-fresh eggs, organic cream cheese, natural sugar, and organic pumpkin pie filling to swirl through in layers.  I had an 8.5" and a 9.5" and wasn't sure which to use, since the recipe calls for a 9".  So, I used the 8.5" thinking it would be better than having a too-thin cheesecake.  I should have used the larger springform pan!  The cheesecake puffed well over the top of the pan and took 30 minutes longer to cook.  The edges did crack, and they browned quite a bit in order to get the middle set.  It's not quite as beautiful a result as I would have liked, but the taste made up for it!!  I will try this again sometime with the other pan and hope that the aesthetics match the deliciousness.

A delicious and easy cheesecake recipe. I only have 7 inch springform pan so I scaled the recipe down to 6-8 servings and baked for 1 hour 20 mins. I didn't know how to do the water bath. But did it anyway. I am not sure if the springform pan should be immersed on the baking dish, but I figured if I immerse it, the water would sip in to my cheesecake. So what I did was , I put a wire rack on the baking dish then placed the springform pan on it then poured just enough water on the baking dish making sure that it didn't reach my springform pan. Is that how you do water bath? Well wrong or correct, my cheesecake turned soft and creamy. 

Also I don't use electric beater, I just use scraping spoon to mix and avoid over-beating that will cause cracking.

attributes.source_text: my cheesecake turned soft and creamy
my cheesecake turned soft and creamy

reviews.review_text: This cheesecake is amazing. If your cheesecake didn’t turn out, it’s not this recipes fault. I followed the instructions almost exactly and got a perfect cheesecake. Make sure your cream cheese is at room temp, only mix until creamy, over mixing will cause cracking. I usually only use an electric mixer for the cream cheese and sugar and then do the rest of the mixing with a wooden spoon or sometimes a whisk. The only thing I did differently is baked it for about an hour and fifteen minutes and then just turned off my oven amd left the door closed for about 30 min then opened the door, slid a knife around the edges to prevent sticking when it shrinks and let it sit for about 2 hours in the warm oven before putting it in the fridge. Sudden temperature changes can cause cracking as well. It was so good. I drizzled white chocolate on top. I think next time I will do a little bit more crust for my personal taste but it was delicious the way it is.

OK, so judging by the rest of the reviews, I need to attempt this again.  I didn't make the crust b/c I didn't have anything on hand to make the crust with - no biggie.  I THINK, however, that using the homemade neufchatel may have been a bit of a mistake: the cake came out of the oven beautifully set up, no cracks, even without the water bath, BUT it was very weepy and the texture was off somehow.  For that, I'm really glad I didn't have a crust, it would've been terribly soggy and gross.  It was also a bit too sweet for me, next time I'll reduce the sugar a bit.  I did use lime zest instead of lemon, as that's what I had in the fridge.  Lovely lime flavor came through.  Next time, I will try store bought (not as tasty by itself, but obviously superior for cheesecake making!) cheese, and will review again at that point.

attributes.source_text: Lovely lime flavor came through

reviews.review_text: I wanted to use this as a layer between two red velvet cake layers to make a red velvet cheesecake (so I didn't use a crust). Since I wanted it to be a little thinner, I prepared three fifths of the recipe. I used a regular 9" cake pan lined with parchment paper instead of a spring-form pan. I cooked it at the same temperature, but only for about 40 minutes. Then I turned off the oven, opened the door and let it cool for about an hour in the oven. Fast forward through overnight refrigeration and red velvet cake baking to assembly. The cheesecake came out of the pan easily and held together nicely to make the middle layer of my cake. Not only did it look beautiful, but it tasted delicious!

To say this recipe is outstanding is a huge understatement. I made this last night and let is 'season' overnight in the fridge. I used 1 tsp. of vanilla bean paste (to get the flecks in the cake) and 1/2 tsp. of real vanilla. I also doubled the crust as it did not appear 2 cups would be enough from other reviews - and I am glad I did! The crust came all the way up the side of the pan. I baked at 325 for 1 hr. 45 mins. in a water bath and then opened the oven door, turned the oven off and let it cool there - no cracks!!! I topped this beauty the next day with Kittencal's Delicious Skillet Apples and a slight drizzling of caramel topping. Thanks for posting - this was a remarkably easy cheesecake with stunning results!!

The BEST cheesecake.  It really was quite simple...just make sure ingredients are at room temperature before starting.  This does affect the final product. I made this for a holiday dinner.  It was fabulous!  I didn't mess with the ingredients, but adapted the baking directions to eliminate cracking on the top.  I baked for 1 hour at 325*, then turned off the oven and left the cheesecake in the oven for an additional 30 minutes.  Removed from oven, let sit for 30 minutes.  Ran knife around the edge, removed the edge and let sit out until cooled. Then refrigerated for two days before serving.  DELICIOUS....

attributes.source_text: I made this for a holiday dinner

reviews.review_text: This cheesecake is absolutely fabulous!!  I had always wanted to try my hand at making a New York style cheesecake, but since I don't have a springform pan I didn't know how to go about it.  Then I had a thought.  Why not use a store bought graham cracker pie crust and just make 1/2 the recipe?  So that's exactly what I did.  I bought a 9 inch shell, but think 8 inch would have worked better.  If you bake 1/2 recipe, like I did, it will take between 55-60 minutes.  I baked it in a water bath just to be on the safe side, and it was perfect.  I omitted the lemon zest because I wanted the vanilla flavor to shine.  Mmmmm, it's so good!!  Thank you Bev, for sharing your recipe!  I can't imagine a better cheesecake recipe than this one!

attributes.source_text: I wanted the vanilla flavor to shine

reviews.review_text: I am giving this recipe 5 stars because I'm sure it deserves it. I don't know what I did wrong but this Cheesecake came out a disaster for me! 1st, it was the first one I ever made in my life. I think I totally misjudged the baking time cause I well over cooked the crumbs. They tasted bitter to me (which means I burnt them) the photos submitted for this recipe look wonderful. I bet if I had better luck, mine would have been fantastic. Because I must have did something wrong, it's my own fault. I think the taste however and appearance is a 5 star! I am going to try it again for sure. Better luck next time I hope! :(  Mine had potential to look and taste as good as the photos.

This is a rich, delicious fool-proof recipe!! I had to laugh at all the reviews which state that the hubby's wanted it for birthday cake because that's exactly why I made this too! :) I attempted cheesecake 16 years ago when he asked for it, but I didn't put the pan together right and it ended in cheesecake tragedy. I told myself that I was never going to make another cheesecake again after the mess of cleaning it out of my oven. But I decided the other day to give cheesecake another shot and I found this recipe. I'm so glad I did!!!! Making it was super easy and I love that no water bath was required. It turned out like a dream! It's not overly sweet, which is perfect because I don't like things too sweet, but it was wonderful for my husband once I got cherry pie filling on top of his slice. It's a GREAT recipe. And basic enough that you could add to it with ease. It made a beautiful, rich thick dessert. I'm happy that dh finally got his homemade cherry cheesecake. :)

attributes.source_text: This is a rich, delicious fool-proof recipe
It made a beautiful, rich thick dessert
It made a beautiful, rich thick dessert
it was wonderful for my husband once I got cherry pie filling on top of his slice

reviews.review_text: Good cheesecake. I read the reviews and debated using a water bath/lining the pan with foil but decided to follow the recipe to a "T" since this was my first cheesecake. I gave it 4 stars and not 5 because the cake cracked badly and was almost overcooked (very brown on top) at 1 hour 25 minutes, and the lemon overpowered the delicate flavors of the cake itself. I will probably make this again, but I will follow other reviewer's advice and cook it at 300, line the bottom of the pan with foil (I did have some leakage) and use a water bath. And next time I'll cut the lemon to 1/2 teaspoon.

This is, by far, the best cheesecake I've ever eaten, not to mention the easiest I've ever made. I was surprised that I didn't have to bake the crust first, as is instructed in most cheesecake recipes. Nonetheless, the crust was excellent and didn't fall apart. I used NeufchÃ¢tel cheese instead of cream cheese but no one will be able to tell the difference. The flavor of the lemon rind was present but not overbearing. I used a water bath but still got some cracks and uneven browning on top. My oven is most likely at fault for that. I'll just have to keep a better eye on it next time around. Making cheesecake has always intimidated me but this recipe changed all that!!

attributes.source_text: The flavor of the lemon rind was present but not overbearing
the crust was excellent and didn't fall apart

items.label: Artichoke and Chicken Bake
items.name: Artichoke and Chicken Bake
items.description: This easy but elegant entree first appeared in "Quick Cooking" magazine. Someone posted this at the Somersize website, which is where I found it. I usually have this over a bed of fried spinach or zucchini ribbons.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375.
Spray an 11x7 inch baking dish with Pam.
Salt and pepper the chicken breast halves and place in the dish.
In a bowl, combine the artichoke hearts, parmesan cheese, mayonnaise and garlic powder; mix well.
Spread artichoke mixture over chicken breasts.
Bake, uncovered, 30-35 minutes or until chicken juices run clear.

reviews.review_text: This dish was so wonderful that my husband licked his plate!  Based on other reviews, I made the following changes.  1. Used 1.5 lbs of chicken tenders, seasoned with garlic pepper, browned in light virgin olive oil to add color and to make sure chicken was cooked thoroughly  2. added 1 lb of sliced mushrooms sauteed in light olive oil seasoned with garlic pepper and onion powder  3.  substituted 1 can reduced sodium cream of mushroom soup and 1 can of roasted garlic mushroom soup for mayo because I don't like mayo  4. used marinated artichoke hearts  5. added frozen, baby sweet peas.  I mixed shredded parmesan cheese with the peas, artichoke hearts, soup, and a little milk in the pan with the sauteed mushrooms.  Placed the chicken in bottom of glass pan and covered with the stuff from the pan.  Served with chicken flavored rice pilaf and fresh baked french bread.  It was delicious, just wish I had used .5 lbs more chicken tenders.

attributes.source_text: my husband licked his plate

reviews.review_text: My chicken brreat halves were super big and the dish had to go back in the oven for just a bit longer. Cutting them in half lengthwise would've made just the right serving size as well. Live and learn.... I drained a small jar of marinated artichoke hearts and marinated the breasts in the juice, then sliced up the marinated artichokes a bit and added them into the mayo-Parm mixture....and also used a drained can of sliced mushrooms as another reviewer did. A very tastey dish indeed. This is going on the list of easy but elegant for when there are guests. I'm wondering about simmering some rice in the dish juices to go with the leftovers tomorrow night. I bet asparagus spears laid on top and coated w/ olive oil would've cooked just fine in the 35 min at 375.

attributes.source_text: easy but elegant for when there are guests

reviews.review_text: Super delicious. After reading many of the reviews, I made a few tweaks. Many said it was basically artichoke dip over chicken, and I have a favorite artichoke dip recipe. So changes I made were: 1. Decided to dice the raw chicken breasts into one inch cubes. Seasoned them well with kosher salt, black pepper and a little seasoned salt. 2. Used marinated artichoke hearts (a first for me...next time I would probably use half packed in water and half marinated). 3. We don't do mayonnaise, so substituted what I had on hand...half greek yogurt and half ricotta cheese. 4. Seasoned the wet mixture with garlic powder, onion powder, a couple of splashes of Worcestershire sauce and a couple of splashes of hot sauce...just for flavor and a hint of heat. This is definitely a "come as you like it" kind of recipe. Have fun with it. It's delicious no matter how you put it together!

attributes.source_text: just for flavor and a hint of heat

reviews.review_text: An instant favorite! I can't believe how easy this was - even though I had to make my own mayo because my jar was empty! I used Recipe #71967 for the mayo, adding in a large clove of garlic and I think it made the dish even more special. I layered some chicken flavored rice on the bottom of my casserole dish followed by cubed chicken breast and the artichoke mixture on top. Added some Italian blend cheese during the last few minutes of baking - not that it needed it but because we are suckers for cheese! Think I'll have to make this when Mom comes to visit. Thanks! :)          (Note:  Don't use chicken thighs if you are making this into a casserole - everything got really greasy and seemed to take forever to bake)

attributes.source_text: adding in a large clove of garlic and I think it made the dish even more special
because we are suckers for cheese

reviews.review_text: I am sorry.  I just didn't like this dish.  I had high hopes for it, as every review was positive.  However, when the mayo and cheese cooked together, they left a huge amount of grease behind.  I thought I could get passed that, but as I ate the chicken, I noticed a layer of grease forming on my lips.  Now mind you me, I am not opposed to grease, but the sight of it in pools around the chicken was unappetizing.  Even the next day, the grease was still there.  The chicken was very moist, but I couldn't enjoy it.  I am sorry I didn't enjoy it.

attributes.source_text: The chicken was very moist

reviews.review_text: Yooper this is delish!  So easy to prepare and simple ingredients....just my kind of recipe.  Two of my friends tried it and gave it a thumbs up.  I served it with wild rice, corn niblets and green beans.  It was good leftover as well.  I was the one who inquired about mayo in step 4....for some reason when I printed this it left out the word mayo but when I view the recipe on my monitor it does clearly state when to add the mayo.  Sorry if I caused any confusion with the question.  Thanks again for posting such a delightful recipe.

attributes.source_text: Two of my friends tried it and gave it a thumbs up

reviews.review_text: I really liked this dish because you can make it as directed and its good and easy, or you can add what you have on hand and really turn it into something special.  I made as directed except that I had marinated artichokes, not waterpacked.  I also lined my 13x9 pyrex with foil, sprayed it with Pam and then put my heavily seasoned, thinly sliced, pounded out chicken breast tenders down.  I spread the mayonnaise, artichoke, parmesan spread all over the chicken pieces.  I had some yellow bell pepper which needed to be used up so I chopped that up and spread that all over the chicken in addition to some sliced mushrooms( uncooked ).  I then baked it at 350 for about 30 minutes.  Then, I poured about 1/4 to 1/2 cup of heavy cream all over it and sprinkled that with cayenne pepper.  Then I used up some fresh spinach leaves I had by spreading that all over.  Then(phew!!) I had some sliced provolone cheese which I covered the spinach with and I then sprinkled a bit more parmesan all over everything and cooked it for about 15 minutes more until the spinach was wilted and the cheese was bubbly.  Thats the nice thing about this dish.  Anything that you like can be added and it tastes fabulous.  Try it!

This was sooooo good and incredibly easy and fast to make!  I seasoned the chicken breasts with salt and pepper after I rinsed and dried them.  I also spread the artichoke mixture on the underside of the chicken breast so it wouldn't slide off.  I used garlic and onion powder and a pinch of cajun seasoning in the artichoke mixture.  My kids ate it and actually enjoyed it.  My DH went back for seconds which he never does with meat.  I look forward to making this again and again!  Thanks for posting the recipe.

attributes.source_text: My kids ate it and actually enjoyed it
My DH went back for seconds

reviews.review_text: I absolutely loved this!  All my favorite tastes in one dish-delicious!!  I followed the recipe, but since I had a few misc. ingredients to use up I added them in there.  I added 2 roma tomatoes (more would be fine too), approx. 1 cup chopped red onion, extra garlic powder and a splash of tabasco sauce for a slight kick!  Also-I only had lite mayo so that is what I used and could tell nothing "off" about it whatsoever!  Will defintely add to my regular recipe file!  Thanks Yooper~

A very easy recipe to prepare indeed!!!  Did I also mention delicious?  I used two chicken breasts and the remains of a jar of artichoke hearts that were in the refirgerator.  I also threw in some sliced mushrooms ( they needed to be used up) and a little shredded mozzarella.  I did go light on the parmesan and mayo... I added just enough mayo to moisten the mixture.  I piled it high on the chicken and it turned out beautiful... it really is nice enough to serve company.  I seasoned the breasts with salt and pepper before topping just to make sure they would not turn out bland. Great, rich and filling entree...  I served it with Recipe #128563 and some steamed broccoli with a little butter and lemon juice.  The lemon really went well with this dish b/c it helped "brighten" up some of the flavors and richness...  Thanks for sharing!!!

attributes.source_text: Great, rich and filling entree

reviews.review_text: This was delicious!  I made this yesterday, using a jar of marinated artichoke hearts that I drained very well, then chopped up.  Because they were already seasoned with spices I left out the garlic powder.  I did everything else as the recipe stated and then spread it on half a chicken that I had cut into serving size pieces and then baked it in the oven as stated in the recipe.  The chicken turned out beautiful with such a lovely flavour.  Thanks Yooper for yet another winner!

This was very good, but "rich" was an understatement.  I will make this again, but will likely cut back on the mayonaisse.  Don't get me wrong, I love artichoke dip so these flavors are among my favorite, but after eating 1 chicken breast I felt like I ate an entire artichoke dip appetizer.  That's not necessarily a bad thing, however.  :)  I can see why some people gave this a 5 star, but they must have a much higher "richness" tolerance than me.  4 stars is as high as my overstuffed belly can go.  Thanks for the recipe!

In this case, the dish does taste as good as the photo.  I chose the recipe because I had artichokes in the refridgerator that needed to be used.  I came across Yooper's recipe and the picture of the dish was mouthwatering.  I found humanely raised chicken at the local grocery store so I feel I used the highest quality chicken available which for me made this dish very special.  It is so easy and quick to make I would make this for a large crowd and be sure no one would be disappointed.

I was really surprised at how good this is.  It is now one of our all-time favorites.  I used two cans of artichokes and rinsed them to decrease the tart taste (we love artichokes!).  I also used two cloves of fresh garlic - minced which gave it a wonderful flavor.  I always buy a large bag of seasoned chicken in the bulk section and this gave it more even more flavor.  And to decrease the calories and fat - I used Best Foods Reduced Fat Mayonaise.  Suberb!  I will have to double the amounts next time.

attributes.source_text: two cloves of fresh garlic - minced which gave it a wonderful flavor

reviews.review_text: Did the browning on the Chicken and added some salt/seasoning/make sure you use a little bit of red pepper flakes. Also made some sauteed mushrooms, then put the parm(regiano)/marinated chokes/ handful of frozen baby peas/light mayo/bit of milk to dilute mixture into the pan and combined for a bit as was suggested. Smothered the chicken then sprinkled Panko overtop. Served with herbed rice. Was flavourful and excellent. Overcooked the chicken slightly so will compensate next go round - 20 mins in oven should do it. Delish.

This recipe has to be tried!  it is such an easy quick "cooks itself" recipe that tastes like it was worked on over a stove.  short ingredient list makes it even more applealing.  the house smelled wonderful while it cooked.  i had  no mayo at the last minute; so i subbed tarter sauce.  the taste was phenomenal.  creamy and rich but not overfilling.  such a nice blend of flavors; they all balanced nicely.  i am making this again next week with fish.  thanks for the great recipe!

attributes.source_text: creamy and rich but not overfilling
they all balanced nicely

reviews.review_text: This was very good and rich! I added my own twist to this recipe, and turned it into a casserole. I made 2 cups of rice cooked in chicken broth, and made that the bottom layer in a large casserole dish. Ontop of that, I layered the seasoned cubed-up chicken. And ontop of that, I layered the artichoke/mayo/parmesan mixture. I added sauteed onion and spinich to it also. Baked as called for, and it was really good! Did I say this dish tasts sooo rich? I used reduced fat mayo.

attributes.source_text: This was very good and rich!
this dish tasts sooo rich

reviews.review_text: I made this without the artichokes and it was a big hit!  I made 4 chicken breast halves, 2 for hubby and one each for my sons.  Well... my husband ate THREE of them, one son got a piece, and the other (who came home late) had to make do with ramen noodles!  Those who got to try it said it was very yummy and I need to keep this recipe.  Just using the mayo, cheese and garlic powder, I had enough to spread over a few more chicken pieces if I had them, so I spread it on both sides.

attributes.source_text: my husband ate THREE of them
one son got a piece

reviews.review_text: My husband said that this was a once a week recipe which means that he could eat it once a week for the rest of his life and not get tired of it.  My mom brought one of those Costco sized artichoke heart jars for Christmas so this was an easy throw together post Christmas.  We had it with Caramelized Butternut Squash, Recipe 106627, which is also a good recipe.  I think having them in the oven a bit longer, as another reviewer noted, gives the topping a nice crispness.  Thanks.

attributes.source_text: My husband said that this was a once a week recipe

items.label: 24k Carrots
items.name: 24k Carrots
items.description: Carrots coated with a yummy butter, brown sugar and ginger sauce. I grew up eating these in Texas. Easy, quick and yummy!-- GREAT way to get kids to enjoy this veggie! If you like a lot of sauce double the sauce ingredients. I posted this less 'saucy' to keep the fat and calories down. The sauce is yummy and great on rice or just on a spoon! Hope you enjoy it as much as we do!  I am so honored that this simple little recipe of mine has been so well received. Thank you all for your reviews!
instructions: Cook carrots until tender- or to desired doneness. (I usually steam them to retain the most flavor).
Melt butter and add brown sugar and ginger, stirring to blend.
Add sauce to carrots and stir to coat.

reviews.review_text: Yummy! I always use carrots with other vegetables, so it was nice to use just carrots and make something very simple yet tasty at the same time! I sliced my carrots and sauteed them till they softened. A bit of water helped them along as well. I think I'll probably add more ground ginger next time since I think I added a touch less than recommended, or try fresh ginger for a nice little kick. I might microwave the carrots next time like other reviews have suggested and see how it compares time-wise. Hmm maybe some honey instead of brown sugar.. or even some herbs. Oh the possibilities.. :) Thanks for a lovely recipe!

attributes.source_text: sauteed them till they softened

reviews.review_text: Thank you!!! I hated cooked carrots until now. Temporary following a low residue diet and need to eat well cooked or canned vegetables with no skin. I had some canned ones in the pantry that I knew I should use or donate. I made the sauce in a small skillet and tossed the drained carrots and heated till warm. I also added a little sauce to my plain white rice and it was very nice for a change. This would be great for the microwave or to make camping as it is super easy!!!

These are definitely delicious carrots and SO simple to make. I used a bag of baby carrots and just threw all of the ingredients into a pot with 1 cup of water. Then I brought it to a boil, covered the pan and reduced the heat to a simmer. I simmered the carrots covered for 15 minutes and then uncovered for 10 minutes until the sauce was reduced. My 80 year old Dad looked at the plate and said: "CARROTS? YUK!" I told him to just try 'em, and he did.... He then requested seconds!

attributes.source_text: He then requested seconds!

reviews.review_text: Another rave for you, Hope.  Missy (next door neighbor) came over and asked me if I knew how to make glazed carrots.  This is the only recipe I ever use, but haven't rated it (I'm a lazy bones sometimes!)  She gave it a rave, but left out the ginger because she didn't have any.  Said it was just like the school's (which she loves - our school had good food!).  Rylee (her DD) also gobbled these up...well, part of them.  The other part ended up in the floor, on the high chair, and in her hair.  :D

attributes.source_text: She gave it a rave
Rylee (her DD) also gobbled these up

reviews.review_text: Very yummy!  Made these to go with dinner last night.  I used 1/2 lb of the frozen crinkle cut carrots.  I kept the sauce ingredients at 2 tbsp brown sugar and 2 tbsp margarine but decreased the ginger to 1/4 tsp which was plenty for my family's tastes. I'll definitely  increase the sauce ingredients in the future to make it more 'saucy' though.  I also think next time I'll try subbing cinnamon for the ginger because my family likes cinnamon on carrots and I think it will work well with this method.  Thanks for posting!!!!!!!!

attributes.source_text: Made these to go with dinner last night

reviews.review_text: I followed Mama's recipe and found that I prefer the less saucy version - to keep it healthy. The kids liked it, it was easy to make - I steamed baby carrots, then mixed them into a bowl with the brown sugar, butter and ground ginger.  Because the butter was not melted yet, I mixed what I could and then added the hot carrots, which then dissolved and turned the mix into the sauce.  I will be making this again.

attributes.source_text: The kids liked it

reviews.review_text:
UPDATE On 6/20/10: I've made these carrots so many times and can't believe I've never posted a photo. Well, I've made these again and here's the photo. And I have to say they are just as good if not better than the first time they were made. My first time to review this recipe was November 3rd,2006
I just want to say that my SO and I really enjoyed these carrots very much.I thought that the ginger and brown sugar gave the dish that "something special"that is usually missing from carrots.These will be made again,Thank you for posting.

attributes.source_text: my SO and I really enjoyed these carrots very much

reviews.review_text: These had good flavor, BUT, I did not rate them because I followed the other reviewer's suggestion and microwaved them. I have never done that before and DO NOT recommend it. The first batch I made using the directions given in the review resulted in horribly shriveled and overcooked carrots. The second batch, I halved the amount of cooking time and still they came out shriveled and overcooked but somewhat edible. However, as I stated before, the flavor was still good. So, next time I will go back to making them via stovetop and I'm sure I will love them!

These are fabulous! My fiance bought a huge bag of baby carrots and I needed to find a way to fix them. Neither of us particularly like cooked carrots, but these are the exception! I steamed the carrots and microwaved the butter, brown sugar and ground ginger for 30 seconds. Then, I drained the water from the pan, added the carrots and sauce and voila! A ridiculously easy, DELICIOUS one-pot side! The ginger flavor isn't obvious, but gives these something extra.

attributes.source_text: The ginger flavor isn't obvious, but gives these something extra
one-pot side

reviews.review_text: These carrots are superb!  I had a 1 lb bag of baby carrots left over from a veggie tray I made for by DIL's baby shower.  I did an ingredient search for carrots to find a different way to use these up.  I like glazed carrots and I like ginger.  When I read this recipe, I knew I couldn't go wrong.  I use an extra tablespoon of brown sugar, but followed the rest of the recipe as written.  These were the best glazed carrots that I have ever had.  The ginger and the brown sugar are a wonderful combination.  I am putting this recipe in my binder of "special" recipes.  I would like to try these with fresh, grated ginger root as some of the others suggested.  Thanks for another amazing recipem, mama!

attributes.source_text: I like glazed carrots
The ginger and the brown sugar are a wonderful combination

reviews.review_text: I made these for dh as a quick side for his work lunch (Spam and mustard sandwiches). He loved them and said they complimented the sandwiches well. He also said it made carrots much more enjoyable to eat. I love how easy they are to cook and I used the microwave suggestion of another review to steam the carrots. I let dh do the rating as I am not the carrot lover. My little one still preferred them raw. Thank you mama's kitchen !!!

attributes.source_text: He loved them
for his work lunch
as a quick side

reviews.review_text: Not that you need another 5 star review, but this recipe is super yummy!!  I'm not normally a huge fan of sweetened veggies, but the brown sugar and ginger was a great combo.  Even got my 4yo veggie hater to clean his plate!  That's saying something.  I melted the butter, brown sugar and ginger in a serving dish in the microwave. Then just added my boiled, sliced carrots and tossed to combine. Thank you for the great recipe!

attributes.source_text: Even got my 4yo veggie hater to clean his plate

reviews.review_text: oh these are sooooooooo good. i just prepared them today prior to a family gathering tomorrow. i was intending to heat them quickly in the microwave tomorrow. and guess what? i've eaten the lot of them. for sure i am making these often.  thanks for a lovely recipe - i am sure my kids will be encouraged to eat healthily with these (thats if i leave them any). Great!!!

I totally enjoyed these.  Not only were they simple, but delicious.  I might try fresh ginger the next time, because I love an intense ginger flavor, but these are a winner just as they are.

I just upped the stars.  I saved a small amount of these and reheated them after 3-4 days.  I liked them even better.  I had them tonite with just a simple pot pie.

These were absolutely great.  Really enhances the natural sweetness of the carrots. Made them with little shatanay carrots, halved lengthways. I cooked 500g for my little boy and I, and we ate the lot! Ive passed the recipe onto my friend whos little boy has an aversion to veg, with the promise "he WILL eat these!" :o) thank you very very much for the recipe.

attributes.source_text: enhances the natural sweetness of the carrots
I cooked 500g for my little boy and I, and we ate the lot!

reviews.review_text: Rave reviews from my family this last Easter.  I was looking for soemthing simple and just a little different but not so much so fussy eaters wouldn't try it.  This was a real winner and really fit the bill.  I had many requests for the recipe and have had them ask for it again.  Think I will add to my Easter menu every year thank you!

attributes.source_text: Rave reviews from my family
this last Easter

reviews.review_text: Wow! This was amazing. I can't stand ginger normally but this converted me. I steamed the carrots and whipped up some rice. And I mixed the rice and coated carrots together. A great, filling, fairly healthy meal (better than the potato chips I was going to eat). For a little kick I added some crushed red peppers. I will take this recipe with me when I head off to college.

attributes.source_text: For a little kick I added some crushed red peppers

reviews.review_text: Most of the family really liked this. DH even took the leftover sauce and poured it over some ice cream with bananas for instant bananas foster dessert. I did add a small dash of cinnamon, just because that smelled right. My DD and I still agree that even with a sweet sugar coating, carrots are the most vile, evil vegetable ever created. ;) I will be making this again. One day, I may even taste it! Thanks! :)

attributes.source_text: Most of the family really liked this
DH even took the leftover sauce and poured it over some ice cream with bananas

items.label: Amish Baked Oatmeal
items.name: Amish Baked Oatmeal
items.description: Make and share this Amish Baked Oatmeal recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Grease a 13 x 9 x 2 baking pan.
Combine all ingredients together.
Spread on prepared baking pan.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until the edges are golden brown.
Immediately spoon into a bowl.
Top with warm milk, fresh fruit or brown sugar if desired.

reviews.review_text: This is the only way I want oatmeal now. Very good flavor. I did add a bit of cinnamon too ours. Also, we didn't have quick cooking oats, so we made our oatmeal first and then added all the other ingredients and baked it. It's still a very soft oatmeal that way, but I can't get over the wonderful blend of flavors. My husband however made it another time without pre-cooking it and he still loved it. A bit crunchier version. Thanks for the great recipe. Next time going to add some raisins and apple bits too.UPDATE: I just made this again but this time added raisins.  Came out wonderful!  I added a photo showing the raisins.  Again, since I like it a bit softer I used regular oats and cooked them first, then proceeded with the recipe as written. Drizzled with a tiny bit of pancake syrup. Yummy!

attributes.source_text: It's still a very soft oatmeal that way
A bit crunchier version
My husband however made it another time without pre-cooking it and he still loved it

reviews.review_text: What a wonderful recipe!  Like many others, I added cinnamon and half brown sugar.  I also added some walnuts.  The kids absolutely loved it!  They are begging for me to make it again!  This was so simple and there are so many things you could do with it!  I think next time I will add some slivered almonds, some strawberries, and some almond extract...any way I can't imagine this being bad!  The only complaint that I have is the serving size is very small if made according to recipe....I would definately recommend upping the ingredients if serving more than 3 or 4.  Thank you Shari2 for posting such a wonderful recipe!

attributes.source_text: The kids absolutely loved it!

reviews.review_text: This recipe is amazing! I made this last night to bring to work this morning for breakfast.  I almost couldn't wait for that oven timer to go off so I could take it out and taste it!  It couldn't have been any easier and the taste is  sinful!  I replaced the white sugar with brown sugar, threw in a handful of craisins, and added a small mixture of sliced almonds, chopped walnuts and chopped pecans to the mix.  The nuts give it a fantastic pop of texture. I only used two tablespoons of butter, and used skim milk...Absolutely delicious! Even my picky fiancee who tends to not enjoy anything healthy loved this.  I am eating it plain for breakfast, but think it would be amazing served warm with a scoop of lowfat vanilla ice cream for dessert also.  Can't wait to try that :-)  I am so happy to have found this simple and healthy recipe to add to my collection.  I will make this often, thank you so much!

attributes.source_text: to bring to work this morning for breakfast
Even my picky fiancee who tends to not enjoy anything healthy loved this
I am eating it plain for breakfast

reviews.review_text: We usually have a hot bowl of oats on most mornings, but this is the first time I've ever heard of baking it. This was soooo good. I was trying to figure out a way to get more fruit into my toddler, so decided to top his with applesauce and raisens. I tasted it and it was even better. Two days later, I made this again made a few changes to the recipe. First I eliminated the salt since I used salted butter. Then I added about 1/4 cup finely chopped apple (with skin) and about 1/2 cup of raisens, 2 tsp of cinnamon (we love it!), and a tablespoon or two of applesauce. Finally, I used an 11 X 7 X 1.5 pan instead of the pan recommended because I wanted a thicker result.  This second batch tasted so good, my husband (for the first time in 10 years) asked for an entire bowl after allowing me to force a spoonful into his mouth!!  This is a man who has made fun of my oatmeal ritual for YEARS and now he wanted his own serving. This is a sweet, nicely textured oatmeal, we'll enjoy for years to come! Thanks

attributes.source_text: This is a sweet, nicely textured oatmeal
my husband (for the first time in 10 years) asked for an entire bowl

reviews.review_text:
Loved this for several reasons. First, it was quick and easy to mix up. It didn't make a mess. And, it was SO good. I cut the sugar back to 1/4 cup and decreased the salt a little. Took another reviewer's advice and added some cinnamon. Also went by the advice of another review and used a smaller pan. Even in a 2 1/2 quart casserole dish it seemed a little thin but definitely worked. The warm milk is excellent on this... adds some needed moisture. Also added fresh blueberries which were delicious.

I don't think the full 30 minutes is necessary. Also, I would never try to feed this to six people. My two young girls and I polished this off ourselves! Granted I'm stuffed. But in a good way. Thanks! We will definitely make this again. Perfect for a rainy, stay-at-home day.

attributes.source_text: My two young girls and I polished this off ourselves
adds some needed moisture
Perfect for a rainy, stay-at-home day

reviews.review_text: Wow.....This is soooooo good. I made this using old fashion oatmeal and it was probably not nearly as moist as quick cook would have been but I did add extra milk and cut the sugar back a bit. I put it into a 9 x 9 inch glass baking dish as suggested by another reviewer and it was the perfect size. I served it with home canned peaches and heated half and half and it was delicious! This says a whole lot cuz I'm really not an oatmeal fan. But DH is and he agreed. I plan to mix up a triple batch next time we have overnight company and just put it in the fridge overnight to pop in the oven when I get out of bed. Pretty sure this will be a hit!! I'm pretty sure a lot of different toppings would be fun to offer with this dish. Thanks for sharing this, Shari!!

attributes.source_text: DH is and he agreed

reviews.review_text: I made this yesterday, with a few changes.  I do not like hot oatmeal at all, but LOVE oatmeal cookies!!  So, I baked the entire recipe in an 8x8 pan, and added about 6 minutes onto the time - it came out like a soft granola bar - and VERY tasty.  Next time, and there will be a next time for sure, I think I'll try adding a little more oats and some raisins or cranberries or walnuts and maybe using the Splenda brown sugar instead of the regular Splenda baking sugar.  Thank you for a great and tasty recipe!!  I might even get some peaches and vanilla ice cream as suggested by WJKing, and then make it a healthy and delicious dessert !!

attributes.source_text: it came out like a soft granola bar

reviews.review_text: Delicious!  The first time I made it as written, topped it with a little more brown sugar just because I was craving that real indulgent cookie taste.  Imade it again yesterday, with a few tweaks for my family's personal preference:  I cut back the sugar slightly, and used brown sugar, added a dash of cinnamon.  I only used 1 tablespoon of butter, and after it baked I pulled it out, crumbled it all up in the pan and stirred it well, then put it back in the oven and immediately turned the oven off, left it for about 15 minutes.  DH and the kids preferred it like this, with the crunchier texture, and the taste was still amazing.  We had it as cereal, and then as a topping for fresh fruit and frozen yogurt.  Thank you for posting!

attributes.source_text: DH and the kids preferred it like this

reviews.review_text:
Overall, this is just delicious! I lightened this recipe a bit by cutting the butter back to 2 Tbsp, using 2 egg whites instead of one whole egg and using 1% milk.  I also used long cooking oats, a bit more vanilla and added some cinnamon to the mix.  I tried substituting brown sugar for white sugar, but I didn't like it as much.    

It reheats well in the microwave, but is best straight out of the oven. YUM!   And it really DOES taste like a warm, soft oatmeal cookie!! 

Thanks so much for posting this Shari2.  I am always looking for a healthy and delicious way to start my day!

reviews.review_text:
Sep12/09- To this I added Kellogg's Guardian Cinnamon cereal (trying to get rid of it) You can see it at the edge of the baking dish in the picture I posted. I also added a generous sprinkling of cinnamon on the top. This was good and I could take a piece with me as I headed out the door because it was kinda cake-like.
Nov09 - Made this again but followed the recipe more closely. This time I only added a dash of allspice, a couple dashes of cinnamon, and 1/4 psyllium husks. I doubled the recipe and put the mixture in a greased muffin tin. Perfect grab'n'go breakfast!

attributes.source_text: Perfect grab'n'go breakfast!

reviews.review_text: this was great. i used old fashioned oats and anctually made it the night before so i just had to pop it in the oven when i woke up. i added a little rum extract as well and some raisons and walnuts to the mix. then i sprinkled some more walnuts on top and dusted with a brown sugar/cinnamon mix. it smelled sooo good baking and i actually over cooked it way toooo long.. so i dumped it in a bowl chopped a banana on it and poured a bit of milk on it. it was DeLisHiouS! even over cooked. my husband says he's glad i burnt it but next time i'll be more careful.. yum  yum. thank you.

attributes.source_text: my husband says he's glad i burnt it

reviews.review_text: Never tried baked oatmeal before but was intrigued by any recipe that might be able to get me to like oatmeal!  The taste of the final product was good, but I am completely perplexed because the final product didn't even go a quarter inch from the bottom of the pan (and barely covered the bottom before cooking) so that was quite disappointing.  Half of the pan barely netted 1/2 cup which is quite a measly serving for anyone's breakfast.  I'll have to play around with the recipe, perhaps double the ingredients but use splenda to keep the calories low.  Thanks for posting.

attributes.source_text: a measly serving for anyone's breakfast

reviews.review_text: Yum!  You're right, this does taste like an oatmeal cookie!  This was my first experience making baked oatmeal as well.  I did follow the recipe, except I halved it and accidently used a whole egg instead of just half.  I think that the final result was that my oatmeal was a bit firmer than it would have otherwise been, but it still turned out great!  We served with a little cream and milk and it was just delish.  I did use brown sugar for the sugar (yum, brown sugar and oats!), and  like Miss Annie said, I think the additions you could make to this are endless- raisins, apples, nuts, anything!  I did add a dash of cinnamon, which I definitely recommend.  I like that this is so easy to just throw in the oven and let cook while you're getting ready or preparing other breakfast dishes.  I'm always keen on breakfast recipes that can be cooked in the oven, since breakfast seems to be so often an event where every dish requires a burner (pancakes, eggs, bacon and so on!)  The only thing is, I made a half recipe, which was supposed to be 3 servings... I split it between BF and myself and it really wasn't enough for me to consider it a whole meal.  I guess its 3 servings if you are planning on this as a side, but next time I will make the full recipe for the two of us.   I'd rather have leftover than not enough.  I too thought that the pan size seemed rather small (I used an 8x8 for the half recipe), but this sort of crisps like a cookie on the outside and gets wonderfully creamy on the inside, sort of like, as another reviewer stated, granola.  All-in-all, we enjoyed this very much and I think its a great low-maintenance and fairly healthful breakfast dish!

a great low-maintenance and fairly healthful breakfast dish

reviews.review_text: Edited to fix the fact that my 5-star rating did not show up, just the comment part.  I know this has tons of reviews, but when I found this recipe from my Spring PAC 2008 baby, Shari2, I had to try it. My bf and I love oatmeal, but neither one of us has ever had (or cooked) baked oatmeal before. This smells wonderful as I'm baking it, and bf came out to the kitchen to comment on how the good smell is making him hungrier than he already is. When I told him what I was going to make, he thought it sounded interesting and different. I halved this recipe to serve 3 but realized that it would barely serve 2 as a full meal, so I mixed up another half batch. I used an 8x8 pan for the full batch, as the larger pan seemed too big. I added a dash of cinnamon to this, and because of my IBS, used Fresh & Easy brand Unsweetened Organic Soy Milk, Eggbeaters, and Smart Balance Spread with Flaxseed Oil. I decided to try this with white sugar, as recipe states. Bf's first response to trying his bowl (plain with nothing on/with it) was 'Mmm!' After acclimating myself to the different texture of oatmeal, I agree. It's quite sweet too, all on its own. I did add a tad bit of soy milk to my bowl Bf said he'd like me to make this again and gives this 4 stars. He looks happy while eating this, lol, so I feel pretty confident that this recipe is a winner for us. The more I keep eating this, the more I love it. The edges are delicious, lol. I agree with other reviewers, this is like eating an oatmeal cookie for breakfast. The 8x8 pan for the full recipe made barely enough for 2 of us, but I think the texture, flavor, and thickness in that pan was perfect. When bf came back for 2nds, he was scraping up every last bit in the pan; I had to stop him before he took my 2nd serving! Obviously, Shari2, this got rave reviews here. Thanks so much for sharing and I'm glad I chose this for for one of the recipes in Spring PAC 2008. Served this with recipe #107440.

reviews.review_text: I have made this many times, and it always turns out wonderfully.  I melt the butter in a glass 9-inch pie plate.  I have used both white sugar and brown sugar (both are good), a few times I have also reduced the sugar to just over a 1/4 c.  I generally add a few TBSP's of ground flax seed meal.  I mix up the dry ingredients in a covered bowl the night before, for a quicker preparation on a busy morning.  I like mine with a bit of milk, and my hubby eats his plain or with maple syrup.  It's even good straight out of the fridge the next day.  I love this recipe.

reviews.review_text: Been making this for awhile now and can't fathom eating oatmeal any other way. Plus, the recipe is so easy that I can enlist the help of my toddler in the kitchen (a very positive experience for both of us). Sometimes we experiment by substituting brown sugar and/or Splenda for the sugar...and it just wouldn't be complete without the extra milk or bananas on the finished product! Mmmm, mmmm good!  EDIT:  My apologies for the 4 stars...I meant to put 5- it's that good!!!  Really love that my kids (toddler and teen both) not only request it, but want to help prepare it too!

reviews.review_text: This is delicious!  One of those recipes you really wish you could give more than five stars!  I made this with brown sugar instead of white, and mmmmmmm...was it good.  I would say as much as we love sweet things, it has plenty of sugar & didn't need more added before or after cooking!  It came out different than I imagined, kind of dry like granola.  But, you can stir in some milk (warm it or it turns the oatmeal cold & you have to nuke it) and make it more like regular oatmeal.  Better than regular oatmeal for sure, kind of chewy & crunchy...just like an oatmeal cookie.

It was SO good and has made it to the top of our breakfast dish list!  I had to add extra milk and am glad I did because it was a bit dry, even with extra. items.label: Bev's Sauteed Yellow Squash
items.name: Bev's Sauteed Yellow Squash
items.description: This is the way I have been serving summer squash to my family to years. It is so easy and tastes great. I hope you enjoy it too!
instructions: Melt butter in large skillet.
Add onion and cook just till tender.
Add yellow squash and continue cooking over medium heat, stirring until squash begins to soften.
Cover and continue cooking over low heat until nice and tender (usually about 20-25 minutes).
I add lots of salt and pepper.

reviews.review_text: I never liked squash and so never even tried to cook it before I tried Bev's recipe. Squash seemed too intimidating to cook and since I didn't care for them I didn't try very hard. But my son and husband love squash and when I saw this recipe I decided to give it a try. What do you know? Now I like squash as much as they do! This is a great recipe to start with and wonderful just the way it is, although I like to soak 5 minutes in buttermilk first. And sometimes I use a little bacon grease to cook them in and use the bacon for a topping. Optional items I sometimes add are paprika, garlic powder, sugar, lemon pepper, or Paula Deen's House Seasong. Not all of these additions at once, of course, just one or two for variation, but usually always Paula Deen's House Seasoning. Thanks, Bev!

Oh. My. Goodness!  I like squash, and this was the best squash I've ever eaten.  My family loved it too.  I normally would have substituted olive oil for the butter because of the saturated fat in butter, but because of the rave reviews, I decided to splurge and cook this with butter.  I'm glad I did.  I will experiment with this later, though.  I'll try olive oil.  Also, I'll try using Fleischman's Margarine made with olive oil.  This was as easy as it was delicious.  Also I'm looking forward to experimenting with adding tomatoes and maybe some other veggies to this.

attributes.source_text: My family loved it too

reviews.review_text: Excellent recipe. Simple recipe that does not taste at all like the "watered down" limp squash dishes that you find at most restaurants. Although my vegetables were from the market, I can only imagine how good this dish is with squash straight from your garden. I added one zucchini during the last 5 minutes for color, and it was delicious. I recommend cutting your squash in thick rounds and then half those - resulting in chunks. Don't overcook this recipe; you really just need to saute and cover for 10-15 min. Thanks Bev for sharing!

I just posted a picture of my version of this recipe. I actually use a little brown sugar in my recipe, and use both squash and zucchini. Sorry, I don't usually comment on recipes that I've altered, but I honestly can't remember where I got the original squash recipe that includes the sugar. I make this at least once a week and my 3 and 5 year olds actually eat it, even though you can definitely see the onions in it! Usually I have to "hide" onions by finely chopping or food processing :)

attributes.source_text: my 3 and 5 year olds actually eat it

reviews.review_text: Bev... the flavor of this dish is excellant, very easy to prepare.  I used a minced garlic clove with the onion and instead of all salt, I used 1/2 tsp. Season salt and 1/2 tsp/ emeril's original essence.  Dh loved it, said it's  deservant of more than 5 stars., which I totally agree. Thanks for the recipe, I will be making this again soon...

We love our veggies "au natural" but this recipe for squash was oh so good.  Simple and tasty.  I sauteed 2 cloves minced fresh garlic with the onions.  Next time I will try with mixture of zucchini and yellow squash. Recipe does not take away from the natural flavor of the veggies, only enhances it.  Thanks Bev for another winner.

For me, this dish is a wonderful taste of southern-style home cuisine, reminding me so much of my mom's cooking.  I might have moved away from the South, but I feel right back at "home" every time I prepare this. items.label: Debbie's Crock Pot Chili
items.name: Debbie's Crock Pot Chili
items.description: Everybody who tries this chili loves it. The girls at work always like when I bring leftovers in! Everyone takes a copy of this recipe.
instructions: Mix together seasoning mix.
Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. (You will only use 5 tsp in this recipe - save the rest for next time!).
In a skillet, cook ground beef until no longer pink.
Drain.
Add onion and 3 tsp of seasoning mix.
In Crock-Pot, add tomatoes, tomato sauce, one can of beans and two more teaspoons of seasoning mix.
Place the other can of beans in a blender and process until smooth.
Add beans and meat to the crock pot.
Stir together.
Cook on low for 6 to 8 hours.

reviews.review_text: Just want to get this recipe into my reviews. - doubled the recipe....5 stars for simplicity.....will rate again after the chili cookoff at work on Thursday. I used a combo of ground moose, ground deer and ground pork for total 3 lbs. Used 32 oz homemade canned tomato sauce from a friend, 1 28oz can whole tomatoes and 1 28oz can italian plum tomatoes which I cut up. Used 1 can white kidney which I tried mashing in the crockpot then I pureed 1 can red kidney in my bullet plus 2 cans red kidney. Used spices as specified but instead of minced onion I used dehydrated onion. Can hardly wait to taste and will additional comment in a couple of days. Its not cook off yet but we had some for our supper tonight and we found it soupy and bland so I added in the remaining spice blend and its back on the burner to try and thicken up. Added some more cayenne and cumiin plus some worster sauce. At the last hour before serving today I added a dollop of my tomatillo salsa made with thai chilies and finally I was happier with it. Folks loved the texture and the folks who like a good bowl of chili really enjoyed this.

Let me first say I made this once a few months ago, and would have rated it a 3.  But after some tweaking I now rate it a 5!<br/><br/>The first time I followed the recipe exactly and it came out too soupy for my taste (literally my husband joked it was chili soup) and didn't have as much flavor as I would have expected.  However, after a few days in the fridge it did thicken up/get better so I knew there was certainly potential. My recommendations: <br/><br/>1. make sure to drain all of the beans, this was not clear in the recipe to me. I also added an additional can of white beans (drained). <br/><br/>2. I added a small can of tomato paste to thicken it up a little bit<br/><br/>3. I added some fresh garlic to the beef as well as the white onions.<br/><br/>4. I also added more chopped onions directly to crock pot.<br/><br/>5.  I added about 1 extra tsb each to seasoning to beef and crock pot ...probably would add even more the next time I make it as its really a great flavor and not too over powering at all.<br/><br/>6. Oh I also added more beef than it called for...more like 2 lbs.<br/><br/>*Note this made for a nice chunky/hearty chili that has great flavor but I would not say was spicy.  So if you like it more spicy perhaps add some hot sauce or more cayenne.  But that can easily be added after it is done cooking.

this made for a nice chunky/hearty chili
I would not say was spicy

reviews.review_text: This chili turned out great, but, like most of the other posters, I did feel that I needed to make a few modifications/additions. I wanted the consistency to be heartier and also to increase to heat of the dish. I doubled the meat, added almost one extra can of crushed tomatoes, and one extra can of drained beans (altogether 2 cans black beans and 1 can chili beans). In order to increase the heat of the chili I used one can diced tomatoes with jalapenos, and the chili beans mentioned above were in a spicy sauce prior to draining. I also used the entirety of the spice mixture. To add some additional flavor, I used three cloves of garlic, one onion, and one green bell pepper added to the beef while cooking. I also added about 1 tsp of salt to the chili halfway through. Overall, I was glad to have this recipe as a starting point, but not sure if I would have liked it more or less had I followed the original recipe. I enjoyed the final product with the changes I made!

This really is VERY good chili!  i had never made chili before, this fit the bill PERFECTLY because it was so nice and THICK (i hate "soupy" chili), i used a can of refried instead of putting the beans in the blender and i think that makes all the difference in the world  as to the consistency of the dish...THICK! i also used a pound and a half of ground beef and a half pound of ground (Jimmy Dean) sausage.  i then added some finely diced green pepper and onion (about a 1/4 cup of each that i saute'd with the meat) a little Frank's Hot Sauce, a small can of tomato paste, a couple dashes of Worstechire and about 2 tsps of cocoa powder and it was PERFECT.  it was hard to let it sit and cook for 6 hours in the crock pot without running over and "tasting" it every few minutes!  I'll definitely be keeping this chili recipe...it was awesome.  Thanks Debbie!!

attributes.source_text: as to the consistency of the dish...THICK!

reviews.review_text: I really like this recipe, and it is the baseline for how I make my chili. I make the following modifications for the seasoning: I substitute parsley for coriander (since I hate coriander/cilantro), add 1 tsp. of paprika, 1/2 tsp. onion powder, and 1/4 tsp. crushed red pepper flakes. For the chili itself, I substitute fresh onion (1/4 cup, cut in large chunks--so that I can avoid them!), add 1 rib of celery (finely sliced), and start with dried pinto beans instead of the canned beans. I pre-soak the beans for at least 18 hours in water with some baking soda mixed in to neutralize the phytic acid in the beans. If I take the time to pre-cook the beans/they are tender, I simply add half the mixture to the crock pot at the beginning and mash them with a potato masher (if they aren't tender enough, you would need to use a blender or food processor as the recipe suggests).

This was super great chili!  I have my own tried and true recipe, but I figured I would try this since I needed to use the crock-pot.  Well, my family flipped over it and my husband said I outdid myself! (I explained that I couldn't take the credit!)  I used small white beans and light kidney beans for the puree.  I didn't put them in the blender, instead I put them in the crock-pot first and mushed them up with a potato masher.  I love this part of the recipe, because my family is getting more fiber and they don't have a clue!  I have never used cumin or coriander and was worried they might be too strong but the chili tasted like...well...Chili!  Thanks so much for sharing!  P.S.  I used 2 lbs. of ground beef...otherwise, didn't change a thing.  NOTE: The spice mix makes enough for at least two batches of chili.

attributes.source_text: my family flipped over it
my husband said I outdid myself

reviews.review_text: Ok, I made this as a standalone dish and also for coney's.  I really like the recipe and spices n herbs chosen.  I think people lean to overrate things and do NOT base it on the stand-alone recipe, as-is, but some alternative or something they come up with.  I did EVERYTHING exactly as said except adding the additional can of puree'd beans, but that would have done nothing more than add filler and no real change to flavor.  The recipe as a few folks DID point out (pat yourself on the back for getting it right) that the recipe is bland as all!  I even added 1t of salt.  BLAND.  It was ok once the mustard and onions where added in addition for coneys, but stand-alone....NO.  If this was served in a restaurant, I would have either sent it back or ate it, but never order again and may not go to the place that served it again as a reflection of their food!  I would NOT recommend THIS recipe.  I'm not sure how to correct it.  Maybe MORE spice than 5t in total AND addition of salt (at least 1t), but I would not waste my time.  There is other recipes and more worthy.  Beware!

Great! We decided to make chili for the big game (Superbowl XLVII) and since we got a crockpot for Christmas I thought it should be crockpot chili. I stumbled over this recipe while searching Food.com from my phone. It looked pretty easy and sure enough it was easy and very tasty.

The only change we made was to use ground turkey and ground hot Italian turkey sausage. Oh, and we put in one can of tomato paste into the mix for a little more tomato taste. It was a big hit and something we'll be adding to our recipe box. I also want to experiment with some of the other suggestions the other chefs have made.

Also, I was thrown off a little bit. You end up making more seasoning mix than you need to use. I guess it's so you can make more chili!

reviews.review_text: Wow! I love finding a good chili recipe and the concept of this one got my attention. The basic recipe is very good as is, however, I did make several changes to suit my tastes in a chili. The seasoning mix is very good and I used as is. To make the meat mixture I added 1lb of chopped sirloin, 1/2 lb groung turkey, a cup of chopped onion, 1/2 cup of green pepper, and 1/4 cup of jalapeno pepper (seeded and chopped) when browning the meat. Then added 3 cloves of fresh chopped garlic to the meat during the last minute of browning to release some flavor. When assembling in the crock pot I substituded spicy V8 for the tomato juice (I like to know I get some kick in any chili), added 2 shots of expresso, and a tablespoon of chopped semi-sweet chocoIate. At the end I added another teaspoon of cumin and cayanne after putting all ingredients in crock pot to add some heat and get more of a smoke flavor going. Pureeing the beans made a big difference in the texture; great idea. When pureeing I drained the beans and added a tablespoon of chili sauce to loosen up the mixture. The basic recipe as is is very good and has great texture. EXCELLENT RECIPE!

reviews.review_text: Great Chili! I have been using this recipe for about a year now, and always get lots of compliments. My husband calls it the best he has ever eaten, though I think he may be a little biased. When I initially made it I mistakenly added tablespoon-sized portions of the seasoning mix to the chili instead of teaspoon size, and I used fresh garlic instead of garlic powder. The mistake turned out great. The chili had a little extra kick to it. I have since continued to use the tablespoon size. You'll still have extra seasoning mix, and I just keep it for next time. I also added a half of an onion, instead of a tablespoon. This chili is great on it's own or can definitely be changed up a bit by adding additional ingredients.

attributes.source_text: My husband calls it the best he has ever eaten

reviews.review_text:
Recipe is fine for fairly experienced cooks, but the directions are weak for newbies.  
-- You really should SAUTE the onions until translucent.  
-- Instruction # 2 is wrong about how much seasoning mix he recipe uses.  (See steps 5 and 6.)  
-- Definitely needs more onion, and every mainly-meat dish needs at least some salt; should sprinkle generously after browning meat and sauteing onion.  
Lastly, if you're cooking the meat in a large and sturdy pot, it's simple to make this entirely on the stove top in far less than the stated time ...  and then you have no crock-pot to wash.
All told:  a fine "slate" to modify based on experience (with delicious results), but not for beginners.

Rating is based on recipe without modifications. With my modifications, it gets 5 stars! Excellent spice blend. Even my mom who dislikes chilli liked this and ate seconds! My modifications: I did 1.5x the recipe but did 1.5lbs of pork, 1.5lbs of beef, a full onion, half of a green and red pepper, and minced garlic with the meat. I added in 1/4 cup of brown sugar, 1/2 tbsp of worchestershire sauce, a hearty sprinkling of smoked paprika, and 1 tsp salt. I also did 1 can (28 ou) crushed tomatoes, 1 can diced, 1 can tomato sauce, 1 can red kidney beans, 1 can white kidney beans. I blended an additional can of red kidney beans. It is now officially the best chilli I have ever had! The whole family agrees :)

reviews.review_text: Incredible recipe! I didn't change anything (except a little extra cayenne and garlic powder,) since this was my first time making chili, and EVERYONE LOVED IT! My Mom is known to make a good chili, and she even admitted it was much better than her's, and that she was annoyed at the fact since I had never attempted to make chili before. Loved it! Will try experimenting with some extra add-ins next time, I think it would be even better with some green pepper and with the spicy- factor kicked up a knotch or two! I'm so glad the recipe for the seasoning mix makes so much more than you need for a single batch. I will definitely keep this seasoning mix handy, and since money is tight this holiday season maybe I'll get some nice little jars, print some labels, and give out a slightly spicier version of this seasoning mix to a few chili-lovers I know!

reviews.review_text: My love affair with Chili began 25 years ago in Stratton, Vermont.  A restaurant in the Village called Mulligans had in my opinion the best chili anywhere.  I've made many recipes that I thought would come close to what I was looking for.  They were just that; close but no cigar.  This recipe is what I've been searching for.  I made it this afternoon and the aroma was amazing.  I made a few substitutions   We're watching fat intake so I used ground turkey instead of beef.  I didn't have any  coriander on hand.  Instead I used my go to spice, Kirkland Organic no salt seasoning.  Also, I only had 1 8 0z can of tomato sauce so I used that & 1 cup V-8.  The result was fantastic.  My whole family raved!

attributes.source_text: My whole family raved!

reviews.review_text: This was a great and tasty chili. I like to try different chilis and I loved that this one was supposed to be made in the crock pot. I cooked it on low for about 12 hours (that's how long I ended up being out of the house) and the meat was tender and the flavor was fantastic. I used a little extra of the spice mix (yay for not reading the recipe very well) and I used Penzy's ground chipotle pepper instead of chili powder and it was quite spicy, but not TOO hot--and quite smoky, too. I threw in some red bell peppers I had on hand as well as most of a large onion (instead of the tablespoon) and I only had 1 lb of ground beef. Obviously this recipe is made to tinker with! Thanks once again, I had it for lunch a day or two later and it only got better with time!

reviews.review_text: I made this and  it was delcious. Most everyone had seconds. The way the ingredients on the recipe were written for the seasoning it appeared dry minced onion belonged in the seasoning. So I put the minced onion in that mix but then it said to cook the minced onion with the meat. I did both. It cooked for 8 hours and was wonderful. As a previous poster did I added one can of refried beans in for one can of the kidney beans blended as I didn't have a working blender and it was great. This is a less chunky chili so if you prefer more chunks add some bell pepper, more beans or chunks of onion or even chunks of beef. If not enjoy it's smooth texture. Served with bowls of cheese, white raw onion, avocado etc for toppings. Thanks Debbie. Enjoy! Chef DLH
