reviews.review_text: The BEST I've found, crispy on the outside and soft in the middle.  I did change the measurements to 10 dozen to use 1 cup of butter--all the other measurements were easy to convert (I used 3 eggs and 3 tsp vanilla), and this amount still fit in my 4.5 qt Kitchenaid.  I made them with my big cookie scoop and baked them for 12-13 minutes until just barely brown around the edges.  I got 32 huge cookies, 8 on each large cookie sheet.  I'm going to stop looking for the perfect chocolate chip cookie- this is it!!

attributes.source_text: crispy on the outside
soft in the middle

reviews.review_text: My daughter beat me to the punch.  I was going to make these today but my daughter made them last night. She said as she munched on her first tray of cooked cookies, "A very easy recipe to make for such a wonderful flavoured and textured Chocolate Chip Cookie recipe."  My daughter hide a litre ice-cream container full of these biscuits so she could take them to work because then she could be assured that she would get to eat some of the cookies.  Just as well too; because when my daughter and I woke up this morning, her brother who studies in the wee hours of the morning, had eaten about half of the remaining chocolate chip cookies.  So I reckon that that speaks for itself on how good these cookies are!!!  Just the best Chocolate Chip Cookies I have tasted as I slink off with a small container of these cookies to hide in my room so my son doesn't eat these too

reviews.review_text: Before today, my favorite choco chip recipe was the deli-style chocolate chip cookies. These have become my new number one! I didn't have shortening, so used half coconut oil and half butter as a substitute; used the recommended amount of butter as listed, as well. I also ran out of eggs, and had to use egg beaters, but guess what? These cookies came out sooo perfect, that I don't think I'll even try the recipe with shortening! Sweet, soft, chewy with just a bit of crisp when your teeth touch the cookie. Purrrrfect!

attributes.source_text: Sweet, soft, chewy with just a bit of crisp
Sweet, soft, chewy with just a bit of crisp

reviews.review_text: A+++ Hands down this is the perfect Chocolate Chip Cookie recipie!! I think that they are better than Mrs. Fields from the Mall, and better than the Tollhouse Chocolate Chip Cookie recipie. I love Chocolate Chip Cookies. I have bought some from our local Bakery (tasted average) and even tried Matt's Chocolate Chip Cookies (to soft and wheaty tasting). I also bought Mrs Fields from Jewel her cookies on the shelf (YUCK, to soft and rubber like ). But these are good enough to be called gourmet! Makes alot of cookies and mine all turned out great! I'm glad I tried this recipie first, as there are many on Recipiezar. I read all the reveiws and thought I will try this recipie, I am glad I did! So again Thank-you so much for posting it! *From A Chocolate Chip Cookie lover*

Had a craving for something sweet at 9 p.m. last night.  Nothing in the house, so decided to make cookies (what else do you do at 9 p.m. at night when you have a sweet tooth??!!).  Made a batch, ate some, refrigerated the rest of the dough and went to bed with the intention of baking the remaining batches this morning.  Let the dough come back to room temperature, and it produced many additional batches of delicious cookies (made mine with peanut butter chips and pecans) -- YUM!  Very nice, not-too-sweet recipe.

attributes.source_text: not-too-sweet recipe

reviews.review_text:
I made these on New Years when my husband's and my friends came over to play videogames and ring in the new year. I also bought $15 worth of snacks. By the end of the night, the snacks were virtually untouched, but the cookies were nearly gone! I gave my hubby a big box to take with him to work. At first they were a bit leery, but hubby walked away to greet a customer, and when he returned, his coworkers were shoveling them in their mouths! They were GONE in less than 10 minutes!

All in all, I must say they were a smashing success!

I have used this recipe for years.  I also got it from a Betty Crocker Cookbook (orange cover).  
My family likes soft cookies so I add 15oz of choc. chips and cook at 325 for 12-15 minutes.  I remove them from the oven while the middle still has a tiny bit of shine and leave them on the pan until cooled.  (the heat of the pan will help them to finish cooking).  Everyone that has had these cookies tell me they are the best they have ever eaten.  Needless to say they never last long.

attributes.source_text: My family likes soft cookies
soft cookies

reviews.review_text:
Sorry, but these cookies are by far not the best I have eaten. The dough mixes up dry and crumbly, and there is very little flavor. I have made many, many different recipes for chocolate chip cookies, these are not great. I only made half a batch, and am glad I did. 
 I have come across recipes like this before where the dough was dry and crumbly. You could add a few drops of milk to the batter. Any cookie made with shortening will cut down on the taste. It will give a nice crispness though which is one thing I wanted with this batch. Anyhow, thankyou for posting.

This are AMAZING! I just finished baking them and they turned out perfect!  I actually made the dough yesterday and put if in the refrigerator till today and then baked them. I rolled them into balls and then pressed down on them slightly. I think this helped them not to flatten out too much and stay moist on the inside. I baked them at 375 for 10 minutes on stoneware.  They are a slightly crisp on the edges and perfectly chewy in the center. I will definitely bake these again. Thanks!

perfectly chewy in the center

reviews.review_text: These are sure to become a favourite in our house too! I made these cookies with my kids and even though the recipe makes a huge batch, we did our fair share of snacking on these already! I used mini chocolate chips for the chocolate chips and followed everything else as written. The first few cookie sheets I baked for about eight minutes and they were perfect for me, I kind of lost track of the last sheet and they were still good but crisp, so bake a few minutes longer if a crispy cookie is desired :)

attributes.source_text: if a crispy cookie is desired

reviews.review_text: Truly the best CCC recipe I've ever tried. Made these with my daughters (by hand, no electric mixer) and they turned out great. Made the recipe as stated, with the exception of butter flavored Crisco in place of plain shortening. Made about 6 1/2 dozen. I switched the cookie sheets from top to bottom halfway through baking (a trick I learned some time ago,) and the cookies look beautiful and are the perfect texture and taste. This is what I will use for CCC's from now on!

My mom had a Betty Crocker recipe box -- and this was the recipe that I tried as a teenager and have used for over 20 years.  It's awesome.  Over the years I've done a little tinkering (adding more chocolate chips, adding slightly more flour, changing the butter / shortening ratio, using parchment paper, using the insulated baking sheets) but it's a great recipe.  People ALWAYS ask me to bring these in.  The one main thing is to not overbake if you like a chewy texture.

attributes.source_text: if you like a chewy texture

reviews.review_text: I was visiting a friend whose husband was raving about the soft, delicious chocolate chip cookies someone had made. We were told the secret to the perfect cookie was to use a combination of butter and shortening. So I searched for a recipe and came across this. These were great right out of the oven, warm, soft and chewy. But they lost that as they cooled and became more of a crispy cookie. Everyone has their favorite characteristics they look for in cookies so this maybe perfect for some, just not for me.

attributes.source_text: warm, soft and chewy
warm, soft and chewy

items.description: This is a quick and easy recipe that never fails to please even my picky DDs. Since chicken thighs are usually inexpensive it makes a economical meal. I like to serve these with some type of rice side dish and a green salad.
instructions: Spray large frying pan, preheat.
Rinse and pat dry thighs.
Season with salt and pepper.
Brown well on all sides.
Cover, reduce heat to medium and cook for approximately 25 minutes,or'til thighs are done depending on size.
Add shallots,cook for 2-3 minutes,until they soften.
Stir in balsamic vinegar, cook for about 1 more minute,turn chicken to coat thoroughly.
Spoon sauce over thighs to serve.

reviews.review_text:
The sauce was YUMMY- but I was not overly impressed with the chicken...so it gets 4 stars, not 5. 
I made this just as written (the photo must have more then 1/4 cup shallots in it! or they used onions). I served it with instant couscous (Near East brand- roast garlic and olive oil flavor) and I could have eaten bowls and bowls of the couscous with the sauce on it!!! But the chicken was kind of bland compared to it. Next time I think I will add the shallots and balsamic and let it cook into the chicken a little longer, so that it has the same flavor as the sauce. 
This needs a little tweek- but for as quick as it is to throw together, you can't beat it!! I want to try it with onions too, just to see if the shallots really make a difference- I will let you know.

This was pretty bad.  I agree with the previous reviews about the balsamic vinegar being overpowering and the chicken having a bland taste.  I had to make some major modifications.  After following the recipe, I added these ingredients and proceeded to cook it longer (about half hour more, totaling 1 hour):
-Mrs. Dash original seasoning
-1 can 14.5 oz Italian diced tomatoes
-1 medium eggplant, cut in quarters
-1/4 cup water
I added Mrs. Dash on both sides of each chicken thigh, then added half the canned tomatoes on top of the chicken and some water and let that cook for 15 min under med. high heat.  Then I added the eggplant and added the rest of the canned tomatoes on top and cooked for another 10-15 minutes.  If you want, you can let it simmer for a little longer after this is all done.  The more it sits in these ingredients, the more flavorful.  This was a great modification, gave it more of a Mediterranean taste.  I guarantee you'll like it!

attributes.source_text: gave it more of a Mediterranean taste

reviews.review_text: Oh, yes, yes, YES!  Whenever I see a recipe such as this with balsamic vinegar, I'm all ears.  I love how it cooks up into this amazingly rich glaze.  I used skinless and boneless chicken thighs (it's what I had).  Obviously they cooked up in less time than the 25 minutes.  Next time, I will try the bone-in skinless thighs.  But these were so delicious.  My husband won't touch "dark" meat -- so I fixed him something else -- and had the thighs all to myself.  If you are a fan of balsamic vinegar (used similar to the same way it's used in this recipe) check out my Salmon with Balsamic (#144318) and my Rosemary Chicken (#176427).  Thank you, Mickie for this outstanding recipe.

attributes.source_text: amazingly rich glaze

reviews.review_text: This is really good. I used 1/4 cup chopped red onion and 1 tsp minced garlic cloves since I didn't have any shallots. The rest was the same except I didn't take the skin off the thighs because I was in a hurry, but I won't do that again - way too much grease. I went ahead and cooked the chicken in the sauce much longer in the end to let it reduce and it really adhered to the chicken very well. I made it for lunch today and saved a couple pieces for my husband. He had them when he got home from work and is ready for me to make more. :-) This is a solid 4.75 stars from us! Thanks so much for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: I made it for lunch today
saved a couple pieces for my husband

reviews.review_text: This was not only delicious, but came up with a side that compliments this dish really well. I will share. Cook some orzo. In a second fry pan use about 5 tbs of ollive oil and saute a package of sliced mushrooms. When cooked ad 1/4 cup of chopped sun dried tomatoes, 1/2 cup of basil, and 1/4 cup of pine nuts. Ad 1/4 stick of butter. Rinse and drain orzo and ad to mushroom mix. I put my balsamic chicken on top and the glaze over it. The flavor mixed very well together with the orzo and my family loved it! Will make this again soon! I made the chicken exactly as per instructions.

attributes.source_text: my family loved it

reviews.review_text: I was in the mood for an early dinner tonight. I had all the ingredients on hand for this so decided to give it a shot....AWESOME!!!  The only change I made was to add 2 Tbsp. butter after taking the chicken out of the pan.  I cooked it down to the point that it was almost to a glaze-like consistency. YUMMY!  Served with thinly sliced zuchinni that I put into the "glaze" for about 1 minute.  This was excellent served with the chicken.  Next time I am going to try adding cabbage(I ate all the zuchinni right off the bat and grabbed a jar of kimchi from the refridge).  Delicious and VERY easy to make dinner.  This could easily be made a crockpot dish, too.

attributes.source_text: I was in the mood for an early dinner tonight
VERY easy to make dinner

reviews.review_text: Thank you so much for this fantastically tasty AND easy recipe! I used the 2lbs of b/less s/lessential chicken thighs. I didn't measure my balsamic vinegar but used a little more than 1/2c. & added 2 teaspoons of sugar for balance. YOU MUST USE SHALLOTS, not onions... two totally different results! I added my vinegar early also. It can cook down quickly so be careful. However this seems to make the chicken more flavorful. I added about two cups of steamed broccoli & served over rice. This was sooo yummy! Next time will be easier because I didn't know shallots dice exactly like garlic & I you tubed it, lol.

I was skeptical going into this recipe. So simple and easy to make. And I was very concerned about the acidity of the balsamic as well. I took one little precaution and added two tsp of brown sugar to the balsamic before adding it to the chicken. I also mixed a bit of garlic powder in with the salt and pepper as recommended by a few reviewers. Other than that I followed the recipe to a tee and was SO impressed. Definitely a keeper. I'd even recommend adding a bit more balsamic and simmering it down a little longer, turning the chicken thighs a few times in it to ensure they're coated well. And in my opinion - do NOT substitute onions for shallots. I'm no food snob, but shallots are far more delicate and really take this dish to the next level. Thanks Mickie49!

Well you certainly don't need another review but I bet you love to see them so here goes! I was very skeptical after reading the tiny list of ingredients but I love balsamic vinegar so I thought I would give it a try. Never one to follow a recipe, I did stay true to this one with the exception of adding a cup of sliced fresh mushrooms 1 minute before it was done. I think they sucked up the sauce as I had none left but that is ok cause I really think they added to the dish. Both hubby & I really liked this recipe & it will be going into my rotation. Thanks so much mickie!

attributes.source_text: Both hubby & I really liked this recipe

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe just now (with some modifications, thus the lower star rating) and thought it tasted good. I made this with 4 chicken breast Then I made the sauce with 1/10 soy sauce and then added enough balsamic vinegar to reach 1/4 cup, a few tbsp of sugar, minced garlic and sliced scallions. Cooked the chicken as directed, drained oil and then placed chicken back into the pan, added the sauce and cooked for about 2 mins and then served over rice, along side braised carrots.

As I learned when I lived in France, you do not need lots of ingredients to make an excellent dish. This recipe proves that point. I loved it and so did my 11 year-old son! I did not alter it, but I did simmer the chicken a long time in the balsamic so that it reduced, and I made sure to turn the chicken so that it was coated. I don't get the folks saying it's "bland" or vinegary, but I'd definitely suggest letting the vinegar reduce longer because the taste is wonderful. We mixed in steamed broccoli at the end and it made this a great, healthy marathon-training meal for Mom! Total winner.

attributes.source_text: so did my 11 year-old son

reviews.review_text: These were fantastic.  I was pretty shocked, to be honest!  While I was cooking this up, all I kept thinking was "balsamic and shallots...that's it?  Really?"  But I was very pleasantly surprised with the very first bite.  The balsamic adds so much flavor but isn't overpowering at all, and the shallots add just the perfect amount of texture and flavor.  It's also quite possibly the easiest dish to make on the planet.  This is one that I wish I could give 10 stars!  I'm now going to check out your other recipes to see what other goodies you've got hiding, mickie.  THANKS!

reviews.review_text: I cooked the chicken (4 thighs and 4 legs), removed it to a plate and covered it, then drained off most of the drippings. Added sliced mushrooms and a couple of large shallots, sliced thin. Sauteed for a bit, then added back the chicken pieces and 1/2 cup of balsamic vinegar. Cooked gently, turning the chicken over and over until the sauce reduced and coated the chicken nicely. Every one loved it, even the kids. Served with some orzo with spinach and parmesan added.

items.label: Tilapia Al Ajillo (Garlic Tilapia)
items.name: Tilapia Al Ajillo (Garlic Tilapia)
keywords: c("Spanish", "European", "Very Low Carbs", "High Protein", "High In...", "< 30 Mins", "Stove Top", "Easy")
items.description: You can do this with any white fish, sea bass is great this way. Fish is often served this way in the Canary Islands, though usually it is the whole fish instead of fillets. YUM!
instructions: Season tilapia fillets with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Put fillets in first, and when they start to turn color a bit (after 1-2 minutes) add garlic slices.
Continue cooking about 4 minutes or so, then flip fillets.
Fry until cooked through, and fish flakes easily with a fork-- this will depend entirely on the thickness of your fillets, so you will need to watch them carefully.
The garlic should turn a dark golden brown, but not be burned, if you notice that the garlic is starting to burn, spoon it over the fish, so it is no longer in contact with the pan.
Serve with freshly squeezed lemon juice and garnish with chopped parsley.

reviews.review_text: Stupendous! This will be in our rotation from now on! Easy and fast with TONS of great flavor. I doubled the garlic- we LOVE garlic. I am famous for burning it so I let it cook in the evoo on the back burner on med-low while I prepared the sides- the garlic released wonderful flavor into the oil. I removed the garlic when ready, cranked up the heat and added the seasoned fish. I used sea salt and McCormick Grinders Peppercorn Medley which has a little whole allspice and whole coriander along with three kinds of peppercorns all for less than $2! Ok commercial over.. Cooking the garlic this way let me concentrate on browning the fish and not worry about burning the garlic. When all the fillets were done I returned the garlic to the pan for a few minutes to lightly brown them then poured all over the fillets. Topped with some fresh chopped parsley and drizzled with lemon juice. Thank you Canary girl for a fantastically fast and easy recipe that is superb! My chef's hat is off to you!

attributes.source_text: I doubled the garlic- we LOVE garlic

reviews.review_text:
I made a few slight changes, but this is possibly one of the simplest, yet most delicious fish recipes I've ever made!! Both my boyfriend and I LOVED it!

This is my second time making it, and this time I chopped up maybe a bit less than 1/4 of an onion (I was only making it for 2, though), and about 1/3 of a green bell pepper and sauteed them first. While those were cooking up a bit, I seasoned the fish (I used Orange Roughy) with pepper, garlic powder, a tiny bit of salt, and a bit of dried parsely. After I added the fish to the pan I added maybe 1/4 tsp. of chopped garlic to the TOP of each fish. I covered and then continued cooking. I didn't have any lemon juice, so I didn't use any...although I'm curious how it tastes with it on.

The fish comes out with so much flavor, I love it! I've never thought of adding the chopped garlic to the top of something before, I'm so used to just adding it to the pan, but it really is so delicious!

attributes.source_text: Both my boyfriend and I LOVED it

reviews.review_text: Outstanding, Canary Girl, A very simple, very clean tasting, and very quick dish too.  We had the bag of frozen tilapia fillets which are individually wrapped, one pound bag had six small fillets.  I prepared one each and after tasting the fish, my boyfriend wanted more!  So, I got the rest out and made them.  I always soak fish in milk prior to cooking to remove the fishy taste.  Tilapia doesn't typically taste fishy, but just in case - after being frozen and all.  I didn't have parsley so I chopped some fresh chives.  I tend to agree with Seattle Jim, the calories shown are probably higher than actual.  My one pound package indicates the tilapia to be 4 servings @ 100 calories per serving, then there's only olive oil and not that much and besides that, most of it remains in the pan...Very, very good, thank you!

attributes.source_text: very clean tasting
my boyfriend wanted more

reviews.review_text: This is so easy and tasty.  Reminds me of when my husband and I honeymooned in the Canary Islands (Lanzarote island, in particular.)  I tweaked in a couple of places: 1) I don't like fried garlic, so I added the garlic slices at the very end so they cooked and softened, but did not brown.  And 2) I did not have lemon so I squirted the fish with lime juice, instead, and left out the parsley.  My fillets were pretty thick, so I ended up frying them for about five minutes on each side, and turned off the stove when the edges started to turn a golden brown.  Thanks for posting!

We eat tiapia frequently, and usually buy a flat of fillets, much smaller than the pre-packaged frozen "loins" we picked up this time.  This was outstanding for flavor and fresh tasting - more so than the little skinny pieces.  The garlic made a BIG difference. and simmerered just a few minutes until browning.  We didn't even have the parsley, but was SUCH a tasty, healthy dinner with Haricot Vert with Shallots and Fingerling Potatoes with EVOO, garlic and lemon with grated parmesan, roasted in the oven.
Thanks, canarygirl, for a quick saturday night home dinner !
Janey

attributes.source_text: fresh tasting
The garlic made a BIG difference
a tasty, healthy dinner
a quick saturday night home dinner

reviews.review_text:
This was quite simple and tasty...and much quicker than our oven-method.  We will definitely be incorporating this method into our repetoir!

Took longer than recipe stated because we used whole fish (my husband be-headed them!).  Also, we didn't use the lemon juice because we enjoy the fish taste.

The only thing was that, being that it is called "tilapia al ajillo," I definitely expected it to taste more garlic-y...maybe if it were a thin filet.  And maybe if we ate the skin...we just don't like to eat the skin.

This was extremely easy and it tasted wonderful. Just the perfect amount of garlic to make it nice and garlicky. I would suggest using a non-stick pan because Talapia is so fragile. I didn't use non-stick and mine stuck a little to the pan even though I have a nice heavy bottom one. It didn't matter though because it was awesome! I have yet to be disappointed by one of your recipes! 
Oh yeah... I served this with garlic mashed potatoes, roasted yellow and green squash and garlic bread. It was a major garlic night for us!

attributes.source_text: the perfect amount of garlic to make it nice and garlicky

reviews.review_text: Phew!  Talk about a speedy dinner!  This was on my bf's plate in 10 mins.  I didn't have fresh garlic so used jarred minced.  I used the full amt of garlic and olive oil, but only 2 fillets.  I didn't have fresh lemons so used a bit of lemon juice.  I never have fresh herbs for some resson, so I used a bit of dried parsley.  Bf said it was very good.  I agree, thank you for a really quick recipe and another nice way to cook tilapia, canarygirl! :)

attributes.source_text: Bf said it was very good

reviews.review_text: We couldn't believe how good this was with such simple ingredients and cooking instructions!  There were no leftovers which is practically unheard of at our house since we like leftovers for lunches and usually double recipes.  This one never made it to the next day.  I was worried about burning the garlic but it was easy to place the garlic pieces on the fish to prevent that from happening.  Mild yet flavorful, the fish took on a slight caramelized taste from the garlic/olive oil combo. Thank you for sharing!

attributes.source_text: Mild yet flavorful
the fish took on a slight caramelized taste

reviews.review_text:
I was underwhelmed by this recipe. It was pretty bland and didn't have enough going on for my taste. I feel like it's not a recipe, just a cooking method- saute fish in olive oil, voila! For me, tilapia tastes like dirt, and you have to add a little bit of something-something to cover that up. I liked the idea of slicing the garlic, because it was easier to move around in the pan than if it were crushed/minced. 
I ate this with roasted broccoli and sriracha mayo, which definitely helped to liven it up a bit.

What a great recipe! The only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 is because I halved the recipe, and it was a little bland. I think this is because I only used 2 garlic cloves, so the oil wasn't particularly garlicky. The plus side was that my toddler ate it up (because it was bland), but next time I'll try using 3-4 cloves in the halved recipe. If I have better results, I'll update my review to 5 stars. Thanks for posting!! :-)

attributes.source_text: my toddler ate it up

reviews.review_text: There is no better recipe for tilapia out there! I had run out of fresh garlic so I sprinkled garlic powder on the tilapia and continued cooking as stated (I can only imagine how much better it will be now that I have fresh garlic again!!!). DH had one bite and immediately said, "five star" ... a compliment indeed since he mostly gives 3 or 4 stars! Thanks for posting Canary Girl!

attributes.source_text: DH had one bite and immediately said, "five star"

reviews.review_text: This recipe is OUTSTANDING!!!!!  Was looking for something quick and so glad I found this.  Used my cast iron skillet. I placed 2 tablespoons of butter with a little bit of olive oil in the pan.  Lightly dusted the fish with flour per Pebbles suggestion.  Sprinkled a little of Emeril's Original Essence Seasoning to add some "BAM" for flavoring.  Really liked the garlic being sliced.  The fish, flounder, came out perfect.  The garlic was a real bonus in this recipe.  Will be making this once a week for sure.

attributes.source_text: Really liked the garlic being sliced
The garlic was a real bonus in this recipe

reviews.review_text:
Great recipe!  Quick, easy and delicious. If you love garlic, this is one is for you.

I was worried about having enough pan space and didn't want to worry about the garlic burning so I decide to forgo the skillet for the oven. 

I coated the bottom of the baking dish in olive oil, flipped the fish once it was browned on one side and then added the garlic.  Fantastic!

attributes.source_text: If you love garlic

reviews.review_text: Oh my goodness, Canarygirl, this is great!!!  My husband, who has high triglycerides and should eat more fish, said that he could definitely eat more fish if it was cooked like this.  It was very easy to cook and had wonderful garlic flavor.  I used plenty of salt and pepper and lots of lemon and could not be happier with this recipe.  This will be added to our rotation.  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: My husband, who has high triglycerides and should eat more fish, said that he could definitely eat more fish if it was cooked like this
had wonderful garlic flavor

reviews.review_text:
Excellent.  First time making tilapia and liked your recipe ingrediants.  I love garlic so served it with a side of garlic smashed potatoes and beans.  Delicious and in my cooknook dor the next meal.
i am going to try dusting with italian bread crumbs next time to see if the flavor changes or enhances.  I also plan to use this recipe for perch as my Dh likes to fish and we have some in the freezer.  Great Lent recipe for my Greek family.

attributes.source_text: Great Lent recipe for my Greek family
Great Lent recipe for my Greek family

reviews.review_text:
The flavor of this was really yummy, nice and lite.  Mine cooked quicker than stated.   I usually bake it in the oven, and did find that even with all of the olive oil, it still wanted to stick to the pan.  Didn't look very pretty afterward, but it tasted great.  5 and 2 year old DDs ate all of it.  The 2 year old "liked that chicken".  Love it when I can get the kids to eat fish.

Thanks for posting!

items.label: Faux Febreeze
items.name: Faux Febreeze
items.description: A wonderful dirt cheap alternative to buying a $5 bottle of Febreze. This version is about 5 cents to make and the scent is much nicer too. I use it all the time.
instructions: Put Downy and water in bottle and spray on furniture, carpeting, pillows, shower curtains -- etc --  To do a fabric test, spray small amount in an area where it cannot be seen.
I never sprayed this on anything white, but I spray it all over my house, once a week.

reviews.review_text:
Hi I wanted to pop over and say that I have been using this for about two years now.  I adjust the strength a little (4 oz) to use this as a de-wrinkler.  I have used it for de-wrinkling clothes that I forget to take out of the dryer long long before they started marketing what you see in the stores now for the same purpose.  I hardly use it for febreeze but it's great in the car for that purpose.  My latest discoveries are this:  It's a great softener for pesky hard to remove wallpaper.  Use this stuff, a bit stronger than 4 oz BEFORE you go buy any expensive chemical..use the tiger blade thing that perforates the paper up, then mix this recipe with boiling water and spray on, then scrape with a stiff putty knife or other scraper.  Works well on really old wallpaper!  But, there's another great use...I used this to clean old grease film off of my upper cabinets and oven hood and vent screen.  I just used a 4 oz strength, sprayed it on and used a double sided sponge scrubber to wipe it off. Also works well with magic eraser for soap scum in the bathroom.  Also, softens stuck on burnt food or stove liners if you spray it on thickly and let sit overnight.  It wont get burnt food right off, but it does soften it and makes it easier to remove! This stuff has pretty much replaced a lot of my old harsh chemicals and it smells so much nicer too!  As an added bonus, my hands are softer after using this stuff.  So, thank you so much...it's saved me a bundle. By the way, it has to be ultra downy.  Snuggle or regular concentrates really don't do as well, for some reason.

P.S. I send this to the military overseas and they really appreciate it because they are in smelly situations often. I have been able to send it travels well through the USPS, at least to the APO address I've been sending to.

I am a freshness freak.  As soon as it is halfway decent outside we pop the windows open and air out the house in the spring and fall, but the rest of the year is tough- and with 3 young boys and 2 dogs keeping the house smelling fresh is not easy.  My solution to the musty-closed up smell in the winter is usually to always have something cooking or a candle burning, but the summers are tough, and Febreeze is not cheap.  So I am THRILLED to have come across this 'recipe'!  I made up a batch in an old Febreeze bottle two days ago, am now on my second batch, and have spent only a few pennies to make the house so fresh and clean!  I LOVE this stuff- DH is laughing at me since I just finished spraying down the house again.  The best part is that all I have to do is pick up all the clutter, chase a few sticky finger prints and maybe a light vacuum, and then spritz the faux febreeze around- and the house seems cleaner without having to do a deep clean each day.  Thanks so much for posting!!!

First off, I love Febreeze, but sure don't like the price. This is just as good and so much cheaper. I'm on my second bottle. I can't wait to try different scents of fabric softner. Thanks for an awesome recipe. Somebody said not to spray on microfiber furniture. Does anybody know why not? I did it before I read that, but can't see that it hurt the furniture any. Thanks.  Just wanted to add - I vacuumed one cushion on my microfiber couch and it still left dog hair, so I sprayed another cushion with Faux Febreeze, let it dry a bit and vacuumed.  Not a single dog hair remained and didn't hurt the couch at all.  This is one awesome recipe.

Amazing!  I used Method brand fabric softener (water lily and aloe vera scent), making it practically all-natural and free of animal products/animal testing.  It smelled way better than Febreeze.  I was compelled to spray it on every fabric surface in my house, so I will definitely make this again.  There is an almost-identical recipe (Recipe #84452) for a wrinkle remover.  I found that it worked really well for both purposes, which makes me love it even more!  Thanks for posting this.

What a smart idea,.And the smell is not over whelming.The place smells fresh and clean.Wonder if there is such an idea for smokers.Is there any other ingredient,you could add,or another receipe you could mix up to help with the smell of smoke in all your furniture and curtains etc.If ya know of something,please post it.Im sure i am not the only one who would be ineterested in killing that smell,as fabreeze i found just hid it for a bit. Thank you for such a money saveing way to accomplish a clean smell with out paying the big bucks!

I have been doing this for so long now, I could never live without it! My house always smells like it just came out of the dryer. In the winter it really helps get rid of static shock around the house too. I spray it on all the beds after I make them each day. Sooooo affordable!! Most of all, and anyone who has teenage boys knows this, it actually covers up that "boy smell" in my son's bedroom. And NOTHING, no matter how clean his room is, works better! Thanks for sharing this with everyone, Bethany!

This stuff is awesome! I will never buy Febreeze again. When I went to the store to get the fabric softener, I saw they had Febreeze on sale...for $5 a bottle! :-O I used 4oz. of downy april fresh(I didn't like any of the other scents of fabric softener) with the 25 oz. of water and sprayed it around the house. Several hours later the scent is still detectable and the house smells wonderful. Thank you so much from a mom of a very stinky football player!! This is a keeper!

Do you know how much imported Febreeze costs in Israel?  If you can get it at all?  Wine is cheaper!  I'm so pleased to have found this recipe.  I'm overly-paranoid because we have a dog in the house, and I don't want my house to have that pet-smell.  I used some locally-made laundry softener in orchid scent and spritzed the whole house.  I'm going to invite all my friends over just to come and smell my house!  Thanks Bethany!

This definitely doesn't need another review!! *LOL* But I had to tell you , not only does it work great for what it's actually FOR , but found another use for it , quite by accident! 
I keep it under my kitchen sink. Well, tonight I was doing dishes and afterwards the suds wouldn't go down ... I grabbed this and sprayed 3 or 4 times and BOOM , suds were gone and the sink smelled maaaaaaahvelous ;)  
Great recipe! Thanks!!

Firstly I have to say I am not a big febreeze fan, but considering that this was a quick and easy recipe to make a homemade version, I said why not. I bought some cheeper good smelling softner,but a word to the wise, dont skimp, I think because it wasnt downy it came out weaker smelling, however I used it in my cars and it's a great air freshner for my car. Next time I would definately buy downy, but I will be making it for a car freshner. Thanks for the recipe!

Bethany,,,I just tried this today and wondered why I hadn't done it before!  I did use a product from Sam's that's $10 a gallon you dilute.  My friend uses it in her motel.  It's very good, but I like this much better and it's cheaper too!  I can't add anything that's not been already said,,,just another big THANKYOU!  I did use downey clean breeze as it's my favorite.  dh even likes it better.  Ok, off to spray some more:)        kitty

attributes.source_text: dh even likes it better

reviews.review_text: Well, I guess I have to go against the crowd on this one.  I don't normally use any products like Febreze, but decided to try this.  I sprayed some around the bedroom.  I liked the scent....not too overpowering, not too subtle...So far, so good.  Then DH came in and says "What's that smell?"  I ask, "Do you like it?"....and he says "No, it is awful!"  I just laughed and decided to give my 'febreze' to my mom.  She has cats and probably will like it.

items.label: Perfectly Juice Prime Rib
items.name: Perfectly Juice Prime Rib
items.description: This is my "tradmark" Christmas Eve Dinner. DH won't even order prime rib in a restaurant anymore, because he prefers mine. Its a super easy recipe, great for dinner parties, but DO NOT alter cooking times or directions.  And DO NOT carve until just before serving.  Here NEEDS a clarification!!! The salt is only intended to produce a shell to keep the moisture in. It's not intended to be consumed unless of course you like extremely salty foods. AFTER the roast has rested for 15 mins. Lightly scrape the salt away but not so much that you remove all the seasonings
instructions: Combine seasonings, and rub into roast.
Let sit while oven preheats to 375.
Place roast in broiling pan, fat side up or bone side up.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Turn oven off, DO NOT OPEN OVEN.
One hour before serving, turn oven back on 45 minutes.
Take rib out, LET STAND FOR 15 MINUTES.
This is VERY  important, it allows the juices to distribute.
Do not carve \
, either. Scrape off the salt \
The meat directly underneath that will be very salty, but that's usually the fatty part that no one eats, anyways.  The rest of it will be fine, I PROMISE!
Serve with au jus and horseradish sauce.

reviews.review_text:
I personally loved this recipe. I used a 5-lb rib roast and let it come to room temp. Then to adjust the seasonings I used:   
1/4  cup kosher salt  
1/8  cup fresh rosemary allowed to nearly dry then put in a coffee bean grinder until chopped but not powdered  
1/8  cup wasabi powder -just as good as horseradish powder and I found it in the ethnic aisle of my local supermarket.  
1/8  cup garlic powder  
1/16  cup cracked black pepper  

I then rubbed the roast with horseradish and then applied the seasonings. 
I then put roast in a PRE-heated oven for 45min. Shut off after that and left alone for 3 hours. Then turned back on to 375 for an hour. That gives it 15min or so to come to temperature. Reminder NO PEEKING!!! EVER!!!
Produced wonderful results!!! A+++
OK!! Here NEEDS a clarification!!! The salt is only intended to produce a shell to keep the moisture in. It's not intended to be consumed unless of course you like extremely salty foods. AFTER the roast has rested for 15 mins. Lightly scrape the salt away but not so much that you remove all the seasonings. If you've thrown away $50 of prime rib you've just tossed 10% of salty meat and 90% of perfectly fine meat. 
I made this for Christmas Day and we will be making this often in the future!!!
I salute my wine glass to you Elissa!!

P.S. Don't tell anyone how easy this is! They'll never believe you!!

attributes.source_text: I made this for Christmas Day

reviews.review_text: SURPRISE another 5 star rating.  I have used this cooking method several times.  It is the most fool proof way I have ever cooked a rib roast.  I recently had an occasion to try it on a whole (14  lb) top sirloin.  Gave it  about 10 minutes extra on the first cooking, it sat for about 5 hours before the second cooking.  Gave it about 45 minutes on the second cooking, but I was using a meet thermometer, and took it to 140 degrees.  Absolutely perfect.  This is be best cooking method since it doesn't require you to figure out when to start the roast.  I have put the roast on in the mid to late morning, gone out for the day, come home about 5 and done the second cooking at it has always turned out perfect.  BUT I just can't trust it after all these times and I still use a meet thermometer just to make sure.  In any event this is the only way I have cooked rib roasts for over a year and now it is the only way I will cook any big hunk of meat regardless of cut from here on.  Thanks for sharing.

This is only getting 2 stars because the rub is *amazing*, otherwise it would just be 1. Unfortunately, contrary to the description, size DOES matter. Maybe not for smaller roasts, but definitely for larger ones. I should have gone with my gut and used the meat thermometer, but the overwhelming positive reviews blinded me to sense. I used this recipe for a 12 pound bone-in roast (we did a big family dinner) and it was RAW. Luckily, my husband is a great improviser - we cut it into individual servings and he cooked them up quickly in our cast iron skillet - but I was stressed to the max. Because I followed the instructions, we didn't discover that the meat was undercooked until everyone was sitting to eat, so it was very embarrassing. And aggravating - we were HUNGRY! Our oven is less than 2 years old, I have TWO thermometers in it to check temperature (because I'm OCD and don't trust the oven or just one thermometer), and this was the result. I'm sure this recipe has worked for lots of people, and (again) the rub is phenomenal, but I won't be using this methodology again. And I'll never again leave my meat thermometer in the drawer when I'm making something for company!

attributes.source_text: we did a big family dinner

reviews.review_text: Wholly Mackerel, this is by far the best Prime Rib Recipe I have ever come across! I roasted a 12lb (6 rib) roast today. I brought the meat to room temperature and I doubled the rub and used finely grated fresh horseradish, as there was no powdered horseradish at the store. I did use a little olive oil on the sides of the meat so the rub would stick to the sides, which worked great. I Put the roast in the oven for 45 mins at 1pm. Turned it off at 1:45 and Let it sit in there until 4, then I turned the oven back on. I figured I needed to add a few minutes, because the prime rib was so big and my oven is the kind that has a fan to cool it down. When I took the temp at 5pm, I was a little nervous because the temp read 125. I wanted medium rare meat, I thought I might have taken it out a bit too late. But we cut it 30 minutes later and it was a perfect medium rare, and ohh was the meat ever so tender! I just rubbed the salt crust off with my hands, so I didn't get everything, and it was definitely not too salty. I wish I had taken a picture to share, it was a beauty. All of my guests liked it, even my sister who likes medium well meat (she got the end piece) Thank you for a great recipe!!!

attributes.source_text: it was definitely not too salty
ohh was the meat ever so tender
All of my guests liked it
even my sister who likes medium well meat (she got the end piece)

reviews.review_text: Overall a great recipe. Even for a rookie. I tried it twice so far, exactly as suggested  with both an 8.5 and an 11.5 pound bone in (bones lifted) roast. The flavor was outstanding. Both times I had a 2-3 hour rest in between. I like rare meat but the first 8.5 pounder was too rare so I had the oven recalibrated. The 2nd 11.5 pounder was also too rare. In the future I will use this recipe as a guide but count on the meat thermometer combined with an oven thermometer to fine tune it. I will likely make it again for Christmas. Some points of interest: Wasabi powder did work for the horseradish powder but don't accidently get the one with ginger in it. The spices could easily be cut (equally) by 20-40% depending on the size of the roast. I poured about 3/4 cup of Burgandy over the roast, as it rested, and poured that, with the blood after carving, into the au jus. The flavor of this recipe was outstanding. As I am typing this my neighbor just called to thank me for the best meal she can remember. Also, my dog just keeps staring at me waiting for another rib. Thanks for sharing this.

attributes.source_text: my neighbor just called to thank me for the best meal she can remember

reviews.review_text: I thought this recipe worked very well. I concur with the suggestion that a meat thermometer is essential to check the timing. I have only made this dish once but it seems the roast should be 120-125 degrees upon exiting the oven to be at 135 degrees after resting. Even though this recipe suggests it is appropriate for any size roast, in my experience, the ingredients in the rub were perhaps twice what is needed for a 4lb roast. This is a great recipe for celebrations as it is so hands off it allows you to do a lot before guests arrive, spend time entertaining, and still create an enviable feast with minimal effort at the targeted time. I know we are talking about prime rib here, but I wonder if there are healthier rubs or spicing combinations that would employ this novel roasting technique for similar stellar results with lower levels of sodium. Thanks for providing this excellent recipe.

attributes.source_text: This is a great recipe for celebrations

reviews.review_text: I've made prime rib twice in my life. Both times I used this recipe, both times I made a 4 to 5 pound roast and both times my family fell all over themselves exclaiming how wonderful it was and that I should make it far more often. The first time I made it, I followed the recipe exactly and found that I had way too much seasoning left over. This last time, I cut the seasonings by half or more (didn't really keep track because I measured out by teaspoonfuls rather than cups but I used the same ratios) and I put it in an empty seasoning bottle so I wouldn't contaminate any leftover with my hands. I ended up using all of the smaller amount that I made so that worked out great! I agree with some reviews that the outside of the roast is pretty salty, but the rest of it is juicy and tender and wonderful. And the aroma it leaves in your house is fantastic! Even better is it's so surprisingly easy to make! My 6 year old, who is unbelievably picky, wanted two servings! We only gave her the lean part so there was no seasoning on hers, but she gobbled it up and asked for more! My 18 year old said he wished I would make it every day! (ha, ha!) I may try a little less salt next time to see how that works. I give this one 4 1/2 stars easy! :-)

reviews.review_text: I picked this cooking method for this year's Christmas Prime rib after studying, z-mailing many and finally settled on this recipe because we were planning to be gone for several hours close to dinner and I did not want anything to happen to my expensive piece of meat. I really needed to dinner to time out right and not have us sitting around for hours waiting for the meat to be done.  Elissa assured me that I would not mess up my meat even though I was cooking a 14lb boneless piece of meat! I was still skeptical but went for it. I poked garlic cloves into the meat all over and then rubbed with my own rub the night before.  That morning I set the meat out at around 9am (we ate dinner at 6:30pm) and let it sit at room temp. for 1 hour.  Then I followed the directions as listed.  I used a meat thermomter to keep track of the internal temperature. About an hour and half before dinner I turned the oven back on and right at about the 45 minutes mark my meat was at 140 (Rare) - I pulled it out and let it rest for 30 minutes and the meat climbed to 145 (Med rare.)  Perfection!  We always make a side pan of aujus to dip the meat quickly in for those who like med. rare - for those who might want it more done than an end cut we'll leave it in the aujus until it's to their liking.  I will cook all primes this way from now on.  It really is versitile and can let you walk away and not think about dinner until you are ready. I do recommend the use of a meat thermometer so you know exactly where you are at temp. wise for doneness. Thanks for all your personal help and advice on this Elissa. I'm spreading the word on this one.

attributes.source_text: this year's Christmas Prime rib
we ate dinner at 6:30pm

reviews.review_text:
First of all, let me say, size ALWAYS matters.  Now, that I've gotten my mind out of the gutter, I want to tell you that I am not a big prime rib fan.  In fact, I stopped eating it about 5 years ago because I really don't care for it but this was delicious. I actually ate an entire piece. It was so flavorful and tender.  We made a 3.5 lb prime rib for Christmas and it came out medium well which my husband wasn't happy about but he told me to print it and add it to the book because he liked the flavor too.  We were playing around with the auto shutoff and delay start settings on the oven so it did get more cook time than it should have.  I halved all of the seasonings but the horseradish powder like someone else suggested and still had a lot left over but I think horseradish is the ingredient that made the meat so flavorful for me.

Thanks Elissa, keep them coming.

attributes.source_text: so flavorful and tender
We made a 3.5 lb prime rib for Christmas
he liked the flavor too

reviews.review_text: I normally make Kittencal's Prime Rib recipe, but was sick on Christmas Eve and did not get around to inserting the garlic the night before. Since, this recipe did not require overnight marination, I substituted it for the other and it got rave reviews from my guests. I did not have horseradish powder, but used some Tastefully Simple Howlin Horseradish Mix in it's place. I cooked my 6-pound rib-eye roast at 450 degrees for 20 minutes, 375 for 25 minutes, turned off the oven for 3 hours, finally 50 minutes at 375 degrees until my thermometer reached 130 degrees. After sitting 15 minutes it was at 135 degrees and the perfect medium rare. I served this with "Recipe #201984" sauce and it was perfect! For sides I served, "Recipe #183993", Asparagus, and a "Recipe #158283". Fabulous, Christmas Meal. Thanks Elissa for the post that saved my Christmas dinner!

attributes.source_text: it got rave reviews from my guests
Fabulous, Christmas Meal

reviews.review_text: by far the best prime rib recipe EVER!! its so fool proof its crazy!! i bought a 3.6lb prime rib for valentines dinner with my bf and put it in at 2pm. i shut the oven off at 2:45 and turned it back on at 5pm. the roast cameout at 5:40pm and was perfect medium rare with a delicious crust that wasnt too salty because i cut WAY back on the recomended amount of salt. i used horseradish sauce because i couldnt find powder and mixed in some minced garlic (from a jar) and added some of the oil from the garlic jar to the outside. i also cut little slices in the roast and put a tiny bit of minced garlic and dried rosmary in the holes which really traveled throughout the meat and gave it a delicious flavor. i will make this again and again, the boyfriend already  asked for it again this week for dinner.. his family devoured the leftovers and asked for the recipe. this is impossible to mess up!!!!

items.label: Authentic Italian Tomato Sauce
items.name: Authentic Italian Tomato Sauce
items.description: This is a recipe I got from my father who got it from a little old lady he knew from Italy. I always simmer this sauce with my meatballs (recipe posted). You can also add sausage if you like. This sauce is to die for!!!!
instructions: In a large pot, sauté onion and garlic in olive oil.
Empty plum tomatoes into large bowl and squash with your hands.
Add all ingredients (including any meatballs or sausage you want to add) to pot and simmer for 3 hours.

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe along with the meatballs. I had never made spaghetti before and it turned out great. I only did a couple tweaks. I browned the meatballs in an iron skillet before adding them to the sauce (as another poster suggested) and I made them 2/3 ground beef and 1/3 hot Italian sausage. And, I also cut the cloves down to 1 and tripled the garlic. I only gave it 4 out of 5 stars because it doesn't seem authentic (or is it?). I as hoping to find a recipe using all fresh ingredients, but this one was quick and easy - after its all together you just need to stir the pot occasionally. Next time I am going to do the meatball equal parts beef, hot italian sausage and lamb. I really liked how the sauce turned out. It really cooked down a lot and was super thick when it was time to serve - perfect for adding a little noodle juice to make the sauce really bind to the pasta.

attributes.source_text: was super thick when it was time to serve

reviews.review_text:
I wanted to add my experience regarding how you saut? the onion and garlic in the same pan and then adding sugar to the recipe. Here is what I%u2019ve learned from my own cooking experience and from reading hundreds of recipes. Many recipes tell you to saut? the onions in the same pan in which you make your sauce as it adds more flavor to the dish. The recipe as posted says to use olive oil and if you have that in the bottom of your pan, you are not likely to burn the onions unless you are saut?ing them at too high a heat. Any sticky bits should then be scraped up as you are adding the other wet ingredients (tomatoes). This only adds flavor, unless you%u2019ve burned them. So cook slowly only until onions soften.
As for sugar being added to the recipe, I have two things to say. The poster of this recipe, %u2018InMemoryofBrats%u2019, says that this recipe was given to her father from a lady from Italy. Most people from Italy didn%u2019t use canned (from the store) tomatoes; they would have used fresh or something they canned themselves. Tomatoes and the sweetness of those tomatoes vary from season to season and sometimes from fruit to fruit on the same bush. To avoid bitterness that some tomatoes have, you can add sugar to make up for not having a sweet tomato. So, check your sauce and if you feel it%u2019s too bitter, add some sugar, a little at a time. Of course then there are some people that just love a sweeter sauce and for them, the two tablespoons of sugar may be needed. I just wanted to clarify this to new cooks and hope it helps someone.

I made this sauce to accompany your meatball recipe. I threw everything into my crockpot and cooked it on high for 4 and a half hours. I was feeding a crowd and everyone enjoyed the sauce but my family prefers the one that I usually make;I guess old habits are are to change. I did love the fact that I keep most of these ingredients as staples in my house and it is easy to whip up this recipe. I also love how cheap this sauce is and how much better it tastes than store bought. I'm sure without including the items that I usually have on hand, the cost for the sauce was less than $5.00. So if I add the cost of the meatball...I made a spaghetti,meatballs & sauce dinner for less than $1.00 a serving--you can't beat that! Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: I was feeding a crowd and everyone enjoyed the sauce
I made a spaghetti,meatballs & sauce dinner

reviews.review_text: Allie, this couldn't be any easier!  And I can honestly say that this is the BEST sauce recipe I've tried.  I'm abandoning my other recipe for this one. It's delicious, light-not heavy, and not too acidic.  I think it's because of the absence of tomato paste, which isn't needed.  The simmering time thickens it very nicely.  I followed the recipe to the letter with no changes.  My entire family loved it--my husband came home and was dipping bread in the pot right away.  He said to tell you that your sauce and meatballs are heirloom quality recipes to pass on to the kids. He has never said that before--but he's really serious about tomato sauce and meatballs, lol.  This is the best!  Oh, I had the sauce (w/ the meatballs in it) going at a good bubbling simmer, and everything was ready after about 1 1/2 hours, but I let it simmer longer anyway.  Thank you for sharing your recipe!

reviews.review_text: I'll add my five stars to your ever-collecting list of reviews here ; )  This sauce is delicious, Allie!  I changed nothing, as I wanted to see exactly how  this recipe turns out, and I feel it is restaurant quality. I tasted this sauce after simmering for 1 1/2 hours and I have to say, I liked the flavor better at the end of the first half of the cooking.  The second hour and a half thickened the sauce, but seemed to me to change the flavor. I served it with your recipe for meatballs which were  a great addition to this sauce.  I do have to add that my family still wants me to continue making my own sauce, but with me, this one deserves a winning review! I plan to use the leftover sauce to make some ziti ; )  Thanks for the wonderful supper, Allie!

reviews.review_text: I had made some changes while I prepared this sauce.  I had fresh tomatoes on hand that I wanted to use up...used 4 garlic instead of 2...and added about 1 T of hot chili paste. The sauce turned out quite thick, so I added water to make a better consistency.  The cloves imparted a unique taste that I quite enjoyed.  I added a parmesan rind for flavor.  To prevent the onions and garlic sticking, I sprayed my Dutch oven with Pam and cooked them at a lower heat and had no problems with burning.  Next time, I would probably use fresh basil for a fresher taste. I used your recipe for meatballs and just plopped them in the Dutch oven, let them cook for  about 10 minutes, then stirred them around...then simmering them for 3 hours.  This is not the "run of the mill" type of sauce and turned out something quite unique.  The cloves do make a difference, but you have to like the taste in the first place!  This was a very easy recipe to put together, and I would do this one again!

attributes.source_text: The sauce turned out quite thick

reviews.review_text: I was very excited to make an authentic Italian spaghetti sauce since my husband is 100% Italian. I thought this would really be wonderful, but was very disappointed. I was expecting it to have lots of flavor, but it mostly tasted like cooked tomatoes. I know it's called "tomato" sauce, and I guess that's the way it was supposed to taste, but I'm used to more seasoning. When it was about done and after tasting many times, I had to give in and add a package of Lawry's spaghetti seasoning. That helped some, then added another packet a bit later. It still wasn't what I was hoping for. I will stick to making my own which in never quite the same each time but still has more of what I want than this recipe. Sorry! Wish I could say it was wonderful. I'm happy for those who loved it.

attributes.source_text: authentic Italian spaghetti sauce

reviews.review_text: Made this almost completely as written ( i did not have cloves). Everything was going well, tasting as I went along. as soon as I added the cheese I felt like it went off! I persevered and simmered for about an hour. At that point I was convinced that the cheese was darkening the tomato flavor. I added a t salt and eventually a T oregano to try and distract from the cheese flavor but in the end I feel like the cheese is a blight on this recipe. It came out fine...I mean, it tastes about like a store bought jar of "three cheese" sauce or something, but when I do it again, I will definitely leave out the cheese (and then won't add oregano either). My thought is this. If I am going to spend the time making my own sauce, I really don't want it to taste like Ragu.... In the end, not a bad sauce, nothing wrong with it, but not a fresh, vibrant sauce IMHO.

This recipe is amazing! I grew up with an Italian Grandmother making a big pot of Gravy every Sunday.. She passed away when I was a teenager and I have always tried to figure out her recipe but something was always missing it did not taste like her gravy. Then I found this recipe and all along the one thing I was always missing was the cloves. Took me back to my childhood! I did use brown sugar instead of regular sugar. I also added half a small can of tomato paste while to onions and garlic (I used 4 cloves) are sauteing (it brings out the flavor) then I add everything else. With the empty can of tomatoes fill about 1/4 way full with water mix the rest of the tomatoes with it and put in pot. This is the best Sunday gravy! I do make mine with his meatball recipe which is amazing and I also add raw sausage to the pot as well. and I let it simmer all day. This is an amazing Football Sunday meal!

attributes.source_text: This is an amazing Football Sunday meal

reviews.review_text: Beware Brits.  If you are cooking this then don't do what I did and use the tomato puree as we know it in UK.  As I have since found out, the Americans call what we call Pasatta, Tomata Puree.  In UK tomoato puree is the thick concentrated stuff that the Americans call tomato paste.  It was like wallpaper paste when finished and a bit too tomatoey, but i still ate it, not wasting that many meatballs :).  Anyway, since finding this out I have re-tried the recipe with tomata pasatta instead of puree and it is an absolute gem of a recipe.  thanks.

Very good!! Even better the next day, if you can believe that. I didn't have tomato puree, so I took canned chopped tomatos and whirled them in my food processor. I simmered them for 3 hours, when I served it up with your meatballs, the sauce was a little watery, but I'm sure it's because I used the tomatos instead of the puree. So I simmered for a few more hours. I put in in the fridge over night, when I warmed it up today, a nice thick sauce. This will be put in my tryed and true cookbook. Thanks so much for sharing this recipe.

attributes.source_text: a nice thick sauce

reviews.review_text:
This sauce is fantastic! Followed the recipe the first time but was a little bland and too heavy on the cloves, with a few tweaks for my own flavour I have made this the last 5 Sundays in a row and guests DEMAND to take leftovers home!

My tweaks:
-1 Can Crushed, Diced and Whole plum tomatoes but I use the good quality ones - huge difference.
-double the garlic (rule of thumb)
-4 cloves
-doubled basil, salt, pepper
-use honey instead of sugar
-I remove the casing from italian turkey sausage and crumble it in.
-Let it simmer for 3-4 hours and in the last 15mins remove the lid to get rid of some of the extra water.

Guests don't even add salt/pepper to this - the eat it up and clean their plates!!

reviews.review_text: This Paisana loved this sauce. My whole family gave this 5 stars! Even my Italian mother loved it!  I loved the flavor, the texture, the simplicity, the smell and the ease of this recipe. I was skeptical about the cloves and I might put in 2 less next time (I'm just not a clove fan in general), but it added a very interesting dimension. I did add 4 more garlic cloves because 2 didn't seem enough for the volume of sauce and I might even put in more next time. I made the sauce with the meatballs simmering in it - so easy! I can't resist weighing in on the oregano issue: my mother (who's Italian family is right off the boat in NYC) agrees that the only good use of oregano is on pizza. It's a very strong and distinct flavor and we don't happen to like it. I guess it's like the cloves, a matter of personal taste. Say NO to oregaNO!

I am not too keen on cloves so I have not added them in with any of the sauces I made and I increased the garlic as I love garlic. reviews.review_text: Being 100% Napolitano born in America, traditional core italian recipes were taught and passed down from my Grandmothers. Both were from mountain villages outside Naples, about 50 miles from each other but divided by mountains. I mention this because most traditional recipes are the same or very similar. This sauce recipe is very close to how we make our sauce...almost identical, we only add bay leaves. The best traditional italian or Napolitano recipes are all very simple but fresh ingredients. Canned American puree is a newer convenience but does not deter from the end result. If you grew up with this version of sauce, it's a comfort food staple, with meatballs and italian sausage...always.

reviews.review_text: Good tomato sauce, but definitely not what I was expecting. The cloves added a strange vibe to the sauce that made it different from the "authentic" Italian sauces I'm used to. I'll definitely start cooking my meat in the sauce from now on, both came out super tender and a lot more healthier without sauteeing them first. I'll probably try this recipe again, but will leave out the cloves or cut back on them some next time.

reviews.review_text: I'm Italian, this sauce isn't authentic, even though it's not too far from how we make it. First of all do not add the sugar, that is something it can be done ONLY if the tomatos are too acid. Secondly if you want a sauce with the meat you have to brown the meat in the oil before adding anything else. Then you can put all the other ingredients. As for the simmering, you can't give a specific amount of time. It depends on how much thick you want the sauce, so you can simmer it starting from 1 hour to even 6.

Whoa. This sauce is so delicious!!! Even my father couldn't stop tasting it. I actually halved the recipe (in case it was gross) but I added way more garlic. I also substituted cinnamon for cloves (didn't have any), put about a half a teaspoon. Also added a touch of italian seasoning with the basil. You don't really taste the cinnamon, it just really adds to the flavor. We are having it with fried calamari, scallops, and shrimp. YUM! This is my new tomato sauce recipe, and I'll never buy jarred again!!

items.label: Greek Chicken and Potatoes
items.name: Greek Chicken and Potatoes
items.description: This is a deceptive recipe: quick and easy to make with a simple ingredient list but which really delivers the flavor. What more could you want from chicken and potatoes? I find one large lemon yields just about 1/4 cup juice. This recipe makes 4 servings, but my husband and I eat this easily between the two of us.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F Place chicken, potatoes, and garlic in a 9 X 13 inch glass baking pan.
Mix well to get everything evenly distributed in the pan.
Season with salt and pepper.
Pour the chicken bouillon over all.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice and crumbled oregano together.
Pour evenly over chicken and potatoes.
Bake approximately 30-35 minutes until chicken is cooked through and potatoes are tender and golden brown, basting occasionally with pan juices.

reviews.review_text: I cut this in half and cooked in a 9x9 casserole dish, which I feel was a little too small because everything did not brown properly.  I couldn't help myself and added a bit of chopped onion that needed to be used and a bit of feta that's been sitting around collecting dust (not literally).  Still, I have to agree with  MacV, I found this a little bland and like it was wanting something more.  BF liked it a lot so I may try it again and see what I can work out (in a larger pan, particularly because I was irked that a lot of my potatoes weren't browning well !) But overall I think this is a good recipe!  I never would have thought to cook the chicken with the potatoes and they really add to each others flavors in doing so.  I think this recipe would also be very kid-friendly and, like Latchy said, a good stanby where you know you will always have all the ingredients on-hand.  Thanks for a nice dinner, FlemishMinx.

attributes.source_text: BF liked it a lot
Thanks for a nice dinner

reviews.review_text:
I made this for the first time tonight for my boyfriend and I, and promptly forgot the garlic, or the garlic powder I was going to substitute it with. I also had to use parsley instead of oregano, but that's not really what I was worried about.
I was worried about how the chicken and potatoes would absorb the taste of the liquid - would it be too strong?
My boyfriend cut the potatoes a little too large, so I had to cook for 45 minutes, but even with the missing ingredient and substitution, it came out really well. The potatoes didn't brown (they were cooked and tasted good!), but I was playing a bit of hookey on the amounts of juice, as I doubled the recipe on the fly.
Oh, and I had to cook it in a metal pan because apparently we don't have a glass dish. 
Anyways, I will cook this again, because it was such a success, and I think the sauce would go really well as a bread topping.

We loved this! The recipe was simple in ingredients and preparation and the flavor was great.  Based on the previous reviews about the potatoes not cooking through, I tried 2 things.  First, I cut them about half size of the chicken pieces (about a 1/2 inch cube) and second, I covered the dish with foil for the first 10 minutes. I am not sure if it was one technique or both, but the chicken came out tender and the potatoes soft. I also minced the garlic and made a paste with the salt, oregano and lemon pepper and rubbed it all over the chicken pieces, refrigerated for 2 hours, then stirred in the potatoes and addend the rest of the ingredients.  This wonderful recipe is going in my book for keeps, and I am already thinking of flavor variations!

attributes.source_text: the chicken came out tender
the potatoes soft

reviews.review_text: This recipe has so much potential.  Potatoes will not be cooked enough if you use boneless chicken breasts and are baking for only 30 minutes...can't be done.  Might I suggest bone-in chicken, then you would cook an hour.  Half the potatoes and slice.  If you are keeping the skin on the chicken, don't add the oil....way too greasy.  You need onion in this, add half an onion.  I used 5 large cloves of garlic and the oregano was just not enough.  You need to double it.  The lemon flavor was faint, too faint.  I would add 1/3 of a cup.  I agree with another reviewer that the potatoes need to be on top of the chicken.  But what I think I might do next time is take all the spices, herbs and liquids and marinate the chicken and potatoes in it, then bake.

The first time I made this recipe, it turned out absolutely fantastic. I loved it so much, I decided to make it for family the first night I moved back home. Because of the change in region (I moved from NY to Cali), the type of potato I used the second time around  changed as well, from white to red. The red potatoes took much longer to cook, and it made the chicken terribly dry. I was very embarrassed. Now, I'm not ruling out the possibility that it turned out differently b/c I doubled the recipe, its very possible, but what I'm suggesting is that maybe why this recipe got mixed reviews is b/c the type of potato to use is not specified. Other than that, I followed the recipe to a "T" the first time around and is was flavorful, healthy, the chicken was juicy, and it was overall satisfying meal.

attributes.source_text: the chicken was juicy

reviews.review_text:
Update: This is such a flavorful recipe. I've made this several times and haven't had any problems with the chicken being too dry or the potatoes underdone. Perhaps it's because I use a 9x13 enameled dish instead of pyrex. I wonder if the folks with this problem might try preheating the oven to 400 with the diced potatoes and a half of the sauce in the dish. Then add the chicken and remaining sauce when the oven reaches temperature. It might require a little extra sauce to accomodate evaporation and will take longer for the oven to preheat with the dish in it. But perhaps that would help cook the potatoes more evenly and not dry out the chicken.
*************************************
My husband loved this!! I had only about 3/4 of the lemon juice that the original recipe calls for. But it seemed to be enough because it was still tangy and very tasty. I used a 13x9 baking dish so that the chicken and potatoes were evenly distributed. The potatoes came out nicely browned and slightly crunchy and the chicken was tender and flavorful. We will be enjoying this gem often. Thanks FlemishMinx.

attributes.source_text: My husband loved this!!
it was still tangy
slightly crunchy

reviews.review_text: We just finished dinner and everyone really like this recipe. I also used chicken broth instead of bullion, less salt, but otherwise, I followed the recipe as written. I was dissapointed that mine didn't seem to be browning at all even after 40 minutes, so I poured a little of the liquid off, turned up the heat a bit, and let it go for about another 10 minutes. It still didn't really brown at all, and the chicken dried out. Can't figure what went wrong, but the flavor was terrrific. So, all in all, I will make this again, but try to figure out the browning situation. Thanks for a quick and yummy dish.

We really enjoy this easy meal, thank you FlemishMinx.  I made a couple of changes because my husband is on a total fat free diet.  I left out the olive oil and I also added an onion, which I sautéed in a little vegetable stock whilst I was preparing the potatoes and chicken.  My lemon was too small to give me ¼ cup of juice so I added some lemon zest to make up.  Although I cooked it for the required time some of the potato cubes were a little hard, I will give it a stir during cooking next time.  Most of the potatoes browned up very well even without the oil. This was such a success I will make it often.

Lemon in a chicken dish is an instant winner here.  I made a couple of tweaks on the recipe. Added 2 teaspoons of oregano along with a 1/2 teaspoon of thyme. Used halfed baby yukons  instead of cubed potatoes. Also, at the end of 35 minutes the chicken was still pinkish and the potatoes not quite tender. Rearranged things in the pan so the chicken was on bottom and potatoes were on top. Cooked another 12-15 minutes and I got the crispy skin on the potatoes while keeping the chicken moist.  Loved the final result and will certainly prepare this again. Thanx Minx!!
