keeping the chicken moist

reviews.review_text: This was a disappointment. We were really looking forward to it after all the high reviews.  I followed this exactly and the potatoes did not brown and by the time they were even cooked enough, then chicken was dry.  The sauce was good and tangy, which is why I am giving this 3 stars. I think if you used whole chicken breasts it would be better because then the chicken would not be dry by the time the potatoes are done.  I don't think the potatoes will brown no matter how long you cook them, though.  So don't be waiting for that!  I will try it again with whole chicken breasts and see how it does.

attributes.source_text: The sauce was good and tangy

reviews.review_text: The flavours in this dish were really a treat.  Every ingredient really complemented the others.  I added some red onion and feta cheese (as per another reviewer's comments) and increased the garlic to 5 cloves.  I also used red potatoes (skin on) to add some extra colour to the dish.  The only thing I changed the second time I made it was to parboil the potatoes for about 10 minutes before combining with the other ingredients...  This helped them cook completely in about the same length of time as the chicken pieces.

This recipe was indeed very easy and simple.  I loved that it was a one dish meal.  We had Greek salad with it, so clean up was a breeze.  My DH and kids gobbled it down.  It's been added to our permenant recipe list.  I changed a couple of things though: 4 garlic cloves as opposed to 3, I changed the amount of water to 1/2 cup, and added 1 t. of basil in with the olive oil, lemon, and oregano mix.  I also added a bit more lemon juice.  Still, the chicken and potatoes were absolutely wonderful, as was the aroma during baking.  Thanks for posting, FlemishMinx!

attributes.source_text: My DH and kids gobbled it down
My DH and kids gobbled it down

reviews.review_text: I really liked this dish, my dh thought it was o.k.  I found it to be light, refreshing, and something different.  I did use 1 large lemon as the description suggested, and was a little short of the 1/4 cup.  I would like to try making it again with 1/3 cup lemon juice.  For anyone doing weight watchers, I calculated it to be 6 points per serving.  I used some of the excess juices from the dish and used it to toss my green beans.  I bet this would be really yummy with some feta cheese sprinkled on top.  I also thought about

attributes.source_text: I found it to be light, refreshing, and something different
I found it to be light, refreshing, and something different

reviews.review_text:
We enjoyed this very much.  I had decided to serve some fresh green beans with this and decided at the last minute to just throw them in with the chicken and potatoes instead.  What a great compliment to this dish.

I like the idea of adding basil, will probably do that the next time I make this along with a bit more oregano.  

It did take about 15-19 minutes longer to cook than what the recipe suggested, the potatoes and chicken were just not done after 35 minutes. 

All and all, we really enjoyed this very easy to assemble dish.

Wow, this really exceeded my expectations! Very flavorful simple dish from ingredients on hand for an easy weeknight dinner. Smells so wonderful while it cooks! The secret to this dish is to use fresh garlic, I used 3 large cloves, fresh lemon juice, about 2 regular lemons, and good olive oil, as well as Kosher salt and fresh ground pepper. I didn't baste. Tagged this recipe in the gameroom, mainly because I had some potatoes to use up, and am thrilled to have found a new easy dish. Thanks so much, FlemishMinx!

attributes.source_text: for an easy weeknight dinner
for an easy weeknight dinner

reviews.review_text: This was a great dish!  I love that it was a one dish meal too!  I also added some feta to the dish as well as some garlic and some italian seasoning.  The taste was fantastic and the potatoes were perfectly tender.  I did have to cook it longer than stated and I noticed that the tops of the chicken weren't cooking so I had to flip them all partway through.  I think if you also just gave the dish a stir halfway through along with basting it would be alright.  This was a very simple meal and I will definately be making it again!

attributes.source_text: the potatoes were perfectly tender

reviews.review_text: Just finished enjoying this wonderful dinner. My DH and I both loved the tangy flavor of the fresh lemon juice in the potatoes and chicken. I used chicken broth instead of bouillon, increased the garlic and sprinkled crumbled feta over our servings as suggested by others. I had to bake it about 10 minutes longer than suggested to get the nice carmalized edges on the potatoes. It's true....the house smells amazing while this is baking. My co-workers will be drooling over the leftovers tomorrow at lunch. Thanks so very much for posting!

attributes.source_text: Just finished enjoying this wonderful dinner
My DH and I both loved the tangy flavor
loved the tangy flavor of the fresh lemon juice
the leftovers tomorrow at lunch

items.label: Thai-Style Grilled Chicken Thighs
items.name: Thai-Style Grilled Chicken Thighs
keywords: c("Chicken", "Poultry", "Meat", "Asian", "Very Low Carbs", "High Protein", "High In...", "Summer", "Brunch", "< 30 Mins", "Beginner Cook", "Easy")
items.description: This is my first recipe - please be kind! My kids love it and when I take it to a BBQ everyone wants the recipe. It is a variation on one I found in epicurious a while ago. It is very easy and very yummy!!
instructions: Combine all ingredients except chicken in a bowl.
Mix thoroughly.
Add chicken and leave to marinate at least one hour, preferably longer.
Grill chicken on the BBQ, hotplate or in the griller until golden brown and cooked through.
Ususlly you would expect 12 thigh fillets to feed 4 to 6 people- in my family the kids eat 4 each so this recipe serves 3.

reviews.review_text: I really loved this recipe. I will be making it again. The marinade is delish and I recommend you double or triple it. I didn't have basil so I used the paste in the tube. Also used ginger and lemongrass in tubes, as well as fresh ginger and cilantro. I doubled all the liquids, minced one Serrano and one jalapeno pepper (it added a touch of mild spice). I also added sweet Thai chili sauce and marinated for over one hour. I didn't grill it, I cooked everything in a roaster pan at 250-300 degrees x 35 min Also added 3/4 cup of water to mixture so it wouldn't dry out while cooking. I can't wait for the next time I make this. I'm going to need double the chicken thighs. It was so easy.

attributes.source_text: it added a touch of mild spice

reviews.review_text: My family loved this!! I would give it more stars if I could. I used 12 thigh fillets, intending to freeze 2 meal portions, but the 3 of us ate 9 pieces so I only have 3 left.  Not enough for a meal.  I had to make some changes due to what I had on hand.  I used a minced basil and garlic concentrate instead of fresh basil, no coriander and extra soy sauce instead of fish sauce.  Also, I marinated this for approx 30 hours. I baked it at 200 C for 20 minutes, it came out very juicy but not golden.  I will be trying this as a  "dump chicken" sauce.  I use my freezer a lot and hope to make good use of this recipe.

attributes.source_text: My family loved this!!
it came out very juicy

reviews.review_text: We made these this past weekend and they were OMG amazing. Super flavorful and moist, while not being difficult to make at all. We followed Barb's advice and marinated them longer, about 2 hours. Also, we made a ton to feed a large family group, so we increased everything several fold. We couldn't find the little red Asian chilis, so we substituted some nice Fresno chilis which worked fine. Someone suggested adding sesame oil and spicing the recipe up, which sound like nice ideas to try as well. Don't let the fish sauce scare you; there is absolutely no fishy taste, just savory goodness that anyone in the family will enjoy. This is a keeper and our new favorite grilled chicken recipe!

attributes.source_text: moist
anyone in the family will enjoy
just savory goodness
there is absolutely no fishy taste

reviews.review_text: I've made this twice now and each time my family has gobbled it up. This is so tasty and easy to make! I used boneless, skinless chicken breasts. The first time I made it I cut the chicken up, marinated for 4 hours and stir fried it in a wok. The 2nd time, I pounded the chicken breast lightly so that it was an even thickness, marinated for 5 hours and grilled it. It was delicious both ways. I served it with Thai Chicken Fried Rice with Basil - Kao Pad Krapao Recipe #32321 (minus the chicken). My family requested that next time I double the recipe so they could have it for lunch the next day. It's great finding new recipes for chicken! Thanks barb63!!

attributes.source_text: my family has gobbled it up
My family requested that next time I double the recipe

reviews.review_text: This was a terrific recipe. I was having a bunch of people over and marinated 3 lbs. of boneless, skinless thighs with this recipe and had another recipe for the other 2 1/2 lbs. I cut each boneless thigh into four pieces and threaded the pieces on bamboo skewers. I used Asian hot pepper paste in place of the chile as I wasn;t sure what was meant by that-chili powder or diced chili peppers or sauce. I marinated it maybe 3 hours and then grilled them. This was excellent. Nine adults and 2 children went through six pounds of chicken. Most people preferred this to the other recipe. I would definitely want this again and will be forwarding the recipe as people have asked me for it.

attributes.source_text: Nine adults and 2 children went through six pounds of chicken
Nine adults and 2 children went through six pounds of chicken

reviews.review_text: This was super easy.  The only ingredient I didn't have on hand was the ginger.  I used the frozen cubed basil, cilantro and garlic instead of fresh.  I marinated the chicken for almost an hour and a half then grilled on high (about 350 degrees) for 5 minutes each side then turned the grill to low and let the chicken cook for about 40 minutes with the lid closed.  The chicken was juicy and tasted great. What a great taste! I will definitely keep this recipe and look forward to making it again.  Thanks so much for posting!

attributes.source_text: The chicken was juicy

reviews.review_text:
I just tried your recipe on the Weber kettle grill, cooked over hardwood charcoal chips, and loved it! 

To the cooked chicken I added a sweet and spicy dipping sauce from  a recipe on Hot Sour Salty Sweet: A Culinary Journey Through Southeast Asia by Jeffrey Alford and Naomi Duguid. (I am a big fan of all of their books!) The dipping sauce is made from 1/2 cup rice vinegar, 1/2 cup sugar, 2 cloves chopped garlic and about a tablespoon of hot red pepper flakes (I used a fresh Thai birdseye chili instead of the peper flakes and it wasn't very hot), brought to a boil and cooked for 5 minutes.  

I served a salad of mixed baby greens, fresh sugar pod peas, sweet red peppers and English cucumbers dressed in lemon juice, dijon mustard, honey, and olvie oil.

I made Indian white rice and used up the last of some canneloni dried beans which had been soaked, cooked and cooled, then dressed in the same dressing as the salad but with salt added. 

Very satisfying!  The chicken was the star!

Recently deconverted vegetarian learning to cook meat. This recipe is great. I’ve read Chicken legs (dark meat) especially thighs because of the fat get super tender. Skin on all the way. Absolutely no change to the marinade except I tripled it and reduced (boiled) the leftover on the stove for 5 minutes to baste on before finish and this was where the magic happened. I did purée everything but the basil. I assumed the stalks might make it bitter. It was gingery but reduced dramatically after cooking. Paired with an Asian salad with mango and jasmine rice. I could sell this.

attributes.source_text: get super tender
It was gingery

reviews.review_text: Patch63, You can remove  (please be kind) from the discription of this recipe! A nice first! I DID USED SKINLESS BUT THE CHICKEN DID HAVE BONES. I used frozen basil and had to put the cilantro on my pieces of cooked chicken. DH doesn`t like cilantro and I love it. Marinated over night. I did grill the chicken on lightly oiled foil. Grill on high 5 minutes turned and reduced the heat to low very low! For 40 minutes. The chicken was not over direct fire. It came out very tender. My DH had no idea what it was marinated in. First words out of his mouth was OHHHH AHMMMMMMMM this is good! Well between 3 of us it`s all GONE! Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: First words out of his mouth was OHHHH AHMMMMMMMM this is good!
It came out very tender

reviews.review_text:
This reminded me of a chicken veggie curry recipe that is much loved in our house! I used red curry paste cut with a little coconut milk whisked to smooth out instead of the chili since I wasn't really clear on what that ingredient was. Mixed everything else very well and grilled after a 4 hour marinade time. Sprinkled with a little fine chopped green onion and sesame seeds for bling after cooking. Fabulous!
Served with tofu spaghetti sauteed up with a little extra virgin coconut oil and lots of fresh veggies.
I'm also guessing this would be really good with wings on the grill.

I tried this tonight using a large family pack of wings, tips cut and wings split at the joint. <br/>I got got some fresh Thai Basil and Cilantro  while at the farmers market this morning.<br/>Everything else I had in the cupboard. I added a bit of Sesame Oil to he marinade and let the wings marinate for about 4 hours, turning every hour to coat well. I then took another review suggestion and made lemon and ginger rice and got some fresh okra going in the wok with Sesame and Chili oils. Grilled the wings and the entire dinner was a success. Thanks for sharing! Barb!

attributes.source_text: the entire dinner was a success

reviews.review_text: Well done, barb63!  Utterly delicious marinade. I used boneless breasts cut into chunks, and skewered onto kebabs with tri-color peppers and onions.  What a hit with our company, served with fried brown rice and grilled pineapple slices.  Hint to others:  make a triple amount of this sauce, and keep in a big jar, so that next time you're in the mood for this dish, you just pour!  I always end up throwing a lot of cilantro away because it's so hard to use up all at once, and this would be a good use for it.

attributes.source_text: What a hit with our company

reviews.review_text: WOW!! Wonderful flavor. My husband likes thighs and I prefer breasts so I used 3/4 lbs. boneless, skinless thighs and 3/4 lbs. boneless, skinless breasts. I wasn't sure about what kind of chili pepper to use so I used about 2 tablespoons of Thai chili sauce. I was tempted to use dried basil since I didn't have any fresh but I got some for this recipe and it was well worth the trip to the store! I marinated for about 3 hours and cooked this on the grill. A keeper for sure. Thanks for sharing :)

Thank you.  Finally a recipe for the best part of the chicken (my opinion).  Since breasts are so popular I want to keep it that way. (keeps price down).  My hint, always leave skin on.  When I used to remove skin as the popular thing to do, I ate 3.  With skin on I am satisfied with 2.  Removing skin therefore did not help with weight problems.  I am 76 and now back to same weight as in my 20's.  Eating fat does not increase weight. Eating too much does.  Will be trying tomorrow.

Delicious!  I used oyster sauce in place of the fish sauce, as that was all I had on hand, and dried red pepper flakes instead of the chiles.  DH requested white meat next time (though I loved it with the chicken thighs!) and a little more sweetness, so next time I'll up the sugar just a little bit, or top it with a glaze right at the end.  These smelled fantastic when they were cooking, our neighbor rounded the fence to ask what we were grilling.  This will be a part of our regular rotation.  Thanks so much for sharing!

This is a great grilled chicken recipe! My DH kicked it up a notch with extra chili paste and it was umm umm good! This recipe is a keeper!

Update from DH: I did this recipe again today, and it was even better.  I put some apple wood chunks (for smoke) in my Big Green Egg and cooked low (about 225 degrees) for about 20-30 minutes.  Then I kicked the heat up to about 400 until done just to give them a little char.  The apple wood smoke added a really nice touch to an already awesome recipe.

attributes.source_text: The apple wood smoke added a really nice touch

reviews.review_text: How easy! I simply tossed all the marinating ingredients into the blender and pulsed briefly instead of chopping. I also added a good amount (say two tablespoons) of Thai chili sauce. The smell was amazing. I grilled in my micro on high for 20 minutes, turning halfway through. Amazing chicken, tender but delicious. Served it with brown rice and broccoli stir-fried with garlic and fish sauce. My only nitpick is that it isn't spicy enough, but that seems to be a matter of personal taste.

attributes.source_text: tender but delicious

reviews.review_text: I decided to make this for dinner tonight since I had all the ingredients on hand, and we love Asian flavors. This was a definite hit. The only substitution I made was swapping the minced chili with chili garlic sauce. I roasted the chicken on a lightly oiled baking sheet at 400 flipping several times until they were done - since there's about a foot of snow covering my grill at the moment. Can't wait for warmer weather so I can make this on the grill!

attributes.source_text: make this for dinner tonight
we love Asian flavors

reviews.review_text: These were so delicious and easy - thank you!!! I have been looking for a new recipe for grilled chicken, and came across this. I had all the ingredients on hand (except fresh basil), and they were delicious for a quick post-work dinner even with only 30 minutes to marinate. My 9 year old son loved them too! Since I didn't have basil, I added a little lime juice to the marinade, and then sprinkled fresh mint on at the end after cooking. Yum!! Can't wait to make them again.

attributes.source_text: for a quick post-work dinner
My 9 year old son loved them too

items.label: Do at Home Onion Rings
items.name: Do at Home Onion Rings
items.description: Make and share this Do at Home Onion Rings recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Mix egg, oil, and milk on low speed of mixer for 1 minute.
Add dry ingredients and mix until smooth.
Coat onions in flour.
Dip in batter.
When one side is golden turn to the other side.
Fry in hot oil 375* until desired shade of brown.

reviews.review_text:
Passed the taste test of the 19 year old who works at a burger joint with flying colors. "Mom, you know *real* restaurants serve their onion rings just like this", while she devoured a plate with some ketchup on the side. 
When I made the batter (with whole spelt flour, because that's my favorite flour), I thought it would be too much for two onions, but very little was left by the end. I floured and battered three whole mushrooms with the rest. Yum! These were so much easier and successful than I remember any onion rings ever being. Thanks so much for the recipe!
Next time I will probably try adding a little bit of spice also. I like the idea of a little hot pepper and a touch of salt. But even just exactly as the recipe, these were great.

attributes.source_text: Passed the taste test of the 19 year old who works at a burger joint with flying colors

reviews.review_text:
Ms. Willenborg:

This recipe was great.  My family and myself were eating leftover polish sausage and meatballs from the holidays and I wanted to compliment the meal with something other than a potato recipe. As a previous review stated the only thing difficult about the receipe was to keep the rest of the family away while making them.   The only thing that I would change about your recipe is to inform the next reader to cut their onion about 1/2 inch. Other than that I would NOT change a thing.

Kelly

Yumm, yumm, yumm!! Although quite greasy, they taste great! Even for me, who has not been eating deep fried onion rings at fast food places :) I used half batter, cos I did not have all the ingriedients right amount, and it was just enough for two medium size onions. Mayb the reason is, I added just a zip of water to batter, cos it seemed little too thick. But it was good either way! Sprinkeled salt on top to balance the sweetness onion gives. Ups, now I see, i forgot to dip the onian in flour first, beafore the batter... no biggy, maybe next time :D Still turned out great! One suggestion, do not let these get cold, they taste soo much better hot! Thanks for sharing this recipe!

attributes.source_text: the sweetness onion gives

reviews.review_text: In my opinion the flavor of the batter is brilliant although there are a few problems with it that I came across. 1. With how thick the batter is, it makes the onion ring expand a ton making the ring mold huge the moment it hits the fryer ( I would add more milk and make it batter thinner) 2. With how how large the onion ring is when it hits the fryer it absorbs a ton of frying oil and is just soaked. It doesn’t allow for the oil to drip out and become a nice crisp like an onion ring should because of the large fluffy mold it has.

Found this one and decided to try it. DH and I are always on the hunt for a decent "do at home" onion ring recipe and boy did this one fit the bill!! Taking notes from previous reviews, we did decide to omit the oil, and honestly they were still incredible. I did fix the recipe and tried a batch exactly as directed, then "doctored" a lil, to our taste. I added another 1/2tsp of salt and a 1/2tsp of cayenne as well as double dipped for the thicker crunch. We're southern and love anything crispy. lol. These are by far, the best tasting onion rings we've found for do at home. A definite do again in our house!! Thanks for sharing. :)

attributes.source_text: DH and I are always on the hunt for a decent "do at home" onion ring recipe and boy did this one fit the bill
We're southern and love anything crispy

reviews.review_text: By far “This Onion Ring recipe” is simple and Scrumptious down to every little morsel. The only thing I did different was I did not add the oil, they were going to be deep-fried in oil anyway. I also added a pinch seasoning salt to my Flour and baking powder... Yummy!!! These Onion Rings were by far the best onion rings EVER!! I used a few to Top my steak burgers last night, “ yummy “ My husband raves about them.. The way to your mans heart is through his stomach.. I hit a home run with your Onion Ring recipe.. Thank you for sharing...

attributes.source_text: My husband raves about them

reviews.review_text:
Hi MizzNezz;
These are the most scrumptous, crispy and easy to make ONION RINGS. They cooked so quickly and had a nice golden brown color.  They are the best that I have ever made or had for that matter.
Took me a while to find your recipe.  I got a craving for Onion Rings and started to look through the ZAAR, and there you were, how lucky for us.  Will be passing your recipe on to all my friends.
Thank you for posting and sharing with us.
"Uncle Bill"

attributes.source_text: crispy

reviews.review_text: I was going to give these 3 stars because they were way too greasy but they looked soo pretty.  Just as good as a restaurants looks.  Next time I will not add the oil to the batter and hopefully that will help. I have never had onion rings turn out so perfect looking.  It must be the mixture of the flour coating and the baking powder.  Even my husband asked how they looked soo good.

I've tried a number of onion ring recipes, all of which seem to fall short of the mark.  Make this recipe, and it was very good, but we like crunch onion rings.  After the first batch came out of the fryer, I topped the batter with Panko bread crumbs.  OMG.......they were amazing.  Even my DH (a self appointed connoisseur of all things fried), raved and said..."top shelf", "best onion rings ever".  Thanks for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: we like crunch onion rings
Even my DH (a self appointed connoisseur of all things fried), raved

reviews.review_text: Mizz Nezz, these are great onion rings. Time consuming but definitely worth it! DH and three kids loved these! The only thing that I didn't do was make a batter,I messed up! I read this in a hurry and left the egg,milk and oil seperate from the flour mixture. They still turned out great.. I dipped in egg then in flour mix, egg again then flour! Even though I messed up they were great!

attributes.source_text: DH and three kids loved these
DH and three kids loved these

reviews.review_text: It made a great thick batter for the onion rings and it didn't fall off as batter can be prone to do. After I added some seasoned salt and a little garlic powder then I was really happy with the batter. Without the added seasoning I think it was a bit bland. I also successfully used it for cauliflower, zucchini, broccoli and mushrooms. The cauliflower and brocolli were blanched first of course. :-)

attributes.source_text: It made a great thick batter

reviews.review_text: I halved the recipe and I added seasoning salt and cayenne pepper to the dredging flour & was glad I did, otherwise the onion rings would have been VERY bland w/out it. Next time I'll add even more seasoning. I also just used a splash of olive oil instead of 1/8 cup. Even after halving the recipe, one whole onion was a bit much for two people unless it was served as a main dish. But as a side dish or an appetizer, the full recipe would easily feed 5-6 people.

attributes.source_text: as a side dish
or an appetizer

reviews.review_text: These are just awesome.  I made these for New Year's Eve and family members were telling me to open an onion ring stand.  For a really easy time frying the rings, I recommend picking up a mini-fryer like a Fry Daddy.  I never tried one before and it made everything so much easier (although I suddenly wanted to fry everything in the house).  I did add some pepper and might add paprika next time.  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: I made these for New Year's Eve
family members were telling me to open an onion ring stand

reviews.review_text: These turned out so great! The onions were cooked perfectly and don't pull out of the crispy outside when you bite down on them. Definitely some of the best onion rings I've ever had. We didn't change a thing about the recipe and I was actually surprised that the batter puffed up so nicely on the rings because it was so thin. These were awesome dipped in fry sauce and we'll definitely make them again!

attributes.source_text: the crispy outside
the batter puffed up so nicely

reviews.review_text: Excellent!  Wife and I both loved these.  I will use more salt next time but that's kind of a personal preference thing.  CROWD WARNING!  Don't let anybody "sample" them before you're done cooking.  If you do they'll be gone as fast as you can make them and you won't get any.  I guess everybody doesn't hang around with bikers though.  lol

attributes.source_text: Wife and I both loved these

reviews.review_text:
Very tasty! I messed up the batter a bit by using buttermilk instead of regular milk, which made the batter thick and difficult to work with. I thinned it out with some water and everything worked just fine. The batter was puffy and crispy, which I love; it was a bit bland so I added some Tony's to remedy that.

In the future I'd like to use apple rings with the batter to make fritters. I'll come back when I have results.

attributes.source_text: The batter was puffy and crispy
The batter was puffy and crispy

items.label: Brown Sugar Meatloaf
items.name: Brown Sugar Meatloaf
items.description: I use chili sauce or salsa instead of ketchup to give a nice contrast to the sweetness of the brown sugar.  A lighter version can be made using Splenda brown sugar blend, skim milk, and Egg Beaters. Got this one from the AllRecipes website. It's one of their most popular recipes.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Lightly grease a 5x9 inch loaf pan.
Press the brown sugar in the bottom of the prepared loaf pan and spread the ketchup over the sugar.
In a mixing bowl, mix thoroughly all remaining ingredients and shape into a loaf.
Place on top of the ketchup.
Bake in preheated oven for 1 hour or until juices are clear.

reviews.review_text: I just made this and love it! I did have to make some adjustments though. Instead of using saltine crackers I used Italian bread crumbs as I never keep crackers in the house. I used frozen onions and green peppers in place of the raw onion, and only 1/4 cup of brown sugar so it wouldn't be too sweet (as others suggested). Others have said that you shouldn't use 80/20 ground beef but I did and it still came out great. You just have to use a bit more bread crumbs to suck up the grease and then immediately remove the loaf to a different platter, leaving the grease behind in the cooking dish. I also had to bake it for about an hour and a half because it wasn't done in an hour. I think that the next time I make it I will place the brown sugar and ketchup on top so that the grease from the 80/20 ground beef doesn't ruin it. Thank you Yooper for such a wonderful recipe!

attributes.source_text: so it wouldn't be too sweet

reviews.review_text: This is one good meatloaf, Yooper!  I took your advice & used the chili sauce & really liked the resulting combo of sweet & slightly spicy.  I switched oatmeal for the crushed crackers, cause I really like oatmeal in meatloafs (& didn't have any crackers anyway) & used the onion flakes since I couldn't find any onion in the fridge.  It was delicious!  This will be on the frequent flyer list for sure.  I did find that it was hard to check for doneness by the juices running clear, since the pan was so full of the juice from the sugar & chili sauce, but it was done perfectly  at about 55 minutes.

attributes.source_text: really liked the resulting combo of sweet & slightly spicy
really liked the resulting combo of sweet & slightly spicy

reviews.review_text:
Woooooow!! What a terrific meatloaf recipe! Before I give the full feedback let me advise that I did change some things ONLY because I had to use turkey and that was a first. The basics of the recipe remained the same however in fear that the turkey would make the recipe bland I made the following modifications..... please know that this is my new ONLY meatloaf recipe and turkey may be the permanent replacement for ground beef (it was so tender and moist).
Added: heaping half cup of celery sauteed it with the onion with salt. pepper, and Italian seasonings with butter and olive oil. Also added a bit more bread to the cracker crumbs (3 dinner rolls); Put 1/3 c brown sugar into the mix, 3/4 cup ketchup, 1 Tsp chicken base, garlic & onion powder. Love this site and love this recipe. Thanks for sharing.

attributes.source_text: it was so tender and moist
it was so tender and moist

reviews.review_text: I have made this recipe twice. The first time I followed the recipe exactly. After cooking for 1 hour, my loaf was a little too pink inside for my taste and I did not care for the ginger taste. The secon time I omitted the ginger and baked it for 1.5 hours. It was perfect for me anyway. BTW, 4 stars from my hubby, which is high praise from him...plus I historically make the worst meatloaves. Thanks for the recipe Yooper.  Nov 2008.  I wanted to add to my review.   I make this meatloaf all the time!  Last week being pressed for time, I put approx 1 TBS brown sugar and a dollop of ketchup into 8 indivdual muffin tins and baked for 30 minutes.  It was fantastic!

attributes.source_text: 4 stars from my hubby, which is high praise from him

reviews.review_text: We had this last night and we all loved it. I'm a bit of a splosher not exact with all measurements, probably used only slighty less sugar and ketchup than recommended, and was still great. I agree with Nurse Di, you have to spoon the sauce over when you've cut it, keeps it moist and adds to the flavour. The only change I made was I fryed my onions till they were a rich brown (add a little water, let it disolve, add a little more water, let it disolve etc). Something my Mother-in-law has instilled in me when it comes to meatloves and rissoles. We will definitely be having this as a regular, so tasty and easy to make. items.name: Awesome Blueberry Muffins
items.description: This is a awesome Blueberry muffin recipe. Double it to make large muffins. I sometimes add cinnamon to the batter.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Grease muffin cups or line with muffin liners.
Combine 1 1/2 cups flour, 3/4 cup sugar, salt and baking powder.
Place vegetable oil into a 1 cup measuring cup; add the egg and enough milk to fill the cup.
Mix this with flour mixture.
Fold in blueberries.
Fill muffin cups right to the top, and sprinkle with crumb topping mixture.
To Make Crumb Topping: Mix together 1/2 cup sugar, 1/3 cup flour, 1/4 cup butter, and 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon.
Mix with fork, and sprinkle over muffins before baking.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes in the preheated oven, or until done.

reviews.review_text: This rating is for the muffin, not the topping. For taste, I give it 4 stars but because of the ease and minimal dish use, I gave it the extra star.   I doubled the batch and these were some of the easiest muffins to put together...putting the oil and eggs into one measuring cup, beat with a fork to break up the eggs and then filling up to the 1 cup line is ingenious...all the wet ingredients in just the one measuing cup!    For those who say the recipe is dry, I am wondering if they are just measuring out the 1/3 cup milk and not actually putting the oil and eggs in a measuring cup and then filling it to the 1 cup mark with the milk, as the recipe stated.  I definitely think that more than 1/3 cup milk is used...it will depend on how large your eggs are.  For taste, there is something sort of missing...I wonder if vanilla would do the trick....but I suspect that those who think something's missing might prefer the tanginess in sourmilk/buttermilk batters which are also a mainstay for blueberry muffins, banana bread and other quick breads.  I tasted the muffin batter raw (gasp!) and noticed right away that it was delicious, but not at all tangy.  Finally, I used just over 1/2 the sugar called for and I did up the blueberries a bit.  For me, full sugar would have been way over sweet...I would definitely cut out at least 1/4 cups of the sugar called for if your berries are sweet.

Excellent flavor, nice and easy. I substituted whole wheat pastry flour, half ev olive oil for half the veg oil, and half sucanat for half the sugar. I didn't have time for the topping, but instead sprinkled with cinnamon sugar. I used frozen wild blueberries, which are much smaller than normal ones, and while I think it worked better for the mini muffins, if you're a true blueberry freak like I am, you may want to use the big ones, so that you get that big burst of flavor and warm juice. Some of mine were crumbly upon removing from the pan, but that was just because we were famished and couldn't wait another minute for breakfast! The ones that stayed longer to cool were fine.

attributes.source_text: couldn't wait another minute for breakfast

reviews.review_text: These were soo good!!  I did make a few adjustments according to my tastes.  I added about 2 T. more sugar to batter and used a little less than 1 C. blueberries.  For the topping I decreased the flour to 1/4 C., the butter to 1/8 C. and only added a couple dashes of cinnamon.  The first time I made these the cinammon overpowered the muffins, I felt, and the extra butter made the topping kind of hard.  By making these changes to the topping it was light and sugary.  These were so easy and delicious I will make them all the time now from scratch!  Forget the store bought muffin mix!

reviews.review_text: These muffins are delicious. I did double the batter recipe and make big muffins. The topping recipe is enough without doubling. I didn’t change anything. The blueberries I used were very large and perfectly ripe. The only thing I will change for next time is to use liners in the muffin tin. With the large muffin tops the muffins are difficult to remove from the pan without liners. Oh one more tip- for baking in general really, if you don’t use pure cane sugar for all of your baking you should try. You will NEVER go back to regular white sugar!!

Works with fresh OR frozen berries (***see below for note)  These muffins are deliciously AMAZING.  Super easy.  A double-batch makes 21 muffins with a 2oz. scoop or 24 with 1 1/3oz. scoop.  2oz. scoop is equivalent to filling the muffin paper all the way to the top...this is my preferred size since it makes a very nice size muffin top!  A lot of reviewers pointed out them drying out if not eating on the first day.  I added 1/2 c. plain greek yogurt (or use sour cream) for a doubled recipe and it solved the problem.  They were still moist on day two.  However, the only one that lasted until day two was the muffin I specifically hid to test for dryness because these muffins were completely hoovered by my 4 boys and hubby.  :o)  A single batch of topping is sufficient for a double batch of muffins, IF you make the measurements just a teeny more generous.  Brown sugar tasted better than white...and always do, IMO for muffin toppings.  The butter for the topping makes a nicer texture and presentation if used "really soft" vs. "melted".  ***Re: fresh vs. frozen blueberries ...  If using fresh, roll in flour before you fold into the batter.  It will prevent the berries from sinking to the bottom during baking.  If using frozen berries, these will turn out just as amazing but there are a few steps to prepare the berries first (I've gone through a lot of trial and error about this.)  Take out the frozen berries and thaw in a strainer under luke warm water until the water runs clear.  Pat dry on paper towels very gently so as not to burst any berries.  Then, just like you do with the fresh berries, roll carefully in the flour to coat...they will be super fragile.  Gently fold into batter.  They will cook exactly like fresh berries and the batter will not be an icky color...it will stay white with the pop of bright juicy berries!  I love this recipe...it is my new go-to for berry muffins.  I can see it working well with ANY berry.

items.name: My Mama Iuliucci's "Don't Skip a Step" Spaghetti Sauce
items.description: My mom made this every Sunday for as long as I can remember. I recall coming home from wherever I was and smelling this incredible sauce! I would immediately reach for the Italian bread to start dipping before dinner. My mom always said it wasn't done yet, but I didn't care! My brother would go through a half a loaf of white bread with this sauce before dinner...it was that good. Try to make it exactly as it is written out...you will be pleasantly surprised and your house will smell heavenly! The little bit of extra work is worth it!!!
instructions: Combine tomato products in large stock pot or dutch oven.
Add a 28 ounce can of water and stir.
Bring to a boil and reduce to a simmer.
Sprinkle with sugar, salt, pepper, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, parsley and grated cheese and stir to combine.
In a frying pan, heat about 1/4\

reviews.review_text:
I have tried MANY sauce recipes and this is BY FAR the most delicious one I have ever used. I have gone to every website and tried their first three best recipes and none compare. For mine, I use one can of crushed tomatoes with basil, one can of crushed tomatoes in puree with basil and one can of puree (all Tuttorosso brand) and then just Hunt's tomato paste. The only difference in my sauce is I do throw in about a teaspoon of basil.
Also, for the absolute best meatballs, I use the Sunday Gravy (Real Italian Spaghetti Sauce)and Meatballs from this website (only the meatball recipe). After I cooked the meatballs, I browned up some chunks of boneless pork spare ribs and then I cooked up a few pieces of Italian sausage. I have found my recipes for keeps! This has always been my favorite meal but just never found the exact perfect recipes for me.

I made this tonight for the first time, along with Mama's meatballs, which I loved. I followed this recipe exactly, except I didn't add any other meats but some extra ground beef-aside from the meatballs-because my family loves meaty sauce, but I knew-correctly that they would be freaked out by the addition of the other meats-since we are by no means Italian, we are not familiar with that! LOL! I cooked it very slowly for about 4-5 hours, and by the time it was done, it was so thick it didn't come through the holes in a drain spoon! I loved the addition of the parmesan cheese-great addition. We were divided on the taste-some of us thought it was a little bland, some of us thought it was a great taste. I am divided on whether the taste was worth all the extra work, since I am one who usually opens a jar and doctors it-and I found this to be a lot of extra work. Time will tell! Thanks for the chance to try an authentic recipe!09/02/07 Update: The other day we went to a new upscale Italian restaurant in our town. I would swear they must be using your recipe! :) Theirs was a little saltier than when I made it, but otherwise the taste was identical.

reviews.review_text: Wow...wow and wow!!! I have company coming at the end of this month, so I will be making this recipe again to impress them!  Karen, my many thanks to your Mama!!!

My changes are as follows...I used 100 ounces of san marzano plum tomatoes that I puree'd, I added hot italian sausage and used  Kittencal's meatballs recipe.  I added way more garlic and seasoned with Garli Garni.  I used only 20 ounces of water and 1.5 cans of tomato paste.  I used 1 medium onion and deglazed my pan with 1/2 cup of red wine.   The smell, the taste, the texture...sheer perfection!!!  My husband is one of those guys that never veered from his families recipes and always asked "why look for a new one when this one is fine?"  He's now a total believer.  This is a 10 star from me.  Good gravy is hard to perfect...this is darn near perfect. reviews.review_text: Absolutely the best spaghetti sauce I have ever made...or tasted... by far!!!  I cut the recipe in half b/c I wanted to test out the recipe, but I should have known by the rave reviews that the sauce was going to turn out terrific.  Even though my BF and I had two huge helpings, we had plenty left over.  I followed the recipe as directed...used romano cheese in the sauce which gave it a richness I have never tasted in a sauce before.  Frying the onions and garlic in the oil I used to fry the meat-a-balls in really made the sauce out of this world.  I seemed to have a very large amount of oil in the pan after frying the onions and garic, so I scooped them out and added them to my sauce, but poured out the excess oil before using red wine to deglaze the pan. The drippings and reduction added to the sauce really put it over the top!  This is a keeper for life!  Thank you for sharing with all of us!

attributes.source_text: gave it a richness I have never tasted in a sauce before

reviews.review_text: Ymmy!! Just made today with the meat-a-balls, delicious!! I have been fairly incapable of making a good sauce for several years, I think I have reactive pans that always make it taste bad. However this I made in the slow cooker (ceramic insert) to avoid the issue...and absolutely amazing this was! I made as according to recipe (except 8 hours on low), including a chicken drumstick and 1 sparerib. I just now realized I had bought the pepperoni to put in, but totally forgot! Anyhow the sauce was perfect, no acidy aftertaste, just wonderful!! I highly recommend it! As for those of you concerned about the sparerib-my DH told me a few days ago he doesn't normally like the taste of it in sauce...however he had no idea I put it in anyway. I think it did add something to the sauce, but unless you leave large bits of meat in the sauce no one will be able to pick out the taste. I just made sure I removed it while he was not around to spy :) Thanks so much!!

attributes.source_text: no acidy aftertaste

reviews.review_text: Not so much work and at first taste the angels sang! Thank you thank you Mama Iulliucci where ever you are. I forgot the cheese but I tend to prefer it just on top anyway. This sauce is "clean" and fresh and so full of flavor. I browned pork rib tips (no spareribs avail) then tied them up in a cheesecloth to add to the pot, along with the chicken in a seperate pack as I'd already picked the meat off the bones and put in the sauce. Doing so made sure I didn't accidentally leave a bone in the sauce. The pork of course fell right off and those luscious bits of meat really enhanced the sauce! It's spectacular as is, as a dip for bread or cheese sticks, and I can't wait to try it over pasta with Mama's meat-a-balls! I can think of no reason to ever make any other sauce or to buy any. Make enough to have some on hand in the freezer and have happy meals while you listen to the angels singing with each bite.

attributes.source_text: The pork of course fell right off

reviews.review_text: OMG!  This sauce is delicious.  I made it exactly by the directions.  I found that my ribs and chicken fell off the bones and I had to fish the meat chunks and bones out of the sauce- so next time I might tie them up in cheesecloth, but maybe not.  I didn't chop the meat and add it back I just discarded the big hunks, but smaller pieces were left in.  I also made the Mama Luliucci's meatballs.  They were to die for.  I generally just use a frozen meatball but never again.  It took a little longer to prep than indicated- about an hour to get the sauce going and meatballs made, but this recipe makes enough to serve 4 and have plenty of leftovers for freezing.   Awesome recipe!

Oh so good!  I made these with Mama Iuliucci's meatballs.  I substituted beef stock for the water in step 2, and cooked up some finely shopped red bell pepper and mushrooms in with the onions and garlic.  I also subbed some grape jelly for the sugar (something my Italian neighbor always told me to do) and deglazed the pan with 3/4 c leftover red wine instead of water in step 11.  Everything was delicious- and my house DID smell amazing.  My elderly Italian neighbor scolded me several years ago for serving red sauce the same night I cooked it- so I made this in advance to let the flavors meld in the fridge.  I DID use some sauce the first night as a base for some french bread pizzas, it was soooooo good- My kids and DH keep asking when we are having the spaghetti!  Thanks for some great recipes!

reviews.review_text: We thought this was a great 5 star meal. I had never tried making my own sauce before. It was really easy to get together, and I did allow it to simmer for probably 6 or 7 hours until we actually ate dinner. I used all the optional meats, and I also made your meatballs to go into the sauce. My 1 year old LOVED the meatballs, and since they were simmered all day in the sauce they were so nice and moist. I had tons of leftover sauce and I don't know that I would even bother to buy spaghetti sauce again- a couple hours of cooking yields enough sauce to last us quite awhile. Thanks so much for posting the recipe.

reviews.review_text: This will forever be my favorite recipe to turn to wheneer i make spaghetti. This sauce is just pure excellence! its not too sweet like some sauces are, its got just the right sweet to mildness ratio and that is what makes a darn good sauce. i tend to cut back on a little less parm. cheese but thats just personal preference. i have made this sauce more than 5 times already and everytime i make this its tastes better and better and i always find more and more people wanting to come over for homemade spaghetti and meatballs. i tend to make this on a friday, cause then ill be able to beat my parents home from work and already have them a meal ready to eat and the house smelling like a classic mamma and pappa itallian restaurant. i plan to keep this recipe in my head (and stomach)forever. thank you karen for giving out this wondeful recipe that will be making so many families happy for a long time.

It has a robust flavor that mine was missing.  I had some sliced peperoni in the fridge which i added to it as well as my homemade meatballs.  The amount of sauce this recipe made allowed us to have different Italian style dishes every night for a week.  My hubby and son also really enjoyed it as well.<br/>Thanks for a great recipe, it is now in heavy rotation at our home.

reviews.review_text: MY BF decided he wanted to find a spaghetti sauce recipe and this is the one he chose. WONDERFUL. Directions/steps are easy to follow and the suggestions practical. We concur, it is a terrific sauce. It does make a lot. We had a hearty 4 portion meal, plus froze 2 1/2, 4 cup containers of it for future use. Since making and freezing last week, we have used 2 of the containers. We amped one up for more pasta with additional Italian sausage, mushrooms and pepperoni - which was terrific. And the second one we used as sauce for homemade pizza. That was the REAL test of this sauce. We sneaked it in on the picky 15 yr. old (who can spot even the most tiniest of onion bits a mile away). She enjoyed it as well. But we're not telling her it was the spaghetti sauce just in cases. lol

reviews.review_text: Hi Karen.  Don't even know if you still post on Food.com, but here's a review of your mother's sauce.  OUTSTANDING.  I have been making it for about 2 years now and apologize for not posting sooner.  I remember MY MOM making spaghetti sauce in a big, old kettle and it was excellent.  That was years ago.  Mom has passed away and I never got her recipe!!!  THIS is EXCELLENT.  Crazy as it may seem, it relaxes me to make it and ALWAYS brings back memories of my mom making HER sauce.  Thank you so much for posting this.  It's just hubby and I now as we are retired and away from our kids/grandkids.  BUT, I always make the ENTIRE recipe and freeze because even once thawed YOU CAN'T BEAT THIS SAUCE~~~!

I have never made sauce before. I live in Europe and the cost of quality jarred sauce is soooo expensive. So my motivation was the cost. It made three times as much for a third of the price. I followed it exactly with one exception. I used my hand blender to blend the crushed tomatoes because I do not like chunky sauce. 
I used a pork chop from dinner last night and the sauce is outstanding! The flavor makes you want to dip anything in it.
I keep walking by tasting. Thank god it makes so much. The smell is amazing. It was really quite easy to prepare and I am sure that my family is going to love what is left by the time that dinner rolls around!

I tripled this and made an enormous pot of sauce.  I love my own sauce, but thought it would be good to try something new.  I I followed this to the letter, added all the optional ingredients too.  As a mum of four small children, all four little plates were clean, one even licked their plate!  Perfect, don't change a thing.  My only thing I recommend is making a double, triple or quadruple pot and freeze in bags for sauce on hand.  If you are going to make such an effort - make lots!!!!  Thanks Karen, it tastes like the sauce at my Italian restaurant.

reviews.review_text: I followed this recipe exactly and it by far was the best I have ever had. I used pepperoni and two ribs and chopped them up at the end and added them back to the sauce. I also added a whole container of fresh mushrooms. I also used Mama luliucci's Famous Meat-A-Balls and it was all amazing together! I served with fresh salad and freezer bought bread sticks. Next time, I will add more garlic and a bit more salt. I had so much sauce left over I made baked Zitti and that was wonderful as well! P.S. I made this in a 7 qt crock pot and it fil perfectly.

items.label: Most Incredible No Fail Pie Crust
items.name: Most Incredible No Fail Pie Crust
items.description: This is absolutely the best pie crust I have ever used. It never fails me and always comes out flaky and perfect. This recipe is enough for 2 - 9" crusts.
instructions: Cut together flour, shortening and salt until it resembles small peas.
Combine the egg, water and vinegar and gradually add to flour mixture.
Stir just until moistened and a soft dough forms.
Divide into 2 disks.
Wrap and refrigerate until ready to use.
Roll out and use with your favorite pie recipe!

reviews.review_text: Before trying this recipe I was sold on the one that I used during culinary school.  The only problem was the recipe was scaled for 25 crusts.  I did manage to get it down to 5 crusts, but I only needed one.  So, I jumped onto food.com and spotted this one.  With all the reviews I decided to give it a go for a Rustic Spiced Caramel Apple Tart that I was making.  I used half butter and half lard instead of shortening (I only use shortening when I have no other choice), and it came out gorgeous.  It was easy to work with and baked up flaky and tender.  Now I have a new favorite crust recipe.  I made sure that all the fats that I used were cold, straight from the fridge.  Also, using a trick I learned in school, I made a glass of ice water and used that water(minus the ice) for this recipe.  If your kitchen is very warm, you might consider putting even your flour in the fridge or freezer to cool it down.  Above all, handle the dough as little as possible once you add the water.  Working the dough too much will develop gluten and cause a tough crust. You want to mix it just until it comes together, and there may be dry spots in the dough.  Simply wrap it in plastic and place in the fridge for 24 hours and the moisture level will even out.  I highly recommend using half butter and either half lard or half shortening, the flavor and texture will be perfect.

attributes.source_text: baked up flaky and tender
baked up flaky and tender

reviews.review_text: This was my first time making pie crust, because before this I didn't think I could. Now, I can go forth with confidence! Thank you so much for posting such an amazingly simple and tasty recipe. My crust turned out perfectly flaky. The only changes I made was to use just the yolk of the egg, 1/2 shortening, 1/2 lard and 1/2 flour and 1/2 cake flour. I also made this in my kitchenaid mixer, which was a lot easier to to clean and get the dough out of, than I think a food processor would be. It's taking all my will power not to have more than one piece of pie! The whole family loved it. I didn't have any issues working with the crust at all. Granted, when I was rolling it up on the rolling pin to put it in the pie tin, it did have some sticky areas. With careful scraping with a spatula as I went, that problem went away. I also put plastic wrap over the dough when rolling it. I also brushed the bottom crust with egg yolk and the top one after I put that on. I would really give this recipe 10 stars if I could.

attributes.source_text: My crust turned out perfectly flaky
The whole family loved it

reviews.review_text: This is a nice easy pastry recipe to put together. I have a very good recipe that makes 4 crusts but I needed one for only 2 and this will be my go-to for 2 for sure. I did have to use an extra tablespoon of water which I think is in part due to the fact that I live in a very dry climate. I let it rest for at least a couple hours before rolling it out and it rolled out easily. I also basted the crust with an egg/mild wash prior to putting in the apple filling I was using, this seals the crust from the inside and ensures that it bakes through and doesn't come out soggy. I used this pastry for a slab pie so baked it for 45 min or so @ 375 .. tu

attributes.source_text: doesn't come out soggy

reviews.review_text: Karen...this recipe is really no fail.  My challenge to myself was to perfect a homemade pie crust and I have not been successful until now.  Made it as directed substituting lard for the shortning.  Used the food processor to mix it all up.  Have to admit I was a tad nervous because the dough was so soft, but had faith in you :-)  Left the two portions wrapped in plastic in the fridge for about 4 hours.  By that time the dough was awesome.  Rolled them out on a lightly floured board.  Found the dough easy to work with and the amount was more than enough for an extra large deep dish pie plate.  I even had some left over for some nice decorative leaves, etc. on the top.  Brushed lightly with milk before baking my apple pie.  But the acid test was final appearance and taste.  The pie came out looking as though I had bought it at an upscale bakery and even though I baked it at 400 and then 375, the rim did not burn.  DH and I really analyzed the crust for texture, taste and mouth feel.  It earned 5 points on each.  This is now my only crust recipe.  Thanks so much for sharing.

I had never made a pie crust from scratch and was looking for something incredible and fail-proof...
This recipe turned out very well; a nice balance to some very sweet pies. I used half butter and half crisco buttersticks, cubed and frozen before mixing. I also used ice water, and let the dough rest, wrapped in plastic, in the fridge for a while (some is still resting in the fridge in case I get a sweet tooth). I roll it out between sheets of parchment paper as it makes transport of the rolled crust easier and also keeps the kitchen cleaner. It does get a little crumbly after resting, so I just wet my fingers and work it into the dough if it starts to crack while rolling. Thanks for sharing.

Several years ago, after many frustrating attempts to make a good pie crust like my mom's, I decided that I would only use store bought crusts.  As my cooking skills have improved, I've decided to give it another try.  This crust was quick to put together and pretty easy to work with.  I've discovered that even if it doesn't roll out perfectly, which for me it never does, it isn't that hard to make it look good in the end.  I agree with other reviewers that it is just a bit dry with 5 tbsps of water, but I didn't add more this time and it worked out fine - just slightly crumbly.  Next time I'll add just a few drops more.  My Thanksgiving pumpkin pie looks beautiful and I used the left over scraps and filling to make some bite sized pies that taste great!  This will definitely be a go-to crust for me!   Thanks and Happy Thanksgiving!

reviews.review_text: This is terrific! I've been using a recipe that calls for a mix of butter and lard, but with the cost of butter going through the roof, I thought I'd give this one a try. Well......this is going to be my standard recipe now. I made tarts, and even after reworking the dough several times, it still came out tender and flaky. My husband said that he will have to sit in the tub to eat them, just to keep the flakes at bay. Thanks Karen for a wonderful, wonderful recipe!!!! Forgot to mention... mixed it in the food processor. How easy is that!  *UPDATE* Mar 17/09  When I made this dough in Aug 08, I made a large batch and froze some.  Yesterday I removed one from the freezer, and thawed at room temperature.  Rolled out beautifully, with a sprinkling of flour on the counter.  Filled and baked as normal.  Well, let me tell you, this was even better than when it was freshly made.  The 'flake' was not to be believed.  Absolutely AWESOME recipe.  I'll never use anything else but this.  Thanks again Karen.

I used margarine for the shortening and 1/2 whole wheat flour for the flour and had to add more water to get it to all stick together.  Once it stuck together it was easy to roll out and I had quite a bit left and I had made the crust thicker than I normally do.  This makes a lot of crust.  So I made what my mom calls ding a lings.  Roll out the left over crust and sprinkle with cinnamon and sugar.  Then roll up and cut into pieces.  Bake these for 15 minutes along with the pie (don't forget about them).
This is a good recipe.  Thanks!

reviews.review_text: I really like this recipe!  I'm not good with doughs, especially when it comes to rolling them out.  This one worked perfectly and tasted great.  I used butter instead of shortening, but besides that followed the recipe.  Using the food processor to crumble the dry ingredients with the butter and then add the wet and pulse until combined made it super quick and easy and rolling it out worked like a dream.  I followed the suggestion of one reviewer and kept out 1/4 c. of the flour when mixing the dough and used it to flour the surface, rolling pin, etc.  I also did the trick of brushing the bottom crust with egg white before adding in my filling (chicken pot pie in this case).  I made a two crust pot pie and it turned out fantastic, even with a sub par filling (didn't make it from scratch).  I had enough extra dough to make a quick apple turnover of sorts.  It tasted great with both savory and sweet and I'll definitely use this as my go to recipe.  It was so quick and simple to make (and didn't require sitting in the fridge overnight, great even using it right away) that I'm planning to do a full apple pie tomorrow since one of my daughters didn't get to sample the mini one tonight.  Thanks for a simple, versatile, and delicious pie crust recipe!

Ok. I'll start off that I am VERY inexperienced in pie making...
I made mine using a food processor. Not sure if that's a no-no with this recipe or not.
I used the crust on an apple pie. I agree with other posts that this would be an excellent crust for savory pies, it wasn't sweet to go with the apples. I had to work with the dough A LOT to get it to roll out- I found it pretty crumbly, but once it warmed up a bit it rolled much easier.
The texture was incredibly flaky and tender, and you can't taste the vinegar at all. I think it was good that I used a crust with egg in it since I think it held together better while baking (DH enlisted me in the challenge of making a 16-apple pie like he saw on food network).
I think overall its a good crust, but a little bit hard to work with for us beginners.

reviews.review_text:
Excellent recipe!!! For several years, I have wanted to enter our local 4th of July Apple Pie contest. This year was the year...Or so I thought! First, I needed a recipe. :) I chose this for the pie crust and another recipe I found on another site for the filling. I spent the Sunday before the 4th making a trial pie at my parents' house. My dad kept stressing that an apple pie (or any pie, for that matter) is all about the crust. He wasn't that confident in my ability to produce a masterpiece, seeing as I hadn't ever made my own pie crust before.
In hopes of decreasing the risk of a soggy bottom crust,I brushed the bottom layer of the pie crust with egg whites before I put in my apple filling. I also brushed egg whites on the top of my lattice crust before baking.
When it came out of the oven, it looked perfect! After my dad had his FIRST slice, he proclaimed it the best pie he has had in 30 years!!! He said the crust was AMAZING!! My mom was raving about it as well! Fast forward to the next morning, the 4th...I decided I was too tired to wake up early...and thus, I still haven't entered a pie in a 4th of July contest...Next year!! :) My parents finished the pie in 3 days. Every time I speak to them on the phone, they ask when I will be making them another. Thanks for a great recipe!!
