items.label: Basil Cream Chicken
items.name: Basil Cream Chicken
keywords: c("Chicken", "Poultry", "Vegetable", "Meat", "European", "Very Low Carbs", "Kid Friendly", "< 30 Mins", "Stove Top", "Easy", "Inexpensive")
items.description: This is the easiest and one of the most impressive chicken dishes I make. Serve with grated parmesan at the table.
instructions: Saute chicken, onions, and mushrooms in oil for 4 minutes.
In lg saucepan, melt butter; stir in flour until smooth.
Add chicken broth, boullion and cream.
Stir in basil and pepper.
Bring to a boil; cook and stir for 2 minutes.
Combine with the chicken mixture.
Serve over fettuccini.

reviews.review_text:
OH MY GOSH PEOPLE!! This was AMAZING! I would give this 10 stars if I could!! If you love pasta with a rich & creamy flavour packed sauce this is the dish for you! I had some chicken that needed to be cooked and some leftover whipping cream from a dessert that I made for Thanksgiving, so I came in search of a pasta recipe and I am soooo glad I chose this one! The only thing that I did that was even slightly different was that I cut my chicken in strips instead of cubes and I used 2 tsps. dried basil because I didn't have fresh.
When I poured the sauce over the chicken mixture I found that I wanted it slightly thicker, so I whisked in a little more flour. I served over fettuccine as directed and it was to die for! Better than some pasta I have had in restaurants! Not the most heart healthy dish in the world but such a treat! And we were even extra naughty and grated fresh parmesan over it!!!!! I am already looking forward to making this again, next time with a nice bottle of white wine! Definitely one of the BEST dishes I have made from Zaar so far! Thanks so much for sharing this recipe...it's a winner!!

attributes.source_text: rich & creamy flavour packed sauce

reviews.review_text:
MizzNezz,
I get the wonderful turn once a month to host game night at my home.  Which entails my cooking, cleaning, supplying the drinks and of course, the board game.  Well, I took a chance with making this recipe with my brother being one of my guests.  The picky brat that he is(35 year old Research Scientist and chef extraordinaire) makes me cringe every time I cook because he will ALWAYS find something wrong with it.  Something is always missing, you know those types, right?
Well, I made this.  And what a HIT!  While I was boiling the water for the fettuccine, I sauteed the chicken, onions and mushrooms - oh I also added a diced clove of garlic in Olive oil.  Then while the fettuccine is cooking, I made the sauce.  Unfortunately, my grocer was out of fresh basil so I used dried.  I could not believe the compliments it received! This is definitely a keeper!  
Edit: Forgot to add that I also took the other cooks' advice and sprinkled FRESH parmesan cheese!

attributes.source_text: I get the wonderful turn once a month to host game night at my home
my brother being one of my guests

reviews.review_text: While DD didn't care for this dish, everyone else enjoyed it after a few changes.  I originally made it as written with the exception of being a little short on the heavy whipping cream so I had to top it off with a touch of fat free half and half to get the amount needed.  I also had to saute the chicken, onion and mushroom mixture longer than called for as it wasn't done when my timer went off.  I served it over spinach fettuccine.  We all felt it was lacking something.  So I topped it with shaved Parmesan cheese.  It still need something.  I added some garlic parsley and that did the trick.  We really enjoyed it this way.

Amazing!  I must have cut my chicken in larger chunks than the recipe calls for because it took my chicken more than 4 minutes to cook.  Actually, I browned the chicken first, then added the onions and mushrooms and cooked for about 10 minutes more.  The onions caramelized nicely.  I also felt the sauce was too thin.  Next time I'll reduce the amount of liquid since we only used about half of it anyways.  I used 1/2 tablespoon of "Better than Bouillon Chicken Base" instead of bouillon and Half & Half instead of whipping cream.  This is going in my Permanent Addition cookbook.

I made this the other day and to be honest I was not very impressed.  Thought it was on the bland side.  Figured I would write a review the next day or two.  Good thing I waited. I ate some of the leftovers the next evening and the flavors had really developed.  It went from a 2 star to a 4 star for me.  I wish I had left the chicken in the basil cream mixture sit longer the first day.  I think I plated it too quickly, plus I used dried basil.  I mixed the leftover fettuccini with the sauce and the fettuccini flavored very well throughout and did not get mushy, stayed very close to al dente. I will definitely keep this recipe.

attributes.source_text: did not get mushy
stayed very close to al dente

reviews.review_text: Tnanks to Juju Bee's pic and review, I knew we just had to try this!  And boy am I sure glad we did.  Only problem with the recipe was that I didn't have fetuccine, so plain old spaghetti was substituted and other than the texture of the pasta, I don't think it effected the recipe at all.  Used less mushrooms as it was only DS & I eating the dish and he's not a big fan of mushrooms, so they just went on my plate :)  Did the rest of the recipe to a "T" and would definately recommend making this dish as it's great comfort/winter warming meal to devour!  Thanks MizzNezz for a real winner and will be definately making again when DH is home for dinner!  Hope you don't mind the pic using the spaghetti, but I thought it would show how versitle this recipe is with the pasta choice.

attributes.source_text: when DH is home for dinner
great comfort/winter warming meal

reviews.review_text: Like others have already wrote this is definitely an excellent recipe. One thing i really enjoyed is the strong chicken flavor which was quite distinct. I can tell you just don't add any extra salt to the sauce until you taste it because the salt content was just right without adding any extra salt (an extra and it would have been to salty). My wife even loved this recipe and she, in general, does not like cream sauces.<br/><br/>If i had to say anything negative its just that i really didn't taste the basil that much. I will definitely add a lot more next time but even with that i think its a 5-star recipe. Thanks Inez for the recipe.

attributes.source_text: the strong chicken flavor which was quite distinct
the salt content was just right without adding any extra salt
My wife even loved this recipe

reviews.review_text: This is an absolutely delicious dish with a beautiful presentation. I had to tweak the recipe a little bit. I used one percent milk in the sauce because that was all I had on hand. It still tasted rich and delicious. I just had to thicken it a little longer. I used frozen cubes of freshly minced basil because I didn't have any fresh on hand. It was still very flavorful. I didn't have onion or mushrooms on hand and I blended some parmesan cheese and garlic into the sauce. Instead of cooking the chicken in oil, i marinated it in some fresh garlic and more basil and grilled it on my george forman grill. It turned out absolutely wonderfully! I loved the flavour that the basil and the chicken broth/bouillon gave. It definitely tasted like something one would order in a restaurant. I will be making it again very soon probably using the same substitutions I did this time.

attributes.source_text: It still tasted rich
I loved the flavour that the basil and the chicken broth/bouillon gave

reviews.review_text: Loved this recipe!  It was great.  I followed the recipe except that I used whole breasts and sliced them before placing on top of the pasta.  I thought there may be a strong onion taste but I used a sweet yellow onion and it did not  over power the other flavors.  I also seasoned the breasts with garlic salt prior to cooking and cooked them longer than the recipe stated.  This is fabulous and I can't wait to try some of the other additions that other people have recommended. Simply delicious!  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: I thought there may be a strong onion taste but I used a sweet yellow onion and it did not  over power the other flavors

reviews.review_text: Very good family dinner, served with garlic bread. I scaled this to 6 servings. I used half button mushrooms and half baby bellas and added 3 cloves of minced garlic. I was a little short on the whipping cream, so I subbed 2% milk for 1/3 of the cream. I also added 1/4 cup parmesan to the cream mixture before combining it with the chicken. It worked great. For my taste it could have done with less onion and maybe a little more basil, but my family and guests raved, so we will definitely make this again. Thanks for sharing.

attributes.source_text: Very good family dinner
my family and guests raved
my family and guests raved

reviews.review_text: Good basic pasta recipe.  I had to add salt, and you definitely need to sprinkle parmesan on the top before eating it.  I cooked the chicken breasts in some chicken broth first, then halved each one before adding them and cooking them with the main basil mushroom sauce towards the end.  Why does my fettuccine always stick together?????  My heavy cream had seen better days, so I had to use milk and extra flour instead.  Next time I will be sure to use the cream for more flavor.  Adding garlic like some other reviewers did sounds good.  The fresh mushrooms and basil make this dish stand out from other pasta dishes, although I used dried basil.

I made this recipe the other night and thought it was pretty good. The next day I reheated a small portion of it and it was bursting with flavor....a lot more than the previous evening. The flavors had married overnight and it went from pretty good to GREAT! Next time I will put the dish together ahead of time and let it set overnight or at least a few hours and then bake it just before serving. This will make it more flavorful and a great do ahead for a dinner party. Serve with a good Caesar salad and garlic bread.

After all the great reviews I had to try this.  I'm sure glad I did because it is exactly as promoted - easy, but impressive!  I used some low-fat half and half in place of the whipping cream because it is what I had on hand.  The sauce was still thick and creamy.  I used fresh lemon basil from my garden.  This is a very elegant looking, delicious  dish which would be perfect to impress company.  I served this with your Crusty Bread Salad #18964.  Very, very good meal.  Thank you for sharing this recipe.

attributes.source_text: The sauce was still thick
thick and creamy

reviews.review_text: This recipe was DELISH and so easy to make! I was even able to modify the sauce to make it dairy free! I used cashew cream instead of regular cream (1/2 cup cashews blended with 3/4 cups water until smooth and creamy - add more water if needed). I also had to use vegetable bouillon instead of chicken because that's all I had at home. I suggest increasing the chicken to 2 lbs and doubling the mushrooms because this makes a lot of sauce and it is excellent eaten as left-overs the next day. YUM!

I will have to try this one again, because I left out a very important ingredient -- the chicken boulion. I found the flavor to be very bland as we were eating it, and I realized I left that out. OOPS! I think it definitely needs the salt from the boulion. So that was my fault. Everyone still really liked it, but I'm sure it would've been much better with that ingredient. I did put Parmesan on top and that did help. Will try it again!

This is the second time I've made this recipe...my husband suggested we add bacon this time, so I snipped and sauteed 4 slices of center-cut bacon in the oil first.  When it was crispy, I drained it on paper towels and then added it back into the sauce with the basil.   My husband said it was a "restaurant-quality" dish!  Oh, and I served with with small shells...not as impressive-looking as fettucine, but they really captured the sauce well!  Thanks for the recipe!

attributes.source_text: My husband said it was a "restaurant-quality" dish!

reviews.review_text: Purty Good.  Filling.  Did everything as listed.  Thought that the sauce tasted like a can of Cream of Mushroom soup with some pepper & basil.  Actually, we smelled the basil more than we tasted it--fresh picked basil too.  Probably as a short cut you could make the sauce just using the can with some milk and flour to thicken it.  Agree with TheRealDealMeal that it took longer than 2 minutes to thicken the sauce, even then pretty thin. Thanks for sharing it!

This was truly fantastic MizzNezz! Thankyou so much my husband and I both said Mmmmm...throughout the meal. The only thing I changed was to add some sundried tomatoes, a splash of white wine and some garlic salt. I also thickened it a bit with a touch of additional flour. This is definitely a keeper and my DH said the house smelled like a Bistro. I served with Caesar salad and french bread with foccacia seasoning and mozzarella. Very Tasty!!!!

attributes.source_text: my husband and I both said Mmmmm...throughout the meal

reviews.review_text:
I made this tonight and followed the recipe and ingredients as written.  It was good but I have to agree with the reviewers who found it to be on the bland side.  Maybe I am just used to a lot more flavor.  My sisters liked it but my brother in law only ate half of it.  I might try it again with alot more basil and maybe some garlic.  I also thought the boullion flavor was more dominant than the basil so I was a bit surprised.
I enjoyed dipping Italian bread in it though and so did my sisters.

attributes.source_text: My sisters liked it

items.label: Basic Machine French Bread
items.name: Basic Machine French Bread
items.description: This is my winner with Tammiev and our friends. This recipe is for a 2 pound loaf and has never failed me. I think it is the lack of oil and sugar that they like in this one.
instructions: Add to the bread pan in the order yours needs.
For mine it is water first.
Then I add half the flour and the salt followed by the rest of the flour and the yeast on top.
This will run well on the normal, rapid, and delay start cycles.

reviews.review_text: FABULOUS!!! I rolled it out after the dough cycle like Diggy's review. Then I decided to make a spread of butter, garlic, and grated parmesan which I spread over the rectangle. Then sprinkled freshly grated parmesan cheese over that. I then rolled it up, and baked it on a pan brushed with olive oil for 30 minutes at 350. We only ate 1/3 of the loaf so sliced the rest and put it in the freezer. I will repost as to how it was warmed over. Thanks for a great recipe rickv. This will be a family favorite.  Note: We ate 1/4 of the loaf and I sliced the rest and froze it.  Then put it in the oven to reheat later.  It was equally as good.  Thanks again for a great recipe.

This is one AWESOME bread!  I made it on the dough cycle, and then took it out, rolled it out into a 15x8 rectangle and then rolled it up on the 15 inch sides.  Then I pinched the edges together to be "seamless" and then rolled it back and forth, gently, to taper the ends (bring to almost a point) and then put it on a greased baking sheet with a little cornmeal.  I put a few slits in the top about 1/4 inch deep and brushed on a little bit of cold water all over the top of the loaf.  Let it rise for another hour and then used 1 egg white to brush over the top of it, and then baked it at 350 for 25-35 minutes (when it was a golden brown and sounded hollow when I thunked it).  This turned out to be one of the best tasting loafs I have ever had!  I will make this again and again....no more buying french bread for me!!!

I used the flour I had lingering in the back of the pantry. You know the one: you think it came with the house. It was 3g of protein a serving but I used it because that's what I had. I cooked it in the bread maker instead of rolling it out and it was great. For the record, my order was: water first, flour, salt and yeast on top. I set it for french, rapid (I was in a hurry), and light on the crust. The hardest part of this was getting it out of the breadmaker's tray. The second hardest part was trying to cut it without smooshing it down. Very good. Very easy. No eggs or milk (which the mixes had). Fantastic! Thank you so much for posting it! Served this with minestrone soup (#77585).

They say that bread making is a science...   and I can tell you now that just THAT little bit of flour or salt... or NO oil.. makes a huge difference. I've been experimenting for a while now with different bread recipes and you'd think that just a 1/4 cup of this or a 1/4 tsp. of that wouldn't change it much... well... let me tell you..   it is a difference of great proportions in taste. This is THE recipe ........  I made 3 different recipes today (for the football playoff game) (each has been reviewed here previously) and hands down.. this is the winner. I didn't bake this in the machine.. I split it into two long loaves and baked at 400° for about 25 minutes (I sprayed the oven with a spritz of water when I put them in).. Thanks for a taste that we've been searching for. I think I need to bake it a bit longer for a crispier crust. YUM.. :-)<br/>UPDATE: 11/06/13 This is still a terrific recipe. I've replace one cup of whole wheat flour for a cup of white bread flour and added a little Vital Wheat Gluten. I made two baguettes and they turned out beautifully.

attributes.source_text: for the football playoff game

reviews.review_text:
I wanted a recipe to use my 4-grams-of-protein-per-1/4-cup-serving flour (King Arthur's Sir Lancelot high-gluten flour) that said *only* to use in ABM because it's so tough to knead.  After 5 minutes of mixing, I checked on this loaf (I needed to add three more splashes of water, but high protein flour does need more water).  After the additional water worked in, I checked on it again by poking it.  The crucial water-to-flour ratio was right, but I could also tell that this dough would be a beast to knead by hand.  It felt very TOUGH and CONTRARY.  [This is due to the flour, not the recipe!]  In fact, when my dough cycle was over, I told it to start over so the bread machine did the second kneading for me too.  Yes, the dough was that tough.  I was relieved that it rose well both times.

After the machine kneading, I shaped it into a log and placed it in a stoneware french bread baker to rise once more then bake.  Since the dough was so difficult, I was pleasantly surprised at the final results.  The crust is chewy (I could have softened the crust by letting it sit in the cooled oven overnight, but my mom prefers chewy bread), yet the bread is remarkably soft.  I think of french bread as being chewy all the way through, and this isn't, but the results are quite nice.

I suspect I could have had results closer to thicker-crust all-chewy french bread if I had put a pan of water in the oven while baking.  But then again, this recipe turned out so nicely, I'm not sure I need to mess with a good thing!

attributes.source_text: The crust is chewy
the bread is remarkably soft

reviews.review_text: This was delicious and very easy, once I quit trying to overcomplicate it. Since it was "French" bread I set up the frenc bread setting on my bread machine and tried that. The first loaf rose high then fell during the baking. But it tasted great- just ugly. I tried again because it was so good and made the house smell wonderful- this time with new flour and new yeast (just in case that was the problem). Same thing happened and then I noticed that the recipe does NOT say to use a french bread setting. So I tried again with the regular basic bread setting and Success!! Delicious and I will make again because I have a LOT of yeast to use up and we loved this recipe for it's simple ingredients.

I can't get enough of this bread!  I will be making this often.  I did as Miss Diggy instructed, put it in my bread machine for the dough cycle, rolled it out, shaped it into a long loaf, let it rise for another hour, brushed with egg and then baked it.  It made a very large loaf so next time I think I will make it into two loaves.  The ingredients were just right for my bread machine, I didn't have to add any thing, the dough came out looking like a dream.   It is such a simple sturdy bread, I can't get over how much I like it, I keep going back and cutting myself another slice!

attributes.source_text: such a simple sturdy bread

reviews.review_text:
Really great bread.  I always use my bread maker to make dough and then bake it in my oven.  This recipe made three baguettes which I baked in my baguette pan (a specialty pan with holes throughout to make nice crusty bread).  The dough was really nice and firm and very easy to work with.  For the baguettes, I rolled 1/3 of the dough into a 15x4 inch rectangle and rolled on the diagonal.  Then I just rolled it by hand to an even roll with tapered ends.  I also made the characteristic slices on the diagonal of the bread.  I baked at 350 degrees for about 25 minutes.
Thanks for a great recipe.

attributes.source_text: to make nice crusty bread

reviews.review_text: My dinner guests gave it rave reviews!  I used bread flour and the "French Dough" setting on my ABM.  I rolled it into a 6x16 rectangle on a lightly floured surface, then folded the long sides in toward the center.  I flipped it over and cut four slits in the top and let it rise for an hour.  I baked it at 350 for 35 minutes and let it cool.  I then sliced the top off and buttered both sides, sprinkled on some garlic powder and shredded parmesan, and threw it back in the oven at 400 for ten minutes.  The HUGE loaf was gone before I could blink my eyes!  My guests told me they'll be expecting this every time, and I will enjoy making it again and again!

attributes.source_text: My dinner guests gave it rave reviews!
My guests told me they'll be expecting this every time

reviews.review_text: YUM!  I used my dough cycle for this.  When it was done, I oiled my hands to prevent sticking and kneaded it a few times.  Then I shaped it into 12 rolls and put on a cookie sheet. (I should have oiled the cookie sheet!) I covered them with a tea towel and let rise for 30 minutes.  At this point, I also turned the oven on to 450F and let it start heating.  After 20 min., I added a pan of water.  After the rolls had risen, I put them in for 10 minutes, turned the heat down to 400F and left them in for another 10 minutes.  Perfect!  Soft nice texture inside, crusty outside.  Thank you for posting!

attributes.source_text: Soft nice texture inside
crusty outside

reviews.review_text: My dog LOVED your bread. She ate more than I did. I baked this wonderful loaf, left it cooling on the kitchen table, ran some errands, and when I came home, the crust was gone and the bread was on the floor. I had a slice before leaving and my dog looked so guilty when I walked in, I couldn't be mad at her. Take that as a compliment. :) The only problem I had is this bread broke the motor on my bread maker during the kneading cycle. It was really heavy and thick and kept pulling the kneading blade out of place. Now, the machine motor is not working. Just wanted to warn others, if your machine has a hard time kneading this bread, pull it out before it's too late.

JUst made this this morning and all I can say is THANK YOU!  This is so easy to prepare in the bread machine.  I did your recipe on dough cycle, then let sit for a bit, rolled into 2 small small loaves about 15 in each and put in oven for 30 min at 350 degrees.  Fabulous.  I am now making a 2nd batch so I can make a regular loaf of french bread and then my 3rd batch YES 3rd will be made into sandwich shaped bread right in the machine.
Thank you for such an easy and simple recipe to follow that uses on hand materials.

Great and easy bread!  I made the dough in the bread machine.  I added in between two layers of flour a few cloves of garlic, some italian herbs and 3/4 tsp sugar.  After the dough was finished I shaped it into a cob loaf, let it rise 10 minutes then cooked it at 375 for 35-40 minutes.  I made it a little high though, when it rose it rose straight up!  But it worked well as a bowl for my hot bread dip :)  Next time I might make bread rolls.  We made another one in the bread maker as the dipping bread on the French setting and it was excellent as well.

attributes.source_text: a few cloves of garlic
some italian herbs

reviews.review_text:
FABULOUS and PERFECT!!! This is my second time making this recipe. I use the bread machine for the first hour (roughly the dough cycle, I got the machine without instructions)
I then pinch the dough in half and make long shaped loaves, no rolling or pinching  like ms diggy, I couldn't figure that out... just quickly shaped into long loaves... cut slits, brushed lightly with cold water, rise for 25 min or so, egg wash, at 375 for 25-30 min. My hubby and I ate both loaves in 3 days last time!!!!! THANK YOU!!!!!! I'll keep this recipe forever!

attributes.source_text: My hubby and I ate both loaves in 3 days last time

reviews.review_text:
I make this all the time following Diggy's recipe.  It comes out nice and crispy.  Well, yesterday I ran out of eggs, so I used half and half as the prebake wash.  I baked it for 20-25 minutes, and when I took it out of the oven, I melted butter on top of it.  Then I returned it to the oven, placing it directly on the oven rack, and left it for 3-5 more minutes.  
This is the softest bread ever!
So if you want a soft bread, I would suggest the cream wash, if you want a crispy crust, go with the egg wash.  They are both great.

attributes.source_text: It comes out nice and crispy
This is the softest bread ever!

reviews.review_text: Used the 'dough cycle' only on the machine.  Then I shaped 4 long hoagy loaves to use for French-Dip Sandwiches.  I used a hint suggested in another French bread recipe.  I put a 9 x 13 inch pan with hot water on the rack below the rack which held my large rectangular bread stone covered with parchment paper.  I then baked for about 30 minutes at 350 degrees.  It was very tasty and the hot water in the oven helped to make a more crisp crust.  I don't like my loaves too soft when using them for dipped sandwiches.  Good Recipe.

attributes.source_text: helped to make a more crisp crust

reviews.review_text: This was FABULOUS!  My husband wanted to make french toast for the kids this morning but we didn't have the right kind of bread in the house.  I went in search of a bread machine recipe that could cook in the machine during the night and came across this one.  I baked this on in my machine and set the timer to be ready for 6:30 this morning.  FABULOUS!  I almost hated to waste this on french toast but it made a great french toast AND the bread alone was perfect!  Why buy it in the store when it could be made so incredibly at home?  THANK YOU!!

I pulled my breadmaker out of storage( it is 5 years old and used only about 4 times... I always make my bread by hand) well I could not find my owners manual/recipe book. Wow I really had a problem!!! My loaf exploded!  It finished off like a spent volcano! Yikes!  I won't rate this but WILL try it again as soon as I get ahold of a manual for order of ingredients etc.  I have a B & D horozontal, in case you or any one else has an idea where to get this info.  I will use try baking in the oven next time :) will update later

I cooked mine in the machine and I was sure it wasn't done and I'd ruined it because it didn't look cooked.  I think I used a light setting.  Anyway, I dumped it out and it was crispy all around.  I let it cool a little then sliced it and it was perfect.  This morning I had some toast for breakfast and it was WONDERFUL.  I couldn't believe the texture and flavor.  You will love this.  I'm sure baking it in the oven vastly improves it's appearance but as lazy as I am, I will just slice it before I let anyone see it. lol

attributes.source_text: it was crispy all around
for breakfast

items.label: Blender Quiche - or Whatever You Have in Your Kitchen Leftover
items.name: Blender Quiche - or Whatever You Have in Your Kitchen Leftover
items.description: The great part is you can use whatever leftovers (well...almost) you have on hand. This dish can be served hot or cold. Freezes very well! Use any cheese of your choice.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Generously grease a 9 inch pie pan.
Spread shredded cheese across bottom of pie pan.
Cover cheese with meat and vegetables.
In a blender, combine eggs, baking mix, salt, garlic powder, onions, parsley, and milk.
Blend until smooth, then add olive oil.
Blend until combined, then pour mixture over meat and vegetable layer.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake in preheated oven for 40 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes before serving.

reviews.review_text: Very good! My husband loved it (and he is sooooo picky, so that's really a compliment) and I liked it very much and will make it again.  It was delicious the next day cold too! I like the ease and versatility of this recipe.  I was a little short on supplies the day I made it so here are my few changes: I used 2 parts swiss cheese, 1 part cheddar and tossed 1 1/2 T of a good quality freshly grated parmesan cheese thru it.  For meat and veggies, I used only bacon and sliced canned mushrooms and spring (green) onion.  We use 2% milk in this house so I used 1 1/4 c of the 2% milk, and 1/4 c of heavy whipping cream.  Instead of dried onion flakes, I sliced the two green onions into thin rounds, including about 1 inch of the green section of the oven. I sauteed 1/2 of the onion in the bacon grease very lightly and drained well. The rest of the onion I tossed into the recipe raw. I would suggest doubling the amount of green onions I used, to anyone wanting to use them in this recipe. Can't wait to try this with even more goodies packed into it.  Thank you for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: My husband loved it

reviews.review_text: I absolutely love this recipe!  This one is a keeper!  I made it for a church "pot luck", and was asked for the recipe twice!  I did make changes, because I didn't have everything, but that is the beauty of this recipe, you can alter it to suit you!  I didn't use a blender, I used an electric hand mixer.  I doubled the recipe and used about 2/3 cup of baking mix (I used pancake mix), and added 2 more eggs instead, because I like mine more eggy than doughy.  I used broccoli, and about 1/2 cup of chopped green bell pepper.  I used 2 cans of Hormel Canned Ham, the flaky kind, kind of like a can of tuna.  I used less onion flakes b/c I was out, but I personally think it would be better with sauteed real onion, instead of onion flakes.  YUMMY!!

attributes.source_text: I made it for a church "pot luck"

reviews.review_text:
This is a GREAT recipe! We modified it quite a bit and it turned out yummy! Whatever you have is right!

My sister and I sliced up a few fresh snap peas, finely chopped a carrot and a bit of onion. We sauteed the veggies in some margarine until tender. We used chopped, sliced deli ham. We didn't have quite enough cheddar, so we also used some mozzarella. We didn't have baking mix, so we substituted pancake mix. Instead of fresh parsley, we used dried. I forgot the paprika. Instead of one pie pan, we filled 12 muffin cups and they were about 3/4 - 7/8 full before baking. We baked them for 38 minutes. They didn't overflow and filled the cups nicely.

Turned out beautiful and delicious! I'm going to freeze the leftovers as Queen Zan suggested. Thank you, Tish!

Oh Tish!  I've been meaning to write you about your quiche!  This is going to be a big help for my husband and me since we've gone on a low carb diet!

I don't know, maybe I used too much filling, but I had to use a 10 inch deep dish (2") pyrex pie pan.  And I had to bake it for a full hour.

But this is a wonderful recipe and definitely a keeper!

Today I used:
8 oz ground beef browned with 2 tablespoons of Taco Seasoning. 
I used 4oz of cheddar cheese, 
1 4oz Can of diced green chilies and a small garlic clove instead of the garlic powder.  
Also, I didn't need the oil.  I used it the first time and it did make the crust crisp and gave it a nice texture - but I'm trying to omit where I can. 
I also tried using less egg yolks and more egg whites but the flavor just wasn't there - so 3 eggs it is!

This is going to be great for our breakfast!  

Good job!

attributes.source_text: it did make the crust crisp
This is going to be great for our breakfast

reviews.review_text:
What's a review without details of one's own variation? I used leftovers of three cheeses -- Swiss, Cheddar and Mozzarella -- as well as nearly old fresh spinach, a can of sliced mushrooms and, since I had no leftover meats in the house, sprinkled real bacon pieces (bought for salads), about 2 T. Had to eyeball making the baking mix, as we've not yet unpacked any measuring spoons/cups yet! YUM YUM YUM. Too bad no one's home yet to share it, but I'm saving some, don't worry ...

Thanks! I have a feeling this will appear in many different versions in my home from now on. AND it's easy enough for my elementary aged children to create their own masterpieces.

I made this with spinach, mushrooms, and zucchini.  I got carried away with the veggies as I always do, so I reduced the ham to keep the total volume of veg   meat the same.  It didn't fly.  I like my meal proportions to lean heavily to vegetables, so that wasn't the problem.  I think this recipe works best with tastily-spiced leftovers, not starting with unseasoned fresh ingredients.  Still, what I made was good enough to eat, and tasty enough to try variations on it later.  Cheese on the bottom ended up a lot like crust ... I could see mixing everything (but more heavily seasoned, possibly with less baking mix or none if veggies are well-drained) and pouring it in a crust for yummy!  This recipe is a framework, so it should always be a work in progress; and for that, it's a great start!

attributes.source_text: Cheese on the bottom ended up a lot like crust

reviews.review_text: Made this for supper tonight - used 1/2 cup each diced onion & green pepper sauteed in bacon fat, then added some finely chopped mushrooms & crumbled bacon until heated through.  I used a mixture of shredded cheddar, co-jack & parmesan for the cheese crust - spread the onion mixture on top of the cheese, and topped that with some chopped tomatoes before adding the egg mixture.  The quiche came out a little too mushy, but might have been from the extra moisture from the tomatoes.  Had good flavor though - basically a Denver omelette in a pie dish.  DH didn't care for it (mostly due to the texture), so I will probably chop up the rest of the quiche, scramble it with an extra egg and make breakfast burritos out of it.  Not sure if I will make this again, but it was a quick & easy recipe.  Thanks for posting. -M =)

attributes.source_text: Made this for supper tonight

reviews.review_text:
These turned out great and were very easy to make.  I did add some powdered chicken bouillon (soup base works great, too) to the blender when I whipped up the mix, and it added a light, delicious underlying flavor.  I also used a premade crust bottom instead of the cheese bottom.  I just prebaked the crust for 10 minutes in the pie pan, then added the ingredients & egg mixture.

I used many different combinations of ingredients and found the basic recipe to be completely versatile.  I got rave reviews from everyone who tried them at the baby shower.  My combinations:

--Lorraine (ham, crumbled bacon, and italian cheese)
--Greek (feta, sliced black olives, diced tomato, red onion, parsley)
--Veggie (green & red pepper, red onion, cheddar cheese)
--roast potato & garlic chicken-sausage with onion & italian cheese

attributes.source_text: at the baby shower
it added a light, delicious underlying flavor

reviews.review_text: I hesitate to post a review since I really didn't follow this recipe...I just used what I had, but I think that's the point of the recipe. I used a bit of leftover cornish hen meat, left over spinach, only 1/4 cup of olive oil, omitted the parsley, and used pancake mix for the baking mix. The cheese I used was mild cheddar that was left over from taco salad night. I also got to use up the last of the milk that was about to expire. I was super happy to use up all these things but a little concerned about how it would actually taste. It was awesome. Definitely not what I would serve as a real quiche, but great for leftovers. My husband ate 3 large pieces!

attributes.source_text: My husband ate 3 large pieces!

reviews.review_text: What a fabulous "get rid of leftovers" recipe!!!  I had leftover steamed broccoli and was searching the internet for something to do with it, but everything had cans of cream soup or cups of mayonnaise as ingredients... too heavy and fattening for my tastes!  So, when I stumbled upon this recipe I thought it would be worth a try.  I used my leftover steamed frozen broccoli, and chopped it in small chunks, grated some fresh carrots into it and set it to the side.  Then I sauteed diced onion and diced deli smoked ham till the onions were soft.  Mixed this with the carrot and broccoli mixture, and spread it over the cheddar cheese in the pie plate.  I don't care for "baking mix" so I made my own...  flour, baking powder, salt, and butter (i'm anti shortening).  Also, I had made pastry cream the week before and still had all the egg whites left over, so I used that.  Only had skim milk, so this recipe was extra healthy!  Mixed in the chopped fresh parsley from my garden and the spices.  Poured over and sprinkled with paprika and a little more cheese.  Baked for 40 minutes, but I don't think that was long enough, as it was still a little gooey on the inside... or it could be from the skim milk and egg whites being too much liquid in the mix.  Either way, I'll adjust next time accordingly.  Thanks for a great recipe I'll use again and again!  ****Love this recipe!! Just made it again using hot Italian Turkey sausage, potatoes, onions, mushrooms, sharp cheddar cheese, and garnished with paprika and scallions.  Yummy!  The only thing I will say against the recipe is that I think its silly to put the cheese at the bottom of the pie plate... it dissipates that way and you don't get the cheesy goodness of a real quiche.  I did layers of cheese in this one, and it's in the oven now smelling amazing!  Try this recipe and adapt it any way you like!!! THANKS FOR A LIFESAVER RECIPE!!!

Update: green Chile onion sausage....as muffins...LOVE THIS RECIPE.  I needed something for a last minute breakfast at work function and this was PERFECT!  I used muffin pan as suggested in other reviews.  Had fresh spinach so I sauteed that down in garlic-infused olive oil and also added in mushrooms, chicken, and bacon.  As others recommended, I put a smidge of cheese on top just before paprika.   I also used skim milk and reduced fat Bisquick.  12 muffins total - recipe's total calories 1680 -- so 140 cals per muffin.  I also reduced baking time to 37 minutes (did 35 and then another 2) due to use of muffin pan.  I will definitely be making again!

attributes.source_text: a last minute breakfast at work function
a last minute breakfast at work function

reviews.review_text:
I totally forgot to add my zukes, but I doubt it would have made much difference.  The result was a delicious quiche that I will try again.

I gave this recipe 5* for taste, but 3* for looks.  I think I prefer the look of a quiche with a crust and without Bisquick.  With this recipe, I think zapping the Bisquick and oil and substituting a pie crust will work, and I'm trying that the next time.

Thank you, Tish, for a lovely lunch today (and the rest of the week).  I forgot to add the sun dried tomatoes I asked about, so next time, I'll do the zukes and tomatoes and see what happens.

attributes.source_text: for a lovely lunch today

reviews.review_text: The flavour of this quiche was very good.  I used leftover turkey, 2 strips of precooked bacon, broccoli, a combination of old and mild cheddar cheeses, and instead of the oil I used about a tablespoon of butter.  While we all really enjoyed the flavour, the texture wasn't something that was enjoyed.  I will continue to use the filling but put it in a regular pie shell instead of using Bisquick.  ****I made this again last week when I was running short of time and cooked the quiche a little longer.  The texture was much better, lighter and fluffy, than my previous attempt.  So if you are not happy with the result, perhaps you may wish to cook it a little longer.  Thanks again Tish for posting.

attributes.source_text: lighter and fluffy
lighter and fluffy

reviews.review_text: This recipe is going in my desperation meal cookbook.  I had a 1/2 C. leftover biscuit mix that I didn't know what to with, 1 leftover chicken breast that I didn't know what to do with, and a 10 oz. pkg. frozen spinach.  This recipe was the perfect solution.  So easy and very frugal!  I used my Kitchenaid to mix it because my blender is not working.  I omitted the paprika and added 1/4 t. ground nutmeg and fresh ground pepper to the spinach mixture since I love nutmeg with spincah.  It tasted awesome - not at all like a throw together meal, hence the 5 stars.  Thanks!!!

Made this for dinner one night for me and my guy while we were kidless for the evening.  There were no leftovers as he ate what was left the next morning.  I love the no crust aspect of it and i really did throw a lot of things in it.  I did bacon crumbles and then in the grease I sauteed some onion, ham, green and red peppers and at the last bit some fresh spinach.  I did not have a pie pan so I used a small square casserole dish and I did have to bake extra long but also i did have a lot of fillings in it.  It was easy and oh so tasty! The boyfriend has been asking for it every week since we had it!

attributes.source_text: Made this for dinner one night
The boyfriend has been asking for it every week since we had it!

reviews.review_text: I liked this recipe alot because it is easy and uses what we have on hand.  I used 1/2 onion, 1/2 green pepper, and a small fresh tomatoe.  I sauteed the onion and green pepper in butter and added tomatoe and 1 tsp. minced garlic at the end.  I mixed the other ingredients in my food processor along with 1 tsp. italian seasoning.  I used mozzarella instead of cheddar.  I sprinkled a little asiago cheese on top of the mozzarella.  I omitted the garlic powder and onion flakes.  When I took this out of the oven, it is true that it wasn't real firm.  After it was in the fridge overnight, though, it firmed up.  Yum.  Excellent recipe.

attributes.source_text: it firmed up

reviews.review_text: We loved this as a light meal to eat on a hot night.  I changed it, I didn't put any meat in it, or zucchini.  What I did was used fresh chopped carrots and beans, frozen peas and corn (all cooked).  Also I sauted chopped capsicum, onion and garlic.  I didnt use the baking mix, I merely tossed the vegie mix through a very small amount of plain flour, enough to coat them.  This is a very good substitute for baking mix.  I also used 4 eggs as we needed to use them up.  All in all a good base to start with and work with.  Thanks for posting.

I found this recipe to be amazing . I had never made quiche before and I was happy with how simple it was to make. I didnt quite understand what baking mix was so I used bisquick. I also had no vegtables in the house except frozen corn and the only meat I had was what was left from my Quiznos sandwich that day. I used real onion instead of flakes and still came out with an amazing supper that my husband couldnt keep his hands off. I guess that proves this really is the leftovers quiche and nomatter what you use its definitly something to add to your cookbook

attributes.source_text: came out with an amazing supper
my husband couldnt keep his hands off

reviews.review_text: Thank you for this terrific quiche. I used bacon for the meat and sauteed some zucchini and mushrooms for the vegetables. (I didn't have any leftover veggies) The taste and texture were great. I would, however, recommend a pan a little larger than a 9-inch pie pan for a single recipe. The pan was very full and difficult to get into the oven without spilling. I've already given this recipe to my sister for a brunch she is planning.  UPDATE:  I have made this many, many times, and we always enjoy it.  I've found, however, that fresh mushrooms can be used without cooking them first, and they are delicious.  Just wanted to let everyone know.

items.label: Cornbread
items.name: Cornbread
items.description: I love tasting different cornbread recipes, and I have to admit, I think this is the best that I've ever tasted. Usually I have to put tons of butter on it, because it's so dry and just doesn't have much taste to it, but this recipe is very moist, and you can eat it alone, it's got a great sweet taste to it. Try it...and let me know what you think. Thanks to Betty Crockers Big Red Cookbook for this great recipe.
instructions: Heat oven to 400³F.
Grease bottom and side or round pan, 9x1 1/2 inches, or square pan, 8x8x2 inches, with shortening.
Beat milk, butter and egg in large bowl with hand beater or wire whisk.
Stir in remaining ingredients all at once just until flour is moistened (batter will be lumpy).
Pour into pan.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown and toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Serve warm if desired.

reviews.review_text: I took the suggestion to cut the sugar (in half in my case) and use two eggs. I also replaced 1/4 cup of milk with butter milk, and added 1 teaspoon(ish) of ginger (that could probably be bumped up to 1 tbsp add some Old Bay). Since I was cooking in a cast iron skillet out in the smoker, I fried 2 strips of bacon first, crumbled that into the batter, then poured the batter back into the hot skilled and fried for about 5 minutes before transferring to the smoker. It turned out pretty good, but the lesson to be learned from this is let just get a kiss of smoke for no more than 5 minutes then cover to prevent discoloration. It seemed especially fluffy, probably from the buttermilk. Overall everyone liked it and I'll be making this again.

attributes.source_text: It seemed especially fluffy

reviews.review_text: Look no further -- this is an amazing cornbread recipe. Didn't want to run to the store for buttermilk, so I landed on this one because I had all the ingredients. A couple of considerations: I saw the suggestions for adding bits of bacon and corn, and the suggestion for baking it in a cast iron skillet -- so I did all 3! Amazing. I first fried up the bacon in the cast iron skillet then took out the bacon and left the bacon grease in the skillet. I made the batter, added the chopped up bacon and some corn, then I poured the batter in the skillet until the edges were starting to separate from the skillet and I transferred to the oven for about 17 minutes. The edges were crisp and it was very moist!

attributes.source_text: The edges were crisp
it was very moist

reviews.review_text: This has become my go to recipe for cornbread. Takes all of 10 minutes to mix up and 25 minutes to bake. I use a wire whisk. I do reduce the sugar and add one additional egg, as I like to add sweetness through honey or jam depending on what its being paired with (i.e. BBQ Ribs, Chili, eggs for breakfast with sliced avocado sprinkled with fresh ground pepper, salt and olive oil drizzle). Additionally, I've used Almond milk as a substitution for regular milk and it tastes the same (be weary of nut allergies of course). I find it keeps for about 3 days on the counter covered...I do suggest if not eating it right after its prepared, slice up and throw it on a grill pan to toast it up!

Whoa BABY! I've been looking for a recipe like this for so long...

It was moist, held together well, it cut well, it crisped on the bottom but didn't get too done in the middle and best of all, it was hands down the best tasting cornbread I have ever eaten. We eat beans and rice once a week and I will be making this every week now that I have found it. I'm not kidding..you can stop looking! This is it.

I used a cast iron skillet that I heated on the stove and greased with shortening. This did result in a crispy bottom but didn't really shorten the cooking time (oddly enough). I used stick margerine. I was concerned about how much sugar was in this recipe. I thought it would be too sweet but it was PERFECT. LOVE IT. Thank you for posting this!

attributes.source_text: It was  moist
it crisped on the bottom
I thought it would be too sweet but it was PERFECT
This did result in a crispy bottom

reviews.review_text: I read every single review before I made this...I love to read what others have done, and much they did or did not like it! This was my second time ever making cornbread. First time was from a mix, which I did not care for at all. This tastes even better than my grandmother's recipe, which is saying a lot, because was a southern woman, born in 1906. She used to heat the shortening in her cast iron frying pan on the stovetop on very high heat, then pour the batter into it. There would this huge roar of sizzling sounds! Then she'd pop it into the oven to bake. That was her secret to a beautiful, crispy crust! I didn't have a cast iron pan, so I used a round cake pan. I chose to what many others here did, and used only 1/4 cup of sugar, and two eggs. Other than that, I followed the recipe exactly. It turned out beautifully! So moist, with just the right amount of sweetness and beautiful golden crust! Thanks to everyone who took the time to review this recipe...I will never need another! ?

attributes.source_text: with just the right amount of sweetness
So moist
beautiful, crispy crust

reviews.review_text: First time I made this it turned out terrible. Dry, flavorless, not sweet at all and I think I figured out why. I doubled the recipe and I think I may have forgotten to double the sugar, so to see if that was the case I made this again, just a single batch this time and it was very very good. Very moist, just enough sweetness but I think I could add a bit more sugar and like it a bit more as well. Only problem is that Im noticing the taste of the baking powder coming through. I did ad just a hair less than 1 tablespoon and Im wondering how much less I could decrease it by without harming its rising ability. Any suggestions would be helpful. Can email me at shelly_23f@yahoo.com if you could help me out a bit

attributes.source_text: Very moist
just enough sweetness

reviews.review_text:
Well I was cooking Chilli for our evening meal last night, and thought I would give a Corn Bread a try. Now you are looking at a Corn bread virgin here. It isn't something we Brits go for .Chilli generally comes with rice!Chose this recipe because it didn't have oil in it, and I'm so glad I did. Lovely husband and I  REALLY enjoyed it. Never made Corn Bread before but will certainly make it again and again. What else can you serve it with? and can you put corn kernels in it as well? 
 Well done for a great  recipe

attributes.source_text: for our evening meal last night

reviews.review_text:
Excellent recipe!  I have been looking for it for quite some time.  I am excited, and I also believe I now have my 'go-to' recipe. 
It had all the right ingredients perfectly measured/proportioned.  
 I added some leftover chopped green onions I had in the fridge as well as a minced jalapeño,....because momma is always loving it with a little more zip.  ;o)
I also reduced the sugar to half - 1/4 cup - because I just don't like it too sweet.  I baked it as muffins.  Excellent ! 

Thanks again for this expertly balanced as well as wonderfully tasting recipe !

The best cornbread I've tasted, and very easy, too. I made three different "versions" of this with all the same ingredients except replacing milk with buttermilk then half buttermilk and half milk. I wanted to see which will taste the best. Your original recipe with just milk is great. I mean, slightly sweet, crispy edges, omygosh I ate 7 in all (from the different versions). When I replaced it with buttermilk, it made it fluffier and softer in the inside but it was very sweet (I recommend reducing the sugar). The same was with the half buttermilk half milk. There was not much difference with the full buttermilk and this one. It was still too sweet. But the original recipe- omygoshhh it was great. Best cornbread I've tasted.

attributes.source_text: slightly sweet
crispy edges

reviews.review_text:
I made the 2 egg and 1/3 c. sugar version and used buttermilk in place of the milk. 
I preheated a cast iron skillet greased with bacon fat :) in the oven and added the batter to the hot skillet. 20 minutes later my husband cut into what he declared was 'the best cornbread' he'd ever had. The crumb was decent and it was slightly sweet. I am glad I reduced the sugar. It was moist yet had a nice crisp crust. Nothing better than cornbread in cast iron. I will use this as a base recipe for cornbread again!

attributes.source_text: it was slightly sweet
It was moist
had a nice crisp crust

reviews.review_text: This was perfect cornbread!  Just the right amount of sweetness, even served with a Mexican style dinner.   I used butter, not margarine, and yellow cornmeal instead of white or blue.  Just like Mom used to make!  Not really... My mother's cornbread always tasted so good, but when I asked her for the recipe, she told me it was the Jiffy mix, which is full of hydrogenated oils.  I've been hoping I'd come across a recipe that was better than that, and this is it.  Next time I'm going to kick up the heat and add some finely chopped jalapeno.  Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: Just the right amount of sweetness

reviews.review_text: I am a seeker of 'The Best Ever' recipes and have been looking for a delicious and most moist cornbread recipe for ovr 30 years.  I have to say, this is the one with a little tweaking, which I always do.  I used buttermilk and added a 1/4  of Vermont maple syrup to this one and it was phenominal.  I served it with homemade chili and it was even better the next day.  Great buttered, but it really doesn't even need it.  This is 'The Best Ever' cornbread recipe I will use from now on!  Thank you so much!! : )

attributes.source_text: most moist cornbread recipe

reviews.review_text: This is the best cornbread I have ever had! I've been told by all my family that it is better than any restaurant. I constantly get requests to bring this to pot lucks and parties. I have made it jalapeño cornbread by adding 2 freshly chopped de-seeded jalapeños. It is not hot at all but adds an amazing flavour to the loaf. Also I sometimes put shredded cheddar on top after pulling it out of the oven. I have also made it maple cornbread by exchanging the sugar in the recipe for granulated maple sugar. You just can't beat this basic recipe! Its sweet, southern, classic recipe with simple ingredients that are always on hand! I love it.

attributes.source_text: Its sweet, southern, classic recipe
Its sweet, southern, classic recipe
I constantly get requests to bring this to pot lucks
I constantly get requests to bring this to pot lucks and parties

reviews.review_text: This was very unpleasant. It was sweet enough to be a dessert. I had it with some Boston Baked beans, which were also horribly sweet. My father's comment was that this was "the strangest meal I've had in a long time".<br/><br/>I should let everyone know that we're British, and so as far as we know this may be a very authentic recipe. But to our taste it was far more like a Victoria sponge cake than it was to any kind of bread.<br/><br/>If you've never had cornbread before, you should avoid this recipe or you may get a nasty shock. Unless that is you're looking for a quick and easy cake to go with coffee or tea.

This is FABULOUS! Better than my mother's recipe for Johnnycake, which I grew up on.. This produces the kind of cornbread I dream of when I get a yen for this particular kind of quick bread.<br/><br/>I've actually got a plate of this cornbread next to me as I type this. It's moist (incredibly moist) and delicious. I found it a tiny bit too sweet so I'll be doing the suggested reduction of sugar to 1/3 cup in future. I did add two eggs and it worked like a charm.

Excellent!
Its almost midnight now but I just finished baking this delicious cornbread for tomorrow's breakfast. Of course I had to have a small piece before rating LOL! It's sooo good! 
I had been looking for a recipe that didn't call for more flour than cornmeal as I prefer the gritty texture of the cornmeal. I wish I had found this recipe before Thanksgiving s this is so much better than the one I served. Very easy and mess-free, I made it after everyone had gone to bed. 
THANK YOU!

attributes.source_text: for tomorrow's breakfast
I prefer the gritty texture of the cornmeal

reviews.review_text: i've sure picked a winner of a cornbread recipe with this one! REALLY good, sweet, and soft & with the perfect ratio of moisture to crumbley-ness... We loved it! It's nice that this recipe doesn't call for much butter. I used buttermilk because we didn't have regular milk. I made it to accompany chili, then had it for breakfast warmed up with butter in the morning. UPDATE: I made this again, but increased the buttermilk to 1-1/4 cups, and it made the cornbread so tender and moist. I loved it even more! I just make chili as a excuse to make this recipe!!

reviews.review_text: This is good, and I've had satisfactory results using a little less sugar and substituting some/all of the canola oil for butter.  I would describe the original recipe as good, moist, sweet, and slightly crumbly.  The oil substitutions seemed to result in a slightly dryer and less crumbly cornbread.  I love having cornbread with chili.  I'm intrigued by suggestions to try this in a cast iron skillet greased with bacon grease... maybe I'll try that someday.  Thank you for the recipe!  :)

attributes.source_text: good, moist, sweet, and slightly crumbly
good, moist, sweet, and slightly crumbly
slightly crumbly

reviews.review_text: I made these this morning and they were gobbled up by my family right out of the oven!  Unfortunately, I started to make them before realizing that I had corn FLOUR and not cornmeal, but they still turned out great with a cup-for-cup substitution.  The only major difference was that the batter was quite thick and didn't even out as they baked, so the tops were lumpy rather than flat and smooth.  This made 15 medium-size muffins for me.  Quick, simple, and yummy!

attributes.source_text: gobbled up by my family right out of the oven

reviews.review_text: I know this rating is harsh, but I want to warn the unwary that this tastes more like corn cake than cornbread, as it is sooooo sweet, even with the reduced sugar (1/3 cup). I agree with other reviewers that it is moist, has a nice texture, crunchy crust and cuts well. It is perfect if you want to eat it as a dessert with fruit and cream. But our family found it quite odd to eat sweet corn cake with a savoury food like beans. If I made it again I'd reduce the sugar to one tablespoon.

attributes.source_text: it is moist

items.label: Ww 5 Can Soup
items.name: Ww 5 Can Soup
items.description:
This recipe is from a Weight Watchers meeting. It is so quick -- I ate it daily when I was on maternity leave with my second son. If I am making it for the week, I just empty the cans into a plastic container and warm up 1 serving in the microwave. I have also made it using frozen corn and mixed vegetables.

Those who enjoy this may also be interested in #57009 - "5 cans and a jar".
instructions: Mix all ingredients in a pot and warm.

reviews.review_text:
This soup is really yummy and I always have the ingredients on hand. Sometimes if i want to add a little kick I use the Diced tomatoes with green chilies instead of the plain ones. I also add some shredded cheese every time I make a bowl. Thanks for posting
UPDATE: When i first had this I wasnt on Weight Watchers. Now that I am, I have made a few changes. :) Since some reviewers said the soup was salty, I rinsed the black beans, corn and mixed vegetables. Since that took away some of the liquid I added all natural chicken broth (ZERO POINTS!) Then instead of using regular tomatoes, I used fire roasted so it wouldnt be so bland. I also only had the 10 oz can of minstrone so I used my biggest loser scale and added an extra 4 oz from a second can. This still comes out to 5 points and lower sodium. :) Thanks again for this recipe! It will really benefit me in my weight loss journey :)

I must say I am pleasantly surprised. I can honestly say, I have seen this recipe several times, and looking at the simple ingredients, I  assumed it could not really be that great...Boy, was I wrong!! Quick, easy and DELICIOUS! I used great northern beans, as that is what I had on hand, and a can of diced tomatoes with green chilis. I added some fresh garlic, 2 bay leaves and get this.. the leftover sloppy joe mix from last night's dinner!! It is so good, I am still surprised at the flavor of this 5 can soup. I will use this recipe often. I can see where any leftover meat or veggies can be substituted with great results. I loved the beans so much, I think I may add 2 cans next time! Thanks again for sharing a new favorite.

This soup is sooo unbelievably YUMMY!!! Even my dad, whom is a die-hard "Meat and potatoes" man, loves this soup. Now that he is living on his own, he is absolutely delighted that it is so easy to make, as he is not one for recipes that require more than a few steps. I actually had this recipe a few years ago, and managed to lose it (which is not very difficult for me;), and I am soooo delighted that you posted this!!! I only add ground black pepper and some garlic powder...Very hearty and filling soup, and good for you yet to boot!!! Thanks for posting! A DEFINITE MUST-TRY!!
~Manda

attributes.source_text: Even my dad, whom is a die-hard "Meat and potatoes" man, loves this soup

reviews.review_text:
5 Stars and then some! Wow! Made this yesterday for my wife and I. I NEVER would have imagined that "five cans" could taste so good. I have been trying to lose weight, but I have not been looking for "diet" meals. I have been looking for healthy alternatives to fast food. This is amazingly good. 
    What I actually did was combine this recipe with another, #57009 "5 Cans and a Jar Soup Recipe". I highly recommend it! The added chicken broth and medium-hot salsa and kidney beans (I used one can of red, one white), and used fire-roasted diced tomatoes for additional flavor. A couple of sprigs of basil and a few bay leaves are the only additions I made. Combined, I was blown away. One of the most flavorful soups, -meals-, I have ever made! And really, "no cooking" is necessary! You are really just heating this up to meal temperature. Yes, I let it simmer a good hour or more, until my wife got home from work. I cannot recommend this enough! 
    This is my new EASY, healthy, favorite! And my little dog, a "schnoodle", LOVED it as well! :)

I used Hot Petite Diced Toms and it give the soup PLENTY of kick. Almost a bit too spicy, but we like things hot. There is not much cooking involved, just dump from cans and heat, but it still tasted good for such a quickie meal, and makes plenty for lunch leftovers. I used Progresso Minestrone, and with the addition of the other ingredients, it was definitely a "souped up" can soup. It still has that slight tin flavor that canned soups have, but not as much. Next time I may add more beans, and 2 cans of tomatoes- one hot one not, to balance the heat.

attributes.source_text: it give the soup PLENTY of kick

reviews.review_text: I feel repeative reviewing this recipe, but it is awesome.  I have seen it floting around at my Weight Watchers meeting and on their website.  It has been one of those I have been meaning to try recipes.  I am sure glad I finally did.  Nice texture, really good taste, and very colorful.  I literally opened up cans and dumped ingredients into my pot and warmed on the stove as I got ready for work this morning.  I then packed my prepared thermos with nice, hot, good smelling soup just before heading out the door.   Thanks for a stress free recipe.

I am not on weight watchers-- but I love this soup!! I have made it about a hundred times since I found this recipe and I have passed it on even more! This recipe is wonderful the way it is, and it's easy to change for variety. My whole family eats this-- including a picky 2 year old! I usually add salt, pepper and tabasco, plus drain the vegetables and add a can of stock for more of a homemade flavor. I have also added onions, garlic or leftovers-- cooked chicken, hamburger or vegetables. I have used kidney beans instead of black beans. Thanks for the EASY and FABULOUS recipe!!

attributes.source_text: My whole family eats this
including a picky 2 year old

reviews.review_text: I thought it was super easy and tasted great. I just made a few changes. I added an extra can of diced tomatoes. I got 1 can regular diced tomatoes and 1 can italian diced tomatoes (to add a little extra seasoning). I also used frozen mixed veggies. I also drained the beans and added a little chicken stock. I also added a few egg noodles and some broccoli. A little garlic powder and black pepper also added a little more seasoning. Made an excellent hearty veggie soup for me to take to work!

attributes.source_text: Made an excellent hearty veggie soup

reviews.review_text: This was awesome and so healthy! I chopped up some parsley, about 1/2 cup onion, and maybe 2 tsp minced garlic and threw it in there. I also drained the veggies and added about 2 cups chicken broth. This would also be great with veggie or beef broth. I like a little heat so I added some hot sauce as well. I served it with garlic bread and couldn't get enough! Thanks for the great recipe! Next time I may omit the can of corn since the minestrone already had corn in it.

This was so tasty and incredibly easy.  It did become 4 can soup for me as I did not have any canned mixed vegtables, but that's ok.  I used tomatoes with chilis and lime which added a nice taste.  The kids really enjoyed it.  My husband actually drained the liquid off and rolled his in a tortilla.  So it is versatile too!  This will definitely be something we use when time is tight as it was healthy, fast, and easy.  Thanks so much!

attributes.source_text: The kids really enjoyed it
My husband actually drained the liquid off and rolled his in a tortilla

reviews.review_text: Great soup that tastes perfect and good enough for company.  I tweaked it by skipping on the mixed veggies and adding a can of Progresso Vegetarian Vegetable soup instead (used Progresso Minestrone for the other) - that adds a little bit of pasta and more veggies without all the salt from the can of mixed veggies.  Love that it comes together so simply and fills up my family easily.  Will fall back on this recipe many times through the colder months.

attributes.source_text: good enough for company

reviews.review_text: Why didn't I think of this before!  Minestrone on its own (from cans) is so bland, but add veggies + tomatoes, and you have this hearty, wonderful easy soup.  My b/f raved over it and I really liked it too.  This is a great way to get vegetables in.  For some reason mine came out super spicy: one of the cans must have had some extra kick to it.  This will definitely become a regular in our house.  I can't wait to share this idea with my father and other men in my family (who don't like to cook) to get them to eat healthier too!

reviews.review_text: This is a wonderful soup. DH2b walked in the kitchen practically drooling from the aroma. And it could not be ANY easier! I didn't drain anything (except the beans, which I had to rinse.) Then I brought everything to a boil, lowered to a simmer. I used great northern beans, since that is what I had, and they worked fine. I'm sure it changed the flavor some, but we could easily tell this is a 5-star keeper with just about any type of bean.

I looked for this recipe all day. I don't know why I didn't save it to my cookbook when I first saw it. Zaar doesn't recognize the number "5" in the search for recipes (yet).  Well.. I finally found it and yes... to add to the other reviews it's a keeper. I added chopped habaneros and used the Progresso Minestrone idea as Kard229 suggested. I also added a small can (15-1/2 oz. ) of chicken broth to increase the number of servings.

I loved the ease and was surprised at the comforting and wonderful taste of this recipe.  My chopped tomatoes were Italian blend, and I have more than 6 people to cook for, so I used 2 cans of Progresso minestrone to stretch it. I also used frozen mexi-corn with black beans in addition to the can of black beans.  So easy to fix during the holidays, and my family of 9 all loved it. I'm buying all the ingredients to have on hand at all times from here on.  Thank you for a winner of a recipe!

attributes.source_text: the comforting and wonderful taste

reviews.review_text:
For taste, I would give this 4 stars, but because it was so easy, it gets 5 from me. I think this soup really needs to simmer for a while to let the flavors blend. Just heating it up isn't enough, in my opinion. After tasting it, I thought it needed something, so I added 1/2 teaspoon each of garlic and onion powder, which I think helped a lot. reviews.review_text: I made this soup with frozen white corn and frozen mixed vegetables.  It was very fast and easy to prepare and had a very good flavor.  I did add a can of beef broth to it.  I reheated a cup of the soup and added some lean, diced ham to it.  That was very good.  I will be making this recipe again for noon meals.  I took it to work and had it with some good rye bread. items.label: Roasted Garlic Mashed Potatoes - the Best You've Ever Had
items.name: Roasted Garlic Mashed Potatoes - the Best You've Ever Had
items.description: Make and share this Roasted Garlic Mashed Potatoes - the Best You've Ever Had recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Separate head of garlic into individual cloves.
Toss in olive oil and wrap tightly in small piece of aluminum foil.
Bake in 350°F (180°C) oven for 45 minutes.
When the garlic has cooled to the touch you should be able to squeeze it out of the 'paper' shell of the individual cloves.
Mash the roasted garlic with a fork, or force through a fine strainer.
If you use a ricer as recommended below, simply rice the garlic along with the potatoes.
Peel and boil potatoes in salted water until tender.
Force the cooked potatoes through a ricer (recommended) or mash by your usual method.
Put the riced potatoes, garlic, sour cream, butter, and salt and white pepper in a mixer bowl, and whip at medium speed until smooth.
Add cream or milk to adjust consistency.

reviews.review_text: These are great potatos, however I would like to share a easy way to do roast garlic. Just slice the top of the whole head off just enough to expose the cloves inside. Drizzle the head with olive oil, then wrap in foil. Cook at 350 for about 40 minutes. When it has cooled enough to handle hold the whole head and squeeze. The cooked cloves will come out just like squeezing tooth paste. Squeeze directly in your potato's and mash as usual. For more garlic flavor and another head. Hope you find this helpful..thank you.

I made these for Christmas because I've been wanting to make this recipe AND I wanted to make potatoes ahead of time.

These got enthusiastic reviews--and people asked for the recipe.  I made these ahead and rewarmed with extra milk and butter on top in the oven.  Stirred in the butter and milk before serving.

This gets accolades for being extra good AND for being adaptable as a make ahead dish.  However, I do plan to make and consume this without preparing it ahead of time.

Delcious.

This recipe also contains an easy way to roast garlic, which I had never done before but I heard some people call it tricky.

reviews.review_text: Yes, Yes, Yes...these ARE the best garlic mashed potatoes I have ever made. :-) Thank you so much Mimi Bobeck. This was the easiest recipe. Your directions were "spot on" as the saying goes. I cook all of the time yet mashed potatoes were something that I couldn't quite get just as I wanted them. Well now you have helped me to accomplish that and for that I thank you. And my husband thanks you. We try not to eat too many potatoes around here but I have the feeling that we will be eating lots more because of this very simple yet very tasty recipe. Yummy. Hugs to you, Susie

attributes.source_text: best garlic mashed potatoes
my husband thanks you

reviews.review_text: I've always wanted to try making garlic mashed potatoes---boy did I pick the right recipe to try! I finally used the ricer my Mother bought me last year and had never used (Thanks Mom!) I cooked the garlic with the beef roast I had slow cooking for about a hour.  Some reviewers suggested cooking the garlic with a bit more oil for added flavor..next time I will.   This is going to become my main mashed potato recipe..thank you so much for sharing.

reviews.review_text:
Delicious! Yukon Gold potatoes are best, but Russett potatoes are also very tasty when prepared this way.
I made 3 minor alterations both times I prepared this dish, and will probably repeat them in the future:
1. I had no sour cream, so I substituted 4 oz. of softened cream cheese.
2. I did need to add milk or cream to get the desired consistency, and I used a full pint of whipping cream. It's so rich that it's best saved as a special treat, but it is wonderful.
3. I added chopped fresh chives right before serving.

reviews.review_text: These were fantastic!  I used fresh ground pepper, not white, and used red potatoes- i also halved the recipe because there was only two of us- made enough for about 3-4!  Great side dish, the garlic takes time, but it is worth it!  I didnt have a ricer so i used am old fashoned potato smasher and pushed it through a regular strainer so it came through smooth, and i pushed the garlic through a fine strainer with a spoon- they both worked great and did the job...thanks Mimi i will definately make these again!

reviews.review_text: Just made these to go with My Family's Favorite Sloppy Joes by Hey Jude and sorry to say we were dissapointed; certainly not 'the best we've ever had'; in fact, that was DH's response to the whole meal 'Sorry to say, not your best meal ever'. These had too much garlic (I usually quadrouple the amount of garlic in a recipe, but as written the flavor in this was over the top) and they didn't have enough butter. I would recommend usuing cream instead of milk as I used milk thinking the sour cream and butter would make them rich and creamy, but I guess there just wasn't enough of either to do much good in 2 lbs of potatoes. And just so people know, this recipe makes a ton of mashed potatoes, far more than necessary for 4 people as a side dish.

reviews.review_text: We loved how wonderful these potatoes tasted when done! I had no way of judging pounds of potatoes but used about 6 regular sized russets for the amounts listed above. It made enough for approx 4 poeple the way I did it. Fabulous tasting potatoes. Don't miss putting the white pepper in. I thought it added an elegant zing to the taste. If you're not sure about the garlic do like I did and try 1/4 + 1/8 TSP of garlic powder. It seemed to be enough without being overpowering but more would have been too much. Thanks for posting!

items.description: I love these rich, very sweet, addictive cookies. I adapted this recipe from one I found and loved on allrecipes.com. I have altered it somewhat to suit my tastes and my preferred baking techniques but this is based on the recipe known there as Aunt Cora's World's Best Cookies. Cook time is per batch, cooking one sheet at a time.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325 degrees F.
Have ready at least 2 baking sheets lined with parchment paper.
Cream butter until smooth.
Add peanut butter and both sugars and beat until combined well.
Add egg and beat well.
Stir in flour and baking soda gradually until well combined.
Stir in chocolate chips by hand.
Using a meatball scooper or a spoon, scoop out small portions of dough and drop onto parchment lined cookie sheets, leaving 2\

reviews.review_text: Awesome!  I did make a few changes - I used Organic, All Natural Smooth Peanut Butter that has no added oils or sugars or anything.  I also decresed the amount of white sugar to 1/2 cup and subbed 1/2 whole wheat flour - These were great!  Next time (oh, yes, next time) I'll leave out the white sugar completely, use all whole wheat flour and add 1 tsp. vanilla - I'll also decrease the baking time to about 12-13 minutes as I like a chewy cookie.  Great recipe as is though!

I wanted to make a special treat for some wonderful people today. When asked what kind of cookies I should make, the first responders were "peanut butter" and "chocolate chip". I didn't have time to make both so I searched for a peanut butter/chocolate chip recipe and found this one. I followed the recipe as written, used Jif Creamy Peanut Butter and, since these cookies need to be extra special, I splurged and used Ghirardelli Milk Chocolate Chips. I am renaming the recipe 1 measuring cup cookies. Love the fact that I did not have a sink full of measuring cups after mixing the ingredients. Baking time was exactly 15 minutes - the cookies came out of the oven slightly crisp on the edges and soft in the middle, just the way I like them. Here's hoping my cohorts at Muskegon Summer Celebration enjoy the cookies as much as I do. Thank you for sharing this recipe, it deserves 10 stars.

ETA - cookies are completely finished - recipe yielded a full 8 bakers dozen (2" cookies) - probably would have had a few more cookies but somebody tested the raw dough :)

Also, I made a bunch of substitutions which did not impact them in any noticeable way. I used Earth Balance (nondairy) instead of butter, I ran out of baking soda, so I used baking powder, also the PB... I froze my extra dough, unbaked on a cookie sheet, then transferred to a plastic bag (so that they don't freeze together in a big lump) and future self looks forward to them-THANKS!!
