items.label: Adam's Ribs
items.name: Adam's Ribs
items.description: Different, unusual way to prepare ribs. The soda pop tenderizes the meat. Untried recipe but they sound so good I just had to post them!
instructions: Place ribs in large stock pot and pour Dr. Pepper over ribs to cover.
Add garlic, liquid smoke and onion.
Bring to a boil, lower to simmer and cook until ribs are tender.
Place ribs in baking pan and pour BBQ sauce over ribs.
Bake at 350 degrees for about 30 to 45 minutes.
Or they can be put on BBQ grill.

reviews.review_text:
This recipe is the BOMB....I made it this last past Memorial day and added a few things to it, First I rubbed the ribs down with the following:
1 1/2 tsp.cumin
1 1/2 tsp. chili powder
1 tsp. paprika
1/2 tsp. white pepper
2 tsp. nutmeg
1 tsp. kosher salt
1 1/2 tsp. dry ground musturd
1 tsp. dried basil


I mixed all of this together and rubbed it on the ribs ands let it sit for about 2 hours, then I got a deep sauce pan and placed the ribs in it and poured a 2 liter bottle of Dr.Pepper over it til it was covered....and I let the ribs sit in this marinade bath all nite in the fridge. The next morning I boiled them on low for about 2 1/2 hours( this is right outta the fridge so I needed to give extra time to reach the desired heat) when the meat was real tender I removed them and slattered them with sweet Baby Rays BBQ sauce and put on the grill just to carmelize the BBQ sauce......wow...they were finger lickin good....everyone wanted more...thats how fast they went......AWESOME Recipe...thanks soooo much.

attributes.source_text: I made it this last past Memorial day
when the meat was real tender

reviews.review_text: Great ribs!  I used 1 3/4lbs of country style boneless pork ribs and cooked them a bit differently:  I marinated them in the soda for about 1/2 hour, removed the pork onto a baking sheet lined with 2 layers of foil.  I poured just a bit of the soda on top of the ribs, along with the garlic, liquid smoke and onion; I sealed them tightly in the foil and baked them at 300 degrees for about 3 1/2 hours.  Removed them from oven, turned up the oven heat to 450 degrees and brushed on some Cattleman's BBQ Smokehouse sauce.  I wrapped the ribs back up, baked them for another 15 minutes, unwrapped the ribs, brushed on more sauce and baked for another 10 minutes, unwrapped.  They were so tasty and moist; we absolutely loved these ribs!

attributes.source_text: and moist

reviews.review_text: Boiling ribs? Shameful! Next thing someone will write is they’re boiling their Turkey to speed up the process and make it tender! If you’re not going to smoke them outside, put a dry rub on the ribs. Lay them out on a rimmed sheet pan. Cover with plastic wrap ( no, it won’t melt), then Tightly cover with foil. Place in 235 degree oven for 4.5 hours. Carefully remove, peel back one corner of foil and plastic wrap ( be careful of the steam) drain the liquid then unwrap completely. Brush liberally with your favorite BBQ sauce once and wait 15-20 minutes for it to absorb into the meat. Then, I like to brush on Mae Ploy brand Sweet Chile Sauce (or more BBQ success) and place the sheet pan under a hot broiler for 2-3 minutes or until the sauce starts to bubble, to let the sugars caramelize. Remove, cut and enjoy!!

Excellent rib recipe!!  I used Sweet Baby Rays sauce.  I simmered for only about 40 minutes and then put in the oven to bake.  I was worried because once I had it in the oven I read other reviewer suggestion of simmering at least double the time I had but could put back into the pot because I already had smothered the ribs in my only bottle of BBQ sauce.  I compensated by lowering the baking temp and cooking that an hour and a half and they still turned out tender!  Next time though I will heed other reviewers advice and go longer on the simmering part and I want to try it with Jack Daniels No7 sauce as my husband prefers it.  Really good and this is the way I plan on cooking ribs from now on.  Thank you, JoAnn!!

attributes.source_text: they still turned out tender

reviews.review_text: Not possible!  The very best ribs I've ever tasted even above my favorite steakhouse!  I used a large crock pot.  Filled it with one 2-liter Dr Pepper (non-diet), exact amount of liquid smoke and garlic. Went to AJ's and picked up a small slab of baby back ribs.  But knowing my husband is wierd about ribs and fat I also picked up a very lean pork loin.  I cut the ribs in sections and put the pork loin in the same mix. Also used a crock pot liner which makes clean up easy.  Cooked on high for 2 hours and 4 hours on low.  At the end I took each piece out, covered with sauce and baked in oven as directed for about 35 minutes.  Some mention end product is too sweet.  I can't stand anything too sweet and am raving this is best I've tasted.  Make sure you use the liquid smoke.  Also, if you don't like sweet pick the proper Barbecue sauce.  I used Cattleman's Authentic.  I will make all barbecued items this way even chicken from now on.  Painfully good!!!!!  Many thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: I can't stand anything too sweet and am raving this is best I've tasted

reviews.review_text: These look delicious! I haven't tried them yet but I most definitely will. I've cooked a pork roast in a crock pot with Root Beer before. I rub it with a brown sugar spice rub. I also add onions and a little pickle juice. Root Beer and pickle juice sound gross together but cooked together, it's awesome!! After it's thoroughly cooked, I put the meat on a plate, de-fat the broth, add Jack Daniel's BBQ sauce (the only kind I use), shred the tender meat and onions and put in back in the sauce. I make sliders using King's Hawaiian Sweet Rolls. I put on a slice of a grilled pineapple ring and a spoon of slaw and dig in. Great, now my mouth is watering. I can't wait to try the Dr. Pepper ribs! It seems futile using a diet drink. The sugar in the BBQ sauce and Dr. Pepper caramelize perfectly for sticky, messy, succulent ribs. We would never use diet. Fake sugar tastes nasty and makes me run to the bathroom too much.

OMG, WOW!  These were incredibly tender.  I had about 2 lbs country style ribs and boiled them for about 1 hour 30 min.  Then baked them for 45 min.  I slathered them with Sweet Baby Rays BBQ sauce and they came out so tender that they fell apart.  DELICIOUS!  This is going to be the way I make these all the time now.  I made country style ribs a couple other times with some other recipes where you just boil them in water and seasonings, then bake them.  They didn't turn out half as tender as they did in this recipe.  Im so glad that I found this recipe!  Thanks! :)

After reading the post that it smelled awful, plus a post crock-potting it - I cooked it about 3 hours on high, 4 hours on low in 2L generic dr pepper, onion, garlic, and smoke. reviews.review_text:
Tried these tonight as a test run before we have guests this weekend. 
I wanted to test them because never thought of cooking with a Soda, let alone Dr Pepper.  
After the boil we left the ribs to marinade overnight in a Shop Own Brand sticky BarBQue sauce (didnt want to waste the Baby Rays on test run!) [ dont think that is necessary, just fit in with our preparation.
Having just finished eating them, they are the best ribs I've had and am now looking forward to our weekend second serving...
Thanks for posting this!

This was a really delicious way to cook ribs.  I used half Dr. Pepper and half chicken stock; just enough to cover.  Also added onions, carrots and celery and some onion powder and garlic powder.  Slow simmered for around and hour.  The meat had a subtle sweetness which went really well with the BBQ sauce(Sweet Baby Rays).  Crisped them up on the BBQ, served with steamed broccoli and smashed spuds.  I was left with a sweet but delicious meat stock so I am going to make split pea soup out of it.  Thanks for the great recipe!

reviews.review_text: These ribs were okay.  My daughter and boyfriend thought they were good, but they were too sweet for my taste. I think cooking in sweet soda followed by a sweet barbeque sauce such as Sweet Baby Ray's was too much sweetness.  I think I would try a sauce that was spicer or smokier next time.  I was also really put off by the "scum" that formed while simmering the meat in the soda.  It was black and I had a hard time scraping it off before covering with the barbeque sauce. Having said that I think I would try this recipe again using ribs with the least amount of fat and a spicer/smokier BBQ sauce and maybe a clear soda.

attributes.source_text: My daughter and boyfriend thought they were good
My daughter and boyfriend thought they were good

reviews.review_text: 5 stars without a doubt!  Ribs were very tender and flavorful.  We used 4 (12oz) cans of Diet Dr. Pepper (that's all we had on hand).  Since the recipe specifically calls out NOT to use diet, we added about 1/4 C of sugar.  We added enough chicken broth to cover the ribs.  Since we didn't have liquid smoke, we decided to use some wood chips while grilling to give it that smoky flavor; but forgot when the time came.  They came out fantastic anyways.  We definately will be making these again.

attributes.source_text: Ribs were very tender

reviews.review_text: I was a bit hesitant to try this recipe. We love ribs in our house and are pretty picky...OMG...These ribs were SOOOO yummy! We used 2 racks of baby backs (approx. 4.5 lbs.), a 2 liter of Dr. Pepper, minced garlic and a medium quartered onion. Simmered for a little over an hour and baked with BBQ sauce for about 35-45 min. All i have to say is THIS IS A KEEPER!!! Easy enough for a work night dinner. The flavor is amazing! I don't get it...Dr. Pepper??!?! Who woulda thunk it! Thank you for posting this recipe.

attributes.source_text: Easy enough for a work night dinner
Easy enough for a work night dinner

reviews.review_text: I made these for New Year's Eve and they are amazingly good. (DH says I must use the word AWESOME!) I've never made ribs before and was surprised by how easy this is. I'm glad another reviewer mentioned that they don't look good while in the pot, because I was a little worried for a minute. I used 3 1/2 pounds of babyback ribs, simmered for a little over an hour and baked about 45 minutes. They were so tender and the flavor was outstanding. The meat tasted great even in spots that had no sauce. A VERY good recipe!

attributes.source_text: I made these for New Year's Eve
DH says I must use the word AWESOME!

reviews.review_text: very good recipe and my guys liked it too. Used Jack Daniels Original Recipe #7 Sauce which, by the way, is a pretty good sauce. Living in Alabama, I like a mustard based BBQ sauce with a little "twang" to it instead of the sweet BBQ sauces that most people gravitate to. Will probably do this recipe again with one of the local BBQ sauces like 13th Street BBQ sauce or Mike and Ed's BBQ sauce. For those curious, this is available if you live in East Alabama Phenix City or Columbus, GA area.

Now this is what you call Lip Smacking good! My neighbors and I fixed  this with 6 pounds of country style ribs last weekend and they turned out Awesome. I used Jack Daniels bbq sauce but no matter what sauce you use on these I don't think it would matter. This Dr. Pepper trick really makes for some outstandiing ribs. We can't wait untill we get a weekend with no rain so we can do these on the grillle because we have 8 lbs. of babby backs in the freezer just waiting.  Thanks for a fabulous recipe. Tis a keeper for sure.

items.label: Honey Roasted Pork Loin
items.name: Honey Roasted Pork Loin
items.description: Make and share this Honey Roasted Pork Loin recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375.
Season the pork and place in a roasting pan.( consider  browning on  all sides).
In a separate bowl, mix together the honey, juice, oil and thyme.
Pour over the pork.
Add the broth to the pan.
Bake until internal temperature reaches 150 (45-60 minutes).
Baste frequently.
Strain the pan juices into a saucepan small amount gravy flour .
Reduce until slightly thickened.
Serve over the sliced pork.

reviews.review_text: Excellent. I thought I had thyme in the garden but I didn't so I used 1 tsp dried. On the seasoning the pork loin part, I just peppered it with fresh ground pepper. No salt since I figured I'd get plenty in chicken broth (even though I used reduced sodium). I also doubled the sauce because my loin was 3 pounds. I also faked a roasting pan (going to get one one of these days) by making little donuts out of aluminum foil on the bottom of the pan and putting the loin on top. Keeps the bottom of the meat off the bottom of the pan and lets me get to the juices for basting. Since my hunk of meat was a little bigger, it ended up cooking for about 1 1/2 hours and I checked with a thermometer to make sure it was done. The taste was kinda like a ham. Meat was very tender and moist. Was great with sweet potato. Very pretty dish as well with the color and thyme speckles.

attributes.source_text: The taste was kinda like a ham
Meat was very tender
Meat was very tender and moist

reviews.review_text: I have never cooked a pork loin before but had one in the freezer; was putting it off because I didn't want to over cook and dry it out...This was a very easy cooking method and sooo GOOD!! I doubled the sauce as others suggested; I marinated the pork in the sauce (minus broth) for about 4 hours, then put it in the pan seasoned with salt and pepper and poured sauce on top and continued as directed. I was pressed for time so at the end I added a little corn starch to the sauce to thicken it and it was heaven!! I have another tenderloin in the freezer since there were 2 in the pack and will be making this again in a copuld weeks when my mom comes to town!! Thanks Lisa in Oregon!!

This is a good pork loin more like 3 + stars, it would have been 4  if it had been more roasty.  I debated whether or not brown the meat before roasting as I usually do, and wished I had. 
The meat itself was pretty basic, but nice and juicy. I cooked a 4 1/2 lb loin which I studded with slivers of garlic. I sort of tripled the sauce except the honey which was just doubled. I cut back on the thyme and added some rosemary - which went really well with it, and some oregano. I subbed beef broth for the chicken which I was out of. As others did I found the sauce to be a bit sweet, but it still needed some zip, so I added several tablespoons of balsamic vinegar, some while cooking and some in the saucepan later. The loin cooked in hour - faster then I expected, to 160 then rested for a bit till guests arrived. I left the pan in the oven to cook down the sauce a bit then transfered it to  sauce pan and slightly thickened it with corn starch. The sauce was a big hit. We had this with Rosemary Blue cheese Scalloped Potatoes, which was the perfect side dish.
I will make this again with a few more adjustments, to suit our tastes thank you for the inspiration.

attributes.source_text: nice and juicy

reviews.review_text: What a fabulous recipe! I've never cooked pork loin before, so I looked through all the recipes posted here and I'm glad I just happened to pick this one--no need to try any other. It's absolutely delicious. The meat was very tender and flavorful. I cooked it just over an hour. When I added the orange juice I used a spoonful of oj concentrate and added enough water to make two tablespoons, so it was extra strong, which I liked. I also ended up peppering the roast VERY liberally (my pepper shaker's fault). I normally don't like a lot of pepper but it made the sauce even better, if that's possible, by giving it a slightly spicy zing. Great recipe. I'm going to make this one often.

attributes.source_text: The meat was very tender
giving it a slightly spicy zing

reviews.review_text: I was so impatient to get dinner going last night that I goofed up and made a mistake when preparing this recipe, but it didn't ruin a thing: this was delicious! I didn't notice that the chicken broth was separate from the other sauce ingredients, and so I mixed everything up, then looked at the recipe and went "Oops!" It didn't matter; this turned out very well. I made three small modifications: I doubled the sauce ingredients, I used freshly squeezed orange juice so I also added some freshly grated orange zest, and I used maple syrup instead of honey. This recipe is easy and quick enough to prepare for any family dinner, yet tasty and presentable enough for a company meal. I garnished my platter of pork slices with some fresh orange slices and was so pleased with dinner!

attributes.source_text: to get dinner going last night
prepare for any family dinner

reviews.review_text: While I will agree that this pork tenderloin is very moist, I must admit this was not a winner amongst my family.  The flavor from the basting and the reduced sauce is much too sweet for our tastes. Also, this comes out looking grey and unattractive when ready to serve.  We cook pork tenderloin often and just prefer a more golden brown crust from a spice rub or a marinade (non-basting method)that is seared before cooking. I followed the recipe exactly but added some crushed garlic.  I also had to really doctor the pan gravy with some roasted garlic and brown gravy mix to make it less sweet and more savory. The basic ingredients are good, however I would reduce the amount of honey and add some creole or dijon mustard, balsamic vinegar and perhaps some worcestshire if I make this again.

attributes.source_text: this pork tenderloin is very moist

reviews.review_text:
This is the BEST recipe for pork loin I've ever had. My family loves it. I've also made it with apple cider and it was awesome. I even froze a couple of them with the sauce and after defrosting in the microwave I cooked as directed. A weeknight dinner in about 40 minutes! 

Update: I neglected to mention that I use a pork "Tenderloin" and not just a regular pork loin hense the reason I can get dinner on the table in such a hurry! Also, I usually mix all the ingredients together before I pour it on the tenderloin because it ends up mixed together anyway during cooking. Still LOVE this recipe!

attributes.source_text: My family loves it
A weeknight dinner in about 40 minutes

reviews.review_text: Turned out great, very easy! I added some bacon wrap and let marinate for a few hours before cooking (just because I wanted to get the prep done early and have an easy dinner).  Basted every 10 minutes while cooking for about 45 minutes, at which point it registered 170 on a meat thermometer.  So I probably could have taken it out closer to 30 minutes.  Served with the sauce and a spicy Chinese style rice.  Overall I would say it is very good and I will make it again but probably tweak it by adding some pineapple for a sweet & sour flair or maybe some mustard for a honey dijon flavor.

attributes.source_text: have an easy dinner

reviews.review_text: This was really simple to make. I contemplated using lemon juice in place of the orange juice to cut down on the sweetness of the honey. I will try lemon juice next time, my kids loved it but I found it much too sweet for my taste. The tenderloin was wonderfully tender, I shredded it with forks then put the meat back into the reduced sauce and served it over brown rice. I added garlic to the sauce when it was reducing and will maybe try worchestershire the next time to cut down the sweetness. But overall it is a good recipe, thank you!

The tenderloin was wonderfully tender

reviews.review_text:
Just an amazing recipe.  Have made this many times since my first review of it in October, 2003. My family prefers this over pork chops and it makes it way into my menu at least once or twice a month. 
Also wanted to let everyone know that the sauce works wonderfully when smoking chickens on the smoker.  Make a double batch of the sauce.  Have a small coffee can below the chicken with half of the sauce so that it steams it and use to other half of the sauce to inject into the chicken.  It is awesome.

attributes.source_text: My family prefers this over pork chops

reviews.review_text: I loved this.  I used 1 lb. of pork loin and used all the remaining ingredients.  So that tells me to double the sauce if I make this again with the recommended 2 lbs. pork loin!  I didn't have time to simmer the juices at the end, so I just poured over the pork as is.  It was delicious.  I served with my Easy and Savory Boiled Potatoes, and with steamed corn.  These flavors worked so nicely together, and none were too overpowering.  Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: none were too overpowering

reviews.review_text: If I could give you 10 stars I would!!  We loved this!  I used a 1 lb pork T-loin and baked for 1 hour basting every 15 min.  Came out perfect!  I also seasoned with garlic powder when seasoning with salt and pepper.  I added about 1/4 tsp of red pepper flakes to the liquid in the roasting pan.  Use the best honey you can find...I love my Orange Blossom honey from local farmers in our area.  I served this with Curried Couscous with Chickpeas (#203405). I didn't have orange juice so I substituted apple juice and it was absolutely delicious. We served it with roasted potatoes (and salad) and the sauce was excellent on the potatoes too.  The pork came out moist and delicious.  We cooked it at 375 in the convection oven, so it only took about 25 minutes.  We are going to try the sauce on chicken next.  Thanks for the wonderful recipe!!

reviews.review_text: OMG...What a pork loin..so moist barely needed a knife...Had a four pound loin only about 35 minutes more to cook.  I doubled the sauce and so glad  I did...great on the rice.  I had fresh rosemary and added garlic but other than just the same recipe...My DH told me it was one of the best I have ever cooked...we have been married 25 years....so this recipe stays in my rotation!!!!!!..Everyone else raved on this as well....Thank you

items.label: Puppy Chow or Monkey Munch
items.name: Puppy Chow or Monkey Munch
items.description: Make and share this Puppy Chow or Monkey Munch recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Measure cereal in large bowl.
Set aside.
Microwave chocolate chips, peanut butter and butter for 1 minute on high.
Stir.
Cook for 30 seconds longer or until smooth.
Add vanilla.
Pour mixture over cereal, stirring until coated.
Pour mixture into large Ziploc bag and add powdered sugar.
Shake until well coated.
Spread on waxed paper to cool.
Store in Ziploc bags or large sealed bowl.
Recipe Note: It helps to add cereal mixture a little at a time if you only have small bags.

reviews.review_text: LOVE IT!!!!  I've been making puppy chow on a fairly regular basis for longer than i'd like to admit:) A few tricks I've learned along the way; 1) instead of using a zip lock back, I put half or more of the powdered sugar in the bottom of a large plastic bowl -one with a lid- pour the chocolate cereal mixture on top and then sprinkle the remaining powdered sugar over that. Put the lid on and shake it up! No need to waste a zip lock bag every time you make it.  I usually then store the chow in that same bowl, for the few minutes it lasts. 2) this is more of a preference but often I will put the puppy chow in the fridge for 15-20 minutes after making or before eating.  Something about it being slightly cool tastes really good! Also, I think rice chex works best.

Thank you so much for posting this recipe.  My husband just asked for some last night and I couldn't find my recipe anywhere!!  This is exactly how we make it (although I always double, sometimes even triple the recipe) and it is always a crowd pleaser!!  Thank you for coming to my rescue!!  Like others mentioned, we tend to store ours in a tupperware container so rather than dirty more dishes, I usually mix it in the bowl.  Lastly, I prefer to use a double boiler and slowly melt the chocolate and peanut butter rather than the microwave only because I am terrible at scorching the chocolate via the microwave.  Enjoy, this treat never lasts long at our house!

Saw this one Jon&Kate+8.  Very easy to make, a nice sweet treat.  We used wheat chex cause we had a lot of it.  I would recommend going with corn or rice chex...wheat chex is rather hard and crunchy. :)  Not messay to make at all--melted my sweets in a BIG bowl in microwave, stirred in the chex.  Poured into a gallon sized baggie with the sugar in there (it all fits in one bag).  Zip and shake!  Used part leftover baker's chocolate squares and Ghiradelli chips, no problem.  Could stand some more add-ins:  pretzels, peanuts, M&Ms?  Would probably need to increase your meltables, though.  Thanks.

attributes.source_text: a nice sweet treat

reviews.review_text: We've been using this recipe for a few years now, it's the exact same one that comes printed on the side of the Rice Chex cereal box. A few helpful hints: Divide the cereal and the chocolate/peanut butter mixture between a few gallon sized zip lock bags. It'll make mixing it all easier and cleaner! Also, I found that this is too sweet for me personally so we created what our family calls "The Salty Dog". I sprinkle the whole batch of finished puppy chow with about a teaspoon of salt. It adds a really nice sweet/salty flavor to each bite. A girlfriend of mine adds crushed up pretzel pieces to the cereal before she coats it with chocolate/peanut butter

attributes.source_text: It adds a really nice sweet/salty flavor to each bite

reviews.review_text:
Yummy! Just one thing- there should definatly be a disclaimer listed- THIS IS NOT A NEAT THING TO MAKE!! Every surface in my kitchen had chocolate or powdered sugar on it by the time I was done!! I have never made anything so MESSY! I mixed all the cereal with the chocolate mixture at once but added small amounts to the ziplock baggie (a big one) at a time. Next time I will mix half the cereal at a time with the chocolate. I like the trash bag idea someone else suggested!!!
I definatly used more then a cup and half of powdered sugar but I didn't measure it- just sprinkled it in.
Oh, it's all worth it when you taste them though!!

we make this as a special treat for the kids (ok, and adults) when we go to the lake every summer... i think chex in canada are different from those in the u.s. the first time we used canadian chex and they are so soft they broke into tiny crumbs  - too small for the kids to eat without making a colossal mess (although it made an incredible topping for ice cream!!) so we use quaker oat squares or quaker corn bran squares, which i think is more comparable to the american version of chex. we keep everything else the same.  i don't actually measure the sugar, i just dump it until it looks right, butwe use a fair bit less than 1.5 cups. our monkey munch is more brown than white, but thats just a personal preference. oh, also, i just work it around in a giant stainless mixing bowl - we found the ziplock broke up the cereal more.  i just finished making a batch with my 3 year old son, and we are off to the lake tomorrow!!!

we make this as a special treat for the kids

reviews.review_text:
Very good! The kids loved it, me too. I halved the recipe but ended up using more chex cereal. 
I didn't have enough chocolate chips in the house, so I used  unsweetened bakers squares to make up the difference.  It worked beautifully. Once the cereal was sprinkled with the powdered sugar, you will never know the difference. 
I assembled everything in a very large mixing bowl, sprayed w/ nonstick  spray. This step made cleanup much easier.

attributes.source_text: The kids loved it

reviews.review_text: This recipe is FABULOUS...I started eating this as a child when my grandmother made it.  She called it "WHITE TRASH" because she would make 2 or 3 batches at a time.  She would skip the Ziploc bag altogether and use a kitchen size trash bag.  I'm now 32 years old and make it every Christmas for my family.  I also send this to school as a teacher gift...I send it in with the recipe attached in early December though because I've learned that teachers get ALOT of sweets the last day of school before the Christmas break!

My DH loves it and even though I doubled the recipe, it was very simple. I used a big bowl to measure out the cereal (that's 18 cups guys!!) and poured the chocolate mixture over it in two batches. Then I used a regular kitchen trash bag to mix in the powdered sugar. Quick and painless. Stored it in a giant rubbermaid bowl, SUPER easy to transport. Thanks for a fun and yummy recipe!

reviews.review_text: I loved this and my family is crazy about it, too.  I read some of the reviews before I made it and since Nutella was suggested by one reviewer and since I have two huge jars of Nutella, I made it with Nutella.  I didn't have Chex but I did have a  Chex-like corn cereal that is new from Kashi, some puffed millet cereal and good ole Cheerios and used a third of each to fulfill the recipe.  I forgot the vanilla and used one third less confectioners sugar and it turned out just great.  It'll be fun to put this recipe thru different changes.  I'd like to add some nuts and seeds and, once I've used up the Nutella, I want to try semi-sweet or milk chocolate chips, or even white chocolate.  I love reviews, there is always so much to learn and so much to share!

items.label: Wholesome Homemade Honey Whole Wheat Bread
items.name: Wholesome Homemade Honey Whole Wheat Bread
items.description: This is the most awesome wheat bread I have ever eaten. It is worth the extra effort and because this recipe makes 4 loaves, you can freeze them and have enough for awhile :) Rising time included in prep.
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm water.
In a large bowl, combine butter, molasses, honey and salt and mix well.
Add yeast mixture and then gradually add flours.
Turn onto floured surface and knead until smooth.
Place in buttered bowl and let rise until double.
Punch down and let rest for a few minutes.
Divide dough into 4 parts and shape into loaves.
Place in greased pans and let rise for about an hour.
Bake at 375* for 35 to 40 minutes.

reviews.review_text: Wonderful! I halved the recipe. For the whole wheat flour I used 2 cups of wheat and ground it fresh in my blender. It made about 2 3/4 cups of flour. Plus I added 2 heaping Tablespoons of wheat gluten. Other than that, I followed the recipe, but had to add more white flour to make the dough manageable. It rose very well in the bowl, so I divided into 3 loaves. I thought they would continue to rise in the oven (they didn't). I used an egg wash just before baking and sprinkled sesame seeds on one loaf, rolled oats on another and left the last one plain. They came out pretty small, about 3 inches tall, but the one I already tried was light and delicious. Will definitely make this recipe again. BTW, I live just over a mile above sea level, so baking is always a challenge here.

attributes.source_text: was light and delicious

reviews.review_text: This bread was absolutely "delicious". I made it for the first time and it came out perfectly. I took the time to read all the reviews before beginning and that helped. I made a couple very minor adjustments. I added an extra half teaspoon of salt. I used my kitchenaid mixer. I turned the oven down to 350 degrees,. I also  added melted butter on top of the bread before baking. I tented the loaves about 20 minutes in and baked for 40 minutes. I made 3 loaves instead of what I thought would be 4 smaller ones. I was glad I did as the 3 came out a good size. I also made one a cinnamon, sugar, and raisin loaf. This recipe is definitely a keeper! The dough was smooth as silk as I was rolling it for the pan. Thanks for sharing!!

This bread is incredible! Great flavor, texture, and it slices like a dream! I made very few changes - used bread flour in place of the all-purpose and, since I had no molasses, replaced them with 3 tablespoons brown sugar and 1 tablespoon extra water. I also followed another reviewers suggestions and allowed the mixture of yeast, brown sugar, honey, salt, and flour to "sponge" for 45 minutes. I think that made all the difference! Important things to remember about bread-making: knead it well, especially whole wheat, to develop the gluten. Allow to rise for the full amount of time or until doubled, DON'T rush it! Throw ice cubes in the oven immediately after placing the bread in to form a great crust, and DO NOT open the oven for at least 10 minutes when first baking to ensure proper rise and baking. Allow bread to cool fully before cutting as well, or you'll end up with smooshed bread :) Enjoy!

One word.  Yum!  A friend had posted on FB that she tried your recipe and loved it.  I asked her for the recipe # and I have since made it.  The texture is nice and light.  I followed your ingredient list to a "T" but added in 2 TBSP gluten.  I make our own wheat bread regularly so followed the same guidelines while working with your wheat recipe.  This is what works for me...
I combined the yeast, water, molasses, honey, salt, gluten and 3 cups whole wheat flour.  I let is sit or "sponge" for about 45 minutes.  I then added the butter and remaining flour - both wheat and white.  It didn't take the full hour to rise in my bowl.  Maybe 40 minutes.  I put the divided dough in my bread pans and it rose for another 30 minutes.  I got 4 really good size loaves from the recipe.  Thanks for sharing!

attributes.source_text: The texture is nice and light

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe today for stuffed breads...I'm from Louisiana and yes, that's what we call them.  This is, without a doubt, the most forgiving yeast bread recipe I've ever used.  I threw everything into my stand mixer in the amount and order listed and turned on the dough hook.  I ended up with a big, super sticky glob so I started adding white flour by the 1/4 cupful (almost another cup and a half) until the dough started coming together.  I still had to peel it off of my dough hook to turn it out and kneading it was impossible.  It was like glue!  I added even more flour and finally got it to let go of my hands then I tossed it into the buttered bowl in disgust and covered it with a towel.  Lo and behold, it doubled in size!  By the time I was done, I had added about 2 1/2 cups more flour but I was working with small pieces not big loaves.  About 3/4 went into the stuffed breads (and they are AWESOME!  Next time they'll be crawfish!) and the rest got left in a pile and baked into what a bakery would call an "artisan" bread....lol!  This dough has great stretch and the bread has really nice flavor and texture.  This is my new favorite bread recipe!

attributes.source_text: This dough has great stretch

reviews.review_text: All the rave reviews are justified.  I tried this recipe mostly just for fun--as a treat for my family.  Those first four loaves disappeared with lightning speed, and this bread immediately replaced store-bought bread for us.  I make 4 loaves each weekend, and freeze 3 of them, which gives me a small "stash' of frozen loaves so that I can skip the occasional weekend if I'm not feeling well.  The frozen loaves thaw beautifully, and taste freshly made.  This bread feeds my family on a daily basis---we use it constantly.  It reminds me of the way bread used to taste when I was a kid, not the processed mess we have now.  Thank you, Karen!!!!!!!!!!!!!

attributes.source_text: as a treat for my family
This bread feeds my family on a daily basis

reviews.review_text: I thought I would update my review, just in case it sells this recipe better.  I have been making this bread for over a year now and is part of my best recipes collection.  I have discovered that in weight, the wheat flour is 2 lb. and 4 oz. and the white flour is 1.5 lb.  This makes the prep even easier.  This bread has it all; perfect structure and texture, incredible flavor, beautiful crust, and versatility...it toasts up very nicely.  I don't understand those who have altered their baking times and temperatures...375 for 40 minutes has worked every time for me, and the crust is supposed to be a bit on the dark side...perhaps your ovens are out of sinc?  I have easily made around 200 loaves with this formula since I found it, and it is always met with appreciation and grattitude.  My sister even offered to buy 8 loaves from me to give away as Christmas gifts, and she said each recipient loved it.  Awesome recipe!

I've made this bread three or four times now, and  each time it turned out super.  My little kids (5, 3, and 1) love it too...better than store-bought.  I've tweaked it successfully a couple times -- once replacing 1 C white flour with 1 C wheat germ.  Once I added a bit of cinnamon and an extra 1/4 c honey, and it made great morning toast.

I don't preheat my oven when baking bread.  I think that makes it rise a little more.  I use a instant-read digital thermometer to gauge if the bread is done (190 deg) since I'm not good at guessing.  I'm also extra patient with the rising as it seems to take extra long for my dough to rise...but it does get there in time.

reviews.review_text: Let me start by saying that yeast and I do not get along, so to take on a bread recipe such as this one, that yields four loaves of bread, was pretty ambitious of me.  On my first try, my bread turned out FABULOUS! I was so proud, that I was sending pictures to everyone.  Ladies and gentleman, I am here to tell you that if I can make bread using this recipe, anyone can.  It is easy to follow, and the ingredients are perfect. You will look like a seasoned bread baker.  The flavor is warm and homemade, everything wheat bread should be. Thanks for sharing such a wonderful recipe.

I have larger bread pans, so this makes 3 of them...lovely texture.  Waited until last 15 minutes before I put extra soft butter on the crust...substituted 4 Tablespoons brown sugar for the molasses, which I put in with the yeast and water (at my son's house when I made this and he was out of molasses).  Wonderful flavor!  Hey!  It has disappeared!!!!!!!
Tried it again today and as good as it was yesterday, today when I added the molasses, my family said the taste was "just okay"... of course, I made two recipes of it, so now I have twice as many "just okay" loaves of bread...anyone need some extra bread?  Probably won't make it again.

I am so impressed with this bread!  I can't believe that a bread that has more whole wheat flour than white flour can be so soft and tender; most whole wheat bread recipes yield a very dense, dry loaf.  Not this one!  It is perfect!  And it doesn't dry out, even after 4 or 5 days!  I subbed oil for the butter.  I didn't care for the molasses flavor, so I just used more honey.  In the loaves I have rising right now, I subbed brown sugar for the molasses.  DH and I  agreed it needed more salt, so I increased it by 1/2.  I also make 2 loaves instead of 4, since there are just two of us.  And yes, I end up adding 1/2 C. more white flour during the kneading because the dough is quite sticky.  The best WW bread I've ever made!  Thanks for sharing this great recipe!

I baked mine at 350 for 30 minutes since that's the way I bake all of my loaves and it turned out perfectly. They are perfectly cooked and not overly crusty.

EDIT to add: I just tried subbing a cup and a half of the all-purpose flour with baby oatmeal (dry) and it turned out fantastic! I brushed the loaves with an egg wash before baking and sprinkled with oats. When they came out of the oven I brushed them with a honey wash for a little extra sweetness. I love this recipe so much!

I used sugar instead of honey, but did add the molasses. It's pretty sweet (I'm not complaining). I did a slow rise in the fridge for about 7 hours then left them on the counter for about 2 hours, then cooked until they got to about 205* (which, according to Alton Brown is like *the* temp. for bread because it's right below where water boils so you know there's still moisture but not too much...or something). They are perfect...wonderful...lovely. Thank you!

reviews.review_text:
Delicious! I used to make this for DH and I, but our kids have to have spelt so I went in search of a spelt bread recipe. One day I FINALLY realized I could replace all the flour with whole grain spelt flour (it doesn't rise as much as it might with some white, but it tastes great so none of us care!), and sometimes I sub a cup of flaxseed meal for a cup of flour.
I usually just do honey instead of keeping molasses around and use olive oil in place of the butter. All of us love it! Plus, I don't have to knead it forever, which is a plus with two toddlers who might cause destruction if I'm elbow deep in bread dough for a half hour.

reviews.review_text: This is an awesome recipe! It turned out wonderfully on my first try, so either I've got a knack for bread making, or the recipe and directions were superb. I'm betting on the latter! =) I didn't have molasses on hand so I subbed in brown sugar like some other reviewers recommended, and it still turned out well. I'm trying it again today with molasses, and I'm sure it'll be even better, though I'm surprised at how much the molasses seemed to affect dough consistency. Ah, the musings of a beginner... =)  Thanks so much for sharing! I'll be making this a lot. ~Laura

Great in the bread machine, too! 1/4 recipe = 1 pound loaf, 1/2 recipe = 2 pound loaf. For bread machine, put liquids in the bottom, then whole wheat flour, then white flour, then yeast on top.

My new favorite whole wheat recipe. I have a hard time finding any whole wheat bread that I like. I think the molasses really makes the difference. You don't actually taste the molasses, but it really enhances the nut-like flavor of the whole wheat. I'm looking forward to experimenting with other flours and whole grains.

It was fun to make and I learned about being patient while the bread had to rise.  I liked the texture, it was crusty on the outside and soft on the inside.  We will make it again.  Thankyou." love, Veronica

items.label: Our Favourite Lemon Loaf
items.name: Our Favourite Lemon Loaf
items.description: This is soooo nummmmy!! for lemon lovers. Very good warm or cold. (have been making this for years and cannot remember where it came from, probably from my Mom.)
instructions: In a large bowl, cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating until creamy.
Blend in milk.
In another bowl, mix together flour, baking powder, salt and lemon rind.
Pour into batter.
Stir to moisten.
Scrape into greased 9 x 5 inch loaf pan.
Bake in 350f degree oven for 55 to 60 minutes.
Cool in pan for 5 minutes.
Remove to rack and while still hot, with a toothpick poke holes all over the top of the loaf, and spoon glaze evenly over.
Cool.
Glaze: Combine lemon juice and sugar in saucepan.
Stir and heat till sugar is dissolved.
Spoon evenly over top of hot loaf.

reviews.review_text: Holy heck, this recipe is amazeballs ... I was actually looking for a different lemon recipe (pie) and stumbled across this loaf recipe .. I decided to forget the pie and make this instead ... am I ever glad I did! I used the suggested 1/4 cup lemon juice and 1/4 cup milk, other than that followed the recipe exactly ... and I finally got to use the lemon zester that i purchased from Epicure 8 years ago (seriously, it was still in the plastic!). And the loaf tastes even better the next day (only one piece survived the kitchen frenzy that ensued once the loaf came out of the oven). This recipe is a keeper, trust me! :)

reviews.review_text: Very good!  I have a friend who buys starbucks lemon loaf for breakfast every day.  I made this for him. He said the flavor was right-on.  However, said Starbucks was just a little lighter.  And the icing was different.  Next time, I think I will beat the egg whites separately & fold them in.  We'll see if that works.  On it's own, this is a very nice recipe that I will make again.  Thanks for sharing!!

I also decreased the sugar to 1/2 cup and it came out GREAT.  The only odd thing was the icing--should it be powdered sugar, perchance?  Mine came out watery so I just poked holes in the cake and poured it on top.    Heaven.  Heaven heaven heaven.  Thank you soooo much for posting!

We are big lemon lovers in my house so the only change I made was to use the zest of 2 lemons and the juice of 1 of the lemons in the batter (the juice of the other was for the glaze). It was perfect. My DH always laughs and says my loaves/baking only last 2 days in the house, well this one lasted less than 24 hours between him and my son. LOL Great recipe. I will keep this in my "favorite" cook book for years to come!
