items.label: Pizza Hut Style Pizza Dough (Bread Machine)
items.name: Pizza Hut Style Pizza Dough (Bread Machine)
items.description: I came across the recipe from a copy cat recipe source. The 2 hours includes dough cycle time. This is one of the best pizza dough recipes I have found.
instructions: Add ingredients (except for cornmeal) to machine bread pan in order as per manufacturer's instructions.
Set to \
cycle.
Lightly grease one 9 x 13-inch pan and sprinkle with cornmeal.
When the dough cycle is complete, roll out dough and place in pan.
Let rest in pans for 10-15 minutes.
Add toppings of your choice.
Bake at 350°F until done (approximately 20 minutes, depending on the thickness of toppings).
I make the pizza in 9x13 rectangular pans rather than the round pizza pans, because the squares pieces are easier to reheat and pack in school lunches.

reviews.review_text: I used to work at Pizza Hut.<br/>The way they used to do the "pan" dough is this way.<br/>Out of dough, make a dough ball(s) and then using a rolling pin evenly roll it out into a round or whatever shape you desire. <br/>Then, you oil the deep pan well (the whole bottom must be covered)<br/>Place the rolled dough into the pan and spray with an oil spray.<br/>Cover the pan with a lid or plastic and place into a warm place for about 40-70 minutes. (since you don't have the equipment Pizza Hut has, you will need to keep an eye on it )<br/>A good idea for this is to warm the oven to "just-barely-warm" and turn it off, placing the pan with dough in.<br/>Once you take it out, sauce the pizza taking care not to press hard with spoon/spatula.<br/>Spread a cup of cheese on top of sauce and then your toppings, starting with meats ending with veggies.<br/>Top with another cup of chz<br/>Pop it in the oven.<br/>IF you are making a pepperoni only pizza, place all the cheese on the bottom.

This is the closest I have come to Pizza Hut pizza crust.  I was fortunate enough to get similar pans to the ones they use at Pizza Hut at Farm & Fleet.  I ended up doing this in my kitchen aid mixer, letting the dough rise about thirty minutes then rolling it and letting it rise in the pans for an hour.  The reason for the long rising was that I was trying to make this fit into two 14â€? pans.  Next time I will make a recipe and a half for two 14â€? pans we like it thicker and it did not quite make it to the edge of the pan.  Thank you for positing this recipe, it will be made weekly in our house. Also I doubled the garlic and onion powder omitted the msg.  For those of you that think itâ€™s not quite like Pizza Hut.  Try putting 4 to 5 Tablespoons of vegetable oil in the pan tilt it good to get the surface coated with the oil.  Then put your dough in carefully not to get to much oil on the top, let it rise in the pan then top and enjoy.  Some will say I do not want the extra oil but that is the way Pizza Hut pan pizza is made.

attributes.source_text: we like it thicker

reviews.review_text: I have researched Pizza Hut dough recipes for awhile, and it is true - they do use a lot of oil in the pans to get that way, so that is what I did today. I followed the recipe directions exactly, but when it came time to pan it, I poured an (admittedly) disgustingly large amount of olive oil in the pan. About an 1/8" deep worth of oil.. I have a 14" deep dish pan. I patted the dough into place, it was swimming in it, lol.. I let it rise in there for about an hour. Then I baked it for 15 minutes at 450.. topped it off, then baked again for another 15 minutes. LOL - it came out EXACTLY like Pizza Huts! The flavor and texture were dead-on, and my grown kids couldn't believe I made it myself, lol.. Trust me folks - if you truly want to get the Pizza Hut effect, use THIS recipe and follow my techniques - you won't be disappointed! Thanks for the post, judge!

This was really, really good crust especially for how easy it was. Not the exact same as Pizza Hut's but definitely don't feel gross after eating it the way I do at the Hut....made the dough in the bread machine exactly as recipe stated except didn't use msg. Yes, it is a bit sticky, but I floured my counter and lightly greased and floured my hands and had no problems whatsoever rolling it into a circle, I actually found the dough pretty easy to work with. Since I was using a pizza stone I put the cornmeal down and a good drizzle of EVOO. Baked the dough no toppings at 400 for 15 mins, probably could have gone a few mins longer. Topped and baked another 15 mins. My sun dried tomato topping started to look extra crisp at this point so took it out. Pie was just cooked all the way through but think I'll bake a bit longer before topping next time as it was still lighter than I would have preferred. Two of us motored through half this pizza in one sitting!! Thanks for posting, can't wait to make it again.

attributes.source_text: it is a bit sticky

reviews.review_text:
I wanted to add a update to my last review so I copied what I had previously written and added the following note.  I made 2 large cookie sheets full of pizza.  I had an entire pizza left after dinner because the men in my family weren't very hungry that night.  I thought great, I will free the other whole pizza and will have a home cooked entire pizza for next time.  Wrong...within 2 days they cut and microwaved the entire frozen pizza and ate it for snacks!  I guess that says what they thought of it big time!

Here is my original review:I used this recipe because it had such unusual ingredients. I have been searching in vain for a long time, for a good recipe which would satisfy my family who likes thick crust and myself who doesn't. It seemed I never before was able to achieve a happy medium which made everyone happy. I spread my dough onto 2 cooky sheets. I let them raise slightly and put the toppings on. I baked them both on the top rack of my oven for 20 minutes. They turned out perfect. For the first time not only was everyone happy but I finally got a crust that was done all the way through and yet not burned at all! Thanks a lot! This is a keeper...just because it is great, not because it is a copycat recipe.  I only used the dough recipe not the rest.

attributes.source_text: after dinner
ate it for snacks
satisfy my family who likes thick crust
likes thick crust

reviews.review_text: A really great crust.  I will definately make this one again!  I have been searching for years for a good pizza crust.  My husband loves when I make homemade pizza, but I was never happy with my crust before -- that is until now!  I followed a couple of the above suggestions, I also used 1 tsp each of the  garlic and onion powders.  And, I put a little BBQ sauce (we had BBQ chicken pizza) on the crust and baked it for a couple minutes before adding the chicken, red onions and cheese.  I also sprinkled just a little cornmeal on my cookie sheet.  I liked it.  It was just a little something different.  The dough was thin, but not paper thin and it wasn't too thick.  My cookie sheets are 13 x 18 (they're like the heavy ones they use on cookie shows) and I only got one pizza.  But I liked the thickness of the crust, so if I wanted more than one pizza in the future I would double the recipe.  One thing, I did have to add a little flour to the dough after it was finished in the machine because it was really sticky.  A little flour folded/kneeded into it and it pressed right into my cookie sheet and was quite tender but still able to hold the toppings really well.  Give this one a try, it's a keeper in our house!

attributes.source_text: The dough was thin, but not paper thin
it wasn't too thick
was quite tender
My husband loves when I make homemade pizza

reviews.review_text:
I ran across this recipe last month and my family loves it! I use my zoji breadmaker or my kitchenaid stand mixer and the recipe comes out fine for me. I did double this recipe for both appliances and did decrease the water. I use pizza stones, olive oil and cornmeal dusted on the stones and a temp of 425 and prebake for 10 mins before adding toppings and then decrease the temp to 375 and bake for another 15 or 20 mins. The crust turns out chewy but light. I have a large family and I get 4 "16" INCH crusts since I doubled the recipe. I do add parmesan cheese(sp) and italian seasoning to the mix along with the onion and garlic powder. I do add the accent to it and have made it without and taste was no different. I am going to start using half wheat flour and half bread flour the next time I make this.
This also makes great bread sticks and calzones. All in all this recipe is a definate keeper, it may not taste exactly like pizza hut but its close and I would know, I worked there for 5 years LOL.

attributes.source_text: my family loves it
The crust turns out chewy but light
The crust turns out chewy but light

reviews.review_text: Ok, here is what I did....First I tripled the recipe and I made two batches. So that is a total of x 6!!! I took both batches and divided the dough into 16 even rounds. Rolled them out into individual pizzas, I had a total of 32 rounds. I preheated my oven to 450 and poked each with a fork, brushed with olive oil and grated fresh parm. on them. Baked 3 to a sheet for 6-8 minutes, cooled and stored in large bags. I made my own sauce and had all the kids at youth group make their own pizzas and cooked again with toppings on for about 5-10 minutes @ 450 to warm the toppings and melt the cheese. I was the love of the party, Thay can't wait until we do it again. Thank you so much.

attributes.source_text: had all the kids at youth group make their own pizzas
I was the love of the party

reviews.review_text: Yum!  Wow, so good!  I had enough dough to make a pizza and some cheesy bread.  I added some random Italian seasons and one teaspoon of gluten, and it was ridiculous,  Like a bunch of reviewers said, I baked my crust for a few minutes before loading it up (lost track exactly due to wine consumption) but couldn't be more than 5-7 minutes.  I also brushed the entire thing-pre-topping-with a mix of melted margarine and garlic powder.  I am notorious for making nasty, hard, flavorless pizza crusts, and this was divine!  (Ok, I'll give most of the credit to the bread machine.)  If you've been scared of pizza crusts, like me, give this a try, you will feel like you should be on Food Network!

attributes.source_text: a mix of melted margarine and garlic powder

reviews.review_text: I have made this a few times now and it is my favourite pizza dough recipe.  After reading the reviews and experimenting I add an extra 1/2 tsp of both garlic powder and onion powder.  I also add about a teaspoon of italian seasoning.  <br/><br/>I received a round Cuisinart pizza stone for Christmas and was eager to use it.  I was at a loss of how exactly to adapt this recipe to use it.  After a little research I decided to place the the stone in the rack one above center in the oven, to warm the pizza stone from a cold oven to 450 for 25 minutes prior to cooking.  We do not like cornmeal so I placed a piece of parchment paper under the pizza dough after taking it out of the breadmaker.  This ensured that the dough did not stick to the stone.  I did not oil the bottom of the dough.  After allowing 15 minutes for the dough to rest, I topped it and brushed melted butter around the edges.  I left the oven temperature at 450 and cooked the pizza for 18 minutes, at which time it looked perfectly cooked on the top.  At around 14 minutes, I added more butter to the crust (we like it to be a little bit soft.   It was perfectly browned on the top and bottom.  <br/><br/>The amount of dough was a little too much for my small stone but it made for a wonderfully thick crust that did not droop. <br/><br/>I did not have a peel to put the pizza on the stone so I used a rimless cookie sheet.  I was able to pull the pizza off the stone easily to a plate as the crust was perfectly cooked.<br/><br/>Thank you for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: wonderfully thick crust
we like it to be a little bit soft

reviews.review_text: I have made this recipe several times now and am very happy with the results.  I don't have a bread machine, so what I do is: mix one cup of warm water and one teaspoon of sugar in a bowl and sprinkle yeast on top.  I let it sit for about 10 minutes until yeast is foamy.  Then I add the yeast/water mixture to the flour/baking powder/salt/garlic powder/and remaining teaspoon of sugar (I omit the msg for health reasons and onion powder because I don't have it... also, because many readers have commented on there being too much water, I reserve the remaining 1/3 cup of water and add it as necessary).  I bake my dough on a pizza stone in a 500 degree oven.  Before putting the dough in I put a little sauce on and brush the crust with olive oil and sprinkle generously with garlic powder.  Then I bake the crust alone for about 5 minutes; remove and top with more sauce and cheese (and toppings); and return to the oven until cheese is melted and bubbly.  Works like a charm :)

yuck. i tried this once a couple years back. tooke me a while to find the perfect pizza crust. you want to make a REAL pizza crust? the easiest recipe ever from peter reinhart. just mix together 4 1/2 cups flour, 1/2 tsp yeast, 1 3/4 tsp salt, 1/4 cup oil, 1 3/4 cups COLD water. don't add any more flour. you want a wet dough. if it's hard for you to knead (if you're not using a dough hook on a mixer), let it sit in the fridge for a half hour. then stretch it out, and fold it a few times. then let that sit in the fridge 1-5 days (vital, 3 days is perfect). you will get a bubbly pizza crust with a lot of bite and flavor. then never  make this recipe again.

Wonderful. I've got my crust recipe now!
I don't have a bread machine, so I proofed the yeast with the 2 tsp of sugar and then 1/4 cup warm water.
When making the dough, I added 2 teaspoons of oregano, and only 1 cup of water (making the water count 1 1/4 cup). I did layer oil in when the dough was rising. I made breadsticks out of them instead of pizza, and they were great! They rose really nicely. I cooked at 400 degrees like other people suggested, but it got done a lot quicker-- I think it would have burned had I returned to put pizza topping on it. The oil in the rising made the bottom come out crunchy like Pizza Hut. Thank so much!

attributes.source_text: made the bottom come out crunchy

reviews.review_text: Five stars!  It turned out beautifully, and I don't believe I'll ever need to try another crust recipe! The texture was great. Hubby and son both complimented me on the pizza, and came back for extra helpings! Instead of using onion powder (which I didn't have), I used garlic bread sprinkle.  (Tip: Before rolling out the dough, sprinkle with flour knead it well to eliminate air bubbles.)  Once dough was placed in pans, I brushed it with olive oil, and put it in the oven for 5 minutes.  Lastly, I layered the toppings on the base and popped it back in the oven for an additional 15 minutes. This recipe has earned a permanent place in my recipe box!

attributes.source_text: Hubby and son both complimented me on the pizza
Hubby and son both complimented me on the pizza

reviews.review_text: I just cooked this on my outdoor charcoal grill last night and it was PERFECT! It does have a Pizza Hut taste to it, but honestly I think this version tasted better! I left out the MSG as well, but it still turned out fine. I will never EVER be buying store brought pizza dough again! If youâ€™re thinking about making this recipe, I highly recommend it. The bread machine did all the work while I cleaned house, and when it was done I wrapped it up in a lightly oiled zip lock bag until I needed it. And I donâ€™t know about youâ€¦ but Iâ€™ve never been a fan of homemade pizza because itâ€™s such a letdown after youâ€™ve had the real deal at a restaurantâ€¦ but this recipe is sure to PLEASE and tastes as good if not BETTER than the real thing. My only advice is to use good cheese (preferably cheese youâ€™ve shredded yourself). I used whole real mozzarella cheese balls that I sliced with cheap canned spaghetti sauce and a few fresh basil leaves!!!! Magnificent, I must make it again and again and again!!

We made this recipe this evening and it was the best pizza dough that I have ever tried. I did add about 1/4 cup extra of the flour and omitted the MSG (for health reasons). The dough was still sticky, but easy to handle. I made one large pizza and an order of breadsticks (just rolled out the dough & covered it with olive oil, garlic salt, parsley, and shredded cheese, then sliced with a pizza cutter before baking). I cooked the pizza at 450 degrees for ten minutes with nothing on it except a drizzle of olive oil for ten minutes. Pulled it from the oven and then added my toppings. I returned this (and the breadsticks) to the oven and then baked for an additional twenty minutes. The pizza came out perfect.

It has a wonderful texture and does not rest heavy (probably do to the baking powder) as most crusts seem to do. The cornmeal adds texture, but doesn't create that grainy taste in your mouth.

This is my new favorite bread recipe and kudos to you for sharing it!

attributes.source_text: The dough was still sticky
does not rest heavy

reviews.review_text: CullinaryJudge, I really enjoyed this pizza crust and so did my family-- yum! I reduced the water to 1 1/4 c, replaced 1/2 c of the white flour with soy flour, and omitted the MSG (but added some gluten and ascorbic acid). I coated the bottom of an 11x15" pan with a tbsp of olive oil, pressed the crust in, brushed it with another tbsp of olive oil and baked it for 10 min at 400 F. Only took another 10 minutes once the toppings were on it. What a wonderful thick, pan pizza crust, which actually reminded me of the crust at a place called Rocky Rococo's (a chain of pizza places, mostly in Wisconsin). Very good. Thanks!

attributes.source_text: What a wonderful thick, pan pizza crust
so did my family

reviews.review_text: WOW--so delicious!!  Thumbs up!  Made this tonight...the crust was tender-crisp.  A nice crunchy, chewy dough.  By far a much better crust than Pizza Hut or any Italian pizza joint in our area.  I didn't use MSG because I didn't have any, so in place,  I added a Tbsp of Italian Seasoning and increased the galic and onion powder to 1/2 tsp each.  Since I was adding Italian sausage as a topping, I baked the crust (brushed with a coat of olive oil) at 400 for 8 minutes.  Then topped the pizza with sauce, mozzarella, sausage and baked at 350 for an additional 15 minutes.   Thanks for a filling and delicious dinner.

attributes.source_text: the crust was tender-crisp
A nice crunchy, chewy dough
A nice crunchy, chewy dough
Thanks for a filling and delicious dinner

items.label: Mexican Enchilada Sauce
items.name: Mexican Enchilada Sauce
items.description: I got this recipe from by grmil who was born and raised in Mexico City. The secret to its flavor is the cocoa
instructions: Combine all dry ingredients in a small bowl.
Stirring constantly, slowly add enough of the water to make a thin paste.
Pour into pan and add rest of water.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens.
Stir in tomato sauce.
Use in your favorite enchilada recipe.
The amounts on the ingredients are very flexible.
For instance, if I am feeding my kids who do not like\
, I will halve the chili powder and double the tomato sauce.
Experiment to suit your taste, but don't leave out the cocoa.
For a quick meal, we will soften a corn tortilla in a bit of hot oil, drag it through the sauce, and lay it flat on a plate.
cover it with grated cheddar cheese, sprinkle with chopped onions and sliced black olives.
Then cover with another softened sauced tortilla and melt the cheese in the microwave for 1 minute on high.

reviews.review_text: I like enchiladas but they can be gratuitiously calorie laden.  And the sauce you buy inthe store is not that good.  But I had some chicken I wanted to make enchiladas with AND I thought this recipe looked good.  The allowed by to avoid over-fatting the tortillas.  I just drug them through the warm enchilada sauce and made chicken cheese enchaladas with a little extra sauce poored over the enchiladas.  And cheese.  I was short of time so I nuked the enchiladas.  These were surprisingly good nuked.  And since it is just DH and I, I have left over enchilada sauce.  Will be making more.  And I say that with anticipation.

This is a keeper, although I did very slightly alter it to suit my taste. It also makes WAY more than I can use, so I found a solution that works for me. I take all the dry ingredients, double or triple, and put them in a spice jar. When I want to make this I can use the amount that works for me - just add a squirt of paste & the water. Canned sauce today was $1.58. My little spice jar - that will go mucho further - much less. Not to mention that in a small kitchen the spice jar takes up far less space than a can.

Don't skip the cocoa.

I debated and debated about how to review this recipe.  First I want to say that it is delicious and it seemed to get better the next day.  However, I did take some liberties in how I prepared this.  I was cooking some pork strips (shoulder cuts) in the crock pot, found some tomatoes that had been cooked down in the freezer so I wanted to use up both of them together.  Was thinking Italian until I saw this recipe and immediately switched as I have all ingredients on hand.  I omitted the water and tomatoe sauce in lieu of the cooked tomatoes.  Put everything in the crock pot except the flour and cooked on low until i got home from work (9 hours or so).  I then took the pork out and let it cool, prepared the flour by making a slurry with water and added that to the crock, turned it to high.  I shredded the pork and made enchiladas with the pork and this lovely dark rich colored sauce.  They were good that night, but even better the next day!  It makes a mighty tastey enchilada. I will be passing this on to my daughter as it fixable for a vegetarian.  Thank you for posting this wonderful sauce Ms Mattthews :)

attributes.source_text: this lovely dark rich colored sauce

reviews.review_text: Simpler being better, this is really good as is.  Albeit, like most humans, I find myself unable to escape meddling and "leave well enough alone;" thus, I have to say a touch more garlic is indeed an enhancement. I also replaced a couple teaspoons of water with ketchup to afford enough sweet to contrast the aromatics and salt--a bit of brown or white sugar would suffice. Finally, an ever so small--I'm talking teensty-weentsy pinch; in fact "pinch" is too much--just the tiniest nearly unoticable hint of chinese 5 spice actually improves upon this recipe's excellence. Just my humble opinion.

This has got to be the BEST sauce I've ever had, it is sure going into my BEST of 2013 Book.  Was making recipe 121147 and didn't have any canned so choose this one to try.  You are so right about the cocoa being a much needed for this recipe.  The only thing I did differant was cut it in half as it was just DH and me but should have made the full amount to have on hand.  Next time I'll also try the cumin but don't know how it could be any better.  DH said "make sure you tell everyone how great it is" that's some compliment as he never says much.  I also liked that it was pretty fast, without a long simmer time.  The photo is not the prettiest but it sure tasted great

Thank you Donna- this sauce is so good I could cry.  I grew up in California with mexican food a staple in my diet.  However for the past 20+ years have been living in north eastern Canada.  Needless to say Mexican cooking is a rarity here as most ingredients are difficult to find.  This recipe has expanded the repitore of meals I can serve family and guests and it gives me a boost when feeling homesick.  

I added the chili powder one T at a time but ended up using it all ;)  I also used fresh garlic, and a bit of cumin and cinnamon.  Wonderful!!!

I just love,love, love this sauce. When we were in Europe I missed enchilada sauce so much that I hunted forever a sauce recipe that would fulfill my expectations. This is it! Now that we are back in the US canned sauce abounds. But not for us. I use this for enchiladas and is my secret weapon in my chili. I have used different types of chili powder, my personal favorite being a "dark chili powder". You can't go wrong with this one. And of note, if you fell like your hanging out at the stove for ever waiting for this to thicken (I did at first) simply turn up the heat and keep whisking slowly. I make this in my big open high sided non-stick pan. Works great! Thanks for sharing.

The use of cocoa in the sauce made it attractive to me, since I love Mole.  It added smokiness and depth, but did not make the sauce sweet.  Since I knew I was making the recipe for chicken enchiladas, I boiled 3 extra large chicken breasts in water to cover, and used 3 C. of the remaining "broth" to replace the water.  Replaced garlic salt with 1 tsp. jarred, roasted garlic.  Added 1/2 tsp. cocoa powder and 1-4 oz. can diced green chiles to deepen the smokiness flavor.  Next time may cut the chili powder a bit.  My fiance and I have a high tolerance for heat/spices -- but to me, the chili powder flavor predominated.  This may be the result of the brand of chili powder I used.   McCormack brand seems more powerful than bargain powder, and McCormack is what I used. For the recipe:  corn tortillas, shredded chicken moistened with the sauce and shredded cheddar inside, sauce on the bottom of the baking dish and over the top of the assembled enchiladas, and extra shredded cheddar on top.  This sauce is much better than canned sauce, and low fat too!  If my fiance liked sour cream, I would've added a bit to the sauce.  Next I'll ry add a bit of cream cheese to thicken, and mellow the overall flavor.

attributes.source_text: It added smokiness and depth
did not make the sauce sweet

reviews.review_text: This is the recipe I've been looking for my whole life! I was really dubious about the tomato sauce and am grateful that you made the comment that you did about it. I detest tomato based enchilada sauces. I'm glad I trusted your recipe! I couldn't get mine to thicken, however, and increased the flour to five tablespoons. I've made this recipe twice now and it's awesome. I also added two tablespoons of cumin and several dashes of Cholula to spice it up. And I tripled the oregano (because I love oregano). I didn't have garlic salt and used 1 tsp garlic powder and 2 teaspoons of salt. Yeah, I'm a saltaholoic. But it was fabulous and hubby and I both give this recipe a huge thumbs up. Thank you thank you thank you! Oh.. by the way, I also added olive oil. I think it helped enchance the flavors and gave it a bit of smoothness. I'd love to know how your friend in Mexico City serves it. I read somewhere that these casserole style enchiladas are not Mexican tradition at all and that the sauce is used more like a dip. Do you think she could fill you in on how it's served???? Thanks!

attributes.source_text: several dashes of Cholula to spice it up
gave it a bit of smoothness
hubby and I both give this recipe a huge thumbs up

reviews.review_text: My first attempt at making my own Enchilada sauce and I don't know if I'll ever want to try making any others.  Husband and I loved this sauce.  Since we were serving to our young boys, I started with just 2 tbsp. of chili powder and followed the rest of the recipe as stated except I doubled the tomato sauce as the author suggested when feeding to her kids - great tip.  I let it simmer on the stove for awhile and then used it to make some bean and cheese enchiladas - it was fantastic.  The sauce is so easy to make and the cocoa powder gives it great depth.  I used what little sauce I had left to drizzle over some rice I served with the Enchiladas.  Husband said it was the best Enchilada sauce he has had.  Great easy recipe - a real keeper!

attributes.source_text: Husband and I loved this sauce
Since we were serving to our young boys
the cocoa powder gives it great depth
Husband said it was the best Enchilada sauce he has had

reviews.review_text: This sauce is delicious. Itâ€™s very close to what Iâ€™ve had in Mexican restaurants. I used it on cheese enchiladas, and the dark color threw me off a little bit. At first I thought I had burned it, but it was from the coca. I made one change to the recipe. I only had a 14 ounce can of tomato sauce, and because I didnâ€™t want to refrigerate half a can, or double the recipe, I added the whole can. The flavor was still rich with just the right amount of spiciness. I will be using this sauce again and again. Thank you for the recipe!

attributes.source_text: The flavor was still rich
just the right amount of spiciness
very close to what Iâ€™ve had in Mexican restaurants

reviews.review_text: I waited all week to try this recipe- I've been looking for a good enchilada sauce recipe for a casserole I like to make.  Saturday finally rolled around and I gathered all my ingredients together only to find that I had run out of chili powder!  Instead, I used 1 and 1/2 tablespoons of sweet paprika and crossed my fingers.  And it turned out great!  So, if you are ever in a pinch or just don't want any of the spice, you can use sweet paprika.  Of course, I can't wait to try it again with the chili powder.  Really great recipe!!

OMG!!!  I made this recipe because I had a pound of lean ground beef in my fridge, 7 corn tortillas in a bag and no money for the next couple of days.  The sauce reminded me of the food I had in Mexico a few years back.  Absolutely SUPER, easy to make, and altogether wonderful.  I used a 5.5 oz can of V8 to make the paste, cut the chili powder back to 2 instead of 3 Tbsps. and cut the water by 1 cup.  It's fabulous and I can't thank you enough!!!!

attributes.source_text: The sauce reminded me of the food I had in Mexico a few years back

reviews.review_text: Found this recipe kind of by mistake.  What a wonderful mistake!  The cocoa intrigued me.  I had to make it. I was planning enchiladas for a future night, but I couldn't wait. I love that all the ingredients are those that you have on hand. I made them tonight and we loved this sauce. I will never buy a can again. I made it a little spicy, but we like it that way. Very much like what I had in Mexico. I didn't have any trouble with it thickening.  And yes...it freezes very well. Enjoy!!!

attributes.source_text: I made it a little spicy, but we like it that way
Very much like what I had in Mexico

reviews.review_text: This was so good, i used it for "easiest beef enchiladas ever" recipe # 17586; i took the advice of a couple of the reviewers and added about 1/4 tsp. cumin, and i substituted half the water for beef broth, i also let it simmer, uncovered, and reduce down about 1/4 of the way, about 40 minutes. I will never use canned enchilada sauce again, this sauce taste better, and it was so easy to make, with ingredients i always have in my pantry. This also freezes really well. Thanks Donna.

This is the one! I was looking for a enchilada sauce that tasted as good as what our favorite Mexican eatery serves. This is it! I used chicken broth in place of the water, but used the full amount of spices called for. It was just right. My dh and sons agreed that we want to use this for not only enchiladas but also tacos and all other Mexican meals that need a sauce. This is a real money saver too. Tonight I used this sauce with(recipe #165113). Thanks Donna for this delicious recipe.

attributes.source_text: tasted as good as what our favorite Mexican eatery serves
My dh and sons agreed that we want to use this
My dh and sons agreed that we want to use this

reviews.review_text: Made this sauce last night to use in the Enchilada casserole #21410.  I agree with other poster about not liking the sauce when I made it but it was fantastic in the casserole. The sauce is easy to make and as Donna points out, adjust the spice to suit your tastes. I find canned tomato sauces lacking in sweet tomato flavor so I added a can of tomato paste to bump up the flavor.  Very nice.  I will use again for any red enchilada recipe.

I've been using this recipe for years now. I don't even have to review it, I have it memorized. Such an easy and great sauce. You can tweak it to taste. Mild chili powder for the "no spice" people, or hot chili powder for the adventurous. I add a bit more flour and have been using this for my vegetarian chili with beans since shortly after I started using it. It is every ones favorite chili. Even people who don't like chili, love mine! You have to try this recipe!

items.label: 1 Pan Fudge Cake
items.name: 1 Pan Fudge Cake
items.description: This is my favorite chocolate cake. No fuss, no mess and very moist. Back in the early days when it was paycheck to paycheck, this simple dessert made it into his lunchbox many a day because it was cheap and simple. No eggs, no milk.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
In an ungreased 9 x 13 pan- yes UNgreased, sift all dry ingredients.
Add the liquids and stir just until blended.
Bake for 25 minutes.
Frost with your favorite frosting, cake is extremely moist so care must be taken that you don't tear up the top of the cake.

reviews.review_text: I'm adding my vote to this quick cake.  Had a cake craving for the last couple days, but didn't want to do a full-out baking session.  I remembered that I used to make a one pan cake when my boys were younger, and search zaar for one.  Since it's only the 2 of us, I halved the recipe.  Used dark cocoa, all coffee (from the morning) and also sprinkled some caramel/milk choc chips, mini marshmallows, and some crushed brown sugar glazed pecans on top.   It smelled wonderful, and was delicious.  Best of all, we don't have the whole 9x13 pan to eat (and I would too).   Good quick dessert - will make again.  Now looking for a spice or carrot cake one.   Hubby says not as good as my regular desserts; but since I'm the one who makes it - it will be made again.

attributes.source_text: Good quick dessert

reviews.review_text: Just as good as the old fashioned coffee/egg/milk moist chocolate cake recipes. The changes I made were to cut the flour to 1 1/2 cups and add about a tablespoon of instant coffee to the liquids. I also sprayed the entire pan lightly with pam, lined the bottom with fitted parchment paper, and then gave another quick spray of pam. I let the cake sit about 10 minutes after coming out of the oven, inverted it onto a plastic flexible cutting board, and then easily peeled off the parchment. I frost with a buttercream frosting consisting of 1 stick of butter, 2 cups of powdered sugar, and a few tablespoons of milk (I usually double the frosting recipe). Nothing but rave reviews. This is a keeper.

attributes.source_text: moist chocolate cake

reviews.review_text: DH just became vegan and I've been searching for a cake that he can eat. I came across this and tried it today.  2 of my kids are home and descended on it as soon as it came out of the oven (I barely had time to dust it with powdererd sugar).  DH is away and won't be home until tomorrow, and  I'm sure that there will be none left for him.....I guess I'll just have to make it again! The only problem I had was that after 25 minutes, the cake did not look done.  I left it in for another 5 minutes.  By then it looked good; but after cooling for a few minutes it sank in several spots, and on tasting, it wasn't cooked through in those spots.  I will have to not be afraid to let it bake for maybe a full 35 minutes next time.

attributes.source_text: 2 of my kids are home and descended on it as soon as it came out of the oven

reviews.review_text: What a fantastic, easy scratch cake recipe - reviews were truly correct - I made it this morning & can't stay away from it!  I substituted hot-brewed morning coffee in place of the 1 1/2 c. water since it brings a deeper chocolate-taste out (I do this in brownies too) & used Hershey's Special Dark Cocoa.   Then made a simple glaze of One Bowl Easy Chocolate Glaze while the cake was still very warm: 8 oz tub of frozen Cool Whip (I used Lite) & 6 squares Baker's Semi-Sweet Chocolate; microwave both in a glass bowl on high for 1 min; stir; microwave an add'l 30-60 sec & stir until completely melted, shiny & smooth; pour entirely over warm cake.  It's the tastiest & I'll be making this repeatedly!

attributes.source_text: brings a deeper chocolate-taste out

reviews.review_text: Great recipe!  I found this recipe the other day, and I thought there was no way it could be that easy -- so I went home that night and tried it.  It was that easy!  The only problem I had was that it seemed a little difficult to mix the ingredients in the baking pan, so I was afraid I had mixed it too much since the recipe said "just until blended."  But it still turned out great.  I topped it with a pecan/coconut frosting, and everyone loved it.  I'll definitely keep this recipe and make it again and again and again.  Thanks for posting this recipe for all of us chocoholics!

What a super and easy cake!  I wanted to whip something up to treat the girls at work, and being short of time, this cake really fit the bill.  I put in a generous 1/2 c. cocoa, but that was the only change.  Very dark and moist.  I left it un-iced, and really felt it stood well on it's own.  Stirring the ingredients in the pan definitely decreased clean up, but because of the shape of the pan, it took a teeny bit longer to get all the ingredients incorporated well than it may have in a bowl -- definitely not a concern, just an observation.  A terrific snack cake, a great budget stretcher and super speedy!

It is easy to even quarter this recipe for a single portion or two since there are no eggs! very easy to make, okay flavor! thanks for the recipe!  
EDIT:  the flavor really grew on me, and its great with some icing, i made cupcakes today and prefer this over them with the same frosting!  love it!  will use this forever.  plus i have a friend who is vegan so this will be great for her.

This cake is absolutely DELISH! but a bit rich.  If you eat it fresh out of the oven with a nice cold glass of milk or better yet, a bowlful of vanilla ice cream, it is unimaginably tasty.  Be careful as it is quite crumbly, but so so so tasty.  After eating this, I have been told a number of times that I could open up a bakery with this!  it's that good. items.label: Quick Yellow Cake
items.name: Quick Yellow Cake
items.description: Make and share this Quick Yellow Cake recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Heat oven to 350*.
Mix dry ingredients in lg bowl.
Add shortening, milk and vanilla.
Beat on med for 2 minutes.
Add eggs and beat for 30 seconds more.
Bake in greased 13x9 pan for 35 minutes, or until pick comes out clean.

reviews.review_text: I made this cake last night as a pineapple upside down cake. It turned out great!!! I made a few changes as others have. I used only butter. (But will try to use half butter half applesauce next time) Used a half a cup of the juice from the can of pineapple and a half a cup of milk. I also added an extra teaspoon of vanilla. For the topping of the cake i used about 6-7 tablespoons of butter, melted it in a 9x13 pan, added one cup of dark brown sugar, stir to combine. Then layered out one can of pineapple on it. Topped with cake batter. Only thing is i had to cook it alot longer then said in the recipe. Set the timer for 38 mins, but had to cook for about another 20 mins. My oven temp varies so this might be why i had to bake so long. End result was a absolutely delicious cake!! I will definitely use this recipe again and again.

When this cake came out of the oven, I couldn't believe I actually baked this! It was moist, fluffy, light, and "eggy". I must admit, this was the first sheet cake I've ever made and I've never tried the "betty" kind, tho having tried this I wouldn't go for the commercial kind in the future. 
I don't have a mixer, so I do everyhing by hand. it toke me a while to get the mixture free of lump before adding the eggs, but it was fun to do! I separated the eggs, beat the egg white til fluffy, and add the yolk then fold in whites (something I picked up from foodnetworkCanada). It wasn't hard to make at all! Most importnat of all, it lifts my curse as "queen of burnt baker" and gives me alot of confidence! Thank you SO MUCH. I just served the cake slices with strawberry+sugar syrup and alittle powdered sugar. I think frosting wouldn't do this cake justice. Thank you again MIssNEzzz!

reviews.review_text: I tried this cake recipe today. The only change I made was to use margarine instead of shortening and a 9x5 loaf pan. Big mistake! It was cooking beautifully around the sides but taking for ever for the middle to cook. I finally left it in the oven after turning off the oven and about 10 mins later it was cooked through.  It tasted a bit egg-y. I will use more vanilla next time, but that didn't bother me as much as the fact that didn't come out of the pan in one piece, but split down the center horizontally. Perhaps I removed it from the pan too soon. I will make this again using the right pan size and a bit more vanilla. Will wait till it cools before removing from pan. It has the makings of a great cake. Will rate when I make it again.

I made two cakes, one with light butter and the other with short. My toothpick came clean in exactly 26 min. in each cake. My first cake's bottom really stuck in the pan (but I was able to scrape it off in one piece and place it back on, so the second time I line with parchment paper, which didn't stick). Both were very fluffy, just like you'd think of an "old-fashioned" cake. I added about 3 drops of yellow extract and my cake was a natural yellow color. I used Recipe #44126  which I highly recommend, since it spread perfectly, leaving a nice finish (with a great chocolate flavor). This is a wonderful "all-purpose" cake that I'll be sure to make again! Thanks MizzNezz, for posting.

reviews.review_text: This cake was super easy. After reading all the positive reviews, I looked forward to making it. And then after reading the negative (cake was already in the oven), slightly worried about my cake. I was reassured when I took it out of the oven, and all seemed to be well, if I had left a review right then, it would have been a good one. Sigh, I sincerely hate to leave bad reviews, but this just didn't work. Everything seemed fine at first, I followed the directions exactly, and everything looked good. After letting the cake cool, I went back into the kitchen to frost it, here is where it all fell apart, literally. I don't mean that the cake split in half, or a chunk of the corner fell off, I mean the entire thing CRUMBLED. It was like powder. I am not new to baking. I have many years of cakes under my belt. I have had many disastrous outcomes. As well as many delicious ones. This was unlike anything I have ever seen. Boyfriend said, "It's kind of like corn bread." And I guess that would be the best way to describe it, except cornbread is dense, this was like...old foam. The green kind they used to put in fake potted plants, that just crumbled into dust after 20 years in the sun. I have no idea how it went from looking so good to corn bread cake dust in just a few hours. I'm sorry, it was just a complete fail. :(

This cake is indeed very quick to make. I actually like that it doesn't rise quite as much as other cakes, because it didn't have that dome shape and I didn't have to trim the tops off. It's very moist and tastes pretty good on it's own, and I'm not one to munch on cake without some frosting on it. My only real problem was that it stuck to my cake pans like crazy. And I DID grease the pans. Maybe it will be better when I can get a new bottle of Wilton Cake Release (am all out, used cooking spray which I've used many times before for other cakes with no problems). I have to agree with a previous review that this is closer to a white cake than yellow, but I think that makes it a good basic cake to jazz up in lots of ways. Overall it's not bad, and I'll be making it again.

items.label: The Perfect Burger
items.name: The Perfect Burger
items.description: Here are the ingredients & the instructions to make the perfect burger! Although it may not be the healthiest, use medium ground beef for moistness & flavour. The leaner varieties produce burgers that are drier with a denser, tighter texture. Don't use previously frozen meat as juices are lost during defrosting. If making ahead, cover with plastic wrap & refrigerate for no more than a day. Enjoy!
instructions: Lightly oil grill& heat BBQ to medium.
Whisk egg in a bowl& add next 6 ingredients.
Add any of the <U+0093>stir-ins<U+0094> that appeal to you.
Crumble in beef& using your hands or a fork, gently mix together.
Handle the meat as little as possible <U+0096> the more you work it, the tougher it gets.
Gently shape (don<U+0092>t firmly press) mixture into burgers about ¾ inch thick.
Using your thumb, make a shallow depression in the centre of each burger to prevent puffing up during cooking.
Place burgers on the grill, close lid& BBQ until NO LONGER PINK INSIDE, turning once, about 6 <U+0096> 8 minutes per side.
An instant read thermometer should read 160F.
Don't abuse your burgers by pressing with a spatula, pricking with a fork or turning frequently as precious juices will be lost!
Tuck into a warm crusty bun& add your favourite toppings.

reviews.review_text:
Just trying this burger for the first time and I added most of the flavour perk stir-ins. I added a tablespoon of worcestershire sauce instead of one teaspoon, 2 garlic gloves instead of 1 and a pretty medium sized onion instead of a small one. The flavour perks I added were: 

fresh lime rind (a little under 1 tablespoon)
1 tablespoon grated gingerroot
1 tablespoon ketchup
1 teaspoon of dried oregano AND dried thyme
1 tablespoon fresh herb (rosemary and thyme chopped finely)
2 tablespoons cajun seasoning (i didn't have any so i made some homemade seasoning just by adding a teaspoon of salt, pepper, paprika, garlic powder, white pepper and a little more than a teaspoon of cayenne pepper)

If you want a simple burger then you should probably stick to the original recipe but if you're looking for something packed with flavour like I am, you should definitely use the stir-ins! I fried two mini burgers to check the flavour and it was really good! 

N.B. I also added a little breadcrumbs to help keep my burgers together as I realized the mixture was very moist and I also added one bullion seasoning cube.

These were definately lovely and moist. I think leaving out the breadcrumbs is a great idea as is the cooking technique. The only other thing I added to the burger mix was about a tablespoon of tomato ketchup and a small handful of mixed herbs.  Now I make my burgers the Aussie way and here's how it's done.  First put a squeeze of tomato ketchup on the bottom of the toasted bun then followed by an iceberg lettuce leaf, a slice of tomato then place the burger (which should have a slice of melted cheese on that I place during the last minute of cooking), then I add some fried onions (never raw onions), a slice of bacon and topped with a fried egg and then the top bun. It's a mouthful but well worth the effort.

attributes.source_text: lovely and moist

reviews.review_text: I've made these burgers several times now. Each time using the base recipe (except for the egg) since I only make 2 for us. I do use a few tablespoons of broth to make sure they are juicy and once added a bit of ketchup, once a tablespoon or 2 of Lipton's onion soup mix. They were GREAT each time! I know you are supposed to rate them for how the recipe states, but for those who gave low ratings.....use your heads ladies and gentlemen and if a whole onion is too much, cut back on it. If you don't like Worcestershire sauce, leave it out. So make your burgers exactly how YOU like them and then submit that and see how people rate your recipe. I don't suppose you'll get all 5 star ratings because everyone's tastes are different. And please be kind at least with your words. Thanks for the recipe Country Lady.

reviews.review_text: Made these last night for my niece's birthday celebration. My sister in law wouldn't stop raving about how amazing these were and how I was her favourite sister in law LOL. I think I may have added more onion than what I should have, easily happens since there's no measurement (in cups) for the amount of onion needed, so might have to go ahead and do these a few more times to get it perfect. I didn't add to the recipe any of the add ins, and grilled in a regular grill with charcoal - very old school. Also, I used 50% regular ground (which I think is the standard for the highest fat content in ground beef) and 50% 90/10 beef (for the lack of something else when I went shopping), and I think they turned out gr-eat! I did 150 gram (5.29 oz) patties and got 8 and 3/4's patties (I doubled the recipe). Followed the instruction of another reviewer and placed the patties in the grill and only flipped them once, need to make sure the heat is medium / high and that you're flipping them in one movement cause shaky hands can definitely get them to split (also low heat - happend to me twice). All in all these are great and will most likely be making them again in the future.

reviews.review_text: Everyone having issues with their burgers falling apart on the grill are using ground beef that is too lean (anything leaner than 85/15 will likely fall apart). I recommend using 80/20 for the binding properties the fat provides,not to mention, the flavor it adds. Much of it will cook down, but understand it will make the burger a little greasier in the end. No problem though, as that is where the best flavors come from. Another reason people can't keep their burgers from falling apart are cutting their onion and other fillers too big. Remember, we want the ingredients to be as small as possible to mesh with the meat. Also, the onion (as well as other ingredients like garlic), will release some moisture, causing the meat to come apart, especially when it's not cut/chopped small enough. Lastly, make sure your cooking surface is hot enough before you place your burgers on it. I prefer to grill my burgers over charcoal, as it provides a superior flavor, and my grill temperature over the coals is roughly 450-500 degrees Fahrenheit. I usually arrange the coals to leave a cooler zone (indirect heat) where the burgers can be moved after they are seared to cook a little slower under less heat. The high heat sears the outer layer of the burger and locks the juices in the center, which slowly cooks while over indirect heat. Every bite is incredible when cooked this way, and I guarantee it won't fall apart if you use a fattier ground beef, properly cut and prepare the patties, and cook over the proper heat.

A slice of pepper jack cheese, cook another minute. Cover and cook 2 more minutes and Voila! Perfection confirmed. Like I said, the flavor was good.......just wish we could have eaten patties instead of scrambled hamburger.

Made them with the standard options, no mix-ins, and we loved them.  Fry up some home made potato chips to serve with these and have a delicious burger.  One comment though, I'm not sure how small you mean by a small onion. reviews.review_text: This is my go-to burger recipe. I've made these numerous times - have also expanded the recipe to feed a crowd. Flavour is fabulous (I haven't felt the need to use the add-ins) I have never had them fall apart when cooking. I chill them prior to grilling, which may help to firm them up. I use a burger press and put parchment between the patties. One other thing I can think of that could be causing that issue is the onion. Egg is a good binder but the onion could cause an issue too much is added (recipe calls for one small, which we might all interpret differently) or if it isn't finely grated.

These burgers were a huge hit. Everyone enjoyed them, even my middle daughter who rarely eats meat. We entertained the neighbors with them on New Year’s Eve, and I was proud to serve them - after I did a test burger in the kitchen to make sure they would come out okay. I don’t have a grater, so I finely chopped red onion and it was awesome. I quintupled the recipe for 5lb of ground beef, and I made 17 burgers from that (as opposed to the 20 that would have yielded with 1/4lb burgers). Anyway, these are delicious. It will be my new go-to recipe and I can’t wait to pick different mix-ins each time. This time I mixed in chile chipotle powder, oregano, and cajun spice. 5 stars!

reviews.review_text: I had to write a review after seeing all the other reviews. I am currently living and working abroad with my partner, who is Irish, the hardest things to find in this part of the world is a proper ulster fry and a darn good ol' American Burger. I have now made this numerous times and it always comes out perfectly no matter which add ins I've put in. I generally follow the recipe with the 2 lbs of really good ground beef, even if it costs a little extra, cause I think the meat can make or break this recipe. I make a large batch keep the rest in the fridge for the week and when my partner has a late night he just takes a patty out slap it in the pan add some cheese and he's got a nice healthy burger dinner. reviews.review_text: I used this recipe as the base, but I doubled it, and pureed all the seasoning ingredients (everything except the egg and beef) along with 2 pieces of white bread, crusts removed, and a couple pinches of Italian parsley. Then I poured over the beef along with 1 lightly beaten egg and gently mixed together. I only used 1 egg for 2lbs of beef, and it held together just fine. The bread acts as an extra binder / glue. I found pureeing everything made the mixing process go faster, so I handled the meat considerably less than if I hadn't. This is a really good recipe!

I'm sorry, but this was unfortunate. I followed the recipe to the letter (no alterations or substitutions) and didn't include any of the "flavor perk stir-ins" (so I could taste the base recipe). The result was waaaaay too onion-y and garlic-y... and it reminded me of a weird A1 steak sauce level of tartness... It was just... unfortunate. I'd honestly hesitated a couple times before finally adding all that shredded onion and the entire clove of garlic to just 1 lb of my quality 90/10 ground Angus. Just as I did with the worchestershire and mustard. Really wish I'd followed my instincts and substantially reduced those ingredients, so they would complement rather than overpower the beef flavor. Then again, I truly enjoy the flavor of high quality beef... so my ideal burger patty is ground Angus chuck or sirloin seasoned with coarse sea salt and black pepper. I've enjoyed flavored, stuffed burgers, but this one was just not good. PRO: It did look really nice and held together just fine. CON: It tasted awful. Sorry. :-(

items.name: Creamy Macaroni and Cheese
items.description: This is my absolute very favorite macaroni and cheese recipe and I have a large collection of m/c recipes. Adapted from Southern Living. I don't make this very often because I could literally eat the whole thing and lick the dish clean.
instructions: In a big skillet, melt the butter over medium-high heat.
Whisk the flour in gradually until the mixture is smooth.
Cook and whisk continually for 2 minutes.
Add in salt, pepper, cayenne, and garlic; stir to combine.
Gradually whisk in half-and-half and milk.
Cook and whisk continually for 8-10 minutes or until mixture is thickened.
Add in half of the sharp cheddar cheese; stir.
Add in all of the extra-sharp cheddar cheese; stir until smooth.
Take skillet off stove burner.
Mix together the cooked macaroni and cheese mixture; transfer to a greased 13x9 inch casserole dish.
Sprinkle with the remaining sharp cheddar cheese.
Bake in a 350° oven for 20 minutes (may need to bake longer for a crispy top).

reviews.review_text:
Ultimate comfort food! I've made this recipe twice now, and both times have gotten excellent comments about how good this mac and cheese tastes.  My DD doesn't give compliments easily and she proclaimed it "the best"!
The first time I prepared this dish, I must have used too much flour because it really was too thick for my taste, so now I have a light hand when measuring. Removing the pan from the heat when adding the cheese is another important tip, as another reviewer mentioned, so that the cheese doesn't get grainy, but stays smooth and creamy. 
While I won't be making this dish very often because of the amounts of cream and cheese and butter, it will definitely be the recipe I choose when I want to splurge and throw diet to the winds.

reviews.review_text: Ok first of all, I rarely give a recipe a 5. I a tough reviewer :). I will be honest, ive made a few recipes for "Oven" macaroni and cheese and never have really liked any of them. They were dry and just not that great. My girlfriend just loves macaroni and cheese from cracker barell. She knows i'm a very accomplished cook. She requested i make mac & cheese for her. I searched and searched and found this recipe. I thought what they hey i will give it a shot. Hopefully its not a totally disaster and she doesn't like it. I made this and OMG. It was the bomb. This recipe yielded a lot of mac & cheese and i thought it would end up going bad but we ate it until it was gone :). It was even awesome left over which is more than you can say for most mac & cheese. I will make a small note. I had to add a little more milk to the cheese cause because the quantity of liquid wasn't enough. I probably added an additional 1-1.5 cups. Other than that i will put this recipe down as one of my favorites.

I'm not an inexperienced cook, but if I would have ordered this in a restaurant, I would have sent it back. I love the creamy mixture of the cheese. The Cheyenne pepper gives it an unexpected kick that I loved. However, there is SO much cheese! (30 ounces) The top had grease floating on it. I liked the suggestion of the bread crumb topping. This would absorb much of that. I would also recommend par boiling the macaroni. Cook for just a few minutes until it is firm to the bite. you may need to adjust your baking time so the macaroni cooks. The baking process will absorb some of the liquids and it won't be quite as "soup" like.

reviews.review_text:
Made this a few weeks ago ... sorry, just got around to the review. Made it for a potluck luncheon.

Turned out perfect. Two changes, I added a extra sharp WHITE cheddar, but that really didn't change the flavor, just the color. And, a few fresh bread crumbs as a topping. But again, it didn't change the flavor of the dish. Just a little crunchy topping.

It was creamy, easy and delicious. I honestly prefer mine NOT as creamy, but that is my personal recipe; however, I have found a creamier mac and cheese is preferred and this is very very good. I would make this any time. The first time I added some bacon, because my friend asked me too. That was equally as good.

There is only one thing I might try. Mom always added just a bit of mustard for a little tang. Next time I might try just a bit of mustard in the sauce.

But, a fantastic recipe and very easy to make.
NOTE: to new cooks ... make sure to use a quality cheese and shred it yourself. Pre-shredded have chemicals in it to prevent molding and for preserving. Fresh grating cheese is the key.

Also, when adding cheese to your sauce ... remove from the heat, and add a little at a time until creamy. Add to HOT HOT sauce and too much at once can cause it to separate and get grainy. And then don't bring back to a boil. It is already melted, keep on medium low heat.

GREAT recipe!

items.name: Lisa's Swirled Chocolate Chip Cookies
keywords: c("Dessert", "Cookie & Brownie", "Kid Friendly", "Baking", "< 30 Mins", "For Large Groups", "Oven")
items.description: This is a chocolate chip cookie recipe that my friend DeLynn's best friend gave to us. This is the recipe I use for normal chocolate chip cookies, but I've recently been making them with Nestlé's new White & Milk Chocolate Swirled chips. This is a yummy soft and delicious cookie!
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
Mix butter, granulated sugar, brown sugar, vanilla and eggs in a large bowl.
Stir in the flour, baking soda and salt.
Stir in 2 cups of Swirled Chocolate Chips.
Drop dough by rounded measuring tablespoons, about 2-inches apart, onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Place the several of the reserved swirled chocolate chips on top of each cookie.
Bake 9 to 12 minutes or until light brown.
Cool slightly.
Remove from cookie sheet.
Cool on wire rack.

reviews.review_text: Delicious cookies. As I was out of brown sugar I also only used white sugar. Instead of placing choc chips on top of the cookies, I took the lazy route and just stirred in all 4 cups of chips (in step 4) and omitted step 6 -- it worked out for me but probably following the directions as directed would have resulted in the pretty cookies you see in the photo previously submitted by another reviewer, still we enjoyed these cookies immensely. These make a lot of cookies - perfect for cookie exchanges or when you need to bring cookies to a bake sale. Thanks for sharing this keeper!

These are simply heaven! FH and I were itching for something sweet the other night and thought we'd give these a shot, and are some happy we did. I lost my favourite chocolate chip cookie recipe in the course of moving from town to town, and thought I would never find one that I loved as much - or more - until now! reviews.review_text:
I have begged the place where I eat mexican food to give me recipe for the queso blanco and she wouldn't do it, after making your recipe we ate there again and I was bragging about finding the recipe for it..she smiled and said "So you found the secret was to add a touch of chicken boullion and cumin with the hot green chilies" ...well I had been using mild chili and didn't have the cumin or chicken boullion. It is wonderful the way it is written but I'm telling ya it just gets better with these additions..making sure to use enough cream not to get dip too thick.
Wonderful recipe ..thanks so much for posting!!!

This is so good. When I lived in San Diego, I always went to this restaurant called Miguel's because they had this sauce there and I loved it. I was happy to see it on here and make it myself. I modified the recipe a little. I used 12 slices (9 oz) of individually wrapped store brand white american cheese. (That saved me a lot of money because the store brand slices were on sale for 99 cents for 12 slices, and the land o' lakes was $6.99 a lb).  I accidentally bought heavy 'whipping' cream and I don't know if this is the same as heavy cream, but either way it worked just fine. I will definitely make this again!

This was freaking amazing. Even my lactose-intolerant husband popped his meds to pig out. Exactly like the restaurants. Used the white American cheese at the deli, they didn't have L O'L brand, but Didn't have diced green chilies, but did have a can of sliced pickled jalapenos I got from the Mexican foods section at the grocery store. Chopped them up and added them to cheese. I made about 1/4 the original amount and found the microwave to do a great job of melting without any problems. Did 15-30 second increments. When cheese became thicker as it cooled, I just popped it back into the microwave again. Will add Spanish (not Mexican) chorizo, Italian sausage, bacon, or other pork product next time, although this doesn't need it, but I like to gild the lily XD.

attributes.source_text: Even my lactose-intolerant husband popped his meds to pig out

reviews.review_text: What an easy, tasty and quick warm dip recipe!  I made this dip the night before, refrigerated overnight, reheated in microwave and served warm out out my Little Dipper crockpot with tortilla chips for dipping.  The girls at work loved it and want the recipe.  I used 1 cup of heavy cream.  I also used deli store- brand American cheese.  I, personally, would've preferred the dip to be a bit more spicier in taste; next time I will add a can of jalapeno's to the mix, in addition to the green chilies.  The recipe makes just about 3 1/2 cups of dip.  Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: The girls at work loved it

reviews.review_text: Great base recipe! I have Celiac so I can't go to any Mexican restaurants around me so I'm so glad to be able to finally make the queso at home. I've been making it for just myself (my boyfriend doesn't like queso, crazy right?!) so I quartered the recipe but it was still a lot for just me. I read the comments and added a pinch of cumin and chicken bouillon. My local taco shop serves their queso with a spoonful of quac and their hot sauce on top, so I replicated it with a spoonful of Herdez medium quacamole salsa in the center which added some heat. The second time I made it (pictured) I realized while melting the cheese that my cream had gone bad so I used a splash of 2% milk and it worked just as well, I can't tell the difference. I also didn't have the salsa so I added a dash of chipotle powder. I used boar's head cheese (gluten free and on sale!) and it worked perfectly. Next time I'm going to try it with homemade chips!

attributes.source_text: which added some heat

reviews.review_text: I made this for a little dinner party and this was a big hit! One of the men even asked for the recipe!  After searching through two large cheese sections at the grocery store, I finally found the white American cheese in the deli section.  I'm so glad that I did! Unfortunately, after finding the white American cheese, I forgot to buy the cream.  I had to make an emergency subsitution so I used three tablespoons of butter and a little less than one cup of skim milk. Thank you for sharing this terrific recipe, I'll be making this one again for sure!

reviews.review_text:
Love this! Exactly what is served at a popular mexican restaurant here in my area. Great over spanish/mexican rice also.

Just a note to those who couldn't locate the Land o' Lakes brand of white american--any white american cheese sold at your deli counter will work. Same place you buy fresh sliced lunch meat. American cheese melts better than cheddars and jacks which can get oily, stringy and grainy. You can make it using cheddars but then you really need to stand by and stir often and keep and eye on it. Cheddars are also stronger in flavor which will change the end result of this dip's taste.

I came across this when I was searching for a good dip recipe.  I have had this in the Mexican restaurants around here and knew how good it was, so I decided to make it for me and my friend so we could dip in while watching some chick flicks.  We ate and ate and were so delighted with the ease of making this recipe and the wonderful outcome of the recipe.  Very easy to make up and one you won't be able to just eat 2 or 3 chips with!  These are definately moreish!  Thanks for sharing your recipe with us Wildflour!  Absolutely awesome from the first one to the last! By the way I made them with Tortilla scoops so we could spoon on the scoops and each one would hold a lot of cheese.  Yum yum yummy!

reviews.review_text: Amazing is all I can say about this little gem of a recipe!  So simple to make and so darn tasty!  I have been looking and looking for this recipe, and FINALLY I have found it... I have had this dip on several occasions at Mexican restaurants, and have never been able to find a recipe for it... This is it!  Thanks so much Wildflour.  I especially love it on Enchilladas and Mexican Rice, and always ask if they have the sauce instead of red sauce... Some do, and some don't know what the heck I am talking about... Yeah, now I can make it myself. YUM!

I have been on a kind of a Mexican kick and had to try this and quick.  I was tickled pink I found this particular recipe and was hoping it was what I thought it was.  Well guess what?  It WAS!!!  This stuff is addicting and so good you can't stop eating it!  One bite and you are hooked for at least 1 bowl of warmed tortilla chips, but not me, I had to have 2 bowls!  What a piggy I am!  Shame on me, but really, I couldn't help myself!  Will enjoy this TV snack often and plan to share it with my friends. I know they will love it too.

reviews.review_text: Fantastic recipe! I have made this queso between 5 to 10 times now and it continues to get better and better each time! The first couple of times I had been using, ignorantly I should add, Rotel with Diced Tomatoes and Green Chilies. It wasn't until my most recent trip to the store that I realized they carried Green Chilies without the tomatoes. Both ways were very good, but the recipe as written, is exceptional! Thanks Wildflour for a terrific recipe!

This is amazing! I made it exactly as the recipe stated, starting with the 1/2 cup heavy cream. That was extremely thick for us, so I slowly added more until it was the right consistency for us. I didn't measure it after the 1/2 cup. I think I might have ended up using just a little over 1 cup. I cannot wait for our next carry-in at work so that I can take a crock pot full of this!!

Hubby did say he'd like it to have a little more heat to it. Personally, I like my Mexican food kind of on the mild side so it was perfect for me. Next time, I'll split it up and add more heat to his.

attributes.source_text: I like my Mexican food kind of on the mild side so it was perfect for me

reviews.review_text: Fabulous dip!  I got a little over a pound of cheese at the deli and used about 1 1/4 cup heavy cream.  I was afraid that I got the dip too thin, but it turned out wonderful!  I cooked it on the stove and then transferred to my Lil Dipper crock pot.  We used small bowls for individual servings at dinner.  My hubby mixed some salsa in with his, and it was really good.  I mixed some taco meat in with mine, and it was also very good.  But I still think it was the best just as the recipe is! Thanks so much for sharing!

My hubby mixed some salsa in with his, and it was really good

reviews.review_text: This was so yummy! We found the Land O'Lakes white American at Giant Eagle, but as others have mentioned, any good-quality white American cheese would do. Next time, though, I think I'll use half and half cream or whole milk in lieu of the heavy cream, as it was very RICH! I added a few dashes of salt, and may add a little diced jalapeno for kick next time, too. We used it on loaded nachos which consisted of Tostitos Cantina Style tortilla chips, Southwest-seasoned ground beef (compliments of McCormick), this wonderful queso, and Southwest Guacamole. ("Viva Mexico Guacamole" recipe with fire-roasted corn--also from Giant Eagle--in the frozen section, and black beans added to it.) They were delicious . . . better than any restaurant's nachos, and thoroughly enjoyed in the privacy of our patio alongside less-pricey beers! ;-) This queso would surely be awesome as just a dip, but is certainly versatile enough to also be used on tacos, burritos, French fries, grilled chicken or steak, burgers, etc. Thank you so much for sharing this recipe! :-)

This dip was great! I also thought it needed some zing so I added just a pinch of onion powderand garlic salt and that seemed to help, but I must have had the worlds whimpiest chiles because I ended up adding almost a 1/4 c of jarred jalapeno liquid and some cayenne. I had sooooo many oohs and ahhs over this dip, it was certainly a hit and I would NEVER have thought to use white American cheese. This dip will be making many return appearances at our house thanks for posting!

items.label: Sausage Balls
items.name: Sausage Balls
keywords: c("Pork", "Meat", "High Protein", "High In...", "Christmas", "Thanksgiving", "< 15 Mins", "For Large Groups", "Easy")
items.description: A crowd-pleaser for Holiday gatherings. This is my most requested recipe.  These are best served with Versatile Mustard Dip (Recipe #150023).
instructions: Allow cheese and sausage to reach room temperature.
Place in mixing bowl with Bisquick and blend until smooth. (I've had great success using my hand-held electric mixer to incorporate ingredients).
NOTE:  Mixture will be quite dry.
Line a cookie sheet with aluminum foil.
Spray well with vegetable oil spray.
Press/roll mixture into 1 inch balls by hand; place on cookie sheet about 1 inch apart.
Bake in 400 degree Fahrenheit oven for 10 to 12 minutes, or until golden brown.
Drain on paper toweling.
Serve warm with Versatile Mustard Dip (Recipe #150023).

reviews.review_text: I used 1.5 cups of bisquick, 10 oz of sharp cheddar cheese, a spash of milk, 1 lb of sage sausage, and added 1/4 cup of Rhubarb Jelly (what I had on hand). I waited for sausage to come closer to room temperature and mixed it with the bisquick and splash of milk 1st in the mixer with the dough hook. Then added the cheddar and the jelly and mixed it again . I lined a cookie sheet with foil and sprayed it with PAM. I cooked these at 375 for 10-15 min. I was able to get 43 out of the batch. They were moist and held the shape that I rolled them into. The sight sweet taste was so yummy!

attributes.source_text: They were moist
The sight sweet taste was so yummy!

reviews.review_text: I've made these for 35 years.  The problem with the dry dough is that the original recipe, which is 35 years or more old, used sausage that had higher fat content and the cheese we used back then, was grated by hand.  Pre- packaged shredded cheese is coated with something that keeps the cheese from sticking together and it doesn't come together as well or melt as well. So the "gold old days" recipe, while identical to this one, had different quality to the ingredients.  Today's pork sausage has less fat and most of us buy the pre-packaged shredded cheese.  I found adding a little milk helps this recipe as it is too dry. Also add some garlic powder.  It is really a crowd favorite.

Found out at the last minute that I needed to bring an appetizer to a Christmas Party last night.  I found this recipe, and was thrilled to discover that I had all the ingredients in the fridge, except the Bisquick.  I found an easy Bisquick Clone recipe here on Zaar, and whipped that up in no time.  These were prepared in 20 minutes, start to finish.  And they were a big hit at the party.  I just served them with Dijon Mustard, but no one really needed it.  They are delicious by themselves, and so quick and easy.

reviews.review_text: I have made this with 1/2lb fennel Italian sausage and a 1/2 lb hot sausage. I also use 2c sharp shredded cheddar. To make mixing a bit easier, I add some milk and then by hand using latex gloves I make the the sausage balls. I cook at 375° for about 20 min. Then I freeze them on a cookie sheet. When flashed frozen, into a zip lock bag and back into the freezer. So when I need them I take what I need and bake at 375° for about 15 to 20 min. to heat up. No dipping sauces needed. They are that good.

I made these yesterday for dh to take to an office party. I tried a WEE bit of one (tummy issues prevent me from eating them) but.. they went over 100% fantastic. I used Tennesse Pride Hot sausage and I thought I had Bisquick on hand but it was NOT bisquick it was Pioneer (brand) buttermilk baking/pancake mix. I am told by many of my dh's office workers they are the BEST they have ever had. I got to thinking about it later and realized maybe one reason pple loved them more than their own mommas made was the mix I used. The Pioneer brand of buttermilk mix, is finer than Bisquick and also more "whiter", if that makes sense. But dh tells me from living in the South and having tried many sausage balls these are the greatest. So if anyone gets a chance to try this recipe using that mix or a buttermilk baking mix I suggest it. I also only used 1 1/2 cups of mix. Thanks for the recipe, I am now required to make it more lol.

reviews.review_text:
Jelly was a genius idea! These are great as is but if you don't know by now, sugar or any sweetener is the secret ingredient to almost all recipes. Good restaurants have known this for ages. This is what makes the dishes addicting. I even put a little Agave syrup in my albondigas and it makes a world of difference. It is not enough to be noticeable but enhances the flavors exponentially.
For my recipe apricot or peach preserves seem to work well too. Thanks for this unusual and versatile recipe.

My cousin Wendy says she can't cook.  Why am I telling you this in my review?  I gave her this recipe to fix for our Cousins Christmas party and they were PERFECT!  Easy enough for her, delicious enough for us all to eat.  We do make these quite a bit, but I don't need a recipe.  So I emailed her the recipe and VIOLA...made her an instant chef. reviews.review_text: I love this super-simple recipe.  I didn't have add milk as some did, I found that patient kneading made the mixture hold together just fine.  I used Jimmy Dean Hot sausage.  I made a couple batches as my entire family loves these.  I added finely chopped apple to one batch and those went even faster than the basic recipe. The recipe is so basic I imagine you could add quite a few different stir-ins for variety and still have a hit.

attributes.source_text: my entire family loves these

reviews.review_text:
10 stars Fauve! Why? super mega wonderfully ridiculously easy to make, cheap for anyone on a budget, they freeze well, look great and very very best of all: my mega fussy 4.5y/o DD (of the "Miss-hates-it-before-she's-even-tried-it" variety) shocked us by siezing one, bit into it, smilingly called it "kipjes"(=little chickens) and obviously thought it was a chicken nugget Down that little hatch they have been going ever since ! Yeah !!! that gets an instant 5 stars from me for that alone... :)everyone who's tried them liked them and I've been so busy making them that I haven't managed a review before now I did try and take one shortcut... I thought I whip a few of the uncooked ones out of the freezer and fry them instead of sticking a whole tray in the oven... the fried ones were rejected as quickly as the oven ones were inhaled.. why? I simply don't know... but into the oven they go from now on, 'cos once they have been oven cooked and later frozen, you only have to pop them in the microwave to heat though and they are just as popular as the ones fresh out of the oven. We 'll be calling them 'kipjes' in our house from now on (why ruin a good thing when it's going so well?) and I'll be making these as fast as I can keep up with DD's eating them. Please see my rating system, you are a genious, a hugely deserved 5 stars ! BTW In one of the photo's the sausage balls *were* piled high in the dish... but by the time I came back with the camera only these few were left ! 10 stars, if only I could give them. mega thanks...andria:) 
Review editited to add: we don't have Bisquick here in NL, so I just substituted some plain flour, salt, baking powder and a tiny bit of butter (since I consider my sausage meat fatty enough) maybe that made the difference between my results and the other reviews here where the result didn't turn out as well as expected ??? I made these yet again this weekend... another batch in the freezer to keep DD happy... Thanks !
