items.label: Throw Away the Bread Machine Instructions!.... White Bread
items.name: Throw Away the Bread Machine Instructions!.... White Bread
keywords: c("Breads", "Healthy", "Kid Friendly", "Brunch", "Bread Machine", "< 15 Mins", "Beginner Cook", "Small Appliance", "Easy")
items.description: Make and share this Throw Away the Bread Machine Instructions!.... White Bread recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Place the water into the bread pan.
Sprinkle the sugar then the yeast over the water; allow the yeast to foam for 10 minutes.
Add in the melted butter, oil, flour and salt.
Select the BASIC or WHITE BREAD setting and press start.

reviews.review_text: I'd given up on making bread.  I didn't like the bread machine results, or shape, and the instructions always sounded too vague.  Dissolve yeast in warm water?  How warm?  How long?  My bread would never rise. This recipe sounded more specific.  I bought a Breadman machine from the thrift store and tried it, using all butter instead of oil and butter.  Rolled it up jelly roll style for the final rise in a bread pan.  It rose sky high and the results were perfect!  I was so excited I posted the photo to Facebook so my family could see it.  I think the temperature for dissolving the yeast and the 10 minute wait before adding the other ingredients is key.  I'm so inspired I have since adapted the basic instructions to wheat bread and swirled cinnamon-raisin bread with great results.

Have to echo everyone else.  This bread is incredible!  Made it exactly by the recipe, using King Arthur Bread flour the 1st time and King Arthur All Purpose the 2nd time, plus Rapid Rise Yeast both times.   It had fabulous flavor and texture.  It can also be sliced very thin for marvelous sandwiches.  Sold my two Zoji bread machines (2 mini and 1 regular size) when we moved 3 years ago but was never that happy with their output anyway and was making bread by hand till I got too lazy.  Broke down and bought a vintage Farberware bread machine at a garage sale last weekend but it had no manual so was looking for a recipe because I didn't want to wait till the manual I ordered arrived.  Really happy I stumbled on this one.  Much superior to any bread I have ever made in a bread machine and so easy.  My only problem is that it rises so high it sticks to the top of the machine and causes the bread to cave in slightly and not brown on the very top.  Looking at the King Arthur website though, I believe I need to cut the water back by a few tablespoons.  I'll try that on my 3rd loaf - we've already finished the first 2.  If that doesn't work I will try cutting the yeast back or using regular yeast rather than the rapid rise.   Someone was asking how to store homemade bread.  I use the Debbie Meyer Breadbags from Amazon.  They are reusable and are wonderful for keeping the bread fresh and accessible.  You just stick the bread in and fold the excess under.  No twist ties or ziplocks.  Thanks for a life changing recipe.  This is my go-to from now on.

This is the easiest bread to put together! I did follow my bread machine instructions (I think it's ingrained in my head) and used all butter, no oil. I also used regular white flour (subbing 3 teaspoonfuls with 3 teaspoons of wheat gluten) I used the 'dough' setting on my machine, and ended up with TWO loaves because the first rise was a big rise, let rise for the second time, and followed previous reviews by baking at 350 for 25 minutes. I think I will bake a little longer next time as mine were still fairly light. But still, they were beautiful loaves, great texture, soft yet chewy. Can't wait to use them for sandwiches!! I think this may be a staple recipe in this house now. Thank you for another amazing recipe!

attributes.source_text: soft yet chewy
soft yet chewy

reviews.review_text: This bread is absolutely delicious! The first time I made it I forgot to choose a loaf size so my machine defaulted to 2 lbs. which resulted in dough that rose excessively and collapsed -- but it tasted awesome so I tried again on the 1.5 lbs. setting with better results. After that I tweaked the recipe a bit, using the oil to make it easier (I bake bread every other day or so) and decreased the yeast to 1.5 tsp. as I prefer a denser loaf. I process the ingredients in the bread loaf until the dough is kneaded the final time then let it rise in a greased bread pan and finally bake it at 350° for 31 minutes. After baking, I let the bread cool for half an hour or so then place close it in a bag to soften the crust for easier slicing.

attributes.source_text: I prefer a denser loaf
to soften the crust

reviews.review_text: Nice fluffy bread with a good texture. Loaf sinks in the middle but I'm sure it's where there was too much liquid to dry ingredients. Would be easier if there was weights using the metric recipe but it says 709.77 ml white bread flour?? Strange way to measure a dry ingredient in the metric recipe as it gives grams for the yeast but that's it, everything else is in mls including sugar so you might just as well use the us measurements as I think they just converted us cups into metric hence the mls instead of grams. This is my fave recipe now, I just need to sort the flour issue

attributes.source_text: Nice fluffy bread

reviews.review_text: I bought a bread machine at a resale shope, and it didn't come with the instructions. I tried this and it was perfect! fool proof, seriously! I didn't have bread machine yeast, so I used a package of regulare yeast, and I didn't have bread machine flour, so again, I used regulare (great value walmart brand) flour, and it was perfect. I did use only butter, not the oil. I set the machine before we left for church, on the 1.5 lbs setting, and when we came home a wonderful warm loaf was waiting for us! My two kids, age 7 and 4 ate the whole loaf that night! I had to make more to pack for lunches the next day! This is so easy! SO yummy! (I have the toastmaster 1148x)

attributes.source_text: My two kids, age 7 and 4 ate the whole loaf that night!

reviews.review_text: i've made this recipe 4 times now - perfect EACH time!  Its Betsy-proof!<br/><br/>The first 2 times, i made it with all purpose flour, because thats all i had, turned out just fine- then made it with bread flour and wowzers! Fluffy, light with a nice golden crust. It lasts about 2 days in a cereal bag, decent softness after 2 days, its never stuck around for more than four days in our house.  Day three it was more like crusty bread but still just as good. I havent frozen it yet so i cant comment on that.<br/><br/>I use my electric knife to cut it and it slices beautifully.<br/><br/>i like that its so easy to memorize with not a lot of ingredients in this recipe. When im in a hurry i can just throw it together.<br/><br/>good job. this is my go-to white bread recipe

attributes.source_text: Fluffy, light with a nice golden crust
Fluffy, light with a nice golden crust
a nice golden crust
decent softness after 2 days
Day three it was more like crusty bread but still just as good

reviews.review_text:
Thank You Kittencal! You saved my bread machine from the trash bin.

Wonderful recipe. No more hockey pucks for me.  Makes the greatest toast too, which my husband truly appreciates.

I wish the bread machine instructions would tell you, you can proof your yeast. I think the sugar makes all the difference. Of course I don't think you could do it this way on Delay Start, but I never do that anyway. 

Love the name too. Really caught my attention and was true. Followed your instructions to a T. I do so appreciate your posting this. Terry

attributes.source_text: which my husband truly appreciates

reviews.review_text: Bought a bread machine during Prime Day and have been looking for recipes to try. The instructions are very clear that I should only do the one's in the book, but I've never been good at following direction. This recipe was perfect. I used the 4TB of butter melted instead of combining Oil and Butter. I let the yeast, sugar and warm water foam in a glass bowl first and then poured it into the bread maker bowl. My yeast was old and I wanted to make sure it foamed. Then I added the butter and the salt and flour (sifted first). It came out looking great and smelling amazing.

Best ever! It's so versatile, it's practically the only recipe I ever use. It's my default recipe for soft white sandwich bread, but it's also fabulous with half whole wheat flour + vital wheat gluten. It makes perfectly soft and fluffy burger and hot dog rolls. One thing to note, it rises so high that you'll only need 2 ounce portions for hot dog rolls. I like using milk or milk powder for extra flavor, but that's just personal preference, it's delicious as written. This should be everyone's very first bread machine recipe. If it were, there'd be a lot fewer machines sitting idle or showing up in thrift shops.

attributes.source_text: perfectly soft and fluffy burger and hot dog rolls
perfectly soft and fluffy burger and hot dog rolls

reviews.review_text: I can't believe this recipe!!! This is THE FIRST bread machine recipe that I have really and truly enjoyed. I have always gotten tough, chewy, heavy, and just plain boring bread from my bread machine. It's a very nice, and expensive machine too! I lost the manual to my machine so I got online to find a recipe to make today for Sunday dinner. I did not expect this to turn out so well. This is by far the best bread I have ever had out of a bread machine. I was a little dubious to say the least because the recipe is so simple. The bread was tender, light, and browned perfectly. The entire loaf was consistent and just top notch! In fact, we snarfed down the entire 3lb loaf and I was forced to make another loaf. I can't say enough good about this recipe. I had to add just about three tablespoons more warm water. Other than the water, the recipe was just BOMB!

attributes.source_text: The bread was tender
light
for Sunday dinner

reviews.review_text: Thank you so much for this recipe. I started to think my bread machine was a dud. I carefully tried other recipes and could not succeed in a perfectly risen loaf. This comes out perfect every time. I've baked a few loaves now in the bread machine. They rise so well that its a rather large loaf. Today I doubled the recipe still using the dough cycle on the machine but separated dough into 3 standard loaf pans and baked in the oven at 350 for 20 min. Once again, perfect as can be. Turns out super soft but still slices beautifully with great texture and flavor.

attributes.source_text: perfectly risen loaf
Turns out super soft

reviews.review_text: Completely fail proof method! I've made it a number of times, and added some variations but the basic method works every time. The biggest difference is that I do on the dough setting and bake in the oven to avoid the bread machine hole! One change I've made that I really like is to use the basics of this recipe for whole wheat. To do so I cut the sugar to 1tsp and then added 1.5TBS of honey to the water before I add the yeast. I also cut the oil to 3 TBS and used 2cup of Whole Wheat Bread and 1 cup on White. One thing that really helps the texture is the use Bread Flour. AMZING!

This recipe is soooo forgiving! I have now made about 6 loaves and am in love with this recipe! I usually make a loaf of 2 cups wheat flour/1 cup white. I have played with the sugar, using Demarra, brown sugar, molasses, honey, and plain white. The recipe does not seem to care what kind of sugar I use. I use my machine only for the dough cycle, and bake the bread in my oven to 190F internal temp on an instant read thermometer. I have one that alerts me when my desired temp is achieved. No more inedible crusts! This morning I really went outside my comfort zone and used this recipe as the basis for parmesan-herb-garlic-rolls. They are gorgeous! I added 2T fresh minced rosemary and oregano, (80% rosemary, 20% oregano - a little oregano goes a long way!), a full cup of fresh parmesan, and I replaced the regular salt with garlic salt, as I realized at the last minute that I didn't have fresh garlic. I also used olive oil for the oil/butter. I put the fresh herbs in my small food processor with the oil and pulsed it a few times to mince the herbs and infuse the oil. Proofed my yeast, then threw everything into the machine and let her rip! I watched a video from another website to learn how to cut and shape the rolls. They came out fantastic! I didn't even have to grease my hands to cut and shape the dough! The one thing I will do next time is up the garlic salt to at least 1.5 teaspoons, and sprinkle some garlic salt on the top of the baked rolls to enhance the garlic flavor.

attributes.source_text: to enhance the garlic flavor

items.label: Refried Beans
items.name: Refried Beans
items.description: I got this recipe from a little old lady who ran a cantina near the beach in Ensanada Mexico. Black beans are the best for this recipe. If the color throws you use red.
instructions: In a large pan saute the onions and garlic to just translucent.
Add the jalapenos and continue to saute until JUST beginning to brown.
Add the beans, 2 cans rinsed and drained, two with juice.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer for around 1 1/2 hours, adding beer as needed.
You don't want the beans to dry out.
If there's any remaining beer left drink it.
Sometimes 2 cans are needed.
Don't add salt until dish is done and taste first.

reviews.review_text:
I owe you for another one! I can't understand why I've never sent in a review of this one. I guess I am getting old! Well, Here goes!
I double the recipe. It freezes and reheats wonderfully and you can never have too many refried beans on hand.I add 1/2 tsp freshly ground Cumin. I also like the flavor of dried New Mexico chilies so I top one, split it in half lengthwise, seed, and vain it. I bring 1/2 pint of the local microbrew's English style Brown Ale to a slow boil in a small sauce pan and boil the chili for 20 minutes. I lift the chili halves out of the ale and onto a plate. I scrape the pulp form the skin with the edge of a spoon and added it and the ale to the beans. When done I make 10 bean and cheese burritos, put the rest in freezer containers and froze the lot. The burritos were wrapped in freezer paper of course. All in all, a fun dish to prepair and many delightful meals stored in the freezer. Once again my Thanx!

Love these beans! I started by frying up some bacon like is called for in Recipe #41168, another good recipe but not homemade. I doubled this recipe so I used 10 pieces of bacon to start with then used that grease to fry up 2 onions and 2 yellow chili peppers. I was afraid to use 4 onions since I was doubling and am glad because it turned out good with the 2. I also was nervous to use the jalepenos since kids will be eating these beans so thats why I opted for the yellow peppers. Turned out maybe a little jalepeno could have been used, so to spice mine up I added a little bit of cayenne, not too much tho. I also used 2 cans of black beans and 2 cans of pinto. The beer made them awesome I am surprised I hadnt thought of that before since I add beer to most everything. I loved this recipe it turned out great. Thank you for sharing, my family really enjoyed it.

attributes.source_text: my family really enjoyed it
kids will be eating these beans

reviews.review_text:
And yet another FANTASTIC recipe from "DiB's".  Anyone who regulary visits recipezaar.com knows that a recipe from "DiB's" guarantees to be THE BEST!

I've tried her Pickled Eggs, Spaghetti Sauce, Homemade Ketchup, and many MANY more of her recipes.

Diana, thanks for this WONDERFUL recipe!  I have to admit, when I saw there was beer in it, I thought it would turn out a little bland.  But I trusted that because it came from you, it would be great!

Because my DH & kids love spicy food, I saved 1/2 the batch as the recipe calls for EXACTLY, and also added some ground cumin & chili powder to the other half.  Last night I put some tortilla chips on a plate, added the refried beans with the cumin & chili powder, put some lettuce & tomato on it, and some homemade salsa & taco sauce.  IT WAS TO DIE FOR!!!

If someone isn't worried about high sodium, I also recommend using bacon grease instead of the oil.  But if you're looking for a lower fat refried beans recipe, use the oil!!!

From a Recipezaar member FEVERISHLY looking for "DiB's" recipes,

Janine from Illinois

We topped nachos with these last night for dinner and finished them off as bean burritoes for lunch today.  Yum.  I used half black beans and half red beans, just because I ran out of black beans.  I made them from dry beans and just as an FYI for anyone who would like to do this, 2 cups dry beans=6 cups cooked beans and 6 cups cooked beans=4 cans (about 1.5 cups of beans per can).  I used New Belgium's Trippel (BF is a beer snob, and he thought these tasted off, so I got them for cooking).  I just used 1 12-oz bottle, and added leftover cooking liquid from the beans as needed. I did add the optional garlic.  I didn't have the jalepenos, so I just used some Zhoug  #57689 (which I made with serranos, jalepenos and habeneros) and that worked very well.  Let me say that you should be sure to not use a dark beer for this, as it will get a very bitter taste.  A lighter beer is better.  I had to cook mine for longer than prescribed, but I think that it's because my beans were a little undercooked to start.  The one thing I might change about this next time is to use lard or bacon grease instead of the oil for some extra flavor.  There is lots of yummy flavor from the cooking in beer, though I don't think it really tastes specifially like beer, which is nice, but I think that using fat with some more flavor would be even tastier.

attributes.source_text: for dinner
for lunch today

reviews.review_text:
I have made this several times now -- just excellent. I make a large batch and freeze some for later -- no need for canned refried beans in recipes any more. I use about 1/2-2/3 can of beer since we don't like that strong of a beer flavor. I also add a bit of cumin. I have made this with canned black beans, canned pinto beans, and "reconstituted" dried black beans or red beans or pinto beans. They have all turned out well. I also use frozen jalapenos (harvested from my garden). Just throw washed whole jalapenos (or halved, seeded ones if you prefer) in a plastic bag in the freezer. You can chop them while they are still frozen.

I recently made dinner for a vegetarian friend of mine. I stuffed corn tortillas with these beans and cheese, covered with a homemade enchilada sauce, and baked. Topped with some sour cream, avocado and cilantro. Got rave reviews.

attributes.source_text: I recently made dinner for a vegetarian friend of mine
I recently made dinner for a vegetarian friend of mine
I recently made dinner for a vegetarian friend of mine

reviews.review_text: Now this is a great recipe.  You just need some time to do it.  Gave me great beans that have already been used in making other recipes and some that will be eaten alone.  Mine never did get dry, so I dumped in some beer just to get the taste in there.  Then I turned up the heat to cook it down a little faster and wound up burning beans to tohe bottom of the pan.  Be careful of this, 2 days later and I'm still scrubbing the pot.  I used all kidney beans as that was what was available here.  I wound up using bière blanche, a weird thing, but that is what was in the fridge and it was fine.  I think any beer would work.  I can't get refried beans here, but now it is no longer a problem.

This was the very first recipe I read on this site.  I finally got around to making it.  I made half the recipe.  I fried up some bacon and used the dripping in place of the oil.  I used one jalapeno, one medium onion and about 3 cloves garlic.  I used one can of black and one can of pinto beans, only one with juice.  I used half a bottle of Sam Adams Boston Lager.  I didn't know whether I was supposed to cover or not with a lid, so I did for the first hour, then removed it for the last half hour.  I also used a wisk to break up the beans a little.  At the one and a half hour mark it was still a little wet, but I spread some on a flour tortilla and sprinkled with a little Mexican blend shredded cheese and rolled up.  It was so delicious.  I knew it would be because of all the great reviews, but it is absolutely delicious.  I am serving with a roast that I am making in the crockpot with some mexican seasonings.  I plan on shredding and filling some tortillas with these wonderful beans and the meat and whatever else sounds delicious.  Try these, you won't be disappointed unless you just don't like beans, onions, garlic or jalapenos.  Thanks DiB!

This was quite a treat, as I was raised to believe refried beans were strictly to be enjoyed straight from a can. I used Tecate beer, (sticking with the Mexican theme), which provided a perfect flavor when taste-tested after the proper cooking time. The problem was, I started my enchiladas late, so I had to keep adding more and more beer to keep the beans from burning. The end result, with 2 cans of beer, and about 2 and a half hours of cooking time was slightly bitter, so I wouldn't do what I did. Despite this, the refried beans were stiil delicious.

Okay, I'm going to be the black sheep here. I had really high hopes for this recipe, given the high ratings. I made this with a bottle of Dos Equis Amber (12 oz) and freshly cooked black beans. At first, there were three very prominent flavors, all fighting for the top spot: beer, onions and jalapeno. It was tasty enough, if not strange (in the realm of refried beans). It also stunk up the house something fierce.

Beans are almost always better the next day. These tasted like my work boots after a day in the sauna. Beer became the most prominent flavor, followed by watery onion. The jalapenos waved their arms, hoping to be rescued and not wanting to be part of this any longer. I ate the beans, but they were awful. My wife tried to eat them, but couldn't. I tried eating them again and again, until finally my wife told me to stop torturing myself and toss them.

I want to try this again with a lighter beer, but my wife has threated to move out (not divorce, just move out) if I make them again. If I get a chance to make them again, I'll update the review if they turn out better.

These are really good! I've made them many times now, and have even made them using home-cooked pintos and they came out well. As others have said, you can experiment by adding some cumin or bacon grease to amp up the flavor if you like. To those who are having trouble with the beer - I'd say it's best to use a lager in this recipe, like a Corona, Tecate or Budweiser - you don't want to use a dark beer in this recipe, and I would especially avoid any beer that is overly "hoppy", such as an IPA, as that would add a lot of bitterness once the beans cook down.

Sometimes I try recipes that I find at Zaar and wonder what I ever did without it.  This is certainly the case here.  These beans are wonderful!  Sadly, I had to tone down the jalapenos, so I used mild green chiles instead...but I had a bottle of Cave Creek Chile beer (with a jalapeno in it) and used that to cook the beans. I couldn't resist tasting along the way, and they just got better and better.   In the end, I didn't need to add a bit of salt because the flavors were so wonderful without it.  Di, thank you for sharing this wonderful recipe.

I recently used this recipe for the second time and it is awesome! I cut it in half both times, (there's just two of us). The second time I left both cans of beans undreined and still used a whole bottle of Miller Lite 64, I like my beans really moist. They don't even compare to canned, which I won't buy anymore because now I'm spoiled. I keep them in the fridge for a low fat somethng whenever I'm hungry. Spread some on a tortilla with a sprinkle of cheese or whatever I have for leftovers, Chicken, rice, tomatoes, a little cilantro, taco meat the list is limited only to the imagination! Thank you so much!

attributes.source_text: I like my beans really moist

reviews.review_text: Oh my Gosh!!!! I am so glad I didn't half this recipe! I was going to and then at the last minute decided to mix 2 can black beans and 2 cans pinto beans. Yum!!! I would have been really sad not to have the full four cans of beans. I think the combo of the two is beautiful. I used ONE jalapeno and I'm glad I did because it was just the right amount of heat. I think two would have been too hot and we love spicy food. I used Budwiser beer--I think a good choice. I will NEVER go back to can refried beans and I can't wait to make this again. I made them with Recipe #271347 Mexican style Lime and Cilantro Chicken with corn tortillas and Guacamole. Perfect!

attributes.source_text: it was just the right amount of heat

reviews.review_text: This is spooky - I know for a fact that this was one of the very first recipes that I made and reviewed shortly after I joined Recipezaar about 7 or 8 months ago! Darned gremlins! In any case, I have made them many times since then in my "Death to Canned Refried Beans" campaign. I always make them with Guinness stout or a good strong British brown ale instead of beer. I've eaten them as a side dish, and they have become a staple ingredient any time I make a recipe that calls for refried beans as an ingredient.

attributes.source_text: I've eaten them as a side dish

reviews.review_text: I was surprized that this recipe was a disappointment. I really like regulat old canned refied beans so I was anxious to try this. I made this recipe using hald dark red kidney & half black beans. I followed recipe to a T. The texture was great but the flavor had a beer taste that took away from the beans. I used a light beer thinking that the beer taste would simmer away. I didn't add salt but I don't think that would have made any difference. Maybe these are authentic tasting - but I will stick with the ones on the store shelf.

These beans turned out great!  I will never buy the canned refried beans again!  I cut the recipe in half and used 2 cans of pinto beans (because DH doesn't like black beans).  I used a little less than 1/2 a bottle of beer and topped them in grated Monterey Jack cheese just before serving!  Once they came to a boil, I cooked them over medium heat and stirred more often because I started them late  They only took about 30-40 minutes (after boiling).  Thanks Di, I'll be making this one over and over again!

I think these would be good without the pepper. I like spicy but these were way to spicy. My DH does not like anything spicy - he took one bite and said YUCK!! Maybe I had a hot pepper but it overpowered the whole dish. If I try these again I will try it without the pepper. I guess I thought the flavors would meld together but all you could taste was spicy hot. I used light red kidney beans (We don't like black beans) and 1 can of coors light beer. Maybe they are supposed to be very spicy ?????? I did like the texture and think it would have been yummy but we did not like it because of the spicy hot flavor - Sorry

I'm not the biggest fan of refried beans, canned or fresh, but the DH LOVED it! I felt it was a bit "dry" and may incorporate some additional oil or butter? I'm not sure yet... and I will research a bit before altering the final product.  I made this a day before a huge Mexican feast, and I am hoping (am confident really) that the flavors will blend even more! But I must say, this bean dip has a FRESH taste to it that I've never experienced before, even in the "finest" of Mexican restaurants. THANK YOU for posting!

attributes.source_text: the DH LOVED it
this bean dip has a FRESH taste to it

items.label: Homemade Drain Cleaner and Declogger
items.name: Homemade Drain Cleaner and Declogger
items.description: For those of you who hate poison-type drain cleaners, use white vinegar and baking soda. This will clean and unclog a drain. Also drops of white vinegar in your pet's water will keep away fleas and ticks!
instructions: Pour baking soda into drain.
Follow with vinegar.

reviews.review_text: I'd tried this before and it helped somewhat (1 min. longer to start to back up).<br/><br/>It was my kitchen sink so clog may be way down  by the bend...here's what I did <br/><br/>this time:  I got a long straw, wrist-elbow (like from coffeehouse) & had a small <br/><br/>funnel (can buy from cheap store most important is that straw fits in or outside <br/><br/>of the stem pretty close.  I then took a piece of napkin & wrapped so the straw <br/><br/>was snug and duck taped the outside.  Stuck it down the drain and poured the <br/><br/>baking soda down.  Took out straw and poured vinegar down.  (I had the duck <br/><br/>tape out since I had a splinter in my thumb and I heard wearing duck tape over <br/><br/>it for 2-3 days will have the splinter slip out.)  When boiling the water, I made <br/><br/>edamame you could do eggs, etc. After 1/2 hr, poured the boiling water down <br/><br/>the drain & since my tap water is hot, kept it going for 12 min SUCCESS!!  <br/><br/>Note, this was done on side w/o disposal since straight down.  Also, had saran <br/><br/>wrapped & rubber banded the air gap on top of sink and secured the other side <br/><br/>with saran wrap and a stopper.  Ann

Oh, I can't thank you enough for putting this tip up under drain declogger!!  I'd give this 6 stars if I could. I was amazed at how well this worked!  I also poured down a tea kettle worth of boiling water after letting it sit for some time.  It even cleared up the shower drain in this apartment (has to repeat it 3 times) and it is a repeat offender of horrible clogs - brooklyn filth, dust, my hair, my cat's hair, you-name-it- horrible clogs where the water will not go down for a couple of hours!  The pro drainers at the supermarkets are really expensive (where 1 bottle is 1 or 2 uses only!), but this is so cheap I will be using this as a preventative maintenance cleaner biweekly or more!  I am so happy to know I will be able to keep my drain clearer all the time and without really dangerous chemicals.  No more horror clogs!! Thank you so much, Mirj!

Mirj, if I could give you 100 stars for this gem of a recipe, I would do it! My sink has had serious probs for over 2 months (closer to 3) now. I've used Draino, among other things, and plunged repeatedly. This morning I was standing there cussing the darn thing as I used the plunger and then happened to remember this recipe I had once read with so many great reviews. Not being able to locate it, I posted a msg on the board. Thank goodness! You have saved me mega bucks, but the plumber probably isn't too happy. lol....Big hugs and many thanks to you for posting such a fantastic money saver that works like a dream!!! It ALMOST makes me feel like I owe you the money I saved on the plumber. *wink* Thanks again.
...txgammi

It fizzed, it bubbled, it worked like magic in a cup! Wow, Mirj Momma, you are amazing! Thanks to you, now, I have a homemade solution to the problem of my bathroom drain that gets filled with my falling hair when I shampoo. No more wasting Rials on drain cleaners(unfortunately, I bought one on the 14th) that use chemicals; this is cheaper, natural and available right in the house! I followed Donna M's review - I did this then waited for 10 minutes and then poured a pan of boiling water over this. The drain cleared within seconds!
My dad will be really glad with this recipe of yours :)
Thanks SO MUCH, {{{{{Hugs to you}}}}}}}}, for sharing this.

I would have spent $50 for this recipe!!! I have been in a rent house for 2 years and the bath tub never drained well.  It took about an hour to drain and that made cleaning it very difficult.  I've tried everything!!!  I just bought a product off of HSN called Professor Amos for $35.  I sent it back.  I tried this today because last night Walgreens was out of vinegar.  I couldn't wait.  I came home on lunch and OMG!!!  Woo Hoo!!!  My drain is clear.  Now... it's time to test it for the fleas and mosquitos.  Thank you sooooooo sooooo sooooo much.  I cannot rave enough about this.  These clear pipes is my 2nd most excitement this year next to seeing Kirk Franklin in concert.

Mirj -- great idea to post this "recipe". It works very well, I've used this combination many times. Here's another one for you: I had already tried this remedy on a REALLY bad grease clog, to no avail. My grandpa just happened to call at that time, and I --- well, I whined to him. He told me what he used to do when he was the manager/fix-it guy for a trailer park: get out your handheld blow-dryer. Make sure there is no water on the floor where you're standing so you won't electrocute yourself, then open up the access to the drain pipe - that little trap thingy. Aim the hot air right on that, and it will melt the grease and let everything slide on through. My Grandpa Rocks!

Fantastic! I knew this worked for drains, but who knew it works for toilets?  My 3 year old put almost an entire roll of toilet paper down the toilet and tried to flush it before I found out....as you can imagine the toilet was pretty clogged.  An hour of plunging off and on did not fix it..we thought maybe she stuffed something else down there, until I remembered this recipe.  IT WORKED!  I let the water recede and added the baking soda then vinegar and let it sit and foam for about 5 min, flushed to fill the toilet with water and got a little more suction and was so happy to see everything go down quickly.  The toilet is back in working order again thanks to this recipe! Much appreciation to you for posting it!

I have been using this "recipe" for almost 2 years now... I hate using commercially available drain cleaners and this works like a charm.  I like to use this monthly to keep the drains fresh and clean and running smoothly.  I like to pour the baking soda into the drain, them add a few drops of lemon and orange essential oils before pouring the vinegar over it and letting it work its fizzy magic.  Then I pour a large pot of boiling water to flush it through... Leaves the drain smelling like a citrus garden and running so smoothly!  Thanks for sharing a very helpful and environmentally friendly household hint!!!

My bathroom sink had been getting progessively slower and I kept bugging DH to clean the trap out with no luck.  Turn to zaar - there's got to be a solution for me there.  Sure enough!  One treatment and my bathroom sink is free flowing like new again.  I did the recipe "as is" let it sit for 5 minutes and then flushed with tea pot full of boiling water.  When DH came home I told him he owed me $58 for fixing the bathroom sink and not having to call a plumber to do it. :)(In case you want to know he just laughed and told me it was all MY hair that had plugged it up in the first place!)  Oh well, a great fix and it certainly saves a TON of money.

This seems to work, but I did not have a big problem with clogged drains, so I am unable to say that this "saved" me (5 stars). The ingredients are "green" so I will continue on other drains and toilets throughout the house, and if I notice improvement in their draining, I shall return to upgrade my review. I followed the style of one reviewer and poured a pot of boiling water down the drain 5 minutes after the baking soda and vinegar treatment. One question: when I first learned to cook, "vinegar" always meant apple-cider vinegar, and "white vinegar" was always written out when it was to be used. I wonder if it even makes any difference whether apple-cider vinegar or distilled white vinegar is use. Used this method based on Color Guard's review for "I Recommend" tag. UPDATED FROM 1/11/2009 REVIEW ON 3/16/2018: Nix on the boiling water - it cracked the porcelain in my sink, so now I must replace it.

After trying several name brand drain cleaners, to no avail, I found this recipe online. Guess what, IT WORKS!!!!! When I think back to all the money I have wasted buying harsh chemicals....and here all I needed was two simple ingredients and most households have both on hand anyway. AND no harsh fumes to choke or gag me! My grandmother used to do this same thing with her dishwasher. For anyone who hasn't tried it yet....I highly recommend this!!! I don't give out good/bad reviews until I have actually tried something first.

items.label: Bread Machine Cinnamon Buns
items.name: Bread Machine Cinnamon Buns
items.description: Make and share this Bread Machine Cinnamon Buns recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Put yeast in bread machine first on bottom, then flour, sugar and salt.
Then melt butter in microwave.  Add beaten egg, milk and water.
Pour onto dry ingredients in bread machine on the dough setting.
When dough is done, put it onto a lightly floured surface.
Knead in enough flour to make it easy to handle.
If it is  too elastic, cover and leave 10 minutes.
Use floured rolling pin to roll out dough on floured surface.
Roll out into rectangular shape to approx 1/4-inch thick.
Use filling and spread over entire surface of dough with spoon.
Roll up dough.
Cut into circle with a sharp knife about 1-inch thick; place these in a greased 9x13-inch pan.
Cover with a tea towel and leave in a warm place for approx 30 minutes, until double in size.
Bake in a 350° oven for about 25 minutes, light brown on top.
When done, make glaze and swirl over buns.

reviews.review_text: My bread machine says to put in wet ingredients first and then dry with yeast on top. So that's what I did. I used bread machine yeast and let it run the full dough cycle (2 hours). The dough was sticky so I added some more flour and kneaded it until it was rollable (I rolled it out to 12"by 16"). The filling I used was 1/3 butter, 3 tbsp cinnamon and 1 cup packed brown sugar. I mixed them together and spread it on the dough. Next time I'll spread the butter and then sprinkle the cinnamon and brown sugar overtop. Rolled it and used floss to cut them into 12 rolls. Let them rise and baked them for 25 mins. I let them cool at least a half an hour before glazing so the glaze doesn't melt off. I increased the glaze to around 2 cups powdered sugar, 8 or so teaspoons of milk and about 1 tsp of vanilla (enough liquid to get it the right consistency). I started with double the glaze but needed a little bit more so that's why I'm not 100% sure on the measurements. I'll definitely be making these again!

I've made these two times now. Both times the dough was very easy to work with, but the first time they came out a little dry and pinpointed it to the filling. So, the second time around I used the filling and frosting from a Copycat recipe, but kept everything about the dough recipe as is. It's very easy to make. My friend uses the Copycat dough that calls for vanilla pudding and punching, waiting, punching, waiting. I like putting everything into the bread machine and walking away until it's time to roll out and cut the dough. Hers ARE somewhat lighter and tastier (hence the 4 stars instead of 5), but this dough is still very good for the ease factor. I was able to get 24 nice-sized rolls both times. For the filling I used 1/2 c. butter (at room temp.) spread over the dough and mixed together 2 c. brown sugar and 2 t. cinnamon to sprinkle over the butter. The frosting was 1 3/4 c. powdered sugar, 1/2 T. milk, 4 oz. cream cheese & 1/4 c. butter (both at room temperature), and 1/2 t. vanilla stirred together with a mixer. (You probably won't need all the frosting, but I haven't taken the time to adjust the correct amount to go with this dough recipe yet. You might be able to cut it by 1/2 if you don't want a ton of frosting.)I'll keep the listed glaze recipe, too, though, since it was good and light, and considerably less calories because there's no butter or cream cheese involved. Enjoy!

attributes.source_text: it was good and light

reviews.review_text: SO- this totally may be a 5 star and ended up being a 4 star because of my own fault but I'm not entirely sure- I followed everything correctly, the dough was absolutely beautiful after my bread machine mixed everything. I saw a few people on reddit and here say it's fine if you put it in the fridge overnight so I plopped it in an oiled mixing bowl, punched down the dough, put saran wrap over it and put it in the fridge. It rose again in the fridge, everything was great. Proceeded as usual from there. But, they did *not* rise any more in the 30 minutes you're supposed to cover them after cutting and placing in the pan. I assumed this was due to them rising already in the fridge over night and was normal? Now- I didn't end up having a large dish like suggested or like everyone used in their photos so i used a springform pan that I've had great success with in the past when baking the typical canned Pillsbury cinnamon rolls so I figured this would be fine. What ended up happening was, for some reason, the dough on the outside became crispy almost like a bread crust and it by itself tastes like bread. I have no idea if the bready yeast-y flavor was enhanced by the second rise in the fridge overnight or this is normal and my buns just got crusty due to me not jamming all of them inside of this one pan, thus providing too much heat contact and crisping them? Or is this all because they rose in the fridge overnight and did not rise after being cut and placed in the pan+covered with a towel?? I am so confused and not sure if I should try this again with bread flour or just get a different pan or what. Otherwise they're not bad and taste very much like Cinnabon but I find the texture to be very dense and not super light and airy (though the middle of it is!) so I may just end up trying again with bread flour, not putting them in the fridge overnight and jamming more of these in to the pan *worth maybe mentioning that I used instant rise yeast....... Not sure if that's a huge no-no but I read elsewhere that it would be fine?

attributes.source_text: though the middle of it is!

reviews.review_text: I was initially skeptical about making the dough as in the recipe as the bread machine instructions are otherwise. As the other reviewers had tried the recipe method I decided to give it a try.I thought the dough would not rise while in the bread machine but after the kneading period the dough rose just to the brim of the pan.With regards to the filling, the sugar was way too much for me and I had plenty left over,which I will use when I bake my next batch.I find that it is easier to spread the softened butter first on the rolled dough and then sprinkle the cinnamon sugar. Am not sure if its me but I find that the baked rolls were a little difficult to separate, they were kinda stuck together rather firmly and I had to gently prise them apart. All in these are wonderfully soft and fluffy,just how I like them!

attributes.source_text: wonderfully soft
fluffy

reviews.review_text: I made three batches of these this past weekend for a volleyball tournament hospitality room for coaches and officials. Before the end of the tournament, they were all gone!  Several coaches complimented me and several moms who worked that day asked for the recipe.  I used a different recipe last year and these are by far better than that one.  This will be my staple cinnamon roll recipe from now on.  I loved how easy it was to make these too.  The bread machine does all the work.  I know how long it takes for the dough to make, so I popped in the ingredients, did whatever I needed to do, and came back and finished.  I actually made two batches a couple days ahead knowing I had this tournament, so I froze them after filling them.  I set them out for an hour or so and then put them inside the oven with pans of boiling water underneath and they rose beautifully.  I couldn't tell the difference between the fresh or frozen batch when done.  I used this glaze recipe on half and a cream cheese icing for the other half.  Perfect!  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: for a volleyball tournament hospitality room

several moms who worked that day asked for the recipe

reviews.review_text: These were amazing!!! I followed the recipe exactly. I did use instant yeast that I just purchased. As it was mixing I noticed the dough still a bit too wet. I added about 3 level tablespoons of flour. Let the machine continue mixing. I had to add about 1 more tablespoon of flour to get the best feel to the dough. I used a full size baking sheet to roll out the dough with a floured rolling pin. I put the butter in microwave to soften and added another 2-3 tablespoons. Spread the softened butter then added the other ingredients across the buttered dough. Definitely added more cinnamon. Rolled the dough. Divided by 12 placed in 9x13 pan. I turned the oven on 200 until it reached temperature. Turned it off then placed the rolls in oven covered with towel until they rose over the side of pan. Baked about 20-25 minutes until lightly browned. I found these better then the cinnamon rolls you get at the Malls. Thank you for such an amazing recipe

Wonderful rolls! I used the bread machine the night before, formed the rolls and refrigerated covered overnight, then finished rising in the morning before baking. Check at 18 minutes, mine were done at 20. Found the dough very easy to work with. Only sub I made was my usual: instead of all-purpose flour, I used half white whole wheat flour and half unbleached all-purpose. Got 12 good-sized tender rolls with lots of cinnamon flavor. Used Vietnamese cinnamon which is better than the typical grocery store variety in my opinion. Did make the light glaze as stated in the recipe which was good, the rolls are sweet enough to do without a heavy icing, but for the icing-loving kids, I might use this favorite next time: a stick of butter (8 T), 1 1/2 c powdered sugar, 1/4 c cream cheese, 1/2 t vanilla and 1/8 t salt. My kids love cinnamon rolls and were thrilled to wake up to these this morning. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

reviews.review_text: These were easy to make. Really rich and flavorful. I have a bread maker with a horizontal loaf pan. Putting the dry ingredients in first as specified made for a little trouble getting the bread machine to pick up all the ingredients to blend them. Helped it along with a spatula and problem was solved quickly. I warmed the milk a little. I also mixed my yeast with my flour as I added it to insure it wouldn't be stuck in a corner on the bottom and lost. The dough was a little sticky and I basically just tossed it around on flour to make it workable and just rolled it out. I used all the brown sugar and cinnamon. They were not too sweet. They rose well and the final baked product is soft and moist. Not a bready texture but a true roll. Definitely will use this recipe exclusively in the future.

reviews.review_text: I have tried several recipes for cinnamon rolls but never found one I really liked until now.  My rolls were fluffy and soft even though I did overbake them a bit.  I put them in the oven at 350 for 25 minutes then went outside to help my husband.  When I came back in I still had a couple of minutes left on the timer but the rolls were darker on the top than they should have been.  Also, I didn't worry about putting the ingredients in the pan in any certain order - I just threw things in as I got them out.  I didn't use the frosting recipe as I had a bunch of canned frosting to use up.  Also when the rolls came out of the oven I did rub them with butter to make the overbaked tops a bit softer.

attributes.source_text: My rolls were fluffy
and soft

reviews.review_text: DELICIOUS!  Everyone loved them here.  One thing I did not like however were the directions, or lack thereof.  "Use filling..." ok... but how is it prepared?  I took a wild guess and mixed the filling ingredients in a bowl and then spooned that over the dough. But it could be easily taken as spread butter, than spoon brown sugar then cinnamon on top of the dough.  That was what I thought I had to do but decided instead to mix it up together.  Same for the glaze. Two or three spoons of milk... why two or three? What texture are we looking for?  I made it a caramel cream-like texture and thickness.  I never made buns before so I really dislike when recipes just assume you know what to do!  But that being said, they were WONDERFUL, fluffy, tasty, sweet (but not too sweet), and the smell in the house...exquisite!  I made the dough and rolled up the buns the night before and I let the whole thing rest in my (unheated) oven overnight.  I baked them this morning. What a way to start a Sunday!  Thank you for this great recipe.

reviews.review_text: I made these at 4 a.m. trying to be very quiet as my son was asleep in the living room just off of the kitchen. Very little light and no "readers" viewing the tablet so I didn't follow the correct order of the ingredients. My machine calls for wet on the bottom & dry on top with yeast being the last to add. It didn't matter though, the dough came out just perfect! I also added brown sugar to the filling and used cream cheese in the frosting. Everyone awoke to the wonderful smell of fresh rolls and really enjoyed them. This will be my "go-to" from now on. Thank you for sharing!

Oh my goodness Krusty...these are probably the best cinnamon buns that have come out of my bread machine yet, The dough is just wonderful..... the finished result, was a perfect texture, and very light cinnamon bun... it just melts in your mouth...not like some of the dough recipes that I have tryed in the past, they have produced a very heavy textured dough.... this one is even better than the sweet roll dough recipe that was featured in the recipe book that came with the bread machine. I have already entered this recipe in my 10 star bread machine recipes folder, and will definetely be making this again,  (probably tonight, cause I don't think these will last very long!)...5 stars all the way.. I will be using this dough recipe for many other uses...a keeper for sure...thanks :-)  :-)

reviews.review_text: Made the dough exactly as is! Perfect, tender and absolutely amazing. I made my own filling (doubled the margarine, added pumpkin pie spice, nutmeg and finely diced apples) and glaze (powdered sugar, bailey's liquor, coffee and vanilla extract) Pefect! I've already made sure to write this cinnamon roll recipe in my book as it is the best and most tender roll recipe I've made yet!! Love how easy it is in the bread machine. Im done looking! I'm glad I read the reviews and made sure not to let it rise in the bread machine, but pulled it out before the rise cycle and continued on with the recipe.

the best and most tender roll recipe I've made yet

reviews.review_text: I can not believe that I am the first one to try and rate these fabulous (what I would refer to as cinnamon rolls)we had a rainy dreary day today and so I decide to perk it up with a treat for the family. These rolls came out so big and fluffy and the filling reminded me of the cinnamon fried pies my mom would make when I was a kid. So comforting and amazing delicious. I will admit I did use another recipe for the icing as my family prefers a cream cheese base icing, but the winner is really in the roll it's self. Krust I wish I could give you more than 5 stars! Thanks for bringing back my childhood if only for a few hours!

reviews.review_text: These were great!  The order of ingredients was opposite of my bread machine's instructions so I was skeptical but they came out wonderfully.  The dough was very thin when the kneading started so I added about 1/4c to 1/2c of flour.  When it came time to knead on the board, I hardly had to add any flour at all.  The rolls tasted wonderful and I liked the filling.  I used a recipe previously that called for a lot more butter and  it all ran to the bottom of the pan while baking.  These did not have that problem.  I also liked the glaze.  It reminded me of the glaze my mother used when I was young. I will definately continue to use this recipe!

I can't rate it yet because I didn't go the entire way with recipe.  I used a cream cheese frosting (because it is amazing). Otherwise I would like to rate the dough: 5 stars!!!!!  To all the new bakers (like myself): You have to try this!  I first called myself crazy for wanting to make it, but after seeing all of the pictures, my mouth watered and there you go.  I had to make them.  Besides, these do remind me of my childhood, the good old days.  As someone else stated before, the dough is very easy to work with and not sticky.  Perfect for new bakers like me who fear sticky dough.  I actually made the mistake of not letting it sit enough, therefore they didn't rise as high as some of the buns in the pictures.  But really good anyway.  Yum Yum Yum.

attributes.source_text: not sticky

reviews.review_text: I just got my first bread machine & wanted to try the dough setting. Since my husband and 3 sons love good, sweet, fluffy but gooey centers, cinnamon rolls (which I've yet to get right the standard kneading way), I thought I try this recipe.  It turned out PERFECT THE FIRST TIME!  I made them the night before and baked them the next morning before Mass (church), and it actually got everyone out of bed, the smell was soooooo good.  A few sidenotes for beginners like me:  Wait until your dough cycle is done, since it does all the kneading, resting, and 1st rise inside it.  Mine took an hour and half.  I did use butter, but I melted it first, let it set for an hour on the counter, then spooned it liberally but not too much as I did not want mushy or gooey dough.  I cut 1 inch slices and used a 9x13" glass pan and it took 15 rolls all touching cozy like, then stuck them in the fridge.  I DID NOT use this frosting, but the cream cheese frosting mentioned here in the comments by another rater.  It was delicious.  I left it in the bowl when done then put in the fridge also over night.  Covered everything with plastic wrap.  This morning I preheated the oven to 350, took rolls and frosting out of fridge and let sit on counter.  In the ten minutes the oven preheated, the rolls rose very little, and I was worried they would stay flat.  They didn't, they were fluffy and light and cooked to perfection!  Since my oven runs hot, I cooked them on the rack just below the middle of the oven and only baked for 16 minutes.  They were lightly browned on top and the filling was bubbling softly.  The frosting was still a bit firm from the fridge, but a spoonful melted quickly on the hot rolls and I just lightly spread it around with the back of the spoon, and was thick enough to make my husband happy, but not so thick that all you tasted was frosting. Even though the rolls were all together, they held their shape removing from pan and my husband ate 6 immediately.  And, he only likes the centers usually, but he remarked, "Honey, the whole thing is delicious!"  My picky son also ate all of his and had a second, eating it all too.  I hope this is helpful.  Suzie Doer

items.label: Bestest Hamburger Soup
items.name: Bestest Hamburger Soup
items.description: I think this is our #1 all time family favorite and it's often requested for birthday dinners. It's the 'Bestest' because my daughter described it as such when she was little.  This freezes well and I've added directions for that and for reheating.
instructions: In a large saucepan, brown meat, drain excess fat.
Add salt, pepper, oregano, basil, seasoned salt, and onion soup mix.
Stir in boiling water, tomato sauce, and soy sauce.
Cover and simmer for about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare celery, celery leaves, and carrots; Then add to simmering mixture with split peas and continue to cook for 30 minutes.
Add macaroni and simmer for 30 minutes longer, adding more water if necessary and stirring occasionally.
Serve sprinkled with Parmesan cheese over individual servings.
To freeze: place soup in a rigid container and freeze.  To reheat: remove from freezer and thaw.  Place soup in saucepan and heat, stirring, until hot.

reviews.review_text: Ok, first off I combined two recipes and put in this recipe what it was lacking from the other that I used.  Here are my vairations....I found that I added more salt than specified here....I added one cup of shredded cabbage, one cup of cubed potatoes and 1/3  cup of rice, 2 small bay leaf, one can diced tomatoes and one tsp of thyme...I also doubled most everything used for the broth because I found it didnt have enough to compensate for the addition of other ingredients....I also added a sausage called Linguica (dont cook , just slice and drop into pot while cooking) or chourico would do well...It gave it a real nice flavor...I did add a bit of red pepper flakes....It turned out so good and I had nothing left....I did use two envelopes of the onion soup mix and used two cloves of garlic and cook it with my ground beef....Thanks for a great recipe...Sharon

Fantastic!!!  I'm a vegetarian who loves to modify recipes to my diet so here's what I did...  I used 1 1/2 packages of Morningstar vegetarian beef crumbles and sauteed it along with all of the vegetables and seasonings in olive oil...  To avoid pre-packaged onion soup mix, I made my own mix using 1/3 c. dried minced onion, 1 1/2 tsp. onion powder, and an 1/8 tsp. celery seeds...  Nothing to the exact, I measure everything in my hand...  And instead of adding 6 c. H2O, I added 8 c. vegetable broth and next time I might add even more...  Oh!!!  And in my opinion, you CANNOT make soup without onion and garlic, so I added 1 whole dice onion and 4 cloves garlic...  And, yeas cook the macaroni separately...  Thanks for an awesome recipe!!!

I've made this a few times with a bit of my own twist. I did only use 1 lb of ground beef because 2 just seemed excessive. I don't use celery because I rarely have it. I use 15 oz of tomato sauce and 4 cups of water and eyeball all the seasonings which probably get at least doubled. I also add a bit of dried red pepper flakes for a bit of heat. I use 2 carrots and add 2 cubed potatoes and add garlic and some chopped onion. I omit dried split peas and instead use about a cup each of frozen peas, frozen corn, frozen blackeyed peas or whatever I have in the freezer. I use rice instead of elbow pasta and cook it separately and just add to the bottom of the bowl. Everytime we have it DH and DS eat it up! I usually serve with corn bread or warm rolls. Thanks for a great base recipe Hey Jude!

attributes.source_text: Everytime we have it DH and DS eat it up!
Everytime we have it DH and DS eat it up!

reviews.review_text: I love it when a recipe delivers beyond expectations and this one certainly does just that! I have made this twice now, first following the recipe exactly and everyone devoured it and thought it was very good.  I made it again last night and added a can of tomato soup, subbed beef broth for 1/2 of the water and added a drained can of green beans, a cup or so of frozen corn and worcestshire sauce instead of soy sauce, and mini penne instead of macaroni and it was even better. My family tends to not be soup lovers, but add some homemade french bread to this soup and there was not a drop left. My husband is very picky and tends to frown when he finds out we are having any kind of soup or stew for dinner, well... he ate three bowls! Fantastic recipe and one that I know will become a staple in our house. Thanks!

reviews.review_text: If I owned a restaurant, this would be my soup-of-the-day EVERY day! No kidding -- WONDERFUL, BEST-EVER soup! I was a little concerned at first that it would be slightly light on herbs/spices/salts but, no, it is perfectly seasoned as listed (I like moderate salt, my wife likes very light and we were both happy with the seasoning) -- I stayed exactly with the recipe, measuring amounts precisely, except that I had no dried split peas so I used dry LENTILS instead. Perfect. The cooking time on the lentils was just right. I don't know what more to say except that I feel strongly that this is one of those rare recipes which could not possibly be improved. As suggested, I did add a couple of extra cups of water near the end of cooking time and it did not dilute the flavor in the slightest. You could add chicken stock instead but I think it would be remiss to mess with this recipe. It already has BIG flavor and does NOT need the stock, an ingredient which I use quite often in soups, along with bouillon, to boost flavor. My wife (my biggest food critic) gave it a big two thumbs up and said, "Make it again," which is the very pinnacle of her food rating system. For the ground beef, I would definitely recommend using good ground chuck instead of ground round because you drain the fat off anyway and the ground chuck yields much more flavor. Beyond that, all I can say is you're a darling, Hey Jude, and thank you SO much for posting this MAGNIFICENT recipe. I'll be making this at least twice monthly in the future. pat, the old bone man.

reviews.review_text: This was great & my whole family enjoyed it!  I also substituted frozen peas for the split peas, but think the split peas would be good also!  I added more water part way through & compensated for the dilution by adding garlic salt, onion powder & a little italian seasoning.  A healthy helping of parmesan sprinkled on top is especially more delicious!!  :)  I cooked the ground beef the night before, which made throwing it together today even easier!  I also kept a close eye on it and was able to shorten some of the cook times.  It was so tasty I didn't wait for supper, but had a bowl at 3:30!!  Thanks!

reviews.review_text: What can I say but delicious....I made have the recipe and this is what I did.  I added some red pepper flakes for a little zing, minced a large clove of garlic to brown with the meat, added chopped onion, 2 small potatoes cubed, fresh corn cut off the cob, the celery and celery leaves and carrots,  about a half a can of white beans, and some barley.  I used all the seasonings it called for and for the tomatoe sauce I used a can of V-8 juice.  I also had to add more liquid but I did put extra stuff in the pot.   DH and DH's dad loved the dish.  There is still some left so I am going to add more liquid and have it for lunch tomorrow.  Thank you for a DELICIOUS and adaptable recipe!

reviews.review_text: Incredibly delicious, but I had to add water twice, as it kept evaporating. I halved the recipe as it was only DH and I. I skipped the seasoning salt, using extra celery seeds in the copycat Lipton's onion soup mix recipe 24952 instead. I also skipped the peas, and I do say I missed the colour. In serving, instead of parmesan cheese, I toasted breadcrumbs with garlic on a browning plate in the microwave (try recipe 291042), and it gave a fantastic crumbly texture to the final thing. I was full after eating a quarter serving; DH ate every bit of the rest of it. Nothing leftover at all.

reviews.review_text: My family enjoyed it.  I feel like there is something missing for me though so I am going to have to play with the spices a bit.   Guess that says I will be making it again. ")  I did substitute Kidney beans for the split peas and they were great, and brown rice for the noodles which was great as well.  I didn't have Lipton Onion soup Mix so I used a substitute recipe I found on the 'Zaar, and I was out of tomato sauce so I used paste watered down to equal the sauce.  It worked out well in the end.  We had the leftovers tonight and they reheated well.  I just added a boullion cube and a cup of water to compensate for the water absorbed into the rice.  Thanks!

reviews.review_text: This was a really good recipe, but the spicing of it was terrible for our tastes. My room mates and my husband found it to be rather bland. I even doubled the spices. NOW that isn't to say it didn't have its positive points. It was very hearty, and I think I will use the leftovers in a shepherds pie sometime next week. I will make this again, but next time i will cut the water in half  or maybe down to a third. I will substitute pasta sauce for the rest of the water, and I might even throw in a bouillon cube. Next time I will also add some ground red pepper, and pizza seasoning. The veggies were perfect in it, I don't think I'd change them, but maybe add a bell pepper to the mix. I want to give it more stars because it really is so incredibly versatile but the original really is so bland.

We all loved this soup recipe and have made it twice in 10 days!  The flavor was just right and it was a fairly quick meal to put together.  I thought I had everything to follow the recipe the first time, but halfway through I discovered that I only had lentils (worked out just fine) and egg pastina (teeny tiny little pasta stars, which also worked fine and cooked in only 5 minutes).  I also omitted the seasoning salt.  The second time I made this, I used ground turkey, which my kids liked even better!  Thanks so much for posting this recipe, it'll be enjoyed often.

reviews.review_text: This is definitely a very thick soup. I found for me it needed a bit extra salt and for me it seemed to be missing something else, but not sure what.   I followed the recipe exactly except for the tomato sauce, I had opened up a 15 oz can and used it all up. I also cooked the pasta separately and then added it to the soup. I would make this again but I would adjust the seasonings for my own tastes. Thanks for sharing your recipe Hey Jude

reviews.review_text: Should be called 'Kitchen Cupboard Stone Soup' ! Had the burger & onion soup, that's where things went wrong. Darn! And I'm a poster child for Mise en place ;>)

Hubby even said it should have more than 5 stars :-) I left out the salt & seasoning salt as I didn't think it was needed, used a jar of pasta sauce for the tomato sauce, added fresh onion & garlic because we like them, but everything else I followed. This soup will be a addition to our meals on these cold days.  The best is for last which is the soup itself.  I am excited to try this with venison. Great soup Jude!  I had three bowls of this and can't wait to have it again during the football game!  Hey guys it's great with a bottle of beer too!  Best soup I've had!!!

reviews.review_text: Loved this. I'm doing WW Core, so used whole-wheat noodles (ones I had on hand were rotini) and ground turkey breast. I left out the parmesan cheese, as well. Other changes were 1 lb of meat instead of 2 and the addition of 2 tsps of minced garlic cause I'm a garlic addict. The idea of split peas adds a nice texture and I want to incorporate that in some of my other soups. This had a diverse and  tasty blend of flavors with wonderful aroma. I made this for dinner last night. I also used 2 packets of onion soup. Discovered I didn't have tomato sauce, so used tomato soup as suggested by another reviewer. Instead of split peas and pasta, I used about a half cup each of barley and wild rice. I rinsed the beef under hot water after browning to remove more fat. reviews.review_text: I made this soup as specified, except I left out the added salt, since many of the ingredients are already salty. (Onion soup mix, soy sauce.) It was still VERY salty. I also took other people's advice and cooked the pasta on the side to add to each portion as needed and avoid sogginess. I used some of the pasta water to add to the soup to make it less salty.<br/><br/>On the plus side, it is very easy and the flavour is nice once you cut the salt. Hearty and good texture. With the added liquid and pasta on the side, I'd give it four stars.

I've made this soup about a dozen times.  My family loves this soup.  It's my go to recipe when the kids are sick.  My can of tomato soup is 14 oz.  I also increase the seasonings and liquids because the kids love the juice.  So I add 1 1/2 times the amount of seasonings and juices (except for the salt which I don't add).  Instead of peas, I use quick cookig barley the last 20 minutes.  I cook the pasta separately and then have the family add it to their soups.  Thanks for the wonderful recipe.

items.label: Easy Creamy Sour Cream Chicken Casserole
items.name: Easy Creamy Sour Cream Chicken Casserole
items.description: This is one of the first recipes I really "mastered" when I was learning how to cook. My husband got to enjoy this recipe at least twice a month because it was one of the few dishes I knew how to make. Now, that I'm a much better cook, we still have this delicious dinner on our menu at least monthly. It is so easy to put together and very good. If you like your casserole's creamy, then this is one you've gotta try! I hope you enjoy it as much as we do!
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Boil chicken breast until tender; drain and cube.
Spread evenly over the bottom of a square casserole dish.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Mix sour cream and chicken soup in a separate bowl.
Spread the sour cream and soup mixture over the chicken in the casserole dish.
Crush the Ritz crackers and spread over top of the casserole.
Spoon melted butter on top over all.
Bake in a 350°F oven until top is golden brown, approximately 20-30 minutes.

reviews.review_text:
I remembered a similar recipe from my childhood that I have been searching for ever since. I was so excited to find this. The only change I made was I added cooked Brown Rice as the bottom layer. (I thought I remembered that from the other recipe). Although it did make the recipe stretch further I don't think it really needed it. It was excellent on day one and two. I popped it in a cold oven (I was using a glass dish) and reheated that way. From cold oven to reheat it took about 20 -25 min. Oh, I also added about 1 1/2 tsp of Poppy Seeds (which I was sure of from the old recipe) into the sauce mix.

Thanks so much for posting. It really hit the spot!

This was a decent recipe the first time I made it, but tweaking it really brought it to the next level. I'm giving it three stars because the original recipe was "good" and easy, and it's not fair to rate it after making a bunch of changes. Here's the suggestions hubby made that really helped:<br/><br/>Sauteed some chopped white onion in butter and combined it with herb stuffing to make a "crust" on the bottom of the pan. Salt, pepper and poultry seasoning on the cubed chicken, which I placed on top of the stuffing (raw, because boiling it is an extra, unnecessary step.) Added corn and green beans to the sour cream/soup mixture to give it some veggies and texture. Poured over the chicken and baked until bubbly. Added shredded sharp cheddar in the last few minutes. Let it sit for 10 minutes to thicken. YUM! <br/><br/>Really, it's a totally different recipe at this point I guess, but I would have never thought to make this without a good base. We really liked the sour cream in it! Thanks!

Very good recipe.  The only thing I didn't like about it was the fact it was just chicken.  No rice, no noodles so I made this my own.  I added 1 cup of cooked mixed veggies, 6 ounces of cooked extra broad egg noodles, sauteed 4 stalks of diced celery along with 1/2 half of a vidalia onion in 2 tablespoons of butter.  I took the Ritz crackers and mixed in 1/2 cup of parmesan cheese to them and toasted them in 3 tablespoons of butter in a pan.  I assembled the recipe according to the directions but added the veggies, noodles and celery/onions to the soup mixture.  After mixing this well, I spread it over the chicken as usual and them topped with the toasted Ritz.  Baked for 30 mins per usual.  Thank you great recipe!

This gets top scores for ease of preparation, and is pretty tasty too.  It lends itself well to variations and tweaking, as evidenced by all the alterations in previous reviews.  I did not want to boil the chicken, so I simply seasoned it with garlic powder, salt, pepper, and a little poultry seasoning and baked at 350 until done.  I then cubed and prepared the recipe as directed.  I really wanted to use the cream of chicken soup, but realized I only had cream of mushrooms.  I did find garlic butter Ritz crackers, though!  All in all, this is simple, quick and appealing to most palates.  Thanks for sharing.

I wrote a review for this a while back, but since it never showed up, I'm trying to remember what I did.

I thought it was a little too much sour cream (for me).  I had made only half the recipe, so I cut everything in half except the soup, and used the entire can of that.  

I used salt when cooking the chicken, so I used just a little mixed in with the soup, and added pepper to my taste.

I didn't use the entire soup mixture, and put a little in the freezer.  When I made it a second time, I did the same, and thus had a little more soup (maybe 1/4 c.) to add to that reserve.

This is a very good and easy chicken dish.  It's not gourmet, but it's one that I've made once a week now, and I enjoy.  

I used chicken soup once, and mushroom soup once, and there's no difference.  I would guess you could use any of the cream soups to your liking, and the dish would still be quite good.

I really liked this recipe but the original recipe as written just didn't seem like enough. The second time I made it I added a frozen veggie mix that I cooked ahead of time (it was corn, carrots and asparagus) and I also added some spices and seasoning to the soup/sour cream mixture (a few pinches of mild chili powder, dried onions and dill) and it was really good. I also melted the butter and mixed it with the Ritz crackers before I put them over the top to get a good even brown. I really do like how the sour cream adds a whole new taste to the boring old cream soup taste. This is really a comfort casserole at it's best! Thank you for posting! I'm pretty sure that the family will ask for this again!

attributes.source_text: the sour cream adds a whole new taste

reviews.review_text: Excellent comfort food! My wife and I have been making something similar to this for some time, but I only recently found this recipe and other peoples comments. I did what some others have done and added a layer of cheese before putting the crackers down and also put a cup of frozen peas in the sour cream and soup mixture. I did two other things I think elevated it to another level, however. First, I used rotisserie chicken which adds a lot more flavor than just boiling chicken. When you work out the price, it usually comes out cheaper and easier to use rotisserie chicken anyways for casseroles. Secondly, I added the butter to the crushed crackers before I added them to to the top. I think this way allows the top to form more of a crust and lets the crackers crisp up a bit more. <br/><br/>Our favorite way to serve it is over fluffy white Jasmine rice with a side of fresh green beans or broccoli. Leftovers are always great, too!

It was extremely easy and tasted just as I expected :)  I have 3 different eaters in the house, all men....my husband, who looks everything over twice, dug right in and inhaled bite after bite...my 12 year old son, who is very picky, didnt hesitate on trying it and ate 3 servings...and my 4 year old son who eats everything but the fork and plate enjoyed every bite of it!!! What a hit in our house!! We will be adding this to our favorites!  Thanks for sharing :)

items.label: Secretly Delicious Spinach Pie
items.name: Secretly Delicious Spinach Pie
items.description:
The tortilla adds a delicious crunchy shell and it smells so good while it is cooking. I actually made up this recipe from items in my kitchen and couldn't believe how wonderful it tasted! It is now a hit in my family and so EASY to make. Please rate and give feedback.  


Update: Since I first made this five years ago, we still enjoy this at least once a month. I have found that I can alternate the ingredients to use up items I have in the fridge. I have used mushrooms, sauteed onions, cherry tomatoes and even feta cheese instead of cheddar cheese. And it always comes out fantastic. I have also found that there are times I need to use more or less eggs depending on the ingredients. Also, a glass pie pan is so much better than a metal as it toasts the tortilla just right. Such an easy recipe with gourmet taste!
instructions: Mix the first six ingredients (eggs, bacon, milk, garlic, lemon pepper and salt) in a bowl.  Set aside.

Lay the flour tortilla in a glass pie dish, press gently - does not need to lay perfectly flat against dish.  I don't spray it prior and have never had any issues with it sticking.  Especially when made using a glass pie pan.
Sprinkle only 1/2 cup cheese on tortilla.
Sprinkle remaining cheese and the spinach onto tortilla in layers, and press gently.  I don't chop or tear the spinach but you might opt to do this.
Pour egg mixture evenly over spinach, be careful not to pour any outside of tortilla as this causes it to stick to pan.
Bake in oven at 365 degrees for 35 to 45 minutes.  Insert fork in center and it should come out clean.
Use sharp knife to cut into pie slices and serve hot.
Other options: Instead of garlic, you can use 1/4 cup onions.  For added flavor, serve with homemade salsa.

reviews.review_text: I would NEVER have thought of using a tortilla as a quickie for making quiche!!! It's a lot less calories too (for those of us that need less lol!). My attempt was very good with a ceramic pan which heats to high temperatures, don't know if it could be bettered. I sauteed veggy bacon; when that had cooled a little, I chopped it while sauteeing onions & the garlic; I then added them to the egg mix. I was, ahem, more generous with the cheese! I used cheddar/Mexican (which in UK has red/green peppers & spices in it & is deep yellow). Next time, I'll try Blue cheese. The recommended servings were TINY - 5/6 people? Maybe for a buffet, but for dinner with salads, it serves two. Variations on this recipe that I didn't know I wish I had will be eaten often here. Good for lunchboxes too.

attributes.source_text: for dinner with salads
Good for lunchboxes too

reviews.review_text:
I have made this recipe twice. The first time I made it, I prepared it exactly as called for in the recipe except for the lemon pepper and the bacon (don't eat meat). It was ok, good actually but nothing to rave about. (I actually didn't think I would make it again as I already have a hard time getting the kids to eat spinach and I didn't need a recipe to make it any harder. )
The most I would have given it was three stars.
The second time I made it, it was much MUCH better.
I cut up plenty of onions and garlic ( I love both) and sauteed the spinach in them. I added some steak seasoning I like to use ( a blend of herbs and spices) and I squeezed a liberal amount of lemon to give it a slightly tart taste -to replace the lemon pepper. 
Then halfway thru I realized I had NO eggs! I was going to make a soy flour mix that you can usually susbstitute eggs for in baking recipes but something told me to abandon that idea. After dumping my soy flour concoction in the compost bin I decided that the eggs in the recipe probably served as a binder so I thought that I would just forge ahead without a substitution. But then I saw that I had some evaporated milk lieing around so I used that instead. I drizzled it on top, sprinkled some permesean cheese and it turned out Oh so GOOD!!!

I've decided to omit the eggs entirely and follow this version. Oh and I used cheddar cheese on mine. This goes into my regular rotation AND the kids loved it!!!
Five stars!
