reviews.review_text: after pawing through reviews, i came to my own conclusions.  i could not, for the life of me, find my glass pie plate, so i used another instead, but was sure to give it some non-stick spray love.  i also only had a head and a half of UNROASTED garlic on hand, so i sauteed three cloves, some chopped onion, chopped white mushrooms, aaaand the spinach for a few minutes, while the oven preheated.  my cheese selection consisted of leftover pizza-blend [mild cheddar and mozzarella], swiss, and parmesan.  i used a whole half a dozen of eggs, medium sized.  i omitted the bacon, but can only imagine how it would have enhanced the flavor.  this was SO GOOD.  thank you, so much!

Made this for dinner last night, I modified it a bit and it turned out great!  I used medium sized tortillas and put 2 in the bottom of my pie plate for a slightly thicker crust.  I only used 5 eggs instead of 7 and doubled the bacon.  I added a tsp. of lemon juice because I couldn't find my lemon pepper and used a Tbsp. of minced garlic.  I mixed everything together (all the eggs, cheese, meat, chopped fresh spinach) before pouring into the pie plate.  This was less work than creating layers.  It came out perfectly crisp, it looked like a beautiful personal breakfast pizza (but definitely served 2-3 people).  I made a 2nd one and added mushrooms but used my pampered chef small stoneware, it stuck horribly and the crust was soggy, never again, the glass pie dish is the way to go!  DH said this can be a staple item in our house and wants to try it with sausage next time.  I'm excited that I found a dish with a large serving of spinach that he will eat!

If not, perhaps I should have sprayed the pan, but I didn't b/c it wasn't in the directions.  I also felt it was too garlicy, but I used the chopped garlic in the jar (to the equivalent). I had my daughter help by tearing the spinach and layering it with the cheese and I have to be honest, she thought it looked rather disgusting. reviews.review_text: I made an "inspired by" version of this recipe, but I'm thankful for the proportions, and it turned out great.  Substitutions: plain goat's milk yogurt for the milk,  1/4 tsp garlic powder, juice of 1/2 lemon and some zest, black pepper (and a bit of cayenne), 2 links of browned chopped hot Italian turkey sausage, 1.5 cups shredded goat's milk cheddar, and 10 oz thawed drained frozen chopped spinach ~1 cup, (no tortilla)!  I ate it hot, but I'm pretty sure it's just as good cold.  I plan on trying different variations, depending on what's on hand.  Thanks!

I wont rate the recipe because I made modifications when I tried it. But here are some tips and thoughts based on my experience: 1. The glass pie plate worked out fine, but I realized while it was in the oven that an iron skillet might have worked even better. With a seasoned iron skillet, there wouldn't be a worry about the tortilla sticking (whatever your size of tortilla in comparison to skillet size), and you can easily preheat the skillet with some butter; put the tortilla on the hot butter; and pop it in the oven beore filling for a few minutes for a crispier crust. 2. The reviews that indicate this could benefit from more flavor are true. I doubled the lemon pepper and added another herb/spice mix. I don't recommend adding more salt, as the cheese already has plenty. I would recommend choosing your seasoning based on the cheeses (for example, if doing a feta-based mix, I'd go in a more Greek direction...lemon is good as is anything you'd add to spankopita). 3. I am a vegetarian and worried about not adding bacon (given the "needs more flavor" reviews), so I threw in some veggie sausage I had on hand. That was fine but unnecessary. It would have had enough on its own. If anything, it muddled the flavor direction. 4. My wife and kids ate it without complaint but when asked for feedback said it was too much spinach (I packed it when measuring). I, on the other hand, thought it was the right amount of spinach but also too much cheese. They didn't agree about the cheese. 5. The tortilla need not determine the flavor direction of the dish. I had buttered the bottom of the pan, and my family thought I had made the crust with potatoes (the egg mixture rose quite a bit and my tortilla was small, so there were no visible crust edges). The flavor of everything else overpowered the tortilla.

I made this on the spur of the moment. It only took a few minutes to get into the oven. I used pepper jack cheese on first layer, then cheddar. I sprinkled liberally with garlic pepper and garlic powder blend and used ready cooked bacon. I used 7 large eggs (was wondering since others used various amounts). I didn't have a pie plate and layered two tortillas in a oblong pan (probably pretty close in size). This turned out great. The combo of flavors is so tempting that even my family liked it (not spinach lovers). I really liked my combo of cheeses and will do it that way again. The bacon added a great flavor, too. Served with some leftover Carmelized Butternut squash by PianoLady.

Roxygirl

items.label: Perfect Basic White Rice
items.name: Perfect Basic White Rice
items.description: You do not need to be afraid of cooking rice again! lol Real rice is so much better for you than instant. So here is a basic recipe that will have you cooking rice like a pro! Check out the options too! Your friends and family will think you're a star!
instructions: In a saucepan with a good fitting lid bring water, salt and optional ingredients if desired to a boil.  The salt and butter are simply for flavor. The vinegar keeps your grains separated and gives you a prettier dish. No one will taste the vinegar at all!
Add rice and stir.
Cover and reduce heat to low. You will know that your temperature is correct if a little steam is visible leaking from the lid. A lot of steam means your heat is too high.
Cook for 20 minutes.
DO NOT LIFT LID!
The steam that is trapped inside the pan is what allows the rice to cook properly.
Remove from heat and fluff with fork.
Serve!

reviews.review_text: This is truly the only way to make white rice; I have never made it any other way, and it comes out perfectly every time, just leave your mitts off the lid as stated by others.  After the water comes to a boil and you lid the pan and turn down the heat, you only want to see steam seeping from the lid, if there's a lot of steam, the heat's too high; turn it down. If you follow these simple directions, you'll be very pleased with the results.  As a side note, I have added various seasonings and/or sauces to the boiling water just prior to adding the rice (give it a quick stir) with great success.  Another nice variation is to replace the water with equal amounts of canned broth (chicken, beef, vegetable, etc.) lower sodium broth is preferable.  I seldom add the optional butter, it's not needed; neither is the salt; the decision is yours in regards to these additions, but don't alter the method, it's critical to a successful pot of rice. Thanks Mama's Kitchen for adding a recipe that is so needed by so many and yet so very basic.  Sometimes we overlook the everyday basics when it comes to cooking.  Enjoy!

I agree that this is the perfect way to make rice.  My mother taught me how & insists this is the way to make good rice each and every time. I saute my rice with a little butter before adding the water.  Then I add the water, stir occassionally until it comes to a boil and then turn down the heat to low and cover with the lid.  The key is to not ever lift the lid during the 20 mins of cooking.  I know you want to stir it but DON'T Ha ha!  Also, I sometimes add dried or fresh herbs, & onions to the saute step.  Nice aromatic rice is what you'll get after 20 mins of impatience!  Good recipe, as there are some of us who take simple cooking for granted.  I still can't make homemade choc chip cookies LOL

items.label: Kittencal's Onion Patties/Latkes
items.name: Kittencal's Onion Patties/Latkes
items.description:
I have been making these for over 20 years, I usually get about 15 patties but it depends on the size of the batter that you drop in the pan, these are better if fried to very brown and crispy, you can make a double recipe, fry them then freeze them on a tray then pop them into freezer bags, then just warm them in the oven to crisp up, they are very addicting and I can tell you I eat half before they even get to the table lol!  If you plan on doubling the recipe then make two separate recipes in two bowls, I have doubled the recipe into one bowl and for some reason they just are not as good ---  if desired you could add in a slightly beaten large egg and reduce the milk by 1/4 cup --- you will *love* these!  also see my
recipe#186700 *and*
recipe#244592
instructions: Chop the onions finely (I chop them about 1/4-inch) then place into a bowl.
In another large bowl mix together the flour, sugar, baking powder, seasoning salt, cayenne, garlic powder (if using) and a small amount of black pepper; mix to combine well.
Add in the milk and whisk until thoroughly combined (the batter will be thick!).
Add in the chopped onions and green onions and mix with a wooden spoon until combined.
In a large non-stick frypan, heat a small amount of oil to medium-hot, adding in more oil as needed as the patties will absorb too much oil if you add in a large amount of oil at one time.
Drop the batter from a tablespoon (no more than about a tablespoon!) into about 1/2-inch of hot oil (I slide the batter off using off another spoon).
Flatten slightly with the spoon or spatula.
Sprinkle with a little salt.
Fry until crispy and brown on both sides.
**NOTE** these tend to hold a bit of oil so drain well on paper towels.

reviews.review_text: I know you don't need another 5 star review, but I couldn't let it go without thanking Kitten for ANOTHER great recipe!!    Because of all of the people who thought the batter was a little thin I went with 2/3 cup milk as a precaution but I don't think it would have been necessary.  I will note that I made a few for us to taste to see if we were even going to like them...obviously we did...then waited another 1/2 hour or so to make the rest.  It did seem like the batter was a little thinner after sitting awhile.  Perhaps this was the problem some of the reviewers had.  I served with Blooming Onion sauce # 70382.  We'll be doing this again and again!!  I'm anxious to see if they reheat as well as everyone says they do.

These taste great without a doubt! But I had no flour (silly me) so I used a baking mix and I used the same measurements as for the flour and my patties didn't hold together very well, so I had a hard time making these at first, so I added in more baking mix and that seemed to help them stay together.And I think you really have to be careful in how much oil you use to fry these as they do take in A LOT of oil when cooking like Kittencal warns so I had to remove some of the oil with the first batch. I was eating them as I took them out of the pan they were delicious. Also I dont know about everyone else but it took me a while to chop up all those onions and I think it would have made it a lot easier if I had a food chopper type thing, so I don't know if I would make these all the time but they would be a great treat once in a while. I have to say I just found this site a couple day's ago and I think it is the best recipe site on the web. Thanks Kittencal for all of your great recipes ( I have made quite a few of yours already).

I used the suggestion to replace 1/4 c milk with an egg and it was great.  I was a bit nervous that these would come out tasting like raw onions and was skeptical to try it out.  After going back to this recipe a few times I decided to give it a try.  The onions cooked beautifully and did not taste raw at all.  My husband requested that I make these on Hannukah instead of traditional potato latkes.  I used much less oil than recommended and they came out delicious.  I sprayed the pan with Pam and just used a bit of oil with each batch.  I froze the leftovers and then reheated them in the toaster oven and they were just as good as the day I made them.
Highly recommended!

reviews.review_text: UNREAL. Ok, I love onions, but I never would have thought they could be THIS good. This is the kind of recipe that could make me a vegetarian. A vegetarian who only eats onions. Who only eats THESE onions. Slight alterations based on the commandments of my tongue and what I had on hand: I used one large yellow onion and three scallions, just a pinch of cayenne and both the optional ingredients - garlic powder and pepper. I fried them at about 275-300 degrees for roughly 6 minutes on each side until dark brown (the way God intended!), flattening them a bit before flipping. This goes right into my "Encore" cookbook with much appreciation to you, KITTENCAL!

Great recipe; I tried popping these in the oven as another reviewer had suggested (15 minutes on one side, then 10 minutes on the other).  To my dismay, the batter felt thin when I spooned them onto the cool, oiled baking sheet.  Upon turning them, I found that the oil hadn't been absorbed and rather clung onto the patties, which felt more like crepes with their thin edges.  Once the patties were done cooking, I popped them onto a hot skillet; that helped a bit with the texture.  As I would like to limit the calorie intake in my household, I think I'll try the baked version again but up the flour content and shorten the baking time and finish cooking on a skillet next time.  Also, I found the patties a tad sweet for my taste (I did not use sweet onions - not easy to find in my new home above the Arctic Circle) so I might lower the sugar by 1/2 a tablespoon next time.

After so many high ratings, I'm not sure why this recipe didn't work for me. My husband and I love onions, and I was really hoping it would work. The taste was not an issue, they did have a good taste. I followed the directions exactly, however once all mixed, my mixture was not especially thick. It just slid off the spoon into the oil. And I followed the directions of only adding a bit of oil at a time, however they soaked up a tremendous amount of oil and even when drained on paper towels, they just never were crispy, just full of oil. If I could have found a way to get them to fry without so much oil and could make them crispy, then I would have rated these much higher.

I cannot believe I haven't reviewed this recipe yet! Let me start by saying that my family and I don't even like onions. For some strange reason, however, this recipe appealed to me and I just had to try it. Am I ever glad I did! We managed to scarf down each and every crisp, delicious patty - with the exception of the few I reluctantly shared with my MIL. I have brought these to several family functions just so I could sit back and revel in the raves and compliments. heheh Of course, I do humble myself just enough to let everyone know that it isn't MY recipe. I have found that by using my electric griddle, I am better able to control how much oil is absorbed by these patties - plus I am able to make much more at one time. This is especially helpful seeing as how they are otherwise gobbled up as soon as they are cool enough. Using the griddle, I am able to enjoy seeing a pile of them, if only for a moment. Thank you for posting this dangerously delicious recipe.

have them as a decadent fat-rich side for an otherwise low-fat meal

reviews.review_text: Kittencal...I was looking for an interesting side dish to go along with grilled chicken sandwiches... my husband immediately requested a double batch hoping to snack on the leftovers...needless to say, they were a major hit...I had to use olive oil, because we didn't have any other on hand...I'm sure there is a good reason for not using it, but fortunately they cooked well, and tasted fine to us... I have a feeling this recipe is going to get a lot of use by our family...thank you for sharing this unique and wonderful recipe.

attributes.source_text: an interesting side dish
my husband immediately requested a double batch

items.label: Cheesecake Cookies
items.name: Cheesecake Cookies
items.description: Make and share this Cheesecake Cookies recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Heat oven to 350.
In a medium bowl blend thoroughly butter, brown sugar and flour with a fork until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Put 1 cup of the mixture aside for topping.
Press remaining mixture into an 8x8x2 inch baking dish sprayed lightly with cooking spray; bake for 15 minutes.
In another bowl combine sugar and cream cheese, mixing until smooth.
Thoroughly beat in egg, milk, lemon juice and vanilla.
Spread over the baked crust and sprinkle with remaining brown sugar mixture.
Bake for 25 minutes.
Let cool, then chill for at least 1 hour.
Cut into 16 squares; serve.

reviews.review_text: I wish I could have had one! (Don't forget to spray your dish.) I doubled the recipe for a school concert and filled a 9x13 quite easily.  I let it cook an extra 5 minutes.  After letting it cool I put 24 marashino cherries on the cheesecake and melted chocoalate with some evaporated milk and drizzled that over the cherries.  I then put in the frigde(barely able to wait).  It was a wonderful sucess. Now I must make some more.  Thank you so much for sharing.  I will be making this for years to come.

attributes.source_text: I doubled the recipe for a school concert

reviews.review_text: Like everyone else who has tried this recipe, I love these cookies!  For the crust, I used brown sugar splenda and some of Penzey's baking spice and freshly ground nutmeg and it  tasted good even before I baked it.  I'll be using this crust again in other recipes.  I used fat free cream cheese with extra lemon juice and grated rind.  I was a little worried at how thin the batter was.  It was in the oven the initial 15 min, plus about 45 min more to finish baking, but it was well worth the wait.  I topped it with raspberry topping and it went over big with my husband.  From one Bev to another, these are amazing cookies!  Thanks.

attributes.source_text: it went over big with my husband

reviews.review_text: It's taking all of my strength not to explode right now, I just ate the easiest, most delicious rendition of cheesecake I have ever put past my lips. I made a few changes, I doubled the batch, made it in a larger pan and skipped the topping. I sprinkled about 3/4 of a bag of semisweet chocolate chips on the top 5 minutes after I took them out of the oven and let them melt, then spread the chocolate evenly over the cheesecake. I wish I could eat these every day (several times a day). I thank you from the bottom of my heart (and so do my research lab fellows, my friends, and especially my daughter). Oh, and by the way, I made this with 1/2 neufchatel cheese and it turned out perfect. I'm going to go get another one!

attributes.source_text: so do my research lab fellows
my friends
especially my daughter

reviews.review_text:
Bev, being #18 I'm not sure what else to say but these were fantastic!! I made these earlier today and did as I was supposed to (it was really hard though) and let them cool. And I hate to say it but they are just about gone!! And I only had one brick of cream cheese. I think I may have to take a trip to the store today even though I don't want to, but for more of these? Oh yeah! I have just eaten my 3rd one. Yum, Yum. Thank you so much for this great recipe. I will make sure this stays along with my other recipes that I bake on a regular basis. Again, Thanks Bev.
Hugs to you, Susie.

These were great with a few changes that I felt were necessary.  The cookies are too sweet with all the sugar in the crust PLUS the sugar in the cream cheese mixture.  Next time I will reduce the sugar in the crust or filling or both.  I also reduced the amount of top crumbs and reserved only 2/3 cup instead of the 1 cup as the recipe instructs.  I also agreed with another reviewer that baking the bottom crust for 15 minutes results in it being too hard, so I reduced the baking time for the bottom crust to 10 minutes, and I might reduce it to something like 7 next time I make it.  I would probably also increase the vanilla and maybe add a little lemon rind to the filling.  But it still deserves 5 stars!

It's okay - I think I could have reduced the initial time baking the crust to 10 minutes, because when I finished the entire bake time the cheesecake portion was overbrowned in some areas.  I left 1/2 cups for the top and it was fine, but didn't completely cover the top, which was fine by me.  I added Reddiwhip and half a strawberry, though it did not satiate my cheesecake craving or DH's  =P  The kids were okay with them - only for the fact it had whipped cream, lol  Thanks anyway

Another winner from Bev!  I've made these twice in one week - once for a high school church event and tonight for guests to my home.  Everyone loved them.  My friend who hosted the church event had to send the very few leftovers home with me so she wouldn't eat them all!  I followed the directions as written, but doubled the recipe and put it in a 13X9 for the first event.  Tonight I used the 8X8 and both times were great.  Thanks for another 5 star addition to my cookbook!

attributes.source_text: tonight for guests to my home
My friend who hosted the church event had to send the very few leftovers home with me so she wouldn't eat them all
once for a high school church event

reviews.review_text: Surprisingly bad! For something with so many good reviews, the cookies/bars had no taste at all. The consistency was rubbery, and the crust was almost like a bread or a cake - I think it would be much better with graham crackers. The cheesecake batter itself was lacking in flavour. I knew it wouldn't be as good as my mother's recipe (which I've never found another cheesecake to trump) but I thought for a quick snack, instead of making a full cake I would try this. That was not a smart move on my part. Next time, I'll just make my own full cheesecake.

These are really good!  I wasn't sure about the crust at first b/c it seemed so crumbly and didn't want to stick together.  It also didn't really brown much in the oven and came out w/crack.  I took the advice of other reviewers and only saved 1/2 c for the topping and put a layer of strawberry preserves in between the crust and the cheesecake layer.  However, the preserves broke up the crust in a few places.  It turned out really well.  This is a great recipe.  Thanks for sharing!

A great recipe! I don't have an 8 x 8 inch pan so I used a 20 cm x 15 cm instead (a bit smaller than called for); lined the pan with foil and then greased the foil. As per suggestions reserved only 1/2 cup of topping and baked a minute or two longer because of my smaller pan. Absolutely delicious - the crust has a caramel-like taste and the cheese part is fresh and not overly sweet. These instantly became my DH's new favourite! Thanks so much for the recipe Bev!

attributes.source_text: the cheese part is fresh
not overly sweet
These instantly became my DH's new favourite

reviews.review_text: 100 stars! I am not a cheesecake fan mainly because I don't care for the richness of the cream cheese - my husband is a huge cheesecake lover - these are just perfect little "bites" that satisfy both of us - AND he can have as many as he likes! Changes I made were: lemon zest and sour cream (1/4 cup) - for the crust I added 1/4 cup oats and coconut for texture. I served the squares with strawberry sauce and whipped cream. By the way - they freeze very well. Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

attributes.source_text: my husband is a huge cheesecake lover

reviews.review_text: Delicious! I was looking for a cheesecake type dessert that used only 1 package of cream cheese. I'm so glad I chose this one! We all loved it. We ate them plain the first night, after a meal of chicken soup and Recipe #96447. The second day I had prepared Recipe #15525 for another reason but the kids wanted to try some on the leftover cheesecake cookies. They loved them that way too. This recipe is very easy to fix and I know I'll be making it again. Thanks for sharing, Bev!

attributes.source_text: a cheesecake type dessert
They loved them that way too

reviews.review_text:
This recipe is incredibly hard! It is hard to wait until they have chilled and are cooled to eat them. Once you get to eat them, it's hard to justify not eating the whole pan! It's hard to share them with others. It's hard to believe that with simple ingredients you have on hand, you can make something so yummy!
All kidding aside, these are fantastic! A quick fix for a cheesecake craving without all the work! Fantastic!

Made as written for the Best of 2014 event, recommended by lazyme & so worth every star awarded w/all the reviews. Loved this for its flavor & easy-fix. Although not in need of a topping, I did top it w/a rhubarb compote that was among my own Best of 2014 recipes .. http://www.food.com/recipe/kisels-pureed-fruit-dessert-307776 by MarraMamba. Thx so much for sharing this recipe w/lazyme so she could share her appreciation of it w/us.

I just finished making these cookies, and couldn't wait til they cooled to try them. Took one out before I put them in the frigde to cool. These are yummy. Like a little piece of cheesecake. I imagine they would be great with some strawberry topping also. Thanks for the wonderful recipe.  Be careful when doubling this recipe....make sure u use the same size pans, otherwise one turns out to be too thin and bakes up harder than the other.

attributes.source_text: Like a little piece of cheesecake

reviews.review_text: I made this fabulous recipe last night & my family loved it!  It was so easy to make, but it tastes like you spent all day in the kitchen.  I added a little extra butter and took the advise of another reviewer and only used 1/2 cup of the crust mixture for the topping because I also like my crust a little thicker.  I will definitely add this to my FAVORITES and make this over & over agian.  Thanks for the GREAT recipe!

attributes.source_text: my family loved it

reviews.review_text: Had a package of cream cheese in the fridge left over from Christmas & noted it was due to expire next month so went in search of a recipe to use it up.  Found this one for Cheesecake Cookies (though they are more of a bar) and am I ever glad I did!!  They are absolutely delicious and so simple to make.  Definitely worthy of 5 stars.  I know these will be made again and again.  Thanks, Bev.

Great recipe. Quick, easy, and fairly foolproof. Having the topping means that you don't have to worry about cracking on the top. One of my guests thought the topping gave it a slightly toffee-like effect. I liked how the bottom was very firm and robust. I added cinnamon to the crust/topping mixture for a bit of extra oomph. The filling came out with a perfect texture and flavor. This is definitely a great shortcut to cheesecake.

attributes.source_text: the bottom was very firm and robust
One of my guests thought the topping gave it a slightly toffee-like effect

reviews.review_text: These were excellent tasting and so easy to make. I added a 1/2 tsp. of cinnamon to the crust and 3 whole graham crackers crumbled for a little extra crunch - I don't know that they were really needed. I lined my pan with foil  before spraying. After cooling the cookies I lifted the foil out and was able to cut them up nice and neatly with out any breakage and it made for easy cleanup.

These are superb! I made them exactly as directed, but in a cake pan. It looked elegant and smelled heavenly. I would probably call it a cheasecake tart. The crust is almost like shortbread and the dish melts in your mouth. It was extremely fast and easy and very impressive. I served it with fresh fruit and it was a big hit. This is definitely a keeper and is what i'll go to when i need something impressive and easy.

items.label: Double Chocolate Banana Muffins
items.name: Double Chocolate Banana Muffins
items.description: Make and share this Double Chocolate Banana Muffins recipe from Food.com.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the first six ingredients.
In a small bowl, combine bananas, oil and egg.
Stir into dry ingredients just until moistened.
Fold in chocolate chips.
Fill greased or paper lined muffin cups three fourths full.
Bake at 350 deg F for 20-25 minutes or until muffins test done.

reviews.review_text:
Whenever I see one of Charishma's recipes, I know it will be everything I'm hoping for! 

Baked up a batch of these last night, and by some miraculous act of willpower, I haven't eaten one yet! They sat there staring at me last night, taunting me with their fresh-from-the-oven chocolately goodness (yes Mel, they do just beg to be eaten, don't they?). I made them to take to my nephew's first b-day party so I resisted the urge to devour them, and instead, leaned over them and inhaled deeply. 

Prepared as directed, minus the choco chips because I didn't have any on hand and didn't feel like walking to the store. This lazy baker loaded them into 12 extra-deep muffin tins, and baked to perfection for exactly 25 minutes. I can hardly wait to get to the party tonight so I can bite into one of these gems!

attributes.source_text: my nephew's first b-day party
fresh-from-the-oven chocolately goodness

reviews.review_text:
This is a update, enjoy: I´ve now made this muffins twice because the yare so good!! The second time  they where even better and I frooze most of them so that I wouldn´t eat them all at once. and i just had one and it was just as moist  as when it was freshly baked. these ar ea definite winner in muffins heaven!!
I made the procedure even simpler this time:
egg,bananas, oil, sugar and salt goes in the food processor and is mixed until smooth.
flour,cacao, baking powder and soda is sieved and stirred together with chocolate chips in a bowl. then i just pour in the banana batter into the flour mix and fold til the mixture is smooth. soooo simple and sooooo good!!

If I can give higher than 5 stars I will. The muffin turned out great!!! I prefer to test the original recipe first before I make some changes to know which I have to. But due to our dietary restrictions, I have to cut back 1/4 cup the sugar and used brown granulated sugar and add 1/2 tsp of vanilla only. My son loves to bring 2 muffins at school and my husband requires only 1. The recipe yield 6 smaller muffins and 4 bigger ones. I posted pics for the comparison of the size, white and red muffin paper liner to see the size difference. Since I am a dark chocolate lover, I put some chunks on top and 1/2 cup only of semi sweet to balance the taste of banana and chocolate. The muffin so moist and not too sweet! I am so grateful to choose this recipe and now enjoying a very delicious muffin at the moment. More power to you and will try more of your recipes.

attributes.source_text: My son loves to bring 2 muffins at school
my husband requires only 1
The muffin so moist
not too sweet

reviews.review_text: LOVELY. I used 1/3 cup melted margarine instead of the oil and and a bit over 0.75 cup wholemeal flour instead of all white. Cut back the sugar a tiny bit just for the sake of it. I used frozen bananas - 2 large, 1 small. I really can't extol upon these enough; they are SO delicious. I ate one on the day and I was disappointed, but I always am with banana-y goods. Froze the rest and today defrosted one on the counter and warmed for 10 secs in the microwave. They are really just amazing - really chocolatey with a nice banana undercurrent. I used white chocolate chunks as I'd run out of milk chocolate bars. Works really well. Also, just wanted to throw this in, these are the first muffins I had that actually domed, so they look and taste awesome!

attributes.source_text: really chocolatey
with a nice banana undercurrent

reviews.review_text: These are absolutely amazing!  I've made them at least three times already and can't get enough!  :)  I have played around with the recipe a little to make them more healthy... white whole wheat flour for the all purpose flour, 1/2 c. honey for the sugar... And I have even chopped up a 72% dark chocolate bar to replace the chocolate chips... good for the chocolate lover and not quite as sweet.  Thanks for a great recipe that we love even more than banana bread! (Oh, I have also make mini loaves and just baked them a tad longer...)

Get a tall glass of milk ready!  These are wonderfully decadent breakfast muffins! I used King Arthur White Whole Wheat flour, I added a bit of Vietnamese cinnamon to the batter and I put them in a mini loaf pan. I sprayed the pan with Baker's Joy and they popped right out of the pan with very little to clean up. I also placed some extra mini chocolate chips on top of each loaf prior to baking--it made them look even more delightful.  This recipe made 9 heavenly mini loaves!  Thank you for taking the time to post this recipe!

attributes.source_text: breakfast muffins

reviews.review_text: Perfect!! I just had one of these hot out of the oven and they are scrumpdeliumptious! I'm trying to refrain from having a second and I don't think I'm going to able to last much longer. They came together easy and baked up perfectly. I made 6 large muffin tops and 6 small ones using cupcake papers. 25 minutes seemed to cook them to perfection. The only thing I did different was I added a little bit of vanilla and probably had a little bit of extra banana. Thank you so much for a fantastic recipe! We'll be making these often!

Okay, this was hilarious 'cause I obviously had never made these before so my stepdaughter flipped out when she saw them and at one... I said, 'how are they?" and she said, 'OMG, they are moist and amazing!!"  So there you have it, they are a huge hit!  I didn't even have enough time to take a picture of them to post on here lol Everybody sucked them down fast!!  The only changes I made were:  I used 1/2 cup of cocoa instead of 1/4 cup and because I didn't have chocolate chips, I used chopped up mini Tootsie Rolls and were they ever nice & gooey!  Thanks for this recipe!!

attributes.source_text: my stepdaughter flipped out when she saw them
they are moist and amazing
were they ever nice & gooey

reviews.review_text: I've had this recipe printed for the last 2 batches of ripe bananas and finally got to it.  They are like eating a chocolate-covered banana, and I ate mine warm which made it even better.  I might have added too much banana, I got distracted and thought I'd added enough but it would stir to get moist so I added an additional 2/3 C (I doubled the recipe).  So I either added enough or more.  I also got 24 from the double batch and they baked in 15 mins.  I thought they'd be a good breakfast but they're going to be dessert or treats.

attributes.source_text: They are like eating a chocolate-covered banana
they're going to be dessert or treats

reviews.review_text: My guy is a chocoholic, so even though I don't make these exactly to the recipe, I've been using this recipe as a base and they've turned out great every time.  I usually use 1/2 whole wheat and 1/2 white flour.  I also add some ground flax seeds, molasses, spiced applesauce and/or blueberries.  I also cut the sugar down and remove the oil.  I guess that changes it quite a bit, but I wanted to thank you for a great recipe.

I've been making these muffins for many years. And as a matter of fact, I'd made them this morning; except I used the regular size chocolate chips, (instead of the miniature choc chips) plus I like to top the batter with 4 chocolate chips each, before baking muffins in the oven. These are always sooo good. And with this recipe, I've found it makes 16 muffins, rather than 12. If you like choc, muffins, and bananas, then you will love these!!!

attributes.source_text: If you like choc, muffins, and bananas, then you will love these
If you like choc, muffins, and bananas, then you will love these

reviews.review_text: These muffins are EXCELLENT---MOIST and FLAVORFUL!!!  We loved them.  I did make a few changes, such as using only one cup of flour and adding 1/2 cup of rolled oats.  I also cut the sugar in half and cut the oil in half and replaced the other half with applesauce.  I did not use the chocolate chips, but instead put in diced dried plums.  I added some vanilla, too.  I also did as one reviewer suggested and put all liquid ingredients in the blender.  I will definitely make this again.

attributes.source_text: MOIST and FLAVORFUL

reviews.review_text: Yummmmm,I made these this morning and I think there is maybe 1 left from 12 muffins? <br/>yes, we are a bunch of chocolate lovin' pigs and we know it! I used 4 badly spotted banana's because I hate wasting food,and I only had about 3/4 of a cup of regular sized semi sweet choc chips so I used those,otherwise followed recipe and everyone loved them.Thanks for a new "get rid of those icky looking bananas" recipe;)

As many have stated before me, these are absolutely delicious. You can taste the banana and yet they are so chocolately. I followed the recipe except I only had about 1/3 cup of miniature chips, so I subbed the rest with regular chips that I chopped a little. I had to have one immediately when they were done, they smelled so wonderful. I used an ice cream scoop to get even size muffins and got 17 muffins that baked in 18 minutes. I can't wait to have one with my morning coffee. Thanks for sharing.

attributes.source_text: You can taste the banana
they are so chocolately

reviews.review_text: Have made these twice...Absolutely delicious! I didn't have any miniature semisweet chips, so I used five Dove brand "Promise" DARK chocolate candybars (about 25 individual squares), chopped down to make 1 cup. Some of the chocolate flaked off into smaller pieces, but I just threw it all in the bowl. When they were gone, I said my only mistake was not doubling the recipe. My family said next time I should "quadruple" it!

attributes.source_text: My family said next time I should "quadruple" it!

reviews.review_text: Satisfied that chocolate craving very nicely!  I added 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract with the wet ingredients and only used 1/2 cup of the mini chips.  They were perfectly balanced between chocolate and banana flavors.  Divided the batter between 10 muffin cups and they baked up with that lovely mushroom shaped top. (I think 1/3 cup chopped up walnuts would be a nice addition.  Will try that next time, and there definitely will be a next time!) Thanks so much for sharing your recipe, Charishma!

attributes.source_text: Satisfied that chocolate craving very nicely!
perfectly balanced between chocolate and banana flavors

reviews.review_text: Really great muffins. I got 14 muffins from the batter. I was going to make them jumbo but I made standard muffins instead and I'm glad I did because they're very rich and chocolatey. (But that's a good thing ;) ) They are a little sweet though so I think next time I'd cut back on the sugar. The bananas and chocolate go so well together. They turned out nice and moist and they're wounderful fresh from the oven. I'd make these again. Thank's for sharing!

attributes.source_text: they're very rich
very rich and chocolatey
They turned out nice and moist

reviews.review_text: WOW!  What a great flavor combination!  This is a terrific recipe.  It was a big hit in our house today.  The only thing I did differently was to skimp on the sugar a little (I usually do), used about 1/4 cup chocolate chips less, and added vanilla.  Instead of muffins, I made 2 small loaves.  They are absolutely delicious and the smell while baking is unbelievable.  Most definitely will make this recipe again.

wow!  chocolate-y banana-y goooodness!  had one out of the oven last night cause i could hardly stand it anymore smelling the cocoa fill the house and it was soooo melty and yummy.,.. had another one for breakfast because they're staring right at me on the counter as i was making my coffee saying "eat me now, who cares about a healthy breakfast" and they are even better today!  as banana flavoured desserts usually are better the next day.... ooooh so gooooood!  thank you :)

banana flavoured desserts usually are better the next day

reviews.review_text: i was craving for something with chocolate... i have tried many others chocolate muffins recipes but there's NO OTHER that tastes like this. these muffins are the best chocolate muffins i've ever tried (and i can't wait to add the chocolate chips since i didn't have any the first time). i'm so excited that this recipe turned out this good... finally i've found the perfect chocolate muffins recipe. thanks a bunch!

attributes.source_text: craving for something with chocolate

items.label: Pumpkin Muffins
items.name: Pumpkin Muffins
items.description: Make and share this Pumpkin Muffins recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Blend pumpkin, eggs, water, and shortening in large bowl.
Sift together remaining ingredients and add to pumpkin mixture.
Fill greased muffin tins about 3/4 full.
Bake at 350 degrees about 30 minutes or until set when touched.

reviews.review_text: I just tried these Muffins today  and they are Great!    ( I added a 1/4 cup of applesauce and  a 1/4 cup of the canola oil instead of just the canola Oil in the recipe to try it out.). , and the sugar I used was 1 cup of white sugar and  1/2 cup of brown sugar.  Then I added some  dried Cranberries  and Golden Raisins  (after  plumping them up in a bit of water in the microwave and then draining). I use the large  Muffin -cup pans and got 7 large muffins . I sprinkled a bit of  cinnamon sugar on the  top before baking.(  may try a crumb topping on the next ones   too as I often do on muffins ).. They turned out great and so moist and spiced just right  ! YUM ! Thank you for sharing your recipe with us!  This will become one of my favorite recipes in my recipe box!

attributes.source_text: so moist
spiced just right

reviews.review_text: These are FANTASTIC!! I was having a pregnancy craving :) for something with pumpkin and really wanted to use my filling I had on hand. This was perfect. I 1.5x the recipe so I could use all 15oz of the can (no point to me otherwise) and it was the perfect proportions. I did some substitutions I felt important. I did 1 stick organic butter plus 1/4 cup coconut oil instead of shortening. I use 2 cups dehydrated cane juice and 1/4 cup agave instead of the sugar. And I didn't have cloves so left them out. This made 29 muffins (from regular cupcake tins). And 30 minutes was perfect. I will definitely be making these again!

I doubled the recipe to use a whole 15oz can of pumpkin, and made a couple alterations - 1 cup of brown sugar in with the pumpkin and then 1 cup of white sugar with the flour (instead of 3 cups total), 3 eggs instead of 4, 1/2 cup applesauce plus 1/2 cup oil, and a little ww flour.  made 24 perfectly sized muffins (not the huge ones) which baked in about 25 minutes, and they are moist, nicely sweet, and delicious!  I will definitely make them again but likely with more spices, maybe raisins, or even streusel on top if I am feeling decadent.  Thank you!

attributes.source_text: they are moist
nicely sweet

reviews.review_text: I'm adding yet another 5 star review! These muffins were moist and delicious. I did make some modifications to make them more diet-friendly. I substituted applesauce for the oil, used egg whites instead of whole eggs and used 1/2 Splenda and 1/2 sugar. I forgot to add the water but it didn't affect the recipe. I also used 1/2 wheat and 1/2 white flour and added 1/3 cup of ground flaxseed. These made 6 Texas-sized muffins. I will certainly make these again--thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: These muffins were moist

reviews.review_text: Mmmmmm, these muffins were great!!! I say were because we ate them all already :) I reduced the sugar to 1 cup, used 1 1/4 cups all purpose and 1/2 cup whole wheat flour, and used 1/4 cup apple sauce, 1/4 melted coconut oil (in place of shortening). I got 48 mini muffins, baked them for 20 mins and used a cream cheese icing to top them. My family went crazy for them!! I'm not a huge pumpkin fan, but I thought they were really yummy too. I'll be making these again, probably today :) Thanks for a great recipe.

attributes.source_text: My family went crazy for them

reviews.review_text: These are absolutely amazing!  I made them to take with us skiing tomorrow, and I will now have to make batch #2 cause 6 are already gone and one more has disappeared every time I enter the kitchen.   I didn't have any shortening and only had less than a 1/4 cup of oil in the house so I made up the rest with applesauce and they were still incredibly moist.  The only other thing I had to change was that I didn't have any nutmeg or cloves so I used pumpkin pie spice (along with the requested amounts of cinnamon and ginger) and it worked perfect.  Moist,light (so little fat!!) and perfectly spiced.   This one goes to the top of my muffin recipes.  Thanks for a DELICIOUS recipe!

attributes.source_text: they were still incredibly moist
Moist,light (so little fat!!)
Moist,light (so little fat!!)
perfectly spiced

reviews.review_text: These are awesome!  My kids are gobbling them up.  I added a tiny bit of nutmeg to the recipe but otherwise followed it exactly.  For the kids I made mini muffins and for us I made big texas ones that I added walnuts & brown sugar to the tops (next time I think I'll have to also put butter on the nuts as the brown sugar just crumbles).  They all came out perfect and this will be The recipe I come back to again and again for pumpkin muffins!    I have been trying to copy the Honey Bear Bakery pumpkin muffins for years (in Seattle) and this is the first recipe to come very close... just have to perfect the walnut topping.

attributes.source_text: My kids are gobbling them up

reviews.review_text: These were wonderful! I doubled the recipe and used 2 c. sugar (they were still plenty sweet). I also didn't have shortening on hand, but used canola oil in its place with great results. They were moist and rose up nice. Doubling the recipe (using the entirety of the 15oz can of pumpkin) and cutting back on the sugar yielded a very nice Bundt size pan of bread (to which I added raisins) & 12 large muffins. The flavors were wonderful. My DD ate hers with whipped cream piped on top, they were delicious. I might even try an addition of cranberries next time! Thanks for sharing, these will be a staple as we roll into fall!<br/>Update: I had some pomegranates & pumpkins  to use & was inspired by recipe #197372. I knew this recipe was a winner, so I combined the 2 using this & stirred  1 c. Pomegranate seeds into the dry ingredients before stirring into the wet. items.label: Crazy Crust Pizza
items.name: Crazy Crust Pizza
items.description: Whenever you need pizza quick, this is the recipe to go for! It is not a traditional yeast dough crust...it actually starts out with a batter that turns into a crust. It is extremely easy to prepare, very good and you could probably have it done and on your table before the pizza parlor could :)
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Grease and flour a pizza pan or 10 x 15 baking sheet (with sides).
Combine flour, salt, oregano, pepper, eggs and milk and mix well.
Pour batter in pan and tilt pan around until bottom of pan is evenly coated.
Sprinkle the cooked meat, onions and mushrooms over the batter.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Remove from oven and drizzle on pizza sauce.
Sprinkle evenly with cheese.
Bake for about 5 more minutes, or until cheese is bubbling.
Slice and serve!

reviews.review_text: I did the math on this recipe if one slice is a serving the calories are wrong. LOL This recipe has about 700 calories for the whole crust. Which isn't bad for pizza crust at all. I followed the recipe exactly although I prebaked my crust in a 9x13 pan for 8 minutes took it out topped it with green and red peppers, pepperoni, onions and cheese. Then I cooked it for 10 more minutes. In my opinion It was kind of soggy, but that is not a deal breaker I cut it in half and rolled the half up and ate it as a pizza wrap. I think this is a very good crust. I will definitely will be making this again ( I eat pizza every day. My lunch was about 700 calories which is an excellent lunch for me because I only eat pizza and ramen noodles and I have lost over 50lbs since May) I really like this crust. I have to see if I have a pizza stone, because someone said it made it crispy. We will see GREAT RECIPE.

attributes.source_text: My lunch was about 700 calories

reviews.review_text:
This was very easy and quick.  I have a problem with the 2 bake times, however.  I'm thinking the first 20 minutes might be too long and the last 5 minutes isn't long enough.  I say this because the crust was plenty done after 20 minutes but then I had to put it BACK in the oven for the last 5 minutes to melt the cheese but then the cheese barely had a chance to melt.  Also, the sauce didn't get very hot in those crucial 5 minutes and it was a little "saucy" in some spots.  But I WILL make this again!  I will probably try adjusting these cook times to see what works for me. It was a fun recipe to make and totally unique.  I love a "quickie" meal!
Thanks Karen!

I was skeptical that this could be any good, especially after putting the uncooked batter in the oven,  but I was so wrong. It tasted great to me. We did a veggie pizza and after reading some of the other reviews I decided to par-bake the crust for 5 mins before putting the veggies on, cooked for 20 mins, topped with 1 cup of homemade thick sauce and baked about another 10 mins. I baked mine on a foil lined tin and wont use foil next time. The edges were nice and crisp, but the center was still a little soft . It's not pizza crust, but with the toppings it has all the flavors and you can eat it like pizza. I love that I didn't feel grossly full after eating three slices. Thanks for sharing this fun recipe, I'll be making it again.

attributes.source_text: The edges were nice and crisp

reviews.review_text: Oh boy, was I pleasantly surprised. Never make pizza at home because I don't want to mess w/the crust. I used 1/4 c of wheat flour instead of all white flour, added fresh basil in the crust. Only had egg beaters, so I had to use those in place of the eggs. The sky is the limit on ingredients here. I sauted some onions and green and red bell peppers along with a can of mushrooms. My meat was turkey bacon and pepperoni. I made my own pizza sauce from a can of tomato sauce and topped it with an italian cheese blend. I served it with a sprinkle of crushed red pepper flakes and parmesean. My dh then adds his favorite topping of worchestershire (salsa ingles s/p?) Thanks for this keeper. I will be passing this along to my pizza loving friends.

attributes.source_text: My dh then adds his favorite topping

reviews.review_text: I have tried some of the other Crazy Crust Pizza on this site, but we actually liked this recipe better as the dough doesn't fill you up on one slice of pizza.  Next time, I would take the comment of Cajun Baby and maybe pour the dough onto a hot pizza stone because once cooked up, the middle does stays a little doughy, especially if you have gone a little overboard with the toppings (like we all do!!)  I used SAMS_Club's Ultimate Pizza Sauce (114392) and used 6 small fresh mozzarella balls and about 6 fresh mushrooms, sliced.  I don't do fresh onions or garlic very well well, so I used about 1 cup of onions and 3 garlic minced, sauteed into Italian sausage.  DH and I really enjoyed it, but being just the two of us, I am wondering if I could cut the recipe in half.  The crust seems pretty flexable, so next time I will cut the recipe in half, top it with shredded chicken, pizza sauce, mushrooms and cheese...all done on a pizza stone.  Thanks for the posting and the idea.

attributes.source_text: The crust seems pretty flexable
DH and I really enjoyed it

reviews.review_text: This recipe was a fantastic starting point. I used half reg flour, half whole wheat flour and added 1/2 tsp of baking powder and 1 tsp of garlic powder to the recipe. Living at 5600ft I also added 6 minutes to the total cooking time. I used an 8"x11" pan sprayed with Pam. I also did not use sauce as I made a "Greek" version with the ground beef, onion, one pkg of frozen spinach (cooked and pressed of all liquid), then instead of mozzarella I added chopped calamata olives and roughly 1 cup of French feta cheese. I tried adding sundried tomatoes but they got too crispy cooking for 20-ish minutes. Maybe I'll add them at the end next time. What a delicious dinner!!!

attributes.source_text: What a delicious dinner!!!
I made a "Greek" version

reviews.review_text: I really like this recipe; thanks for sharing! When really hungry for 'normal' pizza, this probably won't cut it. But when trying to eat healthy and still wanting pizza, this is marvelous! The crust is thin and soft- not quite able to eat with your hands. I want to record my changes for when I make it again (I have made it twice this month): Cut the salt to 1/2 tsp in the crust. Bake the crust for 10-15 mins alone. Top partially-baked crust with 7oz. pizza sauce, shredded zucchini, shredded carrot, diced bell pepper, diced onion, diced sun-dried tomatoes, then the cheese and some turkey pepperoni. Bake for 10 mins before serving.

attributes.source_text: The crust is thin and soft
The crust is thin and soft

reviews.review_text: Just want to take a moment and defend the fact that this IS in fact a "under 400 calorie" recipe. As MOST cooks know, a recipe is not designed for 1 person to eat. This is a pizza, pizzas have 8 slices, each slice is considered a serving. In this recipe, each slice is 238 calories (per serving) so it is in fact under 400 calories. I know, most people eat more then 1 slice, I know I do. But none the less, still healthier then ANY pizza you'll buy or order. Eat smart throughout the day and by dinner time, 3 slices won't break the bank :-)

This worked out really well for us. I did change the topping ingredients. I used chunks of chicken I marinated in a herb and garlic dressing then cooked. I also cooked some onion slices, and added some thinly sliced tomato. I put these 3 ingredients on the crust for the first 20 mins bake. Then I added chopped up fresh basil, some Parmesan cheese, then the 2 cups of mozzarella. cooked another 5-7 mins... it was really good... very mild in flavor so may not be to everyones taste. You could always add your own spices and such to 'zing' it up a bit. I've added a photo of the finished result.

attributes.source_text: very mild in flavor

reviews.review_text: I was really looking forward to making recipe and tonight I finally got to make it, but the crust was too eggy and not at all like a crust for me. I would cut it down to only one egg. I also followed another reviewer's suggestion and sprayed my pan and then used corn meal instead of flour.. but the crust practically GLUED itself to the pan. I've never had anything get that stuck to a pan before! So after dinner I ended up with half the whole crust still stuck on there and the poor pan's soaking as I type this. I probably won't try this one again till I get a silpat! But other than the egginess in the crust, I really do love this pizza. I really love how easily it all came together and the flavours were to die for. I'm still craving some!

Great recipe, especially for someone like me who lives alone.  I make 1/2 of the recipe and bake it in a cornmeal sprinkled pie plate.  And as far as toppings, anything goes.  I've made completely without any kind of meat as well as with the beef and/or pepperoni.  I especially love it with only greens, mushrooms, and grape tomatoes.  I usually eat 1/2 of it, wrap the rest in plastic wrap and heat it the next day for lunch.       <br/><br/>I really like this recipe.  It satisfies my pizza cravings without adding so many calories.

I didn't add sausage because it isn't our thing.  I did prebake the crust as other suggested for about 8 min then added my sauce, toppings and cheese.  Then baked for another 15 min at least.    Make sure you leave a nice amount of crust around the edges because it gets crispy and so tasty.     Thanks for sharing the recipe.!

reviews.review_text: I wanted to make a breakfast pizza but I  didn't have any crust, quick or ready made... and no yeast, so my choices were limited... so, early in the morning I found your recipe, was extremely skeptical but got high praises. I did omit the oregano for the breakfast pizza, pre-baked it for 10 minutes at 350 and then added country gravy, bacon, sausage and scrambled eggs and cheese.. and WOW! reviews.review_text: Talk about an easy family meal.  I agree that as other said, the crust is different and definitely not like regular pizza crust - but that's why the name is 'crazy' crust.  The crust has a texture like maybe a thick crepe, so expect that going into it. I was looking for a fast meal to use up a pound of ground sirloin I had thawed out.  This worked great as it used up many other things I had on hand...a half a jar of spaghetti sauce, mushrooms that were on their way out, cheese I had too much of. reviews.review_text: I was another skeptic but my DH loved loved loved this pizza!!  I baked the crust alone with no toppings for 20 minutes.  Then I added italian sausage, olives, onions, and colby jack cheese.  Then I baked it another 23-30 minutes because I was trying to get all the edges golden brown. I made my own spaghetti sauce by mixing a can of tomato sauce with a bunch of italian herbs and it was perfect.  Will make this again and again.  Next up is a chicken BBQ pizza with this crazy crust!

reviews.review_text: This was pleasantly surprising.  I tried it because I was intrigued by the concept, and I wasn't disappointed. I will likely keep this recipe and use it when we decide we want pizza but I don't have time to put a crust together. Wasn't sure how it would be, because honestly, it just seemed too easy. While it's not perhaps quite as good as the pizza crust I make with yeast, it is not very far off. Still has the fresh homemade taste. It was a hit with my teenage daughter and friends. I used turkey Italian Sausage and made everything else pretty much as directed. The beauty of course is that this quick, easy and exceptionally yummy pizza crust can be used with pretty much any toppings a person could come up with. Will be making this often!

I used italian sausage and Ragu jarred pizza sauce.  My husband said next time to use hamburger and a different pizza sauce.  Stil in the end we decided it was a keeper!  Thanks for this easy and great pizza recipe!

It was gone instantly. It's nice not having thin sections of dough from not rolling out perfectly and the crust wasn't soggy anywhere. I could have cooked it a little in the oven before I topped it just to get the bottom crisper but it was still well cooked. Thanks for giving a busy mom a fast, easy healthy pizza recipe!!!!

items.label: Breakfast Casserole Supreme
items.name: Breakfast Casserole Supreme
items.description: Make and share this Breakfast Casserole Supreme recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Melt margarine and place in the bottom of 9\
baking pan.
Spread potatoes (still frozen is okay) in bottom of the pan.
Sprinkle chopped vegetables over potatoes.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Sprinkle meat over potatoes and vegetables.
Note: At this point you may continue or casserole may be refrigerated overnight.
Pour beaten eggs over potatoes.
Bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes.
Remove from oven and sprinkle cheese evenly over top.
Bake another 5-10 minutes or until cheese is hot and bubbly.
Remove from oven and let set for approximately 5 minutes.
Cut into 2.5\
squares and serve with a spatula. Enjoy.

reviews.review_text: We absolutely LOVE this! I've made it countless times since I found it on here about three years ago. Sometimes when I'm in a crunch for time and don't want to dice all of the veggies I will use the frozen onion and green pepper mix that you get at the grocery store. I've also drained canned tomatoes and used those in a rush too. It does taste best with fresh vegetables though. We are doing low carb now and I substitute cauliflower for the potatoes. It is just as delicious! I can probably say that I've cooked this recipe more than any other on this site. Thanks!

I make a similar recipe to this when the school I work at has breakfast potlucks for the teachers, with a few minor changes. Since I have to leave for work at 6:45 am, I do most of the prep work the night before, with cooking the sausage and draining the fat, then putting the sausage into a small roaster oven pan (I use a 6 quart roaster) with frozen hash browns and chopped onions. The next morning when I wake up, I scramble 2 1/2 dozen eggs in a mixing bowl with a little sour cream, salt and pepper, then pour it over the sausage, onion and potato mixture, letting it start baking in the roaster oven at 325 degrees while I shower and get dressed. After about 20 minutes in the roaster, I stir, add some shredded cheese, and let cook about 10 minutes more. When I get to work, I plug the roaster in set on warm, melt a little cheese on top, and let people help themselves - last time I made it for work, it served about 20 people. I had a lot of teachers asking for the recipe, and since normally our breakfast potlucks consist of mostly muffins, bagels and donuts, eggs were a really nice change.

attributes.source_text: breakfast potlucks
breakfast potlucks
I had a lot of teachers asking for the recipe

reviews.review_text: This was very good. I was looking for a b'fast casserole to serve at a work function, so I needed a way to keep it hot.  I had seen another crockpot casserole on another site, but liked this one better, so wound up combining the two.  Here's what I did... I was feeding a crowd, so I increased the recipe a bit (32oz frozen hashbrowns). In the greased crockpot insert, I layered the hashbrowns, then onion, green bell pepper, tomato, salt/pepper over all that, then the crumbled cooked sausage, then cheese.  I made 3 layers of that, ending with the cheese on top. The eggs I increased to 15 due to the additional hashbrowns, 1/3 C milk, 1/4 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper, pinch of baking powder.  Poured that carefully over the layers. Cooked on low for 6-8 hours. I was very pleased with the result, & it was a crowd pleaser for sure!  Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: a b'fast casserole to serve at a work function
to serve at a work function

reviews.review_text: This is an easy-to-make and filling dish. I put all the ingredients together in the morning immediately before baking it.  I chose cooked crumbled breakfast sausage, and the only change I made was using melted butter, since I don't keep margarine on hand.  We were a little disappointed when the hash brown potatoes were soggy and didn't have much flavor. Overall, it was tasty enough with more salt and served with salsa.  Since there was just two of us, I cut the remaining casserole into 3-inch squares and put them in baggies and froze them.  When we wanted a couple for breakfast, we thawed them in the fridge overnight, and in the morning put them into a non-stick skillet with some oil over a medium-high to high flame and browned the bottom, turned the heat down, put a lid on the pan to heat the squares through and melt the cheese.  That worked well! Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: When we wanted a couple for breakfast

reviews.review_text: We rarely give five stars, but this one is worth it.  It's Mothers' Day and we wanted something special to make at home, because on this holiday, restaurants are jammed with people who do not know how to order.  So we chilled a bottle of Mumm's and baked this one.  It was superb!  I added a light dusting of Creole seasoning and a dash of garlic powder before baking.  It took a bit more than the recommended baking time, but finally did set up solidly.  It was well worth the effort.  I used Canadian bacon for the meat.  Gramma, you did a fine job on this one.

attributes.source_text: It's Mothers' Day and we wanted something special to make at home
finally did set up solidly

reviews.review_text: I absolutely love this recipe! I make it every year for Christmas breakfast. It tastes wonderful, and I love that I can prepare most of it the night before. I use one pound of Jimmy Dean sage sausage, cooked. Instead of seasoning the potatoes, I add seasoning salt to my eggs as I’m beating them, then pour over the top for a consistent flavor. This recipe is so versatile! I sometimes mix things up using chopped red, orange, and green bell peppers. Even frozen pre-chopped onions work great during the busy Christmas season. I’ve enjoyed making this with hash browns, but it also works with potatoes o’brien (with the chopped veggies already added). This is a great crowd pleaser and is delicious! Thanks for a recipe that our family will enjoy for years to come.

attributes.source_text: I make it every year for Christmas breakfast
for Christmas breakfast

reviews.review_text: I must have done something wrong, given such positive reviews from others.  It looked so pretty coming out of the oven.  I let it set for about 10 min. prior to serving.  Then I cut into it and it was a watery mess at the bottom.  When I came back to get another serving, it was sitting in even more water.  I made sure my tomatoes were drained well (I used canned petite diced) I don't know what else could have done it.  I think it had potential, but given the mess I had, I'm not sure if I'll try it again.

This was WONDERFUL! I used smoked ham. Instead of the chopped tomatoes, I used a can of diced tomatoes with green chilies (drained), a 4 cheese blend instead of the straight cheddar and omitted the green peppers just because I didn't have any. I did the overnight thing and it turned out perfect. The tomatoes with green chilies gave it a nice kick. It's just Hubby and me, so I was able to freeze part in individual baggies for convenient, microwave breakfasts throughout the week for both of us. Thanks so much for sharing. I can't wait to try it again with sausage and bacon!

attributes.source_text: gave it a nice kick
microwave breakfasts throughout the week

I used the Hashbrowns that had the onions and peppers already in it, added the extra fresh onion and left out the pepper and used combination of bacon and diced ham for the meat. I used smoked ham, but next time I think I'll try bulk sausage.  I think a spicy version with jalapeno, some cumin, and hot sauce would also be excellent.  This also reheated well so you could even bake ahead of time and simply reheat in the morning.  Thanks for the great recipe!

attributes.source_text: I made this for the in-laws when they came to visit and everyone liked it a lot

reviews.review_text: I made this for Christmas morning with chorizo, and then made a smaller version with ham, green peppers, mushrooms, and green onions for just the two of us today for New Years Day. Both versions were very tasty! I keep wanting to try it in the crockpot, but haven't yet lol. Today I took the leftovers , cut them into strips and folded them into tortillas, wrapped  deli wrap and put them in the freezer. We will enjoy them for quick work breakfasts!

I used the frozen hash browns that already have the onions and great and red bell peppers diced and mixed in. This made it REALLY easy! Although I realized I didn't have 6 eggs- made it with 4. Was still delicious. I baked it for longer than specified, and even so the peppers and onions were crisp-tender, which I thought we wouldn't like. But we did! Great flavor! (Oh, and I added about 1/2 tsp. chipotle seasoning and 1/4 tsp. smoked paprika to the eggs.)

This is a very flavorful breakfast casserole chocked full of lots of wonderful vegetables and I used some leftover ham from our Christmas dinner.  The only thing lacking in this recipe is salt and pepper which is easy enough to remedy. items.label: Blue Ridge Mountains Chocolate Chip Cookies
items.name: Blue Ridge Mountains Chocolate Chip Cookies
keywords: c("Chocolate Chip Cookies", "Dessert", "Cookie & Brownie", "Kid Friendly", "Sweet", "< 30 Mins", "For Large Groups", "Easy")
items.description: These cookies have been served for over 75 years in the quiet village of Orkney Springs, VA. We have stayed in this  retreat center called Shrine Mont where people come for rest, devotion, and fellowship. A couple of things set these cookies apart: butter and shortening ensure a thick cookie, soft in the middle, with a touch of almond extract.
instructions: Note: The recipe initially calls for 2 1/2 cups flour, but with the added note if you want them more softer and rounder cookie to add 1/4 cup flour. I add the 1/4 cup making it 2 3/4 cups total.
Cream shortening, butter, sugars, then eggs and vanilla and almond extracts.
Blend dry ingredients and add to mixture.
Stir in Chocolate chips.

Drop by large tablespoons (I use cookie scoop) onto ungreased cookie sheet, leaving 2-inches room in between to allow cookies to spread. I press down lightly with a measuring cup to bake more uniform cookies).
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes until lightly brown.
Makes 2-3 dozen cookies depending on size.

reviews.review_text:
These are really yummy! I made them twice, once with the original recipe, and once with the extra flour.

ORIGINAL RECIPE: These didn't 'spread out' as much as I'd hoped... but they were really good. The dough was smelling very almond extract-y, but once the cookies were baked I could tell I would have missed the almond if it wasn't there.

EXTRA FLOUR: Wasn't much different from the original... didn't spread out any more/less... and tasted the same. I completely forgot I had no brown sugar left... so I used all white sugar with a tsp molasses. I only used 1 cup CC just to cut down on the sugar, and because I made smaller cookies anyways it was fine (2 tsp icecream scoop, baked 8-9 minutes).

My opinion is just to use the regular recipe because there wasn't an overall noticeable difference to use your flour for. I also only used margerine because I had no butter at the time, and never use shortening. Sorry if you feel this would have affected the cookies... but I rated 5 stars so it shouldn't be a problem? :) Thanks for the great recipe, will be using again!

items.label: Caesar Pork Chops
items.name: Caesar Pork Chops
items.description: I am always looking for new and delicious ways to prepare pork chops.  These are delicious, easy to put together and use things that are in most people's pantries.  A real family pleaser.  Serve with rice pilaf and a green vegetable.
instructions: Heat oven to 375*F.  Spray a 12 X 8 inch glass baking dish with cooking spray.
In pie pan or shallow dish, mix flour and Italian seasoning.  Pour dressing into another pie pan or shallow dish.
Coat both sides of each pork chop with the flour mixture; dip into dressing, coating both sides well.  Place in baking dish.  Sprinkle with cheese. Discard any remaining flour and dressing.
Bake uncovered, 35 to 40 minutes or until pork is no longer pink in center.

reviews.review_text: I didnt follow the recipe as much as the method.  I had 1 inch boneless pork loin chops. I also had snap peas and match stick carrots I wanted to use up so asian was the way I wanted to go. I floured my chops and the flour was seasoned with an asian seasoning (premade) that had garlic, ginger, black and white sesame seeds in it. I used a high quality commercial made ginger sesame salad dressing in lieu of the ceasar and topped it with additional asian seasoning. I baked at 375 in a convection oven for 35 minutes. I used the fat/juice that was off the pork chops to saute the peas and carrots. This was delicious! It's all about the method IMO. My husband commented that the pork was like butter and these chops were VERY lean to begin with making them hard to cook sometimes without drying out! I will use this method with other flavor combos!!!!

reviews.review_text: This was just wonderful! I made changes by adding garlic powder to the flour mixture and I also sprinkled some on the chops along with salt and pepper. I then hit each chop with a meat mallet, tossed them in flour, brushed on some Ken's Creamy Caesar Dressing, threw some baby portabella mushrooms in the pan, and put it in the oven. After about ten minutes (because I forgot lol) I added grated Parmesan cheese and let them finish cooking. After I took the pan out of the oven I threw on some chopped fresh parsley and oregano. Really, it was divine. I think next time I will sprinkle some lemon juice on top before serving and I can't wait to try this recipe with chicken, mushrooms, and broccoli. Honestly, I used some really cheapo blade steaks and they came outt delicious and perfectly tender. This recipe is so quick, simple, and awesome that it can't help but be a part of my regular rotation. Thanks Tasty Tidbits. This one's a serious keeper!

reviews.review_text: I loved this- and I even messed up following the simple directions! It was so quick to make with just a few ingrediants. I doubled the recipe and used 8 boneless pork loin chops and used ranch dressing instead of caesar. I was worried that it might be a little bland, so I added some dry Italian dressing mix (maby 1-2 tsp?) and 1 1/2-2 tsp Italian seasoning to the flour. I got mixed up on the directions, I first generously coated both sides of the pork chops in ranch and THEN coated them in the flour mixture. I baked them for about 35 minutes and when I took them out I realized I forgot to put the cheese on top. I was out of parmesan, so I sprinkled a shredded mozzarella pizza blend on top and put it back in the oven for about 2-3 minutes so it could melt. I served it with green beans & stuffing and we all cleaned our plates. My youngest even had seconds! This is definitely going in our menu rotation!

reviews.review_text: Reading through a lot of the reviews, I find it strange that some people would make a recipe when they obviously are not very keen on the ingredients, or they make substantial changes -- and then they say they didn't like it much! We like these flavours, and the recipe is so quick and easy. I also wonder if cooks who were not happy with the results really used real Parmesan and a good creamy Caesar salad dressing? I only added a very little extra seasoning-with-a-bite (dry Piquante Pepper seasoning/Peppadew) to the Italian herbs, but used the recipe unchanged. My chops were nicely cooked after 25 - 30 minutes, but cooking times depend so much on the different ovens. The flavour was great -- mild but tasty. I did not use loin chops (terrified of their notorious "dryness"), but a chop cut which had some marbling running through them. So they were juicy. I should add we don't mind a little fat at all ... I'm pleased to see that some doctors and dieticians are coming round to the idea that a little animal fat (used for 1,000's of years, after all!) are not at all bad for us!! Thanks, Marie-Alice, for a recipe I'll use again. Should be great with chicken too.
