items.description: Make and share this Cube Steak and Gravy (Crock Pot) recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Salt and pepper the steak to your liking, then dredge in the flour.
Fry steak until brown and place in crock pot.
Add water, soup, and gravy mix.
Cover and cook on low 6 to 8 hours.
Serve with mashed potatoes or rice.

reviews.review_text: Everyone in our house loved the recipe. I made only a few changes to it. It being my first time making this meal and reading a lot say the meat was mush I kept a check on it with a fork and found that in my crock pot 4 1/2 hours on low worked great. The meat wasn't mush and you could cut it easily with a fork. I did quarter a big onion and added it at the beginning of the cooking. After I noticed my meat getting about done I added a can of mushrooms. The gravy was really good. I fried pieces of bread and we topped the bread with the remaining gravy. We will definitely be having this again. Thanks for sharing the recipe.

attributes.source_text: The meat wasn't mush
you could cut it easily with a fork

reviews.review_text: A+++++Dish! My husband loves this.  I sent it for lunch today. This is my story: I have been trying to pack him a hearty lunch because he works outside and it is cheaper and healthier.  So last night I did not get home until about 11:45p.m. and my husband let's go to bed it's late it took me five minutes to salt,pepper, flour I also cut up a half onion and saute until brown and throw everything in the crock pot.  A life saver, my husband said he didn't get a chance to taste this morning and he was worried because it literally took me five minutes to do everything.  He was in love and he wants more for tomorrow, he didn't pack enough and I did not have time to make rice or mashed potatoes(I make these from scratch).  Super easy recipe.

attributes.source_text: My husband loves this
I sent it for lunch today
He was in love and he wants more for tomorrow

reviews.review_text: Yes, this recipe is bland IF you do not make a few changes.  Reading some of the complaints, I made a few simple modifications and it really made this delicious.  First and foremost, to prevent a mushy steak, I cooked it for a total of 3.5 hours (high for 1.5 hours and low for 2).  The texture was perfect as I like a little chew to my meat.  Like many others I put salt, pepper and garlic powder on the steaks before dredging in flour.  To the soup/gravy mixture I added a a generous pinch of salt, couple shakes of Worcestershire, a clove of crushed garlic and a rough chopped onion.  It was delicious.

attributes.source_text: I like a little chew to my meat

reviews.review_text: This was so easy to put together and turned out really nice and tender. I hadn't planned ahead, so my cube steaks were frozen so I just put them in the crock pot, added the soups and water and turned the crock pot on. When they were cooked, I pulled the steaks out and thickened the liquid in the crock with flour and seasonings. This worked out well. Since there's only 2 of us, I have frozen the gravy and remaining cube steaks for another meal. Than you for posting this recipe. I'll make it again for sure.

attributes.source_text: turned out really nice and tender

reviews.review_text: I am really shocked out of 48 reviews no one commented on the cook time! 6-8 hours on low for pre-browned cubed steak (it is almost pourous afterall)! It was almost done before it was cooked for 7 hours, My DS's complained they couldn't even spear it with their fork, it broke up into a crumbled/hamburger consistency, and no my crockpot doesn't need to be replaced, The sauce we found to be bland, and I used cream of mushroom soup with roasted garlic. I would recommend that it be cooked 3-4 hours on low. My DH comment-Well it's still meat, just not a steak.

Quick and easy too...tasted even better than that!  Came home from work and it smelled devine.  Instant mashed potatoes with chives and some green beans and supper was another success.  I doubled it and used a can of cream of chicken and one of cream of celery ( i hate mushrooms).  Was perfect for me but made the mistake of telling the family that is is supposed to be made with mushroom soup and so now I will have to make again the correct way.  For them I will also add a can or two of mushrooms.  Thanks for putting this recipe in my cookbook!

This is delightful! I also accidentally used a different mix--brown gravy mix as opposed to the onion, but it tasted wonderful nonetheless. I've made recipes combining cream of mushroom soup with onion soup mix, and I think I like this one better! The gravy had wonderful flavor, and the cube steaks were very tender. I did do a few things differently--I browned the steaks in a large skillet with some sliced fresh mushrooms, foregoing the crock pot only because I had lots of dishes already, and didn't want to make more. Lol  While they were browning, I combined the soup with the gravy mix and water, and upon noticing it wasn't onion gravy, added a few tablespoons of dried minced onions. When the steaks were browned, I poured the gravy mixture into the skillet, covered it, set it to "simmer", and then let it do its thing for about 2 hours. The result was yummy! I also only had a pound of cube steaks, but prepared and used the entire amount of gravy. (Recommended.) Or, if you do have the two pounds, you may want to double the sauce if you're serving with mashed potatoes, noodles, dumplings, or fries, etc. I served ours with American cheese and potato pierogies, ladling the luscious gravy over all. But we could have used even more, since as it cooks, the gravy tends to thicken, and reduce to some extent. Next time I'll try it with the onion gravy mix, and transfer the cube steaks to the crock pot. Thank you Southern Chef, for sharing your recipe! This is a definite keeper!

attributes.source_text: the cube steaks were very tender
the gravy tends to thicken

reviews.review_text: Loved this,of course it fell apart, its cube steak, thats what you want.  I browned the night before and put into the crock dish, with the fixings: did not find onion gravy so used onion soup mix and 2 cups home made beef bullion and 1 cup water( had about 3 pounds of beef).  Put chilled dish into crock on low in the morning so it had time to come up to temp and cook, left it for about 10 hours.  Very little thickening needed, served over egg noodles, great deep flavor, thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: of course it fell apart, its cube steak, thats what you want
great deep flavor

reviews.review_text: I am trying to cook real whole foods I did NOT use cream soup nor onion mix nor flour. .  I simply pour  2 cups of cold  water and sprinkled  3 TBS of cornstarch to the crock pot along with 4 large onions thinly sliced.  I only briefly stirred it   I was in time crunch so I  cooked on high for 2hrs 45 minutes..   The cube steak was incredibly tender yet firm enough to cut with a fork without falling apart.   The gravy was the perfect consistency .... because cornstarch rarely gets lumpy like flour.

attributes.source_text: The cube steak was incredibly tender
yet firm enough to cut with a fork without falling apart

reviews.review_text: This was wonderful!!!  I wanted a recipe that was similar to what my mother cooks for Sunday dinner.  She cooks her cube steak in a pan for several hours.  I do not have time to cook on top of the stove for several hours on a weekday, so I started looking for a crockpot cube steak recipe.  This was easy and had the same things in it that my mother's recipe included with the exception of the onion gravy mix.  I did not use onion gravy mix - I used onion soup mix and it was a WONDERFUL addition.  To me that is truly what made mine better than hers.  It was also so tender.  My husband loves my mother's recipe, but he said that mine topped hers - he even got seconds!!  I served it with NurseDi's Ranch Potatoes, and they were a delicious compliment to this dish.  Definitely a keeper!!

attributes.source_text: It was also so tender
he said that mine topped hers - he even got seconds

reviews.review_text: Very good & Very easy!!! Although I must confess my eyes were playing tricks on me and I used 1 package dry onion soup mix and 1 can of cream of onion soup instead of the listed ingredients. Oops! I also dusted the meat with pepper and garlic powder as I was browning and forgot the flour. I think I must have still been half-asleep. Anyhow, cooked it on high for 6 hours and it turned out great - plenty of flavorful gravy for mashed potatoes or noodles. Meat was fork-tender but not at the "mushy" stage. Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: Meat was fork-tender
not at the "mushy" stage

reviews.review_text: This recipe was fantastic! I needed a quick meal and I used the suggestions of Suzie#5 and did this on the stovetop! Fabulous and received rave reviews from the whole family! I did not have onion gravy but I mixed brown gravy & beef mushroom gravy mixes and it turned out great! 1/24: Made this again and added thinly sliced vidalia onions! Perfect served with mashed potatoes for the extra gravy.  Mushrooms would make a great addition (but unfortunately, DH doesn't like them). reviews.review_text: I have actually been making a variation of this recipe for over 40 years.  I season the meat, brown on both sides and add to the crock pot with cream of mushroom or cream of chicken soup, cut potatoes and green beans.  I cook on low for 8 hours and the meat just falls apart and melts in your mouth.  Served with a loaf of warm bread, it is the best all-in-one dish I have ever made.

items.label: Spicy Sweet Potatoes
items.name: Spicy Sweet Potatoes
items.description: Make and share this Spicy Sweet Potatoes recipe from Food.com.
instructions: In a zip-top plastic bag, toss potatoes and oil.
Combine remaining ingredients; add to bag; toss to coat.
Transfer to a greased 11x7 inch baking dish.
Bake, uncovered, at 400 degrees for 40-45 minutes or until potatoes are tender, stirring every 15 minutes.

reviews.review_text: These may have replaced candied sweet potatoes as my favorite way to eat sweet potato. Seriously. It's a nice warm heat that starts on the first exhale after your first bite and while it builds slightly it never leaves the realm of flavor and goes into pain or discomfort. It's a nice twist and I think would be really complimentary with other foods on a Thanksgiving plate. The warm would go well with the cranberry sauce/jelly instead of competing with it for sweet, for example. Seriously good. I highly recommend it. Next time I'll probably toss in some bacon crumbles afterwards just because, but it doesn't need anything in my opinion. (Picture is before I cooked them)

it never leaves the realm of flavor and goes into pain or discomfort

reviews.review_text: These were SO delicious!  I had 4 small sweet potatoes, so I used those and I think it was maybe 3 cups worth...and my husband and I ate them ALL!  I didn't have any cayenne, so I subbed with red pepper flakes.  I also added some freshly minced garlic and added it about 5 minutes before they were done.  Although mine cooked up in about 20 minutes...I think I cut my cubes much smaller than 1 inch.  But it was really great with the garlic!  MMMMM :)  I think I'll be making this often just for myself for lunch and what not for the upcoming winter :)  Thanks!!

attributes.source_text: my husband and I ate them ALL

reviews.review_text: The potatoes were very tender and subtly sweet (like the delicate natural sweetness in roasted carrots)with a hint of heat.  I baked these with skinless chicken breasts rolled in onion soup mix, chicken seasoning and paprika; these two dishes worked well together in the opinion of my husband and myself.  The only things I did differently included (aside from using the potatoes as a bed for my chicken) using 2 potatoes instead of 3 and also a more liberal usage of brown sugar.  I just like brown sugar.  Very, very good and quite easy.

reviews.review_text:
I was having a Thanksgiving-ful of European guests who do not have the sweet tooth for America's traditional marshmallow-y sweet potato dishes. I searched and searched through this site's "Sweet Potato" recipes until I came across this one; it read well and looked like it would be a nice addition to a ham dinner.

What a GREAT choice! Every single nugget of the spicy s.potato chunks were snapped up, and everyone requested the recipe! There were NO leftovers, (not even for snacks that night), so I ended up making these for the next 3 days, so our guests and family could have them with each meal.

Didn't change a thing; didn't need to! Wonderful addition to my permanent recipe collection.

Served it with the Copy-Cat Corn Souffle on this site and both got 5 star reviews. Thank you*THANK YOU for solving a dinner problem with such panache!

reviews.review_text: Made for Thanksgiving 2009.  I decided to try this sweet potato option because it was one of the lower-carb (considering it's sweet potatoes) options I made to help my diabetic father-in-law have more options on the table.  I ended up using 4 sweet potatoes and cubed them up smaller than 1-inch.  I did have to make some adjustments in the spices based on what I had on hand, personal preferences, and dietary restrictions.  I omitted the salt and and had to substitute additional chili powder for the cayenne (mother-in-law forgot to bring it).  I decided to add 1/4 tsp cinnamon and 1/4 tsp nutmeg to the spice mix as well.  I found that what worked best for me was to double the amount of the spice blend that I used, so what I ended up using was 4 tbsp brown sugar, 3 tsp chili powder, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, and 1/2 tsp nutmeg.  I prepared and roasted the potatoes (baked for about an hour) the day before Thanksgiving and then just reheated them on Thanksgiving while other dishes baked.  Preparing ahead worked out well for me.  Thanks so much for posting this idea!  I can definitely see us using it again in the future.

attributes.source_text: Made for Thanksgiving 2009

I sliced these into about 1/2 inch or slightly less slices.  Overlapped them in a pyrex dish after tossing them in olive oil.  Mixed the rest of the ingredients together and sprinkled over the top.  The bottom sorta caramelized and the top was spicey sweet, without being over sweet or spicey.  Made a yam lover out of me :)  I will fix these again!  Thanks for posting ratherbeswimming.

Sweet potatoes with chili powder? Cayenne pepper? You must be crazy! Nope. These sweet potatoes are fantastic & have become my most favorite way to eat sweet potatoes! No more marshmallows for me! I use olive oil for our hearts & Splenda brown sugar to lower the calories. 
This recipe, along with Tangy Marinated Yellow Squash #343, are my most favored recipes from Zaar. If you like different, give these a try!

I agree this is a wonderful recipe for sweet potatoes. I was looking for something a little different and I am glad I tried this one. These are not too sweet, nor too spicy. I went easy on the chili powder because I was kind of worried about them being too spicy, but next time I'll put the full amount called for- I think the oven mellows the spiciness. items.label: Chocolate Chocolate Chip Sour Cream Banana Bread
items.name: Chocolate Chocolate Chip Sour Cream Banana Bread
keywords: c("Breads", "Breakfast", "Lunch/Snacks", "Tropical Fruits", "Fruit", "Toddler Friendly", "Kid Friendly", "Sweet", "Weeknight", "For Large Groups", "Oven", "< 4 Hours", "Inexpensive")
items.description: Do not let this banana bread's long name fool you! Very easy to make, and WONDERFUL bread is the result.
instructions: Cream the butter, sugar and vanilla together.
Then add the eggs and mix.
Then put in the dry ingredients and mix well.
Add the bananas and sour cream and mix.
Then add in the chocolate chips and pour into 3 greased loaf pans.
Bake at 350 for 1 hour, or until a toothpick that has been inserted into the center comes out clean.

reviews.review_text:
Moist, taste chocolatey/banana and smelled great while baking!...I did a healthier spin on it and it turned out just as wonderful!!...
I cut the recipe to one loaf and here are my changes:
-REPLACED 7/8 cup white flour WITH 1/4 cup whole wheat flour/1/4 cup brown rice flour/
slightly less than a 1/4 cup whole grain pastry flour

-REPLACED sugar WITH splenda (kind that measure cup for cup)

-added 1/4 tsp dough enhancer (makes whole grain loaves lighter)

Dough enhancer can be found at a health food store and whole grain flours can be found in the health food dept. or baking aisle of regular grocery store.

attributes.source_text: Moist

reviews.review_text: I halved this recipe because I only had 2 bananas.  I decided to make it as a two layer cake and it baked in exactly 25 minutes to perfection.  I used mini semi-sweet chocolate chips and frosted it with Top Secret Peanut Butter Frosting (#87058) and topped with more mini chips.  WOW.  We have a houseguest he has said multiple times, "I think that was the best cake I've ever had."  My husband and kids just gobbled this up.  Thanks for posting and I can't wait to make this next time I have ripe bananas!  It's going into my list of favorites!!!  This is a winner!!!!

reviews.review_text: Substitued sour cream. I used drained, non-fat plain, yogurt. I take my container of yogurt and put the yogurt in a sive ( I have sometimes lined it with cheese cloth first) and let all the liquid drain off (for an hour, or leave overnight in the fridg.). Then it is thick like sour cream (will become like greek yogurt). I also only had a bar of dark chocolate that I cut up into small pieces. Great flavor. I added coarsely chopped walnuts too. Will use hazle nuts sometime. I whiz my bananas in my blend to puree before adding to recipe. Makes a nicer texture to the finished bread.  This bread is the very best banana bread ever! Also like it because it uses lots of bananas, I seem to end up often with over ripe banans and don't like to eat them at that stage, but love banana bread, and banana and chocolate a perfect combo.

This is SERIOUSLY CHOCOLATE bread.  And the banana-chocolate connection is just amazing!  This bread is dense, wonderfully moist and just plain marvelous.  I did make a couple of adjustments which I'll pass along.  My blackened bananas were small so I used 5 of them.  Also, my preference for most everything is to use mini chocolate chips because, unlike their big brothers, they melt...which, in this case, made for a wonderfully smooth texture.  Although 3 pans were called for (no size given), I decided to use two 8 X 4 loaf pans.  This produced two very full, high topped loaves of bread.  One hour was just right for the baking time.  I halved both loaves to share with 3 neighbors as little thank you gifts... to rave reviews, I might add! Of course that left one half for me!!!  Such chocolate bliss!...GB

reviews.review_text: I've made these twice now--both times as muffins and with a few low-fat tweaks--and they've turned out absolutely scrumptious! First, I made just a third of the recipe and got a yield of 12 muffins/cupcakes. Here are the modifications I made -- I used 2 Tablespoons of butter and 3 Tablespoons of applesauce in place of all butter; I used EggBeaters in place of the eggs; I used two bananas; and finally, I used low fat sour cream. Also, I placed a pan of water in the oven with my muffins as they cooked to help keep them moist. Now, I don't know what this recipe tastes like without these changes, but with them it is AWESOME! Even my husband devours these! As a personal preference, I used Hershey's Special Dark cocoa and semisweet chips, which make them dark and fudgy and delicious. I will make these again and again -- next time I may even try it with part whole wheat flour, but that just might be a bit too crazy!!

The raspberries gave the muffins a great tangy taste.  Cut back on the sugar by about 1/2 cup and they still taste great.  The recipe made one loaf and about 12 medium sized muffins (cooked the muffins for about 30 minutes.)  Next time I will make lots of extras too freeze! Thanks!!

attributes.source_text: The raspberries gave the muffins a great tangy taste

reviews.review_text: What a delicious way to use up odds and ends in your kitchen!  I didn't have enough cocoa but had a bit of leftover Ghiardelli hot chocolate mix so I used that.  I only had 1/4 C. of milk chocolate chips so I threw in some white chocolate chips.  I also was able to use up the ripe bananas and the sour cream I had on hand.  End result is 3 beautiful loaves of terrific tasting banana bread!  Thanks for posting this Diggy and thank you TaraK for suggesting it to me in my ripe banana thread :)

Very good recipe; excellent as cupcakes or as loaves.  I left out the choc chips, used thawed frozen banana(along with the resulting liquid that came out of them as they thawed) and whatever sugars I could find (was almost out of white sugar.) Also, I don't think there was quite a cup of the sour cream left in the container.  Definitely a keeper; this recipe is quite forgiving if you don't have everything on the list!  Thanks for sharing!

~*Miss Diggy*~, What a lovely treat allot more like a cake than a bread but nevertheless wonderful. I followed the directions and made no alterations to the recipe. My chocolate chips did not fall to the bottom as I dredged them in flour. I will definitely be adding chopped pecans next time and icing to the banana bread as to me this banana bread is more like a cake brownie. I will bake this recipe in a bunt pan and serve with ice creme or whipped creme. Thank you for posting a truly original recipe!

Today I will be making this again for the 2nd time. I forgot to tell everyone how much everyone loved it! I used King Arthur's white whole wheat flour and cut the sugar to 1 1/4 cup and it was just as moist and yummy if not yummier than any white flour bread/cake I've made. Also used dark chocolate chips (60% cocoa) and it was just the thing for a banana-y rich chocolate treat. I got it all into one bundt pan but this time I will use a loaf pan too as it rose nice and high. Thanks so much MissDiggy!

items.label: Healthy No Bake Cookies
items.name: Healthy No Bake Cookies
keywords: c("Dessert", "Cookie & Brownie", "Grains", "Egg Free", "Toddler Friendly", "Kid Friendly", "Free Of...", "Sweet", "< 15 Mins", "Beginner Cook", "Stove Top", "Easy", "Inexpensive")
items.description: I played around with my family's No Bake Cookie recipe and produced a single portion of this cookie that I feel is healthy enough to eat as a meal.  They’re still very good but are much healthier. I keep getting asked for the recipe, so I finally decided to measure out the exact portions and post the recipe. THIS RECIPE IS VERY FLEXIBLE! When I make them I NEVER measure out anything and I often add more or less of ingredients and they still taste great.  I sometimes leave out the wheat germ and flax seeds and just add more oatmeal.  I have made these replacing the sugar with about 3 tablespoons of honey.  I have changed the recipe from 1 tsp. to 1 Tbsp. of cocoa powder.
instructions: Heat milk, sugar and cocoa powder over high heat until boiling, stirring constantly.
Take off heat and stir in vanilla and peanut butter; stir until peanut butter has melted completely.
Stir in wheat germ and oatmeal.
Drop by large spoonfuls onto wax paper or eat immediately.

*As I noted above, this recipe is VERY flexible.  If you don't have wheat germ or flax seed, just use more oatmeal.  The recipe above should work out just perfectly and does most of the time, but if your cookies come out crumbly, use less oatmeal next time.  If they never set, use more oatmeal next time.

reviews.review_text:
As promised this is my re-comment.  I rated it as a 4 star recipe since I did not follow exactly though.
I went ahead and tripled the recipe and yielded 33 fabulous cookies (couldn't help sneak in a bite or two LOL!) that set up perfectly within minutes of finishing. 
The only real changes I made was instead of skim milk I used half 1% milk and half evaporated milk for a total of 1/2 c plus 1 Tbsp. Also did not use any flax seed or wheat germ, but may try it next time.  
To the milk I added:
1 1/4 c. sugar
3 Tbsp. cocoa powder (heaping)
Once it came to a boil I did continue to cook for about 45 seconds before removing from the heat.
Added:
1 tsp. vanilla (plenty)
1 c. creamy peanut butter
stirred until melted...then
3 c. oats

Cookies turned out nice and chocolate-y and with a fudge like texture.  A keeper!! Thanks!!

attributes.source_text: Cookies turned out nice and chocolate-y

reviews.review_text: I couldn't believe how good these were!  I didn't have all of the ingredients so I had to play around a little bit.  Used regular oats instead of quick - I just added a little bit extra milk and "cooked" it for a few minutes with the milk and peanut butter.  I used honey instead of sugar and not very much - maybe a tablespoon.  I used oatbran instead of wheat germ and natural smooth PB. I did use the ground flax, maybe even a little bit more than in the recipe.  I also threw in some raisins just to sweeten things up since I didn't use much honey.  They turned out great.  My toddler kept asking for more, more.  I will double the batch the next time.

attributes.source_text: My toddler kept asking for more, more

reviews.review_text: The are really delicious!!!  This is my new "go-to" no bake cookie recipe.  It's the best tasting one I've ever tried & the most healthful one too!!  I triple the recipe when I make them using 1/2 c.+1T. milk, 1c. sugar, 3T. cocoa, 4t. vanilla, 1c. peanut butter, 3/8c. wheat germ, 5t. ground flax seeds, & 3c. oatmeal.  This is absolutely a flexible recipe!  I've varied the amounts of one or two of the ingredients or added  coconut in place of some of the oatmeal with success.  I have also substituted agave nectar or honey for the sugar (using 1/2c. of either for the tripled recipe).  I like them best with the agave nectar or honey because that makes them even healthier.  When I use agave nectar or honey I store them in the freezer because they don't set up quite as firm as they do with sugar.  Thanks for a real keeper!!

Thanks so much for this recipe,it is just what I needed.I am on a low calorie,low fat diet and had a sweet craving that this satisfied.I did change it tho,omitted the wheat germ and flax.I only used 1 tsp cocoa,in place of sugar I used 3 packets sweet n low.I added 1/4 c dried cranberry's and used 2 packets of instant oatmeal along with the milk and p'nut butter.These are great.I made only 6 medium size cookies and with changes I have no idea of calories or fat.Can't be too much.I will use this one over and over adding what is on hand probably but sticking to the main ingredients.Thanks!

attributes.source_text: had a sweet craving that this satisfied

reviews.review_text:
So, I've been making these cookies about 3x a week since I came across it a few months ago. I have tinkered with the recipe to ease up the calorie count and have made some decisions regarding this recipe...

First, I know other reviewers have subbed old-fashioned oats for quick-cooking but I've done it several times and it always leads to a gross, cardboard texture so I make a point to stick with quick-cooking or instant. Secondly, I've tried using Splenda for the cookies but it makes for a salty & unedible cookie so I use regular sugar. I have subbed reduced fat pb for regular pb with no problems, and also have used Nutella in place of the peanut butter (or by using half pb, half Nutella.) I prefer dutched-cocoa powder (better chocolate-y taste) to natural cocoa (almost no chocolate flavor.) And I almost always put them in the freezer for 10 minutes to set up quickly because I am in a hurry to eat them :) I've shared this with friends who are also trying to watch their weight so thanks for a great recipe!

attributes.source_text: better chocolate-y taste
I've shared this with friends

reviews.review_text: I whole-heartedly agree with all the other reviewers that you are a genius in developing a healthy no-bake cookie! I always thought the original recipe was way too sweet and fussy, sometimes too  dry, sometimes too chewy, I could never get them right! These were perfect, I loved the ground flax seed and wheat germ in it, and I loved that they weren't too sweet.  It was a major suprise that my picky daughter thought they were delicious too.  I used natural peanut butter, scharffenberger cocoa powder, and a high quality real vanilla extract and the batch did not last long. I used a very small cookie scoop and got exactly 12 cookies. Be careful! Eating one cookie can be considered healthy, but eating the whole batch.....not so healthy! LOL Thanks for a recipe i know we will use often!

attributes.source_text: I loved that they weren't too sweet
my picky daughter thought they were delicious too

reviews.review_text: Have made this 3 times recently.  Only slight changes.  I use demerara (evaporated cane sugar juice) instead of refined white sugar, making these even  healthier since demerara has not been stripped of nutrition and is lower glycemic than white sugar.  Also doubled the recipe and added 1 scoop of chocolate protein powder.  I am now experimenting with adding unsweetened finely grated coconut.  I may lower the amount of peanut butter next time as it over powers the coconut taste.  I also want to try these using almond butter.  Will update after doing so.

I think I probably like the taste of the regular no bake cookies better, but will make these instead for two reasons. 1. They are healthier 2. They set up perfect each time I made them. The consistency is different than the gooey mess I would get occasionally with regular no bake cookies- much better. We did not use wheat germ because I don't have it, but just used some extra ground flax seeds. I also used regular oats - not quick. My daughter said she likes these better than the others I used to make. We will definitely be switching to these for good- THANK YOU!!

reviews.review_text: I am sorry to find that these cookies were not so great. However, I'll be lenient with my review, as I made some changes. I used splenda in place of sugar, and creamy peanut butter, since it was all I had. While the creamy peanut butter worked just fine, I think the cookies definitely would have benefited from a little crunch. I found that they tasted very oaty-- and not much else. There was a faint hint of peanut butter, but no chocolate flavor. It's surprising, because I considered 1/3 cup of sugar to be a lot for this recipe-- but these cookies are not very sweet at all. Really, I think it just comes down to personal taste. The cookies could have been a little moister as well-- I had trouble getting the mix to stick together as balls.

reviews.review_text: It has taken me a year to get around to making this, and I'm sorry it took me so long!  These were great.  I included the flax seeds, used rolled oats instead of quick oats (I like the texture much better -- much chewier), and added a quarter cup of coconut.  I'm happy to report they hold together beautifully (I guess others have had a little trouble) and that I got 16 cookies (and I thought they were awfully big!).  Thanks so much for figuring this recipe out -- you've got a real winner here.

reviews.review_text: WOW, these are good. My husband (a traditional cookie fan) likes them, too.  I'd planned to bake a (healthy) berry crumble for dessert, but the oven went out!  I was so glad to find this convenient recipe using stuff I already have.  This recipe is a keeper. The cookies are very quick and easy to make, and very satisfying to eat. I will make these again and again.

items.label: Weight Watchers General Tso's Chicken
items.name: Weight Watchers General Tso's Chicken
items.description: Make and share this Weight Watchers General Tso's Chicken recipe from Food.com.
instructions: In a medium bowl, whisk together broth, cornstarch, sugar, soy sauce, vinegar and ginger; set aside.
Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Add scallions, garlic and pepper and cook 2 minutes. Add chicken and cook until browned all over, about 5 minutes.
Add reserved sauce and simmer until sauce thickens and chicken is cooked through, about 3 minutes.
Serve chicken and sauce over rice. Yields about 1 cup of chicken and sauce and 1/2 cup of rice per serving.

reviews.review_text: Not ever having the real thing before I can't compare it but this recipe has a great taste.  I changed the sweetness because I'm not a fan of sweet and sour.  I doubled the recipe but not the chicken.  Added some chopped mushrooms and asparagus, cut on the diagonal to replace the chicken amount.  Used a whole can of chicken broth and decreased the corn starch to 3 level tablespoons.  I used 1 teaspoon of vinegar and 1/2 t. sugar.  Per serving I only used 1/2 c. rice and 1 c. of the chicken and sauce.  I didn't figure out the calories but it has to be a lot less than the nutritional information for this recipe.  Delicious!!  I foresee making this many times in the future.  Thanks for posting!!

This is a little different than General Tso's chicken, but it was absolutely delicious. Am trying to make every dish a little healthier lately and was not expecting such a great flavor in such a simple to make dish.
I didn't change any ingredients, but did cut the sugar down to 1 1/2 T., but after eating it, I think next time I will only use 1 T. (I don't think we will miss the extra sweetness, and it saves a few calories.)
I also almost doubled the chicken broth because the sauce got very thick quickly, and we like ours not quite so "gelatinous", if that is a word.....??
Any recipe that makes my family go back for seconds is 5 stars in my book.
Next time I will add water chestnuts, green pepper strips, and some asparagus.
Donna
.

Very nice entree. I read many reviews and took ideas from all. I served it with white rice and egg rolls. I added red bell pepper, onion and garlic to the chicken as I browned it in sesame oil. I added water chestnuts just to heat and I followed other reviewers advice and cut the corn starch to 1 Tbsp and used 1 1/2 Tbsp of Splenda instead of sugar.
I will add a little more soy sauce next time for a little more depth of flavor. I too am a whimp when it comes to hot stuff so cut the red pepper flakes to 1/4 tsp. I used regular onions instead of scallions. I used skinless boneless chicken thighs and they were moist and tender. All in all a nice oriental dish and we will have it again. Thanks,
Carole in Orlando

reviews.review_text: Easy to prepare and delicious.  I was a little worried when I made the sauce because the vinegar smelled too strong, but in the end, it blended very nicely.  I had a second moment of concern when the sauce thickened.  It doesn't LOOK very appealing at that point, but once you taste it, you get over the snotty look.  Next time I may add a little more red pepper flakes as we like our food pretty spicy.  I served it over a brown rice/wild rice combo to up the fiber and steamed broccoli and fresh cauliflower and carrots.  I'm looking forward to the leftovers!  Thanks for sharing this recipe.  It will go a long way toward making my Weight Watchers journey interesting!

This was incredibly good! The only thing I did differently was to use rice wine vinegar since that's what I have and cut up chicken thighs since I've come to prefer them. Otherwise, I followed exactly as is, and I wouldn't change a thing! I love ginger, so it was the perfect amount for me, even if I can understand others who are not such fans using a bit less. The amount of spiciness was perfect, too - spicy, but not too spicy. I liked that the sauce was thick because it made the whole thing taste that much more decadent while still being guilt-free healthy! The portions were on the smaller side, but that's probably sort of the point of Weight Watchers, I'd guess... I held myself to just my portion, but I look very forward to more for lunch tomorrow :) I'll be making this again and again. Thank you for sharing a winner!

Silly me forgot to saute the pepper flakes/garlic so I just threw it into the sauce--but it wasn't spicy enough for hubby so will make sure I do it right next time! reviews.review_text: Delicious!!! I will agree - this isn't like the General Tso's you get at a restaurant, and for that I am eternally grateful. "Real" General Tso's is usually gummy, overly sweet, and made with questionable meat. This has INCREDIBLE flavor and won't send you into a diabetic coma or cardiac arrest. The only adjustments I make are to decrease the red pepper to 1/4 tsp (I'm a weenie when it comes to heat - my husband just sprinkles more on his serving), and to serve it over brown rice. We prefer the flavor, and for those on WW - or just trying to eat better - it's better than white. This is in my keeper file and used frequently!

This was pretty good...but I don't  think it  tasted like General Tso's, at least not any I have ever had.  DH didn't care for it at all and was quite disappointed. 

I followed the directions exactly. Mine did not turn out nearly as dark as it should have, or as pictured here.  Again, it was good - just not what I expected. I would make this again but it will have to be on a night when DH is out of town or something.

I was really hoping to like this recipe more, as I am following WW and love General Tso's chicken.
