The spice was just right for me

reviews.review_text: This has great flavor! i did have a little problem with the sauce though, it didnt seem to get thick enough.Iam not sure why, i followed all the measurements exactly! (?) I only had a bite and i put the rest in the fridge yesterday for hubby's dinner(we work opposite shifts) well i havent asked him yet but i think he really liked it because when i got home today its all gone! :) I will definately be making this again and hopefully i will get a whole serving! lol. thanks for sharing!

attributes.source_text: i think he really liked it because when i got home today its all gone

reviews.review_text:
This was easy to make and VERY GOOD!!!  It is definitely going into my regular dinner rotation!!!
I left the chili's out of the cooking process for the kids and added crushed red pepper on mine and DH after serving.  I was freaking out because I didnt have the vinegar or oil, but having read MANY reviews on this site, one thing I noticed is most dont let that stop them.  So, I used sesame oil and rice vinegar, since they were on hand, and it turned out great!!!

attributes.source_text: going into my regular dinner rotation

reviews.review_text: I am not a fan of dredging food through goo and then batheing it in hot oil so I thought this might be a good alternative.  Made this last night and it was a HUGE hit.  As my BF said, it tastes "cleaner" without all the oil and it doesn't sit as heavy on your stomach either.  We both love the General's chicken but I rarely make it as it is just too fatty.  Thanks for posting this recipe.  Now we can have the General's chicken as often as we want.  The only change I made was I bumped up the amount of hot pepper as we like things quite spicy

attributes.source_text: As my BF said

reviews.review_text: My BF said give this 5 stars, he loved it! I was suprised how easy it was to make. Didn't have any peanut oil so I substituted sesame oil, and used splenda instead of sugar. I had left-over rice so this meal was ready in under 15 minutes. Served with stir fried green beans on the side. With the sauce I didn't even miss the breading on the chicken. Actually I think it's better without it. Thanks for posting this recipe, it's a keeper for us.

attributes.source_text: My BF said give this 5 stars, he loved it!

reviews.review_text: We loved this.  We liked it better (for homemade) than the traditional fried kind.  Very simple to make and really tasty.  My 14 year old son loves General Tso's Chicken and making it at home with my old recipe was such a hassle with all the batter and frying. This is WAY easier and much healthier! I have made it a few times and cannot say enough good things about it.  It always turns out wonderful.  I always double so that we have left overs. Try this one!

This was really, really bland to me.  I did not like it very much.  I prepared it exactly as directed.  It just really lacked the 'punch' I have come to know and love from genuine General Tso's sauce.  The reason I am giving it a "liked it" review is because I sprinkled the red pepper flakes on mine at the end so I could give my kids some that wasn't spicy.  However, even with that taken into account the underlying sauce also very much lacked in flavor.  Sorry!

items.label: Maryland Crab Cakes
items.name: Maryland Crab Cakes
items.description: If you have ever been to the Maryland area or once lived there you would know how AWESOME the seafood is! This recipe will not disappoint you! It was handed down to me from my Mommom, who has lived in Delaware ( Maryland's Neighbor) her entire life. Please try it and I hope you enjoy it as much as I have over the years!
instructions: Mix together eggs, mayo, OLD BAY, pepper, worcestershire sauce, and mustard, until creamy.
Add bread crumbs, mixing evenly.
Add in the crab meat, being sure to mix evenly.
Shape into cakes.
Makes 6 large or 9 medium crabcakes.
Saute in pan with a little oil for about 5 minutes on each side.
You can also broil them until brown. This may require you to flip them, depending on your pan.
Serve with tartar sauce and lemon.
Tip: Try a crabcake sandwich. I use a Martin's Brand potato roll topped with tartar sauce and crisp lettuce.

reviews.review_text: We had just caught some blue and stone crabs and I decided to try this recipe for something different. Well when I started to make it, I realized the the seasonings were way off for us. I boil my crabs with crab boil and a lot of extras thrown in. So I just used a shake or two of the Old Bay Seasoning. Also I only used 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce as we wanted to taste the crab and not the sauce. Lastly, for the same reason, I only used 1/4 teaspoon mustard. Everyone at the dinner party, wanted the recipe. I will continue making this my way, but I want to thank you for posting the recipe. For us it was a great starting point; therefore, I do not know how to rate this.

attributes.source_text: Everyone at the dinner party

reviews.review_text: This was really great - I'm only giving it four stars b/c I made some changes.  I used seasoned bread crumbs and doubled the Old Bay (based on other reviews).  I think these would have been somewhat bland w/o those changes.  Also, I baked mine at 400 degrees for 10 minutes, then broiled on high for 5.  I sprayed the pan and the cakes with butter spray to make up for the lack of frying.  I chilled my cakes for several hours before cooking, so they'd hold together.  This is a typical step used in making crab cakes, and I was surprised it wasn't mentioned.  These were truly delicious, and I'll be making these again with those substitutions.

Excellent recipe!  We had leftover King Crab from Mother's Day and I made the recipe "as is" plus a bit.  I didn't have quite a pound of crab so I added a bit more bread crumbs, some finely minced red pepper and a little parsley.  The bread crumbs I used were seasoned.  With other suggestions here I refrigerated them for about an hour before cooking.  I pan fried one for my son who was eating earlier than us and baked the others for the rest of us.  I baked at 475 degrees for 8 minutes and then broiled about 2 1/2 minutes on each side.  Either cooking method worked out great.  I served them with Remoulade Sauce #87124.  Delish!

I have been making this recipe for years, and tonight to spice it up I made homemade breadcrumbs.  Much easier than I thought and worth every minute.  A few pieces of stale bread in a food processor and the some zest from a lemon.  Heat up about half a stick of butter with the breadcrumbs, salt, pepper, and old bay.  Stir on medium heat for about 10-15 minutes. Let cool. I used about 3/4 cup because it was lighter than dried. I chilled the crab mixture for a few hours then formed patties and dipped them in the leftover breadcrumbs.  I refrigerated for another hour.  I fired them in olive oil for about 8 minutes per side. This was already my favorite crab patties recipe, but the homemade breadcrumbs made it mind blowing.

Used 2 cups (equivalent to 1 lb) of fresh Dungeness (out of the water last night) for these crab cakes.  More or less followed the recipe and they are perfect...because all you really want is the crab meat for flavor!  Didn't use any seasonings other than herbs in my homemade breadcrumbs and a bit of Worcestershire and salt and pepper.  Refrigerated for 2 hours after putting the mixture together.  Coated with breadcrumbs again before baking.  Baked at 425 for 20 minutes rather than frying...flipped with 5 minutes remaining so brown on both sides.

attributes.source_text: all you really want is the crab meat for flavor

reviews.review_text:
Would like to give it 4.75 stars -- darn good recipe! Read through most of the reviews and saw several comments about the crab not coming through and one that stuck out was a person that used canned crab. I've made this several times now and this past time I bought a cheap can of canned "white crab meat". Followed the recipe with the exception of increasing the old bay by 25% (love old bay)! Even with the canned crab meat this recipe shines. I do drizzle a little butter over it and prefer baking it as others have done...also followed the suggestions regarding chilling it for an hour or so before making the cakes.

The only reason I fall a little short of the 5 stars is I'm use to something else in there. A very little bit of onion, little bell pepper..something. That being said - that I'm "use to that" -- I like the recipe the way it is and will continue to make it without adding anything other than butter. I know that sounds wrong to take a star off because it doesn't have something that I'm not going to add back in -- it's simply that I've never had a Maryland crab cake (in Maryland) that did not have a little something else in it.. but I do LOVE these!!!

Great recipe!  I tweaked it a bit.  I used a container of Phillip's lump crabmeat and added some ingredients to the mix from their recipe (on the container):  dried parsley, lemon juice, melted butter and mustard.  Like another reviewer said, I baked them at 425 degrees for 20 minutes, but used parchment paper on a baking sheet instead of grease.  The bottoms were a little dark, so I may cut the baking time if I make them again.  My husband and I really enjoyed them.  I had mine plain....he used cocktail sauce.  I got 8 cakes out of the recipe.

attributes.source_text: My husband and I really enjoyed them

reviews.review_text:
Hands down the best crab cakes ever.  After reading many of the reviews, I made a few changes to the recipe.  First, I added 1 tablespoon of Old Bay instead of the 1 teaspoon.  I also melted 1 tablespoon of unsalted butter and mixed in 1/2 teaspoon fresh lemon juice.  I drizzled this over the tops of the cakes before I baked them.  I baked them at 475 (because the roasted broccoli I made with it required a 500-degree oven) for 8 minutes and the broiled on high for 5 to get nice, golden brown tops.  I did not flip these over to brown both sides.  The cakes I made were about 2 1/2 inches in diameter and about an inch thick.  This recipe made 8 of those--and they're filling.  This is a perfect recipe for 4 diners.  I served mine tonight with Recipe #69240 and 
Recipe #87124.  It was phenomenal.  The only think I would add would be a nice rice pilaf.  Top notch recipe, Leslie O!  Thanks so much for the great dinner!

attributes.source_text: about an inch thick
Thanks so much for the great dinner

reviews.review_text: This one is a bit more involved than the one I learned. This Virginia kid learned that the crab cake is best when simple. We'd pick up crabs and crab meat at the dockside boats in Washington, DC. So very fresh. The crab cake is Lump Crab meat, just enough unsalted soda cracker crumbs to help bind with the egg. Old Bay (original) to taste. Fry in a little oil or oil/butter mixed until golden on each side - about 4 minutes. Serve with a bit of Old Bay in Mayo for a sandwich. For either bite size or plated for dinner offer the Mayo mix and cocktail sauce. If you really want tartar sauce do it home made and with dill relish.

attributes.source_text: plated for dinner

reviews.review_text: Great recipe! I live in Delaware at the beach and have been trying out different recipes for crab cakes. When I mixed this up, I knew I would be baking/broiling them as that is how DH and I like them, and they seemed as if they would fall apart. I just scooped out six helpings and they sat perfectly on the baking sheet. I did over cook them but your recipe is right on the money. Next time will bake at 350 instead of 400 for 10 minutes and broil for 4....I am pretty sure that will keep the moistness. Even overdone, they had the flavor we have been looking for. Thanks Leslie O!!!

I read through all the reviews, and made changes accordingly. I used a little more old bay (we like old bay quite a lot), added a little parsley, two tablespoons of a vidalia onion and used freshly ground black pepper. I also rolled them in crumbs at the end, and brushed them with a lemon-butter mixture (literally, just some butter with a little lemon squeezed into it). I baked at 350 for 10 mins, then broiled both sides for a couple minutes for some "crisp". They were outstanding. I was lucky enough to have fresh, real crab, and these were perfect. Thanks! :)

attributes.source_text: broiled both sides for a couple minutes for some "crisp"

reviews.review_text: Very good! I used leftover King Crab legs and decided to use half of the Old Bay Seasoning since the King Crab was salty enough. I put a small dab of butter on the top of each and baked them in a small muffin tin at 350 for 10 minutes and Broiled for 5 minutes thanks to Peter Pan. I also found this sauce from KitenCal which goes well with these- 1 cup mayonnaise with 1/2 teaspoon mustard powder, 2 tablespoons honey and pinch cayenne peper; mix and chill until ready to use.

All I can say is YUMMY!! I love this recipe. I am a Marylander and I am not a big seafood eater, shh..that's not something to share around here, especially since I live in Baltimore! I love this recipe so much though! These crab cakes are the best that I have ever made or had ANYWHERE! I do have to say that I LOVE any fried food, that includes some seafood. The only thing that I have change/altered is that I use 2pds. of crab meat and A LOT more Old Bay. I don't like fillers and with the extra pound these crab cakes are De-Lish!
My husband won't eat any other than these! Way to go Mommom!! Thanks for posting!!

attributes.source_text: My husband won't eat any other than these!

reviews.review_text: These are very similar to my cakes.  I substitute Panko (Japanese Bread Crumbs) or crumbled saltine crackers instead of the regular crumbs (holds them together yet kinda of disolves when they're cooked).  I also use dry mustard and add a little parsley for color.  Before frying them I also roll them in the Panko, or saltines for a crusty finish.  Didn't rate the recipe because I didn't try it as written, but know it's gotta be great cause it's little filler and ALL CRAB!  That's what a Maryland crab cake is all about.

These crab cakes taste wonderful and were very easy to make.  Unfortunately, I could not find Old Bay Seasoning in my grocery store, so I just added my own seasonings (garlic, pepper, season all).  I tried them fried and baked.  Both were excellent, but the baked ones made me feel less guilty.  My family could not believe that I made them in my kitchen (and not purchased from one of our favorite seafood restaurants here in New Orleans).  Great recipe...highly recommended!

attributes.source_text: My family could not believe that I made them in my kitchen

reviews.review_text: I've made these a couple times now and they are some of the best crab cakes I've ever had.  They were so good I didn't put anything on them and ate them right out of the pan and the next day had one as a sandwich.  Although I bet they'd be amazing with a nice creamy sun dried tomato sauce or a creamy cocktail sauce.  If I hadn't made these with my own hands I would have thought they were from a commercial restaurant or professional chef.  Thank you for sharing this super yummy recipe!  Oh and its easily cut in half or doubled and works great.

This recipe was so amazing! My husband and I had been going to a restaurant every Tuesday, for their expensive crab cake night. These were perfect, other than that I had to add a little more breadcrumbs. I had an almost empty bag of Pepperidge Farm Italian croutons, which I crushed up to use in addition to the plain crumbs. I also added a little cayenne pepper because we like things spicy. The cooking time suggestion was perfect. I used a griddle. Thanks so much for the recipe!

This is a fantastic crab cake recipe if you love the flavor of crab!  There isn't much filling, so you mostly taste the crab meat.  Because of that, you want to make sure you use a really good quality crab meat or it may taste a little bland.  I used jumbo lump crab and baked then broiled mine instead of frying to save a few calories and they were really awesome.  If you like the spongey, crab flavored bread balls that most restaurants serve as crab cakes, don't try this recipe.  If you love crab meat, you'll love these!

attributes.source_text: if you love the flavor of crab

reviews.review_text:
Perfect!  My father and I planned a lobster dinner for my mother on Mother's Day, and I volunteered to make crab cakes without any knowledge whatsoever on where to begin.  I searched desperately for a recipe on Mother's Day morning, and decided to try this because it looked quick and easy.

It was so delicious and quick!  I added a little red pepper, green onions, and a bit more Old Bay Seasoning, and everyone raved!

Thank you soooo much.  This is a keeper.

These cakes were very good.  I totally agree with GirlFriday on the amount of Old Bay.  I spent 14 years in Virginia Beach & "there's never too much" Old Bay in a recipe.  I did fry these, but used an oil called, "Enova", it's awesome.  Food never tastes like the oil and it's healthier.  I had them with Shrimp-Stuffed Red Snapper...yummm! (Will be putting recipe on sight soon).  I really enjoyed these and will do them again, next time with a bit of celery and onion.  Thanks Leslie O!!

items.label: Spinach Strawberry Salad
items.name: Spinach Strawberry Salad
items.description: Spinach and strawberries what an odd combination for a recipe. That is what I thought before trying this the first time. Now I get many requests to bring this for dinner parties. The raspberry wine vinegar adds a marvelous taste, and compliments the first two ingredients. This salad is very eye pleasing in crystal.
instructions: Toast pecans over low heat, set aside to cool.
Combine dressing ingredients and shake well.
Toss and garnish with a few sliced strawberries.
Serve immediately.
(Thanks to  Chef #320254's review I'm updating this)  If you'd like, use a high speed mini-mixer to emulsify the dressing.
Roland, makes a Raspberry Flavored Wine Vinegar.

reviews.review_text:
I made this recipe all last spring, and can't believe I didn't review it! This is a wonderful salad! Colorful, beautiful, and very, very good! Sometimes I use toasted almonds instead of the pecans. I also cut back on the oil and vinegar, but that's just our taste preference. 

We grow our own leafy lettuce, so I use that instead of the spinach. Either way, this is a fantastic salad that I couldn't wait to make again once the strawberries came ripe in the garden! Thank you for posting!!

Winner Winner!! We LOVED this salad. I had to make it 2 days in a row we loved it so much! The only changes I made were suggestions from other reviewers. I used 1/2 bag spinach, and 1/2 bag of mixed greens (spring mix). I added a whole container of feta cheese, and lastly, I bought raspberry vinegarite salad dressing instead of making my own. My husband turned his nose up as he saw the bottle, thinking he is not going to like it.. WRONG!!! He loved it, as did I. The Raspberry Vinagirette dressing ties all the ingredients together.. I think some crumble bacon added would be be good too!! Anyway, thank you for posting. We loved it!!

attributes.source_text: He loved it

reviews.review_text: Very tasty as is - though now that I've read thru some of the comments, will have to play with different variations.  (I've been using balsamic in place of raspberry since that what I had on hand - has been well received).  Lately, I've had mountains of spinach to use up, so I've been lightly sauteing the spinach; mixing in the dressing and topping with salt and the toasted pecans (sauteed spinach salad?) - that's also worked out very well.  Thanks for posting the recipe!

Update 4/20/10 
I made this with Easter dinner and it turned out great.  I didn't have pecans, so I used chopped walnuts.    The dressing is divine.  I also used a hand mixer to emulsify it, gave it a creamy texture and took longer for the oil/vinegar to separate.  I also used Splenda and it turned out great.  I find splenda sweeter than sugar, so I cut it in half and then adjusted to our personal sweet/tart preference.
=====================
I haven't made this recipe from here, but it resembles a strawberry/spinach salad from the Best of Bridge Series of cookbooks (Aces to be exact).  I have made that one many times with great success, however, I like the idea of the raspberry vinegar for this one.  Even looking at this, I know this is a winner.  This recipe is a tad different but looks yummy nonetheless.  I will make this version next time so I can compare them.  It is really great to tone down a rich main course!

attributes.source_text: I made this with Easter dinner
I made this with Easter dinner
gave it a creamy texture

reviews.review_text: Yummy! A classic salad. I used Raspberry Balsamic Vinegar instead of the Raspberry Red Wine Vinegar because that is what I had and it gave the dressing a nice additional tang. I did use my mini-prep food processor as recommended, I do this for most of my dressings and it just makes the process so much easier! I also added feta cheese and some arugula. Next time I would add some red onions as well. Thank you very much for a great recipe.

attributes.source_text: it gave the dressing a nice additional tang

reviews.review_text: I took this to my in-law's Memorial Day cookout, and I must say it was a HUGE hit with the crowd.  I have to admit that I did make a few changes though...I used 1/2 baby spinach and 1/2 Italian blend salad greens, I also added blueberries, mandarin oranges and dried cranberries to the salad.  I couldn't find raspberry red wine vinegar, but I did find raspberry balsamic vinegar.  Oh, I also added a teaspoon of ginger to the dressing.  I made a huge bowl of this salad and there wasn't much left at the end of the oookout.  My father-in-law asked me to make this for him for Father's Day.  Made for Diabetic Cooking Tag Game.

attributes.source_text: I took this to my in-law's Memorial Day cookout
Memorial Day cookout
My father-in-law asked me to make this for him for Father's Day

reviews.review_text: WOW Charlotte, this salad was a hit with my family and I'm already planning on when to make it for company.  The only changes I made was to substitute sliced almonds for the pecans, because of our preference, and for the dressing, I used about half of the oil that you listed.  This was SO delicious, I never thought a combo of spinach and strawberries with a raspberry vinaigrette dressing would work, but it DOES!  Thanks so much for this recipe, I can't wait to share it with others!

attributes.source_text: this salad was a hit with my family

reviews.review_text: I just finished reading an article about how a serving of spinach a day reduces risk of macular degeneration by adding to the protective layer of lutein in the eye.  With that in mind I found your recipe and tweaked it for speed.  That translates to spinach with strawberries, pecans and feta with a bottled raspberry-pecan salad dressing.  DH raved and wants it again later this week.  Thank you for some mighty delicious "therapy". ;)

attributes.source_text: DH raved

reviews.review_text: Wow - this is definitely my new favorite salad!  Even my husband, who frowned when I put spinach on the table, took THREE servings of this once he tasted the blend of flavors!  Because I'm not a pecan fan, I used the sugared almonds from recipe #35547.  Also, the sugar really does not want to dissolve in this and I love honey, so I think next time I'll try making the dressing with honey.  Thanks so much for this absolutely divine recipe!

attributes.source_text: Even my husband, who frowned when I put spinach on the table, took THREE servings of this

reviews.review_text: My boss makes this salad and had given me this recipe but I misplaced it before I could try it. When I came across this I decided to try it, made it tonight and it was fantastic!  For the salad I mixed romaine lettuce with baby spinach leaves and since I don't like pecans I added sliced almonds. I couldn't find raspberry vinegar so I used red wine vinegar, omitted the poppy seeds and used an emulsion blender. It was fantastic. I'm taking leftovers to work with grilled chicken for lunch tomorrow.  I can't wait!

attributes.source_text: for lunch tomorrow

reviews.review_text: I made this Easter weekend as a salad to go with some veggie lasagna.  It was enthusiastically received--no surprise.  Only the fickle DS did not like it but all sorts of self-professed non-spinach fans took seconds.  I used Splenda in the salad dressing and probably only used about 3/4 of the prepared dressing.  I also added a can of Mandarin oranges because that is what a version I had tasted had in it and it was good.  "Just" another 5 star review.

attributes.source_text: I made this Easter weekend
all sorts of self-professed non-spinach fans took seconds

reviews.review_text: This salad is to die for! OMG! I didn't have any raspberry red wine vinegar, so I made my own from scratch from a recipe I found on this site. I found that the dressing is GREAT on its own, but even better when refrigerated the night before. My husband LOVED it, and he's normally a STRICT garden salad with RANCH dressing only. I added feta crumbles and some bacon on his and kept mine just like the recipe. DELICIOUS!

attributes.source_text: My husband LOVED it

reviews.review_text:
So so good...I had put it together few months ago and have not stopped making it regularly. But for the first time, I ended up using Raspberry Vinegar...since I never used to have it before...and boy...what a difference! I still don't have dry mustard...so I use regular mustard and yummmm...
This salad is always requested at all family gatherings now...no matter what the menu :)
Thank you so much for posting!

attributes.source_text: always requested at all family gatherings
at all family gatherings

reviews.review_text: Ok, I made this tonight and it was AWESOME!!  It tasted like a great summer refreshing salad.  I didn't toast the pecans and I used Braswell's all natural raspberry vinaigrette dressing because the ingredients were almost identical to the ones in this recipe.  It also saved a lot of money rather than having to buy all the ingredients separately.  Anyway, I LOVE the blend of flavors!!  Will definitely have this again!

attributes.source_text: a great summer refreshing salad
a great summer refreshing salad

reviews.review_text: This is a fanstastic salad.  I was going out of our "comfort zone" with this salad.  We have never tried fruit of any kind with our lettuce or green salads.  I was blown away with this.  I am already planning on making this again tomorrow night, (trying to take advantage of strawberry season).  I have given this recipe to all my friends and they are trying it also.  Thank you for posting and introducing our family to something new.

MMM. My dh said this was a million dollar salad. 

I took the advice and used my mini processor to mix it all. 

Also, I didn't have raspberry vinegar so I used balsamic instead, but I also added three strawberries to the processor and it added lovely colour and favour. 

I also added the feta to the salad. 

The bowl was cleaned out and requested often for the future. 

Thank you for sharing!

attributes.source_text: My dh said this was a million dollar salad

reviews.review_text: Hands down the most wonderful salad that I've ever had.  We made this for lunch.  My husband, who isn't a salad eater at all, even requested it for Dinner that night and again the next night.  And he is a meat and potatoes guy!  I couldn't find any raspberry vinegar, so I opted to buy some raspberry vinegarette salad dressing.  I also added feta cheese and some coconut flakes.  It was amazing!  Thanks for inspiring us with your fantastic salad recipe!!

attributes.source_text: We made this for lunch
My husband, who isn't a salad eater at all, even requested it for Dinner that night
requested it for Dinner that night

reviews.review_text: I've made this salad several times and I get compliments every time I make it! My husband's family liked it so much that I've been nominated as the "Official Salad" person for our family parties! I usually cut down the sugar by about half, I think the salad is already pretty sweet with the strawberries. I've also added feta a couple of times, which adds a nice tang to the salad. Thank you, Charlotte!

attributes.source_text: My husband's family liked it so much
for our family parties
the salad is already pretty sweet with the strawberries
adds a nice tang to the salad

reviews.review_text: This salad was a delicious treat for mother's day.  I actually made TWO dressings - one using this recipe and the other from the Spinach Strawberry salad #35547.  This dressing is very sweet and thick.  It clung nicely to the leaves.  The other is a bit tart (which I love) and thinner which made tossing the salad a wizz bang.  The taste test on both these dressings was a toss up - they're both 5 stars!!

attributes.source_text: This dressing is very sweet
very sweet and thick
a delicious treat for mother's day

items.label: Turkey Meatballs
items.name: Turkey Meatballs
items.description: Make and share this Turkey Meatballs recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Mix all the ingredients and shape into 30 meatballs approximately 1\

reviews.review_text: Love these.  I made 4 batches yesterday in order to keep some as leftovers and freeze some.  The first time I made them I was interrupted and had to bake them without rolling into balls first.  I baked in a 9X9 at 350 degrees, convection bake, for 20 minutes and then cut into squares.  They were fantastic.  I've made them as meatballs ever since, 25 minutes convection bake at 350 degrees and then 4 to 5 minutes broil on high, second rack from the top to brown the tops a bit.  For this big batch, my meat thermometer showed they were over 190 degrees in the middle, so I might be able to cut back on the bake time, but these were still moist.

attributes.source_text: these were still moist

reviews.review_text: I gave a 5 star rating even if I didn't use lean ground turkey... I used one that has about 12g of fat per serving. It keeps them more moist.. for people complaining of dryness, have you thought of using a turkey with more fat? Doesn't mean you need to follow this exact recipe...use this as a guideline.. you hate oregano? Use something else that you prefer.. these are delicious - I made a batch with bread crumbs (Italian seasoned crumbs) and one without bread crumbs & eggs. To be honest with you, they were just as good.. as long as you add enough oil, they'll be moist. I bake them at 350 for 30 minutes, I also grease the pan before placing them in the oven.. add kale... or brocolli (add brocolli in food processor first), or carrots.. overall, this recipe gave me ideas on how to be creative with my own way of making them...

attributes.source_text: It keeps them more moist
they'll be moist

reviews.review_text: I made these tonight, it was a long day and the went together in a flash, I did howewever made a couple of modifications, necessity being the Mother of imvention and all, my bread crums were Italian, so I skipped the extra Oragano, I was out of both fresh and dried parsley, so I minced up some celery leave.  I sprayed a cookie sheet and lightly sprayed th tops of th meatballs with olive oil an baked them.  I had a jar of Alredo Sauce so I used that instead of a red sauce,  threw some sauteed mushrooms in and served it up with some steamed brocoli with lemon zest, and hot bread.  We both really enjoyed it, and I especially appreciate the fact it all came together so fast.  This is a great last minute, lazy day dish...thanks for sharing

attributes.source_text: We both really enjoyed it

reviews.review_text: Much much much easier when done in the oven. Kids love it. Normally I just boiled them but wanted to try something different; definitely a little more painstaking, but a good change of pace. The children described it as being "good and chewy." I didn't have bread crumbs but opted for toasting 4 slices of wheat bread and putting them through the food processor. Wasn't daring enough to use quick oats as someone else had done - maybe next time. I was cooking a bigger batch (2 pounds) but I kept the onion powder down to a minimum - around 1/2 teaspoon and it turned out OK. Didn't have parsley so I used dried oregano instead. Doubled everything else e.g. eggs, salt, pepper, etc. Used garlic powder instead to keep things simple.

attributes.source_text: Kids love it
The children described it as being "good and chewy."
good and chewy

reviews.review_text: This is nearly the identical recipe to the one I use. When a recipe specifies lean ground turkey, I find the 93/7 ration about right. The 85/15 has too much fat, and turkey breast is too dry. However, instead of just oregano, I add Italian seasoning, maybe 1/4-1/3 cup grated Parmesan cheese (and omit the salt altogether), and a splash of milk to keep things moist. I leave out the browning step (because that just dirties an extra pan and creates more work) and bake these on a cookie sheet, preferably lined with non-stick foil, at 400 degrees. How long? If I use the smaller cookie scoop, 14 minutes is just right. If I use the larger cookie scoop (same size as an ice-cream scoop), they take 20 minutes. These are a family favorite and are wonderful leftover if you remember to put some aside;)

attributes.source_text: These are a family favorite

reviews.review_text: I usually make turkey burgers for the kids so decided to try these meatballs after seeing all the positive reviews. Sautéed the onions, garlic and black pepper in a tbsp of olive oil in a non stick pan. Let it cool and mixed all other ingredients as written. Only got 15 meatballs so no leftovers. They smelled so good we wanted to eat them as soon as they came out of the oven (350 for 30min, sprayed my 13x9 glass pan). Sliced them in half, topped with marinara and a sprinkle of cheese on sub rolls, and voila! Kids gave these 5-stars and Mondays have been renamed "turkey-meatball-sub-Mondays" forevermore. I used 94% lean ground turkey, they were a bit sticky to roll but came out moist and flavorful. Will double the recipe next time so I have some for leftovers. My calorie counter said 58 cal per meatball and a great source of protein, woo hoo. Thanks Bergy!

attributes.source_text: Kids gave these 5-stars
came out moist and flavorful

reviews.review_text: Loved this recipe.  I used 2 cloves of garlic instead of 1 and instead of 1/2 cup of breadcrumbs, I felt 1/4 cup seasoned (italian) breadcrumbs was good enough.  I let the mix sit for approx. 20 mins, so all the flavors would mesh well. Moved on to forming the meatballs and then browning the them in vegetable oil on medium high heat.  Once browned, I then put tomatoe sauce (Francesco Rinaldi Origian) in a deep pot, heated it up on high until it somewhat boiled, threw in the meatballs, turned the mix to low and let it simmer for 20 mins. Finalized my dish by serving meatballs with spaghetti.  Delicioso!!!! Thank you for the posting.

I had an odd assortment of ingredients, so here are the changes I made:
breadcrumbs>multigrain crackers
oregano>half oregano, half basil
2 tbsp parmesan
parsley>1.5 tsp dried parsley
1/4 cup onion>1/2 cup onion
I tried cooking them two ways:  according to the directions then added marinara to cook them through, and by another reviewer's advice to bake them at 400 for 30 min. My oven might be different than others and actually at a higher temp than most, but I found that they turned out to be more tender and moist when browned stovetop with sauce.
Thanks!

attributes.source_text: they turned out to be more tender and moist
they turned out to be more tender and moist

reviews.review_text: I just made these for dinner tonight, and had one and a third pound of turkey, way more than enough to make meatballs for just my husband and myself. So, I made 20 meatballs, and a turkey burger for myself now, and one for him tomorrow, out of the same mixture. I'm going to tell you right now, this is awesome! I made a couple changes- added fennel seeds, use some Parmesan in place of part of the bread crumbs, and basil in place of parsley. I am sooooo looking forward to dinner tonight now. I plan on freezing half of these to use in soup or something else later. Try this recipe!! It's easy, and delicious. (Also, I baked them for 30 minutes at 350 instead of pan frying them.)

attributes.source_text: I just made these for dinner tonight

reviews.review_text: Bergy, I'm really sorry but I had completely forgotten to review your fabulous recipe!  My girls left the freezer door open while getting an icecream and I had frozen turkey mince there, defrosting and waiting for me to cook up so I could refreeze.  Turkey mince is quite unusual and expensive for us so I quickly found your recipe and cooked these meatballs in the oven and froze them again.  Well I ended up using them in Recipe #284302 and they were really lovely.  Thank you for this recipe.

I made this recipe on 2/19/13,As I was mixing everything together,I couldn't really smell all the seasonings but resisted the urge to add anything else. After chilling for a couple of hours,all the seasonings seemed to meld together and smelled delightful. And I know the turkey balls were made " WAY " too big,because all I was able to get was 24. I  baked them at 375 degrees for 35 minutes.They turned out incredibly moist and had a very nice flavor. " Keep Smiling :) "

attributes.source_text: They turned out incredibly moist

reviews.review_text: I was craving meatballs but wanted to use a healthier alternative rather than beef. Most of the other ground turkey recipes I've tried came out pretty dry so I was hesitant. However, these meatballs were super moist and delicious! Even my boyfriend couldn't believe how much he enjoyed them (he's very pessimistic when it comes to ground turkey, lol). Like some other reviewers, I chose to bake these at 350 degrees for 30 minutes on parchment paper. This recipe was featured in my blog - http://danasfoodblog.com/?p=629.

attributes.source_text: these meatballs were super moist

reviews.review_text: Bergy,  Thanks for this recipe.  I made them to freeze and have on hand when I need a quick meal for myself that is chalked full of protein.  This worked.  I loved them.  Dad, well he ate them but that's OK he is not a fan of turkey and I have to call them chicken meatballs.  Three of them were too much for me and my lapband but that's good because  I don't have to make them so often.  I honestly think it is the first time I have made anything in my life and gotten the number I am suppose to.  I got 30 just like you said.

Printed recipe and made meatballs within the hour, for company tomorrow.  In a word they are SUPER!  I like onion flavouring but not crunchy bits so I grate it to make a pulp.  Used only 1/4 breadcrumbs to cut carbs and 1 tbsp parsley flakes as I did not have fresh on hand.  Also used 20 oz. pkg of ground turkey.  What a great recipe, think I'll make another batch this weekend and freeze them.  Oven tip for baking was terrific idea, I put them on lightly sprayed wax paper for ease of clean up.  THANK YOU!!!

attributes.source_text: I like onion flavouring

reviews.review_text:
very good recipe and easy to make. I did bake the meatballs and the aroma was wonderful. thank you for a great recipe.  

Had to add....  Since last week I have made 3 additional batches as NONE have made it to the freezer as I originally intended.  Everyone LOVES them.  Shared the recipe with a friend and her two teenage sons gobbled them up.  

I did make one batch using italian style ground turkey.  Other than doing that I have not changed the recipe at all.  It is wonderful as it.  

Thank you for sharing!!!!!

attributes.source_text: her two teenage sons gobbled them up

reviews.review_text: i really loved this recipe. these meatballs tasted great. i used #104944 sweet and sour sauce to put over the meatballs and rice. the only problem i had was cooking them. they seemed to take longer than 5 or 6 minutes and i am wondering if it would just be easier to bake them. i made them the night before also and warmed them up in the oven before serving them. there were no leftovers for these meatballs! i will be using this recipe again. thank you!

I love these meatballs! Due to lack of ingredients on hand, I substituted crushed dried herb stuffing for the breadcrumbs, and 1.5 tablespoons dried parsley for the fresh.  After browning the meatballs, I poured homemade marinara sauce on top and let them simmer (covered) for a few minutes before serving over hot pasta.  The meatballs hold together beautifully and have a wonderful flavor. Thanks, Bergy, for a quick, delicious, healthy recipe!

attributes.source_text: The meatballs hold together beautifully

reviews.review_text: My entire family loved this recipe (including the 6 year old and the 2 1/2 year old). I followed all the instructions in the recipe and then baked them at 350 for 1/2 hour.  They were terrific!  I thought about putting them in the sauce for a while but decided against it as they were terrific on their own.  I served the whole wheat pasta and pasta sauce separately.  I will definitely make these again.  I might try making turkeyburgers with the mixture it was so good.

attributes.source_text: My entire family loved this recipe
including the 6 year old and the 2 1/2 year old

reviews.review_text:
Hey Bergy, I only got 29 meatballs, one short!!  haha! just kidding they are really delicious !   I used roasted garlic in them, made for a lovely flavour!
they stayed together beautifully.  I also cooked them in the oven on a rack, 400f degrees for 25 minutes; turned out almost crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside.  We ate half for supper and I froze the other half for a busy night.  I will try them next time with a sauce but we did enjoy them without.  Thanks for posting, I will be making them again.

attributes.source_text: I used roasted garlic in them, made for a lovely flavour
almost crispy on the outside
juicy on the inside
We ate half for supper

reviews.review_text: Delicious! Me and my boyfriend loved this recipe. Simple and "very tasty" as he said. I pan fried them in a very small amount of oil until the outside was browned then transferred them to a foil pan with chunky marinara sauce in an oven at 350 degrees for 15 min. I added mozzarella cheese as well and then put them in the broiler (or broiler setting) on HI for 2 min to crisp the cheese. I do that with my shrimp Parm as well. Absolutely yummy....

attributes.source_text: Me and my boyfriend loved this recipe
to crisp the cheese

items.label: Weight Watchers 2 Point- Pumpkin Muffins
items.name: Weight Watchers 2 Point- Pumpkin Muffins
keywords: c("Breads", "Lunch/Snacks", "Low Protein", "Low Cholesterol", "Healthy", "< 30 Mins", "For Large Groups", "Easy", "Inexpensive")
items.description: Make and share this Weight Watchers 2 Point- Pumpkin Muffins recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Mix all ingredients in mixer.
Makes 24 muffins.
Cook for 20-25 minutes at 350°F.
They will be very moist.

reviews.review_text: I just made these muffins using a regular spice cake mix (Betty Crocker Delights - Super Moist Spice Cake - 15.25 oz), 1 can (15 oz) Libby's 100% Pure Organic Pumpkin, 1 egg and 1/3 c. water and baked them at 350 degrees for 23-25 minutes. The recipe made 24 small muffins. I put all the ingredients into the WW recipe builder on the app. and came up with 1 pt/muffin (blue plan). I gave each warm muffin a couple sprays of "I Can't Believe It's Not Butter" and they were delicious! I read several reviews and decided to cut back on the amount of water, but they could've used a little more moisture. Next time I'll probably use ½ c. water and ½ c. unsweetened applesauce.

Ok, I was REALLY skeptical about this, but had to attend a pre-Thanksgiving gathering this evening, so I decided to make this, so there would be SOMETHING there I could eat without feeling toooo guilty. The joke was on me, because this went over better than any other desert there. I used a spice cake mix, one can of organic pumpkin, just under a half cup of water an one egg. I baked it a 13x9 inch pan, sprayed with Pam. I did frost it, using 8 oz of fat free cream cheese, a tablespoon of "i can't believe it's butter, light", and half a box of powdered sugar, 1 tsp of vanilla.

I have not figured the points for the frosting, but obviously it's gonna add points. It was the first time I've made cream cheese frosting using the fat free, and frankly you can't tell the difference. Since I only used half the sugar normally called for, I didn't get quite the volume of frosting, but it was quite ample to frost the cake. Anyway, like I said, everyone loved it, there was only 8 in attendance, and there were 2 homemade pies there, one pumpkin and one pecan.. that were hardly touched, I brought home one small piece of the cake. Will definitely make this again, just doing the muffins (no frosting). But I am also going to make it to take to my sister inlaw's for Turkey day. This was so easy, and really yummy.

This is the first time I have made these so I went directly by recipe to see where I wanted to tweak the recipe for next time. The original recipe is great, yet I do want to try some of the suggestions by reviewers. I am curious as to the change in points by adding the oatmeal, craisins, nuts, chocolate chips and/or dates. I am also taken aback by all the options of cake mixes that can be used, amazing. Just by the taste of the final results of the original recipe, I do see that it needs more spices and less water. My husband and I have been on the Weight Watcher plan without going to meetings so we do not get new recipes like this. Thank you for having it available. Our worst time to stay on diet is late at night when the cravings hit. Hopefully this will fulfill our weak moments.

AWESOME! My 3 year old loves them. Last night I made 3 patches for work. I used yellow cake, spice cake and chocolate cake. I love them all. The yellow and chocolate cake mixes taste like a cupcake and the spice is more like a muffin. This will be a dessert staple in our house from now on!!! My only concern on this recipe is that the fat grams listed here I believe are higher then what all 3 of my cake mixes said. They say for just mix it's 3 grams of fat for 12 servings which equals 36 total fate per box...these muffins make 24 (about) so that would be 1.5 grams of fat per muffin, not 3. The pumpkin has no fat, so not sure if I am working this up wrong or the recipe?? Either way, they are 2 points a peice on Weight Watchers, the fat difference doesn't change that. LOVE THEM, everyone must try them! :)

attributes.source_text: My 3 year old loves them
This will be a dessert staple in our house from now on

reviews.review_text:
I didn't have spice cake mix on hand so I used a yellow cake mix and did the following tweaks:

1 egg
1 cup oatmeal
1 1/2 tsp cinnamon
1/2 tsp nutmeg
1/4 tsp ground cloves
1/4 tsp ginger powder
reduced water to 2/3 cup

I found the oatmeal reduced the excess moistness leaving a balanced muffin (moist still but not too moist). I also reduced the water to 1/2 cup because I added an egg to the recipe. The whole house smells like fall when these are being baked! Next time I might add nuts or craisins for extra flavor.
2 points per serving (24 cup cakes)!

attributes.source_text: moist still but not too moist
not too moist

reviews.review_text: I just had to make these. There have been so many recent reviews that I couldn't help my self. DH instantly said to make them again. They are so full of flavor. I sprayed the muffin pans with pam. They do not rise like normal muffins but they are so good. They're very moist to the point you think they are not done. I cooked them for 25 minutes. They also freeze well, and can be zapped in the mircowave for about 35 seconds. I'm thinking about experimenting with this and putting the mixture in a pie pan and top with fat free cool whip. Instant pumkin pie? Thanks nad smith for posting a very delicious recipe.

attributes.source_text: DH instantly said to make them again
They're very moist

reviews.review_text:
SOOO GOOD!!! I made these this morning, and they're so delicious that I'm making my fiance' bring the rest of them to work with him tomorrow so I'm not tempted to eat the whole batch! They taste exactly like pumpkin pie! I followed the advice in some of the reviews, here's what I did:

I used Pillsbury pumpkin bread mix
1 15 oz can of pumpkin
1/2 c. water
2 egg whites


I sprayed a cupcake tin and put them right in there!
I'm glad I did that because they are so moist I think they would have stuck to the paper
I baked at 400 for 20 minutes and the came out PERFECT. :)

attributes.source_text: They taste exactly like pumpkin pie!
they are so moist

reviews.review_text: These are quite yummy!  Only thing I wish I had known was to grease the muffin tins or paper liners.  I used liners and unfortunately the bottom half of the muffins are stuck to the papers.  Mine were done @ 20 mins, but because they were so moist I thought they weren't quite done and kept in the oven for an extra couple of mins - mistake - they were a little too cooked on the bottom.  Overall a great low point snack that I will definitely make again, but I will remember to grease my muffin cups and will take out of the oven at 20 mins.  Thanks!  :)

attributes.source_text: they were so moist
a great low point snack

reviews.review_text: These muffins are wonderful! However, I have always made them with just cake mix and pumpkin, no water.  It's a little tough to mix but the outcome is superb.  Adding a few cinnamon chips to the recipe, as published, is very good. I have also made this recipe with many different flavors of cake mix.   I make it with chocolate cake mix and a few chocolate chips (You won't taste the pumpkin).   The most recent variation I have made is with Strawberry Cake mix, fresh strawberries (cut into small pieces), and white chocolate chips.    I have made this for years and never grow tired of it.

attributes.source_text: Adding a few cinnamon chips to the recipe, as published, is very good
I make it with chocolate cake mix and a few chocolate chips
The most recent variation I have made is with Strawberry Cake mix, fresh strawberries

reviews.review_text: Love!!! My version is the cake mix, pumpkin and instead of water, 1 egg. Then I mix in 1/2 bag of semi-sweet mini chocolate chips. Amazing. This is also a great "foundation" recipe...I'm making it tonight but switching to devil's food cake mix and the semi-sweet chips again. Next time will be milk chocolate cake mix with peanut butter chips. The chips add points, but it makes this SO decadent that it's a great treat. Brought the pumpkin chocolate chip muffins for dessert at a friend's house, everyone loved them, and nobody knew they were "diet"!!!

attributes.source_text: it makes this SO decadent
for dessert at a friend's house

reviews.review_text:
Warning.... do not make this in a 13x9 pan if you are counting WW Points!! I did, and ate half the pan!! They need to be made as muffins so that you will find some self control (or at least "I" need to!) LOL!
I followed the other recommendations and added one egg and cut back on the water. I blended it according to the package, whipping it for 2 mins and baked it in a 13x9 pan for 25 mins. It came out light and fluffy and SOOOOO good! Like I said, I ate half the dang pan! I will be making this again! I would love to try it with chocolate chips, like someone mentioned.

attributes.source_text: It came out light and fluffy
It came out light and fluffy

reviews.review_text: I have made these a few times as per the recipe and they were great.  Everybody in the house really liked them.  This time I made a  few changes based on the reviews, and now they are even better.  Instead of using muffin wrappers I just sprayed the muffin tins and they dropped right out.  (They always used to stuck to the paper and that was annoying as you'd lose some of your muffin.)  Also, I added 1 egg and reduced the water to about a 1/3 of a can.  Now they are not as wet and much more cakey.  I will now be making these more often!

attributes.source_text: Now they are not as wet
much more cakey

reviews.review_text: Gotta love this recipe for a low fat tasty treat.  I happened to have the spice cake mix and pumpkin and could not resist trying these, boy am I glad I did!  Moist and yummy!!!  I did add 1/3 cup ( or approx 2) egg whites and 2/3 cup water and some spices as suggested by some reviewers.  I brought them to work and nobody complained that they lacked any taste, instead mentioned how moist and tasty they were.  Plus I did make a 9x13 cake pan because I was lazy and did not want to deal with muffins on the first attempt.  The oven time was about 22 minutes for my oven.

attributes.source_text: Moist and yummy
how moist and tasty they were
I brought them to work and nobody complained that they lacked any taste

reviews.review_text: I made these with the sugar free vanilla cake mix (39 points), 15 1/2 ounce can of pumpkin (0 points) and about 8 or 9 ounces of Muscle Milk 100 Calorie milk (1 point) - total points is 40 and I mde 48 mini cupcakes so it's actually .833 a point -- so I count each one as 1 point - the muscle milk gives them a sweeter taste and make them a little denser -- they came out perfect and I passed them out at my weekly weight watchers meeting and everyone loved them -- this is a fantastic 1 point food.

attributes.source_text: the muscle milk gives them a sweeter taste
make them a little denser

reviews.review_text: I made these for my family this week, and they were a HUGE hit! I reduced the water to 3/4 cup and added 1/4 cup lite splenda sweetened applesauce. I also added 2 egg whites to help the texture. This added 2 calories and no fat to each muffin. I didn't know if my 6 and 3 year old sons would like them...but they LOVED them! They were eaten as snacks, dessert, and one morning they each had 2 muffins and 2 turkey sausage links for breakfast! This recipe is delicious, simple, family pleasing, and light...a combination I didn't even know was possible from a cake mix! Thanks so much for sharing this recipe!

attributes.source_text: I made these for my family this week, and they were a HUGE hit
my 6 and 3 year old sons would like them...but they LOVED them

dessert
for breakfast

reviews.review_text: OMG these are sooo good.  Instead for going for a third I thought I should write a review instead.  I did cut back the water by 1/4 cup to add an egg in order to make the texture more what the family is used to.  On half of the muffins I added left over streusel topping but I haven't tried that version yet though it looks even more inviting. I like this recipe as well as the Eggbeater version I was originally looking for.  Will try the applesauce instead of water variation too next time.

I have made a similar recipe for years. The only difference is I use NO water. Pumpkin and cake mix only. I have done this in many flavors. The yellow, white and spice mixes taste like pumpkin. The chocolate mix will taste only of chocolate. I make it in muffin cups, cupcake pans, and 13 x 9 pans. They come.out like dense cake. They are moist, but not wet. Just the mix and pumpkin. I think you'll be pleased. I serve it with whipped cream or cool whip. I will spray the pans and if you make it right in the large pan, nothing could be simpler.

attributes.source_text: They come.out like dense cake
They are moist

reviews.review_text: I can't tell you how much I love  these muffins!  I ended up going with the suggestion of 1/2 c water and 1/2 c milk, and I used 1/4 c egg beater for the egg. This gave it a wonderful cake like texture.   I also sprinkled pumpkin pie spice on the top during mixing.  I baked these 3 ways-as regular sized muffins, as muffin tops, and as a small cake with the left over batter.  All 3 turned out wonderfully.  Each of my boys loves these muffins and I will be making them again.  Thanks for sharing!

attributes.source_text: Each of my boys loves these muffins

reviews.review_text:
My husband and toddler can't stop eating these. These are incredible muffins, very moist and taste like pumpkin pie. I found the texture to be a bit off, and plan to add 1/2 to 1 cup of quick cook oats the next time I make them. As long as you are not expecting something sweet, like a cupcake, I'm sure you will enjoy this recipe.
Update:  I made these with the addition of 1 cup of quick cooking oats.  It dramatically improved the texture and did not increase the points per muffin!
