Hi~
I was very disappointed in how good this bread was-I'm trying to keep bread to a minimum and when it's this good, well it's damn hard to resist!
Followed your directions to a T and it came out FANTASTIC!  I did bake for 23 minutes-I wanted it a tad on the moist side as we wanted to slice it and grill it for Bruschetta~I let the loaf (round and baked in cast iron) sit for 10 minutes, sliced and then grilled.

Andypandy, you are my hero! This is truly an amazing, delectable, addicting bread recipe! I made one minor substitution, quite by accident, which, luckily, worked out just fine. Thought I'd share: 
Discovered at the last second that I was out of eggs. I reached into the cabinet for what I thought to be dried egg whites but being blind as a bat, I grabbed meringue powder instead. Didn't discover the switch until my loaf was in the oven. I fretted and stressed until the first bite, which was heavenly! Thank you so much for posting this recipe.

Very very good recipe! Thanks for sharing it andypandy. Used breadflour for the flour. I used my breadmachine for the kneading and the first rise..removed from mache and rolled into a rectangle,handformed it by rolling up the dough and pressing the ends together. The feel of the dough was silken and I knew this was promising to be a keeper recipe right then and there. Baking time was about 30 minutes The interior of the loaf was a perfect density and tender. Thc crust was a rich color gold that had a wonderful chewiness. The flavor was great. A definate "5 Star" bread!

items.label: Crock Pot White Chicken Chili
items.name: Crock Pot White Chicken Chili
keywords: c("Chicken Breast", "Chicken Thigh & Leg", "Chicken", "Poultry", "Beans", "Meat", "Winter", "Beginner Cook", "Stove Top", "Easy", "Inexpensive")
items.description: This white chicken chili recipe is adapted from a Betty Crocker slow cooker recipes cookbook. I often use frozen chicken breasts, and it can also be prepared conventionally on the stove top. Great comfort food!
instructions: Place chicken in a 4 quart slow cooker.
Top with beans and corn.
In a medium bowl, combine taco seasoning, chiles, condensed soup, and chicken broth. Pour over top of ingredients in the crock pot.
Cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours.
Before serving, stir gently to break up chicken, then stir in the sour cream.
Serve topped with green onions and jack cheese, if desired.

reviews.review_text: This is easy, quick, and delicious. My changes: A whole chopped onion at bottom of pot, 1 can yellow corn (drained), one can RoTel Diced Tomatoes with Lime Juice and Cilantro, approx 1 tbsp garlic powder, approx 1/2 cup finely chopped fresh cilantro (leaves & stems), approx 6 oz Trader Joe's Salsa Verde w/Jalapenos, 1 small can diced mild green chilies, 1 small can roasted diced Hatch chilies, Kittencal's Taco Seasoning Mix, approx 1/2 tsp crushed red pepper. I used only 1/2 cup chicken broth. Cooked on High for 1 1/4 hour, then Low for 3 hours. Chicken was perfectly done at this point, so I removed and shredded it, then returned it to the pot. Served with sour cream & chopped cilantro on the side. I used no pepper or salt, as there was plenty from the canned beans & corn and the seasoning mix.  The first time I made this, the only change I made was to add onion; otherwise, I followed the recipe precisely. It was very tasty, but a little bland for my taste. I'm very happy with the changes I made this time; it has more depth and a little kick.

attributes.source_text: it has more depth
a little kick

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe with some changes- wonderful!! But for food safety purposes, I should mention it's not a good idea to cook frozen meat in a crock pot- the low heat element generally does not bring the temperature of the meat high enough, quick enough to keep it out of the danger zone potentially causing illness. With that being said, I made a few changes and this was amazing. I diced up a small onion and let it sweat a few minutes on the stove, and then browned my chicken (a mix of breast and thigh) with the onions. I transferred that to the crock pot, while adding some white corn (drained), a sliced jalapeño, 2 cans of Great northern beans (drained), a can of Rotel, a tablespoon of garlic powder, some dried oregano, a can cream of chicken, and I used half chicken stock half water instead of the broth, and some pepper to taste. I left out salt and waited till the end to see and it definitely didn't need it! When I pulled out the chicken to shred it after a couple hours of cooking, I added a can of puréed beans to thicken this up. It was perfect topped with a little sour cream and some shredded cheese.

This was a wonderful, simple and satisfying dish! I made a few changes, according to what  had in my pantry. I put 1/2 chopped onion in the bottom of the crockpot. I didn't have taco seasoning, so after I placed chicken tenders on the onion, I sprinkled them with some garlic salt and poured on a 10 oz can of green enchilada sauce. After adding the corn and one can of rinsed white beans and one can of rinsed black beans, I mixed another can of green enchilada sauce with the soup, broth and chopped green chilies.  After the chicken was cooked and shredded, and the sour cream was added,  I topped it with shredded cheese and chopped cilantro, since there were already onions in the dish. I served it with cornbread. Some of my kids chose to put the cornbread in the same bowl with their chili (yummy!), and some ate it separately. Either way it was really delicious. My only regret was that, with everyone going back for seconds or thirds, there were no leftovers. I will definitey be making this again soon.

attributes.source_text: Some of my kids chose to put the cornbread in the same bowl with their chili

reviews.review_text: Wow.  This was so good and easy.  I just bought a crock pot, and every dish I've made in it so far - I haven't liked, with the exception of this one!!  I love that you don't have to brown anything in advance - I used raw chicken tenderloins, and placed on top of chopped onions (I used a whole small one).  I used one can cannelini beans and one can white kidney beans (didn't drain either one).  Also added 1 15 1/2 oz can corn (drained) and one can rotel tomatoes with green chilis.  Since I used the rotel, I omitted the can of chopped green chilis.  I also added chopped fresh jalapeno.  Everything else, I kept the same - cooked on high 2 hours and then low 2 hours.  After about 3 hours, I removed the chicken and shredded it and placed it back in.  It was so delicious - I found the consistency was thick enough that I didn't need sour cream, or cheese.  Had fresh cilantro to pass around as garnish.  Next time I think I might try lower sodium taco seasoning - but this dish is totally fantastic and flavorful!!

attributes.source_text: I found the consistency was thick enough

reviews.review_text: This is, by far, my favorite thing that I can cook! I'm alright in the kitchen... but I usually don't stray too far from my comfort zone and I'm not very adventurous when it comes to trying new recipes due to some horrifically failed past attempts. I wanted to make a white chicken chili, though, and decided on this recipe after reading the reviews. I am SO glad I did! I followed the recipe almost exactly - The only substitutions I made were using cream of mushroom soup instead of cream of chicken and, since my kids aren't fans of anything remotely spicy, I added a bit more cream soup than what was called for. I served this with thick slices of baked French bread and a side salad. I also followed other reviewers suggestions and opted for putting a dollop of plain Greek yogurt (instead of sour cream) on top of each individual bowl instead of adding it directly into the crock-pot. My hubby said this is the best chili he's ever had, my kids all loved it... Definitely a new staple in our house :)

attributes.source_text: My hubby said this is the best chili he's ever had
my kids all loved it

reviews.review_text: Delish! I am so excited about this because my kids are picky and I'm tired of tacos! Everyone loved this recipe. I made it as instructed with a few minor exceptions and did not drain the beans although it wasn't clear whether I was supposed to or not. I used three boneless chicken breasts (thawed...dangerous to use frozen, fyi). I used a bag of corn so that's probably more than what comes in a can. And the biggest change I made wasn't noticeable at all. I used a gluten-free cream of chicken soup (Recipe #340988) to make the dish acceptable for me and my daughter. My kids have come back for seconds and I had intended to save the last bit in my bowl to dip a few corn chips into. But before I knew it, I'd eaten it all. Guess I'll just have to get a second helping ;) Thanks for sharing!!

attributes.source_text: My kids have come back for seconds

reviews.review_text: Excellent!!  I read the other reviews and changed a few things:  chopped up half of an onion and layered it under the chicken when I placed it in the bottom of the crock pot, added a can of yellow corn, a can of diced tomatoes, and chopped up half of a jalapeno pepper to add some kick (I'm saving the other half of the pepper to slice as a garnish).  Other than that I did everything the same.  I put everything in the crock pot last night and just shredded the chicken this morning.  It is so SO good, we are having a hard time waiting to get into it before the football game today!  I will serve the sour cream separately.  Right now the soup tastes just perfect and I don't want to change anything!

attributes.source_text: chopped up half of a jalapeno pepper to add some kick
before the football game today

reviews.review_text: I made this w/ 1lb. chicken breast.  I cooked the chicken breast in the crock-pot and shredded it was it was tender enough.  I only used 1/2 packet of taco seasoning and in lieu of the other 1/2 I added a little chili powder, cumin and then sauteed some white onions and garlic and added those in.  I left out the sour cream to make it less caloric/fattening (even though it is not a fattening  chili but I am doing Weight Watchers...I think it ends up being about 4 points per serving.  It came out very thick, like a normal chili but seemed to be lacking flavor somewhere...but I just could not put my finger on it.  My DH said he could tell it was "low-fat" but since he has only had the basic beef chili, he does not have another white chili to compare it to.  Nonetheless it was still good and great for WW as it is filling too.

attributes.source_text: it was tender enough
It came out very thick, like a normal chili

reviews.review_text: I made this for the first time about 2 years ago. It's still my go-to recipe for soup in a crockpot... (that and another awesome clam chowder recipe that was passed along to me)...I don't substitue anything- I think it's pretty perfect as is! My only issue with this recipe is that I wouldn't call it a chili. It's got southwest flavoring more in line with a chicken tortilla soup...I went on a hunt for actual white chicken chili and stumbled on this. I still don't have a recipe for plain old white chili... but this isn't a white chili by any means... it's way to flavorful, so I personally call it Chicken Torchili. hahah! But honestly this is one of the best soup recipes I've got and I always make sure my pantry is stocked with the ingredients just in case I want to make it on a whim.

attributes.source_text: It's got southwest flavoring

reviews.review_text: I tried a White Chicken Chili recipe in the past and wasn't impressed...but my daughter says she likes the dish, so I tried this recipe. I have to say that I was much more impressed with this one. Made just a few changes...cubed the (partially frozen) chicken breasts and used cannellini beans instead of northern or navy. I omitted the corn ($1.75 for a small can of white corn!)  I cooked this only about 5 hours on low and it was plenty of time. Then I mixed about 3 TB of cornstarch and cold water to thicken it up slightly (preference). Also added a tsp of cumin towards the end.  The sour cream was good added in, but (little piggy me) added more at the table, plus some grated jack cheese. Served with Argo's sweet cornbread (our staple) and fruit...a perfect meal for a stormy evening. Thanks, Sams Club, for sharing!

Absolutely Delicious!!! I modified it a tad as did a few of the other posters (to bump up servings). I placed the 2lbs chicken breast on a bed of onions, freelanced my seasoning using FlavorGod’s Taco Tuesday/Pink Himalayan salt seasoning to marinate meat in fridge (for 30 min)...used 1 can each of black and navy beans as well as white and yellow corn, 2 cans of cream of chicken, a can of diced tomatoes with chilies and 1 can of chicken broth. Lastly, garnished with cilantro instead of scallions in addition to cheese/sour cream and enjoyed it with tortilla chips. Awesome recipe and I highly recommend it!!!!

So I googled White Chicken Chili and this recipe popped up.  After reading the reviews, I thought ok, sounds good, but 5 stars-really?  OMG...it is an amazing recipe.  I don't know what makes it so good, but yum!!!  I subsituted a few things too, whatever I had in my pantry.  I used creamed corn, small white beans and the seasoning mix from a chicken chili kit I bought.  Thank God I didn't just use the kit, it would have paled in comparison!!!  The recipe doesn't need any additional salt or seasoning.  The sour cream adds just the right little something!  We now have the makings for this recipe in our house at all times, for cold snowy days and it is our comfort food "go to" recipe!  Thanks food.com!!!

attributes.source_text: for cold snowy days

reviews.review_text: We thought this was excellent! The modifications that I made were, only 1 lb of chicken, no corn [personal pref, hate corn in soups], I used a taco seasoning from this site, and I did add about 1/2 cup of half and half just before serving....whoops just realized the sour cream.  So I guess I subbed half and half for the sour cream.  Would have been decent without. I thought it was wonderful. Too spicy for the kids, there was more heat than I anticipated. The extra shot of half and half really made a difference, although it was really good to begin with [ha!  Without the sour cream]. I'm also on Weight Watchers, but splurged a little with the points for the extra creaminess. A new favorite! Thanks for posting! p.s. no yucky crock-pot taste, some of you may know what I mean.

attributes.source_text: splurged a little with the points for the extra creaminess

reviews.review_text: Sounded fabulous & after reading reviews adjusted the recipe as follows: I used 17 oz College Inn rotisserie chicken fat free broth, can of white corn, Campbell's fat free (actually .05gms fat) Cream of Chicken soup, and Old El Paso hot and spicy taco seasoning mix. I DRAINED the great northern beans and corn, reserving the liquid in case I needed it. I used boneless/skinless chicken breasts. Cooked on low for 8hrs, the chicken shredded nicely and the chili was plenty thick and I didn't need the reserved liquid. Absolutely delicious!

attributes.source_text: the chili was plenty thick

reviews.review_text: I liked this recipe but adjusted it as well. I used 1/3 cup Taco seasoning, added 1 small can of Mexicali corn in addition to the beans and Hominy, one can of zesty diced tomatoes with chilies in place of the broth and 1 diced onion which I placed under the chicken, The sauce seemed salty to me, so I squeezed the juice of 1/2 of a fresh lime into the mix and it seemed to help cut the saltiness and also gave the dish a very subtle tang. I did add the sour cream at the end as directed (added thickness) and also served with corn bread, jalapeños, cheese, avocado, sour cream and cilantro (vs. scallions) per other reviewers. I then cooked on Low for 5 hours which worked out fine. Got rave reviews!

attributes.source_text: gave the dish a very subtle tang
added thickness

reviews.review_text: I made this yesterday and it was great not too spicy.  The only things I did different was I used 1 3/4 cup water and a teaspoon of low salt chicken boulion, because thats what I had on hand, a can of yellow corn thats what I had too and a 24 oz jar of navy beans, I drained the corn and the beans as the recipe did not say to or not.  I also used frozen chicken breasts and cooked it on High for 4 hours then on low for about 3.  the chicken was moist and tender.  I would definately make this again.  I aslo made some cornbread and served the sourcream on the side.  Great recipe.

attributes.source_text: it was great not too spicy
the chicken was moist and tender
the chicken was moist and tender

reviews.review_text: I made this for the first time for my fall festival at church last week and got great reviews. I doubled the recipe and used one fully cooked rotisserie chicken from Wal-Mart. I pulled the chicken off of the bones. It was better than I expected. I shortened the cooking by half. I used my crock pot on low after I boiled it. I drained the corn, but not the beans. It turned out thick enough and not too soupy to me. With added crackers, cheese, and sour cream it was awesome! Great recipe, simple and easy. Will make it again. Thanks and God bless you all.

attributes.source_text: for my fall festival at church
It turned out thick enough
not too soupy to me

reviews.review_text: Delicious!!! So easy and so good! I didn't add the sour cream at the end to save some calories and it was still delicious! I actually made 2 batches at the same time, one in the crock pot with a home mix of seasonings instead of prepackaged taco seasonings and the other on the stove top with the premixed seasonings. I did prefer the one in the crock pot because the chicken shredded so beautifully and the seasonings were better. BUT the other one got great reviews from everyone that had it too. Thank you for such a GREAT & EASY recipe!

There's not much I can say about this recipe that hasn't already been said but I wanted to add my own "WOW" to the reviews. This recipe is so easy to throw together and it is DELICIOUS! My DH does not like sour cream so I didn't add it, I just served it as garnish for those who wanted it (everyone BUT DH). Everyone loved it and DH said it was delicious the next day for lunch as well. Also served it with shredded cheese as garnish and small warmed flour tortillas for dipping. This will be on a regular winter rotation for us for sure!

attributes.source_text: DH said it was delicious the next day for lunch as well
the next day for lunch as well
a regular winter rotation for us

items.label: Light and Fluffy Pumpkin Pancakes
items.name: Light and Fluffy Pumpkin Pancakes
items.description: These little beauties are a beautiful color and will keep you full for hours after eating just one serving. I needed to use up extra canned pumpkin and thought I'd give it a try. - I got it out of the Martha Stewart Living magazine
instructions: Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, spices and salt in a bowl.
In a separate bowl whisk together milk, pumpkin, melted butter, and egg.
Fold mixture into dry ingredients.
Spray or grease a skillet and heat over medium heat: pour in 1/4 cup batter for each pancake.
Cook pancakes about 3 minutes per side. Serve with butter and syrup.
Makes about six 6-inch pancakes.

reviews.review_text: After reading all of the positive reviews for the recipe, I was excited to finally have found the perfect pumpkin pancake recipe.  I followed the directions to the letter, no substitutions.  They smelled and looked amazing as they cooked on the griddle. I let them cook on the longer side - until they bubbled and the bubbles popped, the edges were dry, and the cakes were on the deeper side of golden brown.  However - we cut into the first one and it looked like raw cake batter inside. I put them all of them in a 350 oven for a good 10 minutes to try and get them cooked through.  No dice, they were just as mushy and wet inside as when they came off the griddle.  The spice flavor was nice, but the texture was so unappealing as to nearly rend them inedible.

attributes.source_text: pumpkin pancake recipe

reviews.review_text: Great recipe! I halved the recipe for as I'm cooking for one. I added 1/2 tsp of baking soda, and used 1 tbsp of baking powder instead of 1 tsp, but I like my pancakes super fluffy (I even added a pinch of cream of tartar and whisked it into the liquid mix). I also switched out the butter for applesauce with no ill effects, added 1/2 tbsp of cocoa powder for a hint of chocolate, used only egg white, and used a bit more sweetener (in my case I used stevia). They turned out beautiful, delicious, and low-calorie (only 310 calories for my halved recipe).

attributes.source_text: I like my pancakes super fluffy
for a hint of chocolate

reviews.review_text: Excellent recipe! Only changes I made were to add more cinnamon and use brown sugar instead of white. I also let the batter rest a few minutes before using. The batter will be pretty thick, but will cook up fine. Used 1/4 cup measure as directed and my cakes cooked up in a little under 2 minutes per side on a 375 degree electric griddle. I didn't use any cooking spray since the griddle is nonstick. My yield was about 11 6" cakes. These have a great flavor and are slightly denser than regular pancakes, but are by far the fluffiest pumpkin ones I've ever had! Served with butter, syrup, and candied pecans.

attributes.source_text: slightly denser than regular pancakes
by far the fluffiest pumpkin ones I've ever had

reviews.review_text: These are d e l i c i o u s!!  I added a capful of orange flavoring and used real maple syrup and they were outstanding!  I had to double the recipe because we love pumpkin!!  I lost my original pumpkin pancake recipe that I've had forever and went looking online for another one and came across this recipe and I have to say....I prefer this one!  You won't be disappointed.<br/>I used an electric skillet on 350 and they came out perfect.  When you double the recipe, it takes a cup of pumpkin which is much easier than using tablespoons.

attributes.source_text: I added a capful of orange flavoring
used real maple syrup
we love pumpkin!!

reviews.review_text: Wow! Truly Delish! They tasted like pumpkin donuts without the guilt. I am very particular about my pancakes, and these turned out beautifully. I rarely follow recipes exactly, but I followed this one fairly close. I only use Whole Wheat Flour, so this is a great place to switch your family to whole wheat flour without them knowing it. I used Baking Powder and Baking Soda. I substituted Cardamom for the nutmeg and used extra Cinnamon. Added water for a smoother pour into the buttered pan. I doubled the recipe, cause it makes sense when you have all the ingredients out anyway.

attributes.source_text: They tasted like pumpkin donuts

reviews.review_text: These pancakes were a real hit at my house!  All of my children loved them.  I made a double recipe and ended up with some left over.  Suffice it to say, they freeze and reheat in the toaster nicely.   Just remember to put wax paper between them so they don't stick together. Also, if you are curious, 6 tbs. of pumpkin puree is about 1/3 of a can. Lastly, the batter is a little thick.  If you like a little thinner batter and pancake, plan to add a little extra milk. Thanks for a great recipe!!!

attributes.source_text: All of my children loved them

reviews.review_text: My first attempt and so delicious I almost certainly won't be changing a thing, other than possibly adding some nuts. I will almost certainly now be keeping pumpkin puree in the cupboard, just like I keep ricotta cheese in the fridge for ricotta pancakes. If you must add more liquid would recommend no more than an extra 1/4 cup milk. I think some reviewers have never made homemade pancakes before but rather rely on mixes, or followed the cooking instructions too closely, which would be my only gripe except I knew better to begin with.

I've never eaten many pumpkin flavored foods besides the seasonal pumpkin doughnut from Dunkin' Donuts. Since I really like the flavor of those I decided, why not? Might as well give this recipe a try (and the photos made it look very appetizing as well). In the end, I thought they were really good and tasted similar to the flavor of my beloved doughnuts.However, I might try using a tiny bit less nutmeg and ginger next time since those spices can be strong. If it helps anyone, I followed this recipe exactly (with the exception of skipping the pinch of cloves and using unsalted butter), used my griddle at 375 degrees, and the pancakes took 2 minutes on each side to cook. Also, I used 1/4 cup measure and ended up with 10 light and very fluffy pancakes. Overall, they came out great. Thanks for the recipe.

attributes.source_text: pumpkin flavored foods
10 light and very fluffy pancakes
very fluffy pancakes

reviews.review_text: These are great pancakes , not too spicy or too much pumpkin . I did have a few changes , i only had cinnamon and nutmeg on hand , I used coconut sugar instead of white sugar , coconut milk instead of reg milk ( use about 3tbs extra it's thicker) , and coconut butter instead of butter....the batter is a bit thick but still pancake consistency and I found myself pushing the batter around in the pan to make them rounder and not a lump , but they were fluffy and a good texture ....they are a bit healthier and very tasty even my 18 year old likes them . So I gave it five starts cause I'm sure my changes are responsible for the consistency .

attributes.source_text: not too spicy
they were fluffy
even my 18 year old likes them

reviews.review_text: I make scratch pancakes about once a week, and so I thought I would try something a little different with these. I am a real pumpkin lover and the flavor on these was incredible, BUT they turned out awful. First the batter was too thick and the pancake didn't cook through. Then I tried to thin it some with a little milk and then they were too flat and quite mushy...so I added a tsp of baking powder and tried again. They finally came out *looking* beautiful, and the flavor was just gorgeous, but the texture was still quite off. They were quite moist and perhaps too dense still. I think they were lacking the proper amount of dry ingredients, I will be looking for another pumpkin pancake recipe to use in the future. This was a real disappointment.

These were excellent pancakes! I made this recipe as written, even to trying some pancakes with what seemed to be thick batter. It worked! Oh, I used homemade sweet potato purée instead of canned pumpkin purée, but close enough. Oh, and I added some maple chips for extra zing, also tasty! I whipped the egg into a froth, then added the other liquids, then added to the flour mixture. We got 14 pancakes from the 1/4-cup scoop, and we've always (ALWAYS!) had leftovers from that size batch before. Not this time! Not only did the kids and I eat up what was on our plates, DH (usually a very light eater) kept going back until there were no more.

I found the ginger and nutmeg flavors to be a bit strong, so next time I'll scale back on those two. Obviously it wasn't enough of a problem to stop anyone from cleaning the plate ... Yum!

attributes.source_text: what seemed to be thick batter
the kids and I eat up what was on our plates
DH (usually a very light eater) kept going back until there were no more

reviews.review_text: I had homemade pumpkin purée instead of canned, which has a much thinner consistency. I assumed my batter may be on the thin side because of this. However, the batter was very thick. I was tempted to add more liquid, but decided to attempt it as is. They were so thick that I was afraid they wouldn't cook through. I cooked them at a lower temperature so the outside wouldn't get done before the inside. They turned out fine, very thick and fluffy. It made eight very filling pancakes.

attributes.source_text: very thick and fluffy
very thick and fluffy

reviews.review_text: i made some pumpkin snickerdoodle cookies and had a third of a can of left over pumpkin which I wasn't sure how to use up. I found this recipe for pumpkin pancakes and it was the exact amount of pumpkin I had on hand. This was the first time I had pumpkin pancakes and my husband and I thought they were very good. I saw where one reader used 1 1/2 tsp. baking powder and 1/2 tsp. baking soda so that is what I did. I will definitely fix this recipe again. ??

attributes.source_text: my husband and I thought they were very good

reviews.review_text: Can I give these a million stars? I was looking for a way to use leftover pumpkin puree, and was excited to make this recipe after seeing the pictures and reading the reviews. Made them, and have just one word to say: AWESOME!!! My entire family just loved them. I served them with syrup, whipped cream, and sliced apples. YUMMY! They are SUPER SOFT AND FLUFFY. I am looking forward to making this recipe again. Thank you, Hope's in the kitchen, for posting these!

attributes.source_text: My entire family just loved them
They are SUPER SOFT AND FLUFFY
They are SUPER SOFT AND FLUFFY

reviews.review_text:
All I can say is WOW!! My finicky 9yo dd loved these,even after I told her there was pumpkin in these. My 8 and 7 year old also loved them!! My husband,who normally doesn't like pancakes said these were wonderful and he wanted these often.We had these two mornings in a row!!!
If I could give them 50 stars I would. Served with the cinnamon syrup! These are going to be breakfast when my sisters and their families come in for the holidays!!
Thank you so much for such an awesome recipe!

reviews.review_text: DH and I tried these at a local breakfast spot and he hasn't been able to get them off the brain since.  Looked through a few recipes on Zaar and decided to try this one....we both enjoyed these, though next time I'll definitely increase the sugar.  DH thought they were fine, but I really thought that they were lacking in sweetness and bite from spice.  Easy preferences to fix, though and wonderful to serve as fall kicks into gear.  Thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: we both enjoyed these

reviews.review_text: These pancakes are incredible! My whole family loves them. I served them with recipe#37023 and everyone agreed that the combination was perfectly delicious! I doubled the pancake recipe, added chocolate chips to some for the chocolate lovers in the family, pecans to some (for myself) and left some plain. They were indeed light and fluffy, yet super filling. If you love pumpkin you will go crazy for this yummy breakfast! Thanks for sharing.

attributes.source_text: My whole family loves them

They were indeed light and fluffy
this yummy breakfast

reviews.review_text: The boyfriend and I really enjoyed this pumpkin pancake recipe. It was very fluffy just as is described in the title, and the spices were warm and complimentary to the pumpkin. My only criticism is that the batter could have incorporated either more sweetness (dried fruit or just more sugar) or another flavor component from an extract (maple, rum, etc.) to help give the pancakes a more complex and dynamic flavor profile. Next time, I will try adding raisins!

attributes.source_text: The boyfriend and I really enjoyed this pumpkin pancake recipe

items.label: Chicken Marsala
items.name: Chicken Marsala
items.description: A delicious dish served over fettuccini or linguini. Light enough and yummy enough, even kids enjoy this dish!
instructions: Pound chicken breasts until flat and thin.
Set aside.
Mix together the flour, salt, pepper, and oregano in a pie pan.
Melt oil and butter in a large skillet and bring to a low boil.
Dredge chicken until thoroughly coated through the flour mixture, shake off excess and lightly brown in skillet about 2 minutes.
Turn over chicken pieces and add mushrooms.
Cook until lightly browned.
Add wine and sherry.
Cover skillet and simmer for 10 minutes, turning chicken pieces once.

reviews.review_text:
I am still amazed at how good this recipe is-- and SO easy.  

I made some changes due to allergies:
-no mushrooms (no substitution)
-1 cup dry marsala wine (didn't have sherry)
-soy margarine instead of butter
-gluten free flour instead of wheat flour

Instructions I changed:  
-Make 2 batches of the coating mixture-- I ran out.  Maybe they were big chicken breasts?  The original recipe only covered about 2.5 of them....
-I put the coating mixture in a plastic baggie rather than a pan.

-I tried the recipe both with and without the coating.  The coating is definitely better, but if you're on a diet or have allergies, the recipe is still pretty good without it....
-Next time I will probably cut the chicken breasts in half rather than pounding them flat.  I didn't have enough room in the pan and had to cook them one at a time.

-I made the recipe today with no coating and added a medium handful of fresh dill to the sauce-- incredible!!!

FYI-- the wine I used was:  Cantine Pellegrino Dry Marsala aged more than 2 years in oak barrels (bought at Binny's)

05/22/08 Updates:  
Found out I can use corn starch instead of gluten free flour.  Get a crisper coating this way.

Another great marsala wine from Trader Joe's:  Opici Italian Selection, Dry Marsala.

All I can Say is WOW !!! I had some mushrooms I needed to use and came across this recipe. I have made chicken marsala  in the past and had a great recipe similar to this but misplaced it. Being late at night and home from work I decided to throw this together for a quick and satisfying meal. I honestly did not measure out anything, just kind of eyed it and it came out delicious. I made very small additions. I added some garlic powder to the seasoning and I also added chicken broth to the marsala wine mix, and used only cooking sherry.. I had a little bit of heavy cream so I added 2 or 3 tablespoons to thicken the sauce. WOW... this came out so delicious and took 15-20 min to cook. I had some left over linguine and added the mushroom marsala sauce over it with the chicken breast. Cant wait to have the left overs.. Thanks Kathie O... This is now mt Fav. Marsala recipe !!!!!! Worthy of 6 stars

This was so wonderful I made it on the weekend for my boyfriend and I and he was so impressed.  I did change one thing, instead of the sherry which I do not care for I used the equivalent in chicken broth.  I also sprinkled the flour on the mushrroms first, after taking the chicken out of the pan, then I added my liquid, so it would thickne better.  I added the chicken back in after the suace was done and then I served this over vermicelli.  It was to die for we loved it, I will be making this one again...I have a whole bottle of Marsala to use up now!;) Thanks for sharing really enjoyed it.  Leanne

attributes.source_text: he was so impressed

reviews.review_text: This was really tasty. I made it as written except I only used 2 chicken breasts, butterflied, so it looked like 4. I also added a little flour into the sauce to thicken it. Even my husband who isn't a cooking with wine fan gave this recipe a high rating.  UPDATE 2/8/09 --  Can I please give this ANOTHER 5 stars???  I made this again for supper and this time I added about 1/4 - 1/2 cup of milk (along with cornstarch to thicken) to the sauce.  OMG!   The only down side is I think I may have annoyed my husband by saying "that was yummy' every 20 or so minutes for hours after the meal was over.

attributes.source_text: Even my husband who isn't a cooking with wine fan gave this recipe a high rating
I made this again for supper

reviews.review_text: EXCELLENT!! Was VERY nervous about making this for my new husband who is an international pilot and orders Chicken Marsala everywhere it is on the menu, so I knew this would be held to a high standard.  (I'm a vegetarian and had never had it before, so I was really making this on blind faith, trusting the reviews.)  Well, he LOVED IT, saying it is the best he has ever had!! (He meant it, too, because he has requested it several times since then.)  For the cream sherry, I used "Harvey's Bristol Cream" at the suggestion of the wine store since its fine print states it is sherry.  For the mushrooms, I used portabello.  I doubled the sauce based on reviewer's suggestion, and I am so glad I did because it simmered an hour longer than I'd planned which really thickened the sauce!  FABULOUS!!! I am so grateful for this site and reviewers' suggestions!!! Thanks so much!!!

attributes.source_text: he LOVED IT, saying it is the best he has ever had

reviews.review_text: I loved this dish.  I was a little worried about it upon choosing it, since it seems too simple to be very good.  I stand corrected!  I think pounding the chicken breast is key, and I also tweaked to accomodate what I had on had, pursuant to the recommended substitutions, sort of:  I used 1/2 c. white wine with 2 tablespoons Presidente brandy in place of the marsala wine, and I used chicken broth in place of the sherry.  Also, since my husband is not a thin pasta fan, I served with mashed potatoes and organic corn.  The sauce was great over the mashed potatoes.  Thanks for the recipe!!

This was very good. I'm not sure if it was the quality of the marsala I bought but it wasn't a strong enough flavor for me. Still very very good. I made very few changes. Wanted to make a large batch (cooking for 2 men and wanted left overs) so I doubled everything. Used canned mushrooms, as I don't care to eat them anyway. I browned the chicken in the pan, removed and placed in 13 x 9 pan. Added mushrooms to the oils, made the gravy and poured over the top of chicken. Covered with foil and placed in the oven for 20 min at 350. Very moist and good. Served with saffron rice and side salad.

attributes.source_text: Very moist and good

reviews.review_text: I combined #50979 and #8513, I took your suggestion of mixing flour, salt, pepper and oregano, dredging the chicken in the mixture and cooked it with 2 T of butter as recipe #50979 reads.  I believe, that adding your step really made the meal so much better. The only reason I didn't follow this recipe throughout was because I am not a big fan of sherry wine. However, I had to give you 5 stars for that extra step, without it I don't think my marsala wouldv'e come out the same..my dh loved it.  Thanks again!

attributes.source_text: my dh loved it

reviews.review_text: Wow! I made this last night and it tasted like I brought it home from a restaurant. It could not have been more moist, tender or flavorful. I followed the recipe except I used ICBNB instead of butter and I omitted the cooking sherry (I'm not a big fan) and instead used 3/4 cup of the marsala wine. It was so good that my daughter who "doesn't eat chicken anymore" had two servings! The recipe was easy as well. I made a huge platter and I'm looking forward to the left-overs tonight.

attributes.source_text: more moist, tender or flavorful
more moist, tender or flavorful

reviews.review_text: This dish was absolutely wonderful. Iâ€™ve been looking for a recipe for Chicken Marsala for a while and this was it! While the food was simmering for the last 10 minutes, I clean up all the plates and utensils I used to prepare the dish. By the time everything was ready, all I had to do is serve myself and pack the rest of the food in the fridge. Itâ€™s a great dish with easy clean-up!!! Hint: You can find â€œcream sherryâ€� in fine wine/liquor stores.

Outside of not using oregano (don't like it) and substituting more marsala for the cream sherry (didn't have any) this turned out wonderful! I'd never had chicken marsala and neither had my parents. We were all a little skeptical (never really used wine in a dish) but my mom said it was absolutely wonderful! And hey, that means something. I used the marsala cooking wine you can get in the grocery store. It wasn't a deep wine color you normally see in the pictures, and the taste is probably different but I thought it was great. Thanks for the recipe!

attributes.source_text: my mom said it was absolutely wonderful

reviews.review_text: I was in the mood for Chicken Marsala so I set out to find a good recipe and picked this one. Since I didn't have Marsala wine or cream sherry I decided to substitute white wine and chicken broth and call it chicken & mushrooms in gravy because I was convinced it would alter the taste by substituting. Well it didn't and I can't get over how much it tasted like chicken Marsala! Even my husband, who is not a fan of chicken Marsala, liked it and my son and I loved it! I can't wait to make this easy recipe again.

attributes.source_text: Even my husband, who is not a fan of chicken Marsala, liked it
my son and I loved it

reviews.review_text: My first attempt at chicken marsala and I have to say it was a huge success and so easy to make.  Hubby gave a big thumbs up!!  I did make additions mentioned in other reviews...2 T.heavy cream, finely shopped onion and 2 T. flour to thicken a bit.  I also found the oil and butter to be a little heavy, so next time I will cut that back a bit.  I will definitely make this again, and probably for a company meal.  Looks so elegant on the plate.

attributes.source_text: Hubby gave a big thumbs up!!

reviews.review_text: Excellent, quick and easy recipe! I make this all the time. As is, the recipe is fantastic but I double the spice for the dredge and I add a lot more mushrooms (two whole packages of the pre-sliced kind) because that suits our tastes better. I also make a paste of a tablespoon of the butter (which I melt first) with a tablespoon or two or flour to mix in with and thicken the sauce. I also throw in a couple more splashes of both the marsala and cream sherry. It is excellent! So quick and easy!

Great recipe! I couldn't find another Marsala recipe I had made a while back and stumbled on this one. I needed a good recipe since I was cooking for my boyfriend for this first time, and what can i say, now he's even more in love with me! And it was so simple. I paired it with  some Pan fried Rosemary Garlic Potatoes and some Garlic and Oil Angel hair pasta and it was delicious meal. Definitely would like to make more sauce next time like everyone else suggested since it was so good. Thank you!

attributes.source_text: I was cooking for my boyfriend for this first time, and what can i say, now he's even more in love with me

reviews.review_text: I made this for my boyfriend one night exactly as the recipe says, using italian brown mushrooms and a wonderful dry marsala wine.  The dry marsala with the cream sherry was absolutely delicious together.  The sauce was a beautiful, rich color and delicious with pasta. It is very reminiscent of another chicken dish I love, chicken with port sauce, but the cream sherry adds a really nice touch that stands out. It's a very decadent dish.  Thanks for sharing!

attributes.source_text: I made this for my boyfriend one night
It's a very decadent dish

reviews.review_text: This was fantastic. I can see why it has gotten so many good reviews. It was easy and full of flavor. I used a sweet marsala wine. The recipe didn't specify sweet or dry. I did add two cloves of garlic out of personal preference and subbed dried oregano with a small amount of Italian seasoning because it was all I had on hand. I added more crimini mushrooms than it called for and instead of fettuccine, I used pappardella. I can't recommend this recipe enough. One of the best I have tried on recipezaar.

Nothing I could say would express the words for this wonderfully delightul dish.  It was absolutely FABULOUS!!!  From the smell to the very first bite in my and my hubby's mouth was absolutely BREATH TAKING.  I must say, that my hubby and I thoroughly enjoyed it, as did my 17 month old son.  This is something I will be keeping in my TOP 10 Recipes for SPECIAL OCCASSIONS.  Wonderfully excellent job on making and sharing this dish.  KUDOS, to you!!!

attributes.source_text: my hubby and I thoroughly enjoyed it

items.label: Finger Lickin Good BBQ Sauce
items.name: Finger Lickin Good BBQ Sauce
items.description: Make and share this Finger Lickin Good BBQ Sauce recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Put olive oil in a sauce pan on medium heat and cook onion and garlic until they are soft.
Then add the white vinegar, ketchup, brown sugar, worcestershire sauce, chili powder, and cayenne pepper.
Let this simmer for 30 minutes.

reviews.review_text: I think that this recipe is already a confirmed hit on this site....but I want my say too.  All I can say is that I wish there was a higher rating because this deserves it!  I was a little short on the ketchup, so I subed about half the called for amount with some chili sauce and I reduced the cayenne pepper to 1/8 for the kids, and I also added just a bit more brown sugar and worcestershire sauce as suggested by another review.  I made chicken on the grill and basted the breasts with the sauce and OH WOW!  Thank you so much for this recipe.  I am thinking about giving jars of it for christmas presents this year.  Love it!

Hmmm...What a pleasant surprise. LoL.  I had misplaced a magazine with my all time favourite bbq sauce and was in a desperate search for another recipe. I came across your's and it sounded familiar, but not quite the recipe I misplaced. Lo'and behold! Your recipe was DARN! close (I think my recipe used molasses instead of brown sugar..if I remember right.).  The only thing i did differently was instead of ceyenne, I used a couple of dried chipotle peppers. Gave it a bit of smokey flavour and kicked the heat up (we like spicy sauce).  I definatly won't lose...I mean misplace this recipe and will use it frequently. I will however probably double the recipe, as I like having the sauce on hand when I need it.
Used it on pulled pork butt today. Served on buns. Thanks for saving and making my day  :-)
LeeAnn

attributes.source_text: Gave it a bit of smokey flavour
kicked the heat up (we like spicy sauce)

reviews.review_text: My BF claims to hate vinegar (little does he know) So I used 1/2 rice (lower acidity) half white. Next time will use apple, also used a few tsp shy of the 1/3c Worcestershire with water to compensate for the liquid, seemed like a lot. Threw in a dash of liquid smoke too. SautÃ©eing the onion (finely chopped) with the garlic I think is an important step not to skip. I hate pieces of onions in things but couldn't really detect them so I plucked the cloves out and didn't blend. Simmered covered with a splatter screen (not lid!) so it would be sticky (good for basting and a less "wet" pulled pork)

attributes.source_text: so it would be sticky

reviews.review_text: I just made this sauce; it is simmering on the stove as I write this.Very easy to throw together and tastes great! My husband can't stop talking about how good the house smells! Thanks for a great recipe! You save me a trip to the store for BBQ sauce!!! 2009 Update - I have made this recipe the past few summers and really enjoyed it. Now that we have a soy allergy in our family the worcestershire has to be left out. I used spicy brown mustard instead and it still came out wonderful! I eyeball the ingredients since I'm too lazy to measure out the exact amounts in a recipe like this. I still give it 5 stars!

I've made this twice now, and it is wonderful!  I just made some this morning to use on country style ribs in the crock pot.  It made just enough to cover 2 pounds of ribs..anything more would require a double batch.  I also, this time around, was out of chili powder so I made my own with ground cumin, paprika, onion powder, and a dash of cayenne pepper.  I also added an extra little splash of vinegar because I like the tartness of it.  Lasyly, I used organic ketchup, which is made wihtout corn syrup, so that this recipe would contain only real sugar.  Again, very very good!

attributes.source_text: I like the tartness of it

reviews.review_text: My husband is a picky eater so I am cautious when trying new things. This recipe looked so good I really wanted to try it!  I read another review who was also skepital but said when she started cooking it it smelled great. So my thought was I will have this cooking when he walks in from work, to see what reaction I would get. Well let me tell you when he smelled that he was upset that dinner wasnt ready! I asked him if he wanted to taste it before I put it on the chicken  he said no if it taste as good as it smells there is no need. This tasted so good my husband said this is the only bbq sauce I am to cook with. This is so goooood! Thanks for such a great recipe Wonderful!!!

attributes.source_text: my husband said this is the only bbq sauce I am to cook with
My husband is a picky eater

reviews.review_text: OK, this was THE BOMB!!!  I've made other recipes that always just seemed to be missing something.  It's the chili powder!!!  I thought the comments about 'eating from the pot' were a little far-fetched....till I started doing it myself!  I used it on pulled pork and it was AWESOME!!!  It thickened and caramelized perfectly when baked on the pork in the oven.  You're the best Dana!!  Thank you, thank you, thank you!  I'll never buy BBQ sauce again!

attributes.source_text: It thickened and caramelized perfectly

reviews.review_text: My son started his high school wrestling season and had to adjust his diet to make weight. Therefore, he's eating almost exclusively meals made with a combination of chicken breasts, brown rice, broccoli, green bean and snap peas. I wanted to make him a BBQ sauce to flavor the chicken. I'm so grateful to Dana-MMH for posting her finger lickin- good BBQ sauce because it is DIVINE! This yielded about 24 ounces of sauce and I wanted to store it in a mason jar. Well, that left about 4 ounces extra. I could not stop spooning it into my mouth! It has a perfect balance of sweetness, vinegar, heat and savoriness.

attributes.source_text: a perfect balance of sweetness
a perfect balance of sweetness, vinegar, heat and savoriness
a perfect balance of sweetness, vinegar, heat and savoriness

reviews.review_text: This was a GREAT sauce! I made this on-the-fly because I realized too late that I was out of BBQ sauce. The chicken legs had already been precooked and the family was hungry. I had to shorten the simmering time, used wine vinegar, and also added about 7 drops of liquid smoke. My husband is still talking about it and my 12 yr. old DD even ate it so it gets rave reviews from me! Thanx for a super recipe. I need look no further.

attributes.source_text: added about 7 drops of liquid smoke
My husband is still talking about it
my 12 yr. old DD even ate it

reviews.review_text: Definitely does NOT need the extra vinegar! What a tang it had!  I went on Facebook to ask friends for a remedy before using it on my crockpot ribs recipe I was trying.  The solution was to add dark molasses and some liquid smoke.  I can still taste that sharp tang from the vinegar but at least there's more depth of flavor.  Honestly, I think the liquid smoke MAKES the recipe perfect. If I ever am in a pinch to make BBQ sauce late one night again i'd use this and just not add the vinegar then add the liquid smoke to taste.  Thanks for helping me last minute but don't think I like recipe as written.

attributes.source_text: at least there's more depth of flavor
the liquid smoke MAKES the recipe perfect

reviews.review_text: WOW, WOWZER, WOWZEE!!!!! I'm not a huge BBQ fan but this stuff is food of the gods!  I made this with Splenda Brown Sugar (part sugar and part splenda - remember to use about 1/2 to 1/3 less of Brown Splenda than what the recipe calls for in regular brown sugar.) Dh just delcared that WE'LL never have to go to a BBQ place again - he doesn't know he'll be learning this recipe very soon!!!

attributes.source_text: Dh just delcared that WE'LL never have to go to a BBQ place again

reviews.review_text: What a fabulous recipe!  I prefer a BBQ sauce that's spicy and tangy but not too sweet, and this was perfect.  Just the right spice level for my taste--not too hot, but a nice little kick.  Super easy to make, too.  The only change I made was to run the finished sauce through the blender in order to break up the chunks of garlic and onion for a smoother sauce (which my hubby prefers).  Yummy either way though!  I had to stop myself from getting out a spoon and eating it straight from the pan!

attributes.source_text: a BBQ sauce that's spicy and tangy
a BBQ sauce that's spicy and tangy
but not too sweet
not too hot
a nice little kick
for a smoother sauce

reviews.review_text: I tried this sauce with beef ribs and was shocked how wonderful it tasted! I used a rub on the ribs while I cooked it halfway in the oven with beer, and then I drained the beer/fat and dipped the ribs in the bbq sauce and finished cooking it. I also added a little bit of honey to the sauce to  bring out a sweeter taste. Yum! This I will definitely make again. Thanks for the recipe.

DH and I tried this BBQ sauce in our search for our favorite this spring/summer...this was our first.  Super easy to put together and great because I had all the ingredients on hand.  We both agreed that the vinegar was very strong in this sauce, both in smell and in taste.  I might make this again, but I think I would decrease the vinegar to 1/4 cup and increase the brown sugar to 1/2 cup.  Thanks for posting Dana!

I appreciated the "extra mile" of sauteing garlic and onions for the bbq sauce.  I combined the sauce with pulled pork and served it in bread -- it really saved the pork which was tasteless!  Personally, my only thought was that the sauce was overly vinegary.  For us, white bread wasn't hearty enough to deal with the vinegar taste, but whole-wheat bread did the trick.

What a pleasant surprise. When trying it on the stove DH and I thought it had a strong vinegar taste and we like vinegar. But we went ahead and used it in Recipe #88486. What a difference it makes after baking it on the meat. All I can say is yummy. This is an easy recipe and I always have the ingredients on hand. Thanks for such a great recipe that we will use in the future.

Yummy at first I thought it would be too much worcestershire but upon reading other reviews descided to try all and I am glad I did. I added a little dry mustard and I always substitute apple cider vinegar for white as white vinegar does bad things to your blood system. I think I like this better than bottled sauce. One time it tasted perfect another too much worstershire. I used to remedy that 1 part sugar, 2 parts vinegar and added to take away some of worstershire taste. Funny sometimes worstershire is fine others too much

attributes.source_text: sometimes worstershire is fine

items.label: Thousand Island Dressing
items.name: Thousand Island Dressing
items.description: Make and share this Thousand Island Dressing recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Combine all of the ingredients in a small bowl.  Stir well.
Place dressing in a covered container and refrigerate for several hours, stirring occasionally, so that the sugar dissolves and the flavors blend.

reviews.review_text: This is the quickest, easiest dressing I've ever made (short of oil and vinegar!) It's versatile, as I've made it with apple cider vinegar and white wine vinegar; I've made it will dill relish and bread & butter pickle relish. I agree - dissolve the sugar in the vinegar first, then add the rest of the ingredients. When I first started mixing, I was afraid it was going to be too thick, but it thins to a great consistency as you keep mixing. I made mine in a shaker bottle with a metal ball. I also made it in one of those plastic ones with the wagon wheel inside. YUM YUM YUM!!!

You saved my life. Ordered a fried chicken topped salad from a fast food drive through and got it home to find they had given me light Italian vinaigrette instead of Thousand Island. I don't think so. Had nothing reasonable at home to put on top, but with some quick thinking this recipe took 5 minutes to finish. Used onion powder and simple syrup instead of minced onions and sugar since I was in a pinch (just made an educated guess on the amounts). A little less vinegar since there's water in the simple syrup. Boom, instant Thousand Island. Turned out fantastic.

Skipped backtracking at the grocery store to pick up a bottle of this because I knew I'd find a good recipe here that I could make with kitchen staples and I was right:)

After reading some reviews, I did omit the granulated sugar. I held off adding until everything else was mixed in and tasted. The sugar came from the minced sweet and spicy pickle chunks I used and a tsp or so of the sweet pickle juice from the jar. Usually the only sweet pickle relish I have on hand is Wickles which also has a tiny bit of heat but the jar of pickles was already opened so I went with them. Not a big noticible heat but very good at any rate!

Great recipe and yes, made with stuff I already had at the house so even better!

attributes.source_text: The sugar came from the minced sweet and spicy pickle chunks I used
the minced sweet and spicy pickle chunks I used

reviews.review_text: I can't believe I have forgotten to rate this!  I am making it for the 3rd time and love it.  I will probably never buy store bought again.   These are easy, simple ingredients and you probably have them on hand, if not, once you try this, you will.  It is simply fresh tasting and delicious!  Granted, it is not at thick as Marie's (which I USED to buy) but it makes up for it in taste.  Definitely a keeper, thanks Victoryred!  (I had to come back at add the 5 stars)

attributes.source_text: simply fresh tasting

reviews.review_text:
I am/was in a pinch for Thousand Island Dressing for my Chicken Reuben, since I didn't have any in the pantry!So I took a look here on the Zarr!I was happy to find exactly what I was looking for. I am cooking for 2 tonight, so I changed the serves amount, also chill for awhile before using. This will blend the ingredients all together.This is better and easier than any bottle brand period.One thing, I did not add onion! This is truly a BIG A + and super easy! Thank You  Graybert!
Moontan Master!

We have been craving 1000 Island dressing for a while...  we both loved it as kids and wanted to experience it again as adults...  This dressing was way better than any commercial dressing we ever had as kids!!!  Great balance between sweet and tangy...  My BF was pleasantly surprised when he saw me mixing in ketchup ( he eats it like a side dish more than a condiment, I swear!)  and said it would also be great on hamburgers...  so we will be trying that soon.  I also used rehydrated minced onion flakes since I was too lazy to chop such a small amount and really liked the mellow onion flavor it gave to the dressing...  I am not a fan of strong, raw onion flavor at all...  I just had some today after it has sat all night and it is even better, if that's at all possible!  Thanks for sharing!!!

attributes.source_text: Great balance between sweet and tangy
Great balance between sweet and tangy
really liked the mellow onion flavor it gave to the dressing
My BF was pleasantly surprised

reviews.review_text: I accidentally made it with only 1/3 cup of mayo, and everyone loved it (including my super picky kids). Otherwise I followed the recipe exactly except that I added 1/8 tsp Worcestershire sauce as another reviewer had suggested. Looks like there's a way to get my kids to eat salad! Tonight this was a main dish salad... greens, hard-boiled eggs, tomatoes, carrots, olives. We only needed to add bread. Thanks a million!

this was a main dish salad

reviews.review_text:
Thanks for an AWESOME dressing!!

I think it tastes just like dressing from O'Charley's.  Without the High Fructose Corn syrup.   Of course the ketchup and pickles had it though.  

I added a diced boiled egg and it was awesome!   1 recipe was enough for me, my 4 year old and my husband with just a bit left over.  We all LOVED IT!!   Much much better than store bought.

I am going to try and make my own pickle relish and ketchup this summer without corn syrup.  I can't wait to try this dressing with those!!

We WILL be making this OFTEN!!

reviews.review_text: Wow, I am so glad that I ran out of salad dressing! I made a huge green salad for dinner topped with shrimp, tomatoes, avocado and sliced hard boiled eggs - and then realized I had only greek dressing in the fridge. This might have been okay in a pinch, but this dressing made it awesome! I left out the sugar, because the relish gave just the right amount of sweetness. One of the best salads I have ever had (if I do say so myself)!!

attributes.source_text: for dinner
just the right amount of sweetness

reviews.review_text: I used this super easy recipe to throw together as a sauce for the reubens I was making from our leftover St. Patrick's Day corned beef.... Not only was it fantastic on my reubens but I couldn't help to notice that it was better than the normally greasy/ oily store-bought version... I am not a fan of thousand island as a salad dressing personally, but I love it as a sandwich sauce. I will totally be using this recipe again and again for my cheeseburgers, reubens and other sandwiches. Delicious!

attributes.source_text: better than the normally greasy/ oily store-bought version
better than the normally greasy/ oily store-bought version

reviews.review_text: Made this for my Dad who has eaten 1000 Island dressing for 40 years. He said, "Spot on!" The next time I made it I added a healthy squirt of Siracha...Yum! Update 6.2.18: it's hard to find good sugar free dressings. I made a Low Carb version of this dressing using substitutions of Heinz low sugar ketchup, Mt Olive sugar free sweet relish, and Truvia. It was very good. I have used 'mother' apple cider vinegar sometimes, as well. It changes the flavor slightly but has a good vinegar zingy 'bite' .

attributes.source_text: Made this for my Dad
has a good vinegar zingy 'bite'

reviews.review_text: I have been making this for months.   Seems I can't get enough--so addicting.  Will never buy bottled again. For the salad, I keep it simple using chopped romaine lettuce, bacon bits (turkey bits, actually) and sliced cherry tomatoes.  Love, love, love it.  My husband brought home a head of romaine lettuce -- with a smile I knew he was asking for "our" homemade dressing.  Seems he can't get enough either.

attributes.source_text: Seems he can't get enough either

reviews.review_text: I tweaked this a bit using what I had on hand and it is delicious. I doubled the recipe but substituted Veganaise for the mayo (basically because no one in my house would touch it lol). I also substituted a stevia packet for the sugar, apple cider vinegar for the white and used sea salt. I am thrilled with it. Thank you so much for such a simple base recipe! Nice to know what's in my salad dressing ??????

Super yummy. Thanks for posting Graybert. I needed some for a recipe but forgot to get a bottle at the store as it is not my regular dressing. This tastes just like the way it was when I was a kid and my mom made it.The color is a titch lighter but the flavor is spot on. Definitely better than bottled. I will make again when the need arises as the ingredients were in my pantry or fridge already. Enjoy! ChefDLH

Thank you! This was wonderful. We were tired of Christmas food and wanted pizza and salad. I got home from the grocery store and didn't have any thousand island and DH won't eat anything else. I found this recipe and whipped it up. The only changes I made were homemade, chopped pickle and grandulated onions. It was wonderful. DH asked me where I got the dressing from. Oh, and the kids and I loved it as well.

items.label: Peanut Butter Cup Cookies (Tarts)
items.name: Peanut Butter Cup Cookies (Tarts)
keywords: c("Cookie & Brownie", "Kid Friendly", "Baking", "< 30 Mins", "For Large Groups", "Oven", "Easy")
items.description: I first saw these at a bake sale and was so impressed. You bake a ball of dough in a mini-muffin tin, bake, and press a Reese's peanut butter cup into it after you take it out of oven. You are left with a picture-perfect tart, receiving "oohs and aahs" and "how did you do it?" You could even use the refrigerated sugar/peanut butter cookie dough too.
instructions: Cream peanut butter, butter, sugar and brown sugar until fluffy.
Add egg, vanilla, flour, baking soda and salt' mix well.
Roll into 1-inch balls (I use small cookie scoop) and place in miniature muffin tins(sprayed with PAM) or in mini cupcake wrappers).
Bake 8-10 minutes at 375°F.
When tins are removed from oven, immediately press 1 peanut butter cup into the center of the cookie.
Allow to cool completely before removing cookies from the tin.

reviews.review_text: My first batch still got semi-burned at eight minutes bake time (the tops looked great it was the sides in the muffin pan that got over baked). Anyway, I adjusted the temp which worked out. I took the pieces that didn't look too bad to work and they got gobbled up in minutes. I Thank you for sharing. Still learning! I just wanted to tell you that I think I found my problem. I was watching the Elton Brown Good Eats show the other week and he was talking about baking pans. He made a comment that the color of the pans will affect the baking time ... the pans I used are a dark gray ... absorbs the heat faster ... thus my over baked cookies.  Ran out of reeses ... substituted by pressing about 6 semi-sweet choco chips in each :D

i don't know what else i could say about these wonderful little bites of heaven, but here i go. first of all, the dough was very easy to make,but as some of the other posters stated the dough was a little moist so i chilled it for about half an hour,and it worked just fine.i think i might have made the cookie dough balls just a little smaller than i was supposed to, because i ended up with half a dozen more tarts that what the recipe stated. the baking time was right on the money.if any one is interested a 9.2 ounce bag contains 34 mini reese's cups.this will be on my cookie trays for christmas.thank you for posting.

attributes.source_text: this will be on my cookie trays for christmas

reviews.review_text: I made these last night as a treat for my co workers.  Very easy to make, I had all the ingredietns on hand.  I used my pampered chef small cookie scoop and didn't roll them, just but them in the liner. I had to bake for the whole 10 minutes.  I also had a bit of left over milk chocolate frosting and I thought, what the heck and put a ring of the frosting around each one.  This was great because my 4 year old first counted out the 42 (I got 42) reeces and with my close supervision, helped me push them into the dough.  Thank you so much for a great recipe and fun times with my son.

attributes.source_text: as a treat for my co workers
fun times with my son

reviews.review_text: I've been meaning to try this recipe for a long time but had it in my head that they would be too time- consuming & finicky - NOT SO!  So, so easy & so delicious!!  I made them to take to a housewarming party & they were gobbled up first!  I didn't even bother rolling into balls - I just dropped by teaspoon into the muffin tins & they formed beautifully into tart shells.  I also used the really mini Reese's pb cups that are already unwrapped so that saved time.  I managed to get 4 dozen cookies out of this recipe & there were more than enough pb cups in one bag.

attributes.source_text: to take to a housewarming party

reviews.review_text: I haven't actually tried the finished product as yet, since I made them for Bible Study this coming Wednesday, but I did try the dough and it was yummy!  I got exactly 3 dozen out of this.   For most of the cookies, I used Planters peanut butter cups (which are better than Reeses if you can believe it!), they are a bit bigger than the Reese ones, but this still worked out and they look great!  I can't wait to try them!  Thanks for a great, and easy recipe!

attributes.source_text: I made them for Bible Study this coming Wednesday

reviews.review_text: These are shamefully easy.  I used the "place and bake" refrigerated cookie dough.  The pieces went straight from the package into the muffin tin--no rolling into balls or anything!  And one package of dough exactly filled my 24 cup mini-muffin pan.  I think it took longer for the oven to heat up than it did for anything else.  This is a great recipe for those times when you need to make a LOT of cookies.  They are extremely fast and easy!

What is wrong with me that I didn't think these ridiculously easy cookies were that great. To me they just seemed like a waste of yummy peanut butter cups.  I think I expected them to blend into the dough more, and be transformed from a piece of candy to a cookie. To me it was just a peanut butter cup surrounded with a little bit of cookie.  I took a recommendation to use refrigerated cookie dough, so the preparation of these little sweets didn't take more than 15 minutes...and that's a plus.  My kids didn't think they were all that great either, just tasting one each without the ohhhs and ahhhhs I had hoped for.

These couldn't be much faster or easier to make.  I used my cookie scooper thingy so that all the balls would be the same size.  My scoop is probably 1 1/2 inches instead of the 1 inch called for, so the recipe  made 24 tarts for me.  I did half with the mini p.b. cups and half with Dove milk choc. squares.  I wish I had also bought some Hershey's  caramel kisses, I think they would be great in this cookie.  Will make these for holidays and pot lucks at work.  Thanks for a great recipe, we all loved them.

There is no question in my mind why these little babies got 5 stars!  They were so simple to make and absolutely divine.  I baked the first batch for 10 minutes because they looked really gooey at 9, but then after they sat in the pan to cool, they were a tad over-baked for me.  My second batch only went for 8 minutes, and that was plenty for my liking.  These were so great right out of the pan...I think I'm going to go eat one now!

attributes.source_text: they looked really gooey at 9

reviews.review_text: In the process of making these right now. One batch finished, two to go. I didnt have muffin papers so I decided just to spray the pan a little, well I would suggest using the papers, I will next time for sure. A bit time consuming trying to carefully pull them from the pan without breaking them. Had to put them in the freezer to harden them up enough so they wouldnt break.

Were these ever fun to make. What a great idea, they look so cute on the plate. I found that the cookie part cooked in exactly 8 minutes, you dont want to over cook these tasty lil gems because they have to sit in the pan to cool. The cookie scoop idea worked great. I dont know who had more fun making these me or the kids! Thanks Roxy for another great recipe.

I thought these were wonderful!  A friend of mine tops a similar recipe with a single red or  green M&M at Christmas time (and appropriately colored M&Ms for other holidays).  So I tried that too.  It gives a very pretty finish to these little gems.  They''ll be in my Christmas gifts.  Thanks for these, Roxygirl.  My "friend" would never give me her recipe so I was delighted to find these!
