items.name: Apple Bread
items.description: Make and share this Apple Bread recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Mix flour, cinnamon, soda, salt and baking powder together.
Beat eggs and add sugar and oil.
Add vanilla and dry ingredients.
Stir in apples.
Mix walnuts in a tsp of flour and add to batter.
Pour into 2 greased loaf pans.
Bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour.

reviews.review_text: Made a lot of modifications (some based on the reviews/other posts), but it turned out delicious, spongy, and moist! -4 eggs instead of 3 -4 cups of apples instead of 2 (4 medium-large Fuji) -1 cup Greek yogurt instead of 1 cup oil -2 heaping teaspoons of cinnamon instead of 1.5 -1/2 teaspoon baking powder instead of 1/4 -brown sugar instead of white -no walnuts -added some milk to thin out the batter a bit -only needed 45 min of baking time for a toothpick to come out clean using 9x5 loaf pans I dusted the sides and bottom of my pan with white sugar, and also added a thick crumble topping (flour, sugar, cinnamon, butter). The crumble didn't really mesh well (in part, too much butter) and I'd stick with a lighter cinnamon sugar topping like others used next time.

attributes.source_text: spongy
moist

reviews.review_text: Very nice bread and simple recipe! I had 2 similar recipes from Penzeys Spices catalog. One of them used whole wheat flour and the other had more apples and 4 eggs. Based on those recipes and reviews, I made the following changes. I halved the recipe and baked in glass 8x4 pan, used 1/3 whole wheat flour, used ~ 1.5 times more apples, more cinnamon (1 tsp for half), brown sugar instead of white, substituted applesauce for half of the oil, used 2 eggs for half. Didn’t use nuts. I finely diced the apples to get a piece in every bite (otherwise you’ll have big chunks with pockets around them and then plain bread). After adding the dry ingredients, I gave it just 2-3 turns with a spoon, then added the apples and folded just a few times until no streaks of flour remained. I think it makes sense not to overmix the batter here. The resulting batter was of thick pouring consistency, not like a cookie dough, as others reviews complained. The bread was baked perfectly in 60 min. Very nice texture and flavor. I would not reduce sugar, my apples were plenty sweet and overall the bread had just perfect sweetness to be eaten by itself. This recipe lends itself well to some changes and additions, I’ll definitely be making more.

attributes.source_text: the bread had just perfect sweetness to be eaten by itself

reviews.review_text: I've made this recipe twice now. The first time I made it I followed the recipe exactly and oh my gosh was it delicious. I was licking the batter off the spatula after putting the pans in the oven. I had some red delicious apples that I wanted to get rid of and this was the perfect recipe to hide them in. My co-workers devoured them. The second time I made them I decided to play with the recipe a little. I loved how it turned out the first time, but wanted more apple flavor.  I substituted apple sauce for half the oil and I put in 3 cups of apple chunks instead of 2 like the recipe calls for. It was just as good with the changes. Another change I made was that I made 24 muffins out of the batter instead of 2 loaves. They are the perfect size serving. I only had to cook them for 25 minutes at 350°. I thought they turned out more moist as muffins since I didn't have to cook them forever to make sure the middle was cooked.

attributes.source_text: My co-workers devoured them
they turned out more moist as muffins

reviews.review_text: My daughter could hardly wait for me to take a picture. She said it's "100% fabulous." I read the reviews and thus cooked it in the bundt pan: baked perfectly and looks really pretty. I substituted applesauce for 1/2 of the oil, added almost 2X the apples (nearly 4 cups, diced large) and was very generous with the cinnamon and vanilla. I also added some cloves. The batter was just as it should be I thought: not runny but certainly not too thick. One important thing: I mistakenly added 1 tsp of baking powder, instead of 1/4 tsp. It worked out fine in this case because of weight of all the apples. When I make again, though, I will use 1/2 tsp with all the apples so it will be a little more dense, which is the way we like it. I buttered the pan and dusted with brown sugar/flour. I was worried that it might be dry according to some of the reviews, so I used the extra apples to make a little sauce on the side to eat with the bread if needed. My daughter said it wasn't dry and the sauce wasn't needed -- but she was glad I made it anyway!

attributes.source_text: My daughter could hardly wait for me to take a picture
My daughter said it wasn't dry

reviews.review_text: I made this bread because my mom is coming to visit. Sheâ€™s watching her weight, so I used applesauce in place of the oil, and omitted the nuts (for my 1-year-old). I also used 1 cup of granulated sugar, and 1 cup of brown sugar. Itâ€™s delicious! I might cut down on the sugar by half a cup next time, and use Granny Smith apples (I used Red Delicious). Because so many reviewers said that their bread seemed overdone, I decided to loosely cover my bread with foil about 20 minutes into baking, and baked according to the recipe directions. The crust was perfect; golden brown and not hard or with a burnt taste. Next time, I might reduce the oven temp to 325, bake for the full hour, and see what happens. This recipe would be fun to play around with, because you could use any number of fruit purees in place of the oil (ie: pumpkin, bananas, etc.), and you could easily throw in some shredded zucchini or carrot for an extra punch of nutrition. Great recipe, thanks for posting!

attributes.source_text: not hard

reviews.review_text: I tried this recepie because it had such good reviews...  I used Ida Red apples (because they were available).  I also baked the bread in two 4x8x2  loaf pans - pan size was not specified.  When the batter was mixed, as per the directions, it was pretty stiff.  It did not pour; I had to press into the pans.  And it was considerably lighter brown than the photo.  I baked as directed.  After one hour, a toothpick came out clean.  But about 1/3 of the way into the loaf, there was a void, and it was gooey (undercooked).  So I finished cutting the loaf and finished cooking the slices in the oven; so that part was more like toast.  The baked loaf otherwise had good texture and tasted very good.  I will bake this again but maybe with some applesauce added and probably 75 to 80 minutes, with multiple toothpick tests next time.

This is a delicious bread.I used cinnamon applesauce for half of the oil and it still came out very moist.I also added some fresh blueberries to one of the loaves which was really delicious.This was my first time making apple bread and I didn't expect to like it as much as I did.I used Granny Smith apples and the slight tartness was perfect.Next time I may chop the apples a little smaller but that's just my preference.I plan on making this again very soon.I think I'll add a little nutmeg next time.Thanks for the great recipe! UPDATE I made this again and added about 1/2 tsp of nutmeg and cloves and upped the cinnamon to 2 tsp.I used 1 cup of brown sugar and 1 cup of white sugar.It was so delicious!

attributes.source_text: it still came out very moist
the slight tartness was perfect

reviews.review_text: Excellent sweet bread! I looked at the reviews and picked up some tips that were very helpful. First, I'm so glad that some posted that the batter is very thick--almost cookie dough-like because I may have been tempted to add something to moisten it more. Secondly, I appreciated the post about using a bundt pan, because I couldn't find my loaf pans. But I also wanted that crunchy crust from sprinkling the top with sugar/cinnamon others talked about. I did a little research and learned that you can oil and "dust" the pan with the cinnamon/sugar mixture the same way you would dust with flour. Wow! That wonderful sweet crunchy outer layer tasted like cookies! I also added almost 3 cups of gala apples because that's what I had after I peeled and diced them. Just like the others who posted, I couldn't stop eating this delicious bread! And it was a big hit with my women's bible study group. Will definitely make again over the holidays.

attributes.source_text: Excellent sweet bread!
that crunchy crust from sprinkling the top with sugar/cinnamon
That wonderful sweet crunchy outer layer

reviews.review_text:
This is a five star and more recipe!  The flavour is great.  I used 3 granny smith's apples, which did give me slightly over 2 cups, but I popped it all in anyway.  And it turned out WONDERFUL.  But I think i won't chop the apples up so fine the next time cos, it i would like to TASTE TASTE apple bits, but that is totally a personal preference.  It had just the right amount of cinnamon.  
After popping the first one into the oven, the aroma was just over-whelming, I just HAD to go do another batch.  And it was the right thing to do for sure.  Four loaves, and I have only got half a loaf left in less than 7 hours.  Everyone has attacked them.  5 stars and more!

attributes.source_text: It had just the right amount of cinnamon

reviews.review_text:
Absolutely delicious....I made a quick sugar, cinnamon and finely chopped walnut topping and added before baking. The bread is moist and delicious. I like the idea of substituting applesauce for some of the oil and will definitely try it that way next time.

The only thing I'm surprised about is how many people said their bread took less than 60 minutes to bake. I had to actually ADD baking time to mine....for a total of about 1 hour and 20 minutes. I used two loaf pans...I must admit that the ones I used are just a slight bit smaller than conventional loaf pans. Even so, the extra bake time was worth the wait!

attributes.source_text: The bread is moist

reviews.review_text: This was a nice change from the normal quick breads!  I made two batches of this bread to give as gifts.  The 1st batch was made exactly according to the recipe and for some reason the loaves sunk in the middle (still tasted good although a little too sweet!).  The 2nd batch I made by cutting sugar down to 1 and 1/2 cups, and replaced half the oil with applesauce - this batch rose perfectly (all batches were baked at the same time), and tasted perfect to us.  I took another reviewers advice and sprinkled the tops with cinnamon & sugar - it gave them a very lovely, extra special appearance.  Thanks!

-----Updated-----
On popular request, I've tweaked and made this recipe repeatedly now. I quadruple the apples (I use about 8 small apples per batch) and skip the nuts. Sub applesauce for oil (healthier AND tastier) and top with cinnamon & sugar. Do NOT let the dough sit for a long time -- prepare the apples before mixing the dough. The batter is so dense that it must be mixed by hand; it jammed my big stand-up mixer! Following these tips yields a flavorful, delicious apple bread; as good as any I, or anyone I've served it to, have tasted. Thank you for the recipe, Gingerbear! My family begs for it at every opportunity!

attributes.source_text: My family begs for it at every opportunity

reviews.review_text:
I made this last night and wow, it's delicious! I took the suggestions of others and used half applesauce and half oil, doubled the amount of apples (6 granny smith apples on the downhill side of fresh) and skipped the nuts. I was worried about the intense sweetness in the dough but after it baked, it was just right (and I used all white sugar since I didn't feel like packing brown sugar :) Also, I'm not into chunky-mode so I pulsed the apples a bit in the food processor to get them finely chopped.

Everybody loved it and I'm excited to make it again!

Made this twice because I thought that maybe I screwed something up the first time (and apparently I have oversized loaf pans, because it worked better when I made one loaf from this rather than two). But both times, the bread turned out really dry. The "batter" was more like an overmoist dough, and the bread, while it tasted really good, was so dry that my friends nicknamed it "scone bread." I don't know enough about tea bread recipes to be able to tweak this to make it moist, so I guess I'll have to keep looking for a good recipe Shame, thought, since it really did taste good.

WOW....I put this in the oven after supper last nite, mixed up quick and easy and 2 nice loaves.  By half time of Monday night football, the kids and I had devoured one warm loaf! I managed to hide 2 slices for myself for lunch today, BUT  I made the mistake of letting them sit on my desk and I kept picking at them until they were gone.  That was before 9am.  OMG I never thought when I looked at these just out of the oven that they would be so scrumptious.  I did sprinkle the top with cinnamon and sugar, AND I used half oil and half unsweetened applesauce and baked about 50 minutes. Three Jonathan apples gave me over 2 cups but I dumped them all in anyway.  Making 2 more loaves tonite!  Fantastic!

attributes.source_text: the kids and I had devoured one warm loaf

reviews.review_text: This is just a comment that I would like to make. The breads are in the oven so I haven't had a taste yet to rate them. The ease of this recipe is a 5-star. I love its simplicity. But here's what I ran into. I tend to follow recipes literally. After mixing the recipe EXACTLY as given, the recipe said to "pour" into pans. My dough was not pourable, it was much thicker. I had to "spread" the dough into 2 loaf pans which made me think that there must be a mistake in the recipe. I'm wondering if anyone else ran into this problem.

Ran out of baking powder so I just threw in an extra dash of baking soda. Omitted the walnuts because I didn't have any and no one in the house really eats them, used coconut oil and chopped up 2 regular size red gala apples to make the 2 cupes needed.  Would have been pretty good with 3 cups, too.  I did 1 loaf and the rest made enough for 9 cupcakes.  The loaf came out much more moist, but the cupcakes were a bit of a disappoinment.  Will just stick with the loaf next time.  The sugar and cinnamon on top made for an excellent crispy crust on top - thank you for the delicious tip!

attributes.source_text: The loaf came out much more moist
made for an excellent crispy crust on top

reviews.review_text: This apple bread is SO good. My apples came to 2 1/2 cups, and I had about 1/2 cup of leftover apple pie filling so I threw that in too. And I also substituted half of the flour amount with wheat flour to make it more healthy. The result was a wonderfully soft and moist bread which my family really enjoyed, but the texture was more of a cake like texture than bread,  I had mistakenly added 1 teaspoon of b.p. instead of just 1/4 so I guess that was one of the reasons why. But it didn't matter because the flavor was just great. Thanks for a good recipe :)

attributes.source_text: wonderfully soft and moist bread
wonderfully soft and moist bread
my family really enjoyed

reviews.review_text: Yummy!  The crispy, sweet crust along with the moist, dense interior make this a winner.  I used granny smith apples and since it said "diced", I cut into dice size pieces.  It worked out perfect.  My loaves didn't rise very high (like in the pic), but I am wondering if it is because I used 9 x 5 loaf pans.  I also needed a little bit more time than the 60 minutes and baked in glass pans.  The cinnamon flavor was perfect in this and I detected just a hint of a deliciously different flavor that I never noticed in other apple desserts...maybe the vanilla?  All in all, just fabulous!  Thanks!

items.label: Zesty Low-Fat Chicken Breasts
items.name: Zesty Low-Fat Chicken Breasts
items.description: Make and share this Zesty Low-Fat Chicken Breasts recipe from Food.com.
instructions: Put the breasts in a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Whisk remaining ingredients (except cornstarch) together until they are well blended.
Pour over the breasts.
Coat both sides of the breasts with the sauce.
Bake in 400°F oven for approx 30 minutes or until the chicken is done.
Remove breasts, keep warm.  Pour the sauce into a sauce pan stir in the cornstarch that has been mixed with a tbsp of water, bring to a boil and allow to thicken whisk constantly.
Pour over the chicken & serve.

reviews.review_text: I made this as posted except for adding a few good shakes of hot pepper flakes for heat. I also used only three chicken breasts which were really big, I just cut them in half the long way. For me, the sauce was a bit too sweet and thick, but DH loved it, hence the 5 stars. He like it so much that when he was done with his plate , he went into the kitchen and slathered a plain piece of bread with the sauce and ate it just like that! I was a little repelled but he thoroughly enjoyed it! lol! This was really easy, using things I always have on hand. Thanks for the recipe!

attributes.source_text: DH loved it

reviews.review_text: Our family LOVED this dish! Our picky 6 year-old even ate her entire chicken breast and that rarely happens. There's a fine line between zesty and spicy and this toed it perfectly. I did add a teaspoon of chopped garlic in water and I used spicy brown mustard instead of Dijon mustard since that's what I had on hand and it turned out great. It was also quick to assemble which is a God send for me. I also agree with dale!, I did not have to do anything to the sauce. It stayed on top of the chicken breasts and kind of caramelized while it was cooking. It was so good! Thanks so much for posting!

attributes.source_text: Our family LOVED this dish
Our picky 6 year-old even ate her entire chicken breast
There's a fine line between zesty and spicy and this toed it perfectly

reviews.review_text: This is the second time I've made this and I have to say, it's an ideal middle-of-the-week option for us.  The flavour is quite amazing and the chicken is *unbelievably* fork tender.  Mine hasn't needed thickening either time, as the sauce reduced nicely on its own in the oven.  My husband is profoundly anti-sauce, but even he loves this recipe!  Also, it seems to lend itself to adaptation: I mistakenly doubled the honey last night, added some vinegar to offset the additional sweetness, and it turned out just fine.  Thanks so much for posting!

reviews.review_text: I made this recipe exactly as written with one deviation: I added 1 tbsp of dried minced onion to the sauce. EXCELLENT, EXCELLENT, EXCELLENT! Not very often does a recipe come along that wows me and this one more than wow'd me. My husband thought it was delicious as well and we both agree that it is to be added to the dinner pool. I did my usual brining of the chicken breast ahead of time to ensure that is was juicy and tender. But, this is something that I do to every chicken that crosses my path. Thanks for a fantastic, flavorful and EASY recipe, Bergy.

attributes.source_text: My husband thought it was delicious as well

reviews.review_text: This was super yummy!  In an effort to reduce salt in my diet, I replaced the ketchup with heinz no added salt tomato sauce, and it still turned out beautifully.  I also used my homemade low sodium salsa.  I put the extra sauce left over on my mashed potatoes and it was sooo good -- who needs butter and salt now?  The chili power and cumin kick it up nicely, and the honey adds the perfect amount of sweetness.  Very intensly flavoured dish, with very little guilt.  Thanks!

attributes.source_text: Very intensly flavoured dish
the honey adds the perfect amount of sweetness

reviews.review_text: I really loved this but my husband says it's a high 3 or a low 4.   Based on the other reviews I used equal parts ketchup and salsa.  The salsa I had was a medium southwest style with corn and beans mixed in.  Very tasty.  I didn't have dijon so I used spicy brown mustard.  It came out great.  I served it with brown rice cooked in chicken broth and steamed string beans.  I liked the consistentcy of the sauce so I didn't thicken it.  The sauce was excellent on the rice!  Will definitely add this into our regular rotation!

I made this last night. I cooked two chicken breasts, following the scaled down recipe. I was concerned my other half wouldn`t care for it,because I used a "hot" salsa in the recipe. Surprise! surprise! He said it was excellent,and really enjoyed it.It was  quick and easy to make. Chicken was so moist and tender.  I cooked the chicken  at 400 degrees for the 30 minutes,plated them, while I thickened the sauce.  Served it with balsamic rice and chinese greens with mixed bell peppers.Looked fantastic and tasted even better. Thanks so much for this recipe.

reviews.review_text: I stumbled across this recipe when I was looking for healthy main courses.  I just happened to have all the ingredients at my house that night so...I made it.  This was very good.  Especially for being so low fat!!  Maybe because my chicken breasts were larger than others, but I had to cook mine an extra 15 minutes.  Also, I did use the cornstarch to make the remainder of the sauce thicker and it added a lot to the chicken.  Will definitely make again.

Bergy.. this chicken was AWESOME! After reading the reviews I did cut the ketchup by 1/4 c but replaced with 1/4c ore salsa and cut slits in the breasts and let marinate for 4 hrs. I also added onion, garlic, and wischester sauce to the mix. The chicken was so filled with flavor and moist. DH gobbled it up. This recipe is so easy to pull together with wonderful results. I did not need to ad cornstarch the sauce was thick enough for us. I will make again!

reviews.review_text: This was so easy and I had everything in my cabinet! I used boneless skinless thighs and they worked great. Only thing I wish is that I had doubled the sauce. I did as requested by removing the sauce and adding cornstarch, but it wasn't really necessary. It was already thick...there just wasn't a bunch left over and I had made saffron rice as a side and would have liked to have drizzled some over it. I'll definitely make it again!

attributes.source_text: It was already thick

reviews.review_text: My family and I thought this was really good! The sauce had a kick, but not too much. My seven year old ate it up with mmm's and yumm's! The chicken was really moist! I bet this would be great to make then pull apart and simmer in the sauce for tacos/burittos. Hummm...ideas.... (^_^) (2/23/09) I made this as a quesidilla!!  OMG it was good!!  I left out the chili powder & cumin and sprinkled some taco bell taco seasoning instead and cooked as directed, cooled slightly, then sliced thin.  I added the meat to the sauce (thinned out with a SMALL amt of chicken broth) in a small pan and simmered.  Then made quesidillas as normal.  (Use shredded mex. cheese and 1 slice of american singles) YUMMY YA'LL!

reviews.review_text: Absolutely yummy, and so easy and inexpensive! Made this for dinner last night and the hubby and I loved it! The only thing I changed was spicy brown mustard as I had no dijon on hand. Also, I used homemade garden fresh, medium-hot salsa that was a gift from a friend, and no-fructose ketchup to make it even more healthy. Had to cook for 30 min as the chicken breasts I had were very large, but it still came out nice and juicy and perfectly flavored. Will definitely make again!!!

reviews.review_text: DH and I both thought this was a definite make-again chicken dish. I didn't have quite enough honey so I added a bit of sugar. I did use the cumin and added a sprinkle of garlic powder too. Only other change was to cut each breast into 3 pieces, poured the sauce overtop (which I food-processed to get rid of any chunks), baked in a covered casserole dish at 375 degrees for 40 minutes, uncovered for the last 15 minutes. Great recipe, thanks!

My 11 year old said 5 stars the best nothing can beat it! I couldn't say it any better myself. We are a family of 8 and we all loved it! Thanks so much for such a good easy supper. I made this with skinless chicken bottoms rubbed with garlic poured the sauce over it baked 400 for 1 hour did not have to add corn starch. Served the chicken with tortilla chips covered with salsa and baked rice. Delicious recipe we will use over and over again.

reviews.review_text: I made this chicken this afternoon and thought the smell was wonderful while cooking.  It was nice and moist and had a very unique flavor.  I followed the recipe exactly as written and did use the cumin.  At first I wasn't sure I liked it very much, but the more I ate, the better it got.  I had more several times throughout the day and now I am sure that this is a real keeper.  Thank you very much.

attributes.source_text: It was nice and moist

reviews.review_text: Made this last night using only 2 chkn brst and followed previous advice baking at 375 for 30mins. Did not cut back on the sauce ingredients and so glad - could have used more! The chkn was so moist and the mix of flavors were delicious! Did not need to use the cornstarch - sauce was just fine. Used the tiny bit of leftovers today in my salad - diddn't need any dressing! This recipe has earned a place in my regular rotation!!

attributes.source_text: The chkn was so moist

reviews.review_text: What a quick recipe to make and it tastes wonderful.  I made this for DS and I tonight for dinner and we loved it.  I did halve the recipe so we each had one and one left over to split for lunch tomorrow in a sandwich.  We both really liked the sauce, yummy.  I served this with some rice and DS liked to mix his rice with the sauce.  Thank you Bergy for sharing this great little recipe with me  and my family.  Delicious.
